EDCS-28000396.translation: I ask you, make Marcus Samellius Modestus, worthy of the republic, an aedile.
EDCS-28000396.summary: This inscription is a public plea to elect Marcus Samellius Modestus as aedile, highlighting his suitability for public office.

EDCS-28000403.summary: This inscription names Marcellus, indicating his candidacy or qualification for the position of aedile.

EDCS-28000404.summary: This inscription names Casellius, indicating his candidacy or qualification for the position of aedile.

EDCS-28000406.translation: I ask you, make Lucius Naevius Rufus, a man of [M...], an aedile.
EDCS-28000406.summary: This inscription is a public plea to elect Lucius Naevius Rufus as aedile, mentioning a patron or descriptor 'M.'.

EDCS-28000407.translation: I ask you, make Popidius Secundus an aedile.
EDCS-28000407.summary: This inscription is a public plea to elect Popidius Secundus as aedile.

EDCS-28000412.summary: This inscription names Samellius, indicating his candidacy or qualification for the position of aedile.

EDCS-28000413.summary: This inscription names Albicius, indicating his candidacy or qualification for the position of aedile.

EDCS-28000415.translation: I ask you to make Albucius aedile.
EDCS-28000415.summary: This is a request for the election of Albucius as aedile, likely from a public notice or informal plea.

EDCS-28000416.translation: The woodworkers and wagon-makers ask you to make Marcellus aedile, along with Lassi and Crimio and Gaius Nisio Infantio, everywhere.
EDCS-28000416.summary: This inscription records a plea from the wood and wagon guilds for the election of Marcellus as aedile, mentioning other associated individuals.

EDCS-28000421.translation: The farmers ask you to make Marcus Casellus Marcellus aedile, Fisinerficus.
EDCS-28000421.summary: This is a plea from farmers for the election of Marcus Casellus Marcellus as aedile.

EDCS-28000422.translation: I ask you to make Casellius and Albucius good, worthy men for the Republic as aediles, Secanis[--] and all [?].
EDCS-28000422.summary: This inscription urges the election of Casellius and Albucius as aediles, describing them as worthy of public office.

EDCS-28000425.summary: This inscription simply names Gaius Sallustius, possibly as a candidate or a person of importance.

EDCS-28000426.translation: Novici the innkeeper makes Marcellus and Celsus aediles.
EDCS-28000426.summary: This inscription states that the innkeeper Novici is responsible for the election of Marcellus and Celsus as aediles.

EDCS-28000429.summary: This inscription simply names Marcus Samellius, possibly as a candidate or a person of importance.

EDCS-28000437.translation: Gaius Gavius Rufus asks for Marcus Holconius.
EDCS-28000437.summary: This inscription records a request from Gaius Gavius Rufus concerning Marcus Holconius, possibly related to an election or appointment.

EDCS-28000440.translation: I ask you to make Gaius Cuspius Pansa aedile.
EDCS-28000440.summary: This is a request for the election of Gaius Cuspius Pansa as aedile, likely from a public notice or informal plea.

EDCS-28000441.summary: This inscription nominates or supports Casellius for the position of aedile.

EDCS-28000442.summary: This inscription records the name Quintus Numisius.

EDCS-28000446.translation: Euodus asks for Pansam to be made aedile.
EDCS-28000446.summary: This inscription records a request for Pansam to be appointed aedile, made by Euodus.

EDCS-28000447.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Pansam as aedile.

EDCS-28000450.translation: Marcellus, worthy of public office, as aedile.
EDCS-28000450.summary: This inscription recommends Marcellus for the position of aedile, describing him as worthy of public office.

EDCS-28000451.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Marcus Casellius Marcellus as aedile.

EDCS-28000455.translation: Marcellus asks for [him] to be made aedile.
EDCS-28000455.summary: This inscription records a request for Marcellus to be appointed aedile.

EDCS-28000456.translation: I ask you to make Pansam aedile, and Popidius.
EDCS-28000456.summary: This inscription is a plea to appoint Pansam and Popidius as aediles.

EDCS-28000457.translation: I ask you to make Gaius Calventius, duumvir, and Sittius Magnus.
EDCS-28000457.summary: This inscription is a plea to appoint Gaius Calventius as duumvir and Sittius Magnus.

EDCS-28000458.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Marcus Casellius Marcellus as aedile.

EDCS-28000460.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Casellius as aedile.

EDCS-28000463.translation: Vettius asks for Samellius to be made aedile.
EDCS-28000463.summary: A private request, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, for Samellius to be elected aedile.

EDCS-28000464.summary: A simple designation, possibly a label or a notice, identifying Pansam as an aedile.

EDCS-28000465.summary: A simple designation, possibly a label or a notice, identifying Casellius as an aedile.

EDCS-28000466.translation: I ask you to make Casellius aedile.
EDCS-28000466.summary: A private request, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, for Casellius to be elected aedile.

EDCS-28000469.translation: Fidelis Ebrli makes Marcus Casellius a worthy and suitable aedile for the state.
EDCS-28000469.summary: A declaration of support, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, endorsing Marcus Casellius for the office of aedile.

EDCS-28000470.translation: I ask you to make C(aius) Marcellus, a good and worthy man, suitable for the state as aedile.
EDCS-28000470.summary: A private request, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, for C(aius) Marcellus to be elected aedile.

EDCS-28000471.translation: C(aius) Cusp(ius) Pansam, worthy and suitable for the state as aedile.
EDCS-28000471.summary: A declaration of support, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, endorsing C(aius) Cusp(ius) Pansam for the office of aedile.

EDCS-28000475.summary: A designation of Casellius as aedile, with 'Venus' possibly indicating a patron, a location, or a personal connection.

EDCS-28000488.translation: He asks for Marcellus to be made aedile.
EDCS-28000488.summary: A private request, likely from a wall painting or informal inscription, for Marcellus to be elected aedile.

EDCS-28000490.summary: A simple designation, possibly a label or a notice, identifying C(aius) Cusp(ius) Pansam as an aedile.

EDCS-28000491.summary: This is a dedication to Numerius Popidius, likely on a monument or tomb, whose date is not specified.

EDCS-28000492.translation: I urge you to make Gaius Cuspius Pansas an aedile worthy of the state.
EDCS-28000492.summary: This is a plea to voters to elect Gaius Cuspius Pansas as aedile, portraying him as a candidate deserving of public office, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-28000496.translation: I urge you to make Cuspius Pansas, a young man, honest and worthy of the state, an aedile.
EDCS-28000496.summary: This inscription urges voters to elect Cuspius Pansas as aedile, emphasizing his youth, integrity, and worthiness for public office, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-28000500.translation: I urge you to make Holconius Priscus an aedile worthy of the state; he is worthy.
EDCS-28000500.summary: This inscription advocates for the election of Holconius Priscus as aedile, asserting his worthiness for the role, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-28100001.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Ariecinus Onesimus made this for his deserving patron, Ariecinus Hermes.
EDCS-28100001.summary: This is a tomb inscription by Ariecinus Onesimus for his well-deserving patron Ariecinus Hermes, dedicated to the gods of the underworld, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100002.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aristida, son of Artemidorus, from Rhodes, made this for himself and for his well-deserving wife Petronia Hygia, with whom he lived for 39 years and 11 months, and for his most dutiful son Petronius Dexter, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-28100002.summary: This tomb inscription is dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed by Aristida, a Rhodian, for himself, his wife Petronia Hygia, their son Petronius Dexter, and their freedmen and descendants, indicating a family burial plot from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100003.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Arrius Herax made this for his excellent patroness Arria Moschis, who deserved well.
EDCS-28100003.summary: This tomb inscription by Gaius Arrius Herax is for his excellent patroness Arria Moschis, dedicated to the gods of the underworld, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100004.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Arsinous lived for 25 years.
EDCS-28100004.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Arsinous, stating the deceased's name and age at death, dedicated to the gods of the underworld, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100005.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus hic iacet exanimis puer nomine Atenio qui vixit annis XVIII mensis sic VIII diebus VIII Aurelius Crescens |(centurio) cohortis III vigilum Iulia Manteiane pratroni carrissimo alumno fecerunt\n
EDCS-28100005.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Here lies lifeless a boy named Atenius, who lived 18 years, 8 months, and 8 days. Aurelius Crescens, centurion of the 3rd cohort of vigiles, and Iulia Manteiane made this for their dearest patron and foster-son.
EDCS-28100005.summary: This tomb inscription is a dedication by Aurelius Crescens, a centurion, and Iulia Manteiane for their beloved foster-son Atenius, who died at the age of 18 years, 8 months, and 8 days, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100006.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Atilia Artemisia dedicated this tomb intended for Marcellus Secundus. Flavia Eutycheti gave an offering of oil.
EDCS-28100006.summary: This tomb inscription records a dedication by Atilia Artemisia for Marcellus Secundus, with Flavia Eutycheti making a separate offering, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-28100007.translation: To the departed spirits. [---]a Statilia [to her son St]atiliano, who lived 10 years, 3 months, 3 days. [---] who lived 7 months, 12 days.
EDCS-28100007.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Statilia and her son Statiliano, detailing their ages at death.

EDCS-28100008.translation: To the departed spirits. Attia Psyche and Gaius Attius Alexander, freedpersons, made this monument for themselves, their freedpersons, freedwomen, and their descendants; it shall not follow an heir and is not for sale; entrusted to their good faith, nor shall a trustee have access. In front 18 feet, in depth 38 feet.
EDCS-28100008.summary: A funerary monument inscription by freedpersons Attia Psyche and Gaius Attius Alexander, establishing rules for inheritance and sale of the property.

EDCS-28100009.translation: To the departed spirits. Atticius Procleianus to his son Atticius Hilarus, who lived 1 year, 9 months, 15 days.
EDCS-28100009.summary: A funerary inscription by Atticius Procleianus for his son Atticius Hilarus, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-28100011.translation: To the departed spirits. Aufidia Secunda made this for her most excellent patron, Lucius Aufidius Paternus.
EDCS-28100011.summary: A funerary dedication by Aufidia Secunda to her patron Lucius Aufidius Paternus.

EDCS-28100012.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Alexander lived 30 years, 8 months. Publius Petronius Pelagius made this for his incomparable friend.
EDCS-28100012.summary: A funerary inscription by Publius Petronius Pelagius for his friend Marcus Aurelius Alexander, noting his age at death.

EDCS-28100013.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Athenio to his incomparable, deserving wife Sabina.
EDCS-28100013.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Aurelius Athenio to his wife Sabina.

EDCS-28100014.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Calocaerus [---] to Titus Aelius Felicissimus [---] to Malia Blunda, who [lived ---]. If anyone [---] in this monument [---] 10,000 sesterces for the treasury of the Roman people. In front [---] feet.
EDCS-28100014.summary: A funerary inscription with details about the deceased and a penalty for disturbing the monument, possibly dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-28100015.translation: If anyone places or introduces a corpse of an outsider into this sarcophagus, a penalty of 20,000 sesterces for the treasury of the people. To the departed spirits. Aurelius Irenion, also called Ammonianus, and Aurelia Arpocratiana, siblings.
EDCS-28100015.summary: An inscription on a sarcophagus that stipulates a penalty for unauthorized burials and also serves as a dedication to the deceased siblings Aurelius Irenion and Aurelia Arpocratiana.

EDCS-28100016.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Axius Crispus, son of Gaius Axius, made this for his freedwoman Axiaes Nicene, and for himself, his freedwoman Axia Margarita, and their freedpersons, freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-28100016.summary: A funerary monument inscription by Gaius Axius Crispus for his freedwoman Axiaes Nicene, himself, and other family members and freedpersons, with a clause against it following an heir.

EDCS-28100017.translation: To the departed spirits. Myron made this for his brother Basso, well-deserving, most dutiful.
EDCS-28100017.summary: A funerary dedication by Myron for his brother Basso.

EDCS-28100018.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Betiliena Antiochis made this for her deserving husband, Publius Betilienus Synegdemus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-28100018.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a wife for her husband and their descendants.

EDCS-28100019.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Publius Betilienus Synegdemus and Betiliena Antiochis, under the care of Marcus Cosconius Hyginus.
EDCS-28100019.summary: This inscription records the funerary care provided by Marcus Cosconius Hyginus for Publius Betilienus Synegdemus and Betiliena Antiochis.

EDCS-28100020.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucius Caecilius Victor donatum sibi pavimentum purum virgineum monumenti huius a Perella sic Hieronide et Anniis Vitale et Decia in quo sarcophaga nova sumptibus suis inst<r>uxit fecitque sibi et Caeciliae Hygiae coniugi suae et libertis libertabusque posterisque eorum\n
EDCS-28100020.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Caecilius Victor, having made and furnished the pure and virgin floor of this monument with new sarcophagi at his own expense, made it for himself and for his wife Caecilia Hygia and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-28100020.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Caecilius Victor for himself, his wife, and their descendants, including the installation of new sarcophagi and a decorated floor.

EDCS-28100021.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Maxima made this for her son Socrates and grandson, from the estate of Aurelia.
EDCS-28100021.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Caecilia Maxima for her son and grandson, funded by the estate of Aurelia.

EDCS-28100022.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Calpurnia Ptolemais, daughter of Lucius, made this for herself and for her husband Lucius Calpurnius Ianuarius and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-28100022.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Calpurnia Ptolemais for herself, her husband, and their descendants, with a clause preventing inheritance by others.

EDCS-28100023.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Tiberius Claudius Arphocration, in a plot of land granted to himself by Julia Successa.
EDCS-28100023.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot granted by Julia Successa to Tiberius Claudius Arphocration.

EDCS-28100024.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Epagathus and Claudia Olympias made this for her husband, who lived with her for 52 years.
EDCS-28100024.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Claudia Olympias for her husband, Tiberius Claudius Epagathus, noting their 52 years of marriage.

EDCS-28100025.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Eumenes, freedman of the Emperor, for himself and for his daughters Claudia Phoebe and Fadia Tethis, and for his son Claudius Phoebus, and for Julia Heuresis, his wife, and their descendants.
EDCS-28100025.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Tiberius Claudius Eumenes, a freedman of the emperor, for his family members.

EDCS-28100026.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Eutychus made this for his deserving wife, Claudia Memnonis, and for himself, their children, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument will not pass to an heir. In front 15 feet, in the plot 15 feet.
EDCS-28100026.summary: This funerary monument was created by Tiberius Claudius Eutychus for his wife, children, and descendants, with specific dimensions and a non-inheritance clause.

EDCS-28100028.translation: Octavius Felix and Iunia Maxima and Iunia [---] purchased for themselves in a plot granted by Iulius Zoticus and by Iulia Artemidora, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-28100028.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a burial plot by Octavius Felix, Iunia Maxima, and Iunia [---] from Iulius Zoticus and Iulia Artemidora.

EDCS-28100029.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Herennius Secundus and Cornelia Secunda made this for their most devoted daughter, Herennia Procla, who lived for two years, eight months, and twenty days.
EDCS-28100029.summary: A funerary epitaph for Herennia Procla, set up by her parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100030.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ianuaria Chreste CI Haore Cai fili- HAE Chaerea annos IIII menses V\n
EDCS-28100030.translation: To the departed spirits. Ianuaria Chreste, daughter of Cai Haores, and HAE Chaerea, lived for four years, five months.
EDCS-28100030.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Ianuaria Chreste, with parentage specified, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100032.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a name or a funerary dedication, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100034.translation: Samus, son of Samius, made this for Maecenia Crusopolis.
EDCS-28100034.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maecenia Crusopolis, dedicated by Samus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100035.translation: To the departed spirits. Kania Olympias made this for her most beloved husband, Lucius Malius Natalis, who was placed here, lived for ten months and twenty-nine days.
EDCS-28100035.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Malius Natalis, set up by his wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100036.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Orbius Scapula, an evocatus of Augustus, made this for Onesimus, his excellent slave.
EDCS-28100036.summary: A funerary epitaph for the slave Onesimus, dedicated by his master Marcus Orbius Scapula, an imperial official, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100038.translation: To the departed spirits. Pater Euhodus, his son Euhodianus, his daughter Euhodia, and Philete made this for themselves and for Ostorius Euhodus and his children, and their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-28100038.summary: A family funerary epitaph dedicating a tomb for multiple individuals, including Pater Euhodus and Ostorius Euhodus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100039.translation: To the departed spirits. May the earth be light upon you, Parthenia, my excellent soul. She lived about eighteen years. Marcus Antonius Corymbus made this in the second half of the month of August, when Servianus was consul.
EDCS-28100039.summary: A funerary epitaph for Parthenia, set up by Marcus Antonius Corymbus, with a consular date likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28100040.text_edition: \n Petronia Erotis sibi et Tito Flavio Pharnaci karissimo coniugi suo fecit et is quibus id ius possi dendi testamemto suo legavit posterisque eorum libertis libertabusque in fronte pedes in agro pedes XXV et Zethioni Artemidori filio Rhodio itum ambitum donaverunt\n
EDCS-28100040.translation: Petronia Erotis made this for herself and for her dearest husband, Titus Flavius Pharnaces, and for those to whom he bequeathed the right of burial in his will, and for their descendants, freedmen, and freedwomen; they donated twenty-five feet in front and twenty-five feet in the field, and gifted the surrounding area to Zethion, son of Artemidorus of Rhodes.
EDCS-28100040.summary: A complex funerary dedication by Petronia Erotis for herself, her husband, and others, including a land donation, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100041.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Petronius Andronicus and Petronia Maritima made this for their most devoted daughter, Petronia Stolidis, who lived 20 years, 22 days, and 4 hours.
EDCS-28100041.summary: A funerary epitaph for Petronia Stolidis, set up by her parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100042.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Plautius Primitibus and Iunia Hieronis, having been granted space by the two freedmen of Iulius Zoticus and Aetus, heirs of Iulius Prosdocimus, made two sarcophagi for themselves, and for their most beloved son Plautius Mascellio, who lived for 3 years, 4 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-28100042.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of two sarcophagi by Aulus Plautius Primitibus and Iunia Hieronis for themselves and their son, with the space granted by freedmen.

EDCS-28100043.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Addas made this monument for himself and his wife Plotia Areninenca, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument will not follow an heir.
EDCS-28100043.summary: A funerary epitaph where Lucius Addas dedicates a monument for himself, his wife, and their descendants, stating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-28100044.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For their most dutiful daughter Pomponia Felicia. Pomponia Optata and her father Marcus Caecilius Euodus made this; she lived for 3 years, 8 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-28100044.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Pomponia Optata and Marcus Caecilius Euodus for their daughter, Pomponia Felicia, who died at a young age.

EDCS-28100046.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For my dearest husband. Messia Candida made this for herself, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for their ancestors; the space was granted by Gavinius Crispus and Eutyches and by the two Antonii, Iulianus and Polio, with free ingress and egress.
EDCS-28100046.summary: This funerary inscription records Messia Candida dedicating a tomb for her husband, herself, and their freed dependents, with the space granted by several individuals.

EDCS-28100047.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Mindius Diogae, Iulia Zoe provided for the erection of this tomb for her well-deserving husband, and for herself, and her family, and their descendants.
EDCS-28100047.summary: A funerary epitaph where Iulia Zoe arranges for a tomb for her husband Lucius Mindius Diogae, and for herself and her descendants.

EDCS-28100048.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaurus. Terentia Secunda and Gaurus, son of Gaurus, made this for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-28100048.summary: This funerary inscription records Terentia Secunda and Gaurus dedicating a tomb to their son, also named Gaurus.

EDCS-28100049.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Glycera, the slave woman.
EDCS-28100049.summary: A brief funerary inscription dedicated to a slave woman named Glycera.

EDCS-28100050.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Munatius Licinianus and Curtia Gemella, who is also Flavia. For their most dutiful parents, their son Marcus Munatius Marcianus made this.
EDCS-28100050.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Munatius Marcianus dedicating a monument to his parents, Marcus Munatius Licinianus and Curtia Gemella (also known as Flavia).

EDCS-28100051.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Titus Munatius Proclus, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe. Iulia Procla, daughter of Tiberius, his mother, made this for her most dutiful son; he lived 6 years and 14 days.
EDCS-28100051.summary: A funerary inscription by a mother, Iulia Procla, for her son Titus Munatius Proclus, who died at the age of six.

EDCS-28100053.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Murdia Ampelidis. With the care of the freedmen Ampliatus and Erotus, and the freedwomen Ampelide and Nice.
EDCS-28100053.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb set up for Murdia Ampelidis, with arrangements managed by her freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-28100054.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gaius Marcius Abascantus the younger, who lived 29 years, 2 months, 20 days. Gaius Marcius Abascantus and Marcia Helpis made this for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-28100054.summary: This is a tombstone set up by parents for their deceased son, Gaius Marcius Abascantus the younger.

EDCS-28100055.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gaius Marcius Irenaeus, who lived 16 years and 45 days. His father, Gaius Marcius Nymphius, made this.
EDCS-28100055.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a father for his deceased son, Gaius Marcius Irenaeus.

EDCS-28100056.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Marcius Olympus made this for his most dutiful daughter, Marcia Olympias.
EDCS-28100056.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a father for his deceased daughter, Marcia Olympias.

EDCS-28100058.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcia (?) Donatus [---
EDCS-28100058.summary: This is a tombstone fragment, likely dedicated to a person named Donatus, part of the Marcius family, with incomplete information.

EDCS-28100059.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Felicissima, who lived 14 years, 4 months, 9 days. Felicissimus made this for his most dutiful sister.
EDCS-28100059.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a brother for his deceased sister, Felicissima.

EDCS-28100060.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Frimus Caesaris nostri servus fecit Ius<ti>no vernae suo bene merenti qui vixit annos II menses VII dies VI\n
EDCS-28100060.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Frimus, slave of our Caesar, made this for Iustinus, his own freedman, who deserved well, who lived 2 years, 7 months, 6 days.
EDCS-28100060.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a slave for his freedman, indicating a familial or close relationship within a household likely connected to the imperial family.

EDCS-28100061.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---] Flavius (?) Callist[us (?)
EDCS-28100061.summary: This is a tombstone fragment with a partial name, likely Flavius Callistus, and incomplete dedication information.

EDCS-28100062.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Daphine and Titus Flavius Severus made this for their deserving wife and father, Titus Flavius Felix, freedman of Titus Flavius Aug(ustus).
EDCS-28100062.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a wife and son for their deceased husband and father, Titus Flavius Felix, a freedman of an imperial patron.

EDCS-28100066.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulius Apollinaris made this for his sweetest son, Gavius Iulius Paulinus, who deserved well. Iunia Gallite conceded (?) the place for (a period) of 7 years.
EDCS-28100066.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a father for his son, with a note about the concession of the burial plot.

EDCS-28100067.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Iulius Philippus made this for his freedman, Iason, who deserved well.
EDCS-28100067.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a patron for his deceased freedman, Iason.

EDCS-28100069.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Tyche made this. Flavius Thinnus.
EDCS-28100069.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavius Thinnus for Flavia Tyche.

EDCS-28100071.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Fulcinius Abascantus, with his freedman Fulcinius Hermippus, each contributing half, made this for Fulcinia Callistes, and for himself, and for his daughter Fulcinia Bassilla, and for his wife Fulcinia Daphnis, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. This monument will not be followed by an external heir of the family. This monument will not be followed by an heir.
EDCS-28100071.summary: A complex funerary monument set up by Publius Fulcinius Abascantus and his freedman for family members, with clauses to prevent an external heir from inheriting it.

EDCS-28100072.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Gabinius Longinus and Annia Epictesis made this for their most devoted son, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-28100072.summary: A funerary dedication by Publius Gabinius Longinus and Annia Epictesis for their son, who died at age 16.

EDCS-28100073.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Publius Gabinius Annianus. Annia Ionice for her dearest brother.
EDCS-28100073.summary: A funerary dedication by Annia Ionice for her brother, Publius Gabinius Annianus.

EDCS-28100074.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Galgestius Helius, from a pure place bought from Valeria Trophime, made this little shrine for himself and his family, joined to the wall, on the right side upon entering, in which are 14 jars, in addition to the jar which Trophime donated to Vitalis Galgestius; from which I have donated one jar as a gift to Pomponius Chrysoplus.
EDCS-28100074.summary: A funerary dedication for Caius Galgestius Helius and his family, describing the construction of a burial shrine with a specific number of jars and a donation of one jar.

EDCS-28200171.summary: A tombstone or dedication for Lucius Numisius.

EDCS-28300194.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, the Optimus Maximus Princeps. The decurions and citizens of Surrentum, with collected funds.
EDCS-28300194.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to Emperor Hadrian by the town council and citizens of Surrentum, likely dating to his fifth tribunician power and third consulship.

EDCS-28300195.translation: The courier of Claudia Capitolina lived 29 years.
EDCS-28300195.summary: A funerary inscription for the courier of Claudia Capitolina, who died at age 29.

EDCS-28300196.translation: Chila, freedwoman of Augustus, lived 65 years.
EDCS-28300196.summary: A funerary inscription for Chila, a freedwoman of Augustus, who died at age 65.

EDCS-28300197.translation: Crispus, slave of Augustus, lived 40 years.
EDCS-28300197.summary: A funerary inscription for Crispus, a slave of Augustus, who died at age 40.

EDCS-28300199.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Germo, freedman of Augustus, lived 85 years.
EDCS-28300199.summary: A funerary dedication for Germo, a freedman of Augustus, who died at age 85.

EDCS-28300200.translation: Ianuarius, freedman of the Emperor, lived 1 year.
EDCS-28300200.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Ianuarius, a freedman of the Emperor, at the age of one year.

EDCS-28300201.translation: For Iulia Tertia, the Nymph, whom Nympheros, freedman of the Emperor, greatly esteemed; she lived 25 years.
EDCS-28300201.summary: A tombstone set up by Nympheros, a freedman of the Emperor, for his well-deserving wife Iulia Tertia, who died at 25.

EDCS-28300203.translation: Nicephor, freedman of the Emperor, lived 75 years.
EDCS-28300203.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Nicephor, a freedman of the Emperor, at the age of 75.

EDCS-28300204.translation: Onesimus, freedman of the Emperor, lived 80 years.
EDCS-28300204.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Onesimus, a freedman of the Emperor, at the age of 80.

EDCS-28300205.translation: Primigenius, freedman of Philodespotus the Emperor, lived 11 years.
EDCS-28300205.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Primigenius, a freedman of Philodespotus the Emperor, at the age of 11 years.

EDCS-28300207.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Abascantus at the age of 4 years.

EDCS-28300209.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Claudia Tyche at the age of 40 years.

EDCS-28300210.translation: To Primigenia. Tiberius Claudius Abascantus for his well-deserving wife, lived 40 years.
EDCS-28300210.summary: A tombstone set up by Tiberius Claudius Abascantus for his wife Primigenia, who died at 40 years of age.

EDCS-28300211.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Claudius Abascantus at the age of 50 years.

EDCS-28300212.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Tiberius Claudius Stephanus at the age of 15 years.

EDCS-28300213.translation: Hilarus, son of Plocamus, lived 5 years.
EDCS-28300213.summary: This is a tombstone for Hilarus, son of Plocamus, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-28300214.summary: This is a tombstone for Iulia Fortunata, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-28300217.translation: Plocamus, son of Plocamus, lived 6 years.
EDCS-28300217.summary: This is a tombstone for Plocamus, son of Plocamus, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-28300219.summary: This is a tombstone for Elemonia Iusta, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-28300220.summary: This is a tombstone for Flavius Galata, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-28300221.summary: This is a tombstone for Gellia Soteri, who died at the age of 29.

EDCS-28300222.translation: To the departed spirits, Iunia Myrsine lived 65 years.
EDCS-28300222.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits for Iunia Myrsine, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-28300223.summary: This is a tombstone for Neoptolemus, identified as a 'collactius' (shared nursling), who died at the age of 9.

EDCS-28300224.translation: To the departed spirits, [he/she] made [this] for Pontia Auxonia, a well-deserving wife.
EDCS-28300224.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits by an unnamed individual for his/her deserving wife, Pontia Auxonia.

EDCS-28300226.translation: To the departed spirits, Valeria Epiteusis made [this] for her husband Zoticus.
EDCS-28300226.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits by Valeria Epiteusis for her husband Zoticus.

EDCS-28300269.translation: Claudia Aster of Jerusalem, a captive, managed the affairs. Tiberius Claudius Proculus(?), freedman of the Emperor, I beg you, by law, do not remove my monument; take care of it. She lived 25 years.
EDCS-28300269.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Aster, a captive from Jerusalem, setting conditions for her tombstone and recording her age at death.

EDCS-28300278.translation: To the Divine Shades. For her son T(itus) Flavius Lucrio, and for herself and her kin and freedmen and their descendants.
EDCS-28300278.summary: A funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) by an unknown person for her son T. Flavius Lucrio, and for herself and her family and descendants.

EDCS-28300280.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Iulia Amandas, wife, and Caecilia Cara, aged 13, and Quintus Caecilius Sentianus, aged 9. Quintus Caecilius Sentianus, the father, made [this] for his most cherished wife and most devoted sons.
EDCS-28300280.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Amandas, Caecilia Cara, and Quintus Caecilius Sentianus, commissioned by the father and husband, Quintus Caecilius Sentianus.

EDCS-28300281.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Iulia Apollonia, daughter of Lucius, most devoted mother. Gaius Annius Proculus and Gaius Nymphidius Ogulnianus made [this] for themselves and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, in the front 25 feet, in the land 25 feet.
EDCS-28300281.summary: A funerary dedication for Iulia Apollonia, daughter of Lucius, by Gaius Annius Proculus and Gaius Nymphidius Ogulnianus, who also provided for themselves and their descendants, with dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-28300282.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Iulia Apollonia, daughter of Lucius, most devoted mother. Gaius Annius Proculus and Gaius Nymphidius Ogulnianus.
EDCS-28300282.summary: A funerary dedication for Iulia Apollonia, daughter of Lucius, by Gaius Annius Proculus and Gaius Nymphidius Ogulnianus.

EDCS-28300283.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Iulia Arsinoe. Iulia Asia made [this] for her patroness who deserved well of her, and for herself and her kin and freedmen and their descendants, added, in the front 25 and a half feet, in the land 21 feet.
EDCS-28300283.summary: A funerary dedication for Iulia Arsinoe by her freedwoman Iulia Asia, who also provided for herself and her family, with dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-28300284.translation: Iulia Arsinoe made [this] for herself and her kin and freedmen and their descendants, in the land 16 feet, in the front 13 feet.
EDCS-28300284.summary: A funerary dedication by Iulia Arsinoe for herself and her family, with dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-28300285.translation: To the Divine [Shades]. For Iulia [---]. Gaius Julius [---] for his wife [---] and for himself and [---]
EDCS-28300285.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) for Iulia [---], possibly by her husband Gaius Julius [---].

EDCS-28300287.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Iulia Paullina, a wife who deserved well. Sextus Iulius Armenius made [this].
EDCS-28300287.summary: A funerary dedication by Sextus Iulius Armenius for his deserving wife, Iulia Paullina.

EDCS-28300288.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulia Phronime made [this] for her husband who deserved well of her.
EDCS-28300288.summary: A funerary dedication by Iulia Phronime for her deserving husband.

EDCS-28300291.translation: To Iulia Procula, daughter of Tiberius, who lived 29 years, 11 months. Her mother Munatia Helpis made this for her most devoted daughter.
EDCS-28300291.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Procula, set up by her mother.

EDCS-28300297.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Iunius Gl[---] made this for himself and for Iunia Trophime, his patroness, his deserving benefactor, and [---]
EDCS-28300297.summary: A funerary inscription likely for Marcus Iunius Gl[---] and his patroness, recording a family burial plot.

EDCS-28300298.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Iulianus made this for his well-deserving wife, Iunia Chelidon, and for their son, Iunius Crescens.
EDCS-28300298.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caius Iulius Iulianus for his wife and son.

EDCS-28300299.translation: To the departed spirits. Iunia Primitiba made this for her relative Sextilia Maxima, and for her relative and excellent husband Annio Maximo, to whom I will give thanks as long as I live.
EDCS-28300299.summary: A funerary inscription by Iunia Primitiba for her relative Sextilia Maxima and her husband Annio Maximo.

EDCS-28300301.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Liburcius Marinus, the father, made this for his son Titus Liburcius Marcius Marinus, the best, who lived 26 years, 2 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-28300301.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Titus Liburcius Marinus for his deceased son.

EDCS-28300302.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Licinius Repentinus made this for his most devoted son, Quintus Licinius Primitivus, who lived 5 years and 30 days.
EDCS-28300302.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Licinius Repentinus for his young son.

EDCS-28300303.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Valerius Celer made this for his dearest wife, Licinia Fortunata, and for himself, and for his descendants and their posterity.
EDCS-28300303.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Valerius Celer for his wife, himself, and their descendants.

EDCS-28300306.translation: To the departed spirits of Titus Flavius Nearchus.
EDCS-28300306.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Titus Flavius Nearchus.

EDCS-28300307.text_edition: \n Tito Flavio Augusti liberto Pharnaci fecit Petronia Erotis carissimo viro suo\n
EDCS-28300307.translation: Petronia Erotis made this for her dearest husband, Titus Flavius Augusti liberto Pharnaces.
EDCS-28300307.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Petronia Erotis for her husband, Titus Flavius Pharnaces.

EDCS-28300308.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Polytimus made this for himself and for his dearest wife Posidonia Tertia, and for his children Flavius Polytimus and Flavia Tertia, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their posterity; also Marcus Pistorius Thallus made this monument for himself and his posterity, placed on the right side upon entering, and for Antonia Onesima, his wife.
EDCS-28300308.summary: A complex funerary inscription by Titus Flavius Polytimus for his family and for Marcus Pistorius Thallus and his family.

EDCS-28300309.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Ulpius Proclianus, father, made this for his most devoted son, Titus Flavius Proclus, who lived 21 years, 11 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-28300309.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Proclus, set up by his father, Marcus Ulpius Proclianus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300310.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Saturninus, freedman of the emperor, dedicated this for Estaberius Hilarus and Caledia Aphrodite and their children, and their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, and he commands that his own heir not be troubled.
EDCS-28300310.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Flavius Saturninus for a family and their descendants, possibly from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-28300313.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Alexander, father, made this for Flavia Efia.
EDCS-28300313.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Efia, made by her father Titus Flavius Alexander, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300314.translation: To Flavia Lamyra, who lived 25 years. Gaius Julius Spiclus permitted the place, which had been granted, to be possessed with access and entrance.
EDCS-28300314.summary: An epitaph for Flavia Lamyra, granting rights of passage and access to her burial plot, set up by Gaius Julius Spiclus.

EDCS-28300315.translation: To the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Primigenius, son of Tiberius Claudius, made this. His son Tiberius Claudius Quintilianus, his stepson Aulus Rutilius Pudens, and his freedmen made this from their own shares.
EDCS-28300315.summary: A funerary monument funded by Tiberius Claudius Primigenius' son, stepson, and freedmen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300316.translation: To the departed spirits. Claudius Sotericus Junior, who lived four years, six months, and twenty-one days.
EDCS-28300316.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudius Sotericus Junior, a young child, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300317.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tiberius Claudius Telesphorus.
EDCS-28300317.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Telesphorus.

EDCS-28300318.translation: To the departed spirits. For his daughter Tattia. Tiberius Claudius [---] and Tattia [---] made this from their own shares. From Quintus Septius Abascantus, permitted to have access.
EDCS-28300318.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Tattia, her daughter, Tiberius Claudius, and Quintus Septius Abascantus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300319.translation: To the departed spirits. For Claudia Eumenia.
EDCS-28300319.summary: A brief funerary epitaph for Claudia Eumenia.

EDCS-28300321.translation: To the departed spirits. For Claudia Hammonilla. Claudius Severinus and Claudia Hammonilia made this for their most devoted father.
EDCS-28300321.summary: A funerary monument for Claudia Hammonilla and Tiberius Claudius Severus, made by their son Claudius Severinus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-28300322.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Claudia Helpidi.
EDCS-28300322.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Claudia Helpidi, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300325.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Nice made this for herself and for her son, Claudius Lupercus. Made with permission of Claudius Lupercus. Gaius Nunnidius Fortunatus made this for himself, his children, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-28300325.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Claudia Nice for herself and her son, with a second section by Gaius Nunnidius Fortunatus for his own family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300327.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Claudia Sabina, who lived for 3 years, 10 months, and 22 days. Tiberius Claudius Lusimacus and Claudia Ionice made this for their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-28300327.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Claudia Sabina, a young child, by her parents Tiberius Claudius Lusimacus and Claudia Ionice, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300328.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Claudia Soteris. Ampliatus made this for his well-deserving wife, who lived for 19 years.
EDCS-28300328.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Ampliatus for his wife Claudia Soteris, who died at the age of 19, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300329.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Tyche made this for Claudia Victoria, her granddaughter, and for herself.
EDCS-28300329.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Claudia Tyche for her granddaughter Claudia Victoria and for herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300330.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Clodia Me[---], by Gelas[---] and her son, who made this for themselves. For Lucius Valerius [---] of Eucaris [---]
EDCS-28300330.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Clodia, Gelas(ia) and her son, and Lucius Valerius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300331.translation: Clodia Prepusa, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for herself and for her husband Lucius Clodius Atimetus, well-deserving, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not pass to the heir of the family. Frontage 20 feet, depth 40 feet.
EDCS-28300331.summary: This funerary epitaph for Clodia Prepusa and her husband Lucius Clodius Atimetus includes specific land dimensions and a clause about inheritance, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300332.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Cluentia Successa, granddaughter. Tiberius Claudius Felix made this for his most dutiful daughter, who lived 9 years.
EDCS-28300332.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Tiberius Claudius Felix for his daughter Cluentia Successa, who died at the age of 9, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300333.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cocceia Dynate made this for her well-deserving husband, Marcus Cocceius Crescens, with whom she lived for 28 years, and for herself, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-28300333.summary: This funerary epitaph records Cocceia Dynate's dedication to her husband Marcus Cocceius Crescens and for herself and their descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300334.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Cocceius Daphnus made this for himself and his descendants, and for Marcus Antonius Agathias and his descendants, and for Marcus Ulpius Domitus and his descendants. Frontage 40 feet, depth 40 feet.
EDCS-28300334.summary: This funerary dedication by Marcus Cocceius Daphnus covers multiple individuals and families, including Marcus Antonius Agathias and Marcus Ulpius Domitus, specifying plot dimensions and dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28300335.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Antonius Callistianus, son of Marcus, made this for his most devoted grandmother, Cocceia Doridis, who lived 21 years and 2 months.
EDCS-28300335.summary: A funerary dedication by a grandson for his grandmother, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-28300336.translation: To [---] and Cocceia Secunda for her grandson, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-28300336.summary: A funerary dedication for a grandson, mentioning the surviving relative Cocceia Secunda and the deceased's age.

EDCS-28300337.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Cocceia Tyche made this for Sextus Iulius Armhenius, a deserving friend.
EDCS-28300337.summary: A funerary dedication by Cocceia Tyche for her well-deserving friend, Sextus Iulius Armhenius.

EDCS-28300338.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Considius Secundus and Beronice made this for their deserving father, Gaius Considius Ianuarius.
EDCS-28300338.summary: A funerary dedication by children (Considius Secundus and Beronice) for their deserving father, Gaius Considius Ianuarius.

EDCS-28300339.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Licinius Hermes made this for his deserving wife, Considiae Saturninae, and for himself.
EDCS-28300339.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Licinius Hermes for his deserving wife, Considiae Saturninae, and for himself.

EDCS-28300340.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Corinthus, his [---] deserving [---] his mother and [---] of the same [---] and [---].
EDCS-28300340.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication mentioning a deceased named Corinthus and his mother, with incomplete details about the dedicator(s).

EDCS-29300348.translation: He who writes is loved, he who reads is buggered, he who listens is itchy, he is a sodomite, he who passes by is a sodomite. May bears eat me and may I (have sex with) the writing one who reads.

EDCS-29300433.translation: Propero, farewell my Sava. Make me love you.

To his most indulgent father, Gnaeus Sentius Lucilius Gamala Clodianus.
EDCS-30301641.summary: This is a lengthy funerary inscription honoring Gnaeus Sentius Felix, detailing his extensive career in public office and guild memberships, dedicated by his son.

EDCS-30400523.translation: Chresimus, slave of Lucius Munatius Crescentis, [his] doliare work, from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, under the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-31300259.translation: Marcus Mundicius Malchio and Marcus Clodius Agatho, as magistrates, had this made from pooled funds.

EDCS-31300260.translation: To Lucius Laturnius Gratus, a villager and minister.

EDCS-31500397.translation: To the gods of the departed. For Marcus Antonius Isido, a pausarius (sickle-bearer?) and duplicarius (sergeant) of a quadrireme, who served in the Dacian and Egyptian fleets. He lived 48 years and served 26 years. Maria Eutychia to her well-deserving husband.

EDCS-31500398.translation: To the gods of the departed. For Gaius Lysius Tertullus, a soldier of the praetorian fleet at Misenum, of the ship Minerva, nationality Dalmatian, in the century of Pius, who served for 3 years. To his well-deserving husband.
EDCS-31500398.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Lysius Tertullus, a Dalmatian soldier serving in the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, noting his ship and service duration.

EDCS-31700052.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hilarion Pammus, who died at the age of 15, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-31900256.translation: Lucius Mettius Maximus, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, from Atria, a soldier of the 9th Praetorian Cohort, lies here. He lived for 28 years and served for 11 years, returning the principal of his life to death. 12 feet in front, 16 feet in depth.
EDCS-31900256.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Mettius Maximus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, detailing his age, service length, and burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-32200923.translation: In the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus; from the properties of Eurytus (of the Quintiana tribe?).
EDCS-32200923.summary: This inscription records properties belonging to Eurytus, dated to the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus.

EDCS-32800266.summary: This is a mark from a pottery workshop, identifying its owner and the year of production, marked by the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus.

EDCS-32805485.translation: Acratus with [sums of money]; [---]rus the tiler with [sums of money]; [---]ros the builder with [sums of money]; Metrodas with [sums of money], under Aulus Vitellius and Lucius Vipstanus Poplicola as consuls; Tiberius Claudius Amarantus; Tiberius Claudius Epaphroditus; [---]ctus the steward; [[---]] under Quintus Veranius and Gaius Pompeius Gallus as consuls; [---] the gardener; [---] the sacristan; [---] Amarantus; [---] the prefect of Linius; under Gaius Antistius Vetus and Marcus Suillius Nerullinus as consuls; [---]us the steward; [---]nus the steward; Cosmus; Cautus; under Tiberius Claudius Augustus V and Servius Cornelius Orphitus as consuls; // ; Tiberius Claudius Daphnus; [[---]]; Euphemus the doorkeeper; Claudia Faustina; Aetoria Phlogis; Claudia Hellas with sums of money; under Gaius Lucius Telesinus and Gaius Suetonius Paullinus as consuls; Pannychus; Sita from the infirmary; Aulus Caecilius Atisci[---]; Claudia Corinthia; [[---]]; under Lucius Julius Rufus as consul; Claudia Tyche; Tiberius Claudius, son of Quintus Pontus, the prefect; Antonius Faustus; Albanus the steward; under Publius Galerius Trachalus as consul; Antonia Musa; Claudia Zosime; Iulia Secunda with sums of money; under Sulpicius Galba II and Titus Vinius Rufinus(?) as consuls; [---]allus; [---]s; [---]nus.
EDCS-32805485.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists numerous individuals, possibly recipients of payments or beneficiaries, along with their occupations and names, dated across multiple consular years from the 1st to 2nd centuries CE.

EDCS-32900010.translation: For Valeria Nice, from the estates of Plotina Augusta, product of the pottery workshop, under Paetinus and Apronianus as consuls.
EDCS-32900010.summary: This inscription marks a pottery product, dedicating it to Valeria Nice and originating from the estates of Plotina Augusta, dated by the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-33000001.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Tiberius Claudius Celadus, deserving of favor, from Mammia Sympherusa.
EDCS-33000001.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tiberius Claudius Celadus, set up by Mammia Sympherusa.

EDCS-33000004.translation: To Alcimus, who lived 50 years, 2 months, and 15 days. From Nice, his wife, who deserved well.
EDCS-33000004.summary: This is a tombstone inscription commemorating Alcimus, who lived to be 50 years, 2 months, and 15 days, and was honored by his wife Nice.

EDCS-33000005.translation: To the shades of the departed. Gaius Iulius Priscus to his well-deserving wife Antonia Chysdis, who lived 35 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-33000005.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonia Chysdis, erected by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000008.translation: To the shades of the departed. Salvia Sympherusa to her dearest husband Publius Aelius Perigenes.
EDCS-33000008.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Perigenes, dedicated by his wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000009.translation: Sacred to the shades of the departed. Cnaeus Aius Felix lived 19 years. Charis to her well-deserving son.
EDCS-33000009.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cnaeus Aius Felix, erected by his mother Charis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000012.translation: ... to [his] most innocent... who lived 7 years, 8 months, and 3 days. Gaius Claudius Q. and Afrodisia made [this] for their sweetest son.
EDCS-33000012.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed child, erected by his parents Gaius Claudius Q. and Afrodisia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000013.translation: To the shades of the departed. For Lucius Faenius Alcinus.
EDCS-33000013.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Faenius Alcinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000016.translation: To the shades of the departed. ... Caecilius ... tianus ... [dedicated this] to their most beloved son Caecilius Genialis, who lived 24 years, [and?] 10 months, a well-deserving person, [he?] made [this].
EDCS-33000016.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilius Genialis, likely erected by his parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000017.translation: To the shades of the departed. Aviania Maximilla to her well-deserving husband Publius Rufinus Successus, who lived more or less 60 years. [This was made] by Clodia Felicissima. Plot granted.
EDCS-33000017.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Rufinus Successus, erected by his wife Aviania Maximilla, also noting the granting of the burial plot by Clodia Felicissima, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000018.translation: To the shades of the departed. Nigidia Secunda to her well-deserving husband Sextus Satius Ephemu(s).
EDCS-33000018.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Satius Ephemus, erected by his wife Nigidia Secunda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000020.translation: Sacred to the shades of the departed. Aspasius lived 24 years, 5 months, and 21 days. Heron, Dynamis, and Abdas made [this] for their well-deserving son.
EDCS-33000020.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aspasius, erected by his parents Heron, Dynamis, and Abdas, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000021.translation: To the shades of the departed. Exorata lived 6 years...
EDCS-33000021.summary: A funerary epitaph for Exorata, likely for a child, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-33000025.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sabina, daughter of Gorgias, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-33000025.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sabina, daughter of Gorgias, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-33000028.text_edition: \n AVGEN Aulus Avianius Cilo vixit annos VII dies LVI Aulus Avianius Vestalis pater\n
EDCS-33000028.translation: Aulus Avianius Cilo lived 7 years and 56 days. His father, Aulus Avianius Vestalis.
EDCS-33000028.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Avianius Cilo, who died at a young age, set up by his father.

EDCS-33000031.translation: Secunda, freedwoman of Augustus, a weaver, lived 24 years.
EDCS-33000031.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secunda, a freedwoman of Augustus and a weaver, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-33000032.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Marcus Amullius Epaphroditus.
EDCS-33000032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Amullius Epaphroditus.

EDCS-33000286.translation: From the estates of our Emperor Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus, when Paetinus and Apronianus were consuls.
EDCS-33000286.summary: This inscription records the management of imperial estates under the consuls Paetinus and Apronianus, likely during the reign of Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-33000292.translation: From the estates of our Emperor Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus, when Paetinus and Apronianus were consuls.
EDCS-33000292.summary: This inscription records the management of imperial estates under the consuls Paetinus and Apronianus, likely during the reign of Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-33000293.translation: From the estates of our Emperor Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus, when Paetinus and Apronianus were consuls.
EDCS-33000293.summary: This inscription records the management of imperial estates under the consuls Paetinus and Apronianus, likely during the reign of Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-33200001.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Quintus Sittius Flaccus, primipilaris tribune of the 10th Praetorian Cohort. Anicia Caecilia, daughter of Marcus, made this for her excellent husband.
EDCS-33200001.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Anicia Caecilia for her husband, Quintus Sittius Flaccus, a high-ranking officer in the Praetorian Guard.

EDCS-33400631.summary: This inscription likely refers to property or a dedication associated with Aurelius Caesar.

EDCS-33400723.translation: Publius Helvius, son of Publius, a quaestor, augur, [at his own expense] // for Augustus.
EDCS-33400723.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Helvius, a local magistrate and priest, likely for the emperor Augustus, funded by himself.

EDCS-33400724.translation: To the Divine Manes. Publius Aemilius Genesius made this hypogeum, 14 feet long and 14 feet wide, for his well-deserving wife Plautia Euplia, and for himself and his well-deserving freedwoman Aemilia Athenais. Whoever opens this hypogeum after the three burials above it, or brings in and places a dead person or the bones of the dead, will have to pay a penalty of 10,000 sesterces to the Republic of Puteoli.
EDCS-33400724.summary: A funerary inscription from Puteoli, dated to the imperial period, detailing the construction of a hypogeum and specifying penalties for unauthorized burials.

EDCS-33400726.translation: For her well-being and that of her family, Luccia Primitiva promised this vow to Fortuna Taurianensis on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-33400726.summary: A votive inscription from Puteoli, likely of the imperial period, recording a promise made to the goddess Fortuna.

EDCS-33400732.translation: For Decimus Lucretius Valens, son of Decimus, of the Menenia tribe, who was honored by Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus with public equestrian rank, admitted into the order of decurions at age eight, and later served as aedile and judge. Here, with his father, he presented 35 pairs of gladiators along with their substitutes and a legitimate hunt. The order of decurions decreed that for his funeral he should receive 3,000 sesterces, a burial plot, public praise, and an equestrian statue in the forum to be paid for from public funds. The Augustales, pagans, and their attendants, the Fortunales(?), the scabillarii, and the Foreses also decreed that pedestrial statues and shields be provided. He lived for [age].
EDCS-33400732.summary: A funerary inscription for Decimus Lucretius Valens from Puteoli, likely dating to the mid-1st century CE, detailing his career honors, lavish games, and the public honors decreed for his funeral by various civic bodies.

EDCS-33500407.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Antonius Communis lived for 24 years.
EDCS-33500407.summary: A simple tombstone inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, recording the name and age of the deceased.

EDCS-33500408.translation: To the Divine Manes. Callistus, freedman, made this for Claudia Genice.
EDCS-33500408.summary: A funerary inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, recording the maker and the deceased.

EDCS-34000010.translation: To the Great Genius of the Colony of Puteoli. Marcus Aurelius Hilario, freedman of Augustus, devoted to the divinity of this place, gave and dedicated this gift.
EDCS-34000010.summary: A dedication to the Genius of the Colony of Puteoli by an imperial freedman, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-34000011.translation: To the Divine Manes. Iustitia, of Sardinian origin(?), optio of the liburnian galley I, lived for 32 years and served for 17 years. Her incomparable, most beloved husband Manilia Veneria made this for her, a well-deserving person.
EDCS-34000011.summary: A funerary inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, for a woman who served as an optio on a galley and was married to a soldier.

EDCS-34000012.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Gaius Domitius Aquilinus, a soldier ('manipularis') on the trireme Tauro, who lived 28 years and served 7 years. His heirs, Pontius Memor, a centurion, and Iulius Marinus, from the same unit, took care of this; Valerius Romanus remade it for him, a well-deserving person.
EDCS-34000012.summary: A funerary inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, for a Roman sailor who served on a trireme, with his heirs and another individual responsible for the monument.

EDCS-34000013.translation: To the Divine Manes. For [name and rank] of the quadrireme Minerva, who served for 9 years. His heir Salvius Salutaris, optio of the trireme Venere, made this for him, a well-deserving person.
EDCS-34000013.summary: A funerary inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, for a Roman sailor who served on a quadrireme, with his heir and a superior officer making the dedication.

EDCS-34000014.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Gaius Iulius Saturninus, a soldier ('manipularis') on the trireme Salvia, who served 31 years. Maximius Bettius, Aelius Valerianus, and Didia Amazon made this monument.
EDCS-34000014.summary: A funerary inscription from an unknown location, likely of the imperial period, for a Roman sailor with a long service record, dedicated by three individuals.

EDCS-34000015.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Titus Terentius Maximus, soldier from the trireme Iove, a Bessian by nationality, who lived 40 years and served 20 years. Caius Julius Philo of the trireme Mercurio, Quintus Domitius Optatus of the quadrireme Minerva, his heirs, with Sulpicius Priscus, optio of the trireme Iove, overseeing, have erected this.
EDCS-34000015.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Terentius Maximus, a soldier, with details about his service and the individuals who commissioned the monument.

EDCS-34000016.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Caius Longinius Maximus, from the liburna ship Clementia, a Pamphylian by nationality, who lived 45 years and served 25 years. Lucius Valerius Valens, a scribe and duplicarius, his heir, made this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-34000016.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Longinius Maximus, a sailor, detailing his life span and military service, erected by his heir.

EDCS-34000017.translation: Marcus Antonius Crescens, son of Marcus, lived 13 years.
EDCS-34000017.summary: This is a short funerary inscription for Marcus Antonius Crescens, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-34000018.translation: Caius Attius Princeps, son of Caius, of the Palatina tribe, lived 26 years.
EDCS-34000018.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Attius Princeps, a young man, stating his name, father, tribal affiliation, and age at death.

EDCS-34000019.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Aurelia Marciana, an incomparable woman, who lived 25 years and 7 months. Marcus Aurelius Ptolemaeus wrote this for his deserving wife and for their other children and freedmen.
EDCS-34000019.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelia Marciana, commissioned by her husband, highlighting her exceptional qualities and also including other family members.

EDCS-34000020.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Rebir(a) Primitiva, well-deserving. Julius Maximus lived 60 years.
EDCS-34000020.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rebir(a) Primitiva, stating her name and age at death, commissioned by Julius Maximus.

EDCS-34000021.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Publius Bennis Augendus and Bennis Exoratus and Bennias Charis and their descendants.
EDCS-34000021.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, commemorating multiple members of the Benni family and their descendants.

EDCS-34000023.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Caesias Procula, who lived 39 years and 20 days. Hibius Neptunalis, her son, and Caesia Marciana, her sister, made this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-34000023.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caesias Procula, detailing her age at death and commissioned by her son and sister.

EDCS-34000024.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Cascellius Ingenuus, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-34000025.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Cascellius Stephanus, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-34000027.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Cincia Tyche, his well-deserving wife, Gaius Ducenius Athenodorus made this.
EDCS-34000027.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, Cincia Tyche.

EDCS-34000028.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Claudia Horaea, her patroness, well-deserving, freedwoman, they made this at their own expense.
EDCS-34000028.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by freedmen for their patroness, Claudia Horaea.

EDCS-34000029.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Claudius Victor lived 22 years.
EDCS-34000029.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Claudius Victor, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-34000030.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Cornelia Hermionene, Cornelius Hermogenes and Cornelius Aquilinus made this for their well-deserving mother.
EDCS-34000030.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by sons for their mother, Cornelia Hermionene.

EDCS-34000033.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Feridia Augurina, who lived 9 years and 9 months, her parents made this for their sweetest daughter, well-deserving.
EDCS-34000033.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by parents for their daughter, Feridia Augurina, recording her age at death.

EDCS-34000034.translation: Of the slaves of Fulvius Menophilus: in front 12 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-34000034.summary: This inscription likely records land boundaries or dimensions associated with the slaves of Fulvius Menophilus.

EDCS-34000035.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gaudentius, who lived 12 years and 12 months, Publicius Ianuarius made this for his pupil.
EDCS-34000035.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by Publicius Ianuarius for his pupil, Gaudentius, recording his age at death.

EDCS-34000036.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Genucius Aeros lived 2 months and 7 days.
EDCS-34000036.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and extremely short lifespan of Lucius Genucius Aeros.

EDCS-34000037.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Ignatius Fuscus lived 1 year and 11 months.
EDCS-34000037.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and lifespan of Lucius Ignatius Fuscus.

EDCS-34000039.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Julia Priscilla, who lived 3 years and 31 days, her mother made this for her sweetest daughter.
EDCS-34000039.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by a mother for her daughter, Julia Priscilla, recording her age at death.

EDCS-34000040.translation: To the departed spirits. Helvius Martialis, a grieving father, made this for his cherished adopted daughter Iuliaes Trheptenis, who lived for 6 years, 11 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-34000040.summary: A funerary epitaph for an adopted daughter, set up by her grieving father.

EDCS-34000041.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Naevius Asper made this for his most beloved son, Publius Iuventius Celsus, who lived for 16 years.
EDCS-34000041.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son, set up by his father.

EDCS-34000046.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Oppius Eutychetes Magonianus, his most beloved son, who lived for 10 years and 3 days.
EDCS-34000046.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son who died at a young age.

EDCS-34000047.translation: To the departed spirits. Popilia Zenis made this for her well-deserving patroness Popila, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-34000047.summary: A funerary epitaph for a patroness, set up by her freedwoman.

EDCS-34000048.translation: Marcus Salonius Celsus for himself and for Egnatia Agele and for his son Marcus Salonius Celsus, who lived for 13 years, and for his family.
EDCS-34000048.summary: A funerary epitaph for a man, his wife, his son, and his family.

EDCS-34000049.translation: To the departed spirits. [---] for his son, Gaius Seius Aga[---], who was buried here.
EDCS-34000049.summary: A funerary epitaph, partially restored, for a son.

EDCS-34000050.translation: To the departed spirits. Sela Olympia for her wife [---], with whom she lived for 10 years [---] without any complaint; she lived for 39 years, 3 months [---], and 18 days. She made this.
EDCS-34000050.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her surviving partner, mentioning their years together and the deceased's lifespan.

EDCS-34000051.translation: To the departed spirits. Septymia Elpis for herself, for Publius Trofymus her husband, and for Sextus Prosdocimus, Caia Septymia, Sextus Maximus, and Rodine, her freedwomen, and for Publius Trofymus and her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-34000051.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman, establishing provisions for herself, her husband, freedpersons, and descendants.

EDCS-34000052.translation: Hail! Titinia Danae, freedwoman of Seleucus, lived for 18 years.
EDCS-34000052.summary: A funerary epitaph for a freedwoman who died at a young age.

EDCS-34000053.translation: To the departed spirits. Valeria Nice made this for her well-deserving adopted daughter Valerius Arsenoe, who lived for 8 years, 8 months, and 19 days.
EDCS-34000053.summary: A funerary epitaph for an adopted daughter, set up by her adoptive mother.

EDCS-34000054.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Demetrius made this for his wife, Vibiae Protenis.
EDCS-34000054.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Demetrius to his wife, Vibiae Protenis.

EDCS-34000056.translation: So that you may know, guest, my name was Briseis. I had not yet completed seventeen times seven months, but my fate was unjust; cruel death snatched me away from my parents and my Albano before I could live more years.
EDCS-34000056.summary: This epitaph records the premature death of a young girl named Briseis, who died before reaching 119 months of age.

EDCS-34000057.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Clytius.
EDCS-34000057.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for someone named Clytius.

EDCS-34000058.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Rufina made this for her most dutiful and sweetest son, Demetrius Eutychus. He lived here for 16 years and 5 days.
EDCS-34000058.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Demetrius Eutychus, who lived for 16 years and 5 days, and was commemorated by his mother Rufina.

EDCS-34000060.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus Eutyches lived for 5 years and 5 months. His parents made this.
EDCS-34000060.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus Eutyches, who lived for 5 years and 5 months, and was commemorated by his parents.

EDCS-34000061.translation: Paris, the mulio, beloved of O[...], is buried here.
EDCS-34000061.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Paris, a mulio (mule driver), who was the beloved of someone.

EDCS-34000062.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---]lo Rufus. Rufus, his patron, [---] for the deserving. He lived 20 years [---] days.
EDCS-34000062.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates a man named Rufus, who lived 20 years and was honored by his patron, also named Rufus.

EDCS-34000073.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, mentioning Lucius Balabius Eutactus.

EDCS-34000074.translation: Of Egnatius Certus and his son, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-34000074.summary: This inscription likely records the names and association of Egnatius Certus and his son, possibly as part of a larger monument or dedication.

EDCS-34000075.summary: This inscription is a dedication or commemoration of Publius Manlius Modestus.

EDCS-34000076.translation: Of Publius Octavius Luttatus Quintilianus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-34000076.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Octavius Luttatus Quintilianus, likely honoring him as a distinguished individual.

EDCS-34000367.translation: To Gaius Apollonius Priscus, a soldier of the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, a native of Alexandria, who lived 40 years. Lucius Fabullius Serenus, a duplicarius of the same fleet, his heir, made this.
EDCS-34000367.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Apollonius Priscus, a soldier in the Misenum fleet, with his heir Lucius Fabullius Serenus as the dedicator, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-34000368.translation: Marius Xenophon made this for Marius Priscus, patron, well deserving. [---] of the Praetorian fleet of Misenum [---] who lived 3 years, 10 months [---] made for him well deserving.
EDCS-34000368.summary: This funerary inscription records that Marius Xenophon erected a monument for his patron Marius Priscus, a member of the Misenum fleet, who died young.

EDCS-34100470.translation: To Claudia Laudica, freedwoman of the emperor, who lived 55 years.
EDCS-34100470.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudia Laudica, a freedwoman of an emperor, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-34100471.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Trebia Veneria lived 7 years, 6 months, 3 days. Her father made this.
EDCS-34100471.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Trebia Veneria, who died at the age of 7 years, 6 months, and 3 days, erected by her father.

EDCS-34100475.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Lucius Allius Felix, who lived 21 years, 6 months, 16 days. Lucius Allius Felix and Gavia Successa for their dearest son.
EDCS-34100475.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Allius Felix at the age of 21 and is dedicated by his parents, Lucius Allius Felix and Gavia Successa.

EDCS-34100476.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Calvia Successa, who lived 53 years, 4 months, 13 days. Lucius Allius Felix made this for his incomparable, well-deserving wife.
EDCS-34100476.summary: This funerary inscription honors Calvia Successa, who died at the age of 53, and was erected by her husband Lucius Allius Felix.

EDCS-34100479.translation: The colonists who contributed to the statue: Tiberius Iulius Pistus, Lucius Salvius Mercurialis, Publius Manneius Priscus, Tiberius Claudius Vitalis, Lucius Vipstanius Zeno, Gnaeus Mat(i)cus Valens, Caius Pomponius Amandus, Lucius Domitius Silvanus, Caius Butronius Agrippa, Publius Vocconius Adauctus, Marcus Brittius Mercurialis, Tiberius Claudius Clemens, Caius Verrius Aemilianus, Lucius Manneius Capitolinus the father, Caius Naevius Callistus, Quintus Decimius Iustianus, Lucius Larcius Cornelianus, Publius Mussius Felix, Publius Mussius Proculus, Caius Carrinas Felixs, Caius Carrinas Suavis, Marcus Luscidius Tertius, Caius Iulius Proculus, Tiberius Iulius Faustinus, Caius Pomponius Augustalis, Caius Pomponius Zosimus, Marcus Tatius Largus, Quintus Servilius Marianus, Lucius Manneius Philantus, Lucius Manneius Capitolinus the son, Lucius Manneius Nereus, Lucius Manneius Manneianus.
