EDCS-80000238.summary: This is a dedication by Astylus, likely for Helvium Sabinum, possibly a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-80000241.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a personal note or epitaph, containing a greeting and farewell.

EDCS-80000243.translation: Lucius Caecilius Capella, duovir for dispensing justice.
EDCS-80000243.summary: This inscription records the title of Lucius Caecilius Capella as duovir iure dicundo.

EDCS-80000249.translation: Orphaeus makes Lucius Ceius Secundus aedile.
EDCS-80000249.summary: This is a political appeal from Orphaeus urging voters to elect Lucius Ceius Secundus as aedile.

EDCS-80000250.translation: I ask you, men, to make Lucius Ceius Secundus duovir. Secundanus asks.
EDCS-80000250.summary: This is a political appeal from Secundanus urging voters to elect Lucius Ceius Secundus as duovir.

EDCS-80000251.translation: I ask you, men, to make Lucius Ceius Secundus duovir.
EDCS-80000251.summary: This is a political appeal urging voters to elect Lucius Ceius Secundus as duovir.

EDCS-80000254.translation: ... Lucius Petilius Flaccus asks you to make [him] duovir for dispensing justice. Marcus O[...]
EDCS-80000254.summary: This is a fragmentary political appeal from Lucius Petilius Flaccus seeking election as duovir iure dicundo.

EDCS-80000255.summary: This is an incomplete funerary or dedicatory inscription mentioning Vettius and Gaius Frontonius, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-80000256.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, honoring Lucius Caecilius.

EDCS-80000257.translation: To Suettius and Epidius, the duovirs.
EDCS-80000257.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Suettius and Epidius, who held the office of duovir, likely from the republican or early imperial period.

EDCS-80000258.translation: Vote for Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus as aedile, a good man worthy of the state.
EDCS-80000258.summary: This is a political recommendation urging voters to elect Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus as aedile, likely from the late republican or early imperial period.

EDCS-80100001.translation: To the departed spirits. Catilia Attia made this for her most beloved and well-deserving husband, Titus Clodius Gillianus.
EDCS-80100001.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Titus Clodius Gillianus by his wife Catilia Attia, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-80100002.translation: Lives. Marcus Clodius, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe. In the front, 12 feet; in the rear, 14 feet.
EDCS-80100002.summary: This is a boundary inscription, possibly for a tomb or land plot, specifying dimensions and mentioning Marcus Clodius of the Oufentina tribe.

EDCS-80200055.translation: Spatali, servant of Servius Cornelii Zosimus.
EDCS-80200055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Spatali, who was the servant of Servius Cornelii Zosimus, likely of a humble social status.

EDCS-80200059.summary: This is a brief inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, honoring Lucius Sepunius Symphonius.

EDCS-80200060.summary: This is a very short inscription fragment, likely indicating ownership or dedication by Publius Crusus Faustus.

EDCS-80200074.translation: Of the Flavian Colony Augusta Puteolana, workshop of Caius N(---) S(---).
EDCS-80200074.summary: This inscription identifies the workshop of Caius N(---) S(---) within the Colonia Flavia Augusta Puteolana, likely an official marker from the imperial period.

EDCS-80200075.translation: Of the Flavian Colonia Augusta of Puteoli // From the workshop of Caius, son of N., S.
EDCS-80200075.summary: This inscription likely refers to a workshop or a craftsman associated with the colonia of Puteoli.

EDCS-80200085.summary: This is a personal name, possibly a tomb inscription or a dedication by Gaius Julius Victor.

EDCS-80200108.summary: This inscription records the name of an individual, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication by Er[o]tus.

EDCS-80200109.translation: From Marcus Fabius Eupl[i] / From Marcus Lucretius Epaphra / From Lucius Numisius Me[---]a[---]i / From Lucius Marcius Chryseros / From Marcus Fabius Eu[p]li // [From Marcus Fabius Eupli] 5,000 sesterces for the man
EDCS-80200109.summary: This text appears to be a list of names followed by a monetary amount, possibly related to a funerary monument or a communal expense.

EDCS-80200110.translation: From Marcus Nonius Magnus / [From Publius?] Marcius [---] / From Marcus Caecilius Potitus / From Numerius Blaesius Saturninus / From Marcus Ofillius Longinus / From Marcus Cl[o]dius Magnus Munatianus / From Aulus [Castric]ius(?) [---]r[---]i / From Quintus Junius Secundus / From Gaius Lucius Clemens / From Marcus Calator[ius]
EDCS-80200110.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely representing individuals contributing to a monument or project, possibly from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-80200141.translation: Cuspius / Pansam, aedile // I ask you to make him
EDCS-80200141.summary: This inscription is a plea or recommendation for Cuspius Pansam, who was an aedile.

EDCS-80200142.summary: This is a personal name with manumission indication, likely part of a funerary or ownership record.

EDCS-80200165.summary: This is a personal name, possibly a tomb inscription or a dedication by Marcus Ampliatus.

EDCS-80200170.summary: This inscription records two personal names, possibly indicating a relationship or ownership, with 'Felix' appearing twice.

EDCS-80200173.summary: This inscription identifies 'Florus' with the descriptor 'insularis', likely referring to someone associated with an apartment building.

EDCS-80200174.summary: This is a brief farewell message, likely an epitaph or a casual inscription.

EDCS-80200179.translation: To Modia, may you be fortunate.
EDCS-80200179.summary: This is a short dedication or well-wishing inscription, possibly for a person named Modia.

EDCS-80200182.summary: This is a personal, possibly humorous, inscription about a bodily ailment or condition.

EDCS-80200183.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, identifying an individual and their parentage.

EDCS-80200187.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription for Marcus Suetus.

EDCS-80200188.summary: This is a brief farewell message, likely an epitaph or a casual inscription.

EDCS-80200191.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Avianiae Aegiale, most sweet and most dutiful mother, from her son Atilius Artema. To Masuria, a most excellent wife. Hail and farewell.
EDCS-80200191.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a son to his mother and a wife, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-80200192.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Avianius Felicioni, dearest pupil, was made (this monument) by his parents.
EDCS-80200192.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by parents to their beloved pupil, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-80400048.translation: To Aelius, the priest. Ascalonia, may you be fortunate. Made by the painter Claudius Primus, working for Vaturi(us) Vitalis.
EDCS-80400048.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a priest and a woman named Ascalonia, with the maker identified as a painter, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-80400056.summary: This is a short inscription identifying an individual named Mopsus with the title 'leader', possibly a local official or head of a group.

EDCS-80400063.summary: This is a dedicatory or congratulatory inscription likely to a woman named Cestilia.

EDCS-80400065.summary: This is a personal greeting from Cyrillus to Liccaeus.

EDCS-80400091.summary: This inscription likely describes two enslaved people named Anomalus and Vere.

EDCS-80400092.summary: This inscription identifies a person named Furuncule as a cook.

EDCS-80400094.translation: [---] to the duumvir Decimus P[---], son of Primus, [---] requests and that he may do [---].
EDCS-80400094.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a request or petition directed to a duumvir in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-80700095.translation: In the second consulship of Emperor Agrippa, on the Ides of October, Lucius St[---] Nicephorus says this arrived with [his wife?] Stactene.
EDCS-80700095.summary: This fragment records an event, possibly a shipment or arrival, that occurred during the consulship of Agrippa, identified by its date and a witness.

EDCS-80700118.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment for a very young child.

EDCS-80700130.translation: To [---] Aninius, son of Lucius, [---] free[---]
EDCS-80700130.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to be a dedication or memorial, mentioning a man named Aninius.

EDCS-80700150.translation: Caius Julius Pholi's freedman, Diadumenus, to himself and to his freedmen and freedwomen of either sex whom he remembered in his will.
EDCS-80700150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman, Diadumenus, who is dedicating a tomb for himself and his own freedpeople.

EDCS-80700151.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. His parents made this for Caius Julius Phoebus, who lived 11 years and 6 months, well-deserving.
EDCS-80700151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Caius Julius Phoebus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-80700152.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His parents made this for the well-deserving Iulius Valens, who lived 11 years.
EDCS-80700152.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Iulius Valens, set up by his parents.

EDCS-80700153.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Faltonius Trebelicus, who lived 75 years.
EDCS-80700153.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Faltonius Trebelicus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80700155.translation: Expenses 900 sesterces. Nonia Successa, with Numerius Vibius Clemens as guarantor, on the 4th day before the Nones of November. [List of witnesses/debtors including] P. Fannius Pudentis, P. Flavius Largus, M. Burrius Clemens, Sex. Caecilius Carpus, M. Nonius Cypaerus, Q. Junius Apsyrtus, Cn. Pollus Ianuaris, L. Mammius Felicionis(?), C. Lollius Crescens, N. Vibius Clemens.
EDCS-80700155.summary: A financial record, possibly a loan or debt settlement, with a list of individuals involved, dated to November 1st in the consulship of P. Fannius Pudentis and P. Flavius Largus (or possibly other consuls, depending on the full dating context).

EDCS-81100049.translation: Gnaeus Lucceius, son of Gnaeus, a poet, first in popular plays, second in Atellan farces, and first in 'exodi'. Domitia [dedicates this] to the poet.
EDCS-81100049.summary: An epitaph or dedication for the poet Gnaeus Lucceius, highlighting his achievements in various theatrical genres.

EDCS-81200051.translation: From the pottery works of Publilia, belonging to Zosimus and Iulia Dynamis.
EDCS-81200051.summary: An inscription indicating ownership or origin from the pottery works of Publilia, associated with Zosimus and Iulia Dynamis.

EDCS-81200052.translation: From the estates of Faustina Augusta, pottery work by Victor.
EDCS-81200052.summary: Indicates pottery produced from the estates of Faustina Augusta, made by Victor.

EDCS-81200053.translation: Of Lucius Lurius Priscus (or similar name).
EDCS-81200053.summary: A simple ownership or dedication marking, likely for a property or object.

EDCS-81200062.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Fortuna. Lucius Aemilius Burrus, ship captain. Dedicated on the 6th day before the Ides of April, in the consulship of Rusticus II and Aquilinus.
EDCS-81200062.summary: A dedication to Emperor Augustus and the goddess Fortuna by Lucius Aemilius Burrus, a ship captain, dated to 8 April, in the year of the consulship of Rusticus II and Aquilinus (likely AD 165).

EDCS-81200066.translation: Eufrosyne, who lived in peace for more or less 3 years, 7 months, and 7 days, with her partner, in peace.
EDCS-81200066.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eufrosyne, who died at a young age, mentioning her peace and her partner.

EDCS-81200067.summary: A dedication or epitaph fragment for Pescennia Charitium.

EDCS-81200082.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Numerius Cadio Gallus, likely on a monument or object.

EDCS-81200083.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Isargyros [---]dotos, with the beginning and part of the name lost.

EDCS-81200084.summary: This inscription is a dedication to [---]llius, son of Marcus, with significant portions of the name and description lost.

EDCS-81400212.translation: Marcus Pettilius Alexander arranged for this to be made for his mother, himself, and his family.
EDCS-81400212.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Pettilius Alexander for his family, indicating the construction of a tomb or monument.

EDCS-81500041.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Larcius Gaenialis arranged for this to be made for his wife Martilla Eusaevia, and for his children (sons and daughters), and for her freedmen and freedwomen, and for her children and their descendants.
EDCS-81500041.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Larcius Gaenialis for his wife, children, and her freedmen, specifying beneficiaries of a tomb.

EDCS-81500043.summary: This inscription is likely a funerary dedication or ownership marker for Sextus Pomponius Valens.

EDCS-81600011.translation: Quinctia, daughter of Caius, gave this gift to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-81600011.summary: This is a votive dedication by Quinctia to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia.

EDCS-81800025.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. These three sarcophagi within the tomb were granted to Gaius Terentius Amaranthus and were given as a surrounding area by Vaesonius Faustinianus, Laeta Primitiva, and Secunda.
EDCS-81800025.summary: This inscription records the allocation of three sarcophagi within a tomb to Gaius Terentius Amaranthus, with Vaesonius Faustinianus, Laeta Primitiva, and Secunda involved in the grant.

EDCS-81800026.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelia Crescentia placed this tombstone for her brother Aurelius Crescens, who lived for about 40 years, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-81800026.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Aurelia Crescentia for her deceased brother Aurelius Crescens, providing his approximate age and praising him.

EDCS-81800027.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Olympia, daughter, made this for her most beloved mother Tettienia Capriola, a well-deserving woman.
EDCS-81800027.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Olympia for her mother Tettienia Capriola, praising her and identifying the dedicator.

EDCS-81800053.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lovers of this man, Aurelius Alexander, a deserving friend.
EDCS-81800053.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by friends for Aurelius Alexander, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000090.translation: To Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus, grandson of the deified Julius, prince of youth, pontiff, consul, emperor, who lived 14 years and was designated consul; the colonists of Axurnates [dedicate this] to their patron.
EDCS-82000090.summary: This is a dedication by the colonists of Axurnates to Gaius Caesar (son of Augustus), who died at age 14, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-82000091.translation: To Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, grandson of the deified Julius, prince of youth, augur, whom the people chose as consul, having lived 14 years; the colonists of Axurnates [dedicate this] to their patron.
EDCS-82000091.summary: This is a dedication by the colonists of Axurnates to Lucius Caesar (son of Augustus), who died at age 14, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-82000096.translation: [... from the] fleet of Misenum? served 11 years, lived 37 years. A Dalmatian by birth, Gaius Petronius Palus, his heir, made this memorial for him, a well-deserving person. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-82000096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a sailor from the Misenum fleet, possibly of Dalmatian origin, who served 11 years and died at 37, set up by his heir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82300108.translation: Cn(aeus) Lucceius [dedicates] this sacred offering to Apollo.
EDCS-82300108.summary: This is a religious dedication to the god Apollo by Cn(aeus) Lucceius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82400012.summary: This is a simple ownership mark or a very brief funerary dedication for Marcus Epidius Erastus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82800041.translation: In the consulship of Pupilius Agrippa and Tubero Fabius.
EDCS-82800041.summary: This inscription records a date by naming the consuls Pupilius Agrippa and Tubero Fabius, likely from the Late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-82900002.translation: Lucius Senatius Firmus, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, aedile, for himself and his parents and his freedwoman Daphne.
EDCS-82900002.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Lucius Senatius Firmus, an aedile, for himself, his parents, and his freedwoman Daphne, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82900003.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a funerary epitaph or ownership mark, for Lucius Senatius Firmus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82900004.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or record of manumission for Daphne, a freedwoman of Lucius Senatius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82900005.summary: This is a personal name, likely an epitaph or a dedication by Lucius S<e=I>natius Ianuarius.

EDCS-00380007.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely a tombstone or epitaph, for Caius Cordius Nymphicus.

EDCS-00380014.translation: Chreste, his wife, [erected this] for Marcus Stattaeus Maximus, son of Marcus Stattaeus, Augustalis VIvir.
EDCS-00380014.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a wife to her husband, who held a significant priesthood and civic role.

EDCS-00380017.translation: Behold the tomb of Aeolis, a lively puppy, whom I have mourned as being immoderately snatched away by a swift fate.
EDCS-00380017.summary: This is a funerary epigram mourning the death of a beloved pet dog named Aeolis.

EDCS-00380018.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely a tombstone or epitaph, for Augustas Chrestus.

EDCS-00380024.translation: He who lived 70 years sleeps in peace, deposited here, Cuadra.
EDCS-00380024.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Cuadra, who lived to 70 years of age.

EDCS-00380029.translation: Son of Caius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-00380029.summary: This is a Roman family record or inscription, indicating parentage and lineage for a Caius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-00380030.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription or a dedication related to Lucius Rustius Lygdamus.

EDCS-00380037.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Vitalis, father, and Cyrilla, mother, made [this] for their son, who lived for one year, 3 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-00380037.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child, dedicated by his parents, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-00380039.translation: To the departed spirits. Abascantus, a slave and warehouse worker of Matidia, made [this] for his comrade, well deserving.
EDCS-00380039.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a slave to his 'contubernalis' (a close companion, possibly also a slave or fellow soldier).

EDCS-00380040.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Flavia C.
EDCS-00380040.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Flavia C.

EDCS-00380045.translation: Titus Claudius Fabullus, son of Tiberius, to his physician.
EDCS-00380045.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Titus Claudius Fabullus to his physician.

EDCS-00380047.translation: Titus Claudius Urbanus, freedman of a woman, and Titus Claudius Eros, freedman of a woman, in front 12 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-00380047.summary: This inscription seems to record land dimensions related to Titus Claudius Urbanus and Titus Claudius Eros, possibly for burial plots.

EDCS-00380050.translation: To TYM Mati. Gaius Murdius for himself and...
EDCS-00380050.summary: This is a partial inscription likely recording a dedication or funerary monument initiated by Gaius Murdius.

EDCS-00380059.translation: To Decimus Lucretius Valens, son of Decimus. He lived 2 years.
EDCS-00380059.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Lucretius Valens, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-00380060.translation: To Decimus Lucretius Iustus, son of Decimus, of the Menenia tribe, admitted into the order of decurions without payment. He lived 13 years.
EDCS-00380060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Lucretius Iustus, mentioning his tribal affiliation and public honor, and recording his lifespan.

EDCS-00380061.translation: To Decimus Lucretius Valens, son of Decimus, of the Menenia tribe.
EDCS-00380061.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or funerary monument for Decimus Lucretius Valens.

EDCS-00380069.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Quintus Ollius Felix, likely a name on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-00380072.translation: Vitalis, a boy. He lived 12 years.
EDCS-00380072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a boy named Vitalis, recording his age at death.

EDCS-00380154.summary: This inscription records that Anseghisilus, identified as a priest, was the scribe of the text or document.

EDCS-00380155.summary: This inscription appears to be a short Christian text or personal motto.

EDCS-00380189.translation: Tiberius Natronius Sollers for himself and for his two daughters, Sollertilla and Valerianilla, daughters of Tiberius, and for his wife Valeria Apollonia, and for their descendants and their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-00380189.summary: This is an funerary dedication by Tiberius Natronius Sollers for himself, his family, and descendants.

EDCS-02900015.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, son of Gnaeus, imperator.
EDCS-02900015.summary: This inscription records the title of Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, likely a military leader.

EDCS-02900027.translation: Demetrius, slave of Camidis, son of Marci, made this.
EDCS-02900027.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedman for his former master.

EDCS-03000014.translation: To the memory of Octavia Benenata, his most sweet wife, Eumachius [dedicated this].
EDCS-03000014.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Eumachius for his wife Octavia Benenata.

EDCS-03000015.translation: Aulus Cornelius Dionysius made this for himself and for his wife Leda and for his freedman Secundus, slaves, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, in front 20 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-03000015.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Cornelius Dionysius for himself, his wife, and slaves, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-03000028.translation: She completed the limbs of a chaste virgin, she fulfilled the course of life, she returns to the earth, and preserves her worthy modesty, triumphing, her body laid down for the Lord. The leaders seek this one, the pious crowd seeks this one. Believe what chaste love of faith can do. Laid down on the third day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-03000028.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a chaste virgin, highlighting her virtue and mentioning her burial date.

EDCS-03000039.translation: The place of Proclus and Magna, whose daughter sleeps in peace, Sextilia, aged VI years, X months, and XXV days.
EDCS-03000039.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextilia, daughter of Proclus and Magna, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-03000040.translation: ius, son of Caius Balbus, Ufeius, son of Lucius Trama, [dedicated this] in bronze to Fortuna. Caius Balbus, son of s, Lucius Trama, son of s, in bronze to Fortuna.
EDCS-03000040.summary: This inscription appears to record dedications in bronze to Fortuna by individuals named Balbus and Trama.

EDCS-03000042.translation: Lucius Heleius, son of Kaeso, quaestor, saw to its construction in bronze to Fortuna.
EDCS-03000042.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna commissioned by Lucius Heleius, son of Kaeso, in his role as quaestor.

EDCS-03000043.translation: Sacred to Hercules, Marcus Procilius Augustalis rebuilt and dedicated it, which Quintus Turranius Fonteianus had dedicated from his own land.
EDCS-03000043.summary: A private dedication to Hercules, recording a rebuilding and rededication of a sacred space by Marcus Procilius Augustalis, referencing a prior dedication by Quintus Turranius Fonteianus.

EDCS-03000076.translation: Tertia, his freedwoman, (dedicated this) with her own money.
EDCS-03000076.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a private dedication made by a freedwoman named Tertia.

EDCS-03000107.translation: Pia, frugal, thrifty, Lucilia, daughter of Publius, lived for more than 40 years; she left behind three sons, (but) she herself...
EDCS-03000107.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucilia, daughter of Publius, detailing her virtues, lifespan, and surviving children, with an incomplete final phrase.

EDCS-03300012.translation: Gaius Julius Hilarus, freedman of Augustus, a shipmaster, (dedicated this) for himself and his wife Iulia Nice and their descendants.
EDCS-03300012.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Julius Hilarus, a freedman of Augustus and a shipmaster, for himself, his wife, and their descendants.

EDCS-03300013.translation: Marcus Tontius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus; Marcus Tontius Antenor, freedman of Marcus; Tontia Chiones, freedwoman of Marcus. [---]
EDCS-03300013.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely listing members of a household or family, possibly related to freedmen and freedwomen of a Marcus Tontius.

EDCS-03300040.translation: The best garum of mackerel, from Scaurus, by Marcus's slave.
EDCS-03300040.summary: An inscription advertising a high-quality fish sauce (garum) made from mackerel and attributed to Scaurus, produced by a slave of Marcus.

EDCS-03300044.translation: [This] was distributed by Statanus in the consulship of Aulus Vitellius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Vipstanus Publicola.
EDCS-03300044.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a distribution of goods or resources during the consulship of Aulus Vitellius and Lucius Vipstanus Publicola.

EDCS-03300139.translation: Antistia Asia made (this) for Gaius Aristius Celer, Herculaneus, Augustalis of the municipality of Tibur, and for her most beloved and devoted husband.
EDCS-03300139.summary: A funerary dedication by Antistia Asia for her husband, Gaius Aristius Celer, who held the prestigious positions of Herculaneus and Augustalis in Tibur.

EDCS-03300140.translation: To the departed spirits. Hortensius Macarius made (this) for his wife Cornelia Felicitas, aged 29.
EDCS-03300140.summary: A funerary dedication by Hortensius Macarius for his wife Cornelia Felicitas, who died at the age of 29.

EDCS-03700005.translation: Euticius and Florentina, parents, for their sweetest daughter Hirenetis, who lived 6 years and 30 days, in peace.
EDCS-03700005.summary: A funerary epitaph from parents Euticius and Florentina for their young daughter Hirenetis, who died at the age of 6 years and 30 days.

EDCS-03700023.translation: To Caius, son of Caius, and Euplus and Pothinus, sons of Julius.
EDCS-03700023.summary: This is an incomplete inscription likely recording familial dedications, possibly to deities or as funerary markers.

EDCS-03700028.translation: Sacred to Jupiter in the grove; Cosmus, as a votive offering.
EDCS-03700028.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Cosmus to Jupiter in a sacred grove.

EDCS-03700052.translation: Gaius Sontius, son of Gaius, duovir.
EDCS-03700052.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Gaius Sontius, son of Gaius, who held the office of duovir.

EDCS-03700123.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marcus Apstidinus, son of Lucius, likely a personal or funerary marker.

EDCS-03700124.translation: Scrofarius, son of Scrofarius, grandson of Scrofarius, to his father.
EDCS-03700124.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication from Scrofarius, son and grandson of the same name, to his father.

EDCS-03700130.translation: To Gaius Heiulius Diphilus, freedman of Gaius, master of the Herculaneans, [dedicated to] his mother Heiuliana, freedwoman of Gaius, and to his sister Heiuliana Philema, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-03700130.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Heiulius Diphilus to his mother and sister, identifying his own status as a freedman and his role as a master Herculaneans, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-03700131.translation: To the Divine Manes. Sulpicia Epictesis made this for Avillia Procula, her dearest and most devoted, who deserved well. She lived 20 years, 9 months.
EDCS-03700131.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Sulpicia Epictesis for Avillia Procula, commemorating her devotion and lifespan of 20 years and 9 months.

EDCS-03700132.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Publius Aelius Marcus, most dutiful son, who lived 2 years and 28 days.
EDCS-03700132.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Aelius Marcus, honoring him as a dutiful son who lived for 2 years and 28 days.

EDCS-03700133.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Fabia Prisca, possibly a mother, indicating her age at death was 9 months.

EDCS-04800009.translation: Publius Valerius took care to have the temple of Venus built with his own money.
EDCS-04800009.summary: This inscription records that Publius Valerius funded and oversaw the construction of a temple dedicated to Venus.

EDCS-04800019.translation: To our lords Flavius Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, the Pious, Fortunate, and Triumphant, always Augusti, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-04800019.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperors Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, likely erected in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-04800020.translation: To our lords Flavius Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, the Pious, Fortunate, and Triumphant, always Augusti, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-04800020.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperors Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, likely erected in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-04800021.translation: For Lucius Cornelius Puso Messalla, consul for the seventh time, member of the college of epulones, proconsul; Cornelia Sabina out of respect.
EDCS-04800021.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Cornelius Puso Messalla and was set up by Cornelia Sabina, likely in the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04800025.translation: To the Divine Shades; for Marcus Caelus, of the 3rd cohort, praetorian.
EDCS-04800025.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Caelus, a soldier of a praetorian cohort, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04800026.translation: For Publius Marcius Gallus, son of Marcius, of the Galerian tribe, tribune of the soldiers of the 10th Legion Gemina Pia Fidelis, and of the 1st Legion Minervia.
EDCS-04800026.summary: This inscription records the service of Publius Marcius Gallus as a military tribune in two legions, dating likely to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04800027.translation: To the Divine Shades; for Sextus Rufus Victor, primus pilus of the 4th Scythian Legion.
EDCS-04800027.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Rufus Victor, a high-ranking centurion (primus pilus) of the 4th Scythian Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04800031.translation: To the Divine Shades; for Proculus, freedman of the Augusti, superintendent, who lived 24 years, for his well-deserved service; Aelia Saturnina made this for herself and for her descendants.
EDCS-04800031.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Aelia Saturnina for her freedman Proculus and herself, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04800032.translation: For Gaius Tiburtius Atticus, son of Gaius, four times chief magistrate, Herculanean and Augustal; Gaius Tiburtius Atticus to his most loving father.
EDCS-04800032.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Gaius Tiburtius Atticus, set up by his son of the same name, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04800033.translation: For Cossinia, a Vestal Virgin, daughter of Lucius; Lucius Cossinius Electus Undecies honored her, who served Vesta for 11 years; here rests the virgin, brought by the popular will; her place was granted by senatorial decree.
EDCS-04800033.summary: This inscription honors Cossinia, a Vestal Virgin, and records the senatorial decree that granted her burial place, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04800035.translation: Pinnia, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and for Lucius Pinnius Acastus, freedman of Lucius, master of the Herculaneans, 20 feet of land.
EDCS-04800035.summary: This is a funerary or property inscription concerning Pinnia and Lucius Pinnius Acastus, likely from Herculaneum, dating to the 1st century CE.

EDCS-04800038.translation: To Varenia Major, daughter of Quintus. Diphilus, freedman, gave this place by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-04800038.summary: This inscription records the grant of a burial plot to Varenia Major by her freedman Diphilus, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-04800040.translation: Medus, freedman, and Hilarus, freedman, built this for the third time at their own expense.
EDCS-04800040.summary: This inscription records a public building or structure erected at their own expense for the third time by two freedmen, Medus and Hilarus.

EDCS-04800041.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Cornelia Macrina, wife of Rusticus, member of the republic of Tibur, and for her son Caius Iulius Secundus, to his dearest mother.
EDCS-04800041.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelia Macrina by her husband Rusticus and son Caius Iulius Secundus, likely from Tibur and dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04800045.translation: Glucheria, slave of Hermones Antoni; Aristas Clara; Antoni's slave and Hilarus, freedman; Prima, slave and staminaria; Ai bia, slave; Limne is free; Nicethor, freedman; Nota; Aulia Camula; Hilarus, freedman; Apate, slave; Aratus, slave; Mar, freedman; Gemella, freedwoman; Charis, freedwoman.
EDCS-04800045.summary: This inscription lists numerous individuals, including slaves and freedmen and women, along with their owners or status, likely related to a burial or a social group.

EDCS-04800046.translation: Gaius Aemilius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe. 30 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-04800046.summary: This inscription records a land measurement for Gaius Aemilius, indicating property boundaries, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-04800047.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lucius Aemilius Ianuarius. Aemilia Ianuaria to her father.
EDCS-04800047.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Aemilius Ianuarius by his daughter Aemilia Ianuaria.

EDCS-04800048.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Ampliata, a deserving wife. Mithras made this.
EDCS-04800048.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Ampliata by her husband Mithras, praising her virtues.

EDCS-04800050.translation: Lucius Annius Varus, son of Titus, of the Aniensis tribe. 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-04800050.summary: This inscription records a land measurement for Lucius Annius Varus, indicating property boundaries, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04800051.translation: Philumena, freedwoman of Lucius Antius; Lucius Antius, freedman of the woman; Granicus.
EDCS-04800051.summary: This inscription lists several individuals connected by freedom and ownership, possibly related to a tomb or a legal status declaration.

EDCS-04800052.translation: Marcus Attius Aster, freedman of Marcus and Quintus Rubrius, built for himself, and Gabinia Laudica, freedwoman of Decimus, and Gabinia Damalis, freedwoman of Decimus. 12 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-04800052.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument or tomb for Marcus Attius Aster and two women, Gabinia Laudica and Gabinia Damalis, including land measurements, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04800053.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Avilia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-04800054.translation: To the departed spirits. Erastinus, freedman of the emperors, made this for his most beloved daughter, Aurelia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-04800054.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Erastinus, a freedman of the emperors, to his daughter Aurelia.

EDCS-04800055.translation: To the departed spirits. Besia Pistis, foster-child, lived for 7 years, 4 months, and 25 days. Besia Cirilla made this.
EDCS-04800055.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Besia Pistis, a foster-child, erected by Besia Cirilla.

EDCS-04800057.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Sperata [made this] for her most dutiful sister, Caecilia Benedicta, who lived for 20 years and 4 months.
EDCS-04800057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Benedicta, erected by her sister Caecilia Sperata, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04800058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Arbuscula, a freedwoman of Caius.

EDCS-04800059.translation: To the departed spirits. For Calpurnia Solutrix, our most beloved daughter, who lived for 28 years, 2 months, and 25 days. Varronia Mellita, mother, and her brother Calpurnius Onesimus, and Aurelius Mnasistratus, husband with whom she lived for 10 years and 7 months, [made this].
EDCS-04800059.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Solutrix, erected by her mother, brother, and husband, detailing her lifespan and duration of marriage.

EDCS-04800060.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcus Claudius EVEI Fla AS RO, my husband.
EDCS-04800060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Claudius EVEI Fla AS RO, dedicated by his wife.

EDCS-04800061.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tiberius Claudius Romanus, an incomparable man. Claudius Felix, son, and Claudia Zosime, his wife, made this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-04800061.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by the son and wife for Tiberius Claudius Romanus, honoring his virtues.

EDCS-04800062.translation: To the departed spirits. For Cornelia Nymphenis, who lived for 12 years.
EDCS-04800062.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelia Nymphenis, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-04800063.translation: Parata, freedwoman of Publius, aged 20, mother, and her son Publius Cornelius Publi f. Scipio, aged 6.
EDCS-04800063.summary: This epitaph records the mother, Parata, and her young son, Publius Cornelius Scipio, likely a family funerary monument.

EDCS-04800064.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Atimetus, father, for his most dutiful daughter Cornelia Quartilla.
EDCS-04800064.summary: This is a tombstone for Cornelia Quartilla, set up by her father Atimetus.

EDCS-04800065.translation: For Cossinia, freedwoman of the woman [owner]; for Caesius Posidonius, freedman of Lucius Cossinius; for Disco, freedman of Sextia Eugenia, with front 11 feet and land 15 feet.
EDCS-04800065.summary: This inscription records land dimensions possibly related to a burial plot, mentioning several freedpersons and their patrons.

EDCS-04800066.translation: To Diadochus, to the spirits of the departed. He lived 10 years.
EDCS-04800066.summary: This is a tombstone for Diadochus, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-04800068.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Felix, a son who lived 14 years and 9 months. Clodius Ianuarius, for his well-deserving son.
EDCS-04800068.summary: This is a tombstone for Felix, set up by his father Clodius Ianuarius.

EDCS-04800069.translation: Gaius Fictorius, freedman of Caius, for himself and his family, with front 12.5 feet.
EDCS-04800069.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot, with dimensions provided, set up by Gaius Fictorius for his family.

EDCS-04800075.translation: Nais and his mother made [this] for Ianuarius.
EDCS-04800075.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument or dedication made by Nais and his mother for Ianuarius.

EDCS-04800078.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Caius Iulius Iulianus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe. He lived 2 years and 5 months. His parents made [this].
EDCS-04800078.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Iulius Iulianus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-04800080.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication, possibly for 'Juliani Felix'.

EDCS-04800081.translation: Marcus Lollius Atticus for himself and Lollia Arsinoe and Lollius Dionysius and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants and successors.
EDCS-04800081.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a burial place by Marcus Lollius Atticus for himself, family members, and their descendants.

EDCS-04800082.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lollia Eutyche, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-04800082.summary: This is a tombstone for Lollia Eutyche, freedwoman of Marcus.

EDCS-04800083.translation: Lucius Luttius Trypho, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Luttius Hilarus, freedman of Lucius; Publius Sextius Diphilus, freedman of Publius; Sextia Hilara, freedwoman of Publius; Lucius Luttius Eudamus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-04800083.summary: This inscription lists several freedmen and freedwomen, likely members of the same household or family, with their patrons' names. The approximate date is uncertain without further context.

EDCS-04800085.translation: Her parents, most devoted, made this for Marcia, and Marcius Perennis for his dearest wife, well-deserving.
EDCS-04800085.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their daughter Marcia and by Marcius Perennis for his wife, indicating a familial dedication from likely the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04800086.translation: Caius Matius Hilarus; Pyrine, freedwoman of the woman Matia.
EDCS-04800086.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Caius Matius Hilarus and Pyrine, who was a freedwoman of a woman named Matia; its purpose is unclear without further context.

EDCS-04800091.translation: To Hygia, from Murdia Phiale, for her nurse.
EDCS-04800091.summary: This is a dedication to Hygia, the goddess of health, set up by Murdia Phiale for her nurse, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800092.translation: To the Divine Shades. Mutatus, a slave of Caesar, lived 28 years. Aelius Iunius and Salvianus, born in the household, made this for him, well-deserving.
EDCS-04800092.summary: This is a funerary monument for Mutatus, a slave of Caesar who died at age 28, erected by his fellow household slaves Aelius Iunius and Salvianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800093.translation: Of Publius Naerius Philargyrus, in front 12 feet, in the ground 12 feet.
EDCS-04800093.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Publius Naerius Philargyrus, specifying its frontage and depth in feet.

EDCS-04800094.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titenia Zoe made this for her well-deserving husband, Publius Noni Antigonus.
EDCS-04800094.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Titenia Zoe for her deserving husband, Publius Noni Antigonus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800095.translation: To Numisia, daughter of Marcus, Quartus.
EDCS-04800095.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Numisia Quartes, daughter of Marcus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800097.translation: To the Divine Shades. Onesimus. Laudice, his sister, and Troilus.
EDCS-04800097.summary: This funerary inscription honors Onesimus, with dedications from his sister Laudice and Troilus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800098.summary: This inscription identifies Manius Aurelius as a member of the Salii, a priestly college dedicated to Hercules, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04800100.translation: To [Chi]us, son of Rus, from R. Nusius.
EDCS-04800100.summary: This is a dedication to Chius by R. Nusius, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-04800101.translation: To Tiberius Plautius Primus, son of Tiberius, who lived 18 years and 7 months, Marcus Saufeius Victorinus, to his deserving foster-son.
EDCS-04800101.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Tiberius Plautius Primus, dedicated by his foster-father Marcus Saufeius Victorinus.

EDCS-04800102.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The mother made this for her son Athio, who lived 13 years.
EDCS-04800102.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased son, Athio.

EDCS-04800104.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Rufia Rufina, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-04800104.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Rufia Rufina, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-04800105.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Rutilius Clemens. Titus Flavius [---].
EDCS-04800105.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Rutilius Clemens by Titus Flavius.

EDCS-04800106.translation: [---] made this for Sabina, most rare [---].
EDCS-04800106.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, for a woman named Sabina.

EDCS-04800107.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Sallustia Phorbe, for herself and for her most indulgent husband Quintus Regentinus, son of Publius, and for her freedmen and freedwomen, and for those whom I have given or shall give.
EDCS-04800107.summary: This is a self-dedication and dedication to family members, including a husband and freedpersons, on a funerary monument.

EDCS-04800108.summary: This inscription records the name Survius Pamphilus, possibly identifying a freedman and his patroness.

EDCS-04800109.summary: This inscription records the name Gaius Tiburtius Comus and indicates an age is to follow, likely a funerary epitaph.

EDCS-04800112.translation: Valeria Atenais, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and for Asisa, slave of Polion, and for her own people.
EDCS-04800112.summary: This is a self-dedication and dedication to others, including a slave and household members, by a freedwoman named Valeria Atenais.

EDCS-04800113.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Victoria, the mother, made this for her deserving daughter, who lived 15 years.
EDCS-04800113.summary: A funerary epitaph for a daughter named Victoria, set up by her mother.

EDCS-04800115.translation: For Ulpia Pompeiana, their sweetest daughter, Ulpius Ecatheus and Flavia Irene, her parents.
EDCS-04800115.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpia Pompeiana, dedicated by her parents.

EDCS-04800117.translation: Tertia, freedwoman of Urgulania, daughter of Rufus.
EDCS-04800117.summary: An inscription identifying Tertia, a freedwoman of Urgulania.

EDCS-04800153.translation: To Agapetus, her dearest son, who lived 18 years, 5 months, and 11 days less 17 days. Fenia Maxima, his mother, [erected this] for him deserving of all good things.
EDCS-04800153.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son named Agapetus, set up by his mother.

EDCS-04800200.translation: The image of my dear wife, Albula L. Voltus, O goddess, which I have described, with metal rarely gleaming and with the favor of your divine power, behold, I have placed here by your springs, O nymph, for your health.
EDCS-04800200.summary: A dedicatory inscription by Albula L. Voltus, likely setting up an image or shrine by a spring for his wife.

EDCS-04800205.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucretia Severa, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-04800205.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucretia Severa, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-04800206.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Crispa.

EDCS-04800210.translation: For Gaius, son of Marcus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-04800210.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Gaius.

EDCS-04900006.translation: Graecinia Callirhoe made [this] for her most devoted son Marcus Graecinius Blandus, who lived 36 years, 11 months, and 16 days, and for her most excellent husband Titus Mallius Terptus, deserving of all good things.
EDCS-04900006.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son and husband, dedicated by the wife and mother.

EDCS-04900016.translation: Iulia Tyche, by order of the governor, made this altar for Neptune.
EDCS-04900016.summary: This inscription records an altar dedicated to Neptune by Iulia Tyche, ordered by the governor, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04900019.translation: Lucius Munatius Alexsa, Deicimia, Munatia Ecloge.
EDCS-04900019.summary: This inscription lists names that likely represent a family group or individuals associated with a tomb or property, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900027.translation: Garum, the best flower of mackerel sauce, from the workshop of Scaurus. Garum, flower of mackerel sauce, from the workshop of Scaurus.
EDCS-04900027.summary: This inscription is a repeated advertisement for a fish sauce (garum) product from the workshop of Scaurus, likely from a commercial context in Roman times.

EDCS-04900028.translation: Severus: My thousand ewes were wandering in the Sicilian mountains.
EDCS-04900028.summary: This inscription is a personal statement by Severus about his lost sheep in Sicily, possibly related to ownership or a cautionary tale, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900029.translation: Alce, may you fare well, you who are worthy.
EDCS-04900029.summary: This inscription is a personal farewell or blessing addressed to Alce, likely from a tombstone or a personal dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900030.translation: Tyrpeniys Memor sends greetings to Eucarpus.
EDCS-04900030.summary: This inscription is a personal greeting from Tyrpeniys Memor to Eucarpus, perhaps a fragment from a letter or a dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900031.translation: On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August, Publius Cornelius was here.
EDCS-04900031.summary: This inscription records the presence of Publius Cornelius on a specific date (July 17th), likely related to a visit or event, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900033.translation: Publius Quinctius Salvius, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-04900033.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Quinctius Salvius as a freedman of Publius, likely from a tomb or dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900034.translation: Publius Ancarsulenus Philadelphus, freedman of Publius, the Mercurial master; Ancarsulena Eleutheris, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-04900034.summary: This inscription lists several individuals and their relationships (freedmen/freedwomen, a 'master' of a Mercurial association), likely related to a collegium or family burial, from the Roman period.

EDCS-04900035.translation: [...], Annius [...], Ceius, freedman of Lucius [...], Lucius Mamm[...], Lucius Mammius, freedman of Lucius [...], Lucius Mamm[...], Lucius Mammi[...], [...], ANNIVS [...], Marcus Aemilius [...], Marcus Calatorius [...], Fufius [...], Servius Fulvius [...], Servius Fulvius, son of Servius [...], Servius Fulvius, son of Servius [...], Lucius Junius, son of Lucius [...], Marcus Flavius, son of Marcus [...], Marcus [...], Mammius [...], [...], [...], Lusius [...], Tiberius Mammius [...], Lucius Granius [...], Suessus [...], Clodius [...].
EDCS-04900035.summary: This inscription is a fragmented list of many names, likely recording members of a family, a collegium, or contributors to a project, from the Roman period.

EDCS-05000014.translation: Ulpia Vic... Cassianus here rests, died aged 1 year, ... months.
EDCS-05000014.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpia Vic[---] Cassianus, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000015.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secunda, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000031.translation: Septimius Hermes and Septimia Marcia here rest, [for their] daughter to her parents deserving well.
EDCS-05000031.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a daughter for her parents, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000051.translation: ... Lucius Cornelius [---], magistratus of the Augustan quarter, made the walls around the temple and around the basilica at the decree of the decurions, at his own expense.
EDCS-05000051.summary: A building inscription recording public works by a local official, Lucius Cornelius, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05000060.translation: Publius Timinius Philocalus, freedman of Publius, father; Timinia Auge, freedwoman of Publius, mother.
EDCS-05000060.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Timinius Philocalus and Timinia Auge, likely parents of a freedman, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000061.translation: Publius Timinius Rufus, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, brother; Publius Timinius Niger, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, made [this]; Cocceia Tertia, wife.
EDCS-05000061.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Publius Timinius Niger for his brother Publius Timinius Rufus, and mentioning his wife Cocceia Tertia, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000067.translation: [---] to Crispus and Licinianus, to Licinius and Flavius Claudius Constantinus Caesar, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-05000067.summary: A dedication to emperors and other officials, possibly related to a public monument, dating to the Constantinian period.

EDCS-05000068.translation: To our lords Flavius Valentinianus, Valens...
EDCS-05000068.summary: A dedication to Roman emperors Valentinian and Valens, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-05000069.translation: Marcus Licinius Crassus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, father, ordered [this] to be made to his son Marcus Licinius Crassus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, and to his wife Plaedatia Maxuma, daughter of Caius; Plaedatia Maxuma, daughter of Caius, provided the access.
EDCS-05000069.summary: A funerary monument built by Marcus Licinius Crassus for his son and wife, with the wife's mother providing access, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000070.translation: Gnaeus Rubrius Menophilus, freedman of the woman, for himself and for Rubria, daughter of Gnaeus, his patroness.
EDCS-05000070.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for himself and his patroness, dating to antiquity.

EDCS-05000072.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Atinius Memmianus, likely the owner or builder of these baths.

EDCS-05000074.translation: To Paula Hordeonia, daughter of Lucius, wife of Nasonis.
EDCS-05000074.summary: This is a dedication to Paula Hordeonia, daughter of Lucius and wife of Nasonis.

EDCS-05000077.translation: Under our lord Anastasius, perpetual consul, on the 14th day before the Kalends of December, Socrates, a man of distinction, who lived 48 years, rests here in peace.
EDCS-05000077.summary: This epitaph records the death and life span of Socrates, a man of distinction, during the consulship of Anastasius.

EDCS-05000078.translation: In the consulship of Quintus Futius Lusius Saturninus and Marcus Seius Varanus.
EDCS-05000078.summary: This inscription marks a date by naming the consuls Quintus Futius Lusius Saturninus and Marcus Seius Varanus.

EDCS-05000082.translation: Of Sextus Clodius Paullus, son of Sextus.
EDCS-05000082.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or ownership marker, for Sextus Clodius Paullus.

EDCS-05000083.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Egnatia Apale, possibly for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-05000084.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Lollius Heron, possibly for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-05000085.translation: Of Marcus Nassus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05000085.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Nassus, a freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-05000086.summary: This inscription records the name of Publius Attius Auctus.

EDCS-05000087.translation: Gaius Julius Felix, the stable master.
EDCS-05000087.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Julius Felix as a stable master (stabulario).

EDCS-05000088.translation: Gaius Laelius Varus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05000088.summary: This inscription is a name formula for Gaius Laelius Varus, likely an epitaph or ownership mark.

EDCS-05000089.summary: This inscription is a name formula for Antonia, daughter of Manius, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-05000090.summary: This inscription is a name formula for Maculonia Prima, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-05000091.translation: To Atilia Lucillia, most illustrious woman, most excellent patroness.
EDCS-05000091.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to Atilia Lucillia, honoring her as a patroness, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05000095.summary: This inscription is a possessive name formula, likely referring to the owner of property or a tomb.

EDCS-05000103.summary: This inscription is a possessive name formula, referring to Quintus Mucius of Cyzicus, possibly related to property or a tomb.

EDCS-05000106.summary: This inscription is a possessive name formula, referring to Lucius Ansius Zephyrus, likely related to property or a tomb.

EDCS-05000113.translation: In the consulship of Gnaeus Pompeius Collega and Quintus Iulius Cordus, on the seventh day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-05000113.summary: This inscription records a date during the consulship of Gnaeus Pompeius Collega and Quintus Iulius Cordus, likely marking an event or the completion of a project.

EDCS-05000114.translation: From Aulus Marius Maximus, son of Aulus Marius and grandson of Titus Marius, (as) speculator, (dedicates this to) his brother Titus Marius Pollius.
EDCS-05000114.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Aulus Marius Maximus, a speculator, to his brother Titus Marius Pollius, possibly an epitaph or votive offering.

EDCS-05000116.summary: This inscription is a name formula for Calpurnius Clemens, likely an epitaph or ownership mark.

EDCS-05000117.summary: This is a dedication made by Gaius Crates.

EDCS-05000124.translation: Donata, aged 13, her mother made this for her sweet daughter.
EDCS-05000124.summary: This is a tomb inscription for a 13-year-old girl named Donata, dedicated by her mother.

EDCS-05000171.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcella made this for her most beloved husband, Gaius Annins Capriolus, a deserving man.
EDCS-05000171.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated to Gaius Annins Capriolus by his wife Marcella.

EDCS-05000172.translation: Because she was upright, reverent, and simple, Profutura wrote this for her household slaves, for her patron Pompeianus.
EDCS-05000172.summary: This inscription records a writing by Profutura, dedicated to her slaves and patron.

EDCS-05000173.translation: So that the name of Diomedes may endure forever, his master Claudius Pompeianus wrote this out of his devotion.
EDCS-05000173.summary: This inscription records a master, Claudius Pompeianus, writing the name of his slave Diomedes to ensure its remembrance.

EDCS-05000174.translation: Lucius Petronius Saturninus, son of Spurius, from Sucasana, and Liguria, freedwoman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-05000174.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Lucius Petronius Saturninus and Liguria.

EDCS-05000176.summary: This is a dedication to the divinity of Hope.

EDCS-05000177.summary: This is a dedication made by Liber Horimus.

EDCS-05000179.translation: To Cai Anienus, son of Caupo, patron of the municipality, curator of the aediles, and member of the VIIviri epulones.
EDCS-05000179.summary: This is a dedication to Cai Anienus, who held several important civic and religious positions.

EDCS-05200007.translation: Mesia Titiana, a most distinguished girl, great-granddaughter of Asprus the Younger.
EDCS-05200007.summary: This inscription identifies Mesia Titiana, noting her lineage.

EDCS-05200014.translation: Lucius Annius, freedman of Lucius, Erophilus. Clodia, freedwoman of Lucius Annius Erophilus, Salvia, freedwoman of Lucius Annius Erophilus.
EDCS-05200014.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of freedmen and freedwomen, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-05200017.translation: roni decided on this matter as follows: when it is expedient for this order, as he wishes, Gnaeus Luccius should be honored with a public monument at public expense, he will propose it to the people.
EDCS-05200017.summary: This is a fragment of a senatorial decree concerning the erection of a public monument for Gnaeus Luccius.

EDCS-05200021.translation: Here rests in peace Brunculus, servant of Lord Jesus Christ, who lived for [---] years.
EDCS-05200021.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription for Brunculus, a servant of Jesus Christ.

EDCS-05200031.translation: Here rests Pascasus, who lived more or less 55 years, well.
EDCS-05200031.summary: This is a simple Christian funerary inscription for Pascasus, noting his age at death.

EDCS-05200032.translation: Here rests in peace Criscentia, daughter of Pascasus, a Jewess, wife of [---], who lived more or less 28 years.
EDCS-05200032.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Criscentia, daughter of Pascasus and a Jewess, noting her age and marital status.

EDCS-05200035.translation: Tablets of Lucius Cominius Primus for expenses for Pompeia Anthis, with the assistance of her guardian Gaius Vibius Euryrus, as petitioner, and received the amount paid.
EDCS-05200035.summary: This inscription is a record of financial transactions concerning Pompeia Anthis, with a guardian and a payee identified.

EDCS-05200036.translation: I ask you to make Lucius Munatius Caeserninus, a good man, quinquennial duumvir of Nuceria.
EDCS-05200036.summary: This is a plea to elect Lucius Munatius Caeserninus as quinquennial duumvir of Nuceria.

EDCS-05200039.translation: 40 pairs of gladiators will fight for Publius Furius and Lucius Ram(i?) in Capua on the Ides of January and the 19th day before the Kalends of February; there will be awnings and possibly a naumachia.
EDCS-05200039.summary: This is an advertisement for a gladiatorial spectacle in Capua, detailing the number of pairs, sponsors, and dates.

EDCS-05200040.translation: 24 pairs of gladiators and a hunt will fight in Falerno Foro Popili under the patronage of the Lucii Atilii on the 13th, 12th, 11th, and 10th days before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-05200040.summary: This is an advertisement for gladiatorial games and a hunt in Falerno Foro Popili, sponsored by the Lucii Atilii, with specific dates provided.

EDCS-05700002.translation: By the command of most holy Ceres and the Nymphs, this well was constructed at the entire expense of C. Caecilius Onesimus, patron and perpetual quinquennial of the body of surveyors, and of L. Hortensius Gallus, quinquennial of the boatmen, and of Numerius Trebonius Eutychetes, second quinquennial of the acceptors; dedicated on the 10th day before the Kalends of September, when Lateranus and Rufinus were consuls.
EDCS-05700002.summary: This inscription records the construction of a well, funded by various guilds and officials, and dedicated in the consulship of Lateranus and Rufinus (likely 197 AD).

EDCS-05700003.translation: To the ancestral god, Gnaeus Turpilius Turpilianus, son of Gnaeus, as aedile and praetor, having performed the sacred rites of Vulcan, dedicated a small statue of Vulcan, weighing 15 pounds and 9 scruples of silver, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05700003.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a silver statue of Vulcan by a local magistrate in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-05700007.translation: To the Genius of the foreign soldiers, Optatianus and Pudens, brothers who were grain merchants, fulfilled their vows through service.
EDCS-05700007.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by two grain merchants serving the Genius of foreign soldiers.

EDCS-05700015.translation: Lucius Valerius [Frontinus], centurion of the 5th cohort, while [---] the camp [---] during the [---].
EDCS-05700015.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning a centurion and likely recording an event related to a military camp.

EDCS-05700017.translation: To Hercules and Silvanus, sacred. Tiberius Claudius Diadumenus, the cellarer, made this.
EDCS-05700017.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Hercules and Silvanus by a cellarer.

EDCS-05700020.translation: For the safety and safe return of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus, Augusta Faustina, their children, an altar to the Holy Goddess Isis, the divine Sarapis, the Holy Silvanus, and the Lares, Gaius Pomponius Turpilianus, procurator for oil in the Galba warehouse in the port of Ostia, dedicated as a gift for both ports.
EDCS-05700020.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to various deities for the imperial family by a procurator for oil at the port of Ostia.

EDCS-05700023.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Publius Cornelius Trupo, freedman of Publius, a surveyor, built an altar as seen in a vision, under a precarium.
EDCS-05700023.summary: This inscription records the building of an altar to Jupiter by a freedman surveyor, possibly based on a divine vision.

EDCS-05700025.translation: To Jupiter the Guardian, Quintus Veturius Secundus and Aulus Libius Hilarianus, as quaglatores and curators, gave this gift to the worshippers.
EDCS-05700025.summary: This inscription records a gift dedicated to Jupiter the Guardian by two individuals holding administrative positions.

EDCS-05700026.translation: Flavius Sosius, freedman of Marcus, and Lucius Sosianus [---] son of Marcus, and Aemilia Tio [---] daughter of Crispus, built a small shrine to the Augustan Lares at their own expense for Auro, son of Paritanonius, and Marcus Au [---].
EDCS-05700026.summary: This inscription records the construction of a shrine to the Augustan Lares by several individuals at their own expense, possibly for specific recipients.

EDCS-05700027.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication to Liber Pater by an individual named Chryseros.

EDCS-05700028.translation: Gnaeus Maelius Epictetus dedicated in his own courtyard to Liber Pater.
EDCS-05700028.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Liber Pater made in a private courtyard by Gnaeus Maelius Epictetus.

EDCS-05700029.translation: Gnaeus Maelius Philetus the younger dedicated this altar to Father Liber.
EDCS-05700029.summary: A private dedication of an altar to Liber by Gnaeus Maelius Philetus the younger.

EDCS-05700044.translation: The splendid guild of caulkers, adorned with every amenity, dedicated this sacred offering to the Most Evident Divine Power of Minerva Augusta, our Preserver and Chief Priestess; the patrons Marcii Iulii Carpus, his son Carpus, corporatus Amati Rufinianus, and honoratus Firmus made the dedication.
EDCS-05700044.summary: A dedication by the guild of caulkers to Minerva Augusta, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700047.translation: Decimus Hostius Heraclida dedicated this to the Divine Nymphs.
EDCS-05700047.summary: A private dedication of a shrine to the Nymphs by Decimus Hostius Heraclida.

EDCS-05700050.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Titus Flavius Primigenius, freedman of the emperor, a registrar and assistant, dedicated this.
EDCS-05700050.summary: A dedication to Silvanus by Titus Flavius Primigenius, an imperial freedman and registrar.

EDCS-05700053.translation: Sacred to holy Silvanus. Dorotheus, freedman of the emperor and procurator of the Marianum estate, gave this statue as a gift.
EDCS-05700053.summary: A dedication to Silvanus by Dorotheus, an imperial freedman and procurator of a Roman estate, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700068.summary: An inscription honoring the reigning emperors, possibly on a building or monument.

EDCS-05700074.translation: The company of Acilius Glabrio made this altar for the Mistress.
EDCS-05700074.summary: A dedication of an altar to an unnamed "Mistress" by a group associated with Acilius Glabrio.

EDCS-05700076.translation: [...] and the children of the gods, Felicissimus and [..]nda, and [..] Festa made [celebrations?].
EDCS-05700076.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning individuals named Felicissimus and Festa, possibly relating to a festival or celebration.

EDCS-05700080.translation: Veri dedicated this gift from his own funds.
EDCS-05700080.summary: A private dedication of a gift by an individual named Veri.

EDCS-05700089.translation: [...] to Trajan [...] emperor, consul designate for the 6th time.
EDCS-05700089.summary: A fragment mentioning Emperor Trajan and his consular designation, likely part of a public inscription.

EDCS-05700115.translation: Pudens and Optatianus, brothers, officials concerned with grain, restored the base of the sacred countenances, and Pudens and Optatianus restored the base of the sacred countenances with the addition of more refined ornaments.
EDCS-05700115.summary: This inscription, likely a repetition for emphasis, records the restoration of a base for sacred images by two brothers named Pudens and Optatianus, who held a position related to the grain supply, probably during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700120.translation: To Julia, August, mother of the camps.
EDCS-05700120.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus and mother of Caracalla, identified as 'mother of the camps', likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700121.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, Caesar, son of Imperator Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, father of the country.
EDCS-05700121.summary: This inscription is a titulary for Caracalla, identifying him as Caesar and the son of Septimius Severus, likely dating to the period when he was co-emperor with his father, early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700128.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, pontifex maximus, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, proconsul. The local magistrates and the unit of caligae-wearing soldiers, under the care of Gnaeus Sergius Mercurius, Marcus Licinius Privatus, and Tiberius Claudius Sosipolus, as quinquennial magistrates of the 29th lustrum, honored him.
EDCS-05700128.summary: This extensive inscription honors Emperor Diocletian, listing his numerous titles and achievements, and records its dedication by local officials and soldiers during the 29th lustrum, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-05700130.translation: To Perpetuus, prince, Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus. Gerusius Romulus [dedicated this], through [his] care...
EDCS-05700130.summary: This dedication is to Emperor Maximian, listing him with imperial titles, and indicates it was set up under the care of Gerusius Romulus, probably in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-05700131.translation: To the Restorer of public liberty, defender of the city of Rome, author of the common safety of all, to our Lord Imperator Flavius Valerius Constantine, Pious, Fortunate, Ever Unconquered Augustus. The shipping clerks and the barge operators from the lower harbor, devoted to his divine power and majesty, [dedicated this], under the care of Aurelius Victorinus, a most perfect man, prefect of the grain supply.
EDCS-05700131.summary: This lengthy dedication honors Emperor Constantine I, listing his titles and emphasizing his role as a protector, set up by shipping officials under the supervision of the prefect of the grain supply, likely in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-05700133.translation: To our Lords Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Victor Augustus. [---]
EDCS-05700133.summary: This inscription begins the titulary of Emperor Constantine I, listing him with imperial titles, with the rest of the inscription being lost, likely dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-05700137.translation: The sea-side baths, and the interior with the rebuilding of the cellars, and the addition of a floor outside, our lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, victorious and triumphant always Augusti, from the treasury of the public state of the Ostian city, under the care of Proculus Gregorius, a most illustrious man, prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome, adorned.
EDCS-05700137.summary: This inscription records the refurbishment of the seaside baths and associated structures at Ostia, funded by the state treasury and dedicated by the emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, under the supervision of the prefect of the grain supply, dating to the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-05700139.translation: Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, a most illustrious man and prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome, took care [of this], and the city made it at his own expense.
EDCS-05700139.summary: This inscription records that Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, as prefect of the grain supply, supervised a project that was funded by the city itself, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700140.translation: With our lords Theodosius and Placidus Valentinianus, perpetual Augusti, safe. Flavius Alexander Cresconius, a most illustrious man, prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome, placed this for the adornment of the porticus Placidiana.
EDCS-05700140.summary: This inscription states that Flavius Alexander Cresconius, as prefect of the grain supply, dedicated an addition to the 'porticus Placidiana' in honor of the emperors Theodosius and Valentinian III, likely dating to the mid-5th century CE.

EDCS-05700150.translation: Acceptors of vows, ten-year celebration, successfully! Lucius Valerius Flavianus, Gnaeus Cossius Felicissimus, Marcus Vitrutius Antigonus, Quintus Annius Furianus, Titus Flavius C...icus, Gnaeus Cossius? Felicissimus; Lucius Calpurnius Mitess..., Sulpicius Aume..., Titus Aelius Tinep..., Marcus Pontius Fla..., Caius Sinfo..., Lucius Lamatus.
EDCS-05700150.summary: A list of names, likely officials or members of a collegium, celebrating a decennalia (ten-year anniversary).

EDCS-05700153.translation: To Marcus Acilius Caninus, son of Marcus, quaestor of the city; the traders from the area of Saturn.
EDCS-05700153.summary: An inscription dedicated by traders to Marcus Acilius Caninus, who held the office of urban quaestor.

EDCS-05700154.translation: To Quintus Acilius Fuscus, son of Caius, Papiria tribe, a distinguished man, procurator of the grain supply of our Augusti, patron of Ostia, procurator of the work on the Pompeian theatre, advocate of the treasury, a codicillary official of the department of inheritances and coheirs, priest of the Laurentes Lavinates, the association of fruit measurers, assistants and acceptors of Ostia, for his great kindness towards them.
EDCS-05700154.summary: An honorific inscription for Quintus Acilius Fuscus, detailing his many important administrative and religious roles, including procurator of the grain supply and patron of Ostia.

EDCS-05700157.translation: Necessity armed them for combat, but without practice from the beginning it was useless; without public support, Acholius Abydus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome.
EDCS-05700157.summary: A fragment mentioning Acholius Abydus, prefect of the grain supply of Rome, and the importance of training and support in combat.

EDCS-05700158.translation: Baebia Victoria made this for herself and for her husband Antonio Timocrates, a Roman knight, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, the part of the monument granted to them by Cornelius Zoticus and Epictetianus, and the portico with its small rooms and the bedroom above the memorial.
EDCS-05700158.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing the deceased's family, including her husband, and the specific parts of the monument that were granted or built.

EDCS-05700159.translation: To Publius Bassilius Crescentius, son of Publius, tribune of the 1st cohort of Germans, procurator of the Matutinus school, procurator of the Emperor's grain supply at Ostia. Caius Vettius Mercurius, his cornicularius, on the occasion of the dedication of the statue, gave portions (sportulas) as listed above, individually. Number of caligati of the decuriae: XVI. Collegium fabrum tignuariorum Ostis, with Quintus Turranius Hermogenes, Marcus Octavius Asclepiodotus, and Quintus Tullius Vitalio acting as quinquennial magistrates for the 33rd lustrum.
EDCS-05700159.summary: An inscription commemorating a statue dedication, listing officials of a military cohort and a builders' collegium in Ostia, including the magistrates responsible.

EDCS-05700160.translation: To Quintus Calpurnius Modestus, son of Caius, Quirina tribe, procurator of the Alps, procurator of the grain supply at Ostia, procurator of Lucania. The association of grain merchants, through Marcus Aemilius Saturus and Publius Aufidius Faustianus, quinquennales, by decree of the corporati. Quaestors: Marcus Licinius Victor and Publius Aufidius Epictetus. The place was granted by public decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05700160.summary: An inscription dedicating a space to Quintus Calpurnius Modestus, a procurator with responsibilities in various regions, by the association of grain merchants.

EDCS-05700162.translation: Of Claudius Optatus, freedman of the Emperor, procurator of the port of Ostia.
EDCS-05700162.summary: An inscription identifying Claudius Optatus, an imperial freedman and procurator of the port of Ostia.

EDCS-05700166.translation: To Titus Flavius Verus, son of Titus, Palatina tribe, Roman knight.
EDCS-05700166.summary: A dedication to Titus Flavius Verus, a Roman knight.

EDCS-05700172.translation: To Vincentius Ragonius Vincentius, a most distinguished man, orator, quaestor of the urban forum, praetor, triumphal consul, prefect of the grain supply, who in the earliest years of his service, seeking all the adornments of virtue, flattering himself not at all with the nobility of his lineage, taught how much hope for excellent deeds his advancing age promised; hence it happened that our order, with the consent of the entire citizenry, willingly chose him as their perpetual patron as he deserved.
EDCS-05700172.summary: A lengthy honorific inscription praising Vincentius Ragonius Vincentius for his virtues and distinguished career, culminating in his election as perpetual patron by the city.

EDCS-05700174.translation: To Valeria, daughter of Publius Tussania, [daughter?] of Gnaeus Tussanius, the consul... her heirs.
EDCS-05700174.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely for a funerary monument, from the heirs of Gnaeus Tussanius to Valeria Tussania.

EDCS-05700176.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Marcus Umbilis Maximus.

EDCS-05700177.translation: Lucius Volusius Celer, son of Lucius, also called Ancharius, from the household of Lucius Volusius Saturninus, the consular.
EDCS-05700177.summary: This inscription records the identity of Lucius Volusius Celer Ancharius, likely for a tomb, mentioning his connection to a consular family.

EDCS-05700178.translation: To Volussius, Roman knight; ... to Volussius, Roman knight.
EDCS-05700178.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication to two individuals named Volussius, both identified as Roman knights.

EDCS-05700195.translation: Alcimus, steward of Caesar in charge of the library, made this.
EDCS-05700195.summary: This is a dedication made by Alcimus, a steward responsible for Caesar's library.

EDCS-05700196.translation: To the departed spirits, Andrias, a public slave, made this for himself, his wife, well-deserving, and the departed spirit of Cutia Epigone; the place was donated by Cassia Nigella.
EDCS-05700196.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a public slave for himself and his wife, with the plot donated by Cassia Nigella.
