EDCS-05700199.translation: To the departed spirits, Venerandus, freedman of Augustus and registrar of inheritances, made this for Fuscina, freedman of Augustus, assistant registrar, his kinsman.
EDCS-05700199.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Venerandus to his kinsman Fuscina, both freedmen of Augustus involved in administrative roles.

EDCS-05700201.translation: To the departed spirits, to Onesimus, dearest slave. Genialis, deputy imperial steward, lived for one year and twenty-five days.
EDCS-05700201.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Onesimus, a slave, and stating the lifespan of Genialis, a deputy imperial steward.

EDCS-05700203.translation: The imperial stewards of our emperor made this: Carpus, Zoticus Macrinus, Mhlomusus Berulli, Ulpius Macrinus, Farrius Sarapammon, Leo, Servilius Marianus, Servilius Callistianus, Servilius Lepidianus, Servilius Mansuetus, Aelius Quartio.
EDCS-05700203.summary: This inscription records the names of several imperial stewards who jointly commissioned a monument or work.

EDCS-05700210.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Atilius Probus, veteran of Augustus, made this for Gaius Flavius Valens, a well-deserving friend, who served for twenty-five years.
EDCS-05700210.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a veteran of Augustus to his friend Gaius Flavius Valens, who was also a soldier.

EDCS-05700211.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Marcus Aurelius Minia, veteran. Aurelius Eutyches made this.
EDCS-05700211.summary: A funerary epitaph for a veteran named Marcus Aurelius Minia, set up by Aurelius Eutyches, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700213.translation: Lucius Carutius, soldier of the Second Cohort of Vigiles, for himself and Eufrates and Caecilia, his daughter, and Fortunata, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-05700213.summary: An epitaph for Lucius Carutius, a soldier of the vigiles, and his family, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700215.translation: orius Faventinus, veteran of the Tenth Urban Cohort, and Sossia Euangelia made this for themselves and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-05700215.summary: A funerary monument set up by a veteran of the urban cohort and Sossia Euangelia for themselves and their descendants, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700216.translation: To Marcus Gentius Cogitatus, veteran of the First Cohort of Gentius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05700216.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Gentius Cogitatus, a veteran and freedman, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700218.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gaius Julius Maximus, veteran and former evocatus. Gaius Julius Marcellinus and Eusebius, his alumni, made this for him who deserved well.
EDCS-05700218.summary: A funerary monument for Gaius Julius Maximus, a veteran and evocatus, dedicated by his alumni, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700220.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Publius Nymphidius Fuscanius, son of Publius, veteran of the Fourth Cohort of Vigiles, Emperor's soldier. He rebuilt this for himself and for his wife Cornelia Filetis, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 22 feet, in the field 18 feet.
EDCS-05700220.summary: A funerary epitaph and tombstone record for Publius Nymphidius Fuscanius, a veteran of the vigiles, indicating dimensions of his property, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700225.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Titus Sextius Julianus, of the Fifth Cohort of Vigiles, aide to the prefect, who lived 29 years, 6 months, and 8 days. Titus Sextius Epaphra, his father, made this.
EDCS-05700225.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Sextius Julianus, a member of the vigiles and aide to a prefect, set up by his father, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700226.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Valerius Vereianus. Marcus Licinius Crassus, Emperor's evocatus, [made this].
EDCS-05700226.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Vereianus, set up by Marcus Licinius Crassus, an evocatus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700229.translation: For the artisans under the tribune Marcus Septimius Victor and the centurion Civius Flavius in the Fifth Cohort, and the optio Marcus Cippius Primus in the Second Cohort. Lucius Julius Victor, son of Lucius, from the Veturia tribe, sculpted this himself in Ostia. Caius Valerius Verecundus, freedman of Caius, from the Aniensis tribe, undertook [the vow] in Vercellae, paid it on the Ides of April, returned, and dedicated it on the Ides of August, the third day before the Nones.
EDCS-05700229.summary: A dedication by artisans and military officers, possibly related to the construction or repair of a building, with details of their roles and tribal affiliations, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05700230.translation: For Flavius Honorius, a most noble boy, and Flavius Eubodius, in the consulship of Favius Adeodatus, centurion of the Seventh Cohort, and Crispinus, [a soldier] of the Second Cohort, by the citizenship of Ostia. Honor...
EDCS-05700230.summary: A dedication honoring two young boys, Flavius Honorius and Flavius Eubodius, during the consulship of Favius Adeodatus and Crispinus, likely in Ostia, dating to the 4th or early 5th century CE.

EDCS-05700231.translation: He lived for 32 years, served for [unknown duration]; his heir, Antonius Longus, a centurion of the VI Praetorian Cohort, erected this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-05700231.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a soldier of the VI Praetorian Cohort who served for an unspecified period and died at age 32.

EDCS-05700232.translation: To the shades of the departed. Marcus Antonius Valentinus, trierarch [or soldier of similar rank] of Jupiter's [fleet/unit?], lived 35 years, served 15 years. Helvia Spes erected this for her husband.
EDCS-05700232.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Antonius Valentinus, who served for 15 years and died at age 35, erected by his wife.

EDCS-05700233.translation: For Lucius Carisius Valens, soldier of the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, of the century of Dan, of Vessus nation. He served for 21 years, lived for 40 years. Marius Hospitalis, his heir, erected this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-05700233.summary: This epitaph commemorates Lucius Carisius Valens, a soldier in the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, who served for 21 years and died at age 40.

EDCS-05700251.translation: During the consulship of Tiberius Claudius Severus and Gaius Aufidius Victorinus, the college of corporators, rowers, and auxiliary sailors of Ostia, [appointed] their patron Marcus Cipius Vitalis and Titus Antistus Favor. The quinquennales [officials] were Lucius Veius Adiutor, Marcus Cloelius Carus, Publius Ciarcius Vitalis, Marcus Cipius Fortis, Gaius Fonteius Fortunatus, Quintus Atilius Maritimus. The plebs [members] were Marcus Cipius Ostiensis, Publius Cloelius Primus the Younger, Quintus Atilius Lucrio, Publius Clylius Laeonas(?), Quintus Atilius Successus, Publius Cloelius Treptus, Marcus Cipius Felix, Publius Cloelius Vitalio, Marcus Cipius Fortunatus, Publius Ciarcius, Lucius Veius Paratus, Quintus Atilius Successus, Marcus Cipius Felix, Publius Cloelius Primus, Publius Cloelius Abascantus, Gaius Fonteius Victor.
EDCS-05700251.summary: This inscription lists officials and members of a guild of auxiliary sailors and rowers at Ostia, appointed patrons and quinquennales during the consulship of Severus and Victorinus (likely 158 AD).

EDCS-05700257.translation: Veidius Ostiensis, elected quinquennial official. Lucius Veratius Hermeros and Lucius Veratius Martialis, curators. Marcus Valerius Parthenopaeus and Gaius Messius Apollonius, Gnaeus Cornelius Pacatus, elected official. Gaius Baebius Carpio, elected official. Lucius Vincius Annianus, elected official. Gaius Iulius Docimus the Younger and Publius Marcius Romanus, Lucius Vallius Flavinus, elected official. Gaius Servilius Orthrus, elected official. Marcus Manlius Perpetuus, elected official. Gaius Iulius Annianus, elected official. Curator Aulus Herennuleius Eubulides, elected official. Gaius Publicius Chryseros, elected official. Gaius Messius Hagnus, elected official. Lucius Iulius, Lucius Baebius, Marcus Manlius, Aulus Livius, Marcus Cat, Lucius Clodius, Marcus Lucius, Lucius Iulius, Gnaeus Cornelius, Publius Cornelius, Lucius Baebius, Gaius Publicius, Lucius Annius, Gaius Marius, Lucius Iulius, Lucius Baebius, Lucius Varius, Marcus Obellius, Publius Cornelius.
EDCS-05700257.summary: This is a list of officials, including elected quinquennial officers and curators, likely from a collegium or administrative body, with many names appended, possibly as members or contributors.

EDCS-05700259.translation: Caecilius Maiulus, Rutilius Crescens, Lucretius Sodion, Ulpius Rufinus, Arellius Victor, Marius Qu...[illegible]..., Helvius Fecio, Helvius Zevartio, Helvius Linanticus, Lucceius Felix, Valerius Heliodorus, Iunius Fuscus, Aurelius Eracla, Aurelius Vitalio, Valerius Dierofil.
EDCS-05700259.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly of members of a group, patrons, or beneficiaries, with some names partially preserved.

EDCS-05700260.translation: Fortunatus, Magnus Caelianus, ...ius Zoticus, ...ntius Acontius, ...uleius Charito, Abascantus Felix contributed.
EDCS-05700260.summary: This fragmentary inscription records contributions made by several individuals, including Fortunatus and Abascantus Felix.

EDCS-05700262.translation: Vetticius, Caius Iulius Genialis, Caius Aemilius Honoratus, Aulus Fabius Ve..., Caius Rusticelius Feli..., Caius Laevonicus, Lucius Terentius Rapidius, Ep..., Varius Petronius, Cipius Petronius Parinius ius.
EDCS-05700262.summary: This incomplete inscription lists several names, likely members of a group or officials, with some names heavily restored.

EDCS-05700263.translation: Caius Valerius, Publius Ragonius, Marcus Maecenas, Lucius Clodius, Lucius Aufidius, Gaius Grattius, Lucius Pomponius, Iulius Lucius Cornelius [performed] eficius(?).
EDCS-05700263.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly patrons or members of an association, with a partially preserved verb at the end that may indicate an action or dedication.

EDCS-05700264.translation: Rogatianus, Rogatianus the Younger, Marcianus, Fortunatus the Younger, ...ius Alexander, ...ntimus, ...Eutyches, ...Theophilus, ...Proculinus OII.
EDCS-05700264.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely members or officials, with patronymics or agnomens indicated, ending with the abbreviation OII.

EDCS-05700267.translation: Abascantus, freedman of Quintus, Pudentianus, son of Mercurius Maron.
EDCS-05700267.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph, likely for a freedman named Abascantus, with additional names possibly related to his family or patrons.

EDCS-05700271.translation: Trophimianus, son of Marcianus, Ianuarius Junior, Marcus, Marcus, Titus H.
EDCS-05700271.summary: This inscription lists several Roman names, possibly indicating a group of individuals associated with a particular event or location, though its precise purpose is unclear.

EDCS-05700273.translation: Publius, Caius Tuccius Felix, Quintus Caecilius Creticus, Decimus Veturius Ianuarius, Caius Fundanius Philantus, Aulus Hostilius Asiaticus, Aulus Livius Eucaerus, Caius Iu.
EDCS-05700273.summary: This inscription is a lengthy list of Roman names, likely representing members of a collegium or a group of prominent citizens, possibly associated with Ostia.

EDCS-05700275.translation: HS III, HS IIII, Alexander, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, HS IIII, Caius Iulius Fulvius, Caius Iulius Refrius, Iulius.
EDCS-05700275.summary: This inscription seems to record financial contributions or allocations, possibly for a public project or a collegium, with a list of names associated with these amounts.

EDCS-05700280.translation: Patroni: Marcus Acilius Priscus, Aulus Egrilius Plarianus, Larcius Lepidus, Aulus Egrilius Plarianus, Agrippinus, Caius Iulius Istorius Octavianus, who is followed by the entire college of quinquennales. Synethus, quinquennalis and perpetual curator. Proclus, son of Publius. Herennianus, son of [---]. Cocceius Thallus. Egrilius Martialis. Agrius Priscus, son of Lucius. Caius Considius Epagathus. Caius Novius Trophimus. Clasuccius Faustus. Aulus Egrilius Urbicus, quinquennalis and perpetual curator. Caius Cartilius Secundus. Caius Maeclasius Primitivos, priest. Aulus Egrilius Zoilus, quinquennalis and perpetual curator. Caius Silius Vitalis, son of Caius, quinquennalis and perpetual curator. Quintus Patrius Victor, son of Quintus. Publius Aemilius Lupercalis, son of Publius. Titus Atinius Felix, son of Titus, quinquennalis. Caius Cipius Cerinthianus, son of Caius, perpetual quinquennalis. Caius Maeclasius Caedicianus, quinquennalis. Caius Iulius Genialis, senior, son of Caius, quinquennalis. Publius Claudius Abascantus, quinquennalis II. Caius Pomponius Quirinus, father, perpetual patron. Caius Pomponius Quirinus, junior, father, perpetual patron. Caius Iulius Octavianus, patron. Quintus Quintilius Zoticus, perpetual quinquennalis.
EDCS-05700280.summary: This inscription lists numerous members of the quinquennales, a college of officials, along with patrons and curators, likely for the city of Ostia during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700282.translation: The following are inscribed: Aulus Hostilius Asiaticus, Lucius Salonius Verecundus, son of Lucius, Caius Iulius Eutrapelus, Caius Tuccius Receptus, Caius Valerius Apollinaris, Titus Manlius Oceanus, Aulus Egrilius Herma, Quintus Orfitus Dexter, Publius Vannius Primus, Manius Obellius Euaristus, Lucius Licinius Ostiensis, Quintus Curtius Faustus, Caius Marcius Priscus, Publius Aedius Ostiensis, Aulus Livius Eucaerus Sedatus.
EDCS-05700282.summary: This inscription lists a group of individuals, possibly members of a collegium or participants in a public event, from the Roman period.

EDCS-05700286.translation: Manius Acilius Modestus, freedman of Manius, made this for himself and for Acilia Quarta, Eotinus, for himself, he made it.
EDCS-05700286.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Manius Acilius Modestus, a freedman, for himself and Acilia Quarta.

EDCS-05700287.translation: He made [this] for his freedman Leontius, Augustalis, from his own money, for Acutus, freedman of Publius Aemilius Leontis, for Iucundus, freedman of the mulieris Publius, for Hermione, freedwoman of the mulieris, for Cosmo, freedman of the mulieris.
EDCS-05700287.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something by an individual for his freedmen and possibly other freed persons, indicating manumission and familial relationships.

EDCS-05700288.translation: To all who held office as quinquennalis of the body of measurers of the grain supply, and as a mariner of Ostia, Aemilius Trophimas, Titus Aemilius Felix, Lucius Iulius Agathyrsus, and his heirs.
EDCS-05700288.summary: This inscription honors individuals who served in important administrative and maritime roles in Ostia, likely related to the grain supply.

EDCS-05700289.translation: To the Divine Manes of Agria Agathe. Publius Ostiensis Thallus, her tutor, sevir Augustalis, and Agria Tryphosa, her heirs, made this from their own property for her, who deserved well and merited it.
EDCS-05700289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Agria Agathe by her tutor and heir, who held the prestigious position of sevir Augustalis, indicating social status and familial devotion.

EDCS-05700295.translation: To Lucius Antonius Epitynchanus, lictor of the Curiatian decuries, who appears at public sacrifices, quinquennial official of the guild of Ostian carpenters, Augustal seviri in the province of Narbonensis, in the colony of Aquae Sextiae.
EDCS-05700295.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Antonius Epitynchanus, detailing his various official roles and his status as an Augustal seviri in the colony of Aquae Sextiae.

EDCS-05700299.translation: Arpagius Lupus, a most distinguished man, at the request of the citizens, gifted the place to the people, constructed at his own expense from the ground up, for the splendor of the nymphaeum, with which swiftness he fulfilled his vows.
EDCS-05700299.summary: This inscription records a gift by Arpagius Lupus, a distinguished man, of a newly constructed nymphaeum to the citizens.

EDCS-05700303.translation: Aurelius Agathyrus, freedman of Augustus, tabular officer, for the office of quinquennial perpetual magistrate.
EDCS-05700303.summary: This is a fragmentary record of Aurelius Agathyrus, a freedman of Augustus, possibly related to his holding a quinquennial office.

EDCS-05700307.translation: To Lucius Cacius Cinnamus, Augustalis, and to Cacia, wife of Auxinus.
EDCS-05700307.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to Lucius Cacius Cinnamus and Cacia Auxini.

EDCS-05700310.translation: To Lucius Caltilius Hilarus, and to Lucius Caltilius Celer, his brother.
EDCS-05700310.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to two brothers, Lucius Caltilius Hilarus and Lucius Caltilius Celer.

EDCS-05700311.translation: For the inscription of Publius Caninius, with a public funeral, Tiberius Iulius Demetrius.
EDCS-05700311.summary: This records Tiberius Iulius Demetrius arranging for a public funeral for Publius Caninius.

EDCS-05700315.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Lucius Carullius Epaphroditus, VI vir Augustalis, also quinquennial official. I lie here, I who always lived without blame, and whom Fortune had granted me my course, whose bones and ashes this stone within holds. To him, the VI viri Augustales after his quinquennial tenure, shall offer [this memorial], who served for four continuous years.
EDCS-05700315.summary: This is a self-penned epitaph for Lucius Carullius Epaphroditus, a VI vir Augustalis and quinquennial official, detailing his life and requesting remembrance after his tenure.

EDCS-05700316.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Lucius Carullius Epaphroditus, Augustal seviri, also quinquennial official, to his incomparable wife Eutychia, with whom he lived for 30 years.
EDCS-05700316.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Carullius Epaphroditus to his wife Eutychia, commemorating their 30 years of marriage and mentioning his own Augustal and quinquennial status.

EDCS-05700318.translation: For eternal memory. To Catinus Eliodorus, Augustal seviri. Quintus Catinius Castori and Quintus Catinius Ilarus and Quintus Catinius Nicephorus to their dearest father.
EDCS-05700318.summary: This is a memorial inscription set up by sons for their father, Catinus Eliodorus, who was an Augustal seviri.

EDCS-05700319.translation: Celer, freedman, made [this] for himself, for his patron Saturninus, Augustalis, and for Laea, his wife, and for Lanthanusa. He made [it] for his freedmen and freedwomen. DI.
EDCS-05700319.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Celer, a freedman, for himself, his patron Saturninus (an Augustalis), his wife Laea, and Lanthanusa, as well as his other freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-05700322.translation: Tiberius Claudius Germ, his wife Vilia, at her own expense, offered and dedicated this.
EDCS-05700322.summary: This is a dedication of a monument by a wife for her husband, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-05700326.translation: The names of those who [gave money] and on which days their birthdays [fell]... January / January 8th: Publius Claudius Veratus Abascantianus, 6000 denarii, 180 [denarii]; January 25th: Gargilius Felix, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; January 29th: Vivia Successa, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; February 1st: Bellicus Philocyrus, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; February 10th: Gaius Julius Victor Octavianus, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; February 8th: Vennius Faustus; February 10th: Atinius Doryphorianus, 50 [denarii]; February 1st: Julius Theomnestus, 3000 denarii, 90 [denarii]; March; April; Publius Claudius Veratus, 6000 denarii, 180 [denarii]; Pomponius Quirinus, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; May; May 1st: Maius Proculeius Chresimianus, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; May 3rd: Papinius Caricus, 2000 denarii, 60 [denarii]; May 17th: Aemilius Primus, 2000 denarii, 55 [denarii]; May 29th: Claudia Arria, mother, 6000 [denarii]; June 1st: Julius Cocilius Hermetes, [denarii]... Publius Claudius Abascantus, freedman of the three provinces, a marble tablet... June 6th... June 3rd... July 1st... July 7th... August 2nd... August 3rd... August 3rd.
EDCS-05700326.summary: This is a fragmented record detailing financial contributions and associated dates, likely from a funerary or collegial context, possibly from Ostia.

EDCS-05700330.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Urbanus, member of the seviri Augustales, also quinquennial, also decurion of the guild of carpenters of Ostia.
EDCS-05700330.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Urbanus, detailing his various civic and collegial offices, likely from Ostia.

EDCS-05700335.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Annia Ismene to her incomparable husband, Lucius Combarisius Vitalis, son of Lucius, of the Palatine tribe, a Roman knight, decurion of Laurentum and Ostia, who had held all the offices.
EDCS-05700335.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a wife to her husband, a prominent local official in Laurentum and Ostia, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-05700337.translation: Caius Cornelius Avitus, on behalf of Publius Nonius Herculanius the Younger, the cancelarii.
EDCS-05700337.summary: This inscription records a dedication or action taken by Caius Cornelius Avitus for Publius Nonius Herculanius Iunior, possibly related to scribal or administrative staff (cancelarii).

EDCS-05700340.translation: Publius Cornelius Statius, vigintivir, [served] his year, [held] his office, [paid] his expenses. Lucilius Gamala, vigintivir, [served] his year, [held] his office, [paid] his expenses, duumvir, a place and...
EDCS-05700340.summary: This inscription lists the honors and offices held by Publius Cornelius Statius and Lucilius Gamala, likely from a municipal context.

EDCS-05700342.translation: To himself and Cornelia his wife, and their freedwomen, a municipal Augustalis (member of the six priests of Augustus).
EDCS-05700342.summary: This is a dedication of a monument by a municipal Augustalis for himself, his wife, and their freedwomen, indicating a familial and social context.

EDCS-05700343.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Cornelia Cocceia, daughter of Marcianetus, most chaste and most religious, who lived 24 years, 4 months, 7 days. Cornelius Victorinus Isiacus and Cocceia Manliane, parents, [set this up]. Luxury O...
EDCS-05700343.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cornelia Cocceia, detailing her age and virtues, set up by her parents.

EDCS-05700344.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vinus Eduus, a municipal Augustalis, also quinquennial, who lived 2 years, 4 months, 20 days, set this up for himself while alive. Aticus.
EDCS-05700344.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Vinus Eduus for himself during his lifetime, recording his offices and lifespan.

EDCS-05700355.translation: Lucius Faecenius Apollonius, a municipal Augustalis, also quinquennial, made this for himself and for his patroness Faecenia Successa, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front [X] feet, in the field [X] feet.
EDCS-05700355.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Lucius Faecenius Apollonius for himself, his patroness, and their freed dependents, indicating a complex social and familial arrangement.

EDCS-05700356.translation: Sextus Vir Augustalis to his wife Felicitas and to their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, this outer monument, which does not follow an heir, is mine, traveller; know that it is indeed mine.
EDCS-05700356.summary: A funerary monument established by Sextus Vir Augustalis for his wife Felicitas and their descendants, intended to be inherited by them and not by the estate.

EDCS-05700357.translation: The freedman, also a quinquennial, made this for himself and Flavia Secunda, his freedwoman and wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Six and a half feet in front, eight feet in the field.
EDCS-05700357.summary: A tomb established by a freedman, who held the office of sevir Augustalis and quinquennial, for himself and his wife Flavia Secunda and their descendants, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-05700360.translation: To the Divine Shades of Aulus Granius Atticus, sevir Augustalis, chosen among the first quinquennials, perpetual curator.
EDCS-05700360.summary: An epitaph honouring Aulus Granius Atticus, who held multiple prestigious offices within the imperial cult, possibly dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05700361.translation: To the Divine Shades of Aulus Granius Atticus, freedman of Acestis, sevir Augustalis.
EDCS-05700361.summary: A dedication to the Divine Shades of Aulus Granius Atticus, who was a freedman and a sevir Augustalis.

EDCS-05700366.translation: To the Divine Shades, Verecunda set this up for her well-deserving freedman, Helo Hermetus, sevir Augustalis, also quinquennial.
EDCS-05700366.summary: A funerary dedication by Verecunda for her freedman Helo Hermetus, who served as a sevir Augustalis and quinquennial.

EDCS-05700369.translation: Gaius Julius Karus, a member of the college of six Augustales, made this for himself and his two daughters, Julia Damalis (daughter of Gaius) and Julia Kara (daughter of Gaius), and for his wife Niae Damalis, and for his father Julius Erotus.
EDCS-05700369.summary: A family tomb built by Gaius Julius Karus, a member of the college of six Augustales, for himself, his daughters, wife, and father.

EDCS-05700372.translation: To Lucius Lepidius Eutyches, sevir Augustalis, also quinquennial in the colony of Ostia, and in the municipality of Tusculum, and perpetual quinquennial of the college of shipwrights of Ostia. Fortunatus, his freedman, and Alexa Acte [dedicated this].
EDCS-05700372.summary: A dedication honouring Lucius Lepidius Eutyches, who held multiple quinquennial positions in Ostia and Tusculum, by his freedman and possibly his partner or slave.

EDCS-05700377.translation: To the memory of Publius Lucilius Gamala, Gnaeus Sentius Lucilius Gamala Clodianus [erected this] for his father.
EDCS-05700377.summary: A memorial erected by Gnaeus Sentius Lucilius Gamala Clodianus for his father, Publius Lucilius Gamala.

EDCS-05700378.translation: To the Divine Shades of Decimus Lutatius Charitonianus, son of Decimus, of the Palatine tribe, Roman knight, and decurion, having been admitted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05700378.summary: A funerary inscription for Decimus Lutatius Charitonianus, a Roman knight and decurion, honouring his admission by decree.

EDCS-05700379.translation: To the Divine Shades of Aulus Livius Chryseros, sevir Augustalis, quinquennial. Agathangelus, Onesimus, Callistus, and Carpus Hiberus, [dedicated this] to their deserving patron.
EDCS-05700379.summary: A dedication to the Divine Shades of Aulus Livius Chryseros, a sevir Augustalis and quinquennial, by his freedmen and clients.

EDCS-05700381.translation: To Livia Antigone, freedwoman of Aulus, and to her co-freedwoman and wife, Aulus Livius Callistus, quinquennial sevir Augustalis, [dedicated this] to the Divine Shades of Aulus Livius Callistus, quinquennial sevir Augustalis, and to their natural daughter, Acilia Deutera.
EDCS-05700381.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Livius Callistus to his freedwoman and wife, Livia Antigone, and their daughter Acilia Deutera, indicating Callistus's status as a quinquennial sevir Augustalis.

EDCS-05700386.translation: To the Divine Shades of Mundicia Felicissima, dearest wife, who lived 35 years, 3 months, and 12 days, Tiberius Claudius Arrianus, quinquennial sevir Augustalis, made this for herself and himself.
EDCS-05700386.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Tiberius Claudius Arrianus, a quinquennial sevir Augustalis, for his deceased wife Mundicia Felicissima.

EDCS-05700388.translation: By decree of the decurions, they erected [this monument] to Nicon, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-05700388.summary: This inscription records a public honor granted by the decurions to Nicon, a freedman, likely for his service to the community.

EDCS-05700389.translation: Publius Nonius Helianus and Nonia Crispinilla, children, and Nonia Syntrophia, dearest wife, made [this] to Publius Nonius Helio, quinquennial sevir Augustalis.
EDCS-05700389.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by the family (children and wife) to Publius Nonius Helio, who held the prestigious office of quinquennial sevir Augustalis.

EDCS-05700405.translation: To memory, Lucius Publicius Eutyches, quinquennial sevir Augustalis, stipulator and banker, and Publicia Epictesis made [this].
EDCS-05700405.summary: This inscription records the erection of a memorial by Lucius Publicius Eutyches, a quinquennial sevir Augustalis and banker, and Publicia Epictesis.

EDCS-05700413.translation: A // Sergia Prisca [erected this] in honor of Lucius Casius Reburrus, son, twice magistrate and decurions of Ostia decreed a public funeral and statue, and 50 pounds of incense; Lucius Casius Reburrus, having availed himself of the honor, remitted the cost of the funeral.
EDCS-05700413.summary: This inscription details a public honor awarded by the magistrates and decurions of Ostia to Lucius Casius Reburrus, including a funeral and statue, with the costs later waived by the recipient.

EDCS-05700414.translation: To the Divine Shades, Lucius Sextius Eros, to his dearest son, Lucius Sextius Sextianus Agrippinus, Roman knight, decurion of the colony of Ostia, who lived 15 years, 3 months, and 22 days, [made this].
EDCS-05700414.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Sextius Eros to his son, Lucius Sextius Sextianus Agrippinus, a young Roman knight and decurion of Ostia, who died at age 15.

EDCS-05700416.translation: Gaius Silius Iucundus, VI vir Augustalis, made [this] for himself and his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 16 feet in front. Tiberius Claudius Vitalis made [this] for himself and Tettia Homonoa, his wife, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 25 feet in the field. This monument is common with Tiberius Claudius Vitalis.
EDCS-05700416.summary: This inscription records a shared funerary monument, with separate sections allocated to Gaius Silius Iucundus, a VI vir Augustalis, and Tiberius Claudius Vitalis and his wife Tettia Homonoa.

EDCS-05700422.translation: Titus Statilius Ianuarius restored his triclinium at his own expense.
EDCS-05700422.summary: This inscription records the private act of Titus Statilius Ianuarius in restoring a triclinium (dining room) at his own expense.

EDCS-05700425.translation: Testii Helpidianus Priscus, Priscianus, and Felix, sons and heirs, to their dearest father, Titus Testius Helpidianus, quinquennial sevir Augustalis, also patron and quinquennial of the guild of marble workers of Treiectus.
EDCS-05700425.summary: This is a funerary dedication by sons and heirs to their father, Titus Testius Helpidianus, who was a quinquennial sevir Augustalis and a leader within the guild of marble workers of Treiectus.

EDCS-05700430.translation: Lucius Valerius Threptus made this, as quinquennial magistrate of the guild of shipwrights of Ostia, and curator of the merchants of the wine market, and quinquennial magistrate of the guild of the Genius of the wine market, from the property of his father Valerius and Valerius.
EDCS-05700430.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Valerius Threptus, who held multiple offices in Ostian trade guilds, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700433.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Vettia Severa, daughter of Quintus; to the spirits of the departed, Galatian, the Augustalis seviri of Aulus Egrilius Hermetis.
EDCS-05700433.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vettia Severa and Galatian, an Augustalis seviri, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700435.translation: Quintus Vibius Rufinus, son of Quintus, a decurion of the colony of Ostia, who had held honors, made this for himself while alive, and for his wife Claudia Nomina, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; 30 feet in front, 21 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700435.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Quintus Vibius Rufinus, a local official in Ostia, for himself and his family, specifying the dimensions of his plot, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700436.translation: Gnaeus Villius Hilarus, an Augustalis seviri and quinquennial magistrate, made this for himself and for his two brothers Gnaeus Villius Euhemerus and Sextio, and for his sister Villia Eutychia, and for his wife Modia Gemnis, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; 30 feet in front, 35 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700436.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Gnaeus Villius Hilarus, who held multiple civic offices, for himself and his family, specifying plot dimensions, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700438.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gaius Voltidius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, brother of the corporati of the guild of grain measurers of Ostia, who lived [X] years, and for his most sweet wife Voltidia Grapta. By Gaius Voltidius Palatina Cavarius Priscianus.
EDCS-05700438.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Voltidius Priscus and his wife Voltidia Grapta, set up by Gaius Voltidius Priscianus, mentioning his deceased brother's profession in Ostia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700439.translation: To Lucius Volusius, freedman of a woman, Dio, Augustalis seviri, also quinquennial magistrate. Greetings. May you fare well, whoever you are. To Iulia Thais, daughter of Spurius. May the gods treat you well.
EDCS-05700439.summary: This is an inscription addressed to Lucius Volusius Dio and Iulia Thais, both holding high social and religious positions, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700455.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions an Augustan official and possibly a woman of high status, its context and date are uncertain.

EDCS-05700461.translation: Dedicated on the day before the Nones of January, in the consulship of Silanus and Quintus Servilius Silanus, to Nasennius Marcellus, patron of the colony.
EDCS-05700461.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something on a specific date and consular year to Nasennius Marcellus, patron of a colony, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700462.translation: Dedicated on the 4th day before the Ides of March, in the reign of our lord Gordian Augustus and in the consulship of Marcus Acilius Aviola, by Quintus Veturius Felicissimus, elected quinquennial magistrate, and Gaius Julius Evangelus, Titus Marcius Chrysostomus, Titus Aurelius Eutychetes, curators, and Publius Aelius Eutychetes the younger, Lucius Traianus Arabus, Gaius Annius Basilides, Gaius Julius Tertullus.
EDCS-05700462.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument on a specific date and consular year during the reign of Emperor Gordian, listing various officials including elected magistrates and curators, likely from the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-05700463.translation: Dedicated [---] / [---] while [---]lio Hermetes and Quintus [---] were managing the care.
EDCS-05700463.summary: This fragmented inscription records a dedication and mentions individuals responsible for its upkeep, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700474.translation: Nonius Stephanus, a dyer, and his freedwoman Damalis, freedwoman of Lucius, and his freedman Philargyrus, to their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Lucius Caecilius, freedman of Lucius, and his freedwoman Dida Caecilia, freedwoman of Lucius, and his freedman Anteros, to their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Quintus Vibius Rufio and his freedwoman Secunda, freedwoman of Quintus, to their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700474.summary: This inscription records a complex property distribution and inheritance arrangement for freedmen and their descendants, likely related to a burial plot or columbarium, established by several patrons and their freed slaves.

EDCS-05700476.translation: Asclepiades, son of Simon, from Cnidus, made this for himself, his freedwoman Prepus, and his family.
EDCS-05700476.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Asclepiades for himself and his household, including a freedwoman, indicating a late Republican or early Imperial date.

EDCS-05700491.translation: Under the consulship of Lucius Lollianus Avitus and Titus Statilius Maximus, those who contributed to the monument: Publius Apertius Secundus, Aulus Mucius Festus, Gaius Publicius Athenio, Lucius Aufidius Tertius, Tiberius Claudius Claudianus, Aulus Mucius Saturninus, Lucius Aemilius Severus, Publius Aelius Onesimus, Marcus Iul[ius...].
EDCS-05700491.summary: This inscription lists contributors to a monument during the consulship of Lollianus Avitus and Statilius Maximus, likely an honorific monument or a shared funerary structure.

EDCS-05700495.translation: To Acilius Far, who lived... to his dearest son.
EDCS-05700495.summary: A fragmented epitaph for a son named Acilius Far, likely set up by his father, indicating a funerary context.

EDCS-05700496.translation: Acilius Sergianus made this for his dearest son, Acilius Eleusinius.
EDCS-05700496.summary: A funerary epitaph for Acilius Eleusinius, set up by his father Acilius Sergianus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700497.translation: To Acilia Prisca, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-05700497.summary: A simple funerary dedication to Acilia Prisca, identified as a freedwoman of Marcus, suggesting an epitaph.

EDCS-05700498.translation: To Acrantiana, who lived 26 years, 8 months, 13 days, and 2 hours, for her body and incomparable spirit, for the affection joined to her, made by those whom she deserved, in a place granted by Pacedius Fortunatus.
EDCS-05700498.summary: An epitaph for Acrantiana, detailing her lifespan and expressing deep affection, indicating the place of burial was arranged with Pacedius Fortunatus.

EDCS-05700505.translation: [Fragmentary names and titles, possibly related to a dedication or property ownership].
EDCS-05700505.summary: A heavily fragmented inscription with incomplete names and possible titles, its exact purpose is unclear due to damage.

EDCS-05700526.translation: To Aelia Felicissima, deserving well, a place fully given to herself and her arriving husband.
EDCS-05700526.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a burial plot to Aelia Felicissima and her husband, indicating a funerary context and possibly a pre-purchased or reserved space.

EDCS-05700530.summary: A very fragmented inscription, possibly a funerary dedication, to an individual named Aelia S[...].

EDCS-05700532.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Marcus Aemilius Callistratus.
EDCS-05700532.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the deceased Marcus Aemilius Callistratus.

EDCS-05700533.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Lucius Aemilius Daphnus of the Pomptina tribe, who lived 4 years and 6 days. Livia Daphne (made this) for her dearest son.
EDCS-05700533.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Aemilius Daphnus, who died at a very young age, and was dedicated by his mother Livia Daphne.

EDCS-05700534.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Marcus Aemilius Donatus, for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-05700534.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Marcus Aemilius Donatus for his wife.

EDCS-05700536.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Gaius Aemilius Octavius, who lived 6 years, two months, and 20 days.
EDCS-05700536.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gaius Aemilius Octavius at a young age.

EDCS-05700540.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Marcus Aemilius Vitalis, who lived one year, eight months, and 10 days. (From) his parents, for their dearest son.
EDCS-05700540.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Aemilius Vitalis at a very young age and was dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-05700541.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Aemilia Cia, who lived 15 years and 32 days. Marcus Aemilius Heliodorus, her father, made this for his well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-05700541.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aemilia Cia at age 15 and was dedicated by her father, Marcus Aemilius Heliodorus.

EDCS-05700542.translation: Aemilia Auge (made this) for herself and for her dutiful and dearest daughter Vitalia, who lived 24 years.
EDCS-05700542.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Aemilia Auge for herself and her deceased daughter Vitalia.

EDCS-05700544.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Aemilia Phillis, mother. Aemilius Eutyches, son, and Aemilius Restitutus, ward, made this for their well-deserving mother.
EDCS-05700544.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a son and a ward for their deceased mother, Aemilia Phillis.

EDCS-05700547.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Gnaeus Afranius Hermes, (and) for his son Gnaeus Afranius Primigenius, and for posterity.
EDCS-05700547.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Gnaeus Afranius Hermes for himself, his son, and his descendants.

EDCS-05700548.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for the daughter of Publius, Africa. ... paverit.
EDCS-05700548.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the deceased Africa, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-05700549.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Ermogenes, his son, made this for his well-deserving mother Afrodisia.
EDCS-05700549.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a son to his mother, dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700552.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Agathonices, the household slave.
EDCS-05700552.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a household slave named Agathonices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700554.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Agrius Successus Senior made this for himself while alive. No one else is permitted to be buried here.
EDCS-05700554.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, where a man named Gaius Agrius Successus Senior provided for his own burial and reserved the plot.

EDCS-05700555.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Agrius Successus made this for Agria Severa and for himself, and no one else is permitted to be buried here.
EDCS-05700555.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records Gaius Agrius Successus dedicating a tomb for Agria Severa and himself, reserving the plot.

EDCS-05700556.translation: For Agria Eroditus and for himself. Gaius Agrius Eros.
EDCS-05700556.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records Gaius Agrius Eros dedicating a tomb for Agria Eroditus and himself.

EDCS-05700558.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely from the Roman Imperial period, possibly funerary, mentioning Lucius Aius.

EDCS-05700560.translation: [---] Alcimus for his most beloved Agapetus.
EDCS-05700560.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning Alcimus and Agapetus.

EDCS-05700564.translation: To Lucius An[---]ialis. Aulus Marcianus(?), most dutiful.
EDCS-05700564.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning Lucius An[---]ialis and Aulus Marcianus.

EDCS-05700569.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Annianus lived for 2 years, 6 months, 18 days. His parents made this.
EDCS-05700569.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording the short life of Annianus and dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-05700572.translation: To our dearest son Annius Calpurnius, who lived 5 months, 20 days. Annius Agrippa the Younger, father, made this.
EDCS-05700572.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording the death of a young child, Annius Calpurnius, and dedicated by his father.

EDCS-05700577.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Annia Byzantia.
EDCS-05700577.summary: A funerary dedication to Annia Byzantia, likely a tombstone or epitaph.

EDCS-05700578.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: To Annia Ismene, daughter of Publius, for her incomparable wife, Caius Vettius Proclianus.
EDCS-05700578.summary: A funerary dedication from Caius Vettius Proclianus to his wife Annia Ismene, likely an epitaph from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700580.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Antiochis, whom Caius Vettius Fortunatus set up, who lived 14 years, 5 months, and 14 days; to one deserving well.
EDCS-05700580.summary: A funerary dedication recording the lifespan of Antiochis, likely set up by Caius Vettius Fortunatus, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700581.translation: 2 months, 8 days [for Antiochus?]; 11 months, 23 days [for someone else?]
EDCS-05700581.summary: Fragmentary text likely recording durations of life or mourning periods, possibly related to a tomb, with unclear dedicants and recipients.

EDCS-05700584.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Lucius Antonius Euvelpistus, his most dutiful son, Antonia Helpis, mother, set this up; he lived 17 years.
EDCS-05700584.summary: A funerary dedication from Antonia Helpis to her son Lucius Antonius Euvelpistus, recording his age at death, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700586.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Marcus Antonius Ostes, who lived 23 years, 10 months, and 22 days; Antonius Felix and Nonia Marcia made this for their dearest son.
EDCS-05700586.summary: A funerary dedication from Antonius Felix and Nonia Marcia to their son Marcus Antonius Ostes, recording his lifespan and likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700587.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Lucius Antonius Symophorus; his wife Balerias and his brother Quintus Bibius Onesimus [made this].
EDCS-05700587.summary: A funerary dedication from Balerias and Quintus Bibius Onesimus to Lucius Antonius Symophorus, likely an epitaph from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700588.translation: Antonius Valens and Licinia [---]sia his wife, when they shall have been placed in this sarcophagus, let no one else dare to place another body within it, which if they do, they shall pay a penalty of 30,000 sesterces, nor shall their body be accepted.
EDCS-05700588.summary: A funerary inscription prohibiting further burials in a sarcophagus, imposing a penalty for violation, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700591.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Antonia Pelagia, whom Titus Staberius Asiaticus, her freedman, set up for his well-deserving patroness.
EDCS-05700591.summary: A funerary dedication from a freedman, Titus Staberius Asiaticus, to his patroness Antonia Pelagia, likely an epitaph from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700592.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Antonia Thais, Lucius Firmius Fortunatus made this for his well-deserving wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05700592.summary: A funerary dedication from Lucius Firmius Fortunatus to his wife Antonia Thais, also intended for their freed slaves and descendants, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05700593.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Apertius Pius Iunior made this for his well-deserving father.
EDCS-05700593.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Apertius Pius Iunior to his father.

EDCS-05700594.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iunia Eutychia made this for Aphrodites, who lived for one year and eleven months, her dearest freedwoman.
EDCS-05700594.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Iunia Eutychia to her freedwoman Aphrodites, who died in infancy.

EDCS-05700595.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [His] father made this for Tiberius Apolleius Fortunatus, who lived for two years, two months, and twenty days, his dearest son.
EDCS-05700595.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a father to his young son, Tiberius Apolleius Fortunatus.

EDCS-05700596.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Apollonius. Quinta Dionysius made [this] for himself and [Apollonius].
EDCS-05700596.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Quinta Dionysius, likely for Apollonius and possibly for himself as well.

EDCS-05700597.translation: Marcus Appulleius Epaphra made this for himself and for Valeria Donata, his wife, and for Marcus Appullius Vitalis, freedman of Marcus, and for his own people and descendants, numbering ten urns.
EDCS-05700597.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Appulleius Epaphra for himself, his wife, his freedman, and descendants.

EDCS-05700600.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Apuleia Polla, daughter of Publius. Quietus, steward of Caesar.
EDCS-05700600.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Apuleia Polla, daughter of Publius, by Quietus, who served as Caesar's steward.

EDCS-05700606.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ustrinum. Lucius Arrius Asclepius and Lucius Arrius Crispinus restored this for themselves and their families, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 13 feet in front and 13 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700606.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a ustrinum (cremation site) by Lucius Arrius Asclepius and Lucius Arrius Crispinus for their family and descendants.

EDCS-05700607.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Here lies Lucius Arius Asclepius with his wife Tucia Crispina, a virtuous woman.
EDCS-05700607.summary: This inscription records the burial place of Lucius Arius Asclepius and his wife Tucia Crispina.

EDCS-05700608.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Tucia Crispina, his best wife, who deserved well of him. Lucius Arrius Asclepius.
EDCS-05700608.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Lucius Arrius Asclepius to his wife Tucia Crispina.

EDCS-05700609.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Arrius Asclepius made this for Tucia Crispina, his wife.
EDCS-05700609.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Arrius Asclepius to his wife Tucia Crispina.

EDCS-05700613.translation: To the Divine Shades of Arria Rufina.
EDCS-05700613.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Arria Rufina, likely on her tomb.

EDCS-05700616.translation: To the Divine Shades; Lucius Arruntius Asclepius made this for his well-deserving master.
EDCS-05700616.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Lucius Arruntius Asclepius for his master.

EDCS-05700617.translation: To the Divine Shades; Arruntius Ianuarius made this for his deserving wife Maessenia Heleritas, who lived for 18 years.
EDCS-05700617.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Arruntius Ianuarius for his wife Maessenia Heleritas, who died at 18.

EDCS-05700619.translation: Publius Arruntius Vitalis made this tomb for himself and for his wife Servilia Phillis and his daughter Arruntia Ammia, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 20 feet in front and 24 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700619.summary: This is a funerary monument purchased by Publius Arruntius Vitalis for himself, his family, and his freedmen, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-05700620.translation: Artoria Longina, Artorius Felix, and Artorius Capito made this for their deserving brothers.
EDCS-05700620.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Artoria Longina and her brothers Artorius Felix and Artorius Capito for their other brothers.

EDCS-05700621.translation: Artoria Osia, Mamidia Artoria Hygia, and Lucius Mamidius Artorius Dionysius made this for themselves, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 34 feet in front and 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700621.summary: This is a funerary monument purchased by Artoria Osia, Mamidia Artoria Hygia, and Lucius Mamidius Artorius Dionysius for themselves and their dependents, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-05700622.translation: Dasumius Iuvenis made this for Asclepia and for himself.
EDCS-05700622.summary: This dedication was made by Dasumius Iuvenis for a woman named Asclepia and for himself.

EDCS-05700623.translation: Apella, freedman of the woman Asia Euphosia, Felix, freedman of the woman, and Primigenius, freedman of the man Aulus Auctus, made this for their brother Malchio, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700623.summary: This funerary dedication was made by three freedmen for their brother Malchio, specifying the plot size.

EDCS-05700624.translation: To the Divine Shades of Asicia Semniane, daughter of Caius, who lived for 1 year, 1 month, and 12 days; Caius Asicius Eutyches and Caltilia Epithymete, also known as Voconia, her parents, made this.
EDCS-05700624.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Asicius Eutyches and Caltilia Epithymete for their infant daughter, Asicia Semniane.

EDCS-05700625.translation: [---] and for Asinia [---] patrona [---] Quintus Asinius [---]
EDCS-05700625.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication possibly made by Quintus Asinius for his patrona, Asinia.

EDCS-05700626.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Asinia Severa made this for her most dutiful and deserving mother, Asinia Thetis, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-05700626.summary: A funerary dedication made by Asinia Severa for her mother, Asinia Thetis.

EDCS-05700627.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Licinius Alexander made this for his deserving partner in life, Ateria Carrytyche, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-05700627.summary: A funerary dedication made by Licinius Alexander for his partner, Ateria Carrytyche, and their family.

EDCS-05700630.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Atilius Iustus, who lived 23 years, 2 months, and 20 days. Atilia Firmina, his mother, and Euzelus, his father, made this for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-05700630.summary: A funerary dedication made by Atilia Firmina and Euzelus for their son, Lucius Atilius Iustus.

EDCS-05700633.translation: Aulus Atinius Valens lived 45 years. Aulus Atinius Conmunis made this for his deserving patron.
EDCS-05700633.summary: An inscription recording the lifespan of Aulus Atinius Valens and a dedication from him to his patron.

EDCS-05700634.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Attennius, a good and most innocent man, who lived [---] years. Simplicia Fastidita made this for her deserving husband.
EDCS-05700634.summary: A funerary dedication made by Simplicia Fastidita for her husband, Marcus Attennius.

EDCS-05700635.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Atticilla, whose praenomen was Marcia, a plague whom fate denied.
EDCS-05700635.summary: A funerary dedication for Atticilla (Marcia), whose death is lamented.

EDCS-05700636.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sextus Atti, who lived [---] years.
EDCS-05700636.summary: A funerary dedication for Sextus Atti.

EDCS-05700637.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Attius Rufus, son of Lucius, who lived 4 years and [---] months. His most dutiful parents, Popilia Aphrodisia and Lucius Attius Iustus, [made this].
EDCS-05700637.summary: A funerary dedication made by Popilia Aphrodisia and Lucius Attius Iustus for their son, Lucius Attius Rufus.

EDCS-05700640.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aufius Ianuarius and Antilia Dantiba made this for their deserving son, Satus.
EDCS-05700640.summary: A funerary dedication made by Lucius Aufius Ianuarius and Antilia Dantiba for their son, Satus.

EDCS-05700645.translation: Aurelius [---], freedman of the emperor. [---] Aurelius Festiba[---]
EDCS-05700645.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly related to imperial freedmen.

EDCS-05700646.translation: Marcus Aurelius [left this for] Aelia Fi and Marco Opellius Felicissimus, who lived
EDCS-05700646.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a memorial, possibly mentioning Marcus Aurelius as a dedicant for Aelia Fi and Marco Opellius Felicissimus.

EDCS-05700647.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Aurelius bought this new plot for himself, eighty feet long and wide.
EDCS-05700647.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Marcus Aurelius records the purchase of a burial plot for himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700650.translation: [for] 5 months and [3]7 days, [worked] 9 hours. Marcus Aurelius Achilleus, freedman of the Augusti, [dedicated this] in memory of his incomparable wife.
EDCS-05700650.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, is dedicated by Marcus Aurelius Achilleus, a freedman of the emperors, to his wife, detailing her lifespan in months, days, and hours worked.

EDCS-05700653.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelia Chrysocoma [dedicated this] to her husband Canius Spes.
EDCS-05700653.summary: A funerary dedication from the Roman Imperial period, where Aurelia Chrysocoma honors her husband Canius Spes.

EDCS-05700655.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavia Irene made this for her well-deserving husband, Marco Aurelio Diogenes, who lived for 30 years.
EDCS-05700655.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, set up by Flavia Irene for her deceased husband, Marco Aurelio Diogenes.

EDCS-05700657.translation: To Aurelius Faustus, who lived 42 years, 1 month, and 26 days. Fausta Faustus [dedicated this to their] father, Ontia.
EDCS-05700657.summary: A funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, set up by Fausta Faustus for their father, Aurelius Faustus, providing his lifespan.

EDCS-05700658.translation: Marcus Aurelius Felicianus and Ulpia Atticilla made this for themselves and their family.
EDCS-05700658.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records the joint commission of a tomb by Marcus Aurelius Felicianus and Ulpia Atticilla for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-05700664.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Aurelius Iulianus made this for his well-deserving daughter, Aurelia Domitiana, who lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-05700664.summary: A funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, dedicated by Titus Aurelius Iulianus to his young daughter Aurelia Domitiana, specifying her lifespan.

EDCS-05700665.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Lucanus Gratus and Sulpicia Lasciba, parents, [dedicated this] to their most sweet son.
EDCS-05700665.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, where parents Aurelius Lucanus Gratus and Sulpicia Lasciba memorialize their son.

EDCS-05700666.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marco Aurelio Marciano, who lived for 5 years.
EDCS-05700666.summary: A funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period recording the death of a child named Marco Aurelio Marciano.

EDCS-05700669.summary: This inscription is a single name, likely referring to an individual mentioned in another context, possibly an official or a prominent citizen.

EDCS-05700673.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aurelius Valentinus, likely on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-05700675.translation: Aurelius Faustus made this for Aurelia Charite.
EDCS-05700675.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aurelius Faustus erected a monument for Aurelia Charite.

EDCS-05700676.translation: Iulia Felicissima made this for her well-deserving sister Aurelia Felicle.
EDCS-05700676.summary: This funerary inscription states that Iulia Felicissima dedicated a monument to her sister, Aurelia Felicle.

EDCS-05700678.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits of Aurelia Priscilla, who lived 27 years, 3 months, and 5 days, for her well-deserving wife.
EDCS-05700678.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Aurelia Priscilla, detailing her lifespan and noting she was a deserving wife.

EDCS-05700680.translation: To the departed spirits: Aurelia Rodope made this for her sweetest son Aurelius Crescens, who lived 14 years, well-deserving.
EDCS-05700680.summary: This funerary inscription records Aurelia Rodope dedicating a monument to her son, Aurelius Crescens, specifying his age.

EDCS-05700681.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits of Aurelia Valentina; Publius Durdenius Apollonius made this for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-05700681.summary: This funerary inscription states that Publius Durdenius Apollonius dedicated a monument to his incomparable wife, Aurelia Valentina.

EDCS-05700682.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits; Lucius Axilius Ostesis lived 750 years.
EDCS-05700682.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Axilius Ostesis, though the age is likely exaggerated for effect.

EDCS-05700684.translation: Lucius Axilius Parthenopeus made this for his excellent daughter Axsilia Tigris, who lived 21 years and 6 months.
EDCS-05700684.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Axilius Parthenopeus dedicating a monument to his daughter Axsilia Tigris, specifying her age.

EDCS-05700688.translation: Veratia Lacaena for her excellent husband Aulus Baebius Gaetulicus, son of Aulus.
EDCS-05700688.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Veratia Lacaena to her husband, Aulus Baebius Gaetulicus, highlighting his qualities.

EDCS-05700689.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Lucius Baebius Zoticus, and Baebius Auxanon, and Baebia Fotis, parents.
EDCS-05700689.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the parents Lucius Baebius Zoticus, Baebius Auxanon, and Baebia Fotis.

EDCS-05700690.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld: for Baebia Statia, who lived 8 years, 1 month, and 25 days. Baebius Proculus made this for his dearest daughter.
EDCS-05700690.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Baebius Proculus for his daughter Baebia Statia, who died young.

EDCS-05700691.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Caius Baebutius Florus made this for his most beloved wife, Aelia Lucilianetis.
EDCS-05700691.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Baebutius Florus for his wife Aelia Lucilianetis.

EDCS-05700692.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Caius Baebutius Florus made this for himself, and for his wife Fabia Maxima, and for his sons, freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. 14 feet in front, 25 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700692.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Baebutius Florus for himself, his family, and their descendants, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-05700693.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Caius Baebutius Maximus made this for his deserving wife Rubrinia Fortunata. [It is the] 6th [day].
EDCS-05700693.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Baebutius Maximus for his wife Rubrinia Fortunata.

EDCS-05700702.translation: To his most beloved wife: Lucius Iulius Veius Acmetianus.
EDCS-05700702.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the wife of Lucius Iulius Veius Acmetianus.

EDCS-05700703.translation: To Lucius, freedman; Faustilla, freedwoman; Lucius Cacius; Lucius Cacius; Lucius Cacius; Lucius Cacius; Lucius Cacius; Cacia, [daughter] of Lucius.
EDCS-05700703.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, possibly related to a funerary context or family record.

EDCS-05700708.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Lucius Katius Volusianus, who lived 19 years, 1 month, and 26 days. Primitivianus and Volusia, parents, made this, in a place granted by Gabinius Adiectus, their best friend.
EDCS-05700708.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Katius Volusianus, set up by his parents who obtained the burial plot with the help of a friend.

EDCS-05700712.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Publius Caecilius Felix, who lived 3 years, 5 months. Parents made this for their dearest son.
EDCS-05700712.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents for their young son, Publius Caecilius Felix.

EDCS-05700714.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Caecilius Felix, who lived 7 years, 2 months, 5 days. Atilia Clementina made this for her dearest son.
EDCS-05700714.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Atilia Clementina for her young son, Caecilius Felix.

EDCS-05700715.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Clodius Restitutus and Caecilia Italice made this for their well-deserving stepson, Aulus Caecilius Restitutus, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-05700715.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a stepfather and mother for their stepson, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700717.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Successa with her sons for her well-deserving husband, Quintus Caecilius Sotericus.
EDCS-05700717.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife and sons for their husband and father.

EDCS-05700719.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Donata, his wife, and Caecilius Secundus, his son, made this for their well-deserving father, Caecilius Valerianus, son of Lucius, who lived 58 years and 8 months and some days.
EDCS-05700719.summary: A funerary epitaph for a father, set up by his wife and son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700721.translation: Antiochis, freedwoman of Lucius Caecilius, 20 feet in front, 25 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700721.summary: A boundary inscription indicating land owned by Antiochis, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700725.translation: Caecilia Prisca for her son, Aufidius Agatho.
EDCS-05700725.summary: A dedication or memorial stone set up by a mother for her son.

EDCS-05700729.translation: Zethus Caelius inscribed for his freedwoman Aucta and for those who are listed above.
EDCS-05700729.summary: An inscription detailing the granting of property or rights by Zethus Caelius to his freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700732.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Loreia Secundilla made this for her relative Caesellia Specle, who lived 27 years, 3 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05700732.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caesellia Specle, set up by her relative Loreia Secundilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700733.summary: A dedication or memorial inscription for Aulus Caesennius Hermes.

EDCS-05700738.translation: Caesia Tryphaena, freedwoman of Titus, made this for herself and for Titus Caelsius, her dearest ward, who lived 5 years and 9 months, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 15 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700738.summary: A funerary and property inscription set up by a freedwoman for herself, her ward, and future descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700740.translation: Laudice, freedwoman of Decimus, made this for herself and for her most dutiful son, Gaius Gabinius Adauctus, who lived 12 years, and for her partner Gaius Gabinius Adauctus, and for their descendants.
EDCS-05700740.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for herself, her son, and her partner, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700741.translation: Gaius Caetronius Telesphorus, freedman of Gaius, erected this for himself, for his patron Gaius Caetronius Caecilianus, for his patroness Caecilia Moschis, his deserving wife, for Caetronia Gorgene, his fellow freedwoman, for his slave girl Caetronia Telesphoris, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. Forty feet across the front, forty feet in the field.
EDCS-05700741.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a freedman for his family and patrons, with dimensions of the plot specified.

EDCS-05700742.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Calavius, slave of his patroness Calavia, freedwoman of Marcus, erected this for his deserving patroness.
EDCS-05700742.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a slave for his deceased patroness.

EDCS-05700744.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ianuarius erected this for his most dutiful son Callicomas, slave of our Caesar, who lived for 3 months and some days.
EDCS-05700744.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a father for his young son, a slave belonging to the emperor.

EDCS-05700745.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Chryseros erected this for his most beloved Callicrates, who lived 14 years, 10 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05700745.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Chryseros for his beloved Callicrates, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-05700747.translation: EIVOL[---] and Callisti[---] sacred to [---] from [---]
EDCS-05700747.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording dedications or ownership.

EDCS-05700748.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Calpetana Procliane erected this for her most devoted husband Calpetanus Euthucetus, who lived 95 years.
EDCS-05700748.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife for her husband, noting his age at death.

EDCS-05700749.translation: [---] to Lucius' freedman Ca[---] PHO[---] PYTH[---] Calpur[nia?]
EDCS-05700749.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a funerary dedication, possibly mentioning a freedman and Calpurnia.

EDCS-05700752.translation: Marcus Calpurnius Eutychus, freedman of a woman, and Calpurnia Gemellina, daughter of Marcus, inscribed this title with the permission of Marcus Julius Taurion and Gaius Julius Tauriscus and Marcus Itharus, heirs, and Iulius Philumenus, and others, and I restored it and made it for the freedmen and freedwomen of my household and for Calpurnia Proticla.
EDCS-05700752.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of a tomb by Marcus Calpurnius Eutychus, a freedman, for his family and the freedpeople of his household.

EDCS-05700753.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Calpurnius Carpus lived 5 years and 4 months. Calpurnia Fortunula, his pupil, erected this for her most beloved.
EDCS-05700753.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a teacher (Calpurnia Fortunula) for her very young pupil (Caius Calpurnius Carpus).

EDCS-05700754.translation: Decimus Calpurnius Felix, freedman of Decimus, and Calpurnia Felicula, freedwoman of Decimus, daughter of Felix.
EDCS-05700754.summary: This inscription records two freedpersons, Decimus Calpurnius Felix and Calpurnia Felicula, likely on a shared monument.

EDCS-05700755.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Calpurnius Eucharistus made this for his most beloved son, Lucius Calpurnius Helpidianus, who lived 4 years, 7 months, and 20 days; a plot was given by Sextus Flavius Iustianus.
EDCS-05700755.summary: A funerary dedication for a young boy, Lucius Calpurnius Helpidianus, with the plot granted by Sextus Flavius Iustianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700757.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Agathoclia made this for her deserving husband, Gaius Calpurnius Proculus.
EDCS-05700757.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife, Flavia Agathoclia, for her husband, Gaius Calpurnius Proculus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700758.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Calpurnia Damalis made this for her deserving freedman, Lucius Calpurnius Reginus Senior, with whom she lived for 28 years and 6 months.
EDCS-05700758.summary: A funerary dedication by Calpurnia Damalis for her freedman and partner, Lucius Calpurnius Reginus Senior, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700760.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Calpurnius Reginus made this for his most dutiful mother, Calpurnia Damalis.
EDCS-05700760.summary: A funerary dedication by a son, Lucius Calpurnius Reginus, for his mother, Calpurnia Damalis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700761.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Bebius Arrius made this for his deserving freedman, Lucius Calpurnius Silvestris.
EDCS-05700761.summary: A funerary dedication by a patron, Lucius Bebius Arrius, for his freedman, Lucius Calpurnius Silvestris, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700763.summary: A dedication, possibly funerary, of Calpurnia Choran for Calpurnius, whose relationship is unspecified, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700765.translation: Annia Helpistate granted a plot to Calpurnius Pretorinus.
EDCS-05700765.summary: A grant of a burial plot by Annia Helpistate to Calpurnius Pretorinus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700766.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Demetrius made this for his most beloved wife, Calpurnia Turannis, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-05700766.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband, Demetrius, for his wife, Calpurnia Turannis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700767.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caltilia Felicitosa lived 26 years.
EDCS-05700767.summary: A funerary dedication for Caltilia Felicitosa, who died at the age of 26, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700768.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aurelius Reginus made this for his deserving wife, Calvidia Valentina.
EDCS-05700768.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband, Aurelius Reginus, for his wife, Calvidia Valentina, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05700769.translation: To the divine shades. Calvisius Iulianus made this for his deserving freedman Calvisius Faustus, who lived 15 years.
EDCS-05700769.summary: A funerary epitaph for a freedman named Calvisius Faustus, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700770.translation: To the divine shades. Lucius Caninius Felix lived 2 years and 3 months.
EDCS-05700770.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Lucius Caninius Felix, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700771.translation: Gaius Caninius Narcissus and his wife Valeria Priscilla made this for themselves while alive, and for her with whom he lived 23 years.
EDCS-05700771.summary: A funerary monument set up by a couple, Gaius Caninius Narcissus and Valeria Priscilla, for themselves and perhaps her deceased spouse, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700773.translation: Caninia Nothis, freedwoman of Publius and [his wife], made this for herself and for her fellow freedmen Publius Caninius Thalamus, Publius Caninius Mellitus, and Publius Caninius Synegdemus, her sons, and [---].
EDCS-05700773.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a freedwoman for herself and her deceased fellow freedmen, who are also referred to as her sons, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700774.translation: To the divine shades. Donatus Fratoraea, Atticus, Moschas, and Cosmus, freedmen, made this for Canuleia Sperata.
EDCS-05700774.summary: A funerary inscription set up by several freedmen for Canuleia Sperata, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700775.translation: To the divine shades. Numisia Seberina made this for her daughter Capia Augurina, who lived 7 years, 11 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-05700775.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Capia Augurina, set up by her mother, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700778.translation: Gaius Cartorius Genneus made this for himself and for his wife Caecilia Melitina, and for his adopted children and freedmen and freedwomen, and for the descendants of my family.
EDCS-05700778.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Cartorius Genneus for himself, his wife, adopted children, freedpersons, and future descendants, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700781.translation: To Car and Aec, his dearest grandson.
EDCS-05700781.summary: A funerary epitaph for a grandson named Carullus, addressed to his grandparents Car and Aec, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700784.translation: To the divine shades. Cassius Diogenianus made this for his brother Cassius Polynicen, who deserved well and lived 23 years and 51 days.
EDCS-05700784.summary: A funerary epitaph for a brother named Cassius Polynicen, set up by Cassius Diogenianus, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700785.translation: Gaius Cassius Eutyches made this for himself and for his incomparable wife Coelia Victorina.
EDCS-05700785.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Cassius Eutyches for himself and his wife Coelia Victorina, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-05700787.translation: To the departed spirits. Cassius Tyrranus for his dearest daughter Cassia Tyrranidi, who lived 7 years, 7 months.
EDCS-05700787.summary: A funerary epitaph for a daughter, set up by her father Cassius Tyrranus.

EDCS-05700789.translation: Cassia Calibe, freedwoman of Marcus, made this for her most devoted son Marcus Cassius Fatalis, son of Titus, of the Palatine tribe, and for herself, and for her freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05700789.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for her son and herself, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05700792.translation: Castor, who lived 13 years, 8 months, 3 days. Aelia Acte made this for her slave Castor.
EDCS-05700792.summary: A funerary epitaph for a slave named Castor, erected by his owner Aelia Acte.

EDCS-05700794.translation: To the departed spirits. Gnaeus Cattius Onesimus made this for himself and for Cattia.
EDCS-05700794.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Cattius Onesimus and Cattia, set up by Onesimus.

EDCS-05700797.translation: To the departed spirits. Caulia Restituta made this for her deserving patron Quintus Caulus Lenaeus.
EDCS-05700797.summary: A funerary epitaph for a patron, erected by his freedwoman Caulia Restituta.

EDCS-05700798.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Celerius made this for his wife.
EDCS-05700798.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her husband Publius Celerius.

EDCS-05700799.translation: Publius Celerius Faustus made this for himself and for his wife Mucilia Celestina and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for his son Publius Celerius Faustus of the Palatine tribe. Publius Celerius Faustus and Mucilia Celestina made this for their dearest son, who lived 8 years, 9 months, 27 days. In front 13 feet, in the field 26 feet.
EDCS-05700799.summary: A funerary epitaph for a family, recording the dimensions of the burial plot and the life span of a son.

EDCS-05700800.translation: To the departed spirits. Llia Damalis made this for her deserving husband Cerdon, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05700800.summary: A funerary epitaph for a husband, erected by his wife Llia Damalis.

EDCS-05700801.translation: [Restored] Roscius of Bosci, according to public law, 4 plots, from Publius Cerellius, for his monument, from which plots he granted one plot, deserving, well-deserving.
EDCS-05700801.summary: A fragmentary inscription detailing a land grant for burial plots, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05700802.translation: Gaius Cestius Fortunatus purchased a small shrine granted to himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
