EDCS-05700802.summary: A deed of purchase for a small shrine, establishing burial rights for the owner and his descendants.

EDCS-05700805.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Satur made this for his very rare wife Charconia, who lived 28 years.
EDCS-05700805.summary: A funerary dedication by Satur to his wife Charconia, dated by the style to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700809.translation: Chryseis for herself, her husband Chelidonius, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700809.summary: A funerary dedication made by Chryseis for herself, her husband Chelidonius, and their descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700810.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Chryserotus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-05700810.summary: A funerary dedication to Chryserotus, a freedman of Emperor Augustus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700816.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Claudianus, for 9 months and 11 days.
EDCS-05700816.summary: A funerary dedication for Claudianus, specifying a duration of 9 months and 11 days, likely indicating the age of a child, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700820.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudius Urbanus made this for his most beloved son, Claudius Afrodisius, who lived 3 years and 16 days.
EDCS-05700820.summary: A funerary dedication by Claudius Urbanus for his young son Claudius Afrodisius, who died at the age of 3 years and 16 days, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700822.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Claudianus, who was also Marcus Valerius Claudianus, lived 8 years for his beloved uncle Valerius Fuscus and his dearest foster-daughter Valeria Marcellina.
EDCS-05700822.summary: A funerary dedication by Valerius Fuscus and Valeria Marcellina for Tiberius Claudius Claudianus (also known as Marcus Valerius Claudianus), who lived 8 years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700823.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cartilia Tryphosa made this for Tiberius Claudius Epaphroditus.
EDCS-05700823.summary: A funerary dedication by Cartilia Tryphosa for Tiberius Claudius Epaphroditus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700825.translation: Tiberius Claudius Euphemus, freedman of Chrysogonus, for Restituta and Cincia Talia, his freedwomen, daughters, with property and thanks.
EDCS-05700825.summary: A dedication by Tiberius Claudius Euphemus, a freedman, for his freedwomen Restituta and Cincia Talia, indicating a mutual relationship and possibly a funerary context, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700828.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sia Pa made this for her most beloved son, Tiberius Claudius Philadelphus, who lived 5 years, 6 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-05700828.summary: A funerary dedication by Sia Pa for her young son Tiberius Claudius Philadelphus, who died at the age of 5 years, 6 months, and 21 days, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700831.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Egrilia, daughter of Aulus Paetinus, for her well-deserving husband Tiberius Claudius Iaso.
EDCS-05700831.summary: A funerary dedication by Egrilia for her husband Tiberius Claudius Iaso, described as deserving, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700832.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Marcellus lived for 3 years and 54 days. A tombstone for his sweetest son.
EDCS-05700832.summary: This is a tombstone for Tiberius Claudius Marcellus, a child who died young, set up by his parents Viator Zosimi and Claudia Asclepias.

EDCS-05700833.translation: To Marcus Claudius Marcianus, the pious.
EDCS-05700833.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Claudius Marcianus, who is described as pious.

EDCS-05700835.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Mercurius made this for his sweetest son, Tiberius Claudius Pinius, who lived for 14 years and 3 months.
EDCS-05700835.summary: This is a tombstone for Tiberius Claudius Pinius, who died young, made by his father Tiberius Claudius Mercurius.

EDCS-05700836.translation: Claudius Romanus for his sweetest foster-daughter, Claudia Melissa, who lived for 8 years, 9 months, and 19 days.
EDCS-05700836.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudia Melissa, a foster-daughter, set up by Claudius Romanus.

EDCS-05700838.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Marcus Claudius Summachus, also called Nonnus, who lived for 13 years and 6 months.
EDCS-05700838.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Claudius Summachus (also known as Nonnus), who died young.

EDCS-05700839.translation: For Claudius [---], Claudius Arianus [---] his son, for his well-deserving father.
EDCS-05700839.summary: This is a dedication to a well-deserving father, identified as a Claudius, with a partial mention of Claudius Arianus.

EDCS-05700840.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. He made this for his deserving wife, Claudia Natali, who lived for 42 years and 11 months.
EDCS-05700840.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudia Natali, who died at 42, made by her husband.

EDCS-05700841.translation: For his deserving wife, Claudia Ital[a?], and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700841.summary: This is a dedication for Claudia Ital[a?], her husband, and their dependents, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-05700842.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. He made this for his deserving husband, Claudia Asclepiodote, who lived for 10 years. Lucustylysus Nysus Mucus Saturus P M C S Saturus donated the place.
EDCS-05700842.summary: This inscription seems to be a tombstone for Claudia Asclepiodote, made by her husband and including a donation of land by others.

EDCS-05700846.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Claudia Prima. Antonius.
EDCS-05700846.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudia Prima, set up by Antonius.

EDCS-05700847.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Claudia Primitiva, mother, made this for her most dutiful daughter Claudia Restituta, who lived for 18 years, 5 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-05700847.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased daughter, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700852.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Decimus Clodius Ingenus lived for 3 years, 8 months, and 8 days. His father made this for his deserving son.
EDCS-05700852.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a father for his young son, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700857.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Cocceius Carpophorus and Avidia Attica made this for themselves and their family while alive.
EDCS-05700857.summary: A funerary dedication made by a couple for themselves and their household, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700858.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Sextus Cocceius Semno, an incomparable freedman.
EDCS-05700858.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring a freedman, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700859.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Marcus Coelius Abascantus, dearest son. Piladl an...
EDCS-05700859.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period, with an incomplete name or phrase at the end.

EDCS-05700865.summary: A dedication or ownership marker for Gaius Cominius Fortunatus, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700866.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Cominius Restus Quietus Pasianus made this for his deserving father, Gaius Cominius Successus.
EDCS-05700866.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a son for his father, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700869.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly a name on a tombstone or dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700874.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Cornelius Palatinus, son of Nthian. Lived for 9 years and 4 days.
EDCS-05700874.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700875.translation: Gaius Cornelius Abascantus for himself and his family.
EDCS-05700875.summary: A funerary dedication made by Gaius Cornelius Abascantus for himself and his household, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05700876.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cornelius Statilius made this for his well-deserving son, Lucius Cornelius Agathangelus, who lived 9 years, 4 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-05700876.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a boy named Lucius Cornelius Agathangelus, erected by his father.

EDCS-05700877.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Liberalis made this for his well-deserving friend, Publius Cornelius Adiutor.
EDCS-05700877.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Cornelius Adiutor, erected by his friend Titus Flavius Liberalis.

EDCS-05700879.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Safinia Calliste made this for her son Publius Cornelius Artemidorus and for herself.
EDCS-05700879.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Cornelius Artemidorus, erected by his mother Safinia Calliste, who also provided for herself.

EDCS-05700881.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for Titus Cornelius Cerdon.

EDCS-05700882.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Cornelius Zosimus made this for his most rare son, Marcus Cornelius Euhodianus, and for his mother Anthusa.
EDCS-05700882.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Cornelius Euhodianus and his mother Anthusa, erected by Marcus Cornelius Zosimus.

EDCS-05700883.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Cornelius Eutychus made this for himself, and for Cornelia Philematio, and for Caius Cornelius Eutychianus, and for Cornelia Fulvia, who lived 5 years, 6 months, and 15 days, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700883.summary: This is a family funerary epitaph for Caius Cornelius Eutychus, his wife, son, daughter, and descendants, including a young child who died at age 5.

EDCS-05700885.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Leontis for her husband, Lucius Cornelius Felicissimus, who lived 80 years more or less.
EDCS-05700885.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Cornelius Felicissimus, erected by his wife Cornelia Leontis.

EDCS-05700886.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Cornelius the father and Turrania Dionysia the mother made this for their well-deserving son, Caius Cornelius Melior, for themselves and for their household, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700886.summary: This is a family funerary epitaph for Caius Cornelius Melior, erected by his parents who also provided for themselves and their descendants and freedpeople.

EDCS-05700888.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Decimus Otacilius Evaristus made this for his most faithful friend, Titus Cornelius Restitutus.
EDCS-05700888.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Cornelius Restitutus, erected by his friend Decimus Otacilius Evaristus.

EDCS-05700890.translation: Caius Cornelius Speratus for himself and his household.
EDCS-05700890.summary: This is a self-provided funerary dedication by Caius Cornelius Speratus for himself and his family.

EDCS-05700893.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Valerius Cornelianus and Valeria Corneliane made this for their most dutiful grandmother, Cornelia Euhodia.
EDCS-05700893.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Valerius Cornelianus and Valeria Corneliane to their grandmother Cornelia Euhodia.

EDCS-05700894.translation: Cornelia Issula made this for herself and for her freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05700894.summary: A funerary monument made by Cornelia Issula for herself and her descendants.

EDCS-05700897.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Cornelia Zoticus, her most beloved and deserving mother.
EDCS-05700897.summary: A funerary dedication to Cornelia Zoticus by an unnamed individual.

EDCS-05700898.translation: To the Divine Shades. Considius Mercurius made this for his father, Considius Inbenta, who lived for 3 years.
EDCS-05700898.summary: A funerary monument for the child Considius Inbenta, made by his father Considius Mercurius.

EDCS-05700899.translation: Toria Cosmia made this for herself and for her freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, 8 feet in front and 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700899.summary: A funerary monument made by Toria Cosmia for herself and her descendants, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-05700901.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Statius Etheus made this for his freedman Chrysope, who lived 10 years.
EDCS-05700901.summary: A funerary monument made by Lucius Statius Etheus for his freedman Chrysope.

EDCS-05700902.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcia Chrysis made this for her most beloved husband, Caius Urtilius Nervas.
EDCS-05700902.summary: A funerary monument made by Marcia Chrysis for her husband Caius Urtilius Nervas.

EDCS-05700904.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Curtius Hyginus for his dutiful parent.
EDCS-05700904.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Publius Curtius Hyginus to his parent.

EDCS-05700905.translation: Marcus Curtius Sotericus made this for his darling Curtia Felicula, who lived 10 months and 3 days, and her mother Livia Acte. To the Divine Shades. Pompeia Nomas made this for her most sweet mother, Pompeia Chrysida.
EDCS-05700905.summary: Two related funerary monuments: one by Marcus Curtius Sotericus for Curtia Felicula and her mother Livia Acte, and another by Pompeia Nomas for her mother Pompeia Chrysida.

EDCS-05700908.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cnaeus Decimius Hermes made this for himself and for his freedman Cnaeus Decimius Primus and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, 6 and a half feet in front and 10 and a half feet in the field.
EDCS-05700908.summary: A funerary monument made by Cnaeus Decimius Hermes for himself, his freedman, and their descendants, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-05700910.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Decius Eutyches and Decia Thallusa made this for themselves and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05700910.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a couple for themselves and their descendants, indicating ownership of the burial plot.

EDCS-05700911.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Detelius Cyriacos, who lived for 6 years. His grandfather and grandmother made this.
EDCS-05700911.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child, erected by his grandparents.

EDCS-05700914.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with only the name of the deceased, Lucius Diomedes.

EDCS-05700915.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Dioscori, who lived 26 years and 6 months. Verus and Zoe made this for their well-deserving friend.
EDCS-05700915.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Dioscori, set up by his friends Verus and Zoe.

EDCS-05700916.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Luci Divili Fortunati, who lived 27 years. Aebutia Successa made this for her most beloved and well-deserving spouse.
EDCS-05700916.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Luci Divili Fortunati, erected by his wife Aebutia Successa.

EDCS-05700917.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gnaeus Domitius.
EDCS-05700917.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, merely mentioning the name of the deceased, Gnaeus Domitius.

EDCS-05700918.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Domitius Aterianus made this for Sallustia Crisprina, his well-deserving spouse, who lived 15 years and 15 days.
EDCS-05700918.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sallustia Crisprina, erected by her husband Quintus Domitius Aterianus.

EDCS-05700919.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Domitius Deuteros, son of Gaius, who lived 10 years, 8 months, and 28 days. Gaius Domitius Saturninus and Liciniae Thais, parents.
EDCS-05700919.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Domitius Deuteros, set up by his parents.

EDCS-05700921.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Domitia Crescentina, who lived 18 years, 9 months, and 25 days. Her mother made this.
EDCS-05700921.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia Crescentina, erected by her mother.

EDCS-05700922.translation: Domitia Aora made this for Aurelius Ponticus.
EDCS-05700922.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Domitia Aora to Aurelius Ponticus, likely for a monument or gift.

EDCS-05700923.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Marcus Peticius Crescens made this for his deserving wife Domitia Calliste.
EDCS-05700923.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Marcus Peticius Crescens to his wife Domitia Calliste.

EDCS-05700927.translation: Valeria Venuste made this for her sweetest mother Rogata (or Rogatia), deserving.
EDCS-05700927.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by Valeria Venuste for her mother, Rogata (or Rogatia).

EDCS-05700929.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Cai Donnius Hermadion.
EDCS-05700929.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cai Donnius Hermadion.

EDCS-05700931.summary: This inscription records the names of two brothers, Egnatius Dexter and Florus.

EDCS-05700934.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the names of two individuals.

EDCS-05700940.translation: To Aulus Egrilius Epitynchanus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-05700940.summary: This inscription records the name and manumission status of Aulus Egrilius Epitynchanus.

EDCS-05700944.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Aulus Aegrilius Heliodorus made this for his deserving wife Aegrilia Crescentilla, who lived 31 years and 10 days.
EDCS-05700944.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Aulus Aegrilius Heliodorus for his wife Aegrilia Crescentilla, recording her age at death.

EDCS-05700974.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Ernuleia Gaza lived 32 years, 8 months, 22 days, in a plot granted by Atilia Firmina, by her will, for her dearest friend.
EDCS-05700974.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Ernuleia Gaza and mentions the grantor of the burial plot, Atilia Firmina, and their relationship.

EDCS-05700976.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Gaius Erucianus.

EDCS-05700985.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Euphrosyne lived 6 years, 11 months. Faustus, father, made this for his deserving son.
EDCS-05700985.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of a child, Euphrosyne, and was made by her father, Faustus.

EDCS-05700986.translation: Eufrosyne, both to herself and to her own.
EDCS-05700986.summary: A funerary dedication by Eufrosyne, likely for herself and her family.

EDCS-05700987.translation: Quintus Otesius Eupolemus, freedman of Quintus, 20 feet in front and 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-05700987.summary: A boundary or property marker indicating dimensions of land owned by Quintus Otesius Eupolemus.

EDCS-05700990.translation: To Eutyches' son Fortunatus, who lived four years, well deserving; she made (this).
EDCS-05700990.summary: A funerary monument erected by an unnamed mother for her young son, Fortunatus.

EDCS-05700994.translation: To Gaius Fabius Adauctus, and to me, Felicula, his wife, joyful.
EDCS-05700994.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Fabius Adauctus and his wife Felicula.

EDCS-05700995.translation: By the will of Publius Fabius Callistratus, by his order the names of his freedmen and freedwomen: Publius Fabius Ampliatus, Publius Fabius Apsalma, Publius Fabius Adiutor, Publius Fabius Salama.
EDCS-05700995.summary: A list of freedpersons whose names are recorded in the tomb according to the will of Publius Fabius Callistratus.

EDCS-05700996.translation: Callistratus, freedman of Publius Fabius, Fabia Epiphania, Fabius.
EDCS-05700996.summary: A list of names, possibly related to a family tomb or property, including a freedman and two women.

EDCS-05700998.translation: Publius Fabius Ianuarius for himself and Marria Classica, his wife, half of the sepulchrum of Claudianus Turranianus, which is the left part when entering, which was granted by Lucius Turranius Severus, for himself and his freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants.
EDCS-05700998.summary: A record of the division and grant of a burial space within a larger sepulchrum, detailing ownership and inheritance rights.

EDCS-05700999.translation: ..., son of Titus, Philomusus, Fabia Hilara, ...
EDCS-05700999.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely containing names and relationships, possibly funerary or commemorative.

EDCS-05701001.translation: To the divine spirits of Fabia Agathonices, who lived 32 years and 36 days, and to her brother Tiberius Claudius Alexander.
EDCS-05701001.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Fabia Agathonices and her brother Tiberius Claudius Alexander.

EDCS-05701002.translation: All rights of this monument were granted by Fabia Epict[---].
EDCS-05701002.summary: A fragmented inscription indicating the transfer of rights related to a monument, initiated by Fabia Epict[---].

EDCS-05701003.translation: Fabia Secunda, freedwoman of (a woman), [made this for] Lucius Seius Auctus [and others]. For Fabia Irene, [for] Lucius Seius [?].
EDCS-05701003.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fabia Secunda, likely commemorating herself and possibly others, including Fabia Irene and Lucius Seius.

EDCS-05701004.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely recording the names of at least two individuals, Sextus Fad[ius?] and Fadia[?].

EDCS-05701007.translation: Lucius Faecenius Abascantus, freedman of Lucius, made [this] for his wife Calpurnia Fortis, who deserved well of him, 7 feet in front, 4 feet in width.
EDCS-05701007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Faecenius Abascantus for his deserving wife, Calpurnia Fortis.

EDCS-05701008.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelia Cypare made [this] for her husband Tiberius Faecenius Felix and her daughter Egrilia Tryphaenia.
EDCS-05701008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aurelia Cypare for her husband and daughter.

EDCS-05701009.translation: Faecenia Glucina made [this] for herself and for Gaius Julius Philadelphus, son of Gaius Julius, [with] 2 urns, an entranceway, and an enclosing wall, and for her own [family].
EDCS-05701009.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Faecenia Glucina for herself and Gaius Julius Philadelphus, detailing elements of the burial plot.

EDCS-05701011.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Faianius Secundus died first. He lived 17 years, 8 months, and 6 days. May the earth be light for you.
EDCS-05701011.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and age of Quintus Faianius Secundus.

EDCS-05701012.translation: [... ] Favor, freedwoman of a woman, Fel[ix/icia?].
EDCS-05701012.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely recording the name Favor, a freedwoman, and possibly another name.

EDCS-05701013.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Fausius Anthea memo[rial].
EDCS-05701013.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely commemorating Gaius Fausius Anthea.

EDCS-05701014.translation: [... ] Fausta, freedwoman of a woman, for herself and for Caecilius Statius and their descendants, 16 and a half feet in front, in the field [?].
EDCS-05701014.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Fausta, a freedwoman, for herself, Caecilius Statius, and their descendants, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-05701015.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Faustinus.
EDCS-05701015.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription dedicated to Faustinus.

EDCS-05701016.translation: To the Divine Manes, for Felicioni, his pupil.
EDCS-05701016.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Felicioni, likely a student or adopted son, by his patron.

EDCS-05701017.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Baebius made this for his son, Quintus Baebius Felicissimus, who lived 23 years, 3 months, and 10 days, a well-deserving son.
EDCS-05701017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Baebius Felicissimus, set up by his father, recording his age at death.

EDCS-05701018.translation: To the Divine Manes. Felicissimus lived 13 years. Valerius Apollinaris, his patron, made this for him, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-05701018.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Felicissimus at age 13 and was commissioned by his patron.

EDCS-05701019.translation: To the Divine Manes. For most pious Felicissimus, who lived 5 years, 2 months, 13 days, and 11 hours. His most unhappy parents.
EDCS-05701019.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Felicissimus by his parents, detailing his young age at death.

EDCS-05701020.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Felicissima, who lived 34 years, 5 months, and 23 days. Lucius Arrius Eutyches made this for his incomparable wife, with whom he lived 20 years.
EDCS-05701020.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicissima, commissioned by her husband, recording her age and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-05701021.translation: To the Divine Manes. For his sweetest mother, Mmia Felicitas, who lived 15 years. Leo Felius.
EDCS-05701021.summary: This funerary dedication is for Mmia Felicitas, identified as a mother, by Leo Felius.

EDCS-05701022.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Felicitas, who lived 8 years and some months.
EDCS-05701022.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas, recording her young age at death.

EDCS-05701023.translation: [---]etius, freedman of Marcus; [---]stus; Felicula, freedwoman of Marcus; [---]ius, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-05701023.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists several individuals, mostly freedmen, likely related to a funerary context or property ownership.

EDCS-05701025.translation: lived 2 years and 11 days. The place was granted to Marcus Ferranius for his monument, with full rights.
EDCS-05701025.summary: This inscription concerns the allocation of burial space and rights for Marcus Ferranius's monument, noting a duration of 2 years and 11 days.

EDCS-05701026.translation: To the Divine Manes. Aulus Fescenna Satrianus took care to have this made for Fescennia Donata, his freedwoman.
EDCS-05701026.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aulus Fescenna Satrianus commissioned a monument for his freedwoman, Fescennia Donata.

EDCS-05701027.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Fidelis, dearest son, who lived 2 years and 22 days. Donatus and Vitala, parents.
EDCS-05701027.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their young son, Fidelis.

EDCS-05701028.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Clementina, a well-deserving foster child, made this for her foster son Fidelis.
EDCS-05701028.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a foster mother for her deceased foster son, Fidelis.

EDCS-05701029.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Syllia Nemusa made this for her well-deserving slave girl Firma, who lived 15 years.
EDCS-05701029.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by an owner for her deceased slave girl, Firma.

EDCS-05701031.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Firmia Philete, dearest wife.
EDCS-05701031.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to a wife named Firmia Philete.

EDCS-05701032.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Flaccilla, a well-deserving wife, and to her dearest son Neombrotos, who lived 15 years, 3 months, and 17 days, with a miserable father. Ianuarius made this for them as deserving, and for himself.
EDCS-05701032.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Ianuarius for his wife Flaccilla and son Neombrotos, and also for himself.

EDCS-05701035.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Titus Flavius Alexander, who lived 28 years.
EDCS-05701035.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Alexander, who died at the age of 28.

EDCS-05701036.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavia Glycera made this for her well-deserving patron Titus Flavius Amerimnus and for her husband.
EDCS-05701036.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Flavia Glycera for her patron Titus Flavius Amerimnus and her husband.

EDCS-05701039.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Flavius Considianus, son of Caius, of the Palatina tribe, made this for his well-deserving parents, and for himself, and for his wife Flavia Primitiva, and for his sons Caius Flavius Pius and Caius Flavius Sabinus, and for his brother Marcus Farranius Sabinus, and for Quintus Hereius Adiutor, and for Quintus Hereius Karo, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. 27 feet in front, 17 feet in the ground.
EDCS-05701039.summary: A large funerary monument set up by Caius Flavius Considianus for his extended family, including parents, wife, sons, brother, and others, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-05701042.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Flavius Hopsitalis. Flavia Prima, a well-deserving slave girl.
EDCS-05701042.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Flavia Prima for her deceased master, Flavius Hopsitalis.

EDCS-05701043.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Titus Flavius Iovianus, who lived 15 years, 7 months, and 14 days. Titus Flavius Saturus, his son, made this for his dearest father.
EDCS-05701043.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a son, Titus Flavius Saturus, for his deceased father, Titus Flavius Iovianus.

EDCS-05701045.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Euresis [erected this] for her husband Titus Flavius Secundinus, an incomparable man.
EDCS-05701045.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Titus Flavius Secundinus by his wife Aelia Euresis.

EDCS-05701046.translation: Flavius Sabinius purchased this memorial from his own funds for Tamougalis, which he made for his children, grandchildren, and heirs and their descendants.
EDCS-05701046.summary: Flavius Sabinius created a memorial for his family, including his wife Tamougalis.

EDCS-05701049.translation: Titus Flavius Unio, granted the burial plot by Publius Iunius Aprilis, made this [structure] with an additional 18 urns for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701049.summary: Titus Flavius Unio constructed a burial structure for himself and his freedmen and their descendants, using a plot granted by Publius Iunius Aprilis.

EDCS-05701050.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titi Flavius Ursianus. Flavia Hygia [was] his mother, lived 11 months and 12 days.
EDCS-05701050.summary: A tombstone recording the brief life of Titi Flavius Ursianus, son of Flavia Hygia.

EDCS-05701053.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Aphrodisia.
EDCS-05701053.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Flavia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-05701054.translation: For Flavia Caecilia and Quintus Maecius Iuvenalis.
EDCS-05701054.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Flavia Caecilia and Quintus Maecius Iuvenalis.

EDCS-05701057.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Veturius Athenio [erected this] for his most beloved daughter Veturia Athenaïs.
EDCS-05701057.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Veturia Athenaïs by her father Caius Veturius Athenio.

EDCS-05701058.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Helpidi. Ofellius [was] her father, lived 19 years, 3 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-05701058.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flavia Helpidi at age 19, dedicated by her father Ofellius.

EDCS-05701060.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valerius Romanus [erected this] for his most rare wife Flavia Marcella.
EDCS-05701060.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Flavia Marcella by her husband Valerius Romanus.

EDCS-05701061.translation: Flavia Marcellina made a burial place for Flavia Hilaritas, her well-deserving sister, in a granted plot on the right side upon entering, from Plotus Hermetes and Valeria Saturnina.
EDCS-05701061.summary: Flavia Marcellina created a burial place for her sister Flavia Hilaritas, with the plot granted by Plotus Hermetes and Valeria Saturnina.

EDCS-05701062.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Sextius Epafra made this for his dearest wife, Flavia Maxima, who lived 30 years, 6 months, and 18 days, and 4 hours.
EDCS-05701062.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Titus Sextius Epafra to his wife Flavia Maxima, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701063.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavius Primus made this for his well-deserving daughter, Flavia Prima, who lived 3 years, 6 months, and 2 days, and 6 hours.
EDCS-05701063.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Flavius Primus to his young daughter Flavia Prima, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701064.translation: Flavia Rhodine made this for her well-deserving husband, Marcus Licinius Alexander.
EDCS-05701064.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Flavia Rhodine to her husband Marcus Licinius Alexander, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701066.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Hortensius Felix made this for his most holy wife, Flavia Tyrallida.
EDCS-05701066.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Quintus Hortensius Felix to his wife Flavia Tyrallida, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701068.translation: Floria made this for herself and for her wife, Zosime.
EDCS-05701068.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Floria for herself and her wife Zosime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701069.translation: For Flavia Asclepiodote and [her mother] Glycera, dearest mother.
EDCS-05701069.summary: This is a funerary dedication possibly from a daughter to her mother Glycera and another individual named Flavia Asclepiodote, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701070.translation: For Flavia Asclepiodote and her dearest son Bincen(ti)us.
EDCS-05701070.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Flavia Asclepiodote to her son Bincen(ti)us, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701073.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Fortunatus.
EDCS-05701073.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Fortunatus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701080.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Priscianus made this for his well-deserving wife, Fructosa, who lived 21 years, 5 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-05701080.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Priscianus to his wife Fructosa, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701082.translation: Lucius Fulvius Licca, freedman of Lucius, [and] Fulvia, freedwoman of Lucius, for her husband, Fulvia, while she was alive.
EDCS-05701082.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Fulvia for her husband Lucius Fulvius Licca, possibly indicating a joint tomb set up during their lifetime.

EDCS-05701083.translation: Lucius Fulvius Primus, freedman of a woman; Venusta, freedwoman of Lucius Fulvius, freedman of a woman; Hyla, freedman of Lucius Fulvius, freedman of a woman; Ianuaria, freedwoman of a woman; Lucius Fulvius Manius, son of Voturia Martiales; Manius Acilius Faventinus; Attice, freedwoman of Manius Acilius, freedwoman of a man; Anteros, freedman of Manius Acilius, freedman of a man; Pergamis, freedwoman of Manius Acilius, freedwoman of a man; Manius Acilius Restitutus, son of Manius, son of Voturia.
EDCS-05701083.summary: This is a fragmentary list of names, likely from a tomb inscription, recording several freedmen and freedwomen, with some patron-client relationships indicated, possibly dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05701084.translation: Fulvia [daughter of] C.; Caius Fulvius, [son of] Fulvia; Caius Fulvius, freedman of Caius; Valeria, daughter of Lucius; in front 20 feet, in the field [feet?].
EDCS-05701084.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or property record, specifying dimensions of land owned by individuals including Fulvia, Caius Fulvius, and Valeria, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701085.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulia Materna, his wife, made this for Gaius Fundanius Fortis, her deserving husband, and for their sons, to their sweetest father, who lived about 50 years.
EDCS-05701085.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Materna and her sons to her deceased husband, Gaius Fundanius Fortis, indicating he lived approximately 50 years, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701086.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Naevianus made this for his well-deserving wife, Fundania Faustina, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-05701086.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Iulius Naevianus to his wife, Fundania Faustina, stating she died at the age of 25, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701088.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Restitutus and Lucius Felicissimus [made this] for their incomparable father, Lucius Iurio Iucundus.
EDCS-05701088.summary: This is a funerary dedication by two sons, Lucius Restitutus and Lucius Felicissimus, to their father, Lucius Iurio Iucundus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701089.translation: To the Divine Shades. Furius Felicissimus made this for his dearest wife, Furia Aphrodisias.
EDCS-05701089.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Furius Felicissimus to his wife, Furia Aphrodisias, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701090.translation: To the Divine Shades. The sons made [this] for Gaius Anicetus.
EDCS-05701090.summary: This is a funerary dedication by sons to their father, Gaius Anicetus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701092.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gargilius Mercurius made this for his very rare friend, Gaius Valerius Zoticus, who lived 39 years.
EDCS-05701092.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gargilius Mercurius to his friend, Gaius Valerius Zoticus, noting he lived 39 years, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701093.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Gargilius Abascantus purchased for himself and for Octavia Marcella, his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, because for himself while living from the left side [unclear].
EDCS-05701093.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a columbarium, purchased by Marcus Gargilius Abascantus for himself, his wife Octavia Marcella, and their descendants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701094.translation: Four columbaria for Quintus Gavius Verecundus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-05701094.summary: This inscription records the dedication of four columbaria (dovecote-shaped tombs for cremated remains) for Quintus Gavi(us) Verecundus and his family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701095.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Gellius Plotianus made this for himself while alive, and for his sons Gellis T Secundus Junior and Secundinus, and for his Aelianus, and for his wife Calpurnia Euphrosyne, and for his Callyroe.
EDCS-05701095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Gellius Plotianus for himself and his family members.

EDCS-05701096.translation: For Gellia, Titus Perennius made this for his deserving wife and for himself.
EDCS-05701096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Titus Perennius for his wife Gellia and himself.

EDCS-05701098.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Marcius Aquila made this for his deserving wife Geminia Credula.
EDCS-05701098.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Marcius Aquila for his wife Geminia Credula.

EDCS-05701099.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donata, daughter of Marcius.

EDCS-05701100.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Geminia Eutuche, daughter who lived for 2 years, 7 months.
EDCS-05701100.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminia Eutuche, recording her short lifespan.

EDCS-05701101.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Genicia Calliste, Genicia Faentina, her most devoted mother, made this; she lived for 11 years, 10 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-05701101.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Genicia Faentina for her daughter Genicia Calliste, recording her age at death.

EDCS-05701102.translation: Gepidius Hermes and Gepidia Irene made this for themselves while alive, for Iulia Victoriae.
EDCS-05701102.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gepidius Hermes and Gepidia Irene for themselves and Iulia Victoriae.

EDCS-05701103.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gesatia Macrina made this for herself and for her well-deserving husband Marcus Cotisius Alexio.
EDCS-05701103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gesatia Macrina for herself and her husband Marcus Cotisius Alexio.

EDCS-05701107.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Fabia Maximina made this for her most devoted mother Grania Maximilla.
EDCS-05701107.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fabia Maximina for her mother Grania Maximilla.

EDCS-05701110.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Helpidius, an incomparable and deserving mother.
EDCS-05701110.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Helpidius, honoring an incomparable mother.

EDCS-05701111.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Helvia Helpis made this for Lucius Helvius Agrius, her patron and husband.
EDCS-05701111.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Helvia Helpis for her patron and husband, Lucius Helvius Agrius.

EDCS-05701113.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Helvius Restitutus made this for himself and his family, including freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-05701113.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Helvius Restitutus for himself and his household, including freedpersons.

EDCS-05701114.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Heraclitus, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-05701114.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Heraclitus at the age of 25.

EDCS-05701115.translation: Quintus Hereius Eumenes, freedman of Quintus Hereius; Hilara Hereia, freedwoman of Quintus Hereius; Faustus, freedman of the woman of Quintus Hereius; Faustula, freedwoman of the woman of Quintus Hereius; Quintus Hereius; [remainder illegible]
EDCS-05701115.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely members of a freed family, associated with the Hereius gens.

EDCS-05701116.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Hermo, for his deserving patron.
EDCS-05701116.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Hermo for his well-deserving patron.

EDCS-05701118.translation: Hermeros, freedman of the woman Na T [remainder illegible]
EDCS-05701118.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription identifying Hermeros as a freedman.

EDCS-05701120.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Orio, who lived 1 year and 6 months. Hermias [remainder illegible]
EDCS-05701120.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of a child named Orio, with Hermias mentioned.

EDCS-05701123.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Oratia Sabina, who lived 9 years, 10 months, and 13 days. Publius Oratius Victorinus, who lived 4 years and 31 days.
EDCS-05701123.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating two young children, Oratia Sabina and Publius Oratius Victorinus.

EDCS-05701124.translation: [fragmentary text mentioning Cn(aeus) Hordionius, freedman of Cn(aeus) l(iberto) Di[---], and Hordonia Laeta, freedwoman of Cn(aeus); Hordonia, daughter of Gn(aeus) Donatus; to Marcus Pinarius Antho, freedman of Marcus, my husband; Commodus, my slave; [---] by the arbitration of Caius Silius Chilo and Titus Manlius // Hordonia Phy[---], freedwoman of Gn(aeus); Eronis Longi [---]
EDCS-05701124.summary: This complex funerary monument inscription seems to record multiple individuals and relationships within the Hordionius family and their associates.

EDCS-05701127.translation: Aulus Hortensius Polyclitus lived 4 years. Hortensia Phaenusa, their mother.
EDCS-05701127.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aulus Hortensius Polyclitus and mentioning his mother, Hortensia Phaenusa.

EDCS-05701128.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Restituta made this for her most dutiful son Quintus Hortensius Restitutus, and for herself, and for her deserving husband Quintus Allius Tertius, and for her most dutiful daughter Allia Quinti Filia Quinti, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701128.summary: A funerary monument set up by Iulia Restituta for her son, husband, and herself, along with their descendants.

EDCS-05701131.translation: Publius Humanius Pamphilus, freedman of a woman, and Publius Humanius Pelagius, son of Spurius, [occupies] 20 feet in front and 35 feet in depth.
EDCS-05701131.summary: A property boundary marker indicating land measurements associated with Publius Humanius Pamphilus and Publius Humanius Pelagius.

EDCS-05701132.translation: Humania Angelis, freedwoman of Publius; Publius Humanius Diomedes, freedman of a woman; Terpolia Nice, freedwoman of a woman; Humania Iucunda, freedwoman of Publius; Marcus Terpolius Philargyrus, freedman of a woman; Publius Humanius Acastus, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-05701132.summary: A list of names, likely freedmen and freedwomen associated with the Humanii and Terpolii families, possibly on a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-05701134.translation: For Marcus Petronius Sotericus; Petronia Nice, freedwoman of Marcus and a woman; Petronia Leda, freedwoman of Marcus and a woman; Marcus Petronius Hermes, freedman of Marcus and a woman; for themselves and their family.
EDCS-05701134.summary: A dedication of a tomb or property to Marcus Petronius Sotericus and other members of the Petronii family, including freedpersons.

EDCS-05701136.translation: Caius I H, aged 19 years, 11 months, and 10 days; for his own freedmen, and descendants.
EDCS-05701136.summary: A tomb inscription for Caius I H, who died at a young age, also intended for his freedmen and descendants.

EDCS-05701137.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Ianuaria made this while alive for herself, and for her incomparable husband Valerius Lucrio, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Granted to her with the plot of land which is in front of the facade of this monument, extending around by 1 foot and up to the boundary from Aedthania's nephew Otio Prisco, 14 feet in front of the monument and 23.5 feet in depth.
EDCS-05701137.summary: A funerary monument deed specifying land dimensions and usage rights, erected by Ianuaria for herself and her husband Valerius Lucrio.

EDCS-05701139.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Papia, freedwoman of Augustus, made this for Ianuarius, slave of Caesar.
EDCS-05701139.summary: A funerary dedication by an imperial freedwoman for an imperial slave.

EDCS-05701140.translation: For my dear freedman Anthos, freedman of MIA Ingenua, for freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 25 feet.
EDCS-05701140.summary: A dedication of land or a tomb for the freedman Anthos, also intended for his descendants.

EDCS-05701141.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iphitus, slave of Flavius, for his very sweet fellow slave Euhodius.
EDCS-05701141.summary: A funerary dedication from a slave to his fellow slave.

EDCS-05701142.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Trebonius Irenaeus made this for Irene, who lived 6 years, 8 months, and 19 days, his sweet foster-child.
EDCS-05701142.summary: A funerary monument erected by Trebonius Irenaeus for his young foster-child Irene.

EDCS-05701143.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Isidorus lived for 12 years and 11 months. Lucius Aemilius Hermes made this for himself and for his wife Voltidia Cyclas.
EDCS-05701143.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Aemilius Hermes for his son Isidorus and himself and his wife.

EDCS-05701147.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For the repose of Lucius Iulius Albinus. His son Lucius Albinus Pupus erected this in pious memory of his father.
EDCS-05701147.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Albinus Pupus for his father Lucius Iulius Albinus.

EDCS-05701148.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For the cession and donation of the entire monument: from Iunia Anthide and Plotus Hermas, freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. To the spirits of the departed. Apusulenius Servata, for the cession and donation of the entire monument: from Iunia Anthide. To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Antonius Hermetus, for the cession and donation of the entire monument: from Iunia Anthide and Plotus Hermas, freedmen.
EDCS-05701148.summary: A funerary monument record concerning the cession and donation of parts of the monument by Iunia Anthide and Plotus Hermas to various individuals, likely freedpersons and their descendants.

EDCS-05701153.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Iulius Celadus, dearest son, who lived 5 years and 4 months. Gaius Iulius Summachus, father, made this. The plot was given by Virgilla Tyche.
EDCS-05701153.summary: A funerary monument for Gaius Iulius Celadus, set up by his father Gaius Iulius Summachus, with the plot provided by Virgilla Tyche.

EDCS-05701154.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Iulius Chryseros.
EDCS-05701154.summary: A funerary dedication to Lucius Iulius Chryseros.

EDCS-05701156.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Iulius Crescens, who lived for 1 year, 8 months, and 22 days. Marcus Iulius Crescens, father, made this.
EDCS-05701156.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Iulius Crescens for his son of the same name.

EDCS-05701161.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Iulius Eytyches made this for himself, and for Gaius Iulius Hermetus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 24 feet, in the field 23 feet.
EDCS-05701161.summary: A funerary monument established by Gaius Iulius Eytyches for himself, his relative Gaius Iulius Hermetus, and their freedpersons and descendants, with dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-05701162.translation: Gaius Iulius Felicissimus, to Aurelia Sirice, well-deserving, [he] lived.
EDCS-05701162.summary: An epitaph for Aurelia Sirice, erected by Gaius Iulius Felicissimus, possibly indicating her death or the end of her life.

EDCS-05701163.translation: Gaius Iulius Felix Hilarianus made this at his own expense for Menander, servant of Caesar.
EDCS-05701163.summary: A dedication made at his own expense by Gaius Iulius Felix Hilarianus for Menander, a servant of Caesar.

EDCS-05701164.translation: Iulia Themis, to her husband Gaius Iulius Fortunatus, and for herself.
EDCS-05701164.summary: A dedication by Iulia Themis for her husband Gaius Iulius Fortunatus and for herself.

EDCS-05701168.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caltilia Isidora made this for her dearest foster-son, Gaius Julius Ingenuus, also called Mininnus, who lived 8 years, 10 months.
EDCS-05701168.summary: A funerary dedication by Caltilia Isidora to her foster-son, Gaius Julius Ingenuus, dated by his age.

EDCS-05701169.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Iul and Helvia Profutura made this for their dearest son, Julius Marcianus, who lived 2 years, 9 months, 22 days.
EDCS-05701169.summary: A funerary dedication by Aurelius Iul and Helvia Profutura to their son, Julius Marcianus, dated by his age.

EDCS-05701172.translation: Gaius Julius Optatus made this for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701172.summary: A funerary dedication made by Gaius Julius Optatus for himself and his freed dependents.

EDCS-05701173.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Orbia Philumene placed this for her son, Gaius Julius Paulinus, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Quirina, who lived 7 years, 1 month, 7 days.
EDCS-05701173.summary: A funerary dedication by Orbia Philumene to her son, Gaius Julius Paulinus, dated by his age.

EDCS-05701174.summary: An incomplete inscription likely naming a person, Gaius Julius Philodomus.

EDCS-05701179.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. His father and mother made this for their dearest son, Quintus Julius Restitutus, who lived 2 years, 8 months, 26 days, worthy of remembrance.
EDCS-05701179.summary: A funerary dedication by parents for their son, Quintus Julius Restitutus, dated by his age.

EDCS-05701185.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aquiliae Helpidi arranged for this to be made for her dearest son, Gaius Julius Theodorus, and for her well-deserving wife Balentia.
EDCS-05701185.summary: A funerary dedication arranged by Aquiliae Helpidi for her son and wife.

EDCS-05701186.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Julius Zosimus made this tomb for himself and for his most devoted wife, Cassia Paulina.
EDCS-05701186.summary: A funerary dedication made by Marcus Julius Zosimus for himself and his wife, Cassia Paulina.

EDCS-05701190.translation: Iulia, wife of [---]aris, [arranged for the] tomb of Hilar[us].
EDCS-05701190.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription likely mentioning Iulia as the wife of someone and dedicating a tomb for Hilarus.

EDCS-05701193.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Artemisia made this for her well-deserving husband, Sextus Julius Hermetus.
EDCS-05701193.summary: A funerary dedication made by Iulia Artemisia for her husband, Sextus Julius Hermetus.

EDCS-05701194.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ashes of Iulia Auge.

EDCS-05701197.translation: To Iulia Eusebia, daughter of Gaius, and Gaius Iulius Bassus. Magnia Felicula, freedwoman of Titus, made [this] for herself and for Marcus Licinius Eunicus, freedman of Marcus, her cohabitant, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. Numerius Trebonius [---]
EDCS-05701197.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb complex established by Magnia Felicula for herself, her cohabitant, and their descendants, also mentioning Iulia Eusebia and Gaius Iulius Bassus.

EDCS-05701205.translation: Iulia Priscilla lived 25 years. Philocalus [made this] from his own means.
EDCS-05701205.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Iulia Priscilla and mentions Philocalus as the dedicator.

EDCS-05701206.translation: To the Divine Manes of Iulia Quartilla. Iulius Niceforus dedicated [this] to his incomparable wife, with whom he lived for 36 years.
EDCS-05701206.summary: This funerary inscription records Iulius Niceforus' dedication to his wife, Iulia Quartilla, noting their lifespan together.

EDCS-05701207.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes of Iulia Restituta. Marcus Caesius Vitalis made [this] for his excellent wife.
EDCS-05701207.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Caesius Vitalis' dedication to his wife, Iulia Restituta.

EDCS-05701208.translation: To the Divine Manes of Iulia Sereni, who lived 2 years, 8 months, and 10 days. Iulia Bictorina [dedicated this] to her most sweet daughter.
EDCS-05701208.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Iulia Sereni and is dedicated by her mother, Iulia Bictorina.

EDCS-05701209.translation: To the Divine Manes of Iulia Severa. Lucius Aurelius made [this] for his deserving wife, who lived 150 years, 3 months, and 10 hours.
EDCS-05701209.summary: This funerary inscription records the exceptionally long life of Iulia Severa and is dedicated by her husband, Lucius Aurelius.

EDCS-05701210.translation: To the memory of Iulia Silvana, who lived 4 months and 4 days.
EDCS-05701210.summary: This funerary inscription records the brief life of Iulia Silvana.

EDCS-05701211.translation: To the Divine Manes of Iulia Ispeti, his deserving wife. Feistilius Hilarianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05701211.summary: This funerary inscription records Feistilius Hilarianus' dedication to his deserving wife, Iulia Ispeti.

EDCS-05701212.translation: Iulia T made [this] for her deserving [person].
EDCS-05701212.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription mentions Iulia T as a dedicator for an unnamed deserving person.

EDCS-05701213.summary: This inscription, likely from a tombstone, records Iulia Thecla as a mother.

EDCS-05701214.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iulia Tychen, sweetest soul.
EDCS-05701214.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Iulia Tychen, described as a sweet soul.

EDCS-05701216.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iulia Zosima, who lived 8 years, 10 months, 10 days, 10 hours. Quintus Iulius Hermadio and Iulia Procula made this for their beloved foster-daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-05701216.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and details of Iulia Zosima's life and was erected by her foster parents, Quintus Iulius Hermadio and Iulia Procula.

EDCS-05701217.translation: To the departed spirits, for Decimus Iunius Attianus Agrippinus, son of Decimus Iunius Decimus, grandson of Decimus Iunius, great-grandson of Decimus Iunius. He lived 4 months and 15 days. Probus and Agrippina made this for their son.
EDCS-05701217.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Decimus Iunius Attianus Agrippinus and was made by his parents, Probus and Agrippina.

EDCS-05701218.translation: To the departed spirits, for her father, who deserved well. Iunia Hermione, daughter of Decimus Iunius Decimus and his freedwoman Epaphroditus, made this.
EDCS-05701218.summary: This funerary inscription records Iunia Hermione honoring her father, Decimus Iunius Decimus.

EDCS-05701219.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iunius Profuturus and Iunius Ireneus made this for their well-deserving father and mother.
EDCS-05701219.summary: This funerary inscription records Iunius Ireneus honoring both his father and mother.

EDCS-05701220.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Marcus Iunius Protus, who lived 7 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-05701220.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Marcus Iunius Protus and records his lifespan.

EDCS-05701222.translation: To the departed spirits, for Gaius Iunius Vitus, who lived 55 years, and 4 months. Caius Iunius T. for his well-deserving patron.
EDCS-05701222.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gaius Iunius Vitus and is dedicated by his patron.

EDCS-05701223.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iunia Philurtia, from Iunius Ampliatus, for his excellent wife.
EDCS-05701223.summary: This funerary inscription records Iunia Philurtia and is dedicated by her husband, Iunius Ampliatus.

EDCS-05701225.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iunia Restuta, who lived 19 years, 6 months, and 28 days, and for her son Lucius Caecilius Lucilianus, who lived 2 years, 1 month, and 15 days. Marius Eutyches made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-05701225.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Iunia Restuta and her young son Lucius Caecilius Lucilianus, and was erected by Marius Eutyches.

EDCS-05701226.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Salinator Felix and Pompeius Dionysius made this for their deserving wife.
EDCS-05701226.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by two individuals for their wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701227.translation: To Gaius Iuventius Agathemerus, freedman of Capia Quinta, and to Elegans, freedwoman of the Curiatii, and to Iuventia Secunda, freedwoman of the Curiatii.
EDCS-05701227.summary: This is a funerary dedication likely for multiple individuals, possibly freedmen or freedwomen, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701228.translation: The entire right side of the monument upon entering, including the lower burial chamber, belongs to Iuventius Fronto, and Maria and Flavia, Fortunata, daughter of Gaius, their wife, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants are heirs to this tomb.
EDCS-05701228.summary: This is a funerary inscription specifying inheritance rights to a tomb, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701232.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Sextus Laelius Felix.
EDCS-05701232.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) for Sextus Laelius Felix, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701234.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Sextius Aprilis made this for his dearest wife, Laeta.
EDCS-05701234.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by a husband for his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701238.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lappia Zmyrna, who lived 32 years, 7 months, and 11 days. Flavia Rufina for her mother and Flavius Rufinus for his most chaste and deserving wife.
EDCS-05701238.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) with the ages of the deceased, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701239.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aulus Larcius Mercurius, who lived 5 years, 10 months, and 25 days. To the dearest.
EDCS-05701239.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) for a young child, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701240.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Larcia Asclepiodote made this for her dearest daughter, Arruntia Hilara.
EDCS-05701240.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by a mother for her daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701242.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Gaius Levonicus Agathon, parents Gaius Levonicus Philo and Levonica Soteris for their dearest son, who lived 6 months.
EDCS-05701242.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by parents for their young son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701244.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Licinius Eutyches for Licinius Pro[...]
EDCS-05701244.summary: This is a partial funerary dedication (Dis Manibus), likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701245.translation: To Marcus Licinius Hieronimus, to Licinia Flora, daughter of Marcus Licinius, and to Licinia Primigenia, mother.
EDCS-05701245.summary: This inscription is a dedication to three individuals, likely family members, possibly on a tomb monument.

EDCS-05701247.translation: Lucius Licinius Trophimus made this for himself, for his wife Licinia Onomaste, for his most dutiful son Licinius Arescontus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701247.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Lucius Licinius Trophimus commissioned the monument for his family and dependents.

EDCS-05701252.translation: To the divine spirits of Liguria Trophimus.
EDCS-05701252.summary: This is a simple dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (divine spirits of the departed) for Liguria Trophimus, likely a tomb inscription.

EDCS-05701256.translation: Aulus Livius Thallus made this for his freedman Epictetus, a freedman of Aulus Livius Priscus, a deserving patron, and for himself and his own.
EDCS-05701256.summary: This funerary inscription records Aulus Livius Thallus commissioning a monument for his freedman Epictetus and his own family.

EDCS-05701257.translation: To the divine spirits of Aulus Livius Eutychus, son of Aulus Livius, most innocent soul.
EDCS-05701257.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' for Aulus Livius Eutychus, likely a tomb memorial.

EDCS-05701258.translation: To the divine spirits of Aulus Livius Iustus, who lived 13 years, 4 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-05701258.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Aulus Livius Iustus, dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus'.

EDCS-05701260.translation: Marcus Livius Philargyrus made this for himself, for Naevia Venusta, and for Naevia Primigenia, who donated to Annia Zosimena and Gaius Canuleius Venustus, who proved the deed and restored the inscription, for themselves and their own, for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, on land 20 feet wide in front and 13 feet deep.
EDCS-05701260.summary: This complex funerary inscription details the commissioning of a monument by Marcus Livius Philargyrus for multiple individuals, including those who proved a deed and restored the inscription, along with land dimensions.

EDCS-05701262.translation: To the divine spirits of Aulus Livius Restitutus, who lived 2 years, 2 months, and 25 days.
EDCS-05701262.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' for Aulus Livius Restitutus, recording his young age at death.

EDCS-05701264.translation: Livia Verecunda made this for her deserving son Aulus Livius Severus, and for herself.
EDCS-05701264.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Livia Verecunda commissioned a monument for her son Aulus Livius Severus and herself.

EDCS-05701265.translation: To the divine spirits of Aulus Livius Soterichus, [from] Livia Euporia, alumna, to her deserving patron.
EDCS-05701265.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' for Aulus Livius Soterichus, commissioned by his alumna Livia Euporia for her patron.

EDCS-05701266.translation: Aulus Livius Trophimus, freedman of Aulus and Sextilia, [and] freedman of the freedwoman Repentina, and freedman of the freedwoman Dorcas, [dedicates this to] himself and Sextilia, his wife, and to his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, 30 feet of land.
EDCS-05701266.summary: This is an funerary epitaph recording the dedication of land by a freedman to himself, his wife, and his freed dependents.

EDCS-05701267.translation: To the departed spirits of Aulus Livius Verus, son of Aulus.
EDCS-05701267.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Aulus Livius Verus.

EDCS-05701268.translation: To the departed spirits. Savina, wife of Savinus Livius, son of Livius.
EDCS-05701268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Savina.

EDCS-05701269.translation: To the departed spirits. Aulus Livius Erastus made this for his beloved pupil who lived 4 years, 8 months, and 24 days.
EDCS-05701269.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, made by his teacher.

EDCS-05701270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Livia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-05701271.translation: To the departed spirits of Livia Agathonice.
EDCS-05701271.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Livia Agathonice.

EDCS-05701273.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Ariadne, a freedwoman.

EDCS-05701274.translation: To the departed spirits of Livia Crescentina, who lived 19 years.
EDCS-05701274.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Livia Crescentina.

EDCS-05701277.translation: To the departed spirits of Livia Procope. Aulus Livius Restitutus made this for his most pious mother who lived 29 years, 5 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-05701277.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Livia Procope, made by her son Aulus Livius Restitutus.

EDCS-05701278.translation: To the departed spirits of Livia Rufina, a well-deserving mother. [She] made this.
EDCS-05701278.summary: This is a funerary epitaph to Livia Rufina, made by herself or for her.

EDCS-05701280.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Livia Rufina made this for her sister Livia Venusta, who lived 40 years.
EDCS-05701280.summary: A funerary dedication made by Livia Rufina for her sister Livia Venusta.

EDCS-05701281.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Livia Vera.
EDCS-05701281.summary: A funerary dedication to Livia Vera.

EDCS-05701283.translation: Longina made this for the well-deserving, buried here.
EDCS-05701283.summary: A dedication made by Longina for a well-deserving individual buried at this location.

EDCS-05701287.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucceia Agrippina, who lived 21 years, 9 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-05701287.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucceia Agrippina, specifying her lifespan.

EDCS-05701288.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucceia Restituta. Marcus Lucceius Chius [made this].
EDCS-05701288.summary: A funerary dedication made by Marcus Lucceius Chius for Lucceia Restituta.

EDCS-05701289.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucilia. Quintus Lucilius, her father, [made this].
EDCS-05701289.summary: A funerary dedication made by Quintus Lucilius for his daughter Lucilia.

EDCS-05701290.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucius, his foster-son, who lived six years. Lucius Arrius Niceros made this.
EDCS-05701290.summary: A funerary dedication made by Lucius Arrius Niceros for his foster-son Lucius.

EDCS-05701292.translation: For Marcus Lucretius Heraclidas, who lived 5 months. Marcus Lucretius Heraclides, his father, made this.
EDCS-05701292.summary: A funerary dedication made by Marcus Lucretius Heraclides for his son Marcus Lucretius Heraclidas.

EDCS-05701293.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Lucretius Martialis made this for himself, and for Herennia Palladis, his deserving wife, and for their heirs.
EDCS-05701293.summary: A funerary dedication made by Marcus Lucretius Martialis for himself, his wife Herennia Palladis, and their heirs.

EDCS-05701294.translation: Caius Lucretius Paris made this for the well-deserving.
EDCS-05701294.summary: A funerary dedication made by Gaius Lucretius Paris for a well-deserving individual.

EDCS-05701295.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Lucretius Restutus and Pompeia Procula, father and mother, made this for their most devoted daughter. She lived 11 years, 26 days.
EDCS-05701295.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucretia Prima, set up by her parents, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701296.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lusia, his dearest wife. Sala, husband.
EDCS-05701296.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lusia, set up by her husband Sala, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701297.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Decimus Lutatius Carpophorus.
EDCS-05701297.summary: A funerary epitaph for Decimus Lutatius Carpophorus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701301.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sextus Macrinus Rufinus, who lived 2 years, 11 months, 14 days. Sextus Macrinius Successus, father, made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-05701301.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Macrinus Rufinus, set up by his father, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701304.translation: Titus Malius Hermes, freedman of Amaranthus, made this for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701304.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing self-dedication and provision for freedpersons and their descendants, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701305.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Malius Symphorus made this for his most devoted son Titus Malio Melander, who lived 4 years, 8 months, 9 days, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-05701305.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Malio Melander and for the dedicator Titus Malius Symphorus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701306.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Malia Profutura, who lived 12 years, 4 months, 8 days. Licinius Profuturus, father, gave this.
EDCS-05701306.summary: A funerary epitaph for Malia Profutura, set up by her father Licinius Profuturus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701307.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Mallius Saturninus, his dearest son. Statia Pompeia, mother, made this.
EDCS-05701307.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mallius Saturninus, set up by his mother Statia Pompeia, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701308.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Mammius Menander, who lived 3 years. Porcia Asclepiodote made this for her dearest son.
EDCS-05701308.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Mammius Menander, set up by his mother Porcia Asclepiodote, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701309.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Mammius Onesemus made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-05701309.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Mammius Onesemus for his son, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701310.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Mamius Onesimus, most beloved, who lived VI years and [some] months, most beloved.
EDCS-05701310.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a child named Lucius Mamius Onesimus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-05701311.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Mamius Primitivus, Lucius Mammius Felix [dedicated this] as his foster-son.
EDCS-05701311.summary: This funerary dedication records Lucius Mammius Felix honoring Lucius Mamius Primitivus, likely a foster-son.

EDCS-05701317.translation: Aulus Manlius Faustus, Martha Primigenius, freedwoman of Aebutia, daughter of Aulus, and Origo, freedman of the woman [named] Marcus Petronius Atilena, and Felix, freedman of the woman [named] Caius Albius, made [this] for himself and his family. In front 25 feet, in the field 20 feet. To the spirits of the departed, for Marcus Aurelius Bassus, Aurelia Eparcia, freedwoman, made [this] on her own property.
EDCS-05701317.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription detailing land ownership and dedications by several individuals, including Aulus Manlius Faustus and Aurelia Eparcia, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05701320.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Caius Manilius Rogatus, who lived 15 years and 5 months. Manlia Pompeia made [this] for her son.
EDCS-05701320.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Manilius Rogatus, dedicated by his mother Manlia Pompeia.

EDCS-05701321.translation: From the will, 6,000 sesterces, under the supervision of Titus Manlius Nicon, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-05701321.summary: This inscription records a financial bequest from a will, managed by Titus Manlius Nicon.

EDCS-05701322.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Titus Manlius Valens.
EDCS-05701322.summary: A simple funerary dedication to Titus Manlius Valens.

EDCS-05701323.translation: Titus Manlius Venustus [dedicated this] to his father Manlius [---] and to his wife Clopa[---] and for himself.
EDCS-05701323.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication by Titus Manlius Venustus for his father, wife, and himself.

EDCS-05701324.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Manlia, daughter of Marcus, of Civitas, who lived 2 years and 2 months. Marcus Manlius Apsyrtus, father, made [this].
EDCS-05701324.summary: A funerary inscription for Manlia, daughter of Marcus, who died in childhood, dedicated by her father Marcus Manlius Apsyrtus.

EDCS-05701326.translation: To Manlia Montana, freedwoman of Marcus, [and] to Felicula, freedwoman of Marcus Manlius.
EDCS-05701326.summary: This is a funerary dedication honoring two women, Manlia Montana and Felicula, both freedwomen of Marcus (and possibly Marcus Manlius).

EDCS-05701327.translation: Manlia Helpis made [this] for Titus Manlius Halbas, her patron, her husband.
EDCS-05701327.summary: This inscription records Manlia Helpis dedicating a monument to her patron and husband, Titus Manlius Halbas.

EDCS-05701331.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription commemorating at least two freedwomen, Primilla and Syntyche, with the name Marcellinus also mentioned.

EDCS-05701332.translation: To Gaius Marcius Crescent, who lived 14 years and 9 hours. His parents, Gaius Marcius Threptus and Marcia Carpime, made this for their sweetest son, and for themselves, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. The right of way and surrounding space is owed to this monument; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-05701332.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Marcius Crescent, who died at 14 years of age, set up by his parents and including provisions for their freedmen and descendants, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701335.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Antonius Agathon made this for his sweetest daughter Marcia Antonia, who lived 3 years, 3 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-05701335.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcia Antonia, who died at the age of 3 years, 3 months, and 16 days, dedicated by her father, Antonius Agathon.

EDCS-05701338.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For his most beloved infant daughter Marinia, who lived 13 years and 30 days. Aufidius Victor, her father, made this for her and for himself.
EDCS-05701338.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marinia, an infant daughter who lived 13 years and 30 days, dedicated by her father Aufidius Victor.

EDCS-05701339.translation: Publius Marius P., for his parents.
EDCS-05701339.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Publius Marius P. dedicated a monument to his parents.

EDCS-05701341.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For his sweetest son Gaius Marius Epictetus, who lived 3 years and 10 months. His parents.
EDCS-05701341.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by parents to their son Gaius Marius Epictetus, who died at 3 years and 10 months of age.

EDCS-05701343.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Myron made this for his most pious brother Gaius Marius Julianus, who lived 9 years and 4 months.
EDCS-05701343.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Myron to his brother Gaius Marius Julianus, who died at 9 years and 4 months of age.

EDCS-05701345.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Hermes and Deutera made this for their well-deserving fellow freedman Mari.
EDCS-05701345.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Hermes and Deutera to their fellow freedman Mari.

EDCS-05701348.translation: In memory of L. Maria, with whom Varus lived PRE CIAR
EDCS-05701348.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription commemorating L. Maria and mentioning a person named Varus, likely a funerary dedication from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701349.translation: The eternal house of the Marracii.
EDCS-05701349.summary: This is an epitaph for the Marracii family, indicating ownership or dedication of a burial place, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701350.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Maximilla for her foster-child, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-05701353.translation: Publius M[...]vius, freedman of Publius, made this for himself and [...] Publius M[...] ME[...] ME[...]
EDCS-05701353.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication, likely a tombstone, with the dedicant and recipients partially legible.

EDCS-05701354.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Mercurialis lived 5 years and 10 months. Mercurius (his) father made [this].
EDCS-05701354.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life span of a child named Mercurialis and made by his father, Mercurius.

EDCS-05701356.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Messalina, dearest daughter, who lived 29 years, 8 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-05701356.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring a daughter named Messalina and recording her age at death.

EDCS-05701361.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Mesulena Anthioxis, daughter of Dionysiades, who lived 15 years, 2 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05701361.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring a daughter named Mesulena Anthioxis and recording her age at death.

EDCS-05701362.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Publius Metilius Agathyrsus, who lived 9 years, 8 months, and 10 days. His parents [made this] for their most devoted son.
EDCS-05701362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by parents for their devoted son, Publius Metilius Agathyrsus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-05701363.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Marcus Mettius Damas. Helvia Firmina made [this] for her husband.
EDCS-05701363.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Helvia Firmina for her husband, Marcus Mettius Damas.

EDCS-05701365.translation: For Marcus Mevius. Marcus Mevius, (his) son, [made this] for his most excellent father, for himself, and for posterity.
