EDCS-05701365.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a son, Marcus Mevius, for his father, Marcus Mevius, and also for himself and descendants.

EDCS-05701366.translation: Burial place of Minasia, daughter of Caius, of the Marian tribe, wife of Iuventus Fronto, which is a table.
EDCS-05701366.summary: This inscription identifies the burial place of Minasia, daughter of Caius, wife of Iuventus Fronto, and describes the monument as a 'table'.

EDCS-05701367.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Publius Mindius, son of Publius, of the Palatine tribe, Laetus. Genucia Ianuaria, mother, [made this].
EDCS-05701367.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Genucia Ianuaria for her son, Publius Mindius, of the Palatine tribe.

EDCS-05701368.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Mindius Sosibius made this for Lucius Mindius Cornelianus, his ward.
EDCS-05701368.summary: Funerary epitaph for Lucius Mindius Cornelianus, dedicated by his guardian Lucius Mindius Sosibius.

EDCS-05701369.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Laetus, the father, [made this] for Mindia Panthea, his most beloved daughter.
EDCS-05701369.summary: Funerary epitaph for Mindia Panthea, dedicated by her father Laetus.

EDCS-05701371.translation: This sepulchre was granted to Quintus Minucius Glycerus by hereditary right, by which Caius Domitius Saturninus appointed him heir, and to his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701371.summary: Epitaph recording the hereditary grant of a sepulchre to Quintus Minucius Glycerus by Caius Domitius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701373.translation: [...to]oti and to the freedwoman Primigenia, and to Minucius Restitutus, son of my freedwoman, and to Minucius Felix, freedman of Pur[...], and to Minucia Fortunata, freedwoman of Firmu[s?], and to Firmu[s?].
EDCS-05701373.summary: Fragmentary epitaph listing beneficiaries of a burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period, including freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-05701374.translation: [...to] Minucia Corinthis, freedwoman of Quintus, and to [his?] freedman [...]ario, and to his [descendants?], Marcus SNEA to his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701374.summary: Fragmentary epitaph concerning burial rights for freedmen and freedwomen of Marcus SNEA and others, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701375.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Minucia Crotis, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-05701375.summary: Funerary epitaph for Minucia Crotis, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-05701376.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Minucia Vitalis made this for herself and for her dutiful daughter Minucia Thlusa. She lived 20 years, 9 months. In front 7.5 feet, in depth 10 feet.
EDCS-05701376.summary: Funerary epitaph for Minucia Vitalis and her daughter Minucia Thlusa, including dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-05701377.summary: Fragmentary epitaph honouring a woman named Mneme, described as a sister and dutiful wife.

EDCS-05701379.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Modius Asclepiades.
EDCS-05701379.summary: Funerary epitaph for Marcus Modius Asclepiades.

EDCS-05701381.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Modia Arescusa, his dutiful mother. Portumius Rufus, his son.
EDCS-05701381.summary: Funerary epitaph for Modia Arescusa, dedicated by her son Portumius Rufus.

EDCS-05701382.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Modia Atalante.
EDCS-05701382.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Modia Atalante.

EDCS-05701383.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Modia Iusta. Modi Zosime and Atimetus, freedmen patrons, made this for her deserving of good. She lived 14 years, 8 months, and 10 days. She was buried here.
EDCS-05701383.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Modia Iusta, who lived 14 years, 8 months, and 10 days, and was commemorated by her freedmen patrons, Modi Zosime and Atimetus.

EDCS-05701384.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Modia Venerea, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-05701384.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Modia Venerea, the freedwoman of Marcus.

EDCS-05701385.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Modia Urbana, freedwoman of Marcus, made this for herself.
EDCS-05701385.summary: This funerary inscription was made by Modia Urbana, freedwoman of Marcus, for herself, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-05701386.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Modia Zosime. Marcus Modius Atimetus, her husband.
EDCS-05701386.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Modia Zosime by her husband, Marcus Modius Atimetus.

EDCS-05701389.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, recording that someone named Montana made it.

EDCS-05701390.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Munatius.
EDCS-05701390.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Munatius.

EDCS-05701391.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Munatius, freedman. He made [this].
EDCS-05701391.summary: This funerary inscription records that Munatius, a freedman, made this dedication to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-05701392.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Munatia Beronice. Munatius Callistio made [this] for his patroness, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-05701392.summary: This funerary inscription records that Munatius Callistio made a dedication for his patroness Munatia Beronice, who had treated him well.

EDCS-05701393.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Munatia Helpidi. Titus Sergius Eros [dedicated this] to his most holy [wife].
EDCS-05701393.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Sergius Eros dedicating a monument to his wife, Munatia Helpidi.

EDCS-05701394.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Munatia Onesime [erected this] for her freedman Lucius Munatius Primus, who deserved well.
EDCS-05701394.summary: A funerary dedication by Munatia Onesime to her deserving freedman, Lucius Munatius Primus.

EDCS-05701396.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Munatius Trophimus made [this] for his daughter Munatia Urba.
EDCS-05701396.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Munatius Trophimus for his daughter Munatia Urba.

EDCS-05701399.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aepictesina, who lived seventy-five years.
EDCS-05701399.summary: A funerary inscription for Aepictesina, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-05701402.translation: To Gaius Naevius Clodius Venerandus Alexander, son of Publius, of the Palatine tribe. Publius Clodius Verus and Flavius Venerandus [erected this] for their most beloved son.
EDCS-05701402.summary: A funerary dedication for Gaius Naevius Clodius Venerandus Alexander, set up by his fathers.

EDCS-05701407.translation: For Naevia Faustus, freedwoman of the woman. Naevius Sabinus, son of Lucius, of the Voturia tribe. Naevius Celadus, freedman of the woman. Naevia Daphne, freedwoman of the woman. Naevius Amaranthus, freedman of the woman. This monument will not pass to an external heir, by the decision of Lucius Naevius Celadus, freedman of the woman, for his son.
EDCS-05701407.summary: A funerary monument with multiple beneficiaries, likely related to the Naevian family, specifying that it will not pass to external heirs.

EDCS-05701409.translation: Gaius Nasennius Proculus, son of Gaius, of the Voturia tribe, for himself, and for his father Gaius Nasennius Thyrsus, freedman, and for his mother Lucilia Prima, daughter of Decimus, and for his wife Acris, freedwoman of Cnaeus, and for his son Gaius Nasennius Proculus, who lived six years.
EDCS-05701409.summary: A family tomb inscription for Gaius Nasennius Proculus, his parents, wife, and son, also recording the short life of his son.

EDCS-05701411.translation: Nasenia Carpiane, who lived sixteen years and seven months, married on the 16th day before the Kalends (of a month), died on the 6th day before the Kalends of the month mentioned above.
EDCS-05701411.summary: A funerary inscription for Nasenia Carpiane, detailing her age at death and marriage, and the dates of her marriage and death.

EDCS-05701413.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Nasenia Pinyte, who lived twenty years. Farewell.
EDCS-05701413.summary: A funerary dedication to Nasenia Pinyte, recording her age at death.

EDCS-05701417.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Nicephorus. Publius Sabidius Alcon and Iulia Arsinoe, his parents, [erected this] for their most devoted son.
EDCS-05701417.summary: A funerary monument erected by Publius Sabidius Alcon and Iulia Arsinoe for their devoted son, Nicephorus.

EDCS-05701421.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Nonius Hermes and his wife Nonia Auctilla made this for their son Nonius Felix, who lived 13 years, 6 months, and [some] days.
EDCS-05701421.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their deceased son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701423.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Nonius Symphorus made this for his most deserving wife, Calpurnia Aemilia.
EDCS-05701423.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701425.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Nonia Hilaritas, who lived 8 years and 24 days. Publius Nonius Eutyches made this for his most devoted freedwoman, and for his freedmen and freedwomen. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-05701425.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a patron for his deceased freedwoman and other freedpersons, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701426.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Nonia Marcellina, [from] her freedwoman Nonia Syntrophia.
EDCS-05701426.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for her deceased patroness, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701433.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Numisia Urba, who lived 9 years, 1 month, and 20 days. [From] Numisia Severina for her sweetest daughter.
EDCS-05701433.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased daughter, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701434.translation: Obelia Severa made this for her most deserving husband, Tiberius Claudius Carito, who lived 25 years. To the spirits of the departed. Obelia Severa made this for her most deserving husband, Tiberius Claudius Carito, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-05701434.summary: A funerary epitaph for a man named Tiberius Claudius Carito, set up by his wife Obelia Severa, which appears to be a duplication or correction, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701435.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Numerius Obulnius Prothymus made this for himself and for his family, and for their descendants.
EDCS-05701435.summary: A funerary dedication for a family and their descendants by Numerius Obulnius Prothymus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701438.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly identifying Quintus Ogulnius Epagathus as a patron, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701439.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Olia Palladis, [from] her patroness Olia Secundina, for her most devoted freedwoman.
EDCS-05701439.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a patroness for her deceased freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701441.translation: Lucius Oppius, son of Decimus Oppius.
EDCS-05701441.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly recording a man's name and filiation, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05701442.translation: Demetrius, a freedman of Ostiensis, made this for himself and his deserving patroness Emma, because Vettia Danae yielded it, nine feet long and five feet wide.
EDCS-05701442.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a property boundary by a freedman for himself and his patroness, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701443.translation: Lucius Ostiensis Paulinus and Ostiensia Eup[---] [made this for] Lucius Ostiensis Felix, who lived for 1 year, 6 months, and 7 days, their sweetest pupil.
EDCS-05701443.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Lucius Ostiensis Felix, set up by his parents, Lucius Ostiensis Paulinus and Ostiensia Eup---, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701445.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Admia made this for her most dutiful son, Claudius Ostianus, who lived 18 years.
EDCS-05701445.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudius Ostianus, set up by his mother Claudia Admia, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701446.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ostiensis Marullus made this for his deserving brother, Ostiensis Primus.
EDCS-05701446.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ostiensis Primus, set up by his brother Ostiensis Marullus, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701449.translation: While alive: Ostilia Thespia, daughter of Publius [and a woman]. Died: Publius Sulpicius Stabilio, freedman of Publius. Died: Publius Sulpicius Antiochus Varus, freedman of Publius. While alive: Publius Sulpicius Epitynchanus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05701449.summary: This complex inscription records the lives and deaths of several members of the Sulpicius family, including freedmen, with Ostilia Thespia likely being a relative or associated figure, possibly in Ostia.

EDCS-05701453.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Otacilia Alexandria the younger, daughter of Decimus, who lived 6 years, 9 months, and 7 days. Otacilia Alexandria, daughter of Decimus, [made this for] her sweetest sister.
EDCS-05701453.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Otacilia Alexandria, set up by her sister, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701454.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Decimus Otacilius Dioscorus made this for his most dutiful mother, Otacilia Euhodia.
EDCS-05701454.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Otacilia Euhodia, set up by her son Decimus Otacilius Dioscorus, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701455.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Otacilia Euporia, who lived 10 years, 2 months, and 17 days. Decimus Otacilius Polychronius [made this for] his deserving wife.
EDCS-05701455.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Otacilia Euporia, set up by her husband Decimus Otacilius Polychronius, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701456.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Ovinia Optata, daughter of Lucius, who lived 24 years, 4 months, and 19 days.
EDCS-05701456.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ovinia Optata, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701457.translation: Gaius Ovius Agathus, Gaius Ovius Auctus. Gaius Ovius Mus, Ovia Agathe.
EDCS-05701457.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly of a family or a group, with personal names and patronymics, likely in Ostia.

EDCS-05701458.translation: Gnaeus Pacilius Abinnaeus made this for himself and his descendants and for Cloelia Salvia and his freedwoman Cloelia Prepus, [measuring] 30 feet in front and 24 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701458.summary: This is a funerary boundary inscription set up by Gnaeus Pacilius Abinnaeus for himself and his family, including a freedwoman.

EDCS-05701459.translation: To Paconia Faustina, daughter of Sextus, who lived for 13 years and 6 months. Caecilia Isias and Paconius Eudaemon made this for their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-05701459.summary: This is a tombstone set up by Caecilia Isias and Paconius Eudaemon for their deceased daughter, Paconia Faustina, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-05701463.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Papiria Onesime made this for her well-deserving patron, Titus Papirius Mercurialis.
EDCS-05701463.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Papiria Onesime to her deceased patron, Titus Papirius Mercurialis.

EDCS-05701464.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Paphius Honoratus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05701464.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Paphius Honoratus.

EDCS-05701465.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Oppius Ianuarius made this for his well-deserving Parasceve.
EDCS-05701465.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Oppius Ianuarius to Parasceve.

EDCS-05701466.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His fellow slaves made this for Pardalus, well-deserving.
EDCS-05701466.summary: This is a funerary dedication by fellow slaves for their deceased colleague, Pardalus.

EDCS-05701467.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Parthenope, who lived for 1 year, 11 months, and 25 days. Spedia Euplia made this for her well-deserving household slave.
EDCS-05701467.summary: This is a tombstone for the child Parthenope, set up by Spedia Euplia for her deceased household slave, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-05701469.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Publius Aufidius Papianus, who lived for 6 years and 6 days. Publius Aufidius Paulinus made this for his dearest foster child.
EDCS-05701469.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Aufidius Papianus, set up by Publius Aufidius Paulinus for his deceased foster child, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-05701470.translation: M. Pelagius Parthenius for his well-deserving wife, Corneli [---].
EDCS-05701470.summary: This is a funerary dedication by M. Pelagius Parthenius for his deceased wife.

EDCS-05701471.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For their sweetest daughter, Pertennia Crescentina. They made this.
EDCS-05701471.summary: This is a tombstone for Pertennia Crescentina, set up by her parents.

EDCS-05701472.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pescennia lived 45 years, 8 months, and days. Hilarus, Crepereia Parthenope, her relative, Ostiensis Nasennius Salutaris, Veia Iuliane, Veius Iulianus, and Veius Pescennius, her sons, made this for their well-deserving mother. The plot was granted by Flavius Parisacus.
EDCS-05701472.summary: A tombstone commemorating Pescennia, set up by her sons and other relatives, with a note about the plot's acquisition.

EDCS-05701473.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pollea lived 35 years. Petronianus made this for his well-deserving freedwoman.
EDCS-05701473.summary: A tombstone for the freedwoman Pollea, erected by her former master Petronianus.

EDCS-05701476.translation: Petronia Caliste made this for her mother.
EDCS-05701476.summary: A funerary dedication by Petronia Caliste for her mother.

EDCS-05701477.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Petronia Romana, who lived 5 years, 3 months, and 16 days. Petronius Felix made this for his sweetest daughter.
EDCS-05701477.summary: A tombstone for Petronia Romana, a child who died at age 5, set up by her father Petronius Felix.

EDCS-05701478.translation: [dedicated] to Decimus, freedman of Decimus, to Ia, his wife, to Decimus, son of Decimus, to Philadelphus, freedman of Decimus, by Trupera, [erected?] the quae
EDCS-05701478.summary: A fragmented inscription listing several deceased individuals, likely family members and freedmen, connected to a Decimus.

EDCS-05701482.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aelia Eutychis made this for Philotechnus and Felicior.
EDCS-05701482.summary: A funerary dedication by Aelia Eutychis for two individuals named Philotechnus and Felicior.

EDCS-05701486.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pilia Euterpes lived 18 years, 5 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-05701486.summary: A tombstone for Pilia Euterpes, stating her name and lifespan.

EDCS-05701487.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pilia Primitiva made this for herself and for all her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701487.summary: A funerary inscription where Pilia Primitiva dedicates a burial plot for herself and her extended household (freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants).

EDCS-05701488.translation: Pipidia Successa received the plot from Lucius Cominius Fortunatus for the construction of a small shrine. She made this for Pipidius Martialis, her son, for herself and her spouse, and for their descendants. At the front, 2 feet; in the field, 2 feet.
EDCS-05701488.summary: A funerary dedication by Pipidia Successa for her son Pipidius Martialis, herself, her spouse, and descendants, detailing plot dimensions and acquisition.

EDCS-05701489.translation: Caius Plarius Privatus the elder, during his lifetime, ceded the place to his well-deserving freedwoman Plaria Privata for the purpose of burial, with a resting place which is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide, so that she may have the right of entry, access, burial, and sacrifice. On the Tiberius Plarius avenue, on the left side, where the ossuary of Plarius Ianuarius is located.
EDCS-05701489.summary: A legal dedication of a burial plot by Caius Plarius Privatus the elder to his freedwoman Plaria Privata, specifying usage rights and location relative to another tomb.

EDCS-05701491.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Titius Euzelus made this for his sweetest grandson, Quintus Plotius Euzelus, who lived for 3 years, 8 months, 19 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-05701491.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus) recording the death of a child, Quintus Plotius Euzelus, and dedicated by his grandfather, Lucius Titius Euzelus.

EDCS-05701493.summary: A funerary inscription (dis manibus implied) identifying Plotia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-05701495.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Varenia Longina for her sweetest daughter, Plotia Sabina, who lived for 3 years and 2 months.
EDCS-05701495.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus) for a child, Plotia Sabina, dedicated by her mother, Varenia Longina.

EDCS-05701497.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pompeius Helius and Pompeia Callicora for their sweetest daughter, Pompeia Quintus' daughter Aelianna, who lived for 3 years, 6 months, and 14 days.
EDCS-05701497.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus) for a child, Pompeia Aelianna, dedicated by her parents, Pompeius Helius and Pompeia Callicora.

EDCS-05701503.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Pomponia Arsinoe.
EDCS-05701503.summary: A funerary inscription (dis manibus) identifying Pomponia Arsinoe.

EDCS-05701504.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For his dearest son, Pomponia Basilia, who lived for 1 year, 7 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-05701504.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus) for a child, dedicated by Pomponia Basilia.

EDCS-05701507.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Spontius Felix lived for 9 months and 19 days, for his sweetest son.
EDCS-05701507.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus sacrum) recording the death of a child and dedicated by his father, Gaius Spontius Felix.

EDCS-05701508.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pontia Artemisia for her dearest husband, Gaius Pontius Hermetus.
EDCS-05701508.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus) dedicated by Pontia Artemisia to her husband, Gaius Pontius Hermetus.

EDCS-05701509.summary: A funerary inscription recording a relationship (contubernalis, a bond often associated with soldiers or slaves) between the deceased Pontia and the dedicator.

EDCS-05701510.translation: Pontia Felicitas, his wife, made this for him, well-deserving, who lived for 40 years and 2 months.
EDCS-05701510.summary: A funerary monument (dis manibus implied) dedicated by Pontia Felicitas to her husband, who lived to 40 years and 2 months.

EDCS-05701511.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pontia Fortunata lived 55 years, [some] months.
EDCS-05701511.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pontia Fortunata, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-05701512.translation: To the departed spirits of Pontia Hermione, her heirs.
EDCS-05701512.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that heirs are responsible for the memorial of Pontia Hermione.

EDCS-05701513.translation: To the departed spirits of Pontia Hermione, her heirs made [this].
EDCS-05701513.summary: This is a funerary inscription, stating that the heirs of Pontia Hermione commissioned the monument.

EDCS-05701514.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Popilius Antiochianus made [this] for Marcus Popilio Antiochus, his father who deserved well.
EDCS-05701514.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Marcus Popilius Antiochianus honors his deserving father, Marcus Popilio Antiochus.

EDCS-05701515.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Popilius Trofimas made [this] for himself and for Ulpia Serapias, his wife.
EDCS-05701515.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Caius Popilius Trofimas for himself and his wife, Ulpia Serapias.

EDCS-05701517.translation: To the departed spirits. Popilius [made this] for [his wife named] Io Aneme and for Popilia, his wife.
EDCS-05701517.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription, likely dedicating a monument to two women, possibly wives of the dedicant Popilius.

EDCS-05701518.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Attius Vitalis [made this] for Popilia Apollonia, his wife who deserved well.
EDCS-05701518.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Publius Attius Vitalis honoring his deserving wife, Popilia Apollonia.

EDCS-05701520.translation: To the departed spirits. For Poppaea Felicissima, who lived 49 years, 10 months.
EDCS-05701520.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Poppaea Felicissima, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-05701522.translation: To the memory of Posidon, [my] brother.
EDCS-05701522.summary: This is a commemorative inscription honoring the brother of the dedicator, Posidon.

EDCS-05701524.translation: To the departed spirits. Prastinia Quinta made [this] for Gaius Prastinae Nereus, her husband and best patron, with whom she lived 18 years.
EDCS-05701524.summary: This funerary inscription by Prastinia Quinta honors her husband and patron, Gaius Prastinae Nereus, noting their 18 years together.

EDCS-05701525.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Prastina made this for his deserving colleague Nereus.
EDCS-05701525.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Nereus by his colleague Caius Prastina.

EDCS-05701527.translation: To the Divine Shades. Hail, Prima, most holy.
EDCS-05701527.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Prima.

EDCS-05701532.translation: To the Divine Shades. Va Pro Va made this for Zos.
EDCS-05701532.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Va Pro Va for Zos.

EDCS-05701534.translation: Amazo, mother, made this for her daughter Procla.
EDCS-05701534.summary: This funerary inscription records Amazo dedicating a monument to her daughter Procla.

EDCS-05701535.translation: To the Divine Shades. Procope lived 20 years.
EDCS-05701535.summary: This is a funerary inscription noting the lifespan of Procope.

EDCS-05701536.translation: Proto, a freedman, made this; he lived 8 years, 7 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-05701536.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Proto, a freedman.

EDCS-05701538.translation: To the Divine Shades. Victorina made this for her deserving wife Pudentia.
EDCS-05701538.summary: This funerary inscription records Victorina dedicating a monument to her wife Pudentia.

EDCS-05701539.translation: Marcus Pulfatius and Marcus Pulfatius made this for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-05701539.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Pulfatius and Marcus Pulfatius dedicating a monument to their freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-05701540.translation: Lucia Pupia, freedwoman of Lucius Pupius, made this for her patron and for herself, and for Lucia Pupia Glyceris, her freedwoman, and for Lucius Pupius Vestalis, her freedman, and for his son Lucius Pupius Fortunatus, her freedman, and for Fictoria, her slave.
EDCS-05701540.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucia Pupia making provisions for her patron, herself, and several freedmen, freedwomen, and a slave.

EDCS-05701543.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Quieta, most dutiful parents.
EDCS-05701543.summary: This funerary inscription records parents dedicating a monument to their daughter Quieta.

EDCS-05701544.translation: To Gaius Quinctius, [son of] Gaius Quinctius.
EDCS-05701544.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Quinctius to his father, Gaius Quinctius.

EDCS-05701547.translation: To Quintilia Callirhoe, who lived 50 years; Quintus Quintilius Andronicus, her husband, and Quintilia Eufemia, her daughter, made this.
EDCS-05701547.summary: This funerary inscription honors Quintilia Callirhoe, erected by her husband and daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701548.translation: To their wife Quintilia Callirhoene and their daughter Quintilia Eufemia, and to their freedmen and freedwomen, they made this while alive.
EDCS-05701548.summary: This is a funerary monument built by a couple for themselves, their daughter, and their freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-05701549.translation: To Quinto Quintilio Euphemo, who lived 1 year, 6 months, and 4 days, and to Quintilia Dionysias, who lived 3 years, 4 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05701549.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and ages of two young children, Quinto Quintilio Euphemo and Quintilia Dionysias.

EDCS-05701550.translation: Lucius Quintilius Felix for his son Lucius Quintilius Felix, son of Lucius; for his son Lucius Quintilius Aprilis, son of Lucius; for his freedwoman Quintilia Metha; for Lucius Quintilius Iucundus; 12 ossuaries with columbaria.
EDCS-05701550.summary: This is a funerary inscription for several family members and freedmen, possibly marking a columbarium or ossuary complex, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701552.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed: Quinto Quintilio Hermetis made this for his patron Quinto Quintilio Mercurio, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-05701552.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to a patron by his freedman, and also includes provisions for the freedman's own dependents.

EDCS-05701553.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Quinto Quintilio Iustinus, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-05701553.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quinto Quintilio Iustinus, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-05701554.translation: [Lacuna] Rabir[ius?], [Lacuna] Rabir[ius?], Marcus Aelius [---], Aelia [---], Aelia [---], Marcus Aelius? [---], Marcus [---], [Lacuna] Lucius Ca[---], Ca[---]
EDCS-05701554.summary: This inscription is heavily damaged and illegible, but appears to be a funerary dedication potentially naming members of the Rabirii and Aelii families.

EDCS-05701556.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a dedication to Publius Ragonius Marcus, possibly funerary.

EDCS-05701557.translation: Publius Ragonius Lucifer made this for his deserving Publius Ragonius Euposus.
EDCS-05701557.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Publius Ragonius Lucifer honors Publius Ragonius Euposus, likely a family member or freedman.

EDCS-05701558.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Ragonius Secundus lived for 8 years. His father, Publius Ragonius Dius, made this.
EDCS-05701558.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his son, Publius Ragonius Secundus, who died at the age of 8.

EDCS-05701559.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Ragonia Eutychia, dearest mother and nurse. Firmus made this.
EDCS-05701559.summary: A funerary dedication by Firmus to his mother and nurse, Ragonia Eutychia.

EDCS-05701560.translation: To Ragonia Irene, his well-deserving wife. Aelius Iulianus made this.
EDCS-05701560.summary: A funerary dedication by Aelius Iulianus to his wife, Ragonia Irene.

EDCS-05701563.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To his well-deserving son, Sextus Rasio Caro. His mother, Rasia Isias, made this. He lived 25 years and 39 days.
EDCS-05701563.summary: A funerary dedication by Rasia Isias for her son, Sextus Rasio Caro, who died at the age of 25 years and 39 days.

EDCS-05701564.translation: Caius Iulius Capito, his freedman and heir, and Iulia Ianuaria, co-heir, made this for Restituta.
EDCS-05701564.summary: A funerary dedication for Restituta made by her freedman and heir, Caius Iulius Capito, and her co-heir, Iulia Ianuaria.

EDCS-05701565.summary: A very fragmentary funerary dedication for Restitutus, possibly indicating a grant of land by Materfaius.

EDCS-05701566.translation: Gaius Rocius Donatus, his father, [made this] for his son, Gaius Rocius Chrysaon.
EDCS-05701566.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Rocius Donatus for his son, Gaius Rocius Chrysaon.

EDCS-05701567.translation: On land granted by Publius Rocius Homerus, 60 feet in front and 60 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701567.summary: A record of land dimensions granted by Publius Rocius Homerus, likely for a tomb or construction.

EDCS-05701569.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Romania Stratonicena, who lived for 11 years and 3 months and 6 days. Romanius Crescentilianus [made this] for his ward.
EDCS-05701569.summary: A funerary dedication by Romanius Crescentilianus for his ward, Romania Stratonicena, who died at the age of 11 years, 3 months, and 6 days.

EDCS-05701574.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Rubria Daphne, his incomparable wife. Rubrius Telesichorus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-05701574.summary: A funerary dedication made by Rubrius Telesichorus for his wife, Rubria Daphne, and also for himself, indicating it was prepared during his lifetime.

EDCS-05701575.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus Rubrius Euphrosinus made this for his most beloved and deserving wife, Rubria Malia.
EDCS-05701575.summary: This funerary epitaph records Sextus Rubrius Euphrosinus dedicating a monument to his wife, Rubria Malia.

EDCS-05701576.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Rufina, his sweetest daughter, who lived 4 years, 8 months, and M days. Her parents [dedicate this].
EDCS-05701576.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by parents to their young daughter, Rufina, who died at the age of 4 years and 8 months.

EDCS-05701577.translation: Ma Rufria Magna lived 21 years and is buried here. Lucius Oclatius Daphnus made this for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-05701577.summary: This epitaph records the life and burial of Rufria Magna, who died at 21, and was dedicated by her husband, Lucius Oclatius Daphnus.

EDCS-05701578.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Felix, who lived 24 days, made this for Ceius Rufus.
EDCS-05701578.summary: This epitaph, likely erected by a parent, records the short life of Felix, who died at 24 days, and is dedicated to Ceius Rufus.

EDCS-05701580.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Salluvia Arignote made this for herself and for her deserving husband, Lucius Tettius Sotericus, and for her daughters Salluvia Eutychida and Refra Tertulla, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 11 feet in front, 13 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701580.summary: This funerary monument, measuring 11 by 13 feet, was erected by Salluvia Arignote for herself, her husband Lucius Tettius Sotericus, their daughters, and their descendants and freedmen.

EDCS-05701582.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sabidia Heliadis, daughter of Publius, who lived 16 years, 10 months, and 15 days. Publius Sabidius Ingenuus and Pacia Lanthanusa [made this] for their daughter. 8 feet in front, 4 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701582.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Sabidia Heliadis at 16 years, 10 months, and 15 days, and was dedicated by her parents, Publius Sabidius Ingenuus and Pacia Lanthanusa.

EDCS-05701583.translation: ilia Sabina made this for Titus Aurelius Eutychianus, TO TIS, and for his freedmen and descendants.
EDCS-05701583.summary: This funerary monument was erected by 'ilia Sabina' for Titus Aurelius Eutychianus, his freedmen, and descendants.

EDCS-05701585.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Porcia Buniada, his deserving mother, and for Porcius Perseus, his father. His natural son made this while they were alive.
EDCS-05701585.summary: This epitaph was dedicated by a son to his living parents, Porcia Buniada and Porcius Perseus.

EDCS-05701587.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Salinator Martialus, his deserving patron. Marcus Salinator Asclepiodotus and Marcus Salinator Eutyches [dedicate this].
EDCS-05701587.summary: This epitaph records Marcus Salinator Asclepiodotus and Marcus Salinator Eutyches dedicating a monument to their deserving patron, Marcus Salinator Martialus.

EDCS-05701589.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Vibius Helpidius, his deserving wife. Marcus Salinator Scymnus made this.
EDCS-05701589.summary: This epitaph records Marcus Salinator Scymnus dedicating a monument to his deserving wife, Vibius Helpidius.

EDCS-05701590.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Salinator Abascantus made this for his deserving patroness Salvinia Heuresis.
EDCS-05701590.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by a freedman, Marcus Salinator Abascantus, to his patroness Salvinia Heuresis.

EDCS-05701593.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Servilius Florus made this for his deserving wife Salvinia Theusa.
EDCS-05701593.summary: A funerary inscription by Marcus Servilius Florus dedicated to his wife Salvinia Theusa.

EDCS-05701594.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Salonius Restutus made this for his deserving patroness Salonia Agathemeris and for his grandson Lucius Cornelius Verus.
EDCS-05701594.summary: A funerary inscription by Caius Salonius Restutus dedicated to his patroness Salonia Agathemeris and his grandson Lucius Cornelius Verus.

EDCS-05701596.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sattia Athenais made this for her deserving son Sattius Felix.
EDCS-05701596.summary: A funerary inscription by Sattia Athenais for her son Sattius Felix.

EDCS-05701597.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. His mother made this for Severinus, her deserving son, who lived 4 years and 5 months.
EDCS-05701597.summary: A funerary inscription by a mother for her son Saturninus, who died in childhood.

EDCS-05701598.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. His father made this for his deserving daughter, who lived 3 years and 4 months.
EDCS-05701598.summary: A funerary inscription by a father for his daughter, who died in childhood.

EDCS-05701599.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Scanthia Epictesis, his patroness, made this for Publius Scantius Eutyches, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-05701599.summary: A funerary inscription by a patroness, Scanthia Epictesis, for her freedman Publius Scantius Eutyches.

EDCS-05701602.translation: Scantia Epicharis [made this] for herself, and for Publius Scantius Carpus, her father, and for their descendants, 3 jars.
EDCS-05701602.summary: An inscription recording the provision of 3 jars for a family burial plot, dedicated by Scantia Epicharis.

EDCS-05701603.translation: Quintus Scribonius Hermadio, a freedman, and Scantius Secundus and Voltidia Agathemeris made this for Scribonia Pharia, their foster-mother.
EDCS-05701603.summary: A funerary inscription made by freedmen and others for their foster-mother, Scribonia Pharia.

EDCS-05701604.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Scribonia Victoria made this for her deserving husband Vettius Fortunatus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen. In the front, 20 feet; in the ground, 20 feet.
EDCS-05701604.summary: A funerary inscription by Scribonia Victoria for her husband Vettius Fortunatus and their freed dependents, specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-05701605.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Secundus.
EDCS-05701605.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Secundus, likely a deceased individual.

EDCS-05701606.translation: To Secunda, freedwoman of Decimus, his wife, and to A. and Vatinia, and to Secundus, freedman of Quintus, and to Primigenia, freedwoman.
EDCS-05701606.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Secunda, his wife, and other freedpersons, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-05701609.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Selicia Donata. Lucius Selicius Restitutus, Lucius Selicius Artemas, Selicia Sabina, and Selicia Tusca made this for their patroness.
EDCS-05701609.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Selicius Restitutus and others for their patroness, Selicia Donata.

EDCS-05701610.translation: To Sempronia Victoria, his wife, and to their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 20 feet, in the field 43 feet.
EDCS-05701610.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot measuring 20 by 43 feet, dedicated to Sempronia Victoria and her freed dependents.

EDCS-05701611.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Senatia Moderata. She lived 4 years and 40 days.
EDCS-05701611.summary: This is a tombstone for Senatia Moderata, recording her very young age at death.

EDCS-05701613.translation: For our daughter. Lucius Seppius Pudentianus the younger, son of Lucius, and Flavia Data, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-05701613.summary: This inscription commemorates a daughter, dedicated by her parents Lucius Seppius Pudentianus iunior and Flavia Data.

EDCS-05701616.translation: Publius Septimius Latinus, freedman of Publius, made this for Sulpicia Helpis, his dearest wife, and for Septimia Restituta, my freedwoman and dear vernal (a female slave born in the house), and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701616.summary: This tomb inscription was made by Publius Septimius Latinus for his wife, a freedwoman, a vernal, and their descendants.

EDCS-05701619.summary: This is a sacred dedication, likely funerary, to Septimia Sulpiciana.

EDCS-05701620.translation: To Publius Serenius Sotericus. Gavia Cassia, to her dearest husband.
EDCS-05701620.summary: This tomb inscription is a dedication from Gavia Cassia to her husband, Publius Serenius Sotericus.

EDCS-05701621.translation: Gnaeus Sercius Abascantus made this for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701621.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Gnaeus Sercius Abascantus for himself and his freed dependents.

EDCS-05701625.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sertorius Pacatus, who lived 4 years, 10 months, 20 days, 7 hours.
EDCS-05701625.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sertorius Pacatus.

EDCS-05701628.translation: Publius Servilius Eutychus, freedman of Publius, and Octavia Fausta, freedwoman of Manlia and Titus, and Nereis, freedwoman of Manlia and Titus; Marcus Valerius Hermolaus, freedman of Marcus; Marcus Valerius Aphrodisius, freedman of Hermolaus; Publius Aemilius Luniesis, son of Publius; and Spurillia Murtis.
EDCS-05701628.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a funerary monument or property ownership, with individuals identified by their name, patron, and familial relationships.

EDCS-05701629.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Servilius Orthrus made this for his son Caius Servilius Orthrus, who lived 2 years, 9 months.
EDCS-05701629.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where a father, Caius Servilius Orthrus, commemorates his deceased son, Caius Servilius Orthrus.

EDCS-05701631.translation: Servilia Phlegusa made this for her deserving father, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-05701631.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Servilia Phlegusa to her father.

EDCS-05701632.translation: For Servilia Venusta, dearest wife, and...
EDCS-05701632.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning a dedication to Servilia Venusta, identified as a wife.

EDCS-05701633.translation: Publius Sestius Donatus, freedman of Publius, and Sestia Chrysis made this for their most excellent patron, Publius Sestius Blasto, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05701633.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by freedmen (Donatus and Chrysis) to their patron (Publius Sestius Blasto).

EDCS-05701640.translation: Sextius Hyginus restored this monument, which belonged to Vibius Valerianus, and to which rights pertained through the steps of possessions from Aulus Egilius Agathopus. It had fallen into ruin due to age. He restored it for himself, for his wife Helpidius, for his son Gaius Sextius, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701640.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a dilapidated monument by Sextius Hyginus for himself, his family, and his freedmen, indicating a concern for property rights and ancestral legacy.

EDCS-05701641.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaianus and Nepotilla made this for their most beloved mother, Sextia Gaianeti.
EDCS-05701641.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Gaianus and Nepotilla to their mother, Sextia Gaianeti.

EDCS-05701642.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sextia, wife of Titus Polyclitus, deserving.
EDCS-05701642.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Titus Polyclitus to his wife, Sextia.

EDCS-05701643.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sextia Luperca, daughter of Titus, who lived 10 years, 10 days. Titus Sextius Adrastus, father, made this for his son Titus Sextius Magnus, who lived 8 years.
EDCS-05701643.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where a father, Titus Sextius Adrastus, commemorates both his daughter Sextia Luperca and his son Titus Sextius Magnus, providing their ages at death.

EDCS-05701644.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Bellius Eutyches Sallustius had this made for his deserving wife Sextia Panthia.
EDCS-05701644.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextia Panthia, commissioned by her husband.

EDCS-05701648.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sirice, an infant.
EDCS-05701648.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an infant named Sirice.

EDCS-05701650.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sittius Colobius, and for Ianuaria, deserving.
EDCS-05701650.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sittius Colobius and Ianuaria, possibly a couple.

EDCS-05701651.translation: For himself and his wife Soteris, and for freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-05701651.summary: This is a funerary inscription intended for the dedicator, his wife, and descendants.

EDCS-05701653.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Titus Stabrius Alexander, who lived 21 years, 6 months, and 15 days. Antonia Pelagia, mother, [had this made] for herself and for Titus Stabrius Alexander, her husband.
EDCS-05701653.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Stabrius Alexander, commissioned by his mother and for herself and her husband.

EDCS-05701654.translation: Gnaeus Statilius made this for himself while alive, for his most beloved wife Claudia Caletyche.
EDCS-05701654.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Gnaeus Statilius for himself and his wife during his lifetime.

EDCS-05701655.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. From Rentius Statilius Epictetus and Aegrilia Faustina.
EDCS-05701655.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Rentius Statilius Epictetus and Aegrilia Faustina, likely a couple.

EDCS-05701657.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Statilia Crescentiana, daughter of Gnaeus, who lived 24 years and 10 months.
EDCS-05701657.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Statilia Crescentiana, daughter of Gnaeus.

EDCS-05701658.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Statilia Marcellina Cyriae, most beloved daughter, deserving, who lived 11 years and 5 months. Her parents Ragonia and Delicatus, and her brother Firmus, made this.
EDCS-05701658.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Statilia Marcellina Cyriae, commissioned by her parents and brother.

EDCS-05701659.translation: For Statilia Paulina, Lucius Ligurius Fabianus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-05701659.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Statilia Paulina, commissioned by her husband.

EDCS-05701660.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Steius Priscus and Lollia Isias, parents, made this for their sweetest son, Marcus Steius Rogatus, who lived 11 years, 9 months, and 25 days.
EDCS-05701660.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their son, Marcus Steius Rogatus, who died young.

EDCS-05701662.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Philotechnus and Eutychus, parents, made this for their sweetest daughter, Stratonice, a freedwoman of Augustus, who lived 1 year, 1 month, and 4 days.
EDCS-05701662.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their daughter, Stratonice, a freedwoman of an emperor, who died in infancy.

EDCS-05701665.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. [---] Successus, a freedman of Modi Secundus, lived 13 years and 15 days.
EDCS-05701665.summary: A funerary epitaph for Successus, a freedman, who died in his early teens.

EDCS-05701666.translation: [---]nicae, L. Iulius Successus made this for himself, for Nonia Onesima, his sweetest daughter, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Ten feet wide, ten feet long.
EDCS-05701666.summary: A funerary epitaph for a family, including Nonia Onesima and her father Iulius Successus, also providing dimensions for the burial plot.

EDCS-05701669.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Aurelius Aelianus made this for his well-deserving wife, Quintus Sulpicia, who lived 31 years, 8 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-05701669.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, Quintus Sulpicia, detailing her lifespan.

EDCS-05701671.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Sancta made this for Synegdemus, who lived 7 months and 25 days.
EDCS-05701671.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Sancta for Synegdemus, who died in infancy.

EDCS-05701672.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Fannia Beronice, the mother, made this for her sweetest son, Lucius Tadius Sozomenus, who lived 6 years, 7 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05701672.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her son, Lucius Tadius Sozomenus, who died in childhood.

EDCS-05701675.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sextus Tarusius Martialis, made by his well-deserving wife Hostilia Secundilla, daughter of Aulus, and his daughter Tarusia Priscilla, daughter of Sextus, and Sextus Tarusius, son of Sextus and Primigenius, and Ampliatus, son of Aulus Hostilius and mulieris.
EDCS-05701675.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Tarusius Martialis, set up by his wife, daughter, and possibly other family members, including a slave.

EDCS-05701676.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying Tata Eros as a freedman and fellow freedman, possibly set up by a peer.

EDCS-05701677.translation: Tecusa made this for her well-deserving husband, Felix.
EDCS-05701677.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife, Tecusa, for her husband, Felix.

EDCS-05701678.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Pinna, slave of Terentius Alphius, Terentius Callon, with the agreement of his freedmen, made this in testimony of his love for her, as she deserved well.
EDCS-05701678.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Terentius Callon to Pinna, his slave, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701680.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Terentius Fabianus lived for 20 years and 3 months.
EDCS-05701680.summary: This epitaph records the life span of Marcus Terentius Fabianus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701681.translation: This small estate belongs to Titus Terentius Secundus and his daughter Terentia Amplitata.
EDCS-05701681.summary: This inscription concerns property ownership by Titus Terentius Secundus and his daughter Terentia Amplitata, possibly dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05701683.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Terentius Epitynchanus made this for his deserving wife, Terentia Fortunata, and for himself.
EDCS-05701683.summary: This funerary dedication from Marcus Terentius Epitynchanus is for his wife Terentia Fortunata and himself, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701685.translation: Tertius I (lived) well for X years.
EDCS-05701685.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the lifespan of someone named Tertius, with the duration of life being incomplete, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701688.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius G. The made this. M. Flore.
EDCS-05701688.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication with missing information, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701691.translation: To Titus Tinucio Stefano, who lived for 6 years, 9 months, and 1 day, dearest son.
EDCS-05701691.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Tinucio Stefano, a young child, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701693.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Sacrum. ThrHepto lived for 2 years, 3 months, and 13 days. Iucunda, their mother, lived for 22 years and 6 months. Iucunda lived for 1 year, 11 months, and 27 days. Publius Crispius Vitalis made this.
EDCS-05701693.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription recording the lives and deaths of children named ThrHepto and Iucunda, and their mother Iucunda, with the monument erected by Publius Crispius Vitalis, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701695.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Tinucia Maxima, dearest daughter, who lived for 8 years and 2 months. Tinucia Calligenia, mother, made this.
EDCS-05701695.summary: This funerary epitaph is from Tinucia Calligenia for her daughter Tinucia Maxima, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701697.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Titia Palatina. Titius Martialis and Titia Italia, heir.
EDCS-05701697.summary: This funerary dedication is for Titia Palatina by Titius Martialis and Titia Italia, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-05701698.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Trebellius Anthimus lived 30 years. Trebellia Ursilla made this for her well-deserving father.
EDCS-05701698.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a daughter to her deceased father, Caius Trebellius Anthimus.

EDCS-05701699.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Trebius Maximus, a veteran, made this for himself, his wife Tenneia Nicasse, and his descendants Ennius Domitius Montanus and Geminia Certa.
EDCS-05701699.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a veteran, Lucius Trebius Maximus, for himself, his wife, and his descendants.

EDCS-05701700.translation: Caius Trebius Terpnus [made this] for his most beloved wife Otacilia Prima, and for Caius Trebius Trebianus, and Caius Trebius Oceanus, Firmina, and Saturnina, their slaves, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701700.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Trebius Terpnus for his wife, children (presumably), slaves, and descendants.

EDCS-05701701.translation: Olympias, freedwoman of a woman, made this for herself and her slaves, Lucius Trebius Sporus, freedman of a woman, and Lucius Trebius Paezontus, freedman of a woman. The plot, 3 feet long and 3 feet wide, was granted publicly by Gnaeus Pacilius Daphnicus.
EDCS-05701701.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Olympias, a freedwoman, for herself and her freedmen, with a public grant of burial space.

EDCS-05701702.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. [Maria?] Trophima lived 25 years and 6 months. Trophimas [made this] for his most sweet son, well-deserving.
EDCS-05701702.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a son named Trophimas, made by his parent (likely mother, given the context of 'Trophimae').

EDCS-05701703.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. [For?] Trophimes [daughter of ?].
EDCS-05701703.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication, likely for a person named Trophimes.

EDCS-05701705.translation: Caius Tuccius Tertius, freedman of Caius, [made this] for Caius Tuccius Amianthus, freedman of Caius, and Tuccia Epigone, freedwoman of Caius, and their household slaves.
EDCS-05701705.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Tuccius Tertius, a freedman, for his patrons and their household slaves.

EDCS-05701706.summary: This is a simple tombstone or dedication bearing the name Tuccius Zosimus.

EDCS-05701707.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Tullius Repostus made this for his most sweet son, Quintus Tullius Repostus, who lived 7 years and 2 months.
EDCS-05701707.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a father for his young son, Quintus Tullius Repostus.

EDCS-05701708.translation: Eutyches, freedman [of Marcus?], [made this] for Marcus Tullius Stephano.
EDCS-05701708.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman named Eutyches for Marcus Tullius Stephano, likely his former master.

EDCS-05701710.translation: Turellia Pietas, and Cornelius Pius, and Cornelius Epictetus.
EDCS-05701710.summary: This inscription lists the names of three individuals, Turellia Pietas, Cornelius Pius, and Cornelius Epictetus, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-05701712.translation: To the Divine Manes. Turranius Eutyches, the father, made this for his son Quintus Turranius Carpus, who lived 19 years, 9 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-05701712.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Turranius Carpus, set up by his father Turranius Eutyches, providing his age at death.

EDCS-05701713.translation: To the Divine Manes. Tutilia Teni, who lived 3 months. Caius V [made this].
EDCS-05701713.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tutilia Teni, who died in infancy, set up by Caius V.

EDCS-05701716.translation: You who were found temperate and sweet among all, be without care; for this is the way for all mortals. Hail, Valenti Pulveri, fare well.
EDCS-05701716.summary: This inscription is a funerary epigram in Greek, wishing peace to the deceased Valenti Pulveri.

EDCS-05701717.translation: To the Divine Manes. Romanus, the father, consecrated this for Publius Valerius Apelletus.
EDCS-05701717.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Romanus, the father, to Publius Valerius Apelletus.

EDCS-05701718.translation: Marcus Valerius Castus for his patron Marcus Valerius Actius, and for Valeriae Feliculae, Valeriae Nice, and their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701718.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Valerius Castus to his patron Marcus Valerius Actius, and also to Valeria Felicula, Valeria Nice, and their freedmen and descendants.

EDCS-05701720.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Valerius Eutyches, freedman of Marcus, made this for himself and for Calityche, his fellow freedwoman, and for their grandchildren and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, and for the plot of land in front of him granted to himself by Iulia Tyche, his guardian, with the authorization of Titus Flavius Autarches, 13.5 feet in front and 15.5 feet in depth.
EDCS-05701720.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription by Marcus Valerius Eutyches, a freedman, establishing rights to a burial plot for himself, his family, and others, with details of land dimensions and the guardian's consent.

EDCS-05701721.translation: This plot is the property of Valerius Fortunatus, to whom Octavia Zosime granted it.
EDCS-05701721.summary: This inscription records the ownership and transfer of a plot of land from Octavia Zosime to Valerius Fortunatus.

EDCS-05701724.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caius Valerius Caius, who lived 5 years, 3 months, and 10 days. Caius Valerius, his father, made this for his dearest verna (home-born slave).
EDCS-05701724.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Valerius Marc, a child who lived 5 years, 3 months, and 10 days, made by his father Caius Valerius.

EDCS-05701729.translation: Valeria Basilla, daughter of Lucius, for Caius Iulius Agathemerus, her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-05701729.summary: This inscription records the dedication by Valeria Basilla to her husband Caius Iulius Agathemerus.

EDCS-05701731.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valerius Alexander made this for his well-deserving wife, Valeria Dionysiades, who lived 24 years, 6 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05701731.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Valerius Alexander for his wife, Valeria Dionysiades, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-05701732.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Elpidia made this for her patron, Marcus Valerius Impetratus, and for her son, who lived 3 years and 7 months.
EDCS-05701732.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Valeria Elpidia for her patron and her son, noting the son's age at death.

EDCS-05701733.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Made by her fellow freedmen for Valeria Euthenia, the well-deserving.
EDCS-05701733.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by freedmen for their fellow freedwoman, Valeria Euthenia.

EDCS-05701734.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Terentius Onesimus made this for his well-deserving freedwoman Valeria Eutychis, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701734.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Terentius Onesimus for his freedwoman Valeria Eutychis, also including provisions for other freedpersons and their descendants.

EDCS-05701739.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Valeria Fortunata, freedwoman of Titus. Flavia Eutychia and Fortunatus.
EDCS-05701739.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Fortunata, freedwoman of Titus, set up by Flavia Eutychia and Fortunatus.

EDCS-05701741.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Valeria Marcellina.
EDCS-05701741.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Marcellina.

EDCS-05701742.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Equitius Crescens, the husband, made this for his well-deserving wife, Valeria Materna Potentina.
EDCS-05701742.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caius Equitius Crescens for his wife, Valeria Materna Potentina.

EDCS-05701743.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Valeria Filocale.
EDCS-05701743.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Filocale.

EDCS-05701744.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Valeria Primigenia, who lived 8 years, 11 months, and 13 days, her well-deserving mother Valeria Eutychia made this for herself and her own.
EDCS-05701744.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Valeria Eutychia for her daughter Valeria Primigenia, specifying the daughter's age at death, and also for herself and her family.

EDCS-05701745.translation: Valeria Scandilia made this for herself and for Lucius Furius Triumphalis, her husband, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05701745.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Valeria Scandilia for herself, her husband Lucius Furius Triumphalis, and their freedpersons and descendants.

EDCS-05701746.translation: To Thetis Chryseros, a home-born slave of our Caesar, wife of Marcus Valerius Italicus and daughter of Marcus Valerius Italicus, erected this for her husband, who deserved well of her. She lived for 16 years, 4 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-05701746.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Thetis Chryseros, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701747.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Thryphosa, freedwoman of Marcus, and Masclinus, son of Marcus Valerius Palatinus, son of Marcus. 11 feet in front, in the field [unspecified measurement].
EDCS-05701747.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Thryphosa and Masclinus, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701748.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Vitalis erected this for her dear mother, Valeria Tyce, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-05701748.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Tyce, erected by her daughter Valeria Vitalis, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701749.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Valius Phorus and C. Us Dionysius erected this for their devoted wife, Valia Spendusa, daughter of Phorus, and for Attalus, her husband, who deserved well of them.
EDCS-05701749.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valia Spendusa and Attalus, erected by Lucius Valius Phorus and C. Us Dionysius, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701750.translation: To the Divine Shades. Antius Successus erected this for his deserving wife Blastenis, daughter of Varenes, and for himself, and also for his sweetest daughter Antia Successa, who lived longer than her mother by 1 year, 1 month, and 40 days; who at the day of her death was 8 years, 8 months, and 15 days old, and was snatched away as an infant by Pluto's grasp, a beautiful and lovely child not yet filling the home with life's sweet light; her father mourns and asks for the faith of this inscription, that every age may desire for her a light earth. This monument, which is on the right side as one enters, includes 12 columbaria, for freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-05701750.summary: A large funerary monument for the family of Antius Successus, including his wife Blastenis and daughter Antia Successa, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701756.translation: Vedia Voluptas erected this for herself, and for Vedia Veneris, and for Publius Ostiensis Epaphroditus, parents, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701756.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vedia Voluptas and her family, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701757.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Vegoe, sweetest infant. Vitalis, her mother.
EDCS-05701757.summary: A funerary epitaph for an infant named Vegoe, erected by her mother Vitalis, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701759.translation: LTAEMO. Venator. 25 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701759.summary: A funerary boundary marker for Venator, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701761.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Quintus Vennonius Paulinus, who lived 17 years, 5 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-05701761.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Vennonius Paulinus, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701764.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Venustus, son of Marcus Iunius Faustus, who lived 30 years. His wife Iucunda erected this for him, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-05701764.summary: A funerary epitaph for Venustus, erected by his wife Iucunda, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05701765.translation: To the departed spirits. Silia Eutychia made this for her dearest husband, Lucius Veratius Thallus.
EDCS-05701765.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Silia Eutychia to her husband Lucius Veratius Thallus.

EDCS-05701766.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Vergilius Fortunatus, who lived 24 years, 3 months, and 4 days. Quintus Vergilius Leonas, his son.
EDCS-05701766.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Vergilius Fortunatus, erected by his son Quintus Vergilius Leonas.

EDCS-05701767.translation: For Quintus Vergilius Pansa, son of Publius, and Quintus Vergilius Philotimus, freedman of Quintus, his patron; and for Amphion and Apollonius, freedmen of Quintus Vergilius, son of Quintus, after their death, they made (this tomb) for themselves and for Suellia, wife of Mulier, and for Anna, freedwoman of Publius Luscius, wife, and for Hilarius, freedman of Quintus Vergilius, son of Quintus, and for Quintus Vergilius, son of Quintus, and for Veturia R. and for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-05701767.summary: A complex funerary inscription detailing the burial arrangements for multiple individuals within the Vergilius family and their freedmen.

EDCS-05701768.translation: Quintus Vesprius Pardus made this for his deserving wife, Tettia, who was asked (to be obeyed).
EDCS-05701768.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by Quintus Vesprius Pardus for his wife Tettia.

EDCS-05701769.translation: ... for his patron and for Vestilia Hieronica, most dutiful... for themselves and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants... this monument will not pass to an external heir.
EDCS-05701769.summary: A funerary inscription that establishes a perpetual burial plot for a patron, his family, freedmen, and descendants.

EDCS-05701775.translation: To the departed spirits. Antonia Ursula made this for her husband, Lucius Vettius Liberalis.
EDCS-05701775.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Antonia Ursula to her husband Lucius Vettius Liberalis.

EDCS-05701776.translation: For Aria Donata, from Gaius Vettius Successus to Aulus Terentius Ingenuus: 47 feet in front, 33 feet in the field; and on the other side, 16 feet in front, 30 feet in the field, which belonged to Noni Abascanti.
EDCS-05701776.summary: A boundary inscription detailing land dimensions and ownership transfers related to Aria Donata and Gaius Vettius Successus.

EDCS-05701777.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Vettius Verulus. Quintus Vettius.
EDCS-05701777.summary: A short funerary epitaph for Quintus Vettius Verulus, erected by Quintus Vettius.

EDCS-05701779.translation: To the departed spirits of Vettia Erotis. For Tryphosa, her dearest foster-daughter. For Flavius Aequalis, her most loving daughter.
EDCS-05701779.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring both Vettia Erotis and her foster-daughter Tryphosa, with an inscription from Flavius Aequalis.

EDCS-05701780.translation: To the departed spirits. For Vettia Primitiva, his dearest wife, a freedwoman. Titus Flavius Aequalis made this.
EDCS-05701780.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by Titus Flavius Aequalis for his wife, Vettia Primitiva.

EDCS-05701782.translation: To Annia Satta, Sextus Vettulenus Castrensis made [this] for his deserving wife.
EDCS-05701782.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Sextus Vettulenus Castrensis for his deserving wife, Annia Satta.

EDCS-05701783.translation: To the Divine Manes of Gaius Veturius Pantagathus.
EDCS-05701783.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes of Gaius Veturius Pantagathus.

EDCS-05701784.translation: For Veturia, who lived 20 years. Veturius Polus for his most sweet, deserving daughter.
EDCS-05701784.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Veturius Polus for his deserving daughter, Veturia, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-05701785.translation: To Veturia Faustina, his deserving wife.
EDCS-05701785.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Veturia Faustina, a deserving wife.

EDCS-05701787.summary: This inscription records lengths of time, possibly related to the lifespan or service of Quintus Vibius.

EDCS-05701789.translation: For Quintus Vibius Pantagathus and for Junia Rufina, daughter of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-05701789.summary: This inscription commemorates Quintus Vibius Pantagathus and his wife, Junia Rufina.

EDCS-05701790.translation: To Eutychia and Marcus Vibius Victor, most sweet, who lived 4 years and 2 days. Marcus Vibius Onesimus, to his freedmen and to Sextus Julius Stephanus and Julius Asclepiades, his patron.
EDCS-05701790.summary: This inscription records the names of several individuals, including freedmen and a patron, possibly related to a family tomb.

EDCS-05701791.translation: To the Divine Manes of Vibia. Quintus Vibius [dedicated this].
EDCS-05701791.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Manes of Vibia by Quintus Vibius.

EDCS-05701792.translation: To the Divine Manes. Vibius Amphion. Quintus Vibius made [this] for his deserving wife, Vibia Helene.
EDCS-05701792.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Vibius for his deserving wife, Vibia Helene, and dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-05701793.translation: To the Divine Manes of Vibia Hermione. Valerianus S made [this] for his wife.
EDCS-05701793.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Valerianus S to the Divine Manes of his wife, Vibia Hermione.

EDCS-05701795.translation: Vibia Telete, daughter of Lucius, lived for 2 years, 3 months, 22 days, and 6 hours.
EDCS-05701795.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a young girl, Vibia Telete.

EDCS-05701796.translation: Lucius Vibusius Agapetus, who lived for 3 years, 3 months, and 4 days. Lucius Vibusius Flavianus, his father.
EDCS-05701796.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, Lucius Vibusius Agapetus, set up by his father.

EDCS-05701797.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Pontia Trofime made this for Victorinus, her slave.
EDCS-05701797.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Pontia Trofime for her slave Victorinus.

EDCS-05701798.translation: Q. Vindex made this for his well-deserving wife, Tertia.
EDCS-05701798.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Q. Vindex for his wife, Tertia.

EDCS-05701800.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Vipsania Primilla made this for Gaius Vipsanius Saturninus, who lived for 4 years, 4 months, and 8 days, her foster child.
EDCS-05701800.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Vipsania Primilla for her foster child, Gaius Vipsanius Saturninus.

EDCS-05701803.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Ulpius Blastus purchased this for himself, and for Iulia Apollonia, and Aelia Iulianene, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, with 17.5 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-05701803.summary: This is a funerary dedication and land purchase record by Marcus Ulpius Blastus for himself, his family, and descendants.

EDCS-05701804.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Vipsania Galene, mother, made this for her dearest son, Marcus Ulpius Fortis, who lived for 24 years, 8 months, and 2 days.
EDCS-05701804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Fortis, set up by his grieving mother.

EDCS-05701809.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Ulpius Valentinus, who lived for 24 years.
EDCS-05701809.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Ulpius Valentinus.

EDCS-05701810.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Ulpius Victor, who lived for 1 year, 1 month, and 12 days. Ulpius Apollonius, his father, made this.
EDCS-05701810.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Victor, set up by his father.

EDCS-05701811.translation: To Juno and Verecundia. Marcus Ulpius Eutropus, freedman of Augustus, made this for Ulpia Compses, who lived for 6 years, 6 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-05701811.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Marcus Ulpius Eutropus for his daughter, Ulpia Compses.

EDCS-05701812.translation: To the departed spirits. To Marcua Ulpia Elpiduta, incomparable foster-daughter, Marcus Ulpius Paulinus, patron, [erected this] for her deserving well, who lived 21 years, 2 months, and 8 days, innocent.
EDCS-05701812.summary: This funerary inscription honors the foster-daughter of the dedicator, providing her name, relationship, and lifespan.

EDCS-05701819.translation: To the departed spirits. [For] eighteen years, six months, and five days. Vocconius Andricus and Vocconia Chrysanthe, parents, made [this] for their daughter.
EDCS-05701819.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a young woman and was dedicated by her parents.

EDCS-05701821.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Voltidius Dexter made [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-05701821.summary: A self-dedicated funerary monument by Gaius Voltidius Dexter.

EDCS-05701822.translation: [...orna. Gaius] Voltidius Faustinus, son of Gaius, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-05701822.summary: A fragmented inscription likely identifying an individual with their name, father's name, and status as a freedman.

EDCS-05701823.translation: Gaius Voltidius Saturio, freedman of Chiae, made [this] for himself and for Muciae Soteris, his wife, and for Mutiae, freedwoman of a woman, and for Vitalis, and for Auge, freedwoman of a woman, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument is shared with Gaius Voltidius Tertius in front 10 feet, in the field 25 feet. Gaius Voltidius Tertius made [this] for himself and for his patron Gaius Voltidius. Voltidia Primigenia, freedwoman of Gaius, [made this] for Gaius Voltidius Primigenius, freedman of Gaius, and for Gaius Voltidius Felix, freedman of Gaius, and for Talpa, and for Gaius Voltidius Epaphroditus, freedman of Gaius, and for Gaius Voltidius Anthus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument is shared with Gaius Voltidius Saturio in front 5 feet, in the field 25 feet.
EDCS-05701823.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription detailing shared burial plots and dedications by multiple individuals, including Gaius Voltidius Saturio and Gaius Voltidius Tertius, specifying dimensions of their plots.

EDCS-05701824.translation: In memory of Gaius Vultidius Tharsus, father, and Vultidia Hedone, mother. Atinia Marcellina, granddaughter. Lucius Atinius Atinianus and Vultidia Marcella made [this] for their dearest and most reverent daughter.
EDCS-05701824.summary: This memorial inscription is dedicated by Lucius Atinius Atinianus and Vultidia Marcella to their daughter, also mentioning her parents and grandmother.

EDCS-05701825.translation: Voltidia Chrysis made [this] for herself and for her own freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for her husband Titus Statilius Alximus.
EDCS-05701825.summary: Voltidia Chrysis dedicated this monument for herself, her descendants, her slaves, and her husband.

EDCS-05701829.summary: This inscription likely identifies two women, one named Volusia and the other Maechaera, who was a freedwoman named Musa.

EDCS-05701830.summary: A fragmented inscription identifying an individual with their name and father's name.

EDCS-05701832.translation: To the departed spirits. Ociatus Primitivus made [this] for his deserving wife, Urgila Præpida.
EDCS-05701832.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Ociatus Primitivus to his well-deserving wife, Urgila Præpida.

EDCS-05701833.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits of Zenon.
EDCS-05701833.summary: A funerary dedication to the deified spirits of Zenon, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-05701834.translation: To Zmaragdida, my sweetest wife. She lived 15 years. I made this.
EDCS-05701834.summary: A funerary dedication by a spouse to their wife Zmaragdida, who died at age 15.

EDCS-05701835.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Zosimus, most devoted. Successa made this.
EDCS-05701835.summary: A funerary dedication by Successa to Zosimus, described as most devoted.

EDCS-05701854.translation: I bought this for my wife who lived three days.
EDCS-05701854.summary: A funerary inscription stating the purchase of a monument for a wife who died after only three days of life.

EDCS-05701856.translation: For Julius Huporitus, who lived 5 years and 3 months. His mother and father made this for their sweetest son.
EDCS-05701856.summary: A funerary dedication by parents to their son Julius Huporitus, who died at the age of 5 years and 3 months.

EDCS-05701860.summary: A partial funerary inscription likely dedicated to someone named Chrysopaes, noting they were deserving.

EDCS-05701861.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of 'Mother Phorus' as 21 months.

EDCS-05701875.translation: To the most excellent young freedman.
EDCS-05701875.summary: A dedication, likely funerary, to a highly esteemed young freedman.

EDCS-05701878.translation: For his incomparable wife. He lived 21 years. [His] freedman (?) for his patron deserving well.
EDCS-05701878.summary: A complex funerary inscription potentially commemorating a wife and her patron, with a freedman as the dedicator.

EDCS-05701879.translation: [He/She] made this for [himself/herself] and for [his/her] son Bro.
