EDCS-05701879.summary: A self-dedication and dedication for a son named Bro, likely a tomb inscription.

EDCS-05701894.translation: Anicius Auchenius Bassus, a man of the highest distinction, and Turrenia Honorata, a woman of the highest distinction, his wife, together with their children, devoted to the holy gods.
EDCS-05701894.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the holy gods by Anicius Auchenius Bassus, his wife Turrenia Honorata, and their children.

EDCS-05701913.translation: Calpurnia sleeps here with her beloved son.
EDCS-05701913.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Calpurnia sleeps here with her son.

EDCS-05701916.translation: Crescentia to one who deserved well, in peace.
EDCS-05701916.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Crescentia.

EDCS-05701925.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Julius Euresius Filetus, Iulia Felicitas, and Iulia Victorina, the heirs, erected this for their well-deserving patron, who lived 95 years. He sleeps here.
EDCS-05701925.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records the erection of a monument by heirs for their well-deserving patron who lived 95 years.

EDCS-05701926.translation: To Julia Antonia. Pontius Museus to his most cherished wife, who lived 21 years in this world. Tertulla, innocent, who lived 9 years, 7 months, and 7 days, was placed here. She sleeps in Christ's peace.
EDCS-05701926.summary: This Christian funerary inscription records the death of Iulia Antonia and her daughter Tertulla, with a dedication from her husband Pontius Museus.

EDCS-05701931.translation: Marcellus and Aelia sleep here, and this is a place for Marcianus and Aelia.
EDCS-05701931.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Marcellus and Aelia are buried here, and it is also designated as a burial place for Marcianus and Aelia.

EDCS-05701932.translation: ____ sleeps here, daughter of Marcian, and for herself, when God wills.
EDCS-05701932.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcian's daughter and reserves space for the deceased herself for a future time when God wills.

EDCS-05701933.translation: Maxima sleeps here, sweet and well-deserving, lived 3 months and 8 days.
EDCS-05701933.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Maxima, who lived only 3 months and 8 days.

EDCS-05701937.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Saecundianus sleeps here.

EDCS-05701938.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Secundus sleeps here.

EDCS-05701939.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording the death and burial of Stratonice.

EDCS-05701944.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording the death and burial of Cilla.

EDCS-05701959.translation: To the Almighty Father God, and to His Christ, and to the holy martyrs Taurinus and Herculanus, we give thanks at every hour. Naevius Zaristus and Constantia made martyrdoms for themselves.
EDCS-05701959.summary: A dedicatory inscription, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, to God and martyrs, with a dedication by Naevius Zaristus and Constantia.

EDCS-05701960.translation: Aurelius Marcellinus, deacon, made this for his son Aurelius Zinzio, subdeacon, who lived 25 years and sleeps in peace.
EDCS-05701960.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE, for a son named Aurelius Zinzio, set up by his father.

EDCS-05701963.translation: In the consulship of Basso and Philippus, on the Ides of December. Christ [received] Paulina, who lived 23 years, in peace.
EDCS-05701963.summary: A funerary epitaph, dated by consuls to the late Roman period, recording the death of Paulina at the age of 23.

EDCS-05701968.translation: and Aelia Luciliana and Aelia Maxima in peace.
EDCS-05701968.summary: A funerary inscription, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, commemorating Aelia Luciliana and Aelia Maxima.

EDCS-05701969.translation: To Aelia Sabina, Nevia Fortunata's dearest daughter, in peace.
EDCS-05701969.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, from Nevia Fortunata to her daughter Aelia Sabina.

EDCS-05701971.translation: Caelerina Urbica, a virgin of 24 years, sleeps here in peace, [dedicated] to a most sweet fiancée.
EDCS-05701971.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, for Caelerina Urbica, a virgin aged 24.

EDCS-05701975.translation: Euterpe, daughter of Bibia, and Bibius, son of [---], in God.
EDCS-05701975.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, commemorating Euterpe and Bibius, possibly siblings or spouses.

EDCS-05701981.translation: Roscius Restitutus made this for his mother, Roscia Restuta, in peace.
EDCS-05701981.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, set up by Roscius Restitutus for his mother Roscia Restuta.

EDCS-05701984.translation: May you live securely in God.
EDCS-05701984.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from a Christian context, wishing the deceased eternal life in God.

EDCS-05701986.translation: Vonbia Saturnina rests here for her deserving patroness.
EDCS-05701986.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, dating from the Roman Imperial period, recording the burial of Vonbia Saturnina and her relationship to her patroness.

EDCS-05701995.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Matidia, who is identified by her relationship to the emperor.

EDCS-05701996.translation: Under the supervision of the procurator, the freedman of Augustus, [---] Son, from the workshop of Hermes, the freedman.
EDCS-05701996.summary: This is a record of construction or a dedication, dating to the joint reign of Emperors Antoninus and Verus (161-169 AD), detailing the supervision of a freedman procurator and a workshop.

EDCS-05701998.translation: Under the supervision of the procurator, the freedman of the Augusti, Venustus, from the workshop of Titus Flavius Tiridatis, the freedman.
EDCS-05701998.summary: This is a record of construction or a dedication, dating to the reign of Emperors Septimius Severus, Marcus Aurelius, and Geta (c. 209-211 AD), detailing the supervision of a freedman procurator and a workshop.

EDCS-05702003.translation: To Cornelia Praetextata, most distinguished lady.
EDCS-05702003.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Cornelia Praetextata, noted for her high social standing.

EDCS-05702004.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Manilia Flaccilla.

EDCS-05702005.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Manliana Pulchriana Zoe.

EDCS-05702008.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honoring Septimia Callicratia.

EDCS-05702009.translation: From the workshop of Aurelius Valerius.
EDCS-05702009.summary: This inscription likely indicates the origin or owner of a product or workshop, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05702010.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Cornelius Secundinus.

EDCS-05702012.translation: From the workshop of Iulius Leontus.
EDCS-05702012.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object from the workshop of Iulius Leontus.

EDCS-05702014.translation: From the workshop of Aulus Metilius Threptio.
EDCS-05702014.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object from the workshop of Aulus Metilius Threptio.

EDCS-05702015.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Mindius Anoptes.

EDCS-05702018.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Caius Nasenius Museus.

EDCS-05702019.translation: From the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Asclepiades.
EDCS-05702019.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object from the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Asclepiades.

EDCS-05702020.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Caius Ostiensius Felicissimus.

EDCS-05702021.translation: From the workshop of Ostiensis Praetorianus.
EDCS-05702021.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object from the workshop of Ostiensis Praetorianus.

EDCS-05702022.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Quintus Publius Secundus.

EDCS-05702023.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Quintus Vergilius Eupsychus.

EDCS-05702035.translation: Of Epifania, most illustrious woman, wife of Probianus, a man of note.
EDCS-05702035.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Epifania, wife of Probianus, dating from Late Antiquity.

EDCS-05702036.translation: Of Flavius Gregorius, a devoted man.
EDCS-05702036.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription for Flavius Gregorius, dating from Late Antiquity.

EDCS-05702037.translation: From the workshop of Martinus the plumber.
EDCS-05702037.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a work or object from the workshop of a plumber named Martinus.

EDCS-05702038.translation: During the consulship of Emperor Domitian Augustus for the eighth time and Titus Flavius Sabinus.
EDCS-05702038.summary: This inscription provides a consular dating formula, placing it in the year 82 AD.

EDCS-05702039.translation: During the consulship of Vetus and Valens.
EDCS-05702039.summary: This inscription provides a consular dating formula, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05702040.translation: During the consulship of Aviola and Pansa.
EDCS-05702040.summary: This inscription provides a consular dating formula, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05702041.translation: During the consulship of Marcus Antonius and Sisenna, from Lucanon [region?].
EDCS-05702041.summary: This inscription provides a consular dating formula and mentions a location or origin, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05702054.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly representing characters from a play or mythological scene, perhaps for a theatrical or funerary context.

EDCS-05702055.translation: Isis Geminiana // Farnaces the overseer // Abascantus // made (these things)
EDCS-05702055.summary: This inscription records the work of Farnaces, an overseer, and Abascantus, likely related to the cult of Isis Geminiana.

EDCS-05702056.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly a funerary dedication or a record of individuals.

EDCS-05702057.summary: This inscription lists the four seasons, likely a decorative or mnemonic text.

EDCS-05702059.summary: This inscription appears to be a very short dedication or label, possibly for a person or object, with the name Splendor and a description of a trainee.

EDCS-05702064.summary: This inscription is a long series of numbers, possibly representing days or counts, followed by a name and abbreviations, likely a record of some sort.

EDCS-05800002.translation: Sacred to the Lares of the deified Augustus. Primigenia, mother, with...
EDCS-05800002.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication to the Lares of Augustus, mentioning Primigenia as the mother.

EDCS-05800003.translation: Quintus Servilius Eu[--] built a small shrine...
EDCS-05800003.summary: This inscription records Quintus Servilius Eu[--] building a small shrine.

EDCS-05800006.translation: To Publius Aelius Liberalis, freedman of the deified Augustus, procurator of the Ostian annona, procurator of pugilation and of the ships of the fleet, tribune of the collegium magni decuriali of the decuria viatoria consularis, prefect of the geruli, prefect of the nummulary table of the grain treasury of Ostia, honored with ornaments of the decurionate of the colony of Ostia, patron, to the patron of the vici Augustanorum of Laurentum.
EDCS-05800006.summary: This is a lengthy dedication honoring Publius Aelius Liberalis, listing his numerous official positions in Ostia and his patronage of the Augustan vici of Laurentum, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800010.translation: Manius? Publicius? Tyrannus? ... of Augustus ... from his own funds ... placed this cippus? ...
EDCS-05800010.summary: This is a fragmented inscription recording the placement of a cippus (marker stone) by Manius? Publicius? Tyrannus? at his own expense, possibly dedicated to Augustus.

EDCS-05800014.translation: ... son of Publius Flavius Publi [---] and [---] Dom[---]
EDCS-05800014.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, mentioning the father Publius Flavius and another individual.

EDCS-05800024.translation: Gaius Cestius Prunicus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and for his son Gaius Cestius Prunicus; for his daughter Cestia Fortunata, daughter of Gaius; for his wife Cestia Fortunata, freedwoman of Gaius; for his mother Lollia Prima; for his brother Dionysius, son of Ptolemaeus. Gaius Cestius Prunicus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and for his son Gaius Cestius; for his daughter Cestia Fortunata, daughter of Gaius; for his wife Cestia Fortunata, freedwoman of Gaius; for his mother Lollia Prima; for his brother Dionysius, son of Ptolemaeus.
EDCS-05800024.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Gaius Cestius Prunicus, recording his family members including his son, daughters, wife, mother, and brother, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800028.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Lavinia, daughter of Latinus.

EDCS-05800029.translation: Silvius Aeneas, son of Aeneas and Lavinia.
EDCS-05800029.summary: A personal dedication by Silvius Aeneas, likely on a tombstone, naming his parents.

EDCS-05800035.translation: [...] Iunius Priscilianus Maximus, a most distinguished man, curator of the Laurentes Lavinates, dedicated to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-05800035.summary: A dedication by Iunius Priscilianus Maximus, a high-ranking official, to the divine authority of the Roman Empire.

EDCS-05800036.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the most strong and blessed Caesar, prince of the youth, Iunius Priscilianus Maximus, a most distinguished man, curator of the Laurentes Lavinates, dedicated to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-05800036.summary: A dedication by Iunius Priscilianus Maximus to Emperor Constantius Caesar, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-05800037.translation: To our lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most strong and blessed Caesar, prince of the youth, Iunius Priscilianus Maximus, a most distinguished man, curator of the Laurentes Lavinates, dedicated to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-05800037.summary: A dedication by Iunius Priscilianus Maximus to Emperor Galerius Maximianus Caesar, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-05800038.translation: To Caecilia Philete, daughter of Quintus, a senior virgin of the royal household of the Laurentes Lavinates. Quintus Caecilius Papion, her father, [erected this].
EDCS-05800038.summary: A funerary monument set up by Quintus Caecilius Papion for his daughter Caecilia Philete, who held a significant position.

EDCS-05800041.translation: To Valerius Frumentius, a most perfect man, patron and defender, an inhabitant of the city, who after a long time renewed and repeated his offering of devotion, and for his merit, of his generosity, the city council and citizens of Laurentum Lavinas.
EDCS-05800041.summary: An honorific inscription from the city of Laurentum Lavinas to Valerius Frumentius for his patronage and generous renewal of devotion, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-05800043.translation: Moved from a dark place, under the care of Iunius Gallienus, a most distinguished man, father of fathers, pontiff of the unconquered Sun god, under the care of T. L. L.
EDCS-05800043.summary: An inscription indicating the relocation of a monument or object, overseen by Iunius Gallienus, a prominent priest, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800048.translation: Euphrates, freedman of the Emperor, procurator, for the annual yield of one hundred [denarii?] obtained for himself in this post, gave this as a gift to the Genius of this place.
EDCS-05800048.summary: A dedication by a freedman of the Emperor, Euphrates, to the local Genius of a place where he served as procurator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800050.translation: Gaius Agilleius Mundus, son of Gaius, [elected?] king of the priests, aedile [...], flamen dialis, [dedicated this?] to Juno Sospita Magna Regina [...]
EDCS-05800050.summary: A dedication by Gaius Agilleius Mundus to Juno Sospita Magna Regina, listing his religious offices, likely from Roman Italy.

EDCS-05800051.translation: Quintus Caecilius, freedman of Gnaeus Aulus Quintus, [dedicated this?] to Juno Seispites, Mother Queen.
EDCS-05800051.summary: A dedication by Quintus Caecilius, a freedman, to Juno Seispites, likely from Roman Italy.

EDCS-05800052.translation: To Juno the Protector, Mother, Queen, Quintus Olius Princeps, contractor for public works in Lanuvium, gave this gift from his own funds.
EDCS-05800052.summary: A dedication to Juno by a public works contractor in Lanuvium, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800053.translation: Sacred to Silvanus, from Decimus Granius Celer of the Palatina tribe, chief priest.
EDCS-05800053.summary: A dedication to Silvanus by a chief priest of Lanuvium, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800054.translation: For the Storm Gods, Marcus Laberius, son of Gaius, gives.
EDCS-05800054.summary: A dedication to the Storm Gods by Marcus Laberius, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800055.translation: Marcus Caecilius Lupercus of the Teretina tribe gave this gift to the Great Idaean Mother.
EDCS-05800055.summary: A dedication to the Great Mother Goddess by Marcus Caecilius Lupercus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800058.translation: The Senate and People of Lanuvium, from public funds, under Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power II, with Gaius Caecius Pulcher as dictator, and Publius Autronius Celsus and Lucius Laberius Maximus as aediles.
EDCS-05800058.summary: A record of a public work commissioned by the Senate and People of Lanuvium during the consulship of prominent officials, likely from the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-05800062.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus and the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, the Senate and People of Lanuvium built and dedicated a bath complex from the foundations up, using funds acquired from the generosity of our lords, the princes, from honorific sums and from the interest on the hundred-thousand sums, in a location where baths that had fallen out of use due to age no longer served their purpose.
EDCS-05800062.summary: A dedication by the people of Lanuvium to Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla, recording the construction of a new bath complex, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-05800066.translation: Aulus Castricius Myrio, son of Talens, military tribune, prefect of cavalry, and master of the college of Luperci, of the Capitoline, of the Mercuriales, and of the pagani of Aventinus, XXVIvir, purchased [3]moni through multiple [3]I selections.
EDCS-05800066.summary: An inscription detailing the offices and achievements of Aulus Castricius Myrio, a prominent local official, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800067.translation: to Hesperi, freedman and procurator of Augustus, with torcs.
EDCS-05800067.summary: A dedication to Hesperi, a freedman and procurator of Augustus, possibly related to a military or ceremonial context, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800072.translation: to Titus Mu, military tribune, prefect MV.
EDCS-05800072.summary: An inscription honoring Titus Mu, a military tribune and prefect, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800075.translation: To Decimus [3]cirius, son of Decimus, of the Palatina tribe, upon favorable auspices, as aedile of the municipality, curator of the games, the municipal council and the Flamonal Curia [honored him] for his merits.
EDCS-05800075.summary: A dedication to Decimus [3]cirius by the municipal council and curia for his service as aedile and curator of games, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800077.translation: Gaius? Domatius?, aedile of the town.
EDCS-05800077.summary: This inscription records a local magistrate, likely Gaius Domatius, who held the position of aedile in the town.

EDCS-05800078.translation: Gaius Domatius Rufus, son of Gaius, praetor.
EDCS-05800078.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Domatius Rufus, son of Gaius, as a praetor, a high-ranking Roman magistrate.

EDCS-05800079.translation: Publius Furius Flaccus, freedman of Publius; Gaius Luscius Summachus, freedman of Gaius of the Caiorum clan; Lucius Doroteus, freedman of Lucius; Quintus Verna, freedman of Gaius, son of Quintus; they jointly put on games for three days.
EDCS-05800079.summary: This inscription records a joint effort by four individuals, Publius Furius Flaccus, Gaius Luscius Summachus, Lucius Doroteus, and Quintus Verna, to fund public games for three days.

EDCS-05800080.translation: By the authority of Lucius Ocra, dictator of the town, [Name?]oratus and [Name?] Primigenius repaired the apodyterium with plastered work, which was falling into disrepair due to age, and they also built a new pool, and they set up a bronze basin with three naval-themed fountains.
EDCS-05800080.summary: This inscription details the repair of a public building's apodyterium and the construction of a new pool with decorative fountains, funded by two individuals under the authority of the town's dictator.

EDCS-05800083.translation: To Iugoe, aedile of the town of Lanuvium, in which office he died at the age of 17 years, 11 months, and 4 days, their most rare and devoted son, by his most unhappy parents.
EDCS-05800083.summary: This inscription is a dedication by parents to their deceased son, Iugoe, who served as aedile of Lanuvium and died at a young age.

EDCS-05800086.translation: Lanuvian, fulfilling a vow to his native tribe.
EDCS-05800086.summary: This inscription records a vow made by a Lanuvian man to his native tribe.

EDCS-05800096.translation: Lucius Aemilius Fortunatus made this at his own expense for his best friend.
EDCS-05800096.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Aemilius Fortunatus for his best friend, funded by himself.

EDCS-05800099.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or identification of Agilleia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-05800100.translation: To Aquilia, wife of Caricenus. Marcus Cluvius Aquilius Felix. A garden or orchard, enclosed by a wall, 330 feet long and 98 feet wide, belongs to this tomb.
EDCS-05800100.summary: This inscription describes a garden or orchard belonging to a tomb, specifying its dimensions and owner, Marcus Cluvius Aquilius Felix, dedicated to his wife Aquilia.

EDCS-05800104.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Laberius as the freedman of another Quintus.

EDCS-05800108.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pinnia Polla, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-05800120.translation: Teucus gives this gift to Spes.
EDCS-05800120.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the personification of Hope (Spes) by Teucus.

EDCS-05800127.translation: To Anicius Aquilius Glabrio Faustus, most illustrious man, quaestor candidate, praetor in charge of guardianship, count in the consistory, third prefect of the city, judge of both empires, prefect of the praetorium of Italy, Africa, and Illyricum, so that his glory might be a model for the present and an encouragement to virtue for the future, the council and citizens, who had been rescued from intolerable hardships by the most distinguished man's benefits and remedies, have erected this statue on account of the benefits provided to them.
EDCS-05800127.summary: This is a public dedication of a statue to the highly decorated official Anicius Aquilius Glabrio Faustus by the council and citizens of Aricia for his services, likely dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-05800128.translation: Tiberius Latinius Pandusa, son of Tiberius, Horatian tribe, commissioner for the maintenance of roads.
EDCS-05800128.summary: This is a funerary or official inscription identifying Tiberius Latinius Pandusa and his magistracy as a road commissioner.

EDCS-05800129.translation: [The] senate and people [...] Aricinus [...] to Augustus? [...] dedicated.
EDCS-05800129.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording a dedication of a temple or monument to Augustus by a person from Aricia.

EDCS-05800140.translation: Aelius Liberalis made this for Aelia Saenia Nigrina, his deserving wife.
EDCS-05800140.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aelius Liberalis for his well-deserving wife, Aelia Saenia Nigrina.

EDCS-05800141.translation: Marcus Atius, son of Marcus, [H]oratian tribe, [left for] his freedmen and freedwomen [...]. Marcus Atius Salvius, freedman of Marcus. Marcus Atius Hiero[cery]x(?), freedman of Marcus. Marcus Atius Antiochus, freedman of Marcus. Marcus Atius Alexander, freedman of Marcus. Marcus Atius Licaen[...]. Marcus Atius Primus, freedman of Marcus [...]. Marcus Atius Felix, freedman of Marcus [...]. Marcus Atius Ludo[...]. Marcus Atius [...]. Marcus Atius [...]. Marcus Atius [...]. Marcus [...].
EDCS-05800141.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription listing Marcus Atius, his son (possibly), and numerous freedmen and freedwomen, indicating a prominent patron and his household.

EDCS-05800142.translation: Marcus Atius Celer, son of Marcus, Horatian tribe; Atia Ammia, freedwoman of Marcus; Atia Psyche, freedwoman of Marcus; Atia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus; Atia Bazis, freedwoman of Marcus; Marcus Atius Eros, freedman of Marcus; Atia Nice, freedwoman of Marcus; Marcus Atius Primio, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05800142.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing members of the Atius family, including Marcus Atius Celer and several freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-05800143.translation: Quintus Avonius Bello, freedman of Quintus; Ampia Hyaline, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-05800143.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Avonius Bello, a freedman, and Ampia Hyaline, a freedwoman.

EDCS-05800144.translation: Manuis Avonius Menander, freedman of Manuis; Manuis Avonius, son of Manuis, Horatian tribe; [...]. Durmia, freedwoman of Publius [...]. Philumina his wife.
EDCS-05800144.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription for Manuis Avonius Menander, his son Manuis Avonius, and his wife Philumina, with a mention of Durmia.

EDCS-05800145.translation: Valerius Victorinus erected this for Calpurnia Lupa, his deserving nurse.
EDCS-05800145.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Valerius Victorinus for his nurse, Calpurnia Lupa.

EDCS-05800147.translation: Clodia, freedwoman of a woman, to Quintus Accolius, freedman of Quintus, her husband, and to Felix, a freedman.
EDCS-05800147.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Clodia, a freedwoman, to her husband and another freedman.

EDCS-05800149.translation: Quintus Decirius Burrus, son of Quintus; Deciria Tertulla, freedwoman of Quintus; and Deciria Tertulla, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-05800149.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing three individuals: Quintus Decirius Burrus, his freedwoman Deciria Tertia, and his daughter Deciria Tertulla.

EDCS-05800150.translation: Quintus Duronius Pamphilus, freedman of Quintus, for himself and his family, and Duronia Saturnina, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-05800150.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Quintus Duronius Pamphilus, a freedman, for himself and his family, and includes his daughter Duronia Saturnina.

EDCS-05800151.translation: Marcus Fabius Maius, son of Marcus; Roscia, freedwoman of a woman, Pamphila.
EDCS-05800151.summary: This inscription records the names of Marcus Fabius Maius, son of Marcus, and Roscia Pamphila, a freedwoman.

EDCS-05800152.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Titia, a freedwoman of Titus, and two other individuals.

EDCS-05800158.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning Lucretius Sa[---].

EDCS-05800161.summary: This inscription likely records the ownership or dedication by Marcus Metilius Erotis.

EDCS-05800167.summary: This inscription simply records the name Lucius Vitellius.

EDCS-05800175.translation: Sacred to Diana of the Grove. Marcus Acilius Priscus and Egrilius Plarianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05800175.summary: This is a religious dedication to Diana Nemorensis by Marcus Acilius Priscus and Egrilius Plarianus.

EDCS-05800181.translation: To Gaius Salvius Nason, son of Gaius, as propraetorian legate, from Myseus Abba and Epictetus, because he saved them in the Mithridatic War, for his valor.
EDCS-05800181.summary: A dedication to a Roman governor, Gaius Salvius Nason, for his military service in the Mithridatic War.

EDCS-05800182.translation: Gaius Cossutius Myrmex, son of Gaius, aedile. [
EDCS-05800182.summary: The beginning of an inscription, likely an official record or dedication by a Roman official named Gaius Cossutius Myrmex.

EDCS-05800183.translation: Septimius Boethus, a Roman equestrian, and his honorable wife Iulia Iuliane, placed this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-05800183.summary: A funerary monument set up by a Roman equestrian and his wife for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-05800185.translation: Leicinius Voconius, son of Lucius; Lucius [son of Lucius].
EDCS-05800185.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of two individuals, possibly a father and son or two relatives, with their patronymic details, likely on a boundary marker or a simple funerary stone.

EDCS-05800188.summary: A short epitaph for a beloved individual named Ilarus.

EDCS-05800189.translation: To Onesimus, who deserved well, in peace. He himself earned all good things while he lived, and no one can achieve such things. And for his sons, rejoicing in their glorious life, Sextus Iubenis, seeing him and one sister in all good things, to give celestial kingdoms is great piety in Christ, to forgive offenses. If you seek his name, look at the first letters of the verses. For good memory, who deserved well in peace, in peace of Christ, use.
EDCS-05800189.summary: A complex funerary inscription for Onesimus, praising his good deeds and the piety of his son Sextus Iubenis, with a acrostic element for his name and a Christian reference.

EDCS-05800222.translation: To Sol for the health and return and victory of [---] and of the entire divine house [---] III and Tato, father of the sacred rites [---] granting [---
EDCS-05800222.summary: A dedication to the god Sol, likely seeking divine favor for the well-being and victories of the emperor and the imperial family, possibly from a priest.

EDCS-05800224.translation: To Victoria Redux, by our lords, the Emperors Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus and Otacilia [Severa] Augusta, consort of our lord. Soldiers of the II Parthica Philippiana Pia Felix Fidelis Aeterna legion, who began their service under the consulship of Octatinus Adventus, whose names with their fathers are inscribed below, devoted to their divinity and majesty. On the 10th day before the Kalends of August, under Peregrinus and Aemilianus, including centurions and evocati of our Emperors. The care was undertaken by Pomponius Iulianus, centurion of the same legion.
EDCS-05800224.summary: A dedication to Victoria Redux by soldiers of the II Parthica Philippiana legion, honoring the emperors Philip I and Otacilia Severa, and dating to the consulship of Adventus, likely commemorating a military success or safe return.

EDCS-05800225.translation: To Aesopus, administrator for Emperor Caesar Augustus. To Apsyrtianus. To Lucilia Pira, daughter of Gaius. To her dearest husband and to herself and their descendants.
EDCS-05800225.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Aesopus, an imperial administrator, and his wife Lucilia Pira, for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-05800226.translation: To Titus Arruntius Iulianus, prefect of the artisans, and to his daughter Iulia Arruntia.
EDCS-05800226.summary: A dedication or funerary marker for Titus Arruntius Iulianus, a prefect of the artisans, and his daughter.

EDCS-05800229.translation: The heir made the monument. Publius Faltonius Apollonius, son of Publius, freedman, magistrate of the district, appointed, Rubria, daughter of Caius and freedwoman of a woman, Olivia; Liguria, daughter of Aulus, freedwoman, Olympia; Faltonia Hediste, daughter of Publius, freedwoman; Euchrestus, freedman of Publius Faltonius Hedistus.
EDCS-05800229.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary monument, likely set up by heirs and possibly including freedmen and their patron.

EDCS-05800233.translation: to Augustus II / under consuls Modestus II and Probus / Publius Caecilius [---] / Lucius [---] Victor / Marcus Aeb[---] Pothinus / Quintus Lucceius Aemilianus / [---]el Alcimion / [---] Paulus // [---] / [---] / Lucius Lucretius [---] / Gaius [---] / [---] / [---] Elenius [---] / [---] / [---] // under consuls Claudius Pompeianus Sallustius Paelignianus / Publius Plaetorius Zosimus / Lucius Flavius Philippus / Lucius Ulpius Maximus / [---]elorius
EDCS-05800233.summary: This inscription lists names of individuals, possibly officials or members of a college, and mentions consuls, suggesting a public or administrative context.

EDCS-05800234.translation: Iulius S[---] / Opimius Cu[---] / Iulius T[---] / Flavius [---] / Urfi[---] // [---] Aurelius [---] / [---]vairon [---] / [---] Aterius Se[---] / [---] of cohort III / [---] Aurelius Romanus / [---] Aurelius Marcus / [---] Aurelius Alexander / [---] Aurelius Iamianus / [---] of cohort IIII / [---] Romanius Verecundus / [---] Aelius Nestor / [---] Iulius Felicissimus / [---] Aelius Amandinus / [---] Valerius Valens / [---] Pompeius Marcus / [---] of cohort V / [---] Lusius Taurus / [---] Aelius Rufus / [---] Aemilius Amandus / [---] Aurelius Minucianus / [---] Aterius Priscus / [---] impromotus / [---] Domitius Paternus / [---] Considius Apollinaris / [---] Vettius Cianus / [---] Lucilius [Pro]culus
EDCS-05800234.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly soldiers belonging to different cohorts, with some indicated as Aurelius, Aelius, and other Roman cognomina.

EDCS-05800235.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Claudia Firmina, wife and heir, and Aelius Firminus, son, made this for the deserving Aelius Marcellus, soldier of the II Parthica legion, who lived 47 years and served 26 years, and for Valerius, his ward, who lived 4 years.
EDCS-05800235.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelius Marcellus, a soldier in the II Parthica legion, and his ward Valerius, set up by his wife and son.

EDCS-05800241.translation: To [---] / NOSCIFELC[---] / served 20 years / VXI Vettia Fictosa made this for her deserving husband.
EDCS-05800241.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a soldier who served 20 years, set up by his wife Vettia Fictosa.

EDCS-05800246.translation: Aurel(ius) Bitus, soldier of the II Parthica legion, century V, of the front rank of the later cohort, served 25 years; his heir arranged for this to be made for him as he deserved.
EDCS-05800246.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Bitus, a soldier in the II Parthica legion, with his service length and heir mentioned.

EDCS-05800260.translation: Valerius of the II Parthica Severiana legion lived 50 years, served 15 years. Valerius Martinianus and Valeria Flavia, daughter and heir, and Ulpia, wife, and Valerius Sabinianus Secundus, second heir, made this for him as he deserved.
EDCS-05800260.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valerius, a soldier in the II Parthica Severiana legion, listing his age, service time, and the family members who erected it.

EDCS-05800265.translation: To Marcus Aurelius, freedman of the Augusti, Plebeius, elected curator, scribe, and perpetual magistrate of the body of actors of the Latins, for his incomparable integrity in managing the republic of the body above-mentioned, the contractors of the herds of the Augusti [---] and [---]
EDCS-05800265.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Aurelius Plebeius, a freedman and prominent official within a guild of actors, for his service and integrity.

EDCS-05800266.translation: Tiberius Claudius, who was called the Macedonian Phonascus, for himself and for his wife Stlaccia Dignae.
EDCS-05800266.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tiberius Claudius Phonascus and his wife, likely a self-purchase or family tomb.

EDCS-05800284.translation: Precilia Tertia, daughter of Quintus, made this for herself, her husband, son, freedmen, and freedwomen.
EDCS-05800284.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Precilia Tertia and her family, including herself, husband, son, and freed dependents.

EDCS-05800289.translation: Aurelius Clementianus lived for one year and three months; his father and mother set this up for their dearest son.
EDCS-05800289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Clementianus, who died at just over one year old, set up by his parents.

EDCS-05800291.translation: Aurelius Iustinus and Neodora made this for their daughter, who lived seven months; she was most sweet.
EDCS-05800291.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young daughter, made by her parents Aurelius Iustinus and Neodora.

EDCS-05800296.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aurelia Felicissima lived for 23 years. Cesius Secundus made this memorial for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-05800296.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Cesius Secundus for his wife Aurelia Felicissima, who died at age 23.

EDCS-05800300.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Auscia Aricina, who died at age 25.

EDCS-05800312.translation: To Titus [---], freedman Braco. Iustinus, his patron, made this for a well-deserving freedman.
EDCS-05800312.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by the patron Iustinus for his freedman Braco.

EDCS-05800316.translation: To the Genius of Germanicus. Auchenius.
EDCS-05800316.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of Germanicus by Auchenius.

EDCS-05800321.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Diodorus for the memory of his most chaste wife Lucisca, most loving to him.
EDCS-05800321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Diodorus for his wife Lucisca.

EDCS-05800325.translation: Publius Novius Symphorus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05800325.summary: This is a tombstone identifying Publius Novius Symphorus, a freedman.

EDCS-05800326.translation: For Publius Novius Thiasus, freedman of Publius. Publius Novius Callistus made this, according to the will and by order of the patron.
EDCS-05800326.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Publius Novius Callistus for his freedman Publius Novius Thiasus, as stipulated by the will of their patron.

EDCS-05800328.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly for Marcus Petreius.

EDCS-05800331.translation: To Phila, daughter of Lucius Pomponius.
EDCS-05800331.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Phila, daughter of Lucius Pomponius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800336.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary epitaph for someone named Silvanius Socratianus, with the rest of the text lost.

EDCS-05800337.summary: This text likely refers to Quintus Sulpicius Mulsus, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker on an object or monument.

EDCS-05800353.summary: This inscription lists four names: Dionysius, Paulus, Petrus, and Laurentius, possibly identifying individuals associated with a monument or group.

EDCS-05800354.translation: Dedicated to the ancestral father Vedius Vedius, by the gentile tribe of the Julii, the altar of the Alban Law was consecrated.
EDCS-05800354.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to an ancestral figure by the gentile tribe of the Julii, following the Alban Law, likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800377.translation: The Albanians, sons of Flavius Albanus Longanus, to their patron.
EDCS-05800377.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by the citizens of Bovillae, identified as the sons of Flavius Albanus Longanus, to their patron.

EDCS-05800381.translation: Gnaeus Voluntilius Trypho arranged for this to be made at his own expense, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800381.summary: This inscription records that Gnaeus Voluntilius Trypho commissioned a work at his own expense, following a decision by the local council (decurions), likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800384.translation: To his mother, Aemilia Antistia Herennia Postuma, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-05800384.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aemilia Antistia Herennia Postuma, daughter of Caius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800385.translation: Secunda made this for Quintus Arrius Diomedes, freedman of Quintus, and for Arria Iucunda, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-05800385.summary: This inscription records that Secunda created a monument for two freedpersons, Quintus Arrius Diomedes and Arria Iucunda, likely a funerary dedication from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800386.translation: Chryseros, the steward of Tiberius Caesar Drusianus, Philostorgus, and Terpusa made [this].
EDCS-05800386.summary: This inscription records that Chryseros, the steward of Tiberius Caesar Drusianus, along with Philostorgus and Terpusa, commissioned a work, likely a dedication or funerary monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800387.summary: This inscription records a caretaking role, possibly related to a monument or property, attributed to Chrysogonus.

EDCS-05800390.translation: To the Divine Shades. Roscia, a most unhappy mother, made this for her most beloved son Titus Roscio Maximus, who lived 10 years, 1 month, and [some days].
EDCS-05800390.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Roscio Maximus, set up by his grieving mother, dating likely to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800391.translation: Here rests the servant of God C, who lived three years, [some months], and [some days], is laid to rest on the Ides of July.
EDCS-05800391.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the burial of a servant of God on the Ides of July.

EDCS-05800392.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for a person named Optata.

EDCS-05800394.translation: Quintus Victor, son of Pollio, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-05800394.summary: This inscription likely records the name and tribal affiliation of Quintus Victor, son of Pollio.

EDCS-05800404.translation: To the [estate/property] of the eighth cohort of Quintus Vocontius Pollio.
EDCS-05800404.summary: This inscription appears to record ownership or dedication related to a property or estate associated with Quintus Vocontius Pollio.

EDCS-05800407.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Antonius Faustinus, who lived 15 years and [some days].
EDCS-05800407.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades for Antonius Faustinus, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-05800413.translation: Plautia Dynamis, the mother, made this for her most devoted son Gaius Julius Apollinaris, and for Gaius Julius Primus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05800413.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a mother for her son, also providing for other family members and freedpersons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800421.translation: Aurelius Primus, the father, to his dearest son Aurelius Leontius, who lived [some years], 6 months, and 10 days, departed on the day before the August holidays, in peace.
EDCS-05800421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from a father to his son Aurelius Leontius, indicating his age at death and burial.

EDCS-05800423.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the municipium. Quintus Aurelius Faustinianus, aedile, at his own expense.
EDCS-05800423.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of the municipality, funded by Quintus Aurelius Faustinianus, who held the office of aedile.

EDCS-05800424.translation: Sacred to the unconquered Hercules. Marcus Aurelius Stephanus set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05800424.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Hercules by Marcus Aurelius Stephanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800426.translation: Abu(rius) Genialis made this for the Mother of the Gods by order.
EDCS-05800426.summary: This is an inscription recording an offering made by Aburius Genialis to the Mother of the Gods, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800430.translation: For Marcus Aurelius Caesar, consul for the second time, son of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the second time, consul for the fourth time, father of his country; to the decurion of the Castri Moesiensium.
EDCS-05800430.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Caesar, son of Antoninus Pius, likely a dedication from the town of Castri Moesiensium during his consulships and tribunician power, probably mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800433.translation: To Lucius Caecilius Rufus, son of Lucius, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor, proconsul. Sacred to the departed spirits. [Epitaph] of Lucius Caecilius Rufus.
EDCS-05800433.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caecilius Rufus, who held various high offices, set up by his father also named Lucius Caecilius Rufus.

EDCS-05800434.translation: To my sons, torn away by the most unjust fates. Apollonius, father of our Caesar, a courier, most unhappy, and Octavia, a businesswoman, mother.
EDCS-05800434.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the sons of Apollonius and Octavia, expressing their grief and identifying the parents' professions and connection to the imperial household.

EDCS-05800438.translation: Flavia Marcella, freedwoman of Augustus, made this for herself and for Alcmus, freedman of Augustus, her husband, and for Martialis, husband of our Caesar, most excellent, and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. The place was granted by decree of the decurions of Castrimoenium.
EDCS-05800438.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Marcella, her husband Alcmus, and another individual Martialis, detailing the grant of burial space by the local council of Castrimoenium, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800445.translation: Aleia Prima, freedwoman of Caius, gave [this] to Anteros, son of Vedius.
EDCS-05800445.summary: This is a dedicatory or perhaps funerary inscription recording a gift from Aleia Prima to Anteros, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800453.translation: [The tomb of] Faustina. [Faustina?]. Manius Acilius Glabrio Cn(aeus) Cornelius Severus [dedicated this?]. [age] 13 years, 2 months, 11 days. [daughter?] cilla Aciliana. [age] 3 months, 13 days.
EDCS-05800453.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription that records the death and age of at least two individuals, possibly related, and mentions prominent names like Manius Acilius Glabrio.

EDCS-05800457.translation: This entire boundary stone was placed in the land of Publius Pacilius.
EDCS-05800457.summary: This is an inscription recording the placement of a boundary marker in the land belonging to Publius Pacilius, likely a legal or administrative record from antiquity.

EDCS-05800462.translation: Thus you are a servant. Asclepius gave the gift to the counter-scribe.
EDCS-05800462.summary: This is a peculiar inscription where a servant, Asclepius, is described as giving a gift to a 'counter-scribe', possibly related to a legal transaction or a personal note from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800469.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Marcellus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe, quaestor of the province of Narbonensis, tribune of the plebs, praetor, in both these offices a candidate of the deified Trajan Augustus, governor (legatus pro praetore) of the province of Narbonensis and of the province of Baetica, proconsul of the province of Sicily.
EDCS-05800469.summary: This inscription lists the dignities and offices held by Quintus Caecilius Marcellus, a Roman official.

EDCS-05800472.translation: To Marcus Metilius Aquillus Regulus, son of Publius, of the Claudian tribe, Nepos Volusius Torquatus Fronton, consul from the Kalends of January, augur, Salii Collini, member of the college of Flaviales, praetor, quaestor, moneyer (triumvir monetalis) for striking bronze, silver, and gold, prefect of the Latin Games.
EDCS-05800472.summary: This inscription lists the offices and priesthoods held by Marcus Metilius Aquillus Regulus, a Roman official.

EDCS-05800475.translation: Publius Aelius Hilarus, freedman of the Emperors, who managed the accounts of the imperial patrimony at Alexandria.
EDCS-05800475.summary: This inscription records that Publius Aelius Hilarus, an imperial freedman, served as an administrator of patrimonial accounts in Alexandria.

EDCS-05800478.translation: To Gaius Julius Aspro, consul, praetor, curator of the Appian Way, member of the college of the sacred temples; Lucius Metius Mimesius, from the Voturia tribe, his incomparable friend.
EDCS-05800478.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Julius Aspro, listing his offices and honoring him as a friend by Lucius Metius Mimesius.

EDCS-05800482.translation: To Gaius Julius Aspro, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor of the province of Africa, curator of the sacred temples, their patron who deserved well of them.
EDCS-05800482.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Julius Aspro, a Roman official and patron, for his services as curator of sacred temples and his past offices.

EDCS-05800483.translation: To Gaius Julius Aspro, consul, candidate.
EDCS-05800483.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Julius Aspro, noting his consulship and his status as a candidate.

EDCS-05800485.translation: Asper, twice consul, prefect of the city.
EDCS-05800485.summary: This inscription records the high offices of Asper, noting he served twice as consul and as prefect of the city.

EDCS-05800487.translation: To Julia Juliana, sister of Asper.
EDCS-05800487.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Juliana, identifying her as the sister of Asper.

EDCS-05800489.translation: To Callippus, freedman of Quintus Cornelius Campanus, a lictor, for himself and for An Athenaïs, his fellow-soldier (contubernalis), who deserved well of him, and for his son.
EDCS-05800489.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory inscription by Callippus, a freedman and lictor, for himself, his companion, and his son.

EDCS-05800491.translation: Lucius Sextilius Satyrus, a curiate lictor, made this for himself, and for his freedwoman wife Sextilia Agele, who deserved well of him and was most worthy and deserving, and for their son Lucius Sextilius Saturninus, who lived for 3 years and 6 months, and for his son Lucius Sextilius Proculus, son of Lucius, son of Satyrus, who lived for 7 years.
EDCS-05800491.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Sextilius Satyrus, a lictor, commemorating his wife Sextilia Agele and their two sons, Lucius Sextilius Saturninus and Lucius Sextilius Proculus, noting their ages at death.

EDCS-05800494.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bibia Paulina to Publius Aelius Serenus, her son, who deserved well, and to the memory of Polydeuces, who lived 9 years and 7 months.
EDCS-05800494.summary: A funerary dedication by Bibia Paulina to her son, Publius Aelius Serenus, and his companion Polydeuces.

EDCS-05800496.translation: Antalcides, freedman of the Emperors, [dedicates this] to Aelia, his wife, and himself, so that after my death this tomb may belong to the possession of the Naeviani and Calpurniani estates.
EDCS-05800496.summary: A tomb inscription by Antalcides, freedman of the Emperors, for himself and his wife Aelia, with provisions for the inheritance of estates.

EDCS-05800497.summary: A simple dedication to Aelia Rhodilla, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-05800498.translation: To the departed spirits. Appuleius Eutychus made this for his freedwoman Appuleia Helpidius, who deserved well, and for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-05800498.summary: A funerary dedication by Appuleius Eutychus for his freedwoman Appuleia Helpidius, also intended for himself and his family.

EDCS-05800501.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Rustius Celadus made this for his most dutiful mother, Atidia Tertullia, who deserved well.
EDCS-05800501.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Rustius Celadus to his mother, Atidia Tertullia.

EDCS-05800502.translation: Caius Attienus Stephanus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-05800502.summary: An identification inscription for Caius Attienus Stephanus, a freedman.

EDCS-05800503.translation: Caius Attienus Stephanus, freedman of Caius. Attiena Nomas, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-05800503.summary: Identifies two freedpersons, Caius Attienus Stephanus and Attiena Nomas, both freedmen of a 'Caius'.

EDCS-05800504.translation: Marcus Bet[---] to his daughter Tonia.
EDCS-05800504.summary: An incomplete inscription likely recording a dedication or memorial from Marcus Bet[...] to his daughter Tonia.

EDCS-05800505.translation: By the gods above and below, I implore you not to disturb the ossuaries. Marcus Calpurnius Sulla, freedman of Marcus, and Calpurnia Fausta, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-05800505.summary: A plea to respect burial places, inscribed by two freedpersons, Marcus Calpurnius Sulla and Calpurnia Fausta.

EDCS-05800506.translation: To the departed spirits. Bacchis made this for her most dutiful daughter Cassia Magna, who lived 20 years.
EDCS-05800506.summary: A funerary dedication by Bacchis to her daughter Cassia Magna.

EDCS-05800508.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple dedication or funerary marker for Caius Cordius Eros and Cordia Prima.

EDCS-05800509.translation: Lucius Cornelius, freedman of a woman, lives. Lucius Cornelius lives. Cornelia, freedwoman of a woman, lives. Cornelia, freedwoman of Lucius, lives.
EDCS-05800509.summary: This inscription records the survival of Lucius Cornelius and several freedwomen, possibly on a tombstone or boundary marker.

EDCS-05800510.translation: Quintus Zosimus lived and was well for 100 years. His tutor Quintus Allidius made this.
EDCS-05800510.summary: This funerary epitaph records the long life of Quintus Zosimus and was erected by his tutor, Quintus Allidius.

EDCS-05800511.translation: To Gnaeus Dio and his family, and to Marcus Cincins Stephanos and his family, in front 13 feet, in the field [space for more].
EDCS-05800511.summary: This inscription likely records land division or ownership, specifying dimensions and beneficiaries.

EDCS-05800512.translation: To the departed spirits, for Euprepes, his fellow soldier, deserving well.
EDCS-05800512.summary: This funerary dedication is from Nicetas to his deserving fellow soldier (contubernalis) Euprepes.

EDCS-05800514.translation: To the departed spirits, for Felicio, his dearest foster-child of Italy, who lived one year, six months, eleven days, eleven hours.
EDCS-05800514.summary: This funerary epitaph records the tragically short life of Felicio, a beloved foster-child, and was likely set up by her guardian.

EDCS-05800517.translation: To the departed spirits, for Lucius Iabolenus Onesimus, Lucia Epiteuxis made this for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-05800517.summary: This funerary epitaph records Lucia Epiteuxis dedicating a monument to her dutiful son, Lucius Iabolenus Onesimus.

EDCS-05800518.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iavolena Artemisia, Epictetus made this for his most devoted wife, deserving well.
EDCS-05800518.summary: This funerary epitaph records Epictetus dedicating a monument to his devoted wife, Iavolena Artemisia.

EDCS-05800519.translation: To the departed spirits, for Julius Alcibiades, Iulia Aphrodisia made this for her husband deserving well, together with her sons.
EDCS-05800519.summary: This funerary epitaph records Iulia Aphrodisia and her sons dedicating a monument to her husband, Julius Alcibiades.

EDCS-05800520.translation: To the departed spirits, for Caius Julius Pistus, Caius Folius Chrysanthianus made this for his deserving friend.
EDCS-05800520.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caius Folius Chrysanthianus dedicating a monument to his deserving friend, Caius Julius Pistus.

EDCS-05800521.translation: To Julia Anthia, my sister. Iulius Andronicus [erected this].
EDCS-05800521.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated by Iulius Andronicus to his sister, Julia Anthia.

EDCS-05800522.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Lucceius Ephebicus [erected this] to Valeria Frugifera, his wife, and to himself.
EDCS-05800522.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Marcus Lucceius Ephebicus to his wife, Valeria Frugifera, and to himself.

EDCS-05800524.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. To Romulus, my son, who lived 7 months. Lucifer, his father, made this.
EDCS-05800524.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucifer for his son Romulus, who died at seven months old.

EDCS-05800526.translation: Olla (urn) to Secunda. I warn mortals: let no one mourn me, for I was fortunate. Now I am covered by ashes. Here I lie, tranquil, unique above all. My third birthday (of life?) was consumed by love. My third birthday (of death?) - the Ides of May.
EDCS-05800526.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secunda, expressing a defiant joy in death and mentioning her birthday and possibly the date of death or commemoration.

EDCS-05800527.translation: To Marcus Servilius Ianuarius, his excellent freedman. Marcus Servilius Tryphon, his patron, [erected this].
EDCS-05800527.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a patron, Marcus Servilius Tryphon, to his freedman, Marcus Servilius Ianuarius.

EDCS-05800532.translation: Onesimus Iambus Telesphorus [erected this] to Titus Vestricius Iambus and Titus Vestricius Telesphorus, his most excellent patrons, and also to himself, and to Vestricia Myrtis, and to Vestricius Rusticus, and to their descendants.
EDCS-05800532.summary: This is a dedication by Onesimus Iambus Telesphorus for his patrons, his family, and himself, likely a funerary monument or a group dedication.

EDCS-05800533.translation: [Erected by] Lavi [to] Marcus Vibius Nosti, his most excellent friend.
EDCS-05800533.summary: This is an inscription dedicated by Lavi to his friend Marcus Vibius Nosti.

EDCS-05800547.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Sextus Antistius Montanus, who lived 2 years, 2 months, 10 days. Festianus, the steward, made this for one who deserved well.
EDCS-05800547.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Festianus for Sextus Antistius Montanus, who died as a child.

EDCS-05800549.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Cispius Verus, likely a funerary monument or marker.

EDCS-05800550.summary: This is a dedication by Septimius Secundinus, likely a funerary monument or marker.

EDCS-05800551.summary: This is a personal name, likely a funerary or ownership inscription.

EDCS-05800552.translation: Eros, son of Gnaeus, of the Papiria tribe.
EDCS-05800552.summary: This is a personal name with tribal affiliation, likely a funerary or ownership inscription.

EDCS-05800555.translation: Marcus Fourios, son of Caius, military tribune, dedicated from the spoils to Fortuna.
EDCS-05800555.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna by Marcus Fourios, a military tribune, likely dating to the Republican period.

EDCS-05800556.translation: Marcus Fourios, son of Caius, military tribune, dedicated from the spoils to Maurtes.
EDCS-05800556.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Maurtes (possibly a deity or a place) by Marcus Fourios, a military tribune, likely dating to the Republican period.

EDCS-05800557.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Libertas, set up during the aedileship of Publius Valerius Bassus, prefect of the engineers.
EDCS-05800557.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred object to Jupiter Libertas during the aedileship of Publius Valerius Bassus, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05800580.translation: Marcus Fulvius, son of Marcus, grandson of Servius, consul, captured Aetolia.
EDCS-05800580.summary: This inscription records a military achievement by Marcus Fulvius, a consul, likely from the period of the Roman expansion into Greece.

EDCS-05800598.translation: To Ripianus, cavalryman of the Second Cohort of Massilia.
EDCS-05800598.summary: This is likely a dedication or funerary inscription for Ripianus, a cavalryman serving in a cohort stationed in or associated with Massilia, dating probably to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800605.translation: Quintus Coelius, son of Quintus, and Marcus Decimius, son of Decimius, aediles, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-05800605.summary: This inscription records the actions of two aediles, Quintus Coelius and Marcus Decimius, acting on a senatorial decree, likely from the Republican period.

EDCS-05800628.summary: This inscription consists of two personal names, possibly indicating a shared funerary monument or ownership.

EDCS-05800630.summary: This inscription consists of a personal name and his profession, likely a funerary marker or dedication for the poet Diphilos.

EDCS-05800633.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Carpus, slave of Mansuetus Stertinus Quartus, for his brother.
EDCS-05800633.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a slave for his brother, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800634.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Novia Tyche, freedwoman and wife, made this for her well-deserving husband Lucius Novius Sabinus, the pearl-dealer.
EDCS-05800634.summary: This funerary dedication was made by a wife for her husband, a pearl-dealer, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800635.translation: Sosimus, the builder. He dedicated this place from his own property for his wife, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-05800635.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a burial plot by a builder for his wife, who died at the age of 17, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800636.translation: Made by Abescantus, slave of Atimetianus, under the supervision of Alypius, freedman procurator of the Emperor Domitianus Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-05800636.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument or building under the supervision of a freedman procurator during the reign of Emperor Domitian, dating to 81-96 CE.

EDCS-05800642.summary: This is a simple dedication made by Titus Cispius Decor, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800643.summary: This is a simple dedication made by Claudius Felicissimus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800644.summary: This is a simple dedication made by Tiberius Claudius For, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800652.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Faustina, with her mother Prima, made this for her most excellent and deserving father, Titus Aelius Agathemerus.
EDCS-05800652.summary: This funerary dedication was made by a daughter and her mother for the father, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800654.translation: Gaius Annius Helenus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself, his wife Annia Stacte, his brother Gaius Annius Euphron, freedman of Gaius, and his sister Julia Euphrosyne, during his lifetime.
EDCS-05800654.summary: This is a self-funded funerary dedication made by Gaius Annius Helenus for himself and his family members, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800655.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Annius Cataplus and Annia Secunda arranged for this to be made for their deserving patron, Marcus Annius Sincerus.
EDCS-05800655.summary: This funerary dedication was arranged by freedmen for their patron, Marcus Annius Sincerus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800656.translation: To the divine shades. Anthusa lived 25 years, 8 months, and 18 days. Thalassus and Ionicus made this for their deserving wife.
EDCS-05800656.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Anthusa, set up by her husband(s) or partners, Thalassus and Ionicus.

EDCS-05800657.translation: To the divine shades. For Antestius Mercurius, who lived 13 years, from his parents, for their sweetest son.
EDCS-05800657.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antestius Mercurius, set up by his parents.

EDCS-05800659.translation: To the divine shades. For Marcus Arrecinus Zosimus, their deserving father. Arrecina Tatis made this.
EDCS-05800659.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Arrecinus Zosimus, dedicated by his daughter Arrecina Tatis.

EDCS-05800660.translation: To the divine shades. For Arrius Smaragdus.
EDCS-05800660.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for Arrius Smaragdus.

EDCS-05800661.translation: For Marcus Aurelius Nicephor, the most devoted father, who lived 70 years, 1 month, and 21 days. Eustochium made this for her deserving father. (The text seems to contain a corruption 'chla numini'.)
EDCS-05800661.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Nicephor, erected by his daughter Eustochium.

EDCS-05800663.translation: For Quintus Baebius, son of Quintus, son of Fufius. Numisius Rutilius [restored text follows, illegible in parts, relating to boundary or ownership markers].
EDCS-05800663.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or property record, possibly naming Quintus Baebius and Numisius Rutilius.

EDCS-05800666.translation: To the divine shades. Publius Calpurnius Agesilaus and Calpurnia Stefanis made this for their excellent patron, well-deserving. And his son Publius Calpurnius Eumenes.
EDCS-05800666.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed patron, dedicated by his freedmen Publius Calpurnius Agesilaus and Calpurnia Stefanis, with a mention of their son Eumenes.

EDCS-05800669.translation: Festus made this monument for his mother, Claudia Festa. It extends 280 feet into the field and 300 feet in front. Tiberius Claudius Felix made it for Claudia. (The reading E M E L P H is obscure).
EDCS-05800669.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary monument and names the dedicator, Festus (possibly Tiberius Claudius Felix), and the deceased, Claudia Festa.

EDCS-05800671.translation: Of Marcus Cornelius, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, son of Mamulla. Of Marcus Cornelius, son of Marcus, son of Mamulla. Of Eppuleia, daughter of Aulus, wife.
EDCS-05800671.summary: This inscription appears to be a complex genealogical record or property marker, listing several individuals likely related to property ownership.

EDCS-05800672.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Valerius Chryseros made this for his dearest wife Cornelia Epiteuxi, well-deserving, along with his children Valerius Fortis and Valeria Blaste, and for himself, his family, freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. The plot was granted through the generosity of Quintus Pompeius Falconis.
EDCS-05800672.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication of a tomb by Caius Valerius Chryseros for his wife Cornelia Epiteuxi, their children, and his household, with the land granted by Quintus Pompeius Falconis.

EDCS-05800674.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Euhemerus made this for his deserving wife Tryphosa.
EDCS-05800674.summary: A funerary dedication by Euhemerus to his wife Tryphosa.

EDCS-05800675.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Eutactus, the freedman, his deserving [slave], by Aulus Curtius Arruntianus.
EDCS-05800675.summary: A funerary dedication by Aulus Curtius Arruntianus for his freedman Eutactus.

EDCS-05800676.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sextus Onussanius Nepotianus, son of Sextus, made this for his deserving wife Fabia Anthusa.
EDCS-05800676.summary: A funerary dedication by Sextus Onussanius Nepotianus for his wife Fabia Anthusa.

EDCS-05800679.translation: Aulus Folius Felix for himself and for his wife Manlia Optata.
EDCS-05800679.summary: A funerary dedication made by Aulus Folius Felix for himself and his wife Manlia Optata.

EDCS-05800680.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Aulus Fourios, son of Publius, possibly a tombstone or milestone.

EDCS-05800682.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Caius Fourios, son of Marcus, possibly a tombstone or milestone.

EDCS-05800684.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Marcus Fourios, son of Caius, possibly a tombstone or milestone.

EDCS-05800685.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Publius Fourios, son of Caius, possibly a tombstone or milestone.

EDCS-05800686.summary: An inscription recording the name and parentage of Quintus Fourios, son of Aulus, possibly a tombstone or milestone.

EDCS-05800688.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Quintus Furius Turpilianus.
EDCS-05800688.summary: A funerary dedication to Quintus Furius Turpilianus.

EDCS-05800689.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Gellius Maximus [erected this] for Phoebus, his most excellent freedman, who is buried here. Phoebus, formerly the greatest part of Gellius, possesses all affections; this stone barely completed the seven quinquennia of his life-course. Nor did kisses hold his ardent soul. And if the threads of the Fates could be changed, Maximus would rejoice to be buried in this tomb.
EDCS-05800689.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Phoebus, erected by his patron Marcus Gellius Maximus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800690.translation: To the departed spirits. Hateria [erected this] for her most dutiful son Archestratus, who lived 7 years and 2 months.
EDCS-05800690.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Archestratus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800691.translation: To Donatus, freedman of Hirtilius Caius, and Prima, freedwoman of Valeria, and Primus, freedman of Valerius, and Vinuleius Nero, [and] Valerius.
EDCS-05800691.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly indicating a shared tomb or memorial, with complex relationships indicated by 'freedman' and 'freedwoman', dating likely to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800692.translation: To the departed spirits. For Horatia Communis, his most beloved fellow-soldier (contubernalis), who lived 35 years. For Tiberius Claudius Gratus Petronianus, his son, who lived 15 years. Tiberius Claudius Rhodocles [erected this] for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. Two jugera of land must yield to Tiberius Claudius Terminalis, his son, who lived 27 years.
EDCS-05800692.summary: This is a complex funerary monument, likely a family tomb, established by Tiberius Claudius Rhodocles for his wife, sons, and descendants, including provisions for land use, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800696.translation: To Gaius Julius Eros, for Ammia, nurse of Myrsinus, and for Arescusa, [nurse] of Iulia Helpis.
EDCS-05800696.summary: This inscription records a dedication, possibly funerary or votive, to nurses for Gaius Julius Eros and Iulia Helpis, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800698.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Offimus [erected this] for Sabina, his well-deserving wife, [who lived...].
EDCS-05800698.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sabina, erected by her husband Iulius Offimus, indicating she lived for an unspecified number of years, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800699.translation: For [her] most dutiful [grandmother], Iulia Dextriana, her granddaughter, erected [this] for [her] well-deserving [grandmother].
EDCS-05800699.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a grandmother, erected by her granddaughter Iulia Dextriana, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800703.translation: For [her] most dutiful [grandmother], who lived 51 years and 2 months, Lucius Maius Salutaris, [aged] 51, erected [this] for [her] well-deserving [grandmother].
EDCS-05800703.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a grandmother, erected by her grandson Lucius Maius Salutaris, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800704.translation: To the departed spirits. For Manlia Felicula, freedwoman of Manlia, who lived 32 years. Titus Manlius Cosmus and Onesimus, her fellow freedmen, erected [this] for her, a well-deserving woman.
EDCS-05800704.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Manlia Felicula, erected by her fellow freedmen, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800705.translation: Moschus, the steward, erected [this] for Margarita, his fellow slave.
EDCS-05800705.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a fellow slave named Margarita, erected by Moschus, the steward, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800707.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Nice lived 20 years and 19 days. Likewise Macaria lived 18 years and 16 days. Likewise Ideae, their mother, lived 49 years, 7 months, and 15 days. Niger made this for his sons and his deserving wife.
EDCS-05800707.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages of death for Nice, Macaria, and Ideae, and indicating Niger as the dedicator for his sons and wife, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800710.translation: To Pantagathus, freedman of Augustus Peculiaris. Herma and Phyllis made this for their fellow freedman.
EDCS-05800710.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Herma and Phyllis to their fellow freedman Pantagathus, a freedman of Augustus, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800712.translation: Pompeius O [made this] from the tribute.
EDCS-05800712.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning Pompeius and a contribution or tribute, possibly related to a public building or a military context, date uncertain.

EDCS-05800715.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Quinta, who lived 5 years, 6 months, and 20 days. Stephanis, her mother, [made this] for her deserving daughter.
EDCS-05800715.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Quinta and identifying her mother, Stephanis, as the dedicator, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800719.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Rutilius Peto. Rutilia Elpis made this for her deserving patron.
EDCS-05800719.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Rutilia Elpis to her patron Rutilius Peto, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800724.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Sacred to Spenius, who lived 27 years and 1 month and 5 days. [He/She] made this for [his/her] deserving spouse.
EDCS-05800724.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Spenius and indicating the dedicator made it for a spouse, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800727.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Terentia Sophe made this for [her] mother. Terentia Eutychis, her daughter.
EDCS-05800727.summary: A funerary epitaph in honor of Terentia Sophe, dedicated by her daughter Terentia Eutychis, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800729.summary: A simple funerary epitaph or name inscription for Gaius Turpileius, son of Caius, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800730.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Tyche, [slave/freedwoman] of Messalina. For Vilicus.
EDCS-05800730.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tyche, a slave or freedwoman of Messalina, and possibly also for Vilicus, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800734.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Verrius Fronto. For his most beloved father, Verrius Marcianus, and for his most beloved sister, Veria Viola, who lived 17 years, 9 months. [His] father lived 91 years, 3 months. [He] made this.
EDCS-05800734.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Verrius Fronto to his father Verrius Marcianus and sister Veria Viola, recording their ages at death, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05800736.translation: To Titus Vinicius Corinthus, his best and dearest freedman, from his patron.
EDCS-05800736.summary: This is an epitaph dedicated by a patron to his beloved freedman, Titus Vinicius Corinthus.

EDCS-05800737.translation: Quintus Vitellius Agathopus, freedman of a woman, made this for himself and for Vitellia Blastae, freedwoman of Quintus, and for Evaristus, freedman of Quintus Vitellius Agathopus.
EDCS-05800737.summary: This funerary inscription records an individual, Quintus Vitellius Agathopus, who made provisions for himself and other freedpersons.

EDCS-05800754.translation: Hortulus is here; it is the work of Alcinoüs.
EDCS-05800754.summary: This is a funerary marker identifying the owner of a garden plot as Hortulus and attributing its creation to Alcinoüs.

EDCS-05800759.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Her partner Charis, who deserved well, made this.
EDCS-05800759.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Charis, described as a deserving partner ('contubernalis'), with the monument erected by her companion.

EDCS-05800761.translation: To Claudius Eutychion and Claudia Thiagenus.
EDCS-05800761.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Claudius Eutychion and Claudia Thiagenus.

EDCS-05800763.translation: Lucusta, freedwoman, made this for himself (his own family) and his own people, for Gaius Flavoleius Philargyrus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-05800763.summary: This funerary inscription by a freedwoman, Lucusta, commemorates her freedman husband, Gaius Flavoleius Philargyrus, and their family.

EDCS-05800766.translation: Parents made this for Sempronius, their son who deserved well, who lived for VII years.
EDCS-05800766.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from parents to their son Sempronius, who died at the age of seven.

EDCS-05800772.translation: Verus Lucius Caecilius, the agent, erected the altar.
EDCS-05800772.summary: This inscription records an altar erected by an agent named Verus Lucius Caecilius.

EDCS-05800779.translation: To Hadrian Augustus, consul for the third time, father of the fatherland; to Sabina Augusta; publicly, at the direction of the decurions, from the benefactors of the municipality.
EDCS-05800779.summary: This public monument honors Emperor Hadrian and Empress Sabina, funded by municipal officials and benefactors.

EDCS-05800782.translation: To Lucius Antistius, son of Gaius, the veteran, pontiff of the Roman people, Xvir for judging legal cases, quaestor of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, erected by the decurions and the people, the citizens of Gabii, under the prefecture of Sextus Marcius Teris and Gaius Varius Canacis.
EDCS-05800782.summary: This inscription records the honors bestowed by the citizens of Gabii upon Lucius Antistius, a prominent figure with military, religious, and administrative roles, during a specific prefecture.
