EDCS-05800784.translation: To Agusiae Priscilla, daughter of Titus, priestess of Hope and August Health, the town councillors of Gabii decreed that a statue be publicly erected in her honor because, after expenses were incurred in emulation of illustrious women, she promised to repair the portico of Hope, damaged by age, with her own money, on account of her priesthood, and to provide for the people with an exceptional public spectacle of games held for the health of Antoninus Pius Augustus, father of the country, and his children, and by donating religious vestments, she satisfied everyone; content with the honor of her statue, she remitted the expense to the people. The site was granted by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-05800784.summary: This inscription from Gabii records the public erection of a statue for Priscilla, a priestess of Hope and Health, who also funded repairs to a portico and provided public games, for which she was honored by the town councillors.

EDCS-05800785.translation: Publius Clodius Helix and Lucius Atilius Thamyrus, Augustal prefects, erected this base and repaired the statue at their own expense, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-05800785.summary: This inscription records that Publius Clodius Helix and Lucius Atilius Thamyrus, as Augustal prefects, erected a base and repaired a statue at their own expense in Gabii.

EDCS-05800786.translation: To Titus Flavius Aelianus, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, the council and people of Gabii [honored him] as their most faithful patron and curator of public affairs.
EDCS-05800786.summary: This inscription honors Titus Flavius Aelianus as a patron and curator of public affairs by the council and people of Gabii.

EDCS-05800787.translation: Flavia Variane, daughter of Titus, [erected this] on account of the merits of her father Crescentis, freedman of the Augusti, who faithfully discharged all the honors bestowed upon him by our municipality; the town councillors and the people [did this].
EDCS-05800787.summary: This inscription from Gabii honors Flavia Variane, daughter of Titus, and commemorates the distinguished public service of her father Crescentis, a freedman of the emperors, by the town councillors and people.

EDCS-05800788.translation: To Octavia Stratonices, daughter of Caius, [erected by] Flavia Variane, her mother.
EDCS-05800788.summary: This is a simple dedication from Gabii by Flavia Variane to her mother, Octavia Stratonices.

EDCS-05800791.translation: Lucius Pinnius Nedymus, Augustal prefect, and Lucius Pinnius Porphyrio, quaestor, [erected this] (with the participation of Lucius Pinnius [---]).
EDCS-05800791.summary: This inscription from Gabii records the erection of a monument by Lucius Pinnius Nedymus, an Augustal prefect, and Lucius Pinnius Porphyrio, a quaestor.

EDCS-05800805.translation: Your servant, Felix, a man of consular rank, offered this in gratitude for your continuous kindnesses.
EDCS-05800805.summary: This inscription records an offering by Felix, a former ordinary consul, to his patrons or superiors, likely in Rome.

EDCS-05800806.translation: Valerius Romulus, a most distinguished boy, for love and affection to his most benevolent father, Marcus Valerius Maxentius, a man of consular rank, lord and father.
EDCS-05800806.summary: This is a dedication from Valerius Romulus to his father, Marcus Valerius Maxentius, a former ordinary consul.

EDCS-05800807.translation: Valerius Romulus, a most distinguished boy, for love and affection to his dearest mother, Valeria Maximilla, a most noble lady.
EDCS-05800807.summary: This is a dedication from Valerius Romulus to his mother, Valeria Maximilla, a noblewoman.

EDCS-05800808.translation: To Corellia Galla Papiana, daughter of Caius, wife of Caius Corellius, son of Numerius, of the Fabian tribe, who by her will ordered that 100,000 sesterces be given annually to the colony of Menturnae on her birthday, March 6th, for the distribution of pastries and mulsum, and she ordered that 100,000 sesterces be distributed.
EDCS-05800808.summary: This inscription records the testamentary bequest of Corellia Galla Papiana, who left 100,000 sesterces to the colony of Menturnae and 100,000 sesterces to the municipality of Casinum for annual distributions on her birthday.

EDCS-05800809.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Hail to you, Caius Iulius Beronicianus, most sweet, who left sorrow to your guardians; he lived 5 years, 6 months, 15 days. Gnaeus Pompeius Ianuarius and Pompeia made this for a well-deserving person.
EDCS-05800809.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Beronicianus, set up by Gnaeus Pompeius Ianuarius and Pompeia.

EDCS-05800810.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Octavia Aphrodisia, most sweet daughter, who lived 26 years, 4 months. Octavia Pyrriche, mother, made this.
EDCS-05800810.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia Aphrodisia, set up by her mother Octavia Pyrriche.

EDCS-05800812.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Gaius Seius, son of Marcus, Quirina. For Calpurnius Quadratus Sittianus, proconsul of the province Narbonensis, praetor peregrinus, tribune of the plebs, quaestor of the province Africa, IIIvir capitalis, whose body was cremated here.
EDCS-05800812.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnius Quadratus Sittianus, listing his extensive career, and noting his cremation.

EDCS-05800825.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly dedicating something to Augusta, with the name Festa mentioned.

EDCS-05800828.translation: To Aesculapius. By word and deed, Isochrysus.
EDCS-05800828.summary: This is a dedication to the god Aesculapius made by Isochrysus.

EDCS-05800830.translation: Lucius Antistius Vetus, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, augur, to Fortuna Primigenia, from a vow undertaken.
EDCS-05800830.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Antistius Vetus, an augur, to Fortuna Primigenia.

EDCS-05800832.translation: [---] to Fortuna / [---] Primigenia / [---] Marcus Aurelius / [---] Hammonius / [---] the Roman knight / [---]uconiu[---]
EDCS-05800832.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Fortuna Primigenia and a Roman knight, Marcus Aurelius Hammonius.

EDCS-05800834.translation: To Fortuna Primigenia, Tiberius Claudius Thermodon and Mettia Lochias, his wife, daughter of Marcus, gave as a gift two statues of hope.
EDCS-05800834.summary: This is a dedication of two statues to Fortuna Primigenia by Tiberius Claudius Thermodon and his wife Mettia Lochias.

EDCS-05800835.translation: For the safety of Caesar Augustus Germanicus and his return, Quintus Considius Tertius gave as a gift a treasury to Fortuna Primigenia Praenestina at his own expense.
EDCS-05800835.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Considius Tertius for the safety and return of Emperor Gaius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, dedicated to Fortuna Primigenia Praenestina.

EDCS-05800836.translation: Lucius Decumius, son of Marcus, gave a gift to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800836.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Decumius, son of Marcus, to Fortuna Primigenia.

EDCS-05800837.translation: Dedicated on the eighth day before the Ides of August, during the consulship of Emperor Commodus for the second time and Martius Verus for the second time. To Pietas and Fortuna Primigenia, their vows having been undertaken, with the Emperors safe, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Commodus, Fortunatus, a household slave and their steward, and Aurelis Restituta, a freedwoman, gave this gift. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800837.summary: This is a dedication from 177 AD to Fortuna Primigenia and Pietas by imperial freedpersons, with the site granted by local council decree.

EDCS-05800838.translation: Quintus Lollius Apollophanes, father and son, and Aulia Archelais gladly fulfilled their vow to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800838.summary: This records the fulfillment of a vow to Fortuna Primigenia by Quintus Lollius Apollophanes and Aulia Archelais.

EDCS-05800840.translation: Quintus Mecilius C[---] gave [a statue?] to Fortuna Primigenia [---].
EDCS-05800840.summary: This incomplete inscription records a dedication by Quintus Mecilius to Fortuna Primigenia.

EDCS-05800841.translation: Nigrinia Auxesis, with Felix, freedman of the Emperor, and her family, gave and dedicated this statue of justice to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800841.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue of justice to Fortuna Primigenia by Nigrinia Auxesis and Felix, an imperial freedman.

EDCS-05800843.translation: Nothus, son of Ruficana and Plotilla, gave this gift to Fortuna, child of Jupiter, to Primigenia, having been chosen by lot.
EDCS-05800843.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Primigenia by Nothus, who was chosen by lot.

EDCS-05800844.translation: Orcevia, wife of Numerius, gave this gift to Fortuna Diova, daughter of Primogenia, for the sake of her nation.
EDCS-05800844.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna Primigenia by Orcevia, wife of Numerius.

EDCS-05800845.translation: Decimus Poblicius Comicus, the contractor of the shrine for thirteen years, and his daughter Poblicia Quinta and wife Fresidia Palmyris gave gifts to the cellarii Amoenus, Dionysius, and Linus, for Fortuna Primigenia, according to their vow.
EDCS-05800845.summary: This inscription records gifts made to shrine personnel and possibly Fortuna Primigenia by the shrine's contractor, his daughter, and wife.

EDCS-05800849.translation: Publius Annius Herma, heir of Trebonia Sympherusa, [gave this gift] to Fortuna, child of Jupiter, according to the will. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800849.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna, child of Jupiter, by the heir of Trebonia Sympherusa, with the site granted by local council decree.

EDCS-05800850.translation: Decimus Valerius Orop[---], a viator of a tribune [---], [gave ---] to Fortuna Prim[igenia ---] six pounds of silver.
EDCS-05800850.summary: This incomplete inscription records a dedication of six pounds of silver to Fortuna Primigenia by Decimus Valerius Orop[---].

EDCS-05800851.translation: Valeria Tryphosa fulfilled her vow to Fortuna Primigenia. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800851.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Fortuna Primigenia by Valeria Tryphosa, with the site granted by local council decree.

EDCS-05800853.translation: To Fortuna Primigenia, for the health and safety...
EDCS-05800853.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia for health and safety.

EDCS-05800855.summary: A short dedication to the goddess Fortuna Elisioris.

EDCS-05800856.translation: The masters and attendants of the Cisiarii Praenestei gave this gift to Fortuna Primigenia, and had it arranged by Tosenianus, freedman of Lucius, Licinus, Marcus Pompeius, attendant Nicephorus, slave of Caius Talabaras, Nicephorus.
EDCS-05800856.summary: This inscription records a gift to Fortuna Primigenia by the officials (magistri) and attendants (ministri) of the Cisiarii Praenestei, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800858.translation: The artisans gave a gift to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800858.summary: This inscription records a gift given to Fortuna Primigenia by a group of artisans (fabri).

EDCS-05800859.translation: The masters and attendants gave it; it was arranged by Lucius Ligurius, freedman of Lucius; Antiochus; Publius Dindius, freedman of Publius; Davus Calidus; Quintus Petronius, freedman of Quintus; Salvius; Sextus Pontius, freedman of Sextus; Stabilio.
EDCS-05800859.summary: This inscription lists the names of officials (magistri) and attendants who arranged a gift, likely to a deity given the context of other inscriptions.

EDCS-05800860.translation: The masters of the association of cattle merchants arranged it; Lucius Muucius, son of Publius; Caius Vatronius, freedman of Caius; gave a gift to Fortuna Primigenia willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05800860.summary: This inscription records a gift to Fortuna Primigenia made by the masters of the association of cattle merchants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800861.translation: ... masters arranged it; Alexander, slave of Plautius Lucius Marci; ... nus Cordius, slave of Aulus; gave a gift to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800861.summary: This inscription records a gift to Fortuna Primigenia given by officials (magistri) and slaves, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800862.translation: ... of the Valerii // of the eborares(?) gave a gift to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-05800862.summary: This damaged inscription records a gift to Fortuna Primigenia by individuals or a group identified as 'Valer[ ' and possibly 'eborari', likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800864.translation: ... masters arranged it; ... ius, freedman of Caius; Lucius Anicius, freedman of Lucius; ... ei, a slave, gave a gift to Fortuna Primogenea.
EDCS-05800864.summary: This inscription records a gift to Fortuna Primogenea by officials (magistri), freedmen, and a slave, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05800865.translation: ... Aulus Orbius, freedman of Aulus, Eros // ... Publius Lisius, freedman of Publius // ... Philomelus // ... sti, freedman of Caius, Ara[.
EDCS-05800865.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists several individuals, identified by name and patron/status, possibly in connection with a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-05800867.translation: To Fortun[a] Primigen[ia]. L. Arlenus, elected [---].
EDCS-05800867.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia, honoring L. Arlenus.

EDCS-05800868.translation: Lucius Domitius Agathemer, freedman of Paris, moneyer of the Caesars, collector, and Lucius Domitius Epictetus and Curtia Euphrantis gave this gift to Fortuna Primigenia. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800868.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Fortuna Primigenia by Lucius Domitius Epictetus and Curtia Euphrantis, honoring Lucius Domitius Agathemer, who held several civic and financial roles.

EDCS-05800869.translation: To Fortuna Primigenia. Gaius Placuleius Iullianus, son of Gaius Placuleius, and Ampliatus, his uncle, gave this gift as vascularii (makers/sellers of vessels).
EDCS-05800869.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna Primigenia by Gaius Placuleius Iullianus and his uncle Ampliatus, who were vascularii.

EDCS-05800871.translation: To the Genius of the municipality. Gaius Talonius Cypaerus, the father, and Gaius Talonius Cypaerus, the son, gave this gift.
EDCS-05800871.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the Genius of the municipality by a father and son, both named Gaius Talonius Cypaerus.

EDCS-05800872.translation: Gaius Tampius, son of Caius, grandson of Servus, from Tarentum, praetor, willingly gave this gift to Hercules as deserved.
EDCS-05800872.summary: This is a votive offering to Hercules by Gaius Tampius, a praetor from Tarentum.

EDCS-05800873.translation: Quintus Kaeso Cestios, son of Quintus, will give a gift to Hercules.
EDCS-05800873.summary: This inscription records a vow or promise of a gift to Hercules by Quintus Kaeso Cestios.

EDCS-05800874.translation: Lucius Gemenios, son of Lucius, grandson of Peltuinus, from Tarentum, gives this gift to Hercules willingly and as deserved, for his own safety and because the same laws permit an altar to Salutus.
EDCS-05800874.summary: This inscription is a votive offering to Hercules by Lucius Gemenios, also noting the legality of altars to Salutus.

EDCS-05800876.translation: To the great god Silvanus, to Mars, to Hercules, to Zabas. Antullus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05800876.summary: This is a dedication by Antullus to multiple deities, including Silvanus, Mars, Hercules, and Zabas.

EDCS-05800879.translation: A statue of Minerva [---]. To Augustus? Quintus Caecilius Eulogus, praetor?, and the attendants?
EDCS-05800879.summary: This inscription appears to record a dedication of a statue of Minerva, possibly to Augustus, by Quintus Caecilius Eulogus and his attendants.

EDCS-05800884.translation: To Turpenus Pater. Gaius Vatronius and Lucius Orcevius, praetors.
EDCS-05800884.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Turpenus Pater by Gaius Vatronius and Lucius Orcevius, identified as praetors.

EDCS-05800885.translation: To Venus the Fortunate Mother, R. Vibia Secunda and Lucius [dedicated this].
EDCS-05800885.summary: This is a dedication to the goddesses Venus Fortunae Genitrix by Vibia Secunda and Lucius.

EDCS-05800886.translation: Ofillia, daughter of Aulus Secundus, and Bruttia, daughter of Caius Sabinus, gave this gift to Mother Magna.
EDCS-05800886.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Magna Mater by Ofillia and Bruttia, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05800888.translation: Caius Magulnius, son of Caius Scato Maxsimus, and Caius Saufeius, son of Caius Flaccus, as praetors consecrated [this]. Caius Saufeius, son of Caius Flaccus, and Caius Magulnius, son of Caius Scato Maxsimus, consecrated [this].
EDCS-05800888.summary: This inscription records the consecration of a sacred object by two praetors, Caius Magulnius and Caius Saufeius, likely during the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05800889.summary: This is a brief inscription indicating something is sacred, dedicated by Titus Masclius Quintus.

EDCS-05800890.translation: From his own small shrine, Lucius Ianuarius.
EDCS-05800890.summary: This records Lucius Ianuarius dedicating something from his personal shrine.

EDCS-05800891.translation: To Diana Augusta, Fiovia A. [dedicated this].
EDCS-05800891.summary: This is a dedication to Diana Augusta by Fiovia A.

EDCS-05800896.translation: To our Lord Claudius Julianus, victorious and triumphant ever-August, the council and the people [dedicated this].
EDCS-05800896.summary: This is a dedication by the local council and people to the Emperor Claudius Julianus, likely during the reign of Claudius.

EDCS-05800899.translation: The council and the people of the city of Praeneste decreed that this should be erected to Bassus Aniclius Auchienius Bassus, a most distinguished man, proconsul and overseer of the province of Campania, restorer of the Anicii family, because of his outstanding merits.
EDCS-05800899.summary: This inscription records the decision by the city of Praeneste to erect a monument to Bassus Aniclius Auchienius Bassus, a former proconsul, in recognition of his service.

EDCS-05800902.summary: This is a dating phrase indicating a specific consulship of Caesar.

EDCS-05800903.translation: To Flavia Rufina, daughter of Marcus Barbus Fastus, consular governor and patron of the colony, an excellent and deserving native of Praeneste, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800903.summary: This inscription records a posthumous honor decreed by the decurions of Praeneste for Flavia Rufina, daughter of a consular patron of the colony.

EDCS-05800907.translation: To Gaius Julius Cornutus Tertullus, son of Publius, of the Horatia tribe, consul, proconsul of the province of Asia, proconsul of the province of Narbonensis, legate with the rank of praetor of the divine Trajan Parthicus in the province of Pontus and Bithynia, his legate with the rank of praetor in the province of Aquitania, curator for the collection of taxes, curator of the Via Aemilia, prefect of the treasury of Saturn, legate with the rank of praetor of the province of Crete and Cyrene, enrolled among the praetorians by the deified Vespasian and Titus, censors, aedile of the Ceriales, urban quaestor, by his will, Gaius Julius Plancius Varus Cornutus.
EDCS-05800907.summary: This inscription is a dedication of a statue to Gaius Julius Cornutus Tertullus, detailing his extensive career through various high-ranking imperial offices, likely erected by his heir, Gaius Julius Plancius Varus Cornutus.

EDCS-05800908.translation: To Gaius Julius Cornutus Tertullus, for the administration of the provinces of Pontus and Aquitania, Crete and Cyrene, by his will, Gaius Julius Plautus Varus.
EDCS-05800908.summary: This inscription records a bequest by Gaius Julius Plautus Varus to Gaius Julius Cornutus Tertullus, concerning the administration of several provinces.

EDCS-05800912.translation: Gaius Lutatius Cerco, son of Cnaeus, quaestor.
EDCS-05800912.summary: This is a short dedication naming Gaius Lutatius Cerco, son of Cnaeus, and stating his office as quaestor, likely on a monument associated with his public service.

EDCS-05800915.translation: Paean, freedman of the Emperor, procurator of the military treasury, procurator of inheritances, procurator of pleasures, procurator of Alexandria, for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-05800915.summary: This inscription lists the procuratorial offices held by Paean, a freedman of the emperor, for himself and his descendants.

EDCS-05800917.translation: To Postumius Iulianus, of most illustrious memory, a man of most illustrious standing, on account of the merit, love, and devotion which he showed to all citizens, and because, remembering our honor in his will, he left to us, all citizens, the farm called Fulgerita in the territory of Praeneste, which he loved with great affection, and for whom, being most worthy of consideration for the same reasons, we have resolved with a ready spirit to erect a statue, and because of his excessive civic love, it was decreed that the Praenestine citizens, about to celebrate a feast in his honor for more than a year, would erect a statue in the forum bearing his name and inscribe this copy of his will there, and they would not have the power to alienate it, so that if they ever wished to alienate it, the treasury would possess it. Died the 16th day before the Kalends of December, under our lord Arcadius Augustus and Bautonius, most illustrious men, consuls. Dedicated on the 4th day before the Nones of March, under the consuls written above.
EDCS-05800917.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue and the commemoration of a will by the citizens of Praeneste in honor of Postumius Iulianus, detailing his benefaction of a farm and instructions for his perpetual remembrance and the alienation of the property.

EDCS-05800919.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Septimianus, a man of high status, with a lacuna in the name and other details.

EDCS-05800922.translation: To Marcus Venidius Victor, his most beloved brother, son of Marcus Venidius Rogatianus, an outstanding man, from the ducenarii. Marcus Venidius Rogatianus, Roman knight.
EDCS-05800922.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Venidius Victor to his beloved brother, Marcus Venidius Rogatianus, who was a Roman knight and a 'ducenarius' (official with a salary of 200,000 sesterces).

EDCS-05800923.translation: Voluntilius Macer, son of Caius, lictor, member of the XVviri sacris faciundis, scribe of the curule aedileship. Voluntilia Prisca, his wife. [...] this place for burial was granted publicly [...] for himself and his family in the field [...]
EDCS-05800923.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Voluntilius Macer, detailing his priestly and administrative offices, and for his wife Voluntilia Prisca, recording a publicly granted burial plot.

EDCS-05800938.translation: To Titus Flavius Germanus, his nephew, son of Lucius Mantennius Severus, son of Lucius Mantennius Sabinus, tribune of the IIIrd Praetorian cohort, and Flavia Procilla, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-05800938.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Titus Flavius Germanus to his nephew, honoring his father Lucius Mantennius Severus, a tribune in the Praetorian Guard, and his mother Flavia Procilla.

EDCS-05800942.translation: To Telegenia Nobili, his most dutiful mother, and to Marcus Bettius Constantius, his father. Bettius Efficax, evocatus of the Emperor, made this.
EDCS-05800942.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Bettius Efficax, an evocatus of the Emperor, to his mother Telegenia Nobili and his father Marcus Bettius Constantius.

EDCS-05800944.translation: To Attius, son of Gnaeus, of the Tromentina tribe, a Viennese citizen, formerly prefect of the guild of craftsmen twice, by his will, L(ucius) L(onginus) built this. 60 years old.
EDCS-05800944.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument for Attius, identifying his tribal affiliation, place of origin, and former military/civic roles, and noting that his tomb was built by L. Longinus according to his will.

EDCS-05800945.translation: Rufus, legate of the Deiotarian legion.
EDCS-05800945.summary: This is a military inscription identifying Rufus as a legate serving in the Deiotarian legion.

EDCS-05800950.translation: Sabinus, quaestor, three times duovir, his Rufus, his aedile, Valerius, quaestor.
EDCS-05800950.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing civic officials including a quaestor, duovir, and aedile, possibly related to a magistracy or public building.

EDCS-05800951.translation: Marcus Decumius, son of Caius; Caius Paccius, son of Caius; Caius Albinius; Sextus Capivas; Lucius Ferlidius; Caius Ninn; Sextus Po; Caius M(arci) C(ai) f(ilius).
EDCS-05800951.summary: This inscription lists a series of Roman personal names, likely indicating individuals involved in a public commission or a collegium.

EDCS-05800952.translation: Quaestors... Celer, son of Spurius... aediles.
EDCS-05800952.summary: This inscription fragment lists officials, specifically mentioning quaestors and aediles, likely related to the administration of a city or a collegium.

EDCS-05800958.translation: Marcus Anicius, son of Lucius Baaso, and Marcus Mersieius, son of Cai, aediles, gave [money] for making the treasury.
EDCS-05800958.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Anicius Baaso and Marcus Mersieius, serving as aediles, funded the construction of a treasury.

EDCS-05800963.translation: Caius Caesius, son of Marcus, and Caius Flavius, son of Lucius, duoviri quinquennales, supervised the construction of the temple and portico according to the decision of the decurions and approved them.
EDCS-05800963.summary: This inscription records that two quinquennial duoviri, Caius Caesius and Caius Flavius, oversaw and approved the construction of a temple and portico, based on a decision by the decurions.

EDCS-05800964.translation: To Venandi studioso, to Tiberius Claudius Nicostratus, a six-time Augustalis quinquennial for life, by the collegium of the craftsmen of Praeneste. Anneia Procilla, his wife, and his sons Claudius Nicephorianus Proculus and Anneianus.
EDCS-05800964.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a collegium of craftsmen to Tiberius Claudius Nicostratus, a prominent member, and his family.

EDCS-05800965.translation: To Sex(tus?) Decimius... magistrates... Marcus Raecius... Lucius Volumnius... Lucius Annius, freedman of Lucius (plural)... Marcus Alfius, freedman of Lucius... ...IIvir(i?)... ...ministers?... Anthus, son of Mussetus... ...potus, son of Marcus... ...ius of Brittia... ...Domitius.
EDCS-05800965.summary: This is a fragmented inscription listing several names, possibly including magistrates, freedmen, and other individuals associated with a collegium or public office.

EDCS-05800967.translation: Caius Flavius, son of Cai, made the construction... wrote... 30,000 sesterces. The duoviri approved.
EDCS-05800967.summary: This inscription records that Caius Flavius funded a construction project costing 30,000 sesterces, which was subsequently approved by the duoviri.

EDCS-05800969.translation: Gaius, son of Lucius Geminius, commissioned the making of a four-horse chariot.
EDCS-05800969.summary: This dedication records Gaius Geminius commissioning a four-horse chariot, likely for public use or a religious ceremony.

EDCS-05800971.translation: Marcus Iunius Maior, son of Marcus, chief mime and attendant of Apollo, erected this; Postumia Cydilla, freedwoman of a woman, also contributed.
EDCS-05800971.summary: This epitaph records the erection of a monument by Marcus Iunius Maior, a performer, and Postumia Cydilla, likely a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-05800973.translation: Gaius Scato, son of Caius Magulnius, quaestor, saw to the restoration of the railings and guard posts by decree of the senate.
EDCS-05800973.summary: This inscription details the restoration of railings and guard posts by the quaestor Gaius Scato, ordered by a senatorial decree.

EDCS-05800975.translation: To Lucius Nivellius Priscus, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, an augur chosen from among the decurions. Lucius Nivellius Epigenes and Cornelia Ianuaria dedicated this to their most dutiful son. A place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800975.summary: This funerary inscription records the honoring of Lucius Nivellius Priscus, an augur, by his parents, with a plot granted by local authorities.

EDCS-05800980.translation: To Publicia Simili, daughter of Lucius, priestess of the Mother Mactuta. Marcus Aemilius Ulpianus, son of Marcus, dedicated this to his most holy wife. A place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800980.summary: This funerary inscription honors Publicia Simili, a priestess, by her husband Marcus Aemilius Ulpianus, with a plot granted by local authorities.

EDCS-05800982.translation: Gaius Sattius Feidenatius, son of Caius, and the praetors restored this.
EDCS-05800982.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Gaius Sattius Feidenatius and other praetors, likely a public work.

EDCS-05800983.translation: Gaius Saufeius, son of Caius, and Marcus Saufeius, son of Lucius, Pontanes, aediles, by decree of the senate.
EDCS-05800983.summary: This inscription records an action taken by the aediles Gaius Saufeius and Marcus Saufeius Pontanes, as ordered by the senate.

EDCS-05800984.translation: Lucius Saufeius Flacus, son of Caius, quaestor, saw to the paving of the road by decree of the senate.
EDCS-05800984.summary: This inscription details the paving of a road by the quaestor Lucius Saufeius Flacus, following a senatorial decision.

EDCS-05800985.translation: Marcus Saufeius Rutilus, son of Marcus, and Gaius Saufeius Flacus, son of Caius, quaestors, saw to the construction of a kitchen by decree of the senate and also bought a public place for them from Lucius Tondeius, son of Lucius; it is 148.5 feet long and 16 feet wide from the wall to Lucius Tondeius's boundary.
EDCS-05800985.summary: This inscription records the quaestors Marcus Saufeius Rutilus and Gaius Saufeius Flacus commissioning a kitchen and purchasing land for it, with specifications of its dimensions.

EDCS-05800987.translation: To Gaius Septimius Severus, son of Caius, of the Pupinia tribe, patron of the municipality. Titus Sentidius Iulianus, son of Titus, of the Palatina tribe, [dedicated this] to his excellent friend.
EDCS-05800987.summary: This dedication honors Gaius Septimius Severus, patron of the municipality, by his friend Titus Sentidius Iulianus.

EDCS-05800993.translation: Marcus Varenus Tyrannus, freedman of Clarus, [paid for] half of the amphitheater on public land.
EDCS-05800993.summary: This inscription records a private donation for the construction of an amphitheater, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800994.translation: To Decimus Velius Trophimus, Augustal sevir, curator of the public munus, by decree of the decurions, with the people's petition, under the supervision of Victorinus and Aprilis, the two magistrates.
EDCS-05800994.summary: This is a dedication to Decimus Velius Trophimus, a prominent freedman, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800995.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of an individual, possibly Quintus Vettius Pulcher, with incomplete details about his status or deeds.

EDCS-05800997.translation: Quintus Vibuleius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Statius, son of Salvius, the two magistrates, saw to the repair of the baths and the leading of water through public land, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05800997.summary: This inscription records a public works project concerning the repair of baths and water supply, undertaken by two magistrates, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05800999.translation: To Lucius Urvineius Philomusus, freedman of Lucius, master of the college of freedmen, a place for burial and a statue in the forum were publicly granted because he bequeathed free use of the baths for three years and ten pairs of gladiators, and a golden crown weighing one pound to Fortuna Primigenia, and ordered the same games to be held for five days at a cost of 40,000 sesterces; Philippus, his freedman, made the monument at his own expense.
EDCS-05800999.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE, detailing a generous bequest for public games and amenities by a freedman.

EDCS-05801016.translation: Quintus Cacurius [---], measurer of buildings, for Cornelia Ver[---]. Quintus Cacurius [---] Rogatus, [paid] 20,000 sesterces. Cacuria, freedwoman of Sar[---], [---]
EDCS-05801016.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely related to building measurement and a financial transaction, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801017.translation: For the family and freedmen of Quintus Marcius Aeschinus, freedman of Quintus, Primus, the steward, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-05801017.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the 1st or 2nd century CE, recording a tomb built by a steward for the family and freedmen of his patron.

EDCS-05801018.translation: [---]etorius, son of Publius, [---]us, the money-changer, [---]ia, freedwoman of Caius, Flor[---], [---]ius, freedman of Caius, [---], [---]a, freedwoman of Publius, Apoll[---]
EDCS-05801018.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription that appears to list several individuals, including a money-changer and freedmen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801038.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or ownership mark, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801042.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or ownership mark, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801048.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Aptronios, son of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801073.summary: This inscription records the name Spurius Cassios, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801081.summary: This inscription records the name Cincia, daughter of Caius, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801084.summary: This inscription records the name Minor Colionia Artorius the Elder, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801088.summary: This inscription is a farewell to the mother of Publius Cordius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-05801105.summary: This inscription records the name of Aulus Eppoleius, son of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801126.summary: This inscription records the name Geminia, daughter of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801140.summary: This inscription records the name Luscia, wife of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801146.translation: Quintus Magulnius, son of Lucius, grandson of Lucius.
EDCS-05801146.summary: This inscription records the name of Quintus Magulnius, son and grandson of Lucius, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801149.summary: This inscription records the name Trebius Mamios, son of Maius, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-05801159.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Novieia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-05801160.translation: Lucius Numitorius Ruber, son of Lucius, grandson of Lucius.
EDCS-05801160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Numitorius Ruber, specifying his filiation and agnomen.

EDCS-05801170.translation: Lucius Oppius Flaccus, son of Lucius, the father.
EDCS-05801170.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Oppius Flaccus, son of Lucius, noting his role as a father.

EDCS-05801171.translation: Lucius Oppius Flaccus, son of Lucius, the son.
EDCS-05801171.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Oppius Flaccus, son of Lucius, noting his relationship as a son.

EDCS-05801195.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Caius Plautius, son of Caius.

EDCS-05801207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Trebius Pupius, noting he was a freedman of Marcius.

EDCS-05801219.translation: Lucius Samiarius Dorsuo, son of Marcius.
EDCS-05801219.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Samiarius Dorsuo, son of Marcius.

EDCS-05801220.translation: Samiaria Minor, daughter of Marcius, wife of Quintus.
EDCS-05801220.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Samiaria Minor, daughter of Marcius, and her husband Quintus.

EDCS-05801298.translation: Caius Agreius Stepanus, freedman of Caius; Samiaria Dionysia, freedwoman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-05801298.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Caius Agreius Stepanus and Samiaria Dionysia, identifying their patrons and freed status.

EDCS-05801299.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records names and filiations of individuals named Agreius.

EDCS-05801301.translation: To Urion, freedman of Caius; to Alexander; Annia Phile, freedwoman of Tiberius; to Annia, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-05801301.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring several freedmen and women, likely members of the same household or close associates, with the names indicating their patronyms.

EDCS-05801302.summary: This is a brief inscription that records the names of two individuals, Gaius Antonius Florus and Marcia, possibly a couple or relatives, likely on a tomb or other monument.

EDCS-05801308.summary: This inscription simply names Aurunceia Restituta, likely a woman commemorated on a tombstone, with her name suggesting she was of Italian origin and possibly restored to health or good fortune.

EDCS-05801314.translation: Euclesis, freedwoman of Cestia, greetings, farewell.
EDCS-05801314.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Euclesis, a freedwoman of Cestia, containing a standard salutatory and valedictory message common in funerary contexts.

EDCS-05801322.translation: Publius Flavius, freedman of Publius; Flavia, freedwoman of Publius; Publius Flavius, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-05801322.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, all freedmen and women of Publius Flavius, likely marking a family tomb or a shared burial plot.

EDCS-05801332.translation: To Hyano, freedman; to Euphemo, freedman.
EDCS-05801332.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument or burial space to two freedmen, Hyano and Euphemo, possibly related or associated.

EDCS-05801333.translation: To Julia Alce, from Gaius Julius Modestus, for his most excellent mother.
EDCS-05801333.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Gaius Julius Modestus to his mother, Julia Alce, honoring her with the epithet 'most excellent'.

EDCS-05801336.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Luculanus as a freedman of Lucius, typically found on a tombstone to commemorate the deceased.

EDCS-05801342.translation: Gaius Messienus Trophimus; Gaius Messienus Romanus, freedman of Gaius, also his son; Gaius Messienus Licinus, freedman of Gaius; Messiena Secunda, freedwoman of Gaius, wife of Romanus.
EDCS-05801342.summary: This inscription records several members of the Messienus family, including freedmen and their descendants, likely marking a family tomb and indicating complex kinship and manumission relationships.

EDCS-05801343.translation: Lucius Minucius Metrodorus, son of Lucius; Minucia Surilla, freedwoman of Lucius; Cornelia Syntyche.
EDCS-05801343.summary: This inscription names three individuals associated with the Minucius family, including a son, a freedwoman, and Cornelia Syntyche, likely commemorating them on a tomb.

EDCS-05801349.translation: To Corucanius, from Petilia, freedwoman of Lucius, Pe[...]
EDCS-05801349.summary: This inscription, with extensive damage, likely records a dedication or funerary monument to a person named Corucanius, with Petilia as a dedicator or beneficiary.

EDCS-05801351.translation: Plotina, freedwoman of Lucius, Compse; Lucius Plotinus, freedman of Lucius, Iacchus; Plotina, freedwoman of Lucius, Rufa; Lucius Plotinus, freedman of Lucius, Alaucus.
EDCS-05801351.summary: This inscription lists four individuals: Plotina Compse, Lucius Plotinus Iacchus, Plotina Rufa, and Lucius Plotinus Alaucus, likely family members or freedpersons of a Lucius Plotinus.

EDCS-05801354.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication to Pontius Gordianus.

EDCS-05801356.translation: To Popilia, his worthy wife, and to their descendants.
EDCS-05801356.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb or plot to Popilia, a wife, and her descendants.

EDCS-05801358.translation: To Ieria, daughter of Marcus, Sabina Teren[...]; a burial plot for Sabina.
EDCS-05801358.summary: This inscription indicates a burial plot designated for Sabina, possibly identifying her parents or patrons.

EDCS-05801359.translation: Lucius Salvius Antigonus; Cornificia Selenium, freedwoman of Lucius; Lucius Cornificius Aptus; Oppia Urbana, freedwoman of a woman; Billiena Tertia, freedwoman of a woman; Cosentanus Hilarus; Cornificia Daphne; V() S() A() Hilarus.
EDCS-05801359.summary: This is a list of names, possibly associated with a collegium, a shared funerary monument, or a legal transaction, with several individuals identified as freedpersons.

EDCS-05801360.summary: This is a dedication to a wife named Saturia, likely part of a larger funerary or devotional inscription.

EDCS-05801361.translation: To [my] sister; [she] ordered [it to be made]; Serg(ius?) Ruf(us?) made [it].
EDCS-05801361.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the commissioning and making of a monument by Serg(ius?) Ruf(us?) for his sister.

EDCS-05801363.translation: Gaius Statioleius, son of Lucius, [born into the Menenia tribe]; Statioleia Urbana, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife; Lucius Tattius, freedman of Lucius, Epinicus; Tattia Dionysia, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-05801363.summary: This inscription records members of the Statioleius and Tattius families, including freedpersons, likely on a funerary monument or public record.

EDCS-05801368.translation: Marcus Tullius Chilo, son of Marcus; Trebia, daughter of Marcus, his wife; [belonging] to the sons of Marcus Tullius Protius, son of Marcus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-05801368.summary: This inscription records Marcus Tullius Chilo, his wife Trebia, and their children, likely on a funerary monument and indicating family lineage.

EDCS-05801371.translation: Tiberius Varinius Dioplutus, son of Tiberius. Marcia Chrysario, freedwoman of Titus, wife. Aufidia Tyrannis, freedwoman of Gnaeus, wife. Titus Cassius Antiochus, freedman of Titus, son of Caius.
EDCS-05801371.summary: This inscription lists names and familial relationships, likely for a funerary monument.

EDCS-05801372.translation: [...] by will [...] Varronius, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe [...] and Caius Varronius?
EDCS-05801372.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that appears to be related to a will or inheritance, mentioning a Varronius.

EDCS-05801381.translation: Usonia, daughter of Manius, by her will, 100,000 sesterces.
EDCS-05801381.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 100,000 sesterces by Usonia according to her will.

EDCS-05801388.translation: [...]cilia Var [...] for herself; this monument will not follow the heir.
EDCS-05801388.summary: This funerary inscription states that the monument is for the deceased and will not pass to an heir.

EDCS-05801393.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records a name and patronymic.

EDCS-05801395.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05801399.translation: Brittoni or Placido, buried on the 9th day, during the consulship of Arcadio II and Rufinus. Vitalis made [this].
EDCS-05801399.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Brittoni or Placido and names the consuls and the person who made the monument.

EDCS-05801400.translation: Primenius, who lived 16 years, buried on the 18th day before the Kalends of December, during the consulship of the most distinguished Theodorus.
EDCS-05801400.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death and burial date of Primenius, mentioning his consul.

EDCS-05801404.summary: This is a severely damaged inscription, possibly containing names or dates.

EDCS-05801409.translation: [...] Eurodia, buried here on the 12th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-05801409.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Eurodia and her date of death.

EDCS-05801417.translation: Pannius departed on the third day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-05801417.summary: This is a personal note recording the departure of a person named Pannius on a specific date.

EDCS-05801418.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the peaceful rest of a person named Iea.

EDCS-05801421.translation: By command of the lady, sacred offering from Vibius Pumidius Rusticus and Vipsania Tertia.
EDCS-05801421.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering made by Vibius Pumidius Rusticus and Vipsania Tertia, likely dedicated to a female deity.

EDCS-05801429.translation: The order decreed a statue for Lucius Afilanus Provincialis, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, honored with public equestrian rank and designated as Lupercus; Lucius Afilanus Verecundus, having used the honor, remitted the expense; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05801429.summary: This is a decree from the town council (ordo decurionum) granting a statue to Lucius Afilanus Provincialis and recording the financial arrangements made by Lucius Afilanus Verecundus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801430.translation: Valeria Quinta, daughter of Marcus, and her husband Valeria Sympherusa made this for their most dutiful father, Marcus Valerius Admetus, courier of the praetors and consuls, and Augustalis sevir.
EDCS-05801430.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Valeria Quinta and Valeria Sympherusa to Marcus Valerius Admetus, who served as a courier and an Augustalis sevir, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801434.translation: Of the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Optimus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, conqueror of the Parthians.
EDCS-05801434.summary: This is an inscription fragment, likely part of a larger dedication, commemorating Emperor Trajan's titles and victories, probably from his reign (98-117 CE).

EDCS-05801436.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augustus, conqueror of Sarmatia, great conqueror of Germany, pacifier of the world, fortunate, unconquered, Roman, chief pontiff, with tribunician power for the 18th time, Imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 7th time, father of the fatherland, surpassing in all virtues, the town council of Commodiana, through C. Papius Capito and L. Volcius Maximus.
EDCS-05801436.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Commodiana to Emperor Commodus, listing his numerous titles and honors, likely from the period of his reign (177-192 CE).

EDCS-05801438.translation: Aulus Titius, son of Lucius, and Marcus Vergilius, son of Marcus, censors, by decree of the senate. // Marcus Vergilius, son of Marcus, and Aulus Titius, son of Lucius, censors.
EDCS-05801438.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of a census appointment, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period, possibly recording the appointment of censors twice or a correction.

EDCS-05801440.translation: Gaius Suestidius, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, Frege [---]; his sister Pola Suestidia [---] sep[ulcher].
EDCS-05801440.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription that names Gaius Suestidius and his sister Pola Suestidia, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-05801443.summary: This is a simple dedication, likely for a funerary monument, by Lucius Dominoserus Verna.

EDCS-05801448.translation: Livia Nicarus and Livius Nymphodotus, her sons, made this for their most sacred father Marcus Livius Hermes.
EDCS-05801448.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by sons for their father, Marcus Livius Hermes, likely in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801462.translation: To the departed spirits. Arruntia Petale, daughter of Lucius, lived 40 years. Lucius Rupilius Diadumenus, her husband, and Rupilia Blanda, daughter of Lucius, and Lucius Rupilius Secundus, son of Lucius, [dedicated this] to the most devoted [Arruntia Petale].
EDCS-05801462.summary: This epitaph commemorates Arruntia Petale, detailing her age and the family members who erected the monument, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801465.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hosidius Lascivus [dedicated this] to his wife Nia Valeria, with whom he lived for 3 years and 20 days. The wife... [text is incomplete]
EDCS-05801465.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Nia Valeria and the duration of her marriage to Hosidius Lascivus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801466.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Carinatius Papias made this for Lucianus.
EDCS-05801466.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Carinatius Papias for Lucianus, probably from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801467.translation: To the departed spirits. Manlia, daughter of Rhodinus, lived 16 years. Caius Veratius Rhodon, her most unhappy father, [dedicated this].
EDCS-05801467.summary: This epitaph records the death of Manlia, daughter of Rhodinus, and is dedicated by her grieving father, Caius Veratius Rhodon, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801468.translation: Munatia, daughter of Statius. Caius Munatius, freedman of the woman, Pamphilus, in the field, 18 feet.
EDCS-05801468.summary: This inscription seems to mark a burial plot boundary or dedication related to Munatia and Pamphilus, possibly dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801469.translation: Gaius Pirrius [says]: if you say anything as you pass by, whether good or bad, [this belongs to] Pirria, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-05801469.summary: This is a warning inscription, likely related to a tomb or property, set up by Pirria, a freedwoman, concerning any utterances made by passersby, probably from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801472.summary: This is a simple dedication or marker made by Marcus Fulvius Euemerus, possibly for a tomb or a building, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801478.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Cominius Priscus [dedicated this] to his deserving wife Egnatia Ianuaria.
EDCS-05801478.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Caius Cominius Priscus to his wife Egnatia Ianuaria, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801479.translation: To the departed spirits. To Manlia Maximina, daughter of Publius, who lived 6 years, 10 months, and 18 days. Publius Manlius Staphylus and Herennia Marcellina, daughter of Gaius, her most unhappy parents, [dedicated this] to their most devoted daughter and to Caius Herennius Daphnus and to themselves.
EDCS-05801479.summary: This epitaph commemorates Manlia Maximina, detailing her age at death and dedicated by her parents, who also included themselves and Caius Herennius Daphnus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801480.translation: To Titienia Musa, daughter of Sextus, for herself, her husband Muttius Syneros, and their descendants.
EDCS-05801480.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titienia Musa by her husband and likely a relative, establishing a family burial plot.

EDCS-05801504.translation: To Lucius Baebius Balbus, son of Lucius, of the Sergia tribe, military tribune of the Eighth Legion, also military tribune.
EDCS-05801504.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Baebius Balbus, who held military offices including tribune.

EDCS-05801505.translation: To the Divine Shades of Marcus Messi, son of Marcus, of the Galeria tribe; to Rusticus, Aemilius Afra, Cuti Romuli Priscani, Arri Proculi, a decemvir for judging lawsuits. Aemilius Papus and Cutia Prisca, his most unhappy parents, (dedicated this) to their most excellent son.
EDCS-05801505.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Messi, dedicated by his parents who were also prominent citizens, mentioning his judicial office.

EDCS-05801506.translation: To Annius Tineius Tarrutenius Atticus, a man of most distinguished memory, praetor, guardian, and member of the board of fifteen priests for sacred rites, who lived 28 years. Maxima Cai, a woman, erected this memorial from the ground to her most devoted husband, with whom she lived 9 years, 7 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05801506.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annius Tineius Tarrutenius Atticus, who died young, erected by his wife who notes their shared life span and his public offices.

EDCS-05801507.translation: Legate of the Eleventh Claudian Legion, member of the Sodales Titii, decemvir for judging lawsuits, urban quaestor, who lived 10 years.
EDCS-05801507.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription commemorating an individual who held military and public offices and died at the age of 10, likely a child prodigy.

EDCS-05801508.translation: Titus Anniolenus, son of Marcus, (and) Olia, daughter of Anie.
EDCS-05801508.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the names of two individuals, possibly a couple or family members.

EDCS-05801509.translation: Titus Cornelius Phileros, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-05801509.summary: This is a simple dedication naming Titus Cornelius Phileros, identifying him as a freedman.

EDCS-05801510.translation: To Domitius Justus, son of Titus, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-05801510.summary: This is a dedication to Domitius Justus, son of Titus, indicating his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05801511.translation: Publius Forbeius Optatus, freedman of a woman, lived 1 year and 7 months.
EDCS-05801511.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Forbeius Optatus, a freedman who died in infancy.

EDCS-05801512.translation: Gaius Gellius Gellianus lived 24 years and 8 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-05801512.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Gellius Gellianus, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-05801513.translation: Marcus Iulius Celer, freedman of the freedman of Augustae.
EDCS-05801513.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Celer, identifying his manumission history.

EDCS-05801514.translation: In the field, 35 feet are taken up by the approach, enclosure, and burial-sacrifice of this tomb of Marcus Tullius Speratus, for the purpose of performing funeral rites.
EDCS-05801514.summary: This inscription defines the burial plot and rights for the tomb of Marcus Tullius Speratus.

EDCS-05801515.translation: Publius Veturius Phileros, freedman of Publius Veturius, [and] Publius Veturius Felix, freedman of Publius Veturius.
EDCS-05801515.summary: This funerary inscription records two individuals, both freedmen of Publius Veturius.

EDCS-05801517.translation: To the Manes of Parinius, most pious, on the Ides.
EDCS-05801517.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes of Parinius.

EDCS-05801520.translation: To the Manes of Marcus Aurelius Felicissimus. Saturnina made this.
EDCS-05801520.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Aurelius Felicissimus by Saturnina.

EDCS-05801521.translation: Publius Sabidius Dionysius made this. Publius Sabidius Dionysius made this.
EDCS-05801521.summary: This inscription appears to be a duplicated dedication, possibly for a religious offering or a building.

EDCS-05801522.translation: Sacred to the spirit (daimon). From a vow undertaken.
EDCS-05801522.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering made in fulfillment of a vow to a spirit (daimon).

EDCS-05801523.translation: Caius Iulius Iulianus Proculus, son of Spurius, priest, dedicated this gift to Attis Augustus and to the Great Idaean Mother of the gods, from the waters of Alba.
EDCS-05801523.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caius Iulius Iulianus Proculus, a priest, to Attis Augustus and the Mother of the Gods near the waters of Alba.

EDCS-05801525.translation: Sacred to Diana Caelestis. Quintus Cornelius Theophilus, together with Quinctia, daughter of Marcus Luperca.
EDCS-05801525.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Diana Caelestis by Quintus Cornelius Theophilus and Quinctia.

EDCS-05801526.translation: To Diana Opifera Nemorensi. Lucius Apuleius Antiochus, freedman of Lucius Apuleius.
EDCS-05801526.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Diana Opifera Nemorensi by Lucius Apuleius Antiochus.

EDCS-05801530.translation: To Hercules, Gaius Antestius, son of Cnaeus, censor, having completed his tenth year, dedicates again.
EDCS-05801530.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by a censor, possibly related to his office and a decennial review.

EDCS-05801531.translation: To Household Hercules, by Titius Aelius Ruber Superstes.
EDCS-05801531.summary: A private dedication to the household god Hercules, made by Titius Aelius Ruber Superstes.

EDCS-05801532.translation: Sacred to Hercules Saxanus. Servius Sulpicius Trophimus restored the temple, bedroom, and kitchen with his own money and dedicated it himself on the Kalends of December, during the consulship of Lucius Turpilius Dexter and Marcus Maecius Rufus. Eutychus, the slave, supervised the completion.
EDCS-05801532.summary: This is a dedication and rededication of a temple complex (including a bedroom and kitchen) to Hercules Saxanus by Servius Sulpicius Trophimus, with his slave overseeing the work, dated to the consulship of 131 CE.

EDCS-05801537.translation: Gaius Vibius Publilianus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, quaestorian scribe, prefect of the IV Thracum equitata cohort, twice military tribune of the IV Macedonica and XXI Rapax legions in Germania, having returned from there, dedicated this as a gift to Hercules Invictus.
EDCS-05801537.summary: This inscription records the military career of Gaius Vibius Publilianus and his dedication of a gift to Hercules Invictus upon his return from service in Germania.

EDCS-05801541.translation: To Hercules Tiburtinus and the station, Asinius Panaristus.
EDCS-05801541.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Tiburtinus and potentially a 'station' (perhaps a post or lodging), made by Asinius Panaristus.

EDCS-05801543.translation: To Hercules Tiburtinus Victor and the other local gods of Tibur. Lucius Minicius Natalis, consul, augur, imperial legate with proconsular authority of the province of Lower Moesia, made this fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05801543.summary: This is a vow fulfilled to Hercules Tiburtinus Victor and other local deities by Lucius Minicius Natalis, a high-ranking official who served as legate in Moesia, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801544.translation: To Jupiter the Protector. Hercules Victor dedicated (this). Blandus, the praetor, restored it.
EDCS-05801544.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter by Hercules Victor and a restoration by Blandus, a praetor.

EDCS-05801546.translation: Sacred to Jupiter the Guardian. Marcus Aemilius Flaccus, quaestor.
EDCS-05801546.summary: A sacred dedication to Jupiter Custos by Marcus Aemilius Flaccus, who held the office of quaestor.

EDCS-05801547.translation: Sacred to Neptune the Helper. Marcus Aemilius Flaccus, quaestor.
EDCS-05801547.summary: A sacred dedication to Neptune Adiutor by Marcus Aemilius Flaccus, who previously appears as a quaestor.

EDCS-05801549.translation: Optatus, the attendant, and Eumachus, the marble worker, erected the Lares at their own expense.
EDCS-05801549.summary: This inscription records the erection of household shrines to the Lares by two freedmen, an attendant and a marble worker, funded by themselves.

EDCS-05801551.translation: Philomus, slave of Eros Turranius, and Amphio Lateranius (?), the attendants, saw to it that the shrine of the Lares be repaired for Hercules.
EDCS-05801551.summary: This inscription records the repair of a shrine to the Lares and Hercules, carried out by slaves.

EDCS-05801553.translation: Caius Placentios, son of Herius, dedicated this sacred offering to Mars; Caius Placentios, son of Herius, gave this gift to Mars.
EDCS-05801553.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a sacred offering to the god Mars by Caius Placentios.

EDCS-05801556.translation: Amycus of Serona to the Unconquered Sun God Mithras. May it be well. To Sebesius.
EDCS-05801556.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mithras by Amycus of Serona.

EDCS-05801557.translation: Victorinus, an imperial freedman and steward, restored and dedicated this to the present divine power of the Unconquered Sun God Mithras, as he himself commanded in a vision, using his own funds; may it be well for all leaders.
EDCS-05801557.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of a shrine to Mithras by a Roman steward, Victorinus, in fulfillment of a divine vision.

EDCS-05801563.translation: While Lucius Gellius, son of Lucius, was in charge.
EDCS-05801563.summary: This phrase likely indicates the official responsible for a project or a public work.

EDCS-05801565.translation: For Livia, wife of Caesar Augustus, publicly.
EDCS-05801565.summary: This inscription likely records a public dedication or honor for Livia, the wife of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-05801573.translation: In our most blessed age of our lords Constantius and Constantinus, Augusti, the Senate and Roman People reduced the Tiburtine road to a level plain, under the supervision of Lucius Turcius Secundus Apronianus, son of Asterius, Corrector of Flaminia and Picenum.
EDCS-05801573.summary: This inscription records a public works project by the Senate and Roman People to level the Tiburtine road during the reigns of Constantius and Constantinus.

EDCS-05801575.translation: Lucius Cornelius, son of Cnaeus, acting as praetor, consulted the Senate on the third day before the Nones of May, under the temple of the Castors. Aulus Manlius, son of Aulus, Sextus Iulius, son of Sextus, and Lucius Postumius, son of Spurius, were present as scribes. You, Teiburtes, made your statement, and you purged yourselves of the matters about which you spoke. The Senate took your words into consideration, as was just. We had heard from you that these things had been reported to you, but we did not accept them as having happened, because we knew that you could not rightfully do them, nor were you worthy of doing them, nor would it be beneficial to you or to the Republic to do so. And after the Senate heard your words, we were all the more convinced, as we had previously thought, that no offense had been committed by you in these matters. Since you have been cleared before the Senate in these matters, we believe, and you ought to believe, that you will also be cleared before the Roman people.
EDCS-05801575.summary: This is a senatorial decree concerning a legal case, where Lucius Cornelius, as praetor, records the Senate's decision to absolve Teiburtes of certain charges after reviewing their statement and purge.

EDCS-05801576.translation: To Marcus Accennius, son of Lucius, Saturninus, proconsul of the province of Baetica, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor, from Atilia, daughter of Lucius, Balbilla, his most excellent wife.
EDCS-05801576.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Atilia Balbilla to her husband, Marcus Accennius Saturninus, who held various high offices.

EDCS-05801578.translation: Arrianus Aper Severus, consul (serving) 15 times in sacred rites, praetor peregrinus, tribune of the plebs, military tribune of the 15th Apollinaris Legion.
EDCS-05801578.summary: This inscription lists the career of Arrianus Aper Severus, detailing his military and religious offices, including multiple consulships in sacred rites.

EDCS-05801581.translation: Aulus Caelsius Gallus, as plebeian aedile, Ceres' priest, imperial priest, and patron of the colony, ordered this to be made by his will; Publius Curtius Severus, imperial priest, saw to its construction by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05801581.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work, ordered by Aulus Caelsius Gallus in his will and executed by Publius Curtius Severus by decree of the local council.

EDCS-05801583.translation: To Titus Clodius Pupienus Pulcher Maximus, a most distinguished man, consul, curator of sacred buildings and public works, curator of the republic of Beneventum elected by sacred judgment for receiving census returns throughout Belgica province, curator of the republic of Leptis Magna and Tripolis, for the management of public works, proconsul of Macedonia province, curator of the republic of Catania, urban praetor, candidate quaestor, member of the XVvirate for performing sacred rites, moneyer triumvir, the Senate and People of Tibur [dedicate this].
EDCS-05801583.summary: This is a lengthy dedication honoring Titus Clodius Pupienus Pulcher Maximus, listing his numerous prestigious political and administrative offices, likely for a public monument in Tibur.

EDCS-05801584.translation: Furius Maecius Gracchus, a most distinguished man, governor of Flaminia and Picenum, dedicated this decoration for the baths. Dedicated on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May in the year when Gallus and Flaccus were consuls.
EDCS-05801584.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a decoration for the baths by Furius Maecius Gracchus, governor of Flaminia and Picenum, during the consulship of Gallus and Flaccus.

EDCS-05801585.translation: To Titus Marcius, son of Titus, fetial priest, military tribune of the XIIII Gemina legion, quaestor, pro-praetor of Achaia province, secretary of the senate, curule aedile, candidate praetor, curator of the Via Latina, legate of the II Augusta legion. Grania Tertulla [dedicates this].
EDCS-05801585.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Titus Marcius, listing his distinguished career, by Grania Tertulla.

EDCS-05801586.translation: For Matuccia, daughter of Lucius, [in the year] when Marcus Pompeius Macrinus and Publius Iuventius Celsus were consuls.
EDCS-05801586.summary: This inscription records a dedication for Matuccia, daughter of Lucius, during the consulship of Marcus Pompeius Macrinus and Publius Iuventius Celsus.

EDCS-05801588.translation: Postumus Mimisius Sardus, son of Caius, military tribune, quaestor, plebeian aedile, praetor, legate of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, proconsul, prefect for distributing grain by decree of the senate.
EDCS-05801588.summary: This inscription details the career of Postumus Mimisius Sardus, highlighting his military and administrative posts, including his final role as prefect for grain distribution.

EDCS-05801591.translation: To Publius Mummius Sisennas Rutilianus, son of Publius, of the Galeria tribe, consul, augur, proconsul of Asia province, legate of Augustus as pro-praetor in Upper Moesia, prefect of the alimenta along the Via Aemilia, prefect of the Saturnian treasury, legate of the VI Victrix legion, praetor, plebeian tribune, quaestor, tribune of the V Macedonica legion, member of the XVvirate for judging lawsuits, patron of the municipality, curator of the temple of Hercules Victor. The Salii Herculanii Augustales [dedicated this]. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05801591.summary: This inscription honors Publius Mummius Sisennas Rutilianus, listing his extensive public career and patronage, and was dedicated by the Salii Herculanii Augustales, with the site granted by the local council.

EDCS-05801592.translation: In memory of Torquatus Novellus, son of Publius, of Atticus, member of the Xvirate for judging lawsuits, military tribune of the I legion, tribune of detachments of four legions (I, V, XX, XXI), quaestor, aedile, praetor, curator for the distribution of public lands, legate for receiving census returns and for conscription, and proconsul of Narbonensis province, who died in the Forum Julii at the age of forty-four years at the end of his term in office.
EDCS-05801592.summary: This is a memorial inscription for Torquatus Novellus, detailing his distinguished career in military and civil service, and noting his death at age 44.

EDCS-05801593.translation: To Marcus Pacceius, son of Lucius, quaestor, pro-praetor. The shipowners of Ostia [dedicate this].
EDCS-05801593.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Pacceius, a quaestor and pro-praetor, by the shipowners of Ostia.

EDCS-05801594.translation: To Gnaeus Pinarius Severus, son of Gnaeus, consul, augur, king of sacred rites, praetor, candidate quaestor of Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus. The Salii Collini [dedicate this]. Cornelia Manliana [dedicates this].
EDCS-05801594.summary: This inscription honors Gnaeus Pinarius Severus, listing his priestly and political offices, and was dedicated by the Salii Collini and Cornelia Manliana.

EDCS-05801597.translation: To Publius Plautius Pulcher Triumphalis, son of Pulcher, augur, imperial commissioner for minting gold, silver, and bronze, quaestor of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, five-time consul, tribune of the plebs, praetor, treasurer, companion of Drusus, son of Germanicus, uncle of Drusus, son of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, and by him selected by the censor into the patrician order, curator of road paving appointed by his neighbors with the authority of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, proconsul of the province of Sicily, and to Vibia Marsi, daughter of Marsi, born a Laelia Pulchri.
EDCS-05801597.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Publius Plautius Pulcher Triumphalis, detailing his extensive career in Roman public service, including various priesthoods, magistracies, and provincial governorships, likely from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-05801598.translation: To Tiberius Plautius Silvanus Aelianus, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, pontiff, member of the Augustales college, imperial commissioner for minting bronze, silver, and gold, quaestor of Tiberius Caesar, legionary legate of the Fifth Legion in Germania, urban praetor, legate and companion of Claudius Caesar in Britannia, consul, proconsul of Asia, legate with proconsular authority of Moesia, in which province he brought over a hundred thousand people from among the Transdanuvians with their wives, children, and chieftains or kings to pay tribute, and suppressed the eastward movement of the Sarmatians, even though he had sent a large part of his army on an expedition to Armenia; he brought kings of the Bastarnae and Rhoxolani, previously unknown or hostile to the Roman people, to worship Roman standards, and brought them to the bank that he protected; he returned sons of the Dacians, brothers (of the kings) captured or rescued from enemies; he accepted hostages from some of them, through whom he confirmed and extended the peace of the province; he also lifted the siege of the Scythian king from Chersonesus, which is beyond the Borysthenes, and was the first from that province to alleviate the grain supply of the Roman people with a large amount of wheat; the Senate, with the approval of the Emperor Caesar Augustus Vespasian, honored this legate, who had been sent back to Hispania to the prefecture of the city, with triumphal ornaments in the prefecture; according to his speech which is written below: He presided over Moesia in such a way that the honor of his triumphal ornaments should not have been delayed for him, except that a greater title befell him as prefect of the city; Emperor Caesar Augustus Vespasian made him consul again in the same prefecture of the city.
EDCS-05801598.summary: This is a laudatory inscription for Tiberius Plautius Silvanus Aelianus, detailing his military and administrative achievements as legate in Moesia, including managing large populations, suppressing barbarian movements, and securing peace, likely dating to the Flavian period.

EDCS-05801599.translation: To Quintus Pompeius Senecio Roscio Murena Coelius Sextus Iulius Frontinus Silianus Decianus, to Gaius Iulius Euryclus Herculaneus, to Lucius Vibullius Pius Augustanus Alpinius Bellicius Sollers, to Iulius Apro Ducenius Proculus Rutilianus Rufus, to Silio Valerio Nigro, to Clodius Fuscus Saxaeus Amyntianus, to Sosius Priscus, pontiff, member of the Hadrianalian college, member of the Antoninian Verian college, Salian of the Colline region, quaestor, candidate of the Augusti, legate with proconsular authority of Asia, praetor, consul, proconsul of Asia by lot, prefect of the grain supply, member of the board of monetary officials, member of the board of six officials, prefect of the Latin holidays, quinquennial patron, Salian, curator of the Temple of Hercules Victor, by the Senate and People of Tibur.
EDCS-05801599.summary: This is an honorific inscription from the city of Tibur, honoring a group of prominent individuals with various priesthoods and magistracies, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801604.translation: To Marcus Tineius Ovinius Castus Pulcher, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, a most distinguished man, chief pontiff, urban quaestor, senatorial praetor candidate, consul, by the Senate and People of Tibur, son of a patron, grandson of patrons.
EDCS-05801604.summary: This is an honorific inscription from Tibur honoring Marcus Tineius Ovinius Castus Pulcher, detailing his senatorial career and family connections, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05801605.translation: To Uttiedius Afro, son of Lucius, augur, consul-designate, by the people of Carthage, patron.
EDCS-05801605.summary: This is an honorific inscription from Carthage, recognizing Uttiedius Afro, an augur and consul-designate, as their patron, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801608.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Amulius, identified as a pontiff, likely a brief dedication on a public monument.

EDCS-05801612.translation: The equestrians dedicated and commissioned this, by Plautius, son of Titus, decurion.
EDCS-05801612.summary: This inscription records a dedication and commission by equestrian individuals, overseen by Plautius, a decurion, likely from a military context.

EDCS-05801613.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius Disza, an equestrian soldier of our Emperors, lived for 30 years and served for 12 years in the troop of Bassus, of Thracian origin. His heir Septimius Dines and the legatees took care to have this made for him as he deserved well.
EDCS-05801613.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Disza, a Thracian equestrian soldier who served for 12 years, erected by his heir and legatees, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05801619.translation: To Gaius Octavius Graecinus, son of Gaius, military tribune.
EDCS-05801619.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Octavius Graecinus, who held the military rank of tribune, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801620.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Octavius, who held the military rank of tribune, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801621.translation: Decimus Egnatius Rufus, heir, had this erected for Sex. Nio Seneca, soldier of the Praetorian fleet at Ravenna.
EDCS-05801621.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a relative for a soldier of the Praetorian fleet.

EDCS-05801622.translation: To the Divine Manes. Valerius Sudus, soldier of the I Italica legion in the province of Thrace, lived 35 years, 8 months, and 7 days. His brother, with 10 years of service, made this.
EDCS-05801622.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valerius Sudus, a soldier, set up by his brother.

EDCS-05801624.translation: Lucius Numitorius Terminalis Herculaneus Augustalis, priest of Isis, to his very best friend Valerius Super, soldier of the urban cohort and also optio.
EDCS-05801624.summary: This is a dedication from a priest of Isis to a friend who was a soldier and an optio.

EDCS-05801626.translation: Titus Aelius Euhodion, freedman of Augustus, accountant of the villa at Tibur, and Victoria made this for their most beloved son, a deserving recipient.
EDCS-05801626.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by parents for their son, who was an accountant for a villa at Tibur.

EDCS-05801627.translation: To the Divine Manes. Aelius Irenaeus, record-keeper of the villa at Tibur, to his friend and fellow freedman Aelius Probus, freedman of Augustus, a deserving recipient, made this.
EDCS-05801627.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a colleague to a fellow freedman of the imperial household who worked at a villa.

EDCS-05801630.translation: To the Divine Manes. Agele, his father Polydeuces, freedman of Augustus and a steward, made this for his child, who lived 7 years and 11 days.
EDCS-05801630.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child set up by his father, who was a steward and freedman of the emperor.

EDCS-05801631.translation: To the Divine Manes. Zosimianus, freedman of Augustus and a nomenclator in the census office, made this for his dearest wife Aurelia Primitiva while still alive, and for himself, his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-05801631.summary: This is a funerary monument established by a freedman of Augustus for his wife, himself, and his dependents, intended to remain within the family.

EDCS-05801633.translation: Hermes, freedman of Augustus and contractor for the bronze treasury, made this for his son who lived 18 years, and his daughter who lived 9 years, and their mother who lived 40 years and lived well with me.
EDCS-05801633.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Hermes, an imperial freedman involved in coinage, for his deceased wife and children.

EDCS-05801634.translation: To Quintus Hortensius Faustinus, son of Quintus, of the Collina tribe, advocate of the treasury, prefect of the builders, patron of the municipality. The college of builders of Tibur set this up because of his merits, in a place granted by senatorial decree. Under the curatorship of Marcus Helvius Exspectatus and Gaius Allianus of Tibur. Dedicated on the 13th day before the Ides of May, in the consulship of Maximus and Orfitus.
EDCS-05801634.summary: This is a public monument erected by the college of builders of Tibur to honor Quintus Hortensius Faustinus, an advocate and former prefect, with its dedication dated to May 2, 174 AD.

EDCS-05801637.translation: Tiberius Claudius Lysimachus, freedman of Augustus, a viator of the Augustan sodalities, made this for his dearest wife Valeria Donata, and for himself, his descendants, and his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-05801637.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Tiberius Claudius Lysimachus, a freedman of Augustus and member of the Augustan sodalities, for his wife, himself, and their dependents.

EDCS-05801639.translation: Decanus without children has three sons: Honorinus, Laurentius, and Iunianus, growing up. The Tiburtine decanus has one son growing up: Ianuarius, a circitor. Restus, a circitor, without children has four sons: Sabatius, who himself has two sons growing up, Restutus and Augurinus. Sarbaucinus, a circitor, brother of the aforementioned, without children. Muntanus, a circitor, brother of the aforementioned, without children. Lucianus, a circitor, without children. Victor, a circitor, without children. Ianuarius, another circitor, has three sons growing up: Iovinus and Martinus, and one daughter. The circitor has one son growing up: Mercurius, a circitor.
