Romanus, a circitor, has two sons growing up: Silvanio and Leopardus. Ursus, a circitor, has two daughters. Beneriosus, a circitor, without children. Ursus, another circitor, has three sons growing up: Leontius, and two daughters. Ianuarius, a circitor, without children. Repalius, a circitor, has four sons. The circitor has one son growing up: Successus. Exuperantius, decanus, without children. Surus, a circitor, without children. Constantius, a circitor, has one son: Pascaseus, a circitor. Maurus, a circitor, has two sons growing up: Peregrinus and Laurentius. The circitores, together with the decani, will be 3 decani. The circitores of the aforementioned type, 19 in number, 8 growing up, and 2 girls.
EDCS-05801639.summary: This inscription is a list detailing the family status and children of various decani (officials) and circitores (guards or messengers) within a Roman community, likely Tibur, noting their sons, daughters, and those growing up.

EDCS-05801640.translation: To Gaius Aemilius Antoninus, son of Gaius, of the Fabian tribe, a Roman knight, quinquennial official, patron of the municipality, who has honorably discharged all offices, curator of the temple of Hercules Victor, a pontifex.
EDCS-05801640.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Aemilius Antoninus, a prominent local official and knight from Tibur, for his service and for his role as curator of a temple.

EDCS-05801642.translation: Lucius Albius, freedman of Lucius, magistrate of the Herculanei and Augustales. Fultia, freedwoman of Marcus, Psychine. Lucius Albius, freedman of Lucius, magistrate of the Herculanei and Augustales.
EDCS-05801642.summary: This inscription records Lucius Albius, a freedman, serving as a magistrate for the collegia (associations) of Herculanei and Augustales in Tibur, and also mentions Fultia, another freedwoman.

EDCS-05801643.translation: Quintus Aprofenius, military tribune, II vir (a chief magistrate) with judicial power, aedile.
EDCS-05801643.summary: This is a brief inscription listing the public offices held by Quintus Aprofenius in Tibur, including military tribune and II vir iure dicundo.

EDCS-05801644.translation: To Gaius Bicleius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Camilian tribe, who has very well discharged all public offices with merit for the Republic of Tibur. The Senate and People of Tibur. Here he made the Republic of Tibur his heir.
EDCS-05801644.summary: This honorary inscription from Tibur honors Gaius Bicleius Priscus for his distinguished public service and records that he made the city his heir.

EDCS-05801645.translation: Gaius Caesilius, son of Gaius, and Gaius Heiulius, son of Titus, quaestors, have repaired the walls by decree of the senate.
EDCS-05801645.summary: This inscription records the repair of city walls by two quaestors, Gaius Caesilius and Gaius Heiulius, acting on a senatorial decree in Tibur.

EDCS-05801646.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Salvianus Herculaneus, Augustalis, appointed honorary duplicarius.
EDCS-05801646.summary: This dedication honors Tiberius Claudius Salvianus Herculaneus, an Augustalis, for being appointed as an honorary duplicarius (a higher rank or position, possibly in a collegium).

EDCS-05801647.translation: To Claudia Rufina, elected by Julia Heracla from the order into the decuria (of the?) Augustales of the Herculanei. The Senate and People of Tibur. Place granted by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-05801647.summary: This inscription records the honor granted to Claudia Rufina by Julia Heracla, likely an official, and is decreed by the Senate and People of Tibur, granting a place in a collegium.

EDCS-05801651.translation: To Iunia Tyrannis, beloved wife of Gaius Albius Thymelus, freedman of Livilla, Herculaneus Augustalis, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-05801651.summary: This epitaph commemorates Iunia Tyrannis, the wife of Gaius Albius Thymelus, a member of the Herculanei Augustales association in Tibur.

EDCS-05801652.translation: ...ustus, IIII vir (a chief magistrate) with judicial power, in need of repair due to age, with public funds to be restored.
EDCS-05801652.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to a public building or monument in Tibur that requires repair using public funds, and mentions a IIII vir iure dicundo.

EDCS-05801654.translation: Gaius Luttius Aulianus, son of Lucius, Quintus Plausurnius Varus, son of Caius, and Lucius Ventilius Bassus, son of Lucius, and Gaius Octavius Graechinus, son of Caius, as members of the board of four, supervised the construction of a portico 260 feet long, an exedra, a pronaos, and a portico behind the stage 140 feet long, as decreed by the Senate.
EDCS-05801654.summary: This inscription records the construction of public buildings by four magistrates, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05801656.translation: Lucius Nonius Pansa, son of Lucius Tullus, Tullius, son of Tullius, and Gaius Manius, son of Caius, and Lucius Magilius, son of Lucius, serving for the second time as members of the board of four, supervised the construction as decided by the Senate.
EDCS-05801656.summary: This inscription records the supervised construction of a public work by four magistrates, acting for the second time, based on a Senate decision.

EDCS-05801657.translation: Lucius Octavius Vitulus, son of Lucius, and Caius Rustius Flavus, serving for the second time as members of the board of four, supervised the paving of a road as decided by the Senate. Caius Rustius Flavus, serving for the second time, and Lucius Octavius Vitulus, members of the board of four, supervised the paving of a road as decided by the Senate.
EDCS-05801657.summary: This inscription records the supervision of a road paving project by four magistrates, each serving for the second time, by order of the Senate.

EDCS-05801658.translation: Lucius Octavius Vitulus, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, serving for the second time as a magistrate with judicial authority.
EDCS-05801658.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Octavius Vitulus, a magistrate, possibly on a public building or monument, in his second term.

EDCS-05801659.translation: Lucius Orbius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Anilius, son of Lucius, as members of the board of four, under the supervision of Nasica, presented a gift to Lucius Namartenuiai, as decided by the Senate.
EDCS-05801659.summary: This inscription records a gift presented by four magistrates to an individual, approved by the Senate, possibly related to a public ceremony or honor.

EDCS-05801661.translation: Quintus Quinctius, son of Quintus, serving for the third time as a member of the board of four, and quinquennial censor, an augur...
EDCS-05801661.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely honoring Quintus Quinctius, a magistrate and augur, noting his repeated terms in office.

EDCS-05801662.translation: To Titus Sabidius, prefect of a cohort, augur, salius, curator.
EDCS-05801662.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Sabidius, honoring his various public and religious offices.

EDCS-05801664.translation: To Titus Sabidius Phoebus, Augustalis curator, quaestor, my most excellent father.
EDCS-05801664.summary: This is a familial dedication to Titus Sabidius Phoebus, honoring his roles as curator, quaestor, and his paternal virtues.

EDCS-05801665.translation: Marcius Salluius Domitianus will receive water through the first three long holes, each one digit high and ten digits above the opening, and half the opening above the hinge of the water level. The remaining holes, each one digit long and ten digits high, will receive water from the first hour of the night until his hour. Lucius Primus Sosianus will receive water through holes each three and a half digits long and high, from the first hour until the tenth hour.
EDCS-05801665.summary: This inscription is a technical record detailing water distribution rights and capacities for different users, likely for an aqueduct or water system.

EDCS-05801666.translation: The hair weavers of Tibur, for Saufeia Alexandria, a Vestal Virgin, decreed in her lifetime that they would honor her virtue after her death; the Senate granted the location.
EDCS-05801666.summary: This inscription records a posthumous honor for Saufeia Alexandria, a Vestal Virgin, decreed by the Tiburtine hair weavers and approved by the Senate.

EDCS-05801667.translation: Marcus Scaudius, son of Caius, and Caius Munatius, son of Titus, served as aediles from the public treasury.
EDCS-05801667.summary: This inscription records Marcus Scaudius and Caius Munatius serving as aediles, likely in a public context.

EDCS-05801669.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Sextius Eutychus, freedman of Lateranus, and Sextia Graphe made this for their excellent and dutiful son Titus Sextius Magianus, who held the office of aedile, was Augustalis, and lived for 22 years, 4 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-05801669.summary: This funerary inscription records the creation of a monument by Titus Sextius Eutychus and Sextia Graphe for their deceased son, Titus Sextius Magianus, who held several civic and religious offices and specifies his age at death.

EDCS-05801670.translation: Publius Staedius Primus, freedman of Publius, served as magister Herculaneus and Augustalis, and Venuleia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus, [served as his wife?]; [for? Africani].
EDCS-05801670.summary: This inscription records the offices of Publius Staedius Primus (magister Herculaneus and Augustalis) and Venuleia Prima, likely in a religious or civic context related to the cult of Hercules.

EDCS-05801671.translation: Caius Terentius Valens, who held the office of aedile, served as prefect of the quinquennalis, prefect of the upper stream, and patron of the municipality.
EDCS-05801671.summary: This inscription lists the various public offices and honors held by Caius Terentius Valens, including aedile, prefect, and patron of the municipality.

EDCS-05801672.translation: [This monument is for] Threptus Maximus, freedman, governor, mime actor, parasite of Apollo, [and?] the excellent Daphne.
EDCS-05801672.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or epitaph for Threptus Maximus, who held multiple roles including freedman, governor, actor, and parasite of Apollo, and potentially also for Daphne.

EDCS-05801673.translation: Titus Trebulanus Nepos, son of Titus, and a Herculaneus Augustalis, [dedicated this]; Titus Trebulanus Nepos, freedman of Titus, Herculaneus Augustalis, and aedile of the Tiburtine youth; and his wife Publicia Saturnina.
EDCS-05801673.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Titus Trebulanus Nepos, his freedman and namesake who was an aedile of the youth, and his wife Publicia Saturnina, likely related to the cult of Hercules.

EDCS-05801674.translation: Tullus Tullius, son of Tullius, and Publius Sertorius, son of Publius, served as censors.
EDCS-05801674.summary: This inscription records Tullus Tullius and Publius Sertorius serving as censors, a high-ranking civic office.

EDCS-05801676.translation: Marcus Varenus Diphilus, freedman of the woman (i.e., mother) and Marcus Lartidus, served as magister Herculaneus and paid for this to be made at his own expense.
EDCS-05801676.summary: This inscription records Marcus Varenus Diphilus, a freedman, serving as magister Herculaneus and personally funding the construction of this monument.

EDCS-05801677.translation: Marcus Varenus Diphilus, freedman of the woman (i.e., mother) and Marcus Lartidus, served as magister Herculaneus and paid for this to be made at his own expense.
EDCS-05801677.summary: This inscription records Marcus Varenus Diphilus, a freedman, serving as magister Herculaneus and personally funding the construction of this monument.

EDCS-05801680.translation: To Ethenno Lito, Herculaneus Augustalis, and his deserving wife Lesbia.
EDCS-05801680.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Ethenno Lito, who held the religious office of Herculaneus Augustalis, and his wife Lesbia.

EDCS-05801681.translation: The Senate and People of Tibur [dedicated this]. While Marcus Antonius Florus and Gaius Vecilius Karo were duoviri, it was dedicated on the Kalends of March, with Gaius Bellicius Torquatus and Tiberius Claudius Atticus serving as consuls.
EDCS-05801681.summary: A public dedication by the Senate and People of Tibur, dated by the consuls and duoviri.

EDCS-05801686.translation: Take me, I am yours. Damocras, slave of Cotta, made this work.
EDCS-05801686.summary: A work commissioned by Damocras, a slave, for his patron Cotta.

EDCS-05801688.translation: To Titus Sabidius Victor and Decimus Rupilius Menander, scribes of the state.
EDCS-05801688.summary: An inscription honoring two state scribes, Titus Sabidius Victor and Decimus Rupilius Menander.

EDCS-05801691.summary: A work made by Lucius Luttius Victor.

EDCS-05801693.summary: A work made by Lucius Luttius Victor.

EDCS-05801698.summary: A work made by Titus Sabidius Helico.

EDCS-05801699.summary: A work made by Titus Sabidius Helico.

EDCS-05801700.summary: A work made by Titus Sabidius Helico.

EDCS-05801702.summary: A work made by Titus Sabidius Helico.

EDCS-05801704.summary: A work made by Titus Sabidius Helico.

EDCS-05801705.translation: Publius Sabidius Hermes made [it]; Publius Sabidius Hermes made [it].
EDCS-05801705.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating a monument was made by Publius Sabidius Hermes.

EDCS-05801708.translation: Soter, freedman of the woman Aufestia, a doctor, his front 20 feet, in his land 30 feet.
EDCS-05801708.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot owned by Soter, a freedman and doctor.

EDCS-05801709.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Chrysis made [this] for her most deserving husband, Marcus Nummius Proculus, a dealer in silk.
EDCS-05801709.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Valeria Chrysis for her husband, Marcus Nummius Proculus, a silk dealer.

EDCS-05801712.translation: Aulus Perperna Fronto, son of Spurius, scribe, for himself and his people; for the Divine Shades; for Mamidia Daphne, freedwoman of Lucius; for Publius Calpurnius Martialis, his deserving husband; for Perpernia Hilara, mother; for Perpernia, sister; for Quintus Aemilius Antiochus, freedman of Quintus; Aulus Perperna Crescens, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-05801712.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription detailing multiple individuals and relationships, likely for a family tomb.

EDCS-05801713.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Magnilla, who served as a logistician (a financial or supply officer).

EDCS-05801715.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Titus Aelius Geta, freedman of Augustus. His wife Aelia Lais and daughters Aelia Athenais and Hygia made [this] for their sweetest parent.
EDCS-05801715.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the wife and daughters for Titus Aelius Geta, a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-05801716.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Titus Aelius Ianuarius, freedman of Augustus. He lived 30 years, 3 months, and 13 days. Ucena Victoria, his dearest wife, with whom he lived 14 years.
EDCS-05801716.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Aelius Ianuarius, recording his age at death and the duration of his marriage.

EDCS-05801718.translation: For Titus Aelius Volusianus, freedman of Augustus. Iulia Auxesia, for him deserving, and Saturninus, a fellow freedman, and Ulpius, a freedman, his heirs, took care that the monument be made.
EDCS-05801718.summary: This inscription records that Iulia Auxesia, along with fellow freedmen Saturninus and Ulpius, arranged for the construction of a monument for Titus Aelius Volusianus.

EDCS-05801719.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucius Aelius Zenon. Aelia Fortunata, his deserving wife, made [this].
EDCS-05801719.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aelia Fortunata for her husband, Lucius Aelius Zenon.

EDCS-05801721.translation: Gaius Allienus, son of Gaius, and Aulia Rufa, daughter of Quintus, in front 16 feet, in the land 20 feet.
EDCS-05801721.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a land plot belonging to Gaius Allienus and Aulia Rufa.

EDCS-05801722.translation: Amphion lies here, snatched away in his first youth; he had not yet counted thirty years of age. Alas, untimely death hastened to you, Caius Marcius Paulus, for your most devoted son.
EDCS-05801722.summary: This epitaph laments the premature death of Amphion and identifies Caius Marcius Paulus as his devoted son.

EDCS-05801723.translation: Poppidia Callityche gave [this] to Annia Soterini.
EDCS-05801723.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Poppidia Callityche to Annia Soterini.

EDCS-05801724.summary: This is a dedication made by Antiochus to his daughter.

EDCS-05801726.translation: Caius Arrius Chrestus, freedman of Caius, erected [this] for his patron Caius Arrius Dasius, freedman of Caius, while he was alive, and for Alfedia Lucris, freedwoman of Lucius, his concubine.
EDCS-05801726.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Caius Arrius Chrestus for his deceased patron and his living concubine, Alfedia Lucris.

EDCS-05801728.translation: Eros, freedman of Titus and Caius Aurunculeius, lived for [X] years.
EDCS-05801728.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Eros, a freedman of Tituses and Caius Aurunculeius.

EDCS-05801732.translation: To the departed spirits: Sextus Peducaeus Dionysius made [this] for his most sacred wife, Baebia Delphis.
EDCS-05801732.summary: This funerary inscription records Sextus Peducaeus Dionysius dedicating a monument to his wife, Baebia Delphis.

EDCS-05801734.translation: To the departed spirits: Epitynchanus Boethus made [this] for his dearest brother.
EDCS-05801734.summary: This funerary inscription records Epitynchanus Boethus dedicating a monument to his brother.

EDCS-05801735.translation: To Aulus Caelius, son of Aulus, of the Palatine tribe, M[...].
EDCS-05801735.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription that begins with the name and tribal affiliation of Aulus Caelius.

EDCS-05801736.translation: Caesilia Eleutheris, freedwoman of Marcus / Marcus Caesilius, freedman of Decimus, [son of...] / Caesilia Pamphila, freedwoman of Decimus.
EDCS-05801736.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription listing three individuals, likely related, with their freed status and patronyms.

EDCS-05801738.translation: To the departed spirits: Claudius Hermes made [this] for his well-deserving friend, Caius Kannius Felix.
EDCS-05801738.summary: This funerary inscription records Claudius Hermes dedicating a monument to his friend, Caius Kannius Felix.

EDCS-05801739.translation: To Castor, my deserving husband, Lupilla made this.
EDCS-05801739.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a husband by his wife, Lupilla.

EDCS-05801740.translation: Cauponius Geminus, son of Lucius; Cauponia Gemina, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05801740.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, likely siblings, from the gens Cauponia.

EDCS-05801741.translation: To my deserving and most faithful wife for 32 years and 10 months.
EDCS-05801741.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a wife, mentioning her marriage duration.

EDCS-05801742.translation: Tiberius Claudius [did this?] for himself. N.
EDCS-05801742.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or ownership marker by Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-05801743.translation: For Tiberius Claudius Anoptus, freedman of Augustus, and for Iulia Pannychis, [his?] parents, [---]
EDCS-05801743.summary: This is a funerary dedication for parents, setting up a tomb or memorial for them.

EDCS-05801744.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Tiberius Claudius Chares [made this] for Aliae Nebridis, his deserving stepdaughter, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-05801744.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a stepdaughter, made by her stepfather.

EDCS-05801745.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Tiberius Claudius Charopinus lived 25 years. Polybius [his] father and Tiburtia Sphragis [his] mother.
EDCS-05801745.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Charopinus, with his parents named.

EDCS-05801746.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Faustinus, [from?] Claudia [his] patron.
EDCS-05801746.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Tiberius Claudius Faustinus by his patron, Claudia.

EDCS-05801748.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Claudia Lada, a freedwoman, likely by her patron Helpidius.

EDCS-05801750.translation: Cluentia Surisca, freedwoman of Titus; Titus Cluentius Bithus, freedman of Titus. In front 20 feet.
EDCS-05801750.summary: This inscription records the names and status of two freedpersons and specifies a boundary measurement.

EDCS-05801752.translation: Lucius Cornelius Blesamus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-05801752.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Cornelius Blesamus, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-05801753.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Cornelius Hilarius lived 6 years, 10 months. Cornelia Hilara, mother, made this.
EDCS-05801753.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Quintus Cornelius Hilarius, made by his mother.

EDCS-05801754.translation: To the Divine Shades. Servius Cornelius Silvanus lived 7 years, 4 days, 4 hours. Cornelia Nice, mother, for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-05801754.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Servius Cornelius Silvanus, made by his mother, Cornelia Nice.

EDCS-05801756.translation: Crescens, freedman of Faustonis, also a deputy, lived 3 years.
EDCS-05801756.summary: This funerary epitaph records the brief life of Crescens, identified as a freedman and deputy.

EDCS-05801757.translation: Aulus Crispinus Sextianus, son of Aulus, lived 11 months, 15 days.
EDCS-05801757.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Aulus Crispinus Sextianus.

EDCS-05801759.translation: for himself, his wife Eurosyne, and his descendants.
EDCS-05801759.summary: This is a funerary dedication intended for the dedicator, his wife, and descendants.

EDCS-05801760.translation: for himself, his wife Eutychia Liberalis, his children, his excellent parents, and his brothers and all our descendants.
EDCS-05801760.summary: This is a funerary dedication for the dedicator, his wife, children, parents, brothers, and descendants.

EDCS-05801762.translation: To Lucius Faenius Telesphorus, dearest husband. Claudia Ode, freedwoman of Augustus, made this for herself and her descendants.
EDCS-05801762.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by Claudia Ode to her husband Lucius Faenius Telesphorus, and for herself and descendants.

EDCS-05801765.translation: To the Divine Shades. Felicitas, mother, made this for her most dutiful son Felix. He lived 1 year, 8 months.
EDCS-05801765.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Felix, dedicated by his mother Felicitas.

EDCS-05801766.translation: To the Divine Shades. Nicon, for his brother Felix, made this. He lived 61 years, well-deserving.
EDCS-05801766.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Nicon, dedicated by his brother Felix.

EDCS-05801767.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Feridia Rufa, identifying her parentage.

EDCS-05801768.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flaccus, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Lucius Fuscus, (his) freedman, (lies here). 3 feet in front, 2 feet in the field.
EDCS-05801768.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial plot dimensions and names Flaccus, a freedman with a complex manumission history.

EDCS-05801769.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Tiburtius Felix made (this) for his deserving wife, Flavia Nice.
EDCS-05801769.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caius Tiburtius Felix dedicating a monument to his wife, Flavia Nice.

EDCS-05801770.translation: The bones of Sextus Frensidius, freedman of Sextus Arabio, (are) placed.
EDCS-05801770.summary: This inscription records the placement of the ashes of Sextus Frensidius, a freedman.

EDCS-05801771.translation: The bones of Sextus Frensidius [are] here, placed. He lived 14 years.
EDCS-05801771.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Sextus Frensidius, who died at the age of 14.

EDCS-05801772.translation: Son of Caius, freedman of Caius, Bithus.
EDCS-05801772.summary: This inscription identifies Bithus, son of Caius and freedman of Caius.

EDCS-05801773.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Prunicus and Fuficulena Tyche made (this) for their most dutiful daughter, Fuficulena Tyche, who lived 9 years and 8 days.
EDCS-05801773.summary: This funerary epitaph records Prunicus and Fuficulena Tyche dedicating a monument to their daughter, Fuficulena Tyche, noting her age at death.

EDCS-05801774.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. (Fulvia Polycronia) made (this) for her well-deserving parents, Fulvius Polychronius and Iulia Tertia.
EDCS-05801774.summary: This funerary epitaph records Fulvia Polycronia dedicating a monument to her parents, Fulvius Polychronius and Iulia Tertia.

EDCS-05801775.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. (Garcilia Onomaste) made (this) for her dearest husband, Flavius Hermetes.
EDCS-05801775.summary: This funerary epitaph records Garcilia Onomaste dedicating a monument to her husband, Flavius Hermetes.

EDCS-05801776.translation: Hedone, freedwoman of Quintus, made (this) for herself and for her son, Quintus, son of Quintus, of the Palatine tribe, and for Quintus Caecilius Phothus, for herself and for their descendants.
EDCS-05801776.summary: This funerary inscription records Hedone, a freedwoman, dedicating a monument for herself, her son, and Quintus Caecilius Phothus, and their descendants.

EDCS-05801777.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Helvidia Spenis lived for 35 years, 6 months, and 15 days. Quintinus made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-05801777.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Helvidia Spenis and was dedicated by her husband, Quintinus.

EDCS-05801780.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Hordiona, daughter of Quintus. Her most unhappy father made this.
EDCS-05801780.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Hordiona and was dedicated by her father.

EDCS-05801781.translation: Marcus Vetulius Ionius, freedman of Augustus, set this up for his most beloved, deserving wife.
EDCS-05801781.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication by Marcus Vetulius Ionius, a freedman of Augustus, for his wife.

EDCS-05801784.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Consummatus made this for his deserving wife, Volusia Chari, and also for himself.
EDCS-05801784.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication by Caius Iulius Consummatus for his wife, Volusia Chari, and for himself.

EDCS-05801785.translation: Caius Iulius Epaphra, freedman of Caius, and Iulia Lyde, daughter of Glycera, his wife.
EDCS-05801785.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph identifying Caius Iulius Epaphra and his wife, Iulia Lyde.

EDCS-05801786.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a name on a tomb, possibly belonging to Titus Iulius Hymnus.

EDCS-05801787.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Calliope made this for her deserving father, Iulius Philetus.
EDCS-05801787.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication by Iulia Calliope for her father, Iulius Philetus.

EDCS-05801788.translation: Tiberius Iulius Satyrio, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-05801788.summary: This inscription likely records the name and status of Tiberius Iulius Satyrio, a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-05801789.translation: Iulia Eutychia made this for her faithful fellow freedman Caius Iulius Martialis. Turellia Ianuaria made this for her deserving wife.
EDCS-05801789.summary: This inscription records two dedications: one by Iulia Eutychia for Caius Iulius Martialis, and another by Turellia Ianuaria for her wife.

EDCS-05801790.translation: Lucius Iunius, son of Lucius. To his dearest son. Teltediae.
EDCS-05801790.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary epitaph, possibly from an altar, mentioning Lucius Iunius and his son.

EDCS-05801791.translation: Iunia made [this monument] for Sextus Raecius Alexander, freedman of Marcus, and for Raecia Aina, freedwoman of Sextus.
EDCS-05801791.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument dedicated by Iunia for two freedpersons, Sextus Raecius Alexander and Raecia Aina.

EDCS-05801792.translation: Iunia Zosime made [this monument] for her daughter Iunia Martina, most sweet; she lived 28 years, 7 months, 18 days; [she was] placed with her father Euno.
EDCS-05801792.summary: This epitaph records the death of Iunia Martina, who lived 28 years, 7 months, and 18 days, and was placed with her father Euno; it was made by her mother Iunia Zosime.

EDCS-05801793.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Iunius Felix, his freedman, made [this monument] for the well-deserving Iunia Severa, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-05801793.summary: This epitaph, dedicated to the underworld spirits, records the death of Iunia Severa, who lived 16 years, and was made by her freedman Lucius Iunius Felix.

EDCS-05801794.translation: Aurelius Severus [made this monument] for Perpetua Securitas Iustia Nepotilla, his most chaste wife, well-deserving, and for Iustia Praesidia, [his] daughter.
EDCS-05801794.summary: This epitaph records a monument dedicated by Aurelius Severus for his wife Iustia Nepotilla and daughter Iustia Praesidia, praising their virtues.

EDCS-05801796.translation: Licinius Lausus and Ulpia Venula [made this monument] for their dearest son, Lucius Licinius, from the municipality of Saetabi in Hispania Citerior, who lived 22 years, is buried here.
EDCS-05801796.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Lucius Licinius, aged 22, from Saetabi in Hispania Citerior, and was dedicated by his parents, Licinius Lausus and Ulpia Venula.

EDCS-05801797.summary: This very short inscription simply identifies Livia Livilla as the daughter of Caius, likely on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-05801798.translation: This place, enclosed by a wall, is for the religious observance of the burial of Lolliia Attica, [daughter of], and Stactes, [his] wife, and Marcus Lollius Amaranthus.
EDCS-05801798.summary: This inscription describes a burial plot enclosed by a wall, designated for the religious observance of the burials of members of the Lollius family, including Lolliia Attica, Stactes, and Marcus Lollius Amaranthus.

EDCS-05801799.translation: For Marcus Longidius Hebenus, for Tiberius Claudius Celadus, for Gaius Marcius Argaeus, for Gaius Fulvius Successus.
EDCS-05801799.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely funerary dedications or ownership markers for a burial space, for four individuals: Marcus Longidius Hebenus, Tiberius Claudius Celadus, Gaius Marcius Argaeus, and Gaius Fulvius Successus.

EDCS-05801800.translation: Sulpicia Lesbia, wife, [made this monument] for Marcus Lucretius Optandus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-05801800.summary: This epitaph records a monument dedicated by Sulpicia Lesbia for her husband Marcus Lucretius Optandus, who was a freedman.

EDCS-05801801.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Publius Manilius Hymetus, Manilia Primitiva, Publius Manilius Chresimus [made this monument] for Publius Manilius Hyginus. To the Spirits of the Underworld.
EDCS-05801801.summary: This epitaph, dedicated to the underworld spirits, records a monument made by Publius Manilius Hymetus, Manilia Primitiva, and Publius Manilius Chresimus for Publius Manilius Hyginus.

EDCS-05801802.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Marius Secundus.

EDCS-05801803.translation: Aulus Caelius Euphrosynus made this for his well-deserving freedwoman wife, Memmia Deutera.
EDCS-05801803.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Caelius Euphrosynus for his freedwoman wife, Memmia Deutera.

EDCS-05801804.translation: Monime [dedicated this] to the divine spirit of OEIAIO.
EDCS-05801804.summary: This is a dedication by Monime to a divinity identified as OEIAIO.

EDCS-05801805.translation: To the departed spirits of Caius Murdius Felix, who lived 75 years; Murdia Sabina made this for her well-deserving patron and for herself and her descendants.
EDCS-05801805.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Caius Murdius Felix and states that Murdia Sabina erected it for him, herself, and descendants.

EDCS-05801806.translation: Octavius, son of Caius, [and] Camilia Macra.
EDCS-05801806.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, possibly associated with a funerary monument.

EDCS-05801807.translation: To the departed spirits of Gaius Octavius Tatianus, who lived 41 years, 10 months, and 25 days; Publius Iuventius Caesianus and his wife Ulpia Benigna made this for their dearest father, with whom [the deceased] lived for 22 years without any complaint.
EDCS-05801807.summary: This funerary inscription details the life and death of Gaius Octavius Tatianus and is dedicated by his father and stepmother.

EDCS-05801808.translation: Gaius Octavius, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe; Vecula, Optata, daughter of Titus Popillius, and Quartilla, freedwoman of Caelia.
EDCS-05801808.summary: This inscription lists the names of several women, possibly related to a funerary context.

EDCS-05801809.translation: Caius Ofillius Amemptus, freedman of Caius, made this for his well-deserving friends Thallus and Aprilis, children of Gnaeus Sentius.
EDCS-05801809.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Ofillius Amemptus for his friends Thallus and Aprilis.

EDCS-05801810.translation: [Name missing] made this for Onesimus, his son, who lived 3 years and [missing months].
EDCS-05801810.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Onesimus, who died at the age of three.

EDCS-05801811.translation: Publius Pacilius Suavis, freedman of Publius; Publius Acilius Crescens, son of Publius; Petisia Potens, freedwoman of a woman [owner]; Hortensia Anthis, freedwoman of Aulus; Bithus.
EDCS-05801811.summary: This inscription lists the names of several individuals, likely freedmen and freedwomen, possibly in a funerary or collegial context.

EDCS-05801812.translation: Pamphilus, son of Philodamus, was there.
EDCS-05801812.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning two personal names and a place, likely recording attendance or presence.

EDCS-05801813.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Paterno lived 1 year, 11 months, and 20 days. Moschis his mother, who nursed him, [erected this].
EDCS-05801813.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Paterno, detailing his lifespan and mentioning his mother, Moschis.

EDCS-05801814.translation: Publius Pedanius Saturninus, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, [erected this] for his father.
EDCS-05801814.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Pedanius Saturninus to his father.

EDCS-05801815.translation: Aulus Eyteles, freedman of Aulus Perperna.
EDCS-05801815.summary: This inscription records the name and former ownership of a freedman, Aulus Eyteles.

EDCS-05801816.summary: This inscription records the name and former ownership of a freedwoman, Euce.

EDCS-05801817.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Pyrgensis erected this for his well-deserving wife, Petronia Hygeia, who lived 35 years, 8 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05801817.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia Hygeia, erected by her husband, detailing her lifespan and relationship.

EDCS-05801818.translation: Philtate erected this for his well-deserving wife, Philumino, the freedwoman of Caesar.
EDCS-05801818.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Philtate for his wife, Philumino, who was a freedwoman of Caesar.

EDCS-05801819.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Mnasias, freedman of Augustus, erected this for his well-deserving wife, Plaetoria Nupsialis, who lived 15 years, 7 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05801819.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Plaetoria Nupsialis, erected by her husband Mnasias, detailing her lifespan and his status as a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-05801820.translation: Titus Cestrus, freedman of Titus Pompeius, lived 45 years.
EDCS-05801820.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Cestrus, a freedman, stating his lifespan.

EDCS-05801821.translation: Titus Pomponius Philadelphus, freedman of Titus, and Pomponia Doris, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-05801821.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Titus Pomponius Philadelphus and Pomponia Doris, both freedpersons of Titus.

EDCS-05801822.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For my most beloved son, Gnaeus Pontius Antignus, from his father.
EDCS-05801822.summary: A funerary dedication by a father to his son, Gnaeus Pontius Antignus.

EDCS-05801823.summary: The name inscription of Marcus Popillius Rufus, possibly a tombstone or a record of ownership.

EDCS-05801825.translation: To Iunia Prisca, a wife of great merit. She lived 28 years. Iunius Successus made this.
EDCS-05801825.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iunia Prisca, erected by her husband, Iunius Successus, who notes her age at death.

EDCS-05801826.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Altorius, a sharp, active, brave, faithful, and charming man, to whom the house of Assur was ancestral, whose name was Quintius, rests here in eternal bloom, after living twenty-three good years, dedicated this altar for him for his merit.
EDCS-05801826.summary: A funerary altar dedicated to Altorius by an unknown person, praising his character and noting his age at death.

EDCS-05801827.translation: [...] of his sister Quinctia and Marcus Q[uintius(?)]. To be enlarged.
EDCS-05801827.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Quinctia and Marcus Quinctius, with a note about enlarging something.

EDCS-05801828.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Quintia.

EDCS-05801830.translation: Quintus Rabuleius Celer, freedman of Quintus Celeris, 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-05801830.summary: A boundary or property inscription detailing land dimensions associated with Quintus Rabuleius Celer.

EDCS-05801831.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Here lies the body of Restituta, who was truly Restituta in name and character. She lived 21 years. Made for her, who was deserving.
EDCS-05801831.summary: A funerary epitaph for Restituta, who lived 21 years and was praised for her character.

EDCS-05801832.translation: Rubellia Onomaste, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for her son Asto. He lived 2 years.
EDCS-05801832.summary: A funerary epitaph for Asto, erected by his mother Rubellia Onomaste.

EDCS-05801833.translation: Publius Rubrius Barba and Publius Petronius Clemens.
EDCS-05801833.summary: An inscription bearing the names of two individuals, Publius Rubrius Barba and Publius Petronius Clemens, possibly a joint dedication or ownership record.

EDCS-05801834.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Rubrius Nepos made this for his freedman and nurse, who deserved well.
EDCS-05801834.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Titus Rubrius Nepos to his freedman and nurse.

EDCS-05801835.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Rusticelia Triumphalis [made this] for her most excellent husband, Lucius Rusticelius Philomus.
EDCS-05801835.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Rusticelia Triumphalis to her husband, Lucius Rusticelius Philomus.

EDCS-05801836.translation: Sabidinus, military tribune elected by the people, [made this] for Rutilia Rutilia.
EDCS-05801836.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Sabidinus, a military tribune, to Rutilia Rutilia.

EDCS-05801837.translation: Publius Sallius, freedman of Sallius P., [made this] for Sallia, for himself, and for his freedmen and their descendants.
EDCS-05801837.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Publius Sallius for himself, his freedmen, and their descendants, and for Sallia.

EDCS-05801839.translation: Salvilus, son of Antonia M. Siyr, aged 13 years, 2 months, 15 days.
EDCS-05801839.summary: This inscription records the age and name of Salvilus.

EDCS-05801840.translation: Lucius Sellius, son of Lucius, son of Appenninus, of the Vettiena tribe, son of C.
EDCS-05801840.summary: This inscription records the full Roman names and tribal affiliation of Lucius Sellius.

EDCS-05801841.translation: For Sempronia Tyche, most chaste wife. Her husband Antonius Severus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants, this monument or tomb shall not follow its heir.
EDCS-05801841.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Antonius Severus to his wife Sempronia Tyche, establishing an inalienable family tomb.

EDCS-05801842.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Senatius Nephon [made this] for his most excellent wife, Senatia Flora.
EDCS-05801842.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Senatius Nephon to his wife Senatia Flora.

EDCS-05801843.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Servilia Secundilla, daughter of Lucius Servilius Gnostus, and Servilia Soteris, made this for her freedmen who deserved well, as patroness.
EDCS-05801843.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Servilia Secundilla to her freedmen, identifying herself as patroness and daughter of Lucius Servilius Gnostus and Servilia Soteris.

EDCS-05801844.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Septiminus tata made this for Servilius Silvanus, who lived 12 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-05801844.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Servilius Silvanus and its dedication by Septiminus tata.

EDCS-05801846.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sophron, who lived 4 years and 41 days. Sophron, the father, and Eupolis, the mother, made this for their dearest son.
EDCS-05801846.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, Sophron, set up by his parents.

EDCS-05801847.translation: Abascantus, freedman of the woman Claudia Donata, lived 22 years. His mother, Claudia Donata, made this for herself and her family from her own funds.
EDCS-05801847.summary: A funerary epitaph for a freedman, Abascantus, with his mother Claudia Donata as the dedicator, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801848.translation: 2 months, 8 days, 17 hours, 2 minutes. Syneros, Primigenius, Quartilla, and Peculiaris, freedmen, made this for their well-deserving patron.
EDCS-05801848.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by freedmen for their patron, possibly indicating precise measurements of time or age. The date is uncertain but likely Imperial.

EDCS-05801849.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Of Marcus Terentius Fuscus.
EDCS-05801849.summary: A simple funerary dedication to the underworld deities for Marcus Terentius Fuscus.

EDCS-05801850.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Terentia Amona. Terentia Agele, the mother, and Aelius Irenaeus, the father-in-law, made this for the well-deserving woman.
EDCS-05801850.summary: A funerary epitaph for Terentia Amona, dedicated by her mother and father-in-law.

EDCS-05801851.translation: Terpne, the sister, and Anthis, the wife, made this.
EDCS-05801851.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a sister and wife for an unnamed deceased individual.

EDCS-05801855.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Publius Valerius Magnus. Valeria Minois, the mother.
EDCS-05801855.summary: A funerary dedication for Publius Valerius Magnus, initiated by his mother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801859.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Gaius Vecilius Florinus, who lived 40 years, 11 months, 15 days. Gaius Vecilius Florus and his mother Vecilia Primitiva. The mother must have been read before the son.
EDCS-05801859.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Vecilius Florinus, set up by his father and mother, with a note suggesting a correction or clarification about the mother's preceding status.

EDCS-05801860.translation: Titus Ventilius Faustus, freedman of Titus, for his most beloved wife Catia Clymene. Caecilia Sperata and Catia Modesta lived 24 years, 9 months.
EDCS-05801860.summary: A funerary epitaph for Catia Clymene, set up by her husband and possibly including the names and ages of other individuals, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801863.summary: A simple inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, for Lucius Umbrius Apella.

EDCS-05801864.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Urbanus, who lived 73 years and 5 months. His father Ursulus and mother Primilla made this for their sweetest son, and for Caesima, his sister, and Masurius, his brother, who deserved well and died when light was taken from him.
EDCS-05801864.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to Urbanus by his parents and siblings, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801865.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Zosimene, who lived 14 years and 7 months. Her father Zosimus made this for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-05801865.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to Zosimene by her father, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801867.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name of a person, Virgilius, and his origin, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801883.translation: Pura, freedwoman of a man, AGNI.
EDCS-05801883.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Pura as a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801887.translation: To Publius, son of F, from SVI.
EDCS-05801887.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication or funerary marker, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801891.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that seems to be a funerary dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801893.translation: daughter of Pla[tia], son of Cai.
EDCS-05801893.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the parentage of an individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801897.translation: Clodia Exuperia, daughter of Spurius, was placed here on the Kalends of March, after the second consulship of the most excellent man Armatus.
EDCS-05801897.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Clodia Exuperia, dated by consulship to after 396 AD.

EDCS-05801898.translation: A place for Leta with her sons Proclan and Gemmulus. She rests here in peace, a place which she had purchased for herself in the oratory of Saint Alexander, commending their souls to the command of the Lord Heraclius, the Most Pious Emperor, in the first indiction. She rests here in peace. May he who opens the tomb without the parents be cursed.
EDCS-05801898.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Leta and her sons, likely from the Byzantine period, possibly 7th century AD, given the mention of Emperor Heraclius.

EDCS-05801899.translation: Antoninus donated the chest to Blegius.
EDCS-05801899.summary: This inscription records a donation of a chest by Antoninus to Blegius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801906.translation: Gaius Apidius Bassus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, formerly first spear of the XI Legion and a member of the college of eight priests, of Amiternum, erected this according to his will, with the exception of the site, at the expense of 100,000 sesterces, under the supervision of Quintus Orfius Flaccus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, and Gaius Caesar, son of Quintus, of the Sergia tribe, and Nygmus, a freedman.
EDCS-05801906.summary: This inscription records the posthumous dedication of a public monument or building by Gaius Apidius Bassus, a military officer and priest, in Amiternum, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-05801907.translation: To Marcus Julius Saturninus, my darling.
EDCS-05801907.summary: This is a simple dedication to Marcus Julius Saturninus, likely a beloved individual, with no further context provided.

EDCS-05801908.translation: Celadus, freedman of Augustus, gave this gift to the waters of Alba Longa.
EDCS-05801908.summary: This inscription records a gift given to the sacred waters of Alba Longa by Celadus, a freedman of the emperor Augustus.

EDCS-05801909.translation: Ulpia Athenais, wife of Glyptus, freedman of Augustus and his secretary, willingly gave this gift to the most sacred waters of Alba Longa.
EDCS-05801909.summary: This inscription records a gift dedicated to the sacred waters of Alba Longa by Ulpia Athenais, wife of Glyptus, an imperial freedman and secretary.

EDCS-05801910.translation: Gaius Umbreius Lavicanus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the sacred waters of Alba Longa for his health.
EDCS-05801910.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Umbreius Lavicanus, dedicated to the sacred waters of Alba Longa for his own health.

EDCS-05801911.translation: Albulis, you were the source of health for the disabled, from whose waters, once a victim of a wound from an Etruscan boar, he was freed by the physicians, and after the wound healed with a scar, the nerve became thin and he began to run quickly; he now gives you himself as a gift of marble for your merits, O water, into whose stream you rejoice to enter the middle of the road, where the Tiburtine master looks down from his house and the Aelian villa sees with painted facades.
EDCS-05801911.summary: This complex poetic inscription describes a man's recovery from a boar wound thanks to the waters of Albulis and his subsequent dedication of a marble statue to the springs.

EDCS-05801912.translation: Gaius Claudius Severus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, thrice military tribune, to Albul[a?].
EDCS-05801912.summary: This inscription mentions Gaius Claudius Severus, a military officer, and seems to be related to Albul[a], possibly the springs or a deity associated with them.

EDCS-05801913.translation: Pothumenus, slave of Publius Folius Pelops, set this up according to a vision.
EDCS-05801913.summary: This is a dedication set up by Pothumenus, a slave, based on a vision, with no specific deity or location mentioned.

EDCS-05801914.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Fabius Rufinus Lucillus lived for 3 years, 2 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-05801914.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and lifespan of Gaius Fabius Rufinus Lucillus.

EDCS-05801916.translation: To Decimus Herennius, son of Decimus. Herennius Maximus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05801916.summary: This is a dedication or funerary marker for Decimus Herennius, son of Decimus, set up by Herennius Maximus.

EDCS-05801917.translation: To Iulia Procula, from Tiberius Iulius Saturninus, for his most virtuous wife.
EDCS-05801917.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Tiberius Iulius Saturninus to his wife Iulia Procula.

EDCS-05801919.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Munius Hierocles, father, for his dearest son, Marcus Munius Lollianus, honored with the equestrian rank, who lived 13 years, 3 months, and 26 days.
EDCS-05801919.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Munius Hierocles for his son Marcus Munius Lollianus, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-05801920.translation: To Iulia Nebris. Fabianus, steward of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, made this for his most deserving life companion and for her descendants.
EDCS-05801920.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Fabianus, a steward, for his companion Iulia Nebris and her descendants.

EDCS-05801922.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Parents for Titus Sempronius Valerianus, who lived 1 year, 11 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-05801922.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents to their child Titus Sempronius Valerianus.

EDCS-05801924.translation: Synesis, freedwoman of Veturia and her husband, made this monument for herself, her co-freedman Decimus Veturius Maheni, and Decimus Veturius Diophanes.
EDCS-05801924.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Synesis for herself and her fellow freedmen, Decimus Veturius Maheni and Decimus Veturius Diophanes.

EDCS-05801925.translation: Valerius Mettius Martialis lived 6 years, 6 months, and 18 days. Mettia Valeria made this for her son.
EDCS-05801925.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Mettia Valeria for her young son, Valerius Mettius Martialis.

EDCS-05801926.translation: To Diana Rotana, from Caius Claudius, son of Caius, grandson of Servius, of the Lemonia tribe.
EDCS-05801926.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana Rotana by Caius Claudius.

EDCS-05801927.translation: Felix, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, twice prefect, for Albia, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-05801927.summary: This inscription records that Felix, a twice-appointed prefect and son of Lucius, set up a monument for Albia, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-05801928.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Publius Flavius Urbanus.

EDCS-05801933.summary: This is a dedication to a sacred spring.

EDCS-05801945.translation: Lucius Appuleius Asclepiades, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Appuleius, son of Lucius, military tribune, and Appuleia Sophanuba, freedwoman of Lucius, made this at their own expense.
EDCS-05801945.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by members of the Appuleius family, likely for a tomb or public monument, with one individual identified as a military tribune.

EDCS-05801946.translation: Sextus Mutilius Primus, son of Sextus, of the Collina tribe, scribe for a quaestor and for the curule aediles.
EDCS-05801946.summary: This inscription records Sextus Mutilius Primus, identifying his tribal affiliation and his professional roles as a scribe for various magistrates.

EDCS-05801948.translation: Felix, Titus Albius [---], Marcus Antonius [---], Lucius Sextius [---], Publius Aurelius Optatus [---], Gaius Seius Bassus [---], Sextus Minatius, son of Sextus, [---], Gnaeus Munatius, son of Gnaeus, Bassus [---], Gaius Albonius, son of Gaius, [---], Lucius Attius, son of Lucius, Niger [---], Lucius Arrenus [---], Quintus Aelius Artemidorus [---], Marcus Aleius Sponsor [---], Gaius Aurelius Primus [---], Appuleius Felix [---], Banius Diochares [---], Hilario [---], Sosus [---], Optatus [---], Hilarus [---], Fronto [---], [---]cus [---], [---]us [---], C [---], C [---], Gaius Egn [---], Gaius Egn [---], Gaius Eg [---], Gaius E [---], Gaius [---].
EDCS-05801948.summary: This is a fragmented inscription listing numerous Roman names, likely from a funerary monument or a list of officials, with most personal details lost.

EDCS-05801949.translation: Licinius, Publius Laelius, Gaius Lurius, Lucius Memmius, Quintus Magius, Marcius, Manlius, Mucius, Manius [---].
EDCS-05801949.summary: This fragmented inscription lists several Roman family names, possibly from a funerary context or a list of citizens.

EDCS-05801950.translation: Servillus [---], Salluvius Rufus [---], Servilius Salvius Timedius Nepos [---], Fortunatus [---], [---]ius Felix [---], Turpilius Faustus [---], Firmus [---].
EDCS-05801950.summary: This fragmented inscription records several personal names, likely part of a funerary monument or a list of individuals.

EDCS-05801951.translation: [---] V [---], Marcus Vet [---], Valerius [---], Publius Valerius [---], Publius Valerius [---], Sextus Vetulenus [---], Sextus Vetulenus [---], [---] tribune [---].
EDCS-05801951.summary: This is a fragmented inscription listing several names, possibly from a tomb or a record of military or official positions, with the title 'tribune' partially visible.

EDCS-05801952.translation: Gnaeus Munatius Aurelius Bassus, son of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe, procurator of the emperor, prefect of the artisans, prefect of the cohort of archers, prefect for a second time of the cohort of the Astures, census-taker of Roman citizens of the colony of Victrix which is in Britannia, curator of the Nomentana road, patron of the same municipality, perpetual flamen, with duumviral authority, dictator for the fourth time.
EDCS-05801952.summary: This inscription details the extensive career and civic honors of Gnaeus Munatius Aurelius Bassus, a high-ranking official serving in Britain and Italy, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05801957.translation: Gaius Betuinus Licinus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-05801957.summary: This inscription records Gaius Betuinus Licinus, identifying him as a freedman and providing his patron's name.

EDCS-05801958.translation: Gaius Bruttius Primus, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe.
EDCS-05801958.summary: This inscription records Gaius Bruttius Primus, noting his father's name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05801959.summary: This inscription records Bruttia, identifying her as the daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-05801960.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a personal name.

EDCS-05801961.translation: Lucius Caerellius Potitus made [this] for [someone] well deserving.
EDCS-05801961.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Lucius Caerellius Potitus is the dedicator.

EDCS-05801962.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely indicating ownership or a dedication to Quintus Caticanius Bithus.

EDCS-05801964.translation: Claudia Felicissima and Marcus Aurelius, freedman of the emperor, made [this] for [their] daughter and [their] sister Fronto, who was well deserving.
EDCS-05801964.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Claudia Felicissima and Marcus Aurelius for their daughter and sister.

EDCS-05801966.translation: Aelius, freedman of the emperor, [made this] for Felicissimus.
EDCS-05801966.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Aelius, a freedman of the emperor, for Felicissimus.

EDCS-05801968.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or a legal statement, mentioning Quintus Furius.

EDCS-05801969.translation: Lucius Herennius Gallus, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe.
EDCS-05801969.summary: This is a funerary inscription or an indication of citizenship for Lucius Herennius Gallus.

EDCS-05801970.translation: Herennia Merula Maior, daughter of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe.
EDCS-05801970.summary: This is a funerary inscription or an indication of citizenship for Herennia Merula Maior.

EDCS-05801971.translation: Herennia Merula Minor, daughter of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe.
EDCS-05801971.summary: This is a funerary inscription or an indication of citizenship for Herennia Merula Minor.

EDCS-05801976.translation: From the will of Lucius Ogulnius Aeschinus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Ogulnius Phileas, freedman of Aeschinus, took care that the monument be made. For Lucius Ogulnius Saxo, son of Gaius, of the Clustumina tribe. For Lucius Ogulnius, freedman of Aeschinus. For the son of Ogulnia Sostrata and Asandrae. For Lucius Ogulnius Philemo, freedman of Lucius. For Ogulnia Fortunata, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-05801976.summary: This extensive funerary inscription details the arrangement of a monument from the will of Lucius Ogulnius Aeschinus, listing several relatives and freedmen to be commemorated.

EDCS-05801979.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly recording a payment or dedication by Lucius Pacilius, date unknown.

EDCS-05801982.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Scifonia Paulla, daughter of Titus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-05801984.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records the name and origin of an individual named Ander Arius.

EDCS-05801989.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that probably records a Roman name, M. Ulvius Aetioni Partiolu.

EDCS-05801994.translation: To Sextus Pedius Hirruto, son of Sextus, of the Arnensis tribe, praetor; Sextus Pedius Hirrutus, son of Lucius, praetor.
EDCS-05801994.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Pedius Hirruto and his father Sextus Pedius Hirrutus, a praetor, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05801996.translation: To Marcus Valerius Quadratus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, member of the board of six for judging lawsuits, military tribune with broad stripe, sexvir of Roman knights, quaestor of Augustus, plebeian tribune candidate, praetor, member of the board of seven overseers of public feasts.
EDCS-05801996.summary: This is a detailed cursus honorum inscription celebrating Marcus Valerius Quadratus and his career, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05801997.translation: To the holy spirits of the underworld. To Donatus, dearest son. Marcus, father, and Satriane, mother [dedicated this].
EDCS-05801997.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by parents to their deceased son, Donatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801998.translation: To the holy spirits of the underworld. Marcus Oppius Pisibanus erected this at his own expense for Iulia Nic.
EDCS-05801998.summary: This is a funerary inscription erected by Marcus Oppius Pisibanus for Iulia Nic, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05801999.translation: Timotheus, son of Marcus, for himself and [others?].
EDCS-05801999.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary or dedication inscription by Timotheus for himself and possibly other family members, date unknown.

EDCS-05802000.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording that Vibius Coponius Orn S made something, possibly a monument or object, date unknown.

EDCS-05802001.summary: This inscription records a personal dedication by Lucrianus.

EDCS-05802006.translation: Tarquitius Rufus, son of Publius, from the tribe [---], Tarquitianus, urban praetor, prefect in charge of the grain supply, erected this by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-05802006.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Tarquitius Rufus, who held several high offices, likely during the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05802007.translation: To Seia, wife of Aurelianus, daughter of Maxsimus.
EDCS-05802007.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Seia, wife of Aurelianus and daughter of Maxsimus.

EDCS-05802020.translation: In these lands of Aurelia Faustiniana, a bathhouse is maintained in the city style, and all civility is provided.
EDCS-05802020.summary: This inscription describes the amenities provided at a bathhouse on the estates of Aurelia Faustiniana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05802023.summary: This inscription records a personal dedication by Publius Fabius Abascantus.

EDCS-05802024.translation: Grania Dia, most fortunate, and [---] made this for Publius Aelius Fronton, husband of the deceased, most dutiful father, and also for themselves.
EDCS-05802024.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Grania Dia for her husband, Publius Aelius Fronton, and for herself.

EDCS-05802029.translation: Of Gaius Cuspis, son of freedman Gaius, [---]; of Gaius Cuspis, son of freedman Gaius, [---]; Pampilus, son of [---]; Cuspia, freedwoman of Gaius, Ni[---]; Cuspia, freedwoman of Gaius, [---]; Stacta.
EDCS-05802029.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely members of a family and their freedmen, possibly related to a property or association.

EDCS-05802030.translation: [---] Meta, wife of Cutius, and her freedman Eron, and Cutia, freedwoman of Manius, Demetria, for themselves and for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-05802030.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Demetria for herself, her freedmen, and freedwomen, mentioning other individuals likely connected to her family.

EDCS-05802031.translation: To Flavina Astra and Flavina Quintea, freedwoman.
EDCS-05802031.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Flavina Astra and her freedwoman Flavina Quintea.

EDCS-05802037.translation: Publius Petronius Epagathus and his son Erasto.
EDCS-05802037.summary: This inscription records the names of Publius Petronius Epagathus and his son Erasto, possibly a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-05802042.translation: Lucius Soccius Bassus, son of Lucius, freedman.
EDCS-05802042.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph naming a freedman, Lucius Soccius Bassus, and his patron.

EDCS-05802055.translation: Naris made this with complaints. Chronides made this.
EDCS-05802055.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication, possibly naming the deceased and the maker, though the text is fragmentary and difficult to interpret definitively.

EDCS-05802061.translation: Ateius Capito gave this as a gift to Hercules Victor.
EDCS-05802061.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the god Hercules Victor by Ateius Capito.

EDCS-05802068.translation: Lucius Manilius, son of Quintus, and Lucius Marcius, son of Lucius, duovirs of the Public of the Fidenates, established the boundaries.
EDCS-05802068.summary: This inscription records the work of boundary demarcation carried out by two duovirs of Fidenas.

EDCS-05802069.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Aquillius to Nonia.

EDCS-05802071.translation: To Sextus Cocceius Honoratus, his well-deserving brother, Sextus Cocceius Sertorianus made (this) by the judgment of Aurelius Dionysus.
EDCS-05802071.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Sextus Cocceius Sertorianus for his brother Sextus Cocceius Honoratus, with the oversight of Aurelius Dionysus.

EDCS-05802073.translation: To Julia Epictesis, most dutiful, Julius Capitolinus made (this).
EDCS-05802073.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Julia Epictesis by Julius Capitolinus.

EDCS-05802074.translation: To Cn. Minatius [?], Minatia [?], to Pontia [?], to Pontia [?], daughter [?], Mina[tia...
EDCS-05802074.summary: This is a highly fragmented funerary inscription, likely naming members of the Minatia family and possibly a daughter named Pontia.

EDCS-05802075.translation: To Gaius Petronius Optatus, he placed (this). Gaius Petronius Isochrysus, freedman of Optatus.
EDCS-05802075.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Petronius Optatus, erected by his freedman Gaius Petronius Isochrysus.

EDCS-05802076.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph, naming Lucius Salvius and possibly Ositia.

EDCS-05802091.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, in his 32nd year of tribunician power.
EDCS-05802091.summary: This is an inscription recording the tribunician power of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-05802095.translation: Philetus (served) the Rutili, (it) was overseen on the Kalends of April, by Tiberius Plautius Corvinus (!).
EDCS-05802095.summary: This inscription records a transaction overseen by Tiberius Plautius Corvinus, dated to April 1st.

EDCS-05802104.translation: Vitalis... Herennuleius Abascantus... Gnaeus Ostiensis Lu... Marcus Licinius I... Marcus Turranius C... Junior Tiberius Claudius Ce... Junior...
EDCS-05802104.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to list names of individuals, possibly officials or members of a collegium.

EDCS-05802105.translation: Proculus, freedman of Saturninus Calpurnius Innocentius, erected (this) at his own expense with his own money for the three leading men of the collegium of carpenters and furniture makers in the Portensian district.
EDCS-05802105.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Proculus, a freedman, for the collegium of carpenters and furniture makers.

EDCS-05802109.translation: Aninia Anthis, wife, (dedicated this) to Quintus Aeranius Antiochus, Augustal sevir and quinquennial of the same order, and quinquennial adjutant of the grain measurers of Ostia; the place was given publicly by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05802109.summary: This is a funerary or dedication inscription for Quintus Aeranius Antiochus, a prominent local official, set up by his wife, with the place granted by public decree.

EDCS-05802112.translation: To Sextus Publicius Maior, son of Sextus, of the Collina tribe, honored with the public equestrian rank, decurion...
EDCS-05802112.summary: This is a dedication to Sextus Publicius Maior, a member of the equestrian order and a decurion, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-05802121.translation: Lucius Arrius Eutyches made (this) for his dearest wife.
EDCS-05802121.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Arrius Eutyches for his wife.

EDCS-05802123.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely containing names.

EDCS-05802124.translation: To Brenia Fortunata, a well-deserving wife, II CH XVI.
EDCS-05802124.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Brenia Fortunata, described as a deserving wife, with some numerical or dating notation.

EDCS-05802129.translation: Postumulena Symmone made (this) for her well-deserving patron, Postumulenus Atimetus.
EDCS-05802129.summary: This is a dedication made by Postumulena Symmone for her patron, Postumulenus Atimetus.

EDCS-05802131.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rusticanius Felix, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-05802132.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription possibly dedicated to a woman named Venerina by her freedman Stephanus.

EDCS-05802135.translation: Here rests he who lived 7 years and 5 months, buried on the Kalends of February in the consulship of C., when Bonifatius bought the property.
EDCS-05802135.summary: This epitaph records the death of a child, the duration of their life, and the purchase of the burial plot by Bonifatius.

EDCS-05802137.translation: Of Lucius Apuleius Marcellus, of Aulus Fabi Diogenes.
EDCS-05802137.summary: This inscription appears to be a ownership mark or a dedication by Lucius Apuleius Marcellus and Aulus Fabi Diogenes.

EDCS-05802146.translation: Quintus Laberius, son of Quintus, to Iovius Beonus.
EDCS-05802146.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Iovius Beonus by Quintus Laberius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-05802147.translation: Sacred to Mars; it is forbidden for a slave to touch this statue.
EDCS-05802147.summary: This is a dedication of a statue to Mars with a prohibition against slaves touching it.

EDCS-05802150.translation: Son of Colossus, of the Mae(cian) tribe.
EDCS-05802150.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a gentilician name indicating filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05802153.translation: Aerentia, daughter of Lucius, sacred to Diana, gave this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05802153.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Diana by Aerentia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-05802154.translation: Diana, Marcus Livius, son of Marcus, the praetor, dedicated this.
EDCS-05802154.summary: This is a dedication to Diana by Marcus Livius, son of Marcus, who held the office of praetor.

EDCS-05802155.translation: Marcus Servilius Quartus prepared the shield and also what is placed inside for Diana.
EDCS-05802155.summary: This inscription indicates that Marcus Servilius Quartus prepared military equipment and other items dedicated to Diana.

EDCS-05802157.translation: To Diana, from Gnaeus and Quintus, sons of Etrilius.
EDCS-05802157.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana, likely made by two individuals named Gnaeus and Quintus, sons of Etrilius.

EDCS-05802162.translation: Tontius, son of Quintus, gave this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05802162.summary: This records a gift given by Tontius, son of Quintus, to an unspecified recipient or deity, indicating his willing and rightful contribution.

EDCS-05802163.translation: To the Sempronian granaries, near the old bathhouse, 4662 pounds of lead, and four basins, the same person gave as a gift for himself and his family.
EDCS-05802163.summary: This inscription details a donation of lead and basins for the Sempronian granaries and bathhouse, made by an unnamed individual for his family.

EDCS-05802165.translation: To Publius Autro[...], son of [...], a consul [...].
EDCS-05802165.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication or honorific text for Publius Autro, who held the position of consul.

EDCS-05802169.translation: Marcus Iulius, son of Marcus, and Marcus Accoleius, son of Marcus, as aediles, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-05802169.summary: This inscription records an action taken by Marcus Iulius and Marcus Accoleius in their capacity as aediles, acting under senatorial authority.

EDCS-05802170.translation: Lucius Pontius [...], Quintus Petreius [...], Gaius Pupilius [...], Marcus Luvcai [...], Lucius Acculeius [...], Lucius Vecilius [...].
EDCS-05802170.summary: This is a list of names, possibly officials, candidates, or members of a group, with their filiation and partial inscriptions.

EDCS-05802171.translation: Lucius Faenius Faustus, parasite of the fourth cohort of Apollo.
EDCS-05802171.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Faenius Faustus and his role as a 'parasite' (an attendant or cult official) associated with a cohort of Apollo.

EDCS-05802172.translation: Fundilia Rufa, daughter of Caius, patroness of Docti.
EDCS-05802172.summary: This inscription names Fundilia Rufa, daughter of Caius, and designates her as the patroness of someone named Docti.

EDCS-05802173.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that identifies Fundilia Rufa, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-05802174.translation: Quintus Hostius Capito, son of Quintus, teacher of rhetoric.
EDCS-05802174.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Hostius Capito, son of Quintus, and his profession as a teacher of rhetoric.

EDCS-05802175.translation: To Licinia Chrysarionis, Marcus Bolanus Canusaeus, perhaps in honour, perhaps in service, sacred to Diana Nemorensis.
EDCS-05802175.summary: This is a dedication to Licinia Chrysarionis, likely by Marcus Bolanus Canusaeus, possibly honouring her and dedicating something to Diana of Nemi.

EDCS-05802176.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Stacia Quinta, freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-05802177.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly for a person named Cornelius Maior.

EDCS-05802178.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly naming an individual and their patron or family name.

EDCS-05802179.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to name a freedman named Opus and includes illegible text.

EDCS-05802189.translation: [---]us, freedman of Marcus, a soldier of the II Parthica legion, [---]s, seven.
EDCS-05802189.summary: This fragmentary inscription identifies a soldier of the II Parthica legion and potentially mentions his status as a freedman and a number, possibly referring to years of service or rank.

EDCS-05802199.translation: On the seventh day, Acetus set this up for Ammos, his daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-05802199.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Acetus for his deserving daughter Ammos.

EDCS-05802202.translation: Sulpicius Trollus made this for Quintus Voconius Pollio, 15.
EDCS-05802202.summary: This inscription records that Sulpicius Trollus made something (likely a monument or dedication) for Quintus Voconius Pollio, with the number XV (15) possibly indicating a duration or quantity.

EDCS-05802203.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Prota, who lived 19 years, her sister Pia made this.
EDCS-05802203.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Prota, who died at 19 years old, set up by her sister Pia.

EDCS-05802209.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Domitius Telegonus made this for his wife Pettetia Fortunata.
EDCS-05802209.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Domitius Telegonus for his wife Pettetia Fortunata.

EDCS-05802217.translation: Marcus Caerellius Iazemis, quinquennial official, third and perpetual baker, and also a carrier and grain merchant, gave this gift to the Invincible Hercules in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05802217.summary: This is an inscription recording a votive gift by a baker and merchant to Hercules, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05802222.translation: Tiberius Claudius Liberalis Aebutianus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, who held the public equitation, prefect of the engineers, military tribune of the Third Cyrenaic Legion, decurial magistrate of the consuls, with his wife Claudia Nectarea, erected this in honor of Herennia Helvidiana Aemiliana, daughter of Marcus, wife of Lucius Claudius Proculus Cornelianus, the consul and queen.
EDCS-05802222.summary: This epitaph honors Herennia Helvidiana Aemiliana, wife of a consul, and was erected by her husband and their freedman who had a distinguished military and administrative career, likely dating to the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05802223.translation: To Marcus Lollius Paulinus Asiaticus Saturninus, son of Decimus, grandson of Decimus, of the Voltinian tribe, [---] IIIvir for the coining of gold, silver, and bronze, Salii Collini, quaestor of the Emperor Caesar, praetor, and to Ionio Fructus and Con[---]
EDCS-05802223.summary: This is a dedication fragment naming several prominent officials including a moneyer, a Salii priest, a quaestor, and a praetor, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05802229.translation: To Lucius Vipstanus Messala, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, [---] Salii Collino.
EDCS-05802229.summary: This is a fragmented inscription dedicating an honor to Lucius Vipstanus Messala, possibly a member of the Salii Collini, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05802235.translation: To Aemilius Victorinus, son of Aulus, of the Galerian tribe, who served as procurator of the emperor for receiving taxes in the province of Gallia Lugdunensis and in the province of Thrace, and who had performed equestrian military duties and held the public equitation, Gaius Vivius Iulianus, quaestorian scribe, erected this for his excellent friend, the site having been granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05802235.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by a scribe for his friend Aemilius Victorinus, a procurator responsible for tax collection in multiple provinces, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05802241.translation: [---] to Ampliatus, Herculaneus Augustalis, curator, quaestor Augustalis, [---] honor publicly accepted, expense remitted?
EDCS-05802241.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Ampliatus, who held positions related to imperial cult or finance, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05802242.translation: Under the supervision of Marcus Mucius Tiburtinus and Lucius Alfenatius Priscus, the IIIIviri.
EDCS-05802242.summary: This inscription records the work being supervised by two IIIIviri (four magistrates) of a municipality, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05802244.translation: Tullia Berenice, his wife, and Tullia Blaesilla, his daughter, placed this in the site granted by senatorial decree for Marcus Tullius Blaesus, son of Marcus, of the Camilian tribe, pontiff, curator of the temple of Hercules Victor, Salii, patron of the municipality.
EDCS-05802244.summary: This epitaph honors Marcus Tullius Blaesus, a local patron and priest, and was erected by his wife and daughter, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05802250.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning a possible legionary context and a person named Licinus, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05802252.translation: Gaius Aurilius, son of Caius, his second term as praetor, gave this; the same person approved it as consul.
EDCS-05802252.summary: This inscription records an act by Gaius Aurilius, who served as praetor twice and also as consul, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05802253.translation: Gaius Manlius, son of Acilius, consul for the people of Ariminum.
EDCS-05802253.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Manlius, who was consul for the people of Ariminum.

EDCS-05802254.translation: Poublilia Turpilia, wife of Gnaeus, gave this image as a gift to Diana for her son Gnaeus.
