EDCS-05802254.summary: This inscription records a votive gift by Poublilia Turpilia, wife of Gnaeus, to Diana for her son.

EDCS-05802256.translation: Lucius Acilius Ocallus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-05802256.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Acilius Ocallus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-05802257.translation: To Lucius Annius Rufus, son of Lucius, quaestor of Aricia. His wife Prima.
EDCS-05802257.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Annius Rufus, quaestor of Aricia, by his wife Prima.

EDCS-05802258.translation: Gaius Fundilius Doctus, attendant of Apollo. Gaius Fundilius Doctus, attendant of Apollo.
EDCS-05802258.summary: This inscription records the name and role of Gaius Fundilius Doctus, an attendant of Apollo, repeated for emphasis.

EDCS-05802259.translation: To Fundilia, daughter of Caius, patroness.
EDCS-05802259.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fundilia, daughter of Caius, who held the title of patroness.

EDCS-06100061.translation: Aulus Livius Anteros, quinquennial magistrate of the guild of Ostian roofers, for the 17th lustrum, and a six-man official of the Augustan period, working among the naval shipwrights, made this for himself and for Livia Marcellina, his freedwoman wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-06100061.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Aulus Livius Anteros, a quinquennial magistrate of the Ostian roofers' guild, for himself, his wife, and their descendants.

EDCS-06100075.translation: From the accounts of Lucilius Hermes.
EDCS-06100075.summary: This inscription indicates that the following text details expenses or records from the accounts of Lucilius Hermes.

EDCS-06100077.translation: From the accounts of Olympus Caesar.
EDCS-06100077.summary: This inscription indicates that the following text details expenses or records from the accounts of Olympus Caesar.

EDCS-06100096.translation: Marcus Aeficius, son of Marcus, and Aulus Saufeius, son of Lucius, [dedicated this] to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-06100096.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Marcus Aeficius and Aulus Saufeius to Jupiter.

EDCS-06100111.translation: Valerius Paetus, son of Marcius, and Sextus Flavius, son of Lucius, took care to build the theatre from Mars's money to the amount of 12,000 sesterces; the rest of the money was contributed by the pagus Vescinus.
EDCS-06100111.summary: This inscription records the construction of a theatre funded by Valerius Paetus and Sextus Flavius, with additional funds from the pagus Vescinus.

EDCS-06100112.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication to Marcus Orofius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-06100120.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication to Caius Orofius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-06100123.translation: Urbicus, a man worthy of peace, was buried with his parents eight days after the consulship of the most distinguished man Basilius, the consul, who was the chief physician.
EDCS-06100123.summary: This inscription records the burial of Urbicus eight days after the consulship of the consul Basilius, who was a chief physician.

EDCS-06500013.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Baberius Hymnus lived 8 months and 5 days. His mother, Baberia Phoebebe.
EDCS-06500013.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Publius Baberius Hymnus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-06500015.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely dedicating a monument to Lucius Caelius Pan[...].

EDCS-06500018.translation: Floria Albana, freedwoman of Publius, made this for her husband Auctus, freedman of Caius, and for themselves.
EDCS-06500018.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife, Floria Albana, dedicating a monument to her husband, Auctus, and for themselves.

EDCS-06500023.translation: To Caius Curtius Primigenius. His sister Curtia Saturnina.
EDCS-06500023.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Curtia Saturnina to her brother, Caius Curtius Primigenius.

EDCS-06500025.translation: Dionisius. He lived 9 years and 5 months. To his most loving daughter.
EDCS-06500025.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Dionisius at a young age, dedicated by his loving daughter.

EDCS-06500028.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Epillia Put<e=I>olana.

EDCS-06500031.translation: Fronto lived for two years and six months. Octavia Psecas, his mother, paid from her own resources.
EDCS-06500031.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of Fronto, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-06500033.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Liberalis as a freedman.

EDCS-06500034.translation: Phileros, freedman of Numerius Marius, son of Numerius.
EDCS-06500034.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Phileros as a freedman with his patron's full name.

EDCS-06500036.translation: Quintus Mucius Epaphra [and] Quintus Mucius [---] Pappos and Valentis and Helena and Iusta.
EDCS-06500036.summary: This inscription likely records names associated with a tomb or property, possibly listing family members or heirs.

EDCS-06500037.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Dibus as a freedman.

EDCS-06500038.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Gaza as a freedman.

EDCS-06500048.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name of a freedwoman and possibly her patron.

EDCS-06500053.translation: The burial of the holy memory of Grammatius, bishop, on the 8th day before the Kalends of February, under the consulship of Probus, a most distinguished man, who lived in peace for 41 years.
EDCS-06500053.summary: This is a Christian inscription recording the death and burial date of Bishop Grammatius, with a reference to the consul Probus.

EDCS-06500055.translation: The burial of the holy presbyter Rusticus, on the 6th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-06500055.summary: This is a Christian inscription recording the death date of the presbyter Rusticus.

EDCS-06500059.translation: To Publius Vettienus, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe, son of Scaevus Baridus, by the arbitration of Quintus Campilius Celer. To Publius Vettienus, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe, son of Scaevus, by the arbitration of Quintus Campilius, son of Quintus, Celer.
EDCS-06500059.summary: This inscription appears to record a legal arbitration or testament concerning Publius Vettienus, possibly related to inheritance or property, mentioning his father and grandfather.

EDCS-06500063.translation: To Domina Florentia, from her husband Luxurius.
EDCS-06500063.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by a husband to his wife, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-06500064.translation: To Gnaeus Pomponius Hyllus, from Pomponia Vitalis, freedwoman of Gnaeus, for herself and O[...].
EDCS-06500064.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by a freedwoman to her patron and herself, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-06500067.summary: This fragmented inscription contains personal names and is too damaged to provide further details about its content or date.

EDCS-06500069.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple personal attribution, possibly marking ownership or a dedication, with a personal name that could date it to the imperial period.

EDCS-06500078.translation: Here within lies the true, sure, and best man, Publius Octavius Rufus, decurion.
EDCS-06500078.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Octavius Rufus, a decurion, indicating he is buried here.

EDCS-06500079.summary: This is a dedication from Tiberius Claudius to someone named Alcimius.

EDCS-07000150.translation: Publius Aelius Agathemer, freedman of Augustus, an Augustalis and quinquennalis, had this made for himself, his freedwoman Aelia Helpis, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 24 feet in front, 40 feet in the land.
EDCS-07000150.summary: This funerary inscription records the self-funded burial arrangements of a prominent freedman, Publius Aelius Agathemer, who held local magistracies, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-07000151.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. From his heirs Euresis, Isidora, and Marcella, to their well-deserving father, Caius Agrius Felix, an Augustalis.
EDCS-07000151.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by the heirs to a deceased father, Caius Agrius Felix, who was an Augustalis, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-07000152.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Aquilius Dionysius, an Augustalis and quinquennalis, curator of the association of shipowners of the Adriatic Sea, and Nonia Faustina, daughter of Marcus, [made this] for their son Quintus Aquilius Dionysius, who lived 7 years, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. It is 20 feet in front, and adjacent to this monument is an apparatus room.
EDCS-07000152.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates a young boy, Quintus Aquilius Dionysius, and also includes his father, a prominent curator of a maritime association, and his mother, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-07000156.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Canneius Zosimus made [this] for his well-deserving son, Marcus Canneius Zosimianus, a decurion, an admitted member, and a designated flamini of the deified Vespasian, who lived 21 years, 5 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-07000156.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a father, Marcus Canneius Zosimus, to his son, Marcus Canneius Zosimianus, a young man with significant local civic and religious responsibilities, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-07000158.translation: To the departed spirits. Cassius Augustalis, son of Cassius, of the Palatine tribe, a priest of the deified Titus, a decurion elected by decree of the council, made this for his incomparable son, his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-07000158.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Cassius Augustalis for his son, indicating his own civic and religious status.

EDCS-07000159.translation: Claudius Numisianus, son of Tiberius, of the Palatine tribe, prefect of the Third Cohort, procurator of Augustus, patron of the colony of Ostia, made this for himself, his ancestors, and for Egrilia Pulchra, daughter of Aulus, his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen of both sexes, and their descendants.
EDCS-07000159.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Claudius Numisianus, detailing his imperial and civic roles, for himself and his family.

EDCS-07000160.translation: Agathopus, freedman, made this for his patron Proto, former Augustalis, and also quinquennalis.
EDCS-07000160.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for his patron, who held important civic and religious offices.

EDCS-07000163.translation: To the departed spirits. Aulus Egrilius Polytimus Amerimnianus, freedman of Aulus, a debt collector and silversmith, former Augustalis and quinquennalis, made this for himself, and for his most sacred wife, Junia Aphrodite, and for his excellent freedman Egrilius Onesimus Polytimianus, and for his adopted children Egrilia Irene and Egrilia Smyrna, and Aulus Egrilius Florus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument, twenty-three feet in front and thirteen and a half feet in depth, will not pass to a future heir. Egrilis Trophimus, Ariston, and Farnasus, freedmen, [also included].
EDCS-07000163.summary: A large funerary monument established by Aulus Egrilius Polytimus Amerimnianus for his family and freedmen, detailing its dimensions and succession clause, and indicating his various professional and civic roles.

EDCS-07000166.translation: Gaius Junius Felix gave a gift to the decurions.
EDCS-07000166.summary: A record of a gift made by Gaius Junius Felix to the local council members.

EDCS-07000168.translation: To the departed spirits of Manius Obellius Fortunatus, a decurion.
EDCS-07000168.summary: A simple funerary dedication for a decurion named Manius Obellius Fortunatus.

EDCS-07000169.translation: To the departed spirits of Ovinia Villa, daughter of Gaius, most sacred. Gaius Ovinius Antonianus, scribe of the guild of waxworkers of Ostia, son of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, made this for his most dutiful daughter, and for Ovinia Januaria, his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. Marcus Perennius Polycarpus made the adjacent plot for his most devoted Ovinus Festus and his family, and for all their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. And in front, twenty-one feet in front and seventeen feet in depth.
EDCS-07000169.summary: A complex funerary monument with additions, set up by Gaius Ovinius Antonianus for his daughter and wife, and later expanded by Marcus Perennius Polycarpus, detailing familial relationships and dimensions.

EDCS-07000172.translation: His adopted son, for himself and for his beloved wife Ara, his dearest, and for his most dutiful daughter Prima, who lived ten months and days. Aulus Egrilius Primigenius Minor Augustalis, freedman of the Auli freedman Priamus, [made this] for Priamus, pious, faithful, and a abstinent helper.
EDCS-07000172.summary: A funerary dedication by Aulus Egrilius Primigenius Minor Augustalis for his family and for Priamus, a freedman who served as a helper, indicating familial and adopted relationships.

EDCS-07000174.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Uttedius Eleutherus, former Augustalis, quinquennalis, and quinquennalis of the carpenters of Ostia.
EDCS-07000174.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Uttedius Eleutherus, a former Augustalis and quinquennalis who was also a master carpenter.

EDCS-07000179.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Caltilius Epagathus, former Augustalis, and also quinquennalis.
EDCS-07000179.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Caltilius Epagathus, who held the positions of former Augustalis and quinquennalis.

EDCS-07000180.translation: Gaius Iulius Rammius Eutychus made this for himself and for his patron Gaius Iulius Rammius Hilarus, who deserved well, and for his freedwoman wife Iulia Euvennia, who deserved well, and for his daughter Iulia Ingenua, and for his freedwoman daughter Iulia Felicitas, and for his freedwoman Iulia, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. 15 feet in front, 30 feet in the field. This monument will not pass to an heir of an outside family.
EDCS-07000180.summary: This funerary inscription records a man, Gaius Iulius Rammius Eutychus, who built his own tomb for himself and his family, specifying its dimensions and inheritance restrictions.

EDCS-07000184.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pomponius Celsus, a quinquennial and sevir Augustalis, made this for himself while alive, and for his wife Furia Maximilla, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. 20 feet in front, 41 feet in the field.
EDCS-07000184.summary: This epitaph records a man, Lucius Pomponius Celsus, who built his own tomb for himself and his family, specifying its dimensions and his public roles.

EDCS-07000189.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Serapis, and Hercules. Marcus Iulius Chrysophorus, a quinquennial and sevir Augustalis, together with his son Aelianus, who is also called Serapion, and with Zosimus, together with his son Philippus, have fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-07000189.summary: This dedication records a vow fulfilled by Marcus Iulius Chrysophorus, his son Aelianus, and Zosimus, along with his son Philippus, to Jupiter, Serapis, and Hercules.

EDCS-07000192.translation: To Aspasia, my wife, sleeping in peace, and to Sextius Leo, if the god permits.
EDCS-07000192.summary: This dedication is to a wife, Aspasia, and possibly a son, Sextius Leo, whose fate is uncertain.

EDCS-07000193.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Combarissia, a most excellent woman.
EDCS-07000193.summary: This is a short epitaph dedicated to Combarissia.

EDCS-07000194.translation: Julius Petronius Asclepiades and Petronia Procula made an eternal home for themselves and for their sons and for any agnatic relatives among them and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, by concession from Publius Aelius Marcellus Mitilianus.
EDCS-07000194.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a tomb by Julius Petronius Asclepiades and Petronia Procula for themselves and their descendants, with a concession from Publius Aelius Marcellus Mitilianus.

EDCS-07000196.translation: Ichthys. For Caricus's dearest wife, Cornelia Tyche, who lived 23 years.
EDCS-07000196.summary: This epitaph, using the Christian symbol Ichthys, records the death of Cornelia Tyche at the age of 23.

EDCS-07000200.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Potheta, who lived 7 years, 2 months, and 23 days. Her father, Threptus.
EDCS-07000200.summary: This epitaph records the death of a child named Potheta, who lived for 7 years, 2 months, and 23 days, and was honored by her father.

EDCS-07000217.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly honoring a person named Appius Publius Silvius.

EDCS-07000222.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Servilia Rhodine, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Servilius Iustus made this for his excellent mother.
EDCS-07000222.summary: This epitaph records Lucius Servilius Iustus honoring his mother, Servilia Rhodine.

EDCS-07000223.translation: To the Divine Shades. Tiana Arcia, wife, with whom she lived 30 years, and her daughter Prastinia Pratiana made this for Prastina Felici.
EDCS-07000223.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife and daughter for Prastina Felici, likely a relative, with details on their shared lifespan.

EDCS-07000224.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Nnia, daughter of Caius; for Victoria, daughter of Caius; for Oufentina Rufa; [and for] Oufentius Niger, son of Caius.
EDCS-07000224.summary: A funerary inscription listing several individuals, likely family members, to whom cult is paid.

EDCS-07000239.translation: To Isis Regina. Lucius Figillius Fortunatus, *sevir* again, *Augustalis*, priest, a plot of land was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-07000239.summary: A dedication to the goddess Isis Regina by Lucius Figillius Fortunatus, who held several religious and civic offices, with the land granted by local authorities.

EDCS-07000256.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Domitia Elate.
EDCS-07000256.summary: A funerary dedication for Domitia Elate.

EDCS-07000258.translation: May you always use [this] happily. Felicita, live well.
EDCS-07000258.summary: A brief funerary or perhaps tomb inscription with a wish for the deceased's well-being in the afterlife.

EDCS-07000259.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Ciminia Felicitas, dearest wife, who lived 60 years and 10 days, who departed in peace on the seventh day before the Kalends of June. Her husband, the most illustrious Quintus Geminius Felix, with his son.
EDCS-07000259.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband and son for Ciminia Felicitas, providing her age, date of death, and the husband's high status.

EDCS-07400120.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Nnia, daughter of Publius, of the Sebotis tribe. Quintus Minucius Marcellus, son of Quintus, of the Palatina tribe, to his dearest, most dutiful, most chaste wife, who never wanted to go out in public, or to the baths, or anywhere without me. I married her as a virgin at 14 years of age, from whom I have a daughter. With her I saw a sweet time of light, she made me happy. But I would have preferred you to live; she was my happiness. If I had left you surviving me. She lived 21 years, 2 months, 21 days.
EDCS-07400120.summary: A highly personal funerary epitaph from Quintus Minucius Marcellus to his wife, detailing their relationship, her life, and her age at death, reflecting deep affection and grief.

EDCS-07400122.translation: Lucius Spurius Felix made this for his patron and for himself, and for Spuria Luci, freedwoman, his patroness; for Pieris, freedwoman, freedwoman wife of Spuria Luci; for Primilla, freedwoman, daughter of Spuria Luci, freedwoman; for Lucius Spurius, freedman, son of Lucius, and for the freedmen and freedwomen of the women; for Felix, freedman; for Sabbatides, freedwoman, freedwoman of Spuria Luci; for Secundilla, daughter, freedwoman, of Spuria Luci; for Satria Sabina; and for all their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, on condition that they do not sue Cnaeus Pacilius Abinnaeus.
EDCS-07400122.summary: A complex funerary dedication set up by Lucius Spurius Felix for himself, his patron, freedpersons, and their descendants, including a specific legal stipulation against suing another individual.

EDCS-07400123.translation: Claudius Iunianus [made this] for his dearest wife, Egnatia Rhodilla.
EDCS-07400123.summary: A funerary dedication by Claudius Iunianus for his wife, Egnatia Rhodilla.

EDCS-07400124.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Thalassa, daughter, who lived 2 years, 5 months, 17 days. Parents.
EDCS-07400124.summary: A funerary dedication by parents for their young daughter, Thalassa, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-07400128.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Onesimus, son of Stephanius, made this for himself and his nearest heir.
EDCS-07400128.summary: A funerary dedication by Onesimus for himself and his heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400130.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Servandus made this for Tyches, his fellow slave, a deserving woman, and for himself.
EDCS-07400130.summary: A funerary dedication by Servandus for his fellow slave Tyches and himself, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400131.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Milesia made this for her dearest husband Servilius Logismus, with whom she lived for 30 years.
EDCS-07400131.summary: A funerary dedication by Milesia for her husband Servilius Logismus, noting their 30 years of marriage, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400132.translation: Aulus Caedicius Successus, Augustalis priest, also quinquennial official, curator of the shipowners of the Adriatic Sea, also quinquennial official, made this for himself, and for Caedicia Themis, his freedwoman, and for Aulus Iulius Epagathus, and for Pontulena Pyrallis, his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 9 feet, in depth 35 feet.
EDCS-07400132.summary: A funerary dedication by Aulus Caedicius Successus, a prominent local official and maritime trade curator, for his family and freedpersons, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400133.translation: He ordered this to be erected to the Genius of the association of shipowners of the Adriatic Sea, from Titus son of Sergia, perpetual quinquennial official.
EDCS-07400133.summary: An honorary inscription dedicated to the Genius of the Adriatic shipowners' guild by Titus Sergia, a long-standing official of the association, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400145.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Cornelius Hygiaenon made this for Cornelia Fortunata, his deserving wife, and for himself.
EDCS-07400145.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Cornelius Hygiaenon for his wife Cornelia Fortunata and himself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400147.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Agapetus made this for his deserving son Agius, who lived for 5 years, 1 month, [and some] days.
EDCS-07400147.summary: A funerary dedication by Agapetus for his son Agius, recording his young age at death, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400148.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Eraclia made this for her dearest husband Chrysophaetus and for her most pious son Theodorus, a deserving person, who lived for 16 years and 15 days.
EDCS-07400148.summary: A funerary dedication by Eraclia for her husband Chrysophaetus and son Theodorus, noting the son's age at death, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400151.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. His sons made this for Marcus Sentius Alexander, an honorable veteran of the Third Cyrenaic Legion, a deserving man.
EDCS-07400151.summary: A funerary dedication by sons for their father Marcus Sentius Alexander, a veteran of the III Cyrenaica legion, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400152.translation: Genius of Pu, procurator of Augustus. Claudius Livianus, tribune of the V Praetorian cohort.
EDCS-07400152.summary: An inscription mentioning a procuratorial official and a tribune of the Praetorian Guard, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400153.translation: Titus Octacilius, the magistrate, [dedicated] the temple.
EDCS-07400153.summary: This is a dedication of a temple by Titus Octacilius, who held the office of magistrate.

EDCS-07400157.translation: To Lucius Visellius, freedman of Gaius Antonius, Onesimus.
EDCS-07400157.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Visellius, the freedman of Gaius Antonius, by Onesimus.

EDCS-07400160.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Ulpius Didianus made this for his most cherished wife, Octavia Acta.
EDCS-07400160.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Ulpius Didianus for his wife Octavia Acta.

EDCS-07400161.translation: Gaius Fundanus Amarantus donated to Marcus Co[---].
EDCS-07400161.summary: This inscription records a donation by Gaius Fundanus Amarantus to Marcus Co[---].

EDCS-07400165.translation: To Aurelia Phronime, freedwoman of Publius, from her parents.
EDCS-07400165.summary: This is a dedication by parents to their daughter Aurelia Phronime, a freedwoman.

EDCS-07400167.translation: Valerius Vitalis and his wife C[---] made this for their dearest son, Gaius Julius Felix, who deserved well. He lived 32 years.
EDCS-07400167.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Valerius Vitalis and his wife for their son Gaius Julius Felix.

EDCS-07400170.translation: Paculus, the prefect, for the duovir. Pantuleia, Publius Numisius, freedman of Publius, Tertius.
EDCS-07400170.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including a prefect and a freedman, possibly related to a public office or building.

EDCS-07600095.translation: Egrilia Daphne made this for herself and for her son Aulus Egrilius Paterno, Roman knight, aedile, lictor curiatus, flamen of the deified Vespasian, performing the rites of Vulcan, and for her husband Aulus Egrilius Onesimus, coactor, seviri Augustales, and quinquennalis for five continuous years, and curator of them, and for Aulus Egrilius Maro, most worthy, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In the front 40 feet, in the field 35 feet.
EDCS-07600095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Egrilia Daphne for herself, her son, her husband, and descendants, detailing his various public and religious offices and the dimensions of the property.

EDCS-07600098.translation: Caius Lutatius Pinthia, son of Lucius, gave this gift to Apollo, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-07600098.summary: This is a votive offering to Apollo by Caius Lutatius Pinthia.

EDCS-07600105.translation: Avianius Vindicianus, a most distinguished man and former consular governor of Campania, saw to the erection of statues at the crossroads of the city of Tarracina.
EDCS-07600105.summary: This inscription records that Avianius Vindicianus commissioned the placement of statues at a crossroads in Tarracina.

EDCS-07600106.translation: Marcus Crispinus, one of the fifteen men in charge of sacred rites, had this constructed with public funds, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-07600106.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by M. Crispinus, a member of the quindecimviri sacris faciundis, during the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-07600122.translation: To our lords, Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, most noble princes.
EDCS-07600122.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-07600138.translation: Gellius Venerius, placed here, who lived for three years, seven months, and two days. His mother placed this for her dearest son. Placed on the Ides of June.
EDCS-07600138.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Gellius Venerius, commemorating his life and burial by his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000857.translation: A formal agreement was made with Caius Sulpicius Zenon, freedman of Zenobius, from Tyre, for the first hour of the Ides of June. Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus asked for the security that 1200 sesterces be given, and Zenon, freedman of Zenobius from Tyre, promised his security. Done at Puteoli on the 5th Ides of June, when Faustus Cornelius Sulla Felix and Quintus Marcius Barea Soranus were consuls.
EDCS-08000857.summary: This inscription documents a financial agreement (vadimonium) for a debt of 1200 sesterces, finalized at Puteoli with specific consuls and parties, including a freedman.

EDCS-08000867.translation: A formal agreement was made with Trupho, son of Potamon, from Alexandria, for the first hour of the day before the Kalends of October. Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus asked for the security that 1000 sesterces be given, and Trupho, son of Potamon from Alexandria, promised his security. Done at Rome in the Forum of Augustus before the triumphal statue of Gnaeus Sentius Saturninus, at the third hour, when [consuls' names are missing] were consuls.
EDCS-08000867.summary: This inscription records a financial agreement (vadimonium) for 1000 sesterces made in the Forum of Augustus in Rome, mentioning specific parties and a statue of Gnaeus Sentius Saturninus.

EDCS-08000873.translation: Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus stood at the third hour, because he had a formal agreement with Caius [Caesar Augustus Germanicus]...
EDCS-08000873.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus appearing for a legal agreement (vadimonium), likely during the reign of Caligula.

EDCS-08000893.translation: Under the consulship of Caius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and Lucius Apronius Caesianus, on the day before the Nones of February, Caius Sulpicius Faustus testified that he had produced the marked money with the musts [---] to Priscus and [---].
EDCS-08000893.summary: This inscription documents a legal testimony by Caius Sulpicius Faustus regarding the production of marked money, occurring during the consulship of Caligula and Apronius Caesianus.

EDCS-08000917.translation: Tablets of Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus, expenses: 1500 sesterces.
EDCS-08000917.summary: This is a fragment likely recording financial expenses or accounts related to Caius Sulpicius Cinnamus, with a sum of 1500 sesterces indicated.

EDCS-08000930.translation: Under the consulship of Marcus Acilius Julianus and Publius Nonius Asprenas, three days before the Kalends of April, in Dikaiarchia. Menelaos, son of Eirenaios the Ceramieta, wrote: 'I have received from Primus, slave of Publius Attius Severus, one thousand denarii from a sealed charter of freight, which I will repay according to the charter of freight that I have made with him. I have appointed Marcus Barbatius Celer as guarantor for the payment of the aforementioned one thousand denarii.' Quintus Aelius Romanus wrote at the request and command of Marcus Barbatius Celer, because he did not know letters, that he pledges his good faith for those thousand denarii written above to Primus, slave of Publius Attius Severus, for Menelaos, son of Eirenaios the Ceramieta, as written above. By Quintus Aelius Romanus Abascas.
EDCS-08000930.summary: This bilingual inscription (Greek and Latin) records a complex financial transaction involving a debt of 1000 denarii secured by a charter of freight, with a guarantor and a slave acting as intermediary, dated to the consulship of Acilius Julianus and Nonius Asprenas.

EDCS-08000953.translation: Under the consulship of Lucius Vitellius, son of Lucius, Messalla Vipstanus Gallus, on the 16th day before the Kalends of September, Caius Sulpicius Faustus wrote that he had from Tiberius Julius, freedman of Augustus, Myrtilus, [---] 58 pounds [---] at a price of nine denarii per pound [---] was secured by the laws [---] in the year [---] on the first day before the 12th Kalends of March [---] concerning this agreement [---] two hundred thousand sesterces [---] done at Puteoli.
EDCS-08000953.summary: This is a fragment of a legal or financial document from Puteoli, recording a transaction involving Caius Sulpicius Faustus and Tiberius Julius Myrtilus, with specific dates and monetary amounts mentioned.

EDCS-08000961.translation: Gaius Avilius Cinnamus, by his own guarantee, ordered that the sum owed to me by him be paid, executed in Puteoli.
EDCS-08000961.summary: This inscription records a financial guarantee by Gaius Avilius Cinnamus concerning a debt owed to the unnamed recipient, executed in Puteoli, likely in the 1st century BC or AD.

EDCS-08000962.translation: 40,000 sesterces. In Puteoli, executed by Felix, slave of Gaius Julius Trophius, freedman of Gnaeus Pollis Hermogenes, freedman of Gnaeus Pollis Tertius.
EDCS-08000962.summary: This inscription records a financial transaction of 40,000 sesterces, executed in Puteoli and mentioning slaves and freedmen of various prominent individuals, likely from the 1st century BC or AD.

EDCS-08000963.translation: In Puteoli, executed by L. Laelius, freedman of C. Nummius Stasimus, freedman of C. Nummius.
EDCS-08000963.summary: This inscription records a legal execution or transaction in Puteoli, involving freedmen of C. Nummius Stasimus and L. Laelius, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-08000964.translation: Gaurus, slave of Gaius Trebonius Auctus. Epaphroditus, slave of Gaius Marcius. [---]eri, slave of Gaurus, slave of Gaius Trebonius Auctus.
EDCS-08000964.summary: This inscription lists slaves and their owners, Gaius Trebonius Auctus and Gaius Marcius, likely a record of ownership or a sales document from the 1st century BC or AD.

EDCS-08000972.translation: From L. Salle[nius]... M. Marci... Cn. Polli... L. Anni... C. Senti... A. Noni... L. Laelius Ho[--] M. Antoni...
EDCS-08000972.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a contract, business dealing, or property ownership in Puteoli, with a date likely in the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-08000974.translation: Paid for Gaius La[--] on the Ides of January.
EDCS-08000974.summary: This inscription records a payment made on January 13th for an individual named Gaius Laelius, likely a financial record from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-08000975.summary: This inscription simply records the name Gaius Sulpicius Faustus, possibly a dedication or a record of ownership from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-08201356.translation: Fusca, daughter, placed (this) for Marcus Lucilius Faustus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-08201356.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Fusca dedicated a monument to Marcus Lucilius Faustus, son of Marcus, likely from the 1st century AD.

EDCS-08300139.translation: Eutyches lived 7 years, 4 months, and 11 days. Quintus Vibius Chimarus (placed this for his) dearest son.
EDCS-08300139.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short life of Eutyches and dedicated by his father, Quintus Vibius Chimarus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-08400102.translation: Maximus, by the guidance of a divine mind, once [built?] these baths...
EDCS-08400102.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that appears to record the construction of baths by Maximus, guided by divine inspiration, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08500094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Pandusinus, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-08500101.translation: To Claudia Philotera, from Gaius Claudius
EDCS-08500101.summary: This is a dedication to Claudia Philotera by Gaius Claudius.

EDCS-08500105.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription stating that Gaius Terentius Lucilianus created the object or monument.

EDCS-08500141.translation: From the love of our city, the order rejoices in glory; the people of Pavonenses made this under the supervision of Acerius
EDCS-08500141.summary: This is a public works inscription detailing a monument built by the people of Pavonenses and supervised by Acerius, motivated by civic pride.

EDCS-08500145.summary: This is a votive inscription recording that Vincentius fulfilled a vow he had made.

EDCS-08600080.translation: Publius Valerius Philtairus undertook, at his own expense, to have a temple to Venus built
EDCS-08600080.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to Venus, funded and supervised by Publius Valerius Philtairus.

EDCS-08600084.translation: The matrons of Aeretina gave this in recognition of merit
EDCS-08600084.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by the matrons of Aeretina, honoring someone for their merit.

EDCS-08600105.translation: Here rests in peace Salustius, a boy who lived approximately 11 years and 10 months, laid to rest on the 4th day before the Ides of March, three days after the consulship of the most distinguished consul Basilius
EDCS-08600105.summary: This is a late antique funerary inscription for a young boy named Salustius, providing details of his life and death.

EDCS-08600115.translation: Publius Tillius Dexiades set this up for himself and for Syrtis, his freedwoman, and for Harmonia, his freedwoman, and for all of his own. This tomb has Harmonia and Syrtis. The unfortunate elder Dexiades placed this for his wives.
EDCS-08600115.summary: This is a bilingual funerary inscription for Publius Tillius Dexiades, his freedwomen Harmonia and Syrtis, and his family, including Greek text.

EDCS-08900147.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iunia Agathemeris made this for her dearest sister, Iunia Terentina.
EDCS-08900147.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Iunia Terentina by her sister, Iunia Agathemeris.

EDCS-08900148.translation: Saturninus, freedman of the Emperors, and Cocceia Macedonica, not very fortunate, made this for four months and seventeen days and nights.
EDCS-08900148.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 2nd century CE, records Saturninus and Cocceia Macedonica as the dedicants of a tomb for a deceased individual, possibly themselves, indicating a relatively short period of ownership or use.

EDCS-08900151.translation: Gaius Rubrius, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, aedile, prefect of the allies on warships.
EDCS-08900151.summary: This inscription, likely from the 1st century BCE or 1st century CE, lists the career of Gaius Rubrius, highlighting his civic and military offices.

EDCS-08900163.translation: To the most fortunate Diadumenus, his freedwoman Flavia Coetes, for his deserts.
EDCS-08900163.summary: This dedication, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, records Flavia Coetes honoring her patron Diadumenus.

EDCS-08900798.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Voltidius Felicissimus made this for himself while alive, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, except for my abominable freedman Hilarus, so that he may have no access to this monument.
EDCS-08900798.summary: This is a self-dedicatory tomb inscription from likely the 1st-2nd century CE, where Gaius Voltidius Felicissimus excludes a specific freedman from burial rights.

EDCS-08900803.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Hedone made this for her husband Quintus Caecilius Tertius, well deserving and the best.
EDCS-08900803.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, records Caecilia Hedone dedicating a tomb to her deserving husband.

EDCS-08900805.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Vibidius Papias made this for his most pious and well-deserving wife Gorge.
EDCS-08900805.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, records Titus Vibidius Papias dedicating a tomb to his wife Gorge.

EDCS-08900806.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Flaviae I, [daughter of] Titus Flavius Cam, who lived 11 years.
EDCS-08900806.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, records the death of Flaviae I, daughter of Titus Flavius Cam.

EDCS-08900808.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Des and Daphne made this for their relative.
EDCS-08900808.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, records Des and Daphne dedicating a tomb to a relative.

EDCS-08900812.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Salvius made this for his well-deserving wife Hesychiae, and for Hesychus and Chreste, her parents, for their most pious daughter, who lived 16 years, 10 months, and 27 days.
EDCS-08900812.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, records Salvius, along with Hesychiae's parents, dedicating a tomb to her after her death at a young age.

EDCS-08900813.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Orbius Dionysius made this for himself and for his wife Heorte, a twice-married woman without fault, Heorte Dionysius lived well with Silvanus.
EDCS-08900813.summary: This is a self-dedicatory funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE, with a somewhat unusual and potentially boastful or complicated personal statement about the deceased wife.

EDCS-08900814.translation: To Aeolis, freedwoman of Bia, and to Hedone, freedwoman of Gaius Aulus, from her own property.
EDCS-08900814.summary: This is a dedication by two freedwomen to each other, likely on a tomb or a shared monument.

EDCS-08900815.summary: This appears to be a dedication to the god Pantheus by Aphrodilla, with an abbreviation of unknown meaning.

EDCS-08900816.summary: A funerary inscription stating that Gaius Julius Trophimus erected the monument.

EDCS-08900817.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Albus, husband most holy to C. Elvius Romanus.
EDCS-08900817.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for the deceased Albus, husband of C. Elvius Romanus.

EDCS-08900823.summary: This is likely a fragmentary funerary inscription naming Titus Flavius Quintillus.

EDCS-08900831.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Septicia, the best.
EDCS-08900831.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for the deceased Septicia, described as 'the best'.

EDCS-08900833.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Marcus Varenus Valentinus, their dearest son, his parents made this.
EDCS-08900833.summary: A funerary inscription from parents dedicating a monument to their son, Marcus Varenus Valentinus.

EDCS-08900834.translation: May Nicerotus, freedman of Augustus, and Actaronia be well. Located in a happy place. A.s. happily.
EDCS-08900834.summary: A funerary inscription wishing well-being to Nicerotus and Actaronia, with a reference to their burial place.

EDCS-08900847.translation: To Vettia Secundilla, daughter of Titus, wife of Vettius Helioterus, and Eleuteris, freedmen and heirs, for their most excellent patroness.
EDCS-08900847.summary: A funerary inscription from the freedmen and heirs of Vettia Secundilla, dedicating a monument to her.

EDCS-08900864.translation: Here rests in peace Felix, servant of God, who lived more or less years, buried on the Ides of January, 7 days after the consulship of the most distinguished vir, Basil.
EDCS-08900864.summary: A Christian funerary inscription recording the burial of Felix, a servant of God, with a precise date based on the consulship of Basil.

EDCS-08900869.translation: Under the consulship of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, for the second time, and Caesar Decimus Clodius Septimius Albinus, with Marcus Aurelius Appolaustus the Younger serving as Tribune of the Plebs, on the sixth day before the Kalends of January. Present were Caelius Asiaticus, Julius Aurelianus, Julius Caillianus. The opinion of all the phraters concerning this matter was proposed as follows: Since Munatius Hilarianus, a citizen of rightful standing and patriotic spirit, seeing our phratry as unadorned and ancient, and with a brilliant and magnanimous disposition, has adorned the house with varied and the finest, rarest stones, and with luxurious craftsmanship, and has made the roof, spending not a single penny of money or sparing any expense for this purpose. He has made a more solemn dining hall for the phraters of Artemis, and for Artemis herself, after whom the phratry is named, he has constructed a temple worthy of both the goddess and our common piety. It has been decreed by the phraters of Artemis to repay his great goodwill and generosity: first, by honoring him in his disposition and intention, considering him the most intimate, protector, and father, and wishing him a long life in happiness; then, also, to grant him honors according to our ability, which are fitting: the erection of four statues in the phratry, two of Munatius Hilarianus himself, the patriot, and two of his son Marius Verus, the hero; also to erect images in the phratry with golden shields, and to offer him fifty entire plots of land, and to record him in the phratry free of charge. So that not only has our phratry been adorned by us with luxury and beauty of construction and solemnity befitting a shrine, but also by the multitude of those who dwell there. The phratry, honoring Munatius Hilarianus the patriot, has ratified the decree. Caninius Heracleides, the curator of the phratry, has confirmed the decree. Munatius Hilarianus to the phraters of Artemis, greetings. The honors which you have decreed to me, and the gifts in return for my goodwill and eagerness, I have gladly accepted, not for the greatness of what you have shown in your generosity towards me and my son, your hero, but rather for the intention of those giving, because I have recognized you as good and just from your reciprocations. Therefore, I decline the forty plots of land which you offered me, being content with fifteen of these, and with the four images and the four statues. For me, one inscription and one bronze statue will be sufficient. Equal honors are also for the departed. For we have many images and many statues established in your souls. You must, good men and phraters, not only keep these things before your eyes, the phratry and its adornment and luxury, but also expect other things from me. For my goodwill always and increasingly stirs my eagerness for your honor and favor. Farewell. Lucius Munatius Hilarianus to the phraters of Artemis, greetings. The honors which you have decreed to me, and the gifts in return for my goodwill and eagerness, I have gladly accepted, not for the greatness of what you have shown in your generosity towards me and my son, your hero, but mainly for the sake of your intention in decreeing them, because I have understood you to be good and just from your reciprocations. Indeed, I decline the fifty plots of land which you offered me, being content with fifteen of them, and also with the four images and the four statues. For me, one inscription and one bronze statue will suffice. But also for the honor of my son, one statue will be sufficient. For we have many images and statues established in your souls. You must, excellent men and fellow phraters, not only have these things before your eyes, the phratry and its adornment and splendor, but also expect other things from me. My disposition of spirit further urges my willingness towards your honor and favor. Farewell.
EDCS-08900869.summary: This is a decree from the phraters of Artemis in Rome, dated to the consulship of Septimius Severus and Albinus (AD 193-197), honoring Lucius Munatius Hilarianus for his generous renovation of their phratry building and temple, and his response to their honors.

EDCS-08900870.translation: To Publius Plotios Faustus, son of Publius, of the Palatine tribe, public scribe of Neapolis, and former aedile. His wife Plotia Nome. Under the consuls Lucius Acilius Strabo and Sextus Neranius Capito, with Herennius Mnester serving as Tribune of the Plebs for the 18th time, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October. Present were Julius Apollinaris, Domitius Asiaticus, Julius Proclus, Artemidorus. As concerning whom Julius Leuiuanus, the antarchon, brought forward to those in the convocation, and out of sympathy and due remembrance for those who lived honorably, the only comfort in life is the final day, comforting the last day, especially when one, along with gentleness of character and generosity towards the fatherland, has provided as much as possible, just as Plotios Faustus, combining the goodness of his character and the generosity of those entrusted with affairs, having met a jealous spirit, is worthy of testimony from those who have experienced it. Sympathizing with his mourning, we have decided to send 10 pounds of incense and, permitting the funeral arrangements, we give a place for the funeral, whichever his relatives choose, outside of sacred or rented places, of length [---] feet and width [---] feet. The place was given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08900870.summary: This is a decree from the city of Neapolis, dated to the consuls Acilius Strabo and Neranius Capito (AD 175), concerning the funeral arrangements and a gift of incense for Plotios Faustus, a respected citizen who died prematurely.

EDCS-09001173.translation: To the spirits of Marcus Aurelius Claudianus, centurion of the Legio XVI Flavia, chief centurion of the Legio XXII Primigenia, centurion of the Legio XV Apollinaris, centurion of the Legio I Minervia, centurion of the Legio VII Claudia, centurion of the Legio III Gallica, centurion of the Legio XIII Gemina, centurion of the Legio IIII Flavia, centurion of the Legio I Italica, twice centurion of the Legio II Adiutrix; by the will of the same, Vibia Laenilla, his niece and heir, had this made for her most pious uncle.
EDCS-09001173.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Aurelius Claudianus, a centurion who served in multiple legions during the Roman Empire, commissioned by his niece and heir as per his will.

EDCS-09001212.translation: At his own expense, Diogenes, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-09001212.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that Diogenes, a freedman, paid for something, possibly a tomb or a monument, himself.

EDCS-09200070.translation: Tullia Quarta, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for her freedmen and for herself.
EDCS-09200070.summary: This inscription records Tullia Quarta, a freedwoman, dedicating a space, likely a tomb, for her freedmen and herself.

EDCS-09200076.translation: Felix, son of Lucius Domitius Lupus.
EDCS-09200076.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Felix as the son of Lucius Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-09200077.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Eupor as the son of Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-09200078.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Apollonius as the son of Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-09200080.translation: To Fulvia Marcia, freedwoman of Ascanius, Caius Paconius Sabinus made this for his most faithful wife.
EDCS-09200080.summary: This is a dedication made by Caius Paconius Sabinus for his wife, Fulvia Marcia, who was a freedwoman.

EDCS-09200086.translation: The burial of Bonifatius the innocent, who lived about 6 years and 8 days, was placed on the Kalends of December.
EDCS-09200086.summary: This is a burial record for a child named Bonifatius, detailing his age at death and the date of his interment.

EDCS-09200098.translation: Belonging to Caius Lelius Expectatus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-09200098.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Lelius Expectatus, freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-09200101.translation: Follia Augenis, aged 35, is given by Aburia Primigenia, slave of Philositus Cupanius.
EDCS-09200101.summary: This funerary epitaph records Follia Augenis, aged 35, given by Aburia Primigenia.

EDCS-09200105.translation: Virius Lupus Victorius, a most distinguished man and consular of Campania, saw to it.
EDCS-09200105.summary: This inscription records that Virius Lupus Victorius, a distinguished man and former governor of Campania, was responsible for something (likely a public work or monument).

EDCS-09300150.translation: Belonging to Caius Naevius Barnas, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-09300150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Naevius Barnas, freedman of Caius.

EDCS-09300156.translation: Aulus Popillius Rufus, son of Aulus, of the Velina tribe, prefect of the engineers, and having ceased to seek for Aulus Popillius Helenus, scribe and clerk, his life is never interrupted by his own credulity; now he is free from both; his wife, Popillia Charis.
EDCS-09300156.summary: This funerary epitaph, set up by the wife Popillia Charis, commemorates Aulus Popillius Rufus and Aulus Popillius Helenus, noting Rufus's role as prefect of engineers and Helenus's as scribe, and lamenting their deaths.

EDCS-09300158.translation: The devoted people, following the example of the most splendid order, have decreed that ornaments and a statue, to last forever, be erected for Tannus Chrysantus, a most accomplished man, patron of a magnificent and noble lineage, a man of outstanding foresight and integrity, defender of citizens.
EDCS-09300158.summary: This inscription records the decision of the people to erect ornaments and a statue in honor of Tannus Chrysantus, praising his character and lineage.

EDCS-09300806.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Caius Nasennius Felix, likely for a building or object he commissioned.

EDCS-09300807.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph or ownership marker for Lucius Atilius Niger.

EDCS-09300808.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph or ownership marker for Caius Calpurnius Torquatus.

EDCS-09300809.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph or ownership marker for Aulus Egrilius Artemisianus.

EDCS-09300810.summary: This is a dedication or ownership inscription of Caius Herennius Hostilianus.

EDCS-09300811.summary: This is a dedication or ownership inscription of Lucius Sempronius Paternus, who held the office of tribune.

EDCS-09300812.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Hynnerius Rusticus, likely indicating he created the object.

EDCS-09300813.translation: From the workshop of Julius Marcianus
EDCS-09300813.summary: This inscription indicates that the object came from the workshop of Julius Marcianus.

EDCS-09300816.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Caius Nasennius Fortunatus, likely indicating he created the object.

EDCS-09300817.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Caius Nasennius Thalamus, indicating he created the object.

EDCS-09300818.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Aulus Ostiensis Trophimus, likely indicating he created the object.

EDCS-09300819.summary: This inscription identifies Caius Porcius Zosimus as a craftsman (officinator).

EDCS-09300822.translation: Lucius Baesius Serenus, Quintus Gargilius Felix, Marcus Annius, and Avi [---]
EDCS-09300822.summary: This inscription lists several names, likely associated with a commission or group, with the final name incomplete.

EDCS-09300824.translation: Nonius Rufinianus and Tigrana, with his wife, made for themselves an eternal home for their most sweet son Proiecticius, who rests in peace, aged 10 years, 3 months, and 14 days, in the sixth year of our Lord Arcadius and the consulship of the most distinguished Petronius Anicius Probus.
EDCS-09300824.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Proiecticius, commissioned by his parents Nonius Rufinianus and Tigrana, and dated to the consulship of Arcadius and Anicius Probus, likely in the late 4th or early 5th century CE.

EDCS-09300825.translation: Maturus, also known as Sucinus, son of Iuselianus.
EDCS-09300825.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Maturus and his patronymic.

EDCS-09300826.translation: Onesimus, freedman of Gaius Novius, who served as Augustalis and quinquennalis, and Novia, freedwoman of the same woman, made this for themselves and for their children, freedmen, and descendants. In front, 20 feet; in the field, 20 feet.
EDCS-09300826.summary: This is a funerary inscription by freedmen dedicating a tomb to themselves and their descendants, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-09300828.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or dedication by Sextus Annius Aphrodisius.

EDCS-09300832.translation: Quiriacus lived in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-09300832.summary: This is a brief epitaph recording the name of Quiriacus and his Christian faith.

EDCS-09300848.translation: Here lies Laeta, who lived 24 years, buried on the 9th day before the Kalends of January, during the 13th consulship of Theodosius and the 3rd of Valentinian.
EDCS-09300848.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial date of Laeta, within the context of late Roman consulships.

EDCS-09300850.translation: Burial of Ianuarius, who was buried 14 days before the Kalends of May, during the consulship of the most distinguished man, Flavius Messala.
EDCS-09300850.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Ianuarius and the date according to the consulship of Flavius Messala.

EDCS-09300851.translation: Gaudentianus is laid in this tomb, a celibate servant of God, his temporal life's race completed, awaiting the merciful judge, the burial of the holy Gaudentianus on the 5th day before the Ides [of an unspecified month].
EDCS-09300851.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Gaudentianus, a celibate servant of God, likely from the 5th century CE.

EDCS-09300852.translation: Here rests in peace the deacon, buried 14 days before the Kalends [of an unspecified month], during the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-09300852.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for an unnamed deacon, dated by the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-09300855.translation: Iohannes, who lived approximately 6 years, was buried on the 8th day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-09300855.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Iohannes, recording his approximate age and burial date.

EDCS-09300856.translation: Paula, the only child of her parents, a servant in the household of the Lord, chose to have her eternal home here and lies here rejoicing in the altars, a guest in the embrace of the martyr Felicis, who lived 6 years, buried on the 12th day before the Kalends of November, 15 years after the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-09300856.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Paula, a young girl who died after 6 years, buried in the embrace of a martyr, dated relative to the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-09300857.translation: Here rests in peace Laurentius of honored memory, a boy who lived ten years and about three months, buried on the fourth day before the Ides of March, indiction V, in the 16th year after the consulship of Bassilus.
EDCS-09300857.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph for a young boy named Laurentius, noting his age and burial date.

EDCS-09300858.translation: Here rests in peace Laurentius, who lived 40 years, buried on the day of the Nones of July, in the 16th year after the consulship of Bassilus.
EDCS-09300858.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph for Laurentius, recording his age and burial date.

EDCS-09300859.translation: To Varia Felicitas, a sacred virgin, who lived [number] years, deserving well, in peace.
EDCS-09300859.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Varia Felicitas, a sacred virgin, though the age at death is missing.

EDCS-09400108.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Born in the homeland of Puteoli, created from a family of that place, Antonius chose Ostia as his home. I was a fortunate spring (child), I had been greater in the Ostian region. Now I am buried here. Such was my affection that when I lived, I lived well in Ostia. Having accomplished many things, I left my home for the heavens. This is the eternal home. Now you, Lucius Antonius Eglectus, begin from the beginning, a sign. He made this place for himself and his own, a place granted by Publius Tele[---].
EDCS-09400108.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Antonius Eglectus, a native of Puteoli who lived and died in Ostia, commissioned by himself and dedicated by Publius Tele[---].

EDCS-09400109.translation: To our Lords, the most invincible Emperors, Flavius Honorius and Flavius Theodosius, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious, and Triumphant, Always August Emperors. Fundanius Martirius Felix, a most illustrious man and prefect of the grain supply, rebuilt the bridge of the Matidia, which had been cut off from passage and buried by debris, and completed the work, and dedicated it.
EDCS-09400109.summary: This inscription records the repair and dedication of the Matidia bridge by Fundanius Martirius Felix, prefect of the grain supply, during the reign of Emperors Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-09400110.translation: In the most flourishing state of the Roman Empire, Flavius Splendonius Aufidius, a most illustrious and distinguished man, count of the first order and prefect of the grain supply, repaired the bridge, which had collapsed from age, with me, Junius Pomponius Ammonius, a most distinguished man and prefect of the city, also dedicating it.
EDCS-09400110.summary: This inscription commemorates the repair of an old bridge by Flavius Splendonius Aufidius, prefect of the grain supply, and was jointly dedicated with Junius Pomponius Ammonius, prefect of the city.

EDCS-09400111.translation: Here rests the blessed martyr Hypolitus.
EDCS-09400111.summary: This is a short funerary inscription identifying Hypolitus as a blessed martyr.

EDCS-09400122.translation: Euticius and Florentina, parents, to their sweetest Hireneti, who lived 6 years and 30 days, in peace.
EDCS-09400122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from parents Euticius and Florentina to their daughter Hireneti, recording her age at death.

EDCS-09400156.translation: Scribe and clerk of the quaestorian desks, who by his divine will was protected.
EDCS-09400156.summary: This inscription honors a scribe and clerk of the quaestorian desks, attributing his protection to divine will.

EDCS-09400158.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Plotius Hermes, sevir of Aquinum, to his wife.
EDCS-09400158.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Lucius Plotius Hermes, a sevir of Aquinum, to his wife.

EDCS-09400159.translation: Sextus Satripius, of the Oufentina tribe, twelve feet in front and twenty feet in land.
EDCS-09400159.summary: This is a boundary marker indicating land owned by Sextus Satripius.

EDCS-09400160.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Antonius Eutychus lived 31 years, 4 months, 8 days. Publius Rufrius Dius, his father, for his dearest son.
EDCS-09400160.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Antonius Eutychus, set up by his father.

EDCS-09400161.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Crescentina, who lived 14 years. Parents for their daughter.
EDCS-09400161.summary: This is a tombstone for Crescentina, erected by her parents.

EDCS-09400887.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana by Aelia.

EDCS-09400894.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Aurelius Sulycianus, who lived 60 years, 5 months, and 10 days. Aurelia Gamice, his wife, and Calliope, his stepdaughter, set this up for him, who deserved well.
EDCS-09400894.summary: This is a tombstone for Aurelius Sulycianus, erected by his wife and stepdaughter.

EDCS-09400899.translation: She made a tomb structure for her daughter Aproniana, who lived 4 years, 8 months, and 20 days. Decia for her daughter.
EDCS-09400899.summary: This is a tombstone for Aproniana, made by her mother Decia.

EDCS-09400903.translation: The thymele (stage platform or altar) of Caius Allius Optatus, twenty-three feet in land.
EDCS-09400903.summary: This is a boundary marker for the thymele of Caius Allius Optatus.

EDCS-09400904.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a name and possibly a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-09400909.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Diallage, their sweetest daughter. Ignatius and Corinthias, parents.
EDCS-09400909.summary: This is a tombstone for Diallage, erected by her parents Ignatius and Corinthias.

EDCS-09400941.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Appalia Felicitas, their sweetest daughter, who deserved well. Appalius Felicissimus and Appalia Nice made this. She lived 6 years and 40 days.
EDCS-09400941.summary: This is a tombstone for Appalia Felicitas, erected by her parents, Appalius Felicissimus and Appalia Nice.

EDCS-09400942.translation: To Avidius, husband who deserved well, FIBV FA IS made this.
EDCS-09400942.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a husband, made by FIBV FA IS.

EDCS-09400944.translation: To Titus Flavius Primus, freedman of Titus Flavius, of the Quirina tribe, and to his patron Agathon, who deserved well.
EDCS-09400944.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Titus Flavius Primus and his patron Agathon.

EDCS-09400945.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Euplia, wife of Germanus.

EDCS-09400955.translation: To Naevina, daughter of Lucius Aemilius.
EDCS-09400955.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Naevina, daughter of Lucius Aemilius.

EDCS-09400978.translation: To Marcus Titius Ursanus, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe, and to Iulia Thima, freedwoman of Augustus.
EDCS-09400978.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Titius Ursanus and Iulia Thima.

EDCS-09400981.translation: Gaius Pontius, son of Lucius, of the Tromentina tribe.
EDCS-09400981.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Pontius.

EDCS-09400983.translation: To Pedo Urveilius, son of Caius, a piper, and to his wife Fausta, freedwoman of Sepullia.
EDCS-09400983.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Pedo Urveilius, a piper, and his wife Fausta.

EDCS-09400984.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Hilara, freedwoman of Marcus.

EDCS-09400986.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Mami, freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-09400987.translation: Mani Minati Ision, freedman of Mani.
EDCS-09400987.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Mani Minati Ision, freedman of Mani.

EDCS-09401012.translation: Babulleia, daughter of Caius, and Tiberius Pontius, son of Tiberius, an eques, Lachanus.
EDCS-09401012.summary: This inscription lists the names of two individuals, Babulleia and Tiberius Pontius Lachanus, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-09401013.translation: Gnaeus Spurius, son of Ovius; Singullia, daughter of Marcus; Marcus Spurius, son of Gnaeus; Gnaeus Spurius, son of Gnaeus, Frugi.
EDCS-09401013.summary: This inscription records the names of four individuals, possibly family members, with the last one identified by a cognomen.

EDCS-09401354.translation: Lucius Mummius, son of Lucius, consul.
EDCS-09401354.summary: This is a simple titular inscription identifying Lucius Mummius, son of Lucius, as a consul, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09401358.translation: When it came to the specified summons which Gaius Sulpicius Cinnamus had with Fortunatus, and Gaius Sulpicius Cinnamus to him...
EDCS-09401358.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a legal text relating to a summons or a contractual agreement between Gaius Sulpicius Cinnamus and Fortunatus.

EDCS-09401373.translation: To the Divine Manes. Successus made this for his most sweet wife Faceta, who deserved well.
EDCS-09401373.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Faceta by her husband Successus, honoring her memory.

EDCS-09401377.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Numitorius made this for his daughter Felicita, daughter of Aulus, at her funeral; farewell, hail.
EDCS-09401377.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius Numitorius to his deceased daughter Felicita.

EDCS-09700054.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. The regions and colleges set this up for Nasennia Prima, for her well-deserving husband Castricius Liberalis, who was most illustrious, proconsul of Campania, who first carried the fasces in the proconsulate of the province, prefect of the most sacred city, powerful in justice, authority, and munificence, a healthy original patron and overseer.
EDCS-09700054.summary: This complex funerary inscription honors Castricius Liberalis, a prominent official including proconsul of Campania and prefect of Rome, by various groups he served.

EDCS-09700055.translation: The regions and colleges set this up for Claudius Petronius Probus, most illustrious, proconsul of Africa and judging in sacred matters, at the same time II and III praetorian, powerful as ordinary consul, outstanding in nobility and munificence, an original patron.
EDCS-09700055.summary: This inscription commemorates Claudius Petronius Probus, a highly distinguished official who served as proconsul of Africa and held significant praetorian and consular posts.

EDCS-09700056.translation: Anicius Auchenius Bassus, most illustrious, vicegerent proconsul of Campania, ordered this to be made while judging in sacred matters.
EDCS-09700056.summary: This inscription records that Anicius Auchenius Bassus, a distinguished official serving as vicegerent proconsul of Campania, commissioned this monument while exercising judicial authority.

EDCS-09700059.translation: Virius Audentius Aemilianus took care to have this made.
EDCS-09700059.summary: This inscription states that Virius Audentius Aemilianus, identified as a consular figure in Campania, was responsible for its creation.

EDCS-09700525.translation: Alas, son, you lie wretchedly, struck down by cruel fate and unjust gods. You lie in the first bloom of youth, a miserable ruin for your father. Neither piety nor the favor of your countenance helped. You are still worthy of life, and the city has suffered a loss because of you, for you are the thunderbolt of your father, and no remedy can correct this. There is a harsh solace in examples, and the law forbids everything from being overturned. Only patience brings relief. Alas, I, your father, not worthy of this honor, lay you in this tomb and, in a reversed order, bestow this sad burial place.
EDCS-09700525.summary: This is a poignant epitaph composed by a grieving father for his son, Maecius Marullus, lamenting his premature death and the perceived injustice of fate.

EDCS-09700528.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Publius Nonius Karus lived for 8 years, 9 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-09700528.summary: This is a tombstone for a child, Publius Nonius Karus, recording his name and lifespan.

EDCS-09700529.translation: Publius Livius, freedman of Publius, dedicates [this] to Hercules.
EDCS-09700529.summary: This is a dedication of an object or monument by Publius Livius, a freedman, to the god Hercules.

EDCS-09700547.translation: Marcus Nonius Marci libertus M., a physician, a member of the six (body of Augustalis), for himself, his freedmen, and freedwomen.
EDCS-09700547.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Nonius Marci libertus M., identified as a physician and a sevir Augustalis, for himself and his freed dependents.

EDCS-09700549.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Menatia Saturnina made this for her incomparable husband, Gaius Alfius Crescentinus, who deserved well of her, and who lived for 45 years.
EDCS-09700549.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Menatia Saturnina to her highly esteemed husband, Gaius Alfius Crescentinus, providing his lifespan.

EDCS-09700551.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Marcius Floridus for his most rare companion, Clarilla.
EDCS-09700551.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Quintus Marcius Floridus to his highly valued companion, Clarilla.

EDCS-09700552.translation: [She] who lived for X years, months, and days. Flavius Primus [made this] for [her, his] incomparable [companion], for whom he lived for 35 years, 2 months, and 10 days, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-09700552.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Flavius Primus to his esteemed and incomparable partner, recording her lifespan (partially reconstructed) and their time together.

EDCS-09700553.translation: While alive, Gaius Cossuntius Pamphilus [erected this] for his wife, while alive, Ma [Hila].
EDCS-09700553.summary: This is a dedication made by Gaius Cossuntius Pamphilus for his living wife, Ma Hila, likely for a domestic shrine or monument.

EDCS-09700554.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription, possibly a tombstone or marker, for a person named Felici Primitiva.

EDCS-09700556.summary: This is an incomplete inscription that appears to record the name of Lucius Hele Secu, possibly a dedication or a funerary marker.

EDCS-09700557.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. To Gaius Julius Stefanioni, who lived 20 years and 20 months.
EDCS-09700557.summary: A funerary dedication for Gaius Julius Stefanioni, who died at a young age.

EDCS-09700558.translation: Justinus, freedman of Lucius Tertius, made this for the well-deserving Mars, at his own expense.
EDCS-09700558.summary: A votive dedication to the god Mars, funded by a freedman named Justinus.

EDCS-09700561.translation: Of Lucius Pontuleius Pantagathus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-09700561.summary: A funerary dedication or ownership marker for Lucius Pontuleius Pantagathus, a freedman.

EDCS-09700562.translation: Poppuleia, daughter of Caius, her mother.
EDCS-09700562.summary: A funerary dedication by Poppuleia, identifying herself as the mother of the deceased.

EDCS-09700564.translation: Lutae, daughter of Numisius, wife of Marcus Stallius, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe, made this.
EDCS-09700564.summary: A funerary dedication by the wife, Lutae, for her husband, Marcus Stallius, who was from the Teretina tribe.

EDCS-09700566.translation: For Quintus Vibius Quartio, freedman of Quintus, 16 feet in front.
EDCS-09700566.summary: A funerary dedication specifying land measurements for Quintus Vibius Quartio, a freedman.

EDCS-09700567.translation: Lucas Calvus from Alatrium made this palace.
EDCS-09700567.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a 'palace' by Lucas Calvus from Alatrium.

EDCS-09700874.translation: Marcus leius, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, Postumus, duovir of Interamna.
EDCS-09700874.summary: An inscription identifying Marcus leius Postumus, a duovir of Interamna, likely a magistrate's record or dedication.

EDCS-09700875.translation: For Marcus Caprius, freedman of Marcus, for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 12 feet in front and 12 feet of land.
EDCS-09700875.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Caprius, his freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-09700877.translation: To Lucius Valerius Saturninus, the excellent former praetor, from his daughter Brocchilla.
EDCS-09700877.summary: A funerary dedication from a daughter, Brocchilla, to her father, Lucius Valerius Saturninus, who held the rank of praetor.

EDCS-09700886.translation: To Lucius Af[...], XV vir, legate.
EDCS-09700886.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Lucius Af[...], a member of the college of the fifteen, and a legate, likely on a monument.

EDCS-09701393.translation: Ulpius Maximinus served for 25 years and 6 months. His wife Aurelia Martana and his son Iunius Maximus erected this for him, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-09701393.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aurelia Martana and Iunius Maximus erected a monument for Ulpius Maximinus, who had served in the military for 25 years and 6 months.

EDCS-09701400.translation: The entire people, insufficient for his merits, erected a statue to Aemilianus Audentius Aemilianus, a most distinguished man, consular governor of Campania, and a most outstanding patron and admirable judge.
EDCS-09701400.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by the people to Aemilianus Audentius Aemilianus, a distinguished former governor and patron, likely in a public space.

EDCS-09800050.translation: Gaius Cosconius Nicephorus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-09800050.summary: This inscription is a simple identification of Gaius Cosconius Nicephorus, a freedman.

EDCS-09800055.translation: For the safety of the Emperors, Mindis Faustus, with his family, built and made from his own properties and dedicated the ark according to the holy law.
EDCS-09800055.summary: This inscription records that Mindis Faustus, with his family, built, dedicated, and contributed to a structure or ark for the safety of the Emperors, likely in a religious or civic context.

EDCS-09800057.translation: Mantua, if it could reproduce a divine poet, would yield to this cave; and there, the treacherous Ithacans, sluggish from sleep and heavy with wine, and the Ciclops' rocky dens, and the savagery of Scylla, and the ship broken in the whirlpool, he himself would admit that nothing was so skillfully fashioned by any song as by the right hand of the artist, whose art and genius alone surpass nature. Faustinus, fortunate, erected this cave for his masters.
EDCS-09800057.summary: This poetic inscription likely commemorates the creation of an artificial cave or grotto by Faustinus, designed to impress viewers with its artistry, possibly for his patrons.

EDCS-09800061.translation: To Euxinus, the innkeeper, at Pompeii, near the amphitheater.
EDCS-09800061.summary: This inscription records the name of an innkeeper, Euxinus, and his location near the amphitheater in Pompeii.

EDCS-09800062.translation: I make this scurf-picker, made from castor oil and honey, for the quinquennial magistrate Maio, a good man, in his processions in June, with good fortune. Gaius.
EDCS-09800062.summary: This inscription appears to be a playful or humorous dedication, possibly related to a festival or procession, by Gaius for the quinquennial magistrate Maio.

EDCS-10400046.translation: Tiberius Claudius Aegialus made [this] for the [im]perial Claudius Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-10400046.summary: This inscription records that Tiberius Claudius Aegialus constructed something for Emperor Claudius.

EDCS-10400060.summary: This fragmented inscription likely refers to an Augustalis and expresses a sentiment of joy or possession.

EDCS-10400063.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Ulpius Abascantus, freedman of Augustus, made this for Flavia Prisca, deserving.
EDCS-10400063.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for a woman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400064.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Annius Prastina, possibly for a public building or monument.

EDCS-10400065.translation: Philargus, slave of Lucullus Mai, and Aristo, freedmen of Mai, give this.
EDCS-10400065.summary: This inscription records a gift or dedication made by two freedmen for their former master, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400069.translation: ...son, Varronius... military tribune... good... native... after death.
EDCS-10400069.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription for a Varronius, possibly a military tribune, who died as a native of the area.

EDCS-10400075.translation: ...water into the town... Pegasus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-10400075.summary: This fragment mentions an aqueduct and Pegasus, a freedman of Augustus, suggesting a public works project, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400094.translation: To the most illustrious man, Gaudiosa.
