EDCS-10400094.summary: This is a dedication to a man named Gaudiosa, identified as "clarissimus," indicating high social or official standing, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-10400096.summary: This inscription is a simple invocation or dedication to Saint Stephen, likely from the Christian Roman period.

EDCS-10400105.translation: Vaarius Antiochus, freedman of Caius, and Euhodus, freedman of Caleidius Numerius, restored this.
EDCS-10400105.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a building or monument by two freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10400112.translation: Valeria Maxima, mother, and her most sweet daughter Valeria, who lived for 36 years, 2 months, and 12 days, rests in peace on her own estates in the Massa Mandelanae of the Hercules enclosure.
EDCS-10400112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Maxima and her daughter, detailing the daughter's lifespan and burial on their own property, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700632.summary: This fragmented inscription mentions Lucius Fo... and the office of aedile, suggesting a public dedication or record, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-10700649.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content.

EDCS-10700652.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content.

EDCS-10700659.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content.

EDCS-10700772.summary: This is a dedication made by Helvius Rufus, likely for a monument or building.

EDCS-10700773.summary: This inscription simply records the name Gaius Julius Felix, possibly as a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-10700776.translation: Good luck to the youths of Velitrae, good luck to Aruntius Dignus!
EDCS-10700776.summary: This is a congratulatory or celebratory inscription wishing success to the youths of Velitrae and Aruntius Dignus.

EDCS-10700779.translation: Tiberius Claudius Celadus, contractor for internal works, made this for his most beloved wife Claudia Syntyche, and for Julia Nereis, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants, with the exception of the ill-fated freedmen Faustinus and Sabina. To them he bequeaths, in the name of guardianship and by his will, half of this monument with a shop and about eight jugera of land, indivisibly, under this condition: that they possess what has been left to them, and it shall not pass out of their hands, nor shall anyone be permitted to alienate, donate, or sell it. This monument, or sepulchre, with the land, shop, and garden, will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-10700779.summary: This is a detailed will and testament inscription by Tiberius Claudius Celadus, bequeathing a monument, land, and a shop to his family and freedpersons under specific conditions.

EDCS-10700781.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content, though it may relate to descendants.

EDCS-10700784.translation: Decimus Caecilius Helenus, freedman of Decimus, by a vision, to his devoted patron Decimus Caecilius Acastus.
EDCS-10700784.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Decimus Caecilius Helenus to his patron, Decimus Caecilius Acastus, following a vision.

EDCS-10700788.translation: For Celsilla, 3 months; for Catullus, 6 months; he made it and
EDCS-10700788.summary: This inscription likely records the duration of life or service for two individuals, Celsilla and Catullus, but is incomplete.

EDCS-10700821.translation: To the well-deserving, in sweetest peace. Mother, who lived about 60 years and lived as a maiden for 8 years. Buried on the 19th day before the Kalends of November, when our lord Arcadius Augustus and the most illustrious Bautonius were consuls.
EDCS-10700821.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a mother who died after living about 60 years and 8 years as a maiden, with consular dating to the time of Arcadius Augustus.

EDCS-10700823.translation: Martinus, while alive, made this for himself and his wife Hilara, according to his deserts. To his father Martinus, well-deserving, in peace, who lived about 60 years. Buried on the 13th day of the Ides of March, when the most illustrious Flavius Syagrius was consul.
EDCS-10700823.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Martinus for himself and his wife Hilara, and dedicated to his father Martinus, with consular dating.

EDCS-10701675.translation: Lucius Paccius, son of Cai, as aedile, gave the senate-house, record office, armory, and portico to the townspeople.
EDCS-10701675.summary: This inscription records a public building project by Lucius Paccius, son of Cai, in his role as aedile, benefiting the municipium.

EDCS-10900133.translation: IIII vir iure dicundo [for the second time]. Empia, daughter of Marcus. V.
EDCS-10900133.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely commemorating a female official, possibly Empia, daughter of Marcus, who held the office of IIII vir iure dicundo twice.

EDCS-10900136.translation: Decimus Aemilius made me. Decimus Aemilius Ae...
EDCS-10900136.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication or funerary text, mentioning Decimus Aemilius.

EDCS-10900137.translation: Salvia, freedwoman of Lucius Annius Erophilus, freedwoman of Lucius Annius, freedman of Marcus. N...
EDCS-10900137.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several individuals with their patronymic relationships, likely part of a funerary or property record.

EDCS-10900139.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription continuing a name and patronymic, possibly part of a longer genealogical or funerary text.

EDCS-11400594.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the dedication of a temple to Fortuna, with the beginning of a name or verb missing.

EDCS-11400600.translation: To the restorer of his world, to our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, the council and people of Salernum, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-11400600.summary: This is a civic dedication from the council and people of Salernum to Emperor Constantine, praising him as the restorer of the world and acknowledging his divine majesty.

EDCS-11400602.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication or a funerary text naming Anicius Auchenius.

EDCS-11400603.translation: To Annio Victorino, a most distinguished man, corrector of Lucania and Brittia, for his outstanding benevolence, the council and people of Salernum.
EDCS-11400603.summary: This is a dedication by the council and people of Salernum to Annio Victorino, their corrector, honoring his benevolence.

EDCS-11400604.translation: To Gracchus, a most distinguished man, Arrius Mecius Gracchus, a most distinguished man, our patron, so great and so provident to the colony of Salernum, who, by the mere passage of his consideration, recalled our city, which lay destitute and exhausted, to splendor by the flow of water; and who, by his generosity and the arrangements of his character, deigns to relieve the citizens and the exhausted council, and what pertains to the safety of the fatherland, through his foresight; whose merits and love for the council and citizens are so great that if we were to recount all his deeds, the day would not suffice. Therefore, the council and people of Salernum have decreed that a statue be erected.
EDCS-11400604.summary: This is a decree by the council and people of Salernum to erect a statue in honor of Arrius Mecius Gracchus, their patron, for his provident actions and generosity to the city.

EDCS-11400610.translation: To Titus Aelius Celsus, freedman of Augustus, chamberlain. Eutyches, his son.
EDCS-11400610.summary: This is a dedication by Eutyches to his father, Titus Aelius Celsus, a chamberlain and freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-11400613.translation: To Impetratus, our lord's freedman, dispensator of the account for sacred buildings and public works. Herennia Gemella, to her most beloved husband.
EDCS-11400613.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Herennia Gemella to her husband, Impetratus, a freedman of the emperor who managed sacred buildings and public works.

EDCS-11400614.translation: To Quintus Maecius Idaeus, messenger of the plebeian aediles.
EDCS-11400614.summary: This is an epitaph or dedication for Quintus Maecius Idaeus, a messenger for the plebeian aediles.

EDCS-11400615.translation: Titus Tettienus Felix, Augustalis, scribe and clerk of the curule aediles, messenger of the plebeian aediles, accensus, bequeathed 50,000 sesterces to the consul to adorn the temple of Pomona, from which sum the gilded pediment, the marble podium, and the stucco work were made.
EDCS-11400615.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 50,000 sesterces by Titus Tettienus Felix, a public official, for the adornment of the temple of Pomona, specifying the works funded.

EDCS-11400616.translation: Tiberius Claudius Filemo, son of Claudius, to Tiberius Claudius Hellanicus, son of Claudius, born in Forum Claudii, soldier of the tenth praetorian cohort, century of Asprius, transferred from the VI Ferrata Fideli Constanti legion. Titus Flavius Agrippa, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, his pious heir, to one who deserved well.
EDCS-11400616.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Flavius Agrippa to Tiberius Claudius Hellanicus, a soldier of the praetorian guard who had served in various legions.

EDCS-11400622.translation: Valerius Rufinus, evacatus of the third praetorian cohort, served for 20 years.
EDCS-11400622.summary: This is a military record for Valerius Rufinus, stating his service of 20 years in the third praetorian cohort.

EDCS-11400625.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Rennius Proculus made this for his dearest father, Lucius Rennius Philodoxus, freedman of Lucius, quinquennial magistrate of the guild of carpenters of Ostia, who was also Augustalis.
EDCS-11400625.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Rennius Proculus for his father, Lucius Rennius Philodoxus, a magistrate of the carpenters' guild in Ostia.

EDCS-11400639.translation: Here lies Annia Aphrodisia, his most rare wife.
EDCS-11400639.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Annia Aphrodisia, described as a rare wife.

EDCS-11400649.summary: A dedication to Marcus Aurelius Erotis.

EDCS-11400653.translation: To the Divine Shades. His mother [dedicated this] to Constantina, daughter of Calatoria, who lived 26 years, 1 month, and 13 days.
EDCS-11400653.summary: A funerary dedication to Constantina by her mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400656.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Chresimus and Lupulus [dedicated this] to Carpus Superbus.
EDCS-11400656.summary: A funerary dedication to Carpus Superbus by Chresimus and Lupulus.

EDCS-11400664.translation: To Aulus Clodius Anteus, freedman of Aulus, his patron; he gave [this] as a gift.
EDCS-11400664.summary: A dedication to the patron Aulus Clodius Anteus by his freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400665.translation: To Felicula, daughter of Quintus, from Consia. Her father made [this].
EDCS-11400665.summary: A funerary dedication to Felicula by her father.

EDCS-11400671.translation: To the Divine Shades. Feliciss lived [for] years...
EDCS-11400671.summary: An incomplete funerary dedication to Feliciss.

EDCS-11400673.summary: A simple epitaph for Flavia Calemera.

EDCS-11400676.translation: To the Lady Florena. Luxurius, her husband [dedicated this].
EDCS-11400676.summary: A funerary dedication to Florena by her husband, Luxurius.

EDCS-11400680.translation: To Sextus Helenius Demosthenes, freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-11400680.summary: An epitaph for Sextus Helenius Demosthenes, a freedman.

EDCS-11400687.summary: A dedication to Titus Julius Theatricus.

EDCS-11400689.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Iulia Dioclea, possibly indicating her origin or a family connection.

EDCS-11400702.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely naming Quintus Novius and possibly indicating a location or affiliation.

EDCS-11400706.translation: To the departed spirits. Victor lived 20 years. Marcus Claudius Euhelpistus made this for his dearest slave and for himself.
EDCS-11400706.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Victor at age 20 and a dedication by his master, Marcus Claudius Euhelpistus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400707.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text honoring Gaius Plutius Calchedonius.

EDCS-11400712.translation: Gnaeus Rocius for himself and his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Whoever must contribute this monument to the pontifical treasury will pay X feet in front and [---] feet in the field.
EDCS-11400712.summary: This is a funerary inscription establishing burial rights for Gnaeus Rocius and his dependents, with specifications for monument dimensions and a stipulation involving a treasury payment.

EDCS-11400717.translation: Aulus Sergius Cladus and Sergia Lais.
EDCS-11400717.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, Aulus Sergius Cladus and Sergia Lais, possibly as a joint dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-11400720.translation: Thiodotus, who lived 47 years, made this with his partner in the 25th year, in peace.
EDCS-11400720.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Thiodotus at age 47 and a dedication made with his partner, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400722.translation: Gaius Stertinius Priscus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-11400722.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Gaius Stertinius Priscus, son of Gaius, likely a personal name or part of a longer dedication.

EDCS-11400723.translation: Lucius Suavitis, son of Lucius, Buro.
EDCS-11400723.summary: This inscription records the full name and filiation of Lucius Suavitis Buro, son of Lucius, likely a personal name on a monument.

EDCS-11400733.translation: The brothers made this for Vibia Aphroditena.
EDCS-11400733.summary: This is a funerary inscription where brothers dedicate a monument to Vibia Aphroditena, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400735.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Victor lived 20 years. Marcus Claudius Euhelpistus made this for his dearest slave and for himself.
EDCS-11400735.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Claudius Euhelpistus for his deceased slave Victor, also indicating provision for himself.

EDCS-11400736.translation: By the will and piety of Marcus Ulpius Docimus, freedman of Augustus. Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus and Venuleia Corint(h)ias erected this for themselves.
EDCS-11400736.summary: A funerary monument erected by Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus and Venuleia Corint(h)ias, funded by the will of Marcus Ulpius Docimus.

EDCS-11400743.summary: A simple epitaph for Agrippina, indicating her burial in peace.

EDCS-11400744.translation: To Casuria Atria Maximina, my dearest wife, who lived 6 months and 20 days, [died?] the third day before the Kalends of September, buried the day before the Kalends of September. To Octaviae Primigeniae, [my] dearest mother, who lived 13 years, 10 months, 1 day... [illegible] the Kalends of August.
EDCS-11400744.summary: A funerary inscription for a wife and her mother, providing names, ages at death, and burial dates, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-11400746.translation: To Efuria Crispinia, of unique innocence and integrity, my wife, cut off in her youth, who lived joined to me for 1 year, 9 months, and 5 days, because of her services to me. Theodotus, her husband.
EDCS-11400746.summary: A funerary epitaph by Theodotus for his wife Efuria Crispinia, lamenting her early death and praising her virtues and services.

EDCS-11400747.translation: Here you lie, Fortunata, struck down by a sudden ruin; alas, my sweet wife, that weighs on me more. You suddenly closed your life with a cruel death, and my grief does not die while you perish. Chaste, decent, wise, humble, joyful to your husband, you turned my great joys into groans. But this cruel death could harm you in nothing, for your life comes from your merits, for it remains. Here lies also Petronia, born [by fate], whom death, bitter for you, joined with you. Here rests in peace Fortunata, a most distinguished woman, wife of Petrus, a most distinguished man, father of the poor, who lived more or less 36 years, with her daughter Petronia, aged six, buried in peace on the 7th day before the Kalends of February, in this indiction.
EDCS-11400747.summary: A lengthy epitaph for Fortunata, a distinguished woman and wife, and her daughter Petronia, detailing their lives, virtues, and deaths, with the father Petrus also mentioned.

EDCS-11400748.summary: A simple epitaph for Fortunata and Secundianus.

EDCS-11400751.translation: Olympia and [cus?] buried in peace. Ulpius, 13th day before the Kalends [of some month].
EDCS-11400751.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription indicating the burial of Olympia and another individual, with a reference to 'Ulpius' and a date.

EDCS-11400752.translation: To Orreanus, who deserved well, in peace.
EDCS-11400752.summary: A funerary dedication to Orreanus, recognizing his merits.

EDCS-11400754.translation: To Praetextata, our sweetest daughter, who lived 12 years, 4 months, 25 days, buried the 7th day before the Ides of August, in peace. Parents and [also] for themselves made [this].
EDCS-11400754.summary: A funerary monument erected by parents for their deceased daughter Praetextata, also including provision for themselves.

EDCS-11400755.translation: Lucianus is buried here. If anyone wishes to know the name of the buried man, they will learn it from the letters in order, [he who was] deserving, who lived 22 years minus 7 months and 15 days. [Died] 10 days before the Kalends of May, after the consecration of Flavius Gratianus Augustus.
EDCS-11400755.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Lucianus, recording his age and date of death, and indicating it was erected after the consecration of Emperor Gratianus.

EDCS-11400756.translation: Theodotus, who lived 47 years, and his partner, who lived 25 years, made this in peace.
EDCS-11400756.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Theodotus and his partner, stating their lifespans.

EDCS-11400760.translation: To the restorer of the world, the perpetual and most pious Emperor, our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the Greatest, Pious, Fortunate, ever victorious Augustus, by decree of the town council of the Surrentines.
EDCS-11400760.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the Surrentine public to Emperor Constantine, praising his achievements.

EDCS-11400762.translation: To our Lord Flavius Gratianus, ever Augustus.
EDCS-11400762.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Gratianus.

EDCS-11400764.translation: We, the entire council and people of the Surrentines, have resolved to erect a statue to Flavius Furcius Faustus, most distinguished man, tribune from the beginning, our patron, because of his merits from his labours.
EDCS-11400764.summary: This inscription records the decision by the Surrentine council and people to erect a statue honoring Flavius Furcius Faustus for his distinguished service and patronage.

EDCS-11400765.translation: To Gennadius, Marcus Ulpius Pupienus Silvanus, most distinguished man, citizen, orator, our outstanding patron, by the council and people of the Surrentines.
EDCS-11400765.summary: This is a dedication by the Surrentine council and people to their patron, Gennadius Marcus Ulpius Pupienus Silvanus, praising his civic and oratorical virtues.

EDCS-11400775.translation: Anthus, Augural official, of Corinth, for himself and his family.
EDCS-11400775.summary: This is a dedication made by Anthus, an Augustalis and augur from Corinth, for himself and his family.

EDCS-11400776.translation: Athictus, a freedman of Caesar, lived 7 months. Expeditus, his father, placed [this].
EDCS-11400776.summary: This is a tombstone for Athictus, a freedman of Caesar, who died at seven months old, placed by his father Expeditus.

EDCS-11400779.translation: Charito, freedman of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, a landscape gardener, for himself and his family.
EDCS-11400779.summary: This is a dedication by Charito, a landscape gardener and freedman of Emperor Claudius, for himself and his family.

EDCS-11400781.translation: Tiberius Claudius Expeditus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-11400781.summary: This inscription identifies Tiberius Claudius Expeditus as a freedman of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-11400784.translation: Euticus, freedman of the Emperor, a painter, [lived?] 30, 45 years.
EDCS-11400784.summary: This inscription records the age and profession of Euticus, a freedman of the emperor who was a painter.

EDCS-11400789.translation: Fronto, freedman of the Emperor, and Frontonilla.
EDCS-11400789.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of Fronto and Frontonilla, both freedmen of the emperor.

EDCS-11400792.translation: Gaius Julius, freedman of the Emperor.
EDCS-11400792.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Julius, a freedman of the emperor, likely for himself or a monument.

EDCS-11400793.translation: Lalemus, a circitor (an officer of the guard) of the Emperor, a Lycian by birth, made this for his son Donatus and for himself and his family.
EDCS-11400793.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lalemus, a Lycian circitor of the Emperor, for his son, himself, and his family.

EDCS-11400800.summary: This inscription records a dedication placed by a mother for Eleutheris.

EDCS-11400804.summary: This is a possessive inscription or a dedication to Publius Aurelius Lysimachus.

EDCS-11400805.translation: Brasidia, daughter of Lucius, for herself, for Marcus Tanontius, son of Marcus, and for all her relatives.
EDCS-11400805.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Brasidia for herself, Marcus Tanontius, and all their relatives.

EDCS-11400809.summary: This inscription records the beginning of names, likely Gaius Coelius and Agathe, perhaps in a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-11400811.translation: Cosconia Voluptas [erected this for] Cosconia Voluptas, her mother.
EDCS-11400811.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a daughter, Cosconia Voluptas, to her mother, also named Cosconia Voluptas.

EDCS-11400814.translation: Publius Equitius Fav[---] for Publius Equitius Au[ctus(?)] most dutiful and [---] Successa[---].
EDCS-11400814.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or epitaph for Publius Equitius Auctus, honoring his dutifulness, with fragmented mentions of others.

EDCS-11400820.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Helmonius Fuscus.

EDCS-11400825.translation: Marcus Livius Choesimus(?) and Lucius Adrastus for themselves and their families.
EDCS-11400825.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Livius Choesimus(?) and Lucius Adrastus, set up by themselves for themselves and their families.

EDCS-11400826.translation: Marcus Livius Zosimus and Pullia Nempsis for themselves, for Pullia Fortunata, and for their families.
EDCS-11400826.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Livius Zosimus and Pullia Nempsis, setting up the tomb for themselves, Pullia Fortunata, and their families.

EDCS-11400828.summary: This is an inscription dedicating a monument to Lollianus Pancratidus.

EDCS-11400831.translation: A good patron for Pistis, his freedwoman, and for all their families, and for those whom Neronia Lite will have given, and for Marcus Sittius Onomastus, son of Spurius.
EDCS-11400831.summary: This funerary inscription records a patron's provision for his freedwoman Pistis, their families, and others, as well as for Marcus Sittius Onomastus.

EDCS-11400840.translation: To Zosime Lassia Primigenia, slave, for Eutyches, her partner, and for herself, two jars.
EDCS-11400840.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication of two jars by a slave named Zosime Lassia Primigenia to her partner Eutyches and for herself.

EDCS-11400857.translation: Anteros, freedman of Heracles, chief magistrate, gave as a gift to the Lares and the household.
EDCS-11400857.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Anteros, freedman of Heracles and chief magistrate, to the household gods (Lares) and the family.

EDCS-11400860.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carulla Maete.

EDCS-11400861.translation: Titus Cornelius Libanus: I found at last a place where I might rest.
EDCS-11400861.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Cornelius Libanus, expressing his desire for rest.

EDCS-11400863.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gemini Isochryse, with a final farewell.

EDCS-11400870.translation: Here rests in good memory Alexandria, who lived more or less 40 years; her burial was on the sixth day before the Kalends of March, after the consulship of Paulinus the Younger, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-11400870.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Alexandria, recording her lifespan and date of burial in the late Roman period.

EDCS-11400872.translation: To Marcus Lucretius Decidianus Rufus, chief magistrate three times, quinquennial magistrate, pontiff, tribune of the soldiers by the people, prefect of craftsmen, Marcus Pilonius Rufus [erected this].
EDCS-11400872.summary: This is a dedication honoring Marcus Lucretius Decidianus Rufus for his various public offices, likely erected by Marcus Pilonius Rufus, probably in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400873.translation: To Marcus Lucretius Decidianus Rufus, chief magistrate twice, quinquennial magistrate, pontiff, tribune of the soldiers by the people, prefect of craftsmen, by decree of the decurions, after death.
EDCS-11400873.summary: This is a posthumous dedication to Marcus Lucretius Decidianus Rufus for his public offices, commissioned by the town council, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400874.translation: To Gaius Cuspius Pansae, son of Gaius, chief magistrate for the fourth time, quinquennial magistrate, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-11400874.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Cuspius Pansae for his public service, funded by the town council, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400875.translation: To Gaius Cuspius Pansae, son of Gaius, son of Gaius, pontiff, chief magistrate, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-11400875.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Cuspius Pansae for his religious and public roles, funded by the town council, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400878.translation: Vibius Popidius, son of Eppius, as quaestor, arranged for the construction of the portico.
EDCS-11400878.summary: This inscription records that Vibius Popidius, in his capacity as quaestor, oversaw the construction of a portico, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400884.translation: Marcus Porcius, son of Marcus; Lucius Sextilius, son of Lucius; Gnaeus Cornelius, son of Gnaeus; Aulus Cornelius, son of Aulus, as four chief magistrates, by the decision of the decurions, contracted for [this] to be built.
EDCS-11400884.summary: This inscription records that four chief magistrates, acting by the decision of the town council, contracted for a public work, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400890.translation: To Marcus Stlaborius Veio Fronton, augur, chief magistrate for the second time, quinquennial magistrate.
EDCS-11400890.summary: This is a dedication honoring Marcus Stlaborius Veio Fronton for his religious and civic offices, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400891.translation: Marcus Artorius Primus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-11400891.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marcus Artorius Primus, a freedman.

EDCS-11400894.translation: Eumachia, daughter of Lucius, public priestess, in her own name and that of her son Marcus Numistrius Fronto, made the chalcidicum, crypt, and portico of Concordia Augusta with her own money out of piety, and dedicated it herself.
EDCS-11400894.summary: This is a dedication by Eumachia, a public priestess, for the construction of a building complex, funded by herself, likely in the Augustan period.

EDCS-11400897.translation: To Eumachia, daughter of Lucius, public priestess of the fullers.
EDCS-11400897.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the guild of fullers to Eumachia, a prominent public priestess, likely from Pompeii.

EDCS-11400898.translation: By decree of the decurions, a plot of land was given to Gaius Norbanus Soricis, master of the substation of the suburb of Augustus Felix.
EDCS-11400898.summary: This record details the allocation of land by the town council (decurions) to a local official in the suburb of Augustus Felix.

EDCS-11400903.translation: Lucius Caesius, son of Caius, duumvir with judicial power, and Gaius Occius, son of Marcus, and Lucius Niraemius, son of Aulus, as duumvirs, by decision of the decurions, had this constructed and approved from public funds.
EDCS-11400903.summary: This inscription records the construction and approval of a public work, funded by the state and overseen by local magistrates (duumvirs), indicating their official duties.

EDCS-11400907.translation: To Emperor Augustus Caesar, parent of the fatherland.
EDCS-11400907.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Augustus, honoring him with the title 'parent of the fatherland', likely on a public monument.

EDCS-11400913.translation: Gaius Vulius, son of Caius, and Publius Aninius, son of Caius, as duumvirs with judicial power, contracted for the construction of a laconicum and destrictarium, and the repair of porticoes and a palaestra, from public funds that they were obligated to spend on games or monuments, and they saw to their construction and approved them.
EDCS-11400913.summary: This inscription details the construction and repair of public facilities, including a gymnasium and baths, commissioned by duumvirs using funds allocated for public entertainment or monuments.

EDCS-11400914.translation: To Marcus Holconius Rufus, son of Marcus, military tribune appointed by the people, duumvir with judicial power, quinquennial for the second time, priest of Emperor Augustus, patron of the colony.
EDCS-11400914.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Holconius Rufus, listing his numerous civic and religious offices, including military tribune, multiple terms as duumvir and quinquennial, priest of Augustus, and patron of the colony.

EDCS-11400918.translation: Marcus Holconius Rufus and Celer, the crypt, tribunals, and theatre, with their own money.
EDCS-11400918.summary: This fragmented inscription records Marcus Holconius Rufus and Celer funding the construction or renovation of parts of a theatre, including the crypt and tribunals, using their private wealth.

EDCS-11400921.translation: To Marcus Holconius Rufus, duumvir with judicial power for the fourth time, quinquennial, military tribune appointed by the people, priest of Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400921.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Holconius Rufus, listing his distinguished service as duumvir and quinquennial, military tribune, and priest of Augustus, enacted by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-11400922.translation: To Marcus Holconius Rufus, son of Marcus, duumvir with judicial power five times, quinquennial for the second time, military tribune appointed by the people, flamen of Augustus, patron of the colony, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400922.summary: This inscription celebrates Marcus Holconius Rufus, detailing his extensive civic and religious career including multiple terms as duumvir and quinquennial, military tribune, flamen of Augustus, and patron of the colony, as decreed by the decurions.

EDCS-11400924.translation: To Marcus Holconius Celer, duumvir with judicial power, designated quinquennial, priest of Augustus.
EDCS-11400924.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Holconius Celer, noting his roles as duumvir, designated quinquennial, and priest of Augustus.

EDCS-11400925.translation: Marcus Artorius Primus, freedman of Marcus, architect.
EDCS-11400925.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Artorius Primus, identifying him as an architect.

EDCS-11400928.translation: Gaius Quinctius Valgus, son of Gaius, and Marcus Porcius, son of Marcus, as duoviri, by decree of the decurions, contracted for the building of the roof of the theatre and approved it.
EDCS-11400928.summary: This inscription records a contract awarded by two duoviri for the construction of a theatre roof, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400929.translation: Marcus Oculatius Verus, son of Marcus, as duovir, for the games.
EDCS-11400929.summary: This inscription indicates that Marcus Oculatius Verus, serving as duovir, was responsible for providing the games.

EDCS-11400933.translation: Lucius Caecilius Phoebus erected this; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400933.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Caecilius Phoebus for a structure whose site was granted by a local council decree.

EDCS-11400934.translation: Marcus Faecius Suavis // Marcus Faecius Primogenes // from his own funds.
EDCS-11400934.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or donation for a 'schola' (meeting place or school) made by two individuals named Marcus Faecius, possibly father and son, from their own money.

EDCS-11400936.translation: Gaius Quinctius Valgus, son of Gaius, and Marcius Porcius, son of Marcus, as quinquennial duoviri of the colony, out of regard for the colony, undertook the construction of the public spectacles with their own money and granted a site to the colonists in perpetuity.
EDCS-11400936.summary: This inscription by two quinquennial duoviri details their funding and provision of public spectacles and a permanent site for colonists, likely during the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400938.translation: Titus Atullius Celer, son of Gaius, as duovir for the games, arranged for a seating section to be built for the public lights, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400938.summary: This inscription records the responsibility of the duovir Titus Atullius Celer for constructing a seating section for the 'public lights' (likely referring to theatrical performances or games) based on a decurial decree.

EDCS-11400939.translation: Lucius Saginius, duovir for administering justice, for the games and public lights, a seating section, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400939.summary: This inscription indicates that Lucius Saginius, in his role as duovir iuris dicundi, was responsible for a seating section for games and lights, as mandated by a decurial decree.

EDCS-11400940.translation: Lucius Saginius, duovir for administering justice, for the games and public lights, a seating section, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400940.summary: This inscription indicates that Lucius Saginius, in his role as duovir iuris dicundi, was responsible for a seating section for games and lights, as mandated by a decurial decree.

EDCS-11400941.translation: Numerius Istacidius Cilix, son of Numerius, duovir for the games and public lights.
EDCS-11400941.summary: This inscription records Numerius Istacidius Cilix, serving as duovir, who was responsible for the games and public lights.

EDCS-11400942.translation: Aulus Audius Rufus, son of Aulus, twice official for the games.
EDCS-11400942.summary: This inscription records Aulus Audius Rufus, who served as a duovir for the games.

EDCS-11400943.translation: Publius Caesetius Capito, son of Sextus, twice official for the games and festival lights.
EDCS-11400943.summary: This inscription records Publius Caesetius Capito, who served as a duovir for games and festival lights.

EDCS-11400944.translation: Marcus Cantrius Marcellus, son of Marcus, twice official, had the seating tiers made by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400944.summary: This inscription records Marcus Cantrius Marcellus, a duovir, who funded the construction of seating tiers by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-11400946.translation: Gaius Cuspius Pansa, son of Gaius, son of Gaius, pontiff, duovir with judicial authority.
EDCS-11400946.summary: This inscription records Gaius Cuspius Pansa, who held the positions of pontiff and duovir with judicial authority.

EDCS-11400947.translation: To our Genius of Lucius, Felix, freedman.
EDCS-11400947.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Felix, a freedman, to the Genius of Lucius.

EDCS-11400948.translation: To the Genius of our Marcus and the Lares, the two Diadumeni, freedmen.
EDCS-11400948.summary: This inscription is a dedication by two freedmen, Diadumeni, to the Genius of Marcus and the Lares.

EDCS-11400949.translation: Sacred to Augustus; Irenius [dedicated to] Corneliae...
EDCS-11400949.summary: This inscription is a sacred dedication to Augustus, likely by Irenius to Corneliae.

EDCS-11400950.summary: This inscription records a personal dedication made by Antiochus for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-11400951.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Cornelius Rufus.

EDCS-11400952.translation: Primo, son of Numerius, for the treasurer.
EDCS-11400952.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Primo, son of Numerius, for the treasurer (arcarius).

EDCS-11400953.translation: To Marco Tofelano Valentino, son of Marcus, for the gift of one hundred thousand sesterces to a friend.
EDCS-11400953.summary: This is a private dedication recording a financial gift made by an individual to a friend, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-11400955.summary: This inscription names Diogenes, identified as a builder, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-11400971.summary: This inscription simply records the name Marcus Spurius Mesor, probably on a funerary monument.

EDCS-11400972.summary: This cryptic inscription seems to refer to two individuals, Festus and Torquatus, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-11400975.summary: This is an ownership or dedication inscription, likely belonging to or from Marci Pacui Diadumenus, possibly on a tomb.

EDCS-11400977.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Maia, from a decree of the decurions, by order of Marcus Melsoni, son of Aulus, again, and Publi Rogi, son of Publius Vari, duumvirs with judicial authority; and Numeri Pacci, son of Numerius Chilonis, and Marcus Ninni, son of Marcus Pollion, duumvirs for the care of public roads and sacred buildings, in the consulship of Marcus Crassus and Gnaeus Lentulus.
EDCS-11400977.summary: This is a public dedication of a sanctuary to Mercury and Maia, authorized by the local council and officials, dating to the consulship of Crassus and Lentulus.

EDCS-11400978.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Maia, from a decree of the decurions, by order of Publi Rogi, son of Publius Vari, and Marcus Melsoni, son of Aulus, again, duumvirs with judicial authority; and Numeri Pacci, son of Numerius Chilonis, and Marcus Ninni, son of Marcus Pollion, duumvirs for the care of public roads and sacred buildings, in the consulship of Marcus Crassus and Gnaeus Lentulus.
EDCS-11400978.summary: This is a public dedication of a sanctuary to Mercury and Maia, authorized by the local council and officials, dating to the consulship of Crassus and Lentulus.

EDCS-11400981.summary: This inscription names Caius Proculeius the younger, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-11400982.translation: Aulus Veius Phylax, Numerius Popidius Moschus, Titus Mescinius Amphio, and Primus, slave of Marcus Arrunti, ministers of Augustus, by decree of the decurions, by order of Marcus Holconius Rufus, four times, and Aulus Clodius Flaccus, three times, duumvirs with judicial authority; and Publius Caesetus Postumus, and Numerius Tintiri Rufus, duumvirs for the care of public roads and sacred buildings, in the thirteenth tribunician power of Emperor Caesar, in the consulship of Marcus Plautius Silvanus.
EDCS-11400982.summary: This inscription records the names of officials and ministers of Augustus who oversaw a public construction or maintenance project, dated to the consulship of Plautius Silvanus.

EDCS-11400984.translation: Messius Arrius Silenus, and Marcus Decidius Faustus, freedman of the Marci, perfumer, ministers of Augustus, under duumvirs Marcus Numistrius Fronto and Quintus Cotrius, son of Quintus, with judicial authority, in the consulship of Marcus Servilius and Lucius Aelius Lamia.
EDCS-11400984.summary: This inscription names ministers of Augustus and local duumvirs, likely related to a public work or funerary context, dating to the consulship of Servilius and Aelius Lamia.

EDCS-11400987.translation: Inventus Dentatius Daphnus, Felix Melissaei, Faustus Nymphodotus, Helvius Speratus, ministers of Augustus, by order of the city council, by command of the duumvirs for administering justice Marcus Holconius Gellius and Lucius Aelius Tuber, and the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places Caius Vergilius Salinator and Cnaeus Lucretius Decentis, during the consulship of Caius Asinius and Caius Antistius.
EDCS-11400987.summary: This inscription records the activities of the *ministri Augusti* (officials serving the imperial cult) and names several *duumvirs* responsible for public works and justice, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11400988.translation: By decree of the city council, by order of the duumvirs for administering justice and quinquennals Marcus Alleius Lucius Libella and Marcus Stlaborius Fronto, and the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places Quintus Pompeius Macula and Marcus Fulvinius Silvanus, during the consulship of Caius Calvisius and Cnaeus Lentulus.
EDCS-11400988.summary: This inscription details the actions of *duumvirs* responsible for justice and public works, likely erected under the authority of the city council, with a date inferable from the named consuls.

EDCS-11400989.translation: By the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places, during the consulship of Aulus Plautius and [another name].
EDCS-11400989.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to the responsibilities of *duumvirs* overseeing public works and possibly mentions consuls, dating it to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11400991.translation: Philippus Melissaei, Faustus Ianuarius Piricati, Quartio Iucundus Holconi, Anterus Auctus Helvi, Nymphodotus, ministers of Augustus, by order of the duumvirs for administering justice Marcus Lucretius Manlianus and Lucius Albienius Staius, and the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places Lucius Eumachus Fuscus and Numerius Herennius Verus, during the consulship of Cnaeus Domitius Camillus and Arruntius.
EDCS-11400991.summary: This inscription lists *ministri Augusti* and names *duumvirs* responsible for justice and public works, dating it to the consulship of Cnaeus Domitius Camillus and Arruntius.

EDCS-11400993.translation: [Name]simus Messi Fausti, [Name]rcidus Vei Frontonis, Aulus Arellius Graecus, ministers of Augustus, by decree of the city council, by order of the duumvirs for administering justice Caius Caesar and Marcus Vesonius Marcellus, and the prefect [name], and the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places Lucius Albius [name] and Decimus Lucretius, during the consulship of Paullus Fabius Maximus and Lucius Vitellius.
EDCS-11400993.summary: This inscription identifies *ministri Augusti*, *duumvirs* for justice and public works, and a prefect, mentioning specific consuls and an imperial figure, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400996.translation: Adeptus, sius Felicio, Caius Caesar Augustus, Marcus Epidius Flaccus, quinquennalis, Marcus Holconius Macro, prefect for administering justice, Lucius Licinius, Caius Adius, men responsible for roads, public buildings, and sacred places.
EDCS-11400996.summary: This inscription lists various officials, including *quinquennalis* and a prefect, responsible for civic duties and public works, possibly related to a specific honorific decree or magistracy.

EDCS-11400997.translation: Ministers of Augustus, by order of the duumvirs for administering justice, and the duumvirs for overseeing roads, public buildings, and sacred places, during the consulship of Quintus Sanquinius.
EDCS-11400997.summary: This inscription mentions *ministri Augusti* and *duumvirs* responsible for justice and public works, dating it to the consulship of Quintus Sanquinius.

EDCS-11400998.translation: Commodus Stronni, Menophilus Ancarsi, Felix Helvi, [name]idus Arri, sacred [offering], [illegible].
EDCS-11400998.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several personal names, possibly related to a funerary monument or a religious dedication, with some names possibly indicating social status or origin.

EDCS-11400999.translation: Apollonius Badi Primi, minister of Augustus, by decree of the city council, by order of the duumvirs for administering justice Decimus Alfidius Hypsaeus and Publius Vettius Celer, [illegible].
EDCS-11400999.summary: This inscription records a *minister Augusti* acting by order of the city council and *duumvirs*, suggesting a public or religious function, with an incomplete list of officials.

EDCS-11401001.translation: Lucius Ceius Doryphorus, Gnaeus Alleius M. Alexander, ministers.
EDCS-11401001.summary: This inscription simply lists the names of two individuals identified as *ministri*, likely officials serving a public or imperial function.

EDCS-11401002.translation: Tertius Epaphra Haber Citus, freedman of Istacidia Lucia, minister of Augustus, by decree of the decurions, by order of Tiberius Badius.
EDCS-11401002.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a freedman of Istacidia Lucia, acting as a minister of Augustus, following a decree of the local council and an order by Tiberius Badius.

EDCS-11401004.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the god Clymeus, the god Clymeus, Fortuna. By the praefect, Popidius Numerius, by decree of the decurions. By Olius Pontius, son of Abonianus Iucundus.
EDCS-11401004.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Clymeus, and Fortuna, made by a praefect and another individual, following a decree of the decurions.

EDCS-11401006.translation: By decree of the decurions. By Quintus Lollius Ponticus, son of Lucius Habonius Iugus.
EDCS-11401006.summary: This inscription records an action taken by decree of the decurions, involving Quintus Lollius Ponticus and Lucius Habonius Iugus.

EDCS-11401009.translation: By decree of the decurions, by order of Aulus Audius, duumvir with judiciary power.
EDCS-11401009.summary: This inscription records a decree of the decurions and an order issued by Aulus Audius, who held the office of duumvir with judicial authority.

EDCS-11401010.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Faustus Antistius.

EDCS-11401011.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to name Gaius Cor Quintus Lollius and possibly Felici.

EDCS-11401012.translation: Hyalissus, son of Eppius Primi. Optatus, son of Dasian.
EDCS-11401012.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Hyalissus and Optatus, likely indicating a dedication or a tombstone.

EDCS-11401013.translation: Numerius Popidius, son of Ampius. Lucius Caecilius Cer, Suavis Oppius, son of Optatus. Ipodus Staius and C.
EDCS-11401013.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, possibly a group responsible for a dedication or monument, including Numerius Popidius, Lucius Caecilius Cer, and Suavis Oppius.

EDCS-11401014.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription naming possibly Numerius Popidius and Clarus Caecilius.

EDCS-11401016.translation: Dama, freedman of Pupius Agrippa. Manlianus, son of Lucretius. Anteros, son of Staius Rufus. Princeps, son of Mescinius. The ministers of the Suburbane(?) district of Augustus Felix. They set up (this monument) in the second consulship of Tiberius Claudius Nero and Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso.
EDCS-11401016.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the ministers of the Suburbane(?) district of Augustus Felix during the consulship of Nero and Piso.

EDCS-11401019.translation: Agathemer and Heracla, as magistrates, [dedicated this] for the Larentinalia by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11401019.summary: This is a dedication for the Larentinalia festival by magistrates, issued by decree of the town council.

EDCS-11401020.translation: By the command of Physical Venus, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Antistia Methe, daughter of Antistius Primigenius, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11401020.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Antistia Methe, likely on behalf of a cult of Venus, enacted by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-11401021.summary: This is a dedication by Iulia Hygia, reportedly inspired by a divine vision.

EDCS-11401024.translation: To Tiberius Claudius, son of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, father of the country, Nero Caesar, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11401024.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Nero Claudius Caesar, son of the emperor Claudius, issued by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-11401025.translation: [To] Iulia Agrippina, daughter of [Germanicus] Caesar, [daughter of Ti(berius) Claudius] Caesar Augustus [---]
EDCS-11401025.summary: This is a fragmentary honorific inscription for Iulia Agrippina, daughter of Germanicus and likely of Emperor Claudius.

EDCS-11401029.translation: Cuspius, son of Titus, and Marcus Loreius, son of Marcus, as duovirs, by the decision of the decurions, undertook to construct the wall and the lead [sheathing?] and approved it for themselves.
EDCS-11401029.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall and lead sheathing by two duovirs, authorized by the decurions.

EDCS-11401030.translation: Cuspius, son of Titus, and Marcus Loreius, son of Marcus, as quadrumvirs, and Lucius Septimius, son of Lucius, and Decimus Claudius, son of Decimus, as quadrumvirs, by means of public funds and by decision of the decurions, undertook to construct [it].
EDCS-11401030.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by four magistrates (quadrumvirs), funded publicly and approved by the decurions.

EDCS-11401035.translation: To Marcus Holconius, duovir with power to dispense justice, priest of Augustus.
EDCS-11401035.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Marcus Holconius, who held the high municipal office of duovir and served as a priest of Augustus.

EDCS-11401041.summary: This is a dedication to a man named Marcus, son of Rufus.

EDCS-11401042.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring a public priestess named Holconia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-11401044.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Marcus Lucretius Rufus, possibly as a dedicator or the subject of a monument.

EDCS-11401045.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name Marcus Lucretius, possibly as a dedicator or the subject of a monument.

EDCS-11401048.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that records the name of Marcus Popidius, son of Appius, likely as a citizen mentioned on a monument.

EDCS-11401049.translation: To Quintus Sallustius, son of Publius, Philologus
EDCS-11401049.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quintus Sallustius, son of Publius, also known as Philologus, likely on a tomb or public monument, with the name of the dedicator lost.

EDCS-11401050.translation: Aulus Sextilius Gemellus, son of Aulus, for the second time
EDCS-11401050.summary: This inscription records the name Aulus Sextilius Gemellus, son of Aulus, with a notation of his second tenure of an office, possibly as a magistrate or official.

EDCS-11401054.translation: under the consulship of Gaius Poppaeus Sabinus
EDCS-11401054.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely dates the monument or event to the consulship of Gaius Poppaeus Sabinus.

EDCS-11401055.translation: under the consulship of Titus Statilius Taurus
EDCS-11401055.summary: This inscription dates the monument or event to the consulship of Titus Statilius Taurus.

EDCS-11401069.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that records the name Lucius Cerrius Otacilla, likely as a person honored or mentioned on a monument.

EDCS-11401085.translation: Marcus Cerrinius Restitutus, Augustalis, in a place granted by decree of the decurions
EDCS-11401085.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Cerrinius Restitutus, an Augustalis, was granted a location for a monument by a decree of the local town council.

EDCS-11401089.translation: Istacidia Rufilla, daughter of Numerius, public priestess
EDCS-11401089.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Istacidia Rufilla, daughter of Numerius, who served as a public priestess.

EDCS-11401093.translation: Marcia Aucta made this for Gaius Fabius Secundus, for herself, and for her daughter Fabia Gratina, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-11401093.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife for her husband and daughter.

EDCS-11401094.summary: A funerary epitaph likely for Lucius Istacidius.

EDCS-11401095.summary: A dedication to Numerius Istacidius Campanus, possibly on a tomb or a public monument.

EDCS-11401096.summary: A possessive or genitive reference to Istacidius Crisyrus, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-11401098.summary: The name Gnaeus Melissaeus Aper, likely an epitaph or part of a dedication.

EDCS-11401099.summary: A dedication to Juno, made by or for Melissaea Amyces.

EDCS-11401100.summary: An epitaph or record of Melissaea Asia, identified as the freedwoman of Gnaeus.

EDCS-11401103.summary: The name Gaius Venerius Epaphroditus, likely an epitaph or part of a dedication.

EDCS-11401105.summary: An epitaph for Suexpiila, noting her remarkable age of 109.

EDCS-11401110.summary: A dedication to Titus Maior, likely on a public monument or altar.

EDCS-11401114.translation: The town councillors decreed that Aulus Umbricius Scaurus, son of Aulus, of the Menenia tribe, a holder of the office of praetor, should be granted a place for a monument and one thousand sesterces for his funeral, and that an equestrian statue should be erected in the forum. Scaurus, the father, [erected this] for his son.
EDCS-11401114.summary: This is a decree by town councillors granting a burial plot, funds for funeral expenses, and a statue for Aulus Umbricius Scaurus, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11401115.translation: To Secundus, father, and to his heirs Gaius Olious Hermas, Marcia Auge, Rustia and Olia Secunda, for their merits, ornaments, and generosity, from the will.
EDCS-11401115.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a will, honoring Secundus and his heirs for their merits and generosity, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-11401118.summary: This is a simple dedication naming Numerius Istacidius Helenus as a village official ('paganus'), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11401119.summary: This is a dedication to Istacidius Scapidus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-11401124.summary: This inscription names Publius Sittius Diophantus, a member of the Augustales (a college of priests devoted to the imperial cult), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11401125.summary: This is a funerary epigram recording the lifespan of Ancile Cilt Rufi, who lived for 20 years.

EDCS-11401127.translation: To Lucius Ceius Labeo, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, twice duumvir with praetorian authority, quinquennial, by Menomachus, his freedman.
EDCS-11401127.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Ceius Labeo, a prominent local magistrate who held the office of duumvir twice and quinquennial, dedicated by his freedman.

EDCS-11401128.translation: To Ceia, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-11401128.summary: This is a dedication to Ceia, wife of Lucius, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-11401129.summary: This inscription names Lucius Ceius Communis, likely a funerary monument or a personal dedication.

EDCS-11401130.translation: Lucius Ceius Lucifer, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-11401130.summary: This inscription names Lucius Ceius Lucifer, the freedman of Lucius, likely a funerary monument or a personal dedication.

EDCS-11401132.translation: To Diomedes, freedman of Marcus (Arrius), for himself, his family, and memory, as magister of the Augustan prosperous suburban district.
EDCS-11401132.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Diomedes, a magister of a suburban district, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401133.translation: Diomedes (daughter of Marcus, freedwoman of Arria) for herself and her family.
EDCS-11401133.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Diomedes, the freedwoman of Arria, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401134.translation: To Arria, freedwoman of Marcus Utilius.
EDCS-11401134.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Arria, freedwoman of Marcus Utilius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401135.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Arrius Primogenus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401138.translation: Marcus Caledius Antiochus, freedman of Marcus, and Audia, freedwoman of Lucius, and Statia, and Marcus Caledius Libo, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-11401138.summary: This inscription lists the names of individuals, likely related to a family burial plot, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401139.translation: Quintus Cornelius Diphilus, freedman of Quintus (and Publius), and Cornelia Heraes, freedwoman of Quintus, lie here and I have granted this place to my freedmen and freedwomen and all of mine.
EDCS-11401139.summary: This funerary inscription records the allocation of burial space by Quintus Cornelius Diphilus for himself, his family, and his freedpersons, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401141.translation: To Publius Cornelius Potitus, and to Cornelia Quina, and to Publius Terentius Primus, and to Vinullia Maxima, for themselves and their families.
EDCS-11401141.summary: This funerary inscription records the allocation of burial space for multiple individuals and their families, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401144.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Veneria, freedwoman of Marcus (Mescinia), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sornia Secunda, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401155.translation: [A burial place for Gnaeus Clovatius, son of Gnaeus, twice consul with judicial authority, tribune of the soldiers.
EDCS-11401155.summary: This inscription likely records the allocation of a burial place for Gnaeus Clovatius, an official, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11401156.translation: To Marcus Stasius Suavus, freedman of Marcus, Augustalis, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-11401156.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Stasius Suavus, honored as an Augustalis, with the inscription stating it was made according to his will.

EDCS-11401158.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Lucius, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-11401159.translation: To Publius Minicius Apollonius, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-11401159.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Publius Minicius Apollonius, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-11401160.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Thice, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-11401162.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication or tombstone for Vettia Eucumene.

EDCS-11401163.translation: To Gaius Muttius Capito, freedman of Gaius, [and] Sallvia, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife.
EDCS-11401163.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Muttius Capito and his wife Sallvia, both freedpersons, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11401164.translation: Clodia, daughter of Aulus, public priestess of Ceres, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11401164.summary: This inscription honors Clodia, daughter of Aulus, as a public priestess of Ceres, appointed by a decree of the local council (decurions).

EDCS-11401165.translation: Lassia, daughter of Marcus, public priestess of Ceres, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11401165.summary: This inscription honors Lassia, daughter of Marcus, as a public priestess of Ceres, appointed by a decree of the local council (decurions).

EDCS-11401166.translation: Aulus Clodius, son of Marcus, of the Palatine tribe, scribe, magistrate of the fortunate suburban pagi Augusti.
EDCS-11401166.summary: This inscription records the civic and administrative roles of Aulus Clodius, son of Marcus, including scribe and magistrate of a suburban administrative district.

EDCS-11401168.translation: Lucius Cellius Calvos, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, decurion of Pompeii.
EDCS-11401168.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Cellius Calvos as a decurion (local council member) of Pompeii, specifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-11401169.translation: Vibius Coianus, son of Marcus, of the Menenia tribe, from Nuceria, a member of the board of four, according to the will of Vibia Tertia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-11401169.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication made by Vibius Coianus, detailing his tribal affiliation, origin, and a familial connection to Vibia Tertia.

EDCS-11401170.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Nardus as the freedman of Livia.

EDCS-11500013.translation: To Titus Gellius Ingenuus, freedman of Titus, an Augustalis, his excellent patron. Titus Gellius Ingenuus [dedicates this].
EDCS-11500013.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Gellius Ingenuus to his patron, Titus Gellius Ingenuus, who was also his freedman and possibly an Augustalis.

EDCS-11500018.translation: Lucius Albinius, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, according to the will.
EDCS-11500018.summary: This inscription likely records the allocation of a burial plot or a posthumous dedication by Lucius Albinius, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-11500033.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for Valeria Galla.

EDCS-11500039.translation: Here lies in peace Victoria, handmaid of God, who lived seventy-seven years, buried on the twelfth day before the Kalends of November, seven years after the consulship of Basilius, the most distinguished man, in the eleventh indiction.
EDCS-11500039.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Victoria, a 'handmaid of God,' providing her age at death and precise burial date relative to a consulship and indiction.

EDCS-11500040.translation: I[---] Na[---], who lived more or less fifty years, buried on the sixth day before the [---] of [---].
EDCS-11500040.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the name and approximate age at death of a person, with a partially preserved burial date.

EDCS-11500041.translation: To Lucius Claudius Polio Iulianus Gallicanus, of most distinguished memory, consul, patron of the colony and founder of [---] Nola, a descendant. [Dedicated] by freedmen and freedwomen for good memory. Nicomedes and Cuvid[---].
EDCS-11500041.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Claudius Polio Iulianus Gallicanus, a distinguished former consul and patron of Nola, established by his freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-11500049.translation: Born for the good of the state.
EDCS-11500049.summary: This is a very brief epigraphic phrase likely referring to civic virtue or a posthumous honor for an individual who served the public good.

EDCS-11500051.translation: To Gaius Arrius Spedius Actianus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-11500051.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Arrius Spedius Actianus, honoring him as a 'most distinguished man'.

EDCS-11500052.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Frontinus Nigeratus, son of the consul Claudius Frontinus, member of the vigintivirate judging litigations, military tribune with broad stripe of the IV Flavia legion, quaestor pro praetore of the province of Achaia, official for the acts of the Senate, curule aedile, praetor, [honorary] patron of the colony by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500052.summary: This is a funerary inscription honouring Tiberius Claudius Frontinus Nigeratus, detailing his extensive political and military career in the Roman Empire, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11500053.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Saethidas Caelianus, son of the consul Claudius Frontinus, member of the vigintivirate judging litigations, military tribune of the III Gallica legion, quaestor of the province of Sicily, candidate of the emperors Antoninus and Verus Augusti, member of the Sodales Hadrianales, tribune of the plebs, praetor, commissioner of fidelity, legate of the XI Claudia legion, augur, patron of the colony by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500053.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Saethidas Caelianus, listing his significant political and military offices and honors, likely dating to the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-11500054.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Saethidius Cethegus Frontinus, son of Tiberius Claudius Frontinus, legate of a legion, grandson of Tiberius Claudius Frontinus, consul, patron of the colony by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500054.summary: This is a funerary inscription honouring Tiberius Claudius Saethidius Cethegus Frontinus, highlighting his familial connections to prominent figures and his status as patron of the colony, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11500056.translation: To Gaudentius, [addressed to] the most distinguished Gaius Lucceius Petilius, governor, master of the Felices Constantinianae baths in the city of Rome, full of humanity and justice, most wise and eloquent in equity and all authority and benevolence, for his great goodness, the most splendid order of the Abellinatium, always supported by his vigilance, has decreed [this] pedestal, showing his distinguished merit with this and so many other statues placed on foot.
EDCS-11500056.summary: This inscription is a decree by the order of Abellinatium honouring Gaius Lucceius Petilius for his virtues and services, likely related to his administration of public baths, and possibly dating to the Constantinian period or later.

EDCS-11500058.translation: Giamnalivistedici, master of both branches of the military in perpetuity, also for our republic, Caecilianus, praetorian prefect, by the grace of God, for adornment, they decreed, managed by Perenus Paulinus, most distinguished man, consul.
EDCS-11500058.summary: This inscription records a decree honouring Caecilianus, a praetorian prefect, for his services, commissioned by Giamnalivistedici and overseen by Perenus Paulinus, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-11500063.translation: To Marcus Biwellius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe, aedile, quaestor, praetor, duovir, censor.
EDCS-11500063.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Biwellius, listing his civic offices in his local community, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500065.translation: Lucceia Auxesis, freedwoman of Gaius, ordered the portico to be made with her own money for 4,000,000 sesterces, by decree of the decurions; Gaius Lucceius Moderatus saw to its construction.
EDCS-11500065.summary: This inscription records a private benefaction by Lucceia Auxesis, a freedwoman, who funded the construction of a portico, with the execution overseen by Gaius Lucceius Moderatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500066.translation: Gaius Mamercius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe [his name], to his wife Sociia Prisca, daughter of Numerius, of the Socilia tribe; his mother Sociia, [dedicated this] to her son.
EDCS-11500066.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated by Sociia to her son Gaius Mamercius and his wife Sociia Prisca, listing their offices and tribal affiliations, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500069.translation: To Publius Vettienus, son of Publius, of the Galeria tribe, praetor, duovir; and to Gaius Vettienus, son of Publius, of the Galeria tribe, aedile, duovir.
EDCS-11500069.summary: This is a funerary inscription honouring two individuals, Publius Vettienus and Gaius Vettienus, likely brothers, detailing their civic offices within their community, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500070.translation: [dedicated by] aedile? duovir? by the will; they made it: Gaius Allenius, son of Gaius, of the Tertius Galeria tribe [his name]; Gaius Lucceius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe Secundus [his name]; Gaius Lucceius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe Sabinus [his name]; Gaius Abuttius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe Alauda.
EDCS-11500070.summary: This inscription records individuals who fulfilled a public work, possibly related to a portico or similar structure, by will and decree, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500073.summary: This fragment records the completion of an inscription and names the maker, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-11500075.translation: Gaius Arrius Corymbus, freedman of Gaius, an Augustalis of the Claudian guild, by his will and at the direction of his wife Herennia Restituta, a most excellent woman, granted this place for himself and for Urbanus, his freedman.
EDCS-11500075.summary: This funerary inscription records the allocation of a burial plot by a freedman, an Augustalis, for himself and his freedman, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-11500076.translation: Publius Avianus Seleucus, freedman of Gaius, an Augustalis, for himself and Publius Avianus Scitus, freedman of Gaius, and Aviania Prima, freedwoman of Publius [---] L. Ve[---]
EDCS-11500076.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial arrangements made by Publius Avianus Seleucus, a freedman and Augustalis, for himself and other family members.

EDCS-11500078.translation: to Nyso, freedman of Marcus, an Augustalis of Abellinum.
EDCS-11500078.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely funerary, dedicated to Nyso, a freedman and Augustalis from Abellinum.

EDCS-11500082.translation: To Aulus Freius Mercurialis, son of Aulus, of the Galeria tribe, and to his wife Amatia Maxima, daughter of Quintus. The sons, Publius and Lucius Freius, made this.
EDCS-11500082.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument erected by two sons for their father, Aulus Freius Mercurialis, and their mother, Amatia Maxima.

EDCS-11500083.translation: Gaius Lucius Bithus, freedman of Gaius, a Mercurialis, while alive, [dedicated this] to Velleia Philumina, freedwoman of Gaius. What about you?
EDCS-11500083.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument dedicated by a living freedman, Gaius Lucius Bithus, to his freedwoman companion, Velleia Philumina.

EDCS-11500085.translation: [---] Alexander, freedman of Publius, [---] made for himself and his family [---] arranged for the making [---] and for you and yours(?).
EDCS-11500085.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription, possibly a tombstone, indicating that it was made for the dedicator and their family, with a partial address to the deceased or a passerby.

EDCS-11500086.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely a name and filiation, possibly part of a funerary or public monument.

EDCS-11500088.translation: Publius Catienus made this while alive. Publius Catienus A Rufus.
EDCS-11500088.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Publius Catienus, identified also as A. Rufus, erected his own monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-11500089.translation: To the Divine Shades. Trebatia Sabina made this for her mother Cerrinia Veneria, who deserved well.
EDCS-11500089.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a monument erected by Trebatia Sabina for her deserving mother, Cerrinia Veneria.

EDCS-11500090.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Licinia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-11500091.translation: Lucius Livineius Scoxa, freedman of Lucius, and Livineia Martha, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for themselves and their descendants while alive.
EDCS-11500091.summary: This is an epitaph recording the construction of a monument by a freedman and his freedwoman wife for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-11500093.translation: Marcus Ofillius VCX [---] to Marcus Ofillius, son of Marcus [---]
EDCS-11500093.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely commemorating Marcus Ofillius, son of Marcus Ofillius.

EDCS-11500098.translation: Caius Rubrius Hilarus, freedman of Caius, made a monument for himself, and Rubria Hilara, freedwoman of Caius, and Caius Rubrius Acceptus.
EDCS-11500098.summary: This epitaph records the construction of a tomb by Caius Rubrius Hilarus, his wife Rubria Hilara, and another individual named Caius Rubrius Acceptus.

EDCS-11500100.translation: To Publius Spedius [---], to Publius Spedius [---], Macullia [---]
EDCS-11500100.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly a funerary monument, mentioning individuals named Publius Spedius and Macullia.

EDCS-11500101.translation: Spedia Clara, daughter of Publius Libaris, for herself and Caius Hostilius Clementius; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-11500101.summary: This funerary epitaph records Spedia Clara dedicating a monument for herself and Caius Hostilius Clementius, with the stipulation that it does not pass to heirs.

EDCS-11500107.translation: Publius Pomelianus Felicianus, son of Lucius, and his fellow citizens for themselves.
EDCS-11500107.summary: This epitaph records Publius Pomelianus Felicianus and his fellow citizens dedicating something for themselves, possibly a public building or monument.

EDCS-11500108.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Foria Vaetina Piusacus, most beloved daughter, who lived 30 years. Her mother, [---], to set up [this monument].
EDCS-11500108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a mother to her deceased daughter, Foria Vaetina Piusacus, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-11500116.translation: [---]us, son of Caius, of the Galeria tribe.
EDCS-11500116.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a longer text, identifying an individual by name, filiation, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-11500120.translation: Called to the Lord, Nonius Mamercus, a new convert, who, by the will of God, was united with the saints. He lived 59 years and 15 months. Buried on the Ides of July, in the 9th consulship of Constantius Augustus and the 2nd of Julian Caesar. His sons made this for him, well-deserved.
EDCS-11500120.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Nonius Mamercus, a Christian convert, detailing his age at death and burial date, with his sons erecting the monument during the consulship of Constantius Augustus and Julian Caesar.

EDCS-11500121.translation: Here rests in peace the servant of God John, a venerable man and priest, who lived 80 years and was called by the Lord on the 13th day before the Kalends of August, during the consulship of Flavius Basilius, a most distinguished man; he served as bishop for 21 years.
EDCS-11500121.summary: An epitaph for a priest named John, recording his age, service, and the date of his death.

EDCS-11500123.translation: If the holy mind knows not how to die, if the pure will never falls headlong with the limbs, the priest, through his merits in this world, after death, does not hold any tombs for your deeds; you always provided help and solace to the needy citizens with your pious heart and mind; a seeker of justice and a preserver of sacred honour, deceit and trickery never pleased you; always striving for heavenly things, you made daily gains; worshipping God, you never corrupted holy things, nor did your rewards for faith diminish; dear and humble to all, while you held the highest offices, you were always with God; your abundant hand attests to this, O bishop of the repaired Sabine see, to the bright deeds of your famous originator.
EDCS-11500123.summary: A complex epitaph celebrating a bishop, likely of Sabine origin, for his piety, justice, and charitable deeds during his lifetime and his service to the church.

EDCS-11500124.translation: You look upon this narrow tomb, cut from the rock, the dwelling place of Romulus, who now holds the heavenly kingdoms. For who could, with dry eyes, recount his death, his poverty in Christ, and his love for his bishop, Saint Sabinus? Following him with a pure heart, with what prayers, with what laments before the cave of the martyrs, he entreated not to be deprived of the fellowship of his master. His whole homeland is witness that he joined Christ faithfully; he has more easily obtained what he asked for.
EDCS-11500124.summary: An epitaph recounting the pious life and devotion of an unnamed individual to Saint Sabinus, bishop of the local church.

EDCS-11500125.translation: During the consulship of Appius Junius Silanus and Publius Silus Nerva, on the Kalends of January, Lucius Poppaeus Urbanus dedicated a statue, a shrine, and a seat to Apollo.
EDCS-11500125.summary: A dedication of a statue, shrine, and seat to Apollo by Lucius Poppaeus Urbanus during a specific consulship.

EDCS-11500128.translation: The city of Abella, previously deformed by its bareness and ugliness, was adorned and embellished by Pompeianus, son of Barbarius Pompeianus, a most distinguished man and consul of Campania, with stones quarried from the mountains, not brought from ruined monuments. This was carried out under the supervision of Proculus, the patron and curator of the Abellani.
EDCS-11500128.summary: A civic inscription recording the beautification of the city of Abella by Pompeianus, with supervision by Proculus.

EDCS-11500130.translation: The entire people of Abella to Tarquinius Vitalio, a most perfect man, most worthy by birth and origin, a distinguished togatus and the chief defender of the province of Campania, for his merits and innumerable benefits which he deigned to bestow upon his citizens.
EDCS-11500130.summary: A dedication by the people of Abella to their patron, Tarquinius Vitalio, for his merits and benefits to the city.

EDCS-11500133.translation: To Titus Antistius Cilo, son of Titus, of the Galerian tribe, duovir for dispensing justice.
EDCS-11500133.summary: A dedication to Titus Antistius Cilo, honoring his office as duovir.

EDCS-11500134.translation: To Lucius Antistius Tiro, son of Lucius, of the Galerian tribe, prefect of the decurions, by decree, for dispensing justice.
EDCS-11500134.summary: A dedication to Lucius Antistius Tiro, honoring his office as prefect of the decurions.

EDCS-11500135.translation: To Pompeia Rufa, daughter of Caius, mother of Tironis, pious and holy, dear to her family, lived.
EDCS-11500135.summary: An epitaph for Pompeia Rufa, described as a pious and holy mother.

EDCS-11500136.translation: To Avillia Aeliana, mother of Egnatius Rufus, a Roman knight, priestess of Iovia Venus of the Abellani.
EDCS-11500136.summary: An epitaph for Avillia Aeliana, a priestess of Iovia Venus, and mother of Egnatius Rufus.

EDCS-11500140.translation: To Lucius Egnatius Inventus, father of Lucius Egnatius Pollio Rufus, honored with public equestrian rank by the Emperor Antoninus and Verus Augusti, who, on his discharge from office, by the indulgence of the great emperor, obtained permission for a gladiatorial show and the whole spectacle, which he provided at his own expense; the colonists and inhabitants [erected this] in gratitude for his munificence. The site was granted by decree of the decurions. Erected on the 12th day before the Kalends of April, when Clarus and Cetegus were consuls.
