EDCS-11500140.summary: This funerary monument honors Lucius Egnatius Inventus for providing a gladiatorial show at his own expense, funded by the colonists and inhabitants of the town.

EDCS-11500141.translation: Manlius Pacius, because of the office of duovir of the colony, in accordance with Latin rights, [erected this].
EDCS-11500141.summary: This inscription records Manlius Pacius assuming office as duovir in a Latin colony, likely a dedication related to his tenure.

EDCS-11500142.translation: To Mullius Macro, son of Caius, duovir for five years, by his will, under the supervision of Ofillia Rufa, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-11500142.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Mullius Macro, a quinquennial duovir, established by his wife Ofillia Rufa according to his will.

EDCS-11500143.translation: To Aulus Musanus, son of Lucius, aedile.
EDCS-11500143.summary: This inscription records Aulus Musanus, son of Lucius, who served as an aedile, possibly related to a public building or office.

EDCS-11500144.translation: To Gaius Ofillius, son of Sextus, of the Galeria tribe, duovir for the second time, quinquennial.
EDCS-11500144.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Ofillius, son of Sextus, honoring his service as a quinquennial duovir for the second time.

EDCS-11500147.translation: Lucius Vitrovius Lucillus, son of Spurius, and Titus Propertius Thorianus, son of Titus, the duoviri, saw to the construction by the authority of the decurions and approved it for themselves.
EDCS-11500147.summary: This inscription records the completion and approval of a construction project by the duoviri Lucius Vitrovius Lucillus and Titus Propertius Thorianus, acting on the decurions' decision.

EDCS-11500148.summary: This fragment likely records the name and office of a duovir, with incomplete personal and tribal information.

EDCS-11500149.translation: To Publius Aelius Decembrius, from Rubrius Sabinus, kinsman.
EDCS-11500149.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Rubrius Sabinus to his kinsman Publius Aelius Decembrius.

EDCS-11500150.translation: Aulus Fuficius Amphio, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-11500150.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Aulus Fuficius Amphio, a freedman.

EDCS-11500151.summary: This is a partial inscription beginning with the name Gaius Popillius, with the rest of the text missing or illegible.

EDCS-11500152.translation: To Rufo, son of Publius, of the Galeria tribe. [---]
EDCS-11500152.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Rufo, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period, with a patronymic and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-11500153.translation: Of the Galeria tribe, to Rufo. [---] of the tribe Galeria, to Pon[---]. [---] To Philia, daughter of Marcus. [---]
EDCS-11500153.summary: This fragmented inscription likely pertains to funerary monuments, mentioning individuals named Rufo and Philia with their tribal affiliations and a father's name, possibly from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11500156.summary: This is a dedication to a patron named Cillius, suggesting a relationship of patronage, possibly from the late Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-11500159.translation: Praenestina, your Verus fulfills a heavy duty for you, alas, depositing his dear body under this marble. Life has separated us, but the undivided love and faithfulness will live on. Here too, the bond of our marriage will not allow death to create a separation. Christ will call our concordant souls together again. Deposited on the twelfth day before the Kalends.
EDCS-11500159.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph from Praeneste, recording the death and burial of an individual, emphasizing enduring love and the hope of resurrection through Christ, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-11500160.translation: To the well-remembered Zaenobia, deposited on the seventh day before the Ides, to her husband Faustus Iunior, a most distinguished man, during the consulship.
EDCS-11500160.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Zaenobia, dedicated by her husband Faustus Iunior, mentioning her good memory and a consul, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-11500162.translation: [---] suffect consuls: Aulus Plautius, Lucius Nonius. Titus Salvius Parianus, Aulus Terentius, duovirs. Sextus Aponius Proculus, Quintus Nolcennius, aediles. Lucius Cassius Longinus, Marcus Vinicius, consuls. Suffect consuls: Gaius Cassius Longinus, Lucius Naevius Surdinus. Marcus Sentius Rufus, Quintus Vibiedius Sedatus, duovirs. Publius Subidius Pollio, Sextus Parianus Serenus, aediles. Tiberius Caesar Augustus, consul five times. Suffect consuls: on the seventh day before the Ides of May, Faustus Cornelius Sulla, Sextus Teidius Catullus, consuls. Suffect consul: on the Kalends of July, Lucius Fulcinius Trio, consul. Titus Oppius Proculus, Marcus Staius Flaccus, duovirs for the second time, quinquennales. Marcus Atinius Florens, Aulus Cluvius Celer, aediles. Suffect consul: on the Kalends of October, Publius Memmius Regulus, consul. Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, consul. Suffect consul: on the Kalends of July, Aulus Vitellius, consul. Marcus Valerius Postumus, Quintus Lucceius Clemens, duovirs. Gaius Sentius Severus, Lucius Ippellius Atticus, aediles. Servius Sulpicius Galba, Lucius Sulla Felix, consuls. [---]
EDCS-11500162.summary: This is a list of Roman magistrates, including consuls, suffect consuls, duovirs, and aediles, likely related to the administration of a city or colony, with multiple entries for Tiberius Caesar and other prominent figures, spanning various years of the early imperial period.

EDCS-11500163.translation: Decimus Granius [---] dedicated to Diana by imperial order.
EDCS-11500163.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana, possibly an imperial commission, mentioning a Decimus Granius and dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-11500165.translation: Gaius Catius, son of Marcus, as aedile of the four officials, arranged for the field to be leveled at public expense, and saw to it that a wall, lecture halls, and a paved path were constructed at his own expense, in honor of the Genius of the colony and of the colonists, so that they may use them perpetually and happily.
EDCS-11500165.summary: This inscription records a public works project initiated and funded by Gaius Catius, an official, to improve a public space in the colony, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11500167.translation: Sacred to Augustus. The people of Laurinium restored this at their own expense, by decree of the decurions, as worshippers.
EDCS-11500167.summary: This is an inscription indicating the restoration of a sanctuary dedicated to Augustus by the community of Laurinium, following a decision by the local council, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-11500168.translation: To Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus, consul, prince of the youth.
EDCS-11500168.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus, honoring his titles of consul and prince of the youth, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11500169.translation: To Marcus Agrippa, son of Augustus.
EDCS-11500169.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Agrippa, son of Augustus, likely from the late 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE.

EDCS-11500172.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Hadrian, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11500173.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, from the Felix Augusta Colony of Nola.
EDCS-11500173.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the colony of Nola to Emperor Diocletian, dating to his reign (284-305 CE).

EDCS-11500174.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantine, Pious, Fortunate Emperor, ever Augustus, from the council and people of Nola, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-11500174.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the council and people of Nola to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-11500175.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble and blessed Caesar, from the council and people of Nola, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-11500175.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the council and people of Nola to Caesar Constantius, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-11500176.translation: The Nolan council and people dedicated and consecrated this statue to our lords Domitianus and the Barbarians, their gift to the fatherland.
EDCS-11500176.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue by the council and people of Nola to their rulers, facilitated by Ortensius Convianus, governor of Campania, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-11500177.translation: Born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-11500177.summary: This is a commendatory epigram, likely for an official or benefactor, emphasizing their service to the state, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11500178.translation: To Lucius Claudius Pollio Julianus, former duumvir, former quaestor candidate, admitted among the praetorians, former proconsul of the province of Baetica, former legate of the province of Asia, patron of the colony, perpetual flamen, from the council of the Augustales.
EDCS-11500178.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Claudius Pollio Julianus, honoring his distinguished career in various imperial administrative and religious roles, commissioned by the council of the Augustales, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11500179.translation: To Publius Claudius Pulcher, consul, patron.
EDCS-11500179.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Claudius Pulcher, a consul and patron, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11500180.translation: Provoked and captivated by new and almost daily pleasures, the patrons of Salernum dedicated this statue to Cusos Gratianus, a most excellent man.
EDCS-11500180.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue by the patrons of Salernum to Cusos Gratianus, a prominent individual, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11500182.translation: Naeratius Scopius, a most distinguished man, formerly consular governor of Campania, established and decreed this for the splendor of the city of Nola.
EDCS-11500182.summary: This inscription records an action taken by Naeratius Scopius, a former consular governor, to enhance the city of Nola.

EDCS-11500184.translation: Pollio Julius Clementianus, a most excellent man, an inimitable and most generous patron, whose deeds cannot be told, the Iovian district, in consideration of his merits, decreed a statue for him.
EDCS-11500184.summary: This inscription records the decree of a statue for the patron Pollio Julius Clementianus by the Iovian district, praising his generosity and inestimable deeds.

EDCS-11500185.translation: The entire Roman district erected a statue for Pollio Julius Clementianus, the most outstanding patron, supporter of citizens in need, defender of liberty, restorer of the people's road, and renewer of all public works, under the care of Claudius Plotianus.
EDCS-11500185.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue for the patron Pollio Julius Clementianus by the Roman district, highlighting his contributions to the city and its people.

EDCS-11500186.translation: For Clementianus, a most excellent man, with inimitable clemency, for his patron, a statue [...] with a shield [...]
EDCS-11500186.summary: This damaged inscription records a statue dedicated to Clementianus, noting his excellence and clemency.

EDCS-11500189.translation: [...] from paternal property, a unique individual, for the security of citizens, with tireless goodness.
EDCS-11500189.summary: This fragmentary inscription praises an individual for their unique qualities, dedication to citizen security, and goodness.

EDCS-11500196.translation: For Caesias Archenis, concubine of Marcus Critonius Hipparchus, Augustalis, and for Critonia Glycinna, wife.
EDCS-11500196.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Caesias Archenis, concubine of Marcus Critonius Hipparchus, and Critonia Glycinna.

EDCS-11500198.translation: For Fisias Rufina, daughter of Sextus, sister of Fisius Serenus, Augustalis, minister of the Lares; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500198.summary: This inscription records the burial place for Fisias Rufina, granted by decree of the decurions, and dedicated by her brother Fisius Serenus.

EDCS-11500199.translation: Titus Flaminius Longinus, son of Titus, had this made at his own expense.
EDCS-11500199.summary: This inscription records that Titus Flaminius Longinus paid for the construction of this monument at his own expense.

EDCS-11500200.translation: For Marcus Salvius Venustus, son of Quintus, decurion, through the favor of the deified Caesar.
EDCS-11500200.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Salvius Venustus, a decurion, made possible by the favor of the deified Caesar.

EDCS-11500201.translation: For Lucius Sattius Phileros, freedman of Lucius, master priest of Mercurialis and Augustalis, and for Daeria Rufa, freedwoman of [...] wife, and for Lucius Sattius Ampliatus, freedman of Lucius, by the will of Lucius Sattius Phileros, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-11500201.summary: This inscription records the endowment by Lucius Sattius Phileros for his wife Daeria Rufa and his freedman Lucius Ampliatus, establishing religious roles for them.

EDCS-11500205.translation: Quintus Sulpicius Rufus, one of the two duovirs, by decree of the decurions, the measurements and...
EDCS-11500205.summary: This inscription records a public works project ordered by the duovirs, possibly related to measurements, funded by the town council.

EDCS-11500206.translation: Titus Vedius, son of Titus, and Titus Vitorius, son of Gnaeus, the two duovirs, who weighed the goods, with public money by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500206.summary: This inscription records the completion of a project by two duovirs, possibly involving trade or distribution, funded by public money and approved by the town council.

EDCS-11500219.translation: To Tito Baburio Felix, Baburia Quieta, for her most excellent husband, and for herself, the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500219.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot granted by the town council to Baburia Quieta for her husband Tito Baburio Felix and for herself.

EDCS-11500221.translation: ] Caesius C[---], Gaius Caesius, son of Gaius, [---] and his wife L() Aquae [---]
EDCS-11500221.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to name individuals, possibly as dedicators or recipients, with a lacuna obscuring further details.

EDCS-11500224.translation: Lucius Cornelius Optatus, for his syndicate, with his own money.
EDCS-11500224.summary: This inscription records a dedication or contribution made by Lucius Cornelius Optatus for his syndicate, funded with his personal wealth.

EDCS-11500228.translation: To Sextus Firmius Xanthos, and to Firmius Naidus, and to their family.
EDCS-11500228.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Sextus Firmius Xanthos, Firmius Naidus, and their relatives.

EDCS-11500229.translation: To Fisias Rufina, daughter of Sextus, Modesta Fisias Rufina.
EDCS-11500229.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely commemorating Fisias Rufina, daughter of Sextus, with Modesta Fisias Rufina as the dedicator.

EDCS-11500231.translation: Titus Flavius Rufus, son of Titus, Titus Flavius Rufinus, son of Titus, for themselves and their freedmen [---]
EDCS-11500231.summary: This inscription records a dedication or grant by Titus Flavius Rufus and Titus Flavius Rufinus for themselves and their freedmen, with a damaged ending.

EDCS-11500232.translation: Titus Flavius, freedman of the emperor, Terius, with his own money.
EDCS-11500232.summary: This inscription records a private dedication made by Titus Flavius, an imperial freedman, funded by his own resources.

EDCS-11500247.translation: To Novia Modesta, she lived two years, 10 months, [---]
EDCS-11500247.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Novia Modesta, who died at the age of two years and ten months.

EDCS-11500250.translation: To Philemation and Chelidon and [---] and [---] his wife.
EDCS-11500250.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely dedicating a monument to several individuals, including a wife, with much of the text missing.

EDCS-11500252.translation: Gaius Pituanius Rufio, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and for Coelia Tertia, freedwoman of Marcus, while alive.
EDCS-11500252.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-funded burial plot for a freedman and his partner, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11500255.translation: To Publius Sabidius Priscus, freedman of Publius, from Epinicius, his patron, to his most dutiful freedman.
EDCS-11500255.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring a freedman named Priscus by his patron, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11500257.translation: To Aulus Sempronius Lucrio Gallo, freedman of Aulus, and to Alfia Philocompsa, freedwoman of the woman [Alfia's patron?], his wife, according to the will, 3,000 sesterces, as judged by Quintio, freedman.
EDCS-11500257.summary: This is a funerary inscription that records a bequest of 3,000 sesterces for a burial, according to a will, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11500259.translation: Aulus Spurius Antiochus made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-11500259.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a burial plot established for a family by Aulus Spurius Antiochus during his lifetime, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11500260.translation: To Gaius Statius Falerna, son of Quintus, by his heirs, according to the will.
EDCS-11500260.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a burial established by heirs according to a will, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11500263.translation: Marcus Varenus Clarus, freedman of the woman [wife?] and of Marcus Lartidius, during the consulships of Tiberius Caesar IV and Drusus Caesar II.
EDCS-11500263.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Marcus Varenus Clarus, a freedman, and dating the inscription to the consulships of Tiberius Caesar and Drusus Caesar (likely 14 AD).

EDCS-11500264.translation: To Gaius Venelius Falerna, son of Lucius, according to the will, by the decision of the heirs, this monument or sepulchre shall not follow its heir.
EDCS-11500264.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the monument or sepulchre for Gaius Venelius Falerna, funded by heirs according to a will, will not be inherited by a subsequent heir.

EDCS-11500268.translation: Always you surpass the proclamations of praise for your merit and a good offspring will seek your brave deeds; the highest glory of things teaches better to train; indeed your deeds, accomplished in order, would be sung; now love overcomes me and I cannot hold back my grief; always led by the name of Felix, happy, even happier that you might be, you lie faithfully in peace, you depart as was fitting, remaining eternally in peace, deposited in public, Eusebius and Ypatius being consuls, on the sixth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-11500268.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription with poetic elements, celebrating the deceased named Felix and noting his burial in public on June 2nd during the consulship of Eusebius and Ypatius, likely in the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-11500269.translation: Burial of the sacred virgin on the 14th day before the Kalends of March, in the time of Aetius and the presbyter Paul.
EDCS-11500269.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of a 'sacred virgin' on February 16th, during the time of Aetius and the presbyter Paul, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-11500270.translation: The burial of Paulinus the Younger, bishop, on the third day before the Ides of September, when Flavius Dioschorus was consul, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500270.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bishop Paulinus the Younger, dated by the consulship of Flavius Dioschorus.

EDCS-11500272.translation: The burial of the holy virgin Iusta, on the fifth day before the Ides of November, when Flavius Severinus was consul, a man of the highest distinction. Iusta, a virgin.
EDCS-11500272.summary: This inscription records the burial of the holy virgin Iusta, dated by the consulship of Flavius Severinus.

EDCS-11500273.translation: The burial of Victor, a man of note and patron, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, during the consulship of Flavius Severus, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500273.summary: This inscription records the burial of Victor, a man of note and patron, dated by the consulship of Flavius Severus.

EDCS-11500274.translation: The burial of Saint Felix, bishop, on the fifth day before the Ides of February, after the consulship of Faustus, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500274.summary: This inscription records the burial of Saint Felix, bishop, dated after the consulship of Faustus.

EDCS-11500275.translation: The burial of Theodosius, bishop, on the seventh day before the Ides of December, when Flavius Faustus the Younger was consul, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500275.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bishop Theodosius, dated by the consulship of Flavius Faustus the Younger.

EDCS-11500276.translation: The burial of Marcellus Prim of good memory, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of July. Laid to rest in peace, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, after the consulship of Paulinus, the praiseworthy woman.
EDCS-11500276.summary: This inscription records the burial of Marcellus Prim and a praiseworthy woman, dated after the consulship of Paulinus.

EDCS-11500277.translation: The burial of Paul the priest. He rests in peace, on the eighteenth day of January, during the consulship of Agapitus, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500277.summary: This inscription records the burial of Paul the priest, dated by the consulship of Agapitus.

EDCS-11500278.translation: Here rests Priscus, bishop, of holy memory, laid to rest in peace on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, when Flavius Maximus was consul, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500278.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bishop Priscus, dated by the consulship of Flavius Maximus.

EDCS-11500279.translation: The burial of Gaudiosus, laid to rest in peace, on the Nones of September, during the consulship of Maburtus, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500279.summary: This inscription records the burial of Gaudiosus, dated by the consulship of Maburtus.

EDCS-11500280.translation: Here rests in peace Ianuaria, daughter of Lucius, who lived approximately 29 years. With her husband, she lived 15 years, 11 months, and 10 days. Buried on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February, after the consulship of Bilisarius, a most delightful man, in the first indiction.
EDCS-11500280.summary: This inscription records the burial of Ianuaria, daughter of Lucius, providing her age at death and length of marriage, dated by the consulship of Bilisarius and the first indiction.

EDCS-11500281.translation: Here rests in peace the handmaid of God, Reparata, a sacred virgin, who lived for more or less 30 years, buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of November, after the consulship of Basilius, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500281.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Reparata, a consecrated virgin, in the year following the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-11500282.translation: Here rests Lucianus, a defender, of holy memory, who lived for more or less 48 years, buried on the 6th day before the Kalends of December, after the consulship of Basilius, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500282.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Lucianus, a defender, in the year following the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-11500284.translation: Here rests in peace Paulus, a praiseworthy man, a decurion, buried on the Ides of April, during the year following the consulship of Basilius, the consul.
EDCS-11500284.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Paulus, a decurion, in the year following the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-11500285.translation: Here rests in peace Dulcita, daughter of Lucius, who was buried on the 4th day before the Kalends of May, in the year following the consulship of Basilius, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500285.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Dulcita, daughter of Lucius, in the year following the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-11500286.translation: Here rests in peace Felix Christos, who lived for 50 years and six months, and was buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth indiction, in the year following the consulship of Basilius, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500286.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Felix Christos, who lived for 50 years and six months, in the year following the consulship of Basilius and the sixth indiction.

EDCS-11500287.translation: Burial of Reparatus, a deacon, of holy memory, buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of November, 12 years after the consulship of Basilius, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-11500287.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Reparatus, a deacon, 12 years after the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-11500291.translation: Here rests in peace Urbica, who lived for more or less 18 years, buried on the date under the 15th indiction, during the reign of our Lord Justin, perpetual Augustus, in the second year.
EDCS-11500291.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Urbica, who lived for approximately 18 years, during the second regnal year of Emperor Justin and the 15th indiction.

EDCS-11500292.translation: Here rests in peace Apollonia, a sacred virgin, sister of our Lord bishop Leo, who lived for more or less 75 years, buried six times three years after the consulship of Paulinus.
EDCS-11500292.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Apollonia, a consecrated virgin and sister of Bishop Leo, 18 years after the consulship of Paulinus.

EDCS-11500294.translation: Here rests in peace Victuria, who was buried on the 4th day before the Nones, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-11500294.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Victuria in the sixth indiction.

EDCS-11500295.translation: Adeodatus Indignus, archpresbyter of the holy church of Nola, rests here, beloved by God and men; he was truthful in speech, just in judgment, faithful in trust, possessed all that Christ loved: faith, charity, and so on. He was sweet-spoken and always brought abundant gifts in his verses. When he entered the sacred priesthood, there was no priest more precious than he. He lived all the days of his life before his ordination for 30 years, he sat in the priestly order for 50 years, and was buried.
EDCS-11500295.summary: This epitaph commemorates Adeodatus Indignus, archpresbyter of Nola, detailing his virtues, ministry of 80 years (30 before ordination, 50 as priest), and burial.

EDCS-11500296.translation: The deposition of lord Aurelian, bishop of holy memory, in peace, who lived more or less 80 years and presided for 38 years; he was deposited on the eighth day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-11500296.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bishop Aurelian, giving his age, years of episcopacy, and date of death.

EDCS-11500297.translation: Here lies in the sleep of peace Bonitus, son of Stauracus, deceased on the 25th day of Iulias.
EDCS-11500297.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bonitus, son of Stauracus, indicating his age at death and the date of burial.

EDCS-11500298.summary: This inscription records the burial of Clemens.

EDCS-11500299.translation: Of good memory, who lived 10 months and 6 days, Constantius.
EDCS-11500299.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of Constantius, indicating his age at death in months and days.

EDCS-11500301.translation: Here lies Felicellus in peace, who lived until the...
EDCS-11500301.summary: This inscription records the burial of Felicellus, mentioning his lifespan but with a lacuna.

EDCS-11500302.translation: The deposition of the priest Florentius on the third day before the Ides of February.
EDCS-11500302.summary: This inscription records the burial of the priest Florentius, with the date of his death.

EDCS-11500304.translation: Here lies in peace, who lived years and was deposited on the fourth day before the Ides of October, the burial of Gratiosus.
EDCS-11500304.summary: This inscription records the burial of Gratiosus, giving the date of his death and mentioning his lifespan with a lacuna.

EDCS-11500305.translation: Of good memory, of the priest Honoratus, who lived years and was deposited on the fifth day before the Kalends of...
EDCS-11500305.summary: This inscription records the burial of the priest Honoratus, mentioning his lifespan and date of death with lacunae.

EDCS-11500307.translation: Leo the priest, I believe [in] rising again.
EDCS-11500307.summary: This is a short epitaph for Leo, a priest, expressing belief in the resurrection.

EDCS-11500308.translation: Here lies in peace Modesta, who lived 17 years, 3 months, and 13 days devoted to Christ, deposited on the fourth day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-11500308.summary: This inscription records the burial of Modesta, detailing her age at death and her devotion to Christ.

EDCS-11500309.translation: The burial of the priest Patricius on the fourth day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-11500309.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of a priest named Patricius.

EDCS-11500310.translation: I, Senatus the bishop, believe in the resurrection.
EDCS-11500310.summary: This is a profession of faith from a bishop named Senatus.

EDCS-11500311.translation: Here lies in peace Stefanus, the physician, who lived for [X] years.
EDCS-11500311.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Stefanus, a physician, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-11500312.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription mentioning Stefanus.

EDCS-11500313.translation: Here lies in peace Teorus the innocent, who lived for two years.
EDCS-11500313.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Teorus, an innocent child, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-11500314.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Teridius.

EDCS-11500315.translation: The burial of the priest Uranius on the eleventh day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-11500315.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of a priest named Uranius.

EDCS-11500316.translation: Here rests in peace Urbanus the priest, buried on the third day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-11500316.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of Urbanus, a priest.

EDCS-11500318.translation: pray worthy supplications to you Praetius, to Christ, these...
EDCS-11500318.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a prayer or dedication, mentioning Praetius and Christ.

EDCS-11500320.translation: Here lies the sacristan of Saint Nicantcasus, buried on the eighth day before the Nones.
EDCS-11500320.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the sacristan of Saint Nicantcasus, recording his burial date.

EDCS-11500334.summary: This inscription records the names Sanctus Faustillus and Sanctus Felix, likely referring to individuals or possibly saints.

EDCS-11500341.translation: Numerius Egnatius, freedman of Caius, named Anavos.
EDCS-11500341.summary: This inscription records the name Numerius Egnatius, identifying him as a freedman of Caius and also by the name Anavos.

EDCS-11500343.translation: Communis, freedman of Caius Petronius, Saltuarius, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-11500343.summary: This inscription records that the freedman Communis, a freedman of Caius Petronius and named Saltuarius, fulfilled a vow to the god Silvanus.

EDCS-11500347.translation: To the divine Augusta. Lucius Mammius Maximus at his own expense.
EDCS-11500347.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Mammius Maximus at his own expense to the divine Augusta, likely an empress.

EDCS-11500351.translation: To Antonia Augusta, mother of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus. Lucius Mammius Maximus at his own expense.
EDCS-11500351.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Mammius Maximus at his own expense to Antonia Augusta, mother of the emperor Claudius.

EDCS-11500358.translation: To Appius Claudius Pulcher, son of Caius, consul, imperator. The people of Herculaneum, after his death.
EDCS-11500358.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication by the people of Herculaneum to Appius Claudius Pulcher, who held the titles of consul and imperator.

EDCS-11500362.translation: To Marcus Nonius Balbus, son of Marcus, praetor, proconsul, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500362.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Nonius Balbus, who held the offices of praetor and proconsul, made by the local council (decurions).

EDCS-11500363.translation: To Marcus Nonius Balbus, son of Marcus, proconsul. The citizens of Nuceria, as their own.
EDCS-11500363.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the citizens of Nuceria to Marcus Nonius Balbus, who served as proconsul.

EDCS-11500365.translation: To Marcus Nonius Balbus, son of Marcus, praetor, proconsul. The community of Crete [by decree].
EDCS-11500365.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Nonius Balbus, who held the offices of praetor and proconsul, made by the community of Crete.

EDCS-11500368.translation: [To Marcus] Nonius, son of Marcus, [son], praetor, proconsul. The people of Gortyn in bronze [by decree].
EDCS-11500368.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely in bronze and by decree, to Marcus Nonius Balbus, who served as praetor and proconsul, made by the people of Gortyn.

EDCS-11500369.translation: To Volasennia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, wife of Balbus, by the local council and people of Herculaneum.
EDCS-11500369.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription dedicated to Volasennia Tertia by the decurions and plebs of Herculaneum.

EDCS-11500370.translation: To Volasennia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, wife of Balbus, by the council of Herculaneum.
EDCS-11500370.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Volasennia Tertia by the decurions of Herculaneum.

EDCS-11500371.translation: To Volasennia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, wife of Balbus, by the elders.
EDCS-11500371.summary: This inscription honors Volasennia Tertia, daughter of Gaius and wife of Balbus, likely erected by a group referred to as 'veteres' (elders or veterans).

EDCS-11500372.summary: This inscription appears to honor someone named Fvalvius, possibly by a group identified as 'veteres'.

EDCS-11500373.translation: To Marcus Nonius Balbus, son of Marcus, father, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500373.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Nonius Balbus, identified as the father, and was erected by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-11500374.translation: To Viciria Archaide, daughter of Aulus, mother of Balbus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500374.summary: This inscription honors Viciria Archaide, daughter of Aulus and mother of Balbus, erected by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-11500378.translation: Lucius Annius Mammianus Rufus, twice-elected magistrate with quinquennial powers, [funded] the theatre [and] the orchestra at his own expense.
EDCS-11500378.summary: This is a dedication for public works, recording that Lucius Annius Mammianus Rufus funded the theatre and orchestra at his own expense, likely during his term as IIvir quinquennalis.

EDCS-11500379.translation: Lucius Annius Mammianus Rufus, twice-elected magistrate with quinquennial powers, [funded] the theatre [and] the orchestra at his own expense.
EDCS-11500379.summary: This is a dedication for public works, recording that Lucius Annius Mammianus Rufus funded the theatre and orchestra at his own expense, likely during his term as IIvir quinquennalis.

EDCS-11500380.translation: [...], Publius Numisius, son of Publius, of the Menenia tribe, architect.
EDCS-11500380.summary: This fragmentary inscription identifies Publius Numisius, son of Publius, of the Menenia tribe, as an architect.

EDCS-11500381.translation: To Marcus Calatorius Quartioni, son of Marcus, by the fellow citizens and inhabitants, with money collected.
EDCS-11500381.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Calatorius Quartioni, son of Marcus, erected by the local community ('municipes et incolae') through a collection of funds.

EDCS-11500382.translation: To Hymenaeus, freedman of Marcus Claudius Marcellus Aeserninus, an Augustalis.
EDCS-11500382.summary: This is a dedication to Hymenaeus, a freedman and Augustalis, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-11500385.translation: Lucius Mammius Maximus, at his own expense.
EDCS-11500385.summary: This is a record of a construction or dedication paid for by Lucius Mammius Maximus.

EDCS-11500389.translation: To Marcus Remmius Rufus, son of Marcus, by the townspeople.
EDCS-11500389.summary: This is a dedication by the townspeople to Marcus Remmius Rufus.

EDCS-11500402.translation: By decree of the decurions, a burial place was publicly granted to Lucius Ausidius Montanus, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe, companion of Gaius Calvisius Sabinus.
EDCS-11500402.summary: This inscription records the public grant of a burial plot to Lucius Ausidius Montanus by town council decision.

EDCS-11500404.summary: This is a fragmented inscription commemorating Marcus Calatorius Rufus and his brother.

EDCS-11500405.translation: To Eutyches Marcianus, freedman of Marcus Nonius Balbus, by decree of the decurions, a burial place.
EDCS-11500405.summary: This inscription records the grant of a burial plot to Eutyches Marcianus, freedman of Marcus Nonius Balbus, by town council decision.

EDCS-11500407.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription mentioning Marcus Nonius.

EDCS-11500408.translation: Marcus Nonius, from the VIII Menenia tribe.
EDCS-11500408.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Nonius and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-11500412.translation: To Hercules the Unconquered, Publius Vergilius Restitutus, having served as demarch, established this small shrine in honor of the divinity's outstanding [---].
EDCS-11500412.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by Publius Vergilius Restitutus for his service as demarch, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500414.translation: Publius Mevius Eutychus restored the small shrine of Sebethus.
EDCS-11500414.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a small shrine dedicated to Sebethus by Publius Mevius Eutychus.

EDCS-11500418.translation: To our most pious and venerable lady Helena Augusta, mother of our lord Victor, always Augustus, and grandmother of our most blessed lords Caesars, the council and people of Naples decree this.
EDCS-11500418.summary: A public inscription from Naples honoring Empress Helena, mother of Constantine, dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-11500420.translation: Lucius Stertinius Quintianus, son of Caius, of the Maecian tribe, son of Acilius Strabo Caius Curtius Maternus Clodius Nummus, by Julius Atticus, prefect of a cohort.
EDCS-11500420.summary: An inscription likely recording a military or administrative appointment of Lucius Stertinius Quintianus, with Julius Atticus as the dedicator, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500422.translation: The road from the promontory of the villa of Pausilypus, long neglected, he, the most distinguished man of Campania, having become consul, restored for public use.
EDCS-11500422.summary: An inscription celebrating the restoration of a public road near Pausilypus by a distinguished consul of Campania, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500424.translation: Octavius Caprarius to his most pious son Octavius Caprarius, according to the decree of the council. On the 10th day before the Kalends of January, the following were present: Petronius Scaplas, Manneius Preiskos, Poppaeus Severus. Regarding whom the archons Pakkius Kalos and Veibius Pollion brought a petition to the council. Thus it was decided: It is fitting that all citizens share in the grief for the death of a child, and especially for Octavius Caprarius, a man of worth, who lived honorably and served as agoranomos with dignity, having lost his younger son Caprarius, who has been testified by us for the dignity of his character and for the service as agoranomos performed by him, like his father. Therefore, console him publicly and grant him a place for burial, whichever his father chooses. A place was granted publicly by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500424.summary: A decree from a Greek city, likely in Roman Asia Minor, honoring a deceased youth and offering public consolation and burial rights to his grieving father, Octavius Caprarius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500426.translation: To Lucius Munatius Concessianus, a most excellent man, patron of the colony, for his merits towards the citizens with generous bounty, he who had formerly received the highest honor, the present time has passed, during which also his son Munatius Concessianus, holding the office of demarch, displayed to all citizens with greater expenditure and abundance of generosity, for which testimonials of most sincere love, a most splendid primary monument, the Herculanensians have decreed a statue to be erected to their marvelous patron.
EDCS-11500426.summary: An inscription from Herculaneum decreeing a statue to Lucius Munatius Concessianus and his son for their generosity and public service to the colony, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500427.translation: Sacred to the divine shades. For Gaius Octavius Verus, son of Gaius Octavius, prefect of the youth, admitted to public equestrian rank in the V decuries, honored for military service, prefect of the cohort of Africa, high priest of Virbius, augur, and quinquennial Augustan aedile of the youth. Postumia Procula, his wife, to her dearest husband, and Octavia Vera, his daughter, to her best father, made this.
EDCS-11500427.summary: A funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period dedicated to Gaius Octavius Verus by his wife and daughter, listing his many public and religious offices.

EDCS-11500429.translation: Sacred to the divine shades. Felix, the treasurer of the public of the Neapolitans, granted this place to Marcia Melissa, his incomparable wife, with the permission of the magistrate, and Marcius Felix [dedicated this] to his well-deserving mother.
EDCS-11500429.summary: A funerary inscription from Naples dedicated to Marcia Melissa by her husband Felix and their son Marcius Felix, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500430.summary: A simple inscription identifying Emperor Hadrian, likely part of a larger monument or building.

EDCS-11500431.translation: Here lies a man, a native of Paphos, like the wise, a descendant of the Romans, possessing many possessions, called Decimus Servilius, who reached the age of ninety-three years, as they say.
EDCS-11500431.summary: A bilingual (Latin and Greek) funerary epigram for Decimus Servilius, a Roman of Paphian origin, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500433.translation: Marcus Caecilius Eros and Flavia Themis, freedwoman of Marcus, lived 27 years.
EDCS-11500433.summary: A brief funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a couple, Marcus Caecilius Eros and Flavia Themis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500438.translation: To Marcus Cominius Verecundus, son of Marcus, of the Mae(cian) tribe. Quintia Dia [dedicates this] to her most dutiful son. Under the consulship of Gaius Vibius Apronianus and Gaius Fonteius Capito.
EDCS-11500438.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Cominius Verecundus, likely dating to the 2nd century CE, given the consuls named.

EDCS-11500439.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Cornelia Lochias, a freedwoman, with uncertain dating but likely Roman Republican or early Imperial.

EDCS-11500443.translation: For Iunia At[---], freedwoman of Marcus. For Marcus Iunius O[---], freedwoman Clodia Ma[---]. Marcus Iunius, freedman of Marcus, made [this] for himself and [---]o, freedman of Marcus, Onesimus.
EDCS-11500443.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription indicating multiple individuals being commemorated, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500455.translation: John, Marcus, Matthew, Luke, Bitalia, in peace.
EDCS-11500455.summary: This is a simple list of names with the phrase 'in pace', likely from a Christian context and dating to the late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-11500457.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for Eleusinius, likely from a Christian context, with uncertain dating but probably late Roman or early medieval.

EDCS-11500459.translation: Ilaritas lived 45 years. Theotecnus lived 50 years. Nonnosa lived 2 years 10 months, who was buried on the Ides of January. He was buried on the Nones of January.
EDCS-11500459.summary: This epitaph records the ages of death for Ilaritas, Theotecnus, and Nonnosa, with specific burial dates in January, likely from the late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-11500460.translation: To Saint martyr Ianuarius, here rests he who deserved well, in peace. Nicatiola the infant, here rests she who deserved well, in peace. Cominia.
EDCS-11500460.summary: This inscription commemorates the martyrs Ianuarius and Nicatiola, along with Cominia, all resting in peace, likely from a Christian funerary context of the late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-11500461.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Proculus rests here, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500462.translation: Rufina lived 55 years and her daughter, aged 37.
EDCS-11500462.summary: This epitaph records the ages of Rufina and her daughter at their deaths, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500469.translation: Here rests in peace Opilio, a most distinguished man, who lived about fifty years, buried on the 4th day before the Kalends of January, in the third indiction, under our lord Justin, perpetual Augustus, and in the second consulship of the same, in the aforesaid indiction. Here rests Deusdona with her father.
EDCS-11500469.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription for Opilio and Deusdona, dating to the reign of Emperor Justin I (518-527 CE) based on the consular and indiction references.

EDCS-11500471.translation: Death, which never ceases to engulf all in its eternal maw, often claims its own; happy is he who has been able to dismiss his affections safely, for the dying man fears no path. The virtuous matron, Candida, who shone with character, intellect, and dignity, is covered by this present tomb; her sweet enduring wife and surviving son recognize her from her offspring. Always with tears and with voice she prayed this, whose merit now follows and approves her prayers. Although her whole household may never cease to weep, I confess her fortunate to have deserved such a death. Here rests in peace Candida, a most illustrious woman, who lived more or less 50 years, interred on the 4th day before the Ides of September, in the 4th year of our Emperor Maurice, perpetual Augustus, the 3rd year after his consulship, in the 4th indiction.
EDCS-11500471.summary: This is an epitaph for a woman named Candida, detailing her virtues, family, and burial date, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-11500472.translation: Here rests in peace the holy bishop Gaudiosus, who lived 70 years, interred on the 6th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of [---], in the 6th indiction.
EDCS-11500472.summary: An epitaph for Bishop Gaudiosus, recording his death date and age, from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11500473.translation: Here rests in peace the holy abbot Habetdeus, buried on the 7th day before the Ides of May, in the second consulship of Anthem(ius).
EDCS-11500473.summary: An epitaph for an abbot named Habetdeus, recording his burial date and the consulship, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-11500477.translation: In Sleep rests Virciacus Carus, who lived fifty years and ten months, buried on the [---] day before the Kalends of [---].
EDCS-11500477.summary: An epitaph for Virciacus Carus, stating his age at death and burial date, from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11500489.translation: Graeceia Rufa, daughter of Publius, to Diana Lochia. [---] [---] [---]
EDCS-11500489.summary: An inscription dedicating something to Diana Lochia by Graeceia Rufa, daughter of Publius, likely a votive offering from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500491.translation: Titus Vestorius Zelotus, after the dedication of the temple of Fortuna, donated the statue of Pantheus with his own money.
EDCS-11500491.summary: A dedication of a statue of Pantheus by Titus Vestorius Zelotus, funded by himself, for the temple of Fortuna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500495.translation: Diognetus, the steward, made this for the Genius of the Caesars.
EDCS-11500495.summary: A dedication to the Genius of the Caesars by Diognetus, a steward, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500499.translation: To the Genius of the colony of Puteoli, Publius Acilius Hermeros.
EDCS-11500499.summary: A dedication to the Genius of the colony of Puteoli by Publius Acilius Hermeros, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500503.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Caius Marcius Alexander, freedman of Caius, made this. Having vowed as a freedman, he fulfilled his vow. Sacred to Hercules. Caius Marcius Alexander, freedman of Caius, gives.
EDCS-11500503.summary: A dedication to Hercules by Caius Marcius Alexander, a freedman, who made the dedication after vowing it, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500514.translation: Caius Rubrius Orestes dedicated this to the Lares.
EDCS-11500514.summary: A dedication to the Lares by Caius Rubrius Orestes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11500518.translation: Sacred to Father Liber, for the annual festival, Aurelius Draco, freedman of the deified Augustus and priest, dedicated this.
EDCS-11500518.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a sacred object or space to Father Liber by Aurelius Draco, a freedman and priest, likely for an annual festival.

EDCS-11500520.translation: Sacred to Father Liber. Lupercus, freedman of the emperors, dedicated this.
EDCS-11500520.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Father Liber by Lupercus, identified as a freedman of the emperors.

EDCS-11500521.translation: Asclepiades willingly gave this gift to the Great Mother, as deserved.
EDCS-11500521.summary: This inscription records a votive gift to the Great Mother by Asclepiades.

EDCS-11500523.translation: The masters had this made for Mercury for the net-fighters' seventh [game/dedication]. The masters who saw to this were Sextus Calasius, son of Sextus; Numerius Fafinius, son of Numerius; Gnaeus Atanius, son of Caius; Aulus Pontius, freedman of Lucius; Aulus Aemilius, [freedman] of Aemilia; Lucius Pontius, son of Lucius. Ga [incomplete].
EDCS-11500523.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something for Mercury by several masters, likely related to gladiatorial games or a festival for net-fighters, and lists the individuals responsible.

EDCS-11500524.translation: Lucius Pontius Severus willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-11500524.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Mercury by Lucius Pontius Severus.

EDCS-11500531.translation: On the fourth day before the Nones of December [December 2nd], during the consulship of Lucius Lollianus Avitus, Thalame had this buried with her belongings, by the priest Tiberius Claudius Felix.
EDCS-11500531.summary: This inscription records the burial of Thalame with her belongings on a specific date during the consulship of Lollianus Avitus, overseen by the priest Tiberius Claudius Felix.

EDCS-11500545.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording a dedication by Secundus.

EDCS-11500547.translation: Lucius Calpurnius, son of Lucius, built the temple to Augustus at his own expense, with its decorations.
EDCS-11500547.summary: This inscription records Lucius Calpurnius building a temple to Augustus with all its adornments at his own expense.

EDCS-11500550.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Stactia, daughter of Pollio, who is also called Secundus, of Ephesus.
EDCS-11500550.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Augustus by Stactia, daughter of Pollio, also known as Secundus, from Ephesus.

EDCS-11500571.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicating something to the emperor Hadrian Augustus.

EDCS-11500575.translation: To Faustina Augusta, wife of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, in his third tribunician power, in his third consulship. The association of scabillarii (footstool makers or performers?), which is permitted by decree of the Senate, dedicates this place granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11500575.summary: This is a dedication by the association of scabillarii to Faustina Augusta, wife of Antoninus Pius, with a grant of space by local officials, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11500580.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, twice consul, quinquennial magistrate. Dedicated by Flavius Pytheas, a marble worker.
EDCS-11500580.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Commodus by a marble worker named Flavius Pytheas, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11500583.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the country, pontifex maximus, in his fourth tribunician power, commander for the eighth time, consul for the second time, proconsul. From the colony of Flavia Augusta Puteoli.
EDCS-11500583.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar (son of Septimius Severus) by the colony of Puteoli, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11500588.translation: To Felicitas, perpetual patron of our lord Valentinian, victor and triumphant, ever Augustus. Avianius Valentinus, a most distinguished man and consul of Campania, devoted to his numen and majesty.
EDCS-11500588.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Felicitas and Emperor Valentinian by Avianius Valentinus, a consular official of Campania, likely from the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-11500604.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that likely refers to a title related to Parthia, possibly for an emperor or general.

EDCS-11500606.summary: This is a dedication to Aurelius Germanicus, a proconsul and benefactor, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11500618.translation: Born for the good of the state.
EDCS-11500618.summary: This is a short phrase possibly from a funerary or honorific inscription, indicating the deceased's dedication to public welfare.

EDCS-11500621.summary: This is a simple dedication to Paulus Apronianus, likely an honorific inscription.

EDCS-11500622.translation: To Gnaeus Asinius, grandson of Pollio and Agrippa, as public patron of the Puteolani.
EDCS-11500622.summary: This is an inscription honoring Gnaeus Asinius as the public patron of the people of Puteoli.

EDCS-11500623.translation: Avianius Vindicianus, a most distinguished man and consular governor of Campania, arranged for this.
EDCS-11500623.summary: This inscription records that Avianius Vindicianus, a consular official, oversaw the creation of a monument or project.

EDCS-11500627.translation: To Lucius Caesonius Ovinius Rufinus Manlius Bassus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a most distinguished man, Salian priest of the Palatine, former praetor, former quaestor; Lucius Caesonius Hedylus, procurator, [erected this] for his father.
EDCS-11500627.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Caesonius Ovinius Rufinus Manlius Bassus, likely by his son, Lucius Caesonius Hedylus, possibly on a monument or tomb, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11500629.translation: For the prosperity of our Lords Emperors and for ours, Valerius Hermonius Maximus, a most distinguished man, consular governor of Campania, began and completed the bank on the left side of the market, with structures built on account of the threat of approaching storms.
EDCS-11500629.summary: This inscription records the construction of a bank on the left side of a market by Valerius Hermonius Maximus, a consular governor of Campania, to protect against floods, likely dating to the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-11500630.translation: For the prosperity of our Lords Emperors and for ours, Valerius Hermonius Maximus, a most distinguished man, consular governor of Campania, began and completed the bank on the right side of the market, with structures built on account of the threat of approaching storms.
EDCS-11500630.summary: This inscription records the construction of a bank on the right side of a market by Valerius Hermonius Maximus, a consular governor of Campania, to protect against floods, likely dating to the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-11500631.translation: For the good fortune of the times and the prosperity of the public status of our Lords Emperors, Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, perpetual Augusti, Fabius Pasiphilus, a most distinguished man, acting in place of the Praetorian Prefect and the City Prefect, dedicated the bank on the right side of the market and the quay, constructed for the grace and splendor of the city of Puteoli.
EDCS-11500631.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a bank and quay on the right side of the market in Puteoli by Fabius Pasiphilus, acting prefect, to honor the emperors Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, dating to their reigns (late 4th/early 5th century CE).

EDCS-11500640.translation: The most distinguished and honorable order and the honorable people of Puteoli erected a statue to Pontius Proserius Paulinus the Younger, a most distinguished man, consular governor of Campania, patron from the beginning, supervisor of the city, restorer of public works, and most upright judge, on account of his father's and his own merits.
EDCS-11500640.summary: This is a decree by the city of Puteoli to erect a statue honoring Pontius Proserius Paulinus the Younger for his merits as a distinguished official and patron, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11500642.translation: Postumius Lampadius, a most distinguished man, consular governor of Campania, saw to this.
EDCS-11500642.summary: This brief inscription indicates that Postumius Lampadius, a distinguished consular governor of Campania, was responsible for the execution of some work or project, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11500644.translation: To Lucius Publius Petronius Volusianus, a most distinguished man, former quaestor, former member of the college of seven, former praetor, consul, patron of the colony.
EDCS-11500644.summary: This is an honorary dedication to Lucius Publius Petronius Volusianus, listing his distinguished career and his role as patron of a colony, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11500647.translation: With the god Lucius favoring, and with the princes, the highest consulate having all insignia, the curule chair, the fasces, and the purple.
EDCS-11500647.summary: This inscription seems to refer to the honors and insignia associated with a high magistracy, possibly a consulship, under imperial patronage, with an invocation to a deity. The dating is uncertain but likely Imperial.

EDCS-11500658.translation: To Gaius Julius [---], decurial official of Rome [---] [---].
EDCS-11500658.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring a Roman official named Gaius Julius, who held a decurial position in Rome, with the exact date and full context lost.

EDCS-11500662.translation: Gaius Septimius Libo, son of Gaius, aedile, scribe of the curule aediles, for himself and for his wife Laberia Fusca, and for Septimia Amantina, his freedwoman.
EDCS-11500662.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Septimius Libo, an aedile and scribe, for himself, his wife, and his freedwoman, likely on a tomb or a private monument, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11500668.translation: To Sabinus, our emperor's administrator. Aurelia Epimachis, to her deserving husband. He lived and lived for 36 years.
EDCS-11500668.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and dedication of Sabinus, an imperial administrator, by his wife Aurelia Epimachis.

EDCS-11500670.translation: Cnaeus Maetius Felix, trainer of gladiators for the emperor.
EDCS-11500670.summary: A brief inscription identifying Cnaeus Maetius Felix as a lanista, a trainer of gladiators, associated with the emperor.

EDCS-11500672.translation: To Mannius Stichius, Tiberius Caesar's bookbinder.
EDCS-11500672.summary: An inscription honoring Mannius Stichius, identified as Tiberius Caesar's bookbinder.

EDCS-11500681.translation: Lucrius, the emperor's decorator, from the gardens, for himself and his family.
EDCS-11500681.summary: An inscription recording Lucrius, an imperial decorator, acquiring space from the gardens for himself and his family.

EDCS-11500685.translation: Lalus, freedman of Augustus, made [this] for his son Helicon, son of Tiberius Iulius Spurius, and for himself and his family. The plot was granted by decree of the decurions from the family of the Lucullanae estate.
EDCS-11500685.summary: A funerary inscription for Lalus, an imperial freedman, and his son Helicon, with the plot granted by local authorities.

EDCS-11500693.translation: Gaius Cispius Severus, son of Aulus, of the Scaptia tribe, from Florentia, a soldier of the 3rd Praetorian cohort, lived for 43 years, served for 17 years.
EDCS-11500693.summary: A military tombstone for Gaius Cispius Severus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, detailing his age and service length.

EDCS-11500701.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Lucius Cocceius Cogitatus, son of Lucius. Parents [dedicated this]. He lived for 20 years and 11 months, a soldier of the 11th Urban cohort.
EDCS-11500701.summary: A tombstone dedicated by parents to their son Lucius Cocceius Cogitatus, a soldier in the Urban Cohort, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-11500707.translation: Aelia Valeria, daughter of Aelius Sossianus, a centurion of a legion, wife of a patron of the cities.
EDCS-11500707.summary: An inscription identifying Aelia Valeria by her father's military rank and her husband's civic role.

EDCS-11500710.translation: To Gaius Julius Justus, called to service by the emperors. Gaius Julius Bruttianus, centurion of the 6th Ferrata legion, [dedicated this] to his most devoted brother.
EDCS-11500710.summary: A tombstone dedicated by a centurion, Gaius Julius Bruttianus, to his devoted brother Gaius Julius Justus, who served as an evocatus Augustorum.

EDCS-11500713.translation: To Marcus Vettius Pius, son of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe, holding the public horse, prefect of the 6th Cohort of Thracians.
EDCS-11500713.summary: An inscription honoring Marcus Vettius Pius, an equestrian officer who served as prefect of the 6th Thracian Cohort.

EDCS-11500722.translation: To Marcus Octavius Agathas, son of Marcus. In the year when Gaius Domitius Dexter II and Lucius Valerius Messalla Thrasia Priscus were consuls, on the sixth day before the Ides of January, in the curia of the Basilica Augusta Anniana, the following were present for the writing: Aulus Aquilius Proculus, Marcus Caecilius Publiolus Fabianus, Titus Hordeonius Secundus Valentinus, Titus Caesius Bassianus. Because Gnaeus Haius Pudens, an excellent man, requested that a statue which the dendrophori (tree-bearers) erected to Octavius Agathas, our patron of the colony, be inscribed, Gnaeus Papirius Sagitta and Publius Aelius Eudaemon, the IIviri, reported what it would be pleasing to do in this matter, and they decreed as follows: It is pleasing to the entire honorable body of dendrophori to grant an inscription, which belongs to the honor of such a man, and which was inserted by decree [---].
EDCS-11500722.summary: A decree from the IIviri of the colony of Anniana records the decision to grant an inscription for a statue erected by the dendrophori to Marcus Octavius Agathas, a patron of the colony, during the consulship of Dexter and Messalla Thrasia Priscus.

EDCS-11500735.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Sextus Firmus, son of Sextus, Aemilia Sabina, to her excellent husband, aedile of Formiae, and to herself.
EDCS-11500735.summary: A funerary dedication by Aemilia Sabina to her husband Sextus Firmus, an aedile of Formiae.

EDCS-11500743.translation: Publius Octavius Rufus, decurion, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-11500743.summary: A self-funded dedication by Publius Octavius Rufus, a decurion.

EDCS-11500744.translation: Marcus Paccius Bassus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, augur, aedile, IIvir of Volceii, [made this] for himself and his family: for Paccia Bassia, daughter of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe; for Manlia Rufa, daughter of Cnaeus, of the Pomptina tribe; for Paccia Maxima, daughter of Lucius; for Paccia Grata, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-11500744.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Paccius Bassus, an official in Volceii, for himself and various female relatives.

EDCS-11500748.translation: All the people and the elders celebrate the flourishing fame of Chrysanthus, most distinguished patron, worthy of his merits, with their voices and inscribe his honors in clear texts; and yours also will remain, enduring for many years. Be fortunate, O supreme god, and look upon the family of Chrysanthus, seeking worthy descendants.
EDCS-11500748.summary: A poem praising the patron Chrysanthus and invoking divine favor for his family.

EDCS-11500750.translation: To Tannos Boionos Chrysantos, the outstanding boy, patron from birth of the order and the people, for his exceptional merit, the entire order and people have commissioned a statue.
EDCS-11500750.summary: A dedication commissioned by the local order and people for a statue honoring Tannos Boionos Chrysantos, a young patron.

EDCS-11500762.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly naming a flamen named -ledus.

EDCS-11500777.translation: Dedicated on the sixth day before the Ides of August, in the second consulship of Titus Vitrasius Pollio and Marcus Flavius Aper.
EDCS-11500777.summary: A dedication dated to the consulship of Titus Vitrasius Pollio and Marcus Flavius Aper.

EDCS-11500780.translation: L. Nemesis arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-11500780.summary: A brief record stating that L. Nemesis was responsible for the execution of a work.

EDCS-11500793.translation: Caia [dedicated?] the temple and the vicen[alia?].
EDCS-11500793.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning Caia, a temple, and possibly some sort of fee or duty.

EDCS-11500805.translation: Marcus Antonius Trophimus, an Augustalis of Puteoli and Neapolis, a cloth merchant, made this for himself, for his wife Julia Irene, a most rare example, and for Antonia Iucundina, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for Julia Eupheme and her descendants.
EDCS-11500805.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Antonius Trophimus, a cloth merchant and Augustalis of Puteoli and Neapolis, for himself and his family.

EDCS-11500811.translation: Didymus, freedman of Gaius Julius Erastus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, an Augustalis, for himself and his wife Lollia Nereis, who deserved well, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants, this monument or tomb shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-11500811.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Didymus, a freedman and Augustalis, for himself, his wife, and descendants, with a clause that the tomb is not inheritable.

EDCS-11500822.translation: Sextus Publicius Bathyllus, an accensus to a consul, an Augustalis of Puteoli and Venafrum, for himself and his wife Urvineia Modesta, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Lucius Urvineius Adiutor and Gaius Julius Auctus, his brother.
EDCS-11500822.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Publicius Bathyllus, an Augustalis, and his family and associates.

EDCS-11500825.summary: A very brief inscription possibly related to an Augustalis named Publius OI in Puteoli.

EDCS-11500827.translation: Caius Julius Aquilinus built the porticoes and seats from his own funds.
EDCS-11500827.summary: This inscription records the construction of public amenities, porticoes and seats, by Gaius Julius Aquilinus at his own expense.

EDCS-11500868.translation: Onesimus, freedman of Lucius, of Satti Iuli, Faenarius; Domitia Maxima, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-11500868.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely commemorating Onesimus and Domitia Maxima, possibly related to funerary contexts.

EDCS-11500871.translation: [---] of Iulius Satti, freedman of Lucius, Onesimus Faenarius; [---] to his patron Marcus Tutor, freedman of Marcus, son of Marcus [---]; [---] morum pr[---] EV[---]; [---]RMA[---]; [---]S[ // ] Lucilian[---]
EDCS-11500871.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that seems to commemorate a freedman named Onesimus, a freedman named Marcus Tutor, and possibly others, with references to patron-client relationships and possibly professions.

EDCS-11500873.translation: ] Stlaccius, freedman of Caius, A[---] mensor and also sacomarius; for himself and his family. [---] Stlaccius, freedman of Aulus, Maric[---] mensor and also sacomarius; for himself and his family.
EDCS-11500873.summary: This fragmentary inscription records two individuals, both named Stlaccius, who were freedmen and held the roles of mensor and sacomarius, dedicating the monument to themselves and their families.

EDCS-11500877.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Caius Hostius, who was possibly an oil merchant (olearius).

EDCS-11500899.translation: ] of Philippus; [---]pius, son of Caius, Cla[---]; [---]der, scribe.
EDCS-11500899.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning individuals named Philippus and a scribe, possibly related to administrative or funerary records.

EDCS-11500902.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Philargyrus, the supplier of furnishings, lived 35 years and 5 months.
EDCS-11500902.summary: A funerary epitaph for Philargyrus, identified by his occupation, with his lifespan recorded.

EDCS-11500903.summary: A funerary epitaph for Olla, identified by her association with Urbanius, who was a clerk.

EDCS-11500922.translation: Gaius Julius Phileros and his wife Valeria Epiphania, freedwoman of Lucius, and all their family. This is a monument or tomb; it will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-11500922.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Julius Phileros for himself, his wife Valeria Epiphania, and their family, with a clause about inheritance.

EDCS-11500926.translation: Marina, Syrian by birth, lived 30 years, 2 months, and 5 days. Julius Barbarus, her husband, made this for her who deserved well.
EDCS-11500926.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marina, of Syrian origin, erected by her husband Julius Barbarus, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-11500938.translation: Marcus Acutius Aegipas for Silicia Agathe, his conjugal partner.
EDCS-11500938.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Marcus Acutius Aegipas to his 'contubernalis' (conjugal partner or tent-mate), Silicia Agathe.

EDCS-11500971.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. His mother made this for Aemilianus. He lived for 1 year and 3 months.
EDCS-11500971.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aemilianus, erected by his mother, recording his very young age at death.

EDCS-11500980.translation: [...]ius Alexander for [A]vidiae Cytherid[i?], [daughter?] and Iulia [daughter?] of Orionis, freedwoman of the emperor, [for herself?] and her family.
EDCS-11500980.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription likely dedicating a tomb for Avidia Cytheridi and Iulia, freedwomen of the emperor, with the name of another individual partially preserved.

EDCS-11500989.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication, with partially preserved names.

EDCS-11500994.translation: [...] for the patron and possibly his descendants.
EDCS-11500994.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication to a patron and perhaps their descendants.

EDCS-11500999.translation: To Anneia Ampliata, daughter of Spurius, and to my freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-11500999.summary: A funerary inscription setting up a burial place for Anneia Ampliata and her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.

EDCS-11501005.translation: Venenio, drink well! Gregorius, drink well! Vennius Secundus, drink well, Secundus!
EDCS-11501005.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely scratched onto a tomb or drinking vessel, with repeated wishes for the deceased or perhaps living friends to drink well.

EDCS-11501009.translation: In this tomb, enclosed by a wall, [is the eternal home] of Annia Maximina and her sons Celerionis Maximini and Celerinaes, children of Annia Maximina.
EDCS-11501009.summary: This funerary inscription records the eternal home of Annia Maximina and her sons, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE based on naming conventions.

EDCS-11501014.translation: [Belongs to] Antoni, the heir, [who deserves well].
EDCS-11501014.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Antoni and indicating it was set up by an heir.

EDCS-11501028.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Antonia Primigenia.

EDCS-11501032.translation: [Belongs to] Appuleius [---] son of O[---] Aufidius [---].
EDCS-11501032.summary: This is a very fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the names Appuleius and Aufidius.

EDCS-11501041.translation: Numerius Arellius Primogenes, freedman of Numerius.
EDCS-11501041.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Numerius Arellius Primogenes, identifying his patron.

EDCS-11501043.translation: To Arria Aelianen, his wife, who deserves well. Arrius Gratus.
EDCS-11501043.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Arrius Gratus for his wife Arria Aelianen.

EDCS-11501077.translation: This monument or tomb belongs to Publius Avianius Rufus, son of Publius, and Ofillia Psycharis, freedwoman of Decimus, and Aviania Amor, daughter of Publius. Carpus [set this up]. It will not follow its heir.
EDCS-11501077.summary: This funerary inscription records the names of several individuals and states that the monument or tomb is not to be inherited, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11501078.translation: Decimus Avianius Rufus, son of Spurius, [erected this monument or tomb] for his father Decimus Avianius Salvius, for his mother Aviania Chresten, freedwoman of Decimus, and for his friend Publius Aemilius Firmus, and for his own freedmen and freedwomen. It will not follow its heir.
EDCS-11501078.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a family monument by Decimus Avianius Rufus for his parents, friend, and freedmen, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11501084.translation: [This was made by] Flavius Montanus for his kinsman Ladvaiduo and for his son Aurelius Curso.
EDCS-11501084.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the maker, Flavius Montanus, and the recipients of the monument, his kinsman and son.

EDCS-11501114.translation: To Bovia Arbuscula, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-11501114.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bovia Arbuscula, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501117.translation: Gaius Brinnius Nicephorus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-11501117.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Brinnius Nicephorus, a freedman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501118.translation: Gaius Brinnius Nicon, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-11501118.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Brinnius Nicon, a freedman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501120.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Britti Amerimnus Charitosius lived for his beloved Quintus Brittius Clemens for 9 years.
EDCS-11501120.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Brittius Clemens, a child, set up by his beloved Quintus Britti Amerimnus Charitosius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501122.translation: Marcus Bubbius Isocrysus Fortunatus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-11501122.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Bubbius Isocrysus Fortunatus, a freedman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501126.translation: Marcus Caecilius Primigenius with his wife Cossinia Daphne, daughter of Aulus, whom he abducted on the ninth day, leaving his most wretched parents.
EDCS-11501126.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Caecilius Primigenius and his wife Cossinia Daphne, likely a dedication by the parents of one of them, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501143.translation: Caesonia Primigenia to Publius Caesonio Phileto [
EDCS-11501143.summary: This is a funerary inscription potentially for Caesonia Primigenia dedicated to Publius Caesonio Phileto, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501151.translation: Lucius Calpurnius Monimus and Apate, his partner, and their freedman Earino.
EDCS-11501151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Calpurnius Monimus, his partner Apate, and their freedman Earino, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501152.translation: Lucius Calpurnius Olympicus to Calpurnia Ela; Lucius Calpurnius Ampliatus.
EDCS-11501152.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Calpurnia Ela, set up by Lucius Calpurnius Olympicus, and also mentioning Lucius Calpurnius Ampliatus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501162.summary: This is a funerary inscription possibly for Gaius Calvetius Primus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501165.translation: Calvius Ofellius [and his] parents [and] and Chi[---]
EDCS-11501165.summary: This inscription fragment appears to record the names of Calvius Ofellius and his parents, with some names or words missing.

EDCS-11501168.translation: Kania Musa for herself, and for Marcus Canius Protus, her patron, and for Marcus Canius Mopsus, a fellow freedman, and for Marcus Canius Leborianus, and for Marcus Canius Eutychus, freedman, and for her own family.
EDCS-11501168.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Kania Musa for herself, her patron, fellow freedmen, and family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501171.summary: A simple dedication to Carisia Flavia, likely a funerary epitaph or a dedication of a monument.

EDCS-11501177.translation: Gaius Cassius Buccio for himself, and for Zosima, freedwoman, and for Atticus, freedman, and for Felix, freedman, and for Blastus, freedman, and for all his own family.
EDCS-11501177.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Cassius Buccio for himself, his freedmen and their families, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501180.summary: This inscription simply records the name Lucius Cassius Serapion, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-11501186.translation: Gaius Cait[---] Zacynthus [---] for himself and su[---]
