EDCS-11501186.summary: This inscription is a fragment that names Gaius Cait[---] Zacynthus and mentions a dedication for himself and others.

EDCS-11501187.translation: Cattia V[---] for herself and for freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants. Whoever wishes to sell, donate, or bequeath this monument or sepulchre, surrounded by a masonry wall or building, will give to the Republic of the Puteolani 50,000 sesterces.
EDCS-11501187.summary: This is a complex funerary and legal inscription from Puteoli, specifying conditions for the sale, donation, or bequest of a burial monument and setting a penalty for its improper disposition, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501188.translation: Caucia Erotis to Caucia Eleutherine and to Aulus Caucio Epaphroditus, patron, and to Aulus Stlaccius Philadelphus, her husband, and for herself.
EDCS-11501188.summary: This funerary inscription records Caucia Erotis dedicating the monument to Caucia Eleutherine, her patron Aulus Caucio Epaphroditus, her husband Aulus Stlaccius Philadelphus, and herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501200.summary: A dedication to Tiberius Claudius Agathemerus, possibly an epitaph or a dedication of a monument.

EDCS-11501214.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Tiberius Claudius Graphicus and Herennia Cypares, Herennia Fortunata [dedicates this monument] to her well-deserving parents.
EDCS-11501214.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Herennia Fortunata to her parents, Tiberius Claudius Graphicus and Herennia Cypares, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501245.translation: To M(anius) Cluvius Heliodorus, freedman of Manius. A(ulus) Cluvius Nicia, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-11501245.summary: This is a funerary dedication to M. Cluvius Heliodorus, likely by his patron or patron's son, A. Cluvius Nicia, from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501247.translation: To Cluvia, daughter of Manius. A(ulus) Cluvius Nicia, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-11501247.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cluvia, daughter of Manius, by A. Cluvius Nicia, her freedman, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501254.translation: To Coelia Asteris, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-11501254.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Coelia Asteris, a freedwoman, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501258.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication to Coelia Verana, daughter of Caius, from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501260.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. To Cominia Anicia, most beloved daughter, who lived 12 years, 8 months, 5 days, and 3 hours. Her most sorrowful parents, Cominius Apronianus and Flavia Anicia.
EDCS-11501260.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their deceased daughter, Cominia Anicia, detailing her age at death, from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11501266.translation: Marcus Cornelius Balbus made this for Marcus Cornelius Balbus, his freedman.
EDCS-11501266.summary: This is a funerary dedication by M. Cornelius Balbus for his freedman, also named M. Cornelius Balbus, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501268.translation: To Aulus Cornelius Felix. Aelia Caetonis, his wife.
EDCS-11501268.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication by Aelia Caetonis for her husband, Aulus Cornelius Felix, from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501277.translation: The building, with the rooms above and an adjoining memorial bedroom, in granted space with its boundaries, they restored: Antonius Meropius and Lucceia Tertulla for themselves and their descendants, freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11501277.summary: This is an inscription recording the restoration of a building, including a memorial bedroom, by Antonius Meropius and Lucceia Tertulla for themselves and their descendants, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11501278.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cornelia Lacaena, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11501282.translation: This monument or tomb belongs to Lucius Cornificius Epagathus, and to Lucius Cornificius Niger and Lucceia Finice, and to Cornificia Prima, his mother, and to Lucius Cornificius Felix, his brother, and to Cornificia Musa, his freedwoman, and to himself and his family; the heir shall not follow.
EDCS-11501282.summary: This is a funerary inscription establishing a family tomb and stipulating that the heir will not inherit it, likely from the 1st to 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11501283.translation: The bones of Lucius Cossinius are here.
EDCS-11501283.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cossinius.

EDCS-11501284.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for Aulus Cossinius Iucundus Minor.

EDCS-11501306.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Eros Baianus [dedicated this] to Gaius Octavius Philo, freedman of Octavia, and to himself and to Domitia Arescusa, freedwoman, and to Gnaeus Domitius Anterotus, freedman, and to Gessia Asclepias, and to Gnaeus Pitius Chios, and to Domitia Idea, and to Domitia Nymphe.
EDCS-11501306.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Gnaeus Domitius Eros Baianus for himself and several others, including freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-11501321.translation: Gerontia Leontia made this for Ennius Spectatus, her husband, to whom she was married for one year, a deserving man.
EDCS-11501321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gerontia Leontia for her deserving husband, Ennius Spectatus.

EDCS-11501326.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for Gaius Erucius Faustus.

EDCS-11501337.translation: Lucius Fabius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-11501337.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely identifying Lucius Fabius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-11501340.translation: Gaius Fabius Menodotus, freedman of Publius, and Aemilia Calliopa, freedwoman of a woman, and Gaius Fabius Alexander, freedman of Publius, from the will of Publius Fabius Menodotus, for 20,000 sesterces, under the supervision of [arbiters].
EDCS-11501340.summary: This inscription records a burial, funded by the will of Publius Fabius Menodotus, for himself and others, including his freedmen and Aemilia Calliopa.

EDCS-11501342.translation: Marcus Fabius Philocalus, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Valeria Certa, his wife and freedwoman of Marcus, and for the deceased Calpurnia Saturnina, freedwoman of Gnaeus, a deserving woman.
EDCS-11501342.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Fabius Philocalus for himself, his wife Valeria Certa, and Calpurnia Saturnina.

EDCS-11501344.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Fabia Primigenia.

EDCS-11501353.translation: [Faustus], freedman of Titus, for himself and [Priscus], son of Falernus, and [Nothus], son of Sextus Falernus, his comrade, and Clytemnestra, his wife, and [---], a slave, and [---]cundus, a friend.
EDCS-11501353.summary: This funerary inscription records dedications by Faustus, freedman of Titus, for himself, his comrade Nothus, his wife Clytemnestra, and other friends and slaves.

EDCS-11501364.translation: To Marcus Flavius, who lived [number] months.
EDCS-11501364.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument for Marcus Flavius, likely a child, based on the mention of months.

EDCS-11501414.translation: Geminius Crescens lived [duration]. He is buried here. Felicia made this from her own property.
EDCS-11501414.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Geminius Crescens, dedicated by Felicia.

EDCS-11501421.translation: To Granius [name], son of Lucius?, and Aulus?, and Pseca[---], and to Grania [---], Marcus Valerius [---].
EDCS-11501421.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication or a list of names, possibly for multiple individuals, with Marcus Valerius as a potential donor or subject.

EDCS-11501425.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory label identifying Grania Veneria, who was a freedwoman.

EDCS-11501437.translation: Marcus Helvius Asclepius made this for himself and for his wife Julia Ephesia and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, while he was alive. For Lucius Iulius Atemi[...]doros, his patron.
EDCS-11501437.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Marcus Helvius Asclepius for himself, his wife, freedmen, and descendants, with an additional dedication to his patron Lucius Iulius Atemi[...].

EDCS-11501439.translation: Helvius Terentianus made this for a well-deserving friend.
EDCS-11501439.summary: This inscription records a gift from Helvius Terentianus to a deserving friend, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-11501441.translation: To the divine spirits. Lucius Erennius lived 52 years and 29 days.
EDCS-11501441.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Erennius, stating his age at death.

EDCS-11501448.translation: Herennia Serapia, daughter of Lucius, for herself and for her husband Numerius Cluvius Secundio, freedman of a woman, and for Gaius Suettius Blandus and all his family.
EDCS-11501448.summary: This funerary inscription lists multiple individuals for whom the monument was made, including the primary dedicator Herennia Serapia and her husband.

EDCS-11501456.translation: Hetriliae Tuch[---], freedwoman of Hetrilia. Hetrilia Auxi[---]. For Quintus Turranius Ce[---], freedman of Publius Erastus Sev[---].
EDCS-11501456.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record a dedication or funerary notice for multiple individuals, including freedwomen and potentially their patrons.

EDCS-11501478.translation: Gaius Iulius Amphio, Fenestra, Decimus, Lucilius, Philocyros, Lucilia, Sympher[---], and Lucilia Naini dedicated this to themselves while alive, and forever.
EDCS-11501478.summary: This inscription records a group of individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, who dedicated a monument to themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-11501492.translation: Gaius Julius Genialis, son of Spurius, for himself.
EDCS-11501492.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Julius Genialis for himself.

EDCS-11501494.translation: Gaius Julius Hilarus for himself, and for his wife Iulia Arescusa, and for his daughter Iulia Primigenia, and for his grandchildren Iulius Hilarianus and Iulia Arescusa, and for his freedman Iulius Onesimus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants: this monument will not pass to an external heir.
EDCS-11501494.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records a self-dedication and includes family members and freedpersons, stipulating that the monument is not to pass to an external heir.

EDCS-11501501.translation: Iulia Euth[---] made (this) for her well-deserving husband Iulius Honomastianus.
EDCS-11501501.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Euth[---] for her husband Iulius Honomastianus.

EDCS-11501507.translation: Gaius Julius Falerna Rufus, son of Gaius, for himself, and for his father Gaius Julius Menophilus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, and for his mother Curfia Major, daughter of Lucius, and for his brother Lucius Julius Falerna Bassus, and for his own descendants.
EDCS-11501507.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication by Gaius Julius Falerna Rufus, also including his parents, brother, and descendants.

EDCS-11501516.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Iulia Mallisa, daughter of L. simi.

EDCS-11501524.translation: Iulia Casta for herself, and for Flavius Primitivus, and for her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11501524.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication by Iulia Casta, including Flavius Primitivus and her freedpersons.

EDCS-11501540.translation: Titianus (made this) for his daughter Iulia Musa.
EDCS-11501540.summary: This is a dedication by Titianus for his daughter Iulia Musa.

EDCS-11501553.translation: Iulia Zosima, freedwoman of a woman, was placed with her fellow freedman Iulius,”
EDCS-11501553.summary: This inscription records the burial arrangement of Iulia Zosima, a freedwoman, with her fellow freedman Iulius.

EDCS-11501568.translation: Iustuleius, the father, (dedicated this) for his dearest daughter Iustuleia Vera, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-11501568.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iustuleius for his beloved daughter Iustuleia Vera.

EDCS-11501578.translation: Thyrsus: Labeo, I implore you, grant me hospitality, for I have been ejected from the place you gave me among the living. Thyrsus: Labeo, come, everything is ready for me.
EDCS-11501578.summary: This is a dialogue inscribed on a tomb, likely between the deceased Labeo and Thyrsus, discussing hospitality and the afterlife.

EDCS-11501600.summary: A funerary inscription identifying Gaius Lollius Pinus.

EDCS-11501617.translation: His sons erected this for their well-deserving father, Marcus Lurius Valerius.
EDCS-11501617.summary: A funerary monument erected by sons for their father, Marcus Lurius Valerius.

EDCS-11501622.translation: Marcius Maior erected this for Marcius, his fellow servant.
EDCS-11501622.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcius Maior for his fellow slave, Marcius.

EDCS-11501627.translation: Marcus Maecius Polybius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-11501627.summary: An ownership mark or simple identification of Marcus Maecius Polybius, son of Marcus, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-11501638.translation: Gaius Marcius Papia, son of Gaius, for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and this monument or sepulchre shall not follow its heir; may Ariston, the phratarch, or the metal-workers, or the overseer, or the administrators, or any other person of the phratry of Aristaei not have the authority to postpone the sacrifice or the dinner for his own wife Valeria Musa beyond the appointed days, and let him borrow two hundred denarii, not more than two hundred and fifty denarii, in the name of [---]; nor shall the phratarch, or the metal-workers, or the overseer, or the administrators, or any other person of the phratry of Aristaei have the authority to take a phratarch for these names, nor shall it be given on credit. And whoever the borrower gives [---] another phratarch, let him be admitted into the agorai, and if it seems good to the agorai, as has been decreed for the phratarch and metal-workers, then let the administration be carried out by the aforementioned persons. And let those who have borrowed let the bronze [coins?] be brought to the agorai on the seventh day of the month of Pantheon, becoming full, and let the phratry vote on whom they wish to lend to, and only then shall another administration be carried out each year, on those two days on which they sacrifice and dine; let the arrears be given to Valeria Musa. And the inscription which has been written or affixed, the phratarch, or the metal-workers, or the overseer, or the administrators, shall be responsible for handing it over to those who are always appointed by the phratry. And if the phratarch, or the metal-workers, or the overseer, or the administrators, or the borrowers, or any other person does anything contrary to these regulations written above, let him pay two hundred denarii to the sacred property of the phratry gods, and this is the recovery.
EDCS-11501638.summary: This complex inscription outlines the terms for a loan from a funerary endowment managed by a phratry, ensuring that funds are used for sacrifices and a dinner in honor of Valeria Musa and her husband, Gaius Marcius Papia, with penalties for misuse.

EDCS-11501645.summary: A funerary inscription identifying Marcia Venusta.

EDCS-11501646.translation: Gaius Julius Hermeros for his deserving wife Margaridi.
EDCS-11501646.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Julius Hermeros for his deserving wife Margaridi.

EDCS-11501656.translation: For Maria Procula, daughter of Lucius, daughter of Maria Procilla, to her most devoted sister, in her own name and in the name of Maria Musa, her mother, and Maria Caecilia Procilla, her daughter, and Marcus Caecilius Caecilianus, her husband; a plot granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11501656.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maria Procula, detailing her family members (mother, daughter, husband) and noting the plot was granted by official decree.

EDCS-11501657.translation: For Maria Psyche, who deserved well.
EDCS-11501657.summary: A funerary dedication for Maria Psyche, acknowledging her merit.

EDCS-11501664.translation: Medullina Flora, daughter of Caius, for herself and for Medullina Hilara, her mother, and her own [family].
EDCS-11501664.summary: A funerary inscription for Medullina Flora, who made provisions for herself, her mother, and other family members.

EDCS-11501666.translation: Lucius Memmius Graptus for himself and for his dearest wife Iulia Felicula and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-11501666.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-purchase for the deceased and their descendants.

EDCS-11501672.translation: Caius Messius Primigenius, freedman of Caius, for himself and for his children Messius Primigenius and Hilara, and for their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11501672.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-purchase for the deceased and their children and descendants.

EDCS-11501674.translation: In memory of Messia Pompeiana, daughter of Lucius, Aulus Egrilius Maximus [erected this] for his wife, of excellent and rare character.
EDCS-11501674.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Aulus Egrilius Maximus to his wife Messia Pompeiana, highlighting her virtues.

EDCS-11501677.translation: Gnaeus Minatius Musa, and Naevia Chreste, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-11501677.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Minatius Musa and Naevia Chreste, likely a couple.

EDCS-11501682.translation: Minucius Successus, aged 80. Antonia Paulina made [this] for her parent.
EDCS-11501682.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Minucius Successus and states that it was made by Antonia Paulina for her parent.

EDCS-11501689.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content beyond a name.

EDCS-11501695.translation: Lucius Munius Firmus, while alive, for himself and for his son Lucius Munius Firmus, and for his living wife Munia Plocamiae, and for his family.
EDCS-11501695.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-purchase for the deceased, his son, his wife, and his family.

EDCS-11501706.translation: [---] Strobilus [made this] for himself and for his son [---]nius Clementi and for his most dutiful partner Nasuleia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, and for those for whom I shall have provided in my will.
EDCS-11501706.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-purchase for the deceased, his son, his partner, and heirs designated in his will.

EDCS-11501715.translation: In memory of Nicinia Epictesis, Caius Aulius Thallus [dedicated this] for his most chaste wife.
EDCS-11501715.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Caius Aulius Thallus to his wife Nicinia Epictesis.

EDCS-11501716.translation: Caius Ninnius Tertius, freedman of Caius, while alive, [and] Cnaeus Epidius Quartio, freedman of a woman, while alive, [and] Naevia Salvia, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-11501716.summary: This funerary inscription records three individuals (two men and one woman), all freedpersons, who purchased their burial plots during their lifetime.

EDCS-11501720.translation: Nonia Maxsima lived 35 years, and most sadly, her mother made this for her daughter. Cantria Polla, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-11501720.summary: This epitaph records the death of Nonia Maxsima and was erected by her mother.

EDCS-11501722.translation: Gaius Novius Onesimus made this for Gaius Novius Thallus and his wife Novia Euhodia, and for their children Gaius Novius Sabinianus and Novia Iusta, who deserved well, and for himself and his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11501722.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Gaius Novius Onesimus for his family, including his parents and children.

EDCS-11501724.translation: Lucius Licinius Laco made this for his well-deserving wife Numeria Epictesis.
EDCS-11501724.summary: This epitaph records a dedication by Lucius Licinius Laco to his wife.

EDCS-11501735.translation: Gaius Octavius Hicetes for himself, and for his wife Terentia Pia, daughter of Gaius, and for Gaius Octavius Nepos, his father and son, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11501735.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and includes his wife, father, and son.

EDCS-11501762.translation: Marcus Laelius Dardanus, freedman of Gaius, for himself and for his well-deserving wife Paccia Euposio, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-11501762.summary: This epitaph records a self-dedication and includes his wife, Paccia Euposio.

EDCS-11501779.translation: Perpernia Psecas, freedwoman of Marcus, for herself and for her patron Marcus Perperna Eutyches, and for his children and her own.
EDCS-11501779.summary: This epitaph records a self-dedication by Perpernia Psecas and includes her patron and his children.

EDCS-11501786.translation: Phainus for his well-deserving wife and conservator, Iucunda.
EDCS-11501786.summary: This epitaph records a dedication to a wife named Iucunda, calling her a 'conservator'.

EDCS-11501790.translation: [For] herself and for her co-freedman Philippus, Fortunata [for] Philippus... [---]asprenius.
EDCS-11501790.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, likely a self-dedication including a co-freedman named Philippus and potentially another individual.

EDCS-11501799.translation: Perelia Gemella for her well-deserving friend Polybius Amarantianus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-11501799.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Perelia Gemella to her friend Polybius Amarantianus, a freedman of the emperor.

EDCS-11501808.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Pompeius Neapolitanus for his well-deserving freedwoman Pompeia Eutychia.
EDCS-11501808.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Lucius Pompeius Neapolitanus to his freedwoman Pompeia Eutychia.

EDCS-11501809.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia Gluchera, identified as a freedwoman.

EDCS-11501817.translation: Quintus Pomponius Petronianus, had it been possible for him to make it eternal, the Muses would have granted him perpetual safety.
EDCS-11501817.summary: This is a poetic inscription by Quintus Pomponius Petronianus, expressing a wish for eternal safety, possibly on a monument dedicated to him or the Muses.

EDCS-11501820.translation: Lucius Pontius Phegeus for himself and for his most excellent wife Castricia Eutychis, and for my freedmen and freedwomen whom I honored in my will, and for their descendants.
EDCS-11501820.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Pontius Phegeus for himself, his wife, his freedpeople, and their descendants, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-11501835.translation: Mundus Marcellinus dedicated and made this for the Divine Shades of his most holy wife Creonitas Procilla.
EDCS-11501835.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Mundus Marcellinus for his wife Creonitas Procilla, intended for the Divine Shades.

EDCS-11501836.translation: For Procula, for her most sweet, most rare, most dear, and incomparable son.
EDCS-11501836.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Procula to her son, describing him with terms of endearment and praise.

EDCS-11501837.translation: Gaius Proculeius Pylades for himself and for Julia Phaenusa, and for his wife Dynates, and for his family.
EDCS-11501837.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Proculeius Pylades for himself, his wife, and his family, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-11501839.translation: Gaius Publicius Donatus and Publicia Liberalis for themselves and for their family, freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants.
EDCS-11501839.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Publicius Donatus and Publicia Liberalis for themselves, their family, freedpeople, and their descendants.

EDCS-11501854.translation: Ravia Elapio, freedwoman of Gaius. Ravia Callityche, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-11501854.summary: This inscription lists two women, Ravia Elapio and Ravia Callityche, both identified as freedwomen of Gaius, possibly as owners or patrons.

EDCS-11600005.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph recording the name Satur and stating he lived for a certain number of years.

EDCS-11600017.translation: Here rests in peace Maurica, who lived for more or less 40 years, buried on the third day before the Kalends of June, after the consulship of the most distinguished consul Apion.
EDCS-11600017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maurica, stating her approximate age at death and the date of her burial, which is dated after the consulship of Apion.

EDCS-11600018.translation: Marcius Gregarius, servant of God, rested here in peace. He lived for about 60 years, called by the Lord on the day before the Ides of April, during the consulship of Probus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-11600018.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcius Gregarius, noting his life span and date of death during the consulship of Probus.

EDCS-11600020.translation: Alex, consul [for] more than 9 years, was laid to rest on the third day before the Ides [of a month].
EDCS-11600020.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the burial of Alex, mentioning a period of over 9 years as consul and a burial date.

EDCS-11600021.summary: This is a very short inscription identifying Saint John.

EDCS-11600022.translation: John, after it was previously a tomb of small opening, enlarged the obscure sepulchre with worthy honor, so that the altars might be open to eternal sacred rites.
EDCS-11600022.summary: This inscription, likely a dedication, describes John enlarging a tomb and refers to altars for sacred rites.

EDCS-11600025.translation: The watering was opened with the permission and care of Decimus Satrius Rago, curator of the August water supply, on the third day before the Kalends of January, during the consulship of Iunius Blaesus and Servius Lentulus.
EDCS-11600025.summary: This inscription records the opening of a water supply during the consulship of Iunius Blaesus and Servius Lentulus, attributing the work to Decimus Satrius Rago.

EDCS-11600026.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely the name of an individual, Quintus Carisius Diop.

EDCS-11600056.translation: May the Holy Spirit be with you and with me... Alfius... peace.
EDCS-11600056.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription invoking the Holy Spirit and wishing peace, possibly a funerary or devotional text.

EDCS-11700687.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely the name of an individual, Publius Ummidius.

EDCS-11700693.translation: To our Lords Emperors Diocletian Invictus Augustus and Maximian Invictus Augustus and Constantius and Maximian, most noble Caesars.
EDCS-11700693.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Maximian.

EDCS-11700696.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Invictus Augustus, son of the divine Constantius, Pious.
EDCS-11700696.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, acknowledging his divine lineage and imperial titles.

EDCS-11700698.translation: Publius Servilius Timodemus, freedman of Publius. Servilia Sabbis, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-11700698.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedpersons, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-11700700.translation: To Gnaeus Mevius Anterus, Gnaeus Mevius Amarantus, Gnaeus Mevius Felix, Gnaeus Mevius Magnarius.
EDCS-11700700.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely to the gods or to deceased individuals, with multiple names listed.

EDCS-11700701.translation: Diogenes, slave of Pomponia, freedman of Cnaeus, made this.
EDCS-11700701.summary: This inscription states that Diogenes, a slave belonging to Pomponia and freed by Cnaeus, commissioned the work.

EDCS-11700703.translation: To Marcus Mestrius Falco, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe. To Pontia Polla, daughter of Publius. To Marcus Pollio, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe. [To XXX], son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-11700703.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a funerary text honoring multiple members of the Mestrii family, including a restored name.

EDCS-11700704.translation: Quintus Licinius Philodamus, freedman of Quintus, for himself and for Licinia Faustus, freedwoman of Quintus, and for Staedia Hilarus, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-11700704.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to two freedwomen, likely for funerary purposes.

EDCS-11700705.translation: Lucius Heleius, son of Lucius, as quaestor, arranged for this to be made by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11700705.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Heleius, son of Lucius, in his role as quaestor, had this monument constructed by order of the town council.

EDCS-11700706.translation: Sacred to Hercules in the name of Marcus Procilius Maximianus, one of the IIII viri, for legal proceedings in Interamna Lirenas. Marcus Procilius Augustalis, his father.
EDCS-11700706.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hercules, made by Marcus Procilius Augustalis on behalf of his son, Marcus Procilius Maximianus, who held an official position in Interamna.

EDCS-11700707.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Marcus Procilius Augustalis repaired and dedicated this, which Quintus Turranius Fonteianus had dedicated from his own land.
EDCS-11700707.summary: This inscription records the repair and rededication of a sacred monument to Hercules by Marcus Procilius Augustalis, which was originally dedicated by Quintus Turranius Fonteianus.

EDCS-11700709.translation: To Rubria Salvilla, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-11700709.summary: This inscription is a dedication or funerary marker for Rubria Salvilla, a freedwoman.

EDCS-11700712.translation: Marcus Barronius Sura, son of Marcus.
EDCS-11700712.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Barronius Sura, son of Marcus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-11700713.translation: Of Marcus Asellius, son of Caius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-11700713.summary: This is a tribal designation for Marcus Asellius, son of Caius.

EDCS-11700715.translation: Quintus Luccius Geminus, son of Quintus, of the Oufentina tribe, for himself and his family, 14 feet in the field.
EDCS-11700715.summary: This inscription records a land grant or boundary marker of 14 feet for Quintus Luccius Geminus and his family.

EDCS-11700717.translation: Of Numerius, son of Lucius, freedman of Numerius, Philo Africanus // Of Clarus, slave of Lucius, son of Numerius.
EDCS-11700717.summary: This inscription records the ownership or dedication of property by two individuals, Philo Africanus and Clarus, who are freedman and slave respectively.

EDCS-11700721.translation: Of Marcus Surredius, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-11700721.summary: This is a tribal designation for Marcus Surredius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-11700724.translation: To Lucius Sergius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, by his will.
EDCS-11700724.summary: This inscription is a posthumous dedication or record related to Lucius Sergius Rufus, made according to his will.

EDCS-11700726.translation: Of Lucius Aufidius Secundus, son of Spurius, and Aufidia, freedwoman of Lucius, and Pescinnia Iucunda.
EDCS-11700726.summary: This inscription lists individuals, likely family members or beneficiaries, possibly related to property or inheritance.

EDCS-11700727.translation: Caius Marius Maturus, freedman of Caius, lives for Maria Quinta, freedwoman of Spurius.
EDCS-11700727.summary: This inscription records the living arrangement or status of Maria Quinta, who is under the care of Caius Marius Maturus.

EDCS-11700728.translation: Quintus Gustilius Hilarus, freedman of Quintus, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-11700728.summary: This inscription records a land measurement or boundary of 10 feet in the field belonging to Quintus Gustilius Hilarus.

EDCS-11700729.translation: [...] // AEI[3] // Murtius [3] // Rausius [3] // Aemilius [3] // Caecilius Vitalis // Helvius [
EDCS-11700729.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely lists names of individuals, possibly for a funerary or commemorative purpose.

EDCS-11700732.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius, the husband, made this for his most holy wife, a virtuous woman, who lived 26 years and 6 months.
EDCS-11700732.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius to his wife, recording her virtue and lifespan of 26 years and 6 months.

EDCS-11700735.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave named Oarino, owned by Pontia.

EDCS-11700736.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for Pollio, son of Gaius, and Calliopa.

EDCS-11700742.translation: Gaius Com[---], son of Gaius, Secundus, a veteran of the V Praetorian Cohort, century of Aconi, aedile of the colony of Minturnae.
EDCS-11700742.summary: This is an epitaph for Secundus, a veteran of the Praetorian Guard and aedile of Minturnae, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11700744.translation: Tertia, his freedwoman, at her own expense.
EDCS-11700744.summary: This inscription likely records that Tertia, a freedwoman, paid for a monument or dedication at her own expense.

EDCS-11700746.translation: The magistrates restored this. Marcus Sepunius Statius, freedman of Marcus; Aulus Postumius Antiochus, freedman of Gaius; Gaius Papirius Nicephor, freedman of Gaius; Manius Paccius Apollonius, freedman of Manius; Quintus Maecilius Antiochus, freedman of Quintus; Dionysius, slave of Lucius of Volcei.
EDCS-11700746.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a public work or building by several freedmen and a slave, who are identified by their patrons and origins.

EDCS-11900001.translation: Varenus, freedman of Augustus, assistant to the registrar, made this. He willingly set up a vow to the god Apollo.
EDCS-11900001.summary: This is a dedication to the god Apollo by Varenus, an assistant registrar and freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-11900003.translation: Gaius Valerius Myron, a beneficiary of the prefect of the Fourth Cohort of Vigiles, paid his vow to Fortunata Sancta willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11900003.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Valerius Myron to Fortuna Sancta, recorded during his service as a beneficiary under the prefect of the Vigiles.

EDCS-11900018.translation: Lucius Aemilius Euschemus made a vow by the command of Jupiter Sabazius.
EDCS-11900018.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Aemilius Euschemus to Jupiter Sabazius.

EDCS-11900022.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Sextus Caecilius Protus, quinquennial magistrate of the guild of Osian carpenters.
EDCS-11900022.summary: This is a dedication to Mars Augustus by Sextus Caecilius Protus, a magistrate of the carpenters' guild in Ostia.

EDCS-11900028.translation: Gaius Atilius Glyco, son of Titus, from the Palatina tribe, gave this gift to the unconquered god Mithras.
EDCS-11900028.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the god Mithras by Gaius Atilius Glyco, a member of the Palatina tribe.

EDCS-11900029.translation: The slave-woman of Crescentis and Hilaros, from the Doryphoriana of Pompeii, set up this [statue] to the unconquered Sun god Sol from her own money.
EDCS-11900029.summary: A funerary or votive monument erected by a slave-woman to Sol.

EDCS-11900032.translation: Petronius Felix Marsus, son of Marcus Lollianus Callinicus, dedicated this Arimanium statue as a gift.
EDCS-11900032.summary: A dedication of a statue to an unspecified recipient, likely Silvanus, by Petronius Felix Marsus.

EDCS-11900036.translation: Aurelius Crescens, freedman of the emperor, restored this cave for his brothers after it collapsed.
EDCS-11900036.summary: A restoration of a cave structure for his brothers by Aurelius Crescens, a freedman of the emperor.

EDCS-11900037.translation: Hispanus, freedman of the emperor and a clerk, paid his vow to the divine power for [his] promotions.
EDCS-11900037.summary: A votive inscription by Hispanus, a freedman and clerk, to a divinity for career advancement.

EDCS-11900038.translation: Lucius Hortensius Heraclida, ship's captain, made this.
EDCS-11900038.summary: An attribution of a manufactured object or structure to Lucius Hortensius Heraclida, a ship's captain.

EDCS-11900041.translation: Sacred to Silvanus, the god of the imperial household, dedicated by Iuvenis under the supervision of Achilles, freedman of the emperor, with Xanthos in attendance.
EDCS-11900041.summary: A sacred dedication to Silvanus, god of the imperial household, supervised by Achilles, an imperial freedman.

EDCS-11900046.summary: A very fragmentary inscription that may record the name and occupation of an individual.

EDCS-11900048.translation: Anteros and Theodora restored this temple to Silvanus Sanctus, which had fallen into ruin from its foundations, with their own money.
EDCS-11900048.summary: The restoration of a temple dedicated to Silvanus Sanctus by Anteros and Theodora.

EDCS-11900049.translation: To Silvanus Sanctus, Publius Luscius Bergilianus, priest of the god Liber Pater of the Bonadienses, and Silvanus Sanctus, to whom I give great thanks, the contractor of the bird-hunts.
EDCS-11900049.summary: A complex dedication to Silvanus Sanctus by a priest of Liber Pater and a hunting contractor, possibly indicating a joint dedication or a dedication to multiple deities.

EDCS-11900053.translation: Eucarpus gave this gift from his own resources after a vision.
EDCS-11900053.summary: A votive dedication of a gift by Eucarpus, inspired by a divine vision.

EDCS-11900102.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to Emperor Septimius Severus and his campaigns, with the date being inferable from the names of the emperors mentioned.

EDCS-11900103.translation: To Lucius Septimius Severus, [son of] Marcus Aurelius [Antoninus]
EDCS-11900103.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus and likely his son Caracalla, dating to their joint reign.

EDCS-11900105.translation: To Julia Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camps, under Gnaeus Marcius Rustius Rufus, most distinguished prefect of the vigiles, a man of the highest caliber, with Caius Laecanius Novatillianus, subprefect, and Marcus Flavius Raesianus, tribune of the II cohort of vigiles, in charge of the detachment.
EDCS-11900105.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Domna, mother of emperors and commander of the camps, set up under the prefect of the vigiles Cn. Marcius Rustius Rufus during the reign of Caracalla or Elagabalus.

EDCS-11900116.translation: While acting: Aurelius Diza, centurion; Atilius Vitalis, centurion; Lucius Septimius Victorinus, centurion; Marcius Quintus, centurion, cornicularius of the tribune. Cupentius Geminianus. To our lord, the most invincible and, above all, the strongest Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, Pius, Felix, Invictus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, proconsul, father of the country. [[3]]o prefect of the vigiles, a man of the highest caliber, while acting under Aelius Spectatus, subprefect of the vigiles, an outstanding man, and Aurelius Masculus, tribune of the VI cohort of vigiles, in charge of the detachment. Dedicated on the day before the Nones of February, when Emperor Gordianus Augustus and Aviola were consuls.
EDCS-11900116.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Gordian III, listing officials and military personnel involved, and is dated to his second consulship in 240 AD.

EDCS-11900117.translation: To Furia Sabinia Tranquillina, most holy Augusta, wife of our lord Gordianus Augustus, under the supervision of Valerius Valens, a man of the highest caliber, prefect of the vigiles, acting prefect of the praetorian prefects, men of the highest caliber, and Valerius Alexander, an outstanding man, subprefect of the vigiles, and Iulius Magnus, an outstanding man, subprefect of the grain supply, acting subprefect of the vigiles, the seven Gordian cohorts of vigiles.
EDCS-11900117.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Furia Sabinia Tranquillina, wife of Emperor Gordian III, listing various officials involved in the supervision of the vigiles and grain supply, likely dating to Gordian III's reign.

EDCS-11900128.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Valentinian I, likely dating to his reign in the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-11900129.translation: Atuleius Herculius, a most distinguished man, prefect of the grain supply, erected this for the victorious and triumphant always Augusti Valentinian, Theodosius, Arcadius, and Maximus, for the prosperity and happiness and clemency of the times.
EDCS-11900129.summary: This inscription records the construction by Atuleius Herculius, prefect of the grain supply, to honor the emperors Valentinian, Theodosius, Arcadius, and Maximus, likely dating to the late 4th or early 5th century AD.

EDCS-11900172.translation: To Heliodorus, a Roman knight, who lived 27 years, 8 months, and 23 days, to his dearest wife, to Symmachus his brother, and to his pupils Iulia and Iulius Ampiatus, and to his good concubine, 25 feet in front and 25 feet in the rear.
EDCS-11900172.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Heliodorus, a Roman knight, and other family members, providing specific details about their lives and burial plot dimensions.

EDCS-11900177.translation: To Titus Petronius Priscus, son of Titus, of the Aniensian tribe, procurator of the emperor for the iron mines and the grain supply of Ostia, prefect of the II ala of Pannonians, tribune of the VII Gemina Felix legion, prefect of the [[[3]I [3]]] cohort, [---] [---] [---] [---] of the lyntrarii? [land] granted by decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-11900177.summary: This is a military and administrative career inscription for Titus Petronius Priscus, detailing his various commands and procuratorial duties, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11900198.translation: To the divine spirits, for Menander, the treasurer.
EDCS-11900198.summary: This is a dedication to the 'dis manibus' (departed spirits) for Menander, a treasurer, likely a funerary inscription.

EDCS-11900199.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Cornelia or Veratia Rhodope, a deserving wife. Optatus, deputy for the freedman administrator of our Augustus, [erected this].
EDCS-11900199.summary: A funerary dedication for a woman named Cornelia (or Veratia Rhodope) by her husband, who served as a deputy administrator. The inscription likely dates to the imperial period.

EDCS-11900200.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. His sons made this for Valentino, a deserving administrator, who lived for 48 years.
EDCS-11900200.summary: A funerary dedication for an administrator named Valentino, erected by his sons, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-11900202.summary: A fragmentary inscription identifying a military officer, Lucius Aelius Provincialis, who held the rank of centurion and was involved with grain supply, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900206.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Similius, a veteran of the 10th Praetorian cohort, [erected this] for himself, his wife, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, on the front.
EDCS-11900206.summary: A funerary dedication by a veteran of the Praetorian Guard for himself and his family, indicating a wish for their eternal well-being and burial location. Likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900217.translation: [---] 3rd cohort, [---] century of Atti / [---] Mamertinus / [and] Rufus, as consuls / [---] tribune of the 6th cohort / [who died] in a detachment / [at Ostia] on the Ides of [---]
EDCS-11900217.summary: A fragmentary military inscription possibly recording deaths within a vexillation (detachment) of the 3rd cohort at Ostia, mentioning consuls and a tribune. The date is uncertain due to the lacunae but likely falls within the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900219.translation: Severus / [and Antoninus?], Augusti, consuls. / Cohort [---]VI, century Valent(i?), / who died at Ostia in a detachment from the Ides of August to the Ides of December. / [---] Titinius [---], receives public grain on the 8th day, 42nd port. / [---]us, receives public grain on the 22nd day, 40th port. / Lucius Brittius, son of Lucius, [---] receives public grain on the 22nd day, 40th port. / Gnaeus Tuccius, son of Gnaeus [---] Hermes, receives public grain on the 22nd day, 40th port. / Gaius Antonius, son of Gaius [---], receives public grain on the 22nd day, 40th port. / Gaius Julius Secundus, freedman of Gaius, [---] received on the dedicated day, 8 days before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-11900219.summary: This inscription records the deaths of soldiers in a detachment at Ostia and details the distribution of public grain to various individuals, likely soldiers or officials, during the consulship of Severus and Antoninus. It provides logistical information about grain supply and military presence in Ostia during the late Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900222.translation: Cohort III of Vigiles, Maximi's century. Julius Baccius, soldier of Cohort III of Vigiles, Maximi's century. Received grain. Titus Aelius Sarapio, soldier of Cohort III of Vigiles, Maximi's century, became a soldier on the 7th Ides of July under Prefect Aemilianus, Subprefect Senecio. Marcus Atteius Primitivus, soldier, became a soldier on the 7th of July under Umbricius Aemilianus, Prefect, Subprefect Senecio. Receives grain. Receives grain on the first day, 16th port. We died, tent-mates, under the supervision of Tribune Varius Florus, tribune of the First Cohort of Vigiles, the same [under supervision of] Cassius Longinus, tribune of Cohort VII, Aurelius Senecio, tribune of Cohort IIII of Vigiles, Centurion Julius Maximus of Cohort III, Tesserarius Julius Proculus.
EDCS-11900222.summary: This inscription details the service and grain distribution of soldiers within Cohort III of the Vigiles (firefighters and police) in Rome, mentioning officers like Prefect Aemilianus and various tribunes and centurions. It also records the deaths of 'tent-mates' and dates of service, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11900223.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gemellianus Ravi, Caius Nonius, [---] and E. Oppius D(---) OVRBVM [---] from V A IOS XX PI MVVC CIAN VR nus ICAMO VI OISA DIN ITV contubernalis oremucui IV nerunt agents A RVRV BAN S DD CAIV P OM R AMVSVN VIRSOG MV PIAC NOVI VIC I OV VSIMPPR. Oppius Gemellianus wrote that they may go safely and come safely.
EDCS-11900223.summary: A funerary inscription, likely for soldiers, that records the names of several individuals including Oppius Gemellianus, who wrote the epitaph, and expresses a wish for their safe passage in the afterlife. The fragmentary nature makes precise dating difficult, but it is likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900229.translation: Fortunatus, acting as a junior officer (princeps), at the fifth hour. Legally, happily.
EDCS-11900229.summary: A brief inscription possibly marking a duty roster or a personal note, mentioning Fortunatus in a junior role ('princeps') and expressing good wishes, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900233.translation: Cohors [---] Pomponius Gamp, 15 days before the Kalends of June. Cincius Ianuarius. Pomponius Felix. LIC Licinius Primitius. Cohort III, Rubri's century. P. Tiberius Felix. Cohort III. Cohort V. Pomponius Felix. Cohort III. Cohort I. Cohort V.
EDCS-11900233.summary: This inscription lists names and possibly military affiliations (cohorts and centurions), including Pomponius Gamp and others, with a date reference of 15 days before the Kalends of June. It likely pertains to military personnel, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900234.translation: From Hirpini Donati by Mani Murrius, of Cohort VII Vigiles, century of Naevius Di. To the spirits of the departed, with good will.
EDCS-11900234.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hirpini Donati, likely erected by Mani Murrius, and it mentions his military service in Cohort VII Vigiles and the century of Naevius Di.

EDCS-11900235.translation: Marcus Aurelius MXX IA, Aemilius Iunior NVII, NVM Iunius Chresimus, [his] son.
EDCS-11900235.summary: This epitaph records the names of Marcus Aurelius MXX IA, Aemilius Iunior NVII, and Iunius Chresimus, with the latter identified as the son of the former, likely belonging to a military context.

EDCS-11900236.summary: A very brief inscription, likely an epitaph or a simple dedication, identifying Aurelius Hermogenes.

EDCS-11900238.summary: This inscription is a short personal note or epitaph identifying Venustus as a good man.

EDCS-11900239.translation: Venustus, a good man. To our lord Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, we made the station for 30 days, the soldiers of Cohort I Vigiles Severiana. Sicuinius Fidelis, Clodius Floridianus, Mantius Felix, [---] Pertius Nampamo, [cornet player?] of the tribune of the cohort, [---].
EDCS-11900239.summary: This inscription records the construction of a station by soldiers of Cohort I Vigiles Severiana during the reign of Severus Alexander, and lists several individuals, some with military roles.

EDCS-11900240.translation: Caius Licinius Felix and Monna wish all future success. Caius Licinius Felix made [this]. Sulpicius Silvinus, supervisor of the tax collectors, Aelius Mansuetus, the administrator, Iustus Claudius Quintus, Marcius Felix, Caius Salvius Optatus.
EDCS-11900240.summary: This inscription records the creation of something by Caius Licinius Felix and mentions several other individuals involved in administrative or supervisory roles.

EDCS-11900241.translation: Century V, watch duty on the 12th day before the Kalends of March. Marcus Valerius Severus with Matusa Aur T.
EDCS-11900241.summary: This inscription records a military watch duty for Century V on a specific date and names Marcus Valerius Severus and another individual.

EDCS-11900242.summary: This is a short inscription identifying the century of Rufus and naming Varius Inge.

EDCS-11900297.summary: This inscription appears to be a series of names and possibly short dedications or personal notes, potentially related to a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-11900311.translation: Titus Flavius Fortunatus gave a gift to the stonecutters.
EDCS-11900311.summary: This inscription records a gift made by Titus Flavius Fortunatus to the stonecutters.

EDCS-11900347.translation: To Vitalio Mus, Junior, Titus Aulus, Caius, Lucius, Publius, Caius, Lucius, Lucius.
EDCS-11900347.summary: This is a dedication listing several individuals, likely intended for Vitalio Mus, Junior, with a series of names following.

EDCS-11900352.translation: Firmus Gemellus, Hermes, Tinucius Euprepes, Silvanus, Minuleius Istephanus, Mamilius Marcianus, Onesimus, Magnius Cossutianus, Vitalio Calpurnius Felicianus Sollemnis, Italians, Hermes, Hermes, Aelius Satius Chronius, Cornelius Saturninus, Ieracarus, Vincentius, Cornelius, Quintus, Publius Cornelius, Lucius Florius, Caius Prastina, Titus Marc, Publius Cornelius, Quintus, Lucius.
EDCS-11900352.summary: This inscription is a list of names, possibly commemorating members of a group or beneficiaries of a benefactor, with references to 'Augusti nostri' suggesting a connection to the imperial family or administration, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-11900356.translation: Marcus Ulpius Olimpianus and his school approved and dedicated Marcus Ulpius Abascantus, Marcus Ulpius Divus, Marcus Ulpius Eutyches.
EDCS-11900356.summary: This inscription records the approval and dedication of a school by Marcus Ulpius Olimpianus, with other named individuals involved, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900357.translation: Under the consulship of Romanus, Onesimus, Iatius, Hirenius Chrestio, Heraclius.
EDCS-11900357.summary: This inscription records names, possibly officials or individuals mentioned in relation to a specific consulship.

EDCS-11900360.translation: Marcus Aurelius Lucius Plom, Caius Iulius Caius Aurelianus.
EDCS-11900360.summary: This is a list of names, likely indicating individuals, possibly from a civic or military context during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900361.translation: Marcus Atticus Speius, Caius Canus, quinquennials, Marcus Atticus.
EDCS-11900361.summary: This inscription mentions individuals, including 'quinquennales' (officials elected every five years), suggesting a civic or administrative context, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900362.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly commemorating freedmen or individuals associated with a patron, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900363.translation: Iesius, Aurelius Portesis, Bafius Felix, Iulius Romulus Frontinus.
EDCS-11900363.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly commemorating individuals or a group, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900367.translation: Menippus Junior, Fortunatus, Titus, Titus Tinucius Felix, Lucius Clodius Herclanus, Caius Iulius Corinthus, Lucius Septimius Karus, Titus Tinucius Rufus Junior, Aurelius Leo Valerianus, Titus Tinucius Euanthus Junior, Quintus Fuficulenius Secundus, Titus Tinucius Salutius, Titus Tinucius Eros, Iulius Ermes, Tinucius Eros, Tinucius Alexandros, Basileius.
EDCS-11900367.summary: This inscription is a lengthy list of names, likely commemorating individuals, possibly associated with a guild, family, or freedmen, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900368.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription listing a few names, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900369.translation: Titus Flavius Lucius Furius Caius Publilius Claudius Sentius Sempronius Sirius, Lucius Sulpicius Venator, Lucius Gellius Faustus, Lucius Manneius Terminalis, Publius Marius Sabinus.
EDCS-11900369.summary: This inscription lists the names of several individuals, likely officials or prominent citizens, possibly from an honorific monument or a list of benefactors, with no clear date or specific purpose indicated.

EDCS-11900370.translation: Lucius [---] Lucius M. Decimus St. Lucius V. Lucius Pl. Marcus O. Quintus M. Quintus M. Lucius Me. Titus Co. Marcus Co.
EDCS-11900370.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of Roman personal names, with some titles or abbreviations, possibly for an administrative record or a public notice, with no specific context or date provided.

EDCS-11900371.translation: Sosius, freedman of I. VBM, and his son Ruf, freedman of Quintus, and Ero, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-11900371.summary: This inscription records the names and relationships of freedmen, likely as part of a funerary monument or a legal document, with no specific date or patron identifiable beyond their names.

EDCS-11900374.summary: This inscription lists four personal names, possibly of individuals associated with a particular place or event, with no further context or dating information provided.

EDCS-11900375.translation: Caius Avianius, Titus Pomponius, Caius Iulius, Cnaeus Dottius, Marcus Aemilius, Caius Novius.
EDCS-11900375.summary: This inscription enumerates a list of Roman personal names, likely prominent citizens or officials, potentially for an honorific text or a civic record, without specific dating or context.

EDCS-11900376.translation: Caius Mamilius, Publius Tuccius, Marcus Aurelius, Sextus Sertorius.
EDCS-11900376.summary: This inscription presents a list of four Roman personal names, possibly indicating a group of individuals involved in a public or private undertaking, with no further details on their roles or the date.

EDCS-11900385.summary: This inscription records two Roman personal names, possibly as part of a larger list or a dedication, with no specific context, purpose, or date provided.

EDCS-11900387.summary: This inscription appears to contain fragments of Roman personal names, likely from a larger text or monument, with insufficient information to determine its precise meaning, purpose, or date.

EDCS-11900395.translation: He made [this] for himself and for his dearest wife Aelia Helpidia, and for his son Marcus Aurelius Rusticus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-11900395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a sevir Augustalis and former quinquennalis for himself, his wife, son, and their dependents, indicating a mid-to-late Imperial date.

EDCS-11900398.translation: Arius Auctus, sevir Augustalis, by the votes of the decurions. His wife Pelagia and mother Aucta [dedicated this].
EDCS-11900398.summary: This is a dedication to Arius Auctus, a sevir Augustalis, made by his wife and mother, likely on a public building or monument, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900405.translation: Lucius Caelius Aprilis, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, former supervisor of the ships of Carthage, and his wife Arellia Eleuthera, made this for themselves, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-11900405.summary: This is a private funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Caelius Aprilis and his wife Arellia Eleuthera for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-11900406.translation: To the departed spirits. Calpurnius Iovinus made this for his dearest brother, the priest of the Mother of the Gods of the colony of Ostia, who planted 19 trees; he lived 48 years and 2 months.
EDCS-11900406.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnius Iovinus' brother, a priest in Ostia, who was also an orchard planter and died at age 48.

EDCS-11900407.translation: To Gaius Cassius, son of Gaius Cassius, curator.
EDCS-11900407.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Cassius, son of Gaius Cassius, who served as a curator.

EDCS-11900411.translation: To the departed spirits. Claudius Venidius Eupalius, a Roman equestrian, council member of the most distinguished colony of Ostia, made this for himself, his wife Aurelia Helpis, their sons, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants; the front is 10 feet, the back 30 feet. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-11900411.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Claudius Venidius Eupalius, an equestrian and local official, for his family and slaves, indicating plot dimensions.

EDCS-11900412.translation: To Tiberius Claudius of the guild of carpenters of Ostia.
EDCS-11900412.summary: This is a dedication to Tiberius Claudius, associated with the carpenters' guild in Ostia.

EDCS-11900413.translation: C. C. Claudius, nones of December, for Tiberius Claudius, holding the office of quinquennial for the second time.
EDCS-11900413.summary: This is a dedication likely related to an office held by Tiberius Claudius, with a date in December.

EDCS-11900414.summary: This is a very brief inscription referencing Claudius and perhaps a physical matter.

EDCS-11900415.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Suriacus, son of Spurius, council member of the colony of Castronova.
EDCS-11900415.summary: This is a dedication to Tiberius Claudius Suriacus, a local official in the colony of Castronova.

EDCS-11900417.translation: Cornelius, son of Lucius, twice a duumvir, censor again.
EDCS-11900417.summary: This inscription records the political career of Cornelius, son of Lucius, noting his repeated service as duumvir and censor.

EDCS-11900418.translation: To the departed spirits. To Cornelius Nicephorus, Augustan sevirus, also quinquennial. Cornel[ia] Fortuna.
EDCS-11900418.summary: This is a funerary monument for Cornelius Nicephorus, an Augustan sevirus and quinquennial official, with a mention of Cornelia Fortuna.

EDCS-11900421.translation: To Gaius Domitius Hermogenes, son of Lucius, of the Palatina tribe, Fabius, a Roman knight, scribe of the curule aediles, a decurion co-opted into the order, and a priest of the deified Hadrian. In his priesthood, he alone and first held theatrical games at his own expense; the most distinguished order of decurions honored him with a public funeral and decreed that an equestrian statue be erected for him in the forum at public expense, because of his love and every endeavor. They did not deem it necessary to replace him as aedile, as a consolation to his father Fabius, who, because of the honors bestowed upon him, gave 50,000 sesterces to the state. From the interest of this sum, 13 days before the Kalends of August, on his birthday, the following are to be distributed annually from the forum before the statues: to the decurions, 550 denarii; to the curial scribes, 37 and a half denarii; to the librarians, 12 and a half denarii; likewise to the lictors, 25 denarii. Lucius Fabius Eutychus, chief curial scribe and librarian, and the guild of Ostian carpenters and the guild of Ostian carpenters.
EDCS-11900421.summary: This is a funerary and honorific inscription for Gaius Domitius Hermogenes, a Roman knight and official, detailing his public service and the honors he received, including funds for games and a statue, as well as provisions for annual distributions of money.

EDCS-11900424.translation: To the spirits of Aulus Egrilius Primitivus, a member of the Six Commissioners and a quinquennial official; by his heirs.
EDCS-11900424.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Egrilius Primitivus, likely a Roman official, set up by his heirs.

EDCS-11900425.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly dedicating a monument or statue, identifying Fabius Longus as a patron.

EDCS-11900426.translation: To Aulus Fabius Praenestinus, son of Aulus, grandson of Aulus, patron of the cultors.
EDCS-11900426.summary: This inscription dedicates something to Aulus Fabius Praenestinus, identifying his lineage and his role as patron to a group called 'cultors'.

EDCS-11900429.translation: Dama, freedman of Marcus and of Marcus's wife, an Augustalis.
EDCS-11900429.summary: This is an inscription for Dama, a freedman and an Augustalis, honoring him and possibly his patrons.

EDCS-11900431.translation: Augustalis, freedman of Marcus, and Au Publius Suc, the third [member].
EDCS-11900431.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions an Augustalis, a freedman of Marcus, and possibly another individual named Publius, possibly related to a group or magistracy.

EDCS-11900432.translation: To the spirits of Lucius Iulius Crescens, a Roman knight who held all offices, by Cornelia, his most excellent wife, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 20 feet, in the field [area].
EDCS-11900432.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Crescens, a Roman knight, set up by his wife Cornelia and their descendants, with dimensions indicating the plot size.

EDCS-11900433.translation: Gaius Iulius Tyrannus, master of the quinquennial guild of Ostian carpenters, made this for himself and his wife Aegrilia Moscis, who lived with me for 25 years, and for his sweetest daughter Sabina, who lived for 21 years.
EDCS-11900433.summary: This is a funerary inscription and dedication made by Gaius Iulius Tyrannus, a master of the Ostian carpenters' guild, for himself, his wife, and his daughter.

EDCS-11900434.translation: To the spirits of Aulus Livius Agathangelus, a member of the collegium of seven and an Augustalis and quinquennial official; by his heirs.
EDCS-11900434.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Livius Agathangelus, who held positions as a member of a collegium and an Augustalis, set up by his heirs.

EDCS-11900436.translation: Lucilius Gamala, son, made [this] for [his] parents.
EDCS-11900436.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription made by Lucilius Gamala for his parents.

EDCS-11900442.translation: Procula, freedwoman of Lucius Pinnius, made this for Lucius Pinnius Valens, her patron, for their marriage, and for her most dutiful and dearest son, Lucius Pinnius, son of Lucius, and for herself, and for Decimus Gessius Ianuarius, her husband, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 24 feet in front, and for Vettia Severa, daughter of Quintus, and Aulus Egrilius Hermes Augustalis, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for the well-deserving Gaius Fabius Evarius, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 24 feet in the field.
EDCS-11900442.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedwoman for her patron, husband, son, and herself, with specific dimensions for the front and field areas, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-11900444.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning Rufus, who held the office of IIvir (a high municipal magistrate), likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900448.translation: To the departed spirits. For Statia Procula, for her well-deserving husband Hermetes, who was an Augustalis and quinquennalis.
EDCS-11900448.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Statia Procula's husband, Hermetes, who held prestigious civic roles as an Augustalis and quinquennalis, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900449.summary: This inscription identifies Tatianus as a perpetual quinquennalis, a municipal official with a five-year term, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900462.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely refers to someone holding the title of Augustalis, a priest of the imperial cult, probably dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900476.translation: To the departed spirits. For Publius Ragonius Erotianus, a colleague in painting.
EDCS-11900476.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Publius Ragonius Erotianus, identifying him as a colleague in the craft of painting, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900477.translation: To the departed spirits. For [---] notus, a colleague.
EDCS-11900477.summary: This is a very fragmentary funerary dedication to a colleague whose name is mostly lost, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11900479.translation: Gaius Caninius, son of Gaius, urban praetor, judged publicly by decree of the senate.
EDCS-11900479.summary: This inscription records a public judgment made by Gaius Caninius, the urban praetor, acting on a senatorial decree, likely dating to the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11900480.translation: Private property up to the Tiber, as far as the water.
EDCS-11900480.summary: This inscription seems to mark a boundary or property line extending to the Tiber River, likely of Roman imperial date.

EDCS-11900484.translation: Station of Antoninus Augustus noster XXXX. Of Gaul and Spain, here.
EDCS-11900484.summary: This inscription appears to mark a station or stopping point, possibly related to a military or administrative route, dedicated to the emperor Antoninus and referencing the provinces of Gaul and Spain, likely dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-11900485.translation: The Horrea of Epagathus and Epaphroditus.
EDCS-11900485.summary: This is a simple ownership marker for grain warehouses belonging to Epagathus and Epaphroditus.

EDCS-11900486.translation: The duovirs Postumus Plotius, son of Marcus, and Aulus Genucius, son of Aulus, provided the site for the construction of an intersection. Caius Cartilius Poplicola, son of Caius, VII duovir and III censor, moved the intersection. The magistri vici, Decimus Caecilius Nicia, freedman of the Decimi, physician, and Lucius Marcius Stephanus, freedman of Lucius, and Publius Naevius Heraclida, freedman of Publius, made the wall and column at their own expense. Caius Cartilius Hera, freedman of Caius...
EDCS-11900486.summary: This inscription records the provision of a site and the construction/relocation of a street intersection by local officials (duovirs and magistri vici) with contributions from specific individuals, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11900488.translation: Gaius Cartilius Poplicola, son of Gaius...
EDCS-11900488.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely identifying Gaius Cartilius Poplicola, son of Gaius, probably as a magistrate.

EDCS-11900489.translation: Marcus Coelius Trophimus and Marcus Coelius Chrestus give this gift at their own expense.
EDCS-11900489.summary: This inscription records a donation made at personal expense by Marcus Coelius Trophimus and Marcus Coelius Chrestus.

EDCS-11900492.translation: Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome, placed [this] in the same city with his own money for the community of the Ostians.
EDCS-11900492.summary: This inscription records Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, Prefect of the Annona, funding a project for the citizens of Ostia in Rome, likely during the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900494.translation: Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the grain supply of the city of Rome, took care of [this], and the community also made [it] from [their] own resources.
EDCS-11900494.summary: This inscription indicates that Ragonius Vincentius Celsus, Prefect of the Annona, oversaw a project which was also funded by the community, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900497.translation: Adorned from neglected places, for the appearance of the forum and for public view, under the care of Publius Attius Clementinus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the grain supply.
EDCS-11900497.summary: This inscription describes the beautification of the forum, funded or overseen by Publius Attius Clementinus, the Prefect of the Annona, during the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900503.summary: This inscription likely refers to Theodotus and possibly indicates a renewal or restoration due to age or wear.

EDCS-11900508.summary: This is an epitaph or dedication for Saturninus, who was both a freedman and an adopted son.

EDCS-11900516.translation: To Quintus Baebius G[...], son of Marcus. To Obellius N S[...]
EDCS-11900516.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication to two individuals, Quintus Baebius G[...] and Obellius N S[...], likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11900517.translation: Under the consulship of Tiberius Iulius Candidus II and Aulus Iulius Quadratus II.
EDCS-11900517.summary: This inscription records the names of consuls, likely marking a date within their term.

EDCS-11900530.translation: Pudens, the Podargos, Pothiscus, the Barosus.
EDCS-11900530.summary: This inscription lists personal names, possibly of individuals associated with a tomb or property.

EDCS-11900531.translation: Proclus made this at his own expense.
EDCS-11900531.summary: This inscription records an individual named Proclus who funded and constructed a monument or work.

EDCS-11900533.translation: I tread upon you, O Envy.
EDCS-11900533.summary: This is an apotropaic inscription intended to ward off envy.

EDCS-11900535.translation: Mummeia Quinta and Lucius Accius Firmus bought for themselves and for Quintus Mummeius Apollinaris their father, and for Lucius Accius Firminus and Accia Quita their children, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 12 feet in front and 26 feet in the field.
EDCS-11900535.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a burial plot by Mummeia Quinta and Lucius Accius Firmus for themselves and their family members and descendants.

EDCS-11900537.translation: Manius Acilius Marianus, son of Manius, of the Voturia tribe, for himself and for Auscia Eucheni, freedwoman of Marcus, his companion, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants, 28 feet in front; this monument is shared with Cognita Optata, daughter of Cognita, for herself and her family, freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants, and in the field; this monument is shared with Manius Acilius Marianus.
EDCS-11900537.summary: This inscription details the dimensions and shared ownership of a burial monument for Manius Acilius Marianus, his household, and others including Cognita Optata and another Manius Acilius Marianus.

EDCS-11900539.translation: To Grania Aeliana, my most sweet daughter, who lived 20 years, 5 months, and 26 days.
EDCS-11900539.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Grania Aeliana, recording her age at death.

EDCS-11900540.translation: To Gnaeus Aelius Alexander, who lived 20 years, 1 month, and 2 days. Aelia Alexandria, his mother, to her most sweet son.
EDCS-11900540.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Aelius Alexander, dedicated by his mother Aelia Alexandria, and recording his age at death.

EDCS-11900541.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Aelius Decimus Claudianus, who lived 27 years, 11 months, and 28 days.
EDCS-11900541.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelius Decimus Claudianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-11900545.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Aelius Pergamus, a household slave, who lived 4 years.
EDCS-11900545.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelius Pergamus, a young household slave, recording his age at death.

EDCS-11900546.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Passidaenia, wife of Publius Aelius Sumforus, dedicated this to her most beloved husband, with whom she lived for years, by the consent of the Hermiates.
EDCS-11900546.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Passidaenia to her husband, Publius Aelius Sumforus, mentioning the consent of the Hermiates, likely indicating a communal or guild context.

EDCS-11900549.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Aelius Victorinus dedicated this to his most beloved wife, Aelia Januaria, who deserved well.
EDCS-11900549.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Titus Aelius Victorinus to his deserving wife, Aelia Januaria.

EDCS-11900550.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aelia Niceriane, while alive, dedicated this to her freedman Castorius.
EDCS-11900550.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aelia Niceriane during her lifetime for her freedman Castorius.

EDCS-11900552.translation: Anteros, freedman of Sextus Aemilius, son of Sextus, and Helena, freedwoman of Sextus Aemilius, wife of Sextus, [set this up] in front twenty feet and in the field twenty-five feet.
EDCS-11900552.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land owned by two freedpersons, Anteros and Helena, associated with a Sextus Aemilius.

EDCS-11900553.translation: Marcus Aemilius Hermes lived for 4 years, 10 months, and half a day.
EDCS-11900553.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of a child named Marcus Aemilius Hermes.

EDCS-11900554.translation: Marcus Aemilius, son of Marcus, from Malaca, [lived] for years Arrius
EDCS-11900554.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that likely records the name and possibly the lifespan of Marcus Aemilius of Malaca, with a portion referring to an Arrius.

EDCS-11900558.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Lorentius Pudens and his mother Aevillia Helpis dedicated this to their sweetest son, Lucius Lorentius Soterichus, who lived 7 years, 5 months, 10 days, and a night.
EDCS-11900558.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents, Lucius Lorentius Pudens and Aevillia Helpis, to their son, Lucius Lorentius Soterichus, detailing his short lifespan.

EDCS-11900559.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a funerary marker or the names of two individuals, Agathe and Hiacynthus.

EDCS-11900562.translation: Alexander, freedman of Marcus; Sophia, freedwoman; Fortunatus; Secundio; Faustus; Alexandria, slave.
EDCS-11900562.summary: This inscription lists several freedpersons and a slave, possibly related to a property or a burial context.

EDCS-11900566.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Fusca dedicated this to her sweetest vernaculae, Publius Antonius Charito and Ragonia Praepusa, who lived 3 years, 6 months, 9 days, and 6 hours.
EDCS-11900566.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Fusca to two young children, Publius Antonius Charito and Ragonia Praepusa, specifying their short lifespan.

EDCS-11900569.translation: To the Divine Manes. Atimetus, slave of our Caesar, made this for Aquilia Marcia and Traulia Fortunata, deserving persons.
EDCS-11900569.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a slave of Caesar to two women, Aquilia Marcia and Traulia Fortunata.

EDCS-11900573.translation: Valerius Flavianus made this for his most chaste wife Arruntia Chrise, a deserving person.
EDCS-11900573.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Valerius Flavianus to his wife Arruntia Chrise.

EDCS-11900574.summary: This is a very brief inscription that appears to record the name of a person, possibly with an ethnic or place of origin.

EDCS-11900576.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Gaius Atilius, who lived 6 months and [some] days.
EDCS-11900576.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child, Gaius Atilius, who died at the age of six months.

EDCS-11900580.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Publius Aufidius Fortunatus and Aufidia Philetena.
EDCS-11900580.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Publius Aufidius Fortunatus and Aufidia Philetena.

EDCS-11900581.translation: 8 months. Lucius Aurelius Aelianus for his deserving wife.
EDCS-11900581.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment mentioning a duration of 8 months and dedicated to a wife by Lucius Aurelius Aelianus.

EDCS-11900582.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Marcus Aurelius Chronius, dearest son, who lived one year, 3 months, 23 days, and 2 hours.
EDCS-11900582.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child, Marcus Aurelius Chronius, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-11900583.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Marcus Aurelius Parthenopaeus. Not as fate willed, but Palamedes.
EDCS-11900583.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Aurelius Parthenopaeus, with a cryptic remark suggesting an untimely death.

EDCS-11900584.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Marcus Aurelius Ragonius Priscus, son. [From his?] parents.
EDCS-11900584.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by parents to their son, Marcus Aurelius Ragonius Priscus.

EDCS-11900586.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Baberia Eugenia, daughter. Servius Baberius Scupinus and Egrilia Isias, for daughter, who lived 9 years, 27 days. Donated by themselves while living and for themselves. Agape sleeps here.
EDCS-11900586.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Servius Baberius Scupinus and Egrilia Isias for their daughter Baberia Eugenia and also for themselves, indicating a prepaid burial plot.

EDCS-11900588.translation: To the Divine Shades. Baebia Helpis made this for her deserving husband, Quintus Baebius Hermadion.
EDCS-11900588.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900594.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly the name of an individual or a dedication, with no clear dating context.

EDCS-11900595.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caecilia Licinia made this for her deserving patron, Lucius Caecilius Ianuarius.
EDCS-11900595.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedwoman to her patron, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900596.translation: To the Divine Shades. Given as a donation by Caecilius Aprilis to his deserving wife, Caecilia Tyche, who possesses half of this monument.
EDCS-11900596.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, specifying a shared ownership of the monument, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900598.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Caesius Maximus Aeminiensis, aged 26, is buried here. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
