EDCS-11900598.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young man, including a common wish for his repose, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900601.translation: Caletyche, freedwoman of the woman, made the monument at her own expense for her freedwoman, Ma ae, and for Ennio Pylades, freedman of Aulus, and for Ennio Primus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-11900601.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedwoman for herself and other freedpersons, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900602.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gnaeus Turpilius Callistus made this for his deserving wife, Statilia Si.
EDCS-11900602.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900604.translation: Decimus Calpurnius for himself, and for Calpurnia, his pious and modest wife, and for his nurse, Prima.
EDCS-11900604.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a man for himself, his wife, and his nurse, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900605.translation: Calpurnius Paulinus, who lived for 5 years and thirty-one and a half days.
EDCS-11900605.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age of a child, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900606.translation: To the Divine Shades. Licinia Phoebe made this for her most dutiful son, Lucius Calpurnius Phoebus, who lived 45 years, a deserving man.
EDCS-11900606.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her son, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11900607.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Calpurnius Primitibus, freedman of Lucius, made this for Calpurnia Pollita.
EDCS-11900607.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Calpurnius Primitibus for Calpurnia Pollita.

EDCS-11900608.translation: Marcus Calpurnius Restutus made this monument for himself and his wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; it does not pass to an heir. It is accessible from the public road, and must have 14 feet in front and 21 feet in depth.
EDCS-11900608.summary: A funerary monument inscription by Marcus Calpurnius Restutus specifying terms of inheritance and dimensions.

EDCS-11900609.translation: Marcus Calpurnius Restutus made this dedication for himself, his patron Marcus Calpurnius Fortunatus, and his wife, and for himself.
EDCS-11900609.summary: A dedication by Marcus Calpurnius Restutus for himself, his patron, and his wife.

EDCS-11900610.translation: To Calpurnia Philetis, his most devout and incomparable wife, who lived 22 years and 30 days; Caius Clodius Crescens, her husband, also dedicated this for himself.
EDCS-11900610.summary: A funerary epitaph by Caius Clodius Crescens for his wife Calpurnia Philetis, with a dedication also for himself.

EDCS-11900611.translation: Calvia Euthychia, freedwoman of Marcius, made this for herself, her family, and her patron Marcus Calvius Suavius.
EDCS-11900611.summary: A funerary dedication by Calvia Euthychia for herself, her family, and her patron.

EDCS-11900612.translation: lived 6 years and 22 days and [unknown number of] hours, by permission of Caius Cam[...]
EDCS-11900612.summary: A fragment of an epitaph recording the lifespan of a child, possibly named Cam[---].

EDCS-11900613.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Stephanus made this for his most devoted wife, Caninia Hygia.
EDCS-11900613.summary: A funerary dedication by Stephanus for his wife Caninia Hygia.

EDCS-11900614.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Carsidius Heticinus.
EDCS-11900614.summary: A funerary dedication to Carsidius Heticinus.

EDCS-11900615.translation: Carvilius Pamphilus and Publius Carvilius Hilarus made this for themselves, their families, and for Carvilius, their son, and Carvilia Hycenis, a freedwoman.
EDCS-11900615.summary: A funerary dedication by Carvilius Pamphilus and Publius Carvilius Hilarus for family members and freedpersons.

EDCS-11900617.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Castricius Hamillus and Obellia Felix [made this] for their most sweet son, Lucius Castricius Felix.
EDCS-11900617.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Castricius Hamillus and Obellia Felix for their son Lucius Castricius Felix.

EDCS-11900620.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Celadus lived 30 years. His owners Aufidius made this.
EDCS-11900620.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Celadus, commemorating his life and mentioning his owners, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900621.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Servatio made this for her well-deserving Publius Celer Atticus.
EDCS-11900621.summary: This funerary epitaph records Servatio's dedication to Publius Celer Atticus, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900622.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Bera made this for her well-deserving Celsus, a slave, aged 5 years and 7 months.
EDCS-11900622.summary: This funerary epitaph records Valeria Bera's dedication to Celsus, a young slave, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900625.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary text, with illegible content.

EDCS-11900627.translation: Cipia Veneria for her husband Cipius Victor, well-deserving, and her son C. V.
EDCS-11900627.summary: This funerary epitaph records Cipia Veneria's dedication to her husband and son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900628.translation: For Primus and Herm[---] and Here[---]
EDCS-11900628.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text, with partial names preserved.

EDCS-11900630.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Tiberius Claudius Demetrius for himself and for Memmia Ingenua, his incomparable wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 7.5 feet, in the field 23 feet.
EDCS-11900630.summary: This funerary epitaph records Tiberius Claudius Demetrius' self-dedication and dedication to his family, also specifying plot dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900633.translation: Tiberius Claudius Priscus made this for Afinia Venusta.
EDCS-11900633.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Claudius Priscus' dedication to Afinia Venusta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900634.translation: Chrysis, freedwoman of Publius Claudius, made this for herself and for Claudius Rapidus.
EDCS-11900634.summary: This funerary epitaph records Chrysis' self-dedication and dedication to Claudius Rapidus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900635.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Claudia.
EDCS-11900635.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for Claudia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900637.translation: Gaius Clodius for himself and for his wife Annia Eufrosyne, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, 15 feet in front and 20 feet in depth.
EDCS-11900637.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Ostia recording plot dimensions and ownership for Gaius Clodius, his wife, and descendants.

EDCS-11900638.translation: Marcus Clodius made [this] for himself, for Ostese his wife, for his sons, and for Marcus Clodius, Clodia Z, and the sons of Marcus Clodius, and for Clodia Z, for Ostensi his wife, and from Octavia Rufina, and from Octavia, and for freedwomen.
EDCS-11900638.summary: This funerary inscription from Ostia appears to record provisions for Marcus Clodius, his wife, sons, and freedpersons, with a mention of Octavia Rufina.

EDCS-11900639.translation: To the departed spirits. Tiberius Clodius Crescens made [this] for himself, for Passaria Veneria his wife, and for Tiberius Clodius Praesens his son, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, reserving 30 feet in front and 29 feet in depth, which was granted to him by Aurelius Mercurius, to whom the memoria came by hereditary right from the Papirii.
EDCS-11900639.summary: This funerary inscription records the dimensions of a plot and its dedication by Tiberius Clodius Crescens for his family and descendants, noting its acquisition from Aurelius Mercurius.

EDCS-11900640.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Clodius Iulius arranged for this to be made for Fortunula his wife and for Fortunula his daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-11900640.summary: This funerary inscription records a memorial arranged by Lucius Clodius Iulius for his wife and daughter.

EDCS-11900642.translation: Lucius Cocceius, son of Spurius, named Adiutor, made [this] for himself in the left half upon entering from the door, and for Cocceia Tyche his freedwoman, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, so that this part of the monument not be removed from his name, nor should he wish to place another title, nor sell it to another, nor transfer it as a gift; and if anyone does so, he must pay 50,000 sesterces to the Republic of Ostia; 12.5 feet in front and 12.5 feet in depth. Titus Manlius, freedman of Felix, named Bargathes, and Cocceia Tyche his wife made [this] together at joint expense for themselves in the right half upon entering from the door, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants, so that this part of the monument not be removed from his name, nor should he wish to place another title, nor sell it to another, nor transfer it as a gift; and if anyone does so, he must pay 50,000 sesterces to the Republic of Ostia; 12.5 feet in front and 12.5 feet in depth.
EDCS-11900642.summary: This inscription details the construction and regulations for a double tomb in Ostia, built by Lucius Cocceius and Titus Manlius for themselves, their freedpersons, and descendants, with penalties for violating the terms.

EDCS-11900646.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Gaius Cominius Castus, likely the name of the person or the owner of the monument.

EDCS-11900647.translation: To the departed spirits. For Ia Severa Concordia, most beloved. Lucius Tullius.
EDCS-11900647.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Tullius to his beloved Ia Severa Concordia.

EDCS-11900648.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, partially restored, possibly recording a name and a verb related to living or residing.

EDCS-11900651.translation: Publius Gavisidius, freedman of Publius, named Inventus; Publius Cornelius, freedman of Publius, named Flaccus; Cornelia, freedwoman of Publius, named Hilara; Publius Cornelius, freedman of Publius, named Dorio; Cornelia, freedwoman of Publius, named Prima; Publius Cornelius, son of Publius, named Faustus; Titus Statius, son of Titus, named Quirinus Bassus; 14.5 feet in front and 20 feet in depth.
EDCS-11900651.summary: This inscription enumerates several freedmen and their descendants, along with two freeborn individuals, and specifies plot dimensions, likely for a shared burial area.

EDCS-11900652.translation: For Marcus Cornelius, son of Marcus, of the Palatine tribe, for Statius, son of P. [they] made [this].
EDCS-11900652.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made for Marcus Cornelius, son of Marcus, by Statius.

EDCS-11900653.translation: To the Divine Manes of Lucius Cornelius Thiophilus and his wife Cornelia Rufina and their daughter Cornelia.
EDCS-11900653.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Cornelius Thiophilus and his family.

EDCS-11900658.translation: Gaius Critonius Philippus, his freedwoman Critonia Thais, Gaius Critonius, his freedman Philotimus, Critonia's freedwoman Fortunata. In front 20 feet, in the field 25 feet.
EDCS-11900658.summary: This inscription records land dimensions and names associated with the Critonii family, likely for property demarcation.

EDCS-11900659.translation: Gaius Critonius, his freedman Quintius, Critonia's freedwoman Zosima. In front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-11900659.summary: This inscription records land dimensions and names associated with Gaius Critonius and his freedpersons, likely for property demarcation.

EDCS-11900662.translation: Daphne and her freedmen and their descendants.
EDCS-11900662.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely dedicating a burial plot to Daphne and her freed dependents.

EDCS-11900665.translation: To the Divine Manes of Didia Epiteuxis. Valeria Felicissima the heir made this.
EDCS-11900665.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by an heir, Valeria Felicissima, for Didia Epiteuxis.

EDCS-11900667.translation: To the Divine Manes of Domitia Hilariata, who lived 4 years, 11 months, and 15 days. Quintus Domitius Aterianus and Domitia Primitiva, her parents, made this.
EDCS-11900667.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child, Domitia Hilariata, made by her parents.

EDCS-11900668.translation: Thraessa Doridis for 16 days. Caesar and Doris, of Caesar and for themselves, made this.
EDCS-11900668.summary: This inscription records a dedication or a period of service, possibly funerary, for Thraessa Doridis by Caesar and Doris.

EDCS-11900669.translation: To the Divine Manes of Lucius's freedman Dul[---].
EDCS-11900669.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for a freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-11900674.translation: Aulus Egrilius, son of Aulus, and his freedman Aesc. Egrilia, daughter of Aulus, and her freedwoman.
EDCS-11900674.summary: This inscription records familial and freedman relationships within the Egrilii family, possibly marking graves or property.

EDCS-11900675.translation: To the Divine Manes of Egrilius Julianus. Lyciscus the friend made this.
EDCS-11900675.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by a friend, Lyciscus, for Egrilius Julianus.

EDCS-11900676.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Egrilius Magnus, son of Aulus, of the Palatine tribe, lived for 5 years, 9 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-11900676.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, Aulus Egrilius Magnus, detailing his lifespan.

EDCS-11900677.translation: Aulus Egrilius Narcissus, freedman of Aulus, made this for himself, for his wife Egrilia Phoebe, freedwoman of Aulus, and for their children, sons and daughters, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for their descendants. Also for Lucilia Epicharis, freedwoman of Mulier.
EDCS-11900677.summary: A funerary monument inscription set up by Aulus Egrilius Narcissus for himself and his family, including his wife, children, and freedmen.

EDCS-11900678.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Three plots of land were granted by Egrilius Telesporus to Aemilius Picentius and Cuoleia Rufina.
EDCS-11900678.summary: A record of land allocation, granting three plots from Egrilius Telesporus to Aemilius Picentius and Cuoleia Rufina.

EDCS-11900679.translation: He made [this monument] for Egrilia Rara, his wife, and for Aulus Egrilius Zosimus, Egrilia Helpis, Aulus Egrilius Abascantus, Egrilia Thallusa, Aulus Egrilius Speratus, Egrilia Paula, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for their descendants. This monument shall not pass to an external heir. In front, 11 feet.
EDCS-11900679.summary: A funerary monument inscription specifying beneficiaries and prohibiting external inheritance, with dimensions for the front.

EDCS-11900680.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cartilius Euschemon made this for Aegrilia Charite, his most cherished wife, who deserved well.
EDCS-11900680.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Cartilius Euschemon to his beloved wife, Aegrilia Charite.

EDCS-11900681.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Clodius Eutychus made this for Aegrilia Nice, his excellent wife, and for himself, and for Annia Euphrosyne, his wife, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for their descendants. In front, 15 feet; in the field, 20 feet.
EDCS-11900681.summary: A funerary monument inscription by Caius Clodius Eutychus for his wives and descendants, including specific land dimensions.

EDCS-11900682.translation: Egrilia Pia, daughter of Aulus, and Lucius Alfacius Eusebes made this for themselves and for their children, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for their descendants. In front, 20 feet; in the field, 20 feet. PIO T
EDCS-11900682.summary: A funerary monument inscription set up by Egrilia Pia and Lucius Alfacius Eusebes for their family and descendants, with land dimensions.

EDCS-11900683.translation: [for] Elaine, his dearest daughter, and for Antonius and Gaius Julius, and Cornelia Ngula, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, except for Atianus. In the field, 20 feet.
EDCS-11900683.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a plot of land, listing several individuals including Elaine, Antonius, Gaius Julius, and Cornelia Ngula, with a land dimension.

EDCS-11900687.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Cornelius Amarantus willingly made this for Euphrosyne, his most deserving freedwoman.
EDCS-11900687.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Aulus Cornelius Amarantus to his deserving freedwoman, Euphrosyne.

EDCS-11900690.translation: Marcus Opatus, Lucius Fa [restored name] useti
EDCS-11900690.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription mentioning Marcus Opatus and Lucius Fa[---].

EDCS-11900693.summary: This is a dedication to Favius by Favia, likely a funerary epitaph.

EDCS-11900695.translation: Aulus Fabius Zoticus made this at his own expense for himself, his wife Caesetia Fortunata, and his sons Aulus Fabius Epiteuxus and Aulus Fabius Fortunatus, and their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-11900695.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aulus Fabius Zoticus for his family, including his wife and sons, and their freedpersons.

EDCS-11900697.translation: Aulus Fabreinius, son of Aulus, grandson of Aulus, great-grandson of Aulus; his mother was Manlia, daughter of Sabidius.
EDCS-11900697.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the family lineage of Aulus Fabreinius and mentioning his mother, Manlia.

EDCS-11900699.translation: gilius s made this for Lucius gilius, son of Lucius, of C Fabricianus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-11900699.summary: This is a funerary epitaph mentioning the maker and the beneficiaries, including freedpersons and their descendants.

EDCS-11900700.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Faustilla by Felix.

EDCS-11900705.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Fidus Palatinus, son of Aulus, grandson of Aulus, lived for 8 years, 4 months, and 5 days. His father Crispinus Aulus Palatinus made this.
EDCS-11900705.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fidus Palatinus, detailing his lifespan and erected by his father Crispinus Aulus Palatinus.

EDCS-11900707.translation: To Titus Flavius Aristo, dearest son, who lived for 3 years. Titus Flavius Iustus, father [made this].
EDCS-11900707.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Aristo, erected by his father Titus Flavius Iustus.

EDCS-11900711.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Flavia Lucila lived for 28 years, and her son Quintus Sextilius Felix lived for 5 years. nia Politan [set this up].
EDCS-11900711.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Flavia Lucila and her young son Quintus Sextilius Felix, possibly set up by 'nia Politan'.

EDCS-11900712.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Flavia Servilia, well-deserving patron, Titus Flavius Antiochus [set this up].
EDCS-11900712.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Titus Flavius Antiochus to his well-deserving patron, Flavia Servilia.

EDCS-11900713.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Flavia Thais. Amarantus, son [set this up].
EDCS-11900713.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Amarantus to his Flavia Thais.

EDCS-11900715.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, likely an epitaph, mentioning Gaius Fo Fort B. The date and context are unclear due to the fragmentary nature.

EDCS-11900718.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. A son made this for his most beloved mother, Fortunata.
EDCS-11900718.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a son for his mother, Fortunata, honoring the Divine Shades.

EDCS-11900720.translation: Lucius Fulvius Eros, freedman of Lucius, and Dionysia, freedwoman of Marcia, [purchased this land for] twenty feet in front and twenty-five feet in the field.
EDCS-11900720.summary: This inscription records a land transaction or boundary marker, specifying dimensions and naming the freedmen Lucius Fulvius Eros and Dionysia.

EDCS-11900721.translation: Lucius Marius Eutyches made this for his well-deserving wife, Furia Italia, and [made this] also for good ones.
EDCS-11900721.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Marius Eutyches for his wife, Furia Italia, indicating their devotion to each other and possibly other deserving individuals.

EDCS-11900723.translation: Publius Gavisidius Inventus lived 8 years. Gavisidia Fortunata lived 13 years. Gavisidia Anthusa for herself and her children.
EDCS-11900723.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of two children, Publius Gavisidius Inventus and Gavisidia Fortunata, with a further dedication for Gavisidia Anthusa and her children.

EDCS-11900726.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Geminius Ierax and Geminius Rusticus, who lived 10 months and 15 days. Geminia Prima, freedwoman of Caius, made this for her co-freedman and for the young slave Caius Geminius Lucrio. The plot was given by Gaius Fuficius Victor.
EDCS-11900726.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription for two individuals, Geminius Ierax and Geminius Rusticus, with a dedication by Geminia Prima, and mentions a plot allocation by Gaius Fuficius Victor.

EDCS-11900727.translation: Publius Granius Antiochus, freedman of Publius Aulus, and Grania Aphelia, freedwoman of the woman Publia.
EDCS-11900727.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Publius Granius Antiochus and Grania Aphelia, identifying their patrons and indicating their freed status.

EDCS-11900728.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades of Grania Aphrodisia.
EDCS-11900728.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Grania Aphrodisia, honoring the Divine Shades.

EDCS-11900729.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Stratonice made this for her slave Ancilla, the Tyrannian Grania.
EDCS-11900729.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication made by Stratonice for her slave Grania Tyrannis.

EDCS-11900730.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Grattius Verecundus made this for his incomparable father, Lucius Grattius Felix, son of Lucius.
EDCS-11900730.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Grattius Verecundus for his father, Lucius Grattius Felix, praising him as incomparable.

EDCS-11900734.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Aurelius Zoticus made this for Aeliadis, his deserving wife.
EDCS-11900734.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a wife by her husband, Marcus Aurelius Zoticus.

EDCS-11900735.translation: Herennia Tyche, freedwoman of Marcius, made this for herself, and for her husband Marcus Herennius, and for her children Marcus Herennius Cladus, Marcus Herennius Atimetus, and Herennia Rufina, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front 32 feet, in the field [---] feet.
EDCS-11900735.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Herennia Tyche for herself, her family, and descendants, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11900738.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Hieron made this for Sostrates, his deserving brother, who lived 35 years, 5 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-11900738.summary: A funerary dedication by Hieron for his brother Sostrates, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-11900739.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Quintus Hosidius Ampliatus made this for Hosidia Ionice, his freedwoman and dearest wife.
EDCS-11900739.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Hosidius Ampliatus for his freedwoman and wife, Hosidia Ionice.

EDCS-11900740.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Horatius made this for his father, Publius Horatius, who lived [---] years.
EDCS-11900740.summary: A funerary dedication by Publius Horatius for his father, also named Publius Horatius.

EDCS-11900741.translation: Fonteius Euhemer made this for his deserving patroness, Fonteia Irene.
EDCS-11900741.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a patron, Fonteius Euhemer, to his patroness, Fonteia Irene.

EDCS-11900744.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For herself and for Tiberius Julius [---], and for the husband who lived 62 years, [---] cundus, and for Tigris, the freedwomen.
EDCS-11900744.summary: This is a funerary dedication by an unnamed woman for herself, her husband, and freedwomen, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11900746.translation: Marcus Julius and Iulia Severa made this for themselves. In front 10 feet.
EDCS-11900746.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication of burial space by Marcus Julius and Iulia Severa.

EDCS-11900747.translation: Sextus Iulius Eucarpus [made this] for his most dear and deserving fellow slave.
EDCS-11900747.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sextus Iulius Eucarpus for his fellow slave.

EDCS-11900749.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Auxa made this for himself.
EDCS-11900749.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication by Marcus Iulius Auxa.

EDCS-11900750.translation: Gaius Julius Crescens made this for himself and for his wife Aelia Secundina, with whom he lived for 10 years.
EDCS-11900750.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the maker and his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900752.translation: To the Divine Shades. Donatus and his parents [made this] for Julius Mamertinus, who lived for 7 years.
EDCS-11900752.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to a young boy by his parents and Donatus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900753.translation: Lucius Julius Zoilus lived for 9 years and 6 months.
EDCS-11900753.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Julius Zoilus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900754.translation: Aelia Iulia made this for her husband.
EDCS-11900754.summary: A funerary epitaph recording a wife's dedication to her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900756.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Julia Cha the best, [from her...] of the association.
EDCS-11900756.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Julia Cha, likely from the Roman Imperial period, with a partial indication of her affiliation.

EDCS-11900758.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulius Mar [and?] Claudia M [his?] mother.
EDCS-11900758.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph mentioning Iulius Mar and his mother Claudia M, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900759.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulius Agathyrsus made this for his deserving wife, Iulia Reposta.
EDCS-11900759.summary: A funerary epitaph where Iulius Agathyrsus dedicates a monument to his deserving wife, Iulia Reposta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900760.translation: To the Divine Shades. For her dearest daughter, the mother made this for Iulia Beneria, who lived for 24 years, 5 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-11900760.summary: A funerary epitaph from a mother to her daughter, Iulia Beneria, detailing her lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900762.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely mentioning Lucius Iunius Hon, possibly the beginning of a name or title, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900763.translation: Atalante made this for her deserving husband, Marcus Iunius Palladius, a most excellent man, who lived for 35 years and 10 days.
EDCS-11900763.summary: A funerary epitaph from Atalante dedicating a monument to her deserving husband, Marcus Iunius Palladius, detailing his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900765.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aulus Egrilius Celsus made this for Iunia Heliadis.
EDCS-11900765.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Aulus Egrilius Celsus to Iunia Heliadis, likely his wife or relative.

EDCS-11900767.translation: Iustus, son of Publius, by his peculium.
EDCS-11900767.summary: This inscription likely records a freedman, Iustus, dedicating something acquired through his peculium (his own property as a slave).

EDCS-11900769.translation: Decimus Laberius Fronto, son of Decimus, of the Palatina tribe, made this for himself and for Laberia Italica, his freedwoman wife, a most rare woman, and for his two daughters, Laberia Antiochis and Frontina, and for his grandson Decimus Laberius Fronto, son of Decimus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 40 feet, in the field 40 feet.
EDCS-11900769.summary: This is a funerary and property inscription by Decimus Laberius Fronto, establishing a burial plot and potentially dedicating land for himself, his family, and his freedpeople, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-11900771.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Laelius Carpus made this for himself and for his deserving wife.
EDCS-11900771.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Decimus Laelius Carpus dedicates a monument for himself and his wife.

EDCS-11900772.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Laelia Eutychis made this for her very sweet son Cornelius Felicissimus, who deserved it, and for herself, who lived 28 years, 10 months.
EDCS-11900772.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Laelia Eutychis for her deceased son Cornelius Felicissimus and herself, providing his age at death.

EDCS-11900775.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Lepidius Lepidianus made this for his deserving wife, Licinia Pompeia, who lived 46 years, 7 months, 15 days.
EDCS-11900775.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Lepidius Lepidianus for his wife Licinia Pompeia, stating her age at death.

EDCS-11900777.translation: Aulus Livius Eutyches, freedman of Aulus, for his deserving patron Aulus Livius Clemens.
EDCS-11900777.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a freedman, Aulus Livius Eutyches, dedicated to his patron Aulus Livius Clemens.

EDCS-11900778.translation: Publius Lucretius Licinianus consecrated this memorial to the spirits of the underworld for his most virtuous wife, Livia Beronica, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-11900778.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Publius Lucretius Licinianus to his wife Livia Beronica.

EDCS-11900779.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Lollius Sozomenus made this for himself and for his incomparable wife Grania Tryfeneiola, and for his daughter Grania Faventina, and for his students Lollius Caerereinus, Sosontus, Caelestinus, and for his freedmen Caloscius Venerius, and their descendants.
EDCS-11900779.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Quintus Lollius Sozomenus for his family, students, and freedpeople.

EDCS-11900780.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucceius Marinus.
EDCS-11900780.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription dedicated to Lucceius Marinus.

EDCS-11900781.translation: To Hep, for himself and Luccia, and their freedmen and freedwomen, 10 feet in front.
EDCS-11900781.summary: This is a funerary inscription specifying the dimensions of a burial plot in front of the tomb for the owner and their dependents.

EDCS-11900782.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Luscia Metropolis and Lucius Luscius Posidonius made this for their parents, Lucius Luscius Secundus, their most devoted son, who lived 14 years and 9 days, and for themselves and their kin, their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants, 18 feet in front and 20 feet in land.
EDCS-11900782.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Luscia Metropolis and Lucius Luscius Posidonius, commemorating their son Lucius Luscius Secundus and dedicating the tomb for their family and dependents.

EDCS-11900783.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Lutatia Capitoina.
EDCS-11900783.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Lutatia Capitoina.

EDCS-11900784.translation: Marcus M. Min., Marcus Ma., aged 22.
EDCS-11900784.summary: This inscription likely records the name and age of a deceased individual, possibly for a tombstone.

EDCS-11900785.translation: Publius M. rce i. ius for himself and M. rciana, his wife, and Marcia Chloe, his wife, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and Po. e Chloe, 20 feet in land.
EDCS-11900785.summary: This funerary inscription details the owner, Publius M. rce i. ius, and the individuals for whom the burial plot is intended, including his wives and dependents, specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-11900786.translation: Ama made this. Her husband Capriolus and son Secundus made this for their sweetest and deserving mother.
EDCS-11900786.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a husband and son dedicating a monument to their deceased wife and mother, Ama.

EDCS-11900787.translation: Quintus Maecius Iuvenalis for his sweetest wife.
EDCS-11900787.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Quintus Maecius Iuvenalis dedicating something to his wife.

EDCS-11900788.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Titus Magnis Cossutian, his most devoted son.
EDCS-11900788.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Titus Magnis Cossutian by his son.

EDCS-11900791.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Marcus Manlius I. P. and his sweetest Valeria Hel, aged 16.
EDCS-11900791.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Manlius I. P. and his wife Valeria Hel, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-11900792.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely a name on a tombstone, identifying Marcianus Cognatus.

EDCS-11900793.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Maritimus lived 14 years and 3 months. Flavia Asclepias [made this] for her beloved husband Urbanus Successus, her freedman heir, as a deserving monument.
EDCS-11900793.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a boy named Maritimus, set up by his wife and heir, Flavia Asclepias.

EDCS-11900794.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Maritimus, slave of Lucrius Caesar.
EDCS-11900794.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maritimus, a slave belonging to someone named Lucrius Caesar.

EDCS-11900795.translation: Marcus Marius made [this] for himself and for Aelia Pan [and] Publius Aelius Ba[...].
EDCS-11900795.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Marius for himself and his family members.

EDCS-11900798.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a son named Matur, possibly set up by a parent.

EDCS-11900801.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Statilia Rhodope and Servilia Rhodope made [this] for their most sweet mother Mettia Rhodines, with the permission of Statilius Crescentianus.
EDCS-11900801.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mettia Rhodines, erected by her daughters with permission from Statilius Crescentianus.

EDCS-11900804.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Quintus Minucius Felix, son of Quintus.
EDCS-11900804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Minucius Felix.

EDCS-11900807.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caltiliana, freedwoman of Quintus, has erected [this] for herself and for Quintus Munatius Caltilianus Quartio, her patron and freedman of Quintus, and for Quintus Munatius Caltiliano Secundo, freedman of the woman [of Quintus], and for Quintus Munatius Caltiliano Epagatho, freedman of the woman [of Quintus].
EDCS-11900807.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caltiliana, a freedwoman, for herself and several freedmen, including her patron, establishing family and social relationships.

EDCS-11900808.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Mundicius and Legitima, his wife, made [this] for themselves and for their freedmen and freedwomen, [after the] cession to themselves by Antius and Cretonia Fortunata.
EDCS-11900808.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by Mundicius and his wife Legitima for themselves and their dependents, possibly commemorating the transfer of property or status.

EDCS-11900809.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Faustina, [my] most sweet son [Ca issue] to Gaius Cassius Heraclitus.
EDCS-11900809.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a son named Faustina, dedicated to Gaius Cassius Heraclitus.

EDCS-11900810.translation: Naevia Prima, freedwoman of Quintus, [and] Caesetia, freedwoman of Marcus [and] Naevia, [acted] by the authority of Prima, a freedwoman.
EDCS-11900810.summary: This inscription seems to record an action taken by two freedwomen, Naevia Prima and Caesetia, likely related to property or legal matters, overseen by another freedwoman named Prima.

EDCS-11900815.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Publius Nonius, son of Publius Nonius.
EDCS-11900815.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the departed for Publius Nonius, son of Publius Nonius.

EDCS-11900817.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Nonia Symferusa made this for herself and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-11900817.summary: This funerary inscription records Nonia Symferusa dedicating a burial place for herself and her descendants, including freed persons.

EDCS-11900822.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aufidia Felicitas made this for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Octavius Glyco, who lived 56 years and 14 days.
EDCS-11900822.summary: This funerary inscription records Aufidia Felicitas dedicating a tomb to her husband, Lucius Octavius Glyco, who lived 56 years and 14 days.

EDCS-11900823.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Phoebe, daughter of Lucius Octavius, lived 24 years; she was taken away on her birthday.
EDCS-11900823.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Phoebe, daughter of Lucius Octavius, who died on her 24th birthday.

EDCS-11900826.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Ostulenius Menas purchased this tomb for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Longeia Sosthenis purchased this tomb for herself and for her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and for her household slave Publius Gallenius Antistianus; 14 feet in front, 33 feet in area.
EDCS-11900826.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Ostulenius Menas and Longeia Sosthenis purchasing a tomb and associated land for themselves, their freed persons, descendants, and a household slave.

EDCS-11900828.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Paconius Speratus and Caius Mundicius Martialis made this for Paconia Prima, mother most devoted, and for Martialis' wife, most beloved, well-deserving.
EDCS-11900828.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Caius Paconius Speratus and Caius Mundicius Martialis to Paconia Prima (mother) and Martialis' wife (coniugi).

EDCS-11900834.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Petronius Ascanius made this for his most devoted wife, Petronia Ursilia, well-deserving.
EDCS-11900834.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Petronius Ascanius dedicating a tomb to his well-deserving and most devoted wife, Petronia Ursilia.

EDCS-11900835.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Parents made this for their sweetest daughter, Petronia Verecunda, who lived 9 years, 2 months, and 6 days, well-deserving.
EDCS-11900835.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by parents to their daughter Petronia Verecunda, who died at the age of 9 years, 2 months, and 6 days.

EDCS-11900836.translation: While alive, Caius Plat [dedicated this]; while alive, Po O.
EDCS-11900836.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records Caius Plat and Po O dedicating something while they were still alive.

EDCS-11900837.translation: Lucius Plinius, freedman of Lucius Plinius Euhodus, and Hediste, freedwoman of Publius and Pinaria.
EDCS-11900837.summary: This inscription names Lucius Plinius, a freedman of Lucius Plinius Euhodus, and Hediste, a freedwoman of Publius and Pinaria.

EDCS-11900838.translation: Caius Pomentinus Felix and Iulia Apollonia, freedwoman of Caius, made this at their own expense; Lucius Bucius Antiochus.
EDCS-11900838.summary: This inscription records a building or monument made by Caius Pomentinus Felix and Iulia Apollonia, with Lucius Bucius Antiochus also mentioned.

EDCS-11900840.summary: This very brief inscription records that Pompeia commissioned the object or monument.

EDCS-11900841.translation: To the departed spirits. Numerius Tribonius Victor made this for his well-deserving wife, Pompeia Aquilina.
EDCS-11900841.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Numerius Tribonius Victor to his wife, Pompeia Aquilina.

EDCS-11900842.translation: To the departed spirits. The father made this for Pompeia Domitia at his own expense.
EDCS-11900842.summary: This funerary inscription records that the father of Pompeia Domitia dedicated this monument to her.

EDCS-11900844.translation: To the departed spirits. Pompeius Epagathus made this for his well-deserving wife, Pompeia Theophila.
EDCS-11900844.summary: This funerary inscription records that Pompeius Epagathus dedicated this monument to his wife, Pompeia Theophila.

EDCS-11900846.translation: To the departed spirits. Lived 7 years, 25 days. Pomponius Quietus, father, made this for his well-deserving Decimus Pomponius Quietulus.
EDCS-11900846.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of a child, Decimus Pomponius Quietulus, and dedicated by his father, Pomponius Quietus.

EDCS-11900847.translation: To the departed spirits. For Publius Pomponius Trophimianus and Publius Pomponius Celsus, his most dutiful sons. Pomponius Pullas.
EDCS-11900847.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Pomponius Pullas to his two sons, Publius Pomponius Trophimianus and Publius Pomponius Celsus.

EDCS-11900848.translation: To the departed spirits. Aulus Herennuleius Epityches for his most excellent wife, Pomponia Vitalis.
EDCS-11900848.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aulus Herennuleius Epityches dedicated this to his wife, Pomponia Vitalis.

EDCS-11900850.summary: This inscription is a simple identification of a woman named Pontia Apollinaris, daughter of Lucius, possibly on a tombstone or object.

EDCS-11900852.summary: This inscription records the age of Prima, who died at 5 years and an unspecified number of months, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-11900853.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Primus Clementina, to her deserving freedman.
EDCS-11900853.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedman by his patroness.

EDCS-11900858.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Julia Felicitas made this for Lucius Publicius Euaristus, her dearest husband.
EDCS-11900858.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-11900859.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Publicius Eutychus made this for himself, and for his freedwoman Publicia Staphyle, and for his adopted son Publicius Hermes, and for his adopted daughter Procula, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 9 feet in front, 9 and a half feet in the field.
EDCS-11900859.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a family and their descendants, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-11900861.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Quintus Publicius, son of Vet[...].
EDCS-11900861.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Publicius, son of Vet[...].

EDCS-11900864.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Quartio, son of Lucius Rufus, Callistus and Victor, sons of Lucius Capius Severus, to their friend.
EDCS-11900864.summary: This is a funerary dedication by two friends for their friend Quartio.

EDCS-11900865.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Quintus Quintilius Eutyches and Quintilia Euphemia made this for themselves while alive, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 22 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-11900865.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a couple for themselves and their descendants, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-11900866.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Publius Ragonius Crescens made this for his son, and for his wife, and for himself, with the permission of his patron.
EDCS-11900866.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a man for his family and himself, noting permission from his patron.

EDCS-11900867.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Publius Ragonius Abascantus made this for his deserving wife, Ragonia Nymphidia.
EDCS-11900867.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-11900871.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For [---], who lived for 2 months and [---] days. Restitutus made this for his deserving brother, and [---] his incomparable wife.
EDCS-11900871.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a brother and wife for their deceased relative.

EDCS-11900873.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Lucius Rubrius Trofimus, an incomparable man. [---] an incomparable man.
EDCS-11900873.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Rubrius Trofimus, likely a prominent individual.

EDCS-11900875.translation: Urvaus, son of Decimus, and his freedwoman Tryphera Voturia Rufus made this.
EDCS-11900875.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Urvaus and his freedwoman Tryphera made the monument.

EDCS-11900877.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; [he] made this for his incomparable wife, Spurius Rustius.
EDCS-11900877.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Spurius Rustius for his wife.

EDCS-11900880.translation: The sons made this for their incomparable father, Salutaris.
EDCS-11900880.summary: This funerary epitaph states that sons commissioned a monument for their father, Salutaris.

EDCS-11900881.translation: Lucius Sancius Sanbragius made this sarcophagus for himself and for his wife, Cannia Maginetis.
EDCS-11900881.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Sancius Sanbragius commissioning a sarcophagus for himself and his wife, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900886.translation: Titus Re, Gaius Seilius, Gaius Silius, Gaius Silius, Gaius Silius C., Gaius Silius C., freedman E.
EDCS-11900886.summary: This inscription lists several Roman names, possibly indicating family members or an inheritance.

EDCS-11900888.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Septicia Primitiva lived for 21 years. Quintus Gargilius Quietus made this for his most pious wife.
EDCS-11900888.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Septicia Primitiva at age 21 and was dedicated by her husband, Quintus Gargilius Quietus.

EDCS-11900889.translation: To Aulus Titus Flavius Apronianus, son of Titus, to the spirits of the underworld. Septueia Ias made this for herself, for Numisius Stratonicus, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, with sarcophagi and small chapels.
EDCS-11900889.summary: This funerary inscription records Septueia Ias commissioning sarcophagi and small chapels for herself, Aulus Titus Flavius Apronianus, and Numisius Stratonicus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900892.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Servilius Onesimus. Servilianus Onesimus and Fortunata made this for their sweetest parent. To the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-11900892.summary: This funerary epitaph records Servilianus Onesimus and Fortunata dedicating a monument to their parent, Servilius Onesimus.

EDCS-11900893.translation: Theopompus made this for his excellent sister, Servilia Pergamis.
EDCS-11900893.summary: This funerary epitaph records Theopompus commissioning a monument for his sister, Servilia Pergamis.

EDCS-11900894.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Lucius Sestius Antus made this for himself and for Sestia, his freedwoman, also his wife, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front, 20 feet.
EDCS-11900894.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Sestius Antus commissioning a burial space for himself, his freedwoman and wife Sestia, and their descendants, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11900895.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sextorius Mercurialis made this for his wife Setoria Demetriadis, his daughter, the respected Sextilia Cethegilla, well deserving.
EDCS-11900895.summary: A funerary dedication made by Sextorius Mercurialis for his wife and daughter, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11900896.translation: To his mother Severa, daughter of Caius. Aufidius Lucretianus, son of Publius, made this.
EDCS-11900896.summary: A funerary dedication made by Aufidius Lucretianus for his mother Severa, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11900897.summary: A fragment of a funerary dedication for a woman named Severa, the context and dedicant are lost.

EDCS-11900899.translation: To the Divine Shades. They made this for Ragonia Sofia, his foster-daughter, who lived for 2 years and 30 days. For...
EDCS-11900899.summary: A funerary dedication for a young child, Ragonia Sofia, made by an unknown individual or individuals.

EDCS-11900901.translation: ...stat... from Titus, freedman of Caius. Lucius Pr[---]itus, Lucius M[---]us Pr[---]itus, Lucius Caecilius Felicissimus inscribed...
EDCS-11900901.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of freedmen and potentially a tomb builder or commissioner, with significant portions missing.

EDCS-11900903.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gnaeus Statilius made this for himself, his wife, and his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front 22 feet, in the field...
EDCS-11900903.summary: A funerary dedication by Gnaeus Statilius for himself and his family, including future descendants, specifying dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-11900905.translation: To O[---] Stlaccia, to Stlaccius, to his incomparable wife...
EDCS-11900905.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication mentioning Stlaccia and Stlaccius, likely a spouse and husband.

EDCS-11900910.translation: ...Symphorus, freedman, to his freedman, and to his freedman...
EDCS-11900910.summary: A fragmentary inscription that seems to be a funerary dedication involving multiple freedmen, possibly related to Symphorus.

EDCS-11900911.translation: Syntrophus made this with his own money.
EDCS-11900911.summary: A funerary dedication made by Syntrophus for himself or another, funded by his own resources.

EDCS-11900913.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Tannussius Successus, who lived 3 years and 6 months.
EDCS-11900913.summary: A funerary dedication for Quintus Tannussius Successus, likely a child, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11900914.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Telesphorus.
EDCS-11900914.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Telesphorus.

EDCS-11900917.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Thuranius Craterus and Meclasia Basilice for their son Publius Thuranius Eupraxius, most sweet, who lived 6 years and months.
EDCS-11900917.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Publius Thuranius Craterus and Meclasia Basilice for their son, Publius Thuranius Eupraxius, who died at a young age.

EDCS-11900920.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Trophime, freedwoman, for the most dutiful, best, dearest Marcus Sempronius Severus, son of Marcus, who lived 37 years.
EDCS-11900920.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Trophime, a freedwoman, to Marcus Sempronius Severus.

EDCS-11900921.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Trofimus and Rufina made this for themselves and for Iulius Segetus.
EDCS-11900921.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Trofimus and Rufina for themselves and Iulius Segetus.

EDCS-11900922.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Tullius Anicetus.
EDCS-11900922.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Tullius Anicetus.

EDCS-11900925.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Turnus Aurelius Hegemon, a slave born in the household, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 18 days. Aurelius Felix made this for his most sweet natural son.
EDCS-11900925.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Aurelius Felix for his son, Turnus Aurelius Hegemon, who died in adolescence.

EDCS-11900927.translation: Gaius Geminius, son of Publius Geminius, and Publius Geminius, freedmen of Gaius Va[---?].
EDCS-11900927.summary: This inscription records freedmen of the Geminius family.

EDCS-11900932.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Valerius Graptus made this for Lucius Valerius Bassus and Domitia Amanda.
EDCS-11900932.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Valerius Graptus for Lucius Valerius Bassus and Domitia Amanda.

EDCS-11900933.translation: Valerius Donatus made this for himself while alive, and for his wife Aurelia Ianuaria, and for his daughter Valeria Ianuaria, who lived 28 years and 7 months.
EDCS-11900933.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Valerius Donatus for himself, his wife, and his daughter, with the daughter's lifespan specified.

EDCS-11900934.translation: To the spirits of the departed. This was made by Gaius Valerius Hermeros and Cryperia Heuresis for their son Gaius Valerius Proclus, who lived 9 years and 9 months.
EDCS-11900934.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Gaius Valerius Hermeros and Cryperia Heuresis for their son, Gaius Valerius Proclus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-11900935.translation: Lucius Valerius Priscus, son of Lucius Valerius, made this for himself and his sons Valerius Diadumenianus and [---], and his wife Laelia Prima, and his foster-daughter Valeria Rufina, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-11900935.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Valerius Priscus for himself and his family, including his sons, wife, foster-daughter, and descendants.

EDCS-11900936.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Fortunata, mother, made this for Valeria Marcella.
EDCS-11900936.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Valeria Marcella by her mother, Valeria Fortunata.

EDCS-11900937.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Her husband, Philumenus, made this for his deserving wife, Valeria Philo, who was also called Alexandria.
EDCS-11900937.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Philumenus for his wife, Valeria Philo (also known as Alexandria).

EDCS-11900938.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Varia Severina, his sister, made this for her dearest brother, Vario Eutychius, who lived for 30 years, 4 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-11900938.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life span of Vario Eutychius and was dedicated by his sister, Varia Severina.

EDCS-11900941.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that appears to record the name Gaius Venti and possibly his position or a further description, but is too incomplete to determine its full context.

EDCS-11900943.translation: Flo [---] for his most beloved wife Vibiae Panthiae, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In the front part, 15 feet, in the field 10 feet.
EDCS-11900943.summary: This inscription likely records the dedication of a tomb or plot of land to Vibiae Panthiae by her husband, specifying dimensions and including provisions for freedmen and descendants.

EDCS-11900944.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Eutychia, her own slave, made this for Vibia Repentina, who lived for 5 years.
EDCS-11900944.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vibia Repentina, who died at the age of five, and was set up by her slave Eutychia.

EDCS-11900945.translation: Vibia Stacte, freedwoman of Gaius, and Gaius Vibius Nicia, freedman of Caius, [---] 8 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-11900945.summary: This inscription likely marks a property or burial plot belonging to two freed individuals, Vibia Stacte and Gaius Vibius Nicia, and specifies its dimensions.

EDCS-11900947.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that seems to mention the name Victor and a place or family name Usulia.

EDCS-11900948.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aemilius Cassianus made this for his deserving foster-son Vitalioni, who lived for 4 years, 6 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-11900948.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Aemilius Cassianus for his foster-son Vitalioni, detailing his short lifespan.

EDCS-11900949.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to Vitalis and his household.

EDCS-11900954.translation: Amanda, freedwoman of Vestoria, a freedwoman of Aulus, has erected this altar and cippus with her own money to her well-deserving patrons, Ani Volumnio Iucundo and his wife Felici, and their freedwoman.
EDCS-11900954.summary: This is an altar and cippus inscription dedicated by Amanda to her patrons, erected from her own funds.

EDCS-11900957.translation: Decimus Volusius Abies, freedman of Decimus Volusius; Martha Volusia, freedwoman of Decimus Volusius; and Decimus Volusius Bargates, freedman of Decimus Volusius, [set this up]. 10 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-11900957.summary: This is a boundary inscription indicating land ownership or division, set up by three freedmen.

EDCS-11900958.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Volusius Euelpistus made this for his most holy and devoted wife, Volusia Prosode, and for his most sweet son, Lucius Volusius Speratus, who lived 18 years, 8 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-11900958.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Volusius Euelpistus for his wife and son.

EDCS-11900959.translation: To the Divine Spirits. [He/She] lived 2 years, 2 days, and 4 hours.
EDCS-11900959.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of a child.

EDCS-11900968.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning a son named Palatina Pato.

EDCS-11900978.translation: Corios [set up this memorial] from his own resources, to ensure good treatment after death. [He] died at the age of 21 years, 5 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-11900978.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Corios at a young age, with a mention of self-funded arrangements for his memory.

EDCS-12000022.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Quiriacus, indicating a peaceful rest in death.

EDCS-12000024.translation: Filete, the mother, made this for Quintus Critonius Epaphroditus, who lived 24 years and 3 months. Peace be with him.
EDCS-12000024.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a mother for her son, Quintus Critonius Epaphroditus.

EDCS-12000025.translation: Baleria Hilaritas, his wife, made this for her well-deserving husband, Spirito Iuli Calipodis, who lived 31 years, and for her well-deserving daughter, Iulia Calipodia, who lived 2 years and 6 months.
EDCS-12000025.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a wife for her husband and daughter.

EDCS-12000026.translation: Gaius Tatinus, son of Gaius, rests here
EDCS-12000026.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial of Gaius Tatinus.

EDCS-12000027.translation: Urgulania Venustina rests here in peace
EDCS-12000027.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial of Urgulania Venustina.

EDCS-12000032.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Augurinus, who was a consul.

EDCS-12000086.translation: Sextus Valerius Gaius Atius Surus Basus, veteran of two campaigns
EDCS-12000086.summary: This inscription likely records the name and military service of Sextus Valerius Gaius Atius Surus Basus.

EDCS-12000087.translation: Spurius Valetis, son of Icusanius, from Ostia. Farewell.
EDCS-12000087.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial of Spurius Valetis, son of Icusanius, from Ostia.

EDCS-12000103.translation: Titus Manlius Felix, freedman of Titus, gave this gift from his own resources for 1000 sesterces
EDCS-12000103.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Manlius Felix, a freedman, for a gift he provided.

EDCS-12000105.translation: Domesticus gives thanks to his master. I wish you well.
EDCS-12000105.summary: This is a private message of thanks from Domesticus to his master.

EDCS-12000109.summary: This inscription records the name Tiberius Ermadion, possibly on a tombstone or monument.

EDCS-12000111.translation: Agathopus, Prima, and Epaphroditus, three together
EDCS-12000111.summary: This inscription records the names of three individuals, Agathopus, Prima, and Epaphroditus.

EDCS-12000112.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Cepholus and Musice.

EDCS-12000114.translation: Achilleus Hylas: meat for 5 denarii. Baberius: salted fish for half a denarius. Bictor: wine for 2 denarii. Proclus: wine for 2 denarii. Hermes: wine for 3 denarii. Fortunius ADA Maximus: wine for 2 denarii.
EDCS-12000114.summary: This inscription lists various individuals and the prices of goods they supplied, likely a record of provisions or expenses.

EDCS-12000124.summary: This inscription simply lists four names, possibly indicating individuals involved in a religious cult, a group, or a funerary context.

EDCS-12000131.summary: This inscription consists of a single name, Publius Virius Maximus, potentially identifying an individual on a monument or document.

EDCS-12000133.translation: To Gaius Libius Severus, patron, by Modestus.
EDCS-12000133.summary: This is a dedication from Modestus to his patron, Gaius Libius Severus.

EDCS-12000135.translation: From the estates of Matidia Augusta, from the potteries of Claudius Fortunatus.

EDCS-12000191.summary: This inscription records initials or an abbreviation (CPGTT) and is dated by the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
