EDCS-12000201.translation: Lucius Caecilius Maximus made this for the colonists of the colony of Ostia.
EDCS-12000201.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Caecilius Maximus created something for the colonists of Ostia.

EDCS-12000202.translation: Lucius Caecilius Maximus made this for the colonists of the colony of Ostia.
EDCS-12000202.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Caecilius Maximus created something for the colonists of Ostia.

EDCS-12000206.summary: This inscription appears to be an ownership mark or a dedication by Sextus Valerius Zosimus.

EDCS-12000223.translation: Under the supervision of the rationalis Hermippus, freedman of the emperor, a procurator, from the workshop of Hierocles, freedman, of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus.
EDCS-12000223.summary: This inscription details administrative oversight and the origin of goods from the workshop of Hierocles, under the authority of the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-12000229.translation: Of Sextus A[---] P[---], a most distinguished man.
EDCS-12000229.summary: This inscription refers to a very distinguished man named Sextus A[---] P[---].

EDCS-12000232.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcia Caecilia Birroniana Pollitta, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000233.translation: Of Cornelia Praetextata, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-12000233.summary: This inscription records the name of Cornelia Praetextata, a woman of high status, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000234.summary: This inscription records the name of Aulus Fabius Diogenes, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000238.summary: This inscription records the name of Valeria Synphorus, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000240.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Marcius Fortunatus, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000246.translation: From the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Eutyches.
EDCS-12000246.summary: This inscription indicates that something was made by the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Eutyches.

EDCS-12000298.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Iulius Hermodorus, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-12000299.translation: Hold me so I don't flee; I flee.
EDCS-12000299.summary: This inscription is a brief, epigrammatic text, possibly a personal motto or a warning found on a tomb or object.

EDCS-12000316.translation: By decree of the decurions, publicly, for Servius Sulpicius Galba, Emperor Augustus.
EDCS-12000316.summary: This inscription records a public honor granted by the town council to Emperor Servius Sulpicius Galba.

EDCS-12000317.translation: Of Plotina Augusta, wife of the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus.
EDCS-12000317.summary: This inscription records the name of Plotina Augusta, wife of Emperor Trajan, likely on a public monument or a building dedicated to her.

EDCS-12000326.translation: To Julia Augusta, mother of the most noble prince of the camp, of the senate, and of the fatherland, and to their majesty.
EDCS-12000326.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Julia Augusta, likely the mother of an emperor, possibly related to military honors.

EDCS-12000333.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Hermogenes, an excellent man, patron of the colony, priest of the Genius of the colony, son of Aurelius Hermetes, of most perfect memory, son-in-law of Flavius Priscus, most perfect man, patron of the colony, tribune of the XXX Ulpia legion, prefect of the First Thracian ala, procurator of the Emperor's studies, promoted to 60,000 sesterces, to 100,000 sesterces by immunity, supported by the musical council, scribe of the higher tribunate, also of the quaestorian scribes, priest of Videntia. The order of decurions, because of his distinguished affection.
EDCS-12000333.summary: This is a dedication by the order of decurions to Marcus Aurelius Hermogenes, honoring his distinguished career and public service, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12000335.translation: To Flavius Domitianus, prefect of the grain supply, most honorable curator. The order of decurions.
EDCS-12000335.summary: This is a dedication by the order of decurions to Flavius Domitianus, acknowledging his role as curator and prefect of the grain supply, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-12000349.translation: Under Emperor Gallienus Augustus V and Nummius Faustianus, consuls. The names of the collegia. Patrons: Lucius Stennius Clementius, Titus Tinucius Euvantus, Publius Annius Hermogenianus, Claudius Plotus Iulianus, Sempronius Crescens. The common people: Titus Tinucius Rufinus, Titus Tinucius Tinucianus, Veturius Felix Socrates, Quintus Veturius Pudentianus, Titus Tinucius Euvantus the younger, Titus Tinucius Eros, Titus Tinucius Eros the elder, Titus Tinucius Charidemus, Aulus Annius Hilarianus, Titus Tinucius Montius, Titus Tinucius Diogas, Marcus Aurelius Asclepiades, Marcus Junius Eufras. Quintus Maecius Caelestinus, Clodius Plotus Iulianus, Titus Tinucius Dexter, Marcus Marius Verissimus, Aelius Venerius senior, Lucius Pomponius Eutychius, Modius Felix Crementius, Gaius Refrius Calbisius, Tiberius Herennius Purpurius, Lucius Stennius Secundus, Quintus Veturius Apronianus, Calbus Felix Faustus, Fulbius Felix Peribolus, Publius Annius Clarus, Gaius Claudius Felix and Titus Claudius, and Julius Felix Quartus, Lucius Isissinus and Titus Tannonius Concordius, Plotus, Aelius, Sempronius, Crepereius, Sempronius. Patrons: Lucius Sallustius Quartus, an excellent man, Publius Claudius Hermadio.
EDCS-12000349.summary: This inscription lists patrons and members of collegia (guilds or associations) during the consulship of Gallienus and Nummius Faustianus, likely dating to 266 CE.

EDCS-12000350.translation: ader, ---hes, ---odotus, ---alis, ---hus, ---s Felix, ---phor, ---ianus, ---s. Publius A---, Gaius Julius A---, Publius Septimius Z---, Gaius Julius Chrys---, Marcus Petronius Dec---, Sextus Setorius Victorinus, Lucius Octavius Nicias, Titus Tinucius Charidemus, Titus Tinucius Batalus, Lucius Sossius Corinthus, Quintus Maecius Ultor, Marcus Seius Steri--.
EDCS-12000350.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly members of a collegium or community, with several names being incomplete due to damage.

EDCS-12000352.translation: quinquennial, quinquennial, ius, s, ius, s.
EDCS-12000352.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to quinquennial officials, possibly within a municipal or collegial context, with most of the text missing.

EDCS-12000353.translation: s, Tha---, Onesimus, Successus, Quadratus, Agathopus, Severianus, Alexander, Hellenicus, Symphor, Sulpicianus, Graphicus, Rufus, Phoebus, Hermogenes, Fabianus, Epictetus, Victorinus, Syntrophus, Diadumenus, Moschus, Gaius, Iullus, Zosimianus, Aemilianus, Dionysius, Nicias, Charito, Philippus the younger, Severianus, Onesimianus, Cissus, Onesimus, Menander, Ianuarius, Valerianus, Euhodas, Zoticus, Primitivus, Telesphorus, Fortunatus.
EDCS-12000353.summary: This inscription is a list of names, possibly members of an association or benefactors, with many names being Roman and Greek, suggesting a diverse community.

EDCS-12000359.translation: Lucius Cai, Lucius Val, Quintus Pati, Lucius Li.
EDCS-12000359.summary: This is a fragmented inscription consisting of only a few names, likely belonging to a larger text such as a list of members or patrons.

EDCS-12000360.translation: Lucius Lucius M, Caius Se, Marcus Su, Caius.
EDCS-12000360.summary: This is a fragmented inscription containing only a few names, possibly part of a list of individuals or members.

EDCS-12000361.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription containing only a few Latin grammatical particles and suffixes, likely part of a longer text that is now lost.

EDCS-12000362.translation: Sextus Aelius Marcus Litorius Euchus Felicissimus, Iulius Aphrodisius, Flavius Pulcher, Quintus Maecius Iuvenalis, Caius Lasuccius Pylades, Galvenus Epaphroditus, Quintus Maecius Successus, Iunius Fortis, Cloelius Restitutus, Silvius Primus, Cassius Chryseros, Valerius Fortunatus, Sergius Serapion, Marcus Iulius, Lucius Tullius, Quintus Cornelius, Titus Flavius, Severus. [All] living. Marcus Iulius. Living. Lucius Tullius. Deceased. Quintus Cornelius. Titus Flavius. Deceased. Severus.
EDCS-12000362.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary list of names, possibly of members of a collegium, with indications of those who were living and deceased.

EDCS-12000363.translation: Marcus Aemilius Ferox, Quintus Pompeius Heliodorus, Lucius Arrius Eutyches, Lucius Arruntius Hermeros, Publius Ragonius Charito.
EDCS-12000363.summary: This inscription is a list of Roman men's names, likely commemorating them, perhaps as members of a group or for a public work.

EDCS-12000367.translation: To Lucius Aurelius Apolaustus Memphius, freedman of the Augusti, and to Salonina, Augusta, in all things concordant and consort of Gallienus Augustus, our emperor. Flavius Priscus [dedicated this].
EDCS-12000367.summary: This is a dedication by Flavius Priscus to Lucius Aurelius Apolaustus Memphius and Salonina, likely honorific dedications related to imperial figures, dated to the period of Gallienus (mid-3rd century AD).

EDCS-12000369.translation: and to his wife, a freedman, a quinquennial sevir Augustalis, [he] made [this] for his patron. RET
EDCS-12000369.summary: This inscription records a freedman who held the office of quinquennial sevir Augustalis and dedicated something to his patron.

EDCS-12000374.translation: Nerecianus Caecilius Dionysianus gave a gift to the station of the Tiber riverbed.
EDCS-12000374.summary: This inscription records Caecilius Dionysianus donating a gift to the Tiber river station, likely related to its maintenance or operation.

EDCS-12000379.translation: Titus Apusulenus Zethus lived 28 years. Titus Apusulenus, freedman of Apusulena Marcia, Zethus, his father, and Apusulena Marcia, his freedwoman, his mother, made [this monument] for their son and for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-12000379.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by parents for their son Zethus, and also for themselves and their descendants, indicating family relationships and status.

EDCS-12000380.translation: For Vitalis, 9 years, 10 months, 6 days. Arduelius Vitalis made [this] for his most dutiful son.
EDCS-12000380.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Vitalis, set up by his father, Arduelius Vitalis.

EDCS-12000383.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Fortunata [made this] for her sweet daughter Catia, who lived 3 months and 10 days.
EDCS-12000383.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her infant daughter, Catia, who died very young.

EDCS-12000384.translation: Publius Cius [dedicated this] for himself and for C. Caelestinus Redemptus and Caelestina, his children, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, a concession granted to them by Fabia Agrippina.
EDCS-12000384.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Publius Cius for himself, his children, and their descendants, with a concession granted by Fabia Agrippina.

EDCS-12000386.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Cutia Pasagatha and for Cutia Soteris, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-12000386.summary: This is a funerary inscription intended for Cutia Pasagatha, Cutia Soteris, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.

EDCS-12000387.translation: To Egrilius Marcius, for his wife of rare example, LIA, who lived 22 years, 2 months, and 22 days, and for his dearest daughter Egrilia Marcia, who lived 15 years, 1 month, and 18 days, a deserving woman.
EDCS-12000387.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Egrilius Marcius for his wife and daughter, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000388.translation: Felix and Bonifatia made this for themselves and their sons.
EDCS-12000388.summary: This funerary inscription records that Felix and Bonifatia created this monument for themselves and their children, probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000389.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Titus Flavius Le made this for his pupil.
EDCS-12000389.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Flavius Le dedicating a monument to his pupil, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000390.translation: To Victorinus, Caius Fonteius [---] son, who lived 13 years, 5 months.
EDCS-12000390.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Victorinus, son of Caius Fonteius, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000392.translation: To the Divine Spirits, and to Fructuosa, dearest mother of [---]ia Prima, who lived 59 years, 37 days, and 4 hours, a deserving woman. [---] made this.
EDCS-12000392.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Fructuosa, the mother of [---]ia Prima, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000394.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. To Servilia Hermaide, a deserving wife, from Rhodinus.
EDCS-12000394.summary: This funerary inscription by Rhodinus honors his deserving wife, Servilia Hermaide, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000395.translation: In memory of Hilarianus, who lived 1 year, 6 months, and 22 days. Iulia I [---].
EDCS-12000395.summary: This inscription commemorates Hilarianus, who died in infancy, likely set up by Iulia I, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000396.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. To Mas, a deserving wife, from [---]us.
EDCS-12000396.summary: This funerary inscription, dedicated to Mas by [---]us, refers to her as a deserving wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12000397.translation: Caius Iulius [---]gin and his freedmen and freedwomen. On the front, [---] feet.
EDCS-12000397.summary: This incomplete inscription likely records property boundaries or dimensions and mentions Caius Iulius and his freedpersons, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12001316.translation: Cornelia Modesta, wife of Publius Claudius Callidromus, and Callinus [---].
EDCS-12001316.summary: This fragment of an inscription names Cornelia Modesta as the wife of Publius Claudius Callidromus and mentions Callinus, likely a funerary or dedicatory monument from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12400593.translation: Quintus Camurtius, son of Publius, dedicated this gift to Mars.
EDCS-12400593.summary: A dedication to Mars by Quintus Camurtius, son of Publius, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-12401848.translation: To Fabius Maximus, most illustrious man, founder of the public walls, protector of all transgressions, the council and people of Allifae dedicate this to their patron.
EDCS-12401848.summary: An honorary inscription dedicated by the city of Allifae to their patron, Fabius Maximus, praising his achievements as founder of public walls and protector.

EDCS-12401849.translation: Fabius Maximus, most illustrious man, governor of the province, rebuilt the Baths of Hercules, which had been destroyed by an earthquake, from the foundations.
EDCS-12401849.summary: An inscription by Fabius Maximus, governor of the province, recording his restoration of the Baths of Hercules after an earthquake, likely dating to his tenure.

EDCS-12401859.translation: Gnaeus Cluvius, son of Gaius, from the Teretina tribe, who served as aedile, quaestor, and duovir with judicial authority.
EDCS-12401859.summary: A brief career record of Gnaeus Cluvius, listing his magistracies in municipal government.

EDCS-12401880.translation: To Gaius Rufelleius Successor, freedman of Entella, Augustalis quaestor, Rufelleius Futurus, his fellow freedman, dedicated this to his most excellent fellow freedman and to himself.
EDCS-12401880.summary: A dedication by Rufelleius Futurus to his deceased fellow freedman and colleague Gaius Rufelleius Successor, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-12401883.summary: A very fragmentary inscription consisting of a single name, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-12401911.translation: To Gaius Julius, son of Gaius, [---] Zagar[is and] Julia, freedwoman of Gaius, [---].
EDCS-12401911.summary: A fragmented inscription mentioning Gaius Julius, son of Gaius, and Julia, a freedwoman, possibly part of a funerary or dedication.

EDCS-12401944.summary: A highly fragmented inscription containing parts of names, likely from a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-12401949.translation: Who would not grieve or mourn that three sweet sons were offered up to us in this calamity, and that our sons, most sweet, most loving, dearest, most dutiful, are now doing what, ignorant of so much grief, unless your tomb is satisfied, therefore asking and saying, by the living God and the day of judgment, if anyone disturbs these infants, here rests in peace Inportuna, who lived 8 years, 7 months, 15 days, placed in peace on the 15th day before the Kalends of September, twelve years after the consulship of Basilius, most illustrious man, in the first indiction. Honesta, 6 years, 7 months, placed on the Ides of June, 12 years after the aforesaid consulship, in the first indiction. Decoratus lived 5 years, 3 months, 11 days, placed on the Ides of August, 12 years after the aforesaid consulship, in the first indiction. The aforesaid three brothers, who rest here, became Christians.
EDCS-12401949.summary: A Christian epitaph for three brothers, Inportuna, Honesta, and Decoratus, who died at young ages, recording their burial dates relative to a consul and indicating their conversion to Christianity, likely dating to the 4th century AD.

EDCS-12700080.translation: Iunia, daughter of Decimus Libertas, gives and concedes the use and enjoyment of the gardens, buildings, and shops of the Hilaroniani and Iuniani, enclosed by her own wall, which are hers, to her freedmen and freedwomen, and to those who have been or will be manumitted by them and their descendants, and if any of them wishes to sell or alienate or grant to another the use and enjoyment of their portion, until the use and enjoyment reaches one person, and if no one from the family survives, then I wish those gardens, with the buildings and shops, enclosed by their own walls and boundaries, to be the property of the colonists of the public community of Ostia, from whose income I wish the public community of Ostia to expend 100 sesterces for the adornment of the tomb, 100 sesterces for violets, and 100 sesterces for roses. I wish this will to be made public, that the right may belong first to my freedmen and freedwomen, and after them to their descendants.
EDCS-12700080.summary: A detailed will by Iunia Libertas, daughter of Decimus, bequeathing her property including gardens, shops, and buildings to her freedpersons and their descendants, with a provision for the Ostian colony and funds for tomb adornment, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700192.translation: To Geminia Marciana, dearest girl, who lived 8 years and 11 days, died the fourth day before the Kalends of April in the third consulship of Valentinian and Valens. Geminius Felix, father, to his incomparable daughter.
EDCS-12700192.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, dedicated by her father, likely dating to the 4th century AD.

EDCS-12700199.translation: To Salvius Opimianus, son, to his most dear and most dutiful parents: to Salvius Rufinus, son of Titus, of the Papiria tribe, procurator of the province of Asia, and to his daughter Iusta, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-12700199.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a son to his parents, one of whom held an administrative position in the province of Asia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12700209.translation: To my most dear and perfect wife, the object of my longing, my supreme joy, Aurelia Libuscidia Quinta, who lived 25 years, 5 months, and 15 days; to whom I, Murrius Numidius, was joined in marriage for 9 years, 3 months, and 25 days, and with whom I also prepared my rest; deposited the fifth day before the Kalends of July, during the consulship of our lords Constantinus Augustus for the 10th time and Julian Caesar for the 3rd time.
EDCS-12700209.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, detailing her lifespan and the duration of her marriage, and dedicated by her husband, dated by the consuls to 367 AD.

EDCS-12700212.translation: Lucius Catius, son of Lucius, grandson of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, centurion of the emperor's speculatores (bodyguards), for himself and his wife Calenia Bucula, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-12700212.summary: A dedication by a centurion of the imperial bodyguards for himself and his wife, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800219.translation: Marcus Ineius, son of Statius, erected this for his parents and for himself: for Statia, daughter of Ineius, son of Statins, and for Cerna, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-12800219.summary: A funerary monument erected by a son for his parents and himself, identifying familial relationships and likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800305.translation: Fugeo Tullia has taken the dark light from the living.
EDCS-12800305.summary: A very brief, enigmatic epitaph, possibly indicating a death or departure, with no clear dating or context.

EDCS-12800356.translation: Sepstinia Cail(l)a lived 1 year and 5 months.
EDCS-12800356.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a child named Sepstinia Cail(l)a, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800357.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Earinus made this for his most dutiful son, Tiberius Iulius Telephus.
EDCS-12800357.summary: A funerary dedication from a father to his son, invoking the Divine Manes, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800360.translation: Sutoria, freedwoman of Lucius, of the Gamete tribe, [erected this] for Quintus Stnippius Antiochus.
EDCS-12800360.summary: A funerary dedication from a freedwoman to a man, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800361.translation: Numerius Mettius, son of Streb, of the Menenia tribe; Caesia, freedwoman of Caius, named Pamphila; Mettia, freedwoman of Numerius, named Rufa; Numerius Mettius, son of Numerius, named Hilarus; under the arbitration of Numerius Mettius, freedman of Numerius, named Hilarus. You and for you.
EDCS-12800361.summary: A complex dedication or legal record involving several individuals, including freedpersons, likely related to inheritance or property and dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13302446.translation: To Vesta, daughter of Lucius Vesuvius.
EDCS-13302446.summary: This is an epitaph for Vesta, daughter of Lucius Vesuvius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13302457.translation: From the potteries of Quintus Aburnius Caedicianus, both the Tempesian and the Furian workshops.
EDCS-13302457.summary: This inscription indicates ownership or origin from the potteries of Quintus Aburnius Caedicianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13302458.translation: From the estates of Annia Lupula Caepioniana.
EDCS-13302458.summary: This inscription records property belonging to Annia Lupula Caepioniana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13302508.translation: Marcus Alficius Paulus, aedile. Anyone who wishes to throw dung in this place is warned that it is not permitted. If anyone makes an accusation against this, free persons will give a monetary reward; slaves will be warned by beatings in their dwellings.
EDCS-13302508.summary: An inscription set up by the aedile Marcus Alficius Paulus, imposing a penalty on anyone dumping waste and offering a reward for information, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13302714.summary: A very short inscription, possibly religious or funerary, its context is unclear but might relate to an ascension, dating uncertain.

EDCS-13302724.translation: To Publius Lucilius, son of Publius, grandson of Publius, great-grandson of Publius, great-great-grandson of Publius Gamala, who served as aedile, military tribune, and was admitted to the order of decurions by decree of the decurions, free of charge, and as a duovir, by public decree of the decurions, because he pleaded the public case of the colony in the Senate.
EDCS-13302724.summary: An honorific inscription for Publius Lucilius, detailing his career and recognition for public service to the colony, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13400223.summary: A dedication to the deities Aesculapius and Coronide, and to a person named Vedius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500009.translation: Roscia Selene made this monument for herself and for her son Marcus Roscius Sentianus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument will not pass to an external heir.
EDCS-13500009.summary: A funerary monument set up by Roscia Selene for herself, her son, and their freedmen and descendants, with a stipulation against external inheritance, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500013.translation: Sotericus, son of Marcus Salinator Soteric[us] the Younger (?). His father Sotericus made [this] for his most devoted son; he lived 3 years, 5 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-13500013.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sotericus, set up by his father, recording his short lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500027.translation: To Silia Heuresis, her husband(?) made [this].
EDCS-13500027.summary: A funerary epitaph for Silia Heuresis, set up by her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500042.translation: Perhaps Titinius Helis [erected this] for himself and for his wife Titinia.
EDCS-13500042.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording a dedication by a man for himself and his wife.

EDCS-13500049.translation: Marcus Ulpius Mercurius dedicated a sarcophagus to Aelius Thallus and Aelia Donata, and permitted their descendants to access and use the entranceway.
EDCS-13500049.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records a dedication of a sarcophagus and access rights by Marcus Ulpius Mercurius to Aelius Thallus and Aelia Donata.

EDCS-13500063.translation: Ianuaria and (?) Asiatice (?) made [this] for themselves.
EDCS-13500063.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording a dedication by two women for themselves.

EDCS-13500073.translation: Anna, approximately 16 years old, [died] on the Kalends of S [---].
EDCS-13500073.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records the age and date of death of a girl named Anna.

EDCS-13500081.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Myphas, son of Aibpas, [dedicated this].
EDCS-13500081.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, is a dedication to the deified dead.

EDCS-13500126.translation: I remember that a certain girl once died, whose ashes the golden earth may cover.
EDCS-13500126.summary: This epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, is a poetic lament for a deceased girl.

EDCS-13500127.summary: This inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, simply lists several names, possibly of the deceased or those associated with the monument.

EDCS-13500134.translation: Pottery [made] by Anterotis, servant of Severianus Caesar.
EDCS-13500134.summary: This inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicates that pottery was made by a slave named Anterotis belonging to Severianus Caesar.

EDCS-13500135.translation: Pottery [made] by Aprilis, servant of Gnaeus Domitius Agathobulus.
EDCS-13500135.summary: This inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicates that pottery was made by a slave named Aprilis belonging to Gnaeus Domitius Agathobulus.

EDCS-13500136.translation: Pottery work from the estates of our Aurelius Caesar, from the kilns of Fulvianus Successus, slave.
EDCS-13500136.summary: This inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records pottery production from the estates and kilns belonging to Aurelius Caesar and his slave Fulvianus Successus.

EDCS-13500137.summary: This inscription records pottery works produced by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis.

EDCS-13500138.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made pottery works from the smaller Oceanus potteries of our Caesar, when Paetinus was consul.
EDCS-13500138.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery works by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis during the consulship of Paetinus, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-13500139.translation: From the potteries of Lucius Munatius Crescens.
EDCS-13500139.summary: This inscription indicates ownership or origin from the potteries of Lucius Munatius Crescens.

EDCS-13500140.translation: From the estates of Cornelius Severus.
EDCS-13500140.summary: This inscription denotes the origin of goods from the estates of Cornelius Severus.

EDCS-13500142.summary: This inscription records the name Gnaeus Domitius Arignotus, likely as an owner or producer.

EDCS-13500143.summary: This inscription records the name Gnaeus Domitius Clemens, likely as an owner or producer.

EDCS-13500144.summary: This inscription records the name Gnaeus Domitius Chryseros, likely as an owner or producer.

EDCS-13500145.summary: This inscription records the name Gnaeus Domitius Diomedes, likely as an owner or producer.

EDCS-13500146.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Euaristos made [this], may he prosper.
EDCS-13500146.summary: This inscription records that Gnaeus Domitius Euaristos was the maker, with a wish for his prosperity.

EDCS-13500147.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, from Aquinum.
EDCS-13500147.summary: This inscription records pottery works originating from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, located in Aquinum.

EDCS-13500148.translation: The slaves of Lucilla, daughter of Publius, of the family of Domitia.
EDCS-13500148.summary: This inscription records the slaves belonging to Lucilla, daughter of Publius, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500150.translation: From the workshop of Publius Caulus Valentis.
EDCS-13500150.summary: This inscription identifies the workshop of Publius Caulus Valentis, likely a pottery or brick manufacturer, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500151.translation: From the workshop of Publius Caulus Valentis and Caius Statius Capito.
EDCS-13500151.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Publius Caulus Valentis and Caius Statius Capito, associated with a workshop, likely in the pottery or brick industry, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500152.translation: From the Caninian potteries of Titus Greius Ianvarius, belonging to two landowners; may he who made it prosper.
EDCS-13500152.summary: This inscription from the Caninian potteries names Titus Greius Ianvarius and mentions two landowners, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500153.translation: From the estates of Iulia Albana, workshop of Hermias, under the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus.
EDCS-13500153.summary: This inscription records items from the estates of Iulia Albana, produced by the workshop of Hermias, and is dated to the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus (likely 161 AD).

EDCS-13500155.translation: From the estates of Marus Lurius Valentis, under the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus.
EDCS-13500155.summary: This inscription indicates items from the estates of Marus Lurius Valentis, and is dated to the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus (likely 161 AD).

EDCS-13500156.translation: From the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes; Nunnidius Restitutus made it.
EDCS-13500156.summary: This inscription records that Nunnidius Restitutus produced items from the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500158.translation: From the estates of Plotia Isaurica; Caepio, son of Titus Rausius Pamphilus.
EDCS-13500158.summary: This inscription indicates ownership or production from the estates of Plotia Isaurica, associated with Caepio, son of Titus Rausius Pamphilus, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13500159.translation: Under the consulship of Hiberus and Sisenna, from the Rhodinian potteries of Peducaeus Lupus, of our Caesar.
EDCS-13500159.summary: This inscription records items from the Rhodinian potteries of Peducaeus Lupus, associated with the emperor, and is dated to the consulship of Hiberus and Sisenna (likely 133 AD).

EDCS-13500160.translation: The work of Servilius Fortunatus from the estates of Statilius Maximus.
EDCS-13500160.summary: This inscription records a work produced by Servilius Fortunatus from the estates of Statilius Maximus, likely indicating ownership or origin of materials.

EDCS-13500161.translation: Of Publius Servilius Firmus, from the potteries of Furianus Aburnius Caedicianus.
EDCS-13500161.summary: This inscription identifies a product or individual, Publius Servilius Firmus, associated with the potteries of Furianus Aburnius Caedicianus.

EDCS-13500162.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or ownership mark by Marcus Verus.

EDCS-13500163.translation: Of Decimus Veturis Cerdonis, from the estates of Annius Verus, during the consulship of Apronius and Paetus.
EDCS-13500163.summary: This inscription records Decimus Veturis Cerdonis, associated with the estates of Annius Verus, and is dated by the consuls Apronius and Paetus.

EDCS-13500164.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark by Gaius Clodius Successus.

EDCS-13500165.translation: Of Lucius Fabricius Masculus (repeated three times).
EDCS-13500165.summary: This inscription, repeating the name Lucius Fabricius Masculus three times, likely indicates a multiple ownership or a maker's mark related to his work or property.

EDCS-13500168.summary: This inscription indicates that the item or work originated from the workshop of Justus.

EDCS-13500183.summary: This inscription is a dedication recording that Gnaeus Valerius Eros was the maker of the object.

EDCS-13500289.translation: Gnaeus Valerius Eros made this. Lucius Veicius, son of Lucius; Lucius Fulvius, son of Quintus; Marcus Curtius, son of Caius; Lucius Fuficius, son of Lucius; Numerius Arrius, son of Aulus; Numerius Spurius, son of Decimus; Titus Pescennius, son of Titus; Marcus Annius, son of Lucius; Quintus Hostius, son of Quintus; Caius Lucretius, son of Caius; Tiberius Asicius, son of Tiberius; Publius Suesanus, son of Marcus; Publius Baebius, freedman of Numerius, aerarius; Caius Cossutius, freedman of Caius; Gentius Aulus, freedman of Fulvius; Lucius Flavius, freedman of Quintus; Publius Cipius, freedman of Cnaeus; Lucius Nerius, freedman of Marcus; Cnaeus Pescennius, freedman of Lucius; Publius Nerius, freedman of Publius; Caius Cipius, freedman of Caius; Pera Caius Nerius, freedman of Marcus; Publius Caesius, freedman of Marcus; Publius Servius, freedman of Numerius, purpurarius; the Magistri Castor and Pollux and Mercurius Felix oversaw the construction of a vault and the steps above the vault and all the sewers next to the vault, and they also put on games, during the consulship of Publius Rutilius and Gnaeus Mallius.
EDCS-13500289.summary: This extensive inscription records the completion of a vault, steps, and sewers by various individuals, led by the Magistri Castor, Pollux, and Mercurius Felix, who also organized games, and is dated to the consulship of Publius Rutilius and Gnaeus Mallius.

EDCS-13500519.translation: In this sacred grove, where the water sources are frequent, so that one might live and be sustained, a weak health was built, filled with trees and cool and excellently situated waters, so that by its clear and sweet springs, great troubles and cares might be alleviated. Calpurnius, son of Lucius, built it.
EDCS-13500519.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred grove with healing waters and trees by Calpurnius, son of Lucius, intended to alleviate sickness and worries.

EDCS-13600052.summary: This inscription, though fragmentary, likely records the name of a Roman owner, Coelius, and his slaves (vernae).

EDCS-13600055.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to Prima, daughter of someone whose name is lost.

EDCS-13600056.translation: and to his son Priscus, who deserved well.
EDCS-13600056.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a son named Priscus, acknowledging his merit.

EDCS-13600063.summary: This fragmented dedication honors someone named Elpizon for their good service.

EDCS-13600071.translation: to my husband, [---]io, who deserved well, happily [---].
EDCS-13600071.summary: This incomplete inscription appears to be a dedication to a deceased husband, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-13600075.translation: To the spirits of the dead, [---] wine.
EDCS-13600075.summary: This very short inscription is likely an offering to the Manes (spirits of the dead), possibly wine.

EDCS-13600116.translation: To Fortuna Domestica Sancta, for the health and safe return of Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, Lucius Valerius Frontinus, centurion of the II Cohort of Vigiles, erected this at his own expense with his dependents and freedmen, and also Flavius Julianus, centurion of the IIII Cohort of Vigiles.
EDCS-13600116.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna Domestica Sancta by two centurions of the Vigiles, Lucius Valerius Frontinus and Flavius Julianus, for the well-being and return of Emperor Septimius Severus, dating to his reign (193-211 AD).

EDCS-13600117.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the Heliopolitan Genius, for the health of the Emperors Antoninus and Commodus Augusti, Gaionas gave this as a gift.
EDCS-13600117.summary: This dedication to Jupiter and the Genius of Heliopolis was made by Gaionas for the health of Emperors Antoninus (likely Caracalla) and Commodus, dating to their joint rule (c. 195-200 AD).

EDCS-13600125.translation: Work from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, workshop of Mercury.
EDCS-13600125.summary: This inscription indicates that the work was produced from the estates belonging to Aurelius Caesar and originated from the workshop of Mercury.

EDCS-13600126.translation: From the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes, Nunnidius Restitutus made this.
EDCS-13600126.summary: This inscription records that Nunnidius Restitutus created something originating from the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes.

EDCS-13600127.translation: Pottery from the workshops of Claudius Alexander.
EDCS-13600127.summary: This inscription records pottery from the workshops of Claudius Alexander, likely a manufacturer or owner of a pottery business.

EDCS-13600128.translation: Pottery from the workshops of Claudius Alexander.
EDCS-13600128.summary: This inscription records pottery from the workshops of Claudius Alexander, likely a manufacturer or owner of a pottery business.

EDCS-13600300.translation: Pottery from the workshops of Arria Fadilla Caepioniana, belonging to Titus Rausius Pamphilus.
EDCS-13600300.summary: This inscription indicates pottery from the workshops of Arria Fadilla Caepioniana, associated with Titus Rausius Pamphilus.

EDCS-13600302.translation: From the estates of Hadrianus Macedonianus, the workshop supervisor Aulus Memmius Clemens.
EDCS-13600302.summary: This inscription mentions Aulus Memmius Clemens, a workshop supervisor, and the estates of Hadrianus Macedonianus, likely indicating a production or supply context.

EDCS-13600303.translation: From the estates of Plotina Augusta Quintiana.
EDCS-13600303.summary: This inscription refers to pottery or materials originating from the estates of Plotina Augusta Quintiana.

EDCS-13600305.translation: Pottery from the estates of our Augustus, Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-13600305.summary: This inscription marks pottery from the estates of Caius Cominius Sabinianus, referred to as 'our Augustus,' suggesting a high-ranking individual.

EDCS-13600306.translation: From the workshops of Primigenius, freedman of Domitius.
EDCS-13600306.summary: This inscription indicates pottery from the workshops of Primigenius, a freedman of someone named Domitius.

EDCS-13600307.translation: From the estates of Memmia Macrina, workshop of Lucius Memmius Astragalus, in the third consulship of Servianus.
EDCS-13600307.summary: This inscription records pottery from the estates of Memmia Macrina, originating from the workshop of Lucius Memmius Astragalus, dated to the consulship of Servianus (likely 134 AD).

EDCS-13600308.translation: From the workshops of the two Popilii, Severus and Clemens.
EDCS-13600308.summary: This inscription denotes pottery from the joint workshops of Severus and Clemens, members of the Popilius family.

EDCS-13600309.translation: From the workshop of Publius Caulus Valens and Caius Statius Capito.
EDCS-13600309.summary: This inscription identifies pottery originating from the shared workshop of Publius Caulus Valens and Caius Statius Capito.

EDCS-13600310.translation: Brickwork from the estates of Arulenus Epagathus, under the consulship of Maximinus and Avitus.
EDCS-13600310.summary: This inscription records brickwork from specific estates, dated by the consuls Maximinus and Avitus.

EDCS-13600311.translation: Brickwork from the estates of Flavius Aper, belonging to Fadius Euhelpistus.
EDCS-13600311.summary: This inscription records brickwork from the estates of Flavius Aper, owned by Fadius Euhelpistus.

EDCS-13600312.translation: From the estates of Flavius Aper, pottery from the workshop of Publilius, property of Rustius Felix.
EDCS-13600312.summary: This inscription indicates pottery from Flavius Aper's estates, made in Publilius's workshop and owned by Rustius Felix.

EDCS-13600315.summary: This inscription records ownership of property by Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-13600316.translation: Pottery from the workshop of Fortunatus, belonging to Domitia Lucilla.
EDCS-13600316.summary: This inscription notes pottery from Fortunatus's workshop, which was property of Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-13600317.translation: Brickwork belonging to Earinus, agent of Lucilla Verus.
EDCS-13600317.summary: This inscription records brickwork belonging to Earinus, the agent of Lucilla Verus.

EDCS-13600318.translation: Brickwork from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, by Claudius Quinquatralis and Livius Martialis.
EDCS-13600318.summary: This inscription records brickwork produced by Claudius Quinquatralis and Livius Martialis from the estates of Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-13600319.translation: Brickwork from the estates of Verus's Lucilla, under the consulship of Ulpius Anicetianus and Lateranus.
EDCS-13600319.summary: This inscription records brickwork from the estates of Lucilla, dated by the consuls Ulpius Anicetianus and Lateranus.

EDCS-13600320.translation: From the Viccian potteries, belonging to Rutilia Lucia, daughter of Ocratus.
EDCS-13600320.summary: This inscription records ownership of pottery from the Viccian potteries by Rutilia Lucia, daughter of Ocratus.

EDCS-13600321.summary: This inscription records ownership of property by Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-13600322.summary: This inscription records the ownership of Gnaeus Domitius Evaristus, likely related to a property or tomb.

EDCS-13600323.summary: This inscription identifies an individual as the nephew of Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, possibly on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-13600324.summary: This inscription records the ownership of Quintus Oppius Justus, likely on a property marker or tomb.

EDCS-13600325.translation: During the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus, made from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudentis by Marcus M.V.
EDCS-13600325.summary: This inscription records the construction of something from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudentis by Marcus M.V. during the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13600326.translation: Doliar work from the Domitian workshops, by Publicus Consortis.
EDCS-13600326.summary: This inscription records a doliar (tile or pottery) work from the Domitian workshops made by Publicus Consortis, likely related to construction or a brickyard.

EDCS-13600331.summary: This inscription records the ownership or commemoration of Roscianus Domitius Agathobulus, likely on a tomb or property.

EDCS-13600333.translation: From the workshops of Quintus Asinius Marcellus, during the consulship of Quintus Articuleius.
EDCS-13600333.summary: This inscription indicates a product or activity from the workshops of Quintus Asinius Marcellus during the consulship of Quintus Articuleius, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13600335.translation: From the estates of Caius Curiatius Cosanus, the Caepian ones.
EDCS-13600335.summary: This inscription designates property as belonging to Caius Curiatius Cosanus, referring to the Caepian estates, likely a boundary marker.

EDCS-13600337.translation: Doliar work from the workshops of our Fulvia Lucilla.
EDCS-13600337.summary: This inscription records doliar (tile or pottery) work from the workshops of Fulvia Lucilla, likely indicating ownership or production from her brickyard.

EDCS-13600338.translation: Titus Travius Felix from the Furianian pottery, from the workshops of Valeria Polla.
EDCS-13600338.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Travius Felix and his association with the Furianian pottery and the workshops of Valeria Polla, likely concerning brick production or trade.

EDCS-13600339.translation: From the estates of Tiberius Claudius Maximus, of the Isis cult.
EDCS-13600339.summary: This inscription indicates products from the estates of Tiberius Claudius Maximus, who was associated with the cult of Isis, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13600340.translation: From the estates of Tiberius Claudius Maximus.
EDCS-13600340.summary: This inscription records products originating from the estates of Tiberius Claudius Maximus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13600342.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this pottery production from the brickworks of our Caesar, when Propinquus and Ambibulus were consuls.
EDCS-13600342.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis from imperial brickworks during the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-13600344.translation: From the Terentian brickworks of Domitia Lucilla, the Portus Licinia, pottery production of Statia Primula.
EDCS-13600344.summary: This inscription indicates pottery production from the brickworks of Domitia Lucilla at Portus Licinia, associated with Statia Primula.

EDCS-13600345.translation: Pottery production from the brickworks of Tur Seia Isaurica, by Lucius Fadius Passarus Servianus, when he and Varus were consuls.
EDCS-13600345.summary: This inscription records pottery production from the brickworks of Tur Seia Isaurica, produced by Lucius Fadius Passarus Servianus during his consulship with Varus.

EDCS-13600346.translation: Pottery production from the estates of our Augustus, from the Voconian brickworks, by Munatius Anicetus.
EDCS-13600346.summary: This inscription records pottery production from imperial estates and Voconian brickworks, attributed to Munatius Anicetus.

EDCS-13600348.translation: From the estates of our Caesar, of Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus, during the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-13600348.summary: This inscription notes products from imperial estates belonging to Tiberius Claudius Irenaeus, dated by the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-13600350.translation: From the brickworks of Asinia Quadrata, pottery production of Caius Nunnidius Fortunatus, when Lucius Quadratus was consul.
EDCS-13600350.summary: This inscription records pottery production from the brickworks of Asinia Quadrata, by Caius Nunnidius Fortunatus, during the consulship of Lucius Quadratus.

EDCS-13600351.translation: Pottery production of Dionysius, son of Domitia, daughter of Publius, Lucilla, during the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-13600351.summary: This inscription records pottery production by Dionysius, son of Domitia Lucilla, dated by the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-13600352.translation: Pottery production of Doryphorus, son of Domitia, daughter of Publius, Lucilla, during the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-13600352.summary: This inscription records pottery production by Doryphorus, son of Domitia Lucilla, dated by the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-13600353.translation: From the estates of Lucilla Veri, belonging to Tiberius Claudius Secundinus.
EDCS-13600353.summary: This inscription records the ownership of estates, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600354.translation: Nunnidius Restitutus made this from the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes.
EDCS-13600354.summary: This inscription records a private commission or work made by Nunnidius Restitutus from the estates of Quintus Marcius Hermogenes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600355.summary: This inscription records ownership, likely a marker for property belonging to Quintus Oppius Natalis, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600356.translation: During the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus, Marcus M V made this from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens.
EDCS-13600356.summary: This inscription records a private commission, likely a work or dedication, made by Marcus M V during the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus, referencing the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens, probably from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13600357.translation: From the estates of Prastina Pacata, a work by Pontius Longinus, son of Lucius Messalinus Ste[---].
EDCS-13600357.summary: This inscription records a work made by Pontius Longinus from the estates of Prastina Pacata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600358.translation: From the workshop of Publius Caulus Valens, belonging to Gaius Stasius Capito.
EDCS-13600358.summary: This inscription records the ownership or origin of goods from the workshop of Publius Caulus Valens, associated with Gaius Stasius Capito, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600359.summary: This inscription records the status of Apelles as a slave belonging to Stertinia Bassulla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600392.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Aelius Euprepes had this made for his most dutiful son, Publius Aelius Augustus, freedman of Gaudianus, who lived 29 years, 9 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-13600392.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Publius Aelius Augustus, set up by his father Publius Aelius Euprepes, and includes his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700281.translation: From the estates of Lucilla Veri, belonging to Mercurius, freedman of Tiberius Claudius Quinquatralis.
EDCS-13700281.summary: This inscription records the ownership of estates, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700394.summary: This inscription likely refers to a group of ship-owners or merchants from Africa, possibly indicating a guild or association, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13800064.translation: The most honorable people of the city of Minturnae erected this to Flavius Theodorus, a man of praiseworthy character, for his boundless benefits, deeming him a most worthy patron.
EDCS-13800064.summary: A public monument erected by the people of Minturnae to their patron Flavius Theodorus for his great services.

EDCS-13800158.translation: To Cornificia, sister of our Augustus.
EDCS-13800158.summary: A dedication to Cornificia, sister of an emperor, likely from the 1st century AD.

EDCS-13800159.translation: Of Didi Marinus, a distinguished man, and...
EDCS-13800159.summary: An incomplete dedication or epitaph for Didi Marinus, a distinguished man.

EDCS-13800160.translation: From the workshop of Demetrius, freedman, under the supervision of the procurator Pepaminus, freedman of Augustus, and the rationalis.
EDCS-13800160.summary: An inscription relating to the workshop of a freedman, managed by an imperial freedman and a rationalis, likely during the reign of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-13800161.translation: Of Aelius Censorinus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-13800161.summary: An epitaph or dedication for Aelius Censorinus, a man of high standing.

EDCS-13800163.summary: An inscription indicating that Caius Nasennius Musaeus commissioned or created the object.

EDCS-13800164.summary: An ownership mark or dedication associated with Sextus Caecilius Volusianus.

EDCS-13800165.translation: To Lusia Rufia Marcella, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-13800165.summary: A dedication or epitaph for Lusia Rufia Marcella, a woman of notable status.

EDCS-13800166.translation: From the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Eutyches.
EDCS-13800166.summary: An inscription indicating the origin of an object from the workshop of Marcus Ostiensis Eutyches.

EDCS-13800168.summary: An ownership mark or dedication belonging to Servius Scipio Orfitus.

EDCS-13800169.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership marker for Quintus Servilius Pudens.

EDCS-13800170.translation: Valerius Falto Adelfus, a most distinguished and illustrious man, and Anicia Italica.
EDCS-13800170.summary: This inscription names Valerius Falto Adelfus and Anicia Italica, likely a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-13800222.translation: To Cornificia, daughter of our Emperor.
EDCS-13800222.summary: This is a dedication to Cornificia, daughter of the emperor.

EDCS-13800223.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Ducenus.

EDCS-13800224.translation: Sulpicia, daughter of Gallus, granddaughter of Servius, great-granddaughter of Servius Trion, from the province of Lusitania, from the colony of Emerita Augusta; presented by the legates Titus Furius Ocriculanus and Lucius Flavius Urfus.
EDCS-13800224.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sulpicia, detailing her distinguished ancestry and mentioning the legates who presented the monument.

EDCS-13800226.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Gaius Artorius and Venus.

EDCS-13800232.translation: Lucius Albius, son of Lucius, gave this as a gift to Hercules.
EDCS-13800232.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a gift to Hercules by Lucius Albius.

EDCS-13800234.translation: Amarantus, son of Aprilla, lived 4 years.
EDCS-13800234.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Amarantus.

EDCS-13800235.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or ownership marker for Gaius Poppaeus Atticus.

EDCS-13800237.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Gaius Poppaeus Celer.

EDCS-13800238.translation: To Gaius Poppaeus Felicionius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-13800238.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Felicionius, dedicated to his patron Gaius Poppaeus.

EDCS-13800240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Poppaeus Blastus.

EDCS-13800241.translation: Of Alexandrus, freedman of Gaius Poppaeus.
EDCS-13800241.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Alexandrus, freedman of Gaius Poppaeus.

EDCS-13800244.translation: On the first of March, for the profit from the sale of the Cadian farm, Nic(o?) contracted that the upright ones be given correctly. The slave of Herennia Tertia promised: Lucius Annius Agathemer. Done at Nola on the 17th day before the Kalends of November, during the consulship of Marcus Cluvius(?) and Marcus Furnius Augurinus.
EDCS-13800244.summary: This inscription records a private contract for a sale of land, dated to 8 AD in Nola.

EDCS-13800245.translation: Gaius Manlius Tacitus, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe, judge, between Publius Vedius Carus, guardian of Marcus Caecilius Natalis, and Quintus Vibius Ampiatus, guardian of Gaius Caecilius Zenonis, in their presence, judged and absolved Quintus Vibius Ampiatus by the standard legal formula. In council were present: Quintus Hortensius Blasus, son of Quintus, of the Stellatina tribe; Gaius Turranius Calvinus, son of Gaius, of the Sergia tribe. Done on the 10th day before the Ides of April, during the consulship of Gaius Rantius and Marcus Hordeonius. Gaius Manlius Tacitus, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe, judge, between Publius Vedius Carus, guardian of Marcus Caecilius Natalis, and Quintus Vibius Ampiatus, guardian of Gaius Caecilius Zenonis, in their presence, judged and absolved Quintus Vibius Ampiatus by the standard legal formula. In council were present: Quintus Hortensius Blasus, son of Quintus, of the Stellatina tribe; Gaius Turranius Calvinus, son of Gaius, of the Sergia tribe. Done on the 10th day before the Ides of April, during the consulship of Caius Calpetanus Sedatus and Marcus Hordeonius. ...
EDCS-13800245.summary: This is a legal document recording a judgment made by Gaius Manlius Tacitus in a case involving guardians and their wards, dated to the consulship of Rantius and Hordeonius (possibly 21 AD) and repeated with a different consulship (Calpetanus and Hordeonius, possibly 7 AD).

EDCS-13800246.translation: Of the freedmen and freedwomen of Publius Novius Amphion and Zethus, and of the freedmen and freedwomen of Publius Novius Zethus.
EDCS-13800246.summary: This inscription lists the freedmen and freedwomen of two patrons, Publius Novius Amphion and Zethus, and Publius Novius Zethus.

EDCS-13900357.translation: To Gamo, freedman of Marcius Ambitionis, sexvir Augustalis, at Venafrum and Lugdunum.
EDCS-13900357.summary: This is an inscription dedicated to Gamo, a sexvir Augustalis, who served in both Venafrum and Lugdunum, indicating a possible connection to both locations.

EDCS-13900380.translation: Titus Lucius Marcius, freedman of Onius Quinti, freedman of Cossutius Cai, freedman Dionysius, made this section from bottom to top, paved the road, and repaired the steps, and put on the games, during the consulship of these magistrates.
EDCS-13900380.summary: This inscription records the civic contributions of several freedmen who funded and built a section of a road and steps, and sponsored games.

EDCS-13900381.translation: Lucius Quinctius Gelasinus, son of Lucius; Lucius Iuventius Rufus, son of Lucius; Gaius Tittius, son of Gaius; Gaius Helvius Numerius, son of Gaius; Lucius Helvius, son of Lucius; Gaius Helvius Numerius, son of Gaius; Gero; Publius Plinius, son of Marcus; Quintus Matuius, son of Quintus; Gaius Paccius, son of Cnaeus; Marcus Mamius, son of Manius; Gaius Sattius, son of Gaius; Publius Statius Stagon, son of Publius. During the consulship of Sergius Sulpicius Galba, these magistrates commissioned the joining of the wall to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the construction of a pier, and the heaping up of earth for the theatre, and they also presented games.
EDCS-13900381.summary: This inscription lists several magistrates who oversaw public works projects including a wall, a pier, and theatre construction, and also sponsored games, during the consulship of Sergius Sulpicius Galba (possibly 68 AD).

EDCS-13900538.translation: Make Cnaeus Helvius Sabinus, a worthy aedile for the state, that Masculus with the tail-bearers, and everywhere.
EDCS-13900538.summary: This is an electoral recommendation urging voters to support Cnaeus Helvius Sabinus for the office of aedile.

EDCS-13900539.translation: Men, I ask you to make Gaius Gavius Rufus, Marcus Holconius Priscus, two men holding judicial power; I ask you, men, to make Cuspus Pansas, Popidius Secundus, aediles worthy of the state.
EDCS-13900539.summary: This inscription is a political appeal from an unknown author asking the citizens to elect certain individuals as magistrates, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13900540.translation: To Lucius Aelius Magnus, happily. Astylus, son of Iarine, I have [paid?]
EDCS-13900540.summary: This inscription appears to be a private note or receipt, possibly concerning a debt or payment to Lucius Aelius Magnus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900542.translation: Masculus will win, he has won. Iovia. The 6th day before the Nones of April.
EDCS-13900542.summary: This inscription records a victory, possibly in a race or gladiatorial contest, associated with the name Iovia and dated to April 2nd, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900545.translation: On the 4th day before the Nones of July, he paid for a cloak and a mantle for Faustilla, a loan of 50 sesterces, with 14 semis of bronze and an as.
EDCS-13900545.summary: This inscription records a financial transaction for clothing purchased for a woman named Faustilla, detailing the amount paid and the date, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900548.translation: I ask you, men, to make Gaius Numitorius an aedile. Serenus Successus, Fufidius, requests it.
EDCS-13900548.summary: This is a political recommendation urging citizens to elect Gaius Numitorius as an aedile, proposed by Serenus Successus and Fufidius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900550.summary: This is a simple personal name inscription, possibly a tombstone or ownership mark, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900552.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a tombstone or ownership mark, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900553.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a tombstone or ownership mark, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900554.summary: This inscription is a simple greeting or salutation, possibly an epitaph or a dedication, featuring the name Eunus and dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900558.summary: This inscription marks a date or event during the reign of Emperor Vespasian, potentially related to a building project or official act, dating to 69-79 CE.

EDCS-13900560.translation: From Emperor Vespasian, for the fourth time.
EDCS-13900560.summary: A brief inscription, likely marking a work or event sponsored by Emperor Vespasian during his fourth consulship.

EDCS-13900595.translation: I, Quintus Tamudius Optatus, have written and sworn by the Genius of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus and his children, that I was present for Petronia Vitalis when she was with Calatoria Themis concerning her daughter, and that I heard Themis' husband, Stephanus, say to Petronia Vitalis: 'Why do you envy our daughter, when we treat her as our own daughter?' From this, I know that the woman in question is the daughter of Petronia Vitalis and is freeborn. The matter in question is testified by Quintus Tamudius Optatus. I, Quintus Tamudius Optatus, have written and sworn by Jupiter Best and Greatest and the Genius of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus and his children, that I was present for Petronia Vitalis when she was with Calatoria Themis concerning her daughter, and that I heard Calatoria Themis' husband, Petronius Stephanus, say to Petronia Vitalis: 'Why do you envy our daughter, when we treat her as our own daughter?' From this, I know that the woman in question was born free to Petronia Vitalis. The matter in question is...
EDCS-13900595.summary: A legal deposition or sworn statement, likely concerning the status of a young girl as freeborn, witnessed by Quintus Tamudius Optatus and referencing Emperor Vespasian, probably dating to his reign (69-79 AD).

EDCS-14000027.translation: The quaestors, Caius Saufeius, son of Caius, arranged for this to be made for Fortuna.
EDCS-14000027.summary: An inscription recording the construction of something for the goddess Fortuna, commissioned by the quaestors Caius Saufeius and his associate, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-14100188.translation: The officers of the money-changers give [this] to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-14100188.summary: A dedication to Fortuna Primigenia made by the officers (magistri) of the money-changers (Nummularii), probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-14100191.translation: The officers of the Guild of Vine Cultivators have seen to this; slaves of Orestes, servant of Fortuna Primigenia, the freedman of Bufilius; of Glaucia, servant of Publius Vibius; of Camerus.
EDCS-14100191.summary: An inscription related to the Guild of Vine Cultivators, indicating the involvement of freedmen and slaves in a project dedicated to Fortuna Primigenia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-14100192.translation: They give this gift to Fortuna Primigenia; slaves of Popilius, servant of Tremeilius Publius; of Anicius Lucius.
EDCS-14100192.summary: A dedication of a gift to Fortuna Primigenia by slaves, possibly associated with a magistracy within a collegium, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-14100193.translation: Caius Postumius, freedman of Aulus Pilipus, and Gnaeus Octavius, freedman of Lucius Pilonicus, and Orcivius, slave of Marcus, gave [this] as a gift in return for their magistracy of the guild.
EDCS-14100193.summary: A dedication made by freedmen and a slave in honor of their magistracy within a guild, given to Fortuna Primigenia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-14501031.translation: Lucius Caecilius Aemilianus, veteran of the first Praetorian cohort, decurion, duovir of Aelia Uluzibira of Africa, having undertaken the corporative duty, made this in the temple of the wine merchants' forum for himself.
EDCS-14501031.summary: A dedication by Lucius Caecilius Aemilianus, a veteran and former official, for himself in a temple associated with the wine trade and importers, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-15100039.translation: Dedication of the work of the tablets of Gnaeus Allei Nigidius Maius in Pompeii on the Ides of June; there will be a procession, a hunt, athletes, and awnings. Farewell, Nigra Ocella.
EDCS-15100039.summary: An announcement for a public dedication of works related to Gnaeus Allei Nigidius Maius in Pompeii on June 13th, featuring various spectacles and festivities, likely from the 1st century AD before the eruption of Vesuvius.

EDCS-15100140.translation: To Scurracia, daughter of Marcus, his most rare wife. Lucius Laelius Hermes.
EDCS-15100140.summary: A funerary epitaph for Scurracia, wife of Lucius Laelius Hermes, praising her exceptional character, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100141.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secunda, identified as the freedwoman of Anterotis.

EDCS-15100145.translation: Gaius Turcius Crescens erected this for Gaius Sempronius Gallus, son of Lucius, his most excellent patron and deserving of his best efforts, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-15100145.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Turcius Crescens to his patron Gaius Sempronius Gallus.

EDCS-15100169.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription, possibly for Soterichus, son of Lucius, named Corymbus.

EDCS-15100175.translation: The bones of Marcus Stlaccius Ianuarius are here.
EDCS-15100175.summary: A funerary epitaph indicating the burial place of Marcus Stlaccius Ianuarius.

EDCS-15100176.summary: A very fragmented funerary inscription listing several female names, possibly family members or deceased individuals.

EDCS-15100180.summary: A fragmented inscription mentioning Successus, possibly a freedman, with illegible preceding text.

EDCS-15100181.summary: A dedication or epitaph for Suettia Fausta.

EDCS-15100215.translation: Titus Hordionius Phronimus [erected this] for Aulus Titinius Faustus, freedman of Aulus, and for himself, and for his son Aulus Titinius Secundus, freedman of Titus; and for Titinia Suntycheni, freedwoman of Aulus; and for Titinia Urbana, freedwoman of Aulus; and for Aulus Titinius Faustillus, son [of the above].
EDCS-15100215.summary: A complex funerary inscription detailing familial relationships and dedications, likely erected by Titus Hordionius Phronimus.

EDCS-15100229.translation: Marcus Tullius Alexander, freedman of Tullia.
EDCS-15100229.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying Marcus Tullius Alexander as the freedman of Tullia.

EDCS-15100231.translation: Turrania Anna: I have borne my years with you without pain. I beg you, gods above, not to separate me from my husband.
EDCS-15100231.summary: A tomb inscription from Turrania Anna, requesting the gods not to separate her from her husband in the afterlife.

EDCS-15100234.translation: Tyche to her well-deserving brother, made this.
EDCS-15100234.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Tyche for her brother.

EDCS-15100237.translation: Gaius Valerius [---], Gaius Norbanus [---], Lucius Valerius Lu[---], Titus Claudius Himērus, Lucius Octavius Phoebus, Gaius Iulius Euangelus, Titus Oculatius Eutychus, Tiberius Iulius Crescens, Titus Livius Secundus, Titus Rutilius Fructus, Marcus Naevius Auctus, [---] Caninius Agathopus?
EDCS-15100237.summary: A list of names, likely from a funerary monument or a list of freedmen, with much of the context lost.

EDCS-15100240.translation: In his 18th year, 11 months, and 26 days, Quintus Valerius Aspasius, his freedman, made this for him as deserving.
EDCS-15100240.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Quintus Valerius Aspasius and indicating it was set up by a freedman.

EDCS-15100266.summary: A funerary epitaph with only the name of Valeria Paulina.

EDCS-15100272.translation: Valeria Stacte, freedwoman of Aulus Valerius Gallus, son of Aulus Valerius, of the Fabian tribe, for herself and her family. Aulus Valerius Eulimenus, freedman, for himself and his family. This is a monument or sepulchre; may it never be sold by anyone from the family or their heirs.
EDCS-15100272.summary: A funerary monument inscription establishing ownership and forbidding sale, set up by Valeria Stacte and Aulus Valerius Eulimenus.

EDCS-15100279.summary: A funerary epitaph with the name and status of Varia Ephesia.

EDCS-15100288.translation: To Marcus Verrius Flaccus, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe. Celsus, his brother.
EDCS-15100288.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Marcus Verrius Flaccus by his brother Celsus.

EDCS-15100295.translation: Vestoria Helpis, by order of Titus Vestorius Alexander and Titus Vestorius Pelops.
EDCS-15100295.summary: An inscription possibly related to a funerary monument, ordered by Titus Vestorius Alexander and Titus Vestorius Pelops for Vestoria Helpis.

EDCS-15100297.translation: The remains of Caius Vettenus Dionysus and his wife Vettenna Smyrna.
EDCS-15100297.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Caius Vettenus Dionysus and his wife Vettenna Smyrna.

EDCS-15100302.translation: Marcus Vetuvius Crescens, son of Spurius, built the small shrine for himself and for my freedman Marcus Vetuvius Primogenus, freedman of Marcus [---] and his wife.
EDCS-15100302.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a small shrine by Marcus Vetuvius Crescens for himself and his freedman, Marcus Vetuvius Primogenus.

EDCS-15100306.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Vibius Liberalis Nestorianus erected this to his dearest brother, Marcus Vibius Nestor, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus, who lived 29 years and 5 days.
EDCS-15100306.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Vibius Nestor, detailing his parentage, name, and age at death.

EDCS-15100310.translation: Eucalis Tannoni erected this to Vivia Luxuria, an honorable woman; her husband, Chysrinus, placed it.
EDCS-15100310.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband to his deceased wife, Vivia Luxuria.

EDCS-15100312.translation: Gaius Vibidius Adauctus lived 7 years and 6 months.
EDCS-15100312.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Vibidius Adauctus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-15100711.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Licinia Soteris made this for herself and for her well-deserving patron, Licinius Seleucus; whoever my heir shall be who does not place my body in this sarcophagus, incurs a penalty of 25,000 sesterces to the public treasury of Ostia.
EDCS-15100711.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the deceased's wishes for her burial and a penalty for her heir if she is not buried in the specified sarcophagus.

EDCS-15200077.translation: Volusianus, a most distinguished man, formerly prefect, having undergone the taurobolium, gave this gift.
EDCS-15200077.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Volusianus, a former prefect, after performing the taurobolium, likely to a deity.

EDCS-15200080.translation: To the Invincible God Hercules, Hostilius Antipater, a most accomplished man, prefect of the grain supply, curator of the public affairs of the people of Ostia.
EDCS-15200080.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by Hostilius Antipater, who held important administrative positions in Ostia.

EDCS-15200085.translation: Sacred to the divine powers of the imperial household. Lucius Laelius Herennianus, son of Spurius, a clerk of the wax tablet makers, of the college of the standard-bearers of Ostia, gave this gift with his own money.
EDCS-15200085.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the imperial household by Lucius Laelius Herennianus, a scribe and member of a collegium in Ostia.

EDCS-15200089.translation: Sacred to Atti, by the instruction of the goddess.
EDCS-15200089.summary: This is a dedication to Atti, made by Caius Cartilius Euplus under divine instruction.

EDCS-15200090.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing the name Gaius Cartilius, possibly a dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-15200091.translation: Gaius Cartilius Euplus, by the instruction of the goddess, gave this gift.
EDCS-15200091.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Cartilius Euplus, made under divine instruction.

EDCS-15200094.translation: Lucius Porcius Severinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Neptune the Restorer.
EDCS-15200094.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Neptune Redux by Lucius Porcius Severinus.

EDCS-15200183.translation: Marcus Marius, son of Marcus, as praetor, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-15200183.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Marius and notes his position as praetor, acting by senatorial decree.

EDCS-15300346.translation: To Publius Cluvius Maximus Paullinus, consul, VIIvir epulonum, proconsul assigned to the province of Asia, XVvir sacris faciundis, legate of the emperor with proatorial power in the province of Upper Moesia, curator of the Flaminian Way, legate of the Legio XIIII Gemina, proconsul of the province of Sicily, legate of the province of Asia, legate of the province of Achaia, seviir of the III turma of Roman knights, prefect for distributing grain, legate sent by the Senate to Emperor Hadrian when he was returning from Africa, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor of the province of Achaia, tribune of the Legio V Macedonica, IVvir for maintaining roads, Publius Cluvius Maximus Paulinus [dedicated this] to his most excellent father and most excellent mother.
EDCS-15300346.summary: This lengthy inscription details the extensive career of Publius Cluvius Maximus Paullinus and is dedicated by his son to his parents.

EDCS-15300347.translation: Agathangelus, freedman and Augustalis quinquennalis, [dedicated this] to his most worthy patron, Aulus Livius Chryseros, Augustalis quinquennalis.
EDCS-15300347.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription set up by a freedman for his patron.

EDCS-15300349.translation: Felicissimus made this according to his vow.
EDCS-15300349.summary: This is a simple votive inscription, stating that Felicissimus fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-15400228.translation: Doretio made this for Auspicata, his sweetest daughter, and Clariana, his dearest wife.
EDCS-15400228.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Doretio for his daughter and wife.

EDCS-15400549.summary: This is a very brief funerary marker identifying Marcus Ulpius Callistus.

EDCS-15400566.translation: Ulpia Valentina [is buried] here, daughter of Ulpius Callistus.
EDCS-15400566.summary: This is a funerary marker identifying Ulpia Valentina as the daughter of Ulpius Callistus.

EDCS-15400612.translation: [...]mius / freedman of [3]ivatus / and of [3]ia, freedwoman of Caius / [3] most holy / [---]
EDCS-15400612.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the names and relationships of individuals, possibly for a funerary monument.

EDCS-15400620.translation: [...]rbuloi[---] / [---]viae Trii[---] / [---] to his spouse I[---] / [---] Avitus, his son [---] / [---] well deserving [---]
EDCS-15400620.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription that appears to be a funerary monument, possibly mentioning family members and honoring a well-deserving individual.

EDCS-15400628.translation: Most excellent freedwoman of the Augusti, Marcius...
EDCS-15400628.summary: This fragment likely records an honorific dedication to a freedwoman of the emperors, possibly by a man named Marcius.

EDCS-15400661.summary: This inscription records the completion of a work or object by someone named Dinus, possibly indicating a distance of 18 miles.

EDCS-15400680.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Nciateius by someone named Felicissimus.

EDCS-15400686.translation: AQ[---] his wife [---] arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-15400686.summary: This inscription indicates that a wife, possibly named Aq[---], arranged for a monument to be constructed, likely for her husband or family.

EDCS-15400688.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Tronius ssima lived 23 years. May your hair be beautiful, and farewell, mother.
EDCS-15400688.summary: This epitaph commemorates Tronius ssima, who lived 23 years, and offers a farewell to her mother.

EDCS-15400702.summary: This fragment seems to record a dedication or endowment made by someone ending in -nius for himself and for someone named Otini.

EDCS-15400708.translation: To the deserving one who lived 13 years and 3 months.
EDCS-15400708.summary: This inscription is an epitaph honoring a person who lived 13 years and 3 months, likely referring to their merits.

EDCS-15400717.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to Dullania, identified as the daughter of Publius.

EDCS-15400721.translation: Inius Uctus, son of Itus, Flamen Sevir...
EDCS-15400721.summary: This inscription appears to record the name and possibly an office of Inius Uctus, son of Itus.

EDCS-15400728.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, Parent Maxanus and Abacatio, possibly related or in a specific social context.

EDCS-15400729.translation: Saint Theodorus the bishop rests here, who was laid to rest on the third day before the Ides of May in the fifteenth consulship of Theodosius and the fourth of Valentinian.
EDCS-15400729.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Theodorus, dating to the consulship of Theodosius and Valentinian.

EDCS-15400730.translation: Misenus the bishop rests here in peace, who lived about 76 years, laid to rest on the third day before the Ides of January in the consulship of Flavius Felix, vir clarissimus, and he presided for 10 years, months, and 6 days.
EDCS-15400730.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Misenus, recording his age, burial date, and tenure as bishop.

EDCS-15400731.translation: To the sweetest and most loving infant Megetia, Valentinus, formerly a tribune, made this burial chamber.
EDCS-15400731.summary: This is a funerary dedication to an infant named Megetia, made by Valentinus.

EDCS-15400733.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Apol, aged about 40 years, laid to rest on the day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-15400733.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apol, recording his age and burial date.

EDCS-15400734.translation: Here rests in peace Benus, daughter of Abundantius the rebbitis, who lived about 17 years, laid to rest on the second day before the Ides of June.
EDCS-15400734.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benus, daughter of Abundantius, recording her age and burial date.
