EDCS-15400735.translation: Felicianus lived in marriage for six years and 25 days; he is buried here. He lived 33 years and 25 days. Dulcitia made this for her husband against her vow.
EDCS-15400735.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicianus, commemorating his marriage duration, lifespan, and burial, made by his wife Dulcitia.

EDCS-15400737.translation: Flavia Matrona, an infant, who lived [some years], is placed here. Made for the deserving.
EDCS-15400737.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an infant named Flavia Matrona, indicating it was made by a loved one.

EDCS-15400738.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Gen, aged about 20 years. Iulia [made this].
EDCS-15400738.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gen, recording his age and likely made by Iulia.

EDCS-15400741.translation: Sapis rests here in peace. Read, pray for me.
EDCS-15400741.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sapis, requesting prayers from passersby.

EDCS-15400746.translation: M. Gymnasi, of good memory, who lived one year, [this was] made for the deserving.
EDCS-15400746.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for M. Gymnasi, an infant of one year, made by a loved one.

EDCS-15400763.translation: Regarding these buildings and adjacent properties, whether these buildings or the land itself, Publius Aelius Rufus, a soldier, proved through the purchase of his father, Publius Aelius Abascantus, that he possessed them, before Senecio, subordinate prefect of the Praetorian Fleet at Misenum, and deserved the judgment which Senecio, the aforementioned subordinate prefect, decreed for this inscription. Senecio, after deliberation with his council, stated: 'The inspection of the buildings and land, which were brought before me, is clearly shown by the facts. Since I found the buildings to be situated on clear ground and not appearing to be superimposed on or attached to any tomb, their sale was legally made, and they therefore seem to belong to Aelius Rufus, the soldier, by right of purchase. As for the land or property adjacent to the buildings, which Aelius Abascantus, Rufus's father, also bought from the heirs of Patulcus Diocles, since there are many tombs scattered in various places, the right to the land could not be transferred through sale. However, since Rufus's father, and subsequently Rufus himself, have always been in possession, even though the purchase was not legally made, Patulcus has no right to claim this land for himself. It is clear, since I have inspected the spot, that the cippus, where the name of Patulcus is said to have been erased, has clear remaining traces of writing expressing these words: 'Actius Diocles Patulcus, son of Diocles, with his brothers who are now present, sell to Publius Aelius Abascantus a clear plot of land on which no tombs have been made or appear to be attached, for the use of his children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.' Nevertheless, for his contempt, Rufus, son of Publius Aelius Abascantus, shall be deprived of the land, and it shall be made public for the burial of soldiers. The heirs of Patulcus Diocles shall be fined, together with interest at the rate of two percent public Roman interest, for neglecting the sanctity of tombs and secretly corrupting the poor soldiers of the First Praetorian Fleet at Misenum, so that they may not be cared for and buried with contributions. Let everyone know that this judgment is sacred.' All this is attested by the marble.
EDCS-15400763.summary: This is a legal judgment from Misenum, dating to the Roman Imperial period, concerning a property dispute involving buildings and adjacent land. It details a ruling by the subordinate prefect Senecio, upholding the claim of Publius Aelius Rufus, a soldier, to a property purchased by his father, despite issues with scattered tombs on part of the land, and outlines penalties for the sellers and their heirs.

EDCS-15400766.translation: To Jupiter Striganus, by Lucius Varenius Rufus, tribune.
EDCS-15400766.summary: This is a dedication to the god Jupiter Striganus, made by Lucius Varenius Rufus, identified as a tribune, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400770.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, son of Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus Adiabenicus, Father of the Fatherland, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 8th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Proconsul, by the captains and trierarchs of the Praetorian Fleet at Misenum.
EDCS-15400770.summary: This dedication, from the Roman Imperial period, is offered by the naval officers of the Misenum fleet to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar (likely Caracalla), son of Emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-15400772.translation: For the return and victory of Augusta, mother of the camp and of the entire divine house, the decurions of Misenum and Teanum(?) paid [this], the trierarch Pris[---], prefect of the 3rd Gallic Legion, prefect [---], during the consulship of Claudius Severus and [---].
EDCS-15400772.summary: This fragmentary inscription from the Roman Imperial period likely records a dedication for the well-being and victory of the imperial family, possibly made by local officials and naval officers from Misenum and Teanum during a specific consular year.

EDCS-15600055.translation: Chryseros, servant of Caesar. Restituta, freedwoman of Abascanti.
EDCS-15600055.summary: This is a bilingual funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, recording the names and statuses of two individuals, Chryseros (a servant of Caesar) and Restituta (a freedwoman).

EDCS-15600968.translation: Numerius Vesuius, son of Numerius; Marcus Lollius, son of Quintus; Quintus Sextius, son of Caius; Lucius Lollius, son of Lucius; Caius Statius, son of Marcus; Caius Arrius, son of Vibius; Marcus Egnatius, son of Marcus; Numerius Opius, son of Numerius; Marcus Teronius, son of Ovius; Caius Vibius, son of Quintus; Marcus Nerius, son of Ovius; Cnaeus Arrius, son of Cnaeus. These men, serving as magistrates, supervised the construction of this work and approved it for themselves.
EDCS-15600968.summary: This inscription from the Roman Republic or early Empire lists the names of several individuals who served as magistrates and oversaw and approved a public work project.

EDCS-15600969.translation: Lucius Geminius, son of Erius, son of Marcius, called Rufus; Caius Trasius, son of Numerius; Caius Consius, son of Lucius; Marcus Naevius, son of Marcius; Alfius, son of Numerius; Marcus Amatius, son of [---]; Aulus Seius, son of Marcius; Publius Paccius, son of Lucius. These men, serving as magistrates, supervised the construction of the pavement, the repair of the temple, the columns, and gilded statues for the columns, using funds from the treasury of Diana, during the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius.
EDCS-15600969.summary: This inscription from the Roman Imperial period records a public works project, including paving, temple repair, and the erection of gilded statues, overseen by several magistrates and funded by the treasury of Diana, during the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-15601031.translation: For the greatest Sarmatic, greatest Persic, greatest Germanic, seventh greatest Briton, greatest Carpic, greatest Armenian, greatest Median, greatest Adiabenic, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 7th time, Father of the Fatherland, [---]ov[---]ius, a most perfect man, prefect of the Praetorian Fleet, most devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-15601031.summary: This inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, is a dedication to an emperor (unnamed but identified by numerous honorific titles and military victories) by a high-ranking official, the prefect of the Praetorian Fleet, expressing devotion to the emperor's divine majesty.

EDCS-15601034.translation: Septimus, servant and steward of the inventory of the Emperor Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, to his most sacred wife.
EDCS-15601034.summary: This dedicatory inscription from the Roman Imperial period is from Septimus, a servant and administrator for Emperor Trajan, to his wife, likely on a tomb or as a personal dedication.

EDCS-15601038.translation: Felix [---]. Publius Aelius Iunianus, formerly naval captain [---], with Titia Sperata, his [---] his own [---].
EDCS-15601038.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning individuals named Felix, Publius Aelius Iunianus (a former naval captain), and Titia Sperata, likely commemorating a family or relationship.

EDCS-15601045.translation: To Gaius Julius Automatus, freedman of Caesar, trierarch, his sister Iulia Plusia, freedwoman of Gaius, made this for herself and her family.
EDCS-15601045.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a sister for her deceased brother, who was a trierarch in the imperial navy.

EDCS-15601046.translation: Tiberius Julius Diogenes, freedman of Augustus and Augusta, trierarch, for himself, his wife Nigidia Eutychia, and his family. Nigidia Eutychia had the monument made for her friend Margarita, freedwoman of Gaius Stabercus, and it will not pass to her heir.
EDCS-15601046.summary: This funerary inscription records a trierarch, his wife, and a friend, stipulating that the monument is not heritable.

EDCS-15601049.translation: Gaius Marcius Maximus, son of Volso, of the Sergia tribe, tribune, from the liburna ship 'Aquila', for himself, his wife Silia Eutychia, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants. He ordered by his will to be made from 10,000 sesterces. His wife Eosilia Eutychia added 8,333 sesterces.
EDCS-15601049.summary: This funerary inscription details a donation for a military tribune and his family, specifying the amount of money and the additional contribution from his wife.

EDCS-15601080.translation: For Gaius Vettius Gratus, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, architect of the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, for himself and his wife Mevia Quinte, and his mother Sallustia Secunda, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and all their descendants. This monument or tomb will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-15601080.summary: This funerary inscription records an architect of the Roman fleet at Misenum, dedicated to himself, his wife, mother, and descendants, with a non-hereditary clause.

EDCS-15601081.translation: [...] to Vitruvius [...]ioni, architect(?) [...]nius Classic[...], to a well-deserving [...]
EDCS-15601081.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely honors an architect, possibly related to the famous Vitruvius, with a dedication for services rendered.

EDCS-15601097.translation: Marcus Ambibius Celer, of the armor unit of the quadrire(me), made this for Lucius Valerius Crispus, a soldier from the trireme 'Athenonice', his kinsman, who deserved well.
EDCS-15601097.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a military colleague for a fellow soldier, a rower on a trireme, recognizing his merit.

EDCS-15700052.translation: Solon rubbed his belly to help himself defecate well.
EDCS-15700052.summary: This is a humorous, possibly medical, inscription in Latin hexameter.

EDCS-15700054.translation: Thales advised those who were defecating with difficulty to strain.
EDCS-15700054.summary: This is a humorous inscription in Latin hexameter, referencing the philosopher Thales.

EDCS-15700055.translation: No one speaks to you at length while you use Priscianus, for we [take] water [with] the xylospongium.
EDCS-15700055.summary: This is a witty, likely obscene, inscription playing on the Latin word 'Priscianus' and referencing a specific item used in Roman latrines.

EDCS-15700056.translation: The cunning Chilon taught [one] to fart silently.
EDCS-15700056.summary: This is a humorous inscription in Latin hexameter, attributing a dubious lesson to the philosopher Chilon.

EDCS-15700057.translation: Mulio, sit down! You will arrive more quickly, my friend. A proverb has fled you: 'Shit well and mock the doctors.'
EDCS-15700057.summary: This inscription is a humorous, possibly graffiti, quote about a mulio (mule driver) and a proverb, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15700058.translation: Gaius Fulvius Salvis, the haruspex, gives this gift: Sortes Herculis.
EDCS-15700058.summary: This inscription records a divination ritual or object, the 'Sortes Herculis' (Lots of Hercules), dedicated by the haruspex Gaius Fulvius Salvis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-15700060.summary: This very brief inscription simply records the name Epictetus Buticosus, likely a personal dedication or tombstone from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700082.translation: Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the third time, father of the country, saw to its construction. 19.
EDCS-15700082.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work, possibly a road or building, initiated by Emperor Nerva in his consulship, around 97 AD.

EDCS-15700137.translation: During the consulship of Gaius Bellicius Flaccus Torquatus and Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes, the station was dedicated on the fifth day before the Kalends of [Month]. It was overseen by Antonius Ingenuus and Herenuleius Faustus, who placed gifts in the station. Marcus Antonius Ingenuus placed a statue of Caesar Verissimus with a chryselephantine Victoria, a silver image of Antoninus Augustus weighing 1 pound, and for the dedication, 4 sesterces to everyone. Aulus Herenuleius Faustus placed an image of Antoninus Augustus weighing 2 pounds. Gaius Voltidius Martianus placed an image of Caesar Aelius weighing 1 pound. Gaius Antistius Hermes placed a silver image of Concordia weighing 1.5 pounds. Gaius Antistius Onesimus placed a silver image of Caesar Verissimus weighing 1.5 pounds. Gaius Nasennius Felix placed a silver image of Antoninus Augustus weighing 1 pound. Gaius Nasennius Felix the younger placed a silver image of Caesar Verissimus weighing 1 pound. Publius Aelius Eutychus provided 6 benches. Marcus Cornelius Maximus provided 4 tables and 2 stools. Marcus Aeficius Hermes and Gnaeus Sergius Felix placed an acrolithic statue of Lucius Aelius Commodus with their own money. Tiberius Claudius Threptus donated a milestone with a hot bath. Quintus Cornelius Hermes and Lucius Aurelius Fortunatus placed an aereus statue of Antoninus Augustus with a marble base with their own money and for its dedication, they gave 4 sesterces individually. Lucius Cornelius Euhodus [donated] a silver image of Antoninus Augustus. Lucius Aurelius [donated] a pair of candelabra. Lucius Cornelius Euhodus [donated] 6 hemitylia and 4 pitchers. On the 12th day before the Kalends of April, during the consulship of Lucius Aelius Aurelius Commodus and Titus Sextius Lateranus, Publius Sextilius Agrippa offered under the condition that from the interest of the sum written above, each year on the day of his birthday, those who are in the college would feast, and if on the ninth day before the Kalends of September in any year those who are in the college...
EDCS-15700137.summary: This extensive inscription records the dedication of a public station and numerous offerings made by various individuals and groups during the consulship of Atticus Herodes and Lateranus, likely around 140-150 AD, detailing statues, furnishings, and a ritual feast.

EDCS-15900010.translation: From Marcus Sabinus, son of Fadius, called Heras, craftsman, from the liburna 'Taurus Ruber'.
EDCS-15900010.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Sabinus, son of Fadius, a craftsman, and mentions a ship named 'Taurus Ruber', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900029.translation: [...] to Cyrilla, his most chaste and deserving wife. [...]vila, a scribe (?), for a four-oared boat from Dacia.
EDCS-15900029.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for a woman named Cyrilla, mentioning a benefactor named 'vila' and a connection to a Dacian four-oared boat, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900033.translation: Gaius Octavius Fronto, formerly a medic (physician) from the trireme 'Tigris', a Cilician by nationality, and Gaius Julius Favianus, a manipularis, made this for his brother, who deserved well.
EDCS-15900033.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two men, Gaius Octavius Fronto (a physician) and Gaius Julius Favianus, who served on a trireme and in the military, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900039.translation: [...] Herodes [...] from the ship shed (?) [...] deserving well [...] son (?) made (it?) [?]
EDCS-15900039.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that likely records a dedication or memorial for someone named Herodes, possibly related to a shipyard or naval context, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000305.translation: To Quintus Planus Felix, patron of the colony, tribune of the twentieth legion Valeria Victrix, the guild of carpenters, to whom it is permitted to associate by decree of the decurions, has been granted a place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000305.summary: This inscription records the granting of a public space by decree of the decurions to the guild of carpenters, honoring their patron Quintus Planus Felix, a tribune of the XX Valeria Victrix legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000426.translation: To Gaius Cascellius Longinus, optio of the Pentere Victoria, Naevia Eutychia and Blastus, his freedman, for a well-deserving husband and master.
EDCS-16000426.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife and freedman for a deceased optio, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000462.translation: Lucius Domitius Demetrius, son of Demetrius, a subunctor from the trireme Concordia, made this for himself and his wife Arruntia Genna, deserving of good service, and for Lucius Annins Priscus, son of Spurius, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants and all of them.
EDCS-16000462.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Domitius Demetrius, a naval subordinate (subunctor), for himself, his family, and descendants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000509.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name on a tomb or object, mentioning Neratius Pansa and Cleopatra.

EDCS-16000512.translation: Lucius Terentius Secundus, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Forum Iulii, served in the VI Praetorian cohort for thirteen years, lived for thirty-six years. Caius Terentius Fronto, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Forum Iulii, served in the III Praetorian cohort, [made this] for himself and his brother.
EDCS-16000512.summary: This epitaph records the military service and ages of two brothers, Lucius Terentius Secundus and Caius Terentius Fronto, both soldiers in the Praetorian Guard, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-16100330.translation: To the divine spirits. For the most beloved Publius Septimius Getianus, who lived four years and eleven days. Celadus, cashier of Caesar, and for himself, his own [family], and Eutychus, our Augustan overseer of unctors.
EDCS-16100330.summary: This is a touching epitaph for a young child, Publius Septimius Getianus, set up by Celadus, a financial official, and mentioning Eutychus, a supervisor of bath attendants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-16200043.translation: Liber Pater Nysius, Horos, mysteries, Antiope.
EDCS-16200043.summary: This inscription appears to be related to religious cults, possibly Dionysian or Bacchic, mentioning Liber Pater (Bacchus), a figure named Horos, mysteries, and Antiope, suggesting a late Hellenistic or Roman Imperial date.

EDCS-16200536.translation: To the divine spirits. Aquilia Valentina, daughter of Marcus, for Marcus Aquilius Valens, her deserving father, a veteran from the Misenian fleet, and for Aquilia Feliicula, her mother, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and all of them; this monument or tomb will not follow its heir.
EDCS-16200536.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a daughter, Aquilia Valentina, for her deceased parents, Marcus Aquilius Valens (a naval veteran) and Aquilia Feliicula, stipulating that the tomb will not pass to a future heir, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16200553.translation: Marcus Bassus Marcellus, veteran of our Augustus, [---] served for twenty-eight years, made [this] for himself and his family, freedmen, and freedwomen.
EDCS-16200553.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Bassus Marcellus, a veteran who served for 28 years, and was made for himself and his household, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-16200672.translation: Clodia, freedwoman of Publius. Compitalia, you bear it similarly, so that what I wish the time and hour may grant me equally. Two souls in harmony, we lived and died; you see all times. This warning, stranger, the year tells you: the earth which bore [you] will hold you at some time.
EDCS-16200672.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with a poetic epitaph, possibly for Clodia, a freedwoman, reflecting on life, death, and the passage of time, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16200673.translation: To the Lar familiaris. Herma, the steward; Narcissus, the storekeeper; Zora and Carquama.
EDCS-16200673.summary: This inscription lists household staff (steward and storekeeper) and possibly two other individuals, dedicated to the household gods (Lar familiaris), likely from a domestic context in the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16200693.translation: Days of Saturn, Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus. Market days in Pompeii, Nuceria, Atella, Nola, Cumae, Puteoli, Rome, Capua. The 19th, 18th, 17th, 16th, 15th, 14th, 13th, 12th, 11th, 10th, 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd before the Kalends, the Nones. The 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd before the Nones. The 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd before the Ides. The 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd, 24th, 25th, 26th, 27th, 28th, 29th, 30th.
EDCS-16200693.summary: This inscription is a calendrical table listing the days of the week, market days in various cities, and numbered days of the month, likely for public display in Pompeii.

EDCS-16200775.translation: Pontius Salutius, a most distinguished man, formerly consular governor of Campania, had this constructed.
EDCS-16200775.summary: This inscription records that Pontius Salutius, a former consular governor of Campania, commissioned a construction, likely a building or monument.

EDCS-16200787.translation: Catilo, son of pious Pernius Vettius, permits.
EDCS-16200787.summary: This inscription is a permissive dedication, where Catilo, son of Pernius Vettius, grants permission for something, possibly the erection of a monument or an action.

EDCS-16200957.translation: The tribune, patron and defender, son of the patron Iulianus, rebuilt [this] under the supervision of Flavius Vitulus, the second curator of the state.
EDCS-16200957.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding of something by a tribune and defender, who was the son of a patron, under the supervision of a state curator, likely in the Roman period.

EDCS-16201171.summary: This is a dedication of an object or shrine to the god Silvanus by an individual named Captator.

EDCS-16201177.translation: Pertuditus [dedicated this] in Pompeii for Felicio.
EDCS-16201177.summary: This inscription records a dedication made in Pompeii by someone named Pertuditus, possibly for or on behalf of Felicio.

EDCS-16202006.translation: I beg you, Trebius Valens, to make Lucius Popidius Secundus, son of [---], aedile, a good man. [He] sleeps.
EDCS-16202006.summary: This inscription is a plea from Trebius Valens to the public to elect Lucius Popidius Secundus as aedile, describing him as a good man, possibly found on a tomb or electoral notice.

EDCS-16202011.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators and ten pairs of gladiators belonging to Decimus Lucretius Valens, son of the perpetual priest of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus, will fight in Pompeii on the day before the Nones of April; there will also be a hunt and awnings. Polybius.
EDCS-16202011.summary: This inscription records gladiatorial games and a hunt sponsored by Decimus Lucretius Valens, likely in Pompeii, and specifies the date before the Nones of April, possibly for a public festival or dedication.

EDCS-16300125.translation: For the health and victory and return of our invincible lords Augusti Antoninus and Geta, and of Julia Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camps, Antonius and Eugenius, slaves and stewards, have set this up for the Genius of the Vescinian aqueducts.
EDCS-16300125.summary: This is a dedication set up by two slaves and stewards for the welfare of the emperors Antoninus and Geta, and Empress Julia Augusta, and for the Genius of the aqueducts, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16300128.translation: Lucilia Salvia, wife [of ---], to Gaius Arrius Senius, Augustal magistrate.
EDCS-16300128.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucilia Salvia to her husband, Gaius Arrius Senius, who held the position of Augustal magistrate.

EDCS-16300131.translation: Publius Licovius, son of Publius, and Marcus Albius, son of Marcus, as duoviri, willingly dedicated this.
EDCS-16300131.summary: This inscription records a dedication by two duoviri, likely officials in a Roman colony or municipality, possibly for a public building or work.

EDCS-16300132.summary: This is a simple dedication or funerary inscription naming Tiberius Claudius Faustus.

EDCS-16300133.translation: Gaius Carullios, son of Gaius, of the Marcia tribe, dedicated this.
EDCS-16300133.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Gaius Carullios, identifying his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-16300134.translation: To the Divine Shades. Minturnius Successus, freedman of the colony, made this for his most excellent wife, daughter of Marcus Minturnius.
EDCS-16300134.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman, dedicated by her husband, a freedman, who identifies his patron.

EDCS-16300137.summary: This inscription appears to be a label or ownership mark, identifying Aulus Fabius Diogenes.

EDCS-16300153.translation: Oceanus, freedman, won 18 times. Arancitus, freedman, 4 times.
EDCS-16300153.summary: This inscription records the victories of two freedmen, likely in athletic or gladiatorial contests.

EDCS-16300267.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription addressed to Caia Appia Nereis.

EDCS-16300280.translation: From the estates of Lucilius Verus, pottery work from the kilns of Vibius Pudentis.
EDCS-16300280.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of pottery, identifying the owner of the estates and the location of the kilns.

EDCS-16300283.summary: This inscription records the maker of an object or structure, Lucius Rufinus Phoebus.

EDCS-16300288.translation: The aediles Herennius and Suettius request worthy candidates for the Republic.
EDCS-16300288.summary: This inscription is a public notice issued by the aediles Herennius and Suettius, likely regarding an election or appointment.

EDCS-16300290.translation: Amandus the priest asks the aedile for the god Pansas.
EDCS-16300290.summary: This inscription is a private request to an aedile, likely concerning a religious matter, possibly a vow or a cult image.

EDCS-16300292.translation: Fish sauce, the best of mackerel, from the workshop of Scaurus, by Martial, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-16300292.summary: This is a label on a container of garum (fish sauce) indicating its origin, producer, and quality.

EDCS-16300293.translation: Fish sauce, the best of mackerel, from Trebius Sunhodus.
EDCS-16300293.summary: This is a label on a container of garum (fish sauce) indicating its producer.

EDCS-16300436.translation: Doliary ware from the Domitian workshops, the work of Publicus Consortis.
EDCS-16300436.summary: This inscription marks earthenware (doliary ware) produced in the Domitian workshops and attributes it to the craftsman Publicus Consortis.

EDCS-16300444.translation: From the estates of Arria Fadilla, wife of Caepionanis, and Caius Julius Lupio.
EDCS-16300444.summary: This inscription indicates ownership or origin of property belonging to Arria Fadilla and Caius Julius Lupio.

EDCS-16300452.summary: This is a simple ownership mark, likely on property or an object, belonging to Gaius Flavius Secundus.

EDCS-16300455.translation: Doliary ware from the Publian workshops, of Aruntius Felix.
EDCS-16300455.summary: This inscription marks earthenware (doliary ware) from the Publian workshops and attributes it to Aruntius Felix.

EDCS-16300456.translation: Doliary ware of Saturninus from the workshops of Seius Isauricus, the work of Asiaticus II.
EDCS-16300456.summary: This inscription marks earthenware (doliary ware) produced by Asiaticus II, originating from the workshops of Seius Isauricus and belonging to Saturninus.

EDCS-16300465.summary: This inscription lists four names, likely slaves or freedmen, possibly as a group or inventory.

EDCS-16300472.translation: On the eighth, seventh, and sixth days before the Kalends of December, Gnaeus Alfenius Nigidius Maius, the quinquennial magistrate, will fight thirty pairs of gladiators and their substitutes, and there will be a hunt. May it go well for Maius, the quinquennial magistrate! Paris wrote this to Maius, greetings.
EDCS-16300472.summary: This is an announcement for a gladiatorial show and a hunt, specifying the date, participants, and organizers, likely from Pompeii and dating to the period of Maius's quinquennial magistracy.

EDCS-16300475.translation: By the munificence of Numerius Festus Ampliatus, on a high day, Julianus won 15 fights, Nobilior Julianus won 14 fights, Julianus won 16 fights, Julianus was a draw in 14 fights, Julianus won 30 fights, Julianus won 15 fights, Hippolytus was a draw and died, Julianus won 5 fights, Celatus won 6 fights, Nedymus won 5 fights, Julianus was a draw in 15 fights, Julianus won 4 fights.
EDCS-16300475.summary: This inscription lists the results of gladiatorial combats, likely from a list or score sheet, featuring various fighters including Julianus and Nobilior Julianus.

EDCS-16300476.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Numerius Festus Ampliatus will fight again on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of June; there will be a hunt and games.
EDCS-16300476.summary: This is an announcement for a future gladiatorial combat and hunt sponsored by Numerius Festus Ampliatus.

EDCS-16300477.translation: For Maia, the gladiatorial troop of Ampliatus will fight in Formiae. There will be a hunt and displays of nets. My gift, desired by the whole world, will be there always with Pamphilus and Fortunatus.
EDCS-16300477.summary: This inscription announces a gladiatorial show and hunt in Formiae, sponsored by someone associated with Ampliatus, dedicated to Maia, and featuring specific performers.

EDCS-16300479.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Numerius Popidius Rufus will fight in Pompeii. There will be a hunt starting on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, with games and displays of nets. Good fortune to the procurator.
EDCS-16300479.summary: This inscription announces a gladiatorial combat and hunt in Pompeii, sponsored by Numerius Popidius Rufus, with a mention of the procurator's good fortune.

EDCS-16300481.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Numerius Popidius Rufus will fight.
EDCS-16300481.summary: A simple announcement of a future gladiatorial fight by the troop of Numerius Popidius Rufus.

EDCS-16300482.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Aulus Suettius Certus, the aedile, will fight in Pompeii on the day before the Kalends of June; there will be a hunt and displays of nets.
EDCS-16300482.summary: This inscription announces a gladiatorial combat and hunt in Pompeii, sponsored by Aulus Suettius Certus, who held the office of aedile.

EDCS-16300483.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Aulus Suettius Certus, the aedile, will fight in Pompeii on the day before the Kalends of June; there will be a hunt and displays of nets. May all the Neronian games be fortunate. Written by Secundus, whitewashed by Victor, assisted by Vesbinus the contractor.
EDCS-16300483.summary: This inscription announces a gladiatorial combat and hunt in Pompeii sponsored by Aulus Suettius Certus, the aedile, and includes details about the production team.

EDCS-16300484.translation: The gladiatorial troop of Aulus Suettius Certus will fight.
EDCS-16300484.summary: A brief announcement of a gladiatorial fight sponsored by Aulus Suettius Certus.

EDCS-16300487.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators will fight on the Nones of April. Caius Alexis.
EDCS-16300487.summary: This inscription announces a large gladiatorial event with twenty pairs of fighters, scheduled for the Nones of April, and mentions Caius Alexis.

EDCS-16300499.translation: A hunt will take place on the fifth day before the Kalends of September, and Felix will fight against bears.
EDCS-16300499.summary: This inscription announces a future hunt and a specific bear-baiting combat featuring a fighter named Felix.

EDCS-16300500.translation: The gladiatorial school of Pomponius Faustinus. Quintus P...
EDCS-16300500.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to a gladiatorial school belonging to Pomponius Faustinus and mentions Quintus P.

EDCS-16300503.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators of Quintus Monnius Rufus will fight in Nola on the Kalends of May; VI and the Nones of May, and there will be a wild beast hunt.
EDCS-16300503.summary: This inscription announces twenty pairs of gladiators and a wild beast hunt sponsored by Quintus Monnius Rufus in Nola on specific dates in May.

EDCS-16300504.translation: To the divine will of Augustus, twenty pairs of gladiators and a wild beast hunt of Statius Pompei, priest of Augustus, will fight in Nuceria on the third day before the Nones of May and the eighth day before the Ides of May, for the citizens of Nuceria; my duties are certain.
EDCS-16300504.summary: This inscription dedicates twenty pairs of gladiators and a wild beast hunt to the divine will of Augustus, sponsored by Statius Pompei, a priest of Augustus, in Nuceria on specific dates in May.

EDCS-16300506.translation: By Decimus Lucretius Valens, perpetual priest of Nero Caesar Augustus, twenty pairs of gladiators will fight, and by Decimus Lucretius Valens, ten pairs of gladiators will fight in Pompeii on the IV, V, VI, III days before the Ides of April; there will be a lawful hunt and awnings. Written by Celer. Written by Aemilius Celer, the single one, for the moon.
EDCS-16300506.summary: This extensive inscription records gladiatorial games and a hunt in Pompeii, sponsored by Decimus Lucretius Valens, and mentions the scribes Celer and Aemilius Celer, possibly dating to the 1st century AD.

EDCS-16300507.translation: On the fourth day before the Kalends of August in Nuceria, Florus won; on the twelfth day before the Kalends of September in Herculaneum, he won.
EDCS-16300507.summary: This inscription records victories by a gladiator named Florus in Nuceria and Herculaneum on specific dates in July and August.

EDCS-16300511.translation: The gladiatorial school of Aulus Suettius Certus will fight (?).
EDCS-16300511.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions the gladiatorial school of Aulus Suettius Certus, possibly announcing upcoming games.

EDCS-16300513.translation: For the safety of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, in Pompeii, the wild beast hunt of Tiberius Claudius Verus, the athlete, and distributions will take place on the V and IIII days before the Kalends of March, 373 years after the founding of the city. With Claudius Verus, success!
EDCS-16300513.summary: This inscription records a wild beast hunt and distributions sponsored by Tiberius Claudius Verus in Pompeii for the safety of Emperor Nero, dated 373 years after the city's founding (likely 76 AD).

EDCS-16300514.translation: Celer, the rope-maker, honored to Maio, greetings to Maio, prince of the colony, with good fortune.
EDCS-16300514.summary: This inscription honors Celer, a rope-maker, and offers good wishes to Maio, a prominent figure in the colony, likely from the 1st century AD.

EDCS-16300515.translation: To Gnaeus Alleius Maius, prince of the munerarii, with good fortune.
EDCS-16300515.summary: This inscription offers good wishes to Gnaeus Alleius Maius, identified as the 'prince of the munerarii' (those who provide games), likely dating to the 1st century AD.

EDCS-16300516.translation: For Gnaeus Alleius Nigidius Maius, quinquennial magistrate, without public expense, twenty pairs of gladiators and their substitutes will fight in Pompeii. Gavellius Tigillus and Clodius to you, greetings. To Telephus, the most skilled fighter, and Pyladius, the tools of the games, and where you are. Farewell to Diadumenus and Pyladius, with good fortune.
EDCS-16300516.summary: This inscription records gladiatorial games and substitutions sponsored by Gnaeus Alleius Nigidius Maius, a quinquennial magistrate, in Pompeii, and includes greetings and farewells to various individuals involved in the games, possibly dating to the 1st century AD.

EDCS-16300517.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators from Decimus Lucretius Satrius Valens, perpetual *flamen* of Nero Caesar Augustus, and ten pairs of gladiators from his son, Decimus Lucretius Valens, will fight in Pompeii starting the 3rd day before the Nones of April; there will be a hunt and awnings. Polybius.
EDCS-16300517.summary: This inscription announces gladiatorial games and a hunt sponsored by Decimus Lucretius Satrius Valens and his son in Pompeii, dated to the 3rd day before the Nones of April.

EDCS-16300518.translation: On the Ides of June, at the dedication of the works and tablets of Gnaeus Alletius Nigidius Maius in Pompeii, there will be a procession, a hunt, athletes, and awnings. Nigra says goodbye to Ocella.
EDCS-16300518.summary: This inscription announces the dedication of public works and entertainment, including a procession, hunt, and athletes, sponsored by Gnaeus Alletius Nigidius Maius in Pompeii, dated to the Ides of June.

EDCS-16300519.translation: Forty-nine pairs of gladiators from the Capinia family will fight in gladiatorial contests for the Emperors in Puteoli on the 4th day before the Ides of May, the day before the Kalends of May, and the 17th and 15th days before the Kalends of June; there will be awnings. Magus.
EDCS-16300519.summary: This inscription lists gladiatorial contests involving 49 pairs of gladiators from the Capinia family, sponsored in honor of the Emperors in Puteoli, with dates spanning late April and May.

EDCS-16300520.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators from Decimus Lucretius Satrius Valens, perpetual *flamen* of Nero Caesar Augustus, and ten pairs of gladiators from his son, Decimus Lucretius Valens, will fight starting the 5th day before the Kalends of April; there will be a hunt and awnings.
EDCS-16300520.summary: This inscription announces gladiatorial games and a hunt sponsored by Decimus Lucretius Satrius Valens and his son in Pompeii, dated to the 5th day before the Kalends of April.

EDCS-16300528.translation: On the 5th day before the Ides of December, the people of Puteoli will fight for the health of Caesar, Augustus, and Livia Augusta; there will be awnings. Iole says hello.
EDCS-16300528.summary: This inscription records gladiatorial contests held by the people of Puteoli on the 5th day before the Ides of December to pray for the health of the emperors.

EDCS-16300530.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators from Aulus Suettius Parthenio and his freedman Niger will fight in Puteoli on the 16th, 15th, 14th, and 13th days before the Kalends of April; there will be a hunt and athletes and awnings.
EDCS-16300530.summary: This inscription announces gladiatorial games, a hunt, and athletes sponsored by Aulus Suettius Parthenio and his freedman Niger in Puteoli, occurring from the 16th to the 13th day before the Kalends of April.

EDCS-16300532.summary: This is a simple inscription stating that Primus was the author of the text.

EDCS-16300534.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators from Lucius T... Felix and Grosphus will fight on the 4th and 3rd days before the Kalends of November in Prisco, Nuceria. Constantia.
EDCS-16300534.summary: This inscription announces gladiatorial games featuring 20 pairs of fighters sponsored by Lucius T... Felix and Grosphus in Nuceria, scheduled for the 4th and 3rd days before the Kalends of November.

EDCS-16300538.translation: Twenty pairs of gladiators will fight in Calibus on the Nones and the 8th day before the Ides of June; there will be awnings. Celer wrote this.
EDCS-16300538.summary: This inscription announces gladiatorial games and awnings in Calibus on the Nones and the 8th day before the Ides of June, authored by Celer.

EDCS-16300540.translation: A hunt and twenty pairs of gladiators from Marcus Tullius will fight in Pompeii on the day before the Nones of November and the 7th day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-16300540.summary: This inscription announces a hunt and gladiatorial games sponsored by Marcus Tullius in Pompeii, scheduled for the day before the Nones of November and the 7th day before the Ides of November.

EDCS-16300541.translation: A hunt and twenty pairs of gladiators of Marcus Tullius will fight at Pompeii on the day before the Nones of November, the eighth and seventh days before the Ides of November.
EDCS-16300541.summary: This inscription lists a gladiatorial and hunting event scheduled for Pompeii with specific dates in November.

EDCS-16300543.translation: A hunt and twenty pairs of gladiators of Caius Alexis will fight.
EDCS-16300543.summary: This inscription announces a gladiatorial event featuring twenty pairs of fighters associated with Caius Alexis.

EDCS-16300544.translation: At Cumae, twenty pairs of gladiators and their substitutes will fight on the Kalends of October, the third day before the Nones of October; there will be a hunt and awnings. Cuniculus sends greetings to Lucceius.
EDCS-16300544.summary: This inscription details a gladiatorial event with substitutes, a hunt, and awnings scheduled for the Kalends and the days before the Nones of October at Cumae, also including a personal greeting.

EDCS-16300548.translation: Forty pairs of gladiators of Acutus Antullus will fight on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-16300548.summary: This inscription records a gladiatorial combat event featuring forty pairs of fighters sponsored by Acutus Antullus, scheduled for the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

EDCS-16300549.translation: In Nuceria, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May, a spectacle was held in the open air, here, a Nucerian.
EDCS-16300549.summary: This inscription records an open-air public spectacle held in Nuceria on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May.

EDCS-16300550.translation: Marcus Attilius, a novice, won 14 fights, 12 victories, [sent away from the arena]. Marcus Attilius, 1 fight, 1 crown, [sent away from the arena]. Lucius Raecius Felix, 12 fights, 12 crowns, [sent away from the arena]. Princeps Neronianus, 12 fights, 12 crowns, won. Creunus, 7 fights, 5 crowns, [sent away from the arena]. The games of Marcus Cominius Heres, held for four days.
EDCS-16300550.summary: This inscription details the performance records of several gladiators, including Marcus Attilius, Lucius Raecius Felix, Princeps Neronianus, and Creunus, for games sponsored by Marcus Cominius Heres in Nola.

EDCS-16300553.translation: Aegle asks you to make Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus, a worthy aedile for the Republic, [your choice].
EDCS-16300553.summary: This inscription is a plea from Aegle to the voters to elect Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus as aedile.

EDCS-16300559.translation: Avianius Vindicianus, a most distinguished man and consular governor of Campania, took care to erect statues at the crossroads of the city of Tarracina.
EDCS-16300559.summary: This inscription records the erection of statues at crossroads in Tarracina by Avianius Vindicianus, a former consular governor of Campania.

EDCS-16400053.translation: Gelos, slave of Albia, Metrodorus, slave of Calvus Caius, Artemidorus, slave of Callanus Marcius, Comus, slave of Octavia, Philostorgus, slave of Ovius Marcius, Bitus, slave of Albus Marcius, [dedicate this] to Vesonius Lucius Litta, IIII vir for dispensing justice, master of the sacred rites of the Lares.
EDCS-16400053.summary: This inscription is a dedication by several slaves to Vesonius Lucius Litta, who held positions of judicial and religious authority, likely in the 2nd century AD given the consular dating in other inscriptions.

EDCS-16400060.translation: Tempesina, [wife] of Quintus Aburnius Caedicianus, during the consulship of VIPND Capito and Gallicanus.
EDCS-16400060.summary: This inscription commemorates Tempesina, the wife of Quintus Aburnius Caedicianus, and is dated by the consulship of Capito and Gallicanus (likely in the late 2nd century AD).

EDCS-16400062.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Gaius Porcius Agatho made the monument.

EDCS-16400076.summary: This is a funerary inscription belonging to Marcus Aurelius Maximinius.

EDCS-16400086.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Sulla Cornelius.

EDCS-16400134.translation: Titius Rufus, son of Quintus, pontifex and quaestor, dedicated this to Fortuna Redux.
EDCS-16400134.summary: This is a dedication by Titius Rufus, a pontifex and quaestor, to the goddess Fortuna Redux.

EDCS-16400322.translation: Marcus Sura, during his third consulship, and Sura, during his second consulship.
EDCS-16400322.summary: This inscription records the consulships of Marcus Sura and Sura, likely for dating purposes.

EDCS-16400383.translation: Work from the potteries of Macedonia.
EDCS-16400383.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of the work as being from Macedonian potteries.

EDCS-16400507.translation: Sacred to Silvanus, by Gaius Caecina Paetus.
EDCS-16400507.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Gaius Caecina Paetus.

EDCS-16400508.translation: Sacred to Silvanus for the well-being of Gaius Caecina Paetus; Gaius Caecina Talaticus made the altar.
EDCS-16400508.summary: This is a dedication to Silvanus made by Gaius Caecina Talaticus for the health of Gaius Caecina Paetus.

EDCS-16400509.translation: Sacred to Silvanus for the well-being of Gaius Laecanius Bassus, his children, and Theseus the slave; the vow was fulfilled.
EDCS-16400509.summary: This is a votive dedication to Silvanus, fulfilled by the slave Theseus for the well-being of Gaius Laecanius Bassus and his children.

EDCS-16400510.translation: Gaius Cornelius, son of Gaius Cornelius, son of Gaius Cornelius, from the Arriti family, son of Gaius Cornelius Varus, son of Eron.
EDCS-16400510.summary: This inscription lists a complex filiation, possibly for a funerary monument, for an individual named Gaius Cornelius.

EDCS-16400511.translation: To Varius, son of Lucius, duovir; to Varius, son of Lucius, brother; to Varia Quarta, sister.
EDCS-16400511.summary: This inscription honors members of the Varii family, likely as a funerary monument.

EDCS-16400512.translation: To Caecilius Chila, Eron, Anthos, freedman, parents; Caius Caecilius Secundus Augustalis made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-16400512.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Caecilius Secundus Augustalis for his freedmen parents.

EDCS-16400574.translation: Philippus, freedman of Quintus, gladly gives this gift, deservedly, to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-16400574.summary: A freedman named Philippus dedicates a gift to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia.

EDCS-16400576.translation: Roof tile from the pottery works of Tempesinus, of S. Aburnius Caedicianus; Servilius Firmus and Paetus and Aper were consuls.
EDCS-16400576.summary: This is a tile stamp indicating ownership and production details, with a consular date from 42 BCE.

EDCS-16500051.translation: The grape-gatherers ask Casellius to be aedile.
EDCS-16500051.summary: This is a local election notice urging support for a candidate named Casellius for the position of aedile.

EDCS-16500053.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Publius Aelius Hieron, freedman of the emperor, from the admission staff.
EDCS-16500053.summary: A religious dedication to Hercules by Publius Aelius Hieron, an imperial freedman.

EDCS-16500054.translation: Doliar work from the estates of Marcus Augusti Caesaris and Faustina Augusta Mai, slaves.
EDCS-16500054.summary: This is a stamp on pottery indicating that the work came from the estates belonging to slaves of Augustus and Faustina.

EDCS-16500123.translation: Lucius Fabricius Varus, son of Caius; Marcus Saufeius Canies, aediles.
EDCS-16500123.summary: This inscription records the names of two men, Lucius Fabricius Varus and Marcus Saufeius Canies, who served as aediles.

EDCS-16500155.summary: This is a simple inscription with only a name, likely a funerary marker or ownership label.

EDCS-16500164.translation: Felix and Dorus, masters, gave this gift to the Household Gods.
EDCS-16500164.summary: Felix and Dorus, acting as officials called 'magistri', dedicated a gift to the Laribus Familiaribus (Household Gods).

EDCS-16500184.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Proiecta, buried on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the consulship of Flavius Eutharicus Cillicanus.
EDCS-16500184.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Proiecta in October during the consulship of Flavius Eutharicus Cillicanus.

EDCS-16500185.translation: Tax collector, twice *sevir*, Augustalis, for himself and for Albinus his friend and for Fortunata his wife, most excellent and most faithful.
EDCS-16500185.summary: This funerary inscription records a tax collector (*coactor argentarius*), *sevir*, and Augustalis, dedicating a tomb for himself, his friend Albinus, and his wife Fortunata.

EDCS-16500198.translation: To the Celestial Divinity, Publius Clodius Flavius Venerandus, *VI vir Augustalis*, prompted by a dream, made this.
EDCS-16500198.summary: This dedication to the Celestial Divinity was made by Publius Clodius Flavius Venerandus, a *VI vir Augustalis*, who was inspired by a dream.

EDCS-16600240.translation: Ulpia Sophe dedicated [this] to Marciana, freedwoman of the Emperor.
EDCS-16600240.summary: This dedication records Ulpia Sophe dedicating something to Marciana, a freedwoman of the Emperor.

EDCS-16600262.translation: Publius Aelius Apollinaris Arlenius, born on the fourth day before the Kalends of November, educated honestly in life, character, and letters, since he was desired by heaven and freed from his bodily prison on the eighth day before the Kalends of July, in his eighteenth year, asked and obtained from Publius Aelius Apollinaris, his father, prefect of the Vigiles, governor of the province of Corsica, and prefect of the Vigiles, that the estate called 'Ad duas casas,' bordering the territory of Praeneste, be given and handed over to the guilds of the Praenestine community, on the condition that they or whoever succeeds to their rights and persons should not have the power to alienate it in any way, but from the fruits of this estate, banquets should be provided twice annually on the aforementioned days. And that his goodwill might be further enhanced, he asked his aforementioned father to purchase gardens or possessions with five thousand folles, which would be handed over to their rights and persons under the aforementioned condition. And for this reason, all the guild members were brought into the aforementioned estate and the purchased gardens in the aforementioned manner, and because of this benefaction, all the guild members placed a seated statue of him in the forum.
EDCS-16600262.summary: This inscription records a grant by Publius Aelius Apollinaris Arlenius, concerning an estate and gardens for the guilds of Praeneste, with specific conditions for their use and the establishment of banquets, and the subsequent erection of a statue in his honor.

EDCS-16600474.translation: To the god Helios Sarapis and to Isis Myrionymus and the synaous gods. Lucius Minicius Natalis, consul, proconsul of the province of Africa, augur, legate of the emperor with praetorian power in Moesia Inferior, curator of public works and sacred buildings.
EDCS-16600474.summary: This inscription lists the honors and offices held by Lucius Minicius Natalis, including his dedication to Egyptian deities and his service as consul, proconsul, augur, legate, and curator.

EDCS-16600475.translation: If modesty in life is thought to be of any use, Lucretius Fronto, worthy of honor, is here. It is well.
EDCS-16600475.summary: This epigram praises Lucretius Fronto, suggesting his virtue and modesty make him worthy of honor.

EDCS-16700200.translation: Masters: Parhedrus the gluer, Demetrius the garden decorator, Appa the garden decorator, in the consulship of Marcus Furius Camillus and Sextus Nonius. Masters of the political [arts/crafts].
EDCS-16700200.summary: This inscription lists the names of several individuals, identified as 'masters' in various crafts (gluing, decorating), along with two consuls, possibly indicating a collegial or guild context.

EDCS-16700201.translation: To the Divine Manes. For the well-deserving Fabius Augustalis. Charito, his brother, made [this].
EDCS-16700201.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Charito to his brother, Fabius Augustalis, for his well-deserving life.

EDCS-16700259.translation: To Splendophorus, freedman of the Emperor, from the bedchamber.
EDCS-16700259.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Splendophorus, an imperial freedman who served in the bedchamber.

EDCS-16700281.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Lucius Albucius.

EDCS-16700282.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Marcus Valerius Paepus.

EDCS-16800283.translation: I ask you, make Marcus Samellius Modestus, a worthy young man of good character, aedile of the state.
EDCS-16800283.summary: This is a personal appeal recommending Marcus Samellius Modestus for the office of aedile, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16800284.translation: Make Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus and Marcus Samellius Modestus worthy aediles of the state.
EDCS-16800284.summary: This is a public recommendation for Gnaeus Helvius Sabinus and Marcus Samellius Modestus to serve as aediles, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16800285.translation: The neighbors ask you to make Marcus Samellius Modestus aedile to oversee the roads, temples, and public works.
EDCS-16800285.summary: This inscription is a request from neighbors for Marcus Samellius Modestus to be appointed aedile, responsible for public works and religious buildings, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16800287.summary: This inscription likely refers to a freedman or client named Priscus belonging to the Domitii family, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-16800311.translation: Marcus Valerius's [item] for harshness, Marcus Valerius's [item] for discoloration.
EDCS-16800311.summary: This inscription seems to record the names of Marcus Valerius and perhaps two items, possibly related to cosmetic or medicinal preparations, with their intended uses for skin conditions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17100096.translation: Dindia Macolnia gave [this] to her daughter; Novios Plautios made [it] in Rome.
EDCS-17100096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Dindia Macolnia dedicated a monument to her daughter, and that it was crafted by Novios Plautios in Rome, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17100098.translation: Castor, son of Amucos, son of Polouces.
EDCS-17100098.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription recording a man named Castor and his paternal lineage, likely from a Roman provincial context.

EDCS-17100099.translation: Poloces, son of Losna, son of Amuces.
EDCS-17100099.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription recording a man named Poloces and his paternal lineage, likely from a Roman provincial context.

EDCS-17100100.summary: This is an abbreviated dedication by Vibius Philippus to Marsuas Painsscos.

EDCS-17100101.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mercury, likely on an altar or statue.

EDCS-17100102.translation: I ask you, colonists, to make Lucius Aquitius a duumvir, a good man.
EDCS-17100102.summary: This is a request from the colonists to elect Lucius Aquitius as a duumvir, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100104.translation: I ask you to make Publius Carpinus a duumvir, a good man.
EDCS-17100104.summary: This is a request for the election of Publius Carpinus as a duumvir, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100105.translation: I ask you to make Numerius Barcha a duumvir, a good man; may Venus Pompeiana be sacred and holy to you and favorable.
EDCS-17100105.summary: This inscription is a request for the election of Numerius Barcha as a duumvir, invoking Venus Pompeiana for favor, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100106.translation: Marcus Pomponius, aedile, a good man.
EDCS-17100106.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Marcus Pomponius as a good aedile.

EDCS-17100107.translation: I ask you to make Quintus Caecilius a benefactor as quaestor.
EDCS-17100107.summary: This is a request to elect Quintus Caecilius as a beneficial quaestor, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100108.translation: Make Marcus Marius your beloved aedile.
EDCS-17100108.summary: This inscription is a plea to elect Marcus Marius as the beloved aedile, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100109.translation: Colonists, I ask you to make Numerius Veius a duumvir, a good man.
EDCS-17100109.summary: This is a request from the colonists to elect Numerius Veius as a duumvir, likely during an election period.

EDCS-17100110.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Gaius Uulius as an aedile.

EDCS-17100111.translation: I beg you, make Marcus Marius aedile.
EDCS-17100111.summary: A plea to elect Marcus Marius as aedile.

EDCS-17100113.translation: I beg you, make Publius Furius, a good man, duovir.
EDCS-17100113.summary: A plea to elect Publius Furius, a good man, as duovir.

EDCS-17100114.summary: An epitaph recording the death of Numerius Vei Bareca from disease.

EDCS-17100115.translation: Gaius Pumidius Dipilus was here on the 5th day before the Nones of October, when Marcus Lepidus and Quintus Catulus were consuls, with...
EDCS-17100115.summary: A record of presence on a specific date during the consulship of Lepidus and Catulus, likely marking a transaction or event.

EDCS-17100116.translation: Rufius Sitti, slave of Publius, painted this ship on the 10th day before the Kalends of April, when Gaius Caesar and Publius Servilius were consuls.
EDCS-17100116.summary: A record of Rufius Sitti, a slave, painting a ship on a specific date during the consulship of Gaius Caesar and Publius Servilius.

EDCS-17100118.translation: I earnestly beg you, make Gaius Tampius Sabeinus, a good man, tribune of the plebs.
EDCS-17100118.summary: A plea to elect Gaius Tampius Sabeinus, a good man, to the office of tribune of the plebs.

EDCS-17100128.translation: For Diana, deservedly. Paperia the nurse.
EDCS-17100128.summary: A dedication to Diana by Paperia, her nurse.

EDCS-17100204.translation: The council, and the people, who have always been defended by him, decreed a statue to Nicomachus Flavianus, most illustrious man, consular, proconsul of Asia, twice prefect of the city, our original patron, outstanding in all virtues and merits, exceptional in the dignity of his censorship and his moderation, prudent, always energetic, kind, benevolent, most just.
EDCS-17100204.summary: A decree by the council and people to erect a statue to Nicomachus Flavianus, honoring his many distinguished offices and virtues.

EDCS-17200068.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Marcus Junius ؟Priscillianus Maximus, most illustrious man, chief augur, quaestor designate, urban praetor, pontifex maximus, elected pontifex of the god Sol for the legation of the province of Asia, patron, and curator of the Laurentes Lavinates, the priesthood and the people [decreed this].
EDCS-17200068.summary: A dedication to Marcus Junius Priscillianus Maximus, honoring his numerous high-ranking religious and administrative offices.

EDCS-17200071.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Septimius Agrippinus, a most accomplished man, grandson of Lucius Septimius Antonius Agathonicus, a most accomplished man, son of Lucius Septimius Agathonicus, an excellent man, who held the position of 'a rationibus hereditatium' [in charge of inheritance accounts], made this memorial in my lifetime for myself and for my freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, along with the place which is behind the tomb, within its boundaries, together with the cottage and building situated above it; they will belong for the sake of sustenance to the keeper of the place.
EDCS-17200071.summary: A self-funded funerary monument built by Lucius Septimius Agrippinus for himself, his descendants, and his freedmen, specifying its contents and purpose.

EDCS-17200074.translation: Marcus Domitius Polygnos made this, weighing one and a half pounds.
EDCS-17200074.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Marcus Domitius Polygnos, likely related to a weight or measure.

EDCS-17300666.translation: Manius Rustius, son of Marcus, grandson of Manius, as duumvir, dedicates this to Mercury.
EDCS-17300666.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Manius Rustius, who held the office of duumvir, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-17400041.translation: To Julia Augusta, mother of the camps, mother of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Fortissimus Felix, father of the country, and mother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, and of the Senate and the Fatherland, [and to the] most noble Caesar [Geta], the Laurentes Lavinates made this.
EDCS-17400041.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the Laurentes Lavinates to Julia Domna, mother of Emperor Caracalla and Geta, honoring her titles and status, likely from the Severan period.

EDCS-17500069.translation: Fabius Titianus, a most distinguished man, member of the fifteen-man board for sacred rites, ordinary consul for the second time, prefect of the city, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17500069.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Fabius Titianus, who held significant high offices including ordinary consul and prefect of the city, dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-17500179.translation: Lucius Sempronius Proculus, a veteran of the Praetorian fleet, served for 26 years; for himself, his wife, his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-17500179.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Sempronius Proculus, a veteran of the Misenum fleet, who served for 26 years and made provision for his family and descendants, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17500187.translation: Caius Spedius Pidinus, soldier from the liburna Iustitia, served 33 years. [He served] from the liburna Fides. His heir Cassius [erected this].
EDCS-17500187.summary: This inscription records the military service of Caius Spedius Pidinus, a soldier who served on two different liburnae for 33 years, with his heir Cassius erecting the monument, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-17500215.translation: Valeria Mamia made this for her husband Caius Gellius Priscus, a deserving veteran, and for herself, her freedmen, their descendants, and their successors; this monument does not pass to the heir.
EDCS-17500215.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Valeria Mamia for her husband Caius Gellius Priscus, a veteran, and for herself and their descendants, with a clause preventing it from passing to an heir, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17500239.translation: Quintus Tineius Rufus, a patrician, [restored?] to Apollo Cumano.
EDCS-17500239.summary: This inscription records a dedication or restoration made by Quintus Tineius Rufus, a patrician, to Apollo Cumano, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-17500240.translation: Caius Pomponius Zoticus gave as a gift to the Apollinar College.
EDCS-17500240.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Caius Pomponius Zoticus to the Apollinar College, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-17500241.translation: Gnaeus Lucceius the father and son, [as praetor?] restored the temple of Demeter. Lucceia Polla, daughter of Gnaeus, and Lucceia Tertulla Pia, daughter of Gallus, restored the temple of Demeter and what is around that temple and the portico with their own money.
EDCS-17500241.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the temple of Demeter, its surroundings, and a portico, funded by Gnaeus Lucceius (father and son) and Lucceia Polla and Lucceia Tertulla Pia, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-17500243.translation: Gnaeus Lucceius Gemellus, son of Gnaeus, and brother.
EDCS-17500243.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Lucceius Gemellus, identified as a brother.

EDCS-17500246.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Lucceius, likely a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-17500247.translation: To the Lares of Augustus by Agrippa.
EDCS-17500247.summary: This is a dedication to the Lares Augusti, likely made by Agrippa.

EDCS-17500248.summary: This inscription refers to the authority of Agrippa, possibly in a legal or administrative context.

EDCS-17500258.translation: dendrophori, with whom it is permitted by decree of the Senate to associate: Varius Phillius, Vinnius Florus, Nulanius Herma, Mevius Heraclida, Agrius Successus, Seius Euhodus, Eridius Rufus, Marius Lupus, Avienus Quarte[---], Iulius [---], Lucceius Victor, Porphirius Varus, Lucceius Aemilian[---], Lucceius Felix, Vinnius Ianuar[ius], Iulius Rufinus, Claudius Cornelius, Mammius Eucratus, Mammius Eucratianus.
EDCS-17500258.summary: This is a list of dendrophori (tree-bearers), likely from a guild or religious association, permitted by senatorial decree, with a list of members and a possible mention of a funerary plot.

EDCS-17500260.translation: [---] a statue was erected for this service and(?), by decree of the decurions, a chariot in the forum [---] and a burial place was granted publicly by decree of the decurions, and to Antonia [---] her family and to Octavia Valen[---] Quintus Octavius, son of Marcus, of the Palatine tribe, [---] of the province of Dalmatia, most dutiful [---]
EDCS-17500260.summary: This inscription records the public granting of a statue, a chariot in the forum, and a burial place by the decurions, with dedications to Antonia and Octavia, and a mention of Quintus Octavius from Dalmatia.

EDCS-17500272.translation: Images were moved from hidden places to the prominence of the Severian Baths; Audentius Aemilanus, a most distinguished man and consul of Campania, arranged for them to be dedicated and ordered them to be dedicated, under the supervision of Tannonius Chrysantius, a most excellent man.
EDCS-17500272.summary: This inscription records the relocation and dedication of images to the Severian Baths by Audentius Aemilanus, governor of Campania, with Tannonius Chrysantius overseeing the work.

EDCS-17500274.translation: [To Lucius Aelius Aug(ustus)' freedman?], Aurel[ius] Apolaustus, twice crowned hieronikos and parasitos of all, and chief priest of Apollo at Capua. [---]
EDCS-17500274.summary: This is a dedication to Aurelius Apolaustus, a freedman of Lucius Aelius, who held multiple honorary titles including hieronikos and chief priest of Apollo at Capua.

EDCS-17500277.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Cassia, daughter of Caius Spenius, Caius Cassius Alexander and Claudia Pronua, parents, for their most sweet daughter. She lived 19 years, 11 months, 4 days.
EDCS-17500277.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cassia, daughter of Caius Spenius, set up by her parents, recording her age at death.

EDCS-17500278.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Cossinia Asies, Cossinius Hesperus the elder, her husband, with whom she lived from her maidenhood to the end of her life. She died at the age of 36 years.
EDCS-17500278.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cossinia Asies, set up by her husband Cossinius Hesperus the elder, recording their marital duration and her age at death.

EDCS-17500279.translation: Aulus Titinius Castus, freedman of Aulus Titinius, was made by Titinia Ivena, freedwoman of Aulus Titinius.
EDCS-17500279.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by a freedwoman for her freedman husband, likely dating to the 1st century BCE - 1st century CE.

EDCS-17500289.summary: This inscription likely refers to a dedication made during the reign of Emperor Vespasian (69-79 CE).

EDCS-17500291.translation: Gaius Sempronius, son of Tiberius; Appius Claudius, son of Gaius; Publius Licinius, son of Publius: tresviri (moneyers).
EDCS-17500291.summary: This inscription lists three individuals who held the office of tresviri, likely responsible for minting coins, probably in the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-17500294.translation: To Gaius Nummius Constans, son of Gaius, of the Falernian tribe, former centurion of the II Traiana legion, centurion of the II legion III Cyrenaicae, and evocatus in the forum by the officials of the III Praetorian and X Urban cohorts, honored with gifts by Emperor Trajan with necklaces, armbands, and phalerae for the Parthian war, and also by Emperor Hadrian with a golden crown, necklaces, armbands, and phalerae for the Jewish war; his heirs according to his will.
EDCS-17500294.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the heirs of Gaius Nummius Constans, a distinguished soldier who served in multiple legions and received honors from Emperors Trajan and Hadrian for military achievements, likely dating to the early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17500295.translation: Marcus Verrius Abascantus, freedman of Marcus, for his sons Marcus Verrius Celsus, centurion of the III Cyrenaicae legion, and Marcus Verrius Flaccus, and for his associate Marcus Verrius Primigenius, and for his wives Plinia Cykladis, Marcus Plinius Faustus, Marcus Verrius Anthus, and for his wife Plinia Ingenuva, and for his freedwoman Verria Hygeia the younger, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-17500295.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Verrius Abascantus for his sons, associates, wives, and freedmen, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE, given the military context.

EDCS-17500296.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Publius Acilius Vernarius, incomparable son of the II decury of Puteoli, who lived 28 years, 9 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-17500296.summary: This is a tombstone for a young man named Publius Acilius Vernarius, who was a member of the II decury in Puteoli, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-17500302.summary: This is a dedication to a woman named Aufustia Carmei, its purpose and date are unclear without further context.

EDCS-17600016.translation: To our lord, the most unconquered and most excellent Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, most holy, pious, happy, Augustus, greatest victor of Parthia, greatest victor of Britain, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 16th time, emperor for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, proconsul, father of the country, by the Laurentes Lavinates.
EDCS-17600016.summary: This is a monumental inscription dedicating honors to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, reflecting his numerous titles and victories, and showing his association with the Laurentes Lavinates, likely dating to between 175-176 CE.

EDCS-17600192.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying an individual, Lucius Tettius, possibly with a connection to Samos, its context and date are unknown.

EDCS-17600193.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying an individual, Lucius Noni Florus, its context and date are unknown.

EDCS-17600367.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors Theodosius and Arcadius, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-17700004.translation: To Lucius Curredius Modestus, son of Lucius, of the Falernian tribe, and to Curredia Helena, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius? Curred[ius ---] / Valeriae [---] / Varredius, freedman of Lucius [---] / and his family. / To Publius? Arrun[tius? ---] / and to Gaius Buccioni Ap[---], freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-17700004.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for several individuals, including members of the Curredius family and others, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700014.translation: Aparen, daughter of Aulus, virgin, aged thirteen years, her bones are placed here. [---] a distance of X Roman miles. She was buried by [---].
EDCS-17700014.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young virgin named Aparen, recording her age and burial details, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700017.translation: To Gaius Fuficius, son of Gaius, of the Falernian tribe, Fangonius, an honest man, as aedile, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-17700017.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Fuficius, who served as an aedile, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700032.translation: Gnaeus Minatius, freedman of Gnaeus, and Publius Pomponius, freedman of Marcus, carried out the duties of magistrates of the guild of merchants, under the consulship of Calpurnius.
EDCS-17700032.summary: This inscription records the completion of public works by magistrates of the merchants' guild, mentioning Gnaeus Minatius and Publius Pomponius, and dating to the Calpurnii consulship.

EDCS-17700033.translation: ---, freedman of Publius Pilomusus, freedman of Sergius, and Decumius, freedman of Marcus, and Hordionius, freedman of Gaius Lucius, [built/restored] the wall and four pillars, under the consulship of Calpurnius.
EDCS-17700033.summary: This inscription details the construction or repair of a wall and pillars by several freedmen, including Pilomusus and Hordionius, dating to the Calpurnii consulship.

EDCS-17700034.translation: Vivus made [it]. Cornelius, son of Lucius, a leatherworker. Nerius, son of Marcus. Offelius, son of Marcus, a shield-maker. Gaius Maius, son of Numerius. Marcus Vibius, son of Marcus, a handler of rough materials. Lucius Pomponius, son of Lucius. Lucius Olienus, son of Lucius. Under these magistrates, they undertook to have the wall built for Spei, Fidei, and Fortunae, under the consulship of Marcus Minucius and Spurius Postumius.
EDCS-17700034.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall dedicated to Spei, Fidei, and Fortunae by several craftsmen and individuals, under the magistracy of Vivus and the consulship of Marcus Minucius and Spurius Postumius.

EDCS-17700035.translation: Numerius Pumidius, son of Quintus. Marcus Cottius, son of Marcus. Marcus Eppilius, son of Marcus. Gaius Antracius, son of Gaius. Lucius Sempronius, son of Lucius. Publius Cicereius, son of Gaius. Marcus Raecius, son of Quintus. Numerius Arrius, son of Marcus. Lucius Heioleius, son of Publius. Gaius Tuccius, son of Gaius. Quintus Vibius, son of Marcus. Marcus Valerius, son of Lucius. Under these magistrates, Venerus and Iovia undertook to have the wall built, 270 feet, and they made the games, under the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius.
EDCS-17700035.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall and the funding of games by several individuals, including numerus Pumidius and Marcus Cottius, under the magistracy of Venerus and Iovia, and the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-17700037.translation: Titus Iunius, son of Numerius. Gaius Numoleius, son of Gnaeus. Marcus Fisius, son of Marcus. Marcus Fufius, son of Lucius. Gaius Tittius, son of Gaius. Quintus Monnius, son of Numerius. Decimus Roscius, freedman of Quintus. Decimus Iteius, freedman of Gnaeus. Marcus Valerius, freedman of Marcus. Quintus Fulvius, freedman of Fulvia. Publius Pactumeius, freedman of Gaius. Lucius Pomponius, freedman of Gaius. Under these magistrates, they undertook to have the wall and a barrier made for Castor and Pollux, and they also made the games, under the consulship of Quintus Servilius and Gaius Atilius.
EDCS-17700037.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall and barrier dedicated to Castor and Pollux, along with the funding of games, by various individuals including Titus Iunius and Gaius Numoleius, under the consulship of Quintus Servilius and Gaius Atilius.

EDCS-17700038.translation: Servius Suetius, freedman of Servius, a bathhouse keeper. Publius Babrius, freedman of Lucius. Marcus Sextius, freedman of Numerius. Marcus Sextius, freedman of Marcus. Lucius Hordionius, freedman of Lucius Labeo. Gaius Lucretius Apulus. Aulus Gargonius, freedman of Quintus. Babrius, freedman of Lucius. Publius Servilius, freedman of Marcus. Gnaeus Octavius, freedman of Numerius, a cloth merchant. Marcus Ocratius, freedman of Marcus, a baker. Publius Statius, freedman of Publius. Marcus Maius, freedman of Marcus. Nic[---]. Under these magistrates, they undertook to have the wall, eighty feet long and twenty-one feet high, and a barrier made, and they also made the games, under the consulship of Gaius Atilius and Quintus Servilius.
EDCS-17700038.summary: This inscription details the construction of a wall and barrier, along with the funding of games, by numerous individuals including bathhouse keepers, merchants, and bakers, under the consulship of Gaius Atilius and Quintus Servilius.

EDCS-17700039.translation: Lucius Annius, son of Lucius, Hortionius, son of Gnaeus, Egnatius, son of Publius, gladiators; Cnaeus, son of Gnaeus, Egnatius, son of Marcus; Aulus Seppius, son of Aulus; Caius Pompilius, son of Caius; Numerius Rubrius, son of Marcus; Gnaeus Hortionius, son of Gnaeus; Lucius Annius, son of Lucius, a craftsman; Caius Obinius, son of Gnaeus, a butcher. Under these magistrates, Caius Flavius, son of Caius, and Caius Marius, son of Caius, consuls, they took care of the construction of a wall and a parapet 22 feet long and 22 feet high.
EDCS-17700039.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall and parapet by a group of individuals, including gladiators and a butcher, under the consulship of Caius Flavius and Caius Marius.

EDCS-17700041.translation: Marcus, son of Numerius, a craftsman; Marcus Fisius, son of Statius; Marcus Fisius, son of Caius; Marcus Baibilius, son of Lucius; Marcus Vivius, son of Publius; Tiberius Hostius. Under these magistrates, they took care of the construction of two wedges in the theatre.
EDCS-17700041.summary: This inscription records the construction of two wedges in the theatre by a group of individuals, including craftsmen, under certain magistrates.

EDCS-17700042.translation: Alfidius, son of Caius, called Strabo; Marcus Pandius, son of Marcus; Publius Octavius, son of Publius; Caius Cornelius, son of Caius, called Sap; Cnaeus, son of Gnaeus; Marcus Cloelius, son of Caius; Marcus Heidius, son of Marcus; Lucius Decumius, son of Numerius, called Stabilio; Marcus Pontius, freedman of Marcus, called Salvius; Aulus Ocratius, freedman of Marcus, called Alexander; Caius Hostius, freedman of Marcus, called Hermia; Aulus Rubrius, son of Aulus, a herald.
