Under these magistrates, they transferred into the service of Juno Gaura according to the decree of the pagus, a wall.
EDCS-17700042.summary: This inscription records the transfer of a wall into the service of Juno Gaura by various individuals, including a herald, under the consulship of Publius Cornelius Lentulus and Gnaeus Aufidius Oreste.

EDCS-17700043.translation: S., son of Lucius; Lucius, son of Lucius, called Irudiei; Titus Magius, son of Gnaeus; Marcus Ragonius, son of Marcus; Marcus Lollius, son of Marcus; Ale Marcus Grusius, son of Marcus; Magius Cn CI Magius.
EDCS-17700043.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly indicating individuals involved in some undertaking or as part of a larger monument, with no clear context for dating or purpose.

EDCS-17700044.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Marcus Blossius, freedman of Marcus, called Agato; Marcus Consius, freedman of Marcus, called Nicolavos; Sextus Allius, freedman of Quintus, called Sextus Marcus; Atilius, freedman of Marcus, called Apol; Aulus Nasennius, freedman of Aulus, called Port; Lucius Furrius, freedman of Lucius, called Dionysius; Marcus Limbricius, freedman of Marcus, called Diodorus; Caius Tiburtius, freedman of Caius, called Flaccus; Lucius Turius; Lucius, freedman of Caius Publius, called Sand; Aulus Pactumeius, freedman of Aulus, called Philippus; Publius Octavius, freedman of Publius, called Antiocus. Let no one deface this altar.
EDCS-17700044.summary: This inscription, dedicated to Jupiter, lists numerous freedmen and their patrons, and prohibits the defacement of the altar.

EDCS-17700045.translation: Under Drusus Caesar and Caius Norbanus, consuls. To Jupiter Liber. Gnaeus Betutius Primus, Quintus Titinius Felix, Lucius Mamius Secundinus, Lucius Clodius Salvillus, Marcus Baebianus Iucundus, Titus Statius Philodamus, magistrates, at their own expense.
EDCS-17700045.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Liber made at the expense of several magistrates during the consulship of Drusus Caesar and Caius Norbanus.

EDCS-17700046.translation: Dedication of the temple, 3rd day before the Nones of November. Gnaeus Calavius, son of Marcus; Gnaeus Papius, son of Gnaeus; Caius Pomponius, son of Caius; Quintus Numesius, son of Quintus; Caius Carponius, son of Numerius; Aulus Fabius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-17700046.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple on November 3rd and lists several individuals, possibly magistrates or donors.

EDCS-17700048.translation: With these attendants, they took care to have the Lares made: Caius Terentius, freedman of Caius, called Philomusus; Philemo, slave of Aulus Helvius; Helenus, slave of Quintus Hostius; Philotaerus, slave of Terentius; Lucius, slave of Terentius; Philotaerus, slave of Hostius; Philomusus, slave of Sextus; Philemo, slave of Balon; Dipilus, slave of Balonia; Alexander, slave of Marcus Suetius; Nestor, slave of Nae; Flaccus, slave of Nicephor. And they took care to have these weights and this pavement made, under Quintus Caecilius, son of Quintus, grandson of Quintus, and Titus Deidius, son of Titus, consuls.
EDCS-17700048.summary: This inscription records the construction of weights and a pavement for the Lares by various slaves and freedmen, under the consulship of Quintus Caecilius and Titus Deidius.

EDCS-17700050.translation: Hilarus, son of Malchio, with Callicus, under these magistrates...
EDCS-17700050.summary: This is a fragmented inscription listing names and mentioning magistrates, likely recording a dedication or construction project, but the text is too incomplete to determine the exact purpose or date.

EDCS-17700053.translation: Lucius Naevius, son of Lucius, called Gratus, sacred to Diana.
EDCS-17700053.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Diana by Lucius Naevius Gratus.

EDCS-17700056.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication to Hercules, likely from a monument, with a patronymic and the name Herco, possibly a praenomen or cognomen.

EDCS-17700057.translation: Spurius Suetrius, son of Spurius, gives this gift to Hercules.
EDCS-17700057.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Hercules by Spurius Suetrius, son of Spurius.

EDCS-17700663.summary: This is an inscription identifying the owner or name of a workshop, likely an artisan's or manufacturing establishment.

EDCS-17700664.summary: This is an ownership or dedication inscription, possibly relating to a tomb or a commissioned work, belonging to Caius Licinius Donacis.

EDCS-17700788.translation: Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, chief priest, in his ninth year of tribunician power, acclaimed imperator XI times, consul II, father of the fatherland designated for the third time, proconsul, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, in his fourth year of tribunician power, designated consul, proconsul, and Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, restored the wall that had collapsed from age for the defense of the road.
EDCS-17700788.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a defensive wall by the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, likely dating to the period when Caracalla and Geta held the title of Caesar.

EDCS-17800034.translation: The Pagus Herculaneus decided on the 10th day before the Terminalia festival, that the college or magistrates of Iovei Campagei should spend money on repairing the portico of the pagus, according to the pagus law, by the arbitration of Gnaeus Laetorius, son of Gnaeus, the pagus magistrate, and that the college or magistrates of Iovei Compagei should have a place in the theatre as if they had put on games, in the consulship of Lucius Aufustius, freedman of Lucius Strato, Gaius Antonius, freedman of Marcus Nico, Gnaeus Avius, freedman of Gnaeus Agathocles, Gaius Blossius, freedman of Marcus Protemus, Marcus Ramnius, freedman of Publius Diophantus, Titus Sulpicius, freedman of Publius Quinti pupilli Quintus Protemus, Marcus Paccius, freedman of Marcus Philemo, Marcus Licculeius, freedman of Marcus Philinus, Gnaeus Hordeonius, freedman of Gnaeus Euphemio, Aulus Pollius, freedman of Publius Alexander, Numerius Munnius, freedman of Numerius Antiocus, Gaius Coelius, son of Gaius Caldus, Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, son of Gnaeus, consuls.
EDCS-17800034.summary: This inscription details a decision by the Pagus Herculaneus concerning the repair of a public portico and the allocation of space in a theatre, involving various magistrates and listing several prominent citizens and their freedmen, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE based on the consuls mentioned.

EDCS-17800413.translation: Under the administration of Romanus, junior priest: the ferial sacrifices for the lords on the 3rd of the Nones of January; the votive offerings on the 3rd of the Ides of February; the Genialia on the Kalends of May; the purification at the river Casilino on the 3rd of the Ides of May; the rose offerings at the amphitheatre on the 8th of the Kalends of August; the purification at the river on the 6th of the Kalends of August; the procession to the road of Diana on the Ides of October; the vintage at Acerusa by order of the lords. Felix has diligently fulfilled his vow on the 10th of the Kalends of December, during the reign of Valentinian III and Eutropius.
EDCS-17800413.summary: This inscription records a detailed calendar of religious ceremonies, sacrifices, and public events held under the supervision of a priest named Romanus, and later mentions Felix fulfilling a vow during the consulship of Valentinian III and Eutropius, dating it to 440 CE.

EDCS-17800414.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Marcus Ennius Utilis [dedicated this].
EDCS-17800414.summary: This is a simple dedication to Jupiter by Marcus Ennius Utilis, likely from a small altar or shrine.

EDCS-17800422.translation: Titus Flavius Onesimus gave this gift to the Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-17800422.summary: This is a votive offering to the Mother of the Gods by Titus Flavius Onesimus.

EDCS-17800428.translation: Sacred to Pluto. The bones of Caius Laetorius Rufus are placed here. Tullia and [his] mother made [this]. Of Caius Laetorius Rufus, son of Caius.
EDCS-17800428.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Caius Laetorius Rufus, with his bones interred here by his wife Tullia and mother, and it includes his full name and patronymic.

EDCS-17800430.translation: Quarta Confleia, freedwoman of Marcus, fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-17800430.summary: This inscription records a freedwoman, Quarta Confleia, fulfilling a vow, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-17800431.translation: Sequnda Solania, daughter of Lucius, dedicates this.
EDCS-17800431.summary: This is a dedication by Sequnda Solania, daughter of Lucius, on an unspecified monument.

EDCS-17800433.summary: This inscription indicates that Crescens fulfilled a vow, likely on a votive monument.

EDCS-17800437.translation: I vow you, Cnaeus Numidius Astragalus, your life, health, livelihood, and that you be consumed by disease; and I entrust Caius Sextius to be consumed.
EDCS-17800437.summary: This is a complex personal vow, possibly imprecatory, for the well-being of Cnaeus Numidius Astragalus and the suffering of Caius Sextius, inscribed on a private object.

EDCS-17800442.translation: Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 10th time, imperator for the 18th time, consul for the 8th time, censor.
EDCS-17800442.summary: This is a formal inscription recording the titles and powers of Emperor Vespasian, likely on a public building or monument.

EDCS-17800446.translation: The people of Sinuessa gave this gift to Matidia, daughter of Augustus, sister of the divine Sabina, aunt of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-17800446.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the people of Sinuessa to Matidia, a prominent imperial woman, likely on a statue or public offering.

EDCS-17800449.translation: [To Cornelia Salonia] Augusta, wife of our lord Emperor Gallienus Augustus.
EDCS-17800449.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Cornelia Salonia, wife of Emperor Gallienus, likely on a monument or statue in her honor.

EDCS-17900552.translation: Anius the Bastius, freedman of August, for his proconsul of Campania.
EDCS-17900552.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Anius the Bastius, a freedman, to his patron, the proconsul of Campania.

EDCS-17900553.translation: The council and people of Sinuessa decreed a statue for Gaius Appius Eunomius Sapidianus, clarissimus vir, quaestor candidate, city praetor, amplifier of the fatherland, restorer of citizens, their most outstanding patron.
EDCS-17900553.summary: This inscription records the Sinuessan civic authorities decreeing a statue for Gaius Appius Eunomius Sapidianus, a distinguished official, likely on the base of the statue itself.

EDCS-17900554.translation: To Marcus [---], son of Marcus [---], grandson of Marcus [---], great-grandson of Marcus [---], of the Falernian [tribe?], Vicirius [---], Marcus Vicirius [---], clarissimus vir, to his brother [---]
EDCS-17900554.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a member of the Vicirius family, likely from Marcus Vicirius to his brother, with significant lacunae.

EDCS-17900555.translation: The council and people of Hadrumetum, with Flavius Sergius Codeus, a most perfect official designated for the province, overseeing in his private capacity, had this erected in honour of Argentius Brittius Praetextatus, a most illustrious man, curator of Capua, quinquennial consul, and count of the first rank.
EDCS-17900555.summary: This is a dedication by the city of Hadrumetum to Argentius Brittius Praetextatus, a high-ranking official, honouring his service.

EDCS-17900556.translation: To Marcus Campanio Marcello, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, procurator of the Augusti at Mercurium in Alexandria, procurator of the province of Cyprus, prefect of cavalry of the Parthian ala, tribune of the first cohort of Hemesenorum, prefect of the third cohort of Breucorum, Roman citizens in the province of Cyprus.
EDCS-17900556.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Campanio Marcello, listing his extensive military and administrative career in various Roman provinces.

EDCS-17900557.translation: Given by decree of the decurions to Claudius Tiberius, augur, our patron.
EDCS-17900557.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by decree of the local council to Claudius Tiberius, an augur and patron.

EDCS-17900559.translation: To Lucius Tiberius Claudius Aurelius Quintianus, by the tribe Quirina, former moneyer triumvir for striking bronze, silver, and gold, quaestor elect, praetor, consul, and pontifex. Tiberius Claudius Felix, the IIvir, dedicated this place to his incomparable friend by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17900559.summary: This is a dedication by a local official to Lucius Tiberius Claudius Aurelius Quintianus, a prominent figure who held multiple high offices, honouring him as a friend.

EDCS-17900566.translation: To Iulius Aur(elius) Auxontus Leonidas, a most illustrious man, curator of the Capuans for his many outstanding merits towards citizens and homeland and his honourable standing, founder of new and restorer of public works, patron from the origin, most worthy of all praise, from the Regio Compiti.
EDCS-17900566.summary: This is a dedication by the Regio Compiti to Iulius Aur(elius) Auxontus Leonidas, honouring him for his public service and patronage.

EDCS-17900567.translation: Valerius Lupus, a most illustrious man, consular governor of Campania, had this made.
EDCS-17900567.summary: This is a record of a construction or dedication carried out by Valerius Lupus, a former governor of Campania.

EDCS-17900569.translation: The original council of Capua has erected this as a token of their vow and obedience to Postumius Lampadius, a most illustrious and distinguished consular governor of Campania, restorer of the homeland and renewer of public works, provider for the order, and succourer of the people, for his universal and outstanding merits, our patron.
EDCS-17900569.summary: This is a dedication by the council of Capua to Postumius Lampadius, honouring him as a restorer of public works and a benefactor of the city.

EDCS-17900570.translation: Gaius Sempronius Tiberi son Gracchus, Appius Claudius Cai son Polcer, Publius Licinius Publi son Crassus, the three men responsible for judging and assigning lands, [placed this at] Kitra, the eleventh decumanus to the left.
EDCS-17900570.summary: This inscription records the names of three officials responsible for land distribution, possibly marking a boundary or a relevant location.

EDCS-17900571.translation: To Turcia Marcella, a most distinguished woman, daughter and wife of a consular governor of Campania, and to Tussius, a decurion.
EDCS-17900571.summary: This is a dedication to Turcia Marcella and Tussius, a decurion, likely related by marriage and status to a consular governor of Campania.

EDCS-17900575.translation: Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a most illustrious man, consular governor of Campania, had this made.
EDCS-17900575.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication carried out by Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a former governor of Campania.

EDCS-17900576.translation: Concordia Iulia Valeria Felix dedicated and consecrated this, with Capua through Virius Gallus, a most distinguished man, corrector of Campania.
EDCS-17900576.summary: This inscription records the consecration and dedication of something by Concordia Iulia Valeria Felix, facilitated by Virius Gallus, corrector of Campania, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-17900577.translation: By his virtue, wisdom, and genius, Pollens Virius Turbo, a most distinguished man and consular of Campania.
EDCS-17900577.summary: This inscription honors Pollens Virius Turbo, a distinguished consular official of Campania, highlighting his exceptional qualities, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-17900587.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Saturninus and Tarentinus made this for Rufianus, their freedman, a librarian of the records office of the imperial tabularium, a well-deserving freedman.
EDCS-17900587.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Saturninus and Tarentinus to their deserving freedman Rufianus, who served as a librarian in an imperial administrative office, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-17900601.translation: Lucius Hellas of the Falernian tribe, of the VI Legion.
EDCS-17900601.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Hellas, a soldier belonging to the VI Legion and from the Falernian tribe, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000290.translation: To Publius Aelius Philologus, son of Publius, an Augustalis decurion of Capua, honored with a decision of the duovirs. Aelia Aphrodisia, his mother, made this for him and herself.
EDCS-18000290.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aelia Aphrodisia for her son Publius Aelius Philologus, a local magistrate in Capua, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000292.translation: Quintus Alfius Iustus, son of Quintus, of the Falernian tribe, scribe and duovir and quaestor of Capua, made this for himself while alive, at 55 years of age, and [for...].
EDCS-18000292.summary: This is a self-made funerary monument by Quintus Alfius Iustus, a local magistrate and scribe in Capua, who commissioned it during his lifetime at the age of 55, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000297.translation: Herennia, daughter of Marcus, priestess, consecrated to Ceres. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-18000297.summary: This inscription records the consecration of Herennia, a priestess of Ceres, with the burial plot granted by local decree, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000300.translation: To Lucius Mettius Dama, son of Gnaeus. Lucius Mettius, son of Lucius, duovir and aedile, for his father.
EDCS-18000300.summary: This monument was erected by Lucius Mettius, a duovir and aedile, for his father Lucius Mettius Dama, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000302.translation: To Publius Pescennius Secundus, son of Publius, a IIvir for dispensing justice, for recovering the Lucanian territory without expense to the state, by decree of the senate.
EDCS-18000302.summary: This inscription honors Publius Pescennius Secundus, a magistrate in Capua, for successfully reclaiming land for the state without cost, a feat recognized by a senatorial decree, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000303.translation: To Quintus Petticius, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, master of the shrine of Diana, according to the will of Quintus Petticius, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe. // To Lucius Petticius, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, his brother.
EDCS-18000303.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine to Diana by Quintus Petticius, funded by the will of his deceased brother Lucius Petticius, both from the Falernian tribe, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18000305.translation: To Tettia Prisca, daughter of Caius, priestess of the public divinity of Capua, elected by the most splendid order by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-18000305.summary: This inscription honors Tettia Prisca, a priestess of Capua, elected by the decurions, likely on a public monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000306.translation: Quartus Falernus, aedile, son of Lucius Falernus.
EDCS-18000306.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records Quartus Falernus, an aedile, and his father Lucius Falernus, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period in Campania.

EDCS-18000307.translation: Satellia Anus, daughter of Marcus, restored the apodyterium (changing room) to its former condition and decorated it with other marble elements, including epistyles.
EDCS-18000307.summary: This inscription records Satellia Anus, daughter of Marcus, restoring and decorating a public changing room (apodyterium) with marble, likely from a bath complex in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000309.translation: To Gaius Velleius Urbanus, son of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, magistrate of the shrine of Diana Tifatina, honored with the public equestrian rank by the Emperor Antoninus Augustus, when he was 5 years old. Gaius Velleius Urbanus and Tullia Nice, his parents, (this place was) given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-18000309.summary: This inscription honors the young Gaius Velleius Urbanus, son of Gaius, magistrate of the shrine of Diana Tifatina and recipient of equestrian rank, dedicated by his parents with a place granted by the decurions, likely dating to the Antonine period.

EDCS-18000311.translation: Titia Curia, daughter of Marcus, priestess, had this made at her own expense. Cerialis Mundalis.
EDCS-18000311.summary: This inscription records Titia Curia, daughter of Marcus and priestess, who financed the construction or dedication of this item, likely a religious or public monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000328.translation: To Marcus Allius Blastus, freedman of Marcus, Augustalis of Capua, and to his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants: fifty feet in every direction are ceded from the land for this monument.
EDCS-18000328.summary: This inscription dedicates a burial plot or monument in Capua to Marcus Allius Blastus, an Augustalis, and his descendants, specifying land allocation for the monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000330.translation: and to Marcus Carmeius Galatea(?), Augustalis of Capua.
EDCS-18000330.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records an offering or dedication to Marcus Carmeius Galatea, an Augustalis of Capua, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000348.translation: Cornelia, his sister, made this for Quintus Cornelius Rufus, son of Publius, of the vestiary guild, at her own expense.
EDCS-18000348.summary: This inscription records Cornelia commissioning a monument for her brother, Quintus Cornelius Rufus, who was associated with the vestiary guild, likely from a Roman provincial city in the Imperial period.

EDCS-18000353.translation: Marcus Fulvius Apollonius, perfumer, for himself and Valeria Rhodia, his wife, Fulvia Laina, Lucius Cassius Glyco, freedman of Lucius, Nardini.
EDCS-18000353.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Marcus Fulvius Apollonius, a perfumer, for himself and his family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000354.translation: He lived a modest, chaste life, always fair, from Aurunca, named Furius, a schoolmaster, with the utmost chastity towards his students, who also wrote testaments faithfully and never denied anyone or harmed anyone. Thus he ran his life, faithful without fear. His bones are now placed here, set by the centuries.
EDCS-18000354.summary: This epitaph praises Furius Philocalus, a schoolmaster from Aurunca, for his virtuous and just life, noting his faithful writing of testaments and his death, with his remains interred by his community or a group referred to as 'centuries', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000357.translation: To Maria, wife of Suavius, and Peregrina, freedwoman of Suavius, midwife.
EDCS-18000357.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Maria and Peregrina, a midwife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000359.translation: Lucius Novius Lucrio to his patron and to himself.
EDCS-18000359.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording Lucius Novius Lucrio, an unguentarius (perfumer or oil seller), dedicating a tomb for his patron and himself.

EDCS-18000362.translation: The bones of Quinti Pacci Philogeni, freedman of Quintus Paccius, a money-changer, are placed here; CIIIA ACD made it.
EDCS-18000362.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the remains of Quinti Pacci Philogeni, a freedman money-changer, are buried here and attributing the construction to 'CIIIA ACD'.

EDCS-18000363.translation: Publilia, freedwoman of Sextus, to her patron Sextus Publilius Trupho, freedman of Sextus. To Lucius Titius Optatus, goldsmith.
EDCS-18000363.summary: This inscription records dedications on a funerary monument to Sextus Publilius Trupho, patron of Publilia, and to Lucius Titius Optatus, a goldsmith.

EDCS-18000366.translation: Felix, freedman of Marci Sexti Diogenis, a sandal-maker.
EDCS-18000366.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Felix, a freedman of Marci Sexti Diogenis, who worked as a sandal-maker.

EDCS-18000367.translation: To Marcus Stat[---]amo, freedman of Marcus, an oil seller. Philoxenes and Hilario, freedmen. To Hilara, fellow freedwoman. [---]
EDCS-18000367.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary monument dedicated to Marcus Stat[---]amo, an oil seller, and possibly other individuals including freedmen and a freedwoman.

EDCS-18000368.summary: This very fragmentary inscription seems to refer to Sulpicii M, possibly a freedman ('proc' might relate to procurator or a similar office or relationship), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-18000371.translation: Quintus Tullius Paapus, a swordsman. Clodia, daughter of Diamer[---]. To Teophilus, son of Terentius.
EDCS-18000371.summary: This inscription records three individuals: Quintus Tullius Paapus (a swordsman), Clodia (daughter of Diamer[---]), and Teophilus (son of Terentius), possibly related to funerary dedications.

EDCS-18000374.translation: Publius Umeius's cart driver, Odote, his concubine.
EDCS-18000374.summary: This inscription records Odote, the concubine of Publius Umeius, who was a 'plostrarius' (cart or wagon driver).

EDCS-18000375.translation: Acilia Optata, freedwoman of Aulus, made [this] for her parents. [---]lius Orestes [and] Acilia Euthy[---]
EDCS-18000375.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Acilia Optata, freedwoman of Aulus, for her parents, with partial names of others who may be involved in the monument.

EDCS-18000379.translation: To Lucius Alacrius Dasius, to his Primigenia.
EDCS-18000379.summary: This is an epitaph dedicated by Lucius Alacrius Dasius to his Primigenia, likely a freedwoman or daughter.

EDCS-18000381.translation: Tiberius Albius, son of Lucius, grandson of Quintus, [---].
EDCS-18000381.summary: This inscription records the name and lineage of Tiberius Albius, with a lacuna indicating missing information.

EDCS-18000382.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for Alexsa, identified as a fellow freedwoman.

EDCS-18000384.translation: Lucius Alfius Delphio, freedman of Lucius, patron. Lucius Alfius Antiochus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Alfius Flaccus, freedman of Lucius. Delphio, son of Lucius' freedman. Auge, freedwoman of the Lucii. Cleopatra, freedwoman of Quintus and Alfia, by the will of Lucius Alfius Antiochus, under the supervision of Flaccus, a freedman. Marcus Vigellius Lycoraeus.
EDCS-18000384.summary: This complex inscription details the freeing of slaves and the establishment of a patron-client relationship within the Alfii family, likely related to a funerary monument or endowment.

EDCS-18100543.translation: Flavius Stilicho, most illustrious man, count.
EDCS-18100543.summary: This is a dedication or honorific inscription for Flavius Stilicho, mentioning his high rank as a 'vir clarissimus' and 'comes'.

EDCS-18100707.translation: Lucius Sextilius Satyrus, freedman of Lucius, a curiate lictor, made this for himself and for his wife Claudia Acme.
EDCS-18100707.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sextilius Satyrus, a curiate lictor, and his wife Claudia Acme.

EDCS-18100805.translation: The annual magistracies of the Claudial Augustales brotherhood, during the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, for the second time, with Decimus Caelio Balbinus as consul for the second time, Caius Fabius Lucilianus for the second time, Sextus Furnius Sulpicianus for the first time, Lucius Valerius Paetus for the first time, in the year 220 (of the era of the colony?), with Messalla and Sabinus as consuls; Lucius Mantennius Sabinus for the third time, Lucius Insteius Tertullus, Lucius Licinius Sabinus, in the year 221, with Quinto Maecio Laeto for the second time, Marcus Munatio Sulla Cereali as consuls.
EDCS-18100805.summary: This inscription lists the annual magistracies of a brotherhood of Augustales, detailing the consuls and specific years within the reign of Antoninus Pius, likely marking a public building or a record of office holders.

EDCS-18100934.translation: Titus Quinctius, son of Quintus; Lucius Tullius Caltilius, freedman of Caltilia; masters of two pagi and the vici Sulpici.
EDCS-18100934.summary: This inscription seems to record the names and positions of officials responsible for local administrative units (pagi and vici), likely related to a public building or a record of their service.

EDCS-18200237.translation: To Titus Nonius Proculus, son of Titus. Fortunatus and Proculus, sons of Titus Nonius, made this for their most dutiful and well-deserving father. // Of the Iuvenci; they have.
EDCS-18200237.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Nonius Proculus, erected by his sons, with an additional phrase possibly related to a group or location.

EDCS-19301051.translation: Lucius Alfius Maximus, while alive, made this for himself and for the memory of Aelia Chrysopolis, his wife, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-19301051.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Alfius Maximus for himself and his wife Aelia Chrysopolis, indicating it was prepared during his lifetime.

EDCS-19301052.translation: To Gaius Allius, son of Lucius, of the Falernian tribe, by the arbitration of his heirs.
EDCS-19301052.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Allius, son of Lucius, by his heirs.

EDCS-19301053.translation: Allidia Peculium, freedwoman of Sextus, (sets up this monument) for Marcus Equitius Menander, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-19301053.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Allidia Peculium for Marcus Equitius Menander.

EDCS-19301054.translation: To Publius Ampius Lucrio, son of Publius, aged 22. Paccia Laudica, freedwoman of Caius, (made this) at her own expense.
EDCS-19301054.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument for Publius Ampius Lucrio, funded by Paccia Laudica.

EDCS-19301056.translation: Anatollon and Felicula (set this up) for their parents, Statia Anatollon (made this).
EDCS-19301056.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Anatollon and Felicula for their parents, with a contribution from Statia Anatollon.

EDCS-19301060.translation: Lucius Annius Servus, freedman of Caius, a pork-seller, ...
EDCS-19301060.summary: This inscription, though incomplete, appears to be a funerary or dedicatory text for Lucius Annius Servus, a pork-seller.

EDCS-19301062.translation: ... Caius Ansius Lucius ... Secirius ... Publius Cornelius ... Marcus Bentuellius, son of Marcus, ...
EDCS-19301062.summary: This is a fragmented inscription listing several names, likely related to funerary or official records.

EDCS-19301066.translation: Lucius Apo[---] Pius [---] Cogn[---] good [---] Badia [---] sister [---] his [---]
EDCS-19301066.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record names and a familial relationship, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-19301069.translation: To Publius Arrius Glycon, son of Publius, freedman.
EDCS-19301069.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Publius Arrius Glycon, a freedman.

EDCS-19301070.translation: To Marcus Artorius Rufus Zopyrus, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, and to his wife Artoria Callista, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-19301070.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication to Marcus Artorius Rufus Zopyrus and his wife Artoria Callista.

EDCS-19301072.translation: ... son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, for himself ... Marcus Suius Niger, freedman of the freedwoman.
EDCS-19301072.summary: This fragmented inscription mentions a dedication for self and Marcus Suius Niger, a freedman.

EDCS-19301074.translation: From the will of Marcus Aufidius, son of Lucius, son of Fa[...]
EDCS-19301074.summary: This inscription fragment likely records the terms of a will, potentially related to a funerary monument, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19301075.translation: Publius, son of Av, by his will.
EDCS-19301075.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to a bequest or monument established by Publius, son of Av, according to his will.

EDCS-19301076.translation: [...]rio Rufus, greetings(?). Aufillia Appia, freedwoman of a woman, [had this monument] made for Rufus, her husband, and for herself, [and the heir will not follow].
EDCS-19301076.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aufillia Appia, a freedwoman, commissioned a monument for her husband Rufus and herself, stipulating that the heir would not inherit the property.

EDCS-19301078.translation: Gaius Avianus Liccaeus, freedman of a woman; Cornelia Clara, freedwoman of a woman; Aulus Marcius Iucundus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-19301078.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, two freedmen and one freedwoman, likely related to a family burial plot.

EDCS-19301079.translation: Ierta made this. The bones of Caius, freedman of Aulus, and Dacus are placed here. The little daughter lives.
EDCS-19301079.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Ierta created the monument for the remains of Caius and Dacus, and that her daughter is still alive.

EDCS-19301087.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating ownership or dedication by Publius Baebius Hilarus.

EDCS-19301092.translation: Lucius Billienus Marathus for his wife Cornelia Prima and for himself.
EDCS-19301092.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Billienus Marathus for his wife Cornelia Prima and himself.

EDCS-19301096.translation: [Brit]tius Berullus and [Ann]ia Rufa, freedwoman of Lucius, made [this] for themselves and for their sons Brittius and Quintus Pedius Paetus [and others?].
EDCS-19301096.summary: This funerary inscription records the creation of a tomb by Brittius Berullus and Annia Rufa for themselves and their sons.

EDCS-19400172.translation: For Caecilia Heraclea, freedwoman of Marcus, and for Marcus Caecilius Agatho, freedman of Marcus, a most devoted patron, and for Marcus Caecilius Servus, freedman of Marcus. Time, a freedwoman, made [this monument or tomb] for her most devoted patron; the heir will not follow.
EDCS-19400172.summary: This funerary inscription records the commission of a tomb by Time, a freedwoman, for her patron Marcus Caecilius Agatho and other family members, specifying that the inheritance would not pass to an heir.

EDCS-19400176.translation: For Lucius Calpurnius Sotheris. Calpurnia Mele, his wife, [dedicated this] to her deserving husband.
EDCS-19400176.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Calpurnia Mele to her husband, Lucius Calpurnius Sotheris, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19400178.translation: Hilara, the freedwoman, made this for herself and for her patrons, Sextus Caneius Pammyrus and Sextus Caneius Eronius Bassus.
EDCS-19400178.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedwoman for her patrons, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-19400179.translation: Quintus Canius Protus, freedman of Quintus, to his brother Zethus, freedman of Quintus, his patron; and to Quintus Canius Amphion, freedman of Quintus, his brother.
EDCS-19400179.summary: This epitaph honors two brothers, both freedmen of a Quintus Canius, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-19400181.translation: To Carmeia, freedwoman of Iconion, from her will.
EDCS-19400181.summary: This inscription records a bequest made from the will of Iconion for Carmeia, a freedwoman, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400182.translation: Laberia Quarta, the mother, made this for Carponia Ecloca.
EDCS-19400182.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her daughter, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400187.translation: Castricia Nysa, freedwoman of Aulus, made this for herself, her son, and her patron, Aulus Castricius Priscus, son of Aulus, from the Falernian tribe, and for Aulus Castricius Arabus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-19400187.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a freedwoman for herself, her son, and her patron and his freedman, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-19400188.translation: Ius Celer, son of Helius, placed this for his most beloved mother.
EDCS-19400188.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a son for his mother, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400189.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. For Cerialis, who lived 5 years, 5 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-19400189.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of a child named Cerialis, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400190.translation: Here is [---] / Cervonia [---] / innocent [---] / for 12 days [---] / her [---] / deserving.
EDCS-19400190.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription likely dedicated to a woman named Cervonia, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400193.translation: Marcus Cincius Stepanus, freedman of Marcus, [---] from the will of Gaius Statius Dardanus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-19400193.summary: This inscription records a bequest from the will of Gaius Statius Dardanus, as executed by Marcus Cincius Stepanus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-19400195.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription for Gnaeus Cipius Mithridates, possibly a funerary dedication, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19400196.translation: To Publius Cippius Philo, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-19400196.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Philo.

EDCS-19400197.translation: To Halinena, freedwoman of Lucius, and to Zo[...], freedwoman of Lucius, for Cipia and Cipia.
EDCS-19400197.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph honoring two women named Cipia, one of whom is identified as Halinena, a freedwoman.

EDCS-19400203.translation: Marcus Claudius Felix to his well-deserving wife Aemilia.
EDCS-19400203.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from a husband, Marcus Claudius Felix, to his wife, Aemilia.

EDCS-19400206.translation: To Marcus Cloelius Arabus, son of Marcus, from Hordionia Zosari, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-19400206.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring Marcus Cloelius Arabus, dedicated by Hordionia Zosari, his freedwoman.

EDCS-19400208.translation: For the memory of Cluvia Cocceia Severa, most benevolent woman. Aurelius Severus, brother, and Cluvia Cocceia Longina, daughter.
EDCS-19400208.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a brother and daughter to the deceased Cluvia Cocceia Severa.

EDCS-19400209.translation: [...] to his parents [...] and to Cocceia [...] and to himself and his own.
EDCS-19400209.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph where an individual dedicates a monument to his parents, his wife Cocceia, and himself and his family.

EDCS-19400211.translation: To Colchis, from Hesychus, for his wife who deserved well of him.
EDCS-19400211.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by Hesychus to his wife Colchis.

EDCS-19400212.translation: Publius Confuleius Menesteus and Tullia Chelene for themselves and their families.
EDCS-19400212.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by Publius Confuleius Menesteus and Tullia Chelene for themselves and their families.

EDCS-19400215.translation: To Gnaeus Cornelius Flaccus, freedman of Gnaeus, from Ofillia Salvilla, freedwoman of a woman, for herself and her husband.
EDCS-19400215.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by Ofillia Salvilla for herself and her husband to Gnaeus Cornelius Flaccus.

EDCS-19400220.translation: Marcus Cottius, freedman of the Emperor, for himself and for Marcus Cottius, son of Marcus C[...], and for Octavia, freedwoman of a woman Ch[...].
EDCS-19400220.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Marcus Cottius, an imperial freedman, and other family members.

EDCS-19400221.translation: To Marco Cottius, from Diocles, according to the will.
EDCS-19400221.summary: This inscription records a bequest to Marco Cottius, from Diocles, as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-19400226.translation: Decumia Tyche, freedwoman of Publius, [erected this for] Dionysus, freedman of Publius Decumius, and for Faustus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-19400226.summary: This funerary epitaph records the erection of a monument by Decumia Tyche for Dionysus and Faustus, both freedmen of Publius Decumius.

EDCS-19400227.translation: [For] Theophila, freedwoman of Numerius, [and for] Menocrates, freedman of Numerius Dellius, son of Numerius.
EDCS-19400227.summary: This funerary epitaph records dedications to Theophila and Menocrates, both freedpersons associated with the Numerius Dellius family.

EDCS-19400229.translation: Dexsonia Selenius for himself and for his dearest beloved Philema.
EDCS-19400229.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Dexsonia Selenius for himself and his beloved Philema.

EDCS-19400231.translation: The bones of Doroteus are located here. Hilara, his wife, made [this].
EDCS-19400231.summary: This inscription records the placement of Doroteus's remains, with the monument erected by his wife Hilara.

EDCS-19400235.translation: Gnaeus Egnatius Nasica, son of Gnaeus, made [this] for Cantilia, freedwoman of Statius Argyrinus, and for himself.
EDCS-19400235.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Gnaeus Egnatius Nasica for Cantilia, freedwoman of Statius Argyrinus, and for himself.

EDCS-19400239.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sallustia Primitiva [erected this for] Encolpus, freedman of Augustus, her dearest husband.
EDCS-19400239.summary: This funerary inscription records Sallustia Primitiva's dedication to her husband Encolpus, a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-19400240.translation: Ennius Amus [dedicated this] to Memnon and Rustica.
EDCS-19400240.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Ennius Amus to Memnon and Rustica.

EDCS-19400241.translation: Ennia, freedwoman of Caius, made [this] from her own funds for Glaucus, freedman of Caius, and for Philomathius, freedman of a freedwoman.
EDCS-19400241.summary: This funerary inscription records Ennia, a freedwoman, dedicating from her own funds for Glaucus and Philomathius.

EDCS-19400243.translation: Sextia, daughter of Lucius, saw to it that [this monument] was constructed with her own money for Numerius Epidius Falerna, son of Numerius, and for her son Numerius Epidius Falerna Lupercus, son of Numerius.
EDCS-19400243.summary: This inscription records Sextia commissioning a monument from her own funds for her husband and son, both named Numerius Epidius Falerna.

EDCS-19400246.translation: To Equitia Megiste, patroness; to Equitia Daphnis, freedwoman; to Equitia Aucta, daughter; to Marcus Equitius Anterus, brother. Marcus Equitius Auctus for himself and his family.
EDCS-19400246.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Equitius Auctus for his female relatives and himself.

EDCS-19400247.summary: A fragment of an inscription, possibly funerary or dedicatory, with illegible names and details.

EDCS-19400250.translation: Apicula, freedwoman, made this for Quintus Fabius Barnaeus, son of Quintus, freedman.
EDCS-19400250.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a freedwoman to her former master.

EDCS-19400252.translation: Fabia Sabina, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made in her will.
EDCS-19400252.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Fabia Sabina via her will.

EDCS-19400253.translation: To Festus Servianus Eutactianus, a friend, as he deserved.
EDCS-19400253.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring Festus Servianus Eutactianus, set up by a friend.

EDCS-19400254.translation: Ficilia Rodocle, freedwoman of Quintus, made this for her patron, and for herself, and for Tertullia, living freedwoman, and for Agatho, freedman.
EDCS-19400254.summary: A funerary monument erected by the freedwoman Ficilia Rodocle for her patron, herself, and other freedpersons.

EDCS-19400255.translation: Lucius Fudius Auctus, freedman of the woman, to his patroness, and for himself.
EDCS-19400255.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Fudius Auctus for his patroness and himself.

EDCS-19400260.translation: The ashes of Flavia Prima, wife of Celadus, freedman of Augustus, are here. Titus Flavius Acindynus, freedman, most beloved, most dutiful. Titus Flavius Celadus, freedman of Augustus, made this. // To Flavia Nice, freedwoman, most beloved, with her affection, services, and expenditures, she loved her patron. Titus Flavius Celadus, freedman of Augustus, made this.
EDCS-19400260.summary: A double funerary monument erected by Titus Flavius Celadus, a freedman of Augustus, for his wife Flavia Prima and another freedwoman, Flavia Nice, expressing deep affection and gratitude.

EDCS-19400263.translation: [illegible]trilii [illegible]rato, a man, and [illegible] Fortunatus, and his family. This monument shall not follow.
EDCS-19400263.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription with names that are largely illegible, possibly including a prohibition against moving the monument.

EDCS-19400264.translation: Here lie the bones of Freia Maioris, daughter of Gnaeus.
EDCS-19400264.summary: A simple funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Freia Maioris.

EDCS-19400268.translation: Sextus Furius Chilo, freedman of Sextus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-19400268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Furius Chilo and his family, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-19400269.translation: To Publius Furius, freedman of Publius, Mol[---]; Furia [---]AEL[---]; [---]; [---]IS.
EDCS-19400269.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Publius Furius and Furia, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400270.translation: Aulus Gabinius Felix, freedman of Aulus, for himself and his daughter Gabinia Celsa, daughter of Aulus; for his grandson Publius Vibuleius Celsus, son of Publius; for his wife Novia Prima, freedwoman of Aulus; for his freedman Aulus Gabinius Hilarus, freedman of Aulus; for Gabinia Irena, freedwoman of Aulus; for his freedman's freedwoman Novia Optata; for his freedman Aulus Gabinius Philerotus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-19400270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph detailing a complex family structure and the dedicants for themselves and their relatives, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400272.translation: For Publius Gabinius Lyssa, freedman of Publius; for Lucius Maecilius Soso, freedman of Lucius, son of Sextus; for Gabinia Prima, freedwoman of Publius; for Gabinia Dionysia, freedwoman of Publius. He made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-19400272.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for several individuals, likely a tombstone, set up by one of the named individuals for himself and his family.

EDCS-19400274.translation: Gavillia Dynamis for herself, her daughter, and her son. Gavillia Hilara, freedwoman of the woman.
EDCS-19400274.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gavillia Dynamis and her children, mentioning her freedwoman. Likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400275.translation: Silo made [this] for Glaphyrinus, his fellow-slave, and for Campanus, his son.
EDCS-19400275.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Silo to his fellow-slave Glaphyrinus and his son Campanus, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400276.translation: For Sextus Grattius Theogenes, freedman of Sextus. Itum ambitum [this monument] for himself and his family.
EDCS-19400276.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Grattius Theogenes and his family, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400280.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Herennia Iucunda and possibly a name beginning with Ianuar, the purpose is unclear.

EDCS-19400285.translation: His parents made [this] for their freedman Hilarus, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-19400285.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents for their freedman Hilarus, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400293.translation: For Titus Hordionius Hermaphilus, freedman of Titus; for Vibius Thyranninus, freedman of Publius. According to the will, by the arbitration of Aulus Nasennius Philargurus, freedman of the woman.
EDCS-19400293.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Hordionius Hermaphilus and Vibius Thyranninus, executed according to a will and testament, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-19400295.translation: To Hordionia Prima, freedwoman of Hordionia; to Hordionia Lauda, freedwoman of Hordionia; to Hordionia Salvila, freedwoman of Hordionia.
EDCS-19400295.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating plots to three freedwomen belonging to a certain Hordionia.

EDCS-19400296.translation: Hordionia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius, by her will, by the arbitration of Publius Hordionius Hermascius, her heir.
EDCS-19400296.summary: This inscription records the funerary arrangements made by Hordionia Rufa, a freedwoman, according to her will.

EDCS-19400301.translation: To Aulus Hostrius Lucrio, freedman of Aulus, [my] patron. Hostria Augenis lives. Aulus Hostrius Philoxenus, freedman of Aulus, made [this] for his patron and Augenis.
EDCS-19400301.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aulus Hostrius Philoxenus for his patron Aulus Hostrius Lucrio and for Hostria Augenis.

EDCS-19400307.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription for Iucunda Nusia Stati.

EDCS-19400310.translation: To Oresbius, freedman of Gaius Julius Dumanthis. Iulia Ephesia, freedwoman of Gaius, [dedicated this] for her patron and for herself and her own people.
EDCS-19400310.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Iulia Ephesia for her patron Oresbius and her own family.

EDCS-19400313.translation: Iulia Adepta, freedwoman of the woman, for herself and Brittius.
EDCS-19400313.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Iulia Adepta for herself and for Brittius.

EDCS-19400318.translation: Iunia Urbana for herself and her spouse. Marcus Servilius Eros, freedman of Marcus, his bones are laid here.
EDCS-19400318.summary: This funerary inscription records that Iunia Urbana dedicated it for herself and her spouse, and identifies the burial place of Marcus Servilius Eros.

EDCS-19400320.translation: To Lucius Lapscidius, son of Titus. For Lapscidia Cuarta. Viria Chrysaris, freedwoman of Lucius, and Lucius Lapscidius Viator made [this] for their patron.
EDCS-19400320.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Viria Chrysaris and Lucius Lapscidius Viator for their patron, likely Lucius Lapscidius or Lapscidia Cuarta.

EDCS-19400324.translation: To Marcus Limbricius Barnaeus, freedman of Marcus. To Marcus Limbricius Lysimachus, freedman of Marcus. To Procilia Iconio. [Marcus Li]mbricius Barnaeus, freedman of Marcus, for himself and his own people.
EDCS-19400324.summary: This funerary inscription records dedications to Marcus Limbricius Barnaeus, Marcus Limbricius Lysimachus, and Procilia Iconio, with a further dedication by Marcus Limbricius Barnaeus for himself and his family.

EDCS-19400326.summary: This inscription likely relates to a votive offering or dedication to a deity, possibly for personal well-being.

EDCS-19400327.translation: Here lie the remains of Lucceia Aphrodisia. Marcus Vettius Lucceianus, son of Marcus, made [this] for his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-19400327.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucceia Aphrodisia, set up by her son Marcus Vettius Lucceianus.

EDCS-19400332.translation: For Gaius Manneius Nicephorus, freedman of Gaius, by the decision of Pamphilus, freedman.
EDCS-19400332.summary: This inscription records a dedication or commission made by a freedman on behalf of another freedman.

EDCS-19400333.translation: Her father [made this] for Marcia Primigenia.
EDCS-19400333.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcia Primigenia, set up by her father.

EDCS-19400335.summary: This inscription, possibly a funerary marker, mentions Marius Quirinus and the number 451, possibly a date or quantity.

EDCS-19400336.translation: [---]el, daughter of Publius' freedwoman Melitina, [---] made [this] for her mother, the freedwoman of Publius Silon.
EDCS-19400336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, with significant lacunae, indicating a mother made a dedication for her daughter.

EDCS-19400344.translation: Mucia Lais, freedwoman of Publius, [daughter/family member] of Summanina. Patron.
EDCS-19400344.summary: This inscription identifies Mucia Lais, a freedwoman, in relation to her patron and possibly her mother or family member Summanina.

EDCS-19400345.translation: Mulutia Felicula made [this] for herself and her family.
EDCS-19400345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mulutia Felicula, who set it up for herself and her relatives.

EDCS-19400349.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or funerary marker, possibly for Munnia, with connections to Pollai.

EDCS-19400355.translation: For Eron, freedman of [Aulus Nasennius?], freedman of a woman, and for Dardanalia, freedwoman of Aulus Nasennius and freedwoman of a woman. [---] Augustus [---]. For Optatus, freedman of Aulus Nasennius, freedman of a woman, and freedman of Nasennia, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-19400355.summary: This inscription is a complex funerary dedication for multiple individuals, possibly members of the Nasennius family or their freedmen.

EDCS-19400356.translation: Gaius Nasennius Rufio, freedman of Gaius, made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-19400356.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Nasennius Rufio, who established it for himself and his household.

EDCS-19400357.translation: Nasennia, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and for Publius Nasennius, patron, and for Publius Nasennius and for Publius Nasennius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-19400357.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nasennia and other members of the Nasennii family, possibly setting up a shared tomb.

EDCS-19400358.translation: Gaius Nerius Antiochus, freedman of Gaius, and Neria Helena, freedwoman of Gaius, made this for Gaius Nerius, son of Gaius, and for their patron and brother.
EDCS-19400358.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by freedmen for their patron and a relative, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-19400360.translation: Lucius Novius Epicrates, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Vibiai Iucunda, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-19400360.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Novius Epicrates for himself and for Vibiai Iucunda, possibly his wife or relative.

EDCS-19400364.translation: Marcus Numisius Hilarus for his wife, Rabiria Donata.
EDCS-19400364.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Marcus Numisius Hilarus to his wife, Rabiria Donata.

EDCS-19400365.translation: [text missing] for Numisia [text missing] Seneca, daughter of Cetlius.
EDCS-19400365.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Numisia and Seneca.

EDCS-19400367.translation: [text missing] Pius Secundus [text missing] for Numisia Ru[text missing], well-deserving, [text missing] for Lucius Numisius Priscus.
EDCS-19400367.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription honoring Numisia and Lucius Numisius Priscus.

EDCS-19400543.translation: Numerius Celerius Quintio, freedman of Numerius.
EDCS-19400543.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Numerius Celerius Quintio, a freedman.

EDCS-19600001.translation: Lucius Popillius, at his own expense.
EDCS-19600001.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Popillius funded the construction or erection of a monument at his own expense.

EDCS-19600002.translation: Prima, daughter of Satria, freedwoman of a woman, from the household slaves, for Athenio.
EDCS-19600002.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Athenio, set up by Prima, a freedwoman and possibly a slave associated with the household of Satria.

EDCS-19600004.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a child named Primus.

EDCS-19600006.translation: Gaius Prosius Rufus, son of Marcus, from the Falernian tribe, from his will, 2,000 sesterces to Gaius Prosius Aescino, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-19600006.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 2,000 sesterces from the will of Gaius Prosius Rufus to his freedman Gaius Prosius Aescino.

EDCS-19600010.translation: Cornelia Gemella, freedwoman of Lucius, daughter of Lucius, made this for her husband Gaius Gratus, freedman of Gaius. This monument or tomb does not pass to the heir.
EDCS-19600010.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument set up by Cornelia Gemella for her husband Gaius Gratus, stipulating that the property will not pass to an heir.

EDCS-19600012.translation: Gaius Philocomus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself, for his freedman Philotimus, and for his own Phronimus and Scitas.
EDCS-19600012.summary: This inscription records Gaius Philocomus setting up a monument for himself, his freedman Philotimus, and his slaves Phronimus and Scitas.

EDCS-19600013.translation: Gaius Statius, freedman of Gaius Raconius.
EDCS-19600013.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication, likely funerary, identifying Gaius Statius, freedman of Gaius Raconius.

EDCS-19600014.translation: [At]tali Faustus, son of Aulus, freedman of Aulus, son of Aulus Raecius.
EDCS-19600014.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, identifying Attalus Faustus as the son and freedman of members of the Raecius family.

EDCS-19600016.translation: Pharnaces, freedman, [for his] patron Gaius Antigonus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-19600016.summary: This inscription records Pharnaces, a freedman, dedicating a monument to his patron Gaius Antigonus.

EDCS-19600018.translation: [son of Lucius] Rufus; [---]ia, daughter of [---], Tertia.
EDCS-19600018.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that seems to identify two individuals, likely related, with the names Rufus and Tertia.

EDCS-19600019.translation: Rullia Adepta, freedwoman of the woman [owner], made this monument or tomb for herself and for her companion Publius Brittius Epicus, freedman of Publius, and for Gaius Rullius Communis, freedman of the woman [owner], and for her own [family]. This monument or tomb does not pass to the heir.
EDCS-19600019.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument established by Rullia Adepta for herself, her partner Publius Brittius Epicus, Gaius Rullius Communis, and other family members, with a clause preventing inheritance by a successor.

EDCS-19600022.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication, likely a funerary epitaph, of Sacratoria Laudica.

EDCS-19600024.translation: Glyco, freedman of Gaius Sallustius, son of Gaius // Artimo, freedman of Publius Pontius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-19600024.summary: This inscription appears to record two individuals, Glyco and Artimo, both freedmen of different patrons, possibly on a shared funerary monument.

EDCS-19600025.translation: To Sallustia Hedone, her most excellent daughter, from Gaius Cavinnius Tertius and Sallustia Hedone.
EDCS-19600025.summary: This is a tombstone for a daughter named Sallustia Hedone, set up by her father and mother, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600027.translation: To Salvia Nova, from Frugi, casta, proba. The bones lie here. Numerius Vibius made this.
EDCS-19600027.summary: This epitaph for Salvia Nova states that her remains are interred here and that it was made by Numerius Vibius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600029.translation: To Quintus Satrius Dionysius, freedman of Quintus Satrius, and Quintus Satrius Felix, freedman of Quintus, and Montanai, freedwoman of Marcus, wife of Felix.
EDCS-19600029.summary: This funerary inscription names several freedmen and their spouses, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600032.translation: To Marcus Scurracius, son of Marcus of the Falernian tribe, for his father Marcus Scurracius, son of Publius of the Falernian tribe, and Heria, daughter of Gaius of the Falernian tribe, his mother, and Scurracia, daughter of Marcus, his sister.
EDCS-19600032.summary: This funerary inscription honors a father, mother, and sister by Marcus Scurracius, son of Marcus, all from the Falernian tribe, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600035.translation: To Numerius Seius Aescinus, freedman of Numerius, and to his wife Artem[---], freedwoman of Arquinia.
EDCS-19600035.summary: This funerary inscription records Numerius Seius Aescinus, freedman of Numerius, and his wife Artem[---], freedwoman of Arquinia, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600038.translation: To Sempronius Saturninus, son of Marcus of the Falernian tribe, and to their mother Sempronia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, and to their father and mother, and [---]minius, son of Quintus of the Falernian tribe, from Campania.
EDCS-19600038.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication to parents and children, with one part of the inscription mentioning a man from Campania, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600039.translation: To Sergia [---], Sergia [---], for herself and her patron [---] with her own money, she made this.
EDCS-19600039.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription states that Sergia made a monument for herself and her patron with her own funds, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600042.translation: To Gaius Sevius Fidus, son of Gaius of the Falernian tribe, his most devoted son, from his mother Sevia Pthonge, most unhappy mother.
EDCS-19600042.summary: This epitaph honors the devoted son Gaius Sevius Fidus, set up by his grieving mother Sevia Pthonge, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600043.translation: To Sevia Gemella and Fis(i)a Gemella, from Sevia Prisca, for her mother and daughter.
EDCS-19600043.summary: This inscription records Sevia Prisca setting up a monument for her mother and daughter, both named Gemella, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600044.translation: To Marcus Sextius Grypus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-19600044.summary: This is a simple dedication to Marcus Sextius Grypus, a freedman of Marcus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600049.translation: Marcus Spanius Iucundus made this for himself and his family, for his patroness Spania Rufilla, for Marcus Minucius Faustus, for Spania Glycinis, for Spania Daphnen, daughter of Spania Phyrallinus, for his wife Marcus Epidius Celer, and for their children, for Marcus Epidius Celer, their son, and for Epidia Rufilla, daughter of Spania Secundilla, his freedwoman.
EDCS-19600049.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Spanius Iucundus for himself, his family, his patroness, and other associates.

EDCS-19600050.translation: To Lucius Spedius Pamphilus, freedman of Lucius; to Spedia Laudica, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Spedius Pamphilus, freedman of Lucius, and Spedia Laudica, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for her husband and for themselves and for their son.
EDCS-19600050.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Lucius Spedius Pamphilus and Spedia Laudica for her husband and their family.

EDCS-19600521.translation: To Numerius Staius, son of Numerius, of the Pupinia tribe, patron. Numerius Staius Cosmus, freedman, made this for himself, for his fellow freedwoman Staia Dynamis, freedwoman of Numerius, and for Staia Cosmilla, daughter of Staia, freedwoman of Numerius.
EDCS-19600521.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the freedman Numerius Staius Cosmus for himself, a fellow freedwoman, and another woman.

EDCS-19600524.summary: This inscription records a decision or decree made by a person named Suavis.

EDCS-19600529.translation: To [---]onius Syllo, freedman of Marcus; to [---]ua, freedwoman of Lucius, Pamphil(a?); to [---]o, son of Lucius, freedman Hilarus; to [---]o, freedman of a woman, Verna; to [---]o, freedman of Marcus, Hilarus.
EDCS-19600529.summary: This is a fragmented funerary monument listing several individuals, likely freedmen and their relations.

EDCS-19600531.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Tephane lived 28 years. Her devoted mother made this for her deserving daughter.
EDCS-19600531.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a mother for her deceased daughter, Tephane, who died at the age of 28.

EDCS-19600533.translation: The bones of Tertulla are placed here. Her mother Caesia Sammis made this.
EDCS-19600533.summary: This is a tombstone indicating the placement of Tertulla's remains, erected by her mother Caesia Sammis.

EDCS-19600538.translation: To Titia Loga. Gnaeus Munatius Epityncanus for his well-deserving wife. Titius Nicephor.
EDCS-19600538.summary: This tombstone commemorates Titia Loga, set up by her husband Gnaeus Munatius Epityncanus and possibly another person named Titius Nicephor.

EDCS-19600540.translation: To Gaius Titius Philargyrus, freedman of Gaius, according to his will, by the decision of Lucius Noni Bithus.
EDCS-19600540.summary: This inscription records the execution of a will, with Lucius Noni Bithus acting as arbiter for the funerary arrangements of Gaius Titius Philargyrus.

EDCS-19600542.translation: To Tornasia Laina, freedwoman of Lucius. To Lucius Tornasius Servius, freedman of Lucius. To Vinnia Quarta, freedwoman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-19600542.summary: This funerary monument lists Tornasia Laina and Lucius Tornasius Servius, both freedmen, and Vinnia Quarta.

EDCS-19600546.summary: This is an epitaph for Tullia Cleopatra.

EDCS-19600547.translation: The bones of Tullia Calliope, freedwoman of Quintus, are placed here.
EDCS-19600547.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Tullia Calliope, a freedwoman of Quintus.

EDCS-19600548.translation: Tullia Euporia, freedwoman of Quintus, made this for herself and for Lucius Antestius Mona, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-19600548.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Tullia Euporia for herself and her associate Lucius Antestius Mona.

EDCS-19600550.summary: This inscription likely records names and ages, possibly related to a funerary monument, with the date being inferred from the number XIIX (18).

EDCS-19600552.translation: Gaius Valerius [made this] for himself and Gaius Valerius.
EDCS-19600552.summary: This is a funerary dedication initiated by Gaius Valerius for himself and another individual also named Gaius Valerius.

EDCS-19600553.translation: Lucius Valerius Timothes, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-19600553.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Valerius Timothes, identified as a freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-19600557.translation: Lucius Varius Ambibulus, freedman of Actiacus.
EDCS-19600557.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Varius Ambibulus, identified as a freedman of Actiacus.

EDCS-19600560.translation: [Publius] Udios Commodus, son of Publius, for Maria Heraclea, freedwoman of Gnaeus, and for Publius Udios Nicephorus, freedman of Publius. Commodus made this for himself, his father, and his mother while alive.
EDCS-19600560.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Publius Udios Commodus for his parents and himself, indicating it was made during his lifetime.

EDCS-19600561.translation: [---]tius Venustus, freedman of Caius, for himself and for [---]via Charis, freedwoman of Marcus, and [---] Modesta.
EDCS-19600561.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by [---]tius Venustus for himself, his wife [---]via Charis, and another person named Modesta.

EDCS-19600562.translation: To Sextus Veratius Secundus, son of his sister.
EDCS-19600562.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to Sextus Veratius Secundus, who is identified as the son of the dedicator's sister.

EDCS-19600564.translation: Agele, daughter of Spurius Versiculanus, for herself and for her mother Daphne Versiculana, and for those who deserved it; this monument or tomb shall not follow an heir.
EDCS-19600564.summary: This funerary epitaph records Agele Versiculana dedicating a monument/tomb for herself, her mother, and other deserving individuals, stipulating that it is not to pass to an heir.

EDCS-19600567.translation: Gnaeus Vetius Menodorus, freedman of Gnaeus; Thalia, freedwoman of Cerrinia.
EDCS-19600567.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple record of ownership or naming of two freedpersons, possibly associated with a tomb or property.

EDCS-19600570.translation: To Lucius Vettius Eroto, freedman of Lucius, farewell. To Vettia Prima, freedwoman of Lucius. To Lucius Vettius Timon, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-19600570.summary: This epitaph commemorates three individuals: Lucius Vettius Eroto, Vettia Prima, and Lucius Vettius Timon, all freedpersons associated with the Vettia family.

EDCS-19600571.translation: Marcus Vettius Firmus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-19600571.summary: This is a simple dedication or naming inscription for Marcus Vettius Firmus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-19600576.translation: Of Decimus Vibidius Niger, son of Decimus, of the Pupinia tribe.
EDCS-19600576.summary: This is a nominative dedication, likely part of a larger inscription on a tomb or monument for Decimus Vibidius Niger.

EDCS-19600580.summary: A short, informal epitaph or farewell to a person named Victoria.

EDCS-19600582.translation: To Lucius Virius Eutyches, freedman of Atthii Fasta.
EDCS-19600582.summary: This dedication is for Lucius Virius Eutyches, a freedman of Atthii Fasta, likely part of a tomb inscription.

EDCS-19600583.translation: To Marcus Visellius Balitor, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe; and to Atleia Polla, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-19600583.summary: This inscription records a dedication to two individuals, Marcus Visellius Balitor and Atleia Polla, likely on a shared tomb or monument.

EDCS-19600584.translation: Quintus Vitellius Apella, freedman of Quintus and Aulus, made (this); for Vitellia Statia, freedwoman of Quintus and Aulus, and for Venusta, freedwoman of (Caius?); and for Gaius Caristanius Hermaesco.
EDCS-19600584.summary: This inscription records Quintus Vitellius Apella as the maker, dedicating the monument for two freedwomen, Vitellia Statia and Venusta, and for Gaius Caristanius Hermaesco.

EDCS-19600590.translation: To Anthedonius, Volusia made (this); for her sister Creste.
EDCS-19600590.summary: Volusia made this funerary dedication for her sister Creste and possibly for a person named Anthedonius.

EDCS-19600591.translation: The bones of Zephyrinis are placed here.
EDCS-19600591.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the burial place of Zephyrinis.

EDCS-19600598.translation: This stone covers the bones of Frugi, son of Caius, a great man.
EDCS-19600598.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Frugi, son of Caius.

EDCS-19600617.translation: By decision of Eutilius, son of Publius, of the tribe Tromentina, for his mother, daughter of Lucius, [with a donation of] 5,000 sesterces.
EDCS-19600617.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a bequest of 5,000 sesterces for a mother by her son Eutilius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-19600619.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely identifies Ambonius, a freedman.

EDCS-19600620.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Viria Atestiana.

EDCS-19600621.translation: Nonus, tribunate helper, spouse, lived for 20 months.
EDCS-19600621.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short life of Nonus, who served as a tribunate helper.

EDCS-19600624.translation: Made for Perolla, daughter of Herae Venerae, most beloved.
EDCS-19600624.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the beloved Perolla by her mother Herae Venerae.

EDCS-19600627.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name and origin of an individual named Aprus.

EDCS-19600628.translation: ... Arovus, son, for his excellent father.
EDCS-19600628.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription honoring Arovus's father.

EDCS-19600632.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription honoring a mother named Politta.

EDCS-19600635.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph indicating a familial relationship between the deceased and the dedicator.

EDCS-19600639.translation: Confuleia Tertia, freedwoman of Marcus, [left this] to Marcus Confuleius Philargyrus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-19600639.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication of a tomb by a freedwoman to her patron or a relative with the same nomen.

EDCS-19600640.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a freedman.

EDCS-19600644.translation: [---]iratu[---] / [---] son of Sex[tius?] / [---]opi, son of IID[---].
EDCS-19600644.summary: This is a severely damaged inscription that appears to record a dedication or funerary information, possibly naming individuals and their filiation.

EDCS-19600650.translation: Turtur [died?] from Clymeine(?) so that we may sleep well [---] and I will rub your lovely white legs with my penis and your buttocks will help the itching.
EDCS-19600650.summary: This inscription is a coarse erotic or magical text, possibly related to fertility or sexual health.

EDCS-19600652.translation: Primus, most innocent man, who lived 80 years, is buried here. His son Firmus made this for the deserving one. Deposited on the 15th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of our lords X and III.
EDCS-19600652.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Primus, with details about his age, the dedicator (his son Firmus), and the date of burial, likely in the 4th century AD given the consular dating.

EDCS-19600653.translation: Onensimus the innocent is buried here. Indeed, even as a small child he was naturally kind to everyone, but he was suddenly taken from me, who lived 1 year, 10 months, and 19 days. Deposited on the day before the Nones, after the consulship of our lords Valentinianus and Valens.
EDCS-19600653.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Onensimus, detailing his virtuous character, age at death, and burial date, placed during the joint consulship of Valentinian and Valens (likely 366 AD or later).

EDCS-19600654.translation: Alonius Aulius, a new convert (neophyte), who lived 18 years, was buried on the 2nd day before the Nones of September, in the consulship of Flavius Gratianus and Dagalaiphus.
EDCS-19600654.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young man named Alonius Aulius, who is identified as a neophyte, and includes his age and burial date during the consulship of Gratian and Dagalaiphus (366 AD).

EDCS-19600655.translation: Fortunia, who lived more or less 4 years, is buried here. Her parents placed [this for their] most sweet daughter. She completed 7 days [of life? unclear] and was buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gratianus and Probus.
EDCS-19600655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Fortunia, placed by her parents, and includes her approximate age and burial date during the consulship of Gratianus and Probus (likely 371 AD).

EDCS-19600656.translation: Innocentius Dicianus, who lived 18 years and 5 months, is buried here. The deserving ones made [this for him]. Deposited on the 11th day before the Kalends of September, in the time of our lords Valens V and Valentinian.
EDCS-19600656.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Innocentius Dicianus, detailing his age at death and burial date, likely during the joint reign of Valens and Valentinian (post-364 AD).

EDCS-19600657.translation: Prausius the embalmer is laid here, who lived two years and eight months, buried the day before the Kalends of July, when Arcadio Augusto and Bauto were consuls; his parents made this [monument] against their vows.
EDCS-19600657.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Prausius, an embalmer, dating to the consulship of Arcadio Augusto and Bauto.

EDCS-19600659.translation: Here are laid the two innocent neo-martyrs: Dionisius, who lived one year and two months, buried the day before the Kalends of August; Mariniana, who lived three years and three months, buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of November, under our lord Eugenius Augustus.
EDCS-19600659.summary: This inscription records the burial of two young Christian martyrs, Dionisius and Mariniana, during the reign of Eugenius Augustus.

EDCS-19600660.translation: Dianeses the innocent is laid here, who lived two years and two months, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of June, when Flavius Caesarius and Nonius Atticus were consuls; his parents made this for a well-deserving and sweet son.
EDCS-19600660.summary: This is a tombstone for a child named Dianeses, set up by his parents during the consulship of Flavius Caesarius and Nonius Atticus.

EDCS-19600661.translation: Flavius Marianio is laid here, who lived forty-one years; he died and was buried on the day of the Nones of October, during the consulship of Flavius Mallius Theodorus, a most illustrious man, for a well-deserving person in peace.
EDCS-19600661.summary: This inscription marks the burial of Flavius Marianio, who died in the consulship of Flavius Mallius Theodorus.

EDCS-19600662.translation: We celebrate Fabia Scerniola, always loved by us, our joy in old age and comfort in sorrow; we trust you are always living, who, it is known, so avoided evils in the underworld; lived about fourteen years, buried on the 4th day before the Kalends of May, in the consulship of Probinus, a most illustrious man.
EDCS-19600662.summary: This tomb inscription honors Fabia Scerniola, who died around the age of fourteen, and was buried during the consulship of Probinus.

EDCS-19600663.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Sarmata, who lived about seventy years, buried on the twelfth of December, in the consulship of Flavius Acapitus, a most illustrious man.
EDCS-19600663.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Sarmata, who lived to be about seventy years old, during the consulship of Flavius Acapitus.

EDCS-19600664.translation: Here rests in peace Escortia, who lived about sixty-five years, buried on the 10th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of the most illustrious men Flavius Symmachus and Boethius; she lived with her husband for forty-five years.
EDCS-19600664.summary: This inscription marks the burial of Escortia, who lived about sixty-five years and was married for forty-five, during the consulship of Flavius Symmachus and Boethius.

EDCS-19600665.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Guiliarit, who lived about eighty years, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of July, and again after the consulship of Lampadius and Orestes, most illustrious men.
EDCS-19600665.summary: This tomb inscription records the burial of Guiliarit, who lived to be about eighty, during a period after the consulship of Lampadius and Orestes.

EDCS-19600667.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Renobatus, who lived seventy-three years, buried on the Kalends of July, for the fourth time after the consulship of Basilius, a most illustrious man.
EDCS-19600667.summary: This epitaph marks the burial of Renobatus, who lived to be seventy-three, during a period after the fourth consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19600668.translation: Here rests in peace Petrus, a most illustrious man and count, who lived about sixty-four years, buried on the day before the Nones of December, in the tenth indiction, the eighth year after the consulship of Basilius, a most illustrious man.
