EDCS-19600668.summary: This inscription records the burial of Petrus, a count and 'clarissimus', who died at around sixty-four years of age, in the eighth year after the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19700108.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming three men from the Signinus family, all surnamed Geminus, suggesting a family monument.

EDCS-19700167.translation: A gift to Juno Lucina for Gaius Rutilius, son of Publius.
EDCS-19700167.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a gift to the goddess Juno Lucina on behalf of Gaius Rutilius, son of Publius, likely dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-19700168.translation: Publius Rutilius, son of Marcus, dedicated (this) to Juno Lucina, may the gods protect.
EDCS-19700168.summary: This is a votive inscription by Publius Rutilius, son of Marcus, dedicating something to Juno Lucina, with a prayer for divine protection, likely dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-19700171.translation: Lucius Rahius, son of Lucius, as aediles, dedicated (this).
EDCS-19700171.summary: This is a public dedication by Lucius Rahius, son of Lucius, in his capacity as aedile, likely dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-19700360.summary: This is a personal name, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory inscription.

EDCS-19700361.translation: Lucius Canoleius, son of Lucius, made this.
EDCS-19700361.summary: This records a person, Lucius Canoleius, son of Lucius, as the maker of an object or monument.

EDCS-19700362.translation: Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, made this for the people of Calenos.
EDCS-19700362.summary: This dedicates an object or monument made by Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, to the community of Calenos.

EDCS-19700394.summary: This is a personal name, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory inscription.

EDCS-19700395.translation: Servius Gabinius, slave of Titus, made this.
EDCS-19700395.summary: This records a freedman or slave named Servius Gabinius, who was the property of Titus, as the maker of an object or monument.

EDCS-19700396.translation: Gaius Gabinius, son of Lucius, grandson of Titus, from Calenos.
EDCS-19700396.summary: This is a full Roman name and place of origin, likely for a funerary or civic inscription.

EDCS-19700397.summary: This is a personal name, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory inscription.

EDCS-19700502.translation: Cupido, son of Venos, with a laugh.
EDCS-19700502.summary: This inscription appears to be a playful or perhaps ironic dedication, possibly to the personified god of love, Cupid.

EDCS-19700606.translation: Taseos, Luqorcos, Pilonicos, sons of Tasei.
EDCS-19700606.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, Taseos, Luqorcos, and Pilonicos, identifying them as sons of Tasei, likely in a familial or commemorative context.

EDCS-19700609.summary: This inscription lists three personal names: Telis, Ajax, and Alcumena, possibly representing family members or individuals honored together.

EDCS-19700612.summary: This inscription is a very brief dedication or dedication to Victoria Alixentros.

EDCS-19700615.translation: Of Marcus Orcivius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-19700615.summary: This inscription records a patronymic, identifying Marcus Orcivius as the son of Marcus.

EDCS-19700634.translation: Do not touch me. I am Gemucius.
EDCS-19700634.summary: This funerary inscription serves as a warning to passersby, identifying the deceased as Gemucius.

EDCS-19700690.translation: Marcianus rests here in peace, who lived more or less 60 years, buried on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May, in the fifteenth indiction, eleven years after the consulate of the most excellent Basilius.
EDCS-19700690.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcianus, detailing his age and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700691.translation: Rusticus, a most excellent man, son of the deserving Marturius and the respectable Catella, rests here in the sleep of peace, who lived more or less 49 years, 6 months, and 24 days, buried in the days of the Augustae, after the consulate of the most excellent consul Basilius, in the fifteenth indiction.
EDCS-19700691.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rusticus, detailing his age, parentage, and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700692.translation: The most blessed Victor, bishop, sat [as bishop] for 13 years and 38 days, buried on the fourth day before the Nones of April, in the thirteenth year after the consulate of the most excellent Basilius, in the second indiction.
EDCS-19700692.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Victor, detailing his tenure and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700693.summary: This inscription records an offering made by Victor, a bishop.

EDCS-19700694.translation: Iohannis Clarissimus Dultus rests here in the sleep of peace, who lived more or less 92 years, buried on the sixth day before the Ides of March, in the sixteenth year after the consulate of the most excellent Basilius, in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-19700694.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iohannis Clarissimus Dultus, detailing his age and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700695.translation: In this tomb rests Deusduna, son of the late Proberentius, who lived 12 years, buried on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the eighth indiction, the seventeenth year after the consulate of the most excellent Basilius.
EDCS-19700695.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Deusduna, detailing his age and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700696.translation: In the sleep of peace rests here Sapata, an honorable woman, who lived more or less 50 years, buried on the day before the Nones of November, in the nineteenth year after the consulate of the most excellent Basilius, in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-19700696.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sapata, detailing her age and burial date, likely from the 6th century AD.

EDCS-19700698.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Iustus, who lived about sixty years, buried on the 17th day before the Kalends of November, after the consulship of Basilius, a most distinguished man, in the 22nd year.
EDCS-19700698.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Iustus in the 22nd year of an unspecified reign or period, after the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19700699.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Paulinus, innocent, who lived two years and two months, whose memory brought grief to his parents, buried on the 4th day before the Nones of November, in the 12th indiction, after the consulship of Basilius, a most distinguished man, in the 22nd year.
EDCS-19700699.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Paulinus, an innocent child, in the 22nd year after the consulship of Basilius and the 12th indiction.

EDCS-19700700.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Anastasius, who lived sixteen years, six months, and fifteen days, buried in November, after the consulship of Basilius, a most distinguished man, in the 24th year, by law and right.
EDCS-19700700.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Anastasius, who died in November of the 24th year after the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19700703.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Iustina, abbess and foundress of this holy place, who lived about eighty-five years, buried on the Kalends of November, under Emperor our lord Justinus, father of the country, Augustus, in the 4th year after his consulship, in the third indiction.
EDCS-19700703.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Abbess Iustina, the foundress of the monastery, during the 4th year after Emperor Justinus's consulship.

EDCS-19700705.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Agathe, who lived about thirty years, buried on the 3rd day before the Nones of September, in the 3rd indiction, under Emperor Justinus, in the same consulship, in the 5th year.
EDCS-19700705.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Agathe, who died around the age of thirty, in the 5th regnal year of Emperor Justinus.

EDCS-19700706.translation: The most blessed man Probinus, bishop, presided for 1 year, 9 months, and 4 days, buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of September, under Emperor our lord Justinus, in the 7th year after his consulship, in the 5th year, in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-19700706.summary: This is an inscription commemorating Probinus, a bishop, detailing his tenure and burial in the 7th regnal year of Emperor Justinus.

EDCS-19700707.translation: Here rests in peace Leonina, who lived four years and four months, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of April, in the 7th indiction, eight days before Easter.
EDCS-19700707.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Leonina, who died at the age of four years and four months.

EDCS-19700708.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Agnellus, who lived about six years.
EDCS-19700708.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death and burial of Agnellus, who died around the age of six.

EDCS-19700709.translation: To Aurelia Aristoclia, a most dutiful and chaste wife, her husband Megethius placed this; she lived fifty years and six months, buried on the 18th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-19700709.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated by Megethius to his wife Aurelia Aristoclia, recording her age and burial date.

EDCS-19700710.translation: Here is laid Brittius Germanus, who lived six years, four months, and eleven days, to his most sweet son.
EDCS-19700710.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Brittius Germanus, recording his age and a dedication from his parent.

EDCS-19700711.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Certa, dated by her age.

EDCS-19700712.translation: Claudia Innocentia, a most honorable woman, is buried here. Claudia Innocentia, her granddaughter, made this.
EDCS-19700712.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudia Innocentia, erected by her granddaughter, also named Claudia Innocentia.

EDCS-19700713.translation: Felicitas, a woman of all goodness, who lived 30 years, is buried here. She was laid to rest on the 16th day before the Kalends of March during the consulship of [---].
EDCS-19700713.summary: This is a tombstone for Felicitas, a woman of great virtue, providing her age and date of burial, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-19700714.translation: Fermosanus, a priest, rests here in the sleep of peace. I believe I will rise again before my creator. I beg you all, in the Lord Jesus Christ, pray for me, a sinner. Kalends [---].
EDCS-19700714.summary: This is a tombstone for Fermosanus, a priest, requesting prayers for his soul and expressing faith in resurrection.

EDCS-19700715.translation: Flavius Leontius Innocens, who lived 24 years and 5 months, who died on the Kalends of September.
EDCS-19700715.summary: This is a tombstone for Flavius Leontius Innocens, detailing his age at death and the date of his passing.

EDCS-19700717.translation: Guttus, an acolyte of the holy church of Capua, who lived more or less 28 years, rests here in the sleep of peace. He was laid to rest on the day of the Savior.
EDCS-19700717.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Guttus, an acolyte of the church in Capua, providing his approximate age and date of burial.

EDCS-19700719.translation: I beg you all, pray for me, for the Lord Leo, a priest. Lord Jesus Christ, who formed me, have mercy on me forever.
EDCS-19700719.summary: This is a tombstone with a plea for prayers for Leo, a priest, and an invocation for mercy from Jesus Christ.

EDCS-19700724.translation: Secundus, a boy who lived 22 years, is buried here.
EDCS-19700724.summary: This is a tombstone for a young boy named Secundus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-19700725.translation: To the memory of Trifottinus, who lived 35 years, 2 months, and 20 days. Ladice, his wife, with whom I lived 2 years and 2 months, [erected this] for him who deserved well.
EDCS-19700725.summary: This tombstone commemorates Trifottinus, detailing his age and length of marriage, erected by his wife Ladice.

EDCS-19700726.translation: To Benustilla, who lived with me for 65 years, in peace, who deserved well.
EDCS-19700726.summary: This tombstone honors Benustilla, who lived with the dedicator for 65 years, noting her deserving nature.

EDCS-19700728.translation: Here lies the devout, here the modest, the faithful presbyter Bonus, who lived more or less the years gathered. The people of the city of Rome bequeathed him here. His friends inscribed this tombstone, warning and adjuring that whoever sends this monument in my name, may they depart to the condemnation of the Jews, and where the righteous will be rewarded, let them be condemned by the mouth of our Lord.
EDCS-19700728.summary: This is an epitaph for a presbyter named Bonus, dating to late antiquity, which includes a curse against those who would disturb the tomb and a condemnation of Jews.

EDCS-19700735.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace, Indignus the presbyter. I ask you, brothers.
EDCS-19700735.summary: This is a simple epitaph for a presbyter named Indignus, likely from late antiquity, requesting prayers from his brethren.

EDCS-19700736.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace, Venantius.
EDCS-19700736.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for Venantius, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-19700742.translation: To Julia Cornelia Paula, Augusta, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700742.summary: This is an inscription honoring Julia Cornelia Paula, styled Augusta, by local council decision, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-19700744.translation: To Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, son of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700744.summary: This inscription honors the Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus (likely Philippus II), son of Emperor Philippus I, by decree of the local council, dating to the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19700745.translation: To Salonina, Augusta, wife of our lord Gallienus Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700745.summary: This inscription honors Julia Cornelia Salonina, wife of Emperor Gallienus, by decree of the local council, dating to the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19700746.translation: To Publius Licinius Cornelius Valerianus, most noble Caesar, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700746.summary: This inscription honors the Caesar Publius Licinius Cornelius Valerianus (likely Valerian II), by decree of the local council, dating to the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-19700748.translation: The order and people of Trebula gave this statue to Vincentius Celsus, patron of causes, elected quaestor, advisor, for eternal memory.
EDCS-19700748.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue by the town council and people of Trebula to Vincentius Celsus, honoring his public service, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-19700750.translation: [---] MAR[---] / [---] MEC[---] / Marcus Heru[---], one of the four magistrates with judicial authority, [---]
EDCS-19700750.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning a magistrate (IIIIvir iure dicundo) named Marcus Heru[---], likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-19700751.translation: Aulus Rufrius Thamyris and Aulus Rufrius Elegans, Augustales, granted the place by decree of the decurions. And at its dedication, they gave to the Augustales for [a sum of] 5000 sesterces, and to the people for 4000 sesterces.
EDCS-19700751.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a public space by two Augustales, Aulus Rufrius Thamyris and Aulus Rufrius Elegans, by decree of the decurions, with a record of funds contributed, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-19700754.translation: under the arbitration of Anthochus, the freedman.
EDCS-19700754.summary: This inscription records an arbitration, likely related to a legal or property matter, overseen by the freedman Anthochus.

EDCS-19700755.translation: [son] of Numerius, Ruf[---], [son] of Aufustia, [son] of his mother.
EDCS-19700755.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph, naming individuals and their relationships, possibly belonging to a child or relative of Aufustia.

EDCS-19700756.translation: Marcus Marius Sophus, son of Marcus, of the Pupinia tribe, [erected this] for his son Lupercus, son of Marcus, of the Pupinia tribe.
EDCS-19700756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Marius Sophus for his son Lupercus, indicating a family memorial.

EDCS-19700757.translation: from the will, 60 sesterces, under the arbitration of Anterus, possibly a freedman.
EDCS-19700757.summary: This inscription details a bequest of 60 sesterces, to be administered according to the will of the deceased and the arbitration of Anterus.

EDCS-19700763.translation: To Licinius Cornelius Salo, the most noble Caesar Valerian, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700763.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Valerian, likely erected by the town council (decurions).

EDCS-19700764.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pious, Fortunate, Invictus Augustus, and to the most noble Caesar Marcus Aurelius Maximian [---]
EDCS-19700764.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely erected by a public body.

EDCS-19700766.translation: To our Lord Galerius Valerius Maximian, the most noble Caesar.
EDCS-19700766.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Maximian, acknowledging him as a ruler and 'most noble Caesar'.

EDCS-19700768.translation: To Quintus Gavius Proculus, son of Quintus, grandson of Quintus, great-grandson of Quintus, great-great-grandson of Quintus, great-great-great-grandson of Quintus, of the Falerna tribe, tribune of the 15th cohort of Volunteers, tribune of the 8th Augustan legion, by the decurions, the Augustales, and the people of Caiatia, to their most generous patron.
EDCS-19700768.summary: This is a dedication honoring Quintus Gavius Proculus for his public service and generosity by the civic and religious bodies of Caiatia.

EDCS-19700769.translation: To Quintus Gavius Tranquillus, son of Quintus, of the Falerna tribe, quaestor of the city, quaestor of the Narbonensis province, by the council of decurions and the people, to their most generous patron.
EDCS-19700769.summary: This is a dedication honoring Quintus Gavius Tranquillus for his public service as a quaestor by the town council and people.

EDCS-19700772.translation: Gaius Alfius Rufus, son of Gaius, [and] Publius V[---], as duovirs, carried out the construction and approved it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700772.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work or building, overseen by Gaius Alfius Rufus and Publius V[---] in their official capacity as duovirs, and approved by the town council.

EDCS-19700775.translation: Quintus Visellius Gallus, son of Quintus, and Marcus Gavius, son of Titus, as duovirs of five years, made the paving around the forum at their own expense.
EDCS-19700775.summary: This inscription records the construction of paving around the forum by two duovirs.

EDCS-19700776.translation: Marcus Herennius Gallus, son of Marcus, and Quintus Veserius, son of Quintus, as duovirs of five years, had the work carried out and approved by decree of the decurions; the architect was Hospes, slave of Appia.
EDCS-19700776.summary: This inscription records the construction of a work, possibly a public building, overseen by two duovirs and approved by the town council, mentioning the architect.

EDCS-19700778.translation: Marcus Ofilius Tertius, freedman of Marcus and of a woman, as living master of the Mercuriales, [dedicated this] for himself, his family, and Quartae, a freedwoman.
EDCS-19700778.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a freedman who was the master of the Mercuriales guild.

EDCS-19700779.translation: To Lucius Pacideius Carpianus, son of Lucius, grandson of Lucius, great-grandson of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, a splendid Roman knight, who held the priesthood of the Lanuvines, patron of the municipium of Caiatia, and also of the colony of Allifae, and patron and curator of the public affairs of Atina, and also of Saepinum and Teanum Apulum. His wife Domitia Galatia, and his daughters Marcia, a most distinguished woman, and his sons Carpiani, Senior and Junior, [dedicated this].
EDCS-19700779.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Pacideius Carpianus, a prominent local official and patron of several communities, by his wife and sons.

EDCS-19700784.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph commemorating a father and mother.

EDCS-19700791.translation: Quintus Gavius Anoptes, freedman of Quintus, while living, [dedicated this] for himself and for Quintus Gavius Agatocles, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-19700791.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedman for himself and another freedman.

EDCS-19700792.translation: Livi Felcionis made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-19700792.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Livi Felcionis for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-19700794.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication by Caius(?) Neratius.

EDCS-19700795.translation: The patron, Caius Numisius Eronis, freedman of Caius, made [this]; [his bones] are laid here.
EDCS-19700795.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument built by a freedman for his patron.

EDCS-19700797.translation: To Pontidia, daughter of Sexion. Lucius Charindus [dedicated this]. (The meaning of O N S F is uncertain, possibly related to funerary rites or status.)
EDCS-19700797.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Pontidia, daughter of Sexion, by Lucius Charindus.

EDCS-19700798.translation: Under the supervision of Sampsaronis and perhaps Philerotis.
EDCS-19700798.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the supervisors or overseers of a project, possibly related to public works or a building, with names of Greek origin.

EDCS-19700803.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Hedulis, a sweet, modest, and kind woman who lived more or less 20 years; she was buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of October in the consulship of the most distinguished Flavius Basilius.
EDCS-19700803.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Hedulis, who died around the age of 20 and was buried during the consulship of Flavius Basilius.

EDCS-19700804.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Rusticiana, who lived nine years and twelve days; she was buried on the Kalends of July, thirteen years after the consulship of the most distinguished Basilius.
EDCS-19700804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Rusticiana, who died at the age of 9 and was buried thirteen years after the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19700806.translation: To Marcus Agrippa, patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19700806.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or offering to Marcus Agrippa, designated as a patron, authorized by a decree of the local council (decurions).

EDCS-19700813.translation: Lucius Bruttius Epaphroditus, freedman of Lucius and Marcus, for himself and for Brittia Quarta, freedwoman of Marcus, and for his own family.
EDCS-19700813.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Bruttius Epaphroditus, a freedman, who made provision for himself, his wife Brittia Quarta, and their dependents.

EDCS-19700814.translation: Quintus Fabius Philadelphus [---] to his coliberta [---] his [---].
EDCS-19700814.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated by Quintus Fabius Philadelphus to his coliberta (a female freedwoman or fellow freedwoman).

EDCS-19700820.translation: Here rests in peace Beatilla Lucilla, [aged] 22, who lived happily, died happily, [and may] those who read [this be happy].
EDCS-19700820.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Beatilla Lucilla, who died at the age of 22, with a wish for the happiness of the reader.

EDCS-19700821.translation: Here rests in peace Maximina, a distinguished woman who lived 28 years, 4 months, and 12 days; she was buried on Friday, the 9th day before the Kalends of November, in the 18th year after the consulship of the most distinguished Basilius, in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-19700821.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maximina, who died at the age of 28 years, 4 months, and 12 days, and was buried during a specific year and indiction following the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-19700823.translation: Gaius Hinoleios, freedman of Caius, dedicated this gift to Apollon.
EDCS-19700823.summary: This is a dedication of a gift or offering by a freedman named Gaius Hinoleios to the god Apollon.

EDCS-19700836.translation: Lucius Calvius Zetus, freedman of Lucius, a sevir and Augustalis, for himself and for his patron Lucius Calvius Hedulus, freedman of Lucius, and for Atidia Tertia, freedwoman (of a woman), his wife, and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-19700836.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Calvius Zetus, a sevir and Augustalis, who made provision for himself, his patron, his wife, and his freed dependents.

EDCS-19700837.translation: To Gaius Cordius Sosigenes, freedman of Gaius, Augustalis, and to Maculonia Secunda, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-19700837.summary: This is a funerary dedication to two individuals, Gaius Cordius Sosigenes and Maculonia Secunda, one of whom, Gaius Cordius Sosigenes, held the position of Augustalis.

EDCS-19700839.translation: His father erected [this monument] to Gaius Flavius Pollio Auguralis, grandson of Gaius, great-grandson of Gaius, the IIvir iure dicundo, for whom a place was granted by senatorial decree via tablet.
EDCS-19700839.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a father for his son, Gaius Flavius Pollio Auguralis, who held the office of IIvir iure dicundo and for whom land was allocated by senatorial decree.

EDCS-19800051.translation: The bones of Quintus Numpsius Nicephorus, freedman of Quintus, are located here. Carania Philumina, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife.
EDCS-19800051.summary: This inscription records the burial place of Quintus Numpsius Nicephorus and his wife Carania Philumina.

EDCS-19800054.translation: Gaius Octavius Philodespotus, freedman of Gaius, for himself and for Pactumeia Veneria, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Primogenus, a slave. This monument or tomb shall not pass to the heir.
EDCS-19800054.summary: This is an funerary epitaph by Gaius Octavius Philodespotus for himself, his wife Pactumeia Veneria, and a slave named Primogenus, stipulating that the property will not pass to an heir.

EDCS-19800057.translation: Of Lucius Ofillius, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-19800057.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Lucius Ofillius, freedman of Lucius, possibly as part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-19800058.translation: To the genius of Ofillius Rufus.
EDCS-19800058.summary: This is a dedication to the genius (guardian spirit) of Ofillius Rufus.

EDCS-19800060.translation: For Ofillia Rufa, freedwoman of Lucius. This monument or tomb shall not pass to the heir.
EDCS-19800060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ofillia Rufa, freedwoman of Lucius, with a clause preventing the property from passing to an heir.

EDCS-19800063.translation: Rufa, freedwoman of Dianaes, made [this] for Marcus Orfius, son of Marcus, and for her husband.
EDCS-19800063.summary: This inscription records that Rufa, a freedwoman, commissioned a monument for her husband Marcus Orfius and herself.

EDCS-19800064.translation: Iadius, freedman of Gaius, son of Iadius, [from] Q R Panis, to his wife.
EDCS-19800064.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Iadius to his wife, identified as a freedman of Gaius and son of Iadius.

EDCS-19800065.translation: Gaius Ovius Sotericus, freedman of Gaius; Gaius Ovius Eros, freedman of Gaius; Gaius Ovius Carito, freedman of Gaius [---]; they made [this] from their own [means].
EDCS-19800065.summary: This inscription records that three individuals, Gaius Ovius Sotericus, Gaius Ovius Eros, and Gaius Ovius Carito, all freedmen of Gaius, jointly commissioned this monument from their own resources.

EDCS-19800066.translation: Gaius Ovius Surus made this at his own expense for his patrons. Gaius Ovius Parnaces, freedman of Gaius. Fabia Cosmi[3], freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-19800066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for two freedmen and one freedwoman, possibly related, with the first part indicating a contribution for patrons.

EDCS-19800067.translation: Publius Amathystus for himself and his successors, and no one else.
EDCS-19800067.summary: This epitaph records a burial plot reserved by Publius Amathystus for himself and his successors.

EDCS-19800069.summary: This is a simple greeting inscribed for Pacia, daughter of Tiberius.

EDCS-19800071.translation: To Gaius Papius Philemon, freedman of Gaius. To Papia Philema, freedwoman of Gaius, daughter of Papia. To Papia Salv[i]a, freedwoman [of Gaius?], under the supervision of Faustus.
EDCS-19800071.summary: This epitaph commemorates at least three individuals, likely freedmen and freedwomen of the same patron, with a mention of supervision by Faustus.

EDCS-19800072.summary: This is a simple epitaph identifying Papia Restituta.

EDCS-19800074.translation: To Quintus Papirius, son of Publius. Eucumene, freedwoman of Quintus, daughter of Quintus Papirius, for herself and her patron.
EDCS-19800074.summary: This epitaph is dedicated by Eucumene, a freedwoman and daughter of Quintus Papirius, for herself and her patron.

EDCS-19800077.translation: The bones of Parvilia Philumina, freedwoman of Caius, are here [buried] with Caius Parvilius Cerdo, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-19800077.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Parvilia Philumina alongside Caius Parvilius Cerdo.

EDCS-19800083.translation: To Publius Petilius Clemens and Aufeia Faustae.
EDCS-19800083.summary: This inscription records the names of Publius Petilius Clemens and Aufeia Faustae, possibly as dedicants or recipients of an honor.

EDCS-19800085.translation: The bones of Luci liberto Philogeni are here by testament.
EDCS-19800085.summary: This funerary inscription states that the bones of Philogenus, a freedman of Lucius, are interred here according to his will.

EDCS-19800086.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Philomusus to his fellow slave, Primae.

EDCS-19800087.translation: For the incomparably pious, who deserved well, who lived 5 years, 9 months, and 10 days, his most unhappy father and Pieris made this for their wife.
EDCS-19800087.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child, set up by his father and mother.

EDCS-19800090.translation: Publius Plotrius, freedman of Publius, [---]. Plotia Zmyrna, [---] at her own expense.
EDCS-19800090.summary: An inscription likely related to a tomb, mentioning freedmen and patrons, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-19800091.translation: Lucius Plotius Philippus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Staia Rufa, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-19800091.summary: An epitaph recording a man dedicating a tomb for himself and a woman, likely his wife.

EDCS-19800093.translation: Pontiena Polla for herself and for Lucius Cominius Lucrio and Lucius Cominius Gratus.
EDCS-19800093.summary: An inscription indicating a woman dedicating a burial space for herself and two men, likely family members.

EDCS-19800094.translation: Marcus Pompeius Apollonius for himself and for his wife Pontia Hilara // for his freedman Marcus Pompeius Felix / for his freedman Marcus Pompeius Celer / for his freedman Marcus Pompeius Acutus // for Quintus Masurius Atticus / for Quintus Masurius Felix / for Pactumeia Campana // It is not permitted for these to be inscribed unless whose names are written and for whom I have provided // for Marcus Pompeius Ithacus / for Pompeia Urbana, freedwoman of Ithacus.
EDCS-19800094.summary: An inscription detailing the beneficiaries of a tomb, including the dedicator, his wife, freedmen, and others, with a specific clause about who is permitted burial rights.

EDCS-19800095.translation: Titus Pompennius Chrysogonus for Caius Hostius Suavius and Caius Hostius Secundus and his own family.
EDCS-19800095.summary: An inscription by Titus Pompennius Chrysogonus dedicating a tomb or burial plot for two individuals and his own family.

EDCS-19800104.translation: By decree of the Senate, for the honor of Quintus Paconius Leptas, son of Quintus, aqueducts and channels were established and constructed so that purer water could be more conveniently led into his house, because he had often served and deserved well of the state. Quintus Paconius Leptas, son of Quintus, a quinquennial duovir, awarded the contract by decree of the Senate and approved it.
EDCS-19800104.summary: A public works inscription commissioned by the Senate and executed by a local magistrate, Quintus Paconius Leptas, to improve water supply to his house due to his public service.

EDCS-19800105.translation: For Caius Patercilius, son of Caius, of the Pob(lilia) tribe, duovir with judicial power. Patercilia Asia, freedwoman of Caius, for her patron and for herself.
EDCS-19800105.summary: An inscription for a magistrate, set up by his freedwoman who also claims a space for herself.

EDCS-19800110.translation: Augustalis, with triumphal ornaments, paved with his own money the road from the alleyway of the temple of Juno Lucina up to the temple of Matuta, and the slope from the gate to the Gisarii of the Stellate Gate, and the wide road to the Left Gate, and from the forum to the Domestic Gate.
EDCS-19800110.summary: An inscription recording public works, specifically road paving, funded by a man named Augustalis who held high military honors.

EDCS-19800111.translation: TEM SIBE Caius Ervincus sevir Caius Corv
EDCS-19800111.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely commemorating a man named Caius Ervincus, who held the position of sevir, and possibly another individual.

EDCS-19800116.translation: With all his money, [name], [title], Quarta [restored name] dedicated the temple.
EDCS-19800116.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the dedication of a temple by an official named Quarta.

EDCS-19800118.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Lucius Atinius Syneros made the monument.

EDCS-19800120.summary: This inscription records Diodorus purifying something, possibly a religious site or object.

EDCS-19800122.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Annius and Annia.

EDCS-19800124.translation: The bones of Publius Batonius Davus are located here.
EDCS-19800124.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Publius Batonius Davus.

EDCS-19800129.summary: This inscription likely identifies Callinice, a freedwoman of Furia, and possibly mentions her profession or a related detail.

EDCS-19800132.translation: Lucilia Romula, daughter of Marcus, patroness, by will requested, on the land, her heir.
EDCS-19800132.summary: This funerary inscription states that Lucilia Romula, daughter of Marcus and a patroness, designated her heir in her will for a plot of land.

EDCS-19800133.translation: The bones of Minucia Veneria, freedwoman of Caius, are located here; she lived for 18 years.
EDCS-19800133.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Minucia Veneria, freedwoman of Caius, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-19800138.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Procula and her son Proculus, their heirs.
EDCS-19800138.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades for Procula and her son Proculus, with their heirs also mentioned.

EDCS-19800140.translation: Tillia Prisca made this for herself and for Tillius Faustillus Murrasius Optatus.
EDCS-19800140.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Tillia Prisca dedicated the monument for herself and for Tillius Faustillus Murrasius Optatus.

EDCS-19800141.translation: Of Marcus Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the Tromentina tribe, from Caleo.
EDCS-19800141.summary: This is a personal funerary inscription identifying Marcus Tuccius by his name, filiation, and tribe.

EDCS-19800142.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Prisca, daughter of Sextus Tuppurius, lived 28 years, 6 months, 23 days; if the premature fates of destiny had not intervened, she would have had to read this tombstone of her parents before them.
EDCS-19800142.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Prisca, recording her lifespan and lamenting her premature death.

EDCS-19800144.translation: Aulus Valgius Philomusus made this for Publius Valgius Philero, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-19800144.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Aulus Valgius Philomusus for his freedman Publius Valgius Philero.

EDCS-19800145.translation: To Phro, Veturia to her husband.
EDCS-19800145.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Veturia to her husband Phro.

EDCS-19800146.translation: To Marcus Visellius Bithus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-19800146.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Visellius Bithus, freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-19800150.translation: [---]iae, daughter of [---], of the [---]llae family, the most [---]imae, [---]us son of Marcus, [---]pius, dedicated [---].
EDCS-19800150.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription that likely names a woman and her father and includes an unknown male dedicator.

EDCS-19800159.translation: Menius Casia Acila brought back the fates for Junius Setius.
EDCS-19800159.summary: This is a funerary epitaph possibly recording a death and perhaps linking two families through a marriage or other connection.

EDCS-19800167.translation: Dindia Macolnia gave [this] to her daughter.
EDCS-19800167.summary: This is a dedication from Dindia Macolnia to her daughter.

EDCS-19800168.translation: Novius Plautius made me in Rome.
EDCS-19800168.summary: This is a dedication of a manufactured object (likely a statue or similar) made by Novius Plautius in Rome.

EDCS-19800219.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing only a personal name, Lucius Poulilios.

EDCS-19800220.translation: Resting place of Lucia, daughter of Cornelius Lucius.
EDCS-19800220.summary: This inscription is a funerary marker for Lucia, daughter of Cornelius Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800230.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mesa Iris, who lived 25 years, made this out of devotion.
EDCS-19800230.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes by Mesa Iris, who died at age 25, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800231.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name or a name with a cognomen, possibly of a freedman, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800233.translation: Isius Tersia, freedwoman of Lucius, from Chios.
EDCS-19800233.summary: This inscription identifies Isius Tersia as a freedwoman of Lucius and indicates her origin from Chios, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800243.translation: Barbarus lives in peace, laid to rest on the thirteenth day before the Kalends.
EDCS-19800243.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Barbarus on a specific date (likely December 20th), indicating peace in death during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800245.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription recording the death of Severus at the age of 20, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800247.translation: To the most holy Augustus. Ranuus Romanus [has dedicated this] because he carried out two baths for him [with zeal].
EDCS-19800247.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Augustus by Ranuus Romanus, praising him for building two baths, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-19800248.translation: Retus Vedodius Vibius, Autrodius, Cai Spurius Racectius, Spurius Teditius, son of Spurius, commissioned the statues to be erected.
EDCS-19800248.summary: This inscription records a commission for erecting statues by several individuals, including Retus Vedodius Vibius, Autrodius, Cai Spurius Racectius, and Spurius Teditius, son of Spurius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800249.translation: To Appia Veturia Airula Sabinilla, his most illustrious wife, for her husband O[---]P[---]DO[---]SE[---]OROP[---]O[---]P[---]N[---] POS[---]R[---] and patrons [---]DIC[---]M[---]
EDCS-19800249.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription is a dedication to Appia Veturia Airula Sabinilla, described as the wife of the dedicator and also mentions patrons, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800250.translation: To Lucius Vibius Fortunatus, son of Laurentius, [son of] Lavinius, augural haruspex of our Augustus, master of studies, procurator of ducenarius rank, of the office of inheritances at Rome, for his exceptional love towards him, the order and people of Foropopuli offer this to him as a citizen and patron.
EDCS-19800250.summary: This dedication from the town council and people of Foropopuli honors Lucius Vibius Fortunatus, a significant imperial official involved in divination and administration in Rome, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-19800252.translation: To Tiberius Julius Italicus, son of Tiberius, of the Falernian tribe, centurion of the Legio VII Macedonica, centurion of the Legio XV Primigenia, centurion of the Legio XIII Gemina, chief centurion, [to a leader] of the decurions(?).
EDCS-19800252.summary: This inscription honors Tiberius Julius Italicus, a career soldier who reached the rank of chief centurion and possibly served as a leader of decurions, likely set up on a military monument.

EDCS-19800253.translation: Because of the favor of the divine majesty, Aeterius Minucius Aeterius has been treated with consideration in our minds; after performing all the honors merited by our fatherland, he also administered the sacred administration in the city; the centonarii have decreed that a statue should be erected before his seat, as a worthy patron, on the sixth day before the Ides of May, when Lupicinus and Iovinus were consuls.
EDCS-19800253.summary: This inscription records the decree by the centonarii (a guild of cloth workers) to erect a statue honoring Aeterius Minucius Aeterius for his service to the state and city, dated to 6 May, with specific consuls mentioned.

EDCS-19800254.translation: The entire populace of the citizens of Forum Popilii indicates by your labors, Gaius Minucius Aeterius Senior, a man of industry, that you are a greater honor to our fatherland, worthy of the curia and a patron of the people; you have already received your first sons in order and your grandsons into magistracy; the entire populace, together with our children, has decreed that a statue should be erected to you, a worthy patron, in a most frequented place of our fatherland.
EDCS-19800254.summary: This inscription records the decree by the entire populace of Forum Popilii to erect a statue honoring Gaius Minucius Aeterius Senior for his dedicated service and importance to the city and its people.

EDCS-19800259.translation: Curtia Epistolio, freedwoman of Gaius, made [this] for herself and for her husband Gaius Sextius, with the approval of Gaius Sextius Anchialus and Iutor, his freedman.
EDCS-19800259.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Curtia Epistolio, a freedwoman, and her husband Gaius Sextius, indicating it was a private tomb commissioned by specific individuals.

EDCS-19800260.translation: Gaius Julius Agathopus, freedman of Philippus, and Varia Nape, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-19800260.summary: This inscription simply lists the names of two individuals, Gaius Julius Agathopus and Varia Nape, both freedpersons, likely marking a shared tomb or property.

EDCS-19800262.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning the name 'Ciale', daughter of Lucius, and another name fragment 'vinicia'.

EDCS-19800263.translation: To the newly found Nymphs of the villa Surdiniana, from Amemptus, freedman of Caesar, and Orchivia Phoebe, and Rhodinus, their freedman, having been led to that villa, as they themselves revealed themselves to her majesty; in the consulship of Emperor Caesar Vespasian (for the 3rd time) and Marcus Cocceius Nerva.
EDCS-19800263.summary: This inscription dedicates an altar or shrine to newly discovered Nymphs at the villa Surdiniana, likely by the villa's owners and their freedmen, dating to 71 AD.

EDCS-19800266.translation: Sextus Caecilius Birronianus, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, scribe, record keeper, quaestor three times, decurial official, quinquennial magistrate, patron of the colony of Sinuesse, made the podium of the amphitheater from the ground up, with gratitude.
EDCS-19800266.summary: This inscription records the construction of the amphitheater's podium by Sextus Caecilius Birronianus, a prominent local official and patron of the colony of Sinuesse.

EDCS-19800272.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Marcus Maecius Arator, son of Quintus, of the Aemilia tribe.
EDCS-19800272.summary: This is a dedication of an altar or shrine to the god Mercury by Marcus Maecius Arator, likely a private individual.

EDCS-19800273.translation: To Matidia, daughter of Augustus, of the Divine Marciana Augusta, granddaughter of the Divine Sabina Augusta, sister of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, aunt [of the Emperor]; by decree of the decurions of Minturnae.
EDCS-19800273.summary: This inscription honors Matidia, a member of the imperial family, indicating her relation to various Augusti and Augustae, and was erected by a decree of the decurions of Minturnae.

EDCS-19800274.translation: To Matidia, daughter of the deified Augustus, granddaughter of the deified Augusta Marciana, sister of the deified Augusta Sabina, aunt of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-19800274.summary: This inscription honors Matidia, aunt of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely erected by a member of the imperial family or administration.

EDCS-19800275.translation: To Matidia, daughter of the deified Augustus, sister of the deified Augusta Sabina, aunt of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland. By Agathemerus, freedman and procurator.
EDCS-19800275.summary: This inscription honors Matidia, aunt of Emperor Antoninus Pius, erected by her freedman and procurator.

EDCS-19800276.translation: To Matidia Augusta, daughter of the deified Augustus, sister of the deified Augusta Sabina, aunt of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland. By Titus Flavius Onesimus Campanus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-19800276.summary: This inscription honors Matidia Augusta, aunt of Emperor Antoninus Pius, erected by her freedman.

EDCS-19800277.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland. By Suessani.
EDCS-19800277.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus, likely erected by the people or officials of a locality named Suessani.

EDCS-19800279.translation: To Lucius Albinus Saturninus, son of Aulus, of the voting tribe Quirina, consul, proconsul of the province of Asia, legate of the Emperor with praetorian authority in Pontus and Bithynia, proconsul of the province of Achaea, prefect of the Saturnine treasury, legate of the Emperor in Asturica and Callaecia, urban praetor, aedile of the plebs, member of the Sodales Antoniniani, quaestor, patron of the colony, curator of the colony, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-19800279.summary: This is a lengthy honorific inscription detailing the extensive senatorial and administrative career of Lucius Albinus Saturninus, likely set up by his city.

EDCS-19800438.translation: To the deified Fortuna. By Lucius Servienus Diogenes, freedman of Lucius, Augustalis, vestiarius.
EDCS-19800438.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Augusta, likely made by a freedman named Lucius Servienus Diogenes who was an Augustalis and a cloth merchant.

EDCS-20100046.translation: To Gaius Poppaeus Sabinianus, prefect of the annona, by the Colony of Ostia.
EDCS-20100046.summary: This is a dedication by the Colony of Ostia to Gaius Poppaeus Sabinianus, who held the important office of prefect of the annona (overseer of the grain supply).

EDCS-20100052.summary: This is a short Christian epitaph or devotional phrase.

EDCS-20100053.summary: This is a fragment likely naming a bishop named Probinus, possibly part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-20100056.translation: Innocentius the archpriest made this, from the gifts of God and Saint Zmarandus.
EDCS-20100056.summary: This inscription records the construction or dedication by Innocentius, an archpriest, attributing the work to divine and saintly favor.

EDCS-20100059.translation: Lucius Fictorius, freedman of Publius Marcus, gladly gives his tenth [part of his earnings] to Hercules as a deserved reward.
EDCS-20100059.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by a freedman who is gladly giving a tenth of his earnings, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100062.translation: The doctor Timocles gladly gives this gift to Hercules, having made his tenth [payment].
EDCS-20100062.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by a doctor named Timocles who is giving a gift after making a tenth payment, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100063.translation: Lucius Cretarius, son of Caius, gladly gives this [gift?] to Hercules, as deserved, [having paid?] his tenth.
EDCS-20100063.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by Lucius Cretarius, son of Caius, who is gladly giving a gift as deserved, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100068.summary: This is a very brief record of a payment of 12 asses by someone named Asianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100070.summary: This is a name, Passerinus, with an epithet indicating his profession (fellator), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100075.summary: This is a personal name, Rusticelius Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100076.summary: This is a brief record of a payment of 10 asses by someone named Numpuce, who is described with pleasant manners, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100077.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful translation or summary, but it appears to be from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100078.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful translation or summary, but it appears to be from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100083.summary: This inscription records a date, Iulia, on the Ides of November, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20100090.translation: To Lucius Ianus, greetings from your master.
EDCS-20100090.summary: This is a private greeting from a master to his slave, Lucius Ianus.

EDCS-20100094.summary: This is a simple farewell inscription, likely from a private context, to Severius, a freedman.

EDCS-20100097.translation: Hermeros to his mistress Primigenia: come to Puteoli in the Tyanian district and ask the money-changer Messius for Hermeros of Phoebus.
EDCS-20100097.summary: This is a request or message from a slave named Hermeros to his mistress, directing someone to find another individual in Puteoli.

EDCS-20100098.translation: [...] and [...] L. Caninius [...] L. Caninius Taurus [...] of Myronis [...] that the aforementioned girl be healthy, free from theft and harm, that she is not a runaway, and that the double penalty according to the edict of the curule aediles, as is customary, for the purchase and sale of slaves this year, which was stipulated to be given correctly and comprehended, Calatoria [...] acted as surety; Gaius Julius Phoebus pledged. Done at Herculaneum [...] during the consulship of [...].
EDCS-20100098.summary: This inscription appears to be a legal document, likely a contract or stipulation concerning the sale of a female slave, detailing guarantees and penalties, dated to a specific consulship and possibly at Herculaneum.

EDCS-20100105.translation: Of Lucius Arruntius Stella, under the paint workshop.
EDCS-20100105.summary: This inscription likely marks a location or identifies a workshop associated with Lucius Arruntius Stella, possibly related to painting or pigment production.

EDCS-20100106.summary: This is a simple ownership or dedication inscription, naming Quintus Volusius Saturninus.

EDCS-20100107.translation: Of Titus Sabidius Maximus, procurator of the Emperor for grain.
EDCS-20100107.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Sabidius Maximus, an imperial official responsible for the grain supply.

EDCS-20100261.translation: Servius Fulvius Flaccus, son of Quintus, commissioned the wall from the spoils of war.
EDCS-20100261.summary: This inscription records a public works project, the construction of a wall, commissioned by Servius Fulvius Flaccus using military spoils.

EDCS-20100271.translation: Geminia, daughter of Caius, wife of Gnaeus Vatronius.
EDCS-20100271.summary: This is a funerary or family inscription identifying Geminia by her father and husband.

EDCS-20100272.translation: Publius Gessius Valas, son of Publius.
EDCS-20100272.summary: This is a personal identification, likely from a tombstone or public record, for Publius Gessius Valas.

EDCS-20100274.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100275.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100276.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100278.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100281.summary: This is a personal name with manumission information, likely indicating ownership or the deceased.

EDCS-20100282.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100283.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20100284.summary: This is a personal name, likely indicating ownership or the deceased on a tombstone.

EDCS-20400540.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix, son of Lucius, imperator, publicly
EDCS-20400540.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix, a prominent figure, likely for a public monument.

EDCS-20400542.translation: To Gaius Lievrius Tranquillus, a Tockian, a man of consular rank and patrician, the most splendid order of Suessa
EDCS-20400542.summary: This is a dedication by the distinguished council of Suessa to Gaius Lievrius Tranquillus, honoring his consular and patrician status.

EDCS-20400543.translation: The bathhouse of Lucius Maecius Pollus the younger.
EDCS-20400543.summary: This is a dedication of a bathhouse to Lucius Maecius Pollus the younger.

EDCS-20400544.translation: The council, people, and officials of Suessa, bound by love and benefits, have decreed that a statue be set up as an eternal testimony to Lucius Mamillianus Licinianus, a man of the highest distinction, son of Mamillianus Silvinianus, a man of the highest perfection, grandson of Mamillianus Crispus, count, great-grandson of Mamillianus Maximus, a man of the highest perfection, count, and further from the origin of the patrons, who discharged all honors and duties in his homeland with integrity, adding to the dignity of his origin. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400544.summary: This is a decree by the town council and people of Suessa to erect a statue in honor of Lucius Mamillianus Licinianus, a distinguished local official, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-20400547.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Vitius, son of Titus, and Hon[oratus] Vitius, son of Honoratus, [and their] descendants and family, [to their] son, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-20400547.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Vitius and his son Honoratus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, set up by senatorial decree.

EDCS-20400551.translation: To Marcus Tofellanus Murranus, freedman of Catulla, and his freedwoman Domitia, and to Tofellana Murrani, freedwoman of Murranus, and to Tofellana Fortunata, and to Marcus Tofellanus Honoratus, son of Marcus, and to his descendants and all his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-20400551.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Tofellanus Murranus and his extended family, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20400553.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabius Ianus to his most devoted mother, Aedredona, daughter of Altius Justus.
EDCS-20400553.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Aedredona, daughter of Altius Justus, made by her son Fabius Ianus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-20400555.translation: The ashes of Clodia Maxima, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-20400555.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ashes of Clodia Maxima, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-20400558.translation: To Gaius Julius Chrestus Secundus, freedman of Antoniana, most devoted.
EDCS-20400558.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Julius Chrestus Secundus, a freedman, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20400559.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iullia Aphrodisia rests here.
EDCS-20400559.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Iullia Aphrodisia rests here, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-20400565.translation: Titus Varius, son of Titus, of the Aemilia tribe, for himself, for his freedman Hilarus, for his freedman Optatus, and for his freedwoman Faustus, according to his will.
EDCS-20400565.summary: This is a funerary dedication established by Titus Varius for himself and his freedmen and freedwomen, as stipulated in his will, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20400566.translation: Lucius Vettius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, and Vettia Felix, freedwoman of mulieris.
EDCS-20400566.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vettius and Vettia Felix, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20400567.translation: Gaius Vicasius, son of Lucius, [erected this] according to his will.
EDCS-20400567.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Vicasius, whose monument was erected posthumously according to his will.

EDCS-20400568.translation: Helvia Galla, daughter of Lucius, sacred to Juno.
EDCS-20400568.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Juno by Helvia Galla, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-20400574.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar; the public assembly of the Teanenses dedicates this, with Pompeius Faustinus, most illustrious man, corrector of Campania, and Ovinius Gallicanus, most illustrious man, curator, most devoted to their divine majesty.
EDCS-20400574.summary: This is a dedication by the public assembly of Teanum to the emperor Flavius Valerius Constantinus, with local officials Pompeius Faustinus and Ovinius Gallicanus involved in the dedication.

EDCS-20400575.translation: Gaius Cabilenus Gallus, son of Gaius, from the Falernian tribe, of the Eighth Legion Mutinensis.
EDCS-20400575.summary: This is a military inscription identifying Gaius Cabilenus Gallus, son of Gaius, from the Falernian tribe, serving in the Eighth Legion Mutinensis.

EDCS-20400582.translation: Macqui [---], chief public priestess of Ceres.
EDCS-20400582.summary: This is an inscription honoring Macqui, who held the high public office of priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-20400583.translation: A place was granted by decree of the decurions to Staia Pietas, daughter of Marcus, first public priestess of Ceres.
EDCS-20400583.summary: This inscription records a plot of land granted by the town council to Staia Pietas, daughter of Marcus, the first public priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-20400584.translation: His wife SSIA D FS TICA [erected this] for Nasica, quinquennial magistrate, from his will, for 20,000 sesterces.
EDCS-20400584.summary: This funerary inscription states that the wife SSIA D FS TICA erected this monument for Nasica, a quinquennial magistrate, using funds from his will.

EDCS-20400585.translation: To Marcus Pactumeius Fautius, son of Marcus, second-rank magistrate with judicial powers, for the sake of honor, Doia Maior [erected this].
EDCS-20400585.summary: This is a dedication honoring Marcus Pactumeius Fautius, son of Marcus, a magistrate with judicial authority, erected by Doia Maior.

EDCS-20400589.translation: Marcus Aelius Sostratus, Naevia Firma, daughter of Lucius; Marcus Aelius Faustus.
EDCS-20400589.summary: This inscription appears to record a family relationship or inheritance involving Marcus Aelius Sostratus, Naevia Firma, and Marcus Aelius Faustus.

EDCS-20400592.translation: To Lucius Bruttius Festus, son of Lucius. [---]
EDCS-20400592.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Bruttius Festus, son of Lucius, possibly a funerary monument.

EDCS-20400593.translation: To Clodia Primitiva Teanensis, [she] made [this] for [her] well-deserving.
EDCS-20400593.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Clodia Primitiva, a woman from Teanum, by an unknown dedicator, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400598.translation: To Lucius Marius Africanus, son of Lucius. Herennia Paphie, freedwoman of Gaius Decimus, made [this].
EDCS-20400598.summary: A funerary dedication to Lucius Marius Africanus, made by his freedwoman Herennia Paphie, probably dating to the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20400599.summary: A fragmentary dedication, possibly funerary, to Gaius Pontius Messius.

EDCS-20400602.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning Quintus Rapidius, likely a dedication or tombstone from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400603.summary: A highly fragmented inscription possibly related to a will and the disposition of property or a monument.

EDCS-20400604.translation: To Marcus Seppius Philoxenus, freedman of Marcus, [with funds] of 10,000 sesterces by testament, under the supervision of Primigenia, his freedwoman.
EDCS-20400604.summary: A funerary dedication of Marcus Seppius Philoxenus, funded by his will and overseen by his freedwoman Primigenia, indicating a date in the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400605.translation: [---] Marcus Staius Felix made [this] for his well-deserving freedwoman.
EDCS-20400605.summary: A funerary monument erected by Marcus Staius Felix for his freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400606.translation: To Turia Sabina, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-20400606.summary: A dedication, likely funerary, to Turia Sabina, daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-20400608.translation: Gnaeus Vesiculanus, son of Marcus, [erected this] to his wife Turia Sabina, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-20400608.summary: A funerary monument erected by Gnaeus Vesiculanus to his wife Turia Sabina.

EDCS-20400612.translation: [---] Duumvir for dispensing justice. [---] Calpurnius Stel, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe.
EDCS-20400612.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning a magistrate (duumvir) and a member of the Calpurnia gens, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-20400613.translation: Opontia, daughter of Publius, and sister.
EDCS-20400613.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Opontia, daughter and sister.

EDCS-20400615.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Ursidia Galla.

EDCS-20400617.translation: Here lies Domitia, a Roman citizen who lived for more or less 32 years, buried in peace in the Ides of April, ten years after the consulship of the most distinguished consul Basil, in the 13th indiction.
EDCS-20400617.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Domitia, a Roman citizen, with a precise burial date.

EDCS-20400620.translation: To Marcus Agrippa, son of Lucius, patron, by the villagers whose buildings are here.
EDCS-20400620.summary: This dedication honors Marcus Agrippa as a patron by the villagers of a vicus.

EDCS-20400621.translation: Marcus Ennius Vicetinus, son of Manius, of the Menenia tribe, scribe of the curule aediles, armamentarius, decurion of the vicus, decurion of the colony of Saturnia, aedile of the colony of Iulia Felici Classica Suessa. Caius Satilius Pileros, freedman of Caius, attendant of the tribune of the plebs. Satilia, wife.
EDCS-20400621.summary: This is an extensive career inscription for Marcus Ennius Vicetinus, detailing his various civic and administrative roles in several Roman colonies and towns.

EDCS-20400625.translation: To Marcus Baro(nius), son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400625.summary: This is an inscription honoring Marcus Baro(nius).

EDCS-20400626.translation: Publius Stabilio, son of Publius, made this for himself and for his patron Publius <H=IL>ippius, son of Publius, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-20400626.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Publius Stabilio for himself and his patron, Publius <H=IL>ippius.

EDCS-20400628.translation: His children made this for their most devoted parents: for their son Priscus, chief centurion, and for his wife Pollia Prima.
EDCS-20400628.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by children for their parents, a chief centurion and his wife.

EDCS-20400633.translation: Sabidia Cornelia, daughter of Titus, of the Caepionis family, dedicated this gift to the Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-20400633.summary: This is a religious dedication of a gift to the Mother of the Gods by Sabidia Cornelia.

EDCS-20400636.translation: Marcus Valius, son of Caius, gave [this] willingly.
EDCS-20400636.summary: This is a dedication or offering made by Marcus Valius.

EDCS-20400638.translation: Marcus Antonius Crescens gave a place of a thousand feet for friendship to the Herculanii and Hervianii.
EDCS-20400638.summary: This inscription records a grant of land by Marcus Antonius Crescens to two collegia, likely for their use, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400640.translation: The worshippers of Jupiter Caelestis, Gaius [---]alus Justus, Gaius Balbius Speratus, [---] Venafranus Diogenes, [---]dius Cest[---], Gaius Distubuanus Ianuarius, [---] Clodius Primigenius, [---] Adiectus, [---] Secundus, [---]anus Primigenius, [---] Successus, [---]ius Antigonus, [---]VI VNAT[---], [---] Fontanus, [---] Saturnius, [---] Respectus, [---]ennius Verus.
EDCS-20400640.summary: This is a lengthy list of names, likely members of a collegium dedicated to Jupiter Caelestis, with many names being fragmentary, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400643.translation: A place was given to the craftsmen by Marcus Fulvius Marcellus.
EDCS-20400643.summary: This inscription records the grant of a location by Marcus Fulvius Marcellus to the guild of craftsmen, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400646.translation: The people of the city of Venafrum, with the entire multitude of the citizenry, reluctantly moved the statue of Antonius Justinianus, governor of the province of Samnium, begging him to accept it, and placed it because of his merits, by which, along with the most distinguished order, he restored a situation that had already collapsed for the happiness of the age.
EDCS-20400646.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Antonius Justinianus, governor of Samnium, by the citizens of Venafrum in recognition of his restoration of a collapsed structure, likely 3rd century AD.

EDCS-20400647.translation: The entire order and people of the city of Venafrum erected a statue to Marinius Flabius Marinius, an outstanding man, governor of the province, their patron.
EDCS-20400647.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Marinius Flabius Marinius, governor of the province and patron of Venafrum, by the city's order and people, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400649.translation: To Laberia Pompeiana, a most distinguished lady, wife of Marcus [Cl(audi) Claudi] Macrinus Vindex Hermog[e]nianus, a most distinguished man and former consular, for her most rare, exceptional, and generous affection towards him and his children, and her piety, Lucius Gabinius Cosmianus, pontifex, patron of the colony, and father-in-law through marriage, was granted a place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400649.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a place by Lucius Gabinius Cosmianus to his mother-in-law, Laberia Pompeiana, honouring her affection and piety, likely late 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-20400651.translation: The most distinguished order and the entire populace of the city of Venafrum established Maecius Felix, a most perfect man, defender of the city of Venafrum, possessor of the order, and ruler of the province of Samnium, in the vicus Ad Iunctivae, as patron, for his merit in matters concerning the state, and in remembrance of all the benefits which his ancestors had provided to the city.
EDCS-20400651.summary: This inscription records the establishment of Maecius Felix as patron of Venafrum and ruler of Samnium due to his public service and ancestral benefactions, date uncertain, likely 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-20400652.translation: To Sextus Pulfennius Salutarus, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, and Marcus Lucius Valerius Severus Plotinus Cilo, quaestor with pro-praetorian power in the province of Achaia, patron of the colony.
EDCS-20400652.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Sextus Pulfennius Salutarus and Marcus Lucius Valerius Severus Plotinus Cilo, who held various administrative and military posts and were patrons of the colony, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400656.translation: To Sextus Aulienus, son of Sextus, of the Aniensis tribe, primus pilus of the II legion, tribune of the soldiers, prefect of light-armed troops, prefect of the camp of Emperor Caesar Augustus and Tiberius Caesar Augustus, prefect of the fleet, prefect of the fabrum, duovir of Venafri and Foro Iuli, Augustalis priest. Nedymus and Gamus, freedmen.
EDCS-20400656.summary: This inscription honours Sextus Aulienus, detailing his extensive military and civic career, by his freedmen Nedymus and Gamus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-20400658.translation: To Gaius Licinius [---], soldier [---], from his will.
EDCS-20400658.summary: This inscription is a fragment indicating a bequest from the will of Gaius Licinius to a soldier, date uncertain.

EDCS-20400659.translation: To Marcus, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, for himself and for ...sia, freedwoman of Lucius, his wife, and for Marcus, son of Lucius, Sulla, tribune of the soldiers of the Legio II Augusta.
EDCS-20400659.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Marcus, his wife, and his son Sulla, who served as a military tribune, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20400662.translation: Valerius Dizon, a citizen of Philippopolis, centurion of the Legio IIII Flavia, served for 12 years.
EDCS-20400662.summary: This inscription records the service of Valerius Dizon, a centurion of the Legio IIII Flavia from Philippopolis, who completed 12 years of military service.

EDCS-20400666.translation: Gaius Aclutius Gallus, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, twice chief magistrate for building the city walls, twice prefect for dispensing justice, tribune of the soldiers of the Legio I, tribune of the soldiers of the Legio II Sabina.
EDCS-20400666.summary: This is an honorific inscription detailing the extensive public and military career of Gaius Aclutius Gallus, who held multiple high offices in his city and served as a military tribune in two legions.

EDCS-20400668.translation: Marcus Cassius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, ordered this by his will.
EDCS-20400668.summary: This inscription, likely funerary, indicates that Marcus Cassius made provisions for this monument in his will.

EDCS-20400670.translation: Quintus Ervius Bassus, son of Sextus, aedile of Venafrum, for Lusia Thais, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-20400670.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Ervius Bassus, an aedile of Venafrum, to Lusia Thais.

EDCS-20400671.translation: To Gaius Herennius Melas, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, as aedile and twice chief magistrate, was born at 10 AM on the 3rd day before the Nones of September, in the consulship of Lucius Nonius Asprenas; he dies at 10 AM on the 3rd day before the Nones of September, in the consulship of Aulus Gabinius Secundus, for his son Melanta.
EDCS-20400671.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking the birth and death dates of Gaius Herennius Melas, a local magistrate, and mentioning his son Melanta.

EDCS-20400672.translation: Sextus Herius Lepos dedicated the thresholds at his own expense.
EDCS-20400672.summary: This inscription records Sextus Herius Lepos dedicating thresholds, likely for a public building, at his own expense.

EDCS-20400673.translation: For Lucius Hostilius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, P[...]; for Publius Hostilius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, Pi[...], as aedile and chief magistrate; for Marcus Hostilius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, [...]; Hostilia, daughter of Lucius, Pri[...], his sister, made this.
EDCS-20400673.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Hostilia for her brothers Lucius, Publius, and Marcus Hostilius, all of the Teretina tribe, who held local magistracies.

EDCS-20400675.translation: To Gaius Menius Bassus, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, twice chief magistrate, pontiff, and to Munatia Caediana, daughter of Lucius, his wife, a woman of unknown chastity, his parents Meni Bassi, this excellent young man, proved this woman to be so much his [ideal] that his husband, whom she saw as his only one, ... Lucius Munatius Successus for his daughter.
EDCS-20400675.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records the virtues of Munatia Caediana, wife of Gaius Menius Bassus, and is dedicated by her father, Lucius Munatius Successus.

EDCS-20400676.translation: To Marcus Munatius Priscus, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, the people of Aquinum, by decree of the decurions, [as] patron.
EDCS-20400676.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Munatius Priscus of the Teretina tribe as a patron of the people of Aquinum, recognized by a decree of the town council.

EDCS-20400678.translation: Quintus Pescennius, son of Quintus, made this from his will when he was aedile.
EDCS-20400678.summary: This is a funerary monument or dedication made from a will for Quintus Pescennius, an aedile.

EDCS-20400680.translation: Quintus Veronius, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe, provided water at his own expense.
EDCS-20400680.summary: This inscription records Quintus Veronius, of the Teretina tribe, providing a water supply at his own cost.

EDCS-20400685.summary: This is a dedication by Usonius, son of Caius, who served as aedile.

EDCS-20400698.translation: Numerius Papius Menothemis, son of Numerius, freedman, as one of the six imperial officials, for himself and for his concubine Irena, freedwoman of Marcus, and for his freedman Philotimus, son of Numerius, and for his freedman Fortis, son of Numerius, who was also one of the six imperial officials.
EDCS-20400698.summary: This funerary inscription names Numerius Papius Menothemis and several freedmen and a concubine, with Menothemis holding the position of a sexvir and Augustalis.

EDCS-20400708.translation: Caiatia Primigenia, freedwoman of Marcus, his concubine, made this at her own expense for him and his family.
EDCS-20400708.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Caiatia Primigenia, a concubine, for Publius Novius Philosophus, a doctor.

EDCS-20400709.translation: For Publius Philadespotus, son of Publius, freedman, a scribe who wrote wills, aged 25 years, without a legal advisor.
EDCS-20400709.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Philadespotus, a scribe who specialized in writing wills and died at the age of 25.

EDCS-20400713.summary: This is a short epitaph expressing a wish for a happy life for the deceased named Agrestis.

EDCS-20400717.translation: Sextus Aulenus Pilades, freedman of Sextus, and Alfia Arbuscula, freedwoman of the woman [Alfia], and Aulena Pyllis, freedwoman of Sextus.
EDCS-20400717.summary: This inscription lists three individuals: Sextus Aulenus Pilades, Alfia Arbuscula, and Aulena Pyllis, all freedpersons.

EDCS-20400719.translation: From the will of Lucius Berienus, son of Lucius, six hundred sesterces.
EDCS-20400719.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 600 sesterces from the will of Lucius Berienus.

EDCS-20400720.translation: For Caius Blassius Philomusus, freedman of the woman [Blassia], [belonging to] Sextus Essennius Hilarus.
EDCS-20400720.summary: This inscription is a dedication or record of ownership related to Caius Blassius Philomusus, a freedman, and Sextus Essennius Hilarus.

EDCS-20400723.translation: To Cinnam[us], for himself and his family, and to Lucilia, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-20400723.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cinnam[us] and his family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400724.translation: To Marcus Clodius Quartio, son of Marcus, freedman, and to Licustia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, for themselves and their families.
EDCS-20400724.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Clodius Quartio and Licustia Secunda, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400725.translation: To Gaius Cocceius Chilo, freedman of Gaius; to Cocceia Sextula, freedwoman of Gaius; and to Cocceia Dionysis, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-20400725.summary: This is a funerary inscription for several members of the Cocceius family, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400727.translation: To Cornificius Theudas, Cornificia Apollonia, Cornificia Clara, for themselves and their families, and to Cornificius Hippolytus.
EDCS-20400727.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of the Cornificius family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400729.translation: To Egnatia Amoena, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-20400729.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Egnatia Amoena, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400730.translation: To Titus Eppius Pepulus, and to Lucania Cytheris, freedwoman of a woman, for themselves and their families.
EDCS-20400730.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Eppius Pepulus and Lucania Cytheris, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400731.translation: To -ario Eronis, and to Egnatia Optata, freedwoman of Gaius, and to their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-20400731.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Egnatia Optata and others, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400733.translation: To -unda Erotis, and to -unda Rufa, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-20400733.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two individuals, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400738.translation: To Gaius Flavius, son of Gaius, freedman, and to Flavia, freedwoman of Gaius, and to all their family.
EDCS-20400738.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Flavius and Flavia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400741.translation: To Gavia Euphrosyne, freedwoman of Lucius, and to their freedmen and freedwomen, and to the freedmen and freedwomen of Lucius Flavius Faustus, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-20400741.summary: This is a funerary inscription concerning Gavia Euphrosyne and the freed dependents of Lucius Flavius Faustus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.
