EDCS-20400742.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedwoman named Amaryllis, dedicated to her.

EDCS-20400746.translation: To Gaius Lautinius, son of Tiberius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400746.summary: This inscription likely records the name of a Roman citizen, possibly on a tomb or public monument.

EDCS-20400748.translation: To Lucius Lucilius Salvius, freedman of Lucius, and to his mother Lollia, and to Cornelia, freedwoman of Publius Quartus.
EDCS-20400748.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates multiple individuals: a freedman, his mother, and another freedwoman.

EDCS-20400749.translation: To Gaius Lufinius Mahetus, freedman of Gaius. Gaius Lufinius Dasius, freedman of Gaius, [erected this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-20400749.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication of a tomb by a freedman, Gaius Lufinius Dasius, for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-20400750.translation: To Gaius Maenatius Eros, freedman of Gaius, and to Gaius Maenatius Balbus, freedman of Gaius, and to their sisters.
EDCS-20400750.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to two individuals, Gaius Maenatius Eros and Gaius Maenatius Balbus, and their sisters.

EDCS-20400751.translation: Magia Marcellina, daughter of Lucius, farewell.
EDCS-20400751.summary: This is a short epitaph or dedicatory text for a woman named Magia Marcellina, possibly wishing her well in the afterlife.

EDCS-20400752.translation: To Maria Felicula, freedwoman of Gaius. Ursio and Condicio [erected this] to their respected mistress.
EDCS-20400752.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by two individuals, Ursio and Condicio, to their esteemed freedwoman mistress, Maria Felicula.

EDCS-20400753.translation: To the Divine Shades. Mummius Verecundus made this for his most devoted wife, Mummia Septimina, who lived with me for 35 years, well-deserving.
EDCS-20400753.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mummia Septimina, erected by her husband Mummius Verecundus, detailing their years of marriage and her virtues.

EDCS-20400754.translation: To Lucius Muticuleius Nason, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, and to Muticuleia [---]
EDCS-20400754.summary: This inscription begins the names of two individuals, likely Lucius Muticuleius Nason and a Muticuleia, possibly for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-20400755.translation: C. N. Maal, son of Lucius, Agrippa [---]
EDCS-20400755.summary: This inscription starts with a name, possibly C. N. Maal Agrippa, son of Lucius, the context of which is lost due to the lacuna.

EDCS-20400756.translation: To Nasonius, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-20400756.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating a monument or person, identifying them by name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-20400757.translation: To Nonius, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, [from his inheritance/estate] 100,000 sesterces.
EDCS-20400757.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 100,000 sesterces to Nonius, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, as stated in a will.

EDCS-20400760.translation: Of Gaius Octavius Tertius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-20400760.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Gaius Octavius Tertius, a freedman.

EDCS-20400765.translation: Lucius Pescennius Tertius, son of Lucius, [for himself and] for Pescennia Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-20400765.summary: This inscription records a self-dedicated monument by Lucius Pescennius Tertius for himself and his freedwoman Pescennia Primigenia.

EDCS-20400769.translation: Of Gaius Plotius Ac[---], from the will.
EDCS-20400769.summary: This is a fragment indicating a bequest or dedication from the will of Gaius Plotius Ac[---].

EDCS-20400771.translation: Marcus Popillius Cicero, son of Gaius, made [this] while alive for himself and his family, and for Carnia, daughter of Titus, Quartai.
EDCS-20400771.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Popillius Cicero, son of Gaius, dedicated this monument for himself, his family, and Carnia, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-20400772.translation: To Prima, daughter of Sextus, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400772.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Prima, daughter of Sextus, of the Teretina tribe, likely as a recipient of a dedication.

EDCS-20400774.translation: Of Vivius, son of Marcus Publicius, freedman of the colony, Philodamus, and his freedwoman Prima, and their family.
EDCS-20400774.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Vivius Philodamus, a freedman of the colony, for himself, his freedwoman Prima, and their family.

EDCS-20400775.translation: Of Sextus Pulfennius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400775.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Sextus Pulfennius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe.

EDCS-20400777.summary: This is a fragment identifying Sabaeus, a freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-20400778.translation: Lucius Satius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400778.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph or a record of citizenship for Lucius Satius.

EDCS-20400780.translation: To Gaius Seius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe; to Satia, daughter of Lucius; Gaius Seius; Marcus Seius; Publius Seius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe; Lucius Seius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, Ru...; Publius Seius, son of Publius, Cel[---]
EDCS-20400780.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a family funerary monument, listing several individuals belonging to the Seius family and the Teretina tribe.

EDCS-20400782.translation: Marcus Seppius, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, Canus; Gaius Seppius, son of Marcus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-20400782.summary: This inscription records two individuals from the Seppius family, including a father and son relationship, likely for a funerary context.

EDCS-20400787.translation: Gaius Suellius, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, [---]
EDCS-20400787.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Suellius.

EDCS-20400788.translation: To Gaius Teius, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, Capito; to Lucius Maius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, Paetus; to Tillia, mother; by testament.
EDCS-20400788.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely funerary or religious, made by testament to members of the Teia and Mai families, including a mother named Tillia.

EDCS-20400790.translation: Marcus Tetianus, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400790.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Marcus Tetianus, likely for citizenship or funerary purposes.

EDCS-20400795.translation: To Marcus Tillius Theudas, to Marcus Tillius Heron, and to his own Felicioni, aged 12 years; to Vitellia Callistenes; to Tillia Tertia; to Marcus Tillius Gallus; to Marcus Tillius Salvius; to Marcus Tillius Rufus.
EDCS-20400795.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription listing several individuals, including a young boy named Felicioni, and members of the Tillius family, possibly commemorating multiple burials.

EDCS-20400798.translation: To Valeria, [daughter] of Marcus [---]; to Iridis.
EDCS-20400798.summary: This fragmented inscription is likely a funerary dedication to a woman named Valeria and another named Iridis.

EDCS-20400799.translation: To Publius Var[ronius ---]; to Varronia, freedwoman of Publius [---]; Varroni [---]; Varronia, freedwoman of Publius [---]
EDCS-20400799.summary: This fragmented inscription lists several individuals with the name Varronius and Varronia, likely freedmen or members of a freed family, probably funerary.

EDCS-20400804.translation: Vercila Regina [for herself] and for Lucius Nerius, freedman of Lucius, Daphnus, and her own people.
EDCS-20400804.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Vercila Regina for herself and others, including a freedman named Daphnus, likely a funerary or a dedication to household gods.

EDCS-20400806.translation: To Quintus Vibius Gallus, son of Quintus, of the Teretina tribe, patron.
EDCS-20400806.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Vibius Gallus, a patron, and likely records his funerary monument.

EDCS-20400808.translation: To Lucius Vibius Gallus, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400808.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Vibius Gallus, son of Caius, of the Teretina tribe, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-20400809.translation: Iusta made this for Justa Hospita, concubine of Caius Vibius, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400809.summary: This funerary inscription records that Iusta made a monument for her concubine, Justa Hospita.

EDCS-20400817.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription to two individuals named Lollia and Lollena.

EDCS-20400836.translation: Secundio made the temple of Numisia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, wife of Liberius, from the foundations, and placed it with Diana.
EDCS-20400836.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Numisia Prisca, built from the foundations by Secundio and dedicated with Diana.

EDCS-20400837.translation: Achilles, freedman of Augustus, procurator, and his wife Ulpia Nice, dedicated this to Mars or his divine power; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400837.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a religious site by Achilles, a procurator and freedman of Augustus, and his wife, with the land granted by local officials.

EDCS-20400838.translation: Numerius Satrius Stabilio, freedman of Numerius, and Publius Pomponius Salvius, freedman of Publius, gave this offering to Mefitis.
EDCS-20400838.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made to the goddess Mefitis by two freedmen, Numerius Satrius Stabilio and Publius Pomponius Salvius.

EDCS-20400839.translation: Lucius Postumius Surus, son of Marcus, of the Scaptia tribe, [made?] this altar to LAR IEVDI.
EDCS-20400839.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar by Lucius Postumius Surus, son of Marcus, to a deity named Lar Ievidi.

EDCS-20400844.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cornelia Salonina, likely an imperial consort, styled Augusta.

EDCS-20400845.translation: To the deified Caecilia Paulina, the Pious, Augusta.
EDCS-20400845.summary: This inscription is a posthumous dedication to the deified Caecilia Paulina, honored as Pious and Augusta.

EDCS-20400850.translation: To Publius Tettius Rufus Tontianus, son of Publius, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, prefect of the 20th legion.
EDCS-20400850.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Publius Tettius Rufus Tontianus, listing his offices including quaestor, tribune of the plebs, and prefect of a legion, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400851.translation: To Publius Tettius Rufus Tontianus, son of Publius, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor, the Atinate townspeople, his patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400851.summary: This inscription honors Publius Tettius Rufus Tontianus, listing his magistracies and declaring him a patron of the town of Atina by decree of its council, dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400852.translation: To Gaius Vettius Cossinius Rufinus, most distinguished man, prefect of the city, count of our Augusti, corrector of Campania, corrector of Tuscany and Umbria, corrector of Venetia and Istria, curator of the Tiber river and sewers of the sacred city, curator of the Flaminian Way, proconsul of the province of Achaia, chosen pontiff of the god Sol, augur, Salian priest of the Palatine, the council and people of Atina, because during his governorship, which had encountered a most savage tyranny, no injustice was suffered, to their most cherished patron.
EDCS-20400852.summary: This extensive honorary inscription praises Gaius Vettius Cossinius Rufinus for his many high offices and good governance, particularly noting his protection of Atina from injustice during a turbulent period, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-20400854.translation: To Quintus Crittius, son of Gaius, of the Cornelia tribe, thrice chief centurion.
EDCS-20400854.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Quintus Crittius, a soldier of the Cornelia tribe, who achieved the rank of primipilari (chief centurion) three times, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400856.translation: For the sake of the authority of the Roman people, Sidonius, tribune of the soldiers.
EDCS-20400856.summary: This is a brief inscription by Sidonius, a military tribune, likely dedicating something or stating his service, with a possible date in the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400857.translation: To Gaius Avidius Clemens, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, aedile, duovir, with public horse, the townspeople and inhabitants, with money contributed by a decree of the decurions, a site was granted.
EDCS-20400857.summary: This inscription records the granting of a public site to Gaius Avidius Clemens by the citizens of his town, honoring him for his service as aedile and duovir, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400859.translation: To Heria Mansueta, daughter of Quintus, and Marcellina, daughter of Lucius Digitius, to their excellent mother, a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400859.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by decree of the decurions to Heria Mansueta and her daughter Marcellina, honoring the mother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400860.translation: For the chastity of Junia Gratilla, the people of Atina decreed that a statue be publicly erected and they gave a school, which Junius Syriarches adorned and dedicated with his sons.
EDCS-20400860.summary: This inscription records that the citizens of Atina erected a statue and dedicated a school in honor of Junia Gratilla's chastity, with the school being further embellished by Junius Syriarches and his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400861.translation: To Gaius Maius, son of Gaius, duovir, quaestor.
EDCS-20400861.summary: This is a brief honorary inscription for Gaius Maius, son of Gaius, listing his local magistracies as duovir and quaestor, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400864.translation: To Munnia, daughter of Gaius, priestess of Ceres.
EDCS-20400864.summary: This is an inscription honoring Munnia, daughter of Gaius, who served as a priestess of Ceres, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20400866.translation: To Plancia, daughter of Cnaeus, mother of Lucius Postumius Rufus, duovir, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20400866.summary: This is a funerary dedication honoring Plancia, likely erected by her son, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-20400867.translation: Cnaeus Satur, son of Cnaeus, of the Teretina tribe, aedile.
EDCS-20400867.summary: This is an official notice identifying Cnaeus Satur as an aedile, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400868.translation: To Gaius Veturius Aphrodisianus, son of Gaius, of the Teretina tribe, aedile with public equestrian rank. Gaius Veturius Adiectus, son of Gaius, and Tarcia Prima, daughter of Gaius, granted this place to their most dutiful son by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400868.summary: This funerary inscription records the granting of a burial plot to Gaius Veturius Aphrodisianus by his parents, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-20400871.translation: Marcus Salivius Saturninus, of the Sergia tribe.
EDCS-20400871.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Salivius Saturninus by name and tribe, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400872.translation: Gaius Obinius Epicadus, freedman of Gaius, and Aphrodisia, freedwoman of the woman Trebia, managed this household for 14 years.
EDCS-20400872.summary: This inscription records the length of service of a freedman and freedwoman, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400873.translation: Son of Gaius, Balb(us?) Dianus, of the Teretina tribe, and his wife Luci(a?) filia (daughter of Lucius?).
EDCS-20400873.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, likely a couple, with tribal affiliations, probably from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400876.translation: To Diana and Sulpicia, from their mother Felicis.
EDCS-20400876.summary: This is a dedication to Diana and Sulpicia, likely from a mother named Felicis, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-20400877.translation: To Helvia Procula, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-20400877.summary: This is a dedication to Helvia Procula, daughter of Titus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400878.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Herius Leo to his most sweet son, Quintus Herius Felix.
EDCS-20400878.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a son named Quintus Herius Felix, erected by his father Gaius Herius Leo, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400879.summary: This inscription records that Hippocrates made something while alive, likely a funerary monument, from the Roman period.

EDCS-20400880.translation: Gaius Longidius, freedman of Gaius Lucius, Philodamus, made this for himself and for Gentia, freedwoman of Lucius, his concubine, and his family, while alive.
EDCS-20400880.summary: A funerary dedication made by a freedman for himself, his concubine, and his family.

EDCS-20400881.translation: Of Gaius Lucius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-20400881.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely identifying a person and their patron or former master.

EDCS-20400882.translation: Gentia, daughter of Gaius, made this for Gaius Lucius, son of Gaius, her father, Paetus, and for Gaius Lucius, son of Gaius, her son, Rufus.
EDCS-20400882.summary: A funerary monument erected by a woman for her father and her son.

EDCS-20400883.translation: In memory of Gaius Marius Ianuarius, freedman of Gaius Marius. Gaius Marius Mercurius made this for his most devoted brother, who deserved well.
EDCS-20400883.summary: A funerary dedication by a brother for his deceased sibling, identifying them by name and status.

EDCS-20400884.translation: Gnaeus Ofellius Nicephorus, freedman of Gnaeus, and Quinctia Rhoda, freedwoman of Sela, and [another woman], freedwoman of Sela.
EDCS-20400884.summary: An inscription naming three individuals, likely freedmen and freedwomen, possibly related or sharing a tomb.

EDCS-20400885.translation: Gnaeus Offilius, freedman of Gnaeus, [dedicates X amount]. Gnaeus Offilius, son of Gnaeus, [dedicates XIII]. Marcus, son of Gnaeus, Gnaeus Offilius, son of Gnaeus, [dedicates III]. Offilia, daughter of Gnaeus, [dedicates LIV]. Gnaeus, son of Gnaeus, [dedicates C]. [Names] son of Gnaeus, [dedicates XIII]. [Names] daughter of Gnaeus.
EDCS-20400885.summary: A complex inscription likely detailing contributions or property divisions among members of a family, possibly related to a business or inheritance, with numerical values and familial relationships.

EDCS-20400886.translation: Pacc, freedwoman of Paccio, for her freedman Paccio Marci, and for Paccia Tertia, and for Tillia, freedwoman of mulieris, Chelido, they have made [this].
EDCS-20400886.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedwoman for her freedman and other individuals, indicating familial or social ties.

EDCS-20400887.translation: [---] gave this to Punia Mir[---] for a debt of [---] from T.
EDCS-20400887.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly related to a debt or legal transaction.

EDCS-20400888.translation: Teretina Primo Phiso vit [made this for] Gaius Pellius, son of Gaius, grandson of Gaius, great-grandson of Gaius. M [---]
EDCS-20400888.summary: A funerary dedication for Gaius Pellius, tracing his lineage back several generations, made by Teretina Primo Phiso.

EDCS-20400889.summary: A simple funerary dedication to a husband named Quintus Pescenius.

EDCS-20400890.translation: If the untimely laws of fate had not been, my mother should have been read before this inscription; she asks that you say this land, which is not heavy, belongs to Petali, according to the will of fate.
EDCS-20400890.summary: This is a metrical epitaph for a woman named Petali, lamenting the premature death of her mother.

EDCS-20400891.translation: For the merits of Pomponia Graphis.
EDCS-20400891.summary: This is a dedication honoring Pomponia Graphis for her services.

EDCS-20400892.translation: For Pomponius Quintus, son of Philo, and for Pomponia, freedwoman of Quintus, MA, and for Felen, freedwoman of Decimus, Pomponius, 16 feet in front and 15 feet in width.
EDCS-20400892.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Pomponius Quintus and two freedwomen, Pomponia and Felen.

EDCS-20400893.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Pomponius Neon.

EDCS-20400894.translation: Lucius Pomponius Pharnaces, freedman of Lucius, and Rubbia Rhoda, freedwoman of Gaius, and Pomponia Phronime, freedwoman of Lucius, arranged for this to be made during their lifetime.
EDCS-20400894.summary: This is a funerary dedication arranged by Lucius Pomponius Pharnaces and two freedwomen, Rubbia Rhoda and Pomponia Phronime, for themselves and potentially others.

EDCS-20400895.translation: For Lucius Pomponius Rufus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-20400895.summary: This is a dedication honoring Lucius Pomponius Rufus.

EDCS-20400896.translation: Lucius Pomponius Tertius, freedman of a woman, made this himself while alive for himself and for Pomponia Philonica, freedwoman of Gaius Publius.
EDCS-20400896.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Pomponius Tertius for himself and his wife, Pomponia Philonica.

EDCS-20400897.translation: I am Samnis by birth; my parents named me Firminus; joined to my husband, I am Firminus.
EDCS-20400897.summary: This is a metrical epitaph of a woman named Firminus who states her ethnic origin and marital status.

EDCS-20400898.translation: For Gaius Rubbius Heron, freedman of Gaius, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-20400898.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication to Gaius Rubbius Heron, made according to his will.

EDCS-20400899.translation: Chrysogonus, freedman of Gaius, Sabidia, freedwoman of a woman, Palladium, Lucius Clodius Chrysiippus, freedman of Lucius, 14 feet in front.
EDCS-20400899.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a funerary plot belonging to several individuals including freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-20400900.translation: Lucius Saufeius Scurra, freedman of Lucius, erected this for himself and his family, measuring 18 Roman feet in the front and 20 Roman feet in depth.
EDCS-20400900.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Saufeius Scurra for his family, specifying its dimensions, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400901.translation: Marcus Senus Scaeva, son of Publius, and Maria, daughter of Caius, wife of Marcus Senus Scaeva, have erected this monument.
EDCS-20400901.summary: A funerary monument jointly erected by Marcus Senus Scaeva and his wife Maria, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400904.translation: Marcus Tillius, son of Marcus, so that it may be a road for Numerius, daughter of ---
EDCS-20400904.summary: An inscription possibly related to establishing a right of way or boundary, associated with Marcus Tillius and Numeria, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400905.translation: Caius Tillius Sabda, freedman of Caius, for himself and for Caius Tillius, freedman of Caius, and for Hetaer, freedwoman of Caius Tillius.
EDCS-20400905.summary: A funerary monument erected by Caius Tillius Sabda for himself and two freedpersons, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400906.translation: Tillia erected this for her husband, --- of Marcus Aerius, ---
EDCS-20400906.summary: A funerary inscription by Tillia for her husband, mentioning her father and possibly her husband's lineage, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400907.translation: Cnaeus Valerius Philodamus, freedman of Cnaeus, for Cnaeus Valerius Soranus, son of Cnaeus, measuring 16 Roman feet in the front and 20 Roman feet in depth.
EDCS-20400907.summary: A funerary monument erected by Cnaeus Valerius Philodamus for Cnaeus Valerius Soranus, specifying dimensions, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400908.translation: Valerius Philox, son of Cnaeus Valerius Phoenix, freedman of Cnaeus, measuring 11 Roman feet in the front and 10 Roman feet in depth.
EDCS-20400908.summary: A funerary monument for Valerius Philox, son of Cnaeus Valerius Phoenix, specifying dimensions, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400909.translation: Lucius Veibius Trypho, freedman of Ofellius; Caius Vettius Trase, freedwoman of a woman; Marcus Maius Bello, freedman of Marcus; Lucius Herius Apollonius, freedman of Lucius Quinti.
EDCS-20400909.summary: A list of names, possibly of freedmen and their patrons, without a clear indication of a monument type, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400910.translation: Hermes, freedman of Lucius Vettius, Lucius; Luca, freedwoman of a woman of Lucius Arrutius; AproI, freedman of Tiberius Lucilius; (and) Illf, freedman of Caius Plancius, erected (this) for themselves while alive.
EDCS-20400910.summary: A funerary monument erected by several individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, for themselves during their lifetime, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400911.translation: Cnaeus Vetulius Pomponianus, son of Cnaeus Vetulius.
EDCS-20400911.summary: A fragmented inscription that names Cnaeus Vetulius Pomponianus and his father, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400912.translation: Publius Veturius, son of Publius, and Domatia, daughter of Caius, of the Cornelia tribe.
EDCS-20400912.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, likely a couple, belonging to the Cornelia tribe, possibly for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-20400913.summary: This inscription records the name of a freedman named Caius Veturius, identifying his former master.

EDCS-20400914.translation: For Marcus Vibulus, Tillia made this monument.
EDCS-20400914.summary: This inscription records Tillia dedicating a monument to Marcus Vibulus.

EDCS-20400921.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flenno [---?].
EDCS-20400921.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the gods of the underworld, mentioning a name (Flenno) with an illegible addition.

EDCS-20400925.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of an individual, with the beginning illegible.

EDCS-20400927.summary: This inscription possibly indicates a boundary or location marker, with 'Maceria' referring to a wall or ruin, situated on private land.

EDCS-20400933.summary: This inscription likely refers to a funerary context, mentioning a person named Tuacilia and wishing them peace in the afterlife.

EDCS-20400935.translation: His heir made [this] for Caius Herennius Ampliatus, freedman of Caius, a VIvir and Augustalis, at Atina.
EDCS-20400935.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by an heir to Caius Herennius Ampliatus, a freedman who held important religious and civic offices in Atina.

EDCS-20400936.translation: A monument for Aeria Semniat, priestess of Venus.
EDCS-20400936.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to Aeria Semniat, who served as a priestess of the goddess Venus.

EDCS-20400939.translation: Quintus Caesius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Teretina tribe, [dedicated this] from his will to his father Quintus Caesius, son of Quintus, of the Teretina tribe, to his mother Septumia, daughter of Numerius, and to his brother Quintus Caesius.
EDCS-20400939.summary: This funerary inscription, made according to a will, records the dedication by Quintus Caesius Rufus to his father, mother, and brother.

EDCS-20400940.translation: Gaius Crittius Laevinus Pulcer, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, and Marcus Mato, son of Gaius, and Polla Betuedia, caused this to be made by Quintus, the son.
EDCS-20400940.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative monument dedicated by Marcus Mato and Polla Betuedia, who commissioned the work of Quintus, for Gaius Crittius Laevinus Pulcer.

EDCS-20400941.translation: Lucius Hilarus, freedman of a woman, and Offillia Eleusis; Lucius Varus, son of Lucius, lives; they live.
EDCS-20400941.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the names of Lucius Hilarus and Offillia Eleusis, and stating that Lucius Varus and others are alive.

EDCS-20400943.translation: To Lucius Seppius Princeps, freedman of Lucius. He lived 22 years. Do not grieve, mother. Time has turned; this was my fate.
EDCS-20400943.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Seppius Princeps, a freedman, lamenting his death and addressing his mother.

EDCS-20400944.translation: To Potestas, freedwoman of Marcia, a woman.
EDCS-20400944.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Potestas, the freedwoman of Marcia.

EDCS-20400945.translation: Publius Matienus Privatus Reutpompilius died aged 22.
EDCS-20400945.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Matienus Privatus Reutpompilius, recording his death at the age of 22.

EDCS-20400946.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Pomponia, daughter of Aulus.

EDCS-20400949.translation: Spedia, daughter of Quintus, daughter of Marcus son of Quintus, made this.
EDCS-20400949.summary: This is an inscription stating that Spedia, daughter of Quintus and granddaughter of Marcus, made the monument.

EDCS-20400950.translation: Spelia Tertia, daughter of Quintus; Lucius Gallio, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, lives.
EDCS-20400950.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Spelia Tertia, daughter of Quintus, and records that Lucius Gallio is alive.

EDCS-20400951.translation: To Marcus Capitonius, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe; his wife Graicia, daughter of Gaius; and Marcus, son of Gaius, son of Marcus [Staidius].
EDCS-20400951.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Marcus Capitonius, his wife Graicia, and their son Marcus, likely from the 1st century AD.

EDCS-20400961.translation: Epidia Stratonice, freedwoman of Lucius, and Epidia Anacrusis, freedwoman of Lucius, gladly gave this gift to Venus as deserved.
EDCS-20400961.summary: This is a religious dedication by two freedwomen of Lucius, Epidia Stratonice and Epidia Anacrusis, to the goddess Venus.

EDCS-20400963.translation: Lucius Hilarius restored this, having seen it in a dream from Venus.
EDCS-20400963.summary: A private individual, Lucius Hilarius, restored something in response to a dream vision from the goddess Venus.

EDCS-20400968.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus Adiabenicus, by the pagus Lapillanus.
EDCS-20400968.summary: This is a dedication by the pagus Lapillanus to Emperor Septimius Severus, likely during his reign (193-211 AD).

EDCS-20400969.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severo Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 8th time, acclaimed Imperator for the 11th time, Consul twice, Father of the Fatherland, by the college of hornblowers.
EDCS-20400969.summary: This is a lengthy dedication by the college of hornblowers to Emperor Septimius Severus, listing his numerous titles and powers, indicating a date around 200 AD.

EDCS-20400970.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, designated Emperor, son of Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400970.summary: This inscription is a decree by the town council (decurions) in honor of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), designating him as emperor and son of Septimius Severus, likely from the period of their joint rule.

EDCS-20400972.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 3rd time, Consul twice, Father of the Fatherland, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20400972.summary: This is a dedication by the town council (decurions) to Emperor Gallienus, listing his titles and powers, dating it to approximately 255-257 AD.

EDCS-20400975.translation: Petronius Probus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-20400975.summary: This fragmented inscription likely commemorates or identifies Petronius Probus, a prominent individual, possibly in the late Roman period.

EDCS-20400983.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. To Gaius Casinius Fortunatus, soldier of the 5th cohort of vigilum, who lived 25 years and some months.
EDCS-20400983.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Casinius Fortunatus, a soldier in the city watch, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-20400986.translation: Gnaeus Agrius, son of Gnaeus, Pollio; Lucius Laufeius, son of Lucius, Apotheca; the four men responsible for justice.
EDCS-20400986.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Gnaeus Agrius and Lucius Laufeius, serving as magistrates (IIII viri iure dicundo) in a Roman town, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-20400987.translation: Agria Sucia, daughter of Numerus, priestess of Ceres and Venus.
EDCS-20400987.summary: This inscription identifies Agria Sucia as a priestess dedicated to the goddesses Ceres and Venus, suggesting her religious and social standing.

EDCS-20400988.translation: Fabia Philemai, Balonia Philematio, Graecina Myrinna, and Epimedia, not as relatives but with their own money, made this.
EDCS-20400988.summary: This inscription records four women - Fabia Philemai, Balonia Philematio, Graecina Myrinna, and Epimedia - who jointly funded the construction of a monument or building.

EDCS-20400989.translation: Dedicated by Gaius Futius, prefect of the Casinates.
EDCS-20400989.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Gaius Futius, prefect of the Casinates, likely in the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20400991.summary: This inscription is a simple ownership or dedication marker, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400995.translation: Publius Lucretius, a sevir, for his wife Staisia Vitalis.
EDCS-20400995.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Publius Lucretius, a sevir, to his wife Staisia Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400996.translation: To Gaius Paccius Felix, patron, who had held all honors and offices, and for his son Gaius Paccius Felix, patron of the colony of Casinum, whose immense benefits make the fatherland recognized as enriched; to the curator of our public affairs, under whose wise administration we have always prospered; and to the curator and restorer of public buildings, through whose work and solicitude, and at his own expense, after a series of years, the Novian Baths have been restored for our use. For all these labors which he displayed for his fatherland and his citizens, we, the entire people of the colony of Casinum, together with our children, have fittingly decided that a marble statue be erected to this worthy patron.
EDCS-20400996.summary: This extensive inscription from the colony of Casinum records the decision by the entire populace to erect a marble statue to Gaius Paccius Felix, honoring his extensive public service as curator of public affairs and restorer of public buildings, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20400999.translation: To Numerius Savonius, son of Numerius, praetor. Apsennia Paulla, daughter of Quintus, his wife, erected this.
EDCS-20400999.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Apsennia Paulla to her husband Numerius Savonius, a praetor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401001.translation: To Lucius Staldins Priscus, a duumvir of Casinum. Obultronia Prisca, his most unhappy mother.
EDCS-20401001.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Staldins Priscus, a duumvir of Casinum, dedicated by his mother Obultronia Prisca, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401002.translation: Victoricus Asclepiacus, son of Asclepiacus, and Saturninus and Uricus, seven years, three months, and some days old. [---]
EDCS-20401002.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victoricus Asclepiacus and others, likely children, mentioning their ages and possibly their family members, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401006.translation: Of Satrius Melans, son of Rufus.
EDCS-20401006.summary: This inscription is likely a funerary dedication or ownership marker, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401007.translation: Lucius Clodius Antiochus Tuscus, freedman of Lucius, a cook, built this monument in his lifetime for himself and for his freedwoman Aletia, wife of Clodia, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Nicephorus, and for his freedwoman Clodia Appia, freedwoman of Lucius, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Tontianus, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Gae, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Philemon, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Hilarus, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Nicephorus, centurion, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Ampliatus, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Hermias, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Philemon, and for his freedman Lucius Clodius Sasar.
EDCS-20401007.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument built by Lucius Clodius Antiochus Tuscus, a cook, for himself and a large number of his freedmen and freedwomen, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401008.translation: To Vitalis, his wife, who lived 29 years, 3 months. Pollonius Taesueus [erected this].
EDCS-20401008.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Pollonius Taesueus to his wife Vitalis, providing her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401009.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Albia Callituche as the freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-20401010.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Alfia Primitiva, who lived 45 years, 10 months, and 20 days. Lucius Vibullius Gemellus and Lucius Vibullius Proculinus set this up for their well-deserving mother.
EDCS-20401010.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Alfia Primitiva, detailing her age and erected by her sons Lucius Vibullius Gemellus and Lucius Vibullius Proculinus.

EDCS-20401011.translation: For Apicula, freedwoman. Caius Vinius Amphio, freedman of Caius, for himself and for Vinia Chrestine, freedwoman of the woman (Vinia), his fellow freedwoman, 16 feet in front and 14 feet in the rear.
EDCS-20401011.summary: This is a funerary inscription concerning a plot of land intended for Apicula, Caius Vinius Amphio, and Vinia Chrestine, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-20401013.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Lucius Asinius Philinus, son of Marcus, who lived 4 years, 11 months. Marcus Asinius Victorinus, his father, for his most beloved son.
EDCS-20401013.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Asinius Philinus, detailing his young age and erected by his father, Marcus Asinius Victorinus.

EDCS-20401014.translation: For Quintus Postumius, son of Quintus. 16 feet in front, in the rear [---] feet.
EDCS-20401014.summary: This is an inscription concerning land allocation, possibly funerary, mentioning dimensions and the name Quintus Postumius.

EDCS-20401015.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Balonius Pudens. For Balonia.
EDCS-20401015.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Balonius Pudens and Balonia, likely a dedication or a joint epitaph.

EDCS-20401017.translation: Blaia, freedwoman of Gaius; Ri Helvia, freedwoman of Gaius; Di Pineia, freedwoman of the woman; Ri Pullia, freedwoman of the woman; Eu.
EDCS-20401017.summary: This inscription lists four women, all identified as freedwomen of various patrons, possibly indicating a shared tomb or memorial.

EDCS-20401019.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Gaius Caecilius Ionicus the Younger. His parents made this for their well-deserving son. He lived 29 years.
EDCS-20401019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Caecilius Ionicus the Younger, stating his age and erected by his parents.

EDCS-20401020.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Caemia Thetis. Gaius Baebius Secundus for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-20401020.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caemia Thetis, erected by her husband Gaius Baebius Secundus.

EDCS-20401021.translation: For Lucius Fi Heron, freedman of Caius, son of Caius. For Caius Cassius Iucundus. 10 feet in front and 10 feet in the rear.
EDCS-20401021.summary: This inscription pertains to a plot of land, possibly funerary, measuring 10x10 feet, associated with Lucius Fi Heron and Caius Cassius Iucundus.

EDCS-20401022.translation: Quintus Caiatius Phileros [dedicated this] for his freedwoman Caesia Marci, and for Sec Caesia Quinti, his freedwoman. [The property extends] eleven feet in front.
EDCS-20401022.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two freedwomen, Caesia Marci and Sec Caesia Quinti, by their former owner Quintus Caiatius Phileros, likely a boundary marker.

EDCS-20401023.translation: For Publius Caprilius Casinetus, freedman and foster-son. He lived 7 years, 3 months, and 19 days.
EDCS-20401023.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Publius Caprilius Casinetus, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-20401024.translation: For Lucius Ceius Leucarus, son of Caius. [The property extends] thirteen feet in the field.
EDCS-20401024.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary or land ownership for Lucius Ceius Leucarus, son of Caius.

EDCS-20401025.translation: To the Divine Shades. Staedius Invictus made this for his incomparable wife, Cornelia Primitiva, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401025.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a husband, Staedius Invictus, for his cherished wife, Cornelia Primitiva.

EDCS-20401026.translation: To IIO [the gods?]. For Cutia Prisc, son of Marcus.
EDCS-20401026.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely intended as a dedication or funerary marker for Cutia Prisc, son of Marcus.

EDCS-20401027.translation: Lucius Dignius Clarus, freedman of Lucius, and Mammuleia Urbana, freedwoman of Lucius. [The property extends] thirteen feet in front.
EDCS-20401027.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary or property line, mentioning two freedpersons, Lucius Dignius Clarus and Mammuleia Urbana.

EDCS-20401028.translation: For Publius Faracius, son of Caius.
EDCS-20401028.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or funerary marker for Publius Faracius, son of Caius.

EDCS-20401031.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Fufidia Ge as a freedwoman of Titus.

EDCS-20401032.translation: [For?] Furia No[...], the most unhappy mother.
EDCS-20401032.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mourning an unhappy mother named Furia.

EDCS-20401033.translation: Illa, son of Cnaeus, son of Futi. N.O. [perhaps 'non ossa', not bones, or similar].
EDCS-20401033.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary marker, identifying a person named Illa and his parentage.

EDCS-20401034.translation: Quintus Futius Ithris, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-20401034.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Futius Ithris, a freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401035.translation: Caius Futius Philocomus, freedman of Caius, for himself and for Futia Megistene, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-20401035.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caius Futius Philocomus dedicating it for himself and his freedwoman Futia Megistene, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401036.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Futius Successus, son of Caius, who lived 16 years and 4 months. Vibullia Amanda, his most devoted mother, [dedicated this] to her son.
EDCS-20401036.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Futius Successus, a young boy, set up by his mother Vibullia Amanda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401038.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gargilia Pollitta, his wife.
EDCS-20401038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gargilia Pollitta, dedicated by her husband, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401040.translation: Quintus Heleius Rufus, son of Quintus, for himself and for Lollia Polla, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-20401040.summary: This funerary epitaph records Quintus Heleius Rufus dedicating it for himself and his wife Lollia Polla, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401041.translation: For Lucius Helvius Hilarius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Galeria.
EDCS-20401041.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Helvius Hilarius, son of Lucius, and his tribal affiliation, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401042.translation: Of Marcus Herennius Gallus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-20401042.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Herennius Gallus, son of Quintus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401043.translation: Of Quintus Herennius Quartio, freedman of Quintus, 12 feet in front, 16 feet in the ground.
EDCS-20401043.summary: This inscription, likely related to a property boundary or tomb plot, records the name of Quintus Herennius Quartio, freedman of Quintus, and dimensions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401046.translation: Tiberius Iulius S. made [this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-20401046.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Tiberius Iulius S. dedicates a monument to his deserving wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401047.translation: [---] Silvanus, son of Caius, of the tribe Fabia / [---]tia Potentina / [---]
EDCS-20401047.summary: This fragmentary funerary epitaph mentions Silvanus, son of Caius, and Potentina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401048.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Iulius Zoticus Faustus erected this, he who often gave warnings while alive.
EDCS-20401048.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Iulius Zoticus Faustus for himself, with a note that he gave warnings during his life.

EDCS-20401049.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For his most beloved wife, Iulia Secunda, Blastus erected this, well-deserving.
EDCS-20401049.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Blastus to his wife Iulia Secunda, noting her deserving nature.

EDCS-20401050.translation: To Marcus Latius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus; to Lacia Tertia, freedwoman of Marcus; and to Marcus Maius Phileros, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20401050.summary: This inscription records a dedication to three individuals, all freedmen or freedwomen associated with a Marcus.

EDCS-20401051.translation: Gaius Lanius Tertius, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, made this while alive, and for his daughter Tertulla.
EDCS-20401051.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Lanius Tertius during his lifetime, also for his daughter Tertulla.

EDCS-20401052.translation: Of Marcus Latinius Phileros. In front fifteen feet, in the field twelve feet.
EDCS-20401052.summary: This inscription marks the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Marcus Latinius Phileros.

EDCS-20401053.translation: Sextus Latinius Sabo, son of Sextus, grandson of Sextus, great-grandson of Sextus, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-20401053.summary: This is a formal genealogical record identifying Sextus Latinius Sabo and his ancestry, likely for a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-20401054.translation: Of Marcus Longuleius Phileros. For Veia, daughter of Publius. In front five feet, in the field [---].
EDCS-20401054.summary: This inscription indicates dimensions for a plot of land belonging to Marcus Longuleius Phileros and likely intended for Veia.

EDCS-20401055.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Luccia Saturni. Gnaeus Tillius Hym [erected this] II [times? or for two people?].
EDCS-20401055.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gnaeus Tillius Hym to Luccia Saturni, with an unclear numeral that might indicate the number of people or repetitions.

EDCS-20401059.translation: Quintus Mevius Antimachus, freedman of Quintus, for himself and for Critonia Posilla and for his own [family].
EDCS-20401059.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Mevius Antimachus for himself, Critonia Posilla, and his family.

EDCS-20401060.translation: Mevia, freedwoman of Gaius; Athenais, freedwoman of Gaius; Lucius Helvius Felix, freedman of Lucius. In the field twelve feet.
EDCS-20401060.summary: This inscription records the ownership or dimensions of a field associated with Mevia, Athenais, and Lucius Helvius Felix.

EDCS-20401061.translation: To Lucius Munatius Gallianus, who lived 35 years and 5 months. Lucius Munatius Entreghes and Munatia Calliste, most unhappy parents, made this for their most devoted son, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401061.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Munatius Gallianus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-20401062.translation: Sacred to the shades. Festus made this for his brothers Muntanus and Ianuarius Festus, who lived 11 years, 7 months, and 5 days. Festus and Ianuaria made this for their sweetest son.
EDCS-20401062.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates two brothers, Muntanus and Ianuarius Festus, with a specific mention of the latter's lifespan, and was set up by Festus and Ianuaria.

EDCS-20401063.translation: Idius Nitidus, his freedwoman Philargyrus; Lucris, his freedwoman; Charis, Philargyrus' freedwoman. (Boundary marker)
EDCS-20401063.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker, indicating ownership or division of land related to several freedpersons. (VE likely stands for 'viam explevit' or similar boundary-marking formula.)

EDCS-20401064.translation: Gaius Novius Philemon, freedman of Gaius; Byzantium, freedwoman of Novia, wife of Gaius. In front 12 feet.
EDCS-20401064.summary: This is a boundary inscription defining a plot of land 12 feet in front, associated with a freedman named Philemon and a freedwoman named Byzantium.

EDCS-20401066.translation: Fonteius Papia, son of Fonteius; Julia, daughter of Caius. (Boundary marker)
EDCS-20401066.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary, naming individuals associated with land ownership or division.

EDCS-20401068.translation: Prima, freedwoman of the woman Percennia. 8 feet in the field, 8 feet in front.
EDCS-20401068.summary: This is a boundary inscription stating that Prima, a freedwoman of Percennia, has 8 feet in the field and 8 feet in front, likely defining a land plot.

EDCS-20401070.translation: Lucius Pontuleius, son of Caius; Poponia, his wife, daughter of Terentius. (Boundary marker)
EDCS-20401070.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary, naming Lucius Pontuleius and his wife Poponia, with patronymic and tribal information.

EDCS-20401071.translation: To Publius Poppaeus Magnus, son of Publius, of the Oufentina tribe; Secunda, daughter of Lucius, wife of Publius Poppaeus, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-20401071.summary: This is an epitaph set up for Publius Poppaeus Magnus, son of Publius, and possibly also for Secunda, his wife, indicating their family and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-20401072.translation: Postumia, daughter of Marcus; Catinia, daughter of Lucius. Quintus Atrius Philemo, freedman of Quintus. 20 feet in front.
EDCS-20401072.summary: This inscription is likely a boundary marker, designating 20 feet in front and mentioning Postumia, Catinia, and Quintus Atrius Philemo, a freedman.

EDCS-20401073.translation: To Clara, freedwoman of the woman Procilia. 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401073.summary: This is a boundary inscription for Clara, a freedwoman of Procilia, defining a plot of land with dimensions of 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field.

EDCS-20401074.translation: To Lucius Prusinius, son of Lucius, father; to Vibullia, daughter of Caius, mother; to Lucius Prusinius, son of Lucius, brother; to Prusinia, daughter of Lucius, sister. Marcus Prusinius, son of Lucius, and Caius Prusinius, son of Lucius, made (this).
EDCS-20401074.summary: This funerary monument was erected by two sons, Marcus and Caius Prusinius, to honor their parents and sister.

EDCS-20401075.translation: To the Divine Shades. Pharnaces to Pythiades, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401075.summary: This is a dedication to the shades of the departed (Dis Manibus) by Pharnaces for Pythiades.

EDCS-20401078.translation: Of Numerius Savonius Antigonus, 12 feet in front and 10 feet in the rear.
EDCS-20401078.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a funerary plot owned by Numerius Savonius Antigonus.

EDCS-20401079.translation: To Caius Sefronius C. f. Salvius, patron, with honor.
EDCS-20401079.summary: This is an inscription honoring Caius Sefronius Salvius, possibly as a patron, with a dedicatory element of 'CALL VT'.

EDCS-20401080.translation: To Lucius Septimius Hermes. Father (said): He lived 30 years, 6 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-20401080.summary: This tombstone records the life span of Lucius Septimius Hermes, erected by his father.

EDCS-20401081.translation: To Septueia Ge. Of Quintus Septueius. For 2 days.
EDCS-20401081.summary: This inscription likely records a brief period of service or connection for Septueia Ge, possibly related to Quintus Septueius.

EDCS-20401082.translation: To Marcus Som. Philar [son of] Pompe[ius?].
EDCS-20401082.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely naming Marcus Som and possibly his father or origin, Philar Pompeius.

EDCS-20401083.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aemilia Tertia made (this) to her incomparable husband, Staio Iustinus, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401083.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aemilia Tertia for her deserving husband, Staio Iustinus.

EDCS-20401084.translation: To the Divine Shades. Agathias to his deserving wife, Statilia Primitiva.
EDCS-20401084.summary: This is a dedication to the shades of the departed (Dis Manibus) by Agathias for his deserving wife, Statilia Primitiva.

EDCS-20401085.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aemilia Tertia made (this) to her deserving husband, Cornelius Phoebus.
EDCS-20401085.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aemilia Tertia for her deserving husband, Cornelius Phoebus.

EDCS-20401087.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Staedia Synerusa lived 10 months and 19 days. Quintus Staedius Chrysorias and Casinia Synerusa, her parents.
EDCS-20401087.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Staedia Synerusa, who died in infancy, set up by her parents.

EDCS-20401088.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed, for Terentia Felicitas.
EDCS-20401088.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Terentia Felicitas.

EDCS-20401089.translation: Lucius Thoranius Alexander for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-20401089.summary: This epitaph records a self-dedication by Lucius Thoranius Alexander for himself and his freed dependents.

EDCS-20401090.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tutilia Lasciva, a most unhappy mother, made this for her most sweet daughter Tutilia Clymene, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401090.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tutilia Clymene, erected by her grieving mother.

EDCS-20401094.translation: Of Gaius Ummidius Helenus, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-20401094.summary: This is a funerary dedication fragment for Gaius Ummidius Helenus.

EDCS-20401095.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Parents made this for their most dutiful son Ummidius Ianuarius, who lived 3 years, 5 months, and 10 days, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401095.summary: This funerary epitaph records Ummidius Ianuarius, who died in childhood, and was erected by his parents.

EDCS-20401096.translation: Of Gaius Ummidius Iustus, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-20401096.summary: This is a funerary dedication fragment for Gaius Ummidius Iustus.

EDCS-20401098.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary dedication, likely for Ummidia.

EDCS-20401099.translation: For Luccia, freedwoman of Quintus, wife of the freedman Salvius, for her heirs and mine.
EDCS-20401099.summary: This funerary dedication is for Luccia, the freedwoman wife of Salvius.

EDCS-20401106.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning Amomus.

EDCS-20401111.translation: Jupiter the cooked, Gaius Grat [---] for the road
EDCS-20401111.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication to Jupiter, possibly related to a road construction or repair project.

EDCS-20401113.translation: Vepellius L. VK I made [this] for his son, father
EDCS-20401113.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that a father, Vepellius L. VK I, made this monument for his son.

EDCS-20401119.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Idisa Santonia, daughter of Domitius, of the nation of the Titienses, IIII [---] her own
EDCS-20401119.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes for Idisa Santonia, a freedwoman of Domitius, likely from the Titienses tribe.

EDCS-20401123.translation: Hilarus, servant of Christ, rests here
EDCS-20401123.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription commemorating Hilarus, a 'servant of Christ'.

EDCS-20401124.translation: Rubenius Valerius, who lived 25 years and 7 months, was laid to rest in peace on the 7th day before the Ides of June. Rubenius Bracciatus and Licinia Victorina [placed this].
EDCS-20401124.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Rubenius Valerius at the age of 25 years and 7 months, placed by his parents, Rubenius Bracciatus and Licinia Victorina.

EDCS-20401125.translation: To Sol Invictus, companion of our Augustus.
EDCS-20401125.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the unconquered sun god, Sol Invictus, and associates him with the emperor.

EDCS-20401130.translation: For Aprucia Galla, daughter of Marcus, publicly.
EDCS-20401130.summary: This inscription records a public dedication or honor for Aprucia Galla, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-20401133.translation: To Lucius Caucidius Burrus, son of Lucius, former duovir of justice.
EDCS-20401133.summary: This is an inscription honoring Lucius Caucidius Burrus, son of Lucius, for his service as a duovir iure dicundo (magistrate responsible for justice).

EDCS-20401134.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Lucius Cornelius Primus, a member of the college of the Seviri Augustales.

EDCS-20401135.translation: Herennius, son of Lucius C, saw to the making and dedicated it.
EDCS-20401135.summary: This is a dedication inscription where Herennius, son of Lucius C, commissioned and dedicated a monument.

EDCS-20401136.translation: Lucius Laufeius Geta, son of Lucius, quaestor.
EDCS-20401136.summary: This is a career record for Lucius Laufeius Geta, indicating his quaestorship.

EDCS-20401138.translation: Marcus Novius Tubero, son of Marcus, quaestor.
EDCS-20401138.summary: This is a career record for Marcus Novius Tubero, indicating his quaestorship.

EDCS-20401142.translation: Dedicated on the day before the Nones of July, in the consulship of Bassus and Philippus, most excellent men. For Marcus Sentius Redemptus, a man of renown, foremost of our city, who had discharged all duties and honors of his curia, coming from the origins of patronage, who, out of his benevolence towards us, freed his people from the levy of gold and silver, and restored the summer baths, which had fallen into decay and ruin, to their utmost completeness from his own resources; seeing that his so many services towards us were heaped up, the entire people of Interamna resolved that a statue be erected to him in perpetuity.
EDCS-20401142.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Marcus Sentius Redemptus, who freed the people from taxes and restored public baths, likely dating to the consulship of Bassus and Philippus.

EDCS-20401148.translation: Marcus Lucceius Syneros, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen; Marcus Lucceius Diodotus, freedman of Marcus, and their descendants.
EDCS-20401148.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Lucceius Syneros for himself, his freedpersons, and their descendants.

EDCS-20401153.translation: For Terivia Chreste, freedwoman of Marcus Terivius, and for Prima, freedwoman of a woman, his patron, who deserved well.
EDCS-20401153.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Terivia Prima to her patroness, Terivia Chreste.

EDCS-20401154.translation: To Publius Manilius Ligirus, son of Tiberius, of the Palatina tribe, from his will, 60,000 sesterces, under the care of his freedmen Publius Manilius Phaeton, Publius Manilius Homero, and Publius Manilius Hilarus.
EDCS-20401154.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 60,000 sesterces from the will of Publius Manilius Ligirus, managed by his freedmen.

EDCS-20401155.translation: For Caius Valerius Fortunatus, who lived 20 years, 5 months, and 25 days. Caius Valerius Fortunatus, his father, and Tilliana Narria, his mother, for their most excellent and deserving son.
EDCS-20401155.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Valerius Fortunatus, set up by his parents and detailing his lifespan.

EDCS-20401160.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely part of a larger monument, referring to a deified son of a certain Marcus.

EDCS-20401165.summary: This inscription records the name Svdea Procil and her status as an Augustalis, likely a religious official.

EDCS-20401166.translation: To Codennius Severus, son of Aulus, of the Scaptia tribe, who served for 21 years in the 3rd Cyrenaica Legion. Sextus, his brother, and Epaphroditus, his freedman.
EDCS-20401166.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Codennius Severus, a soldier who served 21 years in the 3rd Cyrenaica Legion, set up by his brother and freedman.

EDCS-20401167.translation: To Lucius Cocceius Augustalis of the colonia Neronensis in Puteoli, dedicated by Claudia Augusta.
EDCS-20401167.summary: This is a dedication from Claudia Augusta to Lucius Cocceius Augustalis at Puteoli, likely a public monument from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401171.translation: Publius Stahius, son of Publius, a wreath-maker. Publius Stahius, son of Publius, freedman; Dio. Stahia Ammia, daughter of Publius, freedwoman.
EDCS-20401171.summary: This funerary inscription records the names and relationships of freedmen and freedwomen, likely belonging to the Stahius family, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401173.translation: To Marcus Badio Potitus and Marcus Badio Chariton.
EDCS-20401173.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Badio Potitus and Marcus Badio Chariton, possibly a family monument from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401176.translation: Sacred to the Good and Holy Goddess. Terentia Thallusa gladly made this in fulfillment of a vow made in accordance with desert.
EDCS-20401176.summary: This is a votive dedication to Bona Dea, made by Terentia Thallusa, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401177.translation: Sacred to the Holy Fortune. Terentia Tallusa gladly made this in fulfillment of a vow made in accordance with desert.
EDCS-20401177.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Fortuna, made by Terentia Tallusa, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401178.translation: An offering to Heracles, bearer of the thallus, holy and readily heard. Lucius Cornelius, son of Lucius Cornelius, of the Palatina tribe Terentianus, and Lemnius, freedman, made [this]. To Hercules, the Peaceful, Unconquered, Holy. They willingly made [this] in fulfillment of a vow made in accordance with desert.
EDCS-20401178.summary: This bilingual inscription records a votive offering to Heracles/Hercules made by Lucius Cornelius Terentianus and his freedman Lemnius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401180.translation: Germanicus and Leda fulfilled their vow to the divine power of Isis of Aponus.
EDCS-20401180.summary: This is a votive inscription to the divine power of Isis of Aponus, fulfilled by Germanicus and Leda, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401181.translation: The magistrates give a small temple and a base: Manius Pullius, son of Manius; Manius Ofellius, son of Vibius; Publius Maamius, son of Publius; Publius Servius, freedman of Publius ThrHaso; Lucius Vennonius, freedman of Lucius Prosamus.
EDCS-20401181.summary: This inscription records the construction of a small temple and base by a group of magistrates, likely public officials responsible for civic building projects during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401183.translation: To Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, consul II, [---]
EDCS-20401183.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Augustus, mentioning his titles as pontifex maximus and consul, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20401184.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country.
EDCS-20401184.summary: This is a formal dedication to Emperor Valerian, listing his extensive imperial titles and honors, dating to his reign in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-20401188.translation: To Julia Pelagia, daughter of Caius, wife of Marcus Calpurnius Eregentus, most distinguished man and patron of the colony; for her merits, the entire people of Aquinum decreed this, at public expense.
EDCS-20401188.summary: This is a public monument erected by the people of Aquinum to Julia Pelagia for her merits.

EDCS-20401195.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Herius Verus served for 5 years in the 11th Urban Cohort, to Quintus Herius Sabinianus and Quintus Herius Verinus.
EDCS-20401195.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Quintus Herius Verus, a soldier in the 11th Urban Cohort, with mentions of other family members.

EDCS-20401196.translation: To the departed spirits. To Quintus Titius Rufus, a soldier in the 11th cohort, for 5 years of service, who lived 19 years and 20 days. Iulia Grata, his mother, made this for her most devoted son.
EDCS-20401196.summary: A tombstone erected by a mother for her son, Quintus Titius Rufus, a soldier who died at a young age.

EDCS-20401199.translation: To the departed spirits. Aemilia Restituta, wife of Dentrius Crescentis. Her husband dedicated this. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20401199.summary: A tombstone dedicated by a husband to his wife, Aemilia Restituta, with the burial plot granted by official decree.

EDCS-20401200.translation: Gaius Aiedius, son of Gaius, of the Lemonia tribe, 35 years old, at his own expense.
EDCS-20401200.summary: An epitaph for Gaius Aiedius, indicating his age and that he paid for the monument himself.

EDCS-20401201.summary: An inscription identifying Titus Animisius as a decurion, likely an epitaph or a dedication.

EDCS-20401202.translation: To Aurellia Salutia, dearest and incomparable wife, both for her merits and her obedience, which she showed to her husband, and for the great efforts she made during difficult times, and for remaining pure towards me, and for her son Septimius Reverentius. Septimius Montanus, her husband, made this in memory of her. She came from the Flavian family and lived 55 years, 6 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-20401202.summary: A tombstone erected by a husband, Septimius Montanus, to his wife Aurellia Salutia, praising her virtues and detailing her family lineage and lifespan.

EDCS-20401205.translation: Quintus Decius, son of Marcius. Gnaeus Helv[---]
EDCS-20401205.summary: An incomplete inscription naming Quintus Decius, son of Marcius, and the beginning of another name, possibly an epitaph or dedication.

EDCS-20401208.translation: To the departed spirits. To Caius Iulius Euphrosius, who was aedile twice and duovir in Aquinum, and also patron of the association of brassworkers. Caerellia Phoebe made this for her most devoted and loving husband. They lived together for 23 years and 11 days.
EDCS-20401208.summary: A tombstone dedicated by Caerellia Phoebe to her husband, Caius Iulius Euphrosius, who held several civic and collegial offices in Aquinum.

EDCS-20401210.translation: To Quintus Ovius Urus, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe, duovir with judicial authority in Casinum.
EDCS-20401210.summary: An inscription honoring Quintus Ovius Urus, identifying him as a duovir with judicial authority in the town of Casinum.

EDCS-20401211.translation: Manius Popidius Anteros, a *sevir*, for himself and for Popidia Melpomeni, freedwoman of M. Manius, and for Opetreia Thetis, freedwoman of Publius, and for Manius Popidius Hilarus, freedman of M. Manius, his fellow freedmen.
EDCS-20401211.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Manius Popidius Anteros for himself and his freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-20401214.translation: To Publius Satrius Rufus, our patron, by the *curatores* and *publicani*.
EDCS-20401214.summary: This is a dedication by public officials to their patron, Publius Satrius Rufus.

EDCS-20401215.translation: To Servia, daughter of Caius, priestess of Liber Pater of Aquinum.
EDCS-20401215.summary: This is a dedication to Servia, a priestess of the god Liber Pater in Aquinum.

EDCS-20401216.translation: Lucius Vettius Eros, son of Lucius, a *sevir* once more and the first *Augustalis*, made this for himself, and for his wife Tertia, freedwoman of Cnaeus, and for his freedwoman Aucta, and for Gaius Vettius Avitus, son of Caius, of the Oufentina tribe, while alive.
EDCS-20401216.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Vettius Eros for himself, his wife, and a freedwoman.

EDCS-20401217.translation: Statius Vibius Andricus, freedman of St. Statius, a *sevir*, for himself and for Tilia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus, and for their descendants. In front, 15.5 feet; in the field, 12 feet.
EDCS-20401217.summary: This funerary inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land set aside by Statius Vibius Andricus for himself and his family.

EDCS-20401218.translation: The colonists, by decree of the *decurions*, for Volumnius Pr., their patron, publicly.
EDCS-20401218.summary: This is a public dedication by the colonists of a town to their patron, Volumnius Pr.

EDCS-20401220.translation: He made this while alive, Sextus Pthongus, a *sevir* of the people of Aquinum, for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-20401220.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Sextus Pthongus, a *sevir*, for his family.

EDCS-20401222.translation: I lived twenty-seven years, Gaius Matienus Ovicula, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe, a herald and also a designer. The Fates granted me a long life, but now, from a small pile of ashes, my bones collected, I have been placed beneath this stone, and my voice will answer no companion, nor will solace come to my sweet mother and father, whom no day will see reborn. But my fate, allowed by the Fates, was to be well laid to rest.
EDCS-20401222.summary: This is a personal epitaph of Gaius Matienus Ovicula, a herald, lamenting his early death and thanking the Fates for a peaceful burial.

EDCS-20401223.translation: Of Nammius, freedman of Gaius, the herald.
EDCS-20401223.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nammius, a freedman and a herald.

EDCS-20401224.translation: For Acilaia, daughter of H., his wife, and for his descendants.
EDCS-20401224.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Acilaia and the descendants of her husband.

EDCS-20401225.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aetrilius Severus and Clodia Luperca made this for Marcus Aetrilius Severus, their most dutiful father, and for Clodia Luperca, their incomparable and deserving wife.
EDCS-20401225.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Aetrilius Severus and Clodia Luperca to their father and wife, respectively.

EDCS-20401226.translation: Of Marcion, freedman of Marcus Alphius.
EDCS-20401226.summary: An inscription likely marking a tomb or property belonging to Marcion, a freedman.

EDCS-20401227.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Her parents made this for their sweetest daughter, Alfia Hermaphrodite, a deserving soul, who lived 9 years and 10 days.
EDCS-20401227.summary: A tombstone for a young girl named Alfia Hermaphrodite, erected by her parents.

EDCS-20401228.translation: Of Marcus Allius, son of Lucius, for his descendants for 13 years.
EDCS-20401228.summary: An inscription possibly related to a funerary plot or endowment for the descendants of Marcus Allius.

EDCS-20401229.translation: For Titus Allius, son of Publius, of the Oufentina tribe, for himself and for his freedmen and freedwomen, according to his will.
EDCS-20401229.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Allius, specifying beneficiaries according to his will.

EDCS-20401230.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Julius Crestus made this for Lucius Annius, son of Caius, named Minos, who lived about 45 years, his friend and husband, a deserving husband.
EDCS-20401230.summary: A funerary monument erected by Caius Julius Crestus for his friend and husband, Lucius Annius Minos.

EDCS-20401231.summary: An incomplete inscription that begins to record the lifespan of a person named Apiola.

EDCS-20401232.translation: Apollon, freedman of Publius, husband for himself and...
EDCS-20401232.summary: An incomplete inscription that likely refers to a funerary dedication made by Apollon, a freedman, for himself and possibly his spouse.

EDCS-20401234.translation: The bones of Aquinia, wife of Lucius Tullus.
EDCS-20401234.summary: An inscription indicating the burial place of Aquinia, wife of Lucius Tullus.

EDCS-20401235.translation: Marcus Aruntius, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, while alive, set this up: 8 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401235.summary: A property marker or boundary stone set up by Marcus Aruntius, likely defining the extent of his land.

EDCS-20401236.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Aurelius Priscianus made this for his most dear and well-deserving brother, Marcus Aurelius Calpurnianus, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-20401236.summary: A funerary dedication from a brother to his deceased brother.

EDCS-20401237.translation: Eutyches, freedman of Lucius Aurellius Valens.
EDCS-20401237.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for his patron.

EDCS-20401238.translation: To Paulla, daughter of Marcus, of the Vuncedi family.
EDCS-20401238.summary: An epitaph for a woman identified by her father and family name.

EDCS-20401239.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely identifying a person.

EDCS-20401241.translation: Bambina, freedwoman of Lucius Pergamini, 12 feet in front and in the field.
EDCS-20401241.summary: A property boundary marker indicating dimensions and ownership.

EDCS-20401242.translation: To Prima, freedwoman of Baronia and Decimus.
EDCS-20401242.summary: A funerary dedication by freedwomen to their patrons.

EDCS-20401243.translation: By the arbitration of Gaius Betutius, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, and of Publius Alphius, freedman of Publius, Philomusus.
EDCS-20401243.summary: A legal inscription detailing an arbitration concerning property.

EDCS-20401244.translation: Lexis, freedwoman of Betutia, lived 6 years. Marcus Betutius Ametistus (made this).
EDCS-20401244.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young freedwoman, likely set up by her former owner.

EDCS-20401245.translation: Of Gaius Blaius, freedman of a woman; of Hilarius, freedman of Gaius Blaius and a woman; of Salvia, freedwoman of Gaius Blaius and Hilarius; of Philomusus, freedman of Gaius Blaius and of a woman; of Salvius, freedman of Gaius Blaius and of a woman.
EDCS-20401245.summary: A complex funerary inscription listing multiple freedmen and freedwomen within a family or household.

EDCS-20401246.translation: Of Marcus Blossius, freedman of Marcus; of Maria Hilara, freedwoman of Caius. A place given.
EDCS-20401246.summary: A funerary dedication indicating the allocation of burial space.

EDCS-20401247.translation: Lucius Caerellius Munda, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-20401247.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Caerellius Munda, son of Gaius, who belonged to the Oufentina tribe.

EDCS-20401248.translation: Marcus Caesius Caligar, son of Marcus, son of Mami, lives.
EDCS-20401248.summary: This inscription likely records the survival or presence of Marcus Caesius Caligar, son of Marcus, son of Mami.

EDCS-20401249.translation: Tito Caesonio Liguri, freedman of Titus, son of Titus, of the Oufentina tribe, and to Tito Caesonio, son of Gnaeus, Titus Caesarion ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-20401249.summary: This is a funerary dedication commissioned in a will by Titus Caesonius for his freedman Tito Liguri and another relative, Tito Caesonio.

EDCS-20401250.summary: This is a dedication to Philumina, the freedwoman of Calavia.

EDCS-20401251.translation: Gnaeus Caprus, son of Gnaeus, son of Quintus, son of Gnaeus Caprus.
EDCS-20401251.summary: This inscription names Gnaeus Caprus, son of Gnaeus, son of Quintus, son of Gnaeus Caprus.

EDCS-20401252.translation: To Chilon, son of Gaius Caprus; to Stephen, freedman of Gaius, son of Gaius Caprus; to my father.
EDCS-20401252.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Chilon, Stephen, and the dedicator's father.

EDCS-20401253.translation: Lucius Caprius Rufus, son of Lucius, born into the Vitellia tribe.
EDCS-20401253.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Caprius Rufus, son of Lucius, and notes his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-20401254.summary: This is a funerary marker for Hilara, freedwoman of Sextus, identified as a mother.

EDCS-20401255.translation: Lucius Cominius, son of Lucius, for himself and Lucius Cominius and Caesias.
EDCS-20401255.summary: This is a dedication made by Lucius Cominius, son of Lucius, for himself and for Lucius Cominius and Caesias.

EDCS-20401256.translation: Elegans, during his lifetime, for himself and his wife Quieta, freedwoman of Cupania, and his daughter Cupania Saturnina, and his own [family].
EDCS-20401256.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Elegans during his lifetime for himself, his wife Quieta, and his daughter Cupania Saturnina.

EDCS-20401257.translation: Aulo Dentrio Epacatho lives on, for himself and for Dentria Prima, Tertia, daughter of Aulus Dentrius, and for their descendants; 12 feet in front.
EDCS-20401257.summary: This inscription records a property boundary, likely for a tomb or land, established by Aulo Dentrio Epacatho for himself and his family.

EDCS-20401258.summary: This is a funerary epigram commemorating Dionysia, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-20401259.translation: Of Titus Ennius Auctus, freedman of Titus; 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401259.summary: This inscription indicates property boundaries for Titus Ennius Auctus, a freedman.

EDCS-20401260.translation: Of Marcus Demetrius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20401260.summary: This inscription likely serves as an ownership marker or a dedication for Marcus Demetrius, a freedman.

EDCS-20401261.translation: Opetreia Thetis. Here Vetreia Thetis lies. Here the bone, mixed with ashes when the swift fire fell, and settled on the golden cinders of the pyre, the bones of Thetis are placed, being subject to the weight, more pleasing to the earth than to you, hard stone. This we are, as you see, we are honored by an empty inscription, garlands which often encircle the tomb, and smooth onyxes, slender alabaster bottles, and arranged fruit, all of their season.
