EDCS-20401261.summary: This is a poetic epitaph for Opetreia Thetis, reflecting on mortality, the ashes of cremation, and the ephemeral nature of earthly possessions, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20401262.translation: Lives on! To Gaius Tellutius Protos for himself, and for Ammia Tusca, freedwoman of Lucius, his concubine, and for Tellutia Hilara.
EDCS-20401262.summary: This inscription records a dedication or property marker established by Gaius Tellutius Protos for himself, his concubine Ammia Tusca, and Tellutia Hilara.

EDCS-20401263.translation: The freedmen of Marcus Fuficius Mani, Sextus and Anepetus, live on; 16 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401263.summary: This inscription marks property boundaries for Sextus and Anepetus, freedmen of Marcus Fuficius Mani.

EDCS-20401264.translation: To Furius, son of Caius, a seviri.
EDCS-20401264.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to Furius, son of Caius, who held the office of seviri.

EDCS-20401265.summary: This inscription indicates a bequest or provision made by Gaius according to his will.

EDCS-20401266.translation: Marcus Galgestes, son of Caius, from Po[---].
EDCS-20401266.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or identification marker for Marcus Galgestes, son of Caius, possibly indicating his origin from Po[---].

EDCS-20401267.translation: Maruleia, daughter of Gaius, from the Po tribe, daughter of Lucius, made this for Gennius.
EDCS-20401267.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Maruleia to Gennius, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-20401269.translation: Marcus Helvius, son of Marcus, from the Teretina tribe, made this for his son Rufus, son of Marcus, from the Baiae Ferroniae tribe.
EDCS-20401269.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Marcus Helvius for his son Rufus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-20401270.translation: To Heraclius, son of Menos, from INRVILLUS.
EDCS-20401270.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Heraclius, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-20401271.summary: This is a simple dedication, likely a funerary epitaph, to Marcus Herennius Niger.

EDCS-20401272.translation: Vitellius Appas made this for his dearest, well-deserving sons, Inventa, who lived 3 years, 3 months, and Leon, who lived 4 years, 9 days.
EDCS-20401272.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Vitellius Appas for his young children, Inventa and Leon.

EDCS-20401273.translation: Of Quintus Julius Labeo, son of Quintus, from the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-20401273.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely an epitaph, identifying Quintus Julius Labeo.

EDCS-20401274.translation: To the Divine Manes. Julia Naminiana made this for her most dutiful mother, Julia Fortunata, deserving of good treatment.
EDCS-20401274.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Julia Naminiana for her mother, Julia Fortunata.

EDCS-20401275.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Laberius Charito made this for his incomparable wife, Laberia Felicitas.
EDCS-20401275.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Laberius Charito to his wife, Laberia Felicitas.

EDCS-20401276.translation: Lacutulana Gemella for herself and for her husband Marcus Lacutulanus Lacon, son of Marcus, and for her son Marcus Lacutulanus Marcellus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-20401276.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lacutulana Gemella for herself and her family members, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-20401277.translation: For Quintus Dios, who lived 20 years, piously.
EDCS-20401277.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Dios, noting his piety and age at death.

EDCS-20401278.translation: To Gaius Lepidus, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-20401278.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Lepidus, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe.

EDCS-20401281.translation: Numerius Niserius, freedman of Numerius Lucius, and Rufrania Salvia placed [this monument].
EDCS-20401281.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Numerius Niserius, freedman of Numerius Lucius, and Rufrania Salvia.

EDCS-20401282.translation: For Philerotis, freedman of Lucius Lucius Lucius; for Vitellius, freedman of Lucius Lucius Lucius; for Epaphroditus, freedman of Lucius Lucius Lucius; for Dada, freedwoman of Lucia Lucia; for Daphnenis, freedwoman of Lucia Lucia; for Arbitris, freedman of Lucius Lucius Lucius; for Caterva, freedman of Lucius Lucius Lucius; and for Auge, freedwoman of Tampia, a freedwoman.
EDCS-20401282.summary: This inscription records the dedication to multiple freedmen and freedwomen, likely a family group.

EDCS-20401283.translation: Marcus Lucius Theodorus for himself and for Luciana Laina, his freedwoman colleague, and for Luciana Prima, his concubine, and for his family, [a plot of land] 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401283.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Marcus Lucius Theodorus for himself, his freedwoman colleague, his concubine, and his family, specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-20401284.summary: This is a dedication to Luttia Peregrina.

EDCS-20401285.translation: Of Marcus, freedman of Marcus Mamius, Eunus, and of Mamia, freedwoman of Marcus Mamius, Chelidon.
EDCS-20401285.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedpersons, Eunus and Chelidon, associated with Marcus Mamius.

EDCS-20401286.translation: Of Marcus Mamimenus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-20401286.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Mamimenus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-20401287.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Manlius Glaucio erected this for Lucius Manlius Oufentinas Montanus, son of Lucius, for himself and for Animisia Restituta, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife, and for Lucius Manlius Oufentinas Aper, son of Lucius. Montanus is buried here, snatched away by a wicked woman's hand, unexpectedly. It would have been right and proper for him, having been born, to have performed the funeral rites for us instead, and honored worthy ancestors and parents, had fortune preserved them piously; [and] the vows of parents.
EDCS-20401287.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription and epitaph for Lucius Manlius Oufentinas Montanus, detailing his death and expressing the grief and unmet expectations of his family, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20401288.translation: Medea Ampliata made [this] for herself and for Medea, daughter of Marcus, her patroness Volsca, and for her husband Marcus Satrius Receptus, and for her family, 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field. She lived 19 years.
EDCS-20401288.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Medea Ampliata for herself, her patroness, her husband, and her family, also recording her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401289.translation: To Minatia Helpin, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-20401289.summary: This is a dedication to Minatia Helpin, freedwoman of Gaius.

EDCS-20401290.translation: Murria Antusa, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and her partner Tiberius Claudius Senes, 14 feet of land.
EDCS-20401290.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a land grant by a freedwoman for herself and her partner, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20401291.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Rennius Hilarus made this for his incomparable and deserving wife, Navia Primula, with whom he lived for 22 years.
EDCS-20401291.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Navia Primula, set up by her husband Publius Rennius Hilarus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20401292.translation: To Nicenis, darling of Dionysus, freedman of Publius Alfius, and of Apicla, freedwoman of Lucius, freedman of Publius Alfius. She lived six years.
EDCS-20401292.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Nicenis, likely the pet of a family, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401294.translation: Servus, son of Servus, of the Ofillii, of the Oufentina tribe, lives; 12 feet in the front, 16 feet in the back.
EDCS-20401294.summary: This is a boundary inscription defining a plot of land allocated to Servus, son of Servus, likely from the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20401295.translation: Lucius Coelius Asclepiades, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-20401295.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly recording the name of a freedman and his patron, Lucius Coelius Asclepiades, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401296.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For the sweetest Lucius Ofilius Severus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-20401296.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Ofilius Severus, set up by his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401299.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording the name of Peregrina, daughter of Luilius, possibly a funerary or ownership marker from the Roman period.

EDCS-20401300.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Petronia Epictesis, deserving freedwoman of her patron. Rusticus and Felicissima [set this up].
EDCS-20401300.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Petronia Epictesis, set up by her freedmen Rusticus and Felicissima, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401301.translation: For Petronia Maxima, daughter of Publius. She lived 19 years.
EDCS-20401301.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia Maxima, recording her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401302.translation: Lucius Pomponius, son of Sextus, of the Oufentina tribe, [son] of Farro.
EDCS-20401302.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the full name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Pomponius, likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20401303.translation: To the Divine Shades. Animisius Marcelinus to his incomparable wife, Pomponia Florida, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-20401303.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401304.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, mentioning a name and possibly an age or status.

EDCS-20401305.translation: Prosia, daughter of Marcus. At the front, 16 feet.
EDCS-20401305.summary: This inscription records the funerary plot dimensions, likely for Prosia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-20401306.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Pyladis.

EDCS-20401307.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cnaeus Roscius Primus, for his well-deserving wife, Aufidia Fregellana, made this.
EDCS-20401307.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband, Cnaeus Roscius Primus, to his wife, Aufidia Fregellana.

EDCS-20401308.translation: Rufa, Rasinia, freedwoman of Lucius Dani, and Clara, freedwoman, and Rasinia Felix.
EDCS-20401308.summary: This inscription lists the names of several women, possibly related or freedwomen, the purpose is unclear but likely funerary or commemorative.

EDCS-20401309.translation: To Viria, freedwoman of Publius, for her wife, Rufa.
EDCS-20401309.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Viria to her wife, Rufa, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-20401312.translation: Publius Satrius, son of Lucius, gave this burial plot to Publius Hilarus Tyrannidus, freedman, and to Perennus and Sextus Tertius: 12 feet at the front, 14 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401312.summary: This inscription records the grant of a burial plot by Publius Satrius to his freedman and others, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-20401313.translation: Living: Numerius Satrius Hilarus, freedman of Numerius Satrius; Numerius Satrius Andreas, freedman of Numerius Satrius. At the front, 16 feet; in the field, 16 feet. To Fertoria, his wife.
EDCS-20401313.summary: This inscription records the funerary plot dimensions and names individuals, including freedmen and a wife, likely related to a burial monument.

EDCS-20401315.translation: Sextus Segius, son of Caius, of the tribe Oufentina.
EDCS-20401315.summary: This is a simple inscription recording the name and tribal affiliation of Sextus Segius, likely for a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-20401316.translation: To Titus Septimius Priscus, son of Titus, Titus Septimius Cerealis, to his most dutiful son and to himself and his descendants.
EDCS-20401316.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Septimius Cerealis for his son, Titus Septimius Priscus, and for himself and his descendants.

EDCS-20401317.translation: Aged 70 years, 2 months, and 5 days, Tertulla, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-20401317.summary: This epitaph records the age and parentage of Tertulla.

EDCS-20401318.translation: To Gaius Timinius Olillus, son of Gaius, (and) Timinia Helena, daughter of Gaius, (and) Timinia Arche...
EDCS-20401318.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to members of the Timinius family, likely a husband and wife and their child.

EDCS-20401319.translation: To Travia Tertia, daughter of Quintus, 12 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401319.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Travia Tertia, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-20401320.translation: To Quintus Trebius Quirina, father, to Lucius Trebius, son of Publius, to Quirina, son, 16 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401320.summary: This inscription records land measurements for a funerary plot belonging to Quintus Trebius Quirina and his son Lucius Trebius.

EDCS-20401321.translation: Trebia, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and for Publius Trebius, freedman of Publius, patron, and for Publius Trebius, son of Publius, son, 14 feet in front, 14 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401321.summary: This funerary inscription details land measurements for Trebia and her freedman patron Publius Trebius, and another Publius Trebius.

EDCS-20401322.translation: To Sextus Turvenus, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe, by will, 2000 sesterces; the heir shall not succeed.
EDCS-20401322.summary: This funerary dedication from Sextus Turvenus, son of Gaius, bequeaths 2000 sesterces and stipulates that the heir will not inherit.

EDCS-20401323.translation: Lucius Vitorious, freedman of Lucius, and Clarum, and Dentria, freedwoman of Titus, and Hilara, give.
EDCS-20401323.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication or gift by Lucius Vitorious and his freedwoman Dentria and freedwoman Hilara.

EDCS-20401324.translation: Varia Mamoena, freedwoman of Decimus, (dedicates this) to Lucius Vibius Hilarus, 14 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401324.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of 14 feet in the field, dedicated by Varia Mamoena to Lucius Vibius Hilarus.

EDCS-20401325.translation: Marcus Varus, freedman of Marcus Ucaesius, 14 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401325.summary: This inscription marks the funerary plot of Marcus Varus, freedman of Marcus Ucaesius, with its dimensions.

EDCS-20401326.translation: Mio Verecun lived for 53 years and 9 days. Aurelia La made this for her deserving wife, with whom she lived without offense.
EDCS-20401326.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Mio Verecun and was erected by his wife Aurelia La.

EDCS-20401327.translation: To Vergilia Secunda, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-20401327.summary: This is an epitaph for Vergilia Secunda, a freedwoman of Marcus.

EDCS-20401328.translation: Publius Urtica, son of Publius Vettius, aged 15.
EDCS-20401328.summary: This epitaph records the age of Publius Urtica, son of Publius Vettius.

EDCS-20401331.translation: To Lucius Vibronius, son of Caius, of the tribe Oufentina, a sevirus, 12 feet in front and [---] feet in the field.
EDCS-20401331.summary: This inscription seems to be a boundary marker or land division for Lucius Vibronius, a sevirus.

EDCS-20401332.translation: To Vicrius Iucundus, son of Felix.
EDCS-20401332.summary: This is an epitaph for Vicrius Iucundus, son of Felix.

EDCS-20401335.translation: The bones of Marcus Vicrius Prothymus, son of Numerius.
EDCS-20401335.summary: This is an ossuary inscription for Marcus Vicrius Prothymus, son of Numerius.

EDCS-20401336.translation: To Vicria Prima, [---] feet in front.
EDCS-20401336.summary: This inscription likely refers to a burial plot or boundary marker for Vicria Prima.

EDCS-20401337.translation: To Villia Maxuma, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-20401337.summary: This is an epitaph for Villia Maxuma, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-20401338.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Vitteia Luculla, daughter of Lucius, made this for herself, her father Lucius Vitteius Gemellus, and their descendants, [---] feet in front and [---] feet in the field.
EDCS-20401338.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Vitteia Luculla for herself, her father, and descendants, possibly marking a tomb or land.

EDCS-20401340.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Umidia Servanda made this for her deserving husband, Umidius Secundus.
EDCS-20401340.summary: This epitaph records Umidia Servanda dedicating a monument to her well-deserving husband, Umidius Secundus.

EDCS-20401341.translation: To Pidiana Urbana, daughter of Caius, lived 19 years.
EDCS-20401341.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pidiana Urbana, who died at the age of 19.

EDCS-20401342.translation: To Uttedia Quarta, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-20401342.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Uttedia Quarta, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-20401344.translation: To Lucretus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, [---].
EDCS-20401344.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucretus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe.

EDCS-20401345.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Cefimmitius Lucius Pomponius Festus, son of Marcus, freedman of the MA, and his freedman Festus, son of Caius.
EDCS-20401345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Pomponius Festus and his freedman Festus.

EDCS-20401346.translation: Appius Vecius for himself, and for Vecius, son of Marcus, of the Fidiclanian tribe, and for his family.
EDCS-20401346.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Appius Vecius, his son Vecius, and their family.

EDCS-20401347.translation: His unhappy father [dedicated this] and for himself.
EDCS-20401347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed individual, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-20401351.translation: To Caius Seicimenus, son of Caius, 12 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-20401351.summary: This inscription records land boundaries for Caius Seicimenus, son of Caius.

EDCS-20401358.translation: For Marcus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, 18 feet in front.
EDCS-20401358.summary: This inscription records land boundaries for Marcus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe.

EDCS-20401367.translation: The Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus to Jupiter the Preserver.
EDCS-20401367.summary: This is a dedication by Emperor Diocletian to Jupiter the Preserver, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-20401368.summary: This is a dedication to the Emperor Hadrian, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20401369.translation: To Julia Calvina, daughter of Quintus, of Lucius Alfidius Herennianus, consul, Fabraterni Novani, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20401369.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Julia Calvina, honoring her by decree of the local council, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-20401370.translation: [Praetextatus], member of the board of three for the minting of gold, silver, and bronze, and quaestor.
EDCS-20401370.summary: This fragment names an individual, Praetextatus, and lists his magistracies related to public finance and administration, likely from an official record or monument.

EDCS-20401372.translation: Marcus Trebellius Sextanus, son of Gaius, duovir, duovir quinquennalis, military tribune, prefect of the fabrica, augur, for himself and for his father Gaius Trebellius Sextanus, son of Sextus; for his paternal grandmother Genniae, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-20401372.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the magistracies and family relationships of Marcus Trebellius Sextanus, a prominent local official.

EDCS-20401373.translation: Publius Valgius Barba, son of Publius, grandson of Publius, of the Tromentina tribe, military tribune, duovir, pontifex.
EDCS-20401373.summary: This inscription lists the career of Publius Valgius Barba, a local magistrate and priest, likely set up on a public building or monument.

EDCS-20401375.translation: To Gaius Apidius Fronton, son of Gaius, of the Palatina tribe, duovir, prefect, holder of duoviral power, duovir quinquennalis, patron of the municipality of Fabrateri, most excellent father.
EDCS-20401375.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Apidius Fronton, a patron and high-ranking local official, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-20401377.translation: To Lucius Mundicius Musca, son of Lucius, duovir, by his freedmen.
EDCS-20401377.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Mundicius Musca, a duovir, made by his freedmen, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-20401378.translation: [Pollio], son of Gaius, of the Tromentina tribe, duovir with aedilician power, duovir, duovir for the second time, augur of Fabrateri.
EDCS-20401378.summary: This fragment details the magistracies and religious offices of an individual named Pollio, likely a local official.

EDCS-20401384.translation: To Marcus Trebellius Scurra, freedman of Marcus, Augustalis seviri, Attia Amianthis, freedwoman of Gaius, his wife, for herself and for her son Gaius Attius Nicerotes, freedman of Gaius; for Gaius Attius Faustus, freedman of Gaius; for Trebellia Onomasti, freedwoman of Marcus; for Gaius Attius Felix, the boy, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius. She made it.
EDCS-20401384.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Attia Amianthis for her husband Marcus Trebellius Scurra, a freedman and Augustalis, and other family members.

EDCS-20401391.translation: Sextus, son of C., man of P. F.
EDCS-20401391.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name and tribal affiliation, the exact context or purpose is unclear without further information.

EDCS-20401393.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription bearing the name Annaea Proma Sancta.

EDCS-20401397.translation: Lucius Bruttius Tertius, son of Lucius, of the Tromentina tribe, and his freedwoman Hilara, set up this boundary stone from their own funds.
EDCS-20401397.summary: This inscription records the setting up of a boundary stone by Lucius Bruttius Tertius and his freedwoman Hilara.

EDCS-20401398.translation: Gaius Caecilius Cimber, freedman of Gaius, son of Rufus.
EDCS-20401398.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph for Gaius Caecilius Cimber.

EDCS-20401399.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a record of a transaction involving Gaius Ipius and Marcus Appius.

EDCS-20401401.translation: To Lucius Cornelius Trophimus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-20401401.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Trophimus, a freedman.

EDCS-20401403.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hilara, a freedwoman.

EDCS-20401404.translation: Magullia Rufa, daughter of Gaius, for herself and her family, according to her will.
EDCS-20401404.summary: This inscription records Magullia Rufa setting aside property for herself and her family in her will.

EDCS-20401408.translation: Lucius Mevius Philemo, freedman of Lucius, and Mevia Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius, give from their own property.
EDCS-20401408.summary: This inscription records Lucius Mevius Philemo and Mevia Hilara donating property from their own resources.

EDCS-20401412.translation: Lucius Ovius, son of Numerius, Cornelia; Lucius Ovius, son of Lucius, Cornelia.
EDCS-20401412.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of individuals, possibly related, and their tribal affiliation (Cornelia).

EDCS-20401414.translation: To the freedwoman of Aulus, Natia, and to Quintus Planus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-20401414.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Natia, a freedwoman of Aulus, and Quintus Planus.

EDCS-20401415.translation: To Statius Popillius Theonus, from the will, 50,000 sesterces.
EDCS-20401415.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 50,000 sesterces to Statius Popillius Theonus, as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-20401423.translation: LICINIUS, son of LICINIUS, dedicated to his children.
EDCS-20401423.summary: This inscription, likely fragmentary, records a dedication by Licinius to his children and is presumed to be of Roman Imperial date.

EDCS-20401424.translation: Annia to her husband Maenius and to themselves.
EDCS-20401424.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Annia to her husband Maenius, and is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401437.translation: Mustela rests here in peace, who lived one year, 4 months, and 13 days, buried on the 8th day before the Ides of December, in the consulship of Tatianus and Symmachus, most excellent men.
EDCS-20401437.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Mustela, who died at a young age, and provides a precise date of death based on the consulship of Tatianus and Symmachus in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-20401438.translation: The old cultivators of Hercules, with Caius Vettius Clemens acting as patron, on a site given by Caius Titius Decimus, the patron.
EDCS-20401438.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a site by Caius Titius Decimus to the old cultivators of Hercules, overseen by Caius Vettius Clemens, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401439.translation: Caius, son of Caius, freedman, had this made again from his own money for Juno Regina, he gave it again from his own money.
EDCS-20401439.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Juno Regina made by Caius, a freedman, from his own funds, probably during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401441.translation: To the pious, happy, August Flavius Valerius Constantinus, by the old cultivators of Fabrateria.
EDCS-20401441.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Flavius Valerius Constantinus by the old cultivators of Fabrateria, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-20403127.translation: To the restorer of the Anicii family, for his distinguished services, the order and people of the city of Vetusla, to their most worthy patron.
EDCS-20403127.summary: This inscription honors a patron, likely a member of the Anicii family, for his services to the city of Vetusla, probably dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-20403129.translation: Titus Aelius Aelianus, son of Titus, of the Palatina tribe, patron of the municipality, and the townspeople and people of the old Fabraterni, for his services, made this.
EDCS-20403129.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the citizens and townspeople of Fabrateria to their patron Titus Aelius Aelianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403134.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Aphrodisia, a freedwoman of Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403140.translation: Gravinus, Caius Servilius Anteros, Melanthus, Herennius, Publius Opetreius Hilarus, Eubulus, the six officers of the DE [cult?].
EDCS-20403140.summary: This inscription lists the names of six men who held an office, possibly related to a religious cult ('DE'), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403143.translation: Gaius Vettius Anthus [dedicates to] the Lares and...
EDCS-20403143.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Vettius Anthus to the Lares, with the rest of the inscription missing.

EDCS-20403144.translation: To the Divine Manes. Sextus Satrius Iustus, son of Sextus, of the Oufentina tribe, a soldier of the 10th Praetorian cohort, in the century of Sabinianus, served for 6 years and lived for 23 years. Celer and Appuleia [set this up] for their excellent son.
EDCS-20403144.summary: This is a tombstone for Sextus Satrius Iustus, a Praetorian soldier, set up by his parents, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-20403145.translation: Lucius Valgius Priscus, son of Lucius, a soldier of the 5th cohort of Vigiles, who lived for 20 years and served for 3 years.
EDCS-20403145.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Valgius Priscus, a soldier in the Vigiles, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403147.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Iulius Soterichus, son of Caius, freedman of our Caius, and the college of hunters and priests [set this up]. For 3 lustra.
EDCS-20403147.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Iulius Soterichus by his freedmen and a college of priests, possibly a funerary monument.

EDCS-20403148.translation: Gaius Allius Verus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-20403148.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication or funerary text mentioning Gaius Allius Verus.

EDCS-20403149.translation: Lucius Dotius Antiochus, freedman of Lucius, and Dotia Iucunda, freedwoman of Antiochus, lived [here/on this land] for 17 feet in front.
EDCS-20403149.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a property owned by Lucius Dotius Antiochus and his freedwoman Dotia Iucunda, possibly marking a tomb or boundary.

EDCS-20403150.translation: To Flavia Polla, daughter of Quintus, mother of the Gallioner family.
EDCS-20403150.summary: This is a dedication to Flavia Polla, likely a funerary epitaph honoring her role as a mother within her family.

EDCS-20403151.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph for Lotria Vicia.

EDCS-20403152.translation: Cornelia Histri [from the tribe] Quinti Munati, son of Publius, [and] daughter of Quartus.
EDCS-20403152.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone mentioning Cornelia Histri and her family connections.

EDCS-20403153.translation: Lucius Octavius, son of Lucius, [son] of Octavia, freedwoman of Lucius Quartus, lived [here].
EDCS-20403153.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary marker for Lucius Octavius, indicating his relationship to his parents.

EDCS-20403154.translation: Sacred offering. The magistrates Cilix, freedman of Tullus, son of Lucius, and Teipa, freedman of Precia, and Philotimus, took care to complete it for Mercury, the wool-trader.
EDCS-20403154.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering made to Mercury, the wool-trader, by magistrates and freedmen.

EDCS-20403156.translation: Mancipn, son of Marcus, and Succi, son of Caius, [built?] 320 cubits of wall.
EDCS-20403156.summary: This inscription records the construction of 320 cubits of wall by Mancipn and Succi.

EDCS-20403157.translation: It is permitted to touch. Aulus Trebellius, son of Aulus, and Marcus Aiedius, son of Marcus, and Marcus Anius Ga[...].
EDCS-20403157.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or a prohibition, naming several individuals, likely officials or landowners.

EDCS-20403159.translation: Acerro rebuilt it and the towers again.
EDCS-20403159.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding of something and its towers by Acerro.

EDCS-20403160.translation: Publius Fufidius Notus made this while alive for his sister Fufidia, freedwoman of Publius, called Notae; and for his mother Fufidia, freedwoman of Publius, called Auge; and for Fufidia, freedwoman of Publius, called Saturnina, while alive.
EDCS-20403160.summary: This funerary inscription records that Publius Fufidius Notus built this monument for his sister and mother during his lifetime.

EDCS-20403161.translation: To Marcus Julius Juvenalis, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20403161.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Julius Juvenalis, a freedman.

EDCS-20403162.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Antonia Paulina, his wife, and Antonius Priscus, his stepson, and Aelius Papias, his freedman, were the heirs, according to the will, of Titus Aelius Marinus, veteran and formerly of the emperor's elite cavalry.
EDCS-20403162.summary: This funerary inscription honors Titus Aelius Marinus, a veteran, and lists his heirs.

EDCS-20403163.translation: Publius Aurunculeius, son of Decimus, and Caius Minucius, son of Caius, Thermus, the two duovirs, took care to pave the road with pebbles at public expense, by decree of the decurions, and they approved it.
EDCS-20403163.summary: This inscription records the paving of a road with pebbles by the duovirs, funded by public money and approved by the decurions.

EDCS-20403164.translation: Quintus Pomponius Aeschinus, freedman of Musa, a money-changer for the inhabitants of Cereatae, [dedicated this].
EDCS-20403164.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Pomponius Aeschinus, a money-changer.

EDCS-20403166.translation: To Quintus Annilenus Homillus, freedman of...
EDCS-20403166.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Annilenus Homillus, a freedman.

EDCS-20403167.translation: To Gvl Istiliai Antiochin, daughter of Nis.
EDCS-20403167.summary: This is a dedication from an unknown person to Gvl Istiliai Antiochin.

EDCS-20403168.translation: Aufidia Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius Aufidius Secundus, son of Lucius, and Pescinnia Iucunda.
EDCS-20403168.summary: This inscription records the names of Aufidia Secunda and Pescinnia Iucunda, possibly within a funerary context.

EDCS-20403169.summary: This is a dedication or funerary marker for Capria, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-20403170.translation: Gnaeus Cassius Nestor, freedman of Gnaeus, and Salvia, freedwoman of the woman Cernia, for themselves and their kin.
EDCS-20403170.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication made by Gnaeus Cassius Nestor and Salvia for themselves and their families.

EDCS-20403171.summary: This inscription records the names of Gaius Furius Heros and Athenais, possibly as a joint dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-20403172.translation: For Honesimus, freedman of Publius Pulius Numerius, and for Gavia, his concubine.
EDCS-20403172.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Honesimus and his concubine Gavia.

EDCS-20403173.translation: Lives Maria Quintia, freedwoman of Publius, and Gaius Marius Maturus, freedman of the woman.
EDCS-20403173.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Maria Quintia and Gaius Marius Maturus.

EDCS-20403174.translation: Of Marcus Metilius Anteron, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20403174.summary: This inscription marks the property or tomb of Marcus Metilius Anteron, a freedman.

EDCS-20403177.translation: Ametusa, freedwoman of the woman Publius Petronius, purchased plot for herself and her kin.
EDCS-20403177.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a burial plot by Ametusa for herself and her family.

EDCS-20403178.summary: This fragmented inscription likely lists several names, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-20403184.translation: Marcus Publius Vertuleieis, son of Caius, being distrustful of his own affairs and afflicted by hardships, and fearing as a parent, vowed this vow here. Having paid the tithe and offered the first fruits, they gladly give this gift to Hercules the Mighty, well-deserving, and they beg him together to often bind them to their vow.
EDCS-20403184.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules by Marcus Publius Vertuleieis, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20403191.translation: To Quintus Caprius Philomenus, freedman of Quintus, his patron; Quintus Caprius Tertius, freedman of Quintus, Sextumvir; to Canuleia Tertia, freedwoman of his freedman.
EDCS-20403191.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Quintus Caprius Tertius for his patron, Quintus Caprius Philomenus, and for Canuleia Tertia, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-20403192.translation: to [---]ius, son of Lucius, the pontiff; by the will of Palamedes, his freedman.
EDCS-20403192.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording a bequest in the will of Palamedes for a pontiff, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403194.translation: To Gaius Naevius Antiochus, freedman of Gaius, his patron, the vestiary; Gaius Naevius Antiochus, his freedman; Istiminia Secunda, freedwoman of Publius; Gaius Naevius Diogenes, freedman of Gaius, fellow freedman; Naevia Dorcha, freedwoman of Gaius; Diogenis, freedwoman.
EDCS-20403194.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription listing multiple freedmen and freedwomen, dedicated to Gaius Naevius Antiochus, the vestiary, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403195.translation: To Lucius Vibius Sura, freedman of Lucius, the veterinarian; Vettia, daughter of Lucius, his wife, gives [this].
EDCS-20403195.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Vettia for her husband, Lucius Vibius Sura, a veterinarian, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403196.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or ownership mark, mentioning Aeschin, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-20403197.translation: Of Gaius Arrius Attus, son of Gaius, freedman.
EDCS-20403197.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Gaius Arrius Attus, son of Gaius and freedman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403198.translation: To Publius Arrius Philodamus, freedman of Publius; Publius Arrius Philargyrus.
EDCS-20403198.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Publius Arrius Philargyrus for his father, Publius Arrius Philodamus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403201.translation: Of Quintus Po[---], freedman; Romilia Bestiae.
EDCS-20403201.summary: This fragmentary inscription possibly records a freedman named Quintus Po[---] and mentions Romilia Bestiae, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403202.translation: Of Gaius Epaphroditus, freedman of Gaius; Calidiai Augini, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-20403202.summary: This inscription lists two individuals, Gaius Epaphroditus and Calidiai Augini, likely freedpeople, with their patron Gaius, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403204.translation: To Quintus Cassius Scaeva, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-20403204.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Quintus Cassius Scaeva.

EDCS-20403206.translation: Lives Cupiennia, freedwoman of her master, and for her patroness Cupiennia Lucilia, and for Lucius Aelius Hilarius, freedman of Lucius, her husband.
EDCS-20403206.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cupiennia, her patroness, and her husband, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-20403207.translation: To Marcus Helvius Andrias, freedman of Marcus, and to Vertuleia Amoena, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-20403207.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Helvius Andrias and Vertuleia Amoena, likely a couple, freedmen of the same patron.

EDCS-20403209.translation: Flora, freedwoman of her master, for herself and her relatives.
EDCS-20403209.summary: This funerary inscription records Flora, a freedwoman, dedicating the monument for herself and her family.

EDCS-20403211.translation: Caius Helvius Philonicus, freedman of Caius. Helvia Clara, freedwoman of Caius, fellow freedwoman, made this at her own expense.
EDCS-20403211.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Helvia Clara for Caius Helvius Philonicus, their fellow freedman.

EDCS-20403212.translation: Of Quintus Literrius Priamus, son of Titus, of the Romilia tribe, [and] of Titus Curiatius Priamus, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-20403212.summary: This inscription appears to be a shared funerary monument for two individuals, Quintus Literrius Priamus and Titus Curiatius Priamus.

EDCS-20403213.translation: Of Marcus Magius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-20403213.summary: This inscription is a dedication or funerary text for Marcus Magius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-20403216.translation: Lives T(itus) Synerotis, son of Titus Marius.
EDCS-20403216.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Titus Synerotis, son of Titus Marius.

EDCS-20403217.translation: To Marcus Naevius Balbus, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe. To Naevia Aphrodisia, freedwoman of Marcus, dutiful. To Primus, freedman of Marcus. To Secundus, brother of Primus, freedman of Naevius Balbus.
EDCS-20403217.summary: This funerary inscription honors multiple members of the Naevia family, including Marcus Naevius Balbus, his freedwoman Aphrodisia, and two individuals named Primus and Secundus.

EDCS-20403219.translation: Lives Gaius Nunnnius Bocchus, freedman of his master, 18 feet.
EDCS-20403219.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Gaius Nunnnius Bocchus, a freedman, and specifies the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-20403222.translation: To Marcus Pineius Pycabe, freedman of Marcus, [son of ?] Staediae, from Corn[elia?].
EDCS-20403222.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the freedman Marcus Pineius Pycabe to a certain Staediae, possibly the patroness, from the Cornelia tribe.

EDCS-20403230.translation: Valerius, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-20403230.summary: This is a fragmentary tribal and filiation marker for a person named Valerius.

EDCS-20403236.translation: To Gaius Virius Marulus, son of Gaius, of the Romilia tribe; by his wife, from her own resources.
EDCS-20403236.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Virius Marulus by his wife.

EDCS-20403237.translation: Of Lucius Voltilius Philoclis, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-20403237.summary: This is a funerary dedication by or for Lucius Voltilius Philoclis, a freedman.

EDCS-20403239.translation: To Iegia Egloge, for herself and for her husband, Marcus [---], Lys[---].
EDCS-20403239.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iegia Egloge for herself and her husband.

EDCS-20403244.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning with a praenomen and a gentilicium or cognomen.

EDCS-20403258.translation: To Quintus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, [---], pontifex, duovir; by his wife [---]a.
EDCS-20403258.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus, a local magistrate and priest, by his wife.

EDCS-20403260.translation: By the arbitration of Philar<y>rus, freedman of Lucius, son of Lucius Decius Rufio, and of Decia Fa[---], freedwoman of Lucius, son of Lucius Decius Philargyrus.
EDCS-20403260.summary: This inscription records an arbitration or legal decision involving freedmen and freedwomen, possibly concerning property or inheritance.

EDCS-20403261.translation: To Marcus Julius Iuvenalis, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20403261.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Julius Iuvenalis, a freedman.

EDCS-20403263.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning with a praenomen and a gentilicium.

EDCS-20403271.summary: Fragmentary inscription mentioning Gracchus, likely an official of the corps of engineers, possibly dated to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-20403275.translation: The burial of Marturius, the presbyter, in peace on the Kalends of December, the Lord's Day, in the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-20403275.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Marturius, a presbyter, with a precise date in the 4th century AD.

EDCS-20403276.translation: Marcellus gave this as a gift to the divine power of Fortuna Panthea.
EDCS-20403276.summary: A votive inscription by Marcellus dedicating a gift to Fortuna Panthea, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20500031.translation: Publius Betilienus Hapalus, son of Marcus, in his capacity as one of the IIII viri, arranged for the wall to be built by decree of the senate.
EDCS-20500031.summary: An inscription from an aedile-like official, Publius Betilienus Hapalus, who supervised the construction of a wall by senatorial decree, likely in a Roman colony in the 1st-2nd century AD.

EDCS-20500032.translation: Lucius Betilienus Varus, son of Lucius, arranged for the following to be constructed by decree of the senate: all paths in the town, the portico leading to the citadel, the field where they play, the sundial, the market, the basilica to be paved, seats, a bath complex, a lake by the gate, and the water channel coming into the town, 340 feet long, and he made arches and pipes; for these services, he was made censor twice, the senate ordered that his son receive military stipends, and the people dedicated a statue to Censorinus.
EDCS-20500032.summary: A lengthy public works inscription by Lucius Betilienus Varus, detailing numerous constructions and infrastructure improvements he funded by senatorial decree, and listing honors bestowed upon him and his family, likely from a provincial town in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-20500034.translation: Quintus Minucius Anteros, son of Quintus, freedman, a member of the VI viri Augustales, bequeathed here 10,000 sesterces to the VI viri Augustales of Aletrinum, from the income of which, on his birthday each year, they were to feast for three days.
EDCS-20500034.summary: A bequest inscription by Quintus Minucius Anteros, a freedman and member of the VI viri Augustales, establishing a fund for the collegium's annual celebration, likely from the 1st-2nd century AD.

EDCS-20500036.translation: Marcus Afrenius, son of Sextus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-20500036.summary: A simple tribal indication for Marcus Afrenius, son of Sextus, likely part of a larger inscription or a name tag, from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20500037.translation: Marcus Allius, son of Marcus, is alive. Lucius Allius Cicero, son of Marcus. Albia, mother of Lucius. Marcus Allius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-20500037.summary: A funerary inscription listing several family members, indicating Marcus Allius is alive while others are deceased, likely from the 1st-2nd century AD.

EDCS-20500038.translation: Gaius Coranus... ; Corana, freedwoman of Gaius... ; Corana, daughter of Gaius... and their own freedmen and descendants.
EDCS-20500038.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning members of the Coranus family and their freedmen and descendants, possibly from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20500039.translation: Marcus Decumius... ; Gaius Decumius, son of Quintus...
EDCS-20500039.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning members of the Decumius family, likely part of a larger dedication or funerary text, from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20500041.summary: This inscription is a simple name, likely of a tombstone or a dedication by Gaius Julius Fidus.

EDCS-20500042.translation: as patrons. Rufreius Philus, freedman of Marcus, to himself and his family, and to Rufreius Gallus, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, and to Rufreius, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, and to Posilla, daughter of Lucius, his wife, and to Rufreius, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, and to Dorcas, freedwoman of Marcus, and to Rufa, daughter of Lucius, his sister.
EDCS-20500042.summary: This epitaph lists several family members, including a freedman and his relatives, likely serving as a tombstone inscription from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20500061.translation: To Flavia Cara, daughter of Titus, most splendid.
EDCS-20500061.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Flavia Cara, daughter of Titus, probably on a tomb or a public monument, commending her for her splendor.

EDCS-20500062.translation: Aulus Hirtius, son of Aulus, and Marcus Lollius, son of Caius, as censors, undertook to have the foundations and walls made from the ground, and they approved them; the foundation is XXXIII feet deep in the ground, in the same manner as the silici [wall/structure] above ground.
EDCS-20500062.summary: This inscription records that censors Aulus Hirtius and Marcus Lollius oversaw the construction and approval of foundations and walls, specifying a depth of 33 feet for the foundation.

EDCS-20500063.translation: Aulus Hirtius, son of Aulus, and Marcus Lollius, son of Caius, as censors, undertook to have the foundations and walls made from the ground, and they approved them; the foundation is XXXIII feet deep in the ground, in the same manner as the silici [wall/structure] above ground.
EDCS-20500063.summary: This inscription records that censors Aulus Hirtius and Marcus Lollius oversaw the construction and approval of foundations and walls, specifying a depth of 33 feet for the foundation.

EDCS-20500064.translation: Marcus Lollius, son of Caius, and Aulus Hirtius, son of Aulus, as censors, undertook to have the foundations made and approved them.
EDCS-20500064.summary: This inscription states that censors Marcus Lollius and Aulus Hirtius were responsible for the construction and approval of foundations.

EDCS-20500065.translation: Aulus Hirtius, son of Aulus, and Marcus Lollius, son of Caius, as censors, undertook to have the foundations and arches made and approved them.
EDCS-20500065.summary: This inscription records that censors Aulus Hirtius and Marcus Lollius oversaw the construction and approval of foundations and arches.

EDCS-20500084.translation: I pray that the image of Severus may be [here].
EDCS-20500084.summary: This is a votive or funerary inscription expressing a wish for an image of Severus, possibly in a temple or tomb.

EDCS-20500090.summary: This inscription identifies Anteros as a public official of Ferentinum, likely indicating his name on a public building or monument.

EDCS-20500099.summary: This inscription contains two names or fragments of names with uncertain context, possibly from a tombstone or a list of individuals.

EDCS-20500101.translation: To Celsus, freedman of Lucius Haterius, from Filumina, freedwoman of Lucius Haterius, to her husband Celsus, son of Lucius Haterius.
EDCS-20500101.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a freedwoman to her husband, who was also a freedman.

EDCS-20500102.translation: To Aulus Hirtius, son of Aulus, and Marcus Amo.
EDCS-20500102.summary: This is an inscription likely on a monument honoring Aulus Hirtius and Marcus Amo, possibly as benefactors or in a public capacity.

EDCS-20500118.translation: for their grandchildren. Marcellus(?), pontifex, and his freedmen.
EDCS-20500118.summary: This inscription, partially restored, indicates a dedication by Marcellus, a pontifex, for his grandchildren and freedmen.

EDCS-20500128.translation: [...] O LAC[...] / Titus, son of Publius [...]
EDCS-20500128.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription mentioning Titus, son of Publius, with illegible portions.

EDCS-20600325.translation: To Marcus Arrius Maximus, son of Marcus, IIIvir capitalis, prefect of cavalry, quaestor, proconsul, curule aedile.
EDCS-20600325.summary: This inscription records the career of Marcus Arrius Maximus, detailing his various high-ranking public offices.

EDCS-20600328.translation: To Gaius Abutius Laconi, son of Lucius, who was elected aedile and served again as aedile, pontifex, augur, quaestor, by decree of the Senate, out of love and affection.
EDCS-20600328.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Abutius Laconi for his service as aedile, pontifex, augur, and quaestor, with his selection as aedile noted as being by senatorial decree.

EDCS-20600329.translation: To Aelia Laenilla, freedwoman of Augustus, mother of Ragius Bithynicus, by the XXviri and the honored men, for her merits.
EDCS-20600329.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the XXviri and other officials to Aelia Laenilla, mother of Ragius Bithynicus and freedwoman of Augustus, in recognition of her merits.

EDCS-20600330.translation: Marcus Arrius, son of Marcus, grandson of Lucius, and Lucius Vitorius, son of Caius, elected senators.
EDCS-20600330.summary: This inscription records the election of two individuals, Marcus Arrius and Lucius Vitorius, to the senate.

EDCS-20600337.translation: The Senate and People of Anagnia decreed that a statue be erected to Titus Flavius Karus, former legate of the people, for his outstanding generosity towards them and the state; on the occasion of its dedication, he gave 3 denarii to the decurions, 2 denarii to the sexviri, and 1 denarius to the people.
EDCS-20600337.summary: This inscription records the decree of the Senate and People of Anagnia to erect a statue for Titus Flavius Karus due to his generosity, and his subsequent distribution of money to local officials and the populace upon its dedication.

EDCS-20600345.translation: To C. R. Titus F. Vitalis, prefect, [in the year] Macrinus and Celsus were consuls, on the Nones of October.
EDCS-20600345.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus F. Vitalis, a prefect, dating to the consulship of Macrinus and Celsus in October.

EDCS-20600350.translation: To Nia, daughter of Publius, for herself and for... son of Publius, Caepio... son of Publius, Caepio, and for her brother Pollio, son of Publius.
EDCS-20600350.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Nia to herself and other family members.

EDCS-20600351.translation: Gnaeus Caesius Eutychus, freedman of Gnaeus, erected this for his patron and himself while still alive.
EDCS-20600351.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a freedman for his patron and himself.

EDCS-20600355.translation: Publius Hostilius Primus, freedman of Publius, for himself and for his patron Publius Hostilius Platypodus, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-20600355.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a freedman for himself and his patron.

EDCS-20600358.translation: Caius Novius Meferna, freedman of a woman, lives. Sunethea, freedwoman of a woman, lives. This monument will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-20600358.summary: This funerary inscription records the names of two individuals, likely a couple, and stipulates that the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-20600368.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Rode had this made for her most beloved and deserving mother, Valeria Rodenia.
EDCS-20600368.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to a mother by her daughter.

EDCS-20600369.translation: To the Divine Shades. Here lies in a tomb my dearest friend, whom the gods gave me, if only they had not been envious. These words I speak with tears and weeping, grieving that I could not record more of her praises on this inscription, so that more people would know what she was like; she lived 24 years, 5 months, and 12 days. Lupercus erected this for his deserving friend in remembrance of his love.
EDCS-20600369.summary: This funerary inscription is a poignant epitaph for a beloved friend, detailing her age and expressing the grief of the dedicator, Lupercus.

EDCS-20600371.translation: To Diana Pamnetiana, Quintus Iulius Pomponianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-20600371.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating something to the goddess Diana Pamnetiana by Quintus Iulius Pomponianus.

EDCS-20600380.translation: Manius Memmius, son of Manius, praetor, [dedicated] the standards and base at his own expense.
EDCS-20600380.summary: This inscription records the dedication of military standards and a base by Manius Memmius, who held the office of praetor.

EDCS-20600381.translation: The knights of Signia dedicated this to Lucius Sextilius Tallentius, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-20600381.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the equestrian order of Signia to Lucius Sextilius Tallentius.

EDCS-20600382.translation: Gaius Volumnius Flaccus, son of Gaius, and Quintus Volumnius Marsus, son of Quintus, as IIIIviri iure dicundo, dedicated the crypt, the place where the crypt is, and the area with the gardens in the Signino municipality with their own money.
EDCS-20600382.summary: This inscription records a public dedication of a crypt, its location, and an adjacent garden area by two officials (IIIIviri iure dicundo) of the municipality of Signia.

EDCS-20600387.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record the name Marcus E. and a reference to a municipality, possibly indicating ownership or origin.

EDCS-20600388.summary: This inscription records Lucius Vinius Onesimus as the maker of a monument or object.

EDCS-20600389.translation: Aestlania and Aestlania Ianuaria made [this] for the well-deserving.
EDCS-20600389.summary: This inscription records Aestlania and Aestlania Ianuaria as dedicators of a monument for someone deserving.

EDCS-20600401.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Severinus, who lived for 23 years and 2 months.

EDCS-20600406.translation: To the departed spirits of Virgunia IAE Potentiana, with good will.
EDCS-20600406.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the departed spirit of Virgunia IAE Potentiana.

EDCS-20600410.translation: Sacred to Silvanus, Caius Valerius Martialis, son of Caius.
EDCS-20600410.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Silvanus by Caius Valerius Martialis.

EDCS-20600412.translation: To Lucius Aurelius Commodus Caesar, Germanicus, son of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Parthicus, Germanicus, pontifex maximus, father of the country, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-20600412.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by decree of the town council at public expense to Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-20600413.translation: To Julia Maesa, Augusta, grandmother of the Emperor Caesar [---].
EDCS-20600413.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to Julia Maesa, the grandmother of an emperor.

EDCS-20600414.translation: To the divine Flavius Valerius Constantius, from the colony of Minturnae.
EDCS-20600414.summary: This inscription records the deification of Emperor Constantius I by the colony of Minturnae.

EDCS-20600416.translation: To Aelius Saturninus, freedman of Augustus, procurator of the camp, from the plebs, with money collected, for his constant and generous munificence.
EDCS-20600416.summary: This inscription records a dedication by soldiers to Aelius Saturninus, an imperial freedman and camp procurator, in appreciation of his generosity.

EDCS-20600418.translation: To Marcus Flavius Postumus, a most distinguished man, patron of the colony, the council and people of Minturnae dedicated this.
EDCS-20600418.summary: This is a dedication by the local government of Minturnae to Marcus Flavius Postumus, a patron of the town.

EDCS-20600419.translation: Publius Larcius Publius' freedwoman Neicia Saufeia, Aulus' freedwoman Thalea, Lucius Larcius Publius' son Rufus, Publius Larcius Publius' son Brocchus, Larcia Publius' freedwoman Horaea, having been approved and not approved by good people, I was not approved by any good person; my parents, venerable to my masters, but this one obedient, thus my freedom he bestowed on me, and here he decorated me with a stola. As a young girl, for twenty years I maintained the whole household. The highest judgment of death took my soul, it did not take away the ornament of life. Lucius Eprius Chilo, a courier of the tribunes of the plebs, Epria Cri...
EDCS-20600419.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription, possibly for a freedwoman named Horaea, recounting her life, her relationship with her masters, and her death, with partial mention of a benefactor or relation named Lucius Eprius Chilo.

EDCS-20600420.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Aelius Valentinus, a veteran of our Emperor, formerly a cavalryman in the emperor's guard, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-20600420.summary: This is a self-funded tomb inscription for Titus Aelius Valentinus, a veteran and former imperial guardsman.

EDCS-20600421.translation: Quintus Ancharius, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Pollia, from Narbonne, a cavalryman, an evocatus, aged 23, born in the ala of Scaeva.
EDCS-20600421.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Ancharius, a 23-year-old cavalryman and evocatus serving in the ala of Scaeva.

EDCS-20600424.translation: Publius Baebius Patrophilus commissioned this to be set up for Baebia Prisca, daughter of Publius. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20600424.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Publius Baebius Patrophilus for Baebia Prisca, with the land granted by local decree.

EDCS-20600425.translation: For Gaius Iunius Tertius, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Aniensis, on the public equestrian list, augur, duoviral aedile, prefect of the cohort of the Ubii in Lower Moesia; for Iunia Saturnina, daughter of Gaius; for his mother Iunia Comice; for Iunia Stachis.
EDCS-20600425.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Gaius Iunius Tertius, an equestrian official and military commander, and several female relatives, including his mother and sister.

EDCS-20600426.translation: To Gaius Iunius Dymantes, freedman of Gaius, and to Iunia Donata, his wife, and to Gaius Iunius Tertius, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Aemilia, on the public equestrian list, duoviral aedile, and to Gaius Iunius Maximus, son of Gaius, and to Iunia Procula, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-20600426.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Iunius Dymantes, his wife Iunia Donata, their son Gaius Iunius Tertius (an equestrian official), and their other son Gaius Iunius Maximus and daughter Iunia Procula.

EDCS-20600428.translation: For Pompeia Catulla, daughter of Quintus, priestess of the Augustae. By decree of the decurions, the public money was remitted. Gaius Truttedius Pius, her son, commissioned this. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20600428.summary: This is a funerary monument for Pompeia Catulla, a priestess of the Augustae, with the land granted by local decree and her son Gaius Truttedius Pius responsible for its erection and remission of public fees.

EDCS-20600429.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marcus Raecius as a duovir.

EDCS-20600430.translation: Caius Varius Felix, Augustalis, 13 feet in front, 35 feet in the field.
EDCS-20600430.summary: This inscription records land measurements belonging to Caius Varius Felix, an Augustalis.

EDCS-20600431.translation: Lucius Varius Sabinus, son of Lucius, grandson of Marcus, of the Falerna tribe, a decurion, gave this gift.
EDCS-20600431.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Lucius Varius Sabinus, a decurion, likely to a deity or a public benefactor.

EDCS-20600437.translation: To the household gods of Caius Cidius Agilis.
EDCS-20600437.summary: This is a dedication to the household gods (Lares) of Caius Cidius Agilis.

EDCS-20600438.translation: To the departed spirits. Plautius Pollio made this for his wife Claudia Zosime, who lived 24 years, a well-deserving wife.
EDCS-20600438.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudia Zosime, set up by her husband Plautius Pollio.

EDCS-20600440.translation: Her husband made this for Cornelia, daughter of Marel, a well-deserving wife, with whom he lived 11 years.
EDCS-20600440.summary: This funerary epitaph records a tombstone erected by a husband for his wife, Cornelia, detailing their years of marriage.

EDCS-20600441.translation: lius Eutyches made this for Cornelia Musa, his incomparable and dearest wife, with whom he lived 20 years, a well-deserving wife.
EDCS-20600441.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelia Musa, set up by her husband,lius Eutyches, noting their years of marriage.

EDCS-20600442.translation: For Cornelia Selene, his excellent wife. PA
EDCS-20600442.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Cornelia Selene, described as an excellent wife.

EDCS-20600443.translation: Marcus Cosconius to Marcus Cosconius, to Cosconia, to Cosconia.
EDCS-20600443.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or record of family relationships, listing multiple individuals named Cosconius.

EDCS-20600444.translation: To the departed spirits. Her son made this for Domitia Octavia.
EDCS-20600444.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia Octavia, set up by her son.

EDCS-20600446.translation: To the departed spirits. Galionius Priscus made this for his most virtuous wife, Flavia Sabina, most deserving.
EDCS-20600446.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Sabina, set up by her husband Galionius Priscus.

EDCS-20600447.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Firidius Syntrophus arranged for this to be made for his incomparable wife Geminia Fortunata and their daughter Euhantis.
EDCS-20600447.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Marcus Firidius Syntrophus for his wife Geminia Fortunata and daughter Euhantis.

EDCS-20600448.translation: Hirria Chrysis for herself, for her patron Hirrius Syntrophus, and for her descendants.
EDCS-20600448.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Hirria Chrysis for herself, her patron, and her family.

EDCS-20600449.summary: This is a dedication to Hirva Lycoris, likely on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-20600450.translation: Marcus Longanus to Longana, Marcus Longanus.
EDCS-20600450.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication or ownership by Marcus Longanus to Longana and himself.

EDCS-20600451.translation: For Lucretia Aucta, freedwoman of Publius Lucretius; this monument or external sepulcher shall not pass to heirs.
EDCS-20600451.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucretia Aucta, specifying that the monument is not hereditary.

EDCS-20600452.summary: This is a simple personal inscription, likely identifying an individual.

EDCS-20600453.translation: Lucius Hilarus, freedman of Lucius Manlius, and Masonia Dionysia, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-20600453.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Lucius Hilarus and Masonia Dionysia, both freedpersons.

EDCS-20600454.translation: For Quintus Geminus, son of Quintus; for Baucis, freedwoman of the woman Manlia; for Lochias, freedwoman of the woman Manlia; for Ilias, freedwoman of the woman Manlia; 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-20600454.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to Quintus Geminus and several freedwomen, specifying land measurements for the plot.

EDCS-20600455.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Valerius Florus made this for his excellent wife Maria Fortunata, and Valerius Sabinianus for his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-20600455.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Valerius Florus and Valerius Sabinianus to their wife/mother and mother respectively.

EDCS-20600456.translation: Sextus Menturnius Felix, freedman of the colony, made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-20600456.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Sextus Menturnius Felix, a freedman of the colony, for his family.

EDCS-20600457.translation: Marcus Malchio, freedman of Marcus Minius; Eleutheris, freedwoman of Marcus Minius; Marcus Barnaeus, freedman of Marcus Camidius; Statius Nicia, freedman of Marcus Minius; Philumina, freedwoman of Marcus Minius; Ammia, freedwoman of the woman Badia. This monument shall not pass to heirs.
EDCS-20600457.summary: This extensive funerary inscription names multiple individuals and their patrons, specifying that the monument is not hereditary.

EDCS-20600458.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Octavia, daughter of Lucius, who lived for thirteen years, her brother Marcus Alchius made this for her.
EDCS-20600458.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a brother to his sister, Octavia, who died at age thirteen.

EDCS-20600459.translation: Publius Ogulnius Eutychus and Felicula, freedwoman of the woman Publicia.
EDCS-20600459.summary: An epitaph recording the names of Publius Ogulnius Eutychus and Felicula, a freedwoman.

EDCS-20600460.translation: Lucius Caropinus, freedman of the woman, and Maria Idusa, and for their family, thirteen and a half feet in front.
EDCS-20600460.summary: An inscription likely marking a burial plot, mentioning Lucius Caropinus, Maria Idusa, and their family, with dimensions.

EDCS-20600461.translation: For Marcus Plautius, freedman of Aulus Marcus, and for his descendants. He is alive.
EDCS-20600461.summary: An inscription for Marcus Plautius, a freedman, and his descendants, possibly indicating a living beneficiary at the time of the inscription.

EDCS-20600462.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Rutilius Veratianus, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, made this for Rutilia Polla, his most sacred freedwoman, as she deserved.
EDCS-20600462.summary: A funerary dedication by Publius Rutilius Veratianus to his freedwoman Rutilia Polla, praising her.

EDCS-20600463.translation: For Gaius Stenius Primus, and for his daughter Stenia Prima, for himself and his family.
EDCS-20600463.summary: An inscription dedicating a space or monument to Gaius Stenius Primus, his daughter Stenia Prima, and their family.

EDCS-20600464.summary: A simple dedication or epitaph for Sulpicia Nothis.

EDCS-20800004.translation: the bodies of Sextus' freedman Zoticus, and Asclepia, freedwoman of Sextus, and Liccaeus, freedman of Sextus, buried here.
EDCS-20800004.summary: An epitaph recording the burial of three individuals: Zoticus, Asclepia, and Liccaeus, all connected through Sextus.

EDCS-20800007.translation: F Vellionius, son of Marcus, iscus
EDCS-20800007.summary: An incomplete inscription likely recording the name and filiation of F. Vellionius.

EDCS-20800011.summary: An incomplete inscription referring to 'tteius, son of Caius' and identifying him as a father.

EDCS-20800012.summary: This is a simple gentilician name, likely from a tombstone or a dedication, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20800035.translation: Marcus Ampudius, son of Numerius, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, aedile.
EDCS-20800035.summary: This epitaph records the cursus honorum (career path) of Marcus Ampudius, a Roman magistrate, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20800036.translation: To Quintus Clodius Hermogenianus, most distinguished consular governor of Campania; the council and people of Formiae, to their most outstanding patron.
EDCS-20800036.summary: This is a public dedication by the city of Formiae to their patron, Quintus Clodius Hermogenianus, a distinguished governor, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-20800037.translation: To Fulvia Augurinia, most distinguished lady, wife of Publius Helvius Aelius Dionysius, consular governor and corrector of Campania; set up publicly at Formiae.
EDCS-20800037.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, by the people of Formiae to Fulvia Augurinia, wife of a prominent official, dating to the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-20800038.translation: Onummula, most distinguished lady, mother of Messia. Messia, most distinguished lady, [daughter?] of..., sister of Messia...
EDCS-20800038.summary: This fragmentary inscription names at least two women, likely a mother and daughter, possibly from a tombstone, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20800040.translation: Lucius Munatius Plancus, son of Lucius, grandson of Lucius, great-grandson of Lucius, consul, censor, twice imperator, member of the VIIvir epulonum; he celebrated a triumph over the Raeti, built the temple of Saturn from captured spoils, divided lands in Italy, and founded the colonies of Lugudunum and Rauricam in Gaul.
EDCS-20800040.summary: This is a public inscription detailing the extensive career and achievements of Lucius Munatius Plancus, a prominent general and statesman of the late Roman Republic, including military victories, public works, and colonial foundations.

EDCS-20800041.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription to Pontius Paullinus, who held the high office of consul, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20800042.translation: To Marcus, son of [?], of the ------ tribe, quaestor for judicial business. Emilia S[---], daughter of Caius, made this for her husband. A Sp A RO [---]
EDCS-20800042.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, likely funerary, mentioning a quaestor and a woman who commissioned the monument, possibly from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20800052.translation: To Claudius, son of Lucius, of the Clustumina tribe, prefect of the artificers. [---]ius, freedman, [erected this].
EDCS-20800052.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication to Claudius, a prefect of artificers, and mentions his freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20800053.translation: To Lucius Bruttius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Palatina tribe, with equestrian rank, prefect of the cohort III Augusta of Thracians, cavalry. Lucius Bruttius Primitivos (sic), his father, and Insteia, his mother, set this up with their own money for their excellent son. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20800053.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by parents for their son, Lucius Bruttius Celer, a military officer, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20800059.translation: Gaius Laevius, son of Caius, [PRI]AIVSVIHINA, a member of the college of five (chuir), Flavia Cornicena, his wife, and her children and his children. Clarus lived with his patron.
EDCS-20800059.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for members of a family and mentions a patron-client relationship, possibly dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-20800060.translation: Gaius Magnius, son of Marcus, aedile for the second time.
EDCS-20800060.summary: This is a brief official inscription recording Gaius Magnius, son of Marcus, serving as aedile for the second time, likely in a Roman colony or municipality.

EDCS-20800061.translation: Tiberius Messius, son of Quintus, Gaius Acilius, son of Marcus, and Gnaeus Mevius, son of Gnaeus, as aediles, undertook the construction of a wall and the enclosure of an area, in accordance with a decree of the Senate, and they approved the work.
EDCS-20800061.summary: This inscription records the work of three aediles who, by senatorial decree, built a defensive wall and enclosed an area, likely for public use or defense.

EDCS-20800062.translation: The sons of Sallustia Saturnina, priestess of the goddess Ceres.
EDCS-20800062.summary: This is a dedication made by the sons in honor of their mother, Sallustia Saturnina, who served as a priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-20800066.translation: Gnaeus Anteros, freedman of Gnaeus, Augustalis; Gnaeus Felix, freedman of Gnaeus; Gnaeus Felix, freedman of Gnaeus, a merchant; Gnaeus Amaranthus, freedman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-20800066.summary: This inscription lists four individuals, all freedmen of a Gnaeus Mevius, with one identified as an Augustalis and another as a merchant, possibly a family or business record.

EDCS-20800067.translation: Aulus Plautius Apella, freedman of Theodorus, master Augustalis; to Plautia Rufa, freedwoman of Aulus, fellow freedwoman and concubine, pious; to Plautia Fausta, freedwoman of Aulus and [his wife]; to Gaius Vibius Eutyches.
EDCS-20800067.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Aulus Plautius Apella, an Augustalis, to his freedwoman partner Plautia Rufa, and others, indicating social relationships and honors.

EDCS-20800069.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to mention a person named Viator and possibly an Augustalis, but is too incomplete to provide a definitive summary.

EDCS-20800072.translation: Lips (Southwest wind), son of Libon, South African; Notos (South wind), Auster (South wind), Euru-notos (Southeast wind), Euronotos (Southeast wind), Euros (East wind), Apeliotes (East wind), Hellespontus (East wind), Vulturnus (Southeast wind).
EDCS-20800072.summary: This inscription lists various wind names in Greek and Latin, likely serving an astronomical, meteorological, or perhaps symbolic purpose.

EDCS-20800075.translation: Gaius Arrius Lucrio, freedman of Gaius, a centenarian(?); Lais, freedwoman, made this.
EDCS-20800075.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lais, a freedwoman, for Gaius Arrius Lucrio, who is described as a 'centenarius', possibly indicating a military rank or age, and likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-20800077.translation: Gnaeus Helvius Iola, freedman of Gnaeus, an eye doctor.
EDCS-20800077.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Helvius Iola, a freedman and a practicing eye doctor, indicating his profession and status.

EDCS-20800079.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Gaius Postumius Pollio, an architect.

EDCS-20800080.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the poet Ovidianus is buried here.

EDCS-20800081.translation: To Lucius Abuccius Nereus, his fellow freedman, who deserved well; Abuccia Pieris for herself and for Abuccia Prisca, her daughter.
EDCS-20800081.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Abuccia Pieris for her fellow freedman Lucius Abuccius Nereus and for herself and her daughter Abuccia Prisca.

EDCS-20800082.translation: Lucius Abuccius Rusticus for himself and for Abuccia Neaera.
EDCS-20800082.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Abuccius Rusticus for himself and for Abuccia Neaera.

EDCS-20800083.translation: Acilia Optata made [this] for Publius Acilius [---], her husband.
EDCS-20800083.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Acilia Optata erected the monument for her husband, Publius Acilius [---].

EDCS-20800084.translation: Quintus Aelius Heraclidas, freedman of Quintus, lived.
EDCS-20800084.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating the name and status of the deceased, Quintus Aelius Heraclidas, freedman of Quintus.

EDCS-20800089.translation: [---] Isidor[---], freedman of Quintus, [---] of Quintus Arrius, son of Marcus, [---] for his freedmen.
EDCS-20800089.summary: This is a funerary inscription for freedmen, with lacunae that obscure the precise details of the dedicant and recipients.

EDCS-20800090.translation: Gaius Asinius Martialis lived two months and seven days.
EDCS-20800090.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the brief lifespan of Gaius Asinius Martialis.

EDCS-20800091.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, beginning with the name Lucius? Atra[---].

EDCS-20800093.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning Marcus Bullani and Aemilia Prae[---].

EDCS-20800095.translation: Cinura lived 19 years. Carpus lived 4 years. Sadala, the father, made [this].
EDCS-20800095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cinura and Carpus, with Sadala as the maker, likely a father.

EDCS-20800096.translation: Quintus Cisvitius Philomusus the elder, freedman of Quintus; Quintus Cisvitius Philomusus the younger, freedman of Quintus; Marcus Vitruvius Demetrius, freedman of Marcus, and Vitruvia Chreste; Marcus Vitruvius Artema, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-20800096.summary: This funerary inscription lists several individuals, likely members of freedmen families associated with the Vitruvii and Cisvitii.

EDCS-20800098.translation: Cocceia Antipatra made [this] for Paphia her mother, Antylla her sister, Gaius Julius Bassus her brother, and all her own people, and for Lucius Cocceius Eutyches her tent-mate.
EDCS-20800098.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Cocceia Antipatra to her family members and her tent-mate, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-20800105.translation: Cina, ilia, Cypare, for herself and with her own people.
EDCS-20800105.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cina, ilia, and Cypare, indicating it was for their family use.

EDCS-20800111.translation: Publius Largius Sila, freedman of Publius; Publius Largius Eros, freedman of Publius; Largia, freedwoman of Publius. [---]
EDCS-20800111.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription lists three freedmen and one freedwoman, all associated with a Publius Largius.

EDCS-20800112.translation: Julius Verecundus, son, [made this] for Lucceia, daughter of Marcus, his most sweet mother Nepotilla.
EDCS-20800112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by a son, Julius Verecundus, for his mother, Lucceia Nepotilla.

EDCS-20800114.translation: Macrinius Nestullus for Vinicia Sym[---] his [---].
EDCS-20800114.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Macrinius Nestullus and Vinicia Sym[---], likely a dedication from a husband or relative.

EDCS-20800115.translation: Of Marcus Marius Miccus, freedman of Marcus.
