EDCS-20800115.summary: This is a name inscription, likely from a tomb or monument, identifying Marcus Marius Miccus, a freedman.

EDCS-20800116.translation: Of Gaius Marius, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, for the sons of Quintus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-20800116.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or record related to members of the Marius family, possibly concerning inheritance or lineage.

EDCS-20800118.translation: Mevia Talas, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-20800118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mevia Talas, a freedwoman who was emancipated by a female owner.

EDCS-20800119.translation: To Marcus Minculeius, son of Marcus; to Lucius Acricedius, son of Lucius; to Iunia, daughter of Publius; to Gaius Minculeius, son of Marcus; to Acricedia, daughter of Lucius; Polla Minculeia, daughter of Marcus, [made this].
EDCS-20800119.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing several individuals from the Minculeius and Acricedius families, likely a family monument.

EDCS-20800121.translation: Of Sextus Numisius, son of Caius.
EDCS-20800121.summary: This is a dedication or ownership inscription, identifying Sextus Numisius.

EDCS-20800124.translation: To Papinia Aphrodisia, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-20800124.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Papinia Aphrodisia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-20800129.translation: Parents made [this] for Secundinus; he lived 25 years, 7 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-20800129.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Secundinus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-20800130.translation: To Refria Nice, freedwoman of Caius, mother of Felicis; Refria Lychoris, concubine of Felicis.
EDCS-20800130.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Refria Nice and her concubine Refria Lychoris.

EDCS-20800133.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely a dedication to freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-20800137.translation: Of Suttius Quartus, son of Spurius.
EDCS-20800137.summary: This is a dedication or ownership inscription identifying Suttius Quartus.

EDCS-20800139.translation: To Tittia Daphne, freedwoman of Lucius, by testament with 3,000 sesterces, under the administration of Lucius Plotius Ariorta and his freedman Facetus.
EDCS-20800139.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a legacy of 3,000 sesterces for Tittia Daphne, managed by executors.

EDCS-20800144.summary: This is an ownership or identification inscription for Marcus Vitrubius Arasces.

EDCS-20800145.translation: Quintus Volusius Antiocus; Valeria Nobilis, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-20800145.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Quintus Volusius Antiocus and Valeria Nobilis.

EDCS-20800171.translation: Open your paradisiacal doors and blessed dwelling, receive the merit of Andrew, priest, cultivator of justice, lover of learning and peace. He whom blessed life calls to the highest good, filled with God's love, knew not how to live for the world, but for the servant of Christ. Glory was Christ to him. What he thought in faith and always held in trust carried you to the heavens and above the stars. The divine law never departed from your hands; the Lord's eloquence lived on your lips. He previously adorned the Roman city as presbyter, advanced in honor here, and became father with a righteous and certain rule. And like a good shepherd, he protected the flock from the enemy. Grateful to guests, he gave himself to the needy, satisfying some with words, others with aid. Under such a leader, the mother church grew, increased in gifts and duties. He lived more or less 70 years, as Roman presbyter for 12 years, and in the episcopate for 28 years, 10 months, and 20 days. He rested in peace on the 19th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of Decius Iunior.
EDCS-20800171.summary: This is an epitaph for a Roman presbyter and bishop who lived to be about 70 years old and served as bishop for over 28 years.

EDCS-20800173.translation: For Domitia Paulina, sister of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, father of the country. Fundanus gave (this) as a gift.
EDCS-20800173.summary: This inscription records a gift from Fundanus to his sister, Domitia Paulina, who was the sister of Emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-20800175.translation: To one born for the good of the Republic.
EDCS-20800175.summary: This is a funerary dedication for an individual considered beneficial to the state.

EDCS-20800176.translation: To Gaius Calvisius Sabinus, son of Gaius, consul.
EDCS-20800176.summary: This is a dedication fragment to Gaius Calvisius Sabinus, who held the office of consul.

EDCS-20800177.translation: To Titus Flavius Phoebianus, of the Palatina tribe, most distinguished youth, from Fundanius.
EDCS-20800177.summary: This dedication is from Fundanius to Titus Flavius Phoebianus, identified as a distinguished youth.

EDCS-20800180.translation: To Vinicius Coetaeus, calator and most excellent freedman of the VIIvir epulonum. From his patron.
EDCS-20800180.summary: This inscription honors Vinicius Coetaeus, a freedman who served as a calator and was a member of the VIIvir epulonum, dedicating it to him as his patron.

EDCS-20800182.translation: Publius Bruttius Gratus, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, from Aquileia, a centurion of the I Praetorian cohort, primus pilus of the Legio XIIII.
EDCS-20800182.summary: This is a military career summary for Publius Bruttius Gratus, detailing his service as a centurion and primus pilus.

EDCS-20800185.translation: aedile, interrex. To the son of Gnaeus [Fuscus?]. To his wife Clodia, wife of Gaius Fuscus.
EDCS-20800185.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication for a family, mentioning an aedile and interrex, and honoring a wife named Clodia.

EDCS-20800190.translation: In honor of Marcia, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-20800190.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription in honor of Marcia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-20800191.translation: Marcus Nellius, son of Marcus; Aulus Octavius, son of Caius; Lucius Ursius, son of Aulus, as aediles, undertook the construction of the wall, gate, and tower by decree of the Senate and approved it.
EDCS-20800191.summary: This inscription records the undertaking and approval of the construction of a wall, gate, and tower by the aediles Marcus Nellius, Aulus Octavius, and Lucius Ursius, as ordered by the Senate.

EDCS-20800192.translation: Lucius Numistronius Decianus, son of Lucius, and Caius Lucius Messianus, son of Marcus, son of Lucius, and Marcus Runtius Messianus, son of Lucius, son of Marcus, being aediles, saw to the construction of the gates, towers, and wall by decree of the Senate, and they approved them.
EDCS-20800192.summary: This inscription records the construction of city fortifications, including gates, towers, and walls, overseen and approved by three aediles.

EDCS-20800193.translation: To Lucius Runtius Gemellus, son of Lucius, of the Aemilia tribe, twice aedile and twice quinquennalis, for splendidly administering the duties of public office; the place was granted by decree of the decurions from funds collected by Fundanius.
EDCS-20800193.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Runtius Gemellus for his service as aedile and quinquennalis, with the location granted by decree of the local council.

EDCS-20800194.translation: Gaius Sextilius Longus, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, and Albius Procusius, aedile for the third time and Augustalis, [dedicated this] for themselves and their family; Ocratia Felicula, wife [dedicated this].
EDCS-20800194.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a family, including an aedile, for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-20800195.translation: Gaius Valerius Triarius, son of Gaius, Marcus Runtius Messianus, son of Lucius, for the second time, and Caius Afiedius Sexstianus, son of Gaius, aediles, contracted for the construction by decree of the Senate; Marcus Runtius Messianus, son of Lucius, son of Marcus, and Caius Afiedius Sexstianus, son of Gaius, son of Sextus, approved [the work].
EDCS-20800195.summary: This inscription records the contracting and approval of construction work, initiated by decree of the Senate and overseen by three aediles.

EDCS-20800202.translation: ... of his [father?] by the judgment of Antipater.
EDCS-20800202.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a judgment made by someone named Antipater.

EDCS-20800203.translation: To Gaius Atilius, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, and to Fufidia, daughter of Quintus, mother [of the deceased]; and to Tarquitia, daughter of Gaius, grandmother [of the deceased], in accordance with the will.
EDCS-20800203.summary: This funerary inscription, made according to a will, honors a grandson's mother and grandmother.

EDCS-20900238.summary: This very brief inscription names two individuals, Numerius Bo and Caius Bo.

EDCS-20900239.summary: This short inscription is a dedication or memorial to a woman named Victrix.

EDCS-20900240.translation: Marcus Cloelius, son of Publius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-20900240.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Marcus Cloelius.

EDCS-20900241.translation: Gaius Curtonius, son of Marcus, of the Aemilia tribe; Plotia, daughter of Marcus, wife [of Gaius Curtonius]; Gaius Curtonius, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe.
EDCS-20900241.summary: This inscription appears to be a family record, naming a father, his wife, and their son, all from the Aemilia tribe.

EDCS-20900242.translation: To Decumia, daughter of Marcus; to Decumia, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-20900242.summary: This is a funerary dedication to two women, Decumia, daughter of Marcus, and Decumia, daughter of Spurius.

EDCS-20900244.translation: Hedon, freedwoman of Elias, [for herself] and her family, for 12 feet.
EDCS-20900244.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Hedon, freedwoman of Elias, for herself and her family, possibly concerning a burial plot of 12 feet.

EDCS-20900245.translation: Amia, freedwoman of Quintus, wife of Publius Lepidius, freedman of Publius, made this for herself.
EDCS-20900245.summary: This funerary epitaph was made by Amia, freedwoman of Quintus and wife of Dracontius, freedman of Publius Lepidius, for herself.

EDCS-20900246.translation: [...] Marcius Pamphilus [...] freedman of Dio [...] Mari[...]
EDCS-20900246.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Marcius Pamphilus and a freedman of Dio.

EDCS-20900248.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a name on a tombstone, possibly for Decimus Modius Trebellius.

EDCS-20900249.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Modius Fortunatus, freedman, made this for his deserving patron Lucius Modius Quietus and his excellent wife Trebellia Marcia, and for himself and his descendants, in a place taken away.
EDCS-20900249.summary: This funerary epitaph honors a patron and his wife, and was dedicated by his freedman for them and himself and his descendants.

EDCS-20900250.translation: Tertia, freedwoman of Novia, made this for herself, and for Quintus Verrius Artemon, freedman of Quintus, and for her freedmen.
EDCS-20900250.summary: This funerary inscription was made by Tertia, freedwoman of Novia, for herself, her freedmen, and Quintus Verrius Artemon.

EDCS-20900251.translation: Gaius Numitorius, freedman of Gaius. Statius. Numitoria, freedwoman of Gaius. Moschis. Gaius Numitorius, freedman of Gaius. Eros.
EDCS-20900251.summary: This is a list of names, likely funerary epitaphs, identifying several individuals as freedmen or freedwomen of Gaius Numitorius.

EDCS-20900253.translation: Gaius Pantuleius Onesimus made this for Ionis, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-20900253.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Gaius Pantuleius Onesimus for Ionis, his freedwoman.

EDCS-20900255.translation: Pollia, daughter of Marcus, mother, made this for her sons Gaius Hortorius, Marcus Hortorius, Lucius Racilius Aemilius, and for herself.
EDCS-20900255.summary: This funerary epitaph was made by Pollia, daughter of Marcus, for her sons and herself.

EDCS-20900256.translation: Marcus Racilius Princeps and Racilia Olympias, freedmen, made this for themselves and their sons: Marcus Racilius Potitus, Secunda Quintio, Tertiary (deceased), Quartio (deceased), Eutychus the freedman.
EDCS-20900256.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by freedmen Marcus Racilius Princeps and Racilia Olympias for themselves and their sons, with some of the sons identified as deceased.

EDCS-20900257.translation: Lucius Runtius Hilarus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-20900257.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Lucius Runtius Hilarus as a freedman.

EDCS-20900261.translation: To Fortunatus, an excellent freedman, well-deserving, Caius Tatius Albanus.
EDCS-20900261.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fortunatus, an excellent and deserving freedman, by Caius Tatius Albanus.

EDCS-20900262.translation: Sextilia Helena made this for Marcus Tatius Tertius, freedman of Marcus, and for herself and Sextilia Sophene.
EDCS-20900262.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Sextilia Helena for her freedman Marcus Tatius Tertius and for herself and Sextilia Sophene.

EDCS-20900263.translation: Tatia Andronica, freedwoman of Marcus, for herself and for Tatia Charini, freedwoman.
EDCS-20900263.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing Tatia Andronica, a freedwoman, dedicating the monument for herself and another freedwoman, Tatia Charini.

EDCS-20900265.translation: For Toedia, freedwoman of Caius, her mother made this.
EDCS-20900265.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the mother of Toedia, a freedwoman of Caius, erected this monument.

EDCS-20900266.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription likely dedicated to Marcus Tullius Eutyches.

EDCS-20900267.translation: PV Varronianus saw to its construction at public expense.
EDCS-20900267.summary: This inscription indicates that PV Varronianus supervised the construction of a public work at public expense.

EDCS-20900268.translation: Marcus Verrius [---], Verria, his wife, [erected this for] Marcus Verrius [---].
EDCS-20900268.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely set up by Verria for her husband Marcus Verrius, and possibly for another Marcus Verrius.

EDCS-20900269.translation: Aulus Verrius Papus, freedman of Aulus, made this for himself and [---].
EDCS-20900269.summary: This funerary inscription records Aulus Verrius Papus, a freedman, dedicating the monument for himself and an unspecified person.

EDCS-20900271.translation: To Cita, freedwoman of Iucunda, freedwoman of Oncta.
EDCS-20900271.summary: This is a funerary dedication to freedwomen, likely belonging to a household network.

EDCS-20900274.translation: To Quintianus, son of Vianius, of the Julian tribe.
EDCS-20900274.summary: This is a fragmented funerary dedication likely for a person named Quintianus.

EDCS-20900275.translation: To the Divine Shades of Lucius Ca[---], from PA K II IE D.
EDCS-20900275.summary: This is a fragmented funerary dedication to Lucius Ca[---] with an unclear associated name or group.

EDCS-20900283.translation: To Hilfius, for his most sweet daughter, well deserving, who lived seventeen years and seven months.
EDCS-20900283.summary: This is a tombstone inscription honoring a young girl named Hilfius, detailing her lifespan.

EDCS-20900284.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely the beginning of a name and filiation.

EDCS-20900399.translation: Gnaeus Octavius Eu[---] consecrated the statue of Silvanus with a patera and ---.
EDCS-20900399.summary: This is a fragmented dedication of a statue of Silvanus, likely by Gnaeus Octavius, indicating a religious offering.

EDCS-20900404.translation: Avianius Vindicianus, most distinguished man and consular governor of Campania, arranged for the erection of statues for the adornment of the community of Tarracina.
EDCS-20900404.summary: This inscription records Avianius Vindicianus's contribution of statues to beautify the city of Tarracina, likely dating to his consular tenure.

EDCS-20900405.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus, son of Marcus, gave to the colonists.
EDCS-20900405.summary: This inscription records a donation by Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus to the colonists, likely related to land or resources.

EDCS-20900415.translation: Iulia Regulina made this according to his will to Tiberius Claudius Alcibiades, freedman of Augustus, of the Quirina tribe, his tas[ter] and of the bedchamber of Nero.
EDCS-20900415.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Iulia Regulina from a will for Tiberius Claudius Alcibiades, a freedman who served in Nero's imperial household.

EDCS-20900433.translation: Felix the porter, his wife Cia, Primus Felix the porter.
EDCS-20900433.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication or record of names, mentioning a porter named Felix and his family, possibly from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-21000007.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Domitius Soter, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-21000014.translation: Hebei, freedman oflius Cai, who was a...
EDCS-21000014.summary: This inscription appears to record the name of a freedman named Hebei and his patron, with some text missing or illegible.

EDCS-21000048.translation: [---] Terrinius, son of Lucius, from A[--]
EDCS-21000048.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription naming Terrinius, son of Lucius, with his origin or affiliation incomplete.

EDCS-21100694.translation: freedman of a woman, freedman of Apollon, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-21100694.summary: This inscription lists freedmen, possibly indicating relationships or ownership, with names like Apollon.

EDCS-21100697.translation: C. Longitia, monument from the front of the sea and...
EDCS-21100697.summary: This inscription mentions C. Longitia and a monument located by the sea, with further details lost.

EDCS-21100705.translation: Here rests John of good memory, who lived more or less 60 years, buried in peace on the eighth day before the Ides of February, seven years after the consulship of Basilius, the most distinguished man.
EDCS-21100705.summary: This is a funerary inscription for John, recording his age at death and burial date relative to the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-21100707.translation: Marcus Agileius Faustus, Agileia Paezusa, and Agileia Praetoria gave this gift to the Mother Goddess, and they placed the portico and a bedroom from their own funds.
EDCS-21100707.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Agileius Faustus, Agileia Paezusa, and Agileia Praetoria, who funded a portico and bedroom as a gift to the Mother Goddess.

EDCS-21100709.translation: While our lords Honorius and Theodosius, the most invincible Emperors, were in power, Flavius Nicius Theodulus, the most distinguished man, the vicar of the eternal city.
EDCS-21100709.summary: This inscription commemorates Flavius Nicius Theodulus, the vicar of Rome, during the reign of Emperors Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-21100710.translation: To Gaius Vibius Celer, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, from Papirius Rufus, prefect of the First Cohort of Mountain Troops, tribune of the First Flavian Cohort of Spaniards, milliary, equestrian, prefect of the First Ulpian Cohort of Bodyguards; the people of Circeii, to their patron, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-21100710.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Circeii to Gaius Vibius Celer, a distinguished military and administrative official, honoring him as their patron.

EDCS-21100711.translation: of the Seventh Claudian Legion, curator of the Tiburtine aqueduct; the people of Circeii, to their patron, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-21100711.summary: This inscription, likely a continuation or related to the previous one, mentions the Seventh Claudian Legion and the curator of the Tiburtine aqueduct, with the people of Circeii honoring them as patrons.

EDCS-21100716.translation: Cornelia Anthusa lived with her true, dear, and most sweet mother, Junia Prima, without dispute for 72 years.
EDCS-21100716.summary: This epitaph commemorates Cornelia Anthusa's mother, Junia Prima, and mentions their harmonious relationship and her age.

EDCS-21100717.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Horaea as the freedwoman of Lepidus and giving her name as Philogenes.

EDCS-21100725.translation: To Lucius Aradius Roscius Rufinus Saturninus Tiberianus, Augur, Curio, a most distinguished man, IIIvir for judging lawsuits, Sevirus of equestrian turmae, Quaestor (candidate), the people of Privernum [dedicate this] to their most worthy and outstanding patron.
EDCS-21100725.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription from the people of Privernum to their highly esteemed patron, Lucius Aradius Roscius Rufinus Saturninus Tiberianus, listing his many prestigious offices.

EDCS-21100726.translation: To their uncle, patron, and curator of the colony of Privernum, Nepesinum, Ametinum, and Truentinum, the town council and the people of the colony of Privernum [erected this] because of his exceptional diligence and integrity.
EDCS-21100726.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the town council and people of Privernum to their uncle, patron, and curator, honoring his excellent service to their colonies.

EDCS-21100731.translation: Lucius Titinius Ermopolis, brother of his father, uncle, priest of Isis, willingly paid the expenses.
EDCS-21100731.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Titinius Ermopolis, detailing his familial relationships and his role as a priest of Isis.

EDCS-21100735.translation: Quintus Cassius Faustus and Baebia Saturnina.
EDCS-21100735.summary: This inscription simply records the names of two individuals, Quintus Cassius Faustus and Baebia Saturnina, likely on a shared monument.

EDCS-21200029.translation: To the departed spirits. His patron erected [this] for Prastinius Chrysinnus, who deserved well.
EDCS-21200029.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a patron to his well-deserving freedman or client, Prastinius Chrysinnus.

EDCS-21200037.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. The six Augustales, Marcus Sextilius Cotus, Lucius Quinctius Pothinus, Lucius Nonius Primus, Numerius Aninius Dio, Marcus Ampius Urbanus, Gaius Tullius Menander, made [this] at their own expense.
EDCS-21200037.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred precinct to Mercury Augustus, funded by six members of the Augustales association.

EDCS-21200038.translation: Scaurus, as praetor and proconsul, [dedicated] the basilica.
EDCS-21200038.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a basilica by Scaurus, who held the offices of praetor and proconsul.

EDCS-21200042.translation: Lucius Paconius, son of Tiberius, praetor, dedicated [this].
EDCS-21200042.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument or building by Lucius Paconius, who served as praetor.

EDCS-21200045.translation: The freedwoman Salvia made this for herself, and for Publius Philocenus, freedman of Publius, her patron, and for the six-man official of Augustus, Quinctius Theoxenus, and for Lucius Quinctius Sotericus.
EDCS-21200045.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by the freedwoman Salvia for herself and others, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-21200046.translation: Lucius Sextilius Taurus, son of Quintus, censor.
EDCS-21200046.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the name and office (censor) of Lucius Sextilius Taurus, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-21200048.translation: Gnaeus Veveius Trebianus, son of Gnaeus, herald.
EDCS-21200048.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription recording the name and profession (herald) of Gnaeus Veveius Trebianus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200049.translation: Veveia, daughter of Caius, for her father Caius Veveius.
EDCS-21200049.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Veveia to her father Caius Veveius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200050.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Euangelus for his well-deserving wife, Claudia Galatea.
EDCS-21200050.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Tiberius Claudius Euangelus for his wife Claudia Galatea, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200051.translation: To Tiro, freedman of the emperors, Tiberius Claudius.
EDCS-21200051.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Tiro, a freedman of the emperors, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200052.translation: This is the tomb of Marcus Geminius, son of Spurius. [It is also for] Marcus Geminius Gudas, freedman of Marcus; [and for] Statia Geminia, freedwoman of Marcus; [and for] Gudas.
EDCS-21200052.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the ownership of a tomb for Marcus Geminius and several freedpersons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200054.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording names, possibly funerary or dedicatory, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200057.translation: Quintus Nonius Labeo, son of Quintus, dedicates as sacred to Diana this altar, grove, and spring.
EDCS-21200057.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Quintus Nonius Labeo to the goddess Diana, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21200059.translation: For the safety and return of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian, Geminia Myrtis, with Anicia Prisca, made this temple and dedicated it to the worshippers of Iovis Axoranus, so that they may always feast there in memory of her husband Anicius Priscus.
EDCS-21200059.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Geminia Myrtis and Anicia Prisca for the health of the emperor and to honor a temple of Iovis Axoranus, established for feasting in memory of Geminia's husband, likely dating to the reign of Hadrian (117-138 CE).

EDCS-21200060.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Juno Lucina.

EDCS-21200064.translation: Clesipus Geganius, *magister* of the Capitoline priests, *magister* of the Luperci, *viator* and *tribunicius*.
EDCS-21200064.summary: This is a dedication by Clesipus Geganius, who held several priestly and administrative titles, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-21200066.translation: Gaius Oppius Rufus, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, *pagi magister*, and also *praefectus* at Ulubris, administering justice. May whoever is evil perish evilly. [---] vera pra[---].
EDCS-21200066.summary: This is an inscription recording the career of Gaius Oppius Rufus, a local official who served as *magister* and *praefectus*, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-21200071.translation: For the memory. Marcus Aurelius Papas made this for himself during his lifetime.
EDCS-21200071.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Papas, who commissioned his own tomb during his life, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21200076.translation: Manlia Nais bought two pots for herself and for Manlia Phoebe, her patroness.
EDCS-21200076.summary: This is a purchase record by Manlia Nais for herself and her patroness Manlia Phoebe, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21200211.translation: For the safety of our lord Valentinian, the perpetual Augustus. Paulinus, most eminent man, *praefectus urbi*, made this.
EDCS-21200211.summary: This is a dedication by Paulinus, the urban prefect, likely made during the reign of Emperor Valentinian (either I or III), honoring him.

EDCS-21200215.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription to Vinissia and Nalvinia.

EDCS-21200216.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Gaius Ifibius Flpeus, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-21200220.summary: This inscription records the name Sextus Caecilius Processus, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-21200221.summary: This inscription records the name Gaius Poppaeus Sabinus, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-21200222.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or ownership marker for Lucius Pompeius Fortunatus.

EDCS-21200224.translation: To Publius Annius Septimus Sextus Geganus Fimbria, as one of the two magistrates (duoviri).
EDCS-21200224.summary: This inscription records a dedication or honorific title for Publius Annius Septimus Sextus Geganus Fimbria, who served as a duovir.

EDCS-21200225.translation: Publius Aquilius Gallus, as one of the two magistrates (duovir).
EDCS-21200225.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Aquilius Gallus as a duovir, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-21200229.translation: Of Titus Longus Priscus and Gaius Trebius Planus, and Publius Betilienus Chresimus, as the two magistrates (duoviri).
EDCS-21200229.summary: This inscription records the names of Titus Longus Priscus, Gaius Trebius Planus, and Publius Betilienus Chresimus, serving together as duoviri.

EDCS-21200231.translation: Of Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, as the two magistrates (duoviri).
EDCS-21200231.summary: This inscription names Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, who served as duoviri.

EDCS-21200232.translation: Of Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, as the two magistrates (duoviri).
EDCS-21200232.summary: This inscription names Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, who served as duoviri.

EDCS-21200233.translation: Of Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, as the two magistrates (duoviri).
EDCS-21200233.summary: This inscription names Quintus Mestrius and Gaius Tappurius, who served as duoviri.

EDCS-21200234.translation: Of Marcus Terentius Cl(arens?) and Gaius Caecilius Gav(ianus?), as the two magistrates (duoviri), and Marcus Publius Betilienus Chresimus.
EDCS-21200234.summary: This inscription lists Marcus Terentius Clarens(?), Gaius Caecilius Gavianus(?), and Marcus Publius Betilienus Chresimus as duoviri.

EDCS-21200635.translation: Genialis, slave of Ponticus Rasinus, made this.
EDCS-21200635.summary: This inscription records that Genialis, a slave of Ponticus Rasinus, made the object.

EDCS-21300009.translation: For the memory of Mollicia Tryphera. [She] made this for her beloved Felix, who deserved well.
EDCS-21300009.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication made by Mollicia Tryphera for Felix.

EDCS-21300012.translation: Marcus Calvius, son of Marcus, grandson of Publius, and Caius Crassicius, son of Publius, grandson of Caius, approved and dedicated the temple of Castor and Pollux, which they were to build according to a decree of the Senate, using sacred money; Caius Geminius Mateiclus, son of Publius, grandson of Caius, son of Caius, had overseen its construction.
EDCS-21300012.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to Castor and Pollux by Marcus Calvius and Caius Crassicius, who oversaw its construction with sacred funds, following a senatorial decree.

EDCS-21300014.translation: Caius Curtius Philo, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-21300014.summary: This inscription records the name of Caius Curtius Philo, freedman of Caius.

EDCS-21300015.translation: Marcus Aulius Buxsus, son of Caius, and Lucius Saleivius Philocles, freedman of Lucius, give a statue and base to Concordia.
EDCS-21300015.summary: This inscription records the donation of a statue and base to the goddess Concordia by Marcus Aulius Buxsus and Lucius Saleivius Philocles.

EDCS-21300016.summary: This inscription records the name of Aulius, son of Caius, with some missing parts.

EDCS-21300017.translation: Publius Peilius, son of Lucius, and Caius Calvius, son of Publius, as censors, [dedicated this] to Fortuna Opsequens.
EDCS-21300017.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna Opsequens made by the censors Publius Peilius and Caius Calvius.

EDCS-21300018.translation: To Liber Pater. Spira Ulubrana made this at her own expense.
EDCS-21300018.summary: This is a dedication to Liber Pater by Spira Ulubrana, likely from a private shrine or a public monument funded by her.

EDCS-21300019.translation: Cervaria, daughter of Spurius, as magistra, gave this gift to Mater Matuta.
EDCS-21300019.summary: This records a votive gift from Cervaria to Mater Matuta, given during her term as magistra.

EDCS-21300020.translation: The magistri of Mentis give a performance. Furius, son of Sextus, Vir(); Quintus Vibius, freedman of Quintus, Sabb(); Pollius, freedman of Lucius, Hilarus; R[---]O Publilius Lucius Publilius Pomponius; performed stage plays. The site was granted by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-21300020.summary: This inscription records the staging of theatrical games by several individuals, funded by a site granted by the Senate, likely for public entertainment.

EDCS-21300022.translation: To Good Mentei. The magistri X contributed 3500 sesterces. The magistri V(---?) gave 5000 sesterces. Saleivi P. servus Liberus curated. Timotheus, freedman of Poplilius Lucius Marcus, Antiochus, freedman of the people, curated. Petro, freedman of Furius Lucius Ra(); Furius Lucius, freedman of Lucius Publius Caius; Antiochus, freedman of Utilius Cnaeus, curated.
EDCS-21300022.summary: This inscription details contributions to a cult of Mentei Bonae, likely a local deity, by various individuals and freedmen who also served as curators, with funding from the magistri.

EDCS-21300024.translation: ] to the Augusti. [---]tulus, one of the four magistrates with judicial authority, built a small shrine (?) to them.
EDCS-21300024.summary: This incomplete inscription records the construction of a small shrine by a magistrate (IIIIvir i.d.) to the divine Augusti.

EDCS-21300025.translation: Marcus Manlius, son of Marcus, and Lucius Turpilius, son of Lucius, as duumviri, by decree of the Senate, oversaw the building of a temple and approved it for themselves.
EDCS-21300025.summary: This inscription records the construction and approval of a temple overseen by two duumviri, acting on a senatorial decree.

EDCS-21300026.translation: Paulla Toutia, daughter of Marcus, and her fellow suppliants.
EDCS-21300026.summary: This brief inscription likely refers to a group of women, including Paulla Toutia, associated with a religious cult or petition.

EDCS-21300028.translation: Marcus Calvus, son of Marcus, son of Publius Priscus, of the Papiria tribe. Marcus Calvus, son of Marcus, son of Publius Priscus, his father, added to the senatorial order by Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, as censor among the tribunes. Titus Calvus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-21300028.summary: This inscription details the senatorial career and family lineage of Marcus Calvus, whose father was admitted to the senatorial order by Emperor Claudius.

EDCS-21300029.translation: To the Father of the Immortals, from the people of Comum. DA COP SC D CV Marcus Cal[vus] admitted into the senatorial order.
EDCS-21300029.summary: This inscription, though heavily abbreviated and damaged, likely records a dedication from the people of Comum and the admission of Marcus Calvus to the senatorial order, possibly by an emperor.

EDCS-21300032.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Iustus, son of Tiberius, who held all the offices in Cora. The council and people of Cora honored him for his good services.
EDCS-21300032.summary: This inscription is a public testimonial from the people of Cora honoring Tiberius Claudius Iustus for his service and fulfillment of all local offices.

EDCS-21300033.translation: Maximus, a member of the college of four officials, serving his five-year term.
EDCS-21300033.summary: This inscription records the name and title of a civic official named Maximus, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-21300034.translation: Gaius Oppius Verus and Lucius Turpilius Priscus, sons of Lucius, members of the college of four officials with jurisdiction, brought water, collected from the mountains by a celestial aqueduct, which had been leaking due to a dam that had collapsed, through a channel constructed by their own efforts, into purified pools, using public funds, after a long period of disuse. And PE AO
EDCS-21300034.summary: This inscription details the civic achievement of two officials, Gaius Oppius Verus and Lucius Turpilius Priscus, in restoring a public water supply, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300035.translation: Quintus Pomponius, son of Quintus, and Lucius Tulius, son of Servius, the praetors, purchased (this) with money from Mars.
EDCS-21300035.summary: This inscription records a purchase made by two individuals identified as praetors, possibly related to a military or religious context given the mention of 'money from Mars', dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-21300037.translation: To Tutia, mother of C(aius) Lepanius and Quintus Tudius, by decree of the senate and with the consent of the townspeople, on account of her benefits and generosity.
EDCS-21300037.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription dedicated to Tutia by her sons, honoring her for her benefits and generosity, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300042.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to be a personal name, likely Roman, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300043.translation: and for the Republic of the Corani, Publius Dibus, next to my monument, and from the Republic of the Corani, that they should observe them, so that no one after me is placed with a penalty.
EDCS-21300043.summary: This inscription seems to relate to a public works or monument project commissioned by or for the Republic of the Corani, with provisions for future observation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300046.translation: Arellia Diogis, freedwoman of Marcus. Marcus Arellius.
EDCS-21300046.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or record of relationship between Arellia, a freedwoman, and Marcus Arellius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300047.translation: Obo Aurelius Primitivus and Primitivus made (this) for their dearest father.
EDCS-21300047.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by two sons, Aurelius Primitivus and Primitivus, for their father, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300048.translation: Calvia Helena. Dedicated and consecrated by her own hand.
EDCS-21300048.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, for Calvia Helena, possibly indicating she erected it herself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300049.summary: This is a simple inscription recording the name and filiation of Quintus Furius, likely part of a larger monument or funerary context from the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-21300051.translation: Sindaeus, freedman of Quintus, [for himself] and for Decembrius, freedman of Quintus, and for [his] freedwoman and freedwoman.
EDCS-21300051.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a freedman for himself and his household, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-21300054.translation: The heirs of the freedman Lucilius dedicated this to Aurelia, his mother, on her birthday.
EDCS-21300054.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the heirs of a freedman to his mother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300056.translation: Also for his daughters, for Hygieia, and for Pacuria, who lived for 13 years and 1 month, and for her freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-21300056.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication to several individuals, including daughters and a young girl named Pacuria, and also mentions future descendants, suggesting an Imperial date.

EDCS-21300058.translation: I, the freedman Marcus Secundus, and my freedmen, and not then for the Republic, P C O.
EDCS-21300058.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to be a dedication or declaration by a freedman, possibly concerning his property or obligations, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300059.translation: Sextus Tedius Felix, freedman of Tedia, and Tedia Fortunata, freedwoman of Sextus, [set up] 12 continuous pots above the inscriptions.
EDCS-21300059.summary: This inscription records the placement of 12 pots above inscriptions, set up by a freedman and freedwoman, likely related to funerary arrangements from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300063.translation: Marcus Ofasius Firmus Marus Cornelius Cossinus, son of Marus, son of Cornelius, as *praefectus fabrum*, military tribune of the Legio XIIII Gemina Victrix, curator of the youth games, *duovir* and patron of the colony, dedicated this as a gift to the Antiate Fortunes.
EDCS-21300063.summary: This extensive inscription records the career and dedications of Marcus Ofasius Firmus Marus Cornelius Cossinus, a prominent local official in the colony of Antium, likely dating to the mid-to-late Imperial period.

EDCS-21300064.translation: For the Lares: the magistrates, Marcus Histumennius Flaccus, freedman of Marcus, and Aulus Albius Nicephor, freedman of Aulus, gave from their own funds.
EDCS-21300064.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Lares made by two magistrates, both freedmen, who funded the offering themselves, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300065.translation: [...] for the Lar, for the Mother Goddess of I(daea), [...] wished that [he] have made [it], gave as a gift for HS [...], [...] gave as a gift for HS [....
EDCS-21300065.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication to deities, possibly including the Mother Goddess of I(daea), with a monetary value indicated, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300068.summary: This very short inscription likely records a name and a number or cult association, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21300073.translation: To our Lords Emperors Valentinian and Valens, always Augusts, Lollius Cyrius, principal of the curia and editor of the duodena, restored from his own funds the amphitheater, which had collapsed from age, along with its rear gates and the entire arena structure, to its former state; the grandson of Lollius Cyrius, principal of the curia and former editor, son of Lollius Claudius, principal and patron of the curia, great-grandson of Messius Gorgotis, principal, successfully.
EDCS-21300073.summary: This inscription records the extensive restoration of an amphitheater and arena by Lollius Cyrius, highlighting his family's prominent civic and administrative roles, dating to the reign of Valentinian and Valens (364-375 AD).

EDCS-21300074.translation: To Gaius Galerius Maximus, Flamen of the Claudials, quaestor-designate, Xvir for judging lawsuits, his slave the cashier and [---].
EDCS-21300074.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Galerius Maximus, a public official, by his slave.

EDCS-21300076.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Pomponius Musaeus, who held the office of consul.

EDCS-21300077.translation: To Sextus Varius Marcellus, procurator of the aqueducts (rank 100), procurator of the province of Britain (rank 200), procurator of the imperial treasury (rank 300), who served as vice-prefect of the praetorian guard and of the city, a most distinguished man, prefect of the military treasury, legate of Legio III Augusta, governor of the province of Numidia, by Iulia Soaemias Bassiana, most distinguished lady, with her children, to her most loving husband and father.
EDCS-21300077.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sextus Varius Marcellus, a high-ranking imperial official, by his family.

EDCS-21300078.summary: This inscription records Vergilianus, who served in the judicial role of Xvir stlitibus iudicandis.

EDCS-21300082.translation: To Caius Acilius Marcianus, principal centurion of Legion XIIII Gemina, a Carthaginian, his protégé, Caius Aurelius Onesimus [---].
EDCS-21300082.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Acilius Marcianus, a centurion, set up by his protégé.

EDCS-21300083.translation: To the memory of Caius Alpinus Restitutus, frumentarius of Legion XXII Primigenia, and of Firminus Adventus, freedman, Marcus Firminius Frontinus, frumentarius of Legion VIII Augusta.
EDCS-21300083.summary: This inscription commemorates two individuals, Caius Alpinus Restitutus and Firminus Adventus, with Marcus Firminius Frontinus acting as dedicator.

EDCS-21300084.translation: To Quintus Graius Iamus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, prefect of the arsenal, and to Volusia Maxima, by the care of Atticus, freedman.
EDCS-21300084.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quintus Graius Iamus, prefect of the arsenal, and Volusia Maxima, overseen by their freedman Atticus.

EDCS-21300088.translation: To the honor of Marcus Av[---] Primitiu[s ---] HOI[---] Marcus Ulpius [---] Lec[---] and Sabi[---] Sever[---] M[---] Lucius Mari[---] Ianuar[ius], IIvir [---] Publius Aeliu[s ---] Heliodorus, Marcus Ulpius [---].
EDCS-21300088.summary: This is a dedication honoring several individuals, possibly related to civic or religious office, with multiple dedicator names partially preserved.

EDCS-21300089.translation: Marcus Durmius, for the sacrifice and the washing.
EDCS-21300089.summary: This inscription records Marcus Durmius's contribution for a sacrifice and washing ritual.

EDCS-21300093.translation: Zosimus, and his two [---] with [---] with his own expense arranged to be made, to whom on account of his munificence the order decreed a bisellium, with his son III [---] II with the IIvirs quinq[uennales].
EDCS-21300093.summary: This inscription records the posthumous honoring of Zosimus, likely a prominent citizen, with a bisellium, funded by his family and related to the actions of the IIvirs quinqennales.

EDCS-21300892.translation: The bones of Cornelia, freedwoman of Lucius, [---]
EDCS-21300892.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for Cornelia, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300893.translation: The bones of Decimia (a woman) and Suavis, freedwoman of Marcus Sestius.
EDCS-21300893.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Decimia and Suavis, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300894.translation: To Donatus, for his wife who lived 30 years and 17 days, who lived in marriage 4 years and 25 days, to a well-deserving wife.
EDCS-21300894.summary: This is a dedication on a tombstone to a wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period, noting her lifespan and duration of marriage.

EDCS-21300897.translation: Titus Flavius Philippus for himself and for Flavia Caenis, his wife, from a place donated of four jars by Aleia Felicula, the path and approach to the place of burning, for the purpose of sacrifice, [---]
EDCS-21300897.summary: This is an inscription related to the donation of a burial plot for cremation and sacrifice, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300898.translation: To the Divine Spirits, to the good spirit of Flavia Albina, daughter of A.P., I entrust her ashes in this chest; she lived 24 years, 3 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-21300898.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Albina, detailing her lifespan and the placement of her ashes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300901.summary: This is a short funerary inscription for Gellius Quintus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300904.translation: Caius Lustuleius Farnaces, freedman of Caius, established this monument for himself and for Ceia Olympias, freedwoman of Lucius, while living, and for Ceia Neobe, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-21300904.summary: This is an inscription on a funerary monument established by Caius Lustuleius Farnaces for himself and two freedwomen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300906.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of Marcellus Valerius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300908.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Onomaste, likely from the Roman Imperial period, stating her age at death.

EDCS-21300909.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely funerary, mentioning Lucius Paetinus Agrippa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21300911.translation: To Marcus Porcius Priscus, from Pollia Melie, his wife.
EDCS-21300911.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Porcius Priscus by his wife.

EDCS-21300913.translation: [---] To a most beloved mother, Primus and Artemidorus, sons, made this.
EDCS-21300913.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to an unnamed mother by her sons Primus and Artemidorus.

EDCS-21300915.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Reus Pompeius lived 4 years, 6 months, 10 days. His most unhappy parents made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-21300915.summary: This is a tombstone for Reus Pompeius, recording his short life and dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-21300916.translation: Gaius Roscius Salvius, Gaius Roscius Hermogenes, Roscia Salvia, Daphnus, Faustilla, Prima.
EDCS-21300916.summary: This inscription lists several names, likely members of a family or household, with some restorations needed.

EDCS-21300918.translation: Rutilia, freedwoman of a woman, Nic[---], I made this monument for myself and for my dearest freedman Gaius Primus, and for my darling Gaius Octavius, freedman of Gaius. This monument or sepulchre shall pertain to none of my heirs whom I leave, nor to the heirs of Gaius O[---] anything shall pertain, whom or which Gaius Octavius Av[---] leaves.
EDCS-21300918.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription where Rutilia, a freedwoman, dedicates it to herself and her freedman Primus and her favorite Gaius Octavius, specifying inheritance restrictions.

EDCS-21300926.translation: Claudia Attica, daughter of Atticus, freedman of Augustus, from the accounts office, placed the gods in the sanctuary of Ceres of Antium at her own expense, with Iulia Procula as priestess, during the consulship of Emperor Caesar Domitian Augustus Germanicus XI.
EDCS-21300926.summary: This inscription records Claudia Attica dedicating statues in the sanctuary of Ceres of Antium during the reign of Domitian.

EDCS-21300934.translation: Caius Iulius Chimarus repaired the statues and small shrine and placed the marble seats for Germanicus Caesar, son of Tiberius Caesar, grandson of the deified Augustus.
EDCS-21300934.summary: This inscription details repairs and additions made to a shrine dedicated to Germanicus Caesar by Caius Iulius Chimarus.

EDCS-21300941.translation: During the reign of our lords the Emperors Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, princes most great, the appearance of the baths, which was deformed by ruin, sordid, and threatening falling masses that deterred the bathing public with fear and anxiety, I, Anicius Auchenius Bassus, a most distinguished man, former proconsul of Campania, judging in place of the sacred office, have restored it to firm stability and use, to the better image of the city, excluding all decay of age.
EDCS-21300941.summary: Anicius Auchenius Bassus, former proconsul of Campania, restored a dilapidated bath complex during the reign of Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius.

EDCS-21300950.translation: Eros, freedman of the Augusta, procurator, from Caenis, with his son Marcus Antonius Candidus, of the Quirina tribe, gave this as a gift to the tribunes and fellow soldiers.
EDCS-21300950.summary: Eros, a procurator and freedman of the Augusta, along with his son, donated a gift to the tribunes and fellow soldiers.

EDCS-21300955.translation: Lucius Domitius, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a veteran from the 3rd Praetorian cohort.
EDCS-21300955.summary: This is a personal identification of Lucius Domitius, a veteran of the Praetorian Guard.

EDCS-21300956.translation: Lucius Nonius Rufus, brother and heir of Sextus Nonius Severus, son of Lucius, of the Voturia tribe, veteran discharged from the I Classica cohort after 22 years of service, who lived 45 years, set up this monument for him. He is buried here, a soldier of the I Classica cohort.
EDCS-21300956.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Nonius Severus, a veteran of the I Classica cohort, set up by his brother and heir.

EDCS-21300972.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Titus Atilius Rufus Titianus.

EDCS-21300974.translation: Gaius, son of Tiberius Claudius, made this.
EDCS-21300974.summary: This is an inscription recording the maker of a monument, Gaius, son of Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-21300976.translation: Lucius Titus Flavius Fortunatus made this.
EDCS-21300976.summary: This is an inscription recording the maker of a monument, Lucius Titus Flavius Fortunatus.

EDCS-21300977.summary: This is an inscription recording the maker of a monument, Titus Flavius Modestus.

EDCS-21300978.summary: This is an inscription recording the maker of a monument, Titus Flavius Trophimus.

EDCS-21300979.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Prosia Crispinus.

EDCS-21300980.summary: This is an inscription recording the maker of a monument, Lucius Visullius Antiatinus.

EDCS-21400020.translation: Made for Marcus Antonius Philinus, dearest husband, for himself and for his descendants.
EDCS-21400020.summary: This is an inscription recording the dedication of a monument by a spouse for their husband and their lineage.

EDCS-21400022.translation: For Antonia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, wife of Valeria Asinius Sabinianus.
EDCS-21400022.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Antonia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, wife of Valeria Asinius Sabinianus.

EDCS-21400031.translation: Primitivos, Vestalis, Lucius Cocceius Expectatus, Titus Flavius Severus, Caius Clodius Eutychus, Lucius Setinus Felicitas, Aulus Gavidius Felix, Caius Faustius Primitivos, Caius Clodius Apollonius the second, Caius Avillius Ianuarius, Tiberius Claudius Hypnus, Tiberius Claudius Proculus, Tiberius Claudius Trophimus, Caius Julius Eutychus, Titus Flavius Eupor, Titus Flavius Ianuarius, Caius Memmius Asylus, Tiberius Claudius Iustus, Tiberius Claudius, Caius Aurelius, Caius Aurelius, Tiberius Julius, Tiberius Claudius, Marcus Antias Andro, Tyrannus, Fort, Publius Fabius Poly, Titus Flavius F, Marcus Aemilius, Lucius Vitellius, Lucius Veratius, Marcus Fabius Primus, Lucius Junius, Lucius Ho.
EDCS-21400031.summary: This is a list of names, likely donors or members of a group, possibly associated with a religious or civic context in Roman times.

EDCS-21400035.translation: To Proe, his most dutiful father, and Titus Stailius Merc, his friend, and C. PRAL CVI.
EDCS-21400035.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Proe, a father, and his friend Titus Stailius Merc, with an unclear additional abbreviation.

EDCS-21400038.translation: I, Lucius Fabius Octanianus, withdrew to my small fields.
EDCS-21400038.summary: This is a personal declaration by Lucius Fabius Octanianus of his retirement to his private land.

EDCS-21400039.translation: To Fabia Po Marcella, daughter of M. Calpurnia, wife of To Gargilius Autus.
EDCS-21400039.summary: This is a dedication to Fabia Po Marcella, identifying her paternal lineage and marital connection.

EDCS-21400040.translation: To the Divine Shades, for Fabia Polla, his esteemed patroness, and for Hermes and Felicissima, her freedmen, and Bas, his wife, who deserved well.
EDCS-21400040.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Fabia Polla by her freedmen and their wives, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-21400048.translation: To Hortensia Demetria, my dearest, and for herself.
EDCS-21400048.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hortensia Demetria, likely by a spouse or close relative, possibly for a funerary monument.

EDCS-21400063.summary: This is a dedication by Ari to his freedman Seuth.

EDCS-21400065.translation: To Sextilia Tyches, aged 10, and Sextilia, aged 15.
EDCS-21400065.summary: This inscription commemorates two young girls named Sextilia, likely sisters, possibly as a funerary dedication.

EDCS-21400066.translation: To Sympherusa, my wife, who deserved well.
EDCS-21400066.summary: This is a dedication from a husband to his well-deserving wife, Sympherusa.

EDCS-21400073.translation: Marcus Vibius Severus to his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-21400073.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Vibius Severus to his brother, highlighting familial affection.

EDCS-21400079.translation: Is DEIPHID VI of the family, I hate...
EDCS-21400079.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with unclear content, possibly a curse or personal statement.

EDCS-21400083.translation: ...in the quinquennial magistracy of Lucius Secundus, II vir, and of Marcus Junius Annianus, II vir, and Quintus Julius Antoninus.
EDCS-21400083.summary: This inscription likely records a public office or dedication made during a specific quinquennial term, possibly in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-21400092.translation: When Pontius Nigrinus was consul, M. Lepidus [erected this].
EDCS-21400092.summary: This is a dedication made by M. Lepidus, mentioning the consulship of Pontius Nigrinus, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-21400093.translation: Amycus, the atriensis, made this monument for Urania, freedwoman of Augustus, and for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-21400093.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Amycus for his freedwoman Urania and their descendants, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21400097.translation: Octavianus Primus placed [this] to the memory of Octavius, his father.
EDCS-21400097.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Octavianus Primus in memory of his father, Octavius.

EDCS-21400098.translation: He dedicated [this] to his mother Praxedi.
EDCS-21400098.summary: This is a dedication to a mother named Praxedi, likely a funerary monument or a votive offering.

EDCS-21400106.translation: Marcus Verrius Craterus fulfilled his vow to Apollo and the Nymphs.
EDCS-21400106.summary: This is a votive inscription where Marcus Verrius Craterus dedicates something to Apollo and the Nymphs in fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21400113.translation: Sextus Fabius Gemellus, son of Caius, [dedicated this] to the Nymphs.
EDCS-21400113.summary: This is a dedication by Sextus Fabius Gemellus to the Nymphs, likely a votive offering from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21500462.translation: Under the supervision of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, by Restitutus, freedman of Augustus, the procurator VX.
EDCS-21500462.summary: This inscription records administrative oversight by a procurator during the reign of Emperor Hadrian, likely related to a public building or project.

EDCS-21700014.summary: This is a simple dedication by Julius Salius, likely a funerary monument or a building inscription.

With the favor of God and the good fortune of his reign, through the diligent efforts of the appointed official, and the laudatory efforts devoted to the most clement prince, from the lineage of the Decii, Caecina Mavortius Basilus Decius, a most distinguished and illustrious man, former prefect of the city, former praetorian prefect, former ordinary consul, patrician, who to perpetuate the glory of so great a lord, returned to dryness through many means, previously unknown and exceedingly ancient, the water that had been drained not into the sea, bringing laurel and palm.

EDCS-23400087.translation: In the name of Christ. For Oppius Paulus, dearest son, who lived 5 years, 11 months, 2 days, buried on the 8th day before the Ides of May, of good memory.

EDCS-23400197.translation: Greetings to your patroness, Quartila. Gratus, the architect, sends greetings, having made this for you twice, may you be well.
EDCS-23400197.summary: A friendly greeting and dedication from the architect Gratus to his patroness Quartila.

EDCS-23400199.translation: Gaius Tillius Rufus, son of Caius, and Publius Maccius Melas, son of Publius, the two magistrates, had this made in accordance with the decree of the council of decurions.
EDCS-23400199.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by two magistrates, Gaius Tillius Rufus and Publius Maccius Melas.

EDCS-23400210.translation: To Marcus, son of Marcus, as aedile.
EDCS-23400210.summary: A partial inscription indicating a dedication or honor for an aedile named Marcus.

EDCS-23400214.translation: To EMPRONIUS, for Runtia NGNNA, his wife. (repeated) Wife. Wife.
EDCS-23400214.summary: A funerary dedication for Runtia NGNNA, wife of EMPRONIUS, with a repeated word for 'wife'.

EDCS-23400215.translation: Lucius Cantinius Rufus, son of Caius, from Falerna, former primus pilus of the 7th Macedonian Legion, ordered this monument or tomb to be made in accordance with his will; it will not pass to the heir.
EDCS-23400215.summary: A funerary monument or tomb set up by Lucius Cantinius Rufus, a former primus pilus, according to his will.

EDCS-23400217.translation: Gaius Aufustius [---], Terpnus [---], as Augustalis master [---]

EDCS-23400219.summary: This inscription appears to be a private lot or marker, possibly related to a game or divination, belonging to Publius Cipius Nicomachus.

EDCS-23400220.translation: You will carefully note the writing of Flavinus Rufus at Capua, at Deana, upstream of the Pediae Quetes.
EDCS-23400220.summary: This is a directive, likely on a boundary stone or marker, instructing someone to note a written boundary or property belonging to Flavinus Rufus in Capua.

EDCS-23400221.translation: Three scruples of the weight of Quintus Gupacius, half an ounce, and three small scruples.
EDCS-23400221.summary: This inscription records a precise weight of goods, likely for trade or accounting, associated with Quintus Gupacius.

EDCS-23400243.summary: This inscription honors or commemorates a man named Purpur, described as 'praiseworthy,' possibly on a tomb or honorary monument.

EDCS-23400245.translation: Aulus Hostilius, son of Aulus, Mancinus.
EDCS-23400245.summary: This is a formal Roman naming inscription, likely for an individual named Aulus Hostilius Mancinus, son of Aulus.

EDCS-23400256.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a definitive summary, but may refer to a person or measure with numerical components.

EDCS-23400262.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Octavius Parthenius, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-23400263.translation: To Marcus Octavius Scorpus, his freedman, the patron for his well-deserved services.
EDCS-23400263.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a patron to his freedman, Marcus Octavius Scorpus, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-23400265.translation: Casius, the overseer of a work gang.
EDCS-23400265.summary: This inscription identifies Casius, likely a freedman or slave employed as an overseer (ergastularius) in a large agricultural or mining operation.

EDCS-23400266.translation: The Patrician family protects this house with eternal praise; their souls hold the stars, the earth holds the rest. He rested in peace under Consul D.
EDCS-23400266.summary: This is a tombstone epitaph for a member of the Patrician family, praising their eternal renown and placing their soul among the stars, dating to the consulship of 'D'.

EDCS-23400272.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Aur Secu...
EDCS-23400272.summary: This is a funerary dedication fragment to the departed spirits, likely for a person named Aur Secu...

EDCS-23400277.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Terentia Artemisia, emphasizing her pietas (dutifulness), likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-23400285.translation: Marcus Aplanius Marcellus, son of Quintus, of the Collina tribe, for himself and for his daughter Aplania Onesima, and for his freedwoman, and for the Rosesi...
EDCS-23400285.summary: This is an epitaph for Marcus Aplanius Marcellus, dedicating a tomb for himself, his daughter, his freedwoman, and possibly others named Rosesi.

EDCS-23400286.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a funerary dedication, mentioning individuals named Aelius and Hordio.

EDCS-23400287.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Artorius Cilo, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-23400289.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a dedication or funerary text, for Aulus Carvilius.

EDCS-23400298.translation: Nia, daughter of Aulus, wife of [---]manda, to [---]o, her [---]ri, for himself.
EDCS-23400298.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication, likely for a woman named Nia, to a relative or spouse, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23400300.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Lucius Septimius.
EDCS-23400300.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Lucius Septimius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400301.summary: This inscription names Turrania Lampas, identifying her as a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400319.translation: Barcathes, freedman of Dasis. Marcus Dassius and Marcus Allius Cerdo, having heard the case which he was conducting with Quintus Cava, [ordered?] Caius Vitrasius...
EDCS-23400319.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records a legal or administrative decision involving Barcathes, Marcus Dassius, Marcus Allius Cerdo, Quintus Cava, and Caius Vitrasius, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400324.translation: Pamphilus watched on behalf of the associates.
EDCS-23400324.summary: This inscription records Pamphilus acting on behalf of associates, possibly in a business or legal context, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400325.translation: Darda, daughter of Babi, watched on the Nones of February for Lucius Cornelius and Lucius Valerius.
EDCS-23400325.summary: This inscription records Darda, daughter of Babi, observing or witnessing an event on behalf of Lucius Cornelius and Lucius Valerius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400326.translation: Flaccus, son of Novi, watched on the Kalends of April for Publius Lentulus and Gnaeus Aufidius.
EDCS-23400326.summary: This inscription records Flaccus, son of Novi, observing or witnessing an event on behalf of Publius Lentulus and Gnaeus Aufidius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400327.summary: This inscription records Diodorus, son of Deli, as a witness or observer, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400329.translation: Here rests Catelus, who lived approximately...
EDCS-23400329.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Catelus, indicating his approximate age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400330.translation: Here rests Successa, a woman of most illustrious memory, in the sleep of peace, with the sign of faith, who lived approximately seventy-seven years, interred on the 18th day before the Kalends of...
EDCS-23400330.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription for Successa, noting her age, character, and burial date, likely from the Late Roman Empire or Early Christian period.

EDCS-23400336.translation: Marcus Publilius Satur, freedman of Marcus, erected this at his own expense for himself and his freedman Marcus Publilius Stephano, by the arbitration of Marcus Publilius Timotis, a freedman of Marcus, and the herald Gadis, a freedman of Marcus. He lived 22 years.
EDCS-23400336.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Publilius Satur, paid for by himself, and mentioning his freedman and arbitrators, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400338.translation: By Publius Arruntius, son of Publius, according to his will, by the arbitration of Marcus Magus, son of Marcus, and Lucius Currelius I, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-23400338.summary: This inscription records the execution of a will, mentioning the testator Publius Arruntius and the arbitrators, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400340.translation: To Lucius Clodius Porcianus, according to his will.
EDCS-23400340.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication or bequest to Lucius Clodius Porcianus according to his will, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400341.translation: To Philusa, freedwoman of Marcus, and to Menogenea, freedwoman of Helvia, her mother, and to Dada, freedwoman of Sextus Pomponius, her sister.
EDCS-23400341.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, honors three women: Philusa, Menogenea, and Dada, with familial relationships indicated.

EDCS-23400344.translation: To Servatronia Calityche, deserving of her [good merits].
EDCS-23400344.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph honoring Servatronia Calityche, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400345.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication or epitaph, possibly to a person named Nysa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400350.translation: Quintus Fulvius, son of Quintus, grandson of Marcus, brought this water under the authority of Publius Atilius, son of Lucius, the urban praetor.
EDCS-23400350.summary: This inscription records the construction or provision of a water supply, commissioned by Quintus Fulvius and overseen by the urban praetor Publius Atilius, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-23400352.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that seems to be an epitaph for Hilara, daughter of Alexsa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400353.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Septumia Hilara, daughter of Marcus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400354.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly an epitaph or dedication, mentioning at least two individuals, Tertia and Oufentina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400356.translation: He ordered that it be made for himself and for Lucius Satrius and for Satria, freedwoman of Lucius, by his will.
EDCS-23400356.summary: This inscription records a testamentary instruction for the construction of a monument for the deceased and others.

EDCS-23400359.translation: Aspa Quintus, son of O., O. s. (or similar abbreviation).
EDCS-23400359.summary: This inscription appears to be a very abbreviated funerary or dedicatory text, possibly naming an individual and an abbreviation of their filiation or a related term.

EDCS-23400364.translation: Born for the good of the state.
EDCS-23400364.summary: This inscription likely refers to a person dedicated to public service or born for the benefit of the community.

EDCS-23400365.translation: To the divine shades, for the memory of Fortunatus, freedman of Caius Septimius Caius, a callistrator of the VIIvirate; he lived 90 years.
EDCS-23400365.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Fortunatus, a freedman and callistrator of the VIIvirate, who lived to be 90 years old.

EDCS-23400368.translation: To the divine shades, [for] the foot-race of Lucius Plotium [?], obs[ --- ]
EDCS-23400368.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription mentioning the divine shades and possibly a funerary competition or offering by Lucius Plotium.

EDCS-23400372.translation: Infernal gods, I entrust to you if you have any sanctity, and I hand over Carisius' Tychene, whatever she may do, may everything turn out badly for her, infernal gods, I entrust to you her body, her complexion, her figure, her head, her hair, her shadow, her brain, her forehead, her eyebrows, her mouth, her nose, her chin, her cheeks, her lips, her word, her expression, her neck, her liver, her shoulders, her heart, her lungs, her intestines, her belly, her arms, her fingers, her hands, her navel, her bladder, her thighs, her knees, her legs, her ankles, her soles, her toes, infernal gods, if I see her wasting away, I vow to you, to her parents on her anniversary, willingly, her savings.
EDCS-23400372.summary: This is a dramatic and extensive curse or imprecation against a woman named Tychene, invoking the infernal gods to inflict suffering upon her, possibly by a spurned lover or rival.

EDCS-23400374.translation: To Marcus Nonius and Sempron [---] for himself and in [---]
EDCS-23400374.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording a dedication or funerary commemoration for Marcus Nonius and Sempronius [---].

EDCS-23400375.translation: To Numerius Cepidius, freedman of the woman Diurna. Marcus Pontius, freedman of Marcus, Euphes. Pontia, freedwoman of Marcus, Ce[pidius?]. 12 feet in front.
EDCS-23400375.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or funerary dedication, possibly indicating plot size, associated with Numerius Cepidius and freedmen of the Pontius family.

EDCS-23400376.translation: To Numerius Cepidius, freedman of the woman Diurna. Marcus Pontius, freedman of Marcus, Euphes. Pontia, freedwoman of Marcus, Ce[pidius?]. 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-23400376.summary: This inscription seems to be a boundary marker or funerary dedication, similar to EDCS-23400375, indicating plot size in a field and associated with Numerius Cepidius and freedmen of the Pontius family.

EDCS-23400378.translation: To the most fortunate freedman POST [---]
EDCS-23400378.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a funerary dedication to a freedman named Felix or similar, possibly with a reference to a post or location.

EDCS-23400379.translation: Aeronia Vitalis made this for her deserving husband, Lutatius Romulus.
EDCS-23400379.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a wife to her husband, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-23400382.translation: Menophilus, slave of Abi Lucius, watched over this for Gaius Valerius and Marcus Herennius.
EDCS-23400382.summary: This inscription records a slave, Menophilus, overseeing something for two individuals, possibly a funerary or property marker.

EDCS-23400383.translation: Auxo gladly gave this gift to Isis, deservedly.
EDCS-23400383.summary: This is a votive offering to the goddess Isis, indicating a personal dedication.

EDCS-23400384.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely identifies Junius Bassus, a praetorian prefect, possibly on a monument.

EDCS-23400413.translation: Cn. Octavius Phainus, father, [made this for his own] studies.
EDCS-23400413.summary: This fragmentary inscription indicates a father, Cn. Octavius Phainus, setting up something related to studies.

EDCS-23400429.translation: Aulus Aemilius, alive, for himself and for Aemilia Thymele, his wife, and for Ianthi, freedwoman of Umbilia, and for Hilarus, freedman of Publius Flavius, alive. In the front 20 feet, in the land 20 feet. This monument or tomb is not to follow its heir.
EDCS-23400429.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription from Aulus Aemilius for himself and family members, specifying land dimensions and stipulating that the property does not pass to an heir, suggesting it is a perpetual burial plot.

EDCS-23400437.translation: Lupus, freedman from the camp, freedman of the Emperor, for his patron, and for himself, and for Casticia Capitolina, his wife, and for his freedmen and descendants.
EDCS-23400437.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lupus, an imperial freedman, for himself, his wife, his patron, and his descendants.

EDCS-23400438.translation: Caius Nonius Bassus, evocatus Augusti, for his most devoted brother. In the front 12 feet, in the land 12 feet.
EDCS-23400438.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Nonius Bassus, a soldier of the Emperor, dedicating a plot to his brother.

EDCS-23400440.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely a funerary dedication for Silana, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-23400443.translation: Two columbaria, four urns for Tiberius Claudius Crescens.
EDCS-23400443.summary: This inscription records the construction of burial structures (columbaria and urns) for Tiberius Claudius Crescens, likely a funerary commission.

EDCS-23400445.translation: Gaius Iunius Domitius and Quirina and Dionysius Heraclides made this for themselves and for their sweetest soul Soterini, their daughter, who lived 11 years, 4 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-23400445.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Iunius Domitius and Quirina and Dionysius Heraclides for themselves and their deceased daughter, Soterini.

EDCS-23400448.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for a young child named Primus.

EDCS-23400527.summary: This is a concise funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Successus.

EDCS-23400530.translation: For Lucius Caelsius Labeio, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, and for his father Lucius Caelsius, son of Lucius, of the Menenia tribe, according to his will, by the arbitration of the freedmen Salvius and Cladus.
EDCS-23400530.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Caelsius Labeio and his father, established by their freedmen.

EDCS-23400531.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Ulpius Lucilianus lived 38 years and 7 months.
EDCS-23400531.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Lucilianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-23400534.translation: Fiduia, freedwoman of Ma, for herself and for Marcus Tintorius Hilarus, Augustalis sevirus.
EDCS-23400534.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Fiduia, a freedwoman, for herself and for Marcus Tintorius Hilarus.

EDCS-23400545.translation: Magia Prisca dedicated this image of Jupiter as a gift to Mater Matuta.

EDCS-23800003.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a funerary dedication or ownership mark, for Lucius Canius.

EDCS-23800005.translation: Please ensure that Gaius Aburius, the II vir, a good man, is made.
EDCS-23800005.summary: This is a plea, likely from an election context, to ensure the recognition or election of Gaius Aburius as II vir.

EDCS-23800006.translation: I ask you to make Marcus Tullius a duovir.
EDCS-23800006.summary: This is a plea from an inscription, asking for Marcus Tullius to be appointed to the office of duovir.

EDCS-23800008.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple designation or endorsement of Cassius for the office of duovir.
