EDCS-23800436.translation: I ask you, make Vettius, the aedile, a duumvir for dispensing justice, worthy of the republic; Suilimea asks that you make him so.
EDCS-23800436.summary: This inscription is a popular request from Suilimea asking the voters to elect Vettius as duumvir, indicating a political or electoral context.

EDCS-23800439.translation: Homullus loves Spuncles, Spuncles performs fellatio, Asciola writes with Geminus, for whom [a debt of] four [asses?].
EDCS-23800439.summary: This is a graffiti-like inscription with explicit sexual content and a note about a debt, likely from Pompeii or Herculaneum.

EDCS-23800441.translation: Primio asks that you make Gaius Calventius Sittius duumvir for dispensing justice.
EDCS-23800441.summary: This inscription is a request from Primio to elect Gaius Calventius Sittius as duumvir, likely an electoral notice.

EDCS-23800442.summary: This is a simple designation of Popidius Secundus for the office of aedile, probably an electoral notice.

EDCS-23800443.translation: Publius Paquius, duumvir for dispensing justice, worthy of the republic.
EDCS-23800443.summary: This inscription designates Publius Paquius as a duumvir worthy of public office, likely an electoral notice.

EDCS-23800444.summary: This inscription records that Polites appointed Quintus Postumius to the office of quinquennial, suggesting an administrative or electoral context.

EDCS-23800446.summary: This is a designation of Vettius Firmus for the office of aedile, likely an electoral notice.

EDCS-23800447.translation: I ask you, make Casellius the aedile.
EDCS-23800447.summary: This inscription is a request asking for Casellius to be elected as aedile, indicating an electoral purpose.

EDCS-23800449.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that simply names Lucius Popidius, possibly an electoral notice or a dedication.

EDCS-23800452.translation: Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, son of Lucius, as aedile.
EDCS-23800452.summary: This inscription names Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, son of Lucius, for the office of aedile, likely an electoral notice.

EDCS-23800654.translation: Baebia Thallusa and Teodotus gave this gift to Hilario, their father.
EDCS-23800654.summary: A dedication of a gift by Baebia Thallusa and Teodotus to their father, Hilario.

EDCS-23800655.translation: Belonging to Marcus Cornelius Secundus and Sergia Paula; 17.
EDCS-23800655.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or tomb, indicating ownership by Marcus Cornelius Secundus and Sergia Paula, with the number 17 perhaps denoting a lot or age.

EDCS-23800656.translation: 42; of the most distinguished man Clodius Adelfius and the most distinguished woman Faltonia Proba.
EDCS-23800656.summary: This inscription, possibly related to a tomb or property, identifies the owners or dedicatees as Clodius Adelfius and Faltonia Proba, with the number 42 likely indicating a plot number or age.

EDCS-23800663.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for Simplicia, indicating her place of rest.

EDCS-23800667.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary or commemorative, with names like Quintus, Aulus, and Junius being partially preserved.

EDCS-23800670.summary: This inscription is a simple genitive, likely indicating ownership or dedication by Domitius Crescens, possibly on a tomb or property.

EDCS-23800676.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to list freedmen, one of whom held the rank of Augustalis, possibly related to a burial or dedication.

EDCS-23800678.translation: A public road in common with Marcus Fundilius Melito.
EDCS-23800678.summary: This inscription records the shared use or maintenance of a public road in conjunction with Marcus Fundilius Melito.

EDCS-23800691.summary: A very fragmentary inscription that preserves parts of names, possibly Lucius and Salv[---].

EDCS-23800695.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that includes the names Gaius Sextilius and Longus, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-23800701.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely from a tomb inscription.

EDCS-23800707.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription that appears to contain personal names, possibly from a funerary context.

EDCS-23800715.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Venus made by Titus Pompeius Epitynchanus, with the location approved by local officials, likely from a public space.

EDCS-23800723.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely indicating a tomb inscription for Trebia.

EDCS-23800724.translation: Of Cornelia Anthi, freedwoman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-23800724.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely from a tomb inscription for Cornelia Anthi.

EDCS-23800725.translation: Of Quintus Lutatius Sosicenis, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-23800725.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely from a tomb inscription for Quintus Lutatius Sosicenis.

EDCS-23800726.translation: Of Lutatia Agathameris, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-23800726.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely from a tomb inscription for Lutatia Agathameris.

EDCS-23800727.summary: This is a fragmentary personal name, likely from a tomb inscription for Quintus Lutatius Felix.

EDCS-23800728.translation: Of Quintus Lutatius Eros Maioris, freedman of Quintus.

EDCS-23800730.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelia, daughter of Lucius, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800731.translation: Of Quintus Lutatius Eros, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-23800731.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Lutatius Eros, a freedman, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800734.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Publius Antonius Amaranto, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800735.translation: To Publius Trebius Monocordus, son of Publius.
EDCS-23800735.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Publius Trebius Monocordus, son of Publius, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800738.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lutatia Secunda, a freedwoman, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800739.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Lutatius Philargyrus, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800743.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly indicating a group of freedmen or a family, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800748.translation: To Titus Vestorius Pelops, freedman of Titus, for himself and for Vestoria Chryseis.
EDCS-23800748.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Vestorius Pelops, a freedman of Titus, and Vestoria Chryseis, likely dating from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-23800750.translation: To Jupiter, Flazus, Gaius Pomponius Xystus and Agon, according to their vow.
EDCS-23800750.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter, likely made by freedmen or slaves named Xystus and Agon, with a patron or master Gaius Pomponius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-23800751.translation: Sacred to the citizens of Cumae. Gaius Julius Primigenius gave this gift.
EDCS-23800751.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Julius Primigenius to the citizens of Cumae, likely a public gift during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23800754.translation: Augustales chosen, who contributed to the worship of the divine house. Patrons elected: Titus Vettulenus Nepos, Titus Vettulenus Nemesinianus, [Gaius?] Marcius Secundus, Gaius Marcius Polybius, Marcus Caecilius Quadratus, Titus Vettulenus Nemesinianus, son of Marcus Caecilius Quadratus, Lucius Lollius Hedylalus, son of Lucius Lollius Hedylalus, those with double status. Perpetual curator: Titus Vettulenus Pothus. The plebs: Vettulenus Rufus, Fufius Apollonius, Maetius Eucratus, Voltricius Restitutus, Licinius Restitutus, Vettulenus Hyginus, Varius Epaphroditus, Ulpius Felix, Marcius Apollinaris, Mallonius Epictetus, Pagnius Hesper, Aemilius Esychus. Ofellenius Posidonius, Ulpius Hodiernus, Curtius Epaphroditus, Lollius Victorinus, Accius Statutus, Carsidius Florianus, Carisius Favor, Fufius Eutyches, Lollius Strenio, Cassius Eubulus, Caecilius Eutychas, Herennius Galaticus, Aemilius Primitivos, Marcius Onesimus, Lucius Aemilius Alcibiades. Hermes, collector of the colonists, Arkarius; Vitalis, collector of the colonists, Arkarius; Felix, colonist. Lucius Lollius Augustianus, Osculenus Sosthenes, Lollius Martialis, Lollius Calocaerus, Pomponius Xystus, Lollius Hyginus, Lollius Eutyches. Quintus Varius Epaphroditus gave this gift.
EDCS-23800754.summary: This is a complex inscription recording the election of Augustales and patrons, likely associated with the imperial cult and local administration, possibly in Cumae given the previous inscription, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23800784.translation: To Hercules the Protector, guardian of the Gallonian house, Attius Sabinus, procurator of the Gallonii Nigri and Frontonis, made this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-23800784.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules by Attius Sabinus, a procurator for the Gallonii family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23900010.translation: Shop with a guardroom, monument of Gaius Fonteius C[...]

EDCS-23900034.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Clodia Blaste for her patron Marcus Clodius Philumenus and herself, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23900035.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Clodius Euretus made this for his dearest wife, Clodia Procla, who lived 28 years and 6 months, to one who deserved it well.
EDCS-23900035.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Clodius Euretus for his wife Clodia Procla, detailing her age at death and expressing his affection and esteem.

EDCS-23900037.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication by Quintus Cornelius.

EDCS-23900043.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. [For] Egrilia Spen, [from] her parents, for their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-23900043.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication from parents to their dutiful daughter, Egrilia Spen.

EDCS-23900056.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gargilius Urbanus [made this] for his well-deserving father, Marcus Gargilius Urbanus.
EDCS-23900056.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gargilius Urbanus for his father, Marcus Gargilius Urbanus.

EDCS-23900058.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely refers to a freedwoman and her patroness, Idaea.

EDCS-23900063.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Octavia, daughter of Lucius, lived 22 years. Lucius Licinius Probus, a beneficiary, [made this] for Junia Donata, his most dutiful mother. Obellia Celerina, with Lucius Licinius Probus, the beneficiary, acting as caretaker, lived 38 years. EDCS-23900063.summary: This complex funerary inscription honors multiple individuals, including Iulia Octavia, Lucius Licinius Probus (a beneficiary who appears twice), his mother Junia Donata, and potentially Obellia Celerina and Licinia Trophime, indicating familial and patronage relationships.

EDCS-23900066.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Aelius Pacatus and Lucius Sertorius Pollio, his heirs, made this for their well-deserving friend, Lucius Licinius Probus, the veteran.
EDCS-23900066.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the heirs of Lucius Licinius Probus, a veteran, honoring their friend.

EDCS-23900068.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Maia, freedwoman of Decor, and for Decorus the best freedman.
EDCS-23900068.summary: This is a funerary dedication honoring two freedpersons, Maia and Decorus, who were likely associated as patron and freedwoman or as a couple.

EDCS-23900069.translation: To Manlia Eutychia, his dearest wife, to one who deserved it well.
EDCS-23900069.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Manlia Eutychia by her husband, expressing his deep affection and esteem.

EDCS-23900071.translation: To Marcus Manlius Philargyrus, Manlia Thymele to her excellent husband.
EDCS-23900071.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Manlia Thymele to her husband Marcus Manlius Philargyrus.

EDCS-23900072.translation: Marcus Manlius Symphor made this for himself and his wife Mancia Symposia.
EDCS-23900072.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Manlius Symphor for himself and his wife Mancia Symposia.

EDCS-23900073.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Fabia Helpis made this for Marcia, aged 9, who deserved well.
EDCS-23900073.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Fabia Helpis for Marcia, a child aged 9.

EDCS-23900074.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Marrius Cerdo made this for his most dutiful son Lucius Marri Fortunatus, who lived 34 years, 4 months, and 4 days, and for his very dutiful freedwoman Marria Spei, who lived 22 years, 7 months, and 15 days. Fortunatus was a sevirus Augustalis.
EDCS-23900074.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Marrius Cerdo for his son Lucius Marri Fortunatus and his freedwoman Marria Spei, providing detailed ages and identifying the son as a sevirus Augustalis.

EDCS-24100210.translation: To Popillia Isias, daughter of Lucius. Lucius Popillius Nicia [made this].
EDCS-24100210.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Popillius Nicia to Popillia Isias, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-24100211.summary: This records a funerary dedication by Lucius Popilius Eupalaester for himself.

EDCS-24100212.summary: This funerary inscription records that Lucius Popilius Eupalaester made it, likely for himself or his family.

EDCS-24100213.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, a sacred offering. Lucius Popillius Eupalaester for himself, and for Popillia Isias, daughter of Lucius, and for his wife Popillia Isityche.
EDCS-24100213.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Popillius Eupalaester for himself, his daughter Popillia Isias, and his wife Popillia Isityche.

EDCS-24100214.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Popillius Eupalaester and Popillia Isityche made this for their dearest freedman Lucius Popillius Nicias.
EDCS-24100214.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Popillius Eupalaester and Popillia Isityche for their freedman Lucius Popillius Nicias.

EDCS-24100215.translation: Maximus and A Helena made this for their dearest Marcus Salinator VI, who lived 19 years, 10 months. For freedmen and freedwomen. In front [?], 20 feet in area.
EDCS-24100215.summary: This funerary dedication by Maximus and A Helena for Marcus Salinator VI, a freedman, includes dimensions and mentions other freedpersons.

EDCS-24100216.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Licinius Probus made this for his deserving wife Sempronia Rufina, daughter of Lucius. She lived 23 years.
EDCS-24100216.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his deceased wife, Lucius Licinius Probus to Sempronia Rufina, who died at age 23.

EDCS-24100217.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His sons and Veratius, his son-in-law, made this for Lucius Servilius Servilianus, a good man, who lived 66 years.
EDCS-24100217.summary: A funerary dedication by the sons and son-in-law for Lucius Servilius Servilianus, who died at age 66.

EDCS-24100218.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Titus Statilius Liberalis.
EDCS-24100218.summary: A brief funerary dedication for Titus Statilius Liberalis.

EDCS-24100219.translation: Lucius Terentius Lamper made this for his deserving wife Terentia Musa and for Lucius Terentius Venustus, his patron.
EDCS-24100219.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Terentius Lamper for his wife Terentia Musa and his patron Lucius Terentius Venustus.

EDCS-24100221.translation: Lucius Popillius Eupalaester to his friend Lucius Terentius Abascantus.
EDCS-24100221.summary: A dedication by Lucius Popillius Eupalaester to his friend Lucius Terentius Abascantus.

EDCS-24100226.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Ulpius Frontonus. His relatives made this.
EDCS-24100226.summary: A funerary dedication by relatives for Ulpius Frontonus.

EDCS-24100230.translation: Cha tata made [this] for [him/her/it] at age 10.

EDCS-24100235.translation: The freedman of this woman, Zo, the freedman of this woman, Secundus.

EDCS-24300017.translation: Amplus, a former student of Tibur.
EDCS-24300017.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Amplus, possibly referring to his origin or education in Tibur.

EDCS-24300034.translation: Titus Statilius Florus dedicated this offering to Jupiter Serapis.
EDCS-24300034.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Jupiter Serapis by Titus Statilius Florus.

EDCS-24300036.translation: Son of Marcus, to Jupiter Sol Serapis.
EDCS-24300036.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Sol Serapis, identifying the dedicator as the son of Marcus.

EDCS-24300038.translation: Lucius Arrius Eutyches rebuilt this for Serapis the Holy.
EDCS-24300038.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a structure by Lucius Arrius Eutyches for the god Serapis Sanctus.

EDCS-24300039.translation: Claudius Pompeius Rusticus Diocles, a grain-transporting soldier of the Third Gallic Legion, willingly restored this to Isis and the Genius of the dining hall, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-24300039.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Isis and the Genius of a dining hall, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-24300040.translation: The guild of the six, Marcus Iulius Crysophorus, quinquennial official, along with his son Aelianus, also called Sarapion, and Zosimus, and his son Philippus, made this offering, fulfilling a vow, to Jupiter Best and Greatest Serapis, the Capitoline deities, and the Castors.
EDCS-24300040.summary: This is a dedication made by a municipal official and members of his family to Jupiter and other deities, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24300041.translation: Our Lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, the August Emperors, ordered the temple and portico of the goddess Isis to be restored, under the supervision of Sempronius Faustus, a most distinguished man, the prefect of the grain supply.
EDCS-24300041.summary: This imperial rescript from the late 4th century CE orders the restoration of a temple and portico dedicated to Isis, overseen by an official.

EDCS-24300358.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly of officials or members of a group.

EDCS-24300359.translation: I ask you, make Gaius Gavía Rufus a duovir for dispensing justice.

EDCS-24300362.translation: I ask you to make Priscus aedile.

EDCS-24300380.translation: I ask you to make Cuspium Pansam aedile.

EDCS-24300382.translation: Aulus Suettius Certus, duovir for dispensing justice.

EDCS-24300386.translation: I ask you to make Licinius Faustus aedile and Gnaeus duovir for dispensing justice.
EDCS-24300386.summary: This inscription is a political appeal, likely from an election notice, asking voters to elect Licinius Faustus as aedile and Gnaeus as duovir for dispensing justice.

EDCS-24300395.translation: I ask you to make Gaius Gauius Rufus, duumvir with judicial power.

EDCS-24300396.translation: He wants Lucius Caecilius Capella as duumvir.

EDCS-24600346.summary: This inscription names Apsyrtus, identified as being from Laconia, with the word 'ubique' (everywhere), perhaps indicating his wide travels or ubiquitous presence.

EDCS-24600356.summary: This inscription identifies someone named Max as the 'Magister ludi,' or headmaster of a school.

EDCS-24600357.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a playful message or dedication, possibly by Callistus.

EDCS-24600358.summary: This is a personal name, Gaius T. Luxurius, likely an owner or subject of a monument or object.

EDCS-24600361.summary: This is a personal name, Gaius T. Luxurius, likely an owner or subject of a monument or object.

EDCS-24600369.summary: This is a personal greeting from Castalo, typical of informal inscriptions or letters.

EDCS-24600370.summary: This inscription appears to be a farewell message to Valeri, son of Marci.

EDCS-24600371.summary: This inscription seems to be a personal note or epitaph from Clodius, expressing a friendly sentiment.

EDCS-24600373.summary: This inscription, possibly related to a competition or a list, mentions Paris, girls, and a quantity of 10.

EDCS-24600377.summary: This is likely a personal name, Menedemerumenus, possibly an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-24600378.summary: This is likely a personal name, Menedemerumenus, possibly an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-24600381.translation: Atilius, one as. Atilius, one as. Atilius, one as.
EDCS-24600381.summary: This inscription records a repeated payment or accounting entry of one as by Atilius.

EDCS-24600382.translation: Albanus: one as. Agathemerus: two asses. Agathemerus: two asses. Agathemerus: one as. Acanthus: one semissis.
EDCS-24600382.summary: This inscription appears to record payments or transactions, possibly related to a list of individuals and amounts paid, with names like Albanus and Agathemerus mentioned.

EDCS-24600384.translation: Bread, two asses; seasoning, three asses; pot, one as; oil, one as; wine, one semissis; wine, one as; cheese, one semissis. On the eleventh day before the Kalends (of November?), I received one denarius. Pork, one as.
EDCS-24600384.summary: This is a list of provisions purchased and their costs in asses and denarii, with specific dates and items like bread, oil, wine, and pork.

EDCS-24600386.translation: Cuprionius Romulus in the sky of Mars rides.
EDCS-24600386.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedicatory or honorific text, possibly referring to an individual named Cuprionius Romulus who is associated with Mars and cavalry.

EDCS-24600389.translation: DD R Ata(vus) B SS S CX SS Asellam CXL
EDCS-24600389.summary: This inscription is highly abbreviated and difficult to interpret fully, but it may relate to land or property divisions, possibly mentioning 'Asellam' and a quantity of 'CXL'.

EDCS-24600392.summary: This inscription simply records two names, Macer and Gaius Popillius, possibly as a property marker or a record of ownership.

EDCS-24600397.summary: This inscription consists of a name, Rotundus, followed by repeated letters and abbreviations, which is difficult to interpret without further context.

EDCS-24600398.summary: This inscription records two names, Socius and Vervicius, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-24600399.translation: Menedemerumenus. Menedemerumenus. Menedemerumenus. Menedemerumenus. Menedemerumenus. Menedemerumenus.
EDCS-24600399.summary: This inscription consists of the repeated name Menedemerumenus, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication by this individual multiple times.

EDCS-24600402.summary: This is a short inscription wishing good luck to someone named Fausto.

EDCS-24600404.summary: This inscription appears to be a greeting or farewell, mentioning 'Iris' and 'Acanthus', with a possible reference to a large distance and good wishes.

EDCS-24600410.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Bruttidius Statius.

EDCS-24600411.translation: Ven[i]vit came / mul(i)eri for the woman / D(ecimi) Lucreti Vale(ntis) of Decimus Lucretius Valentis / Onus(tus) the eques (cavalryman) / r(ationis) of the account / Saga / thr(aex) Thracian / m(urmillo) murmillo / I I / XX 20.
EDCS-24600411.summary: This inscription likely records a gladiatorial match or event, mentioning a woman, Decimus Lucretius Valentis, and gladiators with their types and possibly a score.

EDCS-24600412.summary: This is a farewell inscription for Mulierianus, possibly mentioning Aullus.

EDCS-24600414.summary: This inscription identifies Voconius Pacatus as a vexillarius (standard-bearer).

EDCS-24600415.summary: This is a farewell inscription for Matrona.

EDCS-24600419.translation: Urbanus fought here on the sixth day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-24600419.summary: This inscription records a gladiatorial event involving Urbanus on December 7th.

EDCS-24600421.summary: This is a dedication to Publius (?) Postumius Quietus.

EDCS-24600425.summary: This is a dedication to Ancharius and Linia.

EDCS-24600428.translation: Anus remembers the life of Aquitus, weary of death.
EDCS-24600428.summary: This inscription is a memorial by Anus for Aquitus, reflecting on life and death.

EDCS-24600430.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple mention or epitaph for someone named Quadratus, possibly repeated for emphasis.

EDCS-24600435.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Albanius Communis Aurelius Nonus.

EDCS-24600437.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a person named Primus.

EDCS-24600439.translation: Publius Propesicuntus Verpa, if you read this, you are not, by scribal law.
EDCS-24600439.summary: This is a playful or possibly critical inscription, possibly for a scribe named Publius Propesicuntus Verpa.

EDCS-24600441.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Chloe.

EDCS-24600444.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Aristo, a barber.

EDCS-24600445.translation: Eumacia, you will be well, farewell.
EDCS-24600445.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Eumacia.

EDCS-24600446.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Manius Aemilius.

EDCS-24600447.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sautranus.

EDCS-24600448.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sautranus.

EDCS-24600453.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Junius, who is described as poor.

EDCS-24600454.translation: My thousand were wandering among the Sicilians.
EDCS-24600454.summary: This is a personal inscription, possibly a verse epitaph or a playful remark, whose exact meaning is obscure due to its brevity.

EDCS-24600455.translation: Marcus Atillius made this post here.
EDCS-24600455.summary: This inscription records the construction of a post or marker by Marcus Atillius.

EDCS-24600456.summary: This is a short farewell message to Chloe.

EDCS-24600458.summary: This inscription is a label, possibly on a tomb or a personal item, identifying Iucundus with a derogatory term.

EDCS-24600459.summary: This is a personal greeting, likely from a lover or husband, sending good wishes to Lucida.

EDCS-24600460.summary: This inscription appears to be a curse or a malediction from Auctillus to Atilius Casellus.

EDCS-24600462.summary: This is a name and title, likely identifying Lucius Lollius as an imperial agent or manager.

EDCS-24600468.summary: This is a personal greeting from Nauplius to Clappus.

EDCS-24600469.summary: This inscription is a dedication or invocation, possibly to the sea god Oceanus.

EDCS-24600474.translation: Modestus to his Muse, Modestus, Modestus.
EDCS-24600474.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal dedication or expression of affection from Modestus to his 'Muse', possibly his wife or a beloved.

EDCS-24600482.summary: This inscription is a simple name, Lucius Atilius, likely a personal name or a dedication.

EDCS-24600486.translation: Number of centuries. Decimus Iulius Thraso, Sage(n)ius, Coc(c)us, Fabio, Publius Iulius Trifolius. Of Caius Flavius the scribes. Of Caius Flavius the scribes' house. The land bought for eight and a half (asses).
EDCS-24600486.summary: This inscription seems to record the sale or acquisition of land by or for a group of scribes belonging to Caius Flavius and Titus Lollius, with names like Decimus Iulius Thraso and others mentioned. It likely dates to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-24600496.summary: This inscription is a personal name, Titus Cominius, possibly a dedication or owner's mark.

EDCS-24600499.summary: This inscription is a personal name, Marcus Cerrinius, likely a name on a monument or property.

EDCS-24600500.translation: Pacatus remained here with his people in Pompeii.
EDCS-24600500.summary: This inscription records that Pacatus lived in Pompeii with his family or household, suggesting a private dwelling or memorial.

EDCS-24600508.translation: Quintus Caecilius, Quintus Caecilius, Lucius Caecilius
EDCS-24600508.summary: This inscription lists three names from the Caecilius family, likely indicating ownership or a family memorial.

EDCS-24600509.summary: This is a fragment of a word, 'Whoever', likely part of a longer legal or dedicatory text.

EDCS-24600513.summary: This inscription repeats the name 'Leon' four times, possibly indicating multiple individuals or a playful inscription.

EDCS-24600515.summary: This inscription is a personal name, Gaius Lucianus, possibly a dedication or owner's mark.

EDCS-24600521.translation: Lucilius sends greetings to his Lucida everywhere.
EDCS-24600521.summary: This inscription is a personal message from Lucilius to his beloved Lucida, conveying greetings, likely from a tomb or personal item.

EDCS-24600525.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mopsus Krus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-24600530.translation: Lucius Acutius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, magistrate.
EDCS-24600530.summary: This inscription records Lucius Acutius Rufus, a magistrate from the Voltinia tribe, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-24600775.translation: To the departed spirits of Combarissia.
EDCS-24600775.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the household gods for Combarissia.

EDCS-24600778.translation: To the departed spirits, Obellius Trophimus for his excellent friend Aulus Egilius Thallus, VIvir Augustalis and quinquennalis.
EDCS-24600778.summary: This funerary inscription honors Aulus Egilius Thallus, a VIvir Augustalis and quinquennalis, by his friend Obellius Trophimus.

EDCS-24600781.translation: From the estates of Statilius Maximus Severus Hadrianus, from the workshop of Myrinus, during the consulship of Squilla and Titianus.
EDCS-24600781.summary: This inscription indicates goods produced at the workshop of Myrinus from the estates of Statilius Maximus Severus Hadrianus, dated by the consuls Squilla and Titianus.

EDCS-24600782.translation: From the pottery workshops of the Caninii family, of Titus Greius Ianus. May he who made it prosper.
EDCS-24600782.summary: This inscription records pottery from the Caninii workshops belonging to Titus Greius Ianus, with a wish for his prosperity.

EDCS-24600795.translation: Publius Cassius and Gaius Lusidius Adiutor.
EDCS-24600795.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, Publius Cassius and Gaius Lusidius Adiutor, possibly in a business or ownership context.

EDCS-24600797.translation: Marcus M.V. made this from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudentis, during the consulship of Titus Atilius Titus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus.
EDCS-24600797.summary: This inscription records that Marcus M.V. produced an item from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudentis, dated by the consuls Titus Atilius Titus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus.

EDCS-24600799.translation: From the larger workshops of Oceanus, of our Emperor Caesar, a terracotta work by Quintus Perusius Pudentis.
EDCS-24600799.summary: This inscription indicates a terracotta product from the workshops of Oceanus, associated with the emperor, made by Quintus Perusius Pudentis.

EDCS-24600800.translation: From the workshops of Sempronius Mamertinus and Septimianus.
EDCS-24600800.summary: This inscription identifies goods originating from the workshops of Sempronius Mamertinus and Septimianus, likely of pottery.

EDCS-24600802.summary: This inscription names the consuls Sulpicius.

EDCS-24600811.summary: This inscription records a dedication by or to Tiberius Claudius Sabinus.

EDCS-24600814.summary: This inscription records a dedication by or to Gaius Plaetorius Crassus.

EDCS-24600815.translation: Under the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus, from the estates of Claudia Marcellina.
EDCS-24600815.summary: This inscription records goods or activities originating from Claudia Marcellina's estates during the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus.

EDCS-24600816.translation: Of T. Ravi Trophimus, under the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-24600816.summary: This inscription records the name of T. Ravi Trophimus, likely an official or donor, during the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-24600817.translation: From the estates of Stertiniana Bassula, workshop of Claudius Fortunatus.
EDCS-24600817.summary: This inscription indicates a connection between the estates of Stertiniana Bassula and the workshop of Claudius Fortunatus, possibly related to production or distribution.

EDCS-24600818.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Cornelius Natalis.

EDCS-24600820.summary: This inscription records a dedication by or to Marcus Antistius Vitalis.

EDCS-24600822.translation: From the workshop of Marcus Cornelius Valerianus.
EDCS-24600822.summary: This inscription indicates that something originates from the workshop of Marcus Cornelius Valerianus.

EDCS-24600830.translation: The Cassani and Crissani command all [power].
EDCS-24600830.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a political statement or decree, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24600853.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or an epitaph, mentioning the name Pompeianus, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24600871.translation: Having completed all the offices held by Lorianus.
EDCS-24600871.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that seems to refer to the completion of public offices by an individual named Lorianus, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700005.translation: Epicadus, son of Quintus; Annius, freedman of Quintus; Fe; Publius Bivellius, freedman of Titus; Publius Messius, freedman of Quintus; Caius Lusius, freedman of Caius; Publius Ovius, freedman of Publius; Plutus, freedman of Caius; Antonius, freedman of Caius; these magistrates, with the women, made the tribunal, the cunium, and the games, during the consulship of [---].
EDCS-24700005.summary: This inscription records the performance of public duties and games by a group of magistrates and freedmen, likely in the region of Campania, given the mention of 'cunium', during an unspecified consular year.

EDCS-24700006.translation: From the workshop of Lucius Canoleius.
EDCS-24700006.summary: This is a short inscription indicating ownership or origin from the workshop of Lucius Canoleius, likely a craftsman or merchant, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700007.translation: Papius, freedman of Papius; Stepanus, freedman of Marcus; Diogenes, freedman of Titinia; Antiocus, freedman of Lucius; Copio, freedman of Lucius; Nicolavos, freedman of Aulus; Demetrius; Aulus Vibius, freedman of Aulus; Diogenes, freedman of Quintus; Cleo; Publius Fufius, freedman of Publius; Chaeremo; Caius Arotrius, freedman of Artoria; Dipilus; Marcus Alfidius, freedman of Marcus; Sota; Publius Statius, freedman of Publius; Philemo; these magistrates supervised the construction of the lake for Jupiter from the temple treasury and from their own funds, during the second consulship of Gnaeus Papirius Carbo.
EDCS-24700007.summary: This inscription records a group of magistrates who financed and oversaw the construction of a lake for Jupiter, likely in Ostia or a nearby region, during the second consulship of Gnaeus Papirius Carbo (likely 200 BC).

EDCS-24700008.translation: Quintus Sattius, Quintus Minatius, Lucius Opimius, Caius Fabius, Publius Ofellius, Marcus Fulmonius; these magistrates administered the gardens and the court, and the porticoes and royal [buildings] for them, and for Hercules, from their own funds.
EDCS-24700008.summary: This inscription records a group of magistrates who managed public gardens, a court, and porticoes, possibly in a municipal context, and made dedications to Hercules, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700023.summary: This is a simple personal inscription, likely an epitaph or a dedication, identifying Publius Saufeius, son of Mucianus, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700024.translation: The magistrates of the bearers of burdens oversaw: Diogenes, slave of Cordius Numerius; Licinus, slave of Caius Orcivius; Artemo, slave of Magulnus; Flaccus, slave of Fabia.
EDCS-24700024.summary: This inscription records the magistrates of a guild of porters or heavy laborers, listing several enslaved individuals who served in some capacity, possibly as overseers or members, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700028.summary: This is a simple personal inscription, likely an epitaph or a dedication, identifying Anicia, daughter of Sertor, from an unknown location and date.

EDCS-24700029.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Dindia Plautia as the wife of Caius.

EDCS-24700030.translation: Caius Saufeius, son of Caius Sabinus, and Caius Orcevius, son of Marcus, censors, approved these altars for Juno Palostcaria.
EDCS-24700030.summary: This inscription records the approval of altars by two censors, Caius Saufeius and Caius Orcevius, dedicated to Juno Palostcaria.

EDCS-24700032.translation: The Guild of Fullers: Caius Numitorius, freedman of Caius; Publius Ceccius Quintus; Etrilius Antipo; Silucus, slave of Oppius son of Lucius; Touriscus; slave of Cordius son of Marcus.
EDCS-24700032.summary: This is a list of individuals, likely members or officials of the Guild of Fullers, with some identifying their status as freedmen or slaves.

EDCS-24700037.translation: Aulus Livius, son of Aulus, and Lucius Acilius, son of Lucius, as aediles, granted the site.
EDCS-24700037.summary: This inscription records the granting of a site by two aediles, Aulus Livius and Lucius Acilius.

EDCS-24700038.translation: During the second dictatorship of Gaius Julius Caesar and the magistracy of the equestrian Marcus Antonius, the magistrates of the district and intersections, Marcus Blattius, son of Marcus, Marcus Cerrinius, son of Marcus, Marcus Sepullius, Quintus Pra..., Gaius Cornelius..., Publius Rocius..., Salvius... servant of Marcus. During the consulship of Gaius Caesar and Marcus Lepidus, Blattius, son of Marcus, Gaius Hermatorius(?), son of Publius, Marcus...ius, son of Marcus, Plutus, Marcus Stronnius Nic... freedman of Marcus, Marcus Oppius Aes... freedman of Sextus, Gaius Cepidius... freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-24700038.summary: This inscription lists officials and magistracies, including dictator and magister equitum, and likely records the dedication of a public work or a boundary marker, possibly from the late Republican period.

EDCS-24700040.translation: Protemus, freedman of Caius; Dama, freedman of Caius Marcius; the magistri supervised the construction. From the college's decision, they contributed to the construction and connection of a shrine and a small surrounding structure: Lucius Abbius Pilemo, freedman of Lucius; Publius Raecius Protemus, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Ceius Pusio, son of Marcus; Quintus Caecilius Pilotimus, freedman of the Quintorum; Caius Maneius Doroteus, freedman of Caius; Caius Caecilius Pilotimus, freedman of Decimus; Publius Marcius Cimber, freedman of Sextus; Nico.
EDCS-24700040.summary: This inscription records the construction of a shrine and surrounding structure, funded by contributions from various members and freedmen of a collegium, with the magistri overseeing the work.

EDCS-24700054.translation: Quintus Aulus, son of Aidicius of Quintus, and Titus Rebinius, son of Quintus, as aediles, for the market tax.
EDCS-24700054.summary: This inscription records the action of two aediles, Quintus Aulus and Titus Rebinius, in relation to market taxes.

EDCS-24700055.translation: Publius Fourius, dictator for the third time, dedicates this to Hercules, during the consulship of Severus and Antoninus Augustus (likely Caracalla and Geta), for the 6th cohort of vigiles.
EDCS-24700055.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Hercules by Publius Fourius, who held the position of dictator for the third time, and relates to the 6th cohort of vigiles during the consulship of Severus and Antoninus.

EDCS-24700056.translation: Lucius Octavius dedicated this to Hercules.
EDCS-24700056.summary: This is a dedication of an object or place to Hercules by Lucius Octavius.

EDCS-24700059.translation: The custodians of the temple of Castor and Pollux, by decree of the decurions, Manius Avillius Stabilio, freedman of a woman; Publius Anicius, freedman of Publius; Publius Furius, freedman of Publius; Decimus Plaetorius, freedman of Decimus; Caius Volcacius, freedman of Caius, as magistri, supervised its construction.
EDCS-24700059.summary: This inscription records the construction or maintenance of the temple of Castor and Pollux, overseen by magistri who were freedmen, following a decree of the local council (decurions).

EDCS-24700062.translation: Lucius Harines Heri, Marcus Marcus Aturius, Caius Eburis, Pomponius Marcus, Caedicius son of Marcus, Numerius Andripius son of Numerius, Pussolus, Osu, may the gates be straight, may it be as if it were Oulus.
EDCS-24700062.summary: This inscription appears to be a private dedication or charm, possibly related to warding or good fortune, with a list of names and a cryptic phrase.

EDCS-24700114.translation: Caius Carulios, son of Caius Marica, dedicated this.
EDCS-24700114.summary: This is a short dedication inscription recording Caius Carulios dedicating something, likely a monument or offering.

EDCS-24700135.translation: Dionisius willingly gave this gift to Hercules as he deserved.
EDCS-24700135.summary: This is a votive inscription where Dionisius dedicates a gift to Hercules.

EDCS-24700152.translation: Whoever sends this to me, Kavios Monios Qetios, a gift for his son.
EDCS-24700152.summary: This inscription is a dedication of a gift, possibly a tombstone, by Kavios Monios Qetios for his son.

EDCS-24700174.translation: Caius Sulpicius, freedman of Caius; Statius, slave of Clodius; Statius, slave of Anti; Pamphilus, slave of Carisius; Publius Hirrius, freedman of Publius; Philocles, slave of Licovius; Dama, slave of Cervius; Marcus Vitulanius, freedman of Marcus; Hilarus, slave of Epidius; Zetus, slave of Rahi; Barnaeus, slave of Pescenius.
EDCS-24700174.summary: This inscription lists various freedmen and slaves, possibly associated with a single household or group, likely serving as a communal epitaph or record.

EDCS-24700175.translation: Verna, freedwoman of Plotia; Helena, slave of Salvius Statius; Helenion, slave of Statius; Philete, freedwoman of Laelia; Nice, freedwoman of Pomponia; Callipolis, slave of Morasia; Sabidia, freedwoman of Lucius; Salvia Secunda, slave of Naevia; Veturia, freedwoman of Caius; Timotea, slave of Geminius; Mindia, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-24700175.summary: This inscription lists several freedwomen and female slaves, likely forming a group within a household or community, perhaps as an epitaph.

EDCS-24700176.translation: Apollonius, slave of Carisius; Caius Arrius, freedman of Caius; Apella; Menander, slave of Trebius Quintus; Caius, slave of Lucius; Ascla, slave of Sepunius Marcius; Pamphilus, slave of Plotus; Phileros, slave of Apuleius; Sabdas, slave of Aeficius Marcius; Caius Rammius, freedman of Caius; Buccio, slave of Morasius; Zethus, slave of Rahius; Phileros, slave of Tuccius Marcius; Theudorus, slave of Camidius; during the consulship of Lucius Manlius and Lucius Aurelius.
EDCS-24700176.summary: This inscription lists numerous slaves and freedmen, concluding with a consular dating, suggesting it might record a group's activities or a communal benefaction during that specific year.

EDCS-24700177.translation: Sosander, slave of Pomponius Quintus; Menander, slave of Cornelius Lucius; Philargurus, slave of Eppius Caius; Caius Eppius, freedman of the Caiorians; Diodotus; Stephanus, slave of the picarii (tanners/pitch-makers) and associates; Hermogenes, slave of Trebius Caius Lucius; Protogenes, slave of Rocius Lucius; Philargurus, slave of Titinius Publius; Chario, slave of Acerratius Quintus; Philargurus, slave of Acerratius Quintus; Lucius Titinius, freedman of Marcius; Malchion; Chrusippus, slave of Silvius Aulus.
EDCS-24700177.summary: This inscription details a complex network of slaves and freedmen, including members of specific trades (picarii), possibly related to a collegium or a business association.

EDCS-24700178.translation: The duovirs dedicate these magistracyl offices to Venus. Tertia Domatia, daughter of Spurius; Alfia, freedwoman of Mulier; Flora, freedwoman of Cahia; Astaphium; Dosithea, slave of Calidus Numerius; Stolia, slave of Minidia Lucius; Allenia, freedwoman; Salvia Co, freedwoman of Marcius; Creusa Secundassia; Pal... Co Ca...
EDCS-24700178.summary: This inscription records the dedication of magistracies to Venus by duovirs, followed by a list of women, likely including priestesses or members of a cultic group, possibly from the early imperial period.

EDCS-24700179.translation: Furia, freedwoman of Mulier; Thelete; Allenia, freedwoman of Caius; Psycharium; Rufa, slave of Seius; Laelia, freedwoman of Mulier; Lampyris; Acte, slave of Lufinus Manius; Cila, slave of Maecia; Thais, slave of Vibius; Murtis, slave of Helvius Lucius; Metilia, freedwoman of Mulier; Acte, slave of Paccius; Silia, freedwoman of Marcius; Rufa.
EDCS-24700179.summary: This inscription lists a series of freedwomen and slaves, possibly forming a group or association, perhaps serving as an epitaph for its members.

EDCS-24700180.translation: Philargurus, slave of Pistus Gemini; Stabilio, slave of Licovius; Salvius, slave of Trebius; Alexander, slave of Caecilius; Philargurus, slave of Rustius; Chilo, slave of Lucius Clodius Publicus; Lucius, freedman of Helvidius Lucius; and Philomusus, slave of Quintus, gave theatrical performances.
EDCS-24700180.summary: This inscription records a dedication of theatrical performances by several freedmen and slaves.

EDCS-24700181.translation: Antiochus, slave of Pullus Quintus; Bacchides, slave of Paccius Marcus; Seleucus, slave of Marcus Aurelius Marci; Philinus, slave of Caius Cosconius; Philocles, slave of Furius Numerius; Philomusus, slave of Caius Lucius; Gorgia, slave of Caius Allenius; Alexander, slave of Marcus Antonius; Barnaeus, slave of Aulus Morasius; Deiphilus, slave of Publicus Caius Curtilius Titinius; and Sosia, slave of Marcus Badius, give this gift to the Spei (Hope).
EDCS-24700181.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a gift to the deity Spei (Hope) by various slaves, likely in a collegial context.

EDCS-28300260.translation: Peace. Here is placed Flaes the Hebrew.

EDCS-30100387.translation: From the Brutiana estate of Vismatius Felix, from the estates of Rutilius Lupus.
EDCS-30100387.summary: This inscription relates to the Brutiana estate belonging to Vismatius Felix and indicates a connection to the estates of Rutilius Lupus.

EDCS-30200017.translation: Caepioniana, from the estates of Marcus Lucifer, belonging to Plotia Isaurica.
EDCS-30200017.summary: This inscription names the Caepioniana estate, its owner Marcus Lucifer, and its association with Plotia Isaurica.

EDCS-30200018.translation: Caepioniana, from the potteries of Lucius Gellus Prudentis, belonging to Plotia Isaurica.
EDCS-30200018.summary: This inscription identifies the Caepioniana estate, pottery from Lucius Gellus Prudentis, and its ownership by Plotia Isaurica.

EDCS-30200019.translation: Brickworks from the estates of Aurelius Caesar and Faustina Publica his wife.
EDCS-30200019.summary: This inscription records the origin of brickworks belonging to imperial properties, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30200020.translation: From the estates of Titus Statilius Maximus Severus, Brutiana, from the workshop of Myrinus.
EDCS-30200020.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of goods from the estates of Titus Statilius Maximus Severus, specifying a workshop, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30200022.summary: This inscription identifies a product or property belonging to Sextus Vismatius Neritus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30200045.summary: This inscription is a simple name, possibly identifying an owner or commissioner of a work, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30200057.translation: Ummidia Quadratilla, daughter of Gaius, and Asconia Secunda.
EDCS-30200057.summary: This inscription appears to list two individuals, Ummidia Quadratilla and Asconia Secunda, possibly related to property or a tomb, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30200479.translation: To Ulpia Euhodia, his excellent wife, by Titus Flavius Delphicus, freedman of the emperor, scribe in charge of accounts, procurator of the treasury of inheritances for the Alexandrian fiscus.
EDCS-30200479.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Ulpia Euhodia by her husband Titus Flavius Delphicus, who held significant financial and administrative positions, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-30300610.translation: 520 sesterces for a mule sold. Marcus Cerrinius Euphrates declares that he received this money, which Marcus Cerrinius, son of Marcus, freedman, Euphrates, has declared he received in full from Philadelphus, slave of Lucius Caecilius Felix. Done at Pompeii on the 7th day before the Kalends of June, when Drusus Caesar and Gaius Norbanus Flaccus were consuls.
EDCS-30300610.summary: This inscription is a financial record detailing a sale and the subsequent acknowledgment of payment, dated to 23 CE.

EDCS-30300611.translation: Receipt for 1300 sesterces which came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Marcus Alleius Carpus on the first Ides of December. Marcus Alleius Carpus declared that he had received less merchandise than accounted for from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus. Done at Pompeii on the 7th day before the Kalends of December, when Lucius Calpurnius and Marcus Licinius were consuls.
EDCS-30300611.summary: This inscription is a financial record related to an auction sale involving Lucius Caecilius Iucundus and Marcus Alleius Carpus, dated to 24 CE.

EDCS-30300612.translation: 1185 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of boxwood belonging to Gaius Julius Onesimus on the first Ides of July. Gaius Julius Onesimus declared that he had received less payment than accounted for from Marcus Fabius Agathinus, in the name of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus. Done at Pompeii on the 6th day before the Ides of May, when Manius Acilius Aviola and Marcus Asinius Marcellus were consuls.
EDCS-30300612.summary: This inscription is a financial record concerning an auction of boxwood by Gaius Julius Onesimus, handled through Lucius Caecilius Iucundus and Marcus Fabius Agathinus, dated to 54 CE.

EDCS-30300614.translation: Receipt for 11,039 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Umbricia Ianuaria. Umbricia Ianuaria declared that she had received less merchandise than accounted for from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus. Done at Pompeii the day before the Ides of December, when Lucius Duvius and Publius Clodius were consuls. I, Decimus Volcius Thallus, wrote at the request of Umbricia Ianuaria that she received from Caecilius Iucundus 11,039 sesterces from her auction, with less merchandise, following an examination of the signed tablets. Done at Pompeii.
EDCS-30300614.summary: This inscription is a financial record documenting a payment and receipt for an auction involving Umbricia Ianuaria and Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, dated to 53 CE.

EDCS-30300615.translation: Marcus Fabius Secundus stated that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 10,305 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Marcus Fabius Secundus, with the commission less than paid; it was enacted at Pompeii on the Ides of January in the second consulship of Nero Caesar and Lucius Calpurnius Piso, witnessed by Cn. Vibrius Callistus, M. Fabius Diadumenus, N. Veius Martialis, N. Nerius Hyginus, A. Messius Pronimus, N. Popidius Sodalio, M. Fabius Secundus, M. Ve[---], He[---].
EDCS-30300615.summary: This is a record of a debt payment of 10,305 sesterces related to an auction, enacted at Pompeii during the consulship of Nero and Calpurnius Piso.

EDCS-30300616.translation: Record concerning Cnaeus Alleius Chryserotus for 3,341 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Cnaeus Alleius Chryserotus, with the commission less than paid. Cnaeus Alleius Chryseros stated that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 3,341 sesterces, enacted at Pompeii on the Nones of August in the second consulship of Nero Caesar and Lucius Calpurnius, at the request and by the order of Cnaeus Alleius Chryserotus, witnessed by L. Laelius Fuscus, M. Fabius Atticus, A. Veius, P. Terentius Primus, L. Vettius Valentis, C. Poppaeus Fortis, T. Caudius Secundus, A. Fuscus, C. Alleius Chryserotus; enacted at Pompeii on the Nones of August, it was written by order and mandate of Cnaeus Alleius Chryserotus that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 3,341 sesterces for his auction, from the examination of the tablets, for the Ides of February. Enacted at Pompeii.
EDCS-30300616.summary: This document records a financial transaction of 3,341 sesterces related to an auction, enacted at Pompeii during the consulship of Nero and Calpurnius.

EDCS-30300617.translation: 8,662 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Tullia Lampyris, with the commission less than paid. Tullia Lampyris stated that she had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 8,000 and 662 sesterces, enacted at Pompeii on the 10th day before the Kalends of January in the second consulship of Nero Caesar and Lucius Caelsius Martialis, witnessed by L. Vedius Ceratus, A. Caecilius Philologus, Cn. Helvius Apollon, M. Stablus(?) Chryseros, D. Volcius Thallus, Sex. Pompeius Axiochus, P. Sextius Primus, C. Vibius Alcemus; enacted at Pompeii in the second consulship of Nero Caesar and Lucius Caelsius Martialis on the 10th day before the Kalends of January. Sextus Pompeius Axiochus wrote at the request of Tullia Lampyris that she had received 8,000 and 662 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for her auction, from the examination of the signed tablets.
EDCS-30300617.summary: This inscription records a payment of 8,662 sesterces related to the auction of Tullia Lampyris, enacted at Pompeii during the consulship of Nero and Caelsius Martialis.

EDCS-30300618.translation: Record concerning Marcus Atrius Marcellus for 35,270 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Marcus Atrius Marcellus, with the commission less than paid. Marcus Atrius Marcellus stated that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 35,270 sesterces, enacted at Pompeii on the 15th day before the Kalends of October in the second consulship of Nero Caesar and Lucius Caelsius, witnessed by Marcus Atrius Marcellus, Numerius Popidius Narcissus, Marcus Fabius Euporus, Marcus Volusius Faustus, Lucius Cornelius Primogenis, Numerius Herennius Ianuarius, Marcus Epidius Pagurus, Lucius Melissaeus Atimetus, Marcus Ubo Cogitatus, Eutactus Felicio.
EDCS-30300618.summary: This inscription details a financial transaction of 35,270 sesterces concerning the auction of Marcus Atrius Marcellus, enacted at Pompeii during the consulship of Nero and Caelsius.

EDCS-30300619.translation: Record concerning Caprasius Zoenus, Titus Terentius Felix, Publius Pomponius Marcellus, Marcus Fabius Philocalus, Titus Terentius Maximus, Gaius Numitorius Anthus, Gaius Numitorius Iason, Numerius Popidius Olynthus, Numerius Popidius Felicionis, Decimus Caprasius Thi.
EDCS-30300619.summary: This is a list of names, likely witnesses or participants in a transaction, possibly related to an auction.

EDCS-30300620.translation: Record concerning Marcus Epidius Pelops, Cnaeus Alleius Logus, Numerius Popidius Ampliatus, Aulus Messius Pronimus, Venus, Marcus Epidius Pelops, Marcus Helvius Princeps, Aulus Tetteius Festus, Marcus Lucretius Epicadus, Marcus Fabius Secundus.
EDCS-30300620.summary: This inscription lists individuals, likely witnesses or participants in a transaction, possibly related to an auction.

EDCS-30300621.translation: Record concerning Lucius Loppius Proculus, Lucius Seius Rufus, Gaius Gavi Firmus, Gaius Gavi Rufus, Marcus Ni Mar Is, Gaius Iulius Memor, Publius Aefulanius Chrysanthus, Marcus Epidius Bucolus, Lucius Loppius Proculus, Lucius Iunius Corinthus.
EDCS-30300621.summary: This inscription lists names, potentially witnesses or participants in a financial transaction.

EDCS-30300622.translation: Record concerning Mancia Daphnis, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Marcus Fabius Euporus, Sextus Helvius Scamander, Caius or Caius Vibius Palepatus, Lucius Sextilius Abascantus, Lucius Septumius Phontis, Gaius Fundilius Primionis, Lucius Thermus Secundus.
EDCS-30300622.summary: This inscription lists names, likely witnesses or participants in a financial transaction.

EDCS-30300623.translation: Record concerning Melissaia, Quintus Poppaeus Felix, Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, Lucius Magulnus Donatus, Publius Caelis Primogenis, Marcus Stlaborius Nymphodotus, Quintus Poppaeus Soricis, Aulus Herennuleius, Marcus Lucretius Th.
EDCS-30300623.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly indicating participants or witnesses in a financial transaction.

EDCS-30300624.translation: Record of an auction of linen goods concerning Ptolemeus, son of Masyllus, the Alexandrian, Ptolemeus, son of Masyllus, the Alexandrian, Marcus Tettius Rufus, Sextus Pompeius Epaphus, Gaius Arrius Amarantius, Numerius Popidius Sodalio, di ni is santi sodi.
EDCS-30300624.summary: This inscription records an auction of linen goods and names the seller or principal and possibly witnesses.

EDCS-30300625.translation: Record of Marcus Fuficius Fuscus, Aulus Fuficius Certus, Gaius Atullius Evander, Gnaeus Helvius Aprilis, Publius Terentius Primus, Marcus Epidius Urbanus, Marcus Urbanus H., Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus.
EDCS-30300625.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely a financial record or a list of contributors, possibly dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-30300626.translation: Handwritten note. Salvius, slave of the heirs of Numerius Nasennius Nigidius Vaccula, I, have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus three thousand and fifty-nine sestertii in coins for my auction. I have received them in full, as I wished, from him up to this day. Done in Pompeii. Witnessed by Salvius, slave of the heirs of Vaccula; Lucius Aelius Turbonis; Publius Velius Primus, slave of the heirs of Vaccula; Turbonis; Velius Primus.
EDCS-30300626.summary: This is a receipt for a payment of 3059 sestertii received from the banker Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction, dated to the consulship of Acilius Aviola and Asinius, likely in the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-30300628.translation: Record of Marcus Alleius Carpus. Quintus Volusius Saturninus and Publius Cornelius Scipio, consuls. On the 24th day before the Kalends of July. Marcus Alleius Carpus, I, have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus one thousand three hundred and eighty-six sestertii for my auction. Done in Pompeii. Witnessed by Marcus Alleius Carpus; Marcus Alleius Carpus; Marcus Alleius Carpus; Marcus Alleius Carpus. Quintus Volusius Saturninus and Publius Cornelius, consuls. On the 24th day before the Kalends of July. Marcus Alleius Carpus, I, have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 1386 sestertii for my auction, under his stipulation. Done in Pompeii.
EDCS-30300628.summary: This inscription is a record of Marcus Alleius Carpus receiving 1386 sestertii from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction, dated to the consulship of Volusius Saturninus and Cornelius Scipio, likely in the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-30300630.translation: Record of Trophimus. Lucius Duvius Avitus and Publius Clodius, consuls. On the 4th day before the Ides of December. Marcus Helvius Catullus, I have written that Umbricia Antiochidis received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 6252 sestertii for the auction of her slave Trophimus, paid less the fee. Done in Pompeii. Witnessed by Marcus Helvius Catullus; Melissa Fusci; Fabius Proculus; Umbricia Antiochidis; Catullus. Lucius Duvius Avitus and Publius Clodius, consuls. On the 4th day before the Ides of December. Marcus Helvius Catullus, I have written that Umbricia received from Iucundus 6252 sestertii for the auction of her slave Trophimus, paid less the fee. Done in Pompeii.
EDCS-30300630.summary: This inscription records Umbricia Antiochidis receiving 6252 sestertii from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of her slave Trophimus, dated to the consulship of Duvius Avitus and Clodius, likely in the mid-1st century AD.

EDCS-30300633.translation: Record of the denarii of Turdus on the Ides of November. Gnaeus Polus Turdus, Marcus Fabius Thelus, Marcus Fabius Euporus, Marcus Clodius Ampliatus, Gnaeus Polus Turdus.
EDCS-30300633.summary: This inscription lists names and a date (Ides of November), likely pertaining to a financial transaction or a list of debtors/creditors.

EDCS-30300634.translation: Handwritten note of Vesbinus Vibidius Veranus, Vesbinus Vibidius Veranus, Mu Vibidius Veranus, Vibidius Veranus, Vesbinus Vibidius Veranus.
EDCS-30300634.summary: This inscription is a list of repetitive names, likely a record of individuals associated with a specific entity or transaction.

EDCS-30300635.translation: Quintus Coelius Caltilus Iustus and Lucius Helvius Blaesus Proculus, two magistrates with judicial power. The day before the Ides of March. Secundus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia, I, have received from Publius Terentius Primus 776 sestertii, the remainder for the inherited and ancestral property of the Audian farm in the name of Stali Inventus. Done in Pompeii. Witnesses: Decimus Junius Torquatus Silanus and Quintus Haterius Antoninus, consuls. Quintus Coelius Caltilus Iustus and Lucius Helvius Blaesus Proculus, two magistrates with judicial power. The day before the Ides of March. Secundus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia, I have written that I have received from Publius Terentius Primus 776 sestertii, the remainder for the inherited property of the Audian farm, and I received 5224 sestertii before this day. Done in Pompeii. Witnesses: Decimus Junius Silanus and Quintus Haterius Antoninus, consuls. Secundus, slave of the colonists of Venerea. Lucius Helvius Blaesus. Quintus Coelius Iustus. Gnaeus Pupius.
EDCS-30300635.summary: This record details a payment of 776 sestertii and a prior payment of 5224 sestertii related to an inherited property, involving Secundus, a slave of the colonists of Venerea Cornelia, and Publius Terentius Primus, dated to the consulship of Junius Silanus and Haterius Antoninus, likely in the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-30300636.translation: Handwritten note of Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia, for the fullery payments, paid 1652 sestertii for the first year. Sex tus Pompeius Proculus and Gaius Cornelius Macro, two magistrates with judicial power. The 11th day before the Kalends of March. Privatus, slave of the colony, I have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus one thousand six hundred and fifty-two sestertii for the fullery, from the remaining amount of one year. Done in Pompeii. Under Nero Augustus, for the third time, and Marcus Messalla, consuls. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. Of Sextus Pompeius Proculus. Of Sextus Pompeius Proculus. Of Aulus Messius Pronimus. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. Under Sex tus Pompeius Proculus and Gaius Cornelius Macro, two magistrates with judicial power. The 11th day before the Kalends of March. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony, I have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 1652 sestertii for the fullery, from the remaining amount of one year. Under Nero Caesar, for the third time, and Messalla, consuls.
EDCS-30300636.summary: This inscription records a payment of 1652 sestertii by Privatus, a slave of the colonists of Venerea Cornelia, to Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, related to fullery taxes, dated to the consulship of Nero and Messalla, likely in 61 AD.

EDCS-30300637.translation: To Gnaeus Pompeius Grosphus and Grosphus Pompeius Gavianus, two magistrates with judicial power. The 6th day before the Ides of July. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia of the Pompeiani, I have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus one thousand six hundred and fifty nummos, five nummus-units, from the remainder for the fullery of Lucius Veranius Hupsaeus and Albucius Iustus, two magistrates with judicial power, paid. Done in Pompeii. Under Marcus Ostorius Scapula and Titus Sextius Africanus, consuls. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. Of Gnaeus Pompeius Grosphus, Gavianus, Marcus Veso[nius] Marcellus. Of Aulus Clodius Iustus. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. To the two Grosphi, magistrates with judicial power. The 6th day before the Ides of July. Handwritten note of Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. 1651 sestertii for the third year's fullery. Under Titus Sextius and Marcus Ostorius, consuls. The 6th day before the Ides of July. Handwritten note of Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. 1651 sestertii for the third year's fullery. To the two Grosphi, magistrates with judicial power. Under Marcus Ostorius and Titus Sextius, consuls. The 6th day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-30300637.summary: This inscription records a payment of 1651 sestertii by Privatus, a slave of the colonists of Venerea Cornelia, related to fullery taxes for the third year, dated to the consulship of Ostorius Scapula and Sextius Africanus, likely in the late 1st century AD.

EDCS-30300638.translation: To Gaius Cornelius Macro and Sextus Pompeius Proculus, two magistrates with judicial power. The Nones of January. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the Pompeiani, I have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus two thousand six hundred and seventy-five sestertii, from the remainder for the pasturage of Modestus and Vibius Secundus, two magistrates with judicial power. Done in Pompeii. Under Nero Caesar, for the third time, and Marcus Messalla Corvinus, consuls. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. Of Sextus Pompeius Proculus. Of Gnaeus Pompeius Gavianus. Of Publius Terentius Primus. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony Venerea Cornelia. Here, 20. To Gaius Cornelius Macro and Sextus Pompeius Proculus, two magistrates with judicial power. The Nones of January. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the Pompeiani, I have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 2675 sestertii, from the remainder for the pasturage of Modestus and Vibius Secundus. Done in Pompeii. Under Nero Caesar, for the third time, and Messalla Corvinus, consuls. Payment for pasturage for the first year. To Privatus, for the two magistrates Pompeius and Cornelius, I owed from the previous year 2675 sestertii.
EDCS-30300638.summary: This inscription documents a payment of 2675 sestertii by Privatus, a slave of the colonists, to Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, for pasturage dues from a previous year, dated to the consulship of Nero and Messalla Corvinus, likely in 61 AD.

EDCS-30300639.translation: Privatus, slave of the colony of Pompeii, acting for Lucius Veranius Hupsaeus and Lucius Albucius Iustus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction, on the 18th day before the Kalends of July, have written that I received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 1675 sesterces and I received before this day, which was the 8th day before the Ides of June, 1000 sesterces for the public pasture tax, during the consulship of Gaius Fonteius and Gaius Vipstanus. Privatus, slave of the colonists of the colony of Venusia, acting for Lucius Veranius Hupsaeus and Lucius Albucius Iustus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction, on the 14th day before the Kalends of July, have written that I received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 1675 sesterces and I received before this day, the 8th day before the Ides of June, 1000 sesterces for the public pastures, during the consulship of Gaius Fonteius and Gaius Vipstanus.
EDCS-30300639.summary: This is a financial receipt recording the payment of taxes for public pastures in Pompeii, involving slaves acting on behalf of duumvirs, with specific dates and amounts mentioned.

EDCS-30300640.translation: Settlement. For Lucius [---] and Tiberius Claudius Verus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction, on the 3rd day before the Ides of January. Privatus, slave of the colony of Pompeii, have written that I received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 2520 sesterces in the name of Marcus Fabius Agathinus, the owner, for market transactions, at Pompeii, during the consulship of Publius Marius and Lucius Afinius. [---] Tiberius Claudius Verus, Audi Bassus, Marcus Antonius Tertius. For Lucius [---] Claudius Verus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction. Privatus, slave of the colony of Pompeii, have written that I received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus [---] at Pompeii, on the 3rd day before the Ides of January, during the consulship of Publius Marius and Lucius Afinius.
EDCS-30300640.summary: This inscription is a financial settlement recording the receipt of payment for market transactions from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, acting on behalf of Marcus Fabius Agathinus, during the consulship of Publius Marius and Lucius Afinius.

EDCS-30301242.translation: From the estates of the Emperor Antoninus, from the brickworks of Satrius Fortunatus, via the Euripus.
EDCS-30301242.summary: This inscription records goods, specifically bricks, originating from the estates of Emperor Antoninus and the brickworks of Satrius Fortunatus.

EDCS-30301252.translation: Titus Greius Ianvarius, who made the pottery work, may he prosper.
EDCS-30301252.summary: This is an epigraphic maker's mark for pottery, attesting to the work of Titus Greius Ianvarius.

EDCS-30301510.translation: From the brickworks of Titus Rausius Pamphilus, belonging to Arria Fadilla Caepioniana.
EDCS-30301510.summary: This inscription indicates ownership and origin of bricks from the figlinae (brickworks) of Titus Rausius Pamphilus, associated with Arria Fadilla Caepioniana.

EDCS-30301511.translation: From the brickworks of Arrius Antoninus Caepioniana, during the consulship of Servianus III and Varo.
EDCS-30301511.summary: This inscription marks bricks from the figlinae of Arrius Antoninus Caepioniana, dating the production to the consulship of Servianus III and Varo.

EDCS-30301521.translation: From the brickworks of Fulvius Antoninus Caepioniana, belonging to Bruttidius Bassus, during the consulship of Servianus III and Varo.
EDCS-30301521.summary: This inscription denotes bricks from the figlinae of Fulvius Antoninus Caepioniana, associated with Bruttidius Bassus, and dated to the consulship of Servianus III and Varo.

EDCS-30301522.translation: From the estates of Gaius Curiatius Cosanus Caepionianis.
EDCS-30301522.summary: This inscription indicates that the items originated from the estates of Gaius Curiatius Cosanus, associated with the Caepionani.

EDCS-30301524.translation: From the estates of Gaius Curiatius Cosanus Caepionianis.
EDCS-30301524.summary: This inscription identifies the origin of goods from the estates of Gaius Curiatius Cosanus, linked to the Caepionani.

EDCS-30301525.translation: From the estates of Curiatius Cosanus Caricus and Titus Rausius Pamphilus.
EDCS-30301525.summary: This inscription records the origin of goods from the estates belonging to Curiatius Cosanus Caricus and Titus Rausius Pamphilus.

EDCS-30301527.translation: From the estates of Tiberius Tutinius Sentius Satrinus, from the Euripus, from the workshop of Vero and Eggius consuls.
EDCS-30301527.summary: This inscription records the origin of pottery from the workshop of Vero and Eggius, dated by their consulship.

EDCS-30301530.translation: From the estates of Curiatius C o sanus Caricus and Titus Rausius Pamphilus.
EDCS-30301530.summary: This inscription indicates the source of goods from the estates of Curiatius C o sanus Caricus and Titus Rausius Pamphilus.

EDCS-30301642.summary: This inscription lists four personal names, likely indicating ownership or origin, possibly related to individuals or estates.

EDCS-30400054.translation: Pottery from the imperial estates, from the Domitian workshops of Lanius Fortunatus.
EDCS-30400054.summary: This inscription records pottery produced in the Domitian workshops belonging to the imperial estates and managed by Lanius Fortunatus.

EDCS-30400055.translation: Pottery from the imperial estates, from the Domitian workshops of Lanius Fortunatus.
EDCS-30400055.summary: This inscription records pottery produced in the Domitian workshops belonging to the imperial estates and managed by Lanius Fortunatus.

EDCS-30400529.translation: Pottery from the workshops of Domitia Lucilla, of Lucius Munatius Crescens.
EDCS-30400529.summary: This inscription records pottery from the workshops of Domitia Lucilla, associated with Lucius Munatius Crescens.

EDCS-30400530.translation: From the workshops of Chresimus, of Lucius Munatius Crescens.
EDCS-30400530.summary: This inscription indicates pottery originating from the workshops of Chresimus, owned or managed by Lucius Munatius Crescens.

EDCS-30400531.translation: From the Caninian workshops of Domitia Lucilla.
EDCS-30400531.summary: This inscription denotes pottery originating from the Caninian workshops of Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-30400532.translation: Pottery from the Caninian workshops, of Sulpicius Servandus.
EDCS-30400532.summary: This inscription records pottery from the Caninian workshops, associated with Sulpicius Servandus.

EDCS-30400533.translation: From the workshops of Chresimus, of Lucius Munatius Crescens.
EDCS-30400533.summary: This inscription indicates pottery originating from the workshops of Chresimus, owned or managed by Lucius Munatius Crescens.

EDCS-30400540.translation: This pottery was made from the workshops of Domitia Lucilla by Augustalis, Lucius Munatius Crescens.
EDCS-30400540.summary: This inscription records a pottery product from the workshops of Domitia Lucilla, made by Lucius Munatius Crescens, likely during the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-31200895.translation: Among your ancestors and forefathers, and your holy parent, you shone forth with merits and honors of virtues, a great ornament of a noble family and of the Senate, but you were snatched away too soon, holy Kameni, leaving eternal tears, dying in youthful years. Your sweet wife mourns you with tears day and night, along with your small children, grieving that she has lost the comfort of her life, widowed from a chaste bed; nevertheless, she adorns and decorates your tomb with all duties as a final gift and solace for her grief, for Alfenius Ceionius Iulianus Kamhenius, most distinguished man, quaestor candidate, triumphing praetor, member of the VII viri epulonum, father of sacred rites, high priest of the Supreme Invincible Mithras, archibucolus of the god Liber, member of the XV viri sacris faciundis, tauroboliate of the Mother of the Gods, pontifex maior, consular governor of Numidia and vicar of Africa, who lived 42 years, 6 months, 13 days, departed in the consulship of our lord Arcadius and Flavius Bauto.
EDCS-31200895.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Alfenius Ceionius Iulianus Kamhenius, detailing his distinguished career and numerous priesthoods, and mourning his premature death in his youth by his wife and children.
