EDCS-33000316.summary: This inscription records the origin of doliary (pottery) products from the brickworks belonging to Caius Calpetanius Mnester, likely an imperial freedman or contractor.

EDCS-33200002.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Nymphidius Alexander made this in memory of his most sweet sister Domitia Euphrosyne, who lived 27 years.
EDCS-33200002.summary: This bilingual (Greek and Latin) funerary epitaph records the deceased Domitia Euphrosyne, who lived 27 years, and her brother Gaius Nymphidius Alexander as the dedicator.

EDCS-33400727.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Lucius Sextilius Rufus, likely the deceased.

EDCS-33500405.translation: Caius Crupius and his freedwoman Crupia made this for their patron and for themselves, and for Caius Crupius, freedman, and Caius Matius, freedman, and Caius Marcius, freedman, and Crupia, freedwoman.
EDCS-33500405.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary monument dedication made by Caius Crupius and his freedwoman Crupia for their patron and themselves, with further individuals named.

EDCS-33500409.translation: Primius Crassianus, deserving and loyal to his patron, lived 33 years, 5 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-33500409.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Primius Crassianus and states his loyalty to his patron.

EDCS-33500410.translation: Flavia Alexandra, a most unhappy mother, had this made with great expense according to his will for her most dutiful son Gaius Cassius Philota, physician to the emperor, specializing in eyes.
EDCS-33500410.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Flavia Alexandra for her son, Gaius Cassius Philota, an oculist physician to the emperor, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-33500411.translation: This monument or tomb is for Marcus Antonius Atimetus, Zmaragdus, and Antonia Chrotis, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, and the enclosed place with its buildings and shop and whatever pertains to the rights of that place.
EDCS-33500411.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a funerary monument and burial plot, including buildings and a shop, by Marcus Antonius Atimetus, Zmaragdus, and Antonia Chrotis for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-33500412.translation: Prosdocius, freedman of the Emperor, record-keeper of the Via Labicana and Praenestina, gave this as a gift.
EDCS-33500412.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Prosdocius, an imperial freedman and official responsible for the Via Labicana and Praenestina roads.

EDCS-33500413.translation: To Gaius Tatinus, son of Gaius. Died. To Tatinia Salvia, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-33500413.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Tatinus and Tatinia Salvia.

EDCS-33500415.translation: Lucius C of Lucius' freedman Nicia lives in front 11 feet.
EDCS-33500415.summary: This inscription, likely a boundary marker, indicates the extent of Nicia's property.

EDCS-33500416.translation: To the prefect of the cavalry of the Moesian wing of Felix, [a freedman/son] of Quintus, to Secunda, priestess, [a freedwoman/son] of Proculus, brother.
EDCS-33500416.summary: This is a dedication to Secunda, a priestess, by her brother Proculus, who was a prefect of cavalry.

EDCS-33500417.translation: During the consulship of Publius Sulpicius Quirinius and Gaius Valgius, Gaius Statius, son of Gaius, from the Falernian region, magistrate of the pagus, Apollinaris, and also patron, according to a decree of the pagus, from money contributed by those listed below, who are to be buried in this place, the pagus Apollinaris: Gaius Gletranus, freedman of Gaius, 150 sesterces; Lucius Decidius Homuncio, freedman of Lucius, 200 sesterces; Gaius Statius Baguaro, freedman of Gaius, 200 sesterces; Gaius Aurelius Heraclio, freedman of Gaius, 60 sesterces; [freedman of Lucius], 20 sesterces; [freedwoman of Orfus?], 20 sesterces; Odysseus, 20 sesterces; Phaenis, 60 sesterces; Attalus, freedman of Marcus, 40 sesterces; [gave].
EDCS-33500417.summary: This inscription records the contributions made by various individuals, including freedmen and patrons, for a burial plot in the pagus Apollinaris during the consulship of Sulpicius Quirinius and Valgius.

EDCS-33500418.translation: Felix Faustus Faustus Adatrima [son/freedman] of Aug VIII.
EDCS-33500418.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary notice for Felix Faustus, possibly naming relatives or patrons.

EDCS-33500419.translation: Photiaca, Gaius, son/freedman of Lucius Hel..., Adatrima, Gaius, son/freedman of C. H. IV, Faustus Faustus.
EDCS-33500419.summary: This inscription lists several names, possibly a family or group, with indications of parentage or patronage.

EDCS-33600389.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Heliopolitanus, Hermianus the priest, gave as a gift.
EDCS-33600389.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Heliopolitanus by a priest named Hermianus.

EDCS-34000003.translation: under the supervision of Domitius, the procurator.
EDCS-34000003.summary: This fragment refers to the actions of Domitius, a procurator.

EDCS-34000007.translation: Gratus, freedman, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, sacred.
EDCS-34000007.summary: This is a religious dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by a freedman named Gratus.

EDCS-34000022.translation: Marcus Caecilius Clymenus, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Marcus Caecilius Agenor, patron, and for Caecilia Charite, freedwoman of Marcus, his wife, and for Cossinius Pandarus, freedman of Aulus, the banker, and for his own [family/people].
EDCS-34000022.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial arrangements made by Marcus Caecilius Clymenus for himself, his patron, his wife, and others, including a banker.

EDCS-34000026.translation: To Marcus Cattius Puteolanus, his most devoted son, by Cattia Adiecta and Cattius Narcissus, to their husband and to their son Cattius Vestalis and Genialis, and to their freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-34000026.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by a family to their deceased son, Marcus Cattius Puteolanus.

EDCS-34000031.translation: Decia Hegemonis, freedwoman of Aulus, for herself and for Decia Italia, freedwoman of her and a slave woman, and for Decia Epitychia, her freedwoman and slave woman, and for her own people.
EDCS-34000031.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by Decia Hegemonis for herself, her slave woman, and her freedwoman and slave woman, and their descendants.

EDCS-34000032.translation: Lucius Faenius Philomusus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and his own people, a place for burning bodies.
EDCS-34000032.summary: This inscription records a funerary plot for burning bodies, dedicated by Lucius Faenius Philomusus for himself and his family.

EDCS-34000038.summary: This tombstone records the name and age of Gaius Julius Valens, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-34000042.translation: This is a sepulchre, enclosed by a wall with a shop and buildings, for Gaius Larcius Cataplus, for himself and for Larcica Glycera and Larcica Thallusa and Marcus Minucius Zethos, and for their freedmen and freedwomen, and for their descendants.
EDCS-34000042.summary: This inscription records a funerary complex including a sepulchre, shop, and other buildings, dedicated by Gaius Larcius Cataplus for his family and freedmen.

EDCS-34000043.translation: To Marcus Marcius Pothos, freedman, and Chryseros, freedman, and Myrtine, freedwoman, and Psyche, freedwoman, and their own people; this monument or sepulchre will not pass to an external heir.
EDCS-34000043.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by freedmen and freedwomen, stipulating that it cannot be inherited by anyone outside the family.

EDCS-34000044.translation: ] lived [---]. His most devoted mother Nonia [---]
EDCS-34000044.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription mentions a mother, Nonia, and her deceased son, possibly dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-34000045.summary: This is a dedication to Aulus Oblicius Optatus, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-34000055.translation: ]asinus, freedman of Caesar, [---] Poplicolanus, [---] to his fellow freedman Gratianus, [---] and his own freedmen.
EDCS-34000055.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication from a freedman of Caesar to his fellow freedman Gratianus and their respective freedmen.

EDCS-34000365.summary: This inscription likely refers to a performance or ritual involving lamenting foreign women from Memphis.

EDCS-34000366.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or epitaph naming Gnaeus Domitius Arignotus.

EDCS-34100443.translation: To Postumius Lampadius, for his honor and the republic, by A. Pignus, aedile.
EDCS-34100443.summary: This is a dedication to Postumius Lampadius by A. Pignus, likely for his service as an aedile, indicating a date in the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-34100459.translation: In the consulship of Gaius Valerius Marrus and Herennius (consuls).
EDCS-34100459.summary: This inscription records a date according to the consulship of Gaius Valerius Marrus and Herennius, placing it in the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-34100469.summary: This is a simple dedication or maker's mark by Stallianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34100472.translation: Priscus, in the reign of Imperator Primitivus.
EDCS-34100472.summary: This inscription names Priscus and dates to the reign of 'Imperator Primitivus', possibly a local or short-lived title, within the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34100586.translation: To Marcus Lelius, son of Marcus Stadius. Agatoma[---] for herself and her husband.
EDCS-34100586.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning Marcus Lelius and Agatoma, likely a husband and wife.

EDCS-34100587.translation: The following magistrates, Venerus and Iovius, sons of Numerius Pumidius, Marcus Cottius, Marcus Eppilius, Caius Antracius, Lucius Sempronius, Publius Cicereius, Marcus Raecius, Numerius Arrius, Lucius Heioleius, Caius Tuccius, Quintus Vibius, Marcus Valerius, sons of their fathers, supervised the construction of the wall for 270 feet and made the foundations, in the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius.
EDCS-34100587.summary: This inscription records the completion of a public works project (a wall) by several local magistrates under the consuls Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Aurelius, dating it to their consulship, likely in the mid-Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-34100588.translation: Lucius Mevius, son of Lucius, and Titus Vibius, son of Caius Varus, duoviri for dispensing justice.
EDCS-34100588.summary: This inscription names Lucius Mevius and Titus Vibius as duoviri, indicating their civic magistracy in a Roman town, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34300748.translation: To Lucius Cassius, freedman of Lucius, Logo.
EDCS-34300748.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Cassius Logo, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34300749.translation: Numerius Curtius Spurianus, son of Numerius; his brother.
EDCS-34300749.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Numerius Curtius Spurianus and mentioning his brother, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34300755.translation: Titia Vesbina, freedwoman of a man, his freedwoman.
EDCS-34300755.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedwoman named Titia Vesbina, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34300761.translation: Macrinus, administrator for Antonianus, freedman of Emperor Augustus, was here on the day before the Ides of January, when Nerva and Vestinus were consuls.
EDCS-34300761.summary: This is a dedication by Macrinus, an administrator, commemorating his presence at a location on a specific date in 97 CE.

EDCS-34300762.translation: Macrinus, administrator for Antonianus, freedman of Emperor Augustus, walked here on the day before the Ides of January, when Nerva and Vestinus were consuls.
EDCS-34300762.summary: This is a dedication by Macrinus, an administrator, commemorating his presence at a location on a specific date in 97 CE.

EDCS-34300767.translation: Of Tiberius Claudius Celer, and Decimus Junius Modestus, and Junia Vitalis.
EDCS-34300767.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the names of individuals, possibly related to a dedication or funerary monument, tentatively dated to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34400141.translation: Septentrio [---]ulas, hieronices. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-34400141.summary: This inscription indicates that a specific location, possibly a tomb or a public space, was granted by a local council's decision, with a reference to a 'hieronices' and a name fragment.

EDCS-34400156.translation: Tiberius Claudius Athenodorus' freedman Hyginus for himself and for his wife Nympha and for his mother Philumena and for Julius Heracles and for his wife Pontia Vitali and for Cloatia Lanthusa and for his own family
EDCS-34400156.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the dedication of a tomb by a freedman, Hyginus, for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-34500005.translation: Pottery work from the estates of our Augustus, belonging to Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500005.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery from the estates of the emperor, attributed to Caius Cominius Sabinianus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500008.summary: This is a simple ownership mark, indicating that a pottery or a property belonged to Lucius Antonius Protus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500055.translation: Pottery work of Lucius Aquilius Faustus.
EDCS-34500055.summary: This inscription marks pottery produced by Lucius Aquilius Faustus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500059.translation: Pottery work from the workshops of Faustina Augusta, our empress, belonging to Sextus Vimatius Restitutus.
EDCS-34500059.summary: This inscription records pottery produced from the imperial workshops of Empress Faustina, attributed to Sextus Vimatius Restitutus, likely from the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500060.summary: This inscription records the ownership of Sextius Annius Aphrodisius, likely on a piece of pottery or a tile.

EDCS-34500061.summary: This inscription records the ownership of Sextius Annius Aphrodisius, likely on a piece of pottery or a tile.

EDCS-34500069.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus, when Niger and Camerinus were consuls.
EDCS-34500069.summary: This inscription indicates that the doliare ware came from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus and dates to the consulship of Niger and Camerinus.

EDCS-34500070.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of Lucius Aelius Caesar Commodus, from Aristius.
EDCS-34500070.summary: This inscription indicates that the doliare ware came from the estates of Lucius Aelius Caesar Commodus and was made by Aristius.

EDCS-34500071.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of Lucius Verus Augustus, from Caius Nunidius Felix.
EDCS-34500071.summary: This inscription indicates that the doliare ware came from the estates of Lucius Verus Augustus and was produced by Caius Nunidius Felix.

EDCS-34500072.translation: Figlinum doliare ware of Caius Ninidius Felix, for Lucius Aurelius Commodus.
EDCS-34500072.summary: This inscription records figlinum doliare ware produced by Caius Ninidius Felix for Lucius Aurelius Commodus.

EDCS-34500073.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of our Augustus, from Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500073.summary: This inscription states that the doliare ware originated from the estates of the emperor ('Augustus noster') and was supplied by Caius Cominius Sabinianus.

EDCS-34500080.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of Faustiana Augusta, from Lucius Brittidius Augustinus.
EDCS-34500080.summary: This inscription indicates that the doliare ware came from the estates of Faustiana Augusta and was produced by Lucius Brittidius Augustinus.

EDCS-34500082.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of our lord Augustus.
EDCS-34500082.summary: This inscription indicates that the doliare ware came from the estates of the emperor ('dominus noster Augustus').

EDCS-34500083.translation: From Decimus Veturius Cerdon, from the estates of Annius Verus, when Apronianus and Paetinus were consuls.
EDCS-34500083.summary: This inscription records that the material came from the estates of Annius Verus, supplied by Decimus Veturius Cerdon, and dates to the consulship of Apronianus and Paetinus.

EDCS-34500086.translation: Tile production from the estates of Faustina Augusta, by Tiberius Claudius Secundinus.
EDCS-34500086.summary: This inscription records tile production attributed to Tiberius Claudius Secundinus from the estates of Faustina Augusta.

EDCS-34500087.translation: Tile production from the estates of Faustina Augusta, by Lucius Brittidius Augustinus.
EDCS-34500087.summary: This inscription records tile production attributed to Lucius Brittidius Augustinus from the estates of Faustina Augusta.

EDCS-34500089.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Lucius Allius Maximus.

EDCS-34500090.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Antonius Hilarius.

EDCS-34500091.summary: This inscription identifies Apollonius as a slave of Antonius Lucius.

EDCS-34500092.summary: This inscription identifies Apollonius as a slave of Antonius Lucius.

EDCS-34500106.translation: Tile production from the estates of Faustina, by Calpetanus Crescens.
EDCS-34500106.summary: This inscription records tile production by Calpetanus Crescens from the estates of Faustina.

EDCS-34500107.translation: Tile production from the estates of our Emperor, by Gaius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500107.summary: This inscription records tile production attributed to Gaius Cominius Sabinianus from the estates of the Emperor.

EDCS-34500108.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Annius Flamma.

EDCS-34500109.translation: From the pottery works of Marcus Annius Verus.
EDCS-34500109.summary: This inscription indicates production from the pottery works of Marcus Annius Verus.

EDCS-34500112.translation: Publius Raius Ryt made this from the estates of Antonia Manl.
EDCS-34500112.summary: This inscription records a work made by Publius Raius Ryt from the estates of Antonia Manl.

EDCS-34500113.summary: This inscription identifies Apollonius as the slave of Antonius Lucius.

EDCS-34500114.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Faustina Augusta, from the workshop of Metilius Atalus.
EDCS-34500114.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of Faustina Augusta, originating from the workshop of Metilius Atalus.

EDCS-34500115.translation: Doliary work of Aristi Thallus from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus, with Caesar and Nigrus and Camerinus as consuls.
EDCS-34500115.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus, dated by the consulship of Caesar, Nigrus, and Camerinus.

EDCS-34500132.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark belonging to Marcus Antonius Hilarus.

EDCS-34500149.translation: Doliary work of Caius Nunidius Felix from the estates of Lucius Verus Caesar.
EDCS-34500149.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of Lucius Verus Caesar, produced by Caius Nunidius Felix.

EDCS-34500150.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Augustus, by Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500150.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of the emperor, made by Caius Cominius Sabinianus.

EDCS-34500151.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Augusti, by Lucius Lanius Substitutus.
EDCS-34500151.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the imperial estates, made by Lucius Lanius Substitutus.

EDCS-34500152.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our lords Augusti, by Titia Rufina.
EDCS-34500152.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the imperial estates, attributed to Titia Rufina.

EDCS-34500153.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark belonging to Lucius Antonius Marion.

EDCS-34500154.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Apollonius, a slave, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500155.translation: Doliary work from the pottery of Faustina Augusta, our empress, belonging to Sextus Vimatius Restitutus.
EDCS-34500155.summary: This inscription records the production of earthenware from the property of Faustina Augusta, overseen by Sextus Vimatius Restitutus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500156.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus, son of Caesar, during the consulship of Nigro and Camerinus.
EDCS-34500156.summary: This inscription indicates doliary work from the estates of Lucius Ceionius Commodus, dating to the consulship of Nigro and Camerinus (likely 149 CE).

EDCS-34500157.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Lucius Aelius Caesar, son of Commodus, by Aritius Aug[...]
EDCS-34500157.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of Lucius Aelius Caesar, likely from the Antonine period.

EDCS-34500158.translation: Figlinary doliary work from the estates of our Caesar, from the workshop of Caius Calpetanius Pannycus.
EDCS-34500158.summary: This inscription notes figlinary doliary work from the estates of the emperor, originating from the workshop of Caius Calpetanius Pannycus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34500159.translation: From the estates of Sextus Plotus Titianus, belonging to our Caesar.
EDCS-34500159.summary: This inscription indicates ownership of estates belonging to Sextus Plotus Titianus, which were part of the imperial properties, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500160.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Augustus, belonging to Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500160.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of the emperor, managed by Caius Cominius Sabinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500161.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Augustus, belonging to Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500161.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of the emperor, managed by Caius Cominius Sabinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500162.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Augustus, belonging to Caius Cominius Sabinianus.
EDCS-34500162.summary: This inscription records doliary work from the estates of the emperor, managed by Caius Cominius Sabinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500163.translation: From the estates of our Augustus, from the potteries of Pompeius Hele[s].
EDCS-34500163.summary: This inscription records materials from the imperial estates, sourced from the potteries of Pompeius Hele[s], likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34500164.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of our Emperors, from the workshops of Caius Terentius Titianus.
EDCS-34500164.summary: This inscription records the origin of doliare ware, indicating it was produced from imperial estates by Caius Terentius Titianus.

EDCS-34500165.summary: This inscription is a simple ownership or dedication marker for Sextus Annius Aphrodisius.

EDCS-34500166.summary: This inscription is a simple ownership or dedication marker for Decimus Veturius Cerdon.

EDCS-34500167.summary: This inscription is a simple ownership or dedication marker for Antheros, a freedman of the Emperor.

EDCS-34500168.translation: Publius Raius Rytus made this from the estates of Antonia Manlia.
EDCS-34500168.summary: This inscription records that Publius Raius Rytus produced something from the estates of Antonia Manlia.

EDCS-34600004.translation: Titinia Myrtis, freedwoman of Aulus. Aulus Titinius Zyges the Elder, freedman of Aulus. Titinia Heraclea, freedwoman of Aulus.
EDCS-34600004.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, Titinia Myrtis, Aulus Titinius Zyges Maior, and Titinia Heraclea, all freedpeople of Aulus, likely marking a shared tomb or property.

EDCS-34600011.translation: They made this for a most dutiful wife and mother.
EDCS-34600011.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by unnamed individuals for their most dutiful wife and mother.

EDCS-34600013.translation: Chelido, freedwoman of the woman Furia.
EDCS-34600013.summary: This inscription identifies Chelido as a freedwoman of a woman named Furia.

EDCS-34600014.translation: Publius Sextilius Philoxenus, freedman of Publius. Sextilia Prima, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-34600014.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Sextilius Philoxenus and Sextilia Prima as freedpeople of Publius, likely commemorating a shared monument.

EDCS-34700007.translation: Gnaeus Vesiculanus, son of Marcus, for Gerinnia, daughter of Gnaeus, his mother.
EDCS-34700007.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Gnaeus Vesiculanus to his mother, Gerinnia.

EDCS-34700011.translation: Tiberius Claudius Amoenus, messenger, placed this for his wife Caesernina Claudia Restituta.
EDCS-34700011.summary: A funerary monument set up by Tiberius Claudius Amoenus for his wife.

EDCS-34700012.translation: To Acilia Atis, who lived 25 years. Acilia, for herself and for her most dutiful daughter and descendants.
EDCS-34700012.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Acilia for herself, her daughter, and future descendants.

EDCS-34700013.summary: A simple funerary inscription identifying Marcus Benius and his parentage.

EDCS-34700014.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Paccia Marcia to her incomparable and deserving husband, Caius Claudius Viator, with whom she lived for more or less 40 years.
EDCS-34700014.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Claudius Viator, set up by his wife Paccia Marcia, noting their 40 years of marriage.

EDCS-34700016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Annia Iustina to her most dutiful mother, OFI IVN, who lived 40 years.
EDCS-34700016.summary: A funerary epitaph for OFI IVN, set up by her daughter Annia Iustina.

EDCS-34700019.translation: To Iuppa, daughter of Lucius. Tertius, son of Marcus NEI.
EDCS-34700019.summary: A funerary inscription recording the parentage of Iuppa and identifying Tertius.

EDCS-34700021.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Caerellianus Pheobenus, who lived 55 years, 5 months, and 15 days, his most dutiful sons, deserving of his memory.
EDCS-34700021.summary: A funerary monument erected by the sons of Caerellianus Pheobenus, detailing his lifespan.

EDCS-34700022.translation: Caius Campius, son of Caius, from Sil[...].
EDCS-34700022.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription identifying Caius Campius and his origin.

EDCS-34700023.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Sacretia Claudiane, for her most excellent husband, Sacretio Ingenuo, veteran, a most sweet and dutiful man, with whom she lived 25 years, a man of good memory.
EDCS-34700023.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Sacretia Claudiane for her beloved veteran husband, Sacretio Ingenuo, marking their 25 years of marriage.

EDCS-34700026.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Optandus made this.
EDCS-34700026.summary: A funerary monument indicating Optandus as the maker.

EDCS-34700032.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a person named Alumnus, son of Hordionius.

EDCS-34700033.translation: To Lucio Epidius Fav, most beloved of Epidia.
EDCS-34700033.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucio Epidius Fav by his beloved Epidia, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-34700038.translation: Publius Numisius Paculus, son of Publius, of the Oufentina tribe, again prefect acting as duovir. Publius Numisius Festus, son of Publius, of the Oufentina tribe. Pantuleia. Publius Numisius Tertius (?), freedman of Publius.
EDCS-34700038.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription listing multiple members of the Numisius family and their civic roles, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-34700040.translation: Sacred to Diana. Publius Petronius Anicetus, freedman, gave this gift.
EDCS-34700040.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a gift to the goddess Diana by Publius Petronius Anicetus.

EDCS-34700046.translation: Of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus.
EDCS-34700046.summary: This inscription likely commemorates a monument or building related to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, probably from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-34700047.summary: This is a simple dedicatory or maker's inscription by Aurelius Sec.

EDCS-34700055.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Agato, freedman of Caius, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-34700062.translation: Decrees by public officials during the quinquennality of Marcus Aemilius Titius Octavius, under the administration of Quintus Aegerilius Marcius Luccius Q.
EDCS-34700062.summary: This inscription records public decrees made during a five-year administrative period (quinquennality) involving named officials, likely from a municipal context.

EDCS-34700067.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Oceanus, son of Nedimus Hedistus.

EDCS-34700068.translation: To the Emperor, our lord, Maxim(o) always Augustus, for the fifth time.
EDCS-34700068.summary: This inscription honors the emperor, identified as Maxim(o) Augustus, likely a public dedication from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-34700155.translation: To Lucius A. C. and Petronia Venusta and her family.
EDCS-34700155.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius A. C. and Petronia Venusta and her family.

EDCS-34700156.translation: To Gaius Egnatius Certus, son of Gaius, a most distinguished man, consul, patron of the colony, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-34700156.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Egnatius Certus, a consul and patron of the colony, likely set up by the town council.

EDCS-34700157.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Egnatius Certus.

EDCS-34700161.translation: Here rests in sweet sleep Caretosa, daughter of Quirillus, a Roman deacon, who lived about 27 sorrowful years, buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of October, 24 years after the consulship of the most distinguished man Basilius, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-34700161.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Caretosa, daughter of Quirillus the deacon, providing her age and burial date.

EDCS-34700166.translation: Under Emperor Domitian Caesar Augustus, in his 9th consulship, with Marcus Vibius Priscus and Aulus Iustuleius Balbus as duovirs with quinquennial authority, Lucius (?) Tyanisius Dextrus Cenaius Valerius Priscus and Aulus Iustuleius Saturninus as aediles and curator. Vibius Verecundus, Petronius Phoebus, Licinius Himer, Manilius Litus, Manilius Phileus, Turpilius Fortunatus, Geminius Fortunatus, Acellius Tertius, Betilenus Anthus, Crisius Aprilis, Virius Aper.
EDCS-34700166.summary: This inscription records the names of various officials, including duovirs, aediles, and curators, during the reign of Emperor Domitian and lists several other individuals.

EDCS-34700167.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning someone's son and the name DECOLA.

EDCS-34700168.translation: To the departed spirits. Cornelia Vitalis made this for her husband Ianuarius, who lived 62 years, a well-deserving spouse.
EDCS-34700168.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Cornelia Vitalis to her husband Ianuarius, noting his age and her affection.

EDCS-34700169.translation: To the departed spirits. Asinia Nomas for her most excellent husband Tiberius Claudius Myrtillus, son of Tiberius, who lived 86 years, without causing any offense.
EDCS-34700169.summary: This funerary dedication from Asinia Nomas honors her husband Tiberius Claudius Myrtillus, stating his age and virtuous character.

EDCS-34700170.translation: To the departed spirits. For Porcius Am, who lived 9 years.
EDCS-34700170.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription for Porcius Am, noting his young age.

EDCS-34700253.translation: to Zeius, freedman of Gnaeus, a vascularis.
EDCS-34700253.summary: This fragment likely refers to a freedman named Zeius who served as a vascularis.

EDCS-34700257.translation: The bones of Quintus Iactius, who lived 5 years, are placed here. D. Caia, his heir, took care and made this.
EDCS-34700257.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Iactius, recording his age and the provision made by his heir.

EDCS-34700258.translation: Iucundus, freedman of Aulus Iustus, and his freedwoman Ianuaria made this monument for themselves and for their freedman.
EDCS-34700258.summary: A funerary monument inscription recording its makers and beneficiaries, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-34700259.translation: [...] Iustinus and [...] / [...] of Marcellus and A[...]
EDCS-34700259.summary: A fragmentary inscription with names, possibly commemorating individuals or a family.

EDCS-34700260.translation: [...] Aulus Manlius Rufus, son of Aulus; [...] Manlius Quartinus; Annia Selenione; Aulus Manlius Myrtilus(?) for himself and his family.
EDCS-34700260.summary: A funerary inscription naming several individuals, including Aulus Manlius Rufus and his relatives, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-34700267.translation: Lucius Pupponius, son of Lucius; Seppia, freedwoman of |(mulieris); Sepp[...]
EDCS-34700267.summary: A fragmented inscription mentioning Lucius Pupponius and Seppia, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-34700268.translation: To Rubria, daughter of Pu[...]; daughter of Rubrius Pu[...]
EDCS-34700268.summary: A damaged inscription that appears to be a dedication or funerary marker for Rubria.

EDCS-34700269.translation: [...] Salvius, freedman of Marcus; for himself and [...]ima, his wife; [...]
EDCS-34700269.summary: A funerary inscription detailing a monument made for Salvius, his wife, and possibly others.

EDCS-34700271.translation: For Publius Vettius Antiochus, freedman of Publius; For Publius Vettius Hilarus, freedman of Publius; from his own funds.
EDCS-34700271.summary: An inscription recording two dedications made by Publius Vettius Hilarus, son of Publius, for himself and for Publius Vettius Antiochus.

EDCS-34700274.summary: A very fragmentary inscription containing partial names, possibly from a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-34700276.translation: [...]ia, daughter of Aulus, Nic[...]; Maiori; the bones are placed here.
EDCS-34700276.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman identified as Maiori, daughter of Aulus, mentioning her bones are interred here.

EDCS-34700280.translation: Who lived for six years, seven months, and four days, buried on the third day before the Ides of May, in the consulship of Valentinianus and Valens. Marcus Sextinus and Afrinia Quarta made this for their most beloved daughter.
EDCS-34700280.summary: A funerary epitaph for a daughter, likely from the late Roman Empire, given the consuls.

EDCS-34700281.translation: Marcus made this inscription on the first day before the Kalends of September, in the third consulship of Flavius Gratianus Augustus. He lived for 30 years. Equitius.
EDCS-34700281.summary: A funerary epitaph, probably from the late 4th century CE, for a man named Marcus who lived for 30 years.

EDCS-34700285.translation: Vicciana, from the Tonneian workshops, Apollinaris.
EDCS-34700285.summary: An ownership mark on pottery, indicating it originates from the Vicciana workshops and belongs to Apollinaris.

EDCS-34700286.translation: From the Viccianian workshops, of Rutilia, daughter of Lucius Ocratus.
EDCS-34700286.summary: An ownership mark on pottery, indicating it originates from the Viccianian workshops and belongs to Rutilia.

EDCS-34700287.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Seia Isaura, made by Lucius Fadius Pas Servianus in the third consulship of [Servianus] and Varo.
EDCS-34700287.summary: A producer's or owner's mark on pottery, likely from the 3rd century CE, indicating the origin from the Seia Isaura estates.

EDCS-34700288.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Emperor Augustus, from the Voconian workshops of Munatius Anicetus.
EDCS-34700288.summary: A mark on pottery, indicating it originated from imperial estates and the Voconian workshops owned by Munatius Anicetus.

EDCS-34700293.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Seia Isaura, made by Lucius Fadius Pas Servianus in the third consulship of [Servianus] and Varo.
EDCS-34700293.summary: A producer's or owner's mark on pottery, likely from the 3rd century CE, indicating the origin from the Seia Isaura estates.

EDCS-34700294.translation: From the Viccianian workshops, of Rutilia, daughter of Lucius Ocratus.
EDCS-34700294.summary: An ownership mark on pottery, indicating it originates from the Viccianian workshops and belongs to Rutilia.

EDCS-34700297.translation: Vicciana, from the Spurilia workshops, of Florus.
EDCS-34700297.summary: An ownership mark on pottery, indicating it originates from the Vicciana workshops and belongs to Florus.

EDCS-34700304.translation: Doliary work from the estates of our Emperors, from the Voconian workshops of Marcus Licinius Callistianus.
EDCS-34700304.summary: A mark on pottery, indicating it originated from imperial estates and the Voconian workshops owned by Marcus Licinius Callistianus.

EDCS-34700316.translation: Tonneian ware from the Viccianian potteries.
EDCS-34700316.summary: This inscription records brick or tile production from the Viccianian potteries, possibly a maker's mark.

EDCS-34700319.translation: A dolium (large jar) of Tonneian ware, Eutychus, slave of Iulia Procula.
EDCS-34700319.summary: This inscription records a dolium manufactured by Eutychus, a slave of Iulia Procula, likely indicating ownership or origin.

EDCS-34700324.translation: Viccianian ware from the Tonneian potteries, by Apolinaris.
EDCS-34700324.summary: This inscription marks pottery from the Tonneian potteries attributed to Apolinaris, likely indicating the maker or owner.

EDCS-34700325.translation: From the Viccianian potteries, of Rutilia, daughter of Lucius, of Ocratus.
EDCS-34700325.summary: This inscription indicates that the ware originated from the Viccianian potteries and belonged to Rutilia, daughter of Lucius Ocratus.

EDCS-34700326.translation: Viccianian ware from the potteries of Spurilia Florus.
EDCS-34700326.summary: This inscription marks ware from the potteries of Spurilia Florus, indicating the source or owner.

EDCS-34700327.translation: Doliarian ware from the estates of our Emperors, from the potteries of Marcus Licinius Callistianus.
EDCS-34700327.summary: This inscription records dolium ware from imperial estates, produced at the potteries of Marcus Licinius Callistianus.

EDCS-34800314.translation: Doliarian ware of Caius Iulius Fortunatus, from the potteries of our Caesar.
EDCS-34800314.summary: This inscription indicates dolium ware produced by Caius Iulius Fortunatus from the potteries belonging to the emperor.

EDCS-34800315.translation: Ware from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, workshop of Ieronymus.
EDCS-34800315.summary: This inscription records ware from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, produced in the workshop of Ieronymus.

EDCS-34801052.summary: This is a simple ownership or origin inscription for Caius Iulius Fortunatus.

EDCS-34801055.translation: Ware from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, workshop of Ieronymus.
EDCS-34801055.summary: This inscription records ware from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, produced in the workshop of Ieronymus.

EDCS-34801056.translation: Work from the estates of Aurelius Caesar, workshop of Mercury.
EDCS-34801056.summary: This inscription likely records the origin of materials or labor for a project associated with Aurelius Caesar's estates and the workshop of Mercury.

EDCS-34801107.translation: Here rests in peace Apronianus, a chaste boy who lived more or less 15 years, buried on Friday, the 7th day before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Flavius Ricimer, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-34801107.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph for a boy named Apronianus, giving his approximate age and burial date, including the consul.

EDCS-34801109.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Ana, mother of Bishop Iustus of Capua, who lived approximately 70 years, buried on the 10th day of the 6th indiction in the reign of Emperor Justinus Perpetual Augustus, in the year after his consulship.
EDCS-34801109.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph for Ana, mother of Bishop Iustus of Capua, providing her approximate age and date of burial.

EDCS-34801111.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Albinus, son of Magnus, who lived one year and four months, buried on the Kalends of October.
EDCS-34801111.summary: This is a late Roman epitaph for Albinus, son of Magnus, recording his age at death and date of burial.

EDCS-34801114.translation: Chthonic gods, receive Gaius Babulius and his foster mother Tertia Salvia, dedicated to Quartus. Dite, receive them into your home.
EDCS-34801114.summary: This funerary inscription invokes the chthonic gods to receive Gaius Babulius and his foster mother, Tertia Salvia, and is dedicated to Quartus.

EDCS-34801115.translation: To Lucius Caecilius Creticus, son of Lucius, a member of the board of four with judicial authority, and to Lucius Caecilius Nationus, son of Lucius; the town council members and inhabitants [erected this].
EDCS-34801115.summary: This is a public dedication by municipal officials and inhabitants to two individuals, Lucius Caecilius Creticus and Lucius Caecilius Nationus, likely for their service.

EDCS-34801116.translation: To my grandmother and to Aphrodisia, my mother.
EDCS-34801116.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or tomb by an unnamed individual to his grandmother and mother.

EDCS-34801118.translation: Herais, daughter of [name], had this made for her father from her own funds.
EDCS-34801118.summary: This is a funerary dedication commissioned by Herais for her father, specifying that she funded it herself.

EDCS-34801119.translation: Obulcia Iucunda, a freedwoman of a woman, for herself and for her freedwoman daughter Obulcia Hecate and for her freedman Numerius Obulcius Pharnax.
EDCS-34801119.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the dedication of a tomb by Obulcia Iucunda for herself, her daughter, and a freedman.

EDCS-34801120.translation: To Gnaeus Popidius Secundus, son of Gnaeus; to Satria Arescosa, freedwoman of Marcus; and to Myrtale, a freedwoman.
EDCS-34801120.summary: This is a funerary dedication likely by Gnaeus Popidius Secundus to himself, his wife Satria Arescosa, and a freedwoman named Myrtale.

EDCS-34801125.translation: Publius Curtius Rufus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-34801125.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Curtius Rufus, identifying his father.

EDCS-34801131.translation: To Lucio Pactumeio Menodoro, the doctor, for his own bones, well.
EDCS-34801131.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucio Pactumeio Menodoro, a doctor, indicating his bones are well-placed.

EDCS-34801132.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Papia Chelido, identifying her former master.

EDCS-34801133.translation: To Marcus Papirius Chariton, freedman of Marcus; Papiria Nana, freedwoman of Marcus, co-freedwoman.
EDCS-34801133.summary: This epitaph records two individuals, Marcus Papirius Chariton and Papiria Nana, who were freedmen of the same master.

EDCS-34801136.translation: The sister of Secundus Visinius gives her bones here, placed.
EDCS-34801136.summary: This funerary inscription states that the sister of Secundus Visinius has placed her bones here.

EDCS-34801137.translation: Tertia, freedwoman of Suras Minutius, gave.
EDCS-34801137.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Tertia, a freedwoman, made a dedication.

EDCS-34801138.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication from Pacillia to Neicarion.

EDCS-34801139.translation: To Sextus Valerius Ichesius, freedman of Sextus, from his mother.
EDCS-34801139.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication from a mother to her son, Sextus Valerius Ichesius.

EDCS-34801140.translation: Vinuleia Vassa, freedwoman of Marcus, made this for herself and for her daughter Rufa, she lived 27 years.
EDCS-34801140.summary: This funerary epitaph records a woman, Vinuleia Vassa, who dedicated a monument for herself and her daughter Rufa, who died at age 27.

EDCS-34801143.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a freedwoman of Caius, identified as Opa[---].

EDCS-34801147.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Caius Pilotius Salvius, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-34801148.translation: To Arria Erotine, freedwoman of Caius, and to Arria Rufa, freedwoman of the woman [Arria], for themselves and their patroness.
EDCS-34801148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Arria Rufa for herself and her patroness, Arria Erotine, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-34801149.translation: To Numerius' freedman Philomusus, XXX thousand [denarii] to Secunda.
EDCS-34801149.summary: This is an inscription recording a bequest of 30,000 denarii from Numerius' freedman Philomusus to Secunda, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-34900732.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly recording a name and a number, with no clear context.

EDCS-34900742.translation: To the eternal god, for restored health, the man who dedicates this, Lucius Antonius Felicianus, dedicates a small shrine and a contiguous farm of thirty-three jugera with olive grove, extending 580 feet in every direction. From its annual income, on his birthday, the third day before the Kalends of September, after the rites are performed, he shall give a feast to the priests of Aug with these and the Samnites and the rest of our people of Allifae, with crusts and mulsum from 25 [asses]; if he neglects this or spends the money badly from greed, the profits and the municipal priests of Capulati shall take over the farm.
EDCS-34900742.summary: This is a complex dedication inscription from Allifae, dating to the Roman Imperial period, where Lucius Antonius Felicianus dedicates a shrine and farm to an eternal god for his restored health, stipulating its management and an annual feast from its income.

EDCS-34900743.translation: To the shades of the departed. Lucius Iunius Adauctus lived 64 years and Gemella Veneria lived 35 years. They died by the same fate, for both died at the same hour from eating mushrooms. He was involved in business and she in wool-working; and of their belongings no more was found than was sufficient to buy the pyre and pitch with which their bodies were to be cremated. However, the aforementioned property was acquired with the money of friends and a tomb was bought as a gift.
EDCS-34900743.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the deaths of Lucius Iunius Adauctus and Gemella Veneria, who perished together from mushroom poisoning, and details the modest means used for their cremation and burial.

EDCS-34900744.translation: Marcus Oppius, son of Marcus, father of the family, patron of the Allifae colony, gave this gift as duovir quinquennial.
EDCS-34900744.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Marcus Oppius, a prominent citizen and patron of the colony of Allifae, during his term as duovir quinquennial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34900745.summary: This is a very brief, fragmentary inscription, likely part of a longer text, possibly recording a dedication or a list of names, with no clear context.

EDCS-34900746.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly a funerary or dedicatory text, naming Crementius of Sidicinum, with no further context.

EDCS-34900748.translation: To Jupiter, best and greatest. Lucius Oppius, son of Caius, former scribe, dedicated this in his year as aedile with his own money.
EDCS-34900748.summary: This is a dedication inscription to Jupiter, likely from the Roman Imperial period, where Lucius Oppius, a former scribe, dedicates a monument using his own funds during his term as aedile.

EDCS-34900765.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription with the name Salvenale and the gentilician name Cerialis.

EDCS-34900772.translation: Antonius, son of Sextus, made (this monument) for himself while alive.
EDCS-34900772.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Antonius, son of Sextus, erected this monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-34900779.translation: To the Allifani, to Amaris, happily.
EDCS-34900779.summary: This is a dedication or greeting, possibly to a local deity or a group, wishing good fortune to Amaris of Allifani.

EDCS-35000057.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, mentioning the names Secundi and Titus.

EDCS-35001055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary or a dedication, to Annia, daughter of Gemella.

EDCS-35001058.translation: Annnius Hannon, son of Marcus, ordered (this monument) to be made by his heir [ex testam]ento.
EDCS-35001058.summary: This funerary inscription records that Annnius Hannon, son of Marcus, mandated the construction of his monument through his will.

EDCS-35100438.translation: Cnäus Statius Copiosus (for) Statia Glaphyra, freedwoman of a woman, and for himself and his family; this monument or tomb will not pass to an external heir.
EDCS-35100438.summary: This funerary inscription records that Cnäus Statius Copiosus established a monument for Statia Glaphyra and his own family, stipulating it would not pass to an outside heir.

EDCS-35200407.translation: Here Lucianus rests in good peace, innocent, gentle, mild, cheerful, lived as a friend with friends for more or less 50 years, with no complaint remaining. He was deposited in peace on the Kalends of September, when Flavius Marcianus and Zeno were the most illustrious consuls.
EDCS-35200407.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucianus, detailing his virtuous character, lifespan, and burial date during the consulship of Flavius Marcianus and Zeno.

EDCS-35400772.translation: Of Mnesteris, of Caius Calpetanius Favor.
EDCS-35400772.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely indicating ownership or dedication of a tomb or object to Mnesteris, possibly belonging to Caius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400773.summary: This is a dedication or ownership inscription, possibly related to a property or object belonging to Castus and associated with Caesar Augustus.

EDCS-35400774.translation: From the potteries of Claudius Iullus.
EDCS-35400774.summary: This is a maker's mark on a pottery object, indicating its origin from the workshop of Claudius Iullus.

EDCS-35400776.translation: Favor, slave of Gnaeus Domitius, made this.
EDCS-35400776.summary: This is an epitaph or dedicatory inscription by Favor, a slave of Gnaeus Domitius, stating he made the object.

EDCS-35400791.translation: Of Hermetis, freedman of Caius Calpetanius Favor.
EDCS-35400791.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Hermetis, a freedman of Caius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400792.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Gaius Calvisius Amarantus.

EDCS-35400793.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Gaius Calvisius Amarantus.

EDCS-35400798.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Cuspius Melichrysum.

EDCS-35400799.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Fortunatus, associated with two individuals named Domitius.

EDCS-35400801.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Gaius Calpetanius Musophilus.

EDCS-35400808.translation: Of Hermetis, freedman of Caius Calpetanius Favor.
EDCS-35400808.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or patronage related to Hermetis, a freedman of Caius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400812.summary: This is a maker's inscription by Gaius Cassipontius, indicating he created the object.

EDCS-35400814.translation: From the pottery works of Claudia Marcellina, when Asiaticus II and Aquilinus were consuls.
EDCS-35400814.summary: This inscription records the origin of pottery, indicating it came from the workshop of Claudia Marcellina during the consulship of Asiaticus II and Aquilinus (likely AD 148).

EDCS-35400815.translation: From the pottery works of Lucius Cornelius Priscus.
EDCS-35400815.summary: This inscription marks pottery originating from the workshop of Lucius Cornelius Priscus.

EDCS-35400816.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or origin related to Lucius Cornelius Priscus.

EDCS-35400818.translation: From the estates of Cusinius Messalinus.
EDCS-35400818.summary: This inscription denotes goods originating from the estates of Cusinius Messalinus.

EDCS-35400819.translation: From the estates of Cusinius Messalinus.
EDCS-35400819.summary: This inscription denotes goods originating from the estates of Cusinius Messalinus.

EDCS-35400820.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or origin related to Publius Curtius Nysus.

EDCS-35400823.translation: Of Callistus, slave of the Domitii.
EDCS-35400823.summary: This inscription records the ownership of Callistus, who was a slave of the Domitii family.

EDCS-35400824.summary: This inscription identifies Primigenius as a slave belonging to the Domitii family.

EDCS-35400825.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or origin related to Marcus Curtius Metra.

EDCS-35400826.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or origin related to Guspius Sunerotes.

EDCS-35400827.summary: This inscription likely records the ownership or dedication by Cuspius Sunerotus.

EDCS-35400828.translation: Of Daphnis, slave of the Domitii
EDCS-35400828.summary: This inscription records Daphnis, a slave belonging to the Domitii family.

EDCS-35400830.summary: This inscription records Primigenius, a slave belonging to the Domitii family.

EDCS-35400831.summary: This inscription records Antiochus, a freedman of someone named Curtius.

EDCS-35400832.summary: This inscription records Caius Calvisius Amarantius, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-35400838.translation: Of Hermes, favored by Caius Calpetanius Favor
EDCS-35400838.summary: This inscription records Hermes, who was favored by Caius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400839.translation: Of Hermes, favored by Caius Calpetanius Favor
EDCS-35400839.summary: This inscription records Hermes, who was favored by Caius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400840.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Claudius Sabinus, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-35400841.translation: Of Anicetus, freedman of the Domitii
EDCS-35400841.summary: This inscription records Anicetus, a freedman belonging to the Domitii family.

EDCS-35400843.translation: From the workshops of Claudius Iullus
EDCS-35400843.summary: This inscription indicates that the object or place originates from the workshops of Claudius Iullus.

EDCS-35400844.translation: To the Favorable Powers of Gaius Calpetanius Favor.
EDCS-35400844.summary: This is a dedication to the Favorable Powers by Gaius Calpetanius Favor, likely a freedman or slave.

EDCS-35400849.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Cornelius Hilarus.

EDCS-35400850.summary: This is a dedication to Cuspius Melichrysius.

EDCS-35400851.summary: This inscription records Hermes, a freedman or slave belonging to Gaius Calpetanius Favor.

EDCS-35400852.translation: To Marcus Cercinius Fructus, son of Sextus Allius Fortunatus.
EDCS-35400852.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Cercinius Fructus, son of Sextus Allius Fortunatus.

EDCS-35400855.translation: Fortunatus, slave of the two Domitii, made this.
EDCS-35400855.summary: This is a dedication made by Fortunatus, a slave belonging to the two Domitii.

EDCS-35400856.translation: Primigenius, slave of the two Domitii, made this.

EDCS-36100386.translation: Of Gnaeus Domitius Charito, who made it; may he prosper.

EDCS-36100387.translation: Of Gnaeus Domitius Evaristus, who made it; may he prosper.
EDCS-36100387.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory inscription for Gnaeus Domitius Evaristus, identifying him as the maker and wishing him prosperity.

EDCS-36100389.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or memorial for Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-36100390.translation: From the estates of Domitia, daughter of Publius, Lucilla, belonging to Aulus Cornelius Clodianus.

EDCS-36100391.translation: Pottery work from the estates of Lucilla Vera, belonging to Quintus Flavius Aprilis.

EDCS-36100393.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple ownership mark or dedication by Gnaeus Domitius Clemens.

EDCS-36100394.translation: For Abascantus, freedman of Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, under the consuls Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-36100394.summary: This inscription is a dedication or record of service related to Abascantus and Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, dated by the consuls Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-36100395.summary: This inscription is likely a property or ownership marker for Fadius Crescens.

EDCS-36400247.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated to Consia Octavia Paulina, a priestess, with the land grant approved by local officials.

EDCS-36400248.translation: Catulus Agapitus, formerly a consul, repaired (this).

EDCS-37400001.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Victoria Augusta, set up by Fabia Natalis at her own expense, likely during the Imperial period.

EDCS-37801285.translation: To Petronius Probus, a man of consular rank, and Anicia Proba, a woman of consular rank.
EDCS-37801285.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph honoring both Petronius Probus and Anicia Proba, both of high social standing (vir clarissimus), likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-37801293.translation: To Laurentius, a man of praiseworthy character.

EDCS-38000254.summary: This inscription records administrative details concerning Emperor Trajan's property or a public work, supervised by the procurator Hebrus.

EDCS-38000865.summary: This is a funerary inscription in Greek for Sarra, her son, and two daughters, indicating their burial place and ethnic/religious affiliation.

EDCS-38000867.summary: This is a bilingual funerary inscription in Greek for Dori(a)s and Martina, indicating their burial and repose in peace.

EDCS-38000871.translation: Claudius Ioses the archon lived for 25 years.

EDCS-38001191.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Ostiensius Felicissimus erected a monument, likely funerary.

EDCS-38001194.summary: This is a genitive inscription, probably for a tombstone or a dedication, naming Lucius Marcius Germanus.

EDCS-38001208.translation: Of Tiberius Caesar and Julia Augusta.

EDCS-38100022.translation: To my most beloved wife, Marcus Ulpius Dorion made [this] for [her], well deserving.
EDCS-38100022.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Marcus Ulpius Dorion dedicating a monument to his deserving wife.

EDCS-38100033.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Venus by Quintus Raecius.

EDCS-38100039.translation: To Marcia Elpis, his devoted wife, Aulus Veidius [dedicated this] Advotus.
EDCS-38100039.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Aulus Veidius Advotus to his devoted wife Marcia Elpis.

EDCS-38100042.translation: The parents [dedicated] a place to Fila.
EDCS-38100042.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a place by parents to someone named Fila.

EDCS-38100050.translation: [---] Marcellus Claudius, son of Bellicius Sollers, an assistant pontiff, imperial procurator, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-38100050.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument at his own expense by Marcellus Claudius, an imperial procurator, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-38100054.translation: Aulus Murrius Alexander, freedman of Decimus, master of the district, gave an altar to Hercules Opsequens, willingly and deservedly; Publius Murrius Phileros, freedman of Publius, master, restored it; Gnaeus Magnus [also participated].
EDCS-38100054.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to Hercules Opsequens by Aulus Murrius Alexander, master of the district, and its restoration by Publius Murrius Phileros, also a master, with Gnaeus Magnus involved, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-38100055.translation: To Atria Moscharus, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-38100055.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Atria Moscharus, identified as a distinguished woman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-38100056.summary: This inscription appears to be an ownership mark or a dedication related to Quinti Vitelli Alexidis, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-38100061.translation: Here lies the sweet soul Claudia Victoria, who departed this life cruelly. May she find refreshment in dreams. She lived 3 years, 12 months, 22 days. Chrispus and Iulia, her parents, made this.
EDCS-38100061.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Claudia Victoria, recording her short life and commemorating her parents, Chrispus and Iulia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-38100062.translation: Flavius Respectus made this for his well-deserving mother, Flavia Athenaïs. Marius Alexander and Marius Felix, grandsons, [dedicated this to] the priestess of Bona Dea, who lived 7 years, 20 days, and [some] hours. The marble worker carved it with the care of E. L. A.
EDCS-38100062.summary: This tombstone inscription honors Flavia Athenaïs, mother of Flavius Respectus and grandmother of Marius Alexander and Marius Felix, who was a priestess of Bona Dea, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-38100063.translation: Of Publius Tremelius, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, Praeco; of Attia Chelidonis, freedwoman of Publius; of the freedman Romani, of Publius Tremelius; of the freedwoman Albana, of Publius Attius.
EDCS-38100063.summary: This inscription lists individuals, likely related to property ownership or family lineage, connected to Publius Tremelius, Attia Chelidonis, and others, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-38100066.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial from Aelia Aste to Aelia Aste, possibly a mother and daughter or a dedication to oneself, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-38100067.translation: Of Lucius Novius Crispinus, of Lucius Novius Crispinus.

EDCS-38100070.translation: Of Spendophorus, freedman of Augustus, from the bedroom.

EDCS-38100077.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Vettennius Felix.

EDCS-38100083.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Acilius Fortunatus made this for his most cherished wife, who lived 37 years and 3 months.
EDCS-38100083.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Acilius Fortunatus for his wife, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-38100084.translation: Made for the departed spirits. Batinianus made this for his deserving brother Agathopus, who lived [X] years.
EDCS-38100084.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Batinianus for his brother Agathopus, noting the brother's lifespan.

EDCS-38100085.translation: Made for the departed spirits. Baebia Mercuria made this for her grandson Titus Helvius Hymnus and for Lucius Vianu s, most devoted, who lived 4 years, 5 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-38100085.summary: This funerary dedication by Baebia Mercuria honors her grandson Titus Helvius Hymnus and Lucius Vianus, providing their ages at death.

EDCS-38100086.translation: For the departed spirits. Partamenis lived 20 years. His most unhappy mother made this.
EDCS-38100086.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a grieving mother for her son Partamenis, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-38100088.translation: For Adventa, who lived 40 years and 2 months. Her daughter Trophime made this.
EDCS-38100088.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Trophime for her mother Adventa, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-38100089.translation: For the departed spirits. Firmianus made this for his incomparable wife Prosperitas, deserving of all good things, who lived 35 years, 4 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-38100089.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Firmianus for his wife Prosperitas, noting her lifespan and his devotion.

EDCS-38100090.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription referring to a bequest from the will of Arruntius.

EDCS-38100091.translation: Publius Aemilius Victor made this for Tribatia Marcellina.
EDCS-38100091.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Publius Aemilius Victor for Tribatia Marcellina, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-38100094.translation: Demetrius, slave of Lucius Antonius Albus, made this for Lucius Antonius Albus.
EDCS-38100094.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a slave named Demetrius for his master, Lucius Antonius Albus.

EDCS-38100095.translation: Caius Atticus lived... Attia [his mother/wife?] C...
EDCS-38100095.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Caius Atticus and Attia, likely recording a life span or a relationship.

EDCS-38100096.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Aphrodisius, father, for his son Gaius Mallius Abascantus, lived 8 months and 4 days.

EDCS-38100097.translation: Lucius Pullaienus Sabinus made this for his nurse, Pullaiena Privata.
EDCS-38100097.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Pullaienus Sabinus for his nurse, Pullaiena Privata.

EDCS-38100103.translation: To the Spirits of the departed, for Macrothymia.
EDCS-38100103.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a person named Macrothymia.

EDCS-38100104.translation: Aulernius Phileros made this for Cinia Philotis, for herself and her husband.
EDCS-38100104.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Aulernius Phileros for Cinia Philotis and her husband, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-38100112.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Annius Fortunatus Felix, possibly on a monument or building.

EDCS-38100116.translation: Of Marcus Orcius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-38100118.summary: This is the name of an individual, likely Marcus Orcevius.

EDCS-38100121.translation: Oscum and SAII, Aulus Hiritius, legate of Caesar, for our...

EDCS-38100124.translation: To Fortuna Primigenia, Marcus Terentius Sozon, gave the statue.
EDCS-38100124.summary: This is a dedication of a statue to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia by Marcus Terentius Sozon.

EDCS-38100127.translation: Pa...larius willingly and deservedly gave this gift to Fortuna Primigenia; sacred.
EDCS-38100127.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Fortuna Primigenia by Pa...larius.

EDCS-38100133.translation: ...us, freedman of Lucius Caius, to Hercules.

EDCS-38100134.translation: Lucius Aponius Mitheres, with his father, gave this gift to Jupiter Optimus.
EDCS-38100134.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus by Lucius Aponius Mitheres and his father.

EDCS-38100136.translation: Caius Verginius Primus and mia Thu... fulfilled their vow.

EDCS-38100147.translation: NIEI and Eros, son of Lucius, Ann...
