EDCS-39100156.translation: With good fortune! The Alexandrian synod, devoted to the Emperor and Rome, honored Titus Flavius Kyreinas Archibios of Alexandria, lifelong High Priest, Victor of the Xystos, who won the Olympic Games for boys in the 176th Olympiad and the 177th Olympiad in the pankration for men, and at Rome at the great Capitoline Games won the pankration for boys in the third penteteris and in the fourth won the pankration for men and was crowned, and in the fifth was crowned in the pankration for men, and in the sixth was crowned similarly in the pankration for men, first among men at Herakleia at the Neronian Games for the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, crowned in the pankration for boys and in the pankration for men at the Pythian Games, and in the following Pythiad won wrestling and pankration for men, and in the following pankration for men, first among men at Nemea won the pankration for boys, and three times consecutively won the pankration for men, first among men, and won wrestling and pankration for boys at the Actian Games, and in the following won the pankration for men, first among men, won the pankration for boys at Neapolis, and twice consecutively won wrestling and pankration for boys, and twice consecutively won wrestling and pankration for men, and won the pankration for men, first among men, at the Balbillian Games in Ephesos for wrestling, boxing, and pankration for men, first among men, and won the pankration for boys at the sacred penteteric contest in Antiochia at the Actian Games, and in the following penteteris won wrestling and boxing for boys and in the following won pankration for men, and in the following similarly won pankration for men, first among men, won wrestling and pankration for boys at Smyrna for the common festival of Asia, and won the pankration for boys at the sacred penteteric contest in Alexandria at the Actian Games, and after one penteteris won pankration for men, and in the following similarly won pankration for men, and in the following won wrestling and pankration for men, first among men. He also possesses the shield from Argos and has won many other penteteric contests in wrestling and pankration for boys and men.
EDCS-39100156.summary: This is a dedication by the Alexandrian synod honoring Titus Flavius Kyreinas Archibios, a highly decorated athlete who excelled in various games and disciplines, likely in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-39100157.translation: To Titus Flavius Evanthos, son of Titus, who won the Italian Roman Sebasta Isoolympia for boys in political events, dedicated two statues of the Dioscuri in the phratry, along with Titus Flavius Zosimus, his brother, who won in the same contest and received the prize. The phratriarchs, Eumelidae, in return for the honors, dedicated (these) to Sevérus and Herennianus, consuls, five days before the Ides of March. Titus Flavius Zosimus and Flavia Fortunata, parents, having dedicated lamps with lamps and altars to the Dioscuri, again consecrated (them) to the Sebasta.
EDCS-39100157.summary: This is a dedication of statues and offerings by parents to the Dioscuri and the Sebasta, honoring their sons, Titus Flavius Evanthos and Titus Flavius Zosimus, for athletic victories, likely in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-39100163.translation: Apollonius, son of Ammonius, Alexandrian, in the Sebastean judgment, pankratiast. Serapion, son of Publius, Alexandrian, wrestler. Aulus Postumius Isidorus, Alexandrian, in the Sebastean judgment, pentathlete.
EDCS-39100163.summary: This inscription lists athletes from Alexandria who participated in the Sebastean Games, possibly during the reign of the Antonines.

EDCS-39100164.translation: Arou, Antiochene, in the Sebastean judgment, boxer. Nikaios, pankratiast. Inou, Antiochene, ...
EDCS-39100164.summary: This inscription lists athletes, likely from Antioch and Nicaea, who participated in the Sebastean Games as boxers and pankratiasts, with some names being incomplete.

EDCS-39100166.translation: Tettia Casta, priestess of the women's house, by her life, decrees. Under the consulship of Caesar, son of Augustus, Domitianus, and Gaius Valerius Festus, on the 14th day before the Kalends of July, recorded. Present: Lucius Fruggi Cornelius, Kerialis, Junius. Regarding whom Tranquillus Rufus, the proconsul, reported to those in attendance: regarding this matter, he so pleased the opinion of all, acknowledging that the premature death of Tettia Casta, a woman who had shown great zeal for the piety of all and for the goodwill of the fatherland, by making countless offerings of silver statues to the gods, and by generously benefiting the city, is a common grief. To honor her with a statue and a shield inscribed with her name, and to bury her at public expense, with the care of her relatives, whom it is difficult to console, to give a pound of incense and a place for burial, and to expend for these things. Under the consulship of Caesar, son of Augustus, Domitianus, and Gaius Valerius Festus, on the 10th day before the Kalends of July, recorded. Present: Granius Rufus, Lucius Pudes, Poppaeus Severus. Regarding whom Fulvius Probus, the archon, reported to those in attendance: regarding this matter, he so pleased the public expense, which the council, sympathizing, voted to Tettia Casta, and to crown her with a golden crown, testifying to her life with public praise. Under the consulship of Lucius Flavius Fimbria and Ateilius Barbarus, recorded. Present: Ariston, Bukku, Auillius Arrianus, Verrius Liberalis. Regarding whom Julius Leuuiianus, the proconsul, reported to those in attendance: regarding this matter, he so pleased to permit Tettia to build a tomb on a plot of land from the wall, six cubits in width, and from the stele in all directions, no one else is to be given burial in the same place. Domitius Lepidus and to his most sweet mother and Lucius Domitius to his wife.
EDCS-39100166.summary: This is a complex decree honoring Tettia Casta, a pious and generous woman, with public burial, a statue, a shield, and a golden crown, with various officials and dates recorded, likely in the late 1st century CE.

EDCS-39100168.summary: This is a simple greeting inscribed on a monument, likely a tombstone, for Aigle, daughter of Zoilus.

EDCS-39100169.translation: Here, covering the sacred head in the earth, lies the divine Alcibiades, adorner of heroic men. Aurelia Atalante made (this) for her well-lived patron.
EDCS-39100169.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated by Aurelia Atalante to her patron, Alcibiades, who is described as a divine hero, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-39100170.translation: Ammias, daughter of Asclepiades, good, greetings.
EDCS-39100170.summary: This is a tombstone inscription with a simple greeting for Ammias, daughter of Asclepiades.

EDCS-39100172.translation: Antiochus, son of Alexander, from Laodicea, good, greetings.
EDCS-39100172.summary: This is a tombstone inscription with a simple greeting for Antiochus, son of Alexander, from Laodicea.

EDCS-39100173.translation: Be of good courage, Antonius, most fortunate, aged 56.
EDCS-39100173.summary: This is a tombstone inscription with an encouraging message and the age of the deceased, Antonius, who died at 56.

EDCS-39100175.translation: Messenger of Persephone, Hermes, whom do you escort to this place / into the uninviting Tartarus of Hades? / Some grim fate snatched Ariston from the light, / though the boy is only seven years old. / Weeping Pluto, you do not distribute all mortal breaths; / what unripe fruits of youth do you harvest?
EDCS-39100175.summary: A funerary epigram for a seven-year-old boy named Ariston, lamenting his untimely death and addressing Hermes, the escort of souls.

EDCS-39100176.translation: Daphnis made this monument of friendship for Astis, / loving him when alive and longing for him when dead.
EDCS-39100176.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Daphnis to Astis, expressing enduring affection.

EDCS-39100177.summary: The name and origin of an individual, likely an epitaph.

EDCS-39100178.translation: From Augeas. [He] lies here. Let no one wrong [this] person, by the gods.
EDCS-39100178.summary: A warning inscribed on a grave, invoking divine authority to prevent desecration.

EDCS-39100181.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to a beloved child named Dailos.

EDCS-39100199.translation: Stand, stranger, and behold this monument to Cleopatra, / whom Envy, not Time, brought down to Hades. / For beauty, for which Cyprus granted her first place, / and Athena, pleasant works of prudence, / and the Muse, mixing wisdom and the dear, sweet harmony in lovely songs. / And knowing that nothing is sweeter for mortals than life, / live a good life, stretching forth with a favorable breeze of joy. / Even if your new beauty, O Cleopatra, is hidden, / and the tomb and the perishable body have attained dust, / yet the virtue of your life always lives among the living, / the soul testifying to your glorious prudence.
EDCS-39100199.summary: A funerary epigram for Cleopatra, celebrating her beauty, virtues, wisdom, and musical talents, and lamenting her premature death.

EDCS-39100200.translation: This is Kosmos, who prosperously fulfilled all good things. / Here his master placed me with his own hands. / He came weeping to my tomb, believe me. / He stood not far from me, his deceased self, / and as I was an infant, he who was himself an infant longed for me. / And now the old man buries an old man, the devoted one. / My master gave me more than life eternally, / not one of the many, but of a more illustrious family. / Fannianos to Nauios Kosmos.
EDCS-39100200.summary: A funerary epitaph for Kosmos, a distinguished individual, dedicated by his master Fannianos, highlighting their close relationship from infancy to old age.

EDCS-39100203.translation: To Meliton, a good child, who lived 18 years. From his teacher.
EDCS-39100203.summary: This is a tombstone inscription commemorating a boy named Meliton, set up by his teacher, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100205.summary: This is a funerary epigram or greeting, likely on a tomb, for Menophilos, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100207.translation: To Noubia Hermione, daughter. Hermes and Perpetua, parents, in memory. To the Chthonic Gods.
EDCS-39100207.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Noubia Hermione, set up by her parents Hermes and Perpetua, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100208.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Porkia Paula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100210.translation: Procles and Chryseis, both daughters. Their parents made this tombstone for them in memory. To the Chthonic Gods.
EDCS-39100210.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their two daughters, Procles and Chryseis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100211.translation: To Sarapias, also called Ammia Laodice. Marcellus, her husband, for her love. She lived 19 years, 11 months, 5 days.
EDCS-39100211.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sarapias (also known as Ammia Laodice), set up by her husband Marcellus, dated by her age to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100212.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sergius Atticus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100213.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sucesso, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100214.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Stlaccia Storge, possibly a graffito or a small marker, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100219.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription identifying Foronius as the son of Apollophanes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39100220.summary: This is a simple greeting inscription, likely from a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-39100243.translation: To Asclepius and Hygieia, Protogenes gives thanks.
EDCS-39100243.summary: This is a votive inscription expressing gratitude to the gods of healing, Asclepius and Hygieia.

EDCS-39100245.translation: Agathocles, son of Tryphon, lived 90 years. Nigreinos, his brother, dedicated this.
EDCS-39100245.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Agathocles and identifies his brother Nigreinos as the dedicator.

EDCS-39100246.summary: This funerary inscription records the name and age of a young man, Androneikos.

EDCS-39100248.translation: Severianos Asklepiodotos to his most beloved wife, Aurelia Flavia Arria Nicomedissa, who lived 15 years, in memory.
EDCS-39100248.summary: This funerary inscription is a memorial erected by Severianos Asklepiodotos for his wife Aurelia Flavia Arria Nicomedissa, who died at a young age.

EDCS-39100251.translation: To Diodotos, son of Menodotos, of Korykion, to Hygeinos, his most beloved grandson.
EDCS-39100251.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Diodotos, a resident of Korykion, and his grandson Hygeinos.

EDCS-39100253.translation: Epikrates, son of Epikrates, of Nikomedeia, lived 60 years. Farewell.
EDCS-39100253.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, origin, and age of Epikrates, with a farewell to passersby.

EDCS-39100254.translation: Tholomaios, son of Thaimallos, also called Maximus, of Petra, lived 33 years.
EDCS-39100254.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, alternative name, origin, and age of the deceased, Tholomaios.

EDCS-39100255.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Here I lie, Hermes, citizen of Athens, of the Attic soil. Kallistos, a friend, made this tomb monument, having lived twenty years.
EDCS-39100255.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Chthonic Gods and records the deceased Hermes, an Athenian citizen, with his friend Kallistos as the dedicator, mentioning his age.

EDCS-39100256.translation: Kallibia, daughter of Phileggyos, of Kyrene.
EDCS-39100256.summary: This inscription simply records the name and patronymic of Kallibia, indicating her origin from Kyrene, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-39100257.translation: To the Chthonian Gods. Kallityche lies here, who lived 14 years, and Gelasios, who lived 3 years and 5 months. Aurelia Vibibia Sabina [made this] in memory of her worthy foster children.
EDCS-39100257.summary: This is a funerary epigram by Aurelia Vibibia Sabina for her foster children Kallityche and Gelasios, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100259.translation: To the Divine Daemones, from Kastor, son of Blastos, of Korykeion.
EDCS-39100259.summary: This is a dedication to the Chthonian Gods (Daemones) by Kastor, son of Blastos, from Korykeion, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-39100261.translation: For Peios, who lived 10 years, and Nepotil(l)a, who lived 5 years and 5 months.
EDCS-39100261.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating the short lives of Peios and Nepotilla, likely children, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100262.translation: Marcus Septimius [---]tarianus [---] lived [about 40?] years. His patron made [this] for his worthy freedman.
EDCS-39100262.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a patron for his freedman, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100263.translation: Seilios, son of Pompeios, of Korykion, shipowner.
EDCS-39100263.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Seilios as a shipowner from Korykion, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100264.translation: Lucius Trebonius Iambos [made this] for Trebonia Evodia, his wife, in memory.
EDCS-39100264.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Trebonius Iambos for his wife Trebonia Evodia, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100265.translation: Octavia, freedwoman of Gaius, Oikoumene, [made this] for Publius Fulvius Blaestus, freedman of Publius, in memory.
EDCS-39100265.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Octavia, a freedwoman, for Publius Fulvius Blaestus, likely her husband or a close relative, also a freedman.

EDCS-39100282.translation: O UAIA, serpent-bearer, O YTUS AUSAIPEM SN AE. I adjure you, daemones and spirits in this place, both female and male, by the holy name Hermes I THPHEDRDRDRACHARAR DHFTHI, Iao I A BEZEBU THLA ANOUBIS DPHALAL LKTIPAOMOU, Hades the king of all, rise up! King of the dead, arise with the chthonian gods. For these things shall happen through Valeria Kodratilla, whom Valeria Eunoia bore, whom Valerius Mystikos sowed. As I clearly announce to all, may the things accomplished in darkness be hateful. PHO PHORML MENORSEPHEN THS MEN TH I will cut off the wrath... towards those dear to the light, for anger, for the wrath of the gods. Let Valeria Kodratilla, whom Valeria Eunoia bore, whom Valerius Mystikos sowed, come to me, may she hate her, may forgetfulness of her take hold of Vetruvius Felix, whom Vetrubia Maximilla bore, whom Vetruvius Euelpistus sowed. CHEM TYPHON M I OCHI barbarous OYTH DAI IDCHOM, give [strength] to come forth for Vetruvius Felix, whom Vetrubia Maximilla bore, whom Vetruvius Euelpistus sowed, to come forth and to take forgetfulness of the desires of Valeria Kodratilla, whom Valerius Mystikos sowed, whom Valeria Eunoia bore, and may you hold her down with the utmost punishments, because she was the first to break faith with Felix, her husband. And hear YMTO YA
EDCS-39100282.summary: This is a complex magical curse inscription invoking chthonian deities and spirits to punish Valeria Kodratilla for breaking faith with her husband, Vetruvius Felix, and causing him suffering.

EDCS-39100285.translation: To the Chthonian Gods. Zoilus, fellow citizen of Onesikrates of Nikomedeia, made [this] in memory of his friend, who lived 60 years. Greetings.
EDCS-39100285.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Zoilus for his friend, specifying the friend's origin and age, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100288.translation: To the Daemones. Sainius Epaphroditus, who lived one year, 8 months, 20 days. Sainius Epaphroditus and Saina Eukarpia, his parents, made [this] in memory.
EDCS-39100288.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sainius Epaphroditus, who died in infancy, made by his parents, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100289.translation: Elpidios, sailor of the most illustrious Symmachoi, lies here.
EDCS-39100289.summary: A funerary inscription for Elpidios, a sailor, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100297.translation: Julia Marcella, daughter of Julius Bassus, a Commagenian, fare you well without sorrow.
EDCS-39100297.summary: A funerary epitaph for Julia Marcella, daughter of Julius Bassus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100298.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, naming Pakkios Arrios Nuiou.

EDCS-39100299.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Tryphaena, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100306.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Corinthos Tropianos, who held the office of agoranomos, likely from a Greek city during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100311.translation: Athanodoros, son of Agesandros, the Rhodian, made it.
EDCS-39100311.summary: An artist's signature, identifying Athanodoros of Rhodes as the maker of the object, likely from the Hellenistic or Roman period.

EDCS-39100312.translation: Theano, daughter of Eunikos(?), fare you well.
EDCS-39100312.summary: A funerary epitaph for Theano, daughter of Eunikos, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100314.translation: Tauriske, daughter of Staios, fare you well.
EDCS-39100314.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tauriske, daughter of Staios, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100315.translation: O dwellers in the gloomy region below, good spirits, receive me, most wretched, into Hades, snatched not by the judgment of the Fates but by violent, sudden death, angered, just now at the peak of my progress under my master, and now depriving me of my parents' hope, not having completed ten or even twenty years, I weep, I do not see the light. My name is Hypos. I beg my fellow traveler and my parents no longer to weep for me, the wretched.
EDCS-39100315.summary: A tragic funerary poem for Hypos, who died suddenly and young (under 20) while in service, lamenting his lost life and parents' grief, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100319.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Sanctianus Callicles Prousus, who lived 35 years, from the Upian district. Tiberius Claudius Julianus Thrasymedes to his sweetest brother, for the sake of memory. Farewell.
EDCS-39100319.summary: A funerary dedication from Tiberius Claudius Julianus Thrasymedes to his brother Tiberius Claudius Sanctianus Callicles Prousus, who died at age 35, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-39100374.translation: Serenus Xiphidius, the most excellent neokoros, dedicated this from his own funds.
EDCS-39100374.summary: This is a dedication by Serenus Xiphidius, who held the office of neokoros, to an unspecified deity.

EDCS-39100388.translation: Farewell! Magnis from Phrygian Scythia; the steep Maiden nurtured me in the fertile plain of Manthius. Having left the city of Magnes, sail well!
EDCS-39100388.summary: This is a farewell inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, from Magnes in Phrygia, mentioning a person named Magnis and the plain of Manthius.

EDCS-39100396.translation: To the Gods and Daimons, Chrestes Dionysios, his son, made this for his most sweet mother, who lived 40 years.
EDCS-39100396.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Chrestes Dionysios for his mother, who lived 40 years and was dedicated to the Gods and Daimons.

EDCS-39100398.translation: And if anyone dares to be buried with this one, he will pay to the fiscus three times two thousand, and to Portus he will deposit as much. Furthermore, he will pay the penalty for his reckless wrongdoing.
EDCS-39100398.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a severe penalty for unauthorized burials, intended to protect the tomb of the deceased and possibly dedicating funds to the fiscus and Portus.

EDCS-39100402.translation: Successus to Charis in the Lord, greetings.
EDCS-39100402.summary: This is a short greeting inscription from Successus to Charis, possibly a personal note or dedication within a Christian context.

EDCS-39100443.translation: To Isis Pharia, Isis of Menouthi, for the salvation of our lord the Emperor Antoninus.
EDCS-39100443.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Isis, specifically to her cults in Pharia and Menouthi, for the well-being of Emperor Antoninus.

EDCS-39100831.translation: Aurelius Aphrodisius, a soldier of the praetorian guard, to Lucius Aelianus, my guardian, this tomb, and I wish that no one else be buried here. If anyone dares, he will pay a fine of 500 denarii to the most sacred treasury and 200 denarii to the heirs. Farewell.
EDCS-39100831.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Aurelius Aphrodisius, a praetorian soldier, for his guardian Lucius Aelianus, stipulating penalties for unauthorized burials.

EDCS-39101039.translation: To Julia Zenaïs, venerable, incomparable, and ever-memorable soul, Julius Maximos, her husband, dedicated this monument as a remembrance. She, leaving him, brought everlasting sorrow to her husband and parents, most longed-for...
EDCS-39101039.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julia Zenaïs, dedicated by her husband Julius Maximos, expressing deep grief and remembrance.

EDCS-39101925.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Aulus Vibius Diomedes.

EDCS-39300215.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Gaius Curiatius Cosanus.

EDCS-39501151.summary: This inscription appears to be a name, likely an owner or craftsman, associated with Athenian origin.

EDCS-39501385.summary: This inscription likely records a period of office or a context associated with Archidamus of Agriania.

EDCS-39501400.summary: This inscription appears to be a possessive or genitive phrase, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication by Hyllonius of Pacius.

EDCS-39501405.summary: This is a personal dedication or epitaph addressed to Evodus.

EDCS-39501490.translation: From the potteries of Domitia, wife of Domitianus, of Caius Calvisius Mnester Calveis.
EDCS-39501490.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of pottery from the workshops of Domitia and Mnester, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-39700031.translation: Marcus Samiarius, Caius Messienus, Sextus Caesius, Quintus Caleius, Caius Salvius, Lucius Curtius Statiolenus, II duovir; Dolabella, II duovir; Rotanius, aedile; Quintus Flavius, quaestor; Publius Cornelius, II duovir; Lucius Nassius, aedile; Caius Sertorius, quaestor; Titus Lucretius, II duovir; Caius Cassius, quaestor; Marcus Petronius, quinquennial official; Quintus Arrasidius, aedile; Titus Aponius, quaestor.
EDCS-39700031.summary: This is a list of magistrates and officials, including duovirs, aediles, quaestors, and a quinquennial official, likely from a Roman colony or municipality, possibly dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-39700179.translation: Atticus of Sardis, pentathlon; [---] of Athens, wrestling; Lysimachus of Lacedaemon, boxing; Alcimus, also called Mikkalos of Sardis.
EDCS-39700179.summary: This inscription lists victors in athletic games, specifying their events (pentathlon, wrestling, boxing) and origins (Sardis, Athens, Lacedaemon).

EDCS-39700200.translation: To Cominia Ploutogeneia, priestess of Demeter Thesmophorus, daughter of Leucius, wife of Pakkius Kaledos, of senatorial rank, and mother of Pakkius Kaledianus, of the office of agronomos, and grandmother of Kastrikios Pollion, of senatorial rank; Tiberius Kastrikios Kaledianus, having served as demarch, to his great-grandmother, for piety, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-39700200.summary: This is a dedication to Cominia Ploutogeneia by her descendant Tiberius Kastrikios Kaledianus, honoring her various familial and religious roles, including priestess and matriarch, with the dedication made by senatorial decree.

EDCS-39700201.translation: Heia Licinia, farewell. Thus may all enjoy life's passage; and keep this tomb inviolate, of one who died young.
EDCS-39700201.summary: This is a Greek epitaph addressing the deceased Heia Licinia and warning mourners not to disturb her tomb, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-39900028.summary: This inscription identifies the maker or owner of brickwork as Iulius Titianus, indicating a product of his workshops.

EDCS-39900030.translation: From the pottery workshops of Gratia, daughter of Apollinus.
EDCS-39900030.summary: This inscription likely refers to pottery produced in the workshops of Gratia, daughter of Apollinus.

EDCS-39900031.translation: Of Lucius Aemilius Lenaeus, son of Lucius Aemilius Lenaeus.
EDCS-39900031.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker related to Lucius Aemilius Lenaeus.

EDCS-40000001.translation: Fortunatus, the slave of Gaius Vibius Donatus, made this.
EDCS-40000001.summary: This is a dedication by a slave named Fortunatus for his owner, Gaius Vibius Donatus.

EDCS-40000310.translation: 178 1/2 [sestertii] from the money-box of Marcus Terricius Atimetus, 177 1/2 [sestertii] of Varius.
EDCS-40000310.summary: This inscription records financial accounts or sums of money related to Marcus Terricius Atimetus and Varius.

EDCS-40000376.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or ownership mark of Gaius Galerius Restitutus.

EDCS-40000383.translation: In the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus, from the estates of Tiberius Claudius Quartus.
EDCS-40000383.summary: This inscription records property or transactions from the estates of Tiberius Claudius Quartus during the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-40000384.summary: This is likely a dedication or ownership mark of Titus Petisius Orpheus.

EDCS-40000385.summary: This inscription refers to Eupor, likely associated with or owned by Lucius Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-40000386.summary: This inscription refers to Patrobius, likely associated with or owned by Lucius Domitius Lupus.

EDCS-40000388.translation: Leo, the slave of Marcus Petronius Veteranus, made this.
EDCS-40000388.summary: This is a dedication by a slave named Leo for his owner, Marcus Petronius Veteranus.

EDCS-40000391.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording ownership or a dedication by Stabilio, son of Appius.

EDCS-40000393.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Domitius Lupus, likely for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-40000394.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the name Gnaeus Pompeius Herm(es?), possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-40000395.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Valerius Peplus, likely for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-40000396.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Caennius Salvitto, likely for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-40000405.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Licinius Licca, likely for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-40000406.summary: This inscription records the names of brothers identified as Marcus Licinius, possibly indicating joint ownership or a shared dedication.

EDCS-40000410.summary: This inscription records the name Claudia Prima, likely for ownership or dedication.

EDCS-40000412.translation: From the workshops of Marcus Varienus Clemens, Hilarus the slave made it.
EDCS-40000412.summary: This inscription records that Hilarus, a slave belonging to Marcus Varienus Clemens, made this object, likely a pottery item, indicating its origin and maker.

EDCS-40000413.translation: From the workshops of Marcus Varienus Clemens, Hilarus the slave made it.
EDCS-40000413.summary: This inscription records that Hilarus, a slave belonging to Marcus Varienus Clemens, made this object, likely a pottery item, indicating its origin and maker.

EDCS-40000415.summary: This is a private dedication or ownership mark by Caius Plaetorius Iustianus.

EDCS-40000418.summary: This is a private dedication or ownership mark by Titus Statilius Eutyches.

EDCS-40000530.translation: From the workshop of Fortunatus for Domitia Lucilla
EDCS-40000530.summary: This inscription indicates a product made by Fortunatus's workshop for Domitia Lucilla.

EDCS-42300089.translation: Pottery made from the estates of Vibius Aiacianus by Appius Quinquatralis
EDCS-42300089.summary: This inscription records pottery produced by Appius Quinquatralis from the estates of Vibius Aiacianus, indicating a pottery workshop and its owner/supplier.

EDCS-42300090.translation: From the estates of Vismatius Successus, Luscenus Celer
EDCS-42300090.summary: This inscription indicates that Luscenus Celer is associated with the estates of Vismatius Successus, possibly as a manager or owner.

EDCS-42300091.summary: This inscription identifies Vitalis as a freedman of the emperor, likely marking an object or property belonging to him.

EDCS-42300099.translation: In the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus, Claudius Crescens makes [this] from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens
EDCS-42300099.summary: This inscription records that Claudius Crescens created something (likely a monument or product) from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens, during the consulship of Titus Atilius Titianus and Marcus Squilla Gallicanus.

EDCS-42300100.translation: In the second consulship of Iuventius and the second consulship of Marcellus, from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens, under the care of Hedyne
EDCS-42300100.summary: This inscription indicates that goods or a product from the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens were managed by Hedyne during the second consulships of Iuventius and Marcellus.

EDCS-42300101.translation: Workshop of the highest private [property], the Boconian workshop
EDCS-42300101.summary: This inscription identifies a workshop as the 'highest private workshop' and names it the 'Boconian workshop', likely indicating its prestige and owner.

EDCS-42300102.translation: The workshop of the Domitian workshop of the Merchant.
EDCS-42300102.summary: This is a manufacturer's mark on pottery, likely from the Domitian workshop, indicating the owner was a merchant.

EDCS-42300107.translation: Papirius Crescens made this from the pottery works of Aulus Vicir Martius.
EDCS-42300107.summary: This is a maker's mark on pottery, indicating that Papirius Crescens produced it from the figlinae (pottery works) of Aulus Vicir Martius.

EDCS-42300108.translation: The workshop of the Domitian workshop of Victor.
EDCS-42300108.summary: This is a manufacturer's mark on pottery, likely from the Domitian workshop, indicating the owner was named Victor.

EDCS-42300124.summary: This is a repetition of a name, likely an owner or producer's mark on pottery or another object.

EDCS-42400085.translation: 1567 sesterces, which money, concerning an auction of Nymphius Lucius Junius Aquila, came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, with the commission less having been paid, Lucius Junius Aquila said he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, done at Pompeii on the 4th day before the Kalends of July, with Manius Acilius and Marcus Asinius as consuls, Sextus Numisius Iucundus, Lucius Neri Hyginus, Quintus Caecilius Attalus, Marcus Badius Hermas, Publius Paccius Cerinthus, Aulus Vettius Donatus, Publius Aefulanus Chrysanthus, Caius Nunnidius Synus, Lucius Junius Attalus, Lucius Junius Hermas, Paccius Donatus Crusa, Caius Nunnidius Synus, Nymphius; I have written that he received from Lucius Junius Aquila, by mandate and delegation, 1567 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, for the auction of Nymphius Junius Aquila.
EDCS-42400085.summary: This is a financial record dated to 44 BCE, detailing a transaction involving 1567 sesterces for an auction of Nymphius Junius Aquila, with Lucius Caecilius Iucundus acting as the financier and Lucius Junius Aquila as the recipient.

EDCS-42400086.translation: Done at Pompeii on the 8th day before the Kalends of June, with Manius Acilius Aviola and Marcus Asinius as consuls, of Marcus Obellius Firmus, Melissus, Fuscus.
EDCS-42400086.summary: This is a record of a transaction or legal act dated to 45 BCE, mentioning Marcus Obellius Firmus and two other individuals, likely relating to business dealings in Pompeii.

EDCS-42400088.translation: 38079 sesterces, which money, concerning an auction of Marcus Lucretius Leri, with the fifty percent commission less having been paid, Marcus Lucretius Lerus said he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, done at Pompeii on the 11th day before the Kalends of February, with Nero Caesar and Lucius Antistius as consuls, of Laelius Appuleius Severus, Lucretius Lerus Atullus, Euander, Laelius Princeps, Humnerotis, Sestius Maxs.
EDCS-42400088.summary: This is a financial record from 60 CE concerning 38,079 sesterces related to an auction of Marcus Lucretius Leri, with Lucius Caecilius Iucundus as the financier.

EDCS-42400089.translation: 8327 and a half sesterces, which money, concerning an auction of Lucius Papinius Probus, came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, with the commission less having been paid, Lucius Papinius Probus said he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, done at Pompeii, with Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Imperator and Lucius Antistius as consuls, Epidius P. IIVMI R LSEC IIIIII III Sori Popidi V. Nero CV.
EDCS-42400089.summary: This is a financial record from 55 CE detailing 8327.5 sesterces related to an auction of Lucius Papinius Probus, with Lucius Caecilius Iucundus acting as the financier.

EDCS-42400090.translation: Record of Babinia Secunda: 3934 sesterces, which money, concerning an auction of Babinia Secunda, came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, with the commission less having been paid, Babinia Secunda said she had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, done at Pompeii, with Nero Caesar and Lucius Antistius as consuls, Caius Cuspius Secundus, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Quintus Arrius Philetus, Numerius Popidius Amarantus, Numerius Herennius Castus, Lucius Junius Corinthus, Herennius Anthus, Publius Aefulanus Chrysanthus, ti Synerotis, Quintus Primi; with Nero Caesar and Lucius Antistius as consuls.
EDCS-42400090.summary: This is a financial record from 55-59 CE detailing 3934 sesterces related to an auction of Babinia Secunda, with Lucius Caecilius Iucundus as the financier.

EDCS-42400091.translation: Record of Murtius Asclepa: 7020 sesterces, which money, concerning an auction of Lucius Murtius Asclepa, came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, with the commission less having been paid, Lucius Murtius Ascelpas said he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, done at Pompeii, with Nero Caesar and Lucius Antistius Vetus as consuls, Lucius Laelius Fuscus, Quintus Apuleius Severus, Titus Soronius Eutychus, Lucius Laelius Trophimus Holcon, Lucius Junius Corinthus Vibullius Felicior, Lucius Sestius Cytissus, Junius Vibullius Citissus.
EDCS-42400091.summary: This is a financial record from 55-59 CE detailing 7020 sesterces from an auction of Lucius Murtius Asclepa, with Lucius Caecilius Iucundus acting as the financier.

EDCS-42400092.translation: Account of Publius Tiburtius Buttus: He says he has received 11,360 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Publius Tiburtius Buttus, with the commission not fully paid. Recorded at Pompeii under consuls Nero Caesar and Lucius Antistius. Witnesses: Quintus Appuleius Severus, Publius Tiburtius Buttus, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Marcus Fadius Diadumenus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, Aulus Velasius Terminalis, Publius Sittius Speratus, Marcus Gavius Bu[---], Lucius Ceius Quartio.
EDCS-42400092.summary: This inscription is an account or receipt for a payment of 11,360 sesterces related to an auction held by Publius Tiburtius Buttus, recorded at Pompeii in 65 CE.

EDCS-42400093.translation: Account of Numerius Istacidius Amicus: He says he has received 7,390 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Numerius Istacidius Amicus, paid on the first day of the Ides of January. Recorded at Pompeii the day before the Ides of December under consuls Gnaeus Cornelius and Titus Curtilius. Witnesses: Lucius Laelius Fuscus, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Numerius Istacidius Amicus, Publius Aefulanus Chrysanthus, Granius Coniunctus, Menander.
EDCS-42400093.summary: This inscription is an account or receipt for a payment of 7,390 sesterces related to an auction held by Numerius Istacidius Amicus, recorded at Pompeii in 55 CE.

EDCS-42400095.translation: Account of Lucius Ceius Quartio: He says he has received 2,795 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Lucius Ceius Quartio, with the commission not fully paid. Recorded at Pompeii under consuls Gnaeus Lentulus and Titus Curtilius. Witnesses: Quintus Appuleius Severus, Quintus Arrius Philetus, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Sextus Noni Onesimus, Quarti[---]. I have written at the request of Ceius Quartio that he received 2,795 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, based on the examination of signed tablets. Recorded at Pompeii.
EDCS-42400095.summary: This inscription is a receipt for 2,795 sesterces paid to Lucius Ceius Quartio from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction, with a note confirming the transaction and witnesses, dated to 55 CE.

EDCS-42400096.translation: Account of Messius Speratus: [List of witnesses including] Gnaeus Lentulus, Quintus Poppaeus Felix, Marcus Stronnius Secundus, Publius Paccius Cerinthus, Marcus Epidius Stephanus, Marcus Helvius Phoebus, Lucius Caecilius Hermes, Marcus Helvius Saturninus, Publius Terentius Erotis, Publius Furius Fortunatus, Aulus Messius Speratus.
EDCS-42400096.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of witnesses for an account or transaction, possibly related to an auction, with Messius Speratus as the primary figure, dated around 65-70 CE based on consul names in other inscriptions.

EDCS-42400098.translation: Account of Histria Ichimas: She says she has received 6,456.5 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Histria Ichimas, with the commission not fully paid. Recorded at Pompeii on the Nones of November under consuls Lucius Duvius and Publius Clodius. Witnesses: Caius Numitorius Bassus, Lucius Numisius Rarus, Aulus Veius Atticus, Decimus Caprasius Gobio, Lucius Valerius Peregrinus, Cestilius Philodemus, Caius Novellius Fortunatus, Aulus Alphius Abascantius, Lucius Ceius Felicionius. I have written at the request of Histria Ichimas herself that she received 6,456.5 sesterces from Lucius Iucundus for the auction conducted by her slave. Recorded at Pompeii on the Nones of November.
EDCS-42400098.summary: This inscription is a receipt for 6,456.5 sesterces paid to Histria Ichimas from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction conducted by her slave, recorded at Pompeii in 61 CE.

EDCS-42400099.translation: Account of Numerius Blaesius Fructus: He says he has received 6,875 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Numerius Blaesius Fructus, with the commission not fully paid. Recorded at Pompeii on the 15th day before the Kalends of January under consuls Lucius Duvius and Publius Clodius. Witnesses: Lucius Fadius Neptunus, Numerius Oppius Felicio, Gnaeus Helvius, Lucius Vettius Valentis Cerrinus, Numerius Blaesius Fructus, Numerius Veratius Atictus, Caius Vibius Cresimus. I, Numerius Blaesius Fructus, have written at the request of Lucius Duvius and Publius Clodius Thrasia that I received 6,875 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for my auction, based on the examination of signed tablets. Recorded at Pompeii.
EDCS-42400099.summary: This inscription is a receipt for 6,875 sesterces paid to Numerius Blaesius Fructus from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for his auction, with a confirmation of the amount and witnesses, dated to 61 CE.

EDCS-42400101.translation: 1,441.5 sesterces, which money came into the account of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Caesius Optata, with the commission not fully paid. Caesia Optata says she received [this amount] from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus. Recorded at Pompeii on the 7th day before the Kalends of February under consuls Nero Caesar II and Lucius Calpurnius. Witnesses: Pomponius Marcellus, Poppaea Sorix, [---] Erotis.
EDCS-42400101.summary: This inscription records a payment of 1,441.5 sesterces to Caesia Optata from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus related to an auction, recorded at Pompeii in 65 CE.

EDCS-42400103.translation: Account of Decimus Iunius Eros: He says he has received 4,192 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the auction of Decimus Iunius Eros, with the commission not fully paid. Recorded at Pompeii on the 7th Ides of April under consuls Nero Caesar II and Lucius Calpurnius. Witnesses: Marcus Messius Ba[---], Lucius Messius Pronimus, Alfius Vitalis, Gnaeus Helvius Apollonius Barbatus, Cato, Decimus Iunius Eros.
EDCS-42400103.summary: This inscription is a receipt for 4,192 sesterces paid to Decimus Iunius Eros from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction, recorded at Pompeii in 65 CE.

EDCS-42400104.translation: Under consuls Nero Caesar for the second time and Lucius Calpurnius Piso, on the 5th day before the Kalends of July. Aulus Messius Speratus writes that he has received 342 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from his auction, with the commission not fully paid. He says he is indebted to M[---]. Recorded at Pompeii. A summons to court on the 5th Ides [of August?]. Recorded under Nero.
EDCS-42400104.summary: This inscription is a receipt for 342 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus to Aulus Messius Speratus for an auction, and also records a legal summons, dated to 65 CE.

EDCS-42400109.translation: Under consuls Nero Claudius Lucius Calpurnius Piso, the third time. [Incomplete text, possibly related to accounts or payments.]
EDCS-42400109.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a heading or preamble to an account or official record, mentioning consuls Nero and Lucius Calpurnius Piso and a date (possibly the third consulship of Piso), circa 65-69 CE.

EDCS-42400112.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Opta by someone named Nero, likely an epitaph or dedication of a religious nature.

EDCS-42400114.translation: 1,000,000 sesterces, which money came into the bond of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Quintus Pompeius Patrophilus. He stated that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, on account of the first day before the Kalends of November, less the commission, in Pompeii, on the Ides of February, in the consulship of Publius Cornelius Dolabella and Marcus Cornelius Lentulus, from Numerius Tettienus Priscus, Sextus Pompeius A. T. E. I., Marcus Epidius Urbanus, Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, Eutyches Staius Ph., Quintus Pompeius Patrophilus, Publius Calvisius.
EDCS-42400114.summary: This is a financial record, a receipt for a large sum of money received by Quintus Pompeius Patrophilus from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus related to an auction, dated to 44 BCE.

EDCS-42400115.translation: Settlement for Hordionius and Fabius Chryserotus: 1,000,000 sesterces, which money came into the bond of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the received payments of Aulus Hordionius Philostorgus and Marcus Fabius Chryseros. They stated that they had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, for their respective shares, in Pompeii, on the 17th day before the Kalends of Publius, in the consulship of Quintus Valerius Bassus, Aulus Hordionius Philostorgus, Publius Terentius Priscus, Numerius Popidius Amaranthus, Marcus Rufellus Horus, Quintus Caecilius Attalus, Numerius Popidius Sodalionis, Marcus Fabius Chryseros, Gnaeus Helvius Apollonius, Publius [Consul name, illegible].
EDCS-42400115.summary: This is a financial settlement document detailing payments made by Lucius Caecilius Iucundus to Aulus Hordionius Philostorgus and Marcus Fabius Chryseros, dated to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-42400118.translation: Settlement for Aulus Messius Faustus: 2,000 sesterces, which money came into the bond of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of Dionysius. Dionysius stated that he had received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus in Pompeii.
EDCS-42400118.summary: This inscription is a financial receipt, recording a payment of 2,000 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus to Dionysius for an auction, likely from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-42400120.translation: 8,329 and a half sesterces, which money came into the bond of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the auction of S. I. Quintus Caius Saturninus, Sextus Numisius Iucundus, Publius Terentius Primus, Aulus Messius Pronimus, Marcus Stabi Vael, stated that they had received.
EDCS-42400120.summary: This is a financial record documenting 8,329.5 sesterces received by various individuals from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus related to an auction, likely from Pompeii.

EDCS-42400123.translation: I, Marcus Atilius Firmus, have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus 1,613 and a half sesterces for the auction. L. [received] less commission. Settled in Pompeii. Chirograph of Marcus Atilius Firmus, confirming payment by Lucius Caecilius Iucundus of 1,613.5 sesterces for my auction.
EDCS-42400123.summary: This is a personal record of a debt settlement, where Marcus Atilius Firmus acknowledges receipt of 1,613.5 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for an auction, dated to the period of Lucius Caecilius Iucundus's business activities in Pompeii.

EDCS-42400125.translation: Settlement for Hilara: 12,000 sesterces, less 4 [sesterces] commission, from Caius Atullius Euander, Marcus Lucretius Lerus, Herennius Primus.
EDCS-42400125.summary: This is a financial settlement record indicating a payment of 12,000 sesterces, with a deduction of 4 sesterces for commission, to Hilara from Caius Atullius Euander, Marcus Lucretius Lerus, and Herennius Primus.

EDCS-42400126.translation: Settled in Pompeii, in the consulship of Lucius Decimus Caprasius Felix, Laelius Trophimus, Titus Sornius Eutyches, Numerius Gnaeus Vibius Callistus, Marcus Helvius Adeptus, Caius Julius Eutactus.
EDCS-42400126.summary: This is a fragment of a financial record or legal document, listing names of individuals presumably involved in a transaction or legal proceeding in Pompeii, dated by consuls to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-42400127.translation: Fifty thousand [sesterces], settled in Pompeii, by Prepontis Cornelia Saturnini, from Sextus Numisius Iucundus, Prepontis Cornelia Saturnini. Payment of Prepontis Cornelia Saturnini: 10,000 sesterces for slaves which belonged to Me Libur [---].
EDCS-42400127.summary: This inscription records a payment of 10,000 sesterces by Prepontis Cornelia Saturnini to Sextus Numisius Iucundus, possibly related to the sale of slaves, dated to Pompeii.

EDCS-42400129.summary: This inscription is a chirograph, essentially a personal acknowledgement or record of a transaction, belonging to Caius Tettius Faustus.

EDCS-42400134.translation: Record of money paid to Cornelius (consul) by Celer Severus, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Publius Terentius Primus, Cnaeus Helvius Apollonius, Publius Poppaeus Narcissus, Lucius Tetteius Festus, Lucius Caecilius Hermas, Publius Furius Fortunatus.
EDCS-42400134.summary: This inscription is a financial record listing payments made to individuals, likely related to a public or private transaction during the consulship of Cornelius.

EDCS-42400135.translation: Antho, who in (the year of the) consuls Numerius Ninnius Calvus Justus, Lucius Helvius Rufus, Marcus Holconius Rufus, Marcus Cerrinius Restitutus, Numerius Popidius Narcissus, Marcus Lucretius Lerus, Lucius Valerius Peregrinus, and Quintus Caecilius.
EDCS-42400135.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to be a list of names associated with a consular year, possibly related to a legal or administrative record.

EDCS-42400136.translation: For the next Kalends of January, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Decimus Caprasius Erotis, Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, Numerius Popidius Amarantus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, Cnaeus Virbrius Callistus, Marcus Fabius Euporus, Lucius Albius Thesmus, Lucius Sextilius Faustus, being consuls, Numerius Popidius Ampliatus.
EDCS-42400136.summary: This inscription lists individuals and names consuls for the upcoming January, suggesting it's an administrative record or a dedication associated with the beginning of the year.

EDCS-42400139.translation: Record for Marcus Vibius Secundus for 300 mancipia, which money was received into the stipulation of Quintus Britti Balbus, Sextus Attius Amplius, Quintus Postumius Primus, Numerius Neri Hyginus, Cnaeus.
EDCS-42400139.summary: This inscription is a financial record detailing a sum of money related to 'mancipia' (perhaps slaves or property) received by Marcus Vibius Secundus and recorded under a stipulation involving several individuals.

EDCS-42400140.translation: Record for Lucius Ceius Ordo. To have: Lucius Ceius, son of Lucius, Aulus Messius Faustus, Cnaeus Virbrius Callistus, Lucius Aurelius Saturninus, Aulus Messius Pronimus, Lucius Istacidius Eu, Lucius Ceius Ordo, Aulus Paquius Philodes, Quintus Arrius Philo, being consuls. Ceo R V.
EDCS-42400140.summary: This is a financial record listing individuals and mentioning consuls, indicating a transaction or account balance during a specific consular year.

EDCS-42400143.translation: Record: M. C. said for Marcus Lupatus Saturninus, Numerius Neri Hyginus, Aulus Vettius Iliacus, Fufidius Faustus.
EDCS-42400143.summary: This inscription is a concise financial record, possibly a statement of accounts or a confirmation of payment, involving Marcus Lupatus Saturninus and others.

EDCS-42400144.translation: Record for Aefulano Chrysantus, Quintus Coelius, Lucius Marcius Holconius Proculus, Lucius Magulnius Donatus, Caelius Primogenis, Publius Mulvius Frontonius, Lucius Aelius Verus.
EDCS-42400144.summary: This inscription is a financial record detailing a payment or account to Aefulano Chrysantus, listing several other individuals who are likely involved in the transaction.

EDCS-42400145.translation: Record for Audasius Hylas. For Lucius Sevius Rufus, Gaius Gadius Firmus, Marcus Obellius Firmus (father), Venerius Publius Terentius Primus, Numerius Neri Hyginus, Numerius Nasennius Nymperos, Aulus Veius Nymphius, Minicius Atticus, Audasius Hylas, Publius Minicius Atticus.
EDCS-42400145.summary: This inscription is a financial record concerning Audasius Hylas and others, likely detailing a settlement of accounts or a list of debtors/creditors.

EDCS-42400146.translation: Record for Claudius Agrippa, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, Lucius Lucilius Philargyrus, Cnaeus Poppaeus Ephoebus, Decimus Caprasius Gobio, Lucius Ceius Felicionius, Claudius Agrippa, Antonius Optatus, Caecilius Communis.
EDCS-42400146.summary: This inscription is a financial record listing Claudius Agrippa and several other individuals, likely a record of payments or accounts during a specific period.

EDCS-42400147.translation: Record for Epidius Trophimus, Decimus Caprasius Erotis, Sextus Maxsimus, idi hi meni Domitius Polus, Marcus Epidius Bucolus.
EDCS-42400147.summary: This inscription is a fragmented financial record that mentions Epidius Trophimus and other individuals, suggesting a record of transactions or debts.

EDCS-42400148.translation: Record of payments by Marcus Fabius Memori, Niceratus, Herennuleus, Fla Sornius Eutychus, Publius Aefulanus Chrysanthus, Publius Terentius Erotis, Marcus Fabius Memoris, Numerius Istacidius, Orion. (of) Marcus Epidius.
EDCS-42400148.summary: This is a payment record listing several individuals, likely from a business or financial transaction.

EDCS-42400150.translation: Record of payments by Numerius Istacidius Nyptnus, Lucius Volusius Faustus, Gaius Calventius Quietius, Marcus Licinius Romanus, Gnaeus Vibius Callistus, Lucius Iunius Corinthus, Gnaeus Seius Hermas, Claudius M. . . , Numerius Istacidius Nyptni.
EDCS-42400150.summary: This inscription is a financial record detailing a list of individuals associated with payments.

EDCS-42400151.translation: Record of payments by Lidina Tuche, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Lucius Iulius Polubus, Gaius Veturius Sen., Marcus Antistius Faustus, Marcus Veius Felix, Lucius Vettius Auctus, Lucius Flaminius Strobili, Maetennius Daphnis.
EDCS-42400151.summary: This inscription documents a list of names, likely associated with a financial or administrative transaction.

EDCS-42400152.translation: Record of payments by Lucretius Stepanicus, Decimus Caprasius Erotis, Marcus Lucretius Lerius, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Marcus Fabius Secundus A.
EDCS-42400152.summary: This is a fragmented inscription recording a list of individuals, likely related to a financial transaction or accounting.

EDCS-42400153.translation: Record of payments by Mancus Daphnis, Publius Terentius Primi, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Marcus Fabius Agathinus, Numerius Herennius Anthus, Quintus Sulpicius ER, Lucius Avianus V., Lucius Ceius Nymphius.
EDCS-42400153.summary: This inscription lists individuals involved in a payment or accounting record.

EDCS-42400154.translation: Record of payments by Anthus Melissaeus, Marcus Fabius Proculus, Quintus Fabius Proculus, Quintus Atius Florus, Quintus Sulpicius Posporus, Lucius Deccius Hilario, Publius Antistius Secundio, Marcus Holconius Iucundus, Gaius Mintullius Faustus, Publius Terentius Primi, Quintus Caecilius Attalus.
EDCS-42400154.summary: This inscription is a list of names, functioning as a record of payments or accounts.

EDCS-42400155.translation: Record of payments at auction by Aulus Manilius, Lucius Tussidius Verus, Lucius Betutius Iustus, Gaius Gasius Firmus, Quintus Minisius Fructus, Numerius Fufidius Primi, Publius Terentius Apollonius, Salvius Aconius Primi, Gnaeus Seius Hermas.
EDCS-42400155.summary: This inscription records payments made at an auction, listing various individuals.

EDCS-42400156.translation: Record of payments to Publius Gavius Proculus, Quintus Postumius Modestus, Lucius Helvius Proculus, Gnaeus Gasius Proculus, Aulus Vettius Conviva, Lucius Brittius Erotis, Numerius Popidius Amarantius, . . .
EDCS-42400156.summary: This inscription details a list of recipients of payments, likely from a public or private transaction.

EDCS-42400157.translation: Record of payments by . . . Ampliatus, Lucius Faustus, Gaius Sulpicius Phosporus, Lucius Popidius Ampliatus, Lucius Deccius Hilario, Aulus Messius Faustus, Popidius Donatus, Maetennius Daphnis A LIAL.
EDCS-42400157.summary: This inscription is a fragmented record of payments, listing several individuals.

EDCS-42400158.translation: Record of payments to Publius Terentius Prosodus, Q. Tiberius Claudius Nedymus, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Aulus Veius Atticus, Marcus Aurelius Vitalis, Numerius Popidius Sodalionis, . . . Fortunatus, Publius Sittius Zosimus, Publius Terentius Prosodus.
EDCS-42400158.summary: This inscription lists individuals to whom payments were made, likely as part of a financial or administrative record.

EDCS-42400159.translation: Record of Chryseros, slave of Caesar, and of Decimus Lucretius Valens, Aulus Manlius Secundus, Numerius Popidius Amarantus, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Marcus Cestilius Philodespotus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, Cornelius Tagetes, and others, including Panthus, slave of Chryseros, slave of Caesar, and Narcissianus.
EDCS-42400159.summary: This inscription appears to be a financial or administrative record listing several individuals, some identified as slaves.

EDCS-42400160.translation: Record of Veius, son of Marcus, and Pa Numerius Popidius, of the Sodales, and of Publius Melissaeus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, Gnaeus Vibius Callistus, and Tomoteus.
EDCS-42400160.summary: This inscription is a list of names, possibly related to a collegium or association, indicating a record of members or participants.

EDCS-42400162.translation: Record of the Dorophori (bearers), second division. Also Marcus Magius Secundus, Publius Caelius Primogenis, Numerius Epictetus, Aulus Umbricius Modestus, and Lucius Titus.
EDCS-42400162.summary: This inscription lists members or personnel, possibly from a military or civic unit, including a division designation.

EDCS-42400164.translation: Record of Marcus, son of Vibius Macer, Aulus Appuleius Severus, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Decimus Caprasius Atictus Epidius, and others.
EDCS-42400164.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely an administrative or financial record, possibly associated with a property or transaction.

EDCS-42400165.translation: Record of Nasen, for less than the agreed price, and of Marcus Decidius Pauper, Marcus Cr... Aulus Sandelius..., and Lucretius Stephanicus.
EDCS-42400165.summary: This inscription seems to record a transaction with a note about the price, involving several individuals.

EDCS-42400166.translation: Record of Lucius Laelius Trophimus, Lucius Sestius Trophimus, Marcus Epidius Fortunatus, Quintus Lollius Saturninus, and Numerius Veius Martialis.
EDCS-42400166.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely an administrative or financial record.

EDCS-42400167.translation: Record of Marcus Pupius Rufus, Publius Thoranius Secundus, Publius Terentius Primus, Pacuvius Vitalis, Artorius Liberalis, Numerius Popidius Amarantus, freedman of Faustus, and Faustus Peregrinus.
EDCS-42400167.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including a freedman and a peregrinus (foreigner), suggesting a record of transactions or a list of associates.

EDCS-42400170.translation: Record of Gaius Aemilius Severus, Gaius Saturninus, Quintus Appuleius Severus, Publius Caelius Primogenis, Aulus Herennuleius Communis, Titus Sornius Eutychus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, Lucius Volusius Faustus, Publius Cornelius Tagetes, and Aulus Umbricius Modestus.
EDCS-42400170.summary: This is an extensive list of names, likely an administrative or financial record, possibly related to a group or business.

EDCS-42400171.translation: Record of Marcus Lucretius Laerus, Marcus Stlaborius Nymphodotus, Lucius Volusius Faustus, Gnaeus Vibius Callistus, Marcus Hordionius Philostorgus, Aulus Paccius Philodespotus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, and Chrysanthus Primogenis.
EDCS-42400171.summary: This inscription presents a list of names, possibly indicating a group of individuals involved in a financial or administrative matter.

EDCS-42400172.translation: Record of Aulus Veius Atticus, Marcus Ubonius Cogitatus, Gaius Cassius Secundus, Lucius Valerius Peregrinus, and Publius Cornelius Tagetes.
EDCS-42400172.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely an administrative or financial record, possibly documenting individuals involved in a transaction or association.

EDCS-42400173.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Titus Sornius Eutichus, son of Publius Terentius Primus, Marcus Rufellius Horus, son of Cnaeus Helvius Apollonius, Numerius.
EDCS-42400173.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, with several named dedicants, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-42400174.translation: Of Gaius Cnaeus Numerius, son of Aelius Cnaeus Alphius Lucius.
EDCS-42400174.summary: This is an ownership inscription, likely for a tomb or a property, mentioning two individuals by name.

EDCS-42400184.translation: The account of Hyginus Numistra Saturninus.
EDCS-42400184.summary: This records an account or financial transaction managed by Hyginus Numistra Saturninus.

EDCS-42400185.summary: This is likely an ownership inscription, possibly for a tomb, of Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus.

EDCS-42400186.translation: Of Tiberius Julius Gennaeus, son of Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus, Attalus, Marcus son of Au[relius?], Aulus Messius, Sextus Den, Gaius Te, Mu[tius?].
EDCS-42400186.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely patrons or beneficiaries, possibly associated with a monument or funerary context.

EDCS-42400187.translation: Of Quintus Thoranius, son of Marcus Fabius Chryseros, CIAAI Gaius son of Ini[tius?].
EDCS-42400187.summary: This inscription names several individuals, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-42400188.translation: Of Cerrinius Proculus, son of Gaius Nevoleius Felix, son of Gaius Proculeius, Deut [son of?] Callius, Hege [son of?] Fufidius Agathus.
EDCS-42400188.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely indicating family relationships or ownership, possibly for a tomb.

EDCS-42400189.translation: Of Secundus Verus, son of Marcus Rufellius Horrus, son of Marcus Cornelius Maximus, Numerius, son of Numerius.
EDCS-42400189.summary: This inscription names four individuals, likely indicating lineage and ownership, possibly for a funerary monument.

EDCS-42400193.translation: For the inheritance, 138-140 sesterces; for fulling, 141-144 sesterces; for pasture, 145-147 sesterces; for uncertain debts, 148-153 sesterces.
EDCS-42400193.summary: This inscription records sums of money allocated for various purposes, including inheritance, fulling, pasture, and debts, likely a financial record.

EDCS-42400194.translation: On the Ides of February, I, Privatus, a freedman of the colonists of the colony of Veneria Cornelia, have written that I have received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus one thousand sesterces from the remainder for the inheritance of the estate. I, the prefect judging by law, Decimus Lucretius Valens, Marcus Stronnius Secundus, Marcus Venerius Secundus, a freedman of the colonists of the colony of Veneria Cornelia.
EDCS-42400194.summary: This is a receipt for a payment of one thousand sesterces related to an inheritance, recorded on February 13th and witnessed by several officials and a freedman.

EDCS-42400196.translation: To Lucius Albucio Iustus and Lucius Veranius Hypsaeus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction, Privatus, slave of the colony, declares that he received 1,652 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus from the remaining funds for the fuller's shop. The day before the Ides of July. In Pompeii, the 19th day before the Kalends of September, under consuls Aulus Paconius Sabinus and Aulus Petronius. For Privatus, tenant of the colony of Veneria Cornelia. Lucius Albucio Iustus, Marcus Stronnius Secundus, Lucius Veranius Phile, Privatus, tenant of the colony. On the day before the Ides of September, payment to the state for the fuller's shop, 1,652. Written statement of Privatus, slave of the tenant of the colony of Veneria Cornelia. To Lucius Veranius Hypsaeus and Lucius Albucio Iustus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction. The day before the Ides of July, under consuls Aulus Paconius and Aulus Petronius. Payment for the fuller's shop for the second year. To Privatus, tenant of the colony of Veneria Cornelia, slave. To Lucius Veranius Hypsaeus and Lucius Albucio Iustus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction. The day before the Ides of July, under consuls Aulus Paconius and Aulus Petronius.
EDCS-42400196.summary: This is a receipt from a slave named Privatus for 1,652 sesterces paid from the remaining funds for a fuller's shop, dated to Pompeii during the consulship of Aulus Paconius Sabinus and Aulus Petronius.

EDCS-42400197.translation: During the fourth consulship of Nero Caesar and Cossus, the 8th day before the Ides of May. Written statement of Privatus, tenant of the colony of Cornelia Veneria. 1,652 sesterces for the fuller's shop for the fourth year. To Numerius Sandelius Messius Balbus and Publius Vedius Siricus, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction. To Sextus Pompeius Proculus, prefect with the power of jurisdiction. The 8th day before the Ides of May. Privatus, slave of the colony of Pompeii, declares that he received 1,652 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the fuller's shop for the fourth year. In Pompeii, during the fourth consulship of Nero Caesar Augustus and Lentulus. To Numerius Sandelius Messius Balbus and Publius Vedius Siricus.
EDCS-42400197.summary: This is a receipt from Privatus, a slave of the colony of Pompeii, for 1,652 sesterces paid for the fuller's shop in the fourth year of Nero's reign, during the consulship of Nero Caesar and Lentulus.

EDCS-42400198.translation: Seventy-five sesterces for the pasture land ordered by Pompeius Proculus. In Rome, during the consulship of Marcus Valerius Messalla and Gaius Fonteius. By Sextus Pompeius Proculus, tenant of the colony, and Sextus Pompeius Proculus and Gaius Cornelius Macro, duumvirs with the power of jurisdiction. The Ides of July. Privatus, slave of the colony of Pompeii, declares that he received 1,675 sesterces from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus for the pasture land ordered by Pompeius Proculus. In Pompeii, during the consulship of Marcus Valerius Messalla and Gaius Fonteius. Payment for the pasture land for the year, 1,675 sesterces.
EDCS-42400198.summary: This is a receipt from Privatus, a slave of the colony of Pompeii, for 1,675 sesterces paid for pasture land ordered by Sextus Pompeius Proculus, during the consulship of Marcus Valerius Messalla and Gaius Fonteius.

EDCS-42400200.translation: to Gaius Vibius Secundus, duumvir with the power of jurisdiction
EDCS-42400200.summary: This inscription fragment names Gaius Vibius Secundus as a duumvir with jurisdiction.

EDCS-42400202.translation: Iucundus S ten ... of Secundus Claudius
EDCS-42400202.summary: This very fragmentary inscription mentions 'Iucundus' and 'Secundus Claudius', possibly related to a financial transaction or ownership.

EDCS-42400203.translation: of Marcus Licinius Romanus, Marcus Stronnius Secundus, Aulus Messius Phronimus, the public official
EDCS-42400203.summary: This fragment lists several Roman names, including Marcus Licinius Romanus, Marcus Stronnius Secundus, and Aulus Messius Phronimus, who was a public official.

EDCS-42400206.translation: of the Figlinae workshops of the Doppiana estate of Aelius Fuscianus
EDCS-42400206.summary: This inscription refers to the Figlinae workshops belonging to the Doppiana estate of Aelius Fuscianus.

EDCS-42400368.translation: Under consuls Quintus Fabius Catullinus and Marcus Flavius Aper, concerning the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens, under the care of Hedynus.
EDCS-42400368.summary: This inscription records a transaction or management concerning the estates of Quintus Servilius Pudens, overseen by Hedynus, during the consulship of Quintus Fabius Catullinus and Marcus Flavius Aper.

EDCS-42500129.summary: This is a simple Greek greeting addressed to someone named Agathos.

EDCS-42500138.translation: Gorgias, son of Papias, from Nicomedeia, a wool-worker, who lived for 54 years.
EDCS-42500138.summary: This funerary epigram in Greek records the name, origin, occupation, and age at death of Gorgias of Nicomedeia.

EDCS-42500142.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Achilleus, the father, made this for his most pious son Kyrillos Achilleus, who lived 11 years, 5 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-42500142.summary: This is a funerary epigram for a boy named Kyrillos Achilleus, set up by his father Achilleus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-42500143.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Gaios Volcacios Myropnus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-42500147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Telesphoros, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-42500150.summary: This is a short greeting or farewell inscribed on a monument, likely funerary, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-42600046.translation: The martyrs Simplicius and Faustinus, who suffered martyrdom by the Tiber river and were placed in the cemetery of Generosa, near Filippi.
EDCS-42600046.summary: This inscription records the burial place of the Christian martyrs Simplicius and Faustinus, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600051.translation: Primitivus in peace, who after many hardships, a most courageous martyr, lived about 38 years; his most beloved spouse made this for him, his deserving husband.
EDCS-42600051.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the Christian martyr Primitivus, erected by his wife, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600052.summary: This inscription lists the names of the four Evangelists, likely a funerary marker for a Christian, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600053.translation: Agnes Timoteus Sustus Ceprianus Paulus Laurentius Petrus
EDCS-42600053.summary: This inscription lists several Christian names, likely from a funerary context, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600054.translation: Priscus Lupulus Sinotus Rufus Marcellus Augustinus Felicitas
EDCS-42600054.summary: This inscription lists several Christian names, likely from a funerary context, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600055.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Quartus and Quintus, likely from a funerary context, dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-42600056.translation: Abdias, Philippus, Micheas, Iacobus, Hosee, Petrus, Ezechiel, Lucas, Esaias, Matthaeus, Zacharias, Iudas, son of Iacobus, Sophonias, Iacobus, Naum, Thomas.
EDCS-42600056.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of personal names, possibly a register or a dedicatory list from an early Christian context.

EDCS-42600057.translation: Priscus, Felix, Artimas, Aefimus, Eutices, Sosius, Festus, Desiderius, Xistus, Cyprianus, Hippolitus, Canio, Augustinus, Marcellus, Lupilus, Rufus.
EDCS-42600057.summary: This inscription is a list of personal names, likely from a Roman funerary monument or a register, with no further context provided.

EDCS-42600060.summary: This inscription names two saints, Processus and Paulus, likely related to a religious dedication or memorial, possibly from an early Christian era.

EDCS-42700126.translation: Amarantus declared himself to have measured 50 modii; Ingenuus declared himself to have measured 300.
EDCS-42700126.summary: This inscription records a measurement of grain (modii) by two individuals, Amarantus and Ingenuus, likely related to an agricultural or trade transaction.

EDCS-43400122.translation: In the second consulship of Vero, Brutiana, daughter of Lupus.
EDCS-43400122.summary: This inscription likely refers to a property owner, Brutiana, daughter of Lupus, dated by the consulship of Vero, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication.

EDCS-43400155.translation: Of Lucius Vibullennius, son of Lucius, ten.
EDCS-43400155.summary: This inscription seems to record a quantity of ten items or units associated with Lucius Vibullennius, son of Lucius, possibly a record of goods or payments.

EDCS-43400207.translation: From the estates of Flavius Aper, pottery work by Larcius.
EDCS-43400207.summary: This inscription indicates pottery production originating from the estates of Flavius Aper, with the work attributed to Larcius.

EDCS-43400223.summary: This inscription likely refers to a property or object belonging to Vinicius Salvianus, identified as Sulpicianum, possibly a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-43400225.summary: This inscription likely refers to a property or object belonging to Vinicius Salvianus, identified as Sulpicianum, possibly a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-43400227.summary: This inscription likely refers to a property or object belonging to Vinicius Salvianus, identified as Sulpicianum, possibly a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-43400228.summary: This inscription names the Sulpicianum property belonging to Vinicius Salvinus.

EDCS-43400229.summary: This inscription names the Sulpicianum property of Vinicius Pantagathus.

EDCS-43400236.summary: This is a personal dedication or a wish for good fortune for Lucius Atinius.

EDCS-43400256.summary: This inscription records ownership or a dedication by Gaius Licinius Donatus.

EDCS-43400257.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Lucilla, the property of Verus. Ulpius Anicetianus.
EDCS-43400257.summary: This inscription records tile production from the estates of Lucilla, likely by Ulpius Anicetianus, possibly for Verus's property.

EDCS-43400258.translation: Doliary work from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, by Epagathus, son of Claudius Quinquatralis, in the third consulship of Servianus.
EDCS-43400258.summary: This inscription records tile production from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, made by Epagathus and dated to the consulship of Servianus.

EDCS-43400259.summary: This inscription records ownership or a dedication by Quintus Asinius Marcellus.

EDCS-43400268.translation: Of Quintus Lepidus, son of Quintus, the Iduarian.
EDCS-43400268.summary: This inscription records ownership or a dedication by Quintus Lepidus, son of Quintus, who was from the Iduari tribe.

EDCS-43400644.translation: From the workshop of Julius Honoratus of the province of Mauretania Caesariensis, Tubusuctu.
EDCS-43400644.summary: This inscription identifies the origin of a product as the workshop of Julius Honoratus in Tubusuctu, Mauretania Caesariensis.

EDCS-43400786.summary: This inscription likely refers to a dedication or a marker associated with the month of January.

EDCS-43400796.translation: Lea made this [grave marker] on the third day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-43400796.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating the date of construction of a grave marker by Lea.

EDCS-43400827.translation: For the well-deserving one, Furiae, who lived about nine years, departed into the sleep of peace on the third day before the Ides of October, during the consulship of Dioscorus.
EDCS-43400827.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Furiae, who died at a young age around the 3rd Ides of October during Dioscorus' consulship.

EDCS-43400828.translation: For the well-deserving nephew, Sustus, who lived about thirty-two years, was buried on the eighth day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-43400828.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sustus, who died at the age of about thirty-two, buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of October.

EDCS-43400829.translation: Victor, on the Nones of November, was buried here in peace.
EDCS-43400829.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Victor on the Nones of November.

EDCS-43501316.translation: Of the Julian couple, Melissus and Melissa.
EDCS-43501316.summary: This inscription identifies a grave belonging to a couple named Melissus and Melissa from the Julian family.

EDCS-43501318.translation: Of the three Miniciorum: P. Arva.
EDCS-43501318.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or burial rights for members of the Minicius family, specifically mentioning P. Arva.

EDCS-43501320.summary: This inscription indicates a grave belonging to Melissus, associated with the Camilian family.

EDCS-43600099.translation: To the Divine Manes and the immortal spirit, well-deserving: Eros, the protector, from Etry, the prefect; Eutyches, the servant.
EDCS-43600099.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes and the spirit of a deceased individual, listing Eros and Eutyches as offering the dedication.

EDCS-43700614.translation: May the curse of the god strike anyone who damages this tomb, except for Ursu and his wife.
EDCS-43700614.summary: This is a curse inscription warning against the desecration of a tomb, with exceptions for Ursu and his wife.

EDCS-43700717.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Urbanus as the son of Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-43700718.summary: This inscription appears to be a name, possibly of a freedman or someone associated with a member of the Cornelii family.

EDCS-43700745.translation: Valerius was laid to rest here on the Wednesday before the Ides of November in the consulship of Stilicho.
EDCS-43700745.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Valerius on a specific date during the consulship of Stilicho, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-43700751.summary: This brief inscription likely indicates Marcus's merit or good service, possibly on a monument or as a dedication.

EDCS-43700761.summary: This is a dedication to a person named Fedimus, expressing great affection, likely on a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-43800706.summary: This inscription seems to record the name and filiation of Lucius Rasticanus, possibly on a tombstone or a public record.

EDCS-44100243.translation: To Gaius Valerius Paulinus, prefect of the grain supply of Augustus, by the care of Marcus Farranius F..., a most distinguished man, companion...
EDCS-44100243.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Valerius Paulinus, a high-ranking official, likely honoring him for his service in the grain supply by a subordinate or colleague.

EDCS-44100244.translation: Ammias to her most loving husband Mercator, Italicus Deuter to his most dutiful father, made (this).
EDCS-44100244.summary: This is a funerary inscription with two dedications: Ammias to her husband Mercator and sons to their father, likely a tomb monument.

EDCS-44100255.summary: This inscription records the full name of an individual, Publius Vesonius Phileros, possibly on a tombstone or legal document.

EDCS-44100256.summary: This inscription provides the name and filiation of Vesonia, likely part of a funerary or legal record.

EDCS-44100257.translation: To Publius Vesonius Proculus, who lived 13 years.
EDCS-44100257.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Publius Vesonius Proculus, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-44100258.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Vesonia Urbana.

EDCS-44100259.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Eliodorus.

EDCS-44100265.translation: Cn(aeus?) Nassius Cerialis, IIvir, by decree of the decurions, so that he not be under guardianship from a just guardian, by the law of Iulia and Titia, gave Quintus Vibius Ampliatus as guardian to Cornelia Thallusae.
