EDCS-44100265.summary: A legal inscription concerning guardianship, likely from the early imperial period, referencing specific Roman laws.

EDCS-44100290.translation: To the divine spirits. Titianus Victorinus, soldier of the German fleet, a native of Agrippinensis, lived for 28 years and served for 6 years. Secundinus Peculiaris made this for him as a well-deserving recipient.
EDCS-44100290.summary: A funerary inscription for a soldier of the Germanic fleet, noting his age, service length, and the dedicant.

EDCS-44500185.translation: From the Oceanus pottery works, earthenware manufactured by our Caesar, supervised by Oppius Proculus and Oppius Iustus Pudens.
EDCS-44500185.summary: An inscription from a pottery factory indicating the origin and supervisors of the manufactured goods, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-44500186.summary: A very short inscription, likely a name on a property or object.

EDCS-45300147.translation: Lucius Publicius Syneros and for his freedwomen Aebia Faustae and Aebia Hilara, and for his freedman Lucius Aebius Ariston, patron, for himself and his family.
EDCS-45300147.summary: A dedication to patrons and freedpersons, likely on a building or monument, for the benefit of family members.

EDCS-45300155.translation: To the divine spirits. Of Publius Bennius Corinthus.
EDCS-45300155.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Publius Bennius Corinthus.

EDCS-45300170.translation: To the divine spirits. Anthus Primitivus and Attia Efesia.
EDCS-45300170.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Anthus Primitivus and Attia Efesia.

EDCS-45500011.translation: Fortunate, son of Fortunate, though still a child, went to heaven, not knowing bad nor good, what life brings. He lived two years, two months, and five days. Look, this stele, recording these things, says: 'Weep no more, dearest father, nor grieve any longer, holding incurable sorrow in your chest. For Hades, ruler of the underworld, has not hidden me underground, but an eagle of Zeus snatched me away, rejoicing with fire and torch, so that I may be a companion to the bright morning and beautiful evening star. Therefore, father, bidding these tears farewell, sacrifice to me, for you see me riding as a star.' Eutyches, freedman of Augustus, made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-45500011.summary: A bilingual funerary inscription (Greek and Latin) for a young child, Eutyches, expressing the father's grief and the child's ascent to heaven as a star, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-45500020.translation: Why did you wish to increase me, pitying another? Crescens hides himself here. Greetings.
EDCS-45500020.summary: This is a personal epitaph from an unknown location and date, possibly a funerary epigram or a dedicatory text, reflecting personal sentiments and identity.

EDCS-45500045.translation: To [---]anius, son of Quintus, of the Falernian tribe, and Auge, freedwoman of Marcus, according to the will.
EDCS-45500045.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription records the burial of two individuals, [---]anius and Auge, with the burial arranged through a will, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-45500046.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely part of a funerary monument or a property marker, identifying Mellia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-45500051.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly the beginning of a name on a monument or an artifact, identified as Gaius Turel[lius(?)]

EDCS-46400799.translation: Licinia, freedwoman of Gaius. Gaius Licinius, freedman of the woman.
EDCS-46400799.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, Licinia and Gaius Licinius, clarifying their relationship as freedperson and patron, likely from a funerary or legal context.

EDCS-46400940.translation: Sacred to the Great God Liber Pater. Titus Tettienus Felix, son of Titus, scribe of the curule aediles, a viator, aedile of the plebs, accepted patron of the colony of Nola, procurator of the Emperor's patrimony, flamen of the deified Commodus and the deified Antoninus, a quinquennalis, a curator of the great circus, a warden of region VIII, prefect of the cohort of the VI vigilum, erected this at his own expense in bronze, silver, and his own money.
EDCS-46400940.summary: This lengthy inscription records the extensive career and public honors of Titus Tettienus Felix, a prominent official in Nola, dating to the period of the deified emperors Commodus and Antoninus (likely 2nd-3rd century AD).

EDCS-46500014.translation: The trumpet players and lyre players give this gift; the masters oversaw it: Cailius, freedman of Publius, and Sexstilius, freedman of Sextus, a freedman.
EDCS-46500014.summary: This inscription records a gift or dedication made by musicians (trumpet and lyre players) and overseen by their managers, likely related to a religious or civic occasion, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-46500020.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Syriara, his wife, made this for her well-deserving husband, Lucceius Heracledes, who lived...
EDCS-46500020.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a wife, Syriara, to her deceased husband, Lucceius Heracledes, indicating a loving marital relationship and likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500021.translation: The remains of Minucia Triphera, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-46500021.summary: This inscription marks the burial place or commemorates the remains of Minucia Triphera, identified as the freedwoman of Marcus, likely a funerary marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500028.translation: Titus Flavius Delphicus, freedman of Augustus, clerk of accounts, procurator of the treasury of inheritances, of the Alexandrian treasury, made this for himself.
EDCS-46500028.summary: This funerary inscription records the self-funded burial of Titus Flavius Delphicus, a freedman of Augustus who held significant financial administrative positions in Roman Egypt, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-46500031.translation: To Gaius Vibius Taurinus, son of Gaius Vibius, of the Oufentina tribe, son of Gaius Vibius, of the Oufentina tribe, a quinquennial priest (?), [and] Vibius Taurinus, son of Gaius Vibius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-46500031.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vibius Taurinus and possibly another Vibius Taurinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500033.translation: To the 95th Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius Pius Felix Invictus.
EDCS-46500033.summary: This inscription records the titles of Emperor Maxentius, likely displayed on a public monument, dating to his reign (306-312 AD).

EDCS-46500035.translation: Manius Occius, son of Manius, and Titus Manlius, son of Titus, as quinquennial magistrates, by decree of the senate.
EDCS-46500035.summary: This inscription records the names and offices of two quinquennial magistrates (IIII viri iure dicundo), indicating a public commission from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500036.translation: Freedman of Sextus Hordeonius, son of Publius.
EDCS-46500036.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a freedman and his patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500038.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Gaius Claudius Priscus, possibly in a dedication or funerary context.

EDCS-46500039.translation: Marcus Vinicius Lucrio, bath attendant, for himself and for his most cherished wife Mevia, freedwoman of Gnaeus. 'Who during my lifetime sustained me, wretched me, who lost such a good hold!'
EDCS-46500039.summary: This is a humorous funerary epitaph for Marcus Vinicius Lucrio, a bath attendant, lamenting the death of his wife Mevia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500044.translation: To Sextus Stenius, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe.
EDCS-46500044.summary: This is a dedication or funerary epitaph for Sextus Stenius, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500048.translation: [about the property of] that farm and woods... to Minicius Severus and Plotius Marcellus, as consuls.
EDCS-46500048.summary: This is a fragmentary legal or administrative document concerning land, mentioning the consuls Minicius Severus and Plotius Marcellus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46500049.translation: September 1st... on the 6th day... [recorded] by Cassius... by Lucius Caecilius... on the 6th day of the Ides of June, under the consulship of Gaius Marcius Censorinus and Gaius Asinius Gallus. ... from Marcus, son of Lucius, of the Falernian tribe...
EDCS-46500049.summary: This is a fragmentary record of legal or administrative proceedings, mentioning dates and consuls from the late Republic or early Empire, along with names of individuals and a location.

EDCS-46600987.translation: To Veturia, granddaughter of Veturius, most devoted.
EDCS-46600987.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Veturia, dedicated by her grandfather, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46600990.translation: Marcus Cornelius Menander, freedman of Publius, physician.
EDCS-46600990.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Cornelius Menander, a freedman and physician.

EDCS-46600995.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, mentioning several names with missing parts.

EDCS-46600998.translation: To Marcus Granius Philo and his freedmen and freedwomen [---]
EDCS-46600998.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly dedicating a monument or tomb to Marcus Granius Philo and his freed dependents.

EDCS-46601006.translation: To himself and to Pompeia, his well-deserving patroness, and to Pompeia Storg[---] and his own [family].
EDCS-46601006.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where the dedicator honors himself, his patroness Pompeia, and other family members.

EDCS-46601008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Minucia Supera.

EDCS-46601017.translation: Gaius Orchius [---]s to himself [---] Nilus, freedman [---] Nilus to Mariae M[---]ano, freedman [---]
EDCS-46601017.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription detailing dedications by Gaius Orchius and Nilus, a freedman, to themselves and possibly others.

EDCS-46601020.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Avianius Eros.

EDCS-47500672.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Ogulnius Epagathus, identified by his status as patron.

EDCS-47600057.translation: To Titus Clodius Eprius Marcellus, son of Marcus, of the Falerna tribe, twice consul, augur, chief curio, Augustal priest, peregrine praetor, proconsul of Asia for the third time, governor of the province of Cyprus.
EDCS-47600057.summary: This is a highly honorific inscription praising Titus Clodius Eprius Marcellus for his extensive career in Roman public office, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-48000002.translation: To the Genius of Quintus Alfer[---]
EDCS-48000002.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicating something to the Genius of Quintus Alfer[---].

EDCS-48000006.translation: Tonio, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, as a principal assistant(?) to the princeps of the XXII legion.
EDCS-48000006.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a military officer named Tonius, serving in the XXII legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000013.summary: This inscription records the name Gaius Blassius, identified as an Augustalis, likely a public official or priest, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000014.translation: To Marcus Clodius Philargurus, freedman of Marcus; to Clodia Augeni, freedwoman of Marcus; to the hairdresser Marcus Clodius Theudas, freedman of a woman; and to Prima Calpetana, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-48000014.summary: This is a funerary or dedication inscription honoring multiple individuals, including a hairdresser, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000015.translation: Ateia Secunda, freedwoman of Gaius, for herself and for Gaius Palpellius Tertullus, son of Marcus, and for Ateia Tertulla, sister; and for Gaius Ateius Agrippa, freedman of Gaius; and for Hypora, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-48000015.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-dedication and dedications to family members, including siblings, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000018.translation: Titus Florius, son of Titus, [from...], pro[...].
EDCS-48000018.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Titus Florius, son of Titus, likely a personal or dedication record from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000021.translation: To Titus Pomponius, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe; and to Pomponia Elaphio, freedwoman of Marcus; and to Pomponia Clara, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-48000021.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Pomponius and two women named Pomponia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48000023.translation: To Quintus Servilius Quinctio, son of Spurius, in life.
EDCS-48000023.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to Quintus Servilius Quinctio, potentially a funerary monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-48300007.translation: Recognized in the year of the consulship of Felicis, servant of Domitian Augustus, at location 870...
EDCS-48300007.summary: This inscription records an official recognition or verification under the consulship of Felicis, a servant of Emperor Domitian, likely dating to the late 1st century AD.

EDCS-48700041.translation: Here rests Anastasius laneus, who lived more or less 35 years, buried on the day before the Kalends of August in the consulship of Flavius Probus, most noble man.
EDCS-48700041.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Anastasius laneus, who lived approximately 35 years, dated by the consulship of Flavius Probus, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-48700064.translation: Victor and Eutichianus mourn their beloved who died in the flower of youth, and this inscription written on the tombstone attests to their love and perpetual honor.
EDCS-48700064.summary: This funerary epigram expresses grief and love from Victor and Eutichianus for a deceased individual, likely dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-48700136.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman named Servius.

EDCS-48700372.translation: To Spe, honored husband, well-deserving; but whoever after his death shall have provided [for her...].
EDCS-48700372.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a man named Spe, with a clause for future provision.

EDCS-48700389.summary: This inscription likely lists individuals, possibly in a funerary or dedicatory context.

EDCS-48700393.translation: Asclepius, son of Marin, Gaius P[---]
EDCS-48700393.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary dedication or funerary text mentioning Asclepius and Gaius.

EDCS-48700420.translation: from Augustus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, Ma[---]
EDCS-48700420.summary: This fragmentary inscription refers to a person of senatorial or equestrian rank, possibly dedicated to or by someone associated with Augustus.

EDCS-48700516.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely completes a dedication or funerary text, mentioning Felicissima.

EDCS-48700533.translation: To the Divine Manes of Crispinus.
EDCS-48700533.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Crispinus.

EDCS-48700548.translation: Here rests the blessed martyr Ypolitus.
EDCS-48700548.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the Christian martyr Ypolitus.

EDCS-48700891.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Pomponia Clementa.

EDCS-48700893.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Varia, identified by her father's name.

EDCS-48700929.translation: Octavia Italia, pleasing to her family, most faithful to her husband, dear to her relatives. Here, I, Octavia Italia, have been buried.
EDCS-48700929.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia Italia, intended for a tomb.

EDCS-48700932.translation: Lucius Caltilius Pamphilus, freedman of Lucius, of the Collina tribe, with a willing heart, [dedicated this] to his wife Servilia.
EDCS-48700932.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a freedman to his wife.

EDCS-49400026.translation: Incitatus Cassianus, sent off after 1 victory and 1 crown. Serenus Cassianus won 2 fights and 2 crowns. Blastus Cassianus won 3 fights and 1 crown. Aster Iulianus, sent off after 2 fights and 1 crown. [Unknown] sent off. Euthicus Cassianus won 3 fights and 3 crowns. Niger Iulianus, sent off after 4 fights and 3 crowns. Bassus Iulianus won 5 fights and 4 crowns. Chrestus Cassianus, sent off after [unknown] fights and [unknown] crowns.
EDCS-49400026.summary: This inscription records the results of gladiatorial contests, listing the participants, their outcomes (won or sent off), and the number of victories and crowns achieved, likely from a gladiatorial school or arena.

EDCS-49400027.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Adius Saturninus made this for his sweetest wife, Utia Iustina, with whom he lived for 2 years. [Rest of text illegible or in abbreviations].
EDCS-49400027.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Caius Adius Saturninus to his wife Utia Iustina, indicating the length of their marriage.

EDCS-49400044.translation: To Diana. Marcus Antonius Calvinus, son of Marcus, of the Stellatina tribe, Augustalis VI vir, patron of the colony of Venafrum, quinquennial magistrate, and IIII vir of the college of smiths and dendrophores.
EDCS-49400044.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana by Marcus Antonius Calvinus, a prominent local official and patron in the Roman colony of Venafrum, highlighting his various civic and collegial roles.

EDCS-49400046.translation: To Marcus Antonius Calvinus, son of Marcus, IIII vir of the college of smiths of Venafrum, Augustalis VI vir, patron of the municipality and colony of Venafrum, patron of the college of dendrophores. Dedicated with honors by the order of the priests and the people of Venafrum to the divine Juno.
EDCS-49400046.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Antonius Calvinus, a significant local figure in Venafrum, listing his numerous civic and religious offices and his patronage of various groups, dedicated to the goddess Juno.

EDCS-49400047.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Saturius, son of Lucius, of the Cluia tribe, formerly tribune of the VI Gemella legion, prefect of the Scubiculorum cavalry, lived 61 years.
EDCS-49400047.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Saturius, a military officer who served as a legionary tribune and cavalry prefect.

EDCS-49400048.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Viria Valeria made this for her husband, Lucius Virius Firmus, son of Titus, of the Stellatina tribe, a select eques of the emperor, who lived 69 years, 7 months, and 8 days, according to his will.
EDCS-49400048.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Viria Valeria for her husband, Lucius Virius Firmus, a distinguished cavalryman, specifying the details of its erection according to his will.

EDCS-49400049.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Minerva Frugifera. Caius Iulius Rufus, a most distinguished man, former proconsul of Campania, paid his vow.
EDCS-49400049.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Iulius Rufus, a former proconsul of Campania, dedicated to Jupiter and Minerva.

EDCS-49400052.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Lucius Sulla, the Roman dictator.

EDCS-49500018.translation: Galeo, son of [---], on the Ides of May, every year [---] will inhabit [---]
EDCS-49500018.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to record a recurring event or obligation related to Galeo, dating to the Ides of May.

EDCS-49700161.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Tuccius Philocles, freedman of Lucius, the magister.
EDCS-49700161.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mercury by Lucius Tuccius Philocles, identified as a freedman and a magister.

EDCS-49700164.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a monument or property, belonging to Publius Coelius.

EDCS-49800001.translation: To Gaius Pantuleius Epigonus, freedman of Gaius, an Augustalis.
EDCS-49800001.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Pantuleius Epigonus, who was a freedman and an Augustalis.

EDCS-49900003.translation: Marcus Consius Cerinthus, an accensus, veiled, while the consuls were entering office.
EDCS-49900003.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Consius Cerinthus, an accensus, and places the event during the consular transition, likely indicating a specific religious or official ceremony.

EDCS-50500210.translation: Lucius Varius Concordius, son of Lucius, from the Falernian tribe, aedile, patron of the guild of fullers, and Valeria Vitalis, daughter of Lucius, his wife, made this for themselves and their family. Farewell, Scarnius, good man.
EDCS-50500210.summary: This funerary or dedication text records Lucius Varius Concordius, an aedile and patron of the fullers' guild, and his wife Valeria Vitalis, who commissioned the monument for their family.

EDCS-50500212.translation: Peristera, Junia made this at her own expense for Lucius Julius Stratonius, the physician.
EDCS-50500212.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Junia for Lucius Julius Stratonius, a physician, who was likely a client or family member.

EDCS-50500214.translation: Atalante, Claudia Apricula and Lupus (made this) for (their) sister.
EDCS-50500214.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial made by Claudia Apricula and Lupus for their sister, Atalante.

EDCS-50500216.translation: Sura, freedwoman of Marcus CCaius, Marcus Pactumeius arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-50500216.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Pactumeius arranged for a monument to be made for Sura, a freedwoman of Marcus CCaius.

EDCS-50500217.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several Roman names, likely related to a public or private monument, but insufficient for a detailed summary.

EDCS-50500223.translation: To Lucretia Marcellina, my most rare wife, who lived in marriage for six months and twenty-three days, died at the age of fifteen years, four months, and one day. Gaius Laeveius Bassus, her unhappy husband.
EDCS-50500223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased wife, detailing her age and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-50500233.translation: Auli Veturi Auli Rufi lives, twelve feet in the field.
EDCS-50500233.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker, indicating property belonging to Aulus Vetus.

EDCS-51000041.translation: [---] made for his most cherished daughter.
EDCS-51000041.summary: This is a dedication likely made by a parent for their daughter, though the dedicant and specific deity are lost.

EDCS-51000043.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely indicating a work made by 'Firmus' for someone named Antonius.

EDCS-51000045.summary: A very broken inscription, possibly a dedication to deities or individuals named ONCT and Fadius.

EDCS-51000108.translation: Gaius Coelius Hermeros, guardian of this place, made it with his own money.
EDCS-51000108.summary: This is a dedication made by Gaius Coelius Hermeros, identified as the 'antistes' or guardian of a sacred site, funded by himself.

EDCS-51000109.translation: Aulus Aemilius Antoninus, father of Cautus.
EDCS-51000109.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or memorial set up by Aulus Aemilius Antoninus, identified as the father of Cautus.

EDCS-51000110.translation: For the safety of the Emperors, Florius Hermadio, priest, made this offering to Sol Invictus Mithras with his own money.
EDCS-51000110.summary: This is a religious dedication made by the priest Florius Hermadio to the god Sol Invictus Mithras for the well-being of the emperors.

EDCS-51000111.translation: Marcus Umbilius Criton gave this offering to Invictus Mithras, along with Pylades, the steward.
EDCS-51000111.summary: This is a religious offering made to Invictus Mithras by Marcus Umbilius Criton and his steward Pylades.

EDCS-51000112.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Sanctus. Hermes, of Marcus Julius Eunicus.
EDCS-51000112.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object or place to the god Silvanus Sanctus, possibly by a freedman named Hermes associated with Marcus Julius Eunicus.

EDCS-51000113.translation: Sextus Fusinius Felix gave a gift.
EDCS-51000113.summary: This is a dedication of a gift by Sextus Fusinius Felix.

EDCS-51000114.summary: This is a dedication or statement of presence related to the deity Sol, likely from a pagan context.

EDCS-51000143.translation: Caius Novius Philetus, freedman of Caius, made this for himself and for his wife Novia Helpidis, and for his son Caius Novius Palatina Statilio, who lived for 15 years, 5 months, and 7 days, and for his daughter Novia Iusta, and for his freedman Caius Novius Telesphorus, and for his freedman Caius Novius Fortunatus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In his mother Modia Victoria's inherited land, he donated 20 Roman feet, this tomb, which belongs near Modia Marina, to Marcus Arrius Hilarus, her husband, and to their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-51000143.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Novius Philetus, detailing his family members, their lifespans, and the dimensions and location of the tomb, dating likely to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-51000144.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Epiteuxis, for her dearest husband, with her children, for the sake of memory.
EDCS-51000144.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Epiteuxis to her husband, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51000145.translation: To Manlia Antonia, his wife. Annius Esychus, his wife.
EDCS-51000145.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Annius Esychus to his wife Manlia Antonia.

EDCS-51000146.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus made this for his son Marcus.
EDCS-51000146.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus to his son Marcus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51000147.translation: Caius Rusticelius Crispus, freedman of Caius Rusticelius Felix, made this for himself and for his son Rusticelius Crispus and for his wife Clodia Herais and for their descendants.
EDCS-51000147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Caius Rusticelius Crispus, a freedman, for himself, his son, his wife, and their descendants.

EDCS-51000148.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Peducaeus Oriens made this for his daughter Peducea Galatia, and for himself, and for his own family and their descendants.
EDCS-51000148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Titus Peducaeus Oriens for his daughter, himself, and their descendants.

EDCS-51000149.translation: To Salubia Philumena. Marcus Iulius Italicus.
EDCS-51000149.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Iulius Italicus to Salubia Philumena.

EDCS-51000151.summary: This fragment refers to an official, a registrar ('tabularius') of the emperor.

EDCS-51200040.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Veturius Anthenio made this for his most dutiful daughter Veturia Hermione. [---] c m t.
EDCS-51200040.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a father for his daughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200041.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Heracla, of the guild of carpenters of Ostia, [dedicated this] to Mercury, for his well-deserved service. [---]
EDCS-51200041.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a guild of carpenters in Ostia to the god Mercury, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200042.translation: For Statilia Thelonica. Statilia Telesphoris, her mother, [made this].
EDCS-51200042.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a mother for her daughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200054.translation: Here rests in peace the innocent Theodenanda, who lived for more or less 3 years, 6 months, and 9 days. She was laid to rest on the 5th day before the Kalends of October, during the reign of Justin, perpetual Augustus, in his first year, in the same consulship, in the 15th indiction.
EDCS-51200054.summary: This Late Antique inscription records the burial of a young girl named Theodenanda, providing precise details of her lifespan and the date of her interment during the reign of Emperor Justin I.

EDCS-51200055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a larger text mentioning the title of a high-ranking official, possibly an emperor, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200056.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly identifying a freedman named Zopus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200057.summary: This is a simple dedication or commission statement, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51200067.translation: Abundantius, illustrious man and patrician, former supervisor, was laid to rest on the 19th day before the Kalends of January, in the third year after the consulship of Lampadius Orestes.
EDCS-51200067.summary: This Late Antique inscription records the burial of Abundantius, an important official, providing his titles and the date of his interment relative to a consulship.

EDCS-51200070.translation: Burial of the saintly memory of Fortunata, who lived more or less 50 years, taken into the sleep of peace on the 4th Ides of February, buried on the 3rd Ides of February, after the consulship of Anicius Olybrius, a most distinguished man. In the 3rd indiction, Mechir 18.
EDCS-51200070.summary: This Late Antique inscription records the burial of Fortunata, providing her approximate age, the dates of her death and burial, and the consular dating along with an Egyptian month and day.

EDCS-51200071.translation: Burial of Leo, the goldsmith, on the 4th day before the Kalends of October, during the consulship of Flavius Messala, a most distinguished man. FL A
EDCS-51200071.summary: This Late Antique inscription records the burial of Leo, a goldsmith, providing the date of his interment and the consular dating.

EDCS-51200072.translation: Caelis Leo, an *evocatus* (a called-up man, possibly a former soldier), rests here in peace, called by the Lord on the 10th day before the Kalends of May, who lived approximately 60 years, under the consulship of Flavius Eutharicus, a most distinguished man. Palumba, a deaconess, rests here in religious peace, called by the Lord on the 4th day before the Ides of February, who lived approximately 60 years, in the 15th indiction, under the consulship of Flavius Belisarius, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-51200072.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and life span of Caelius Leo and Palumba, a deaconess, under the consulships of Flavius Eutharicus and Flavius Belisarius.

EDCS-51200075.translation: To Hilario of the Flaviani, for himself.
EDCS-51200075.summary: This is a dedication to Hilario, likely a tombstone or memorial for himself.

EDCS-51200081.translation: Vibidia Saturnina and Aulus Furius Saturninus gave these images of the Caesars and the temple of Venus, for the decurions and Augustales [donated?] 20 sesterces and for the townspeople [donated?] 4 sesterces, on the occasion of the dedication.
EDCS-51200081.summary: This inscription records the dedication of images of the Caesars and a temple of Venus by Vibidia Saturnina and Aulus Furius Saturninus, with monetary contributions from various civic groups.

EDCS-51200086.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Caecina Albina.

EDCS-51200097.translation: Lucius Asurtius Bassus, son of Gaius, for himself, and for his wife Quintia, daughter of Lucius, and for his family.
EDCS-51200097.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Lucius Asurtius Bassus for himself, his wife Quintia, and their descendants.

EDCS-51500130.translation: Ius Auctus, a *sevirus Augustalis* (an official responsible for the imperial cult), built this portico for the Augustalian games of Emperor Caesar, son of the deified [Emperor], Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, consul for the 13th time, holder of tribunician power for life, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-51500130.summary: This inscription records the construction of a portico by Ius Auctus for the Augustalian games, funded by public decree.

EDCS-51700939.translation: Lyaeus writes most affectionately to Fabio Rufo.
EDCS-51700939.summary: This is a short, affectionate note from Lyaeus to Fabio Rufo, possibly an epitaph or dedication.

EDCS-51700940.summary: This inscription is a brief statement indicating that someone named Aprilis is being sought or missed.

EDCS-51700942.summary: This is a dedication or memorial from Onesimus to his brother Secundus.

EDCS-51700944.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Marcus Fabio Rufo.

EDCS-51700951.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a text, possibly an epitaph or a dedicatory inscription, with an incomplete personal name.

EDCS-51700966.translation: Romula lives here with her man.
EDCS-51700966.summary: This is likely an epitaph for Romula, indicating she lived here with her partner.

EDCS-51700967.translation: Romula lives here with her man.
EDCS-51700967.summary: This is likely an epitaph for Romula, indicating she lived here with her partner.

EDCS-51700968.translation: Romula performs fellatio here with her man and whatever else...
EDCS-51700968.summary: This inscription is a crude and vulgar text, possibly graffiti, mentioning Romula and sexual acts.

EDCS-51700973.translation: Romula, one thousand three hundred men...
EDCS-51700973.summary: This inscription fragment mentions Romula and a large number of men, but its context and purpose are unclear.

EDCS-51700980.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely an epitaph or a marker, identifying Lavi Senius.

EDCS-51700986.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to refer to a woman named Mescinia, possibly in a context related to a cup or drink.

EDCS-51700988.summary: This inscription likely records the presence or association of Epaphroditus and Thalia, possibly as a pair or in a shared space.

EDCS-51700990.translation: Sweetly to the great sea, Byzantia...
EDCS-51700990.summary: This inscription fragment seems to be an invocation or dedication related to the sea and Byzantia, perhaps a dedication from or to a person from Byzantium.

EDCS-51700997.summary: This inscription appears to be a poetic or invocational text addressed to a nymph, possibly related to love or desire.

EDCS-51701000.translation: Abascantus: 2 denarii, 2 asses. Aplus: 1 denarius, 3 asses. Rectus: 1 denarius, 10 asses.

EDCS-57600008.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or ownership marker for Gaius Naevius Demetrius.

EDCS-57600037.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription that records the name Titus Rapius and indicates a person's lifespan.

EDCS-57700002.translation: Tiberius Maecenas Priscus, quaestor of the alimentary funds.
EDCS-57700002.summary: This inscription records the name and official position of Tiberius Maecenas Priscus, who served as quaestor for the alimentary funds.

EDCS-57700010.translation: Caia Aviaana, Publius Varius, son of Publius, aedile, praetor, duovir.
EDCS-57700010.summary: This inscription lists the names and public offices (aedile, praetor, duovir) held by Caia Aviaana and Publius Varius.

EDCS-57700014.translation: Burial of Paccius Caesianus Providentius, an excellent and leading man, on the 15th day before the Kalends of October, in the consulship of Flavius Theodorus, the most illustrious man, who lived 105 years.
EDCS-57700014.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Paccius Caesianus Providentius, noting his age and the consular date.

EDCS-57700015.translation: Burial of Paccius Caestus Anatholus, a man of principal rank, on the day before the Kalends of December, when Flavius Olybius was consul, a most distinguished man, who lived for 12 years and 11 months.
EDCS-57700015.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Paccius Caestus Anatholus, a prominent individual, specifying his age and the consular year.

EDCS-57700017.translation: Burial of Maecia Rosa, a praiseworthy woman, under the 5th day before the Kalends of November, when Flavius Maximus was consul.
EDCS-57700017.summary: This inscription records the burial of Maecia Rosa, a commendable woman, noting the date and the consul of that year.

EDCS-57700018.translation: Here rests Gemma, who lived for more or less 35 years, buried on the Kalends of August, after the consulship of the most distinguished man Bassilus.
EDCS-57700018.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Gemma, stating her approximate age and the consular period.

EDCS-57700019.translation: Here rests in peace Marciana, who lived for more or less 31 years, buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of September, 12 years after the consulship of the most distinguished man Bassilus, in the second indiction.
EDCS-57700019.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Marciana, providing her approximate age, burial date, and a specific dating reference to the consulship of Bassilus and an indiction.

EDCS-57700020.translation: Burial of Felix, who lived for 20 years, buried.
EDCS-57700020.summary: This inscription records the burial of Felix, stating his age.

EDCS-57700024.translation: R., who lived for 10 years, on the 17th day before the Kalends of [November?], when Dioscorus, a most distinguished man, was consul.
EDCS-57700024.summary: This epitaph records the burial of an individual identified only as 'R.', stating her age and the consular year.

EDCS-57700025.translation: Caesidius Martius, who lived for 17 years, after the consulship of our lord Theodosius for the 18th time and Bassilus Albinus.
EDCS-57700025.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Caesidius Martius, specifying his age and dating the inscription by the consulship of Theodosius and Bassilus Albinus.

EDCS-57700029.translation: Felix, a slave, willingly and deservedly had this made for the Lares with his own money.
EDCS-57700029.summary: This dedication records a slave named Felix making a dedication to the Lares with his own funds.

EDCS-57700030.translation: Marcus Socellius Firmus, freedman of Marcus, made the upper three parts, and Marcus Socellius Auctus, freedman of Marcus, made the fourth part, for their mother Socellia Prima, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-57700030.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by two freedmen, Marcus Socellius Firmus and Marcus Socellius Auctus, for their mother, Socellia Prima.

EDCS-57700033.translation: To Marcus Marius, freedman of Marcus; to Maria(?), freedwoman of Marcus, Tertula; to Marcus Marius.
EDCS-57700033.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary monument recording multiple individuals, likely family members, with their patron and status indicated.

EDCS-57800003.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Cornelius Ursus.

EDCS-57800004.summary: This is a property marker for Caius Popilius.

EDCS-57800010.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Statulius Proculus.

EDCS-57800013.summary: This is a dedication by Caius Popilius Primus, likely for a public work or monument.

EDCS-57800017.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Suillius Philargyrus.

EDCS-58400061.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, restored the aqueduct, springs, and public baths at his own expense, for the most pious prince, by the order of the decurions, through his munificence.
EDCS-58400061.summary: This inscription records the restoration of an aqueduct, springs, and public baths by Emperor Antoninus Pius at his own expense, commissioned by the town council.

EDCS-58700001.translation: Larus Satius Crisantus Rufas willingly, now now lovers, here the heart...
EDCS-58700001.summary: This is a very fragmentary and possibly erotic inscription.

EDCS-58700002.translation: Helena, a lustful lover, prays for penises for us.
EDCS-58700002.summary: This is a crude and explicit inscription likely related to fertility or erotic desires.

EDCS-58700006.translation: Burial of Paccia Marcia on the 14th day before the Kalends of May, after the consulship of Hermeniricus and Basilisus, most illustrious men.
EDCS-58700006.summary: This inscription records the burial date of Paccia Marcia in relation to the consulship of two individuals.

EDCS-58700007.translation: Burial of Fuficius Petrus, an honorable man, who lived 25 years, on the 16th day before the Kalends of November, during the consulship of Flavius Messala, most illustrious man.
EDCS-58700007.summary: This inscription records the burial date and age of Fuficius Petrus during the consulship of Flavius Messala.

EDCS-58700008.translation: Regina rests here in peace, who lived more or less 45 years, and was called on the Kalends of March in the consulship of Flavius Valerius, most distinguished man.
EDCS-58700008.summary: A funerary inscription for Regina, noting her lifespan and the date of her 'calling' (deposition) in the consulship of Flavius Valerius.

EDCS-58700009.translation: Innocens Gratus rests here, who lived 8 years, was deposited on the Ides of March and again, four years after the consulship of Basilius, most distinguished man.
EDCS-58700009.summary: A funerary inscription for Gratus, detailing his age at death and the date of his burial, with a further reference point after a consulship.

EDCS-58800032.translation: Titus Laevius, son of Titus, from Caltranum(?), lived 27 years.
EDCS-58800032.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Titus Laevius, son of Titus, providing his name, filiation, probable origin, and age at death.

EDCS-58800033.translation: Pretiosa, a freedwoman of the woman Paquia, lived 30 years, beautiful.
EDCS-58800033.summary: A funerary inscription for Pretiosa, identified as a freedwoman and described as beautiful, with her age at death.

EDCS-58800036.summary: A very brief funerary inscription for Cucufinus.

EDCS-58900593.translation: The bones of Marcus Aelius Tertius are laid here.
EDCS-58900593.summary: A funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Marcus Aelius Tertius.

EDCS-58900595.translation: Belongs to Eleutherus, freedman of Gaius Trebius.
EDCS-58900595.summary: An ownership or dedication inscription, likely for a tomb or object, belonging to Eleutherus.

EDCS-58900596.translation: For Licinia Prisca, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-58900596.summary: A fragmentary dedication or funerary inscription for Licinia Prisca.

EDCS-59100070.summary: A very brief inscription bearing a personal name, likely a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-59100073.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Ostiensius Felicissimus, likely for a building or object he constructed.

EDCS-59100074.translation: From the workshop of Nasennius Fortunatus.
EDCS-59100074.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object, stating it came from the workshop of Nasennius Fortunatus.

EDCS-59200002.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely for a funerary monument or a personal possession.

EDCS-59200003.translation: Artemius is buried here with his wife, with whom he lived for 25 years, 9 months, and 13 days; they made this for her deserving [self].
EDCS-59200003.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Artemius and his wife, detailing their years of marriage and being erected by themselves.

EDCS-59300046.translation: Publius Carsidius Rufus [dedicated this] to Carsidia Felicissima, his sister.
EDCS-59300046.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Publius Carsidius Rufus to his sister, Carsidia Felicissima.

EDCS-59400002.summary: This inscription records Lucius Pontius Eros adorning a balneum (bathhouse), with the inscription incomplete.

EDCS-59400010.translation: To Lucius Gellius, son of Lucius, consul, patron.
EDCS-59400010.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Lucius Gellius, a former consul and patron.

EDCS-59400011.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring a proconsul whose name is partially lost.

EDCS-59400012.translation: Marcus Papirius, son of Marcus, quaestorian scribe, and Gnaeus Carisius, son of Lucius, praetors, fortified [this] by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-59400012.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Papirius and Gnaeus Carisius, holding official positions, undertook fortifications by senatorial decree.

EDCS-59400014.translation: Lucius Pontius Mela, son of Publius, pontifex...
EDCS-59400014.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Lucius Pontius Mela, son of Publius, as a pontifex.

EDCS-59400016.translation: To Marcus Bennius, candidate praetor, Claudian flamen(?)
EDCS-59400016.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Bennius, who held the offices of praetor and flamen, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-59400017.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Venidia, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-59400019.translation: Lucius Calovius Trypho, freedman of Lucius; Calovia Athenais, freedwoman of Lucius; Lucius Calovius Primus, freedman of Lucius, first Augustalis.
EDCS-59400019.summary: This funerary inscription names three members of the Calovius family, including Lucius Calovius Primus who held the prestigious position of first Augustalis, suggesting a date in the early Imperial period.

EDCS-59400020.summary: This inscription appears to be a brief salutation or invocation to Jupiter and someone named Stallia.

EDCS-59400105.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Secundinus.

EDCS-59400107.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Cornelius Valerianus and Flavia Hygia made this for their well-deserving relatives Iubentia Aphrodisia and Publius Novius Martialis.
EDCS-59400107.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication made by Cornelius Valerianus and Flavia Hygia to Iubentia Aphrodisia and Publius Novius Martialis, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-59400109.translation: Lucius Volumnius Marsus, son of Lucius; Quintus Sextilius Philippus, son of Quintus, censors.
EDCS-59400109.summary: This inscription records the names and offices of two censors, Lucius Volumnius Marsus and Quintus Sextilius Philippus, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-59400110.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that Chronius made something and possibly indicating a payment of 10 units, possibly of currency or in measurement.

EDCS-59400111.translation: In the consulship of Titus Catius Ciltus and Lucius Junius. On the 6th day before the Kalends of September. I, Publius Alfenus Varus, trecenarius of Augustus, have written that I received from Lucius Caecilius Iucundus HS 25,439 nummi from the auction of the property of Publius Alfenus Pollio, decurion(?) of Numerius Eprius Nicias, for his share, which he contracted for by delegation from them. Executed at Julia Constantia Nucheria. [Witnesses:] Publius Alfenus Varus, trecenarius of Augustus; Publius Alfenus Pollio; Titus(?) Trausius Admetus; Publius Alfenus Varus, trecenarius of Augustus; Publius Alfenus Pollio.
EDCS-59400111.summary: This is a detailed receipt and legal document from the year 95 CE, recording a financial transaction concerning property auction and delegation of debt, involving several prominent individuals including trecenarii of Augustus and a freedman of Nuceria.

EDCS-59700009.translation: Gaius Velleius Charidemus, freedman of Gaius, made this for himself and Velleia Civitas, freedwoman of Gaius; for his son Gaius Velleius Crescent, freedman of Gaius; for his daughter Velleia...ula, daughter of Gaius; for his freedman Gaius Velleius Helpidus, freedman of Gaius; for his freedwoman Telete, freedwoman of Gaius; and for my freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-59700009.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Gaius Velleius Charidemus, for himself, his family members, and his freedmen and their descendants, suggesting a date in the Imperial period.

EDCS-59700017.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Quintus Pla[---] who made something, possibly a funerary monument.

EDCS-59700028.translation: Clodia Prepusa, freedwoman of Lucius, made this monument for herself and for Lucius Clodius Atimetus, her well-deserving husband, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants; it shall not pass to an outside fiduciary heir. In the front twenty feet, in the land thirty feet.
EDCS-59700028.summary: A funerary monument erected by Clodia Prepusa for herself, her husband, and their descendants, with specific dimensions and a clause against external heirs.

EDCS-59700030.translation: Iulia Nice, freedwoman of Augusta, and Antigonus made this for Tiberius Claudius Diphilus, freedman of Augustus, and for themselves and their families.
EDCS-59700030.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Iulia Nice and Antigonus to Tiberius Claudius Diphilus, likely a family member or associate, and to themselves.

EDCS-59700045.summary: A fragmentary inscription containing personal names, possibly related to a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-59700046.translation: Marcus [---] died. Marcus [---] died. Titus [---] died. Lucius Po[---] died. Lucius Pos[---] died. Aulus Egri[lius ---] died. Gaius Novi[---] died. EDCS-59700057.summary: A fragmented inscription mentioning 'incomparable' and the name Pylades, possibly a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-59700064.translation: Quintus Iulius Honoratus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, and his heir Iulia Optata Iuniana, have ownership in this sepulchral monument, granted to them by Prastinia Asclepiodota, heir [---], freedmen, freedwomen [---].
EDCS-59700064.summary: A funerary monument grant recorded by Quintus Iulius Honoratus and his heir Iulia Optata Iuniana, acquired from Prastinia Asclepiodota, and mentioning beneficiaries.

EDCS-59700073.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph for Junius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-59700096.translation: Ferox [---] to his freedman Tarius, and to his father [---] and to his mother [---]iae this sepulcrum (?).
EDCS-59700096.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription mentioning Ferox dedicating a tomb for his freedman Tarius, his father, and his mother.

EDCS-59700125.translation: Lucius Domitius Felix, freedman of Lucius, for himself, and for Domitia Musa, fellow freedwoman, and for their freedmen, descendants, and their family.
EDCS-59700125.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Domitius Felix for himself, his fellow freedwoman Domitia Musa, and their descendants.

EDCS-59700129.translation: Utilis made this for Histimniae Venustae.
EDCS-59700129.summary: This is a funerary epigram for Histimniae Venustae, likely set up by her freedman or slave, Utilis.

EDCS-59700142.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Octavia Crescens.

EDCS-59700143.translation: For [---]. The Augustalis and quinquennial of the Augustales, and patron of the guild of grain measurers of Ostia, the adjutor Laurens Lavinas, purchased this for himself while alive.
EDCS-59700143.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Laurens Lavinas, who held several important municipal and guild positions in Ostia and purchased the burial plot for himself.

EDCS-59700146.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph or a dedication by Aulus Tetteius Faustus.

EDCS-59700159.translation: Julius P[---] made this for himself and his family. Julius P[---] made this for himself [and his family ---].
EDCS-59700159.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly a duplicate or revised version, indicating that Julius P[---] dedicated a monument for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-59700165.translation: The perpetual quinquennial members of the body of veterans, permitted to associate by the indulgence of our lord Augustus, [---] Passenius Didymus, Publius Apollonius Barbarus, Quintus Passenius Didymus the son, Lucius Apollonius Rufus the son, the commoners Titus Aurelius Pthongus, Quintus Pinnius Felix the senior, Marcus Fullonius Saturninus, Gaius Minicius Severus, Gaius Julius Felix the senior, Lucius Domitius Fortunius, Publius Apollonius Rufus the son, Titus Aurelius Primus, Marcus Aurelius Metrodorus, Marcus Aurelius Gaius, Titus Flavius Antiochus, Lucius Septimius Diodorus, Titus Flavius Fortunius the son, Titus Aurelius Clemens the son. // Lucius Domitius Dius, Gaius Julius Magnus, Gaius Julius Magnianus, Gaius Minicius Saturninus, Gaius Marius Felicissimus, Marcus Annius Severus.
EDCS-59700165.summary: This inscription lists the names of members of a body of veterans, organized under the indulgence of an emperor, and potentially includes additional members or a second list.

EDCS-59900071.translation: To Lucius Aurelius Augusti libertus Pylades, the foremost pantomime of his time, crowned four times with the hieronic crown, patron of the priests of Apollo, honored synod official, decorated with decurional and duumviral honors, and augur, by decree of the decurions of Puteoli, for his love of country and exceptional generosity in providing gladiatorial games and passive hunts, by the indulgence of the most sacred prince [[Commodus Pius Felix Augustus]] -- the Cornelia century.
EDCS-59900071.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Aurelius Pylades, a celebrated pantomime and freedman of the emperor, with decurional and augural honors by the city of Puteoli, recognizing his generosity and imperial favor.

EDCS-60000006.translation: The veteran Gaius Julius Maximus of the V Praetorian Cohort, Pomponia the founder, [---].

EDCS-62101292.translation: From Domitianus Augustus, according to the accounting of Felix, the servant. In the consulship of Augurinus, year 766.

EDCS-62101298.translation: Epigonus, the pious, lived 4 years and 2 months. He lies here.
EDCS-62101298.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, lifespan, and burial place of Epigonus.

EDCS-62101301.translation: Gaius Antistius Vetus, son of Gaius, grandson of Gaius; Gaius Valerius Flaccus Tanurianus, son of Lucius; Publius Vergilius Pontianus, son of Marcus; Tiberius Vergilius Rufus, son of Tiberius; Publius Catienus Sabinus, son of Publius, supervisors of the riverbanks and channel of the Tiber, by decree of the Senate, established the boundary in a straight line, measuring... feet.
EDCS-62101301.summary: This inscription records the work of four officials, supervisors of the Tiber's banks and channel, who established a boundary line.

EDCS-62101306.translation: Gaius Livinius Victor, freedman of Pelasgus, a lictor from the three centuries which appear in the magistracies and priesthoods of the Caesars, in his own name and that of his son, Gaius Livinius Prosperus, for the honor of the Augustales, undertook the restoration of the bridge, rebuilt at public expense. To the restoration of which he had contributed 2000 sesterces with additional money, he afterwards raised it from the roadside embankment and saw to its roofing, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-62101306.summary: This is an honorary inscription by Gaius Livinius Victor, a freedman and lictor, detailing his contributions to the restoration of a bridge and its roofing, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-62601171.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Crescens, son of Iunius, of the Palatina tribe, made this for himself and for Gaius Iunius Canus, Iunius Crescentianus, Iunia Crescentina, Iunius Crescens, his sons, freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants. In the front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-62601171.summary: This is a funerary inscription setting out a burial plot and naming the deceased and their family members and descendants, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-62601178.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Aulus Egrilius.
EDCS-62601178.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aulus Egrilius.

EDCS-62601180.translation: Publius Decimius Paulus granted the monument to Lucius Caecilius Ce[...]
EDCS-62601180.summary: This inscription records Publius Decimius Paulus granting a monument to Lucius Caecilius.

EDCS-62601187.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Gavius Orfitus and Lucius Arrius Pudens. [...] Patron? // Tannonius // Plebs? [...] // Peduceus Diodorus // ... // Lucius Mummius Callistianus the younger, Marcus Lucceius Deuter, Quintus Patrius Victor, Gaius Ilarius Felix, Gaius Iulius Silvianus, Gnaeus Sergius Hilarus, Lucius Valerius Fortunatus, Marcus Marius Restitutus, Gaius Iulius Firmus, Gnaeus Rulius Hermes the younger, Tiberius Claudius Callistianus, Aulus Caedicius Felix, [...] Felix, [...]ius Polycarpus, Cornelius Zosimianus, [...]eius Lupercus, Tiberius Claudius Telesphorus, Aulus Caedicius Corunthianus, Lucius Messenius Crispinus, // Titus [...], Publius [...], Sextus [...], Quintus [...]
EDCS-62601187.summary: This is a fragmentary list of names, likely attendees or dedicants at a public event or dedication, dated by consuls to the Imperial period.

EDCS-62601188.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Audia, a most chaste woman who lived 10 years and 15 days. Iovianus made this for his most beloved wife, who lived with him from the day of her virginity 19 years and 45 days.
EDCS-62601188.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Audia, commemorating her life and death, and was erected by her husband Iovianus.

EDCS-62601194.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Decimus Iunius Hilarus, her husband. Egrilia Festa made this for a well-deserving husband.
EDCS-62601194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Iunius Hilarus, erected by his wife Egrilia Festa.

EDCS-62900219.translation: To Titius Arborius, against the law of nature, a father to his dearest son, who died on his 25th birthday in daylight.
EDCS-62900219.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for a son named Titius Arborius, set up by his father.

EDCS-62900221.translation: To Marcus Alfius Nicephor, for his son Priscus, aged 4 years.

EDCS-63500017.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a man who held numerous high priesthoods and magistracies for his wife and her descendants, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-63500027.translation: To Julia Paula, his wife. Valerianus, husband, and Cyriaca, daughter.

EDCS-63500050.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to name Lucius Nabur Ae.

EDCS-63500067.translation: Flavia [---] made for (her) most devoted mother.
EDCS-63500067.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Flavia for her mother.

EDCS-63500071.translation: Viria Marcella, a most distinguished lady, made (it).

EDCS-63600417.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Proiecticius, a prefect, providing his lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-63600424.translation: Gnaeus Livinius Suavis, freedman of Gnaeus, and Livinia Asclepia, freedwoman of Gnaeus, for themselves and for their patron Gnaeus Livinius Nicephorus, freedman of Gnaeus.
EDCS-63600424.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by freedmen for themselves and their patron.

EDCS-63600443.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Milara for herself and potentially others, possibly related to a freedman named Aulus Gabinius Datus.

EDCS-63600444.translation: To Lucius Granius Rufus, son of Numerius.
EDCS-63600444.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Granius Rufus.

EDCS-63600445.translation: Tertius, freedman, [erected this] to his excellent patron Trophimus, freedman of Aulus Grattius.
EDCS-63600445.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a freedman, Tertius, to his patron, Trophimus.

EDCS-63600446.translation: Marcus Herucius Bassus, son of Marcus, from the Falernian region, and Arria Nice, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-63600446.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, possibly a couple, Marcus Herucius Bassus and Arria Nice.

EDCS-63600448.summary: This is a dedication to Helena, a freedwoman.

EDCS-63600451.translation: To Novius Nicostratus, for himself and for his wife Iulia, daughter of Gnaeus.
EDCS-63600451.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Novius Nicostratus and his wife Iulia.

EDCS-63600453.translation: To Caius Octavius Protus, freedman of Caius; Octavia [erected this].
EDCS-63600453.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Caius Octavius Protus, erected by Octavia.

EDCS-63600454.translation: To Lucius Ofilus Faustus, freedman, for himself and his deserving family.
EDCS-63600454.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up for Lucius Ofilus Faustus and his family.

EDCS-63600457.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Pellius Labeo.

EDCS-63600459.translation: To Publius Petronius Stephanus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-63600459.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedman named Stephanus, possibly indicating his patron.

EDCS-63600463.translation: To Sylvinia, dearest little daughter of Velleius. We parents, deeply saddened, are deceived by our hopes, and by time. Death mocks our anxious cares; life is nothing.
EDCS-63600463.summary: This is a poignant epitaph for a young girl named Sylvinia, lamenting the brevity of life and the cruelty of death, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63600465.translation: To Varia, daughter of Quintus, mother.
EDCS-63600465.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Varia, daughter of Quintus, honoring her role as a mother.

EDCS-63600466.summary: This is a simple name inscription, possibly for a tombstone or a dedicatory label, for Lucius Visellius.

EDCS-63900040.translation: From the pottery works of the Vicciani family.

EDCS-63900041.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Augustus Fidelis, possibly a freedman or an official.
