EDCS-63900062.translation: To Mother Mainia, Memmia Prisca fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-63900062.summary: This is a votive inscription to the mother goddess Mainia, dedicated by Memmia Prisca.

EDCS-63900064.translation: The deposition of Severinus of holy memory, a deacon of the holy church of Teano, who lived about 66 years, deposited on the 5th day before the Ides of September, after the consulship of Paulinus the Younger, a man of most excellent standing.
EDCS-63900064.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of Severinus, a deacon of the church of Teano, who died around 66 years of age, dating to after the consulship of Paulinus the Younger (likely 491 CE or later).

EDCS-63900070.translation: To the sacred springs, Lucceia Maxima, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-63900070.summary: This dedication to the sacred springs was made by Lucceia Maxima.

EDCS-64000002.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Julius Dynamus, a well-deserving patron, his freedmen.
EDCS-64000002.summary: This tomb inscription honors the freedmen's well-deserving patron, Julius Dynamus.

EDCS-64000004.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Claudius.

EDCS-64000006.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Aurelius Eutychianus on a monument.

EDCS-64000013.translation: Marcus Aurelius Lucretius Lysias, curator of the water.
EDCS-64000013.summary: This inscription records the name and official position of Marcus Aurelius Lucretius Lysias as curator of the water supply.

EDCS-64000037.translation: To the Divine Shades. Atilia Plocamis made this for her most excellent and most holy husband, Cerdon, freedman of Marcus Accenna Saturninus, an actor, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-64000037.summary: This tomb inscription honors Cerdon, an actor and freedman, by his wife Atilia Plocamis.

EDCS-64000103.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Tiberius Teltonius Marcellus, primipilaris, prefect.
EDCS-64000103.summary: This tomb inscription honors Tiberius Teltonius Marcellus, a military officer.

EDCS-64000105.translation: Of Marcus Marcius, freedman of Marcus. Heracleotis, the grammarian. His freedmen Agrippa and Euphronius.
EDCS-64000105.summary: This inscription commemorates Heracleotis, a grammarian and freedman, with a dedication from his own freedmen.

EDCS-64200007.translation: To the Divine Shades. Charite Primitiva, mother, for her daughter.
EDCS-64200007.summary: This tomb inscription records Charite Primitiva dedicating a monument to her daughter.

EDCS-64200008.translation: To the Divine Shades. Of Pomponia Athenais, the mother.
EDCS-64200008.summary: This tomb inscription honors Pomponia Athenais, identified as a mother.

EDCS-64200009.translation: Septimia Synoris lived 18 years. Titus Veturius Erastus dedicated this to his wife.
EDCS-64200009.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Veturius Erastus to his deceased wife, Septimia Synoris, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-64300016.translation: To Decimus Ofillius Pamphilus, freedman of Decimus, according to the will.
EDCS-64300016.summary: A dedication to Decimus Ofillius Pamphilus, a freedman, as stipulated by a will.

EDCS-64300027.summary: A very short funerary inscription wishing farewell to Chloe.

EDCS-64300028.summary: A very short funerary inscription wishing farewell to Chloe.

EDCS-64300038.summary: A brief inscription possibly recording the names of family members, perhaps on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-64300057.translation: My native land is sacred Caesarea; the love of athletes bade me go to the games, through all the East and to the golden city of Rome. Coming to the waters of Puteoli in Baiae to see, I did not get to, alas, left weak by old age; but I got a share of the common fate of all mortals. And if you want to know my name, I will tell you this: they call me Bettinianus, secretary of the Xystus.
EDCS-64300057.summary: An epitaph of Bettinianus, a secretary, lamenting his inability to participate in games due to old age, despite his travels and aspirations.

EDCS-64300058.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Gaius Pompeius Atticatus, your son, who lived 18 years. Gaius Pompeius Atticatus.
EDCS-64300058.summary: A dedication by Gaius Pompeius Atticatus to the Chthonic Gods for his son, also named Gaius Pompeius Atticatus, who died at 18.

EDCS-64400022.translation: In this land, though a stranger, I leave behind the light of my sacred homeland... Leonidas made this tomb for his son Alexander.
EDCS-64400022.summary: A funerary monument erected by Leonidas for his son Alexander, expressing sentiments about being a stranger far from his homeland.

EDCS-64400027.translation: To Octavia Salvia, wife, well-deserving. Gaius Laecanius Alexander.
EDCS-64400027.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Laecanius Alexander to his deserving wife, Octavia Salvia.

EDCS-64400040.translation: ... to Aemilia Exorata, dearest son, they made (this).
EDCS-64400040.summary: A funerary monument made by unspecified individuals for their dearest son, Aemilia Exorata.

EDCS-64400041.translation: To M. Fo[...], of the 2nd Parthian Legion.
EDCS-64400041.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely dedicating something to a person associated with the 2nd Parthian Legion.

EDCS-64400061.translation: Milonia, daughter of Titus, mother, made this from her own funds.
EDCS-64400061.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a woman named Milonia from her own money.

EDCS-64400063.summary: This is a heavily damaged inscription that appears to record the name and filiation of a person, possibly Julius [...]ius.

EDCS-64400064.translation: Lucius Aemilius Zenodotus erected this for Aurelia Mariana, his incomparable wife, and for Aurelia Candida, his daughter.
EDCS-64400064.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Aemilius Zenodotus dedicating a monument to his wife and daughter.

EDCS-64400065.translation: To Lucius Raniu Se[...], who was a most distinguished man and a designated consul, a man of...
EDCS-64400065.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to Lucius Raniu Se[...], who was a distinguished man and a designated consul.

EDCS-64400068.translation: Satricania, daughter of Caius, wife of Lucius Gungius.
EDCS-64400068.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Satricania, daughter of Caius and wife of Lucius Gungius.

EDCS-64400074.summary: This is a simple inscription recording the name and filiation of Lucius Etrillius.

EDCS-64400076.summary: This is a simple inscription recording the name and filiation of Marcus Acutilius.

EDCS-64400077.summary: This is a simple inscription recording the name and filiation of Lucius Caidicius.

EDCS-64400249.translation: Scaeva, son of Caius Veratius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-64400249.summary: This inscription records the name, filiation, and tribal affiliation of Scaeva, son of Caius Veratius.

EDCS-64400432.translation: To Mamia, his dearest mother (?), Marcus Mammius Felix, his son, [erected this].
EDCS-64400432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely dedicated by a son to his mother, Marcus Mammius Felix to Mamia.

EDCS-64400442.translation: To Urania, freedwoman of Titus... by the decision of Urania.
EDCS-64400442.summary: This inscription records a dedication or funerary monument, possibly set up by Urania for someone else, or by someone for Urania.

EDCS-64500150.summary: This is a simple name inscription, possibly for a tombstone or dedication by Marcus Pontius Philegurus.

EDCS-64500151.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Pontia, identified simply as 'mother'.

EDCS-64500152.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Marcus Nonius Salvius, possibly on a tombstone or property marker.

EDCS-64500176.translation: Gaius Heius Epagathus, freedman of Gaius; Heia Tertia, freedwoman of Gaius; Heia Salvia, freedwoman of Gaius; Marcus Heius Simo, freedman of Gaius, grandson of Marcus.
EDCS-64500176.summary: This inscription lists members of the Heia family, including freedmen and their descendants, likely on a shared tomb or monument.

EDCS-64500184.translation: Publius Heius Nicia; Numerius Calinius Canopus.
EDCS-64500184.summary: This inscription appears to list two names, Publius Heius Nicia and Numerius Calinius Canopus, possibly on a tomb or shared monument.

EDCS-64500186.translation: Lucceia, freedwoman of Balbus Clucera; Lucceia, freedwoman of her father Balbus; Dionysia the pious.
EDCS-64500186.summary: This inscription commemorates Lucceia, freedwoman of Balbus Clucera, and Lucceia, freedwoman of her father Balbus, along with Dionysia, possibly family members or associates.

EDCS-64500187.translation: Novia Salvia, freedwoman of Numerius, lived piously and virtuously; here she lies. Hail and farewell.
EDCS-64500187.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Novia Salvia, a freedwoman of Numerius, emphasizing her virtuous life.

EDCS-64500188.translation: Thais, [freedwoman] of Lucius Balbus. Greetings, farewell.
EDCS-64500188.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Thais, a freedwoman of Lucius Balbus, with a common farewell greeting.

EDCS-64500189.translation: Of Publius Anitinus, freedman of Publius Alexander.
EDCS-64500189.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman named Alexander, identified by his patron Publius Anitinus.

EDCS-64500190.translation: Vitrasia Canthara, freedwoman of a woman. Statius Obinius Hermia, freedman of Statius. Statius Obinius Primus, freedman of Statius. Olla(?).
EDCS-64500190.summary: This funerary inscription lists several individuals, including freedwomen and freedmen, associated with names like Vitrasia and Statius Obinius, possibly part of a family or collegium.

EDCS-64500237.translation: Hyperechius, father, and Diomedes and Metrodora to their son...
EDCS-64500237.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription, likely a dedication by parents (Hyperechius, Diomedes, Metrodora) to their deceased son.

EDCS-64500246.summary: This funerary inscription records a mother's dedication for her deceased daughter.

EDCS-64500252.translation: ...parents made to perpetuate the memory of. Marcius, the equestrian, Purra.
EDCS-64500252.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by parents, possibly including an equestrian named Marcius and Purra, to commemorate a deceased individual.

EDCS-64500446.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its content, but it begins with Roman names.

EDCS-64500451.summary: This fragmentary inscription begins to identify an individual named Maecia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-64500570.translation: To Marcus Holocennius, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, his heirs according to his will.
EDCS-64500570.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that heirs, according to a will, established this monument for Marcus Holocennius.

EDCS-64600118.translation: Fabia Domitiana, daughter of Quintus, sacred to Hercules Baianus.
EDCS-64600118.summary: This is a religious dedication to the god Hercules Baianus by Fabia Domitiana, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-64600150.translation: To Julia Nigrina, who lived 7 months and 8 days. Julius Severus, soldier of the II Parthica Severiana legion, to his most sweet daughter, a memorial.
EDCS-64600150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julia Nigrina, detailing her short lifespan and commemorating her with a dedication from her father, Julius Severus, a soldier.

EDCS-64600154.translation: … a soldier … made [this] for one deserving well.
EDCS-64600154.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a soldier, indicating that someone (perhaps a relative or friend) made this monument for him because he deserved it.

EDCS-64600155.translation: Valerius Muscianus made [this] for his well-deserving son.
EDCS-64600155.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Valerius Muscianus for his son, indicating he made this monument because his son was deserving.

EDCS-64600158.translation: Iustinianus, soldier of the II Parthica legion, and his mother Honorata took care to have [this] made for their well-deserving son.
EDCS-64600158.summary: This funerary inscription is from Iustinianus, a soldier in the II Parthica legion, and his mother Honorata, for their deserving son, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-64600160.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Proculus, but provides no further context or information.

EDCS-64600162.translation: Quintus Granius Heliodorus, freedman of Publius, sacred to Venus.
EDCS-64600162.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object or site to the goddess Venus by Quintus Granius Heliodorus, a freedman, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-64600203.translation: Here rests in peace the holy Musonius, bishop, who lived more or less seventy years, was laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of October, after the consulship of Paulinus the Younger.
EDCS-64600203.summary: This is an epitaph for Bishop Musonius, recording his death date as September 19th, 536 AD, based on his age and the consulship of Paulinus Iunior.

EDCS-64600223.translation: Manius Statuleius, son of Maraeus, aged fifty-seven.
EDCS-64600223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Manius Statuleius, son of Maraeus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-64600224.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Socidia Memmia, daughter of Quintus, recording her name and parentage.

EDCS-64600275.translation: For Mecrosae, a praiseworthy woman, under the date of the 5th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of Flavius Maximus.
EDCS-64600275.summary: This is a dedication or commemoration for a woman named Mecrosae, dating to the consulship of Flavius Maximus in 387 AD.

EDCS-64700386.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for a woman named Optata.

EDCS-64700390.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Granius Crispinus I and Grania Libye, husband and wife, [dedicated this] to Granius Antiochus.
EDCS-64700390.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a couple to a deceased person, likely a family member, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800305.summary: This is a simple personal name inscription, likely on a tombstone, from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-64800415.translation: For the family and freedmen of Gnaeus Asinius Rufus.
EDCS-64800415.summary: This inscription indicates a family burial plot or endowment established by Gnaeus Asinius Rufus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800424.translation: Of the most distinguished Furius Placidus.
EDCS-64800424.summary: This inscription likely refers to a funerary monument or honorific dedication for Furius Placidus, a man of high status, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800465.translation: [Dedicated by] Quintus Attius R() IIvir(?), [to Gaius Marius, son of Gaius], seven times consul and tribune of the plebs.
EDCS-64800465.summary: This is a fragment of an honorific inscription for Gaius Marius, a prominent Roman official, possibly dedicated by Quintus Attius, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-64800466.translation: Quintus Attius [dedicated] the temple to the Mother...
EDCS-64800466.summary: This fragmented inscription records Quintus Attius dedicating a temple or shrine to a "Mother" deity, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800467.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary notice, mentioning Gaius Livinius and Quintus Attius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800468.translation: [For...]ia, freedwoman of Publius; [For...]sia, freedwoman of the wife; [For...]cius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-64800468.summary: This inscription lists several freedmen and freedwomen and their patrons, likely part of a funerary monument, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800477.summary: This is a dedication of an object or structure to the god Serapis by Lucius Primitius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800485.summary: This inscription simply records two names, likely a funerary dedication or a notice of ownership, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-64800487.summary: This is a dedication to Sextus Numisius Eron.

EDCS-64800488.summary: This inscription records the name of Maxuma Seiu, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-64800500.summary: This is a fragment possibly referring to the deified emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-64900361.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription naming Messius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-64900506.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, likely to Iulia Ammia Helpidia.

EDCS-64900507.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Gaius Nummius.

EDCS-64900519.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for Lollia Pompeiana, described as dutiful.

EDCS-64900541.translation: She was placed in peace during the consulship of Flavius Appion.
EDCS-64900541.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of an individual during the consulship of Flavius Appion.

EDCS-64900548.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication made by Amplius.

EDCS-64900604.translation: To our lord Constantine Augustus. Memmius Vitrasius Orfitus, most illustrious man, prefect of the city, judge of sacred jurisdictions for a second time, devoted to his divine majesty, under the care of Publilius Caeionius Iulianus, most illustrious man.
EDCS-64900604.summary: This is an inscription dedicating an object or honor to Emperor Constantine, detailing the honors and offices of Memmius Vitrasius Orfitus, under the supervision of Publilius Caeionius Iulianus, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-64900606.translation: Livius, may I lick your cunt, and Tertulla, the Ephesian, loves your cunt; Terisium.
EDCS-64900606.summary: This inscription is an obscene graffito, likely from the Roman period, expressing sexual desires and possibly rivalries.

EDCS-64900770.translation: The things of Oporis and Astronos are free from tax, both words and deeds; the things of Oporis and Astronos are to remain... if anyone speaks otherwise before them, let all be inscribed here.
EDCS-64900770.summary: This inscription, written in Greek, appears to be a declaration or a legalistic statement concerning the property or rights of Oporis and Astronos, possibly setting boundaries or asserting ownership, likely dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-64900876.translation: Of Titus Hordionius, son of Gnaeus, Flaccus of Falerni.
EDCS-64900876.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly naming Titus Hordionius Flaccus, son of Gnaeus, and mentioning his origin from Falerni, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64900878.translation: Of the most distinguished man, Lucilianus.
EDCS-64900878.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely names a man named Lucilianus, described as 'v(iri) c(larissimi)' (of distinguished rank), probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64900972.summary: This inscription is a fragment, possibly part of a funerary monument or a dedication, mentioning 'Augustas' in a context of deposition, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64901015.translation: Gaius Munitius, son of Marcus, Marcus Umedius, son of Lucius, and Sextus Herucius, son of Sextus, as curule aediles, by decree of the senate, took care of the construction of the kitchen.
EDCS-64901015.summary: This inscription records the completion of a public kitchen by three curule aediles, Gaius Munitius, Marcus Umedius, and Sextus Herucius, acting on a senate's decree, likely dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-64901120.translation: Marcus Marcius, freedman of Marcus, Euphronius.
EDCS-64901120.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names Marcus Marcius Euphronius, identified as a freedman of a Marcus, likely a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64901127.translation: To Porcia, daughter of Tullus, of Gaius Cato.
EDCS-64901127.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Porcia, daughter of Tullus, and granddaughter of Gaius Cato, from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-64901128.translation: To Gaius Atrius, freedman of Gaius, of Sinda.
EDCS-64901128.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Gaius Atrius Sindaeus, identified as a freedman of Gaius, originating from Sinda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64901132.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, born for the good of the state, [honored by the decree of] the divine lords our emperors Valentinian, Theodosius, and Arcadius Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-64901132.summary: This inscription is a dedication honoring the emperor Flavius Claudius Julianus and also the emperors Valentinian, Theodosius, and Arcadius, praising them for their service to the state, likely dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-65200007.translation: To Naevia Hilara, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-65200007.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Naevia Hilara.

EDCS-65200009.translation: Sextus Tarnidius Alcon for himself and for Sextus Tarnidius Thalamus; Quintia Saturnina, daughter of Publius (?), his wife.
EDCS-65200009.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Sextus Tarnidius Alcon for himself and another person, and includes his wife, Quintia Saturnina.

EDCS-65200010.summary: This appears to be a funerary dedication for a person named Tullius Tigellinus.

EDCS-65200011.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Valeria Sympherusa.

EDCS-65200012.translation: To Decimus Valerius Tryphon, freedman of Decimus; and to Decimus Valerius Crescent, freedman of Decimus.
EDCS-65200012.summary: This inscription records the burial of two freedmen, Decimus Valerius Tryphon and Decimus Valerius Crescent, both freedmen of a Decimus Valerius.

EDCS-65200019.translation: To Titus Plotidius Silo, son of Titus, for his father Titus Plotidius, his mother Mevia Pacci, his sister Plotidia, for himself, and for his nephew Gaius Pontius Gallus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-65200019.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Titus Plotidius Silo for his family members and himself, as well as for his nephew.

EDCS-65200070.translation: Mettia Pusilla, freedwoman of Marcus, [dedicates this monument or tomb] for Marcus Mettius Princeps, fellow freedman, and for herself and her family, and for Marcus Mettius [---]to, freedman; this monument or external tomb will not follow the heir.
EDCS-65200070.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Mettia Pusilla for her fellow freedman Marcus Mettius Princeps and herself, specifying that the tomb is not to pass to an heir.

EDCS-65200071.translation: [...] to Nutia Maxima, wife of Marcus; [...] to Valeria Paula (?), daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-65200071.summary: This inscription appears to contain funerary dedications for two women, Nutia Maxima and Valeria Paula.

EDCS-65200072.translation: The bones of Ocratia Dioclias, freedwoman of a woman, are placed here.
EDCS-65200072.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Ocratia Dioclias, a freedwoman.

EDCS-65200074.translation: Valeria Polla, daughter of Gaius, for herself and for her son Lucius Annius Celer, son of Lucius, and for her father Gaius Valerius [---] and for her mother Octavia, and for her husband Lucius Annius Pollio, son of Lucius.
EDCS-65200074.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Valeria Polla for herself, her son, her parents, and her husband.

EDCS-65200075.translation: Sextus Antius Salvius set this up to VEN[---]RIDIO.
EDCS-65200075.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Sextus Antius Salvius.

EDCS-65200077.translation: To Marcus Badio Surellus, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, a man, and for himself and [---]
EDCS-65200077.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Marcus Badio Surellus.

EDCS-65200080.translation: To Quintia Salvia, freedwoman of Quintus, [---] to Quintus Curt[ius---]
EDCS-65200080.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly funerary, to Quintia Salvia and Quintus Curt[ius---].

EDCS-65200144.translation: [---], son of Manius, grandson of Manius, [gave this gift?].
EDCS-65200144.summary: This inscription records a gift given by a man identified by his filiation and agnomen.

EDCS-65300063.translation: Caius Diogenes, freedman of Caius Cossutius // Cossutia Phil[---], freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-65300063.summary: This inscription records two individuals, likely a freedman and a freedwoman, possibly as a joint dedication.

EDCS-65300221.translation: [---] to Orfius [---], prefect of the engineers.
EDCS-65300221.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Orfius, who held the position of prefect of the engineers.

EDCS-65300222.summary: This inscription is a simple naming of 'Christophorus'.

EDCS-65300224.translation: Quintus Caecilius Eros, freedman of Capitolini.
EDCS-65300224.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Caecilius Eros, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-65300237.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or funerary text mentioning Andrias and his family.

EDCS-65400049.translation: To Lucius Aemilius Proculus, son of Lucius, of the Voturia tribe, a veteran centurion, from Cumae, by legacy of four thousand sesterces; his wife Aemilia Ephesia, adding six thousand sesterces from her own money, for herself, her freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants, and for Proculus's heirs who were designated in the will regarding the status of freedom, no one shall have the power to sell this monument.
EDCS-65400049.summary: This is a funerary inscription establishing a monument for Lucius Aemilius Proculus and his wife Aemilia Ephesia, detailing legacies and restrictions on the monument's sale, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-65500118.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Colatinus to his sweetest wife Lucretia, incomparable in modesty and a glory to women, who lived 22 years, 5 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-65500118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800101.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800103.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800149.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800157.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800158.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800159.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65900066.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary ownership mark or a label, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65900073.translation: Garum, the best of Aulus Umbricius.
EDCS-65900073.summary: This inscription appears to be a label for a product, possibly garum (fish sauce), from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65900075.summary: This inscription is a title or dedication, possibly related to a literary work or a performance, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65900077.translation: Flos, fifteen years old, of Marcus and Lucius Claudius.
EDCS-65900077.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Flos, dated by the names of his father and grandfather.

EDCS-65900078.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription in honor of Claudio Trophimus.

EDCS-65900079.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription, indicating the deceased Claudius Trophimus.

EDCS-65900081.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription in honor of Aulus Umbricius Abascantus.

EDCS-65900085.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription, naming Lucius Sagius Prodamus.

EDCS-65900086.summary: This inscription records the name Numerius Sillius, likely for funerary or ownership purposes.

EDCS-65900119.translation: Marcus Aurelius Masus, soldier of the II Parthica Severiana legion, century of X, first cohort, who lived 31 years, 2 months, 3 days, served 10 years; Aurelia Dioclea, his wife and heir, made this for him as well-deserving.
EDCS-65900119.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier named Marcus Aurelius Masus, detailing his age, service, and dedication by his wife and heir, with an approximate date inferable from the legion's designation.

EDCS-66700019.translation: P. Caius, son of Caius, of the Pomptina tribe. P. Caius, of the Pomptina tribe, quaestor.
EDCS-66700019.summary: This inscription records two individuals, likely father and son, with one identified as a quaestor, suggesting a career in Roman public life.

EDCS-67000256.translation: Sacred to the Nymphs. Caius Luccius Eros paid his vow.
EDCS-67000256.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the Nymphs by Caius Luccius Eros, indicating the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-67200460.translation: Burial of Marcellinus, a man of good repute, the chief physician, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, under the consulship of Theodorus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-67200460.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Marcellinus, a chief physician, with a precise date provided by the consular year.

EDCS-67400171.translation: To the divine spirits of Quintus Caecilius Hilarus; Caecilia Nicopolis, his wife, and Magna, his daughter.
EDCS-67400171.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Caecilius Hilarus by his wife and daughter.

EDCS-67400188.translation: To Porcia, daughter of Tullius, wife of Cato.
EDCS-67400188.summary: This is a dedication to Porcia, daughter of Tullius and wife of Cato.

EDCS-67400201.translation: Euhemer, a pearl merchant and freedman of Servilia, gave and dedicated this gift to Silvanus.
EDCS-67400201.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Euhemer, a freedman and pearl merchant.

EDCS-67400489.translation: Gnaeus Luccius, father and son, took care of bringing and distributing the water with their own money.
EDCS-67400489.summary: This inscription records the public works undertaken by Gnaeus Luccius, father and son, concerning the water supply.

EDCS-67500094.translation: Tiberius Claudius Eutyches, freedman of Caesar.
EDCS-67500094.summary: This is an identification of Tiberius Claudius Eutyches, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-67700096.translation: Paula, the only servant of her parents, a household slave, chose here for herself a perpetual home and lies rejoicing in the altars, a guest in the embrace of the blessed martyr Felix, where she lived for 6 years; her burial was placed on the 12th day before the Kalends of November, after the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-67700096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Paula, a young slave who died after choosing to be buried in the vicinity of the martyr Felix, with her burial date recorded.

EDCS-67700097.translation: May the spirit of Felix be favorable.
EDCS-67700097.summary: This is a short devotional phrase invoking the spirit of Felix.

EDCS-67700098.translation: Felix Leo and all his household.
EDCS-67700098.summary: This is a simple invocation or dedication involving Felix Leo and his family.

EDCS-67700099.translation: Valerius, may you live and flourish in the blessed martyr Felix with all your household.
EDCS-67700099.summary: This is a blessing or invocation for Valerius and his family, associated with the martyr Felix.

EDCS-67700100.translation: Reverius fulfilled his vow to the Holy Spirit of Felix.
EDCS-67700100.summary: This inscription records Reverius fulfilling a vow made to the Holy Spirit associated with Felix.

EDCS-67700101.translation: May you live happily in God and keep in mind, Happy [one], on the Nones of February.
EDCS-67700101.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal inscription or a blessing, likely from a tomb, dated to the Nones of February.

EDCS-67700102.translation: Happy [one], on the Nones of February.
EDCS-67700102.summary: This short inscription, possibly from a tomb or a personal object, is dated to the Nones of February.

EDCS-67700103.translation: Marcus rendered his vow to the lord Felix Sanctus.
EDCS-67700103.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Marcus fulfilling a vow to the deity Felix Sanctus.

EDCS-67700107.translation: The burial of Mecrosa, a praiseworthy woman, under the day of the 5th day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of Flavius Maximus.
EDCS-67700107.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Mecrosa, dated to the consulship of Flavius Maximus.

EDCS-67700108.translation: The burial of Aurelia, mistress, who lived more or less...
EDCS-67700108.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Aurelia, a 'domina', but the lifespan is incomplete.

EDCS-67700110.translation: The burial of Grammatius, bishop of holy memory, under the day of the 8th day before the Kalends of February, in the consulship of Probus, a most illustrious man, the younger, who lived in peace for 41 years.
EDCS-67700110.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Bishop Grammatius, who lived for 41 years in peace, dated by the consulship of Probus.

EDCS-67700112.translation: Here rests in peace Verolus, a noble man, who lived more or less 50 years; his burial on the day before the Nones of December, in the eleventh indiction. If anyone violates [this], may he have the portion of Judas.
EDCS-67700112.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Verolus, a nobleman who lived about 50 years, dated to the 11th indiction and includes a curse against violators.

EDCS-67700114.summary: This is a short, personal inscription, likely a farewell to the deceased Nymphe.

EDCS-67700125.translation: By order of the Senate, Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine, [erected] 229 paces [and] 240 feet.
EDCS-67700125.summary: This inscription records a senatorial decree authorizing Emperor Augustus to establish boundary markers, likely for land division or public works, dating to his reign (27 BCE - 14 CE).

EDCS-67800001.translation: Of Potitus Poppaeus Sabinus, of Potitus Poppaeus Sabinus.
EDCS-67800001.summary: This inscription appears to be a very abbreviated epitaph or memorial for Potitus Poppaeus Sabinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67800003.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that likely records a woman named Romula in relation to men, possibly a tombstone or a dedication, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-67800006.summary: This inscription, which is sexually explicit, possibly refers to a woman named Romula and her sexual services, with an uncertain date and context.

EDCS-68000048.translation: Sacred to Luna Lucifera; Lucius Aurelius Serinianus [dedicated it].
EDCS-68000048.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Luna Lucifera by Lucius Aurelius Serinianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-68300035.summary: An acclamation to several emperors, likely from the 4th century CE, emphasizing their roles as protectors of the state.

EDCS-68400004.translation: To Cloelia Hypora, well-deserving, Epagathus and Felix. She lived 28 years.

EDCS-68400256.translation: Valeria Hetaera dedicates this sacred offering to Bona Dea Opifera.
EDCS-68400256.summary: A religious dedication by Valeria Hetaera to the goddess Bona Dea Opifera.

EDCS-68500310.translation: To the Chthonic Gods, Gnaeus Iunius Silus. Gnaeus Iunius Primigenius for his dear child and the dead.
EDCS-68500310.summary: A funerary dedication to the Chthonic Gods for Gnaeus Iunius Silus, made by his father Gnaeus Iunius Primigenius.

EDCS-68600050.translation: To the Chthonic Gods, for Aurelius Marcellus, dearest child, who lived two years, 11 months, and 6 days. Aurelia Marcella, his mother.
EDCS-68600050.summary: A funerary dedication to the Chthonic Gods for Aurelius Marcellus, made by his mother Aurelia Marcella, recording his age at death.

EDCS-68600067.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Torquatius Quirinus Novellus, son of Caius, to his wife Valeria Chelidonis, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-68600067.summary: A tombstone for Valeria Chelidonis, set up by her husband Caius Torquatius Quirinus Novellus.

EDCS-69000067.translation: Gaius Clodius Rufus, son of Gaius Clodius, Rufus.
EDCS-69000067.summary: A funerary or commemorative inscription for Gaius Clodius Rufus, possibly repeating his name for emphasis.

EDCS-69100003.translation: Our most glorious lord, and moreover renowned king Theoderic, victorious and triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the state, guardian of liberty and propagator of the Roman name, conqueror of peoples, restored to public use and the safety of travelers the road and places from Tripontium to Terracina, which, having been flooded from both sides by the marshes, had inundated in all past reigns; and through the felicitous favor of the benevolent god, by the diligent efforts on the assigned work and the successful service of the most clement prince, through heralds from the lineage of the Decii, Caecina Mavortius Basil(ius) Decius, a most illustrious and renowned man, formerly urban prefect, formerly praetorian prefect, formerly ordinary consul, a patrician, who, to perpetuate the glory of so great a lord, returned to dryness the waters drained into the sea, unknown to his ancestors and too ancient, granting palm and laurel.
EDCS-69100003.summary: An inscription from the reign of Theoderic (early 6th century CE) detailing the restoration of the Appian Way and associated lands, commissioned by the distinguished official Caecina Mavortius Basil(ius) Decius, to honor the king.

EDCS-69100004.translation: Our most glorious and renowned lord King Theoderic, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, born for the good of the Republic, guardian of freedom and propagator of the Roman name, conqueror of nations, restored for public use and the safety of travelers the Decennovii road from Tripontio to Terracina, and the places which, having been flooded by the convergence of marshes from both sides, had been inaccessible to all previous rulers; and he restored them with the grace of God and blessed fortune, with the work diligently undertaken and successfully accomplished by the clemency of the prince, through Caecina Mavortius Basilicus Decius, a man of highest renown and distinction, former prefect of the city, former praetorian prefect, former ordinary consul, patrician, who, to perpetuate the glory of so great a lord, brought to fruition for many, who had not done so before, channels leading to the sea, with water drawn away, returning dryness and reclaiming for himself palm and laurel, through ancestral traditions and ancient customs.
EDCS-69100004.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the Decennovii road and surrounding marshland by King Theoderic, completed under the supervision of Caecina Mavortius Basilicus Decius.

EDCS-69200012.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely for a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-69200015.summary: This inscription indicates that Julius Felix was the maker of the object or monument.

EDCS-69200019.translation: Felix (Happy) is here. Good for him who wrote this.
EDCS-69200019.summary: This is a playful or informal inscription, possibly a graffiti, indicating someone named Felix is present and praising the writer.

EDCS-69200023.summary: This is a farewell addressed to a young girl named Ione.

EDCS-69200038.translation: Gaius Poppaeus Hymetus lived and loved here; his name was Euhodia, whose number was 190; he loved her, whose number was 450; and of the household, the number was 702.
EDCS-69200038.summary: This funerary epitaph for Gaius Poppaeus Hymetus and his beloved Euhodia uses Greek numerals and Latin text, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200052.summary: This is a fragmentary personal inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, naming Marcus Cornelius Cato.

EDCS-69300002.translation: Marcus Veccius, son of Marcus, twice holder of the office of duovir quinquennalis, had the men's and women's baths, the palaestra, and other amenities constructed at his own expense.

EDCS-69400001.summary: This inscription details a public works project, the roofing of a theatre, commissioned and approved by the duovirs Gaius Quinctius Valgus and Marcus Porcius.

EDCS-70100095.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented name and filiation, possibly from an epitaph or dedication, with a connection to Arretium.

EDCS-70100097.summary: This is an epitaph for an adoptive daughter, Flora, recording her lifespan and identifying the dedicator as her adoptive father and freedman of Lutatius.

EDCS-70100106.translation: Valeria Plaecusa, freedwoman of Lucius, wife, made this monument for herself and her descendants; it will not pass to an heir; in front 32 feet wide, in the field 4 feet long.
EDCS-70100106.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicating it is for Valeria Plaecusa and her descendants and includes dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-70200069.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning a military or engineering official, Lucius Antonius, identified as a prefect of engineers.

EDCS-70400051.translation: To our lord Jovian, ever Augustus.
EDCS-70400051.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the Roman Emperor Jovian, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-70700165.translation: Gaius Licinius Zenobius Augustalis gave from his own funds for the honor of immunity and on the day of dedication to each of the Augustales 800 sesterces.
EDCS-70700165.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Gaius Licinius Zenobius Augustalis to the Augustales, likely during the Roman Imperial period, to secure an honor.

EDCS-70700219.translation: Numerius Popidius Florus to Venus, Liber, and Hercules.
EDCS-70700219.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Numerius Popidius Florus to the gods Venus, Liber, and Hercules.

EDCS-70800050.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus the younger made this for his most devoted father, Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus the elder.
EDCS-70800050.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a son for his father, Tiberius Claudius Ampliatus the elder, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-70800185.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly funerary, with illegible names and a lacuna.

EDCS-70800190.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Octavia Pampila.

EDCS-70800308.translation: Aulus Antiochus, freedman of Marcus Tatius, a silversmith, [and] Marcus, freedman of Marcus Tatius.
EDCS-70800308.summary: This inscription records two freedmen, Aulus Antiochus and Marcus, who were both freed by Marcus Tatius, with Aulus Antiochus identified as a silversmith.

EDCS-70900169.translation: To the spirits of the dead. To Euhodia, the foster-daughter. Ulpia Eulogia.
EDCS-70900169.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Ulpia Eulogia to her foster-daughter Euhodia.

EDCS-70900243.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Annalis.

EDCS-70900381.translation: Here rests in peace, Virina, laid to rest on the fourth day before the Ides of June, with Anthemius as consul for the second time.
EDCS-70900381.summary: This Christian epitaph records the death and burial of Virina during the consulship of Anthemius, indicating a date in the 5th century CE.

EDCS-70900384.translation: Here rests in peace Reparatus, a man of the highest distinction, who lived more or less 45 years, laid to rest on the sixth day before the Kalends of January, after the second consulship of Paulinus the younger, a man of the highest distinction.
EDCS-70900384.summary: This Christian epitaph records the death of Reparatus, a distinguished man who lived about 45 years, and provides a specific date related to the consulship of Paulinus the younger, likely in the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-70900385.translation: Here rests in peace, of holy memory, Biturianus the priest, who lived about 60 years, was buried the day before the Ides of February, six years after the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-70900385.summary: This is a tombstone epitaph for a priest named Biturianus, including his age at death and burial date relative to a consulship.

EDCS-70900672.translation: May the spirit of Felix be favorable, may God and the spirit of Felix be favorable; may Felix Leo be favorable with all his household.
EDCS-70900672.summary: This is a short devotional inscription invoking divine favor for Felix, Leo, and their household.

EDCS-70900678.translation: Aulus Vibius Apollonius, freedman of Lartius, the haruspex.
EDCS-70900678.summary: This is a simple funerary or occupational inscription identifying Aulus Vibius Apollonius, a freedman and haruspex.

EDCS-70900682.translation: To Tannonius Chrysantius, a most distinguished man, first in the toga of the forum of Campania from birth, to his patron and son, Tannoni[us] Chrysantius, a most distinguished man from the consulars of the province of Byzacena, for his merits, the entire council and people erected [this monument].
EDCS-70900682.summary: This is a dedication by the council and people of Campania to Tannonius Chrysantius, honoring him as a distinguished patron and former consular official.

EDCS-70900887.translation: To the companions of Velitrae, may it be fortunate! // To Geminus, the curator, may it be fortunate!
EDCS-70900887.summary: This inscription offers good wishes (feliciter) to the companions of Velitrae and to Geminus, the curator.

EDCS-71000251.translation: Gaius Herennius Nicephorus Gallicanus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-71000251.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Gaius Herennius Nicephorus Gallicanus, a freedman.

EDCS-71000259.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely a tombstone or marker for Aulus Umberius Salvius Felix.

EDCS-71000322.translation: Here rests in peace Felix, a most distinguished man, who lived about 70 years, buried on the 8th day before the Ides of October, during the consulship of Paulinus the Younger, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-71000322.summary: This is a tombstone epitaph for Felix, a distinguished man, providing his approximate age and burial date relative to a consulship.

EDCS-71000511.summary: This inscription simply repeats the name Sabina, likely for funerary or identification purposes.

EDCS-71000520.translation: The inner sanctuary, with ancient venerable worship, now opens a new light with expanded spaces; rejoice, remembering the narrowness of your former seat, seeing how this seat shines to the praise of the bishop. The place was small before for sacred rites, denying supplicants the ability to extend their hands, now it offers spacious altars to the people for pious duties in the heart of the middle martyr. All things please God, for Christ always renews all things and increases them to the fullness of light; thus, honoring the seat of the beloved Felix, He brought forth both splendor and space.
EDCS-71000520.summary: This lengthy inscription is a dedication celebrating the expansion and renovation of a sanctuary, likely honoring a bishop named Felix and referencing Christ's renewal.

EDCS-71000554.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Iustus the bishop, who was in office for three years and eleven months, died on the Wednesday of the Nones of February, after the consulship of Olybrius the Younger.
EDCS-71000554.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Iustus, dating to after the consulship of Olybrius the Younger (491 AD).

EDCS-71100153.translation: Flavius Flavianus, I have approved, I have signed, according to the standard. Flavius Flavianus, I have approved, I have signed, according to the standard. Lucianus, pure gold, I have signed. Flavius Flavianus, I have approved, I have signed, according to the standard. Flavius Flavianus, I have approved, I have signed, according to the standard.
EDCS-71100153.summary: This inscription appears to be a series of approvals and signatures, possibly related to a legal or administrative document or a transaction involving gold, likely authored by Flavius Flavianus.

EDCS-71200695.translation: Because I made this on the 17th day before the Kalends of August, while Iustinus was consul.
EDCS-71200695.summary: This inscription records the completion of a work on July 16th, during the consulship of Iustinus (date uncertain without further context).

EDCS-71400550.translation: Our most glorious and renowned lord King Theoderic, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, born for the good of the republic, guardian of liberty and propagator of the Roman name, conqueror of peoples, restored for public use and the safety of travelers the road from Tripontium to Terracina, with its branches, and the places which had been flooded by the marshes from both sides, a work which all previous rulers had failed to achieve, with divine favor and fortune, through the diligent efforts of the instructed workforce and the successful service to the most clement prince, the decurion Caecina Mavortius Bassilius Decius, a most illustrious and distinguished man.
EDCS-71400550.summary: This inscription records King Theoderic's restoration of the Appian Way, specifically the section between Tripontium and Terracina, highlighting his role as a benefactor and restorer of Roman infrastructure.

EDCS-71400555.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Fortunata, identified as a beloved sister.
