EDCS-73000059.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aelius Genius, identified as the recipient's husband.

EDCS-73000061.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aelius Appianus, freedman of the Emperors, who received a payment of money from Ca hatriae, lived 10 years, 11 months, 21 days, 8 hours. Aelius Eutyches, freedman of the Emperors, made this for his dearest son, and his wicked mother.
EDCS-73000061.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aelius Appianus, son of Aelius Eutyches, who was a freedman of the Emperors, and details his age at death.

EDCS-73000062.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aelius Crescens, while still living, made this for himself and for Aelia Syneti, his wife, and for his grandson Aelius Crescentinus, the elder, for three portions of land.
EDCS-73000062.summary: This is a funerary and self-dedicatory inscription by Aelius Crescens, made for himself, his wife Aelia Syneti, and his grandson Aelius Crescentinus, concerning three portions of land.

EDCS-73000063.translation: Aelius Eutyches and Aelia Do [parents to their most dutiful daughter] for 23 years, 15 days, 6 hours, and to her mother, Eutyches [for] his deserving wife.
EDCS-73000063.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for a daughter and her mother, set up by the parents.

EDCS-73000064.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Titus Aelius Felix, dearest son, who lived 2 years, 11 months, 11 days. Charixenus and Olympias, parents, made this.
EDCS-73000064.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Titus Aelius Felix, set up by his parents.

EDCS-73000065.translation: Aelia Herac made [this] for her mother.
EDCS-73000065.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a mother, made by her daughter.

EDCS-73000066.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aelia Adcenta of Tarracina, her son made this.
EDCS-73000066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Adcenta, set up by her son.

EDCS-73000067.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aelia Epagathe, who lived 2 years, 8 months, 26 days, 6 hours, her father Eutychides [made this] for his most beloved and most longed-for daughter.
EDCS-73000067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Aelia Epagathe, set up by her grieving father.

EDCS-73000068.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aelia Hilara, the deserving. Egrilia Attica, daughter, made this for her mother.
EDCS-73000068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Hilara, set up by her daughter.

EDCS-73000069.translation: Aelia Myrto made this for herself and for her freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-73000069.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aelia Myrto for herself and her household.

EDCS-73000070.translation: For Aelia Salvilla, freedwoman of Lucia. Aelia [made this], freedwoman of her patroness.
EDCS-73000070.summary: This inscription records a relationship between two freedwomen, Aelia Salvilla and Aelia.

EDCS-73000077.translation: Aulus Aemilius Fortunatus made this for himself and for Hermes Bagadates, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 23 feet, in the field 21 feet.
EDCS-73000077.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Aemilius Fortunatus for himself and his freedmen, also specifying land dimensions.

EDCS-73000078.translation: Publius Aemilius Hilarus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-73000078.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Aemilius Hilarus as a freedman.

EDCS-73000079.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Asiatice made this for her deserving husband, Lucius Aemilius Menestheus.
EDCS-73000079.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-73000082.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Cypare made this for her most dutiful daughter Procula, of Lucius, who lived 4 years, 3 months, and 21 days, and for her most excellent patron and husband Lucius Aemilius Epagathus, and for herself, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 25 feet in front, 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-73000082.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aemilia Cypare for her daughter, husband, and herself, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73000083.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Egrilius Rufus made this for his deserving wife, Aemilia Felicissima.
EDCS-73000083.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-73000090.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Aglais, my sweetest.
EDCS-73000090.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to a beloved individual named Aglais.

EDCS-73000091.translation: Lucius Agrius, patron; Agria, freedwoman of Lucius, patroness; Lucius Agrius Dio.
EDCS-73000091.summary: This inscription lists the names and statuses of three individuals, likely related to a patron-freedperson relationship, possibly marking a tomb or property.

EDCS-73000092.translation: Agria, freedwoman of the woman, made this for herself and for Agria Is and for Agria Maru.
EDCS-73000092.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Agria, a freedwoman, for herself and two other individuals.

EDCS-73000094.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Alexander. Victoria, his father's daughter, made this.
EDCS-73000094.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Victoria for Alexander.

EDCS-73000095.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Alfa lived 5 years.
EDCS-73000095.summary: This is a funerary dedication commemorating a child named Lucius Alfa who died at the age of five.

EDCS-73000099.summary: This is a personal dedication, likely funerary, to someone named Ani.

EDCS-73000100.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Anicia Tertulla, her most dutiful mother. Anicia Saturnina, daughter, for herself and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000100.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Anicia Saturnina for her mother, and also for herself and her descendants.

EDCS-73000105.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Annius Agapomenus made this for himself, for his wife Postumia Daphnica, for his son Annius Victor, and for his freedman Annius Pardala.
EDCS-73000105.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Marcus Annius Agapomenus for his family and freedman.

EDCS-73000106.translation: Aulus Annius Symphor made this for himself, for his sons Aulus Annius Artemisius and Aulus Annius Salvius, for his wife Annia Felicula, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 22 feet, in the field 24 feet.
EDCS-73000106.summary: A funerary monument established by Aulus Annius Symphor for himself, his sons, wife, and descendants, with dimensions noted.

EDCS-73000108.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Plinius Hermes the younger made this for his dearest wife Annia Primitiva and for his son Annia Eutychianus.
EDCS-73000108.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Plinius Hermes the younger for his wife and son.

EDCS-73000109.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Parents made this for Annia Threpsitena.
EDCS-73000109.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for Annia Threpsitena.

EDCS-73000110.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Ant
EDCS-73000110.summary: An incomplete funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed, mentioning Marcus Ant.

EDCS-73000112.translation: He made this for himself, for his foster-son Anthos, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front 10 feet, in the field 5 feet.
EDCS-73000112.summary: A funerary monument for the dedicator, his foster-son, and descendants, with land dimensions specified.

EDCS-73000113.translation: For his dearest son, from his mother Cia Anthylla.
EDCS-73000113.summary: A funerary epitaph from a mother for her son, mentioning Cia Anthylla.

EDCS-73000114.translation: For his dearest son, 11 months and 10 days old. Antistius.
EDCS-73000114.summary: A funerary epitaph from Antistius for his son who died at 11 months and 10 days.

EDCS-73000115.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Publius Antistius.
EDCS-73000115.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed for Publius Antistius.

EDCS-73000116.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Antistia Euphrosyne, his incomparable wife, and for himself. Caius Antistius Mercurius, her husband.
EDCS-73000116.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Antistius Mercurius for his wife Antistia Euphrosyne and himself.

EDCS-73000118.translation: To the Divine Manes, for the well-deserving freedman Antonius Gaius.
EDCS-73000118.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes for a freedman named Antonius Gaius.

EDCS-73000119.translation: Antonia M. Antonia V., mother, who lived 5 years.
EDCS-73000119.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of a child named Antonia M. Antonia V., who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-73000121.translation: To the Divine Manes, for Antonia Galas, from Lucius Antonius Melanthus, her most cherished wife.
EDCS-73000121.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Lucius Antonius Melanthus to his wife, Antonia Galas.

EDCS-73000125.translation: Afrodite made this for her husband Eucher, a well-deserving spouse.
EDCS-73000125.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Afrodite to her husband Eucher.

EDCS-73000128.translation: To Lucius Appuleius, freedman of Lucius mulieris, and to his wife Appuleia Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius mulieris, and to Ampliatus.
EDCS-73000128.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Lucius Appuleius, his wife Appuleia Secunda, and Ampliatus, possibly a family group.

EDCS-73000129.translation: Lucius Apuleius Bacchus Leparcus, freedman of Lucius, made this.
EDCS-73000129.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Apuleius Bacchus Leparcus, a freedman.

EDCS-73000130.translation: Sextus Apuleius Glyptus, son of Sextus, made this for himself, for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants, and for his wife Fabia Syra, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-73000130.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication by Sextus Apuleius Glyptus for himself, his family, and his freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-73000131.translation: To the Divine Manes, for the most unfortunate Apusulena Cyria Severa, daughter of Titus, who lived 4 years and 34 days. Her most miserable father, Titus Apusulenus Severus.
EDCS-73000131.summary: This funerary inscription is a lament by Titus Apusulenus Severus for his daughter, Apusulena Cyria Severa, who died at a young age.

EDCS-73000132.translation: To the Divine Manes, for Apusulena Iusta, freedwoman of Titus and mulieris. The body of this holy woman is placed here.
EDCS-73000132.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial place of Apusulena Iusta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-73000133.translation: To the Divine Manes, Lucius Aristius Amemptus made this for himself, for his freedmen and freedwomen, and for his descendants.
EDCS-73000133.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication by Lucius Aristius Amemptus for himself, his household, and his descendants.

EDCS-73000135.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld for Arminia Melissa.
EDCS-73000135.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Arminia Melissa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000136.translation: Gnaeus Arrius Olympus and Julia Vera, daughter of Spurius, his devoted wife, made this for themselves, and for their natural son Gnaeus Arrius Crescent, who lived 14 years, and for Publius Celsus Primus, son of Publius Quirina, their natural son, and for Publius Celsus Verus, their natural son, and for Arria Tertulla, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front, 24 feet.
EDCS-73000136.summary: This funerary inscription records a family monument established by Gnaeus Arrius Olympus and his wife Julia Vera for themselves, their son, a friend, and their descendants, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000138.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Artoria Charite, her pupil, made this for her foster mother Artoria Onesime, who deserved well.
EDCS-73000138.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Artoria Charite to her foster mother Artoria Onesime, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000142.translation: To Lucius Atilius Maximus, my dearest husband, and to myself.
EDCS-73000142.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Atilius Maximus and the dedicator, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000143.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Arillia Severina made this for her most devoted mother, Atilia Eutychia.
EDCS-73000143.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Arillia Severina to her mother Atilia Eutychia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000144.summary: This is a partial funerary inscription recording a dedication by Atticus for himself and others, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000148.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Marcus Aurelius, likely a funerary or honorary dedication from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000153.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Abianius Onesimus made this for his relative Caius Bocconius Heraclidus.
EDCS-73000153.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Caius Abianius Onesimus to his relative Caius Bocconius Heraclidus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000154.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cnaeus Avidius Apollonius, freedman of Cnaeus, made this for himself, and for his family, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000154.summary: This funerary inscription records a family monument established by Cnaeus Avidius Apollonius for himself, his family, and his descendants, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000158.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aurelius Agathemerus, who lived 39 years, 2 months, and 9 days. Pantuleia Damostratia made this for her incomparable husband, who deserved well.
EDCS-73000158.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Aurelius Agathemerus, with a dedication from his wife Pantuleia Damostratia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000161.translation: To Aurelia Chrestene and Aurelius Bassianus, Aurelius Euander made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-73000161.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Aurelius Euander to his wife Aurelia Chrestene and his father Aurelius Bassianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000162.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aurelius Guia made this for himself, his family, and his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. Ten feet in front, [and] feet in the field.
EDCS-73000162.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the construction of a tomb by Aurelius Guia for himself and his descendants, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000163.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Aurelius Mercurius made this for himself while alive. 'Be of good spirit, Concordia!'
EDCS-73000163.summary: This is a self-funded funerary inscription by Marcus Aurelius Mercurius, including a Greek exhortation, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000164.translation: To Aurelia Nicopolis. Gaius Aurelius made this.
EDCS-73000164.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Gaius Aurelius to Aurelia Nicopolis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000166.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Ulpius Similis and Marcus Aurelius Olympus made this for Aurelia Theonide, his well-deserving wife, and their most devoted mother.
EDCS-73000166.summary: This is a funerary inscription erected by Marcus Ulpius Similis and Marcus Aurelius Olympus for Aurelia Theonide, their wife and mother respectively, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000167.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. For Aurelia Valeria, who lived 1 year, 4 months, and 22 days. Marcus Aurelius Valerianus, her most beloved father, made this.
EDCS-73000167.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the infant Aurelia Valeria, detailing her lifespan and erected by her grieving father, Marcus Aurelius Valerianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000170.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to record a familial relationship, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000179.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. A Blaste made this for himself and ... Cosmo us.
EDCS-73000179.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription initiated by A. Blaste for himself and another individual, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000182.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription identifying Gnaeus C. as a freedman and marking a tomb, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000183.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph or dedication, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73000188.summary: This inscription appears to be an incomplete or corrupted text with no clear epigraphic meaning, possibly due to errors in transcription.

EDCS-73000191.summary: This inscription is a very brief mention of the name Quintus Caecilius, likely the subject of a larger, now lost, inscription.

EDCS-73000192.translation: He made this for Decimus Caecilius, deserving of his affection.
EDCS-73000192.summary: This is a dedication from an unknown individual to Decimus Caecilius, honoring him for his merits, likely on a tomb or a statue base.

EDCS-73000193.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caecilia Rufina, daughter of Quitus, lived 24 years, 3 months, 5 days. Pompeia Severa made this for her dearest and most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-73000193.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Rufina, erected by her mother, Pompeia Severa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000194.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lived 8 years, 8 months, 16 days. Aulus Caedicius Felix, father, and Caedicia Cione, mother, made this for their dearest and most dutiful son, and for themselves, their freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Caedicius Priscus, set up by his parents, who also dedicated it for the benefit of themselves and their household dependents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000198.translation: Lucius Caesius Dardanus, freedman of Lucius; Caesia Myrtis, freedwoman of Lucius; Lucius Caesius Euangelus, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Caesius Nicephor, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Caesius Faustus, freedman of Nicephor; Lucius Caesius Felix, freedman of Lucius; Lucius Caesius Fortunatus, freedman of Lucius; Caesia Proba, freedwoman of Felix; Lucius Caesius Eutyches, freedman of Lucius, saw to the construction as provided by the will of Lucius Caesius Faustus for 5,000 sesterces. Caesia Proba died at age 20. Caesia Restituta, freedwoman of Lucius Caesius Felix, died at age 20. In the front 83 feet, in the field 60 feet.
EDCS-73000198.summary: This funerary inscription details the contributions of freedmen and freedwomen based on a will, providing details about their lives and the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000201.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Calimera, deserving mother. She made this.
EDCS-73000201.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Calimera, described as a deserving mother, erected by an unspecified person, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000203.translation: To the Divine Shades. Callistes made this. Lucius Antonius Eutyches.
EDCS-73000203.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Lucius Antonius Eutyches to Callistes, likely on a tomb, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000205.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Calpetana Panthera. Calpetana Agrippina, for her mother.
EDCS-73000205.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Calpetana Agrippina dedicated to her mother, Calpetana Panthera, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000214.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Calpurnia Athenais, freedwoman of Augenda. Attius Chrysion made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-73000214.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Attius Chrysion to his wife, Calpurnia Athenais, who was a freedwoman of Augenda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73000215.translation: To the Divine Manes. Calpurnia Florentina lived for 7 years, 10 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-73000215.summary: A funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Florentina, recording her age at death.

EDCS-73000216.translation: Restituta, freedwoman of the woman Calpurnia.
EDCS-73000216.summary: An inscription identifying Restituta as a freedwoman of a woman named Calpurnia.

EDCS-73000217.translation: Selenio, freedwoman of the woman Calpurnia; Malchio, freedman of Lucius Calpurnius; Nicopolis, freedwoman of the woman Calpurnia; Restituta, freedwoman of the woman Calpurnia. In front 15 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-73000217.summary: An inscription listing several freedpersons and specifying land measurements, likely related to a property boundary or burial plot.

EDCS-73000220.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caltilia Barylla lived for 9 months and 21 days, and Caltilius Optatus lived for 11 months and 22 days. Caltilius Atticus and Nice, parents of Barylla and Optatus.
EDCS-73000220.summary: A funerary epitaph for two children, Barylla and Optatus, with their parents identified, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-73000222.translation: To Camurius, son of Aulus, who deserved well, who lived 16 days. Marcus Valerius, his foster-father, and Hia, his wife, made [this] for him deserving.
EDCS-73000222.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Camurius, set up by his foster-father and his wife.

EDCS-73000227.summary: A dedication to Cartilius, son of Caius, likely on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-73000228.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Caius Cartilius Titianus, who lived 3 months and 10 days, and to Procla, his dearest wife. Caius Cartilius Fortunatus, husband, made [this].
EDCS-73000228.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Cartilius Titianus and his wife Procla, erected by the husband and father.

EDCS-73000231.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Lucius Cassius Theodotos. Caius Julius Maximus made [this] for his incomparable friend.
EDCS-73000231.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Cassius Theodotos, set up by his friend Caius Julius Maximus.

EDCS-73000233.summary: A dedication to a father named Charito.

EDCS-73000234.translation: Charito, freedman of a woman; Charito for himself and Fort[unata/unatus].
EDCS-73000234.summary: An inscription recording a freedman named Charito making a dedication for himself and possibly Fortunata or Fortunatus.

EDCS-73000235.translation: To the Divine Shades of Chryse, a freedwoman, well-deserving.
EDCS-73000235.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a freedwoman named Chryse.

EDCS-73000239.translation: Publius Ciarcius Bitalis made this for himself, Aelia Secunda his wife, and their children, freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants; 16 feet in front, 16 feet in area.
EDCS-73000239.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Publius Ciarcius Bitalis for himself, his family, and their descendants, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-73000240.translation: For Gaius Cincius Primus, freedman of Gaius; for Arescusia, freedwoman of Gaius and his wife; for Gaius Cincius Primigenius, son of Gaius and his wife; for Gaius Cincius Philoterus, freedman of Gaius; for Gaius Cincius Hermetus, freedman of Gaius; for Fortunatus, freedman of Gaius and his wife; for Lucius Libanus, freedman of Aulus Livius and his wife; for Livia Ariadne, freedwoman of Aulus Livius and his wife; for Hermerotus, freedman of the Auli; 25 feet in front, 25 feet in area.
EDCS-73000240.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing multiple beneficiaries, likely members of the extended Cincius and Livius families and their freedmen, with plot dimensions.

EDCS-73000241.translation: The freedman of the citizenry, Dio, who lived...
EDCS-73000241.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning a freedman named Dio.

EDCS-73000246.translation: To Marcus Marcorum, son of Marcus; to Publius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-73000246.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly recording a dedication or a family relationship.

EDCS-73000249.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Claudius Apollonius made this for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; 10 feet in front, [area unspecified].
EDCS-73000249.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Titus Claudius Apollonius for himself and his freedmen and their descendants, specifying part of the plot dimensions.

EDCS-73000250.translation: Tiberius Claudius Euphemus made this for himself and his own, his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000250.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Tiberius Claudius Euphemus for himself and his family, including his freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-73000253.translation: To the Divine Shades. Claudia, who lived X months...
EDCS-73000253.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Claudia, noting her age in months.

EDCS-73000254.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Claudia Charis, an incomparable wife, who lived 30 years, 7 months, 14 days. Gaius Titinius Caianus, her husband, made this.
EDCS-73000254.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Gaius Titinius Caianus for his wife, Claudia Charis, providing her age at death.

EDCS-73000255.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Claudia Hygeia. Lucius Iulius [made this].
EDCS-73000255.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Claudia Hygeia, likely set up by Lucius Iulius.

EDCS-73000257.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Proculeia, daughter of Claudius Sabinus, lived 20 years, 10 months, and 7 days. Gaius Julius Severus made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-73000257.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Proculeia, erected by her husband Gaius Julius Severus.

EDCS-73000258.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Julius Crescens and Gaius Messius Cerialis made this for their deserving mother, Claudia Urbana.
EDCS-73000258.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Urbana, erected by her sons Gaius Julius Crescens and Gaius Messius Cerialis.

EDCS-73000259.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Claudia Victrix, his daughter, who lived 5 years and died the day before the Ides. For Claudia Baccula, her mother, who lived 30 years and died the 7th or 8th day before the Ides. Tiberius Claudius [made this] for his most devoted mother and for himself.
EDCS-73000259.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Victrix and her mother Claudia Baccula, erected by Tiberius Claudius.

EDCS-73000268.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Cocceius.
EDCS-73000268.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph possibly for a person named Cocceius.

EDCS-73000269.translation: [...daughter], lived 13 years and 22 days. Cocceius Probus, her father, [made this]. 10 feet long, 4 feet wide.
EDCS-73000269.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed daughter, specifying dimensions and erected by her father Cocceius Probus.

EDCS-73000270.translation: [...woman], freedwoman of Cia and Cocus, Soteris.
EDCS-73000270.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly identifying a freedwoman named Soteris, associated with Cia and Cocus.

EDCS-73000271.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Coelius Hilarus, who lived 15 years, 4 months, and 10 days. Coelius [made this].
EDCS-73000271.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Coelius Hilarus, erected by Coelius.

EDCS-73000272.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly a dedication or epitaph related to Gaius Cominius Celer.

EDCS-73000274.translation: Aulus Considius Symphor made this for himself and for Aulus Consedius Felix and Ianuaria, his sons, and for Considia Moscharuta, his wife, and for Rubria Athenaïs and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. 12 feet in front, 4 feet in the field.
EDCS-73000274.summary: A funerary monument erected by Aulus Considius Symphor for his family, including his wife, children, and freedpersons, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-73000281.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For [Clau]dius Cornel [ius] Odia[nus]. Lucius V [made this].
EDCS-73000281.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Claudius Cornelius Odianus, erected by Lucius V.

EDCS-73000283.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Cornelius IN
EDCS-73000283.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits of Cornelius IN, likely marking a tomb.

EDCS-73000284.translation: Cornelius Irenaeus and Lucius Cornelius Narcissus, freedmen, made this for their patron, Lucius Cornelius Antiochus, who deserved well of them.
EDCS-73000284.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by freedmen for their deceased patron, Lucius Cornelius Antiochus, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-73000287.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Publius Cornelius Eutychhianus lived for 14 years, 4 months.
EDCS-73000287.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Publius Cornelius Eutychhianus at the age of 14 years and 4 months.

EDCS-73000288.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Cornelius Herculanus, his incomparable wife Tauria Nice.
EDCS-73000288.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Tauria Nice to her late husband, Lucius Cornelius Herculanus.

EDCS-73000289.translation: Marcus Cornelius Successus for himself and his wife Cornelia Victoria, and for his homeborn slaves Rusticus and Urbanus and Recepta, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In the front 25 feet in the field.
EDCS-73000289.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the self-dedication and dedication to family and slaves, with land measurement details, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-73000290.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Cornelius Troilus, for the deserving Bittia Iuliana.
EDCS-73000290.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelius Troilus by Bittia Iuliana, who deserved well of him.

EDCS-73000292.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Cornelia Anthusa lived for 5 years, 10 months, 6 days. Marcus Cornelius Apagathus for his most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-73000292.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Cornelia Anthusa at the age of 5 years, 10 months, and 6 days, set up by her father.

EDCS-73000295.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Cornelia Euploea, who lived 22 years, 11 months, 26 days. Aulus Fabius Synhestius for his most rare wife.
EDCS-73000295.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Cornelia Euploea at the age of 22 years, 11 months, and 26 days, dedicated by her husband.

EDCS-73000297.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Cornelia Exorata, his most sweet mother, deserving well of them. Valerius Crescens, her husband, and his sons Valerius Iuvenalis and Crescens.
EDCS-73000297.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelia Exorata by her husband and sons, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-73000299.translation: Lucius Cornificius Primitivos and Caius Julius Hermes placed this with their own money for themselves, and for Cornificia Tyche, their son Lucius Cornificius Stephanus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000299.summary: This is a funerary monument established by Lucius Cornificius Primitivos and Caius Julius Hermes for themselves, their family, and slaves, funded by their own money.

EDCS-73000302.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Cotusia Rufina made this for her well-deserving husband, Quintus Fructarius Didymus.
EDCS-73000302.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her husband.

EDCS-73000308.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. [He] lived 4 years and 7 months. Parents to their sweetest son.
EDCS-73000308.summary: A funerary dedication from parents to their young son, recording his age at death.

EDCS-73000309.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Scennius Cresecens, patron, well-deserving, [dedicates this]. His freedman, Turus.
EDCS-73000309.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman to his deceased patron.

EDCS-73000310.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Crescentianus, who lived 1 year, 5 months, and 25 days.
EDCS-73000310.summary: A funerary dedication recording the age at death of Crescentianus.

EDCS-73000311.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Eutyches made this for the well-deserving Crescentina.
EDCS-73000311.summary: A funerary dedication by Eutyches for Crescentina.

EDCS-73000312.translation: Cris for himself, his wife Fulvia A, their son Tiberius Claudius, and their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants in front 20 feet.
EDCS-73000312.summary: A funerary dedication for the dedicator and his family, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73000320.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Datus made up [the deficit].
EDCS-73000320.summary: A funerary dedication, possibly relating to a burial plot or fees.

EDCS-73000322.translation: Aulus Decius Eutyches made this for himself, his family, his freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants in front 20 feet, in the land [specify measurement].
EDCS-73000322.summary: A funerary dedication for the dedicator and his family, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73000330.translation: For Lucius Domitius Trophimus and Domitia Tyche, their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants in front 25 feet, in the land 20 feet.
EDCS-73000330.summary: A funerary dedication specifying plot dimensions for the named individuals and their descendants.

EDCS-73000341.summary: The name of a person, likely a funerary dedication or marker.

EDCS-73000343.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Egrilius Faustus.
EDCS-73000343.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Egrilius Faustus.

EDCS-73000345.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelia Emerita and Egrilia Emerita made this for their husband and father, Aulus Egrilius Nicephorus, who lived 48 years, a most sweet husband with whom I lived 23 years, and for their deserving and incomparable father.
EDCS-73000345.summary: A funerary monument set up by a wife and daughter for Aulus Egrilius Nicephorus, providing details about his life and their relationship.

EDCS-73000351.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Egrilia Canis and of Aulus Egrilius Sabinus, her grandson.
EDCS-73000351.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Egrilia Canis and her grandson Aulus Egrilius Sabinus.

EDCS-73000352.summary: An incomplete inscription likely referring to an individual named Egrilius, possibly funerary or dedicatory.

EDCS-73000354.translation: Marcus Ellius Primitivos made this for Marcus Ellius Vestorianus and [---]
EDCS-73000354.summary: A funerary or dedication marker created by Marcus Ellius Primitivos for Marcus Ellius Vestorianus and another individual, likely a family member.

EDCS-73000356.summary: A brief inscription identifying Epaphra Primigenia as a freedman, possibly part of a larger monument.

EDCS-73000361.translation: Epitynchanus and his wife Faustus and Fu [---] and his wife [---] made this for themselves, for Publicia Zoeni, wife of Epitynchanus, and for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 21 feet, in the field 21 feet.
EDCS-73000361.summary: A funerary inscription establishing rights over a plot of land (21x21 feet) for the dedicator, his wife, Publicia Zoeni, and their freedmen and descendants.

EDCS-73000362.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His mother made this for Equitius Crescens, who lived 2 years, 9 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-73000362.summary: A funerary inscription from a mother to her young son, Equitius Crescens.

EDCS-73000364.summary: An inscription identifying Eros as the freedman of Lucius, likely part of a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-73000370.translation: To the spirits of the departed. He made this for his deserving daughter, Eupelastos Secunda, who lived 8 years and 2 months.
EDCS-73000370.summary: A funerary inscription from a father to his young daughter, Eupelastos Secunda.

EDCS-73000371.summary: This inscription is a simple naming, likely a funerary epitaph, of Gaius Eupo Iucundus.

EDCS-73000373.summary: This inscription is a simple naming, likely a funerary epitaph, of Aulus Austasius.

EDCS-73000377.translation: Eutyches erected this for Domitia V. E., spirits of the departed.
EDCS-73000377.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Eutyches for Domitia V. E., honoring the departed spirits.

EDCS-73000380.translation: Eutyches and Epictetus Marcus Junius T.
EDCS-73000380.summary: This inscription lists the names Eutyches, Epictetus, and Marcus Junius T., possibly as joint dedicators or individuals honored.

EDCS-73000381.translation: Eutyches erected this for his well-deserving patroness, and Obellia Iusta.
EDCS-73000381.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Eutyches for his patroness, also mentioning Obellia Iusta.

EDCS-73000383.translation: Aurelia and Augusti ae, and the most beloved Aloius, erected this for iae, the freedwoman of Marcus, their most sweet mother, spirits of the departed.
EDCS-73000383.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Aurelia and Augusti ae and Aloius for iae, the freedwoman of Marcus, their mother.

EDCS-73000385.translation: Felix, the freedman, erected this for Eutychia, spirits of the departed.
EDCS-73000385.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Felix, a freedman, for Eutychia.

EDCS-73000392.translation: Publius Fabius Auctus, freedman of Publius Fabius; Fabia Egloge, freedwoman of Publius Fabius; Fabia Procula; Publius Fabius Fructus, freedman of the woman; Publius Fabius Phoibus, freedman of the woman.
EDCS-73000392.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including freedmen and women, likely associated with the Fabia family, potentially as part of a family record or funerary monument.

EDCS-73000393.translation: Publius Fabius Epaphroditus, Publius Fabius Auctus, Fabia Glaphyra, Fabia Anthusa.
EDCS-73000393.summary: This inscription lists four names, possibly members of a family or individuals associated with a monument.

EDCS-73000394.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Fabi Hilarus, 55 years old, lived for us. (H L N - H(ic) L(ucius) N(ostris) or H(ic) L(ocus) N(oster) or H(ic) L(ux) N(ostra) - Uncertain).
EDCS-73000394.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Fabi Hilarus, who lived to be 55 years old, with an uncertain Latin abbreviation at the end.

EDCS-73000395.translation: To Fabia Marcia, his wife, who well deserved.
EDCS-73000395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fabius Secundus for his deserving wife, Marcia.

EDCS-73000397.translation: Fabia Prepontis made this for herself and for Quintus Fabius Eutychus, Quintus Fabius Ostiensis, Fabia Glauca, and Quintus Fabius Agathopus, her freedmen; in front 25 feet, in the field 28 feet.
EDCS-73000397.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with land dimensions, dedicated by Fabia Prepontis for herself and her freedmen, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-73000398.translation: To the departed spirits. Fabia Heraclia, his freedwoman, and her brother made this for Fabia Zoenus.
EDCS-73000398.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Fabia Zoenus by her freedwoman Fabia Heraclia and her brother.

EDCS-73000400.translation: made for Faenia Felicitas, his incomparable wife.
EDCS-73000400.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment honoring Faenia Felicitas, the 'incomparable wife' of an unnamed man.

EDCS-73000401.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Faianius Pompeianus lived 7 years, 8 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-73000401.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a young boy, Quintus Faianius Pompeianus.

EDCS-73000406.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to a freedwoman named Faust.

EDCS-73000408.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that mentions Faustus and his foster-son.

EDCS-73000409.translation: who lived 15 years, Faustina, his wife, who well deserved, made this, with whom he lived 15 years.
EDCS-73000409.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Faustina for her husband, commemorating their 15 years of marriage and his lifespan.

EDCS-73000414.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph that records the name 'aria Felicitas' and indicates she lived.

EDCS-73000415.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a man named Felicianus, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-73000416.summary: This inscription, possibly from a tomb, records a posthumous dedication by testament.

EDCS-73000417.translation: To the most happy, who lived 10 years, 5 months, 20 days, most chaste, her kinsman.
EDCS-73000417.summary: This epitaph commemorates a young girl, noting her age and virtues, and was set up by her relative.

EDCS-73000419.translation: To the departed spirits. To Felicula, an incomparable wife, who lived 24 years, 11 months, [her husband] made this for her, well deserving.
EDCS-73000419.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to a wife by her husband, emphasizing her virtues and lifespan.

EDCS-73000423.translation: To the departed spirits. Felix made this for his most deserving wife.
EDCS-73000423.summary: This tomb inscription records a husband's dedication to his deserving wife.

EDCS-73000432.translation: To the departed spirits. For Flaccus, well deserving.
EDCS-73000432.summary: This is a dedication to a well-deserving individual named Flaccus, intended for the departed spirits.

EDCS-73000436.summary: This fragment appears to be part of a dedication, possibly mentioning a donor and a recipient named Titus Flavius.

EDCS-73000438.translation: To the departed spirits. For Titus Flavius Anaxilaus, dearest son, who lived 29 years, 10 months. His father made this for him, well deserving, and for himself.
EDCS-73000438.summary: This epitaph is dedicated by a father to his beloved son, Titus Flavius Anaxilaus, and also includes a provision for the father himself.

EDCS-73000440.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Flavius Eutyches.
EDCS-73000440.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits for Lucius Flavius Eutyches.

EDCS-73000441.translation: To the departed spirits. For Titus Flavius Felix, his father. Titus Flavius Felicianus for his most dutiful father.
EDCS-73000441.summary: This tombstone records a dedication from Titus Flavius Felicianus to his father, Titus Flavius Felix.

EDCS-73000443.translation: Titus Flavius Herma and Iulia Epigone made this for themselves and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000443.summary: This inscription records a joint funerary dedication by Titus Flavius Herma and Iulia Epigone for themselves and their descendants and freedpersons.

EDCS-73000444.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulianus, a slave of our Caesar, made this for his well-deserving stepson Titus Flavius Justus, who lived 12 years and 8 months.
EDCS-73000444.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by a slave of Caesar to his stepson, Titus Flavius Justus.

EDCS-73000445.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Flavius Valens for Titus Flavius Luc, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-73000445.summary: This is a tombstone inscription by Titus Flavius Valens for Titus Flavius Luc, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-73000446.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. They set this up for their most worthy patron, Flavius M o, who deserved well.
EDCS-73000446.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates a patron named Flavius M o.

EDCS-73000449.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Ausxānusa made this for her well-deserving student Flavius Martinus, who lived 11 years, 11 months, and 28 days.
EDCS-73000449.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Flavia Ausxānusa for her student Flavius Martinus.

EDCS-73000450.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Helias, who lived 14 years, 13 days, and Flavius Olympos, who lived 11 years, 11 days.
EDCS-73000450.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Flavia Helias and Flavius Olympos, likely siblings, with their ages provided.

EDCS-73000451.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Flavius Asclepiades made this for his well-deserving patroness Flavia Helpidi.
EDCS-73000451.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Quintus Flavius Asclepiades to his patroness Flavia Helpidi.

EDCS-73000452.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Romana.
EDCS-73000452.summary: A simple funerary inscription commemorating Flavia Romana.

EDCS-73000453.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Zosime made this for herself, and for her well-deserving patron Titus Flavius Fortunatus, her husband Titus Flavius Nestor, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73000453.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication by Flavia Zosime, also honoring her patron, husband, and their freedpersons.

EDCS-73000461.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Fortunatus monument for one who deserved well.
EDCS-73000461.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication by Fortunatus for an unnamed individual.

EDCS-73000465.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Fortunata, who deserved well.
EDCS-73000465.summary: A simple funerary inscription dedicated to Fortunata.

EDCS-73000466.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fortunata, identified as 'mother', likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-73000467.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment listing names, possibly related to a funerary or commemorative context.

EDCS-73000468.translation: To [her/him] who deserved well, Lucius Fulcinius Iustus, patron.
EDCS-73000468.summary: This inscription is a dedication honoring someone deserving, made by Lucius Fulcinius Iustus, identified as a patron, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-73000473.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Fulvia Turpia made this for her dearest husband, Marcus Fulvius Lampontis, with whom she lived for 30 years, [wishing him] well.
EDCS-73000473.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fulvia Turpia for her husband Marcus Fulvius Lampontis, detailing their 30 years of marriage.

EDCS-73000475.translation: ... Tiberius to his wife Fulvia and to his son Fulvius and to [his other] son and to their descendants.
EDCS-73000475.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a dedication or will concerning Tiberius's wife Fulvia, their son Fulvius, another son, and their descendants.

EDCS-73000476.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Erotion as the freedwoman of Fulvia, likely on a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-73000477.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Furiius Afrodisius IV.
EDCS-73000477.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the underworld spirits for Furiius Afrodisius IV, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-73000481.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial of Furinia Prima.

EDCS-73000482.summary: This inscription identifies 'G' as the freedwoman of Naevius, likely part of a funerary inscription.

EDCS-73000485.translation: Gabinius Tych [lived] ... years, 6 months, ... days. [He/She] made [this].
EDCS-73000485.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and possibly the dedication of Gabinius Tych, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-73000486.translation: Gallus [son of] Gallia, son of Marcus. Gallia [daughter of] Marcus.
EDCS-73000486.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording family relationships, possibly related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-73000487.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gargilia Arescusa and Lucius Gargilius [dedicated this].
EDCS-73000487.summary: A funerary dedication to the shades of the dead by Gargilia Arescusa and Lucius Gargilius.

EDCS-73000488.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gavius Vitalio, who lived...
EDCS-73000488.summary: A funerary dedication to Gavius Vitalio, with the inscription incomplete.

EDCS-73000490.translation: Geminius Andronicus made this for his dearest son Zethus, who lived for 13 years, 2 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-73000490.summary: A funerary dedication by Geminius Andronicus for his son Zethus, with his age at death provided.

EDCS-73000491.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Geminius Sostratus made this for his wife Geminia Symferusa. Marcus Caesellius Sostratus is also buried here.
EDCS-73000491.summary: A funerary dedication by Geminius Sostratus for his wife Geminia Symferusa, also noting the burial of Marcus Caesellius Sostratus.

EDCS-73100009.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Heliana, identified as a wife.

EDCS-73100015.translation: Sallustius made this for his wife Helpidia.
EDCS-73100015.summary: A funerary dedication by Sallustius for his wife Helpidia.

EDCS-73100016.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavia Zotice made this for her most devoted and deserving husband, Titus Helvius Marianus.
EDCS-73100016.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavia Zotice for her husband Titus Helvius Marianus.

EDCS-73100017.translation: To Helvia Cornelia, his dearest daughter. Quietus, father.
EDCS-73100017.summary: A funerary dedication by Quietus to his beloved daughter Helvia Cornelia.

EDCS-73100023.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Herennia Auge, who lived 24 years, 2 months, and 19 days. Herennius Epictetus made this.
EDCS-73100023.summary: A funerary dedication by Herennius Epictetus for his wife Herennia Auge, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-73100024.translation: Herennia Rufa, daughter of Decimus, for herself and her family; Caius Tutilius Plocamus, freedman of Caius; Felix, freedman of Caius Herennius the woman; Hilara, freedwoman of Caius Tutilius; in front 20 feet, in the field 25 feet.
EDCS-73100024.summary: This inscription likely marks the boundaries of a property and lists individuals associated with it, possibly including owners and freedpersons.

EDCS-73100030.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; Sulpicia Tyche made this for Hermes, who deserved well.
EDCS-73100030.summary: This funerary epitaph records Sulpicia Tyche dedicating a monument to the deceased Hermes.

EDCS-73100033.translation: Hermiona established this for Saturninus and for Choenias and Dia, freedwomen.
EDCS-73100033.summary: This inscription records Hermiona dedicating something, possibly a monument or an endowment, to Saturninus and two freedwomen, Choenias and Dia.

EDCS-73100034.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; for Hermophilus, who deserved well.
EDCS-73100034.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Hermophilus.

EDCS-73100038.summary: This is a very concise funerary marker stating that Hilar is buried in this location.

EDCS-73100041.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed; Hilaritas lived 6 months and 27 days; nus, to his deserving wife, Phoebus made this.
EDCS-73100041.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Phoebus to his deserving wife, Hilaritas, and records her short lifespan.

EDCS-73100048.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; Ianuarius ARCF no
EDCS-73100048.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph, likely dedicated to Ianuarius.

EDCS-73100052.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; Impetrat exa
EDCS-73100052.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph, likely dedicated to Impetrat.

EDCS-73100053.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; for Irene, the most beloved Edia.
EDCS-73100053.summary: This funerary epitaph dedicates a monument to Irene, referred to as 'Edia', who is described as 'most beloved'.

EDCS-73100055.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed; Nia Isias, who lived 33 years, eralis itus
EDCS-73100055.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph for Nia Isias, recording her age at death.

EDCS-73100058.translation: S. Iulia lived here; he is buried and Ter...
EDCS-73100058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for S. Iulia, with an incomplete mention of another person.

EDCS-73100060.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Paulianus to his well-deserving wife, Iuliana.
EDCS-73100060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Paulianus to his wife Iuliana.

EDCS-73100062.translation: Lucius Iulius and Perperni II Lucius Philargurus and Marcus Alliopus for themselves and their families, freedmen and freedwomen. 30 feet in front, 25 feet in depth.
EDCS-73100062.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius, Perperni II, Lucius Philargurus, and Marcus Alliopus, specifying the dimensions of their plot.

EDCS-73100063.summary: This is a brief inscription indicating Lucius Iulius is alive, possibly marking a property or a personal statement.

EDCS-73100065.translation: Quintus Iu Eutyches, son of M. Ips.
EDCS-73100065.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying Quintus Iu Eutyches and his father.

EDCS-73100066.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iulius Iucundinus to his wife, Tina.
EDCS-73100066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Iulius Iucundinus to his wife, Tina.

EDCS-73100070.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Onesimianus to his dearest father, Marcus Iulius Onesimus.
EDCS-73100070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Onesimianus to his father, Marcus Iulius Onesimus.

EDCS-73100072.translation: Lucius Iulius Thalamus and Iulia Daphne, fellow freedmen, made [this] for themselves and their families. 5 feet in front, 10 feet in depth.
EDCS-73100072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius Thalamus and Iulia Daphne, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73100073.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Iulius Vitalis, a well-deserving freedman, from his patron.
EDCS-73100073.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Vitalis, a freedman, dedicated by his patron.

EDCS-73100074.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Iulia, who lived 19 years. Chresime, Chresimus, and Ga Speratus made [this] for their dearest sister.
EDCS-73100074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Chresime, Chresimus, and Ga Speratus to their sister Iulia, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-73100075.translation: To Iulia, my most sacred wife, and to their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-73100075.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Iulia, a wife, and her freedpeople and descendants.

EDCS-73100079.translation: To Iulia Erotis, my wife; to Iulia Primigenia, my daughter; to Exoche, freedwoman of Aburia Lucius, my sister.
EDCS-73100079.summary: This inscription records familial relationships, dedicating it to a wife, daughter, and sister.

EDCS-73100080.translation: To Iulia Faustina, my wife, who lived 40 years, 2 months, and to Furius Faustinus, my dearest son, who lived 19 years, 2 months. Furius Secundus made [this] for [them] who deserved well. Memmia Tzonysas made [this] for her son Furius Paulinianus and for her father Furius Secundus, father of her sons, who lived with me 6 years, for [him] who deserved well.
EDCS-73100080.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Furius Secundus for his wife Iulia Faustina and son Furius Faustinus, and by Memmia Tzonysas for her son Furius Paulinianus and father Furius Secundus, indicating a complex family structure and expressing affection for the deceased.

EDCS-73100081.translation: The bones of Iulia Nices are placed here.
EDCS-73100081.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Iulia Nices.

EDCS-73100082.translation: Iulia Prima, freedwoman of Caius Iulius Familiaris, [dedicated] a small shrine for herself and her own.
EDCS-73100082.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a small shrine by Iulia Prima, a freedwoman, for herself and her family.

EDCS-73100083.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Iulia Saturnina, my most cherished wife, for whom he lived 19 years, 2 months, 8 days; for [her] who deserved well.
EDCS-73100083.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iulia Saturnina by her husband, specifying the duration of their marriage and expressing his affection.

EDCS-73100084.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Symnais made [this] for Iulio Euhelpistus, her dearest son.
EDCS-73100084.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Iulia Symnais for her son Iulio Euhelpistus.

EDCS-73100086.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Iunius.
EDCS-73100086.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication by Caius Iunius.

EDCS-73100088.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Iunius Castus made [this] for himself and for Marcus Iunius Castus.
EDCS-73100088.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Iunius Castus dedicating a monument for himself and another Marcus Iunius Castus, possibly a son or relative.

EDCS-73100089.translation: Iunius Faustus made [this] for himself and for his dutiful wife, the freedwoman Manlia Prima, and for Iunius Dutus.
EDCS-73100089.summary: This inscription records Iunius Faustus dedicating a monument for himself, his wife Manlia Prima, and Iunius Dutus, likely a family member or freedman.

EDCS-73100091.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication from Iunia Agrippa to her parents, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100092.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Iunia Melitina.
EDCS-73100092.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of Iunia Melitina, a common form of epitaph in the Roman Empire.

EDCS-73100093.translation: Iustinus [dedicated this] to his wife, his companion, Iustinus.
EDCS-73100093.summary: This inscription, with Greek text, records a dedication by Iustinus to his wife, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100095.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Laelia Procula, daughter of Lucius, my most virtuous wife. Marcus Coritelius Felix Cornelianus [dedicated this].
EDCS-73100095.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication by Marcus Coritelius Felix Cornelianus to his wife, Laelia Procula, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100096.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Aerius Lamyra. Domitius Crescens [dedicated this].
EDCS-73100096.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Domitius Crescens to Aerius Lamyra, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100098.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Lauricius Gem, who lived [some number] years. Aurelia A [made this].
EDCS-73100098.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Lauricius Gem by Aurelia A, providing partial information about his lifespan, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100099.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Lentuvius Amandus, likely a funerary epitaph from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100100.translation: Lucius Lepidius Telesphorus made [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-73100100.summary: This inscription records Lucius Lepidius Telesphorus making a monument for himself during his lifetime, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100101.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Lepidia Prima. Lucius Lepidius Philonicus made [this] for his patroness and wife, well-deserving, and for himself.
EDCS-73100101.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Lepidius Philonicus dedicating a monument to Lepidia Prima, his patroness and wife, and also to himself, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100102.translation: To Lepidia Secunda, incomparable wife, who lived 53 years and 18 days. Lucius Combarisius Dionysius [dedicated this].
EDCS-73100102.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Lepidia Secunda and is dedicated by her husband, Lucius Combarisius Dionysius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-73100104.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Liberalis, freedman of the Augusti, made this for himself and for his wife Sextia Flora, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-73100104.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-dedicated monument for Liberalis, his wife, and their descendants, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-73100105.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Licinius Telesphorus lived 7 months.
EDCS-73100105.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Marcus Licinius Telesphorus, who died at the age of seven months.

EDCS-73100109.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Livius made this for his son Aulus, who lived [X] years, his dearest son.
EDCS-73100109.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument dedicated by Aulus Livius to his son Aulus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100111.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Vibius Agathemer made this for his wife Livia Acte, daughter of Aulus, his most cherished wife, who deserved well, who lived 23 years, 6 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-73100111.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument dedicated by Caius Vibius Agathemer to his well-deserving wife Livia Acte, providing her age at death, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100112.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Livia Florentina.
EDCS-73100112.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Livia Florentina.

EDCS-73100113.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cocceius Probus made this for his well-deserving wife Livia Hygiae.
EDCS-73100113.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument dedicated by Lucius Cocceius Probus to his well-deserving wife Livia Hygiae.

EDCS-73100117.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lollia, who lived [X] years.

EDCS-73100119.summary: This inscription records the age of Quintus Lollius, identifying him as a father despite his young age, likely a posthumous title or a marker of familial role.

EDCS-73100120.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lollia Iusta made this for herself and for her husband Herodianus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 15 feet, in the field [X] feet.

EDCS-73100121.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Longa, wife of Coetonis, and her husband, who deserved well, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. In front 10 feet, in the field [X] feet.

EDCS-73100126.translation: To the Divine Shades. Antonia Magna made this for her excellent husband, Marcus Lucceius Meleager.
EDCS-73100126.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife for her deceased husband, Marcus Lucceius Meleager.

EDCS-73100127.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucceius made this for Lucceia Helpis, his daughter.
EDCS-73100127.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a father, Lucceius, for his daughter, Lucceia Helpis.

EDCS-73100130.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iunia Domitia made this for her incomparable husband, Publius Lucretius Primitivus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-73100130.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife for her deceased husband, Publius Lucretius Primitivus.

EDCS-73100132.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription containing personal names, likely part of a larger monument or epitaph, but its precise meaning is lost.

EDCS-73100147.translation: Macrina ordered by will that this be made for herself, Tertius, for her dearest companion.

EDCS-73100148.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Maesius Aristo, five months...

EDCS-73100150.summary: This is an epitaph recording the age at death of Malia Titia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-73100154.translation: To the Divine Shades. Manlius Carpus made this for his dearest homeborn slave girl, who lived two years, ten months, and twenty-one days.
EDCS-73100154.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by an owner, Manlius Carpus, for his young slave girl.

EDCS-73100159.translation: To the Divine Shades, sacred. Cornelius Nianus made this for his deserving wife, Sellia Marciana.

EDCS-73100160.summary: This is a dedication made by Titus Marcius, likely a private commission.

EDCS-73100164.translation: To the memory of Marcus Marius Germanus.
EDCS-73100164.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Marcus Marius Germanus.

EDCS-73100168.summary: This inscription simply identifies Maron as a freedman, possibly on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-73100182.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and a dedication by Mindia Sabina to her foster-daughter Fortunata.

EDCS-73100183.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Minucia Mesilla to her well-deserving Quintus Minucius Chryseros.
EDCS-73100183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Minucia Mesilla to Quintus Minucius Chryseros.

EDCS-73100186.translation: Marcus Modius Asclepiades made this for his parent, Marcus Modius Palumbus.

EDCS-73100196.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Munatia Blanda to her husband.

EDCS-73100200.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus N.

EDCS-73100201.translation: Gaius N N made this for himself.
EDCS-73100201.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording a self-dedication by Gaius N N.

EDCS-73100203.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius N. H. who lived.
EDCS-73100203.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a certain Publius N. H.

EDCS-73100204.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius of the Palatine tribe.
EDCS-73100204.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a certain Publius, identified by his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-73100206.translation: To the spirits of the departed, in eternal memory of Naeevia Secundina.

EDCS-73100210.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Furia Felicitas made (this) for Nicon, freedman of Augustus, her husband who deserved well, and for herself, her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73100210.summary: This funerary epitaph records Furia Felicitas dedicating a burial for her husband Nicon, an imperial freedman, and for herself, their descendants, and freedpeople.

EDCS-73100211.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Nicopolis.
EDCS-73100211.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Nicopolis.

EDCS-73100214.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Nigrinius Euangelus made (this) for his deserving wife, Nigrinia Marcellina.
EDCS-73100214.summary: This funerary epitaph records Gaius Nigrinius Euangelus dedicating a burial for his wife Nigrinia Marcellina.

EDCS-73100220.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Obellia Tyrannis, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-73100220.summary: A funerary dedication for a woman named Obellia Tyrannis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100224.translation: Octavius Maximus made this for his mother, well-deserving, [for] 4 months.
EDCS-73100224.summary: A funerary dedication by a son for his mother, mentioning a duration of 4 months, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100227.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Onesimus, well-deserving. Erastus and Phoebus made this for their dearest brother, who lived 10 years, 10 months, and 16 days.

EDCS-73100232.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Otacilia Maximina made this for Pontius Atticus, who lived 3 years, 8 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-73100232.summary: A funerary dedication by Otacilia Maximina for Pontius Atticus, likely her son, specifying his age, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100233.summary: An incomplete inscription fragment, possibly a dedication or funerary text, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100236.summary: A simple dedication by Pantheus, likely for a deity or a funerary monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100237.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, Pantuleia Materna, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100238.translation: Lucius Papirius Felix lived 7 years, 3 months, and 19 days.

EDCS-73100241.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Parmenia Pothusa, who lived well for 45 years and 101 months. Claudius Flaccus made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-73100241.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, Parmenia Pothusa, specifying her age and good character, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100244.translation: Paulinus Fabius Paulinianus to his most beloved brother, [aged] 5 years, 5 months, 11 days.
EDCS-73100244.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Paulinus Fabius Paulinianus, dedicated by a relative.

EDCS-73100246.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Sextus, through Abascantus.
EDCS-73100246.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld deities by Sextus, possibly through a freedman named Abascantus.

EDCS-73100253.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Rutilia Panthia made this for her well-deserving wife Philadespoti, who lived about 45 years.
EDCS-73100253.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Philadespoti, dedicated by her wife Rutilia Panthia.

EDCS-73100257.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Phoebus.
EDCS-73100257.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld deities for someone named Phoebus.

EDCS-73100260.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning 'Pinni' and 'Caius Min[---]'.

EDCS-73100264.translation: Quintus Plarius Eleuther made [this monument] to the spirits of the departed for himself, his wife Trallidi, his freedwoman Plaria Tyche, and his other freedmen and freedwomen.

EDCS-73100268.summary: This funerary inscription records that Plotius Hermadio and Elia Helpis set up a monument for themselves and their sons.

EDCS-73100269.translation: Quintus Plotius Epictetus [made this for] Plotia, daughter of Quintus, who lived 10 years, 11 months, [and 1 day].

EDCS-73100273.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedwoman named Poblicia Philēte.

EDCS-73100274.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus made this for his wife.
EDCS-73100274.summary: This is a funerary dedication, likely on a tombstone, made by Sextus for his wife, Aevia Poli.

EDCS-73100277.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a person named Polygono.

EDCS-73100290.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Pontius Symtrophus for his slave Pontius Felicissimus and his freedwoman Pontia I.

EDCS-73100292.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Porcius Hermetus, well-deserving.
