EDCS-73100319.translation: Rasidia to her husband and herself, in front, feet...
EDCS-73100319.summary: This inscription likely records a land dedication or burial plot size, initiated by Rasidia for her husband and herself.

EDCS-73100321.translation: The freedman Publius Regianus and his son Nycteros and D erected this for their father.
EDCS-73100321.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by a freedman and his son to their father.

EDCS-73100322.translation: To the Divine Shades, Caius Aulius Protus made this for his wife Reia Felicula and for himself and his family.
EDCS-73100322.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Caius Aulius Protus to his wife Reia Felicula, also including himself and his family.

EDCS-73100323.translation: To the Divine Shades, for Aelia Chrsis, a well-deserving nurse.
EDCS-73100323.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a nurse named Aelia Chrsis.

EDCS-73100325.translation: To the Divine Shades, Lucius Romanius Crescentilianus for his dearest freedman Lucius Romanus Fabius.
EDCS-73100325.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Romanius Crescentilianus to his freedman Lucius Romanus Fabius.

EDCS-73100328.translation: To the Divine Shades of Caius Rubbius Epictetus, his wife Rubbia Dionysias. To the Divine Shades of Quintus Vibius Carpus.
EDCS-73100328.summary: This inscription honors two individuals, Caius Rubbius Epictetus and Quintus Vibius Carpus, likely on their tomb.

EDCS-73100339.translation: ...urio for his most esteemed patron Sabinus, son of Titus, 4 feet in front, 8 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100339.summary: This inscription records a dedication of land or a plot, likely funerary, to a patron named Sabinus.

EDCS-73100340.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple dedication or identification, possibly on a tombstone, for Sabina.

EDCS-73100345.translation: To the Divine Shades of Marcus Salinator, a most dutiful father, who lived 59 years, 1 day. Salinator Sec and Baedia A to their sweetest husband with whom he lived...
EDCS-73100345.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Salinator, dedicated by his son Salinator Sec and wife Baedia A, recording his lifespan and marriage duration.

EDCS-73100346.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Salvius Priscinus, who lived 10 years, 11 months, and 6 days. Salvia Pompeia and Albicius Zoticus, his parents, made this.
EDCS-73100346.summary: A funerary epitaph for Salvius Priscinus, set up by his parents, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100347.translation: Lucius Sariolenus Nicetes, freedman of Lucius, made this for himself and for his freedwoman wife, Helpidia, and for his very sweet son, Lucius Sariolenus Successus, freedman of Lucius, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100347.summary: A funerary monument inscription for Lucius Sariolenus Nicetes, his family, and descendants, indicating the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100348.summary: A dedication to the deified Augustus by Caius Pantuleius, likely an inscription on a public monument or altar.

EDCS-73100352.translation: Cnaeus Saturninus, son of Cnaeus, is buried here.
EDCS-73100352.summary: A simple burial inscription for Cnaeus Saturninus, son of Cnaeus, likely from the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-73100354.translation: Lucius Scantius Demetrius, freedman of Lucius, with his own money ordered this to be made for himself and for Lucius Scantius Strato, his patron, and for the freedwoman of Voltidia, Plutinus, freedwoman of Lucius, according to the will.
EDCS-73100354.summary: A funerary commission inscribed by Lucius Scantius Demetrius for himself, his patron Lucius Scantius Strato, and others, indicating a posthumous commission according to a will.

EDCS-73100355.translation: For Scantius Rufus, dearest son, well-deserving, who lived 8 months and [several] days.
EDCS-73100355.summary: A funerary epitaph for Scantius Rufus, a young child, indicating his parentage and short lifespan.

EDCS-73100356.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Scantius Secundus made this for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants. 8 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100356.summary: A funerary monument inscription for Marcus Scantius Secundus, intended for himself and his descendants, specifying the plot dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100357.translation: Scantia. They took care of this during their lifetime.
EDCS-73100357.summary: A funerary inscription by Scantia, indicating that she arranged for her own monument during her lifetime.

EDCS-73100361.summary: A fragmented inscription possibly naming Marcus Caius Seulli and indicating an age at death.

EDCS-73100362.translation: Cnaeus Philetus, freedman of V(oltenus), made this for his freedwoman and wife, well-deserving.
EDCS-73100362.summary: A funerary dedication by Cnaeus Philetus, a freedman, for his freedwoman wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-73100363.translation: To the Divine Manes. Secundus, who lived 10 years, 7 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-73100363.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a boy named Secundus, noting his age at death.

EDCS-73100366.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, likely the beginning of a name or title.

EDCS-73100367.translation: Marcus Segulius, freedman of Marcus, made this for himself and
EDCS-73100367.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Marcus Segulius, a freedman.

EDCS-73100368.translation: Lucius Seius Primus Caprinarius, freedman of Lucius, and Seia Murtis, freedwoman of Lucius, Nicephorus.
EDCS-73100368.summary: This inscription records family members, including freedmen and freedwomen, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-73100369.translation: To the Divine Manes. Septimius Cautus, who lived 35 years.
EDCS-73100369.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Septimius Cautus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-73100370.translation: Gaius Septimius Philocalus for himself and for Septimia Successa, his freedwoman, and for his own people.
EDCS-73100370.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by Gaius Septimius Philocalus for himself and his freedwoman.

EDCS-73100371.translation: To the Divine Manes. Sereni, who lived 2 years and 5 months.
EDCS-73100371.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Sereni, noting their age at death.

EDCS-73100372.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription from Sergius to Thessalonicae, possibly a deity or a person.

EDCS-73100377.translation: To the Divine Manes. Cnaeus Sergius Hilarus, freedman, made this for his well-deserving patroness, Sergia Epiteuxis.
EDCS-73100377.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument dedicated by a freedman, Cnaeus Sergius Hilarus, to his patroness.

EDCS-73100379.translation: To the Divine Manes. [---] Seberianus, who lived 20 years, 11 months, and 3 days. They made this.
EDCS-73100379.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Seberianus, stating his age at death and the makers of the monument.

EDCS-73100380.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Severus, thrice [something].
EDCS-73100380.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Severus, possibly indicating a posthumous honor or status.

EDCS-73100381.translation: From Aulus, son of Sextus, to Merope.
EDCS-73100381.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial from Aulus to Merope, with her patronymic or relationship to Aulus implied.

EDCS-73100387.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Sornia Valeriana, who lived 6 months and 12 days.
EDCS-73100387.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young child, Sornia Valeriana, detailing her short lifespan.

EDCS-73100390.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Statilius Quintianus, who lived 5 years, 2 months, 6 days, and 10 hours. Cnaeus Statilius Abascantus and Pacilia Quintiane, parents, made this.
EDCS-73100390.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy, Statilius Quintianus, commissioned by his parents.

EDCS-73100392.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Statia Glycera, a deserving wife. Pomponius Felicissimus, to his wife.
EDCS-73100392.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a husband, Pomponius Felicissimus, to his wife, Statia Glycera.

EDCS-73100393.translation: Stlacci Eutych made this for Stlacci, his patron.
EDCS-73100393.summary: This is a dedication made by Stlacci Eutych to his patron, Stlacci.

EDCS-73100394.translation: Marcus Sulpicius, son of Caius, for the street, a freedwoman.
EDCS-73100394.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication or action by Marcus Sulpicius related to a street and a freedwoman.

EDCS-73100396.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Synerosa. Delicatus [made this].
EDCS-73100396.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Synerosa, likely made by Delicatus.

EDCS-73100397.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed for Syntrophianus.
EDCS-73100397.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Syntrophianus.

EDCS-73100398.translation: To a brother, for Tatianus, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-73100398.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a brother to Tatianus, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-73100400.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Telustia Eutychia, freedwoman, made this for Lucius Telustius Amarantus and for herself.
EDCS-73100400.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedwoman for her former master and herself.

EDCS-73100401.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Terentia Sabina, who lived 18 years, 7 months, and 25 days. Marcus Mollicius Celerinus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-73100401.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a husband to his wife, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-73100402.translation: ---, freedman of Publius' freedwoman Tertius, freedman of Publius' freedwoman Eutychia, freedman of Publius Pudens, freedman of Publius Anoptes, freedman Trophimus, Calliste, Fortunatus.
EDCS-73100402.summary: This inscription appears to list a series of freedmen and possibly former slaves, likely related to a family or household.

EDCS-73100407.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Threptus, who lived 2 years, 3 months, and 13 days. Publius Crispius Vitalis, father, made this.
EDCS-73100407.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a father for his young son, specifying the child's age at death.

EDCS-73100411.summary: This fragment appears to record the age of a person named Tiburtinus, possibly on a tombstone.

EDCS-73100414.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Titinius Fi and Titinia Comas, while living.
EDCS-73100414.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a couple for themselves while they were alive.

EDCS-73100416.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Numerius Trebonius Zethus.
EDCS-73100416.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Numerius Trebonius Zethus.

EDCS-73100421.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Liber made this for Tullius Iuvenis.
EDCS-73100421.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Liber for Tullius Iuvenis.

EDCS-73100422.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tullia Caelestina made this for her deserving alumna Tullia Chyspis.
EDCS-73100422.summary: This is a funerary dedication from an alumna for her deserving teacher or guardian.

EDCS-73100423.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording the name Quintus Tur Vic and likely his age or lifespan.

EDCS-73100424.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Cnaeus Turellius Eutychianus made this for his well-deserving freedman, Gnaeus Turellius Felix.
EDCS-73100424.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedman for his former slave, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-73100425.translation: Caius Turranius Ofeli made this for himself, for his freedwoman Turrania, his wife, and for his freedman Caius Turranius Doryphorus, and for his freedmen and freedwomen, and for his well-deserving freedman Caius Turranius Ac.
EDCS-73100425.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Caius Turranius Ofeli for himself, his wife, and several freedmen and freedwomen, indicating a concern for family and household members.

EDCS-73100427.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Pomponius Afrodisius made this for Tyrannus, his dearest father.
EDCS-73100427.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Pomponius Afrodisius to his father, Tyrannus.

EDCS-73100432.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius V lived 1 year, 11 months, 11 days.
EDCS-73100432.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius V, likely a child based on the age provided.

EDCS-73100438.translation: For Lucius Va, 72 years, 4 months, by his dearest daughter.
EDCS-73100438.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating Lucius Va, erected by his daughter.

EDCS-73100439.translation: for his incomparable mother, Lucius Valerius.
EDCS-73100439.summary: This fragment likely refers to a funerary dedication for an unknown mother by Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-73100440.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly a name from a larger monument or epitaph.

EDCS-73100441.summary: This is a fragment, likely a name (possibly a freedwoman of Publius Valerius) from a larger inscription.

EDCS-73100443.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Leucus made this for Erius Heraclitus; he lived 4 years, 2 months, 11 days.
EDCS-73100443.summary: A funerary epitaph for Erius Heraclitus, set up by Leucus, and likely recording the death of a child.

EDCS-73100444.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Valerius Sardonychus and Lucius Ostiensius Paulinus made this for their dearest brother, Ostiensia Euploea, who deserved well.
EDCS-73100444.summary: This funerary monument was erected by two brothers for their beloved brother, Titus Valerius Sardonychus.

EDCS-73100446.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valeria Successa made this for her most excellent husband, Marcus Valerius Urbicus, and for herself and her family.
EDCS-73100446.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Valeria Successa to her husband Marcus Valerius Urbicus.

EDCS-73100450.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pompeius Numa made this for his deserving wife, Valeria Deutera.
EDCS-73100450.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Pompeius Numa for his wife Valeria Deutera.

EDCS-73100451.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Fulvius Cinnamus made this for his most holy and deserving wife, Valeria Fortunata, with whom he lived for 33 years and 2 months, and for his daughter Fulvia Italia, and for Lucius Fulvius Cinnamus.
EDCS-73100451.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD, records the deaths of Valeria Fortunata, Fulvia Italia, and Lucius Fulvius Cinnamus, set up by Lucius Fulvius Cinnamus.

EDCS-73100452.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Romanus and Marcella made this for their sweetest daughter, Valeria Romana, who lived 6 years, 4 months, and 28 days.
EDCS-73100452.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD, records the death of Valeria Romana, set up by her parents Romanus and Marcella.

EDCS-73100453.translation: Publius Valerius Saturninus made this for his deserving brother, Titus Manlius Ameno, and his wife Valeria Satura, excellent and most dutiful, out of his own resources; 4 feet in front and 6 feet in the ground.
EDCS-73100453.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Publius Valerius Saturninus for his deserving brother Titus Manlius Ameno and his wife Valeria Satura.

EDCS-73100454.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Valerius Thallus and Claudia E made this for their daughter Valeria Tryphosa, daughter of Marcus, who lived 18 years, 6 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-73100454.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD, records the death of Valeria Tryphosa, set up by her parents Marcus Valerius Thallus and Claudia E.

EDCS-73100456.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primitiva made this for her deserving husband, Valgius Felix, aged 30.
EDCS-73100456.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Primitiva for her husband Valgius Felix.

EDCS-73100457.summary: This is a very short inscription that appears to be a name repeated, possibly for memorial or ownership purposes.

EDCS-73100460.translation: Palladius, freedman of Ventia [daughter of] Valerius Ma[gnus?].
EDCS-73100460.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the freedman status of Palladius in relation to his patroness from the gens Valeria.

EDCS-73100461.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Of Lucius Venustus, son of Aulus Hostilianus.
EDCS-73100461.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Venustus, son of Aulus Hostilianus.

EDCS-73100463.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Bergilius Eutyches made this for his well-deserving fellow freedman, Primitivus.
EDCS-73100463.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Quintus Bergilius Eutyches to his fellow freedman, Primitivus.

EDCS-73100465.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Vettius Firmus and Vettia Tertia, a home-born slave, lived for 2 years and 7 months.
EDCS-73100465.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Vettia Tertia, with Marcus Vettius Firmus and Vettia Tertia likely being her parents or guardians.

EDCS-73100468.translation: for his freedmen and their descendants. For Publius, son of Vi...
EDCS-73100468.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely concerning the dedication of burial places for freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-73100469.translation: Vibianus Antiphon made this for Vitellia Lucil, his most devoted wife, and for his sons Vibianus Antiphon and Venustus.
EDCS-73100469.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Vibianus Antiphon for his wife Vitellia Lucil and their sons.

EDCS-73100478.translation: ...nius Victor made this for the incomparable [dedicant] who deserved well of him.
EDCS-73100478.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording a dedication to an individual named Victor for their good deeds.

EDCS-73100479.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Victorin lived for 9 years and Vital, his dearest sons.
EDCS-73100479.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of two sons, Victorin and Vital, dedicated to the Spirits of the Underworld.

EDCS-73100480.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Eliae Victorinae who lived for 16 years, 8 months, and 1 day. Elia Victorina made this for her dearest daughter.
EDCS-73100480.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Eliae Victorinae at the age of 16 and is dedicated by her mother, also named Elia Victorina.

EDCS-73100482.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. [Us?] Cai Vir IO...
EDCS-73100482.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the Spirits of the Underworld, with the beginning of a name or title.

EDCS-73100483.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Biselli.
EDCS-73100483.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription dedicated to the Spirits of the Underworld for Lucius Biselli.

EDCS-73100486.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Vitalioni, an infant, who lived for 11 years.
EDCS-73100486.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of an infant named Vitalioni who lived for 11 years.

EDCS-73100489.translation: To Marcus Ulpius Callinicus, the best friend.
EDCS-73100489.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Ulpius Callinicus, described as an excellent friend.

EDCS-73100490.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Ulpius Cladeos and Cornelia Fortunata.
EDCS-73100490.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Ulpius Cladeos and Cornelia Fortunata.

EDCS-73100491.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Marcus Ulpius Philoxenus, who lived 17 years, 8 months, [and some days]; for Ulpia Vitalina, who lived 9 months, 18 days, for their well-deserving status; and for Ulpia Dio.
EDCS-73100491.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death of Marcus Ulpius Philoxenus and Ulpia Vitalina, and also mentions Ulpia Dio, likely for a family tomb.

EDCS-73100492.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Ulpia Tyche. Diophantus, freedman of Augustus, to his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-73100492.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Diophantus, a freedman of Augustus, to his wife Ulpia Tyche.

EDCS-73100494.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Volteia Flora and Lucius Volteius Cerdon. Volteia Certina, their daughter, made this for her dearest parents.
EDCS-73100494.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication from Volteia Certina to her parents, Volteia Flora and Lucius Volteius Cerdon.

EDCS-73100495.translation: Gaius Volturcius Olympus made this for himself, for Volturcia Chosmia, his freedwoman and daughter, and for his sons Gaius Volturcius Olympos and Gaius Volturcius Chosmos, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet. Publius Durdenius Acutus, freedman of Publius and a woman, made this for himself, for Durdenia Prima, his freedwoman, his wife, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. In front 16 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-73100495.summary: This is a double funerary dedication, likely for burial plots, made by Gaius Volturcius Olympus and Publius Durdenius Acutus for themselves, their family members, and descendants, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73100497.translation: Lucius Volumnius Crescens, freedman of a woman, made this for himself, for Volumnia Tryphera, his freedwoman, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73100497.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Lucius Volumnius Crescens for himself, his freedwoman Volumnia Tryphera, and their descendants.

EDCS-73100498.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Volumnia Ianuaria, who lived 19 years, 3 months, 23 days. Lucius Ligurius Flavianus and Liguria Irene, her most unfortunate parents, made this for themselves and for Plotius Demosthenes, the betrothed.
EDCS-73100498.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by the parents of the deceased Volumnia Ianuaria to her memory and also includes themselves and her betrothed, Plotius Demosthenes.

EDCS-73100500.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Decimus Volu. Apollonia. Volusia.
EDCS-73100500.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the names Decimus Volu[s], Apollonia, and Volusia.

EDCS-73100502.translation: Gaius Volusius Onesimus, freedman of a woman, to Volusia Salvia, daughter of Spurius, his patroness; and to Axia, freedwoman of Marcus and a woman, his wife. Gaius Volusius Fructus [made this?].
EDCS-73100502.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication from Gaius Volusius Onesimus and Gaius Volusius Fructus to their patroness Volusia Salvia and to Axia, the wife of Gaius Volusius Fructus.

EDCS-73100504.translation: To the Divine Manes. Urbica made this for her dearest son Titus Flavius Timotheus, who lived 8 years, 9 months, and 25 days, deserving of it well.
EDCS-73100504.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Urbica to her son Titus Flavius Timotheus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100505.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Ursilla, deserving of it well.
EDCS-73100505.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicated to Ursilla, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100509.translation: Zoticus made this for his wife, who lived 3 years.
EDCS-73100509.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the death of a wife named Zoticus at the age of three, with the dedicant being her husband.

EDCS-73100597.translation: a beloved woman, a freedwoman, devoted.
EDCS-73100597.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely referring to a freedwoman and her devotion, possibly funerary.

EDCS-73100629.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning two names, Antiantius and Ianus, its purpose is unclear.

EDCS-73100649.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that mentions 'Quinti' and her lifespan, suggesting a funerary context.

EDCS-73100661.translation: who lived 11 years, 6 months. MAM VNA Yllus simis ano
EDCS-73100661.summary: This is a fragmented inscription recording the lifespan of an individual who lived 11 years and 6 months, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-73100664.summary: This fragmented inscription mentions Nnius and his pupil, possibly related to education or a patronage.

EDCS-73100745.translation: To the Divine Manes. Curia Titiana lived 4 years, 3 months, and 25 days. Pomponia Titiana, her dearest daughter, made this.
EDCS-73100745.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Pomponia Titiana to her daughter Curia Titiana, who died at a young age.

EDCS-73100754.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a lifespan of 30 years, likely part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-73100762.translation: For eight days to the incomparable wife.
EDCS-73100762.summary: This inscription is a brief dedication of eight days to a wife, likely commemorating a period after her death or a specific anniversary.

EDCS-73100783.translation: She lived with me, beloved, she denied me nothing. Never in the middle of this wall, on the left side, then the columbarium, to the left of the dining room, adjacent to Mani Acilius Modestus.
EDCS-73100783.summary: This funerary epitaph records a beloved woman who lived with the author and specifies the location of her tomb, adjacent to that of Mani Acilius Modestus.

EDCS-73100784.translation: To Aebutius Diodorus, his most deserving father, and Aebutius Ostiensis, and Aebutia Cale, his very dear son. He lived V. Marcus Aebutius, son of Marcus, and Aebutia Cale, freedwoman of the two Aebutii, Diodorus and his freedwoman, made this, as he asked when dying, for Crescentem and Cale, the well-deserving freedwoman, and for themselves and their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 15 feet in front and 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100784.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Aebutius and Aebutia Cale for their deserving father Diodorus, and other family members, including freedmen and descendants, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-73100786.translation: To Aemilia Ru, to Lucius Aemilius A.m.e, and to Lucius Aemilius Eutyches. His Aelia Gemina, freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73100786.summary: This inscription dedicates a burial plot to Aemilia Ru, Lucius Aemilius, and Lucius Aemilius Eutyches, with the plot being provided by Aelia Gemina for herself, her freedmen, and their descendants.

EDCS-73100787.translation: Caius Annius Nicephorus made this for himself and for his wife Caecilia Licinia, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. And through this gate Aelia Panthea has entrance into his monument, 14 feet in front and 22.5 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100787.summary: This funerary monument was created by Caius Annius Nicephorus for himself, his wife, and descendants, and also grants access through a gate to Aelia Panthea's burial plot, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-73100789.translation: Apusulena Servata, by concession and donation from Iunia Manthis, and also for Plotus Herma, for themselves, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 46 feet in front and 45 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100789.summary: This inscription records the concession and donation of burial plots by Iunia Manthis to Apusulena Servata and Plotus Herma, for themselves, their freedmen, and descendants, with specified dimensions.

EDCS-73100790.translation: Titus Aufidius Antiochus made this for himself and for his wife Antistia Celsina, and for his two Antistii, Victor and Xanthus, and for Sextus Publicius Amethustus, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not pass to an outside heir of the family. 10 feet in front and 13 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100790.summary: This funerary monument was built by Titus Aufidius Antiochus for his family and descendants, stipulating that the property will not pass to external heirs, and providing dimensions.

EDCS-73100791.translation: To the departed gods. Aurelius Hyginus made this for himself and for his wife Ulpia Felicitas, and for his sons, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, by concession from Salinator Ampliatus, the heirs. 30 feet in front and 32 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100791.summary: This funerary monument was created by Aurelius Hyginus for his family and descendants, with the land conceded by Salinator Ampliatus, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-73100792.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a funerary one, indicating that Sextus Ca... made it for himself.

EDCS-73100795.translation: To the departed gods. Decimus Caecilius Musaeus, son, to his most dutiful father, Lucius Cantius Musaaeus. The place was granted by Sextus Melius.
EDCS-73100795.summary: This funerary inscription records Decimus Caecilius Musaeus dedicating a burial plot to his father, Lucius Cantius Musaaeus, with the space granted by Sextus Melius.

EDCS-73100801.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed, given as a donation by Gaius Domitius Trophimus.
EDCS-73100801.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Domitius Trophimus to the 'Dis Manes' (spirits of the dead).

EDCS-73100802.translation: Phoebus, freedman of the freedwoman Publius Durdenius, for himself and for his wife Voltidia, freedwoman of Caius Repentinus, [consecrated] 22 columbaria, in which are 51 ossuary urns, and for his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants and all their posterity and access.
EDCS-73100802.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of 22 columbaria (burial niches) by Phoebus for himself, his wife, and his freedmen and their descendants.

EDCS-73100804.translation: A burial plot granted to the spirits of the departed by Egrilius Polytimus, [in favor of] Aeronia Apolaustus.
EDCS-73100804.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by Egrilius Polytimus to Aeronia Apolaustus, dedicated to the 'Dis Manes'.

EDCS-73100807.translation: For his wife Fabia, [and] for two women [as well?], and for their freedwomen and their descendants, a space 20 feet in front and 22 feet in depth in the land, a monument for himself, granted by Tiberius Claudius Apronius and Octavius Venerius and Claudia Felicitate and Octavius Dionysius.
EDCS-73100807.summary: This inscription details the dimensions of a burial plot granted by several individuals, including Tiberius Claudius Apronius, for themselves and their families, specifying its size and purpose as a monument.

EDCS-73100814.translation: From the left part, a sixth of the property, Aulus Herennuleius Euhemer and Licinia Callirhoe, his wife, for themselves, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-73100814.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Aulus Herennuleius Euhemer and his wife Licinia Callirhoe for themselves and their descendants, stating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-73100816.translation: Gaius Julius Galata made [this] for himself and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, by grant from Alfius and Ianuaria.
EDCS-73100816.summary: Gaius Julius Galata dedicated this funerary monument for himself and his descendants, with permission granted by Alfius and Ianuaria.

EDCS-73100817.translation: For Julia, wife of Gaius Julius [son of] Caius, for Onesima, freedwoman of Julia, his wife, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, whom or which I shall name in my will, 26 feet in front and 26 and a half feet in depth.
EDCS-73100817.summary: This inscription details the dimensions of a burial plot dedicated by Gaius Julius for his wife Julia, his freedwoman Onesima, and other beneficiaries named in his will.

EDCS-73100818.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iunia Felicula granted [permission] to Flavia Tyche that she may be allowed to build a small shrine and to deposit the remains of her husband Gaius Didius Epaphroditus and of their son Caius Didius Florentinus, who lived 17 years, 5 months, and [some] hours.
EDCS-73100818.summary: This inscription records Iunia Felicula granting permission to Flavia Tyche to build a shrine for her deceased husband and son, dedicated to the 'Dis Manes'.

EDCS-73100819.translation: 2 jugera of land which belong to the monument, adjudicated by the sentence of a judge, according to the will of Publius Manius Faustus.
EDCS-73100819.summary: This inscription specifies the amount of land (2 jugera) assigned to a monument, adjudicated by a judge based on the will of Publius Manius Faustus.

EDCS-73100823.translation: To Opius Aebutius, [and] to them, access [is granted] with power.
EDCS-73100823.summary: This fragmented inscription likely concerns access rights or permissions related to a burial plot or property belonging to Opius Aebutius and others.

EDCS-73100824.translation: Lucius Pedanius Onesimus purchased a place in this monument for himself and for his sister Pedania Moschida and for his daughter Pedania Admia, by concession and gift made by Publius Manlius Iucundus and his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument will not pass to an external heir, but half of the plot which is in front of the monument.
EDCS-73100824.summary: This is an epitaph recording the purchase of burial space by Lucius Pedanius Onesimus for himself and his family.

EDCS-73100825.translation: The right to this monument was granted by Plotus.
EDCS-73100825.summary: This is a brief inscription recording the grant of rights to a monument by Plotus.

EDCS-73100828.translation: To the divine shades. Primus made this for his well-deserving wife Kalemera, and one place for himself, granted by Munatia Iusta.
EDCS-73100828.summary: This funerary inscription records Primus dedicating a burial place for his wife Kalemera and himself, with the grant originating from Munatia Iusta.

EDCS-73100829.translation: Sextus Publicius Amethystus and Oppia Rufina, who is also called Tuccia, made this for themselves and their sons, Publicia Augurina and Publicia Capitolina, and for Maior Publicius, and for those who will be born after them, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants whom our sons will choose, in front 23 feet, in the field 10 feet.
EDCS-73100829.summary: This epitaph details the construction of a family tomb by Sextus Publicius Amethystus and Oppia Rufina, specifying the dimensions and beneficiaries of the burial plot.

EDCS-73100831.translation: for herself and for her husband Rufinus.
EDCS-73100831.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely part of a funerary dedication for Rufinus and his spouse.

EDCS-73100835.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely a dedication or ownership marker belonging to Lucius Antistius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-73100836.translation: Marcus Antonius Alexander the younger made this for himself and his family and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, in front 9 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-73100836.summary: This epitaph records the construction of a tomb by Marcus Antonius Alexander the younger for himself, his family, and their freed dependants, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-73100837.translation: To the divine shades. Marcus Antonius Barbarus lived 1 year, 11 months, 28 days. Antoni's two children Nilus and Barbara for their son.
EDCS-73100837.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Marcus Antonius Barbarus, noting his lifespan, and appears to be set up by his parents.

EDCS-73100839.translation: To the divine shades. For Afrodisia, a slave girl of Aretio, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-73100839.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Afrodisia, a slave, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-73100840.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely recording the names of two individuals, possibly associated with a monument or dedication.

EDCS-73100841.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Volusia C. [dedicated this] to her freedman Publius Asinius, son of Publius.
EDCS-73100841.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedman, made by a woman, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100842.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Her parents made this for their most beloved daughter, Attia Celiria, who lived for two years, nine months, and one day.
EDCS-73100842.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Attia Celiria, erected by her parents, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100844.translation: Marcus Aulius Merulus, who lived for twenty years, ten months, and [some days].
EDCS-73100844.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of Marcus Aulius Merulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100848.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Fortunatus.
EDCS-73100848.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tiberius Claudius Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100849.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Theophilus.
EDCS-73100849.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tiberius Claudius Theophilus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100850.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Claudia Philematis.
EDCS-73100850.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Claudia Philematis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100851.translation: Aulus Cominius, freedman of Aulus, made [this] for Vallia.
EDCS-73100851.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Aulus Cominius, a freedman, to a person named Vallia, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100855.translation: To father Euplius, freedman, and steo [---].
EDCS-73100855.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication possibly for a father and freedman, with an unclear final word, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100858.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name Fabius Primigenius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100861.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Felix made [this] for Vitalis, his dearest slave.
EDCS-73100861.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Felix to his slave Vitalis, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73100863.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata, daughter of Helicis.

EDCS-73100864.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Fructuosus lived 5 months and 20 days. His parents [dedicated this] to their sweetest son.
EDCS-73100864.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fructuosus, who died at a very young age, dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-73100868.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Grattius Felix made this to the memory of Lucius Grattius Felix, to his most excellent and deserving father.
EDCS-73100868.summary: This funerary inscription records Grattius Felix dedicating a monument to his deceased father, Lucius Grattius Felix.

EDCS-73100871.translation: Herennia Rufa, daughter of Decimus, for herself and her family. Caius Tutilius Plocamianus, freedman of the Caians, [dedicated this land, measuring] 20 feet in front and 25 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100871.summary: This inscription seems to record a land division or grant associated with Herennia Rufa and Caius Tutilius Plocamianus, likely for funerary purposes, given the context of Roman inscriptions.

EDCS-73100876.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Logismo.
EDCS-73100876.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription dedicated to someone named Logismo.

EDCS-73100878.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Marius Hermes and Maria Philaenis made [this] for Maria Marulla, for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-73100878.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Marius Hermes and Maria Philaenis dedicating a monument to Maria Marulla and their descendants.

EDCS-73100879.translation: Muccia, freedwoman of Aulus, and Lucius Mussidius Herma, parents, made [this].
EDCS-73100879.summary: This funerary inscription records Muccia and Lucius Mussidius Herma, identified as parents, dedicating a monument.

EDCS-73100880.translation: Noni made [this] for his son, who lived 6 years and 3 months and [some] days.
EDCS-73100880.summary: This funerary inscription records Noni dedicating a monument to his son who died at the age of 6 years and 3 months.

EDCS-73100881.translation: Fausta, freedwoman of Mani and Aponia, [dedicated this to] Lucius Cornelius Oppidanus, son of Lucius, of the Anienses.
EDCS-73100881.summary: This inscription seems to record Fausta, a freedwoman, dedicating something to Lucius Cornelius Oppidanus, identifying him by his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-73100882.translation: To Octavia, my dearest wife, and to her freedmen and freedwomen.
EDCS-73100882.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by a husband to his wife, Octavia, and also includes her freed slaves.

EDCS-73100883.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Loratius Asclepius made this for Nomenia, his freedwoman, who deserved well.
EDCS-73100883.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Loratius Asclepius to his freedwoman Nomenia.

EDCS-73100887.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Marcus Popilius Asclepiodotus, who lived 8 years, 5 months, and 20 days. Marcus Popilius Achilleus the elder, to his foster-son.
EDCS-73100887.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, Marcus Popilius Asclepiodotus, set up by his foster-father.

EDCS-73100889.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Rubria Marc, his patroness, and for himself and Vatia Firma.
EDCS-73100889.summary: A funerary dedication potentially by a freedman for his patroness and his family.

EDCS-73100891.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Sualia Thiophila.
EDCS-73100891.summary: A very brief funerary dedication for Sualia Thiophila.

EDCS-73100892.translation: Trop made this for Ragonia Philete, who deserved well.
EDCS-73100892.summary: A dedication of a monument by Trop for Ragonia Philete.

EDCS-73100897.translation: In the forum. Marcus Ulpius TRESISE.
EDCS-73100897.summary: A fragmentary inscription that seems to identify a person, Marcus Ulpius, within a public space.

EDCS-73100915.summary: A very fragmentary inscription that appears to be part of a personal or family name.

EDCS-73100916.summary: An inscription consisting solely of the repetition of the praenomen 'Marcus'.

EDCS-73100933.translation: Caecilius Felicissimus donated two plots, one below, one above, on the right side, to Lucius Cornelius Ianuarius and Antonia Prima.
EDCS-73100933.summary: A property donation by Caecilius Felicissimus to Lucius Cornelius Ianuarius and Antonia Prima.

EDCS-73100995.translation: Septimia Successa, freedwoman of Caius, made this for herself, for her patron Caius Septimius Philocalus, for her daughter Septimia Hipora, for her slave and freedwoman Septimia Felicitas, and for their descendants; this monument shall not pass to an heir or an outside family. In front 20 feet, in the field 10 feet.
EDCS-73100995.summary: A complex funerary monument dedication by Septimia Successa for herself and her family and dependents, specifying property dimensions and inheritance restrictions.

EDCS-73100996.translation: Gnaeus Sergius Herma, freedman of Gnaeus, made this monument for himself, his dearest wife Apidia Felicula, his son Quintus Apidius Herma, and his daughter Sergia Anthis; it will not pass to an heir outside the family; for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73100996.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman for himself and his family, stipulating that the inheritance will not go to an external heir.

EDCS-73100997.translation: To the departed spirits. For Publius Sextius Fotinus, who lived 8 years, 7 months, and 11 days. Iulia Rodia gave this place, a most sweet granddaughter, to him from the heirs of Egrilius Polytimus, and also above him to the same Rodia or to her husband Iulius Uniachus.
EDCS-73100997.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial place for a young boy, Publius Sextius Fotinus, with details about its allocation by his granddaughter.

EDCS-73100999.translation: [...]tius, freedman of Quintus, made this monument for himself, his wife Syntyche, freedwoman of Marcus, most holy, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants; it will not pass to a family member or an outsider; 12 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-73100999.summary: This is a funerary monument established by a freedman for himself, his wife, and their descendants, with specified dimensions for the plot.

EDCS-73101002.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tychicus, with the consent of his fellow workers, who deserved well.
EDCS-73101002.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring a deceased colleague named Tychicus.

EDCS-73101004.translation: To the departed spirits. For Valeria Candida, daughter of Marcus, who lived 35 years. Titus Antonius Faustinus made this for his most holy wife. 8 feet in front, 10 feet in the field. The place was given by Scantius Priscus.
EDCS-73101004.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, specifying dimensions and the source of the plot.

EDCS-73101005.translation: To the departed spirits. For Valeria Epictesis. A place granted to herself by Naevia Iusta.
EDCS-73101005.summary: A funerary inscription recording a burial plot granted to Valeria Epictesis by Naevia Iusta.

EDCS-73101010.translation: Half of a monument, a facade with a tomb, granted to herself and her son Iulianus, and to her freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-73101010.summary: This inscription records the grant of half of a funerary monument, including its facade and tomb, to a mother and son and their descendants.

EDCS-73101012.translation: For himself and his wife Alria, and for his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants. This monument will not pass to an heir unless the freedmen of the freedmen fail. 27 feet in front, 35 feet in the field, and outside the monument's enclosure, near the public road, 13.5 feet in front, 18 feet in the field.
EDCS-73101012.summary: This funerary monument, with extensive dimensions specified, is for the owner, his wife, and their freedmen and their descendants, with a condition for inheritance.

EDCS-73101014.translation: [...]us, freedman of a woman, was buried.
EDCS-73101014.summary: A brief funerary notice indicating that a freedman was buried here.

EDCS-73101017.translation: Upon entering on the left side, for Icianus, who placed [this].
EDCS-73101017.summary: This inscription likely marks a location or dedicates a space on the left side, possibly for Icianus.

EDCS-73101018.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or an inventory label, possibly related to offerings or supplies, of unknown date.

EDCS-73101046.translation: You are generous with kindness, but malicious.
EDCS-73101046.summary: This inscription seems to be a personal epitaph or a curse, of unknown date, expressing a complex sentiment about the deceased or an individual.

EDCS-73400413.translation: To Aurelia Procula, my sweetest mother.
EDCS-73400413.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aurelia Procula by a descendant, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73400452.translation: Of Furius Placidus, a man of consular rank.
EDCS-73400452.summary: This inscription likely refers to Furius Placidus, a distinguished individual, possibly on a monument or a legal document, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73700038.translation: Here rests in peace John, a presbyter, born in the city of Naples and raised in the church of Misenum.
EDCS-73700038.summary: This is a Christian epitaph dating from the post-classical or early medieval period, identifying the deceased and his origins.

EDCS-73800025.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucia Papiria made this for Carisia Maxima, who lived 81 years, her well-deserving mother.
EDCS-73800025.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, dedicated by a daughter to her mother.

EDCS-73800068.translation: Gaius Gaius Gaius Musa, received on the 4th day before the Nones of November, the 6th day before the Ides, the 14th day before the Kalends of March, the 14th day before the Kalends of April, the 3rd day before the Kalends of February, received on the 14th day before the Kalends of September. First distribution of grain. Menophilos, Master; Menophilus, Governor of Eusebeias.
EDCS-73800068.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of grain distribution and appointments, possibly related to a religious or civic office, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73800070.translation: Brixus Amonius, first Flamen Dialis of Tusculum.
EDCS-73800070.summary: This is an inscription identifying Brixus Amonius as the chief priest (Flamen Dialis) of Tusculum, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73800078.translation: Lucius Hostius Gentilis, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-73800078.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or a name inscription identifying Lucius Hostius Gentilis as a freedman, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-73800079.translation: The most excellent man Narsis made this.
EDCS-73800079.summary: This inscription records a dedication or commission by an individual named Narsis, described as 'most excellent', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-74100193.translation: From the Quintanensian estates of Rupilia Faustina, belonging to Decimus Rupilius Doretus.
EDCS-74100193.summary: This inscription records ownership of estates belonging to Rupilia Faustina and Decimus Rupilius Doretus.

EDCS-74100346.translation: Aliffa Termanus dedicated this to Diana Salutaris, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-74100346.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana Salutaris by Aliffa Termanus.

EDCS-74200242.summary: This is a fragment likely recording a dedication to Aphrodite by Menippus.

EDCS-74200309.translation: Earthenware produced from the imperial estates of our Emperors, from the Domitian workshops of Lanius Fortunatus.
EDCS-74200309.summary: This inscription indicates the origin and producer of earthenware from imperial workshops, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-74200605.translation: Gaius Curius, son of Lucius, of the Aemilian tribe.
EDCS-74200605.summary: This is a brief personal inscription identifying Gaius Curius, son of Lucius, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-74700675.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that possibly starts with the name Tiberius.

EDCS-74700681.summary: This inscription appears to be a name, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication by Decimus Laberius Karii, referring to Hermes.

EDCS-74800011.translation: Gaius Quinctius Valgus, son of Caius, and Marcius Porcius, son of Marcius, who held the office of duoviri quinquennales, arranged for the construction of spectacles at their own expense for the honor of the colony and granted the location to the colonists in perpetuity.
EDCS-74800011.summary: This inscription records that two officials, Gaius Quinctius Valgus and Marcius Porcius, funded and provided the site for public spectacles in the colony, likely during their term as duoviri quinquennales.

EDCS-74800032.translation: Lucius Bovius Celer, son of Lucius, from the Falernian tribe, [dedicated this] to his most excellent father, Lucius Bovius Pamphilus.
EDCS-74800032.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription dedicated by Lucius Bovius Celer to his father, Lucius Bovius Pamphilus.

EDCS-74800158.translation: Marcus Novius Tubero, son of Marcus, Tribune of the Plebs, willingly fulfilled his vow with his own money.
EDCS-74800158.summary: This inscription records Marcus Novius Tubero, a Tribune of the Plebs, fulfilling a vow at his own expense.

EDCS-74800488.translation: To Gaius Staius Victor, who lived for one year, ten months, and eleven days, Gaius Staius Priscus and Staia Nysias made this for their sweetest son.
EDCS-74800488.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument dedicated by parents to their young son, Gaius Staius Victor, providing his exact age at death.

EDCS-74900279.summary: This brief inscription marks the burial place of Culcia Iucunda.

EDCS-74900282.translation: Lucius Caesius Bassus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-74900282.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, likely for a tombstone, identifying Lucius Caesius Bassus and his father.

EDCS-74900283.summary: This inscription records the maker of a monument, Marcus Primigenius Fortunatus.

EDCS-74900286.translation: Of Publius Scribonius, son of Lucius Egnatius, decurions.
EDCS-74900286.summary: This inscription likely refers to a public office held by Publius Scribonius, son of Lucius Egnatius, as a decurion (a member of a council).

EDCS-74900287.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Trebius Capito and his position as a duovir, a chief magistrate in a Roman colony or municipality.

EDCS-74900290.summary: This inscription likely refers to a monument or property belonging to Magulnus in his capacity as quaestor, a financial official.

EDCS-74900295.translation: From the workshop of Titus Trebius.
EDCS-74900295.summary: This inscription indicates that the object or structure it is on was made in the workshop of Titus Trebius.

EDCS-75000099.translation: For Callistus, for himself, his family, and their descendants.
EDCS-75000099.summary: This inscription is a dedication for a tomb or monument, intended for Callistus, his family, and future generations.

EDCS-75000101.translation: Statius made this burial plot for himself, his descendants, and for Pomponia, his daughter and patroness.
EDCS-75000101.summary: This funerary inscription records Statius reserving a burial plot for himself, his heirs, and his daughter, Pomponia, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-75000102.translation: Apro, a freedman of Aefria, and Daphne, a freedwoman of Marcus Hirtius.
EDCS-75000102.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apro and Daphne, who were freedpersons.

EDCS-75000120.translation: Alexander Hilarus and the freedmen of Marcus Regillus have seen to the making of this at their own expense for Gaius Vesidius, son of Gaius, aedile and quaestor.
EDCS-75000120.summary: This is a dedication of a public work funded by freedmen for the magistrate Gaius Vesidius.

EDCS-75000323.translation: Of Marcus Priamus, freedman of Marcus, 24 feet in front and 12 feet in the ground.
EDCS-75000323.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Marcus Priamus, a freedman.

EDCS-75000324.summary: This is a self-dedication by Heraclius, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-75200025.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Tiberius Claudius Amphio.

EDCS-75200033.translation: Four vessels weighing 4.5 pounds, 6 scruples, belonging to Marcus Attius Clarus.
EDCS-75200033.summary: This inscription lists the weight and quantity of vessels owned by Marcus Attius Clarus.

EDCS-75200040.translation: Four vessels weighing 3 pounds, 4 scruples, belonging to Pamphilus, freedman of Caesar.
EDCS-75200040.summary: This inscription lists the weight and quantity of vessels belonging to Pamphilus, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-75200041.translation: Four vessels weighing 3 pounds, 4 scruples, belonging to Pamphilus, freedman of Caesar.
EDCS-75200041.summary: This inscription lists the weight and quantity of vessels belonging to Pamphilus, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-75200042.translation: Four vessels weighing 3 pounds, 4 scruples, belonging to Pamphilus, freedman of Caesar.
EDCS-75200042.summary: This inscription lists the weight and quantity of vessels belonging to Pamphilus, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-75200043.translation: Four vessels weighing 3 pounds, 4 scruples, belonging to Pamphilus, freedman of Caesar.
EDCS-75200043.summary: This inscription lists the weight and quantity of vessels belonging to Pamphilus, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-75200048.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Maxima, wife of Tubertus.

EDCS-75200053.translation: To our Maxima, to our Maxima.
EDCS-75200053.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a person named Maxima, possibly a local deity or a venerated individual.

EDCS-75200055.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Maxima, with the repeated letters 'STL' possibly representing a title or abbreviation.

EDCS-75200056.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Maxima, with the abbreviation 'STL' possibly indicating a specific role or status.

EDCS-82800042.translation: Callinice, greetings; may you live, may you prosper, gladiator.
EDCS-82800042.summary: This is a greeting or epitaph for Callinice, a gladiator, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-82900060.translation: Here lies Martinianus, an honorable man of high rank in the city; he departed from this life.
EDCS-82900060.summary: This is an epitaph for Martinianus, an honorable and prominent citizen, likely dating to the late Roman period.
